children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Hara</s>, to <s>Brahmā</s>, to the supreme self,
to the lord of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), who brings about creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
After worshipping <s>Śaṅkara</s> at <s>Śaileśa</s> and <s>Saṅgameśvara</s>,
at <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Svarlīna</s>, <s>Avimukta</s>, and <s>Mahālaya</s>,

children.text: raudre goprekṣake caiva śreṣṭhe pāśupate tathā
children.translated_text: at <s>Raudra</s>, <s>Goprekṣaka</s>, the excellent shrine, and likewise at <s>Pāśupata</s>,
at <s>Vighneśvara</s>, <s>Kedāra</s>, and at <s>Gomāyukeśvara</s>,
at <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Candreśa</s>, <s>Īśānya</s>, and <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>,
and at <s>Śukreśvara</s>, duly and in order, the sage went to <s>Naimiṣa</s>.
Then the sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, seeing <s>Nārada</s>, were delighted in mind.
After honoring him properly, they prepared for him a seat suitable to him.

children.text: so'pi hṛṣṭo munivarair dattaṃ bheje tadāsanam
children.translated_text: He too, delighted, occupied the seat then given by the best of sages.
Being honored by the sages, he sat comfortably on the excellent seat.
He began a discourse of varied meaning, concerned with the greatness of the <s>liṅga</s>.
At just that time, <s>Sūta</s> himself, the reciter of Purāṇas,
the wise one, went to <s>Naimiṣa</s> in order to pay homage to the ascetics.

children.text: tasmai sāma ca pūjāṃ ca yathāvaccakrire tadā ||
children.translated_text: At that time they duly offered him welcome and worship.
Then the sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s> approached the disciple of <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>
with a desire to hear the Purāṇa from him.
Seeing that learned <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> to be exceedingly trustworthy,
all the sages rich in austerity then asked <s>Sūta</s>, the seer,
about the holy Purāṇa-saṃhitā joined with the greatness of the <s>liṅga</s>.
The sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s> said:
O <s>Sūta</s> of great understanding, the sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>
was formerly attended by you for the sake of the meaning of the Purāṇas, and from him you obtained the compendium.
Therefore we ask you, revered <s>Sūta</s>, best of Purāṇic reciters,
about the divine Purāṇa-saṃhitā joined with the greatness of the <s>liṅga</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> too has reached the sacred places of this god, <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme self,
and, having worshipped the <s>liṅgas</s>, O foremost sage,

children.text: iha saṃnihitaḥ śrīmān nārado brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the illustrious <s>Nārada</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, is present here.
He is devoted to <s>Bhava</s>; so are you, and so are we, and so is <s>Nārada</s>.
In the presence of this sage, you ought to recite the holy Purāṇa.

children.text: saphalaṃ sādhitaṃ sarvaṃ bhavatā viditaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Everything accomplished by you would then become fruitful and known.
Thus addressed, that delighted <s>Sūta</s>, the best of Purāṇic reciters,
the wise and holy one, after bowing before <s>Nārada</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>,
and before the sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, expounded the Purāṇa.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s>, to <s>Brahmā</s>, and to <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: munīśvaraṃ tathā vyāsaṃ vaktuṃ liṅgaṃ smarāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: and likewise to the lord of sages, <s>Vyāsa</s>, I call to mind the <s>liṅga</s> in order to speak.
It is sound, directly the body of <s>Brahman</s>, revealing the word-<s>Brahman</s>,
made up of phonemic elements, having the marks of the unmanifest, and established in many forms.
It is the syllables a, u, and m; gross, subtle, beyond the highest,
in the form of <s>oṃkāra</s>, with the <s>Ṛgveda</s> as its mouth and endowed with the <s>Sāmaveda</s> as its tongue.
It is the mighty lord with the <s>Yajurveda</s> as its great neck and the <s>Atharvaveda</s> as its heart,
beyond <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>, free from dissolution and origination.
Through <s>tamas</s> it is called <s>Kālarudra</s>; through <s>rajas</s> it is the golden egg-born one,
through <s>sattva</s> it is all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>; in its qualityless state it is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Having pervaded the constituents of <s>pradhāna</s>, it stands successively in sevenfold form,
and again also in sixteenfold form, and as the twenty-sixth principle, born from the unborn.
It assumes the form of the <s>liṅga</s> for the play of creation, establishment, and dissolution.

children.text: praṇamya ca yathānyāyaṃ vakṣye liṅgodbhavaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Having duly bowed to it, I shall tell the auspicious origin of the <s>liṅga</s>.
Thus ends the first chapter in the holy great <s>Laiṅga Purāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Taking as its subject the events of the <s>Īśāna</s> kalpa,

children.text: brahmaṇā kalpitaṃ pūrvaṃ purāṇaṃ laiṅgam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: the excellent <s>Laiṅga Purāṇa</s> was formerly composed by great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>.
Its measure was a crore of granthas, spread out over a hundred crores,
but it was abridged to four lakhs by the <s>Vyāsas</s> in every interval.
Divided tenfold in the Dvāpara ages beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: liṅgamekādaśaṃ proktaṃ mayā vyāsācchrutaṃ ca tat ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Liṅga</s> is said to be the eleventh; I heard that from <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Here, O twice-born sages, its textual measure is eleven thousand granthas.

children.text: tasmātsaṃkṣepato vakṣye na śrutaṃ vistareṇa yat ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall speak concisely what has not been heard in full detail.
Though it was abridged to four lakhs by <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>,
the arising of the <s>liṅga</s> is taught here in eleven thousand granthas.

children.text: sargaḥ prādhānikaḥ paścāt prākṛto vaikṛtāni ca
children.translated_text: First comes the creation from <s>pradhāna</s>, then the elemental creation and the derivative creations,
the origin of this cosmic egg and the eight coverings of the egg,
the egg-born state of <s>Śarva</s> because of his dependence on the quality of <s>rajas</s>,

children.text: viṣṇutvaṃ kālarudratvaṃ śayanaṃ cāpsu tasya ca ||
children.translated_text: his becoming <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Kālarudra</s>, and his lying in the waters,
the creation of the Prajāpatis and also the raising up of the earth,
and again the reckoning of <s>Brahmā</s>'s day and night and of his lifespan,

children.text: savanaṃ brahmaṇaścaiva yugakalpaś ca tasya tu
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Brahmā</s>'s pressing rite and his yuga and kalpa,

children.text: divyaṃ ca mānuṣaṃ varṣamārṣaṃ vai dhrauvyameva ca ||
children.translated_text: the divine year, the human year, the seer-year, and the year of <s>Dhruva</s>,
the ancestral year, the origin of the ancestors, and the <s>dharma</s> of those in the life-stages,
then the further non-growth of the world and the arising of the Goddess's power,
the female and male state of <s>Viriñca</s> and the creation arising from pairs,
the set of eight names of <s>Rudra</s>, told after his weeping,
the dispute between <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and again the manifestation of the <s>liṅga</s>,
the austerity of <s>Śilāda</s> and likewise the vision of the foe of <s>Vṛtra</s>,
then the prayer concerning a womb-born son and the difficulty of obtaining such a son,
the dialogue of <s>Śilāda</s> and <s>Śakra</s>, and his birth from the lotus-womb.
And the vision of <s>Bhava</s>, as well as that of teacher and pupil in the <s>Tiṣya</s> periods;
and likewise the incarnations of <s>Vyāsa</s>, the <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic aeons), and the <s>manvantaras</s> (Manu-intervals).
The state of being a <s>kalpa</s>, and the <s>kalpas</s> themselves, according to the differences of their names, in order;

children.text: kalpeṣu kalpe vārāhe vārāhatvaṃ hares tathā ||
children.translated_text: and, among the <s>kalpas</s>, in the <s>Varāha</s> <s>kalpa</s>, <s>Hari</s>'s becoming the Boar as well.
The account of the <s>Meghavāhana</s> <s>kalpa</s>, and the greatness of <s>Rudra</s>;
and again the arising of the <s>liṅga</s> of <s>Pinākin</s> in the midst of the sages.
The worship of the <s>liṅga</s>, the procedure for bathing it, and the marks of purity;
and the greatness of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, with a description of the greatness of the sacred field.

children.text: bhuvi rudrālayānāṃ tu saṃkhyā viṣṇorgṛhasya ca
children.translated_text: The number of <s>Rudra</s>'s shrines on earth, and of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s abode;
and in the mid-region and in this cosmic egg, the description of the temples of the gods.
The fall of <s>Dakṣa</s> upon the earth, again in the <s>Svārociṣa</s> interval;
and <s>Dakṣa</s>'s curse, and likewise <s>Dakṣa</s>'s release from the curse.
The description of <s>Kailāsa</s>, and likewise <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga;
the measure of the four <s>yugas</s>, and the <s>yuga-dharma</s> in great detail.
The measure of the twilight portions, and the twilight observance of <s>Bhava</s>;
his dwelling in the cremation ground, and the origin of the crescent moon.
Then the marriage of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, and the begetting of a son;
and the danger, the fear of the destruction of the worlds, through excessive attachment to sexual union.

children.text: śāpaḥ satyā kṛto devānpurā viṣṇuṃ ca pālitam
children.translated_text: The curse placed by <s>Satī</s> upon the gods, and the former protection connected with <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
and the emission of <s>Rudra</s>'s seed, and the birth of <s>Gāṅgeya</s>.

children.text: grahaṇādiṣu kāleṣu snāpya liṅgaṃ phalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: At times such as eclipses, the fruit gained after bathing the <s>liṅga</s>;

children.text: kṣubdhadhī ca vivādaś ca dadhīcopendrayos tathā ||
children.translated_text: and the agitation and dispute between <s>Dadhīci</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.
The origin of the one named <s>Nandin</s>, belonging to the god of gods, the wielder of the trident;
the story of the devoted wife, and the examination of the <s>paśu</s> and <s>pāśa</s> (bound soul and bond).
Knowledge marked by engagement in action, and likewise that which is concerned with withdrawal;
the origin of the sons of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the noble <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>.
The expanded lineage of the sages, and the destruction of <s>Śakti</s> by the king;
then the wickedness of <s>Kauśika</s>, and the binding of <s>Surabhi</s>.
The grief of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> for his son, and the lamentation of <s>Arundhatī</s>;

children.text: snuṣāyāḥ preṣaṇaṃ caiva garbhasthasya vacas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the sending away of the daughter-in-law, and likewise the speech of the child in the womb.
The incarnation of <s>Parāśara</s>, and of <s>Vyāsa</s> and <s>Śuka</s>;

children.text: vināśo rākṣasānāṃ ca kṛto vai śaktisūnunā ||
children.translated_text: and the destruction of the <s>rākṣasas</s>, carried out by the son of <s>Śakti</s>.
The highest truth concerning the deity, and knowledge through grace;
and the making of the <s>Purāṇa</s> at the command of the teacher <s>Pulastya</s>.

children.text: bhuvanānāṃ pramāṇaṃ ca grahāṇāṃ jyotiṣāṃ gatiḥ
children.translated_text: The measure of the worlds, and the motion of the planets and lights;
the procedure for <s>jīvacchrāddha</s>, those fit for <s>śrāddha</s>, and <s>śrāddha</s> itself.
The procedure for <s>nāndīśrāddha</s>, and likewise the marks of study;
the power of the five sacrifices, and also the procedure of the five sacrifices.
The conduct of menstruating women, and the special excellence of sons according to conduct;
and the rule for sexual union, in order, according to each <s>varṇa</s>.
The prescription of what may and may not be eaten for all members of the <s>varṇas</s>;
and expiation for everything, separately and in detail.
The nature of the hells, and punishment according to deeds;
and the marks, in later births, of men who have been in heaven or hell.
Various kinds of gifts, and the city of the king of the dead;
then the rite of the five-syllabled mantra, and the greatness of <s>Rudra</s>.
The great battle of <s>Vṛtra</s> and <s>Indra</s>, and the destruction of <s>Viśvarūpa</s>;
the dialogue of <s>Śveta</s> with Death, and the destruction of <s>Kāla</s> for <s>Śveta</s>'s sake.
The entrance of <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, into the <s>Devadāru</s> forest;
the story of <s>Sudarśana</s>, and the marks of gradual renunciation.
And how <s>Rudra</s> is attainable through faith was then told by <s>Brahmā</s>;
and how, long ago, by <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>, the Lord's course was taken away.
<s>Hari</s>'s becoming a fish in order to recover the supreme knowledge of <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: sarvāvasthāsu viṣṇoś ca jananaṃ līlayaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s birth, in all conditions, simply through divine play.
Through <s>Rudra</s>'s favor, the coming into being of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and of <s>Jiṣṇu</s>;
and <s>Hari</s>'s becoming a tortoise for the purpose of supporting the churning.
The origin of <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, and the rebirth of <s>Kauśikī</s>;

children.text: yadūnāṃ caiva sambhūtir yādavatvaṃ hareḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: the arising of the <s>Yadus</s>, and <s>Hari</s> himself becoming a <s>Yādava</s>.
The wickedness of the <s>Bhoja</s> king, the maternal uncle of the mighty <s>Hari</s>;
<s>Hari</s>'s play in childhood, and his worship of <s>Śaṃkara</s> for the sake of a son.
And likewise the origin of <s>Nara</s>, from <s>Hara</s>, from a skull connected with <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
and <s>Hari</s>'s worship of <s>Rudra</s> for the purpose of removing the burden of the earth.
The ancient institution of milking the earth by <s>Pṛthu</s>, son of <s>Vena</s>;

children.text: devāsure purā labdho bhṛguśāpaś ca viṣṇunā ||
children.translated_text: and the curse of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, formerly received by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the conflict of gods and demons.

children.text: kṛṣṇatve dvārakāyāṃ tu nilayo mādhavasya tu
children.translated_text: In his state as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the residence of <s>Mādhava</s> in <s>Dvārakā</s>;
and the curse obtained from the mouth of <s>Durvāsas</s> for <s>Hari</s>'s benefit.
The curse of the residents of <s>Piṇḍāraka</s> for the destruction of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> and <s>Andhakas</s>;
and the arising of <s>eraka</s> reeds, and the origin of the club.
When the <s>eraka</s> reeds had been obtained, their mutual quarrel and the conflict of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>;

children.text: līlayā caiva kṛṣṇena svakulasya ca saṃhṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the destruction of his own clan by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as an act of play.
By the power of the <s>eraka</s> weapons, his departure entirely by his own will;
and the very extensive knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> and liberation.
Of <s>Andhaka</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Dakṣa</s> in former times, and of <s>Śakra</s> in elephant and deer forms;
of <s>Madana</s>, of the primal god, of <s>Brahmā</s>, and of the enemies of the immortals;
and the contempt shown toward <s>Pinākin</s> by the <s>Hālāhala</s> demon.
The slaying of <s>Jālaṃdhara</s>, and the origin of <s>Sudarśana</s>;
<s>Viṣṇu</s>'s acquisition of excellent weapons, and likewise the action of <s>Rudra</s>.
And likewise the other deeds of <s>Rudra</s>, by the thousands,
and then the majesty of <s>Hara</s>, of <s>Pitāmaha</s>, and of great-souled <s>Śakra</s>,
and the power and experience of them, and the description of <s>Śiva</s>'s world,

children.text: bhūmau rudrasya lokaṃ ca pātāle hāṭakeśvaram
children.translated_text: the world of <s>Rudra</s> on earth, and <s>Hāṭakeśvara</s> in the netherworld,

children.text: tapasāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ caiva dvijānāṃ vaibhavaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the marks of austerities, and likewise the greatness of the twice-born,
the superiority of all forms, especially of the <s>liṅga</s> form,
all this is recounted in this <s>Liṅga</s>, in due order and at length.
Having learned this summary of the Purāṇa, whoever recites it
goes to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, freed from every sin.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The <s>aliṅga</s> (signless principle) is the root of the <s>liṅga</s>; the unmanifest is called the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: aliṅgaḥ śiva ityukto liṅgaṃ śaivamiti smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>aliṅga</s> is called <s>Śiva</s>, and the <s>liṅga</s> is remembered as belonging to <s>Śiva</s>.
What they call <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>prakṛti</s> is the supreme <s>liṅga</s>,
devoid of smell, color, and taste, and free from sound, touch, and the rest.
Without qualities, firm, imperishable, signless, it has the marks of <s>Śiva</s>.
That which is endowed with smell, color, and taste, and characterized by sound, touch, and the rest,
the womb of the world, the great element, both gross and subtle, O best of twice-borns,
the embodied form of the worlds, that <s>liṅga</s> arose by itself from the <s>aliṅga</s>.
Sevenfold, eightfold, and again elevenfold,
the <s>liṅgas</s> of the <s>aliṅga</s> were spread out by <s>māyā</s>.
From them there came to be a triad of principal gods, having the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.
From one, the universe came forth in three; by one it was protected.

children.text: ekenaiva hṛtaṃ viśvaṃ vyāptaṃ tvevaṃ śivena tu
children.translated_text: By one alone the universe was withdrawn, and in this way it is pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: aliṅgaṃ caiva liṅgaṃ ca liṅgāliṅgāni mūrtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>aliṅga</s>, the <s>liṅga</s>, and the forms that are both <s>liṅga</s> and <s>aliṅga</s>
have been described as they truly are; therefore <s>Brahman</s> itself is the world.

children.text: aliṅgī bhagavān bījī sa eva parameśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The signless Lord, possessing the seed, is that very supreme Lord.

children.text: bījaṃ yoniś ca nirbījaṃ nirbījo bījamucyate
children.translated_text: The seed, the womb, and the seedless: the seedless is called the seed.
Here the self called by that name abides among seed, womb, and <s>pradhāna</s>.
The supreme self, the sage, <s>Brahman</s>, by nature eternally awakened,

children.text: viśuddho 'yaṃ tathā rudraḥ purāṇe śiva ucyate ||
children.translated_text: is this pure one; likewise <s>Rudra</s> is called <s>Śiva</s> in the Purāṇa.
When <s>prakṛti</s> was seen by <s>Śiva</s>, it became Śaiva, O twice-borns.
At the beginning of creation, though formerly unmanifest by nature, she became endowed with the <s>guṇas</s>.
From the unmanifest down to the differentiated particulars, the universe arose from her.

children.text: viśvadhātrī tvajākhyā ca śaivī sā prakṛtiḥ smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: She, the bearer of the universe and called the unborn, is remembered as Śaiva <s>prakṛti</s>.
That unborn one, red, white, black, single yet bearing many offspring,
the progenitress, he lay beside, enjoying her who had his own form.
And that same unborn one another unborn leaves behind, after she has enjoyed experience.
The unborn progenitress of the worlds, established by the unborn one,
manifested as the great principle, under the governance of the <s>puruṣa</s>,
by command of the unborn one, at the time of creation of <s>pradhāna</s>, with the three <s>guṇas</s>.
Impelled by the desire to create, entering the imperishable unmanifest,
the great principle, governed by the self, transforms itself into manifest creation.
From the great principle there is its activity, consisting in conception and determination.
From that three-quality great principle arose <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), dominated by rajas.
And properly covered by that, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> dominated by tamas
became the creator of the elements and <s>tanmātras</s> from the great principle.
From <s>ahaṃkāra</s> came the mere sound-potential; from that came imperishable ether.
Then it enveloped ether together with sound, ether being the cause of sound.
Thus the creation of the elements from the <s>tanmātra</s> has been proclaimed to you, O twice-borns.
Likewise from ether came the mere touch-potential; from that came the great wind, O sage.
From that came the mere form-potential, then fire; from that came taste.
From taste came the auspicious waters, and from them the mere smell-potential; then came earth.
And so ether enveloped the mere touch-potential, O best of twice-borns.
Wind, active by nature, enveloped the mere form-potential.
The god <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, fire himself, enveloped the mere taste-potential.
The waters, whose nature is all tastes, enveloped the mere smell-potential.
Therefore earth has five qualities; those born from taste are one less.
The blessed fire has three qualities, and that born from touch has two qualities.
Then the deity that is space has only one measure and is without parts.
The creation of the elements from the <s>tanmātras</s> should be understood in their mutual relation.
The modified, sāttvika creation proceeds all at once,
and even so creation from <s>ahaṃkāra</s> is proclaimed here in this way.
Its five organs of knowledge and five organs of action
exist for the apprehension of sound and the other objects, and the mind is of both kinds.
The principles from <s>mahat</s> down to the differentiated particulars produce the cosmic egg.
From it, like from a bubble in water, <s>Pitāmaha</s> descended.

children.text: sa eva bhagavān rudro viṣṇurviśvagataḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: He himself is the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-pervading Lord.
Within that egg are these worlds and this entire universe.
The egg is covered outside by water ten times greater than it.
The waters, ten times greater, are covered outside by fire.
The fire, ten times greater, is covered outside by wind.
The wind, ten times greater, is covered outside by space.
The wind born from sound is covered by ether, and by <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
The cause of sound is covered by the great principle, and that itself by <s>pradhāna</s>.
They say there are seven coverings of the egg; its self is the lotus-seated one.
Here there are said to be eggs joined with hundreds of millions upon hundreds of millions.
In each and every one, four-faced <s>Brahmās</s>, <s>Haras</s>, and <s>Bhavas</s>

children.text: sṛṣṭāḥ pradhānena tadā labdhvā śambhostu saṃnidhim ||
children.translated_text: were then created by <s>pradhāna</s>, after obtaining the nearness of <s>Śambhu</s>.
Dissolution too, and likewise the mutual ending of these, has been proclaimed.
<s>Maheśvara</s> is the maker of creation, re-creation, and continued existence.

children.text: sarge ca rajasā yuktaḥ sattvasthaḥ pratipālane
children.translated_text: At creation he is joined with rajas; in protection he abides in sattva.

children.text: pratisarge tamodriktaḥ sa eva trividhaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: At re-creation, rich in tamas, he himself proceeds in three forms.
He is the first creator of beings, their destroyer, and their protector.
Therefore the god <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, is the lord even of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Since <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> are all-souled in him,

children.text: ekadaṇḍe tathā lokā ime kartā pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too, in a single sovereignty, <s>Pitāmaha</s> is the maker of these worlds.
This natural creation, presided over by the <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), has been described by me.
And the auspicious primary creation, O twice-born ones, is not preceded by deliberate thought.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Now here the time of that primary creation is remembered as its day.
In brief, the night of the creation is of the same kind for the natural creation.

children.text: divā sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute rajanyāṃ pralayaṃ vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: By day the mighty one transforms creation; by night he brings about dissolution.
This day and night of his are figurative; day and night do not truly exist for him.
By day all evolutes, modifications, and the <s>Viśvadevas</s> are present,
as are all the lords of creatures and the other great seers.

children.text: rātrau sarve pralīyante niśānte sambhavanti ca
children.translated_text: At night they all dissolve, and at the end of night they come into being again.
His day is a particular variant, and the night is remembered as being of that same kind.
At the end of a thousand <s>caturyugas</s> (cycles of four yugas) there are fourteen Manus.

children.text: catvāri tu sahasrāṇi vatsarāṇāṃ kṛtaṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Kṛta</s> age consists of four thousand years, O twice-born ones.

children.text: tāvacchatī ca vai saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca kṛtasya tu
children.translated_text: Its twilight is the same number in hundreds, and so too is the twilight portion of <s>Kṛta</s>.

children.text: triśatī dviśatī saṃdhyā tathā caikaśatī kramāt ||
children.translated_text: In order, the twilights are three hundred, two hundred, and one hundred.
Thus the portion is six hundred, apart from the twilight portion of <s>Kṛta</s>.
And, apart from the twilight portions, the measures are three, two, and one thousand respectively.
I shall tell you of <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Tiṣya</s> in relation to <s>Kṛta</s>.
Fifteen <s>nimeṣas</s> (eye-blinks) make a <s>kāṣṭhā</s> for a healthy person, O well-vowed ones.

children.text: martyasya cākṣṇostasyāś ca tatas triṃśatikā kalā
children.translated_text: And thirty such <s>kāṣṭhās</s>, measured by a mortal's eyes, make a <s>kalā</s>.
Thirty <s>kalās</s>, O brahmins, are conceived as one <s>muhūrta</s>.
Fifteen <s>muhūrtas</s> make the night, and the day is of the same measure.
A month is a day and night for the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors); again there is a division of the two.
The dark fortnight is their day, while the bright fortnight is the night for sleep.

children.text: triṃśadye mānuṣā māsāḥ pitryo māsastu sa smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thirty human months are remembered as one month of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.

children.text: śatāni trīṇi māsānāṃ ṣaṣṭyā cāpyadhikāni vai
children.translated_text: Three hundred months, with sixty more added,
are a year of the <s>Pitṛs</s>, as understood by human reckoning.
What would be a hundred years by human measure

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ trīṇi varṣāṇi saṃkhyātānīha tāni vai ||
children.translated_text: is counted here as three years of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.

children.text: daśa vai dvyadhikā māsāḥ pitṛsaṃkhyeha saṃsmṛtā
children.translated_text: Twelve months, moreover, are remembered here in the reckoning of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.

children.text: laukikenaiva mānena abdo yo mānuṣaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the ordinary measure, that is what is known as a human year.
This is read here in the <s>Liṅga</s> as the divine day and night.
In the divine measure, night and day make a year; again there is a division of the two.
There the day is the northern course, and the night is the southern course.
These two have been specifically enumerated as the divine night and day.

children.text: triṃśadyāni tu varṣāṇi divyo māsastu sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Thirty years are remembered as a divine month.

children.text: mānuṣaṃ tu śataṃ viprā divyamāsāstrayastu te ||
children.translated_text: A hundred human years, O brahmins, are those three divine months.

children.text: daśa caiva tathāhāni divyo hyeṣa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And likewise ten days; this is remembered as the divine rule.
Three hundred years, and also sixty years,
are proclaimed by human reckoning as one divine year.
Three thousand human years by measure,
with thirty more years, are regarded as a <s>Saptarṣi</s> year.

children.text: nava yāni sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ mānuṣāṇi tu ||
children.translated_text: Nine thousand human years,
and ninety more, are a <s>Dhruva</s> year.
Thirty-six thousand human years

children.text: varṣāṇāṃ tacchataṃ jñeyaṃ divyo hyeṣa vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: are to be known as a hundred years; this is remembered as the divine rule.
They say that three <s>niyutas</s> of human years,
and also sixty thousand, are counted by number.

children.text: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ tu prāhuḥ saṃkhyāvido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: People who know calculation call that a thousand divine years.
By the divine measure itself, the reckoning of the yugas is established.
First comes the age called <s>Kṛta</s>; after that <s>Tretā</s> is prescribed.
Then come <s>Dvāpara</s> and <s>Kali</s>; these are the yugas, O well-vowed ones.
Now the years are seen according to human measure.
For the first, <s>Kṛta</s>, O best of brahmins, the divine measure is stated.
There were fourteen hundreds of thousands by count,
and another forty thousand years: that is the <s>Kṛta</s> age.
Likewise, by the count of hundreds of ten-thousand years,
and eighty thousand more, is the time of the <s>Tretā</s> age.
They say there are seven <s>niyutas</s> of human years,

children.text: viṃśatiś ca sahasrāṇi kālastu dvāparasya ca
children.translated_text: and twenty thousand more, as the time of <s>Dvāpara</s>.
Likewise, three hundred thousand years
and sixty thousand more are the time of the <s>Kali</s> age.
Thus the time called a <s>caturyuga</s> is remembered, apart from the twilight portions.
Without the portions, those are exactly thirty-six <s>niyutas</s>.
Here, by count, there are forty-three <s>niyutas</s>,

children.text: viṃśatiś ca sahasrāṇi saṃdhyāṃśaś ca caturyugaḥ
children.translated_text: and twenty thousand more; with the twilight portions, that is a <s>caturyuga</s>.
Thus a little more than seventy-one periods called <s>caturyugas</s>,
made up of <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Tretā</s>, and the rest, are called a <s>manvantara</s> (interval of a Manu).
And the number of a <s>manvantara</s> is proclaimed according to the total of years:
thirty crores of years by human reckoning, O best of twice-born ones...
and likewise sixty-seven other niyutas in addition;

children.text: viṃśatiś ca sahasrāṇi kālo 'yam adhikaṃ vinā
children.translated_text: and twenty thousand: this is the time, apart from the surplus.
This number of a <s>manvantara</s> is proclaimed here in the <s>Laiṅga</s>, O twice-born ones.
And likewise the number of years in a <s>caturyuga</s> has been declared.
One thousand <s>caturyugas</s> are indeed one <s>kalpa</s>, O best of the twice-born.

children.text: niśānte sṛjate lokān naśyante niśi jantavaḥ
children.translated_text: At the end of the night he creates the worlds; during the night living beings perish.
There, of the aerial beings, there are twenty-eight crores.
This is the number in the <s>manvantaras</s>, together with their intervals, exactly so.
There were three hundred crores and also ninety-two crores,

children.text: kalpe'tīte tu vai viprāḥ sahasrāṇāṃ tu saptatiḥ
children.translated_text: and, in the past <s>kalpa</s>, O priests, seventy thousands,
and again eight thousand; this is the total everywhere in brief.
Leaving aside those who belong to the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, when dissolution has arrived,
these people go from <s>Maharloka</s> to <s>Janaloka</s>.

children.text: koṭīnāṃ dve sahasre tu aṣṭau koṭiśatāni tu
children.translated_text: There are two thousand crores and eight hundred crores,

children.text: dviṣaṣṭiś ca tathā koṭyo niyutāni ca saptatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise sixty-two crores and seventy niyutas.

children.text: kalpārdhasaṃkhyā divyā vai kalpamevaṃ tu kalpayet
children.translated_text: This is the divine number of a half-<s>kalpa</s>; one should reckon the <s>kalpa</s> in this way.

children.text: kalpānāṃ vai sahasraṃ tu varṣamekamajasya tu ||
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>kalpas</s> are one year of the unborn one.
Eight thousand years are the <s>Brahmā</s>-cycle, the yuga of <s>Brahmā</s>.
A thousand yugas are the <s>savana</s> (pressing period) of the source of all the gods.

children.text: savanānāṃ sahasraṃ tu trividhaṃ triguṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A thousand <s>savanas</s> are threefold and also three-guṇed.

children.text: brahmaṇastu tathā proktaḥ kālaḥ kālātmanaḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: Thus the time of <s>Brahmā</s>, of the lord whose nature is time, has been stated.
<s>Bhavodbhava</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, <s>Bhavya</s>, <s>Rambha</s>, and again <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Ṛtu</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Havyavāha</s>, <s>Sāvitra</s>, and <s>Śuddha</s>,
<s>Uśika</s>, <s>Kuśika</s>, and <s>Gāndhāra</s>, O best of sages,

children.text: ṛṣabhaś ca tathā ṣaḍjo majjālīyaś ca madhyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Ṣaḍja</s>, <s>Majjālīya</s>, and <s>Madhyama</s>,

children.text: vairājo vai niṣādaś ca mukhyo vai meghavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vairāja</s>, <s>Niṣāda</s>, <s>Mukhya</s>, and <s>Meghavāhana</s>,
<s>Pañcama</s>, <s>Citraka</s>, <s>Ākūti</s>, and <s>Jñāna</s>,

children.text: manaḥ sudarśo bṛṃhaś ca tathā vai śvetalohitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Manas</s>, <s>Sudarśa</s>, <s>Bṛṃha</s>, and likewise <s>Śvetalohita</s>,

children.text: raktaś ca pītavāsāś ca asitaḥ sarvarūpakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rakta</s>, <s>Pītavāsas</s>, <s>Asita</s>, and <s>Sarvarūpaka</s>:
thus the <s>kalpas</s> of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is from the unmanifest, have been enumerated.
Crores upon crores of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, O best of sages,
have passed, and just so many days and nights remain again.

children.text: parānte vai vikārāṇi vikāraṃ yānti viśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the <s>parārdha</s>, transformations everywhere pass into transformation.
The dissolution of transformation takes place solely by the command of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: saṃhṛte tu vikāre ca pradhāne cātmani sthite ||
children.translated_text: When transformation has been dissolved and <s>pradhāna</s> abides in the self,
both <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s> remain in a state of likeness.

children.text: guṇānāṃ caiva vaiṣamye viprāḥ sṛṣṭiriti smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>guṇas</s> are unequal, O priests, that is remembered as creation.
When the <s>guṇas</s> are in equilibrium, there is dissolution; <s>Maheśvara</s> is the cause of both.
By the play of the god of gods, creations of this sort have been made,
countless, though stated briefly, from <s>pradhāna</s> when it is superintended.
Countless are those called <s>kalpas</s>; countless are the grandfathers.
Countless too are the <s>Haris</s>, but <s>Maheśvara</s> alone is one.
Those natural processes beginning with <s>pradhāna</s> proceed by his play.

children.text: guṇātmikā ca tadvṛttistasya devasya vai tridhā
children.translated_text: The activity belonging to the <s>guṇas</s> is threefold for that god.
For that non-material self there is no beginning, middle, or end.
The further span of the grandsire is measured as two <s>parārdhas</s>.

children.text: divā sṛṣṭaṃ tu yatsarvaṃ niśi naśyati cāsya tat ||
children.translated_text: All that is created by him in the day perishes at his night.
There <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svar</s>, and <s>Mahas</s> perish, but not what is above.
At night, when stationary and moving beings have perished, <s>Brahmā</s> sleeps upon the single ocean.
Because he slept in the waters, he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: śarvaryante prabuddho vai dṛṣṭvā śūnyaṃ carācaram ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the night, awakened and seeing the moving and unmoving world empty,

children.text: sraṣṭuṃ tadā matiṃ cakre brahmā brahmavidāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost of knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, then set his mind on creation.
Taking up that earth, flooded by the waters, the eternal one,
having assumed the form of a boar, set it in place as before.
The lord also made the rivers, streams, and oceans as before.
Having carefully made the earth free from low and high places,
he gathered upon the earth all the mountains that had been burned by the former fire.
He arranged the four worlds beginning with <s>Bhūr</s> just as before.

children.text: sraṣṭuṃ ca bhagavāṃścakre tadā sraṣṭā punarmatim ||
children.translated_text: Then the blessed creator again set his mind on creating.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When the great-souled one set his mind on creating, delusion arose in him.
O twice-born ones, it arose deliberately from <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is from the unmanifest.
Darkness, delusion, great delusion, gloom, and what is called blind darkness:
this fivefold ignorance arose from <s>Svayambhū</s>.

children.text: avidyayā munergrastaḥ sargo mukhya iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because the sage was seized by ignorance, that creation is remembered as the primary one.

children.text: asādhaka iti smṛtvā sargo mukhyaḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Remembering the primary creation as ineffective, <s>Prajāpati</s>,

children.text: abhyamanyata so 'nyaṃ vai nagā mukhyodbhavāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: he then conceived another; mountains are remembered as born from the primary creation.

children.text: tridhā kaṇṭho munestasya dhyāyato vai hyavartata ||
children.translated_text: As that sage meditated, his throat became threefold.

children.text: prathamaṃ tasya vai jajñe tiryaksroto mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: First there was born from him, the great-souled one, the creation with sideways current.

children.text: ūrdhvasrotaḥ parastasya sāttvikaḥ sa iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that came the upward-current creation; it is remembered as sāttvika.
There was also the downward-current creation, the creation of grace, and again that beginning with beings.
Of great <s>Brahmā</s>, the first creation is that of <s>mahat</s>, and the second is elemental.
The third creation is sensory, and the fourth is called primary.
The fifth is that of beings born in animal wombs, and the sixth is called divine.
The seventh, O priests, is human; the eighth is remembered as grace.
And the ninth is the <s>Kaumāra</s>; these are the natural and derivative creations.
At first the god created <s>Sananda</s> and likewise <s>Sanaka</s>,
and <s>Sanātana</s>, O best of sages; through freedom from action they reached the supreme state.
Through the knowledge of yoga he created <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
These nine are sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, the best of Brahmins.
They are speakers about <s>Brahman</s>, and are remembered as being like <s>Brahmā</s>.
And <s>Saṃkalpa</s> and <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Adharma</s> near <s>Dharma</s>:
these indeed are the twelve offspring of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth was from the unmanifest.
The eternal one created <s>Ṛbhu</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s> at the beginning.
Those two divine elder brothers were celibate and speakers about <s>Brahman</s>.
The two youths were equal to <s>Brahmā</s>, all-knowing and existing in all beings.
I shall tell you of the families of wives of those sages born first.
In brief, O best of sages, I shall also tell of the arising of progeny.
The lord created the queen <s>Śatarūpā</s> and <s>Virāj</s>.
And the queen <s>Śatarūpā</s>, womb-born from <s>Svāyambhuva</s>,

children.text: lebhe putradvayaṃ puṇyā tathā kanyādvayaṃ ca sā ||
children.translated_text: that meritorious woman obtained two sons and also two daughters.
The younger was wise <s>Uttānapāda</s>; the eldest was <s>Priyavrata</s>.
The elder and excellent daughter is remembered as <s>Ākūti</s>, and the younger as <s>Prasūti</s>.
Then a <s>Prajāpati</s> named <s>Ruci</s> married that <s>Ākūti</s>,
and the blessed <s>Dakṣa</s> married <s>Prasūti</s>, the sustainer of the worlds and a yoginī.
<s>Ākūti</s> then gave birth to <s>Yajña</s>, together with <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>.
The divine <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> gave birth to twelve daughters.
<s>Prasūti</s> bore twenty-four daughters from <s>Dakṣa</s>:

children.text: śraddhāṃ lakṣmīṃ dhṛtiṃ puṣṭiṃ tuṣṭiṃ medhāṃ kriyāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, and <s>Kriyā</s>,

children.text: buddhiṃ lajjāṃ vapuḥśāntiṃ siddhiṃ kīrtiṃ mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Vapus</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Siddhi</s>, and <s>Kīrti</s>, O greatly ascetic ones,

children.text: khyātiṃ śāntiṃ ca sambhūtiṃ smṛtiṃ prītiṃ kṣamāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Sambhūti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s>,

children.text: saṃnatiṃ cānasūyāṃ ca ūrjāṃ svāhāṃ surāraṇim
children.translated_text: and <s>Saṃnati</s>, <s>Anasūyā</s>, <s>Ūrjā</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, mother of the gods,

children.text: svadhāṃ caiva mahābhāgāṃ pradadau ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: and the very fortunate <s>Svadhā</s>; he gave them away in due order.
The thirteen good maidens from <s>Śraddhā</s> through <s>Kīrti</s>
went to <s>Dharma</s> the <s>Prajāpati</s> as husband, exceedingly hard to obtain.
Wise <s>Bhṛgu</s> married that <s>Khyāti</s>, the mother of the Bhārgava line.

children.text: sambhūtiṃ ca marīcistu smṛtiṃ caivāṅgirā muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Marīci</s> married <s>Sambhūti</s>, and the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s> married <s>Smṛti</s>.

children.text: prītiṃ pulastyaḥ puṇyātmā kṣamāṃ tāṃ pulaho muniḥ
children.translated_text: The righteous <s>Pulastya</s> married <s>Prīti</s>, and the sage <s>Pulaha</s> married <s>Kṣamā</s>.
Wise <s>Kratu</s> married <s>Saṃnati</s>, and <s>Atri</s> married that <s>Anasūyā</s>.
The blessed and excellent <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> married lotus-eyed <s>Ūrjā</s>.

children.text: vibhāvasus tathā svāhāṃ svadhāṃ vai pitaras tathā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Vibhāvasu</s> married <s>Svāhā</s>, and the ancestors married <s>Svadhā</s>.

children.text: putrīkṛtā satī yā sā mānasī śivasambhavā
children.translated_text: She who was made a daughter, mind-born and arisen from <s>Śiva</s>,
the sustainer of the worlds, was given by <s>Dakṣa</s> to <s>Rudra</s> himself as husband.
When the golden-egg-born one saw <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s> at the beginning of creation,
and first said, "Divide yourself," then, when she was born, she came into being.
From her portions came all women in the three worlds,
and the eleven kinds of <s>Rudras</s> likewise arose from his portion.
All that has the female mark is she, and the male mark is <s>Nīlalohita</s>.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavān brahmā dakṣamālokya suvratām ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, looking at <s>Dakṣa</s> and the woman of good vows, said:

children.text: bhajasva dhātrīṃ jagatāṃ mamāpi ca tavāpi ca
children.translated_text: "Accept the sustainer of the worlds, both mine and yours.
Because a daughter saves one from the hell called <s>Put</s>, so it is said here of daughterhood.

children.text: praśastā tava kānteyaṃ syāt putrī viśvamātṛkā
children.translated_text: This lovely woman, the mother of the universe, will be an excellent daughter for you.

children.text: tasmāt putrī satī nāmnā tavaiṣā ca bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this daughter of yours will be named <s>Satī</s>."
Thus addressed at that time by <s>Brahmā</s>'s command, the sage <s>Dakṣa</s>

children.text: labdhvā putrīṃ dadau sākṣāt satīṃ rudrāya sādaram ||
children.translated_text: obtained the daughter and respectfully gave <s>Satī</s> herself to <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: dharmasya patnyaḥ śraddhādyāḥ kīrtitā vai trayodaśa
children.translated_text: The thirteen wives of <s>Dharma</s>, beginning with <s>Śraddhā</s>, have been named.
I shall tell, in order, of the unsurpassed progeny of <s>Dharma</s> through them.

children.text: kāmo darpo 'tha niyamaḥ saṃtoṣo lobha eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Darpa</s>, <s>Niyama</s>, <s>Saṃtoṣa</s>, and <s>Lobha</s>,
and <s>Śruta</s>, <s>Daṇḍa</s>, <s>Samaya</s>, and <s>Bodha</s> of great splendor,
and <s>Apramāda</s>, <s>Vinaya</s>, and <s>Vyavasāya</s>, O best of twice-borns,

children.text: kṣemaṃ sukhaṃ yaśaścaiva dharmaputrāś ca tāsu vai ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣema</s>, <s>Sukha</s>, and <s>Yaśas</s> are the sons of <s>Dharma</s> by those wives.

children.text: dharmasya vai kriyāyāṃ tu daṇḍaḥ samaya eva ca
children.translated_text: By <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Dharma</s> had <s>Daṇḍa</s> and <s>Samaya</s>,

children.text: apramādas tathā bodho buddherdharmasya tau sutau ||
children.translated_text: and by <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Dharma</s> had those two sons, <s>Apramāda</s> and <s>Bodha</s>.
Thus these fifteen here are sons of <s>Dharma</s> through those wives.

children.text: bhṛgupatnī ca suṣuve khyātirviṣṇoḥ priyāṃ śriyam ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Khyāti</s>, the wife of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, bore <s>Śrī</s>, beloved of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and two sons, <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, sons-in-law of <s>Meru</s>.

children.text: prabhūtirnāma yā patnī marīceḥ suṣuve sutau ||
children.translated_text: The wife of <s>Marīci</s>, named <s>Prabhūti</s>, gave birth to sons:
<s>Pūrṇamāsa</s>, son of <s>Marīci</s>, and then four daughters,

children.text: tuṣṭirjyeṣṭhā ca vai dṛṣṭiḥ kṛṣiścāpacitis tathā ||
children.translated_text: with <s>Tuṣṭi</s> the eldest, and <s>Dṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Kṛṣi</s>, and <s>Apaciti</s>.

children.text: kṣamā ca suṣuve putrān putrīṃ ca pulahācchubhām
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣamā</s> bore sons and an auspicious daughter from <s>Pulaha</s>:
<s>Kardama</s>, <s>Varīyāṃs</s>, and <s>Sahiṣṇu</s>, O best of sages,
and also golden-yellow <s>Kanakapītā</s>, and <s>Pīvarī</s>, equal to the earth.

children.text: prītyāṃ pulastyaś ca tathā janayāmāsa vai sutān ||
children.translated_text: And through <s>Prīti</s>, <s>Pulastya</s> likewise begot sons:

children.text: dattorṇaṃ vedabāhuṃ ca putrīṃ cānyāṃ dṛṣadvatīm
children.translated_text: <s>Dattorṇa</s> and <s>Vedabāhu</s>, and another daughter, <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>.
Auspicious <s>Saṃnati</s> bore sixty thousand sons.

children.text: kratostu bhāryā sarve te vālakhilyā iti śrutāḥ
children.translated_text: All those, the sons of <s>Kratu</s>'s wife, are known as the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>.

children.text: sinīvālīṃ kuhūṃ caiva rākāṃ cānumatiṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Sinīvālī</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, and <s>Anumati</s>,

children.text: smṛtiś ca suṣuve patnī muneścāṅgirasas tathā
children.translated_text: the wife <s>Smṛti</s> also bore from the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
along with <s>Agni</s>, who had attained power, and the virtuous <s>Kīrtimān</s>.
<s>Anasūyā</s>, wife of <s>Atri</s>, indeed bore six offspring.

children.text: tāsvekā kanyakā nāmnā śrutiḥ sā sūnupañcakam ||
children.translated_text: Among them one daughter, named <s>Śruti</s>, bore a group of five sons.
<s>Satyanetra</s> the sage, <s>Bhavya</s>, <s>Mūrti</s>, <s>Āpaḥ</s>, and <s>Śanaiścara</s>,

children.text: somaś ca vai śrutiḥ ṣaṣṭhī pañcātreyāstu sūnavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Soma</s> also; <s>Śruti</s> was the sixth, and these were the five sons descended from <s>Atri</s>.

children.text: ūrjā vasiṣṭhādvai lebhe sutāṃś ca sutavatsalā
children.translated_text: <s>Ūrjā</s>, loving her children, obtained sons from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
the eldest, lotus-eyed and beautiful-eyed, bore the <s>Vāsiṣṭhas</s>.

children.text: rajaḥ suhotro bāhuś ca savanaścānaghas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Rajaḥ</s>, <s>Suhotra</s>, <s>Bāhu</s>, <s>Savana</s>, and likewise the sinless <s>Anagha</s>,

children.text: sutapāḥ śukra ityete munervai sapta sūnavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sutapāḥ</s> and <s>Śukra</s>: these are indeed the seven sons of the sage.

children.text: yaścābhimānī bhagavān bhavātmā paitāmaho vahnirasuḥ prajānām
children.translated_text: And the blessed Fire, self-conscious, whose nature is <s>Bhava</s>, descended from the grandsire, the life-breath of creatures,

children.text: svāhā ca tasmātsuṣuve sutānāṃ trayaṃ trayāṇāṃ jagatāṃ hitāya ||
children.translated_text: from him <s>Svāhā</s> bore a triad of sons, for the welfare of the three worlds.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: pavamānaḥ pāvakaś ca śuciragniś ca te smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pavamāna</s>, <s>Pāvaka</s>, and <s>Śuci</s> are remembered as the fires.
<s>Pavamāna</s> is produced by churning, while <s>Pāvaka</s> is remembered as lightning-born.
<s>Śuci</s> should be known as solar; these three are the sons of <s>Svāhā</s>.
With their sons and grandsons, their number here is remembered in brief.
After setting apart the first group of seven, they are forty-nine.
These are declared to be the fires, and they are led forth in sacrifices.
All these are ascetics; all are remembered as keepers of vows.

children.text: prajānāṃ patayaḥ sarve sarve rudrātmakāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All are lords of creatures; all are remembered as having the nature of <s>Rudra</s>.
The <s>Pitṛs</s>, both non-sacrificers and sacrificers, are kindly disposed in mind.

children.text: agniṣvāttāś ca yajvānaḥ śeṣā barhiṣadaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Agniṣvāttas</s> are sacrificers, and the rest are remembered as <s>Barhiṣads</s>.

children.text: menāṃ tu mānasīṃ teṣāṃ janayāmāsa vai svadhā
children.translated_text: <s>Svadhā</s> indeed generated for them <s>Menā</s>, mind-born.
<s>Menā</s>, daughter of the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, is mind-born and renowned in the world.
<s>Menā</s> bore <s>Maināka</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>, and his younger sister <s>Umā</s>.
She gave birth to <s>Gaṅgā</s>, daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, purified by the embrace of <s>Bhava</s>'s limbs.
She generated <s>Dharaṇī</s>, mind-born and devoted to sacrifice.
That <s>Svadhā</s>, lotus-faced, was the wife of king <s>Meru</s>.
The <s>Pitṛs</s> are called drinkers of nectar; their extent here is also told.

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca kulaṃ sarvaṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ tatsuvistaram ||
children.translated_text: Now hear in full the entire lineage of the sages.
I shall speak of it separately, arranged in chapters, after this.

children.text: dākṣāyaṇī satī yātā pārśvaṃ rudrasya pārvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> <s>Satī</s> went to the side of <s>Rudra</s> as <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: paścāddakṣaṃ vinindyaiṣā patiṃ lebhe bhavaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Afterwards, denouncing <s>Dakṣa</s>, she likewise obtained <s>Bhava</s> as her husband.
Meditating on her, <s>Nīlalohita</s> created many <s>Rudras</s>.
They were all equal to himself and honored by all the worlds.
When entreated by <s>Brahmā</s>, O tigers among sages, he laughed for a moment.
By them the whole fourteenfold world was covered.
Seeing those various <s>Rudras</s>, stainless and blue-red,
free from old age and death, the grandsire addressed the <s>Rudras</s>:
'Salutation to you, great gods, three-eyed and blue-red.

children.text: sarvajñāḥ sarvagā dīrghā hrasvā vāmanakāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: You are all-knowing, all-pervading, tall, short, dwarfish, and auspicious.

children.text: hiraṇyakeśā dṛṣṭighnā nityā buddhāś ca nirmalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are golden-haired, destructive by your glance, eternal, awakened, and pure.
You are free from dualities and passion, selves of the universe, sons of <s>Bhava</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ stutvā tadā rudrān rudraṃ cāha bhavaṃ śivam
children.translated_text: Having thus praised the <s>Rudras</s>, he then spoke to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Bhava</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>.
After circumambulating him, the blessed one born from the golden egg said:

children.text: namo 'stu te mahādeva prajā nārhasi śaṃkara
children.translated_text: 'Salutation to you, <s>Mahādeva</s>; O <s>Śaṃkara</s>, you ought not create such progeny.

children.text: mṛtyuhīnā vibho sraṣṭuṃ mṛtyuyuktāḥ sṛja prabho ||
children.translated_text: O mighty lord, do not create deathless beings; create beings endowed with death, O lord.'

children.text: tatastamāha bhagavānna hi me tādṛśī sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: Then the blessed one said to him, 'Such is not my condition.

children.text: sa tvaṃ sṛja yathākāmaṃ mṛtyuyuktāḥ prajāḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: You yourself, O lord, create beings endowed with death as you wish.'
Receiving this from <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the four-faced one created the whole,
this moving and unmoving world joined with old age and death.
And <s>Śaṃkara</s> then, with the <s>Rudras</s>, established himself with his self withdrawn.

children.text: sthāṇutvaṃ tasya vai viprāḥ śaṃkarasya mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is the immovable state of that great-souled <s>Śaṃkara</s>, O brahmins.
It belongs to <s>Śambhu</s>, whose self is without parts and whose body is assumed by his own will.

children.text: śaṃ rudraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ karoti ghṛṇayā yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>Rudra</s>, out of compassion, makes welfare for all beings,
he is <s>Śaṃkara</s>; effortlessly, by the science of yoga, one becomes of his nature.
What is called <s>śam</s> (peaceful welfare) is liberation for the detached one established in dispassion.
For the individual, abandonment of sense-objects comes gradually from fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
From detachment, dispassion arises in a person toward further perception.
Turning away is the abandonment of the qualities; it comes from not deliberating over knowledge.
The union of this and that comes through the grace of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
<s>Dharma</s> (righteous order), knowledge, detachment, and lordly power come from <s>Śaṃkara</s> here.
He himself is directly <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Pinākī</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>.

children.text: ye śaṃkarāśritāḥ sarve mucyante te na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All who take refuge in <s>Śaṃkara</s> are liberated; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: na gacchantyeva narakaṃ pāpiṣṭhā api dāruṇam ||
children.translated_text: Even the most wicked do not go to the terrible hell
when they have taken refuge in <s>Śaṃkara</s>; therefore they attain the eternal.
The sages said:
Beginning with <s>Ghora</s> and ending with <s>Māyā</s>, there are twenty-eight crores

children.text: koṭayo narakāṇāṃ tu pacyante tāsu pāpinaḥ
children.translated_text: of hells, and sinners are cooked in them.
They are those who have not taken refuge in <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
the refuge of all beings, the imperishable lord of the worlds,
the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme self, much-invoked and much-praised,
known through darkness as <s>Kālarudra</s>, through passion as the one born from the golden egg,
through purity as all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and in the state beyond qualities as <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: kena gacchanti narakaṃ narāḥ kena mahāmate
children.translated_text: By what do men go to hell, and by what not, O great-minded one?

children.text: karmaṇākarmaṇā vāpi śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: By action, or even by inaction? We are eager to hear.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall proclaim to you the secret of <s>Bhava</s> of immeasurable splendor,
the primal power of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the all-seeing one, in brief.
The yogins, knowers of all principles, established in supreme detachment,
accompanied by the eight practices beginning with breath-control,
endowed with virtues such as compassion, even when they have performed various
actions, go to hell or heaven solely by their own action.
From grace knowledge is born; from knowledge yoga proceeds.
Through yoga liberation is born; therefore everything comes from grace.
The sages said:
If understanding comes from grace, you should tell us its nature,

children.text: divyaṃ māheśvaraṃ caiva yogaṃ yogavidāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: and also the divine <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, O best of those who know yoga.

children.text: kathaṃ karoti bhagavān cintayā rahitaḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: How does the blessed <s>Śiva</s>, free from deliberation,
the mighty lord, bestow grace upon men through the path of yoga, and at what time?
<s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: devānāṃ ca ṛṣīṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ saṃnidhau purā
children.translated_text: In ancient times, in the presence of the gods, sages, and ancestors,
it was told by <s>Śailādi</s> to the son of <s>Brahmā</s>; listen.
The incarnations of <s>Vyāsa</s> at the end of each <s>Dvāpara</s> age, O well-vowed ones,
and likewise the incarnations of the trident-bearing lord as teachers of yoga in the <s>Tiṣya</s> age,
in each case four disciples of the lord, recipients of tranquility,
and their many further disciples: in this way <s>Īśvara</s> shows favor.

children.text: evaṃ kramāgataṃ jñānaṃ mukhādeva nṛṇāṃ vibhoḥ
children.translated_text: Thus knowledge, handed down in succession from the mouth of the lord,
reaches men, beginning with Brahmins and extending to Vaiśyas, through compassion and according to fitness.
The sages said:

children.text: dvāpare dvāpare vyāsāḥ ke vai kutrāntareṣu vai
children.translated_text: Who are the <s>Vyāsas</s> in each <s>Dvāpara</s>, and in which intervals

children.text: kalpeṣu kasminkalpe no vaktumarhasi cātra tān ||
children.translated_text: and in which <s>kalpas</s>? You should tell them to us here.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Listen, twice-born ones, in the <s>Vārāha</s> <s>kalpa</s>, in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> interval,

children.text: vyāsāṃś ca sāmprataṃ rudrāṃs tathā sarvāntareṣu vai ||
children.translated_text: to the present <s>Vyāsas</s> and <s>Rudras</s>, and likewise to those in all the intervals.
The revealers of knowledge concerning the Vedas and the Purāṇas
I shall now declare in order, throughout all the cycles.

children.text: kratuḥ satyo bhārgavaś ca aṅgirāḥ savitā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Satya</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Savitṛ</s>, O twice-born ones,
<s>Mṛtyu</s>, wise <s>Śatakratu</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, bull among sages,
<s>Sārasvata</s>, <s>Tridhāman</s>, and <s>Trivṛt</s>, bull among sages,
<s>Śatatejas</s>, <s>Svayaṃdharma</s>, and the one known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
<s>Tarakṣu</s>, wise <s>Aruṇi</s>, and likewise <s>Deva</s> and <s>Kṛtaṃjaya</s>,
<s>Ṛtaṃjaya</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, best of poets,
the sage <s>Vācaśravas</s> himself, and likewise pure <s>Śuṣmāyaṇi</s>,

children.text: tṛṇabindur munī rūkṣaḥ śaktiḥ śākteya uttaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tṛṇabindu</s> the sage, <s>Rūkṣa</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and thereafter <s>Śākteya</s>,
<s>Jātūkarṇya</s>, <s>Hari</s> himself, and the sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>:

children.text: vyāsāstvete ca śṛṇvantu kalau yogeśvarān kramāt ||
children.translated_text: these are the <s>Vyāsas</s>. Now listen in order to the lords of yoga in the <s>Kali</s> age.

children.text: asaṃkhyātā hi kalpeṣu vibhoḥ sarvāntareṣu ca
children.translated_text: For in the <s>kalpas</s> and in all the intervals of the lord they are countless;
but, because of the importance of the <s>Vyāsas</s> and of the incarnations of <s>Rudra</s> in the <s>Kali</s> age,

children.text: vaivasvatāntare kalpe vārāhe ye ca tān punaḥ
children.translated_text: those in the <s>Vārāha</s> <s>kalpa</s>, in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> interval,
I shall again declare as incarnations, and likewise those in all the intervals.
The sages said:
You should now tell us the <s>manvantaras</s> in the <s>Vārāha</s> <s>kalpa</s>,
and also the perfected ones in the later <s>kalpas</s>, in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> interval.
<s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> said:
The first <s>Manu</s> is <s>Svāyambhuva</s>; then, O twice-born ones, <s>Svārociṣa</s>,
<s>Uttama</s>, <s>Tāmasa</s>, <s>Raivata</s>, and likewise <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>,

children.text: vaivasvataś ca sāvarṇir dharmaḥ sāvarṇikaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Vaivasvata</s>, <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, again <s>Sāvarṇika</s>,
<s>Piśaṅga</s>, <s>Apiśaṅgābha</s>, <s>Śabala</s>, and likewise <s>Varṇaka</s>.
The <s>Manus</s> ending with the sound <s>au</s> and beginning with the sound <s>a</s> have been proclaimed.

children.text: śvetaḥ pāṇḍus tathā raktastāmraḥ pītaśca kāpilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, <s>Rakta</s>, <s>Tāmra</s>, <s>Pīta</s>, and <s>Kāpila</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ śyāmas tathā dhūmraḥ sudhūmraś ca dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Śyāma</s>, <s>Dhūmra</s>, and <s>Sudhūmra</s>, O best of twice-born men,

children.text: apiśaṅgaḥ piśaṅgaś ca trivarṇaḥ śabalas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Apiśaṅga</s>, <s>Piśaṅga</s>, <s>Trivarṇa</s>, and likewise <s>Śabala</s>:
the auspicious <s>Manus</s> have been described by color, with <s>Kālaṃdhura</s> among them.
They have been described by name and by color, and once again by color.
In brief, the lords of the intervals have been named as having vowels as their selves.
<s>Vaivasvata</s> is the vowel <s>ṛ</s>; that <s>Manu</s>, O lord of gods, is black.
I shall speak of his seventh cycle's yogins,
in the <s>kalpas</s> that have passed away and likewise in those yet to come.
The present one should be known in sequence as the <s>Vārāha</s>, the seventh interval.

children.text: yogāvatārāṃś ca vibhoḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ saṃtatis tathā ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell of the lord's yoga-incarnations and the succession of their disciples.
Considering them in all times and likewise in the cycles of yogins:

children.text: ādye śvetaḥ kalau rudraḥ sutāro madanas tathā ||
children.translated_text: in the first <s>Kali</s> age <s>Rudra</s> is <s>Śveta</s>; then <s>Sutāra</s> and <s>Madana</s>,
<s>Suhotra</s>, <s>Kaṅkaṇa</s>, and <s>Lokākṣi</s>, best of sages,
greatly radiant <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, the blessed <s>Dadhivāhana</s>,
and the wise sage <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Subālaka</s>,
and then the blessed <s>Gautama</s>, honored by all the gods,
<s>Vedaśīrṣa</s>, <s>Gokarṇa</s>, <s>Guhāvāsin</s>, and <s>Śikhaṇḍabhṛt</s>,
<s>Jaṭāmālin</s>, <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s>, <s>Dāruka</s>, and likewise <s>Lāṅgalin</s>,
the sage <s>Mahākāya</s>, <s>Śūlin</s>, <s>Daṇḍin</s>, and <s>Muṇḍīśvara</s> himself,
<s>Sahiṣṇu</s>, <s>Somaśarman</s>, and <s>Nakulīśa</s>, teacher of the world:
these have been properly declared as incarnations of the supreme self
as teachers of yoga in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> interval, in all cycles, O well-vowed ones.
And thus, O best of sages, these are the <s>Vyāsas</s> in each <s>Dvāpara</s> age.
Each of the lords of yoga has four imperishable disciples.
<s>Śveta</s>, <s>Śvetaśikhaṇḍin</s>, <s>Śvetāśva</s>, and <s>Śvetalohita</s>,

children.text: dundubhiḥ śatarūpaś ca ṛcīkaḥ ketumāṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dundubhi</s>, <s>Śatarūpa</s>, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, and likewise <s>Ketumant</s>,
<s>Viśoka</s>, <s>Vikeśa</s>, <s>Vipāśa</s>, and <s>Pāpanāśana</s>,
<s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, <s>Durdama</s>, and <s>Duratikrama</s>,

children.text: sanakaś ca sanandaś ca prabhuryaś ca sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sananda</s>, <s>Prabhu</s>, and <s>Sanātana</s>.

children.text: ṛbhuḥ sanatkumāraś ca sudhāmā virajās tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛbhu</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Sudhāmā</s>, and also <s>Virajas</s>;
<s>Śaṅkhapād</s>, <s>Vairaja</s> too, <s>Megha</s>, and likewise <s>Sārasvata</s>,
the best of sages, <s>Suvāhana</s>, and the greatly radiant <s>Meghavāha</s>;
<s>Kapila</s> and <s>Āsuri</s> too, and likewise the sage <s>Pañcaśikha</s>,
and <s>Vālkala</s>, the great yogin: these were righteous and very mighty.

children.text: parāśaraś ca gargaś ca bhārgavaścāṅgirās tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Garga</s>, <s>Bhārgava</s>, and likewise <s>Āṅgiras</s>,
<s>Balabandhu</s>, <s>Nirāmitra</s>, and <s>Ketuśṛṅga</s>, rich in austerity;
<s>Lambodara</s>, <s>Lamba</s>, <s>Lambākṣa</s>, and <s>Lambakeśaka</s>,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ samabuddhiś ca sādhyaḥ sarvastathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvajña</s>, <s>Samabuddhi</s>, <s>Sādhya</s>, and also <s>Sarva</s>;
<s>Sudhāmā</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, and likewise <s>Virajas</s>,
<s>Atri</s>, <s>Devasada</s>, then <s>Śravaṇa</s> and <s>Śraviṣṭhaka</s>,

children.text: kuṇiś ca kuṇibāhuś ca kuśarīraḥ kunetrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṇi</s>, <s>Kuṇibāhu</s>, <s>Kuśarīra</s>, and <s>Kunetraka</s>;
<s>Kaśyapa</s> too, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, and then <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Utathya</s> and <s>Vāmadeva</s>, great in yoga and great in strength;
<s>Vācaśravas</s>, <s>Sudhīka</s>, and <s>Śyāvāśva</s>, lord among ascetics,
<s>Hiraṇyanābha</s> of <s>Kauśala</s>, <s>Logākṣi</s>, and likewise <s>Kuthumi</s>;
the learned <s>Sumantu</s>, <s>Barbarī</s>, <s>Kabandha</s>, and <s>Kuśikaṃdhara</s>,
<s>Plakṣa</s>, <s>Dālbhyāyaṇi</s>, <s>Ketumān</s>, and likewise <s>Gopana</s>;
<s>Bhallāvī</s>, <s>Madhupiṅga</s>, and <s>Śvetaketu</s>, treasure of austerity,

children.text: uśiko bṛhadaśvaś ca devalaḥ kavireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uśika</s>, <s>Bṛhadaśva</s>, <s>Devala</s>, and <s>Kavi</s> too;
<s>Śālihotra</s>, <s>Agniveśa</s>, <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, and <s>Śaradvasu</s>,
<s>Chagala</s>, <s>Kuṇḍakarṇa</s>, <s>Kumbha</s>, and <s>Pravāhaka</s>;
<s>Ulūka</s> and <s>Vidyuta</s>, <s>Maṇḍūka</s> and <s>Āśvalāyana</s>,

children.text: akṣapādaḥ kumāraś ca ulūko vatsa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Akṣapāda</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Ulūka</s>, and <s>Vatsa</s> too;

children.text: kuśikaścaiva garbhaś ca mitraḥ kauruṣya eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśika</s>, <s>Garbha</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Kauruṣya</s> as well:
these great-souled ones are the disciples in all the cycles of the yogins.
They were stainless, chiefly absorbed in <s>Brahman</s>, and devoted to the yoga of knowledge.
These <s>Pāśupata</s> siddhas had bodies dusted with ash.
Their disciples and their disciples' disciples, by the hundreds and thousands,
having obtained <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga, became established for the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Beings beginning with the gods and ending with piśācas are declared to be paśus.
Because he is lord over them, <s>Bhava</s>, lord of all, is remembered as <s>Paśupati</s>.

children.text: tena praṇīto rudreṇa paśūnāṃ patinā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Since it was taught by that <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of paśus, O twice-born ones,
it should be known as <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga, for the manifestation of the higher and lower powers.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Now I shall briefly declare the places of yoga,
which were established by <s>Śiva</s> himself for the welfare of the worlds, O twice-born ones.
What lies a span below the throat and above the navel is the excellent place of yoga.
Below the navel is the yogic place called the āvarta, and the middle point is between the brows.
The yoga of the self is called the accomplishment of knowledge of all objects.
One-pointedness also arises at all times through its grace.
The nature of grace is self-experienced, O best of the twice-born,

children.text: vaktuṃ na śakyaṃ brahmādyaiḥ kramaśo jāyate nṛṇām ||
children.translated_text: and cannot be spoken of even by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others; it arises gradually in human beings.
By the word yoga is meant nirvāṇa, the state of <s>Maheśa</s>.
Its cause, O sages, is knowledge; knowledge comes from his grace.
By knowledge one should burn away sin, always restraining the sense-objects.
For one whose activities of the senses are restrained, success in yoga will arise.
Yoga is the restraint of the movements of the mind, O best of the twice-born.
Its means have been taught here as eightfold for the sake of attainment.

children.text: yamastu prathamaḥ prokto dvitīyo niyamas tathā
children.translated_text: Yama is declared first, and niyama second.
Āsana is declared third, and after that comes prāṇāyāma.

children.text: pratyāhāraṃ pañcamo vai dhāraṇā ca tataḥ parā
children.translated_text: Pratyāhāra is the fifth, and dhāraṇā comes after that.
Dhyāna is said to be the seventh, while samādhi is remembered as the eighth.
Cessation in austerity is also called yama.
Ahiṃsā is the first basis of yama, O best among the self-restrained.
Truth, then nonstealing, and brahmacarya and nonpossession

children.text: niyamasyāpi vai mūlaṃ yama eva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: are rooted in yama itself for niyama too; there is no doubt.
Conduct directed to the welfare of all beings as to oneself
is called ahiṃsā, and it grants the attainment of self-knowledge.
What has been seen, heard, inferred, or personally experienced as it really is,
the telling of that is called truth, when it is free from injury to others.
One should not utter obscene speech; thus is the revelation for brahmins.
And this is another rule: having perceived others' faults, one should not speak of them.
Not taking the property of others, even in distress, after reflection,
by mind, action, and speech: in brief, that is nonstealing.
Abstention from sexual intercourse by action of mind, speech, and body
is called brahmacarya for ascetics and celibate students.
Here too for <s>Vaikhānasa</s> ascetics, and especially for those without wives,

children.text: sadārāṇāṃ gṛhasthānaṃ tathaiva ca vadāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise for householders who have wives, I shall speak to you.
Having approached one's own wife according to rule, and always abstaining from others,
by mind, action, and speech, this is remembered as brahmacarya.

children.text: medhyā svanārī sambhogaṃ kṛtvā snānaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: After intercourse with one's own ritually pure wife, one should perform a bath.

children.text: evaṃ gṛhastho yuktātmā brahmacārī na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus a disciplined householder is a brahmacārin; there is no doubt.
Ahiṃsā too is just so in the worship of twice-borns, gurus, and fire:

children.text: vidhinā yādṛśī hiṃsā sā tvahiṃsā iti smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: whatever violence occurs according to rule is remembered as nonviolence.

children.text: striyaḥ sadā parityājyāḥ saṅgaṃ naiva ca kārayet
children.translated_text: Women should always be avoided, and one should not form attachment.
The wise man should make his mind toward bodies as it is toward corpses.
As at the times of discharging feces and urine, on ground outside, according to one's thought...

children.text: tathā kāryā ratau cāpi svadāre cānyataḥ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too in sexual intercourse, it should be done with one's own wife in her season; how could it be otherwise?
A woman is like a live coal, and a man is like a jar of ghee.
Therefore one should avoid contact with women from afar.
On reflection, there is never satisfaction of sense-objects through enjoyment.
Therefore detachment should be practiced by mind, action, and speech.
Desire is never appeased by the enjoyment of desired objects.
Like the black-tracked fire with oblation, it only grows still more.
Therefore abandonment should always be practiced by the yogin for immortality.
For a mortal who is not detached continues in many wombs.
Immortality is indeed through abandonment alone, O best knowers of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.
It is not through ritual action, offspring, or wealth, O best of twice-borns.
Therefore detachment should be practiced through the actions of mind, speech, and body.
Abstention at each season is remembered as <s>brahmacarya</s> (chastity).

children.text: yamāḥ saṃkṣepataḥ proktā niyamāṃś ca vadāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>yamas</s> (restraints) have been stated briefly; I shall also tell you the <s>niyamas</s> (observances).
Purity, worship, austerity, giving, recitation of sacred study, and restraint of the sexual organ,

children.text: vratopavāsamaunaṃ ca snānaṃ ca niyamā daśa
children.translated_text: vows, fasting, silence, and bathing: these are the ten <s>niyamas</s>.

children.text: niyamaḥ syādanīhā ca śaucaṃ tuṣṭistapas tathā ||
children.translated_text: A <s>niyama</s> may also be desirelessness, purity, contentment, and austerity,
recitation, dedication to <s>Śiva</s>, and postures such as the lotus posture.
Purity has been taught as external and internal; internal purity is superior.

children.text: bāhyaśaucena yuktaḥ saṃs tathā cābhyantaraṃ caret
children.translated_text: Being endowed with external purity, one should also practice the internal kind.
The fiery, watery, and brahmanical bath should be performed by worshipers of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: snānaṃ vidhānataḥ samyak paścād ābhyantaraṃ caret
children.translated_text: After bathing properly according to rule, one should then practice the internal kind.
Even if, up to the end of the body, one always smears oneself with clay and plunges into sacred waters,
one is still impure if devoid of inner purity.
Algae, aquatic creatures, fish, and beings that live on fish,
always plunging in water, are they thereby pure, O best of twice-borns?
Therefore internal purity should always be practiced according to rule.
Having bathed in the water of knowledge of the self, and once having smeared oneself inwardly with intent,
one is purified with the clay of excellent detachment; such is declared to be purity.
Accomplishments are seen for one who is pure, never accomplishments for one who is impure.
The man of good vows who is content with a livelihood that has come by lawful means,
his contentment is constant, and there is no remembrance of what has passed away.
Austerities such as the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> and other very auspicious practices are skillfully performed.

children.text: svādhyāyastu japaḥ proktaḥ praṇavasya tridhā smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Svādhyāya</s> (sacred recitation) is said to be recitation of the <s>praṇava</s>; it is remembered as threefold.
The vocal recitation is the lowest and primary; the whispered one is the very highest.
The mental one is remembered in detail in the ordinance concerning the five-syllabled mantra.
Likewise dedication to <s>Śiva</s> is performed through the actions of mind, speech, and body.
It is knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> and unwavering, firmly established devotion to the guru.
Swiftly drawing back and restraining the senses that are attached
to the sense-objects is, in brief, declared to be <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses).
Fixing the mind is called <s>dhāraṇā</s>; in brief, it is the binding to a place.

children.text: tasyāḥ svāsthyena dhyānaṃ ca samādhiś ca vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: From the steadiness of that, after consideration, come <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption).
There, single-mindedness, free from any other cognition, is <s>dhyāna</s>.
It remains as if empty of the body, with only the object appearing in consciousness.

children.text: samādhiḥ sarvahetuś ca prāṇāyāma iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Samādhi</s>, the cause of all, is also remembered as <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the wind born in one's own body; <s>yama</s> is its restraint.

children.text: tridhā dvijairyamaḥ prokto mando madhyottamas tathā ||
children.translated_text: This restraint has been taught by the twice-borns as threefold: low, middle, and highest.
The restraint of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> is declared to be <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
The measure of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is remembered as twelve <s>mātrās</s> (units of time).
The low form is twelve <s>mātrās</s>; one <s>uddhāta</s> is remembered as twelve.
The middle form is two <s>uddhātas</s>, consisting of twenty-four <s>mātrās</s>.
The chief form is three <s>uddhātas</s>, said to be thirty-six <s>mātrās</s>.
In order, they produce sweating, trembling, and rising up.
For the sake of yoga there is the arising of bliss, and also sleepiness and dizziness,
horripilation, sound, perception, twisting of one's own limbs, and trembling.
When there is whirling, sweat-born sensation, and fainting consciousness,
then that very beautiful <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is called the highest of the highest.
It is said to be with seed and without seed, with recitation and without recitation, respectively.

children.text: ibho vā śarabho vāpi durādharṣo 'tha kesarī ||
children.translated_text: An elephant, a <s>śarabha</s>, or a lion is hard to overcome from afar.
But when captured and being tamed, it becomes according to its own nature.
In the same way, the breath, when unsteady, is hard for yogins to subdue.

children.text: nyāyataḥ sevyamānastu sa evaṃ svasthatāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: But when cultivated according to rule, it thus comes to steadiness.
Just as a king of beasts, an elephant, or a fiercely intoxicated <s>śarabha</s>,
through time, discipline, and great care is tamed,
so through familiarity the breath attains steadiness and evenness.
For one who practices through yoga, no affliction arises.
Thus, when practiced, the sage's breath burns away
the faults born of mind, speech, and body, and protects the body of the doer.
For the wise man who is properly joined with <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
faults therefore perish, and through it the exhalation is digested.
Through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, divine powers such as tranquility are attained in order.

children.text: śāntiḥ praśāntirdīptiś ca prasādaś ca tathā kramāt
children.translated_text: They are tranquility, deeper tranquility, radiance, and serenity, in that order.
At the beginning, the first of the four is here said to be tranquility, O twice-borns.
Tranquility is said to be the quieting of both innate and adventitious sins.
Deeper tranquility is remembered as proper restraint of speech.
Radiance is said to be illumination everywhere and at all times, O twice-borns.
But the serenity of all the senses, and also of the intellect and the vital winds,

children.text: prasāda iti samproktaḥ svānte tviha catuṣṭaye
children.translated_text: is called <s>prasāda</s> (clarity); here, in the inner faculty, it is fourfold.

children.text: prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaś ca udāno vyāna eva ca ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>samāna</s>, <s>udāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s>,
and <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkala</s>, <s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>.
The serenity of these is remembered as the serenity of the vital winds.

children.text: prayāṇaṃ kurute tasmādvāyuḥ prāṇa iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because it makes the forward movement, that wind is remembered as <s>prāṇa</s>.
<s>Apāna</s> carries food and the like downward in due order.
<s>Vyāna</s> pervades the limbs and is the stimulator of diseases and the like.
It agitates the vital points; this is proclaimed as <s>udāna</s>.

children.text: samaṃ nayati gātrāṇi samānaḥ pañca vāyavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Samāna</s> brings the limbs into balance. These are the five winds.

children.text: udgāre nāga ākhyātaḥ kūrma unmīlane tu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s> is named in belching, and <s>Kūrma</s> in the opening of the eyes.
<s>Kṛkala</s> is connected with hunger in the body, and <s>Devadatta</s> with yawning.

children.text: dhanaṃjayo mahāghoṣaḥ sarvagaḥ sa mṛte 'pi hi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanaṃjaya</s>, of great sound, is all-pervading, even in a dead body.
For one in whom the clarity of the ten winds is accomplished through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
that clarity is the fourth designation in the fourfold group, O brahmins.

children.text: visvarastu mahān prajño mano brahmā citiḥ smṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvara</s>, <s>Mahān</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Manas</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Citi</s>, and <s>Smṛti</s>,
then <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Saṃvid</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and also <s>Mati</s>
are declared, O twice-born ones, to be these designations of the intellect, of the great principle.
The clarity of this intellect is accomplished through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
<s>Viśvara</s> is the state of becoming manifold among pairs of opposites, O best of sages.
That which is first-born among all principles and great by measure is <s>Mahān</s>.
That whose cave is right knowledge is <s>Prajñā</s>; that by which one thinks is <s>Manas</s>.
Because of greatness and because it makes things grow, it is <s>Brahmā</s>, O best knowers of brahman.
That which gathers all actions for the sake of experience is remembered as <s>Citi</s>.

children.text: smarate yatsmṛtiḥ sarvaṃ saṃvidvai vindate yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: That which remembers everything is <s>Smṛti</s>; and it is <s>Saṃvid</s> because by it one apprehends.
That which is proclaimed again and again through knowledge and the like is <s>Khyāti</s>.
Because it knows everything, being lord over all principles, it is <s>Īśvara</s>.
