Because it thinks and considers, it is <s>Mati</s>, O best of the intelligent.
And that which makes an object known and understands it is called <s>Buddhi</s>.
The clarity of this intellect is accomplished through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
That restrained ascetic should burn away all faults through <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
He should burn away sin through acts of concentration, and through withdrawal of the senses
he should regard sense-objects as poison, and by meditation burn away the non-sovereign qualities.
By <s>samādhi</s>, O best ascetics, he should increase the growth of wisdom.

children.text: sthānaṃ labdhvaiva kurvīta yogāṣṭāṅgāni vai kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained a place, he should practice the eight limbs of yoga in order.
Having properly obtained the postures for the sake of yogic accomplishment, the knower of the self

children.text: ādeśakāle yogasya darśanaṃ hi na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: should know that the vision of yoga does not arise at an unsuitable place or time.
He should not practice near fire, in water, or on a heap of dry leaves,
nor in a place overrun by creatures, in a cremation ground, in an old cow-pen, or at a crossroads,
nor in a noisy or frightening place, nor in a mass of shrines or anthills,
nor in an inauspicious place, occupied by bad people, or filled with mosquitoes and the like.
He should not practice when the body is distressed or when dejection and the like arise.

children.text: sugupte tu śubhe ramye guhāyāṃ parvatasya tu ||
children.translated_text: Rather, in a well-hidden, auspicious, and pleasant cave in a mountain,

children.text: bhavakṣetre sugupte vā bhavārāme vane'pi vā
children.translated_text: or in a well-concealed holy place of <s>Bhava</s>, in <s>Bhava</s>'s garden, or even in a forest,

children.text: gṛhe tu suśubhe deśe vijane jantuvarjite ||
children.translated_text: or in a very auspicious house, in a solitary place free from creatures,
exceedingly clean, properly smeared, and decorated,
like the inside of a mirror and well perfumed with black aloe,
strewn with many flowers and adorned with a canopy above,
rich in fruits, shoots, and roots, and furnished with <s>kuśa</s> grass and flowers,
seated in a proper posture, he should joyfully practice the limbs of yoga himself.
After bowing down to the guru, to <s>Bhava</s>, to the Goddess, and to <s>Vināyaka</s>,

children.text: yogīśvarān saśiṣyāṃś ca yogaṃ yuñjīta yogavit
children.translated_text: and to the lords of yoga together with their disciples, the knower of yoga should yoke himself to yoga.

children.text: āsanaṃ svastikaṃ baddhvā padmamardhāsanaṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: Having assumed the <s>svastika</s> posture, the <s>padma</s> posture, or the half-posture,
with knees even, or, being wise, even with one knee,
having become steady in an even and firm posture, and having drawn in both feet,
with mouth closed and eyes fixed, holding the chest forward,

children.text: pārṣṇibhyāṃ vṛṣaṇau rakṣaṃs tathā prajananaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: guarding the testicles and then the generative organ with the heels,
with the head slightly raised, he should not let the teeth touch the teeth.
He should gaze at the tip of his own nose and not look toward the directions.

children.text: tamaḥ pracchādya rajasā rajaḥ sattvena chādayet
children.translated_text: He should cover darkness with passion, and cover passion with purity.
Then, established in purity, he should practice meditation on <s>Śiva</s>.
He should meditate on the supreme one denoted by the syllable <s>oṃ</s>, pure and shaped like a lamp-flame,
concentrated in the pericarp of the lotus.
Or the wise man, having meditated below the navel on an excellent lotus,
three finger-breadths away, either eight-cornered or five-cornered,

children.text: trikoṇaṃ ca tathāgneyaṃ saumyaṃ sauraṃ svaśaktibhiḥ
children.translated_text: triangular, fiery, lunar, and solar, together with its own powers,
or solar, lunar, and fiery in that order,

children.text: āgneyaṃ ca tataḥ sauraṃ saumyamevaṃ vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: or fiery, then solar, and lunar, according to this rule,
having thus imagined below the fire the fourfold group beginning with <s>dharma</s>,
and the three qualities in order, he should visualize them above the maṇḍala.
He should contemplate <s>Rudra</s>, established in purity and encircled by his own power.

children.text: nābhau vātha gale vāpi bhrūmadhye vā yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: He may perform meditation according to rule in the navel, in the throat, or in the middle of the brows,
or on the plate of the forehead, or on the crown of the head.

children.text: dvidale ṣoḍaśāre vā dvādaśāre krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: He should remember him in a two-petalled form, or successively in sixteen-spoked or twelve-spoked forms,

children.text: daśāre vā ṣaḍasre vā caturasre smarecchivam ||
children.translated_text: or in a ten-spoked, six-cornered, or four-cornered form as <s>Śiva</s>.
He may visualize him golden in appearance, or like a chamber, or very white,
or shining like twelve suns, or like the disk of the moon.
In a place resembling ten million flashes of lightning, one should contemplate <s>Parameśvara</s>.
Or, composed, one should contemplate him as fire-colored, or like a circle of lightning.
In a place shining like ten million thunderbolts, or even resembling a ruby,
or in a blue-red disk, the yogin should practice <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption).
He should meditate on <s>Maheśvara</s> in the heart, and on <s>Sadāśiva</s> in the lotus of the navel,

children.text: candracūḍaṃ lalāṭe tu bhrūmadhye śaṃkaraṃ svayam ||
children.translated_text: on the moon-crested one at the forehead, and on <s>Śaṅkara</s> himself between the brows.
In the divine and eternal place he should practice meditation on <s>Śiva</s>,
as the stainless, partless brahman, utterly peaceful and formed of knowledge,
without marks, indescribable, smaller than the smallest atom, auspicious,
without support, beyond reasoning, and free from destruction and origination,
as isolation, nirvāṇa, and the unsurpassed highest good,
as immortal, imperishable brahman, wondrous and without rebirth,
as great bliss, supreme bliss, the bliss of yoga, free from illness,
as free from what is to be rejected or accepted, subtler than the subtle, auspicious,
as self-known yet unknowable, that supreme <s>Śiva</s>, consisting of knowledge,
beyond the senses, without appearance, the supreme reality beyond the highest.
He is freed from all limiting adjuncts, reachable through meditation and reflection,
nondual, established beyond darkness as the supreme.
Thus one should contemplate <s>Mahādeva</s> in the mind, or in the lotus of the heart,
and also <s>Sadāśiva</s> in the navel, the all-pervading one whose self is all the gods.
In the middle of the body one should remember the god <s>Śiva</s>, the all-pervading one made of pure knowledge,
and <s>Śaṅkara</s> by the lower method, and also by the upward striking impulse.
In due order, by the lower method, and also by the middle one, O well-vowed one,
the wise man should practice also by the highest <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention).
The intelligent man, composed in heart and navel, should exhale for thirty-two measures,

children.text: recakaṃ pūrakaṃ tyaktvā kumbhakaṃ ca dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, O best of the twice-born, having set aside <s>recaka</s> and <s>pūraka</s>, he should practice <s>kumbhaka</s>.
Directly in complete sameness he should remember <s>Śiva</s> in the middle of the body.
Having thus attained unity, whatever bliss arises there from that essence,
the wise man, standing in direct sameness, knows it as the bliss of brahman.
A <s>dhāraṇā</s> consists of twelve measures, and <s>dhyāna</s> consists of twelve <s>dhāraṇās</s>.
For as long as there are twelve units of <s>dhyāna</s>, that is called <s>samādhi</s>.
Or else, O brahmins, for knowers it arises merely through contact.
By effort the two are equal, whether after a long time or quickly, O twice-born ones.
Then obstacles to yoga arise again for him as he practices.

children.text: naśyanty abhyāsatas te 'pi praṇidhānena vai guroḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet those too disappear through practice and through devotion to the guru.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Laziness is first; afterwards the affliction of disease arises.
There are heedlessness, doubt, and instability of the mind here.
Lack of faith, false vision, and then pain of three kinds,
dejection, and regarding unsuitable sense-objects as suitable:
these tenfold obstacles to yoga arise for the sage.
Laziness is also non-activity, because of heaviness of body and mind.
Diseases arise from imbalance of the bodily constituents, and likewise from karma and from doṣas.
Heedlessness is the failure to cultivate the means to <s>samādhi</s>.
The cognition touched by both alternatives, 'is it this or that?', is doubt about the locus.
Instability of mind is indeed the yogin's lack of firm establishment.
Even when a stage has been attained, it comes from the mind's bondage to becoming.
Lack of faith is a disposition devoid of conviction in the means,
in the goal, in the guru, and in knowledge, conduct, <s>Śiva</s>, and the rest.
Erroneous knowledge is called false vision.
Through ignorance, it is the cognition of self in what is not the self, when that is present.
Pain is said to be internal, and also physical or caused by beings,
and caused by divine forces; thus it is said to be threefold and again innate.
The agitation of the mind caused by the obstruction of desire is stated to be that.
Dejection must be restrained by supreme dispassion.

children.text: tamasā rajasā caiva saṃspṛṣṭaṃ durmanaḥ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: A mind touched by tamas and rajas is remembered as a bad or dejected mind.
When that has arisen in the mind, it is remembered as dejection.
Taking something up by force, from lack of discernment between what is suitable and unsuitable,
and a creature's craving among various sense-objects,

children.text: antarāyā iti khyātā yogasyaite hi yoginām ||
children.translated_text: these are known as obstacles to yoga for yogins.
For one endowed with the utmost effort they disappear; there is no doubt.
When the obstacles have disappeared, O twice-born ones, afterwards for the yogin
the disturbances begin; all of them are signs of non-attainment.
<s>Pratibhā</s> is the first siddhi; <s>śravaṇa</s> is remembered as the second.
<s>Vārttā</s> is the third, O best of brahmins, and <s>darśana</s> is the fourth here.

children.text: āsvādā pañcamī proktā vedanā ṣaṣṭhikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āsvāda</s> is declared the fifth, and <s>vedanā</s> is remembered as the sixth.
By renouncing the small six siddhis, the siddhis become givers of true attainment for the sage.
<s>Pratibhā</s> is illumination, the functioning of illumination, and the state called illumination.
Intellect is discrimination; because it understands what is to be known, it is called intellect.
With regard to the subtle, the hidden, the past, the remote, and the future,
there is knowledge everywhere and always, according to the sequence of <s>pratibhā</s>.
For the yogin, from <s>śravaṇa</s>, there is effortless hearing of all sounds,
even of secret sounds, whether short, long, protracted, and so on.
The attainment of touch is what is set forth as <s>vedanā</s>.
From <s>darśana</s> there is effortless seeing of divine forms.
In that awareness of divine flavor there is indeed effortless <s>āsvāda</s>.
And <s>vārttā</s> is awareness of divine odors through cognition of the subtle elements.
Therefore yogins attain as far as the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, O twice-born ones.
In this world, while embodied, it is equal to sixty-four qualities.
Among these qualities, O twice-born ones, the incidental power is counted as multiplied.
Everything that is incidental to the self is to be abandoned entirely in every way.

children.text: paiśāce pārthivaṃ cāpyaṃ rākṣasānāṃ pure dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the paiśāca sphere is the earthly power, and the watery one in the city of the rākṣasas, O twice-born ones.

children.text: yākṣe tu taijasaṃ proktaṃ gāndharve śvasanātmakam
children.translated_text: In the yākṣa sphere the fiery power is taught, and in the gāndharva sphere the wind-natured one.

children.text: aindre vyomātmakaṃ sarvaṃ saumye caiva tu mānasam ||
children.translated_text: In the aindra sphere all is ether-natured, and in the saumya sphere it is mental.
In the prājāpatya sphere there is ahaṃkāra, and in the brāhma sphere the unsurpassed understanding.

children.text: ādye cāṣṭau dvitīye ca tathā ṣoḍaśarūpakam ||
children.translated_text: In the first there are eight, and in the second likewise a sixteenfold form.
In the third there are twenty-four, and in the fourth thirty-two.
In the fifth there are forty; it is remembered as consisting of the subtle elements.

children.text: gandho rasas tathā rūpaṃ śabdaḥ sparśastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Smell, taste, form, sound, and likewise touch
are each accomplished eightfold; that is the fifth, belonging to <s>Śatakratu</s>.
So too there are forty-eight, and likewise fifty-six.
The brāhma power, O best of the twice-born, obtains sixty-four qualities.
One should abandon the incidental power throughout the worlds up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Having seen through yoga the supreme happiness in the worlds, the knower of yoga should abandon it.

children.text: sthūlatā hrasvatā bālyaṃ vārdhakyaṃ yauvanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Grossness, shortness, childhood, old age, and youth,
a form of many births, and the assumption of a body in four ways:
without an earthly portion, always fragrant and joined with scent,
this is declared to be the eightfold great earthly sovereignty.
Dwelling in water, just as moving out upon the earth,
and being able, if he wishes, to drink even the ocean by himself without distress;
wherever he wishes in this world, there water appears to him.
Whatever object he takes up and wishes to enjoy at will,
that object has the corresponding taste for him, and there is assumption of three bodies.
There is also the holding of a lump of water in the hand without a vessel,
and the woundlessness of the body, joined with the earthly power.
This excellent watery sovereignty is declared to be sixteenfold.
Producing fire from the body, while free from fear of its heat,
and another world, though burned here, remaining unburned by one's own arrangement;
placing fire in the midst of water and preserving it,
holding fire in the hand, and its arrival by mere recollection;
making what has become ashes again as before, according to one's desire;
and producing forms by means of two, or by oneself without those three:
this fiery power, O best of sages, is indeed twenty-fourfold.
The speed of mind, dwelling within beings,
and again carrying on the shoulder great burdens such as mountains;

children.text: laghutvaṃ ca gurutvaṃ ca pāṇibhyāṃ vāyudhāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: lightness and heaviness, and holding wind in the hands;
shaking the earth everywhere by a blow from the fingertip;
and the production of a body from one source: this wind-sovereignty is remembered by the wise.
Production without a shadow, and the seeing of the senses,
constant travel through the sky together with the objects of the senses;
grasping sound at a distance and penetrating all sounds,
grasping the mark of the subtle elements and seeing all living beings:
this is called aindra sovereignty; through these the ancient power has been described.
Obtaining whatever one desires, and departing wherever one desires,
overpowering everywhere, and seeing every hidden thing;
creating in conformity with desire, mastery, and appearing beloved;
and seeing saṃsāra: this is the defining quality of the mental power.
Cutting, striking, binding, and the transformation of saṃsāra,
favor toward all beings, and victory over the time of death:
this excellent prājāpatya power, belonging to ahaṃkāra, has been declared.
Creation of the world without a cause, and also bestowal of favor,
dissolution, authority, and the setting in motion of worldly activity;
this manifest uniqueness, and creation separately, one by one,

children.text: saṃsārasya ca kartṛtvaṃ brāhmam etad anuttamam ||
children.translated_text: and agency over saṃsāra: this is the unsurpassed brāhma power.
This much has been stated as the principle; the preeminent Vaiṣṇava state
can be known by <s>Brahmā</s> through its qualities, but it cannot be known by others.
Beyond that exists the Śaiva state, which is not comprehended by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Pure and possessing countless qualities, who could know that which has <s>Śiva</s> as its nature?
These siddhis, when one has risen from absorption, are also proclaimed to be obstacles.
They must be restrained with effort, and with supreme detachment.
Having understood the surpassing perishability in objects and in dangers,
one should abandon everything through lack of attachment; such a person is called detached.
Freedom from thirst with regard to puruṣa is renowned; freedom from thirst for the guṇas is so called.
By detachment alone the siddhis that are incidental obstacles are to be abandoned.
One should abandon the incidental power throughout the worlds up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Having restrained everything, one should then abandon it; <s>Maheśvara</s> becomes gracious.
When he is gracious, stainless liberation is attained by supreme detachment.

children.text: athavānugrahārthaṃ ca līlārthaṃ vā tadā muniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, for the sake of favor or for the sake of play, then the sage

children.text: anirudhya viceṣṭedyaḥ so'pyevaṃ hi sukhī bhavet
children.translated_text: who acts without restraining them may also be happy in this way.
At one time, abandoning the earth, he plays splendidly in the sky.
At another time he utters the Vedas and their subtle meanings in brief.
At another time, on the basis of what has been heard and its meaning, he composes a verse-form.
At another time he may compose a daṇḍaka-form, thousands of such compositions.
and he obtains knowledge of the cries of assemblies of animals and birds.
Everything beginning with <s>Brahmā</s> and ending with immovable beings becomes like an āmalaka fruit in his hand.
What more need be said here? Thousands of kinds of knowledge
arise for that great-souled sage, O best of sages.

children.text: abhyāsenaiva vijñānaṃ viśuddhaṃ ca sthiraṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Through practice alone knowledge becomes pure and steady.
The knower of yoga sees all forms made of light; he sees everything.
He sees many images of gods and thousands of celestial vehicles.
He sees <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and the others,
and the planets, constellations, stars, and thousands of worlds.
Standing in <s>samādhi</s>, he sees even those established in the levels of the netherworld.
By the lamp of knowledge of the self, steady and unmoving within himself,
filled with the nectar of grace and placed in the vessel of purity,
a person, having destroyed darkness, truly sees the Lord within the self.

children.text: tasya prasādāddharmaś ca aiśvaryaṃ jñānameva ca
children.translated_text: By his grace come <s>dharma</s>, sovereignty, and knowledge,
as well as dispassion and liberation; there is no need for deliberation about this.
Its extent cannot be described even in tens of thousands of years.

children.text: yoge pāśupate niṣṭhā sthātavyaṃ ca munīśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one must stand firm in <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga, O lords among sages.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
For the good, the self-controlled, the manifestly twice-born, O best of twice-born men,
for those who know <s>dharma</s>, for the virtuous, for teachers whose self is <s>Śiva</s>,
for the compassionate, O best twice-born men, and likewise for ascetics,
for renouncers, the detached, the wise, and those whose selves are under control,
for givers, the restrained, and the threefold truth-speakers,
for the non-greedy, those joined with yoga, and those who know <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, O twice-born men,
<s>Maheśvara</s> is gracious to those who do not oppose the <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> traditions.
The word <s>sat</s> is a designation of <s>Brahman</s>; those who attain its end

children.text: sāyujyaṃ brahmaṇo yāti tena santaḥ pracakṣate
children.translated_text: go to union with <s>Brahman</s>, and for that reason they are called good people.
Those who, with respect to the tenfold object and the eight-characterized means,

children.text: na krudhyanti na hṛṣyanti jitātmānastu te smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: neither become angry nor rejoice are remembered as self-controlled.

children.text: sāmānyeṣu ca dravyeṣu tathā vaiśeṣikeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: Because <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>vaiśyas</s> are joined
with common substances and also with particular ones, they are therefore called twice-born.
For one established in the orders and life-stages, bringing happiness such as heaven,
knowledge of the <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> <s>dharma</s> is why he is called a knower of <s>dharma</s>.
Because he practices learning, the student living in celibacy, devoted to the guru's welfare, is virtuous.
And because he performs the prescribed rites, the householder is called virtuous.
Because he practices austerity in the forest, the <s>Vaikhānasa</s> is remembered as virtuous.

children.text: yatamāno yatiḥ sādhuḥ smṛto yogasya sādhanāt
children.translated_text: The striving ascetic is remembered as virtuous because he practices yoga.
Thus they are remembered as virtuous because they practice the duties of the life-stages.

children.text: gṛhastho brahmacārī ca vānaprastho yatis tathā
children.translated_text: The householder, the celibate student, the forest-dweller, and the renunciant:
here <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> have been declared to be these two action-based terms.
Skillful and unskillful action are remembered as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
This great word <s>dharma</s> is proclaimed in the sense of sustaining.

children.text: adhāraṇe mahattve ca adharma iti cocyate
children.translated_text: And in the sense of not sustaining, and in its grave importance, it is called <s>adharma</s>.
Here <s>dharma</s> is taught by the teachers as that which brings about what is desired.
And <s>adharma</s> is taught by the teachers as having an undesired result.
Elders who are not greedy, self-possessed, and free from hypocrisy,
properly disciplined and upright: these they call teachers.
Because he practices conduct himself and also establishes others in conduct,
and because he gathers the meanings of the śāstras, he is therefore called an <s>ācārya</s>.
What is known from hearing should be understood as <s>śrauta</s>; what comes from remembrance is called <s>smārta</s>.
Sacrifice, whose nature is the Veda, is <s>śrauta</s>; what has the nature of the orders and life-stages is <s>smārta</s>.
When asked, one who, having seen the matter as it really is, does not conceal it
but speaks according to what he has seen: here in the <s>Liṅga</s> this is taught as truth.
Celibacy, silence, and fasting,
non-violence, and complete tranquility everywhere are called tapas.
One who acts toward all beings as toward himself, for their welfare and against their harm,

children.text: vartate tvasakṛdvṛttiḥ kṛtsnā hyeṣā dayā smṛtā
children.translated_text: with repeated effort: this whole disposition is remembered as compassion.
Whatever object is most desired and has come lawfully in due order,
that should be given to a worthy person; this is the mark of giving on the donor's part.
This giving is threefold: inferior, superior, and middling.
Sharing with all beings out of compassion is the middling kind.
The <s>dharma</s> enjoined by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, whose nature is the orders and life-stages,
and which does not oppose the conduct of the cultured, is called good <s>dharma</s>.
One who has abandoned illusion, action, and its fruits is proclaimed to have <s>Śiva</s> as his self.
One who has withdrawn from all attachments and is disciplined is proclaimed a yogin.

children.text: asakto bhayato yastu viṣayeṣu vicārya ca ||
children.translated_text: One who, after reflecting on sense-objects as dangerous, remains unattached to them,
is said to be non-greedy and restrained, even when solicited from every side.

children.text: ātmārthaṃ vā parārthaṃ vā indriyāṇīha yasya vai ||
children.translated_text: When a person's senses here, whether for his own sake or for another's sake,

children.text: na mithyā sampravartante śamasyaiva tu lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: do not proceed falsely, that is precisely the mark of tranquility.
He is not disturbed by undesired things, nor does he rejoice over desired things.
Withdrawal from delight, pain, and despair is detachment.
Renunciation is the laying aside of actions, both those done and those not yet done.
The abandonment of skillful and unskillful actions is called renunciation.
In this insentient transformation, extending from the unmanifest down to the undifferentiated,
the knowledge of the difference between the sentient and the insentient is called knowledge.
For one thus endowed with knowledge and endowed with faith, <s>Śaṅkara</s>
is gracious; there is no doubt. And this, O best twice-born men, is <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: kiṃ tu guhyatamaṃ vakṣye sarvatra parameśvare ||
children.translated_text: But I shall tell what is most secret concerning <s>Parameśvara</s> everywhere.
There is devotion to <s>Bhava</s>, without doubt; joined with it, one is released.
Even toward an unworthy devotee, the Blessed Lord, the supreme <s>Īśvara</s>,

children.text: prasīdati na saṃdeho nigṛhya vividhaṃ tamaḥ
children.translated_text: is gracious, without doubt, after subduing the manifold darkness.
Knowledge, teaching, oblation, meditation, sacrifice, austerity, and sacred learning,
giving, study, and everything else are for devotion to <s>Bhava</s>; there is no doubt.
Not by thousands of <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vows, nor by hundreds of <s>prājāpatya</s> rites,
nor by month-long fasts or other observances, O best of sages, is devotion surpassed.
Those without devotion to this Blessed One, who dwells in the mountain cave, in this world
fall for the sake of their own enjoyment, but the devotee is released through devotion.
Merely from seeing devotees, O twice-born ones, heaven and the like are not difficult for men,

children.text: na durlabhā na sandeho bhaktānāṃ kiṃ punas tathā
children.translated_text: without doubt; how much more so, then, for the devotees themselves?
The standing of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Surendra</s>, and likewise of others

children.text: bhaktyā eva munīnāṃ ca balasaubhāgyameva ca
children.translated_text: is through devotion alone, as are the strength and good fortune of the sages.

children.text: bhavena ca tathā proktaṃ samprekṣyomāṃ pinākinā ||
children.translated_text: And this was spoken in the same way by <s>Bhava</s>, the bearer of the <s>pināka</s> bow, after he looked upon <s>Umā</s>,

children.text: devyai devena madhuraṃ vārāṇasyāṃ purā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: sweetly, by the god to the Goddess at <s>Vārāṇasī</s> long ago, O twice-born ones,
as she sat in <s>Avimukta</s> with <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme Self.
<s>Rudrāṇī</s>, having obtained that city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, said this to <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Śrīdevī</s> said:
By what, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, are you made subject, worshipped, and seen, O <s>Īśvara</s>?

children.text: tapasā vidyayā vāpi yogeneha vada prabho
children.translated_text: By austerity, by knowledge, or by yoga? Tell me here, O Lord.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: niśamya vacanaṃ tasyās tathā hyālokya pārvatīm ||
children.translated_text: Having heard her words and looked upon <s>Pārvatī</s> in that way,
the one marked with the young moon, smiling at her whose face was like the full moon, spoke.

children.text: smṛtvātha menayā patnyā girergāṃ kathitāṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: Then, remembering the speech that had once been told by <s>Menā</s>, wife of the mountain,
when she saw the great-souled Goddess staying for a long time on the mountain,

children.text: devi labdhā purī ramyā tvayā yatpraṣṭumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: he said: O Goddess, since this charming city has been obtained by you, you are worthy to ask.
For the sake of a dwelling place, your mother spoke of this here, O playful one, though you had forgotten.
Long ago I was also questioned by the Grandsire, O best among those who ask questions,

children.text: yathā tvayādya vai pṛṣṭo draṣṭuṃ brahmātmakaṃ tvaham
children.translated_text: just as you have now asked me, so that I might be seen as consisting of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: śvete śvetena varṇena dṛṣṭvā kalpe tu māṃ śubhe ||
children.translated_text: In the white kalpa, O fair one, when he saw me, white in color,

children.text: sadyojātaṃ tathā rakte raktaṃ vāmaṃ pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: the Grandsire called me <s>Sadyojāta</s>; and in the red one he called the red form <s>Vāma</s>.
In the yellow one he called the yellow form <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, and in the <s>Aghora</s> one the black <s>Īśvara</s>.
When I was named <s>Īśāna</s>, the one called <s>Viśvarūpa</s> then called me <s>Viśvarūpa</s>.
The Grandsire said:
O <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Sadyojāta</s>, O <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭo mayā tvaṃ gāyatryā devadeva maheśvara
children.translated_text: I have seen you through the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, O God of gods, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: kena vaśyo mahādeva dhyeyaḥ kutra ghṛṇānidhe ||
children.translated_text: By what are you made subject, O <s>Mahādeva</s>? Where are you to be meditated upon, O treasure of compassion?

children.text: dṛśyaḥ pūjyas tathā devyā vaktumarhasi śaṅkara
children.translated_text: How are you to be seen and worshipped by the Goddess? You should tell me, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
The Blessed Lord said:
I said, 'By faith alone am I made subject,' O lotus-born one.

children.text: dhyeyo liṅge tvayā dṛṣṭe viṣṇunā payasāṃ nidhau
children.translated_text: I am to be meditated upon in the <s>liṅga</s> seen by you and by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the ocean of waters.
I am to be worshipped in the five-faced form with the five purifying substances, O twice-born ones.
O <s>Bhava</s>, O first-born from the egg, O teacher of the world, I have been seen by you through devotion.

children.text: so'pi māmāha bhāvārthaṃ dattaṃ tasmai mayā purā ||
children.translated_text: He too spoke to me for the sake of devotion, and it was granted to him by me long ago.
Through devotion and with devotion, O queen of the gods, he saw me, the Lord dwelling in the heart.

children.text: tasmāttu śraddhayā vaśyo dṛśyaḥ śreṣṭhagireḥ sute ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I am made subject by faith and am seen by faith, O daughter of the best mountain.

children.text: pūjyo liṅge na saṃdehaḥ sarvadā śraddhayā dvijaiḥ
children.translated_text: I am to be worshipped in the <s>liṅga</s>, without doubt, always by twice-born men with faith.

children.text: śraddhā dharmaḥ paraḥ sūkṣmaḥ śraddhā jñānaṃ hutaṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Faith is the supreme and subtle <s>dharma</s>; faith is knowledge, offering, and austerity.

children.text: śraddhā svargaś ca mokṣaś ca dṛśyo'haṃ śraddhayā sadā ||
children.translated_text: Faith is heaven and liberation, and I am always seen through faith.
The seers said:
How did <s>Brahmā</s> see <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the great <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the great-souled, best ancient Person?
And <s>Aghora</s> and likewise <s>Īśāna</s>? You should tell it just as it was.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The twenty-ninth kalpa should be known as <s>Śvetalohita</s>.
In that kalpa, while <s>Brahmā</s> was then meditating that supreme meditation,
there arose a boy, crested and white-red in color.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣaṃ śrīmānbrahmā vai viśvatomukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that splendid person, <s>Brahmā</s>, who faces every direction,
placed in his heart the great-souled <s>Īśvara</s>, whose form is <s>brahman</s>.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, devoted to the yoga of meditation, became fixed on <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Knowing the supreme through the yoga of meditation, he worshipped the god, the <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: sadyojātaṃ tato brahma brahma vai samacintayat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> contemplated <s>Sadyojāta</s> as <s>brahman</s> itself.
Thereupon, from his side, white ones of great fame appeared.
They were <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, <s>Viśvananda</s>, and <s>Upanandana</s>.
Those great-souled ones were his disciples, by whom that <s>brahman</s> is always surrounded.
Before him, a great sage named <s>Śveta</s>, shining with white color,
was born; and from him was born that <s>Hara</s>, of great splendor.

children.text: tatra te munayaḥ sarve sadyojātaṃ maheśvaram
children.translated_text: There all those sages approached <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the great <s>Maheśvara</s>, for refuge,

children.text: prapannāḥ parayā bhaktyā gṛṇanto brahma śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: with supreme devotion, praising the eternal <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: tasmādviśveśvaraṃ devaṃ ye prapadyanti vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O twice-born ones, those who take refuge in the god <s>Viśveśvara</s>,
becoming intent on <s>prāṇāyāma</s> and with minds fixed on the supreme <s>brahman</s>,
all of them, freed from sin, spotless, and radiant with the splendor of <s>brahman</s>,
pass beyond the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and go to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thereafter the thirtieth kalpa is proclaimed as the one named <s>Rakta</s>.
There mighty <s>Brahmā</s> assumed a red color.
While the supreme-standing <s>Brahmā</s>, desiring a son, was meditating,
there appeared a boy of great splendor, adorned in red.
He wore red garlands and garments, had red eyes, and was powerful.

children.text: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātmānaṃ kumāraṃ raktavāsasam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that great-souled boy dressed in red garments,
Having resorted to supreme meditation, he perceived the god, the Lord.

children.text: sa taṃ praṇamya bhagavān brahmā paramayantritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, greatly restrained, bowed down to him.

children.text: vāmadevaṃ tato brahmā brahma vai samacintayat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> contemplated <s>Vāmadeva</s> as Brahman indeed.
Thus praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the supreme Lord,
pleased in heart in every way, spoke this to <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
Because, as you meditated desiring a son, I was seen by you, O <s>Pitāmaha</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭaḥ paramayā bhaktyā stutaś ca brahmapūrvakam
children.translated_text: with supreme devotion, and was praised with Brahman first,
therefore, having gained the power of meditation, with effort in every <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle),
you will know me as the renowned Lord, the creator of worlds.
Then four sons of that great-souled one
came into being, great-souled and pure with Brahmanic splendor:

children.text: virajāś ca vibāhuś ca viśoko viśvabhāvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viraja</s>, <s>Vibāhu</s>, <s>Viśoka</s>, and <s>Viśvabhāvana</s>.
Devoted to Brahman, equal to <s>Brahmā</s>, heroic and resolute,
all wearing red garments, red garlands, and red unguents,
their limbs smeared with red saffron and anointed with red ash,
then, at the end of a thousand years, intent on the state of Brahman,
those great-souled ones praised that <s>Vāmadeva</s>-Brahman.
For the favoring of the worlds, and from desire for the welfare of disciples,
those dear ones of <s>Brahmā</s> gave the entire instruction in <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty).
Then once again they entered <s>Mahādeva</s>, the imperishable <s>Rudra</s>.
And whatever other best twice-born men yoke themselves to the leftward Lord,
and behold <s>Mahādeva</s>, being his devotees and wholly devoted to him,
all those, freed from sin, stainless and chaste,
will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, from which return is hard to obtain.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The thirty-first <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle) is remembered as <s>Pītavāsas</s>, 'Yellow-clad,'

children.text: brahmā yatra mahābhāgaḥ pītavāsā babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: in which the blessed <s>Brahmā</s> became clothed in yellow.
As <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme-standing one, meditated desiring a son,
a greatly radiant youth appeared, wearing yellow garments.
His body was anointed with yellow perfumes; he wore yellow garlands and clothing,
with a golden sacred thread, a yellow turban, and mighty arms.
Seeing him, <s>Brahmā</s>, joined with meditation, saw the great lord of the world,
and with his mind sought refuge in the all-pervading creator of worlds.
Then, entered into meditation there, <s>Brahmā</s> saw the excellent <s>Māheśvarī</s> cow,
universal in form, issued from the mouth of <s>Maheśvara</s>.
She was four-footed, four-faced, four-handed, and four-breasted,
four-eyed, four-horned, four-tusked, and four-mouthed,
endowed with thirty-two qualities, a ruling goddess facing every direction.

children.text: sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā mahātejā mahādevīṃ maheśvarīm ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that great goddess, the <s>Māheśvarī</s>, the greatly radiant one,
again <s>Mahādeva</s>, honored by all the gods, spoke.
He sang again and again, 'Thought, memory, intelligence.'
'Come, come, O great goddess,' and he stood with joined palms before the all-pervading Lord.
'Envelop the universe by yoga; bring the whole world under control.'

children.text: atha tāmāha deveśo rudrāṇī tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
children.translated_text: Then the lord of gods said to her, 'You will become <s>Rudrāṇī</s>.
For the welfare of Brahmins you will be the supreme reality.'
Then to the <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, who desired a son and was meditating,
the Lord of gods, the teacher of the world, gave her as four-footed.
Then, recognizing her through the yoga of meditation as the supreme goddess,
<s>Brahmā</s> obtained that <s>Māheśvarī</s> from the guru of the world.

children.text: gāyatrīṃ tu tato raudrīṃ dhyātvā brahmānuyantritaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, meditating on the <s>Raudrī Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> was brought under its guidance.
Thus this Vedic knowledge was declared to be the <s>Raudrī Gāyatrī</s>.
Having recited the great goddess, honored by the worlds,
<s>Brahmā</s> took refuge in <s>Mahādeva</s> with a mind joined to meditation.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the Lord, gave him divine yoga, rich in sacred learning,

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ jñānasaṃpattiṃ vairāgyaṃ ca dadau prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: sovereignty, the attainment of knowledge, and detachment.
Then from his side divine youths appeared,
wearing yellow garlands and garments, anointed with yellow wreaths,
with heads in yellow-bright turbans, yellow faces, and yellow hair.
Then, after dwelling for a thousand years, stainless in vigor,
yogic in nature, gladdened by ascetic heat, desiring the welfare of Brahmins,
endowed with the power of <s>dharma-yoga</s> (sacred yogic discipline), for the long-session sages,
they taught the great yoga and entered <s>Maheśvara</s>.
In this same way, those who have taken refuge in <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and others too, self-restrained, joined to meditation, and with senses conquered,
all those, abandoning sin, stainless and bright with Brahmanic splendor,
enter <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>; for them there is no rebirth.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then, when that yellow-colored <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle) of <s>Svayambhū</s> had passed,
again another <s>kalpa</s> began, called <s>Asita</s>, the Dark one.
At that time, when the single ocean had arisen for a thousand divine years,
<s>Brahmā</s>, wishing to create beings, pondered in sorrow.
As that lord, desirous of a son, was thinking,
a black color arose while the <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> meditated.
Then the greatly radiant one saw a youth who had appeared,
black in color, very powerful, blazing with his own brilliance,
wearing black garments and turban, and a black sacred thread,
adorned with a black diadem and anointed with black garlands.
Seeing that great-souled <s>Aghora</s>, terrible in valor,
he bowed to the wondrous black-and-tawny Lord of gods.
Rich in fortune, intent on prāṇāyāma, having placed <s>Maheśvara</s> in his heart,
and with his mind joined to meditation, he took refuge in that <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: aghoraṃ tu tato brahmā brahmarūpaṃ vyacintayat
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> contemplated <s>Aghora</s>, whose form was brahman.
And as <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme lord, was meditating in that way,
the god <s>Aghora</s>, terrible in valor, granted him a vision.
Then at his side there appeared dark ones, wearing dark garlands and unguents:
four great-souled young princes came into being.
They were <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaśikha</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇāsya</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇavastradhṛk</s>.
Then for a thousand years, by yoga, they worshiped the supreme lord,
the great Yoga, and afterward gave it again to their disciples.
Endowed with yoga through yoga, entering <s>Śiva</s> with the mind,
they entered the stainless, qualityless state, the lord of the universe.
Thus, by this yoga, whatever other wise men also
contemplate <s>Mahādeva</s> will go to the imperishable <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then, when that kalpa had passed, dark-colored and terrifying,
<s>Brahmā</s> praised the lord of the gods, that one whose form was brahman.
Then <s>Hara</s>, pleased, favored <s>Brahmā</s> and said to him:

children.text: anenaiva tu rūpeṇa saṃharāmi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "With this very form I destroy them; there is no doubt.
I destroy terrible sins beginning with the killing of a brahmin, and also others,
lowly ones, O greatly fortunate one, and likewise sins of many kinds;
secondary sins as well, and evil acts, O good-vowed one,
mental sins, very sharp ones, and verbal ones, O Grandfather;
bodily sins, mixed sins, and those arising incidentally,
those done intentionally, and those innate or adventitious;
sins arising from the mother's body, and sins in the father's body:

children.text: saṃharāmi na saṃdehaḥ sarvaṃ pātakajaṃ vibho ||
children.translated_text: I destroy everything born from sin, O lord; there is no doubt.

children.text: lakṣaṃ japtvā hyaghorebhyo brahmahā mucyate prabho
children.translated_text: After reciting the Aghora formula one hundred thousand times, a killer of a brahmin is released, O lord;

children.text: tadardhaṃ vācike vatsa tadardhaṃ mānase punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: half of that is for verbal sin, my child, and half of that again for mental sin.
For an intentional act four times as much is prescribed, and for one done from anger eight times as much is remembered.
A killer of a hero should practice only one hundred thousand recitations; a destroyer of an embryo should practice ten million.

children.text: mātṛhā niyutaṃ japtvā śudhyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: A killer of his mother, after reciting a million times, is purified; there is no doubt here.

children.text: goghnaścaiva kṛtaghnaś ca strīghnaḥ pāpayuto naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A cow-killer, an ingrate, a woman-killer, and a man joined to sin,
after practicing the Aghora formula ten thousand times, is released; there is no doubt here.
A drinker of liquor is released by just one hundred thousand recitations, whether knowingly or unknowingly, O lord;
there is no doubt here, and with half that number one is released from drinking vāruṇī liquor.

children.text: asnātāśī sahasreṇa ajapī ca tathā dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who eats without bathing, and likewise a twice-born man who does not recite, is purified by one thousand recitations;
one who eats without offering oblation and one who does not give are purified by one thousand.
A thief of a brahmin's property and the basest of men, a stealer of gold,

children.text: niyutaṃ mānasaṃ japtvā mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: after mentally reciting ten million times, is released; there is no doubt here.
Even one who has gone to his teacher's bed, or the basest of men who has killed his mother,

children.text: brahmaghnaś ca japedevaṃ mānasaṃ vai pitāmaha
children.translated_text: or a killer of a brahmin, should recite this mentally, O Grandfather.
Sin from contact with sinners is defined as equal to that sin.
Even so, by only ten thousand recitations one is freed from the sin.
A sinner by association should recite one hundred thousand times mentally, with understanding.

children.text: upāṃśu yaccaturdhā vai vācikaṃ cāṣṭadhā japet
children.translated_text: The muttered recitation is fourfold, and the vocal recitation should be recited eightfold.
For secondary sins it is remembered to be only half the amount for a grave sin.

children.text: tadardhaṃ kevale pāpe nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: Half of that is for an ordinary sin; no deliberation is to be made here.
If a sinning brahmin has committed brahmin-killing, drinking liquor, stealing gold,

children.text: kṛtvā ca gurutalpaṃ ca pāpakṛdbrāhmaṇo yadi
children.translated_text: or intercourse with his teacher's wife,
then, O twice-born ones, cow urine from a tawny cow is to be taken with the Rudra Gāyatrī.

children.text: gandhadvāreti tasyā vai gomayaṃ svastham āharet
children.translated_text: With the mantra beginning 'gandhadvāra' one should bring its fresh cow dung.
A wise man should collect ghee from a tawny cow with the mantra beginning 'tejo 'si śukta'.
With 'āpyāyasva' he should bring milk, and with 'dadhikrāvṇa' he should bring curds.

children.text: gavyaṃ dadhi navaṃ sākṣātkāpilaṃ vai pitāmaha ||
children.translated_text: The cow's curd should be fresh, directly from a tawny cow, O Grandfather.
With the mantra 'devasya tvā' he should collect kuśa-water.
Having placed it all together in a golden vessel, or in a silver one with the Aghora mantra,

children.text: tāmre vā padmapātre vā pālāśe vā dale śubhe
children.translated_text: or in a copper vessel, or in a lotus vessel, or on an auspicious leaf of palāśa,
with a kuśa-bunch and rich with all jewels, he should put gold there as well.
He should recite the mantra called Aghora one hundred thousand times and make offerings with ghee and the like,

children.text: ghṛtena caruṇā caiva samidbhiś ca tilais tathā ||
children.translated_text: with ghee, sacrificial porridge, fuel-sticks, and sesame seeds,
and with barley and rice; he should make oblations separately with each.

children.text: pratyekaṃ saptavāraṃ tu dravyālābhe ghṛtena tu ||
children.translated_text: For each substance he should do so seven times; if the materials are unavailable, then with ghee.
Having offered to the lord of gods with the Aghora mantra, and having bathed with the Aghora mantra, O twice-born ones,
having bathed him with eight droṇas of ghee and afterward purified him,
one who has fasted day and night and bathed should drink the kuśa mixture in front of <s>Śiva</s>.
He should perform the brāhma rite, the brahman-recitation, and sip water according to rule.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā kṛtaghno 'pi brahmahā bhrūṇahā tathā
children.translated_text: Having done this, even an ingrate, a brahmin-killer, a destroyer of an embryo,
a killer of a hero, a killer of his teacher, and a betrayer of a friend's trust,
a thief, a stealer of gold, and one always engaged in intercourse with his teacher's wife,
a drinker of liquor, one attached to a low woman, and a violator of another's wife,

children.text: brahmasvahā tathā goghno mātṛhā pitṛhā tathā
children.translated_text: a thief of brahmin property, a cow-killer, and likewise a killer of his mother or father,
one who dislodges a deity and one who destroys a liṅga,

children.text: tathānyāni ca pāpāni mānasāni dvijo yadi
children.translated_text: and if a twice-born man has committed other mental sins,
and likewise thousands of other verbal and bodily sins,
he is immediately released, even from sins of hundreds of other births.
This secret has been taught in connection with the lord <s>Aghora</s>.
Therefore a twice-born man should recite it daily for purification from all sins."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Now another <s>kalpa</s> of <s>Brahmā</s> is taking place, O bulls among sages,
known by the name <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, exceedingly wondrous.

children.text: vinivṛtte tu saṃhāre punaḥ sṛṣṭe carācare
children.translated_text: When the dissolution had ceased and the moving and unmoving world had again been created,
as <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, was meditating with desire for a son,
there appeared <s>Sarasvatī</s>, great-sounding and universal in form,
wearing all garlands and garments, wearing the sacred thread of all sacrifices,
with every turban and every fragrance, mother of all, broad-lipped.
Then the blessed one contemplated <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s>, in such a form,
shining like pure crystal and adorned with every ornament.

children.text: atha taṃ manasā dhyātvā yuktātmā vai pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having contemplated him in his mind, the self-controlled <s>Pitāmaha</s>
bowed to the god <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of all, all-pervading master.
Oṃ. O <s>Īśāna</s>, homage to you; O <s>Mahādeva</s>, homage to you.
Homage to you, O <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s> of all branches of knowledge.
Homage to you, O <s>Īśāna</s> of all beings, bull-mounted one.
To you, lord of <s>Brahmā</s>, to <s>Brahman</s>, to the one whose form is <s>Brahman</s>,
homage to the lord of <s>Brahman</s>; may <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, be auspicious to me.
O embodiment of the syllable oṃ, lord of gods, O <s>Sadyojāta</s>, homage, homage.

children.text: prapadye tvāṃ prapanno 'smi sadyojātāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I take refuge in you; I have come for refuge. Homage indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.

children.text: abhave ca bhave tubhyaṃ tathā nātibhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to you as non-being and as being, and likewise as that which is beyond becoming.
O source of existence, O lord of existence, favor me, O greatly radiant one.
O <s>Vāmadeva</s>, homage to you, and to the eldest and the giver of boons.

children.text: namo rudrāya kālāya kalanāya namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to Time, and repeated homage to the measurer of time.
Homage also to <s>Vikaraṇa</s>, to the one colored by time, to the one possessed of form.

children.text: balāya balināṃ nityaṃ sadā vikaraṇāya te ||
children.translated_text: To strength, to the strong among the strong forever, and always to you as <s>Vikaraṇa</s>.
To the crusher of strength, to the strong one, to the one whose form is <s>Brahman</s>,
to the lord of the lords of all beings and to the subduer of beings.
Homage to you, O god <s>Manonmanā</s>, O greatly radiant one.
Homage to you, O <s>Vāmadeva</s>, O gracious one, O great-souled one.

children.text: jyeṣṭhāya caiva śreṣṭhāya rudrāya varadāya ca
children.translated_text: And to the eldest and the best, to <s>Rudra</s> and to the giver of boons,
homage to you, slayer of time; homage to you, great-souled one.
With this praise he bowed to the lord of gods, whose banner is the bull.
Whoever recites it even once here will go to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: śrāvayedvā dvijān śrāddhe sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Or, if one causes twice-born men to hear it at a <s>śrāddha</s>, he goes to the supreme goal.
As <s>Pitāmaha</s> was thus absorbed in meditation there and bowing down,
the blessed Lord said, 'I am pleased with you. What do you desire?'
Then, having bowed, he addressed <s>Maheśvara</s>, whose speech is pure,

children.text: uvāca bhagavān rudraṃ prītaṃ prītena cetasā
children.translated_text: speaking to the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, who was pleased, with a pleased mind.
This universal form of yours, the universal cow, the auspicious sovereign lady,
I wish to know this: how is she, O <s>Parameśvara</s>?
Who is this blessed goddess, four-footed and four-faced,
four-horned, four-mouthed, four-tusked, four-breasted,
four-handed and four-eyed? How is she remembered as <s>Viśvarūpā</s>?
What is her name and lineage? What is her power, and what is her action?
Hearing that statement of his, the god of gods, whose banner is the bull,
addressed <s>Brahmā</s>, the self-born bull among gods.
This is the secret of all mantras, purifying and increasing nourishment.
Listen to this supreme mystery, just as it was at the first creation.

children.text: evaṃ yo vartate kalpo viśvarūpastvasau mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kalpa</s> that proceeds in this way is regarded as <s>Viśvarūpa</s>.

children.text: brahmasthānamidaṃ cāpi yatra prāptaṃ tvayā prabho
children.translated_text: And this is the station of <s>Brahmā</s>, which you have reached, O lord.

children.text: tvattaḥ parataraṃ deva viṣṇunā tatpadaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Beyond you, O god, that auspicious state was attained by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
by the pure <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, who was born from my left limb.
From that time onward this <s>kalpa</s> is indeed the thirty-third.
A hundred hundred-thousands of self-born ones have passed away
before you, O lord of gods; hear of that, O great-minded one.
He should be known as <s>Ānanda</s>, established in the state of bliss.
Of the <s>Māṇḍavya</s> lineage, through austerity he came to be my son.

children.text: tvayi yogaṃ ca sāṃkhyaṃ ca tapovidyāvidhikriyāḥ
children.translated_text: In you are established <s>yoga</s>, <s>sāṃkhya</s>, ascetic knowledge, and prescribed rites,

children.text: ṛtaṃ satyaṃ dayā brahma ahiṃsā sanmatiḥ kṣamā ||
children.translated_text: cosmic order, truth, compassion, <s>Brahman</s>, non-injury, right thought, and patience,
meditation, the object of meditation, restraint, peace, knowledge and ignorance, intelligence and firmness,

children.text: kāntirnītiḥ prathā medhā lajjā dṛṣṭiḥ sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: beauty, policy, renown, insight, modesty, vision, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ kriyā caiva prasādaś ca pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: contentment, nourishment, action, and grace as well are established.
These are indeed thirty-two good qualities, known by the name of the thirty-two syllables.
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) has been ordained, O <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Maheśvarī</s> is your source,
and also the source of the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> and of others too, O lord.
This blessed goddess, my own source, is established.
Four-faced, womb of the world, <s>Prakṛti</s>, the cow, is established.

children.text: gaurī māyā ca vidyā ca kṛṣṇā haimavatīti ca
children.translated_text: She is <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, and <s>Haimavatī</s>,
and also <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>, as those who contemplate reality call her.

children.text: ajāmekāṃ lohitāṃ śuklakṛṣṇāṃ viśvaprajāṃ sṛjamānāṃ sarūpām
children.translated_text: She is the one unborn female, red, white, and black, producing world-creatures of forms like her own.

children.text: ajo'haṃ māṃ viddhi tāṃ viśvarūpaṃ gāyatrīṃ gāṃ viśvarūpāṃ hi buddhyā ||
children.translated_text: Know me as the unborn one; understand her by insight as that <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, as <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the cow of universal form.
Having spoken thus, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s>, created.
Then, from beside the goddess, boys of every form

children.text: jaṭī muṇḍī śikhaṇḍī ca ardhamuṇḍaś ca jajñire
children.translated_text: were born: matted-haired, shaven-headed, crested, and half-shaven.
Then those of very great vigor, by the <s>yoga</s> just described,
after worshipping <s>Maheśvara</s> for a thousand divine years,
having given the entire instruction in <s>dharma</s> and made it firmly composed of <s>yoga</s>,
disciplined and self-controlled, entered <s>Rudra</s>, the Lord.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus the origin of the <s>Sahya</s> mountains and the others has been briefly declared.
Whoever reads it, hears it, or has it recited to the best of the twice-born,
attains union with Brahman through the grace of the <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
The seers said:
How did the <s>liṅga</s> arise, and how is <s>Śaṅkara</s> to be worshipped in the <s>liṅga</s>?

children.text: kiṃ liṅgaṃ kas tathā liṅgī sūta vaktumihārhasi
children.translated_text: What is the <s>liṅga</s>, and who is the <s>liṅgī</s>? <s>Sūta</s>, you ought to tell us here.
<s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ devāś ca ṛṣayaḥ praṇipatya pitāmaham ||
children.translated_text: In this way the gods and seers, bowing down to the Grandfather,
asked him themselves: 'Blessed one, how did the <s>liṅga</s> come to be?'

children.text: liṅge maheśvaro rudraḥ samabhyarcyaḥ kathaṃ tviti ||
children.translated_text: 'And how is <s>Rudra Maheśvara</s> to be worshipped in the <s>liṅga</s>?'

children.text: kiṃ liṅgaṃ kas tathā liṅgī so'pyāha ca pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: 'What is the <s>liṅga</s>, and who is the <s>liṅgī</s>?' Then the Grandfather too spoke.
The Grandfather said:
<s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) is said to be the <s>liṅga</s>, and <s>Parameśvara</s> is the <s>liṅgī</s>.
For my protection in the ocean, it was there from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O best of gods.
When the aerial creation had gone to <s>Janaloka</s> together with the seers,

children.text: sthitikāle tadā pūrṇe tataḥ pratyāhṛte tathā
children.translated_text: when the time of maintenance was complete and then withdrawn,
at the end of a thousand cycles of four yugas, when the gods had gone to <s>Satyaloka</s>,
when my supremacy as <s>Brahmā</s> was gone and all had become level at the end,

children.text: śuṣke ca sthāvare sarve tvanāvṛṣṭyā ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when all stationary beings had dried up completely through drought,
animals, human beings, trees, piśācas, flesh-eaters,
gandharvas and the rest were gradually burned up by the rays of the sun.
When there was one terrible ocean, surrounded everywhere by darkness,
the pure, untroubled one, whose nature is yoga, slept in the waters:
the thousand-headed, all-formed Self, thousand-eyed and thousand-footed,
thousand-armed, all-knowing, the source of the being of all the gods.
He is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> through rajas, and himself <s>Śaṅkara</s> through tamas;
through sattva he is all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and through being the Self of all he is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He is time itself, <s>Kālanābha</s>, white, black, and without qualities,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> of mighty arms, the Self of all, made of being and non-being.
Seeing that lotus-eyed one lying in such a state,
I, deluded by his māyā and angered, spoke to him:
'Who are you? Speak!' With my hand I lifted up the eternal one.

children.text: tadā hastaprahāreṇa tīvreṇa sa dṛḍhena tu ||
children.translated_text: Then, by that sharp and firm blow of the hand,
he awoke from his serpent-couch and, self-controlled, sat up for a moment.
The blessed <s>Hari</s>, his lotus-like eyes damp with sleep,
saw me standing before him, invested with radiance.

children.text: āha cotthāya bhagavān hasanmāṃ madhuraṃ sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: Then the Blessed One rose and, smiling, spoke sweetly to me once:
'Welcome, welcome, child, O Grandfather of great splendor.'
Hearing that speech of his, preceded by a smile, O bulls among gods,
I, bound in hostility by rajas, addressed <s>Janārdana</s>:
'You call me child, child, though I am the cause of creation and destruction,
speaking here to me with an inward smile, O sinless one, as a teacher to a pupil,
to me, the direct maker of the worlds and the one who sets prakṛti in motion,
the eternal, unborn <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viriñci</s>, source of the universe,
the Self of the universe, the ordainer, the establisher, the lotus-eyed one.
Why do you speak so out of delusion? You should tell me quickly.'
He too said to me: 'I am the maker of the worlds; understand this.
I am their sustainer and destroyer. You, sir, have descended from a limb of my imperishable body.
You have forgotten the lord of the universe, faultless <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the supreme Self, much-invoked and much-praised,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the Lord, the source and origin of the universe.
There is no fault of yours in this; this has been caused by my māyā.
Hear the truth, Four-faced One: this one indeed is the lord of all gods.

children.text: kartā netā ca hartā ca na mayāsti samo vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: I am the maker, guide, and destroyer; there is no lord equal to me.

children.text: ahameva paraṃ brahma paraṃ tattvaṃ pitāmaha ||
children.translated_text: I alone am the supreme Brahman, the supreme principle, O Grandfather.

children.text: ahameva paraṃ jyotiḥ paramātmā tvahaṃ vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: I alone am the supreme light; I am the supreme Self, the all-powerful one.
Whatever is seen or heard in this world, moving and unmoving,
know all that, Four-faced One, to be entirely made of me.
Long ago I myself created the unmanifest, twenty-fourfold principle.
The bound aṇus (individual souls), ending with the eternal ones, and those beginning with the wrath-born were created.
By my favor you create many cosmic eggs here in sport.
Intellect was created by me; in it, afterward, arose ahaṅkāra (ego-principle) in three forms.
From that came the five subtle elements, and mind as the sixth, together with the senses.
The elements beginning with space, and all elemental products, arose in sport.'

children.text: ityuktavati tasmiṃś ca mayi cāpi vacas tathā ||
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus, and when I too had spoken words in the same way,
a very terrible battle arose between the two of us, making the hair stand on end,
in the middle of the ocean of dissolution, as we were bound in hostility by rajas.
In the meantime a <s>liṅga</s> appeared before the two of us,
shining, for the calming of the dispute and for awakening our understanding,
rich with thousands of wreaths of flame, like hundreds of fires of time,
free from decrease and increase, devoid of beginning, middle, and end,
incomparable, indescribable, unmanifest, the source of the universe.
The blessed <s>Hari</s>, bewildered by its thousand flames,
spoke to me, who was also bewildered: 'Let us examine this fire-born thing.
I shall go downward along this incomparable pillar of fire,
and you should quickly go upward with effort.'
Having spoken thus, the Self of the universe then assumed his own form
as a boar; and I too at once became a swan, O gods.
From that time onward they call me <s>Haṃsa</s>, and also <s>Haṃsa Virāj</s>.

children.text: haṃsahaṃseti yo brūyānmāṃ haṃsaḥ sa bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Whoever says to me, "Haṃsa, haṃsa," will become a haṃsa,
very white, fire-eyed, and furnished with wings on every side.
Having become swift as mind and wind, I went upward, O gods;
and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> too, the soul of the universe, took a form like a mass of blue-black collyrium,
ten yojanas broad and a hundred yojanas long,
with the bulk of Mount <s>Meru</s> and with sharp-pointed white tusks,
shining like the sun at the end of time, long-snouted, and loud-roaring,
short-footed, variegated in limb, victorious, firm, and incomparable.
Having assumed the black boar form, he went downward.
Thus for a thousand years <s>Viṣṇu</s> hastened downward,
but as a boar he did not see even the smallest root of this liṅga.
For that same length of time I too went upward, O slayer of foes,
quickly, with every effort, desiring to know its end.
Exhausted and not seeing its end, I came down because of pride.
Likewise Bhagavān <s>Viṣṇu</s>, exhausted and with terrified eyes,
quickly rose up, he whose being is the source of all gods and whose body was great.
Great-minded, he came together with me and bowed down.
Deluded by the māyā (power of illusion) of <s>Śambhu</s>, he stood with agitated mind.
Behind, at the side, and in front of <s>Parameśvara</s>,

children.text: praṇipatya mayā sārdhaṃ sasmāra kimidaṃ tviti ||
children.translated_text: having bowed down together with me, he reflected, "What is this?"
Then there arose there a resonance whose mark was sound,
"Oṃ, Oṃ," O best of gods, very distinct and marked by prolongation.
Wondering, "What is this?", I stood by that great sound.
Then on the southern side of the liṅga he saw the eternal one:
the first phoneme, the letter a; then the letter u on the north;
and the letter m in the middle, ending in resonance: thus it was Oṃ.
He saw the first phoneme on the south like the orb of the sun,
and the letter u on the north, like fire, O best of men,
and likewise the middle letter m, like the orb of the cool-rayed moon.
Above it he then saw the Lord, pure as crystal,
beyond the fourth state, immortal, without parts, free from disturbance,
free from duality, alone, void, devoid of exterior and interior,
with exterior and interior, and abiding with exterior and interior,
without beginning, middle, or end, and the cause even of bliss.
The three mātrās and the half-mātrā, called nāda, are designated Brahman;
the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas are in the form of those mātrās, O <s>Mādhava</s>.
From the sounds of the Veda he contemplated the Lord, the soul of the universe.
Then the Veda became a seer; from that seer came the most excellent auspicious essence.
Through that very seer <s>Viṣṇu</s> came to know <s>Parameśvara</s>.
The god said:

children.text: cintayā rahito rudro vāco yanmanasā saha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> is beyond thought; from him speech together with the mind
turns back without reaching him, yet he is denoted by the single syllable.
By the single syllable that truth is denoted, the immortal supreme cause,
truth, bliss, immortality, the supreme Brahman beyond the highest.
From the single syllable, known as a, came Bhagavān, the golden-egg-born one.
From the single syllable, known as u, came <s>Hari</s>, the supreme cause.
From the single syllable, known as m, came Bhagavān <s>Nīlalohita</s>.
The one known as a is the maker of creation; the one known as u is the deluder;
the one known as m became always the giver of grace to those two.
The lord known as m is the seed-bearer; a is called the seed;
<s>Hari</s>, known as u, is the womb, lord of <s>Pradhāna</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: bījī ca bījaṃ tadyonirnādākhyaś ca maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: The seed-bearer, the seed, that womb, and <s>Maheśvara</s>, called nāda,

children.text: bījī vibhajya cātmānaṃ svecchayā tu vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the seed-bearer divided himself and stood established by his own will.
From this liṅga came the seed, the letter a, of the Lord who possesses seed;
placed in the womb of the letter u, it grew on every side.
The egg became golden, enclosing that first syllable;
for many years that divine egg remained situated in the waters.
Then, at the end of a thousand years, the egg born from the unborn was split in two;

children.text: aṇḍam apsu sthitaṃ sākṣād ādyākhyeneśvareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: standing in the waters, it was directly split by the Lord called the First.
Of that egg, the auspicious golden shell situated above
became heaven, while the other became earth with its five characteristics.
From that egg was born the four-faced one known as a;

children.text: sa sraṣṭā sarvalokānāṃ sa eva trividhaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is the creator of all worlds; he himself is the threefold Lord.
Thus "Oṃ, Oṃ" was spoken, so say the best of the Yajus.

children.text: yajuṣāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā ṛcaḥ sāmāni sādaram ||
children.translated_text: Hearing the utterance of the Yajus, the Ṛks and Sāmans respectfully
then declared the same eternally, O <s>Hari</s>, O <s>Brahmā</s>, as the śrutis.
Then, having known the Lord of gods correctly through the śruti-born
mantras, he praised <s>Maheśvara</s>, the god of very great splendor.
Satisfied by the praise of us two, the stainless one in that liṅga
assumed a divine form made of sound and stood laughing.
The letter a is his head, and the long ā is called his forehead.
The letter i is the right eye; ī is the left eye.
The letter u is the right ear; ū is called the left.
The vocalic ṛ is his right cheek, that of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>;

children.text: vāmaṃ kapolam ṝkāro ﾱ ﾲ nāsāpuṭe ubhe ||
children.translated_text: vocalic ṝ is the left cheek; the corrupted signs, likely ḷ and ḹ, are the two nostrils.
The letter e is his upper lip, and ai, O lord, is the lower.
The letters o and au are the two rows of teeth respectively.
Aṃ and aḥ are the palates of that wise God of gods.
The five syllables beginning with ka are his five hands on the right.
In the same way the five syllables beginning with ca are the five hands on the left.
The five syllables beginning with ṭa are the feet, and likewise the five syllables beginning with ta.
The syllable pa is his belly; the syllable pha is called his side.

children.text: bakāro vāmapārśvaṃ vai bhakāraṃ skandhamasya tat ||
children.translated_text: The syllable ba is indeed the left side, and the syllable bha is that shoulder of his.
The syllable ma is the heart of <s>Śambhu</s>, the yogin <s>Mahādeva</s>.
The seven letters from ya through sa are indeed the seven bodily elements of the all-pervading lord.

children.text: hakāra ātmarūpaṃ vai kṣakāraḥ krodha ucyate
children.translated_text: The syllable ha is indeed the form of the self, and the syllable kṣa is called wrath.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā umayā sārdhaṃ bhagavantaṃ maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: Having seen that blessed <s>Maheśvara</s> together with <s>Umā</s>,
the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> bowed down and again looked upward.
He saw a mantra arising from the <s>oṅkāra</s> and joined with five kalās (parts),
resembling pure crystal, and furnished with thirty-eight auspicious syllables.
It became again a producer of wisdom and an accomplisher of every religious and worldly aim.
He saw a green mantra arising from the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, able to bring under control,
rich in twenty-four phonemes, unsurpassed, and consisting of four kalās.
He saw a black mantra of the <s>Atharva</s>, furnished with eight kalās,
extremely fit for abhicāra (hostile rites), with thirty-three auspicious syllables.
He saw one connected with the <s>Yajurveda</s>, with thirty-five auspicious syllables,
joined with eight kalās, very white, and also pacificatory.
He saw one joined with thirteen kalās, red, together with the child and the others,
arising from the <s>Sāman</s>, beginning with the jagatī metre, and causing growth and dissolution.
The syllables of this excellent mantra are sixty plus six.

children.text: pañca mantrāṃs tathā labdhvā jajāpa bhagavān hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained the five mantras in this way, the blessed <s>Hari</s> recited them.
Then he saw the lord whose kalās and syllables had the forms of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajur</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>,
<s>Īśāna</s>, with <s>Īśa</s> as his crown, with <s>Puruṣa</s> as his face, ancient,
with <s>Aghora</s> as his heart, pleasing, with <s>Vāma</s> as his secret part, <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
with <s>Sadyaḥ</s> as his feet, <s>Mahādeva</s>, adorned with great lordly serpents,
<s>Śiva</s>, whose feet and faces are everywhere and whose eyes and hands are everywhere,
the overlord of <s>Brahmā</s>, the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
Again he praised the boon-giving Lord with cherished words.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:
Obeisance to the one-syllabled <s>Rudra</s>, to the syllable a, whose form is the self;
obeisance indeed to the syllable u, the primordial god, whose body is knowledge.
Obeisance to the third, the syllable ma, to <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme self,
whose colors are sun, fire, and moon, and who is the sacrificer.
Obeisance to fire, whose form is <s>Rudra</s>; obeisance to the lord of the <s>Rudras</s>.
Obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, to the <s>Śiva</s>-mantra, to <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the creator.
To you as <s>Vāma</s>, as <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the boon-giver and immortal one,
as <s>Aghora</s> and the exceedingly terrible one, as <s>Sadyojāta</s>, as speed,
as <s>Īśāna</s>, as the cremation ground, as the very swift and the swift one,
obeisance to you, whose feet are the revelation, whose liṅga rises upward, who bears the liṅga.
Obeisance to the golden liṅga, to gold, to the water-liṅga, and to water.
Obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, to the <s>Śiva</s>-liṅga, to the pervader, the pervader of space.
Obeisance to wind, to the speed of wind; homage to you who pervade as wind.
Obeisance to radiance, to the bearer of radiances; homage to you who pervade over radiance.
Obeisance to water, to the being of water; homage to you who pervade water.
Obeisance to earth and to the midspace; obeisance to the pervader of earth.
Obeisance to the one whose nature is sound and touch, to taste and smell, to the possessor of scent,
to you as lord of hosts, to you who are more secret than the secret.
To the infinite one, the multiform one, and the one who is the health of the infinite beings,
to the eternal, the most excellent, the womb of waters, the yogin.
To the one established in the midst of the waters, whose brilliance stands between us two,

children.text: goptre hartre sadā kartre nidhanāyeśvarāya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the protector, the remover, the constant maker, to dissolution and to the Lord.
To the unconscious, the thinkable, the conscious, the irresistible taker-away,
to the formless, the well-formed, the bodiless, the taker-away of bodies.
To the one whose body is smeared with ash, the cause of sun, moon, and fire,
to the white one, white in color, and the wanderer on the snowy mountain.
To the very white one, the fair-faced one, obeisance also to the white-crested one;
to the white-faced one, the great-faced one; homage to you, white-and-red one.
Obeisance to the excellent savior, to the distinguished one, to the drum-bearer, O <s>Hara</s>.
Obeisance always to the one of a hundred forms and many forms, to the bannered one.
To prosperity, sorrow, and freedom from sorrow; obeisance to the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, the matted-haired one.
To the unfettered one, the well-fettered one; homage to you, destroyer of bonds.
To the good sacrificer, to the oblation, to <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>, to the sage,
to the fair-faced and well-spoken one, to the untamable and to restraint.
To the heron, to the heron-formed one, O you who have made serpents into bracelets,
obeisance to you as <s>Sanaka</s>, O eternal <s>Sanandana</s>.
To the great-souled one who destroys <s>Sanatkumāra</s>'s deer-marked <s>Māra</s>,
to the eye of the world, the three-aboded one; obeisance always to the stainless one.
Obeisance to <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, to the conch, to passion and darkness.
Obeisance to the one belonging to <s>Sarasvatī</s>, to the cloud; homage to you, cloud-vehicle.
To the strong-armed one, the leader of rites, and the giver of boons in disputes,
obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, to Pradhāna; obeisance again and again.
Obeisance to you as the three guṇas; obeisance to the one whose self is the fourfold emanation.
Obeisance to you as saṃsāra; obeisance to the cause of saṃsāra.
Obeisance again and again to liberation, to the form of liberation, to the maker of liberation.

children.text: ātmane ṛṣaye tubhyaṃ svāmine viṣṇave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Obeisance to you as the self, as the seer, as the master, as <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: namo bhagavate tubhyaṃ nāgānāṃ pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Obeisance to you, Blessed One; obeisance to the lord of serpents.
Obeisance to you as the <s>oṅkāra</s>; obeisance again and again to the all-knowing one.

children.text: sarvāya ca namastubhyaṃ namo nārāyaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: Obeisance to you as <s>Sarva</s>, and obeisance also to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Obeisance to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; obeisance to you, primordial god.
Obeisance to the unborn one, the lord of creatures, the cause of emanation.
Obeisance again and again to <s>Mahādeva</s>, the Lord of the gods.

children.text: śarvāya ca namastubhyaṃ satyāya śamanāya ca
children.translated_text: And obeisance to you as <s>Śarva</s>, and to you as Truth and as the Pacifier;

children.text: brahmaṇe caiva bhūtānāṃ sarvajñāya namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and to the Brahman of beings, to the omniscient one, obeisance again and again.
Obeisance to you, great-souled one; indeed, obeisance to you whose form is wisdom.
Obeisance to consciousness, to him whose form is consciousness, and indeed to him whose form is memory.
Obeisance always to knowledge, to him who is reached by knowledge, to awareness.
Obeisance to you as the Peak; indeed, obeisance to <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>, the blue-throated one.
Repeated obeisance to him whose body is half female and half male, to the unmanifest.
Obeisance always to you, the firm one, divided into eleven forms.
Obeisance to <s>Soma</s>, to the Sun, to <s>Bhava</s>, and to the remover of worldly becoming;
to the god who bestows fame, and to <s>Śaṅkara</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>.
Obeisance to the lord of <s>Ambikā</s>; obeisance to the husband of <s>Umā</s>.
To you of golden arms, obeisance; obeisance to you of golden seed.
Obeisance indeed to the blue-haired one, to wealth itself, and to the pale-throated one.
Obeisance to you, the matted-haired one, adorned on your limbs with serpents.
Repeated obeisance to him who rides the bull, the destroyer and maker of all.
To you, mighty lord, obeisance as <s>Vīrarāma</s>, <s>Atirāma</s>, and <s>Rāmanātha</s>.
Obeisance to the king of kings, to you who are attained by kings.
Obeisance to the lord of protectors; obeisance to the cutter of palāśa.
Obeisance again and again to you adorned with armlets, to the lord of cows.
Obeisance to the lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>; obeisance to him who holds a likuca fruit in his hand.
Obeisance to you, god, lord of the worlds, Veda and śāstra.
Obeisance to you as <s>Sāraṅga</s>; obeisance to you as the royal swan.
Obeisance to him who has golden armlets and garlands, and whose sacred thread is a serpent;
to him whose earrings and garland are serpents, and whose waist-cord is a snake.
To you, O <s>Śiva</s>, womb of the Veda, womb itself, womb of the universe.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Having praised him in this way, <s>Hari</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, ceased.
This excellent, holy hymn destroys all sins.
Whoever recites it or causes brahmins who have mastered the Vedas to hear it,

children.text: sa yāti brahmaṇo loke pāpakarmarato'pi vai
children.translated_text: goes to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, even if he is devoted to sinful acts.
Therefore one should mutter it, recite it daily, and cause auspicious brahmins to hear it,
for the purification of all sins; it was explained by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then <s>Mahādeva</s> said, "I am pleased, best of gods.

children.text: paśyatāṃ māṃ mahādevaṃ bhayaṃ sarvaṃ vimucyatām ||
children.translated_text: As you behold me as <s>Mahādeva</s>, let every fear be released.

children.text: yuvāṃ prasūtau gātrābhyāṃ mama pūrvaṃ mahābalau
children.translated_text: You two, mighty ones, were formerly born from my limbs.

children.text: ayaṃ me dakṣiṇe pārśve brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here on my right side is <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of the worlds;

children.text: vāme pārśve ca me viṣṇurviśvātmā hṛdayodbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: and on my left side is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Self of the universe, born from my heart.
I am fully pleased with you two; I grant the boon just as you desire."

children.text: evamuktvā tu taṃ viṣṇuṃ karābhyāṃ parameśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Parameśvara</s>, with his two hands, touched that <s>Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: pasparśa subhagābhyāṃ tu kṛpayā tu kṛpānidhiḥ ||
