children.translated_text: with his lovely hands, out of compassion, the treasure of compassion touched him.
Then, with a delighted mind, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> bowed down to <s>Maheśvara</s>
and spoke to the Lord who stood in the liṅga and yet was free from the liṅga:

children.text: yadi prītiḥ samutpannā yadi deyo varaś ca nau
children.translated_text: "If favor has arisen, and if a boon is to be given to us,
let there be constant, unswerving devotion for us toward you."
The moon-crested god granted to <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>
unswerving faith in himself.
Again <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself, going down to the earth on his knees,

children.text: praṇipatya ca viśveśaṃ prāha mandataraṃ vaśī ||
children.translated_text: bowed to the Lord of the universe and, self-controlled, spoke more softly:
"O lord of gods, lord of gods, this remarkable dispute between the two of us
is the reason you have come here, to pacify our dispute."

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā punaḥ prāha haro harim
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of his, <s>Hara</s> again spoke to <s>Hari</s>,
who stood bowed with his head, his joined hands forming a hollow, while he smiled.
Blessed <s>Mahādeva</s> said:
"You are the maker of dissolution, maintenance, and creation, O lord of the earth.
Dear child, dear child, O <s>Hari</s>, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, protect this moving and unmoving world.
For I am divided threefold, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, under the names <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Bhava</s>,
through the qualities of creation, preservation, and dissolution, though as <s>Parameśvara</s> I am without parts.

children.text: saṃmohaṃ tyaja bho viṣṇo pālayainaṃ pitāmaham
children.translated_text: Give up delusion, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and protect this Grandfather.

children.text: pādme bhaviṣyati sutaḥ kalpe tava pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Padma</s> kalpa the Grandfather will become your son.

children.text: tadā drakṣyasi māṃ caivaṃ so'pi drakṣyati padmajaḥ
children.translated_text: Then you will see me in this way, and the lotus-born one too will see me."
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One disappeared right there.
From that time onward, liṅga worship became well established in the worlds.
The liṅga altar is the great goddess; the liṅga is directly <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Because of dissolution it is called liṅga; in that very place is the whole, O gods.
Whoever daily recites this Liṅga narrative in the presence of the liṅga,

children.text: sa yāti śivatāṃ vipro nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: that brahmin goes to the state of <s>Śiva</s>; no doubt should be entertained here.
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ pādme purā kalpe brahmā padmodbhavo 'bhavat
children.translated_text: How, in the former <s>Padma</s> kalpa, did <s>Brahmā</s> become lotus-born?
And how did <s>Puruṣottama</s>, together with that <s>Brahmā</s>, behold <s>Bhava</s>?
You ought now to tell all this in detail.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
There was a terrible single ocean, undifferentiated and filled with darkness.
In the middle of that single ocean was the bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
cloud-dark, lotus-eyed, crowned, <s>Hari</s>, the lord of <s>Śrī</s>;
<s>Puruṣottama</s>, the Self of all, issuing from the mouth of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
eight-armed, broad-chested, is called the womb of the worlds.
That inconceivable one, whose self is yoga and who knows yoga, entered yoga.
He was of incomparable brilliance, accompanied by a thousand hoods.
Having properly spread out the lofty couch of the great lord of serpents,
the Lord lay down on that great bed in the single ocean.
As <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the mighty Lord, was thus lying there,
By the self-delighting one, for the sake of play, with action unwearied in sport,
a lotus one hundred yojanas wide, resembling the young sun,

children.text: vajradaṇḍaṃ mahotsedhaṃ nābhyāṃ sṛṣṭaṃ tu puṣkaram ||
children.translated_text: with a vajra-like stalk and great height, was created from his navel.
As that praiseworthy god was thus playing, near him
came <s>Brahmā</s>, born from the golden cosmic egg, golden in color and beyond the senses.
Four-faced and broad-eyed, he arrived there by chance,
and saw the auspicious-eyed one, joined with divine splendor, very beautiful and fragrant,

children.text: krīḍamānaṃ ca padmena dṛṣṭvā brahmā śubhekṣaṇam
children.translated_text: playing with the lotus; then <s>Brahmā</s>, beholding him,
came forward in wonder and spoke with a voice endowed with gentleness:
'Who are you, lying here, resting in the middle of the waters?'

children.text: atha tasyācyutaḥ śrutvā brahmaṇastu śubhaṃ vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Acyuta</s>, hearing that gracious speech of <s>Brahmā</s>,
rose from his couch, his eyes wide open with wonder,
and gave this answer: 'In every kalpa I am the refuge;

children.text: kartavyaṃ ca kṛtaṃ caiva kriyate yacca kiṃcana
children.translated_text: what is to be done, what has been done, and whatever is being done,
heaven, mid-space, earth, and the supreme station beyond the earth are myself.'
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> then spoke again:
'Who indeed are you, blessed one, who have come near me, and from where?

children.text: kva vā bhūyaś ca gantavyaṃ kaś ca vā te pratiśrayaḥ
children.translated_text: Where are you to go again, and what is your refuge?

children.text: ko bhavān viśvamūrtirvai kartavyaṃ kiṃ ca te mayā ||
children.translated_text: Who are you, truly of universal form, and what should be done for you by me?'
To <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, who was speaking in this way, the Grandfather replied.
Deluded by the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Śambhu</s> and not recognizing <s>Janārdana</s>,
he addressed the god, who was himself deluded by <s>māyā</s> and unrecognized by the great-souled one:
'Just as you are, so also am I, the first maker, the lord of creatures.'
Hearing the astonishing speech of <s>Brahmā</s>, the arranger of the worlds,

children.text: anujñātaś ca te nātha vaikuṇṭho viśvasaṃbhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, source of the universe, said, 'With your permission, O lord,'
and out of curiosity the great yogin entered <s>Brahmā</s>'s mouth.
Entering, the greatly radiant one saw these eighteen islands with their oceans and mountains,
filled with the four social orders,
and the eternal seven worlds extending as far as <s>Brahmā</s>'s pillar.
Having seen them all inside <s>Brahmā</s>'s belly, mighty-armed <s>Viṣṇu</s>

children.text: aho'sya tapaso vīryamityuktvā ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: said again and again, 'Ah, the power of his austerity!'
After wandering through various worlds and many kinds of abodes,

children.text: tato varṣasahasrānte nāntaṃ hi dadṛśe yadā ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Viṣṇu</s> still saw no end after a thousand years,
then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, whose dwelling is the lord of serpents, emerged from his mouth,
and the sustainer of the world spoke to the Grandfather:

children.text: bhagavānādiraṅkaś ca madhyaṃ kālo diśo nabhaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Blessed lord, you are the beginning and the end, the middle, time, the directions, and the sky.
I do not see the end of your belly, O sinless one.'
Having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s> again said this to the Grandfather:
'Blessed lord, so too am I; indeed my belly is eternal.
Enter it and see these incomparable worlds, best of gods.'

children.text: tataḥ prāhlādinīṃ vāṇīṃ śrutvā tasyābhinandya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his pleasing speech and welcoming it,
the Grandfather again entered the belly of the lord of <s>Śrī</s>.
The one of true valor saw those very worlds placed within the womb,

children.text: paryaṭitvā tu devasya dadṛśe 'ntaṃ na vai hareḥ
children.translated_text: but after wandering through the god's body he did not see <s>Hari</s>'s end.

children.text: jñātvā gatiṃ tasya pitāmahasya dvārāṇi sarvāṇi pidhāya viṣṇuḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing the movement of that Grandfather, <s>Viṣṇu</s> closed all the doors,

children.text: vibhurmanaḥ kartumiyeṣa cāśu sukhaṃ prasupto'hamiti pracintya ||
children.translated_text: and the all-pervading lord quickly wished to compose his mind, thinking, 'I am happily asleep.'

children.text: tato dvārāṇi sarvāṇi pihitāni samīkṣya vai
children.translated_text: Then, seeing that all the doors had been closed,
he made his own form subtle and found a doorway at the navel.
Following the thread of the lotus, the Grandfather saw his way,
and the Four-faced One brought forth his own form from the lotus.
Standing upon the lotus, he shone with the radiance of the lotus-womb:
<s>Brahmā</s> the self-born, blessed lord, womb of the world, the Grandfather.
At that interval, while the conflict between the two of them

children.text: vartamāne tu saṃgharṣe madhye tasyārṇavasya tu ||
children.translated_text: was taking place there in the middle of that ocean,
from somewhere came the immeasurable lord of beings, <s>Īśvara</s>,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, bearing the trident, clad in golden heroic garments,
to the place where that endless <s>Hari</s>, lord of the serpent coils, was.
As he strode swiftly, drops of water, struck and pressed by his feet,
rose up at once into the sky, broad and large.

children.text: atyuṣṇaś cātiśītaś ca vāyustatra vavau punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There a wind, both extremely hot and extremely cold, blew again.
Seeing that great wonder, <s>Brahmā</s> said to <s>Viṣṇu</s>:
'These drops of water, hot and cold, violently shake the lotus.

children.text: etanme saṃśayaṃ brūhi kiṃ vā tvanyaccikīrṣasi
children.translated_text: Tell me this doubt of mine, or what else do you intend to do?'
Hearing that speech of this kind issuing from the Grandfather's mouth,
the blessed slayer of demons, whose deed was without equal,

children.text: kiṃ nu khalvatra me nābhyāṃ bhūtamanyatkṛtālayam ||
children.translated_text: thought, 'What other being has now made its dwelling here in my navel?
He speaks to me very affectionately; has anger in him been caused by me?'
Having reflected thus in his mind, he gave this answer:
'Why, blessed lord, are you today alarmed here on the lotus?

children.text: kiṃ mayā ca kṛtaṃ deva yanmāṃ priyamanuttamam ||
children.translated_text: What has been done by me, O god, that you speak to me with unsurpassed affection?
Tell me truly, best of persons, for what reason.'
When the lord of gods, who follows the course of the worlds, had spoken in this way,
<s>Brahmā</s>, the lord and treasury of the Veda, replied to the lotus-eyed one:
'I am the one who previously entered your belly by your wish.

children.text: yathā mamodare lokāḥ sarve dṛṣṭāstvayā prabho
children.translated_text: Just as all the worlds were seen by you in my belly, O lord,
so too the worlds were seen by me in their entirety within your belly.'
Then, after a thousand years, when I had returned, O sinless one,
by you, wishing to bring me under control out of jealousy,
all the gates were quickly closed on every side.

children.text: tato mayā mahābhāga saṃcintya svena tejasā ||
children.translated_text: Then, O greatly fortunate one, having reflected by means of my own splendor,
I obtained an exit through the region of the navel, out from the lotus-fiber.
"Let there not be even the slightest disturbance of your mind in any way.
This, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is the following course of events, drawing near to their tasks.
Tell me what is next to be done by me; what shall I do?"
Then <s>Hari</s>, the enemy of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, whose self is immeasurable,
having heard from the Grandsire that faultless, dear, desired, auspicious speech,
became free from jealousy and gave this reply to him:
"Indeed, no such act against you was resolved upon by me.
Wanting to awaken you, in playful fashion and by chance,
I quickly closed all the gates of myself.

children.text: na te 'nyathāvagantavyaṃ mānyaḥ pūjyaś ca me bhavān
children.translated_text: This should not be understood otherwise by you; you are honored and worshipful to me.
Forgive everything, auspicious one, whatever offense was done by me against you.
While being carried by me, descend from the lotus, O lord.

children.text: nāhaṃ bhavantaṃ śaknomi soḍhuṃ tejomayaṃ gurum ||
children.translated_text: I am not able to bear you, a radiant and venerable teacher."

children.text: sa hovāca varaṃ brūhi padmādavatara prabho
children.translated_text: He said, "Ask a boon; descend from the lotus, O lord.

children.text: putro bhava mamārighna mudaṃ prāpsyasi śobhanām ||
children.translated_text: Become my son, O slayer of foes; you will obtain fair joy.
Speak a word of good feeling; descend from the lotus, O lord.

children.text: sa tvaṃ ca no mahāyogī tvamīḍyaḥ praṇavātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are that great yogin of ours; you are worthy of praise, whose nature is <s>praṇava</s>.
From today onward, O lord of all, adorned with a white turban,
you will indeed be known by the name <s>Padmayoni</s>, 'lotus-born.'

children.text: putro me tvaṃ bhava brahman saptalokādhipaḥ prabho
children.translated_text: Become my son, O <s>Brahman</s>, O lord, ruler of the seven worlds."

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavāndevo varaṃ dattvā kirīṭine ||
children.translated_text: Then that blessed god, having granted the boon to the crowned one,
said, "So be it," and, pleased in spirit and free from jealousy,
saw <s>Bhava</s> then approaching nearby, like the young sun and great-faced.
Having seen <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, that exceedingly wondrous <s>Bhava</s> then spoke:
"Immeasurable, great-mouthed, fanged, with disheveled hair,
ten-armed, marked by a trident, with eyes set on every side,
the lord of the worlds himself, directly manifest, transformed, and wearing a muñja girdle,
with his great upward phallus, roaring in a very terrifying way,

children.text: kaḥ khalveṣa pumān viṣṇo tejorāśir mahādyutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who indeed is this man, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, a mass of energy and great brilliance?

children.text: vyāpya sarvā diśo dyāṃ ca ita evābhivartate
children.translated_text: Pervading all the quarters and heaven, he advances right here."
Thus addressed by him, the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> spoke to <s>Brahmā</s>:
"From the fall of the soles of whose feet, as he strides in the ocean,
the waters have risen up with great force even into the sky,
and by thick waters from every side you are being drenched, O lotus-born one;

children.text: ghrāṇajena ca vātena kampyamānaṃ tvayā saha ||
children.translated_text: and by the wind born from his nostrils, while you are shaken together with me,
the great lotus born from my navel is being freely tossed about.
The lord of <s>Bhavānī</s> has arrived, beginningless, the lord who brings about the end.
You and I should attend with praise upon the bull-bannered one."
Then, angered, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to <s>Keśava</s>, whose eyes are like lotuses:
"Surely you do not know yourself as the all-pervading lord of the worlds.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāraṃ māṃ na vetsi sanātanam ||
children.translated_text: You do not know me as <s>Brahmā</s>, the maker of the worlds, the eternal one.
Who is that one named <s>Śaṅkara</s>, apart from the two of us?"
Hearing that speech of his, born from anger, <s>Hari</s> replied:

children.text: mā maivaṃ vada kalyāṇa parivādaṃ mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: "Do not, do not speak thus, auspicious one, slandering the great self.
He is <s>Dharma</s>, the kindling of great yoga, unassailable and a bestower of boons.
He is the cause of this world, the ancient, imperishable Person.
Truly he is the seed-bearer of seeds; the one light shines forth.
The god <s>Śaṅkara</s> himself plays with things as with children's toys.
<s>Pradhāna</s>, the imperishable, the womb, the unmanifest, <s>prakṛti</s>, and darkness
are these names of me, whose nature is always generative.

children.text: yaḥ kaḥ sa iti duḥkhārtairdṛśyate yatibhiḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That one, whoever he is, is seen by ascetics afflicted with sorrow as <s>Śiva</s>.
He is the possessor of seed; you are the seed; I am the eternal womb."
Thus addressed, <s>Brahmā</s>, the Self of the universe, asked <s>Viṣṇu</s>:

children.text: bhavān yonirahaṃ bījaṃ kathaṃ bījī maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: "How are you the womb, I the seed, and <s>Maheśvara</s> the seed-bearer?
You ought to cut away this subtle, unmanifest doubt of mine.
Knowing the manifold origination of <s>Brahmā</s>, the ruler of the worlds,
<s>Hari</s> then answered this question concerning the highest likeness:
"There is no other hidden being greater than this.

children.text: mahataḥ paramaṃ dhāma śivam adhyātmināṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is the supreme abode beyond the great principle, the goal of those who know the self.
Having divided himself in two ways, he stands established:
there the partless one is the unmanifest, and the one with parts is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Of him, who knows the ordinance of <s>māyā</s> and is inaccessible and profound,
formerly the seed arisen from the <s>liṅga</s>, the first seed belonging to primal creation,
that seed, joined in my womb in the course of time,
became a golden egg in the boundless, oceanic womb.

children.text: śatāni daśa varṣāṇām aṇḍam apsu pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: For ten hundreds of years the egg remained established in the waters.
At the end of the thousand years it was split in two by the wind.
One shell became heaven; the other shell became earth.
Its caul became the great elevation that is the golden mountain.

children.text: tataś ca pratisaṃdhyātmā devadevo varaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: And then the god of gods, the excellent lord, whose nature is the junction of creation,
the blessed <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, four-faced, was born."
And after beholding the world empty as far as the stars, sun, moon, and nakṣatras,
when he had also meditated, "Who am I?", those Kumāras then came into being.
They were pleasing to behold, ascetics, the predecessors of ascetics, your sons;
again, after a thousand years, your sons came forth from that very source.
They shone like the fire of the worlds and had eyes long like lotus petals:
the illustrious <s>Sanatkumāra</s> and <s>Ṛbhu</s>, both <s>ūrdhvaretas</s> (with seed drawn upward),
<s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and likewise <s>Sanandana</s>.
They were born at the same time, seeing by an insight beyond the senses.
Born as beings whose nature was illumination, causes for the stability of the worlds,
they did not undertake ritual actions, being free from the threefold affliction.
They knew life to have little happiness and much distress, joined with old age and grief,

children.text: jīvanaṃ maraṇaṃ caiva saṃbhavaś ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and death, and birth again and again.

children.text: alpabhūtaṃ sukhaṃ svarge duḥkhāni narake tathā
children.translated_text: They knew that happiness in heaven is small, and sufferings likewise exist in hell;
they knew the whole revealed teaching and the necessity of what must come to pass.

children.text: ṛbhuṃ sanatkumāraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tava vaśe sthitau
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Ṛbhu</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s> standing under your control,

children.text: trayastu trīn guṇān hitvā cātmajāḥ sanakādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the three sons, beginning with <s>Sanaka</s>, abandoned the three guṇas.
Those mighty ones then proceeded by knowledge alone.
Then, when those three beginning with <s>Sanaka</s> had set forth,
you will become utterly bewildered by the māyā of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: evaṃ kalpe tu vaivṛtte saṃjñā naśyati te 'nagha ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when the kalpa has turned, your awareness will vanish, O sinless one.

children.text: kalpe śeṣāṇi bhūtāni sūkṣmāṇi pārthivāni ca
children.translated_text: At the end of the kalpa the remaining beings, subtle and earthly,
are all said to awaken through the sovereign māyā.
Just as this mountain <s>Meru</s> is called the world of the gods,

children.text: tasya cedaṃ hi māhātmyaṃ viddhi devavarasya ha ||
children.translated_text: so know this to be the greatness of that best of gods.
Having understood the true being of <s>Īśvara</s>, having known me, lotus-eyed one,
as <s>Mahādeva</s>, the great being, the lord who grants boons to beings,
then, with the praṇava and with a sāman, after bowing to the teacher of the world,

children.text: tvāṃ ca māṃ caiva saṃkruddho niḥśvāsānnirdahedayam ||
children.translated_text: this one, angered, could burn up both you and me with his breath.
Knowing thus that great yoga, let us rise up to the very mighty one.
Putting you before me, I shall praise him whose splendor is like fire.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then he whose banner bears <s>Garuḍa</s>, placing <s>Brahmā</s> before him,

children.text: atītaiś ca bhaviṣyaiś ca vartamānaistathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: with names past, future, and likewise present,
and also with Vedic names, uttered this hymn.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:
Homage to you, blessed one, of excellent vows and endless splendor.
Homage to the lord of the field; homage to the seed-bearing one, to the trident-bearing one.
Homage to the one with a fine generative power, to the worshipful generative power, to the staff-bearing one, to the one of austere seed.

children.text: namo jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya pūrvāya prathamāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the eldest and the best, to the ancient and the first.

children.text: namo mānyāya pūjyāya sadyojātāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the honored and worshipful one; homage indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Homage to the cavernous one, to the lord of the vessel, and to the one clothed in the sky as his garment.
Homage to you as the source of beings such as ourselves.

children.text: vedānāṃ prabhave caiva smṛtīnāṃ prabhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of the Vedas, and homage to the source of the smṛtis.
Homage to the source of ritual actions, gifts, and substances.

children.text: namo yogasya prabhave sāṃkhyasya prabhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of yoga; homage to the source of sāṃkhya.
Homage to the source of the sages fixed on the pole star.

children.text: ṛkṣāṇāṃ prabhave tubhyaṃ grahāṇāṃ prabhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to you as the source of the constellations; homage to the source of the planets.
Homage to the source of lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, and roaring.
Homage to the source of the great oceans; homage to the source of the islands.

children.text: adrīṇāṃ prabhave caiva varṣāṇāṃ prabhave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of mountains, and homage to the source of the regions.

children.text: namo nadīnāṃ prabhave nadānāṃ prabhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of rivers; homage to the source of streams.
Homage to the source of great herbs; homage to the source of trees.
Homage to the tree of dharma, to dharma itself, to the source of states of being.

children.text: prabhave ca parārdhasya parasya prabhave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of the higher half and to the source of the supreme.

children.text: namo rasānāṃ prabhave ratnānāṃ prabhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of tastes; homage to the source of jewels.

children.text: kṣaṇānāṃ prabhave caiva lavānāṃ prabhave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of moments, and homage to the source of lavas.
Homage to the source of day and night, fortnights, and months.

children.text: ṛtūnāṃ prabhave tubhyaṃ saṃkhyāyāḥ prabhave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you as the source of seasons; homage to the source of enumeration.
Homage to the source of the lower half and to the source of the higher half.
Homage to the source of the Purāṇas; homage to the source of creations.
Homage to the source of manvantaras; homage to the source of yoga.
Homage to the source of the fourfold creation, to the one of endless eyes.
Homage to the source of the winds connected with the arising of kalpas.
Homage to the source of the universe; homage to the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Homage to the source of sciences, and homage to the lord of sciences.
Homage to the lord of vows; homage to the source of vows.
Homage to you as the source of mantras; homage to the lord of mantras.

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ pataye caiva paśūnāṃ pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord of the ancestors, and homage to the lord of beasts.
Homage to you as the bull of speech and as the bull of the Purāṇas.
Homage to the lord of beasts and to the one whose banner bears the lordly bull among cows.
Homage to the lord of the Prajāpatis; homage to the lord of powers of accomplishment.
Homage to the lord of the hosts of daityas and dānavas, and of the rakṣases.

children.text: gandharvāṇāṃ ca pataye yakṣāṇāṃ pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord of gandharvas, and homage to the lord of yakṣas.
Homage to the lord of Garuḍas, uragas, serpents, and birds.
Homage to the lord of all hidden piśācas, to the overlord of hidden beings.

children.text: gokarṇāya ca goptre ca śaṅkukarṇāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage indeed to <s>Gokarṇa</s>, to the protector, and to <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>.
Homage to the boar, to the immeasurable one, to the bear, and to the stainless one.

children.text: namaḥ surāṇāṃ pataye gaṇānāṃ pataye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the lord of the gods; homage to the lord of the gaṇas.

children.text: aṃbhasāṃ pataye caiva ojasāṃ pataye namaḥ
children.translated_text: And homage to the lord of the waters and to the lord of powers.
Homage to the lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and to the protector of prosperity and of the earth.
To the aggregate of strength and weakness, and to the unshakable one who shakes others;
to the bull with blazing horn, the one-horned one, the humped one.
Homage to steadfastness, to embodied form, and to the one obedient to splendor;
homage indeed to the past, the future, and the present.

children.text: suvarcase ca vīryāya śūrāya hyajitāya ca
children.translated_text: To good brilliance and to heroism, to the hero and to the unconquered one;
to the giver of boons, the excellent one, the great-souled <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: namo bhūtāya bhavyāya mahate prabhavāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the one who has been and who will be, to the great one and to the source of being;

children.text: janāya ca namastubhyaṃ tapase varadāya ca ||
children.translated_text: and homage to the generative one; homage to you, to austerity and to the giver of boons.

children.text: aṇave mahate caiva namaḥ sarvagatāya ca
children.translated_text: To the minute one and also to the great one; homage to the all-pervading one.

children.text: namo bandhāya mokṣāya svargāya narakāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Homage to bondage and to liberation, to heaven and to hell.

children.text: namo bhavāya devāya ijyāya yājakāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Bhava</s>, to the god, to worship and to the sacrificer;
to the one who rises up in response, to the blazing one, to reality, and to the one beyond the guṇas.
Homage to the noose and to the weapon; homage to ornament.
To what is offered in fire, invoked, specially offered, and consumed after offering.
Homage to the desired rite, to works of public merit, and to the Agniṣṭoma brahmin;
homage also to the officiating member, to the sacrificial fee, and to the avabhṛtha bath.
To nonviolence, to freedom from greed, to animal-sacrifice formulas and medicines;
homage to the giver of nourishment, to the well-conducted one of good character.
Homage to you as past, future, and present.

children.text: suvarcase ca vīryāya śūrāya hyajitāya ca ||
children.translated_text: To good brilliance and to heroism, to the hero and to the unconquered one;
to the giver of boons, the excellent one, the great-souled <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: namo bhūtāya bhavyāya mahate cābhayāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the one who has been and who will be, to the great one and to the fearless one.
O one perfected through age, homage to you, to the one of iron, the giver of boons.

children.text: adhare mahate caiva namaḥ sastupatāya ca ||
children.translated_text: And to the lower one and the great one; homage to the lord as transmitted in the text.
Homage to the lapping one, garlanded, lord of the senses and their objects;
to the all-formed universe, whose head is everywhere: homage.
To <s>Rudra</s>, whose hands and feet are everywhere, and to the incomparable one;

children.text: namo havyāya kavyāya havyavāhāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: homage to the oblation for gods and ancestors; homage indeed to the carrier of oblations.
Homage to the accomplished, the pure, to the desired one devoted to sacrifice;
to the very heroic and the very terrible, to the unshakable one who shakes others.
To the one with good offspring and good intelligence, to the blazing one and the sun-bright one;

children.text: namo buddhāya śuddhāya vistṛtāya matāya ca ||
children.translated_text: homage to the awakened and pure one, to the vast and the honored one.
Homage to the gross and the subtle, to the visible and invisible in every way;

children.text: varṣate jvalate caiva vāyave śiśirāya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the one who rains and blazes, and to wind and cold.
Homage to you of curling hair, with thighs, chest, and crest;
again and again homage to the golden one, resembling refined gold.
To the uneven-eyed one, to the liṅga, to the tawny one of great force;
homage also to the destroyer of rain; homage to the gentle-eyed one.

children.text: namo dhūmrāya śvetāya kṛṣṇāya lohitāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the smoky, the white, the black, and the red one;
to the flesh-colored, the tawny, the yellow, and the quiver-bearing one.
Homage to you as possessing distinctions; homage indeed to you as without distinction.

children.text: nama ījyāya pūjyāya upajīvyāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the one to be worshiped, honored, and lived upon.
Homage again and again to the secure, the aged, and the affectionate one.

children.text: namo bhūtāya satyāya satyāsatyāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the existent, to the true, and to the true-and-untrue.

children.text: namo vai padmavarṇāya mṛtyughnāya ca mṛtyave
children.translated_text: Homage indeed to the lotus-colored one, to the destroyer of death and to death itself;

children.text: namo gaurāya śyāmāya kadrave lohitāya ca ||
children.translated_text: homage to the fair, the dark, the tawny, and the red one.
To the one colored like a great twilight cloud, beautifully blazing and consecrated;
homage to the lotus-handed one, the sky-clad one, the matted-haired one.
To the immeasurable, the all, the imperishable and immortal one;
homage to form, to fragrance, to the eternal and unwounded one.
To the one who grows in front, to the bewildered one, and to the made one;
to the hard-to-approach, to <s>Maheśa</s>, to wrath, and to the tawny one.
To the one whose body is reasoned and beyond reasoning, to the strong and swift one;
to the sandy one, the flowing one, the standing one, and the spreading one.
Homage to you, wise one, potter, moon-crested one;
to the variegated one, variegatedly dressed, variegated in color, and intelligent.
To the knowing one, the satisfied one; homage to you as the hidden one.
Homage to the patient, the restrained, and the one whose frame is hard as a thunderbolt.
To the destroyer of demons, the destroyer of poison, the blue-throated one with uplifted wrath.
To the lapping one, to death's ender, and to the bearer of sharp weapons.
Homage to you as delight and full delight, knowable to ascetics.
Homage indeed to the painless one, the all, and <s>Mahākāla</s>.
To the praṇava and lord of the praṇava, and to the destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye;
to the deer-hunter, to the skillful one, and to the destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice.
To the one who is the self of all beings, and to the lord of all, surpassing all;
to the destroyer of cities, well-armed, bearing a bow and then an axe.
To the destroyer of <s>Pūṣan</s>'s teeth and to the destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye;
to the giver of desire, the best one, and the burner of <s>Kāma</s>'s limbs.
To the one in the arena, terrible-faced, and serpent-lord-faced;
to the ender of demons and the maker of demons cry out.
To the destroyer of cold, the sharp one, and the wearer of a wet hide;
homage to the one ever delighting in the cremation ground, the bearer of a firebrand.
Homage to you, protector of life, and to the wearer of a garland of skulls;
to the one surrounded by various beings whose sorrows have been cast away.
To the one whose body is male and female, and to the one dear to the Goddess;
to the matted-haired and the shaven-headed one, wearing a serpent as sacred thread.
Homage to the one whose nature is dance and who loves accompanying dance;
homage to wrath, to the lover of song, who is sung by sages.
To the rattling one, the sharp one, the unpleasant and the pleasant one;
to the terrifying and fearsome one, the crusher of <s>Bhaga</s>.
Homage indeed to the greatly fortunate one, sung by hosts of siddhas.
Homage to him of free loud laughter, and to him who roars and claps his arms.
He bellows and leaps about; homage to him whose self is delighted.
Homage to <s>Mṛḍa</s>, homage to him who breathes, who runs, and who presides.

children.text: dhyāyate jṛmbhate caiva rudate dravate namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to him who meditates and yawns, who weeps and rushes on.
Homage to him who bounds and plays, whose body is pot-bellied.
Homage to the improper and the proper, to the shaven-headed one and to the <s>Kīkaṭa</s>.
Homage indeed to him whose body is maddened, and to him adorned with little bells.
Homage to him of distorted dress, to the fierce and intolerant one.
Homage to the immeasurable, the protector, the blazing one, and the one beyond the guṇas.
Homage to the lover of <s>Vāmā</s>, to the left-sided one, and to him who wears the crest-jewel.
Homage to the small and slender one, immeasurable through his qualities.
Homage to the worthy, the hidden one, and to him whose going is inaccessible.
This earth, the bearer of the worlds, is your two feet, served by good people.
Your belly is the foundation of all siddhis and yogas.
In the middle is the vast atmosphere, adorned with hosts of stars.
The splendid necklace on your chest shines like the path of the star <s>Svāti</s>.
The directions are your ten arms, adorned with bracelets and armlets.
Your broad circumference is like a mass of dark collyrium.
Your glorious neck shines, adorned with a golden cord.
Likewise your face is dreadful with fangs, unassailable and beyond comparison.
Heaven is your head, shining greatly, with a turban made of lotus garlands.

children.text: dīptiḥ sūrye vapuścandre sthairyaṃ śaile 'nile balam
children.translated_text: Radiance is in the sun, beauty in the moon, firmness in the mountain, strength in the wind.

children.text: auṣṇyamagnau tathā śaityam apsu śabdo 'mbare tathā ||
children.translated_text: Heat is in fire, coldness in the waters, and sound likewise in space.
The wise know these qualities from the vibration between the syllables.
The muttered recitation and the one to be recited is <s>Mahādeva</s>; the great yoga is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He lies in the city, dwells in the cave, moves in the sky, and moves by night.
He is the treasury of austerity, the secret guru, the delighter, and the increaser of delight.
He is horse-headed, the sustainer of waters, the ordainer, and the maker of beings.
He is to be known, the awakener, the leader, unassailable and hard to shake.
He is great-charioted, terrible in action, great in fame, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.
He loves bells, bears a banner and parasol, bears <s>Pināka</s>, and is lord of armies.
He is armored, armed with a paṭṭiśa, sword-bearing, bow in hand, and axe-bearing.
He destroys sin, is sinless, heroic, king of gods, and crusher of enemies.

children.text: tvāṃ prasādya purāsmābhir dviṣanto nihatā yudhi
children.translated_text: Having propitiated you in former times, we killed our enemies in battle.
You are fire; even while constantly drinking the ocean's waters, you are not satisfied.
You have the form of anger and a serene self; you grant desires, move at will, and are beloved.
You are a brahmacārin, unfathomable, devoted to brahman, and worshiped by the well-bred.

children.text: devānām akṣayaḥ kośas tvayā yajñaḥ prakalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the imperishable treasury of the gods; sacrifice was established by you.
The oblation-carrier bears this oblation of yours, prescribed by the Veda.

children.text: prīte tvayi mahādeva vayaṃ prītā bhavāmahe ||
children.translated_text: When you are pleased, <s>Mahādeva</s>, we become pleased.
You are the lord of <s>Bhavānī</s>, beginningless; for all worlds you are <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator and primal emanation.

children.text: sāṃkhyāḥ prakṛteḥ paramaṃ tvāṃ viditvā kṣīṇadhyānāstvāmamṛtyuṃ viśanti ||
children.translated_text: The Sāṃkhyas, knowing you as higher than prakṛti, enter you as deathlessness when their meditation is fulfilled.

children.text: yogāś ca tvāṃ dhyāyino nityasiddhaṃ jñātvā yogān saṃtyajante punastān
children.translated_text: And the yogins, meditating on you and knowing you as eternally perfected, then abandon those yogas.

children.text: ye cāpyanye tvāṃ prasannā viśuddhāḥ svakarmabhiste divyabhogā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And others too, pleased with you and purified, become enjoyers of divine pleasures through their own actions.
Of you whose principles are innumerable, as far as we know according to our own power,
the greatness of you, the boundless great-souled one, has been praised.

children.text: śivo no bhava sarvatra yo 'si so 'si namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: Be auspicious to us everywhere. Whatever you are, you are that. Homage to you.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Whoever recites with devotion this hymn of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
or, being learned, causes twice-born men to hear it, or listens to it with concentration,
obtains the fruit that one would obtain after performing ten thousand horse sacrifices.
Even a mortal of sinful conduct who listens in the presence of <s>Śiva</s>,
or who mutters it, is released and goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: śrāddhe vā daivike kārye yajñe vāvabhṛthāntike
children.translated_text: At a śrāddha, at a rite for the gods, at a sacrifice, or near the final bath,

children.text: kīrtayedvā satāṃ madhye sa yāti brahmaṇo'ntikam ||
children.translated_text: if he recites it among the good, he goes near <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Seeing them bowed down completely, he whose long eyes were tawny like honey
became exceedingly joyful-faced because of their truthful praise.
The lord of <s>Umā</s>, the odd-eyed one, destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice,
the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, wielder of the broken axe, the three-eyed one, was very pleased.

children.text: tataḥ sa bhagavāndevaḥ śrutvā vāgamṛtaṃ tayoḥ
children.translated_text: Then that blessed god, having heard the nectar of their speech,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, though he knew, spoke as if in play:
Who are you two great-souled ones, seeking each other's welfare,
come together here in this terrible great flood, eating lotus blossoms?
The two great-souled ones, looking at each other, said:

children.text: bhagavān kiṃ tu yatte 'dya na vijñānaṃ tvayā vibho ||
children.translated_text: Blessed lord, how is it that today this is not known by you, O mighty one?

children.text: vibho rudra mahāmāya icchayā vāṃ kṛtau tvayā
children.translated_text: O mighty <s>Rudra</s> of great māyā, the two of us were made by you according to your will.
Hearing that statement of theirs, approving it and honoring it,
the blessed god spoke in a sweet, smooth voice:

children.text: bho bho hiraṇyagarbha tvāṃ tvāṃ ca kṛṣṇa bravīmyaham ||
children.translated_text: Ho, ho, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, to you, and to you, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, I speak.
I am pleased by this devotion, joined with the eternal imperishable.
You both are dearer to this heart of mine than my very heart.
What boon, the desired best of boons, shall I give you two today?
Then the greatly fortunate <s>Viṣṇu</s> spoke this speech to <s>Bhava</s>:

children.text: sarvaṃ mama kṛtaṃ deva parituṣṭo 'si me yadi
children.translated_text: Everything has been done for me, O god, if you are pleased with me.

children.text: tvayi me supratiṣṭhā tu bhaktirbhavatu śaṅkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let devotion to you be firmly established in me, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
When this had been said, he understood and honored <s>Keśava</s>.
And <s>Mahādeva</s> gave him devotion to his own lotus feet.
You are the maker of the whole world; you are its presiding deity.
So then, welfare to you, child. I shall go, lotus-eyed one.

children.text: evamuktvā tu bhagavān brahmāṇaṃ cāpi śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the god <s>Parameśvara</s>, graciously touched <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: karābhyāṃ suśubhābhyāṃ ca prāha hṛṣṭataraḥ svayam
children.translated_text: With his two very beautiful hands, greatly delighted, he himself said:

children.text: matsamastvaṃ na saṃdeho vatsa bhaktaś ca me bhavān ||
children.translated_text: You are equal to me; there is no doubt, child, and you are my devotee.

children.text: svastyastu te gamiṣyāmi saṃjñā bhavatu suvrata
children.translated_text: May there be welfare for you. I shall go. Let consciousness return, good-vowed one.
Having spoken thus, the blessed lord <s>Īśvara</s> then vanished.
The god, lord of the hosts, honored by all the gods, departed.
Having regained consciousness from <s>Govinda</s>, the lotus-born Grandfather
set his mind on creating creatures and performed fierce austerity.
As he was practicing austerity in this way, nothing at all came about.
Then, after a long time, anger arose from grief.
As he was possessed by anger, drops of tears fell from his eyes.
Then from those drops of tears, composed of wind, bile, and phlegm,
there appeared very fortunate, mighty beings, marked with auspicious signs.
Those serpents, with disheveled hair and great poison, came into being.
Seeing those serpents as his first-born, <s>Brahmā</s> reproached himself:

children.text: aho dhik tapaso mahyaṃ phalamīdṛśakaṃ yadi
children.translated_text: Alas, shame on my austerity, if its fruit is of such a kind.
At the very beginning my progeny has been born as a destroyer of the world.
A terrible swoon, born from anger and resentment, came upon him.
Overcome by the burning of that swoon, <s>Prajāpati</s> gave up his breaths.
Then, from the body of that being of incomparable valor, with compassion first,
those eleven <s>Rudras</s> came forth, crying as they advanced.
Indeed, from their crying, <s>Rudra</s>-hood arose among them.

children.text: ye rudrāste khalu prāṇā ye prāṇāste tadātmakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who are <s>Rudras</s> are the vital breaths; those who are breaths have that nature.
The breaths should be known as the breaths of living beings, established in all creatures.
Of that one, very fierce, great, and righteous in conduct,
the blue-red Trident-bearer again bestowed the breaths.
Having received his life-breaths, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s> bowed to the God of gods, the lord of <s>Umā</s>.
Standing there, he saw the Lord of the universe together with <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Seeing and praising the god who consisted of all worlds, the Grandfather
then was filled with wonder and bowed down again and again.

children.text: uvāca vacanaṃ śarvaṃ sadyāditvaṃ kathaṃ vibho ||
children.translated_text: He spoke this word to <s>Śarva</s>: How are you Sadya and the rest, O lord?
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmaṇo bhagavān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of <s>Brahmā</s>, the blessed <s>Bhava</s>,
assuming the form of <s>Brahmā</s>, addressed <s>Brahmā</s> with a smile in order to awaken him.
When the White <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age) existed, I alone existed then.
I wore a white turban, white garlands, and white garments; I was pale.
My bones were white, my hair was white, my blood was white, and I was white-red.

children.text: tena nāmnā ca vikhyātaḥ śvetakalpastadā hyasau ||
children.translated_text: By that name that <s>Śveta</s> <s>kalpa</s> was then renowned.
And the goddess born from me was white-limbed and white-red.
At that time <s>Gāyatrī</s>, called <s>Brahmā</s>, was white in color.

children.text: tasmādahaṃ ca deveśa tvayā guhyena vai punaḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore, O lord of gods, I was again by you, through the secret means,
recognized by your own austerity and came to the state of <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
This is proclaimed as <s>Sadyojāta</s>; this is that secret of <s>Brahman</s>.
Therefore the twice-born who will know this, since it has become secret,
will go to my nearness, from which return is hard to obtain.
And when again there was a <s>kalpa</s> named <s>Lohita</s>,

children.text: matkṛtena ca varṇena kalpo vai lohitaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: by the color produced by me that <s>kalpa</s> is remembered as <s>Lohita</s>.
Then she was born from red flesh, bone, and red milk.
Red-eyed and full-breasted, <s>Gāyatrī</s> was proclaimed as the Cow.
Then, because of her redness and because of a transformation of color,
and because the god was left-sided, the state of <s>Vāmadeva</s> arose.
There too, great being, I was by you, with a disciplined self,
recognized through your own yoga, while abiding in that other color.

children.text: tataś ca vāmadeveti khyātiṃ yāto 'smi bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: Then I became famed on earth as <s>Vāmadeva</s>.

children.text: ye cāpi vāmadeva tvāṃ jñāsyantīha dvijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: And the twice-born here who will know you as <s>Vāmadeva</s>
will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, from which return is hard to obtain.
When again here, in the sequence of ages, I became yellow in color,
by the name made by me that was then the Yellow <s>kalpa</s>.
And the goddess born from me was yellow-limbed and yellow-red.
At that time <s>Gāyatrī</s>, called <s>Brahmā</s>, was yellow in color.
There too, great being, with a mind yoked in yoga,
because I was known by those whose minds were wholly intent on yoga,
there again I was known by you in the state of <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
Therefore this <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>-hood is mine, O born from the golden egg.

children.text: ye māṃ rudraṃ ca rudrāṇīṃ gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram
children.translated_text: Those who know me as <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Rudrāṇī</s> as <s>Gāyatrī</s>, mother of the Veda,
joined with austerity, stainless, and united with <s>Brahman</s>,
will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, from which return is hard to obtain.
When again I was dark in color here, terrifying,

children.text: matkṛtena ca varṇena saṃkalpaḥ kṛṣṇa ucyate
children.translated_text: by the color produced by me that <s>kalpa</s> is called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
There I was like Time, Time who consumes the worlds.
I was known by you, O <s>Brahmā</s>, as <s>Ghora</s>, of terrible valor.
And <s>Gāyatrī</s>, born from me, was dark-limbed and dark-red.
Dark in form, O lord of gods, she was then called <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tasmād ghoratvamāpannaṃ ye māṃ vetsyanti bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those on earth who will know me as having attained <s>Ghora</s>-hood
For them I, undecaying, will be free from terror and peaceful.
And again, O <s>Brahmā</s>, when my state of having the universal form came to be,
then too I was known by you through supreme concentration.
And <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the support of the worlds, became universal in form.

children.text: tasmin viśvatvam āpannaṃ ye māṃ vetsyanti bhūtale
children.translated_text: Those on earth who will know me as having entered that universality

children.text: teṣāṃ śivaś ca saumyaś ca bhaviṣyāmi sadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: for them I shall indeed always be auspicious and gentle.
And because this aeon is proclaimed as universal in form,
so too this <s>Sāvitrī</s> is proclaimed as universal in form.

children.text: sarvarūpā tathā ceme saṃvṛttā mama putrakāḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise all these sons of mine became possessed of every form.

children.text: catvāraste mayā khyātāḥ putra vai lokasaṃmatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those four sons, my son, have been declared by me and are approved by the world.
And because all-variegatedness will belong to creatures,

children.text: sarvabhakṣā ca medhyā ca varṇataś ca bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: she will be all-eating and pure, and manifold in color.
Liberation, <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), wealth, and desire: this is the fourfold set.

children.text: yasmādvedāś ca vedyaṃ ca caturdhā vai bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Because the Vedas and what is to be known will indeed be fourfold,

children.text: bhūtagrāmāś ca catvāra āśramāś ca tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: the groups of beings are four, and likewise the life-stages.
The feet of <s>dharma</s> are four, and my sons are four.
Therefore the world, with its moving and unmoving beings, abides in the state of the four yugas.
It is established fourfold, and it will be four-footed.

children.text: bhūrloko 'tha bhuvarlokaḥ svarlokaś ca mahas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūrloka</s>, then <s>Bhuvarloka</s>, <s>Svarloka</s>, and <s>Mahas</s>,

children.text: janastapaś ca satyaṃ ca viṣṇulokastataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>Janas</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, and <s>Satya</s>, and beyond them the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The world stands in the eight syllables; in each place is that syllable.
<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svar</s>, and <s>Mahas</s> are precisely the four feet.
<s>Bhūrloka</s> is the first foot, and after it <s>Bhuvarloka</s>.

children.text: svarloko vai tṛtīyaś ca caturthastu mahas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Svarloka</s> is indeed the third, and the fourth is <s>Mahas</s>.

children.text: pañcamastu janastatra ṣaṣṭhaś ca tapa ucyate
children.translated_text: The fifth there is <s>Janas</s>, and the sixth is called <s>Tapas</s>.
<s>Satya</s> is the seventh world for those who go to non-return.
The world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is remembered as a place from which return is difficult.
The <s>Skānda</s> and <s>Auma</s> place is likewise endowed with every perfection.
Beyond that is remembered <s>Rudraloka</s>, that auspicious state of yogins.
Free from possessiveness, free from ego, and rid of desire and anger,
the disciplined brahmins whose minds are intent on meditation will see it.
And because this four-footed <s>Sarasvatī</s> was seen by you,
the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> at the end of the feet, and the peaceful, supreme <s>Kaumāra</s>,
the <s>Auma</s> and <s>Māheśvara</s> realms too, she was therefore seen as four-footed.
Therefore all animals will be four-footed.
And so they will have four udders.
Because <s>Soma</s>, joined with mantra, fell from my mouth,

children.text: jīvaḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ brahman punaḥ pītastanāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the life of living beings, O <s>Brahmā</s>, their teats are remembered as drunk again.
Therefore the nectar called life is indeed made of <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: catuṣpādā bhaviṣyanti śvetatvaṃ cāsya tena tat ||
children.translated_text: They will be four-footed, and that is why it has this whiteness.

children.text: yasmāccaiva kriyā bhūtvā dvipadā ca maheśvarī
children.translated_text: And because <s>Kriyā</s>, becoming two-footed, the great goddess,
was again seen just so as this <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the source of the worlds,

children.text: tasmācca dvipadāḥ sarve dvistanāś ca narāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: therefore all fine men are two-footed and have two breasts.
Therefore this unborn great goddess became possessed of every color.

children.text: yā vai dṛṣṭā mahāsattvā sarvabhūtadharā tvayā
children.translated_text: Since she, the great being who supports all creatures, was seen by you,
therefore creatures will have universal form.
And the unborn one, very radiant, will be universal in form.
His seed is unfailing everywhere, and in his mouth is the fire-offering flame.
Therefore <s>Hutāśana</s>, the fire, is all-pervading, pure, and animal-formed.

children.text: tapasā bhāvitātmāno ye māṃ drakṣyanti vai dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those brahmins whose selves have been refined by austerity, who will see me

children.text: īśitve ca vaśitve ca sarvagaṃ sarvataḥ sthitam
children.translated_text: as all-pervading and established everywhere, in lordship and mastery,
freed from passion and darkness, having abandoned the human body,
will come into my presence, from which return is difficult.
Thus, O brahmins, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s> was addressed by <s>Rudra</s>.
Having bowed and become composed, the grandsire spoke again:

children.text: ya evaṃ bhagavān vidvān gāyatryā vai maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: O blessed one, whoever, being wise, thus knows <s>Maheśvara</s> through <s>Gāyatrī</s>,

children.text: viśvātmānaṃ hi sarvaṃ tvāṃ gāyatryāstava ceśvara
children.translated_text: you as the universal self and as all, O lord, through the praise of <s>Gāyatrī</s>,

children.text: tasya dehi paraṃ sthānaṃ tathāstviti ca so'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: grant him the supreme place; and he replied, 'So be it.'
Therefore one who knows the universality of this <s>Gāyatrī</s> and of that great self

children.text: sa yāti brahmasāyujyaṃ vacanād brahmaṇaḥ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes to union with <s>Brahman</s>, by the word of the lord <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard all this as explained by <s>Rudra</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s>, lord of creatures, again bowed to <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the gods, and said:
Blessed lord, lord of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s> of universal form,
<s>Umādhava</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, homage to you, revered by the worlds.
Greatly fortunate one of universal form, in what time, O <s>Maheśvara</s>,
will the twice-born here see these bodies of yours, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, revered by the worlds?
Or at the arising of which age will they see them here?

children.text: kena vā tapasā deva dhyānayogena kena vā ||
children.translated_text: By what austerity, O god, or by what yoga of meditation?

children.text: namaste vai mahādeva śakyo draṣṭuṃ dvijātibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; by what means can you be seen by the twice-born?

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā śarvaḥ samprekṣya taṃ puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his, <s>Śarva</s> looked at him standing before him.
Smiling, <s>Mahādeva</s>, born of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, spoke.
The blessed lord said:
I cannot be seen here by men merely through austerity, conduct, or the fruit of gifts and <s>dharma</s>,
nor through the fruit of pilgrimages, nor through sacrifices with received fees,

children.text: na vedādhyayanairvāpi na vittena na vedanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor through Vedic recitations, nor by wealth, nor by acts of knowing.
I cannot be seen here by human beings except through meditation.
And in the seventh, the <s>Vārāha</s>, then in that age, O <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
then the blessed lord, <s>Kalpeśvara</s>, illuminer of all worlds,
and <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>, your grandson, will come to be.
Then, when that kalpa stands in the condition of the four yugas, at the end of the yuga,
for the sake of favoring the worlds and for the welfare of the Brahmins,

children.text: utpatsyāmi tadā brahman punar asmin yugāntike
children.translated_text: then, O <s>Brahman</s>, I shall be born again at this end of the yuga.

children.text: yugapravṛttyā ca tadā tasmiṃś ca prathame yuge ||
children.translated_text: And then, with the commencement of the yuga, in that first yuga,

children.text: dvāpare prathame brahmanyadā vyāsaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: in the first <s>Dvāpara</s>, O <s>Brahman</s>, when the lord himself is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then, for the sake of the Brahmins, at the end of that age in the Kali age,
I shall become a great sage named <s>Śveta</s>, furnished with a topknot.
On the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>, on the excellent mountain <s>Chāgala</s>,

children.text: tatra śiṣyāḥ śikhāyuktā bhaviṣyanti tadā mama
children.translated_text: there my disciples too will then be furnished with topknots.
<s>Śveta</s>, <s>Śvetaśikha</s>, <s>Śvetāsya</s>, and <s>Śvetalohita</s>,
four great-souled Brahmins, masters of the Vedas,
then, becoming chiefly absorbed in brahman and seeing the supreme course to brahman,
will come near me, devoted to the yoga of meditation.

children.text: tataḥ punaryadā brahman dvitīye dvāpare prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again, O <s>Brahman</s>, when in the second <s>Dvāpara</s> the lord,
the <s>Prajāpati</s> named <s>Sadya</s>, will be <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then, for the welfare of the worlds, by name called <s>Sutāra</s>,
I shall come to be in that Kali age, desiring to favor my disciples.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te śiṣyā nāmataḥ parikīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those disciples of mine are proclaimed by name:
<s>Dundubhi</s>, <s>Śatarūpa</s>, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, and then <s>Ketumānt</s>.

children.text: prāpya yogaṃ tathā dhyānaṃ sthāpya brahma ca bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: Having attained yoga and likewise meditation, and having established brahman upon the earth,
they will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, and indeed to companionship with him.

children.text: tṛtīye dvāpare caiva yadā vyāsastu bhārgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the third <s>Dvāpara</s>, when <s>Bhārgava</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become <s>Damana</s> at the end of the yuga.

children.text: tatrāpi ca bhaviṣyanti catvāro mama putrakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too four sons of mine will come to be:

children.text: vikośaś ca vikeśaś ca vipāśaḥ śāpanāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vikośa</s>, <s>Vikeśa</s>, <s>Vipāśa</s>, and <s>Śāpanāśana</s>.
They too, very mighty, by that same path taught by yoga,
will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, from which return is hard to obtain.

children.text: caturthe dvāpare caiva yadā vyāso 'ṅgirāḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And in the fourth <s>Dvāpara</s>, when <s>Aṅgiras</s> is remembered as <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become one named <s>Suhotra</s>.
There too those four sons of mine, rich in austerity,
will be the best of twice-born men, whose nature is yoga and whose vows are firm:
<s>Sumukha</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, <s>Durdara</s>, and <s>Duratikrama</s>.
Having attained the subtle course of yoga, stainless and with their sins burned away,
they too, joined to yoga and very mighty, by that same path
will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, from which return is hard to obtain.

children.text: pañcame dvāpare caiva vyāsastu savitā yadā ||
children.translated_text: And in the fifth <s>Dvāpara</s>, when <s>Savitṛ</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,

children.text: tadā cāpi bhaviṣyāmi kaṅko nāma mahātapāḥ
children.translated_text: then also I shall become <s>Kaṅka</s>, a man of great austerity.
For the sake of favoring the worlds, as one whose single portion and course are the self of yoga,
four very fortunate, stainless, pure-born ones
will become my disciples, whose nature is yoga and whose vows are firm:

children.text: sanakaḥ sanandanaś caiva prabhuryaś ca sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>, <s>Prabhu</s>, and <s>Sanātana</s>,
<s>Vibhu</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, free from possessiveness and egoism.
They will come near me, where return is hard to obtain.

children.text: parīvarte punaḥ ṣaṣṭhe mṛtyurvyāso yadā vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again, in the sixth turn, when mighty <s>Mṛtyu</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become one named <s>Logākṣi</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te śiṣyā yogātmāno dṛḍhavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those disciples of mine, whose nature is yoga and whose vows are firm,
will be four very fortunate ones, honored by the world:
<s>Sudhāmā</s>, <s>Viraja</s>, and <s>Śaṅkhapādraja</s> as well.
All will be great-souled, whose nature is yoga, with their sins burned away.
They too, endowed with the yoga of meditation, by that same path
will come near me, where return is hard to obtain.

children.text: saptame parivarte tu yadā vyāsaḥ śatakratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the seventh turn, when <s>Śatakratu</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
greatly radiant, named <s>Vibhu</s>, famed in a former birth,
then too I shall come to be at the end of that Kali age.

children.text: jaigīṣavyo vibhuḥ khyātaḥ sarveṣāṃ yogināṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall be <s>Jaigīṣavya</s>, the mighty one, renowned as the best of all yogins.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti yuge tathā ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine will come to be in that age:

children.text: sārasvataś ca meghaś ca meghavāhaḥ suvāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sārasvata</s>, <s>Megha</s>, <s>Meghavāha</s>, and <s>Suvāhana</s>.
They too, devoted to the yoga of meditation, by that same path
will go, great-souled, to the stainless world of <s>Rudra</s>.
And in the eighth turn <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> will be <s>Vyāsa</s>.
When that is so, I shall become one named <s>Dadhivāhana</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā yogātmāno dṛḍhavratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine, whose nature is yoga and whose vows are firm,

children.text: bhaviṣyanti mahāyogā yeṣāṃ nāsti samo bhuvi
children.translated_text: will be great yogins, whose equal does not exist on earth:
<s>Kapila</s>, <s>Āsuri</s>, and likewise the sage <s>Pañcaśikha</s>,
and <s>Bāṣkala</s>, a great yogin; they will be righteous and very mighty.
Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, wise and with their sins burned away,
they will come near me, where return is hard to obtain.

children.text: parivarte tu navame vyāsaḥ sārasvato yadā ||
children.translated_text: But in the ninth turn, when <s>Sārasvata</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become one named <s>Ṛṣabha</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine will be very mighty:

children.text: parāśaraś ca gargaś ca bhārgavāṅgirasau tadā
children.translated_text: <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Garga</s>, and then <s>Bhārgava</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
They will be great-souled Brahmins, masters of the Vedas.
Having approached the path of meditation, they too will go in the same way.
All will be eminent through the power of austerity, skilled in cursing and granting favors.
They too, ascetics, by that same path taught by yoga
they will go to <s>Rudraloka</s>, from which return is hard to obtain.

children.text: daśame dvāpare vyāsaḥ tripādvai nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: In the tenth <s>Dvāpara</s>, the <s>Vyāsa</s> will indeed be named <s>Tripād</s>;
when he will be a brahmin, then I shall become a sage.
On the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>, on the excellent mountain <s>Bhṛgutuṅga</s>,
there will be a peak known by the name of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, worshiped by the gods.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti dṛḍhavratāḥ
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine will be firm in their vows:
<s>Balabandhu</s>, <s>Nirāmitra</s>, <s>Ketuśṛṅga</s>, and <s>Tapodhana</s>.
They will be yogic in self, great-souled, endowed with austerity and yoga;
their sins burned away by austerity, they will go to <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: ekādaśe dvāpare tu vyāsastu trivrato yadā
children.translated_text: And in the eleventh <s>Dvāpara</s>, when the <s>Vyāsa</s> is <s>Trivrata</s>,
then also I shall arise at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s> in the Kali age.
I will be renowned in all worlds as <s>Ugra</s>, of great splendor.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine will be of great might:
<s>Lambodara</s>, <s>Lambākṣa</s>, <s>Lambakeśa</s>, and <s>Pralambaka</s>.

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokaṃ gatā hi te ||
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>Māheśvara yoga</s>, they indeed went to <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: dvādaśe parivarte tu śatatejā yadā muniḥ
children.translated_text: And in the twelfth turn, when the sage <s>Śatatejas</s>,
the very brilliant <s>Vyāsa</s>, best of poets, will arise,
then too, here in the Kali age at the end of the yuga, I shall appear.
Having reached the <s>Haituka</s> forest, I will be known by the name <s>Atri</s>.
There too these sons of mine, bathed and anointed with ashes,
will be great yogins, intent on <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: sarvajñaḥ samabuddhiś ca sādhyaḥ sarvastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvajña</s>, <s>Samabuddhi</s>, <s>Sādhya</s>, and likewise <s>Sarva</s>,

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokaṃ gatā hi te ||
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Māheśvara yoga</s>, indeed went to <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: trayodaśe punaḥ prāpte parivarte krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: Again, when the thirteenth turn has arrived in due sequence,

children.text: dharmo nārāyaṇo nāma vyāsastu bhavitā yadā ||
children.translated_text: when <s>Dharma</s>, named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, will be the <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall be the great sage named <s>Vāli</s>,
in the holy hermitage of the <s>Vālakhilyas</s> on Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine will be rich in austerity:
<s>Sudhāman</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, and also <s>Virajas</s>.
Endowed with the power of great yoga, stainless, and with their seed drawn upward,

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokaṃ gatā hi te ||
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Māheśvara yoga</s>, they indeed went to <s>Rudraloka</s>.
When <s>Tarakṣu</s> will be <s>Vyāsa</s> in the fourteenth cycle,
there too, once again, I shall appear at the end of the yuga.

children.text: vaṃśe tvaṅgirasāṃ śreṣṭhe gautamo nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: In the eminent lineage of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, I will be named <s>Gautama</s>;
that forest, greatly holy, will be called <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti kalau tadā
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine will arise at that time in the Kali age:
<s>Atri</s>, <s>Devasada</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, and then <s>Śraviṣṭhaka</s>.
They will be yogic in self, great-souled, all endowed with yoga;

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokāya te gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Māheśvara yoga</s>, they went to <s>Rudraloka</s>.
Then, when the fifteenth turn has arrived in due succession,
when <s>Traiyyāruṇi</s> becomes <s>Vyāsa</s> in the <s>Dvāpara</s>,
then also I shall be a twice-born named <s>Vedaśiras</s>.
There will be an astra named <s>Vedaśiras</s>, that belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s>.
Of great power, the mountain too will be <s>Vedaśīrṣa</s>;
having reached the back of <s>Himavat</s>, at <s>Sarasvatī</s>, on the excellent mountain,

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: there too these sons of mine will be rich in austerity:

children.text: kuṇiś ca kuṇibāhuś ca kuśarīraḥ kunetrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṇi</s>, <s>Kuṇibāhu</s>, <s>Kuśarīra</s>, and <s>Kunetraka</s>.
Yogic in self, great-souled, all of them with their seed drawn upward,

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokāya te gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Māheśvara yoga</s>, they went to <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: vyāso yuge ṣoḍaśe tu yadā devo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: When, in the sixteenth age, <s>Deva</s> will become <s>Vyāsa</s>,
there, for bestowing yoga upon devotees and self-controlled people,
then too I shall appear, named <s>Gokarṇa</s>.

children.text: bhaviṣyati supuṇyaṃ ca gokarṇaṃ nāma tadvanam ||
children.translated_text: That forest will be very holy and called <s>Gokarṇa</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti ca yoginaḥ
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine will be yogins:
<s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, and then <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
They too, by that very path, endowed with the yoga of meditation,

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ gantāro rudrameva hi ||
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Māheśvara yoga</s>, will indeed go to <s>Rudra</s>.
Then, when the seventeenth turn has arrived in due succession,
when there will be a <s>Vyāsa</s> named <s>Devakṛtañjaya</s>,
then also I shall be named <s>Guhāvāsin</s>,
on the lovely, very high peak of <s>Himavat</s>, at <s>Mahālaya</s>.
The sacred field <s>Mahālaya</s> will be very holy.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā yogajñā brahmavādinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine, knowers of yoga and speakers of <s>Brahman</s>,
will be great-souled, free from possessiveness and without egoism:
<s>Utathya</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Mahāyoga</s>, and <s>Mahābala</s>.
There will then be a hundred thousand disciples of theirs, yogins of meditation,

children.text: bhaviṣyanti tadā kāle sarve te dhyānayuñjakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all of them practicing meditation at that time.
Delighting in the practice of yoga and placing <s>Maheśvara</s> in their heart,

children.text: mahālaye padaṃ nyastaṃ dṛṣṭvā yānti śivaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: having seen the footprint set down at <s>Mahālaya</s>, they go to the state of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: ye cānye 'pi mahātmānaḥ kalau tasmin yugāntike
children.translated_text: And whatever other great-souled people there are in that Kali age, at the end of the yuga,
who fix their mind in meditation, stainless and pure in understanding,
by my grace they will go to <s>Rudraloka</s>, free from fever.

children.text: gatvā mahālayaṃ puṇyaṃ dṛṣṭvā māheśvaraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Having gone to holy <s>Mahālaya</s> and seen the <s>Māheśvara</s> footprint,
a creature who has crossed over causes ten ancestors and ten descendants to cross over;
having caused himself, the twenty-first, to cross over at <s>Mahālaya</s>,
by my grace they will go to <s>Rudraloka</s>, free from fever.
Then, O lord, when in the eighteenth turn

children.text: tadā ṛtañjayo nāma vyāsastu bhavitā muniḥ
children.translated_text: the sage <s>Vyāsa</s> will be named <s>Ṛtañjaya</s>
Then too I shall become one named <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>.
In the very holy <s>Siddhakṣetra</s>, worshipped by gods and Dānavas,
on the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s> there is a mountain named <s>Śikhaṇḍī</s>.
There is also the forest of <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>, resorted to by siddhas.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti tapodhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine, rich in austerity, will come to be.

children.text: vācaśravā ṛcīkaś ca śyāvāśvaś ca yatīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vācaśravā</s>, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, <s>Śyāvāśva</s>, and <s>Yatīśvara</s>,
whose selves are yoga, great-souled, all of them masters of the Vedas,
having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, are established for the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Then, when the nineteenth turn has arrived in order,
the great sage <s>Bharadvāja</s> will be <s>Vyāsa</s> by name.
Then too I shall become one named <s>Jaṭāmālī</s>.
On the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>, where the mountain <s>Jaṭāyu</s> is,

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there too those sons of mine, very mighty, will come to be.
<s>Hiraṇyanābha</s>, <s>Kauśalya</s>, <s>Lokākṣī</s>, and <s>Kuthumi</s>,
powerful in the discipline of yoga, all of them chaste ascetics with seed drawn upward,
having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, are established for the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
And when the twentieth turn comes, then
the great sage <s>Gautama</s> will be <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Then too I shall become one named <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s>.
At that time people too will delight in loud laughter.
There on the very slope of <s>Himavat</s> is the great mountain <s>Aṭṭahāsa</s>,
served by gods, Dānavas, chief Yakṣas, siddhas, and Cāraṇas.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine, very mighty, will come to be,
whose selves are yoga, great-souled, meditative, and restrained in vow:
<s>Sumantu</s>, the learned <s>Barbarī</s>, <s>Kabandha</s>, and <s>Kuśikaṃdhara</s>.

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokāya te gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, they went to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Again, when the twenty-first turn has arrived in order,

children.text: vācaśravāḥ smṛto vyāso yadā sa ṛṣisattamaḥ
children.translated_text: when <s>Vācaśravā</s>, best of seers, is remembered as <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become one named <s>Dāruka</s>.
From that there will arise the auspicious holy <s>Devadāru</s> forest.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti mahaujasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine, very mighty, will come to be:
<s>Plakṣa</s>, <s>Dārbhāyaṇi</s>, <s>Ketumān</s>, and <s>Gautama</s>,
whose selves are yoga, great-souled, restrained, and chaste with seed drawn upward.
Undertaking the lifelong vow, they went to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: dvāviṃśe parivarte tu vyāsaḥ śuṣmāyaṇo yadā ||
children.translated_text: But in the twenty-second turn, when <s>Śuṣmāyaṇa</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall be a great sage in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: nāmnā vai lāṅgalī bhīmo yatra devāḥ savāsavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: named <s>Lāṅgalī Bhīma</s>, where the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s>

children.text: drakṣyanti māṃ kalau tasmin bhavaṃ caiva halāyudham
children.translated_text: will see me in that Kali age as <s>Bhava</s>, bearing the plough as weapon.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti sudhārmikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine, very righteous, will come to be:

children.text: bhallavī madhupiṅgaś ca śvetaketuḥ kuśas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhallavī</s>, <s>Madhupiṅga</s>, <s>Śvetaketu</s>, and <s>Kuśa</s>.
Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, they too are devoted to meditation,
stainless and chiefly intent on brahman, established for the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
In the twenty-third turn, when the sage <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>

children.text: vyāso hi bhavitā brahmaṃstadāhaṃ bhavitā punaḥ
children.translated_text: will be <s>Vyāsa</s>, O Brahman, then I shall again become
a righteous son of a sage named <s>Śveta</s>, great-bodied.
At that time I shall spend my time on that best of excellent mountains.

children.text: tena kālañjaro nāma bhaviṣyati sa parvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because of that, the mountain will be named <s>Kālañjara</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te śiṣyā bhaviṣyanti tapasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: There too those disciples of mine, ascetics, will come to be:

children.text: uśiko bṛhadaśvaś ca devalaḥ kavireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uśika</s>, <s>Bṛhadaśva</s>, <s>Devala</s>, and <s>Kavi</s>.

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokāya te gataḥ
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, they went to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: parivarte caturviṃśe vyāsa ṛkṣo yadā vibho ||
children.translated_text: In the twenty-fourth turn, when <s>Ṛkṣa</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>, O lord,
then too I shall come to be at the end of that Kali age,
a great yogin named <s>Śūlī</s> in <s>Naimiṣa</s>, honored by the gods.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te śiṣyā bhaviṣyanti tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: There too those disciples of mine, rich in austerity, will come to be:
<s>Śālihotra</s>, <s>Agniveśa</s>, <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, and <s>Śaradvasu</s>.
They too, by that same path, are established for the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Again, when the twenty-fifth turn has arrived in order,
when the Vāsiṣṭha named <s>Śakti</s> will be <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become the lord <s>Daṇḍī Muṇḍīśvara</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti tapodhanāḥ
children.translated_text: There too those sons of mine, rich in austerity, will come to be:

children.text: chagalaḥ kuṇḍakarṇaś ca kubhāṇḍaś ca pravāhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Chagala</s>, <s>Kuṇḍakarṇa</s>, <s>Kubhāṇḍa</s>, and <s>Pravāhaka</s>.
Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, they went to immortality.

children.text: ṣaḍviṃśe parivarte tu yadā vyāsaḥ parāśaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: But in the twenty-sixth turn, when <s>Parāśara</s> is <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall become one named <s>Sahiṣṇu</s>.

children.text: puraṃ bhadravaṭaṃ prāpya kalau tasmin yugāntike ||
children.translated_text: Having reached the town <s>Bhadravaṭa</s> at the end of that Kali age,

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti sudhārmikāḥ
children.translated_text: there too those sons of mine, very righteous, will come to be:
<s>Ulūka</s>, <s>Vidyuta</s>, <s>Śaṃbūka</s>, and <s>Āśvalāyana</s>.

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokāya te gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, they went to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Again, when the twenty-seventh turn has arrived in order,
when <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>, rich in austerity, will be <s>Vyāsa</s>,
then too I shall be <s>Somaśarmā</s>, best of twice-born men.
Having reached the <s>Prabhāsa</s> tīrtha, with a self of yoga and renowned for yoga,

children.text: tatrāpi mama te śiṣyā bhaviṣyanti tapodhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: there too those disciples of mine, rich in austerity, will come to be:

children.text: akṣapādaḥ kumāraś ca ulūko vatsa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Akṣapāda</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Ulūka</s>, and <s>Vatsa</s>.
Their selves are yoga, great-souled, stainless, and pure in understanding.

children.text: prāpya māheśvaraṃ yogaṃ rudralokaṃ tato gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, they then went to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Again, when the twenty-eighth turn has arrived in order,
the glorious son of <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the grandsire of the world,

children.text: yadā bhaviṣyati vyāso nāmnā dvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the lord <s>Vyāsa</s> will be one named <s>Dvaipāyana</s>,
then, through a sixth portion, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the best of men,
the best of the <s>Yadus</s>, descended from <s>Vasudeva</s>, will become <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Then I too shall come into being, whose self is yoga, by yogic power,
with the body of a celibate, for the sake of causing wonder in the world.

children.text: śmaśāne mṛtam utsṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭvā kāyam anāthakam
children.translated_text: Seeing in a cremation ground an abandoned dead body, a body without a protector,
I shall enter it by yogic power for the benefit of Brahmins.

children.text: divyāṃ meruguhāṃ puṇyāṃ tvayā sārdhaṃ ca viṣṇunā
children.translated_text: In the divine and holy cave of <s>Meru</s>, together with you and with <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
then, O <s>Brahmā</s>, I shall be <s>Lakulī</s> by name.

children.text: kāyāvatāra ityevaṃ siddhakṣetraṃ ca vai tadā
children.translated_text: Then that accomplished field will indeed be famed as <s>Kāyāvatāra</s>,
and it will be widely renowned for as long as the earth endures.

children.text: tatrāpi mama te putrā bhaviṣyanti tapasvinaḥ
children.translated_text: There too these sons of mine will be ascetics:

children.text: kuśikaś caiva gargaś ca mitraḥ kauruṣya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśika</s>, <s>Garga</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Kauruṣya</s> as well.
They will be yogic in nature, great-souled Brahmins, masters of the Vedas.
Having attained <s>Māheśvara</s> yoga, stainless and with their seed drawn upward,
