they will go to <s>Rudra</s>'s world, from which return is hard to obtain.
These accomplished <s>Pāśupatas</s> will have their bodies smeared with ash,
will be always devoted to worship of the <s>liṅga</s>, established both outwardly and inwardly,

children.text: bhaktyā mayi ca yogena dhyānaniṣṭhā jitendriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: devoted to me with devotion and yoga, fixed in meditation, and with their senses conquered.
For cutting the bondage of saṃsāra and illuminating the path of knowledge,
and for attaining knowledge of one's own nature, there is the great <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga.

children.text: yogamārgā anekāś ca jñānamārgās tv anekaśaḥ
children.translated_text: There are many paths of yoga, and paths of knowledge are manifold,
but they do not anywhere reach cessation without the <s>pañcākṣarī</s> (five-syllabled mantra).
When this man practices austerity free from all pairs of opposites,

children.text: tadā sa mukto mantavyaḥ pakvaṃ phalamiva sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then he should be regarded as liberated, standing like a ripe fruit.
A man who properly practices the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow for a single day

children.text: na sāṃkhye pañcarātre vā na prāpnoti gatiṃ kadā ||
children.translated_text: never fails to attain the goal, whether in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> or in the <s>Pāñcarātra</s>.
Thus this mark of my manifestations has been declared by me,
from <s>Manu</s> down to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in the sequence of twenty-eight ages.
There, when <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> appears in that kalpa,
the division of the collections of śruti, marked by <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), will take place.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard this manifestation of <s>Rudra</s> proclaimed by <s>Mahādeva</s>,
the greatly radiant Blessed One bowed down to <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tuṣṭāva vāgbhir iṣṭābhiḥ punaḥ prāha ca śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: He praised him with cherished words and then again spoke to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:

children.text: sarve viṣṇumayā devāḥ sarve viṣṇumayā gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All gods are pervaded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>; all hosts are pervaded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
No other course equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s> is prescribed.

children.text: ityevaṃ satataṃ vedā gāyanti nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the Vedas always sing; of this there is no doubt.
How then did that Blessed One, the god of gods, become devoted to worship of your <s>liṅga</s>,
that lordly god whose chief concern is bowing to you?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing the words of that supreme <s>Brahmā</s>,
as if drinking them in with his eyes, pleased by the weight of that question,
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, looking upon him, explained to him the procedure of worship:
You, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Śakra</s> himself, O best of gods,

children.text: munayaś ca sadā liṅgaṃ sampūjya vidhipūrvakam
children.translated_text: and the sages, having always worshiped the <s>liṅga</s> according to rule,

children.text: svaṃsvaṃ padaṃ vibho prāptās tasmāt sampūjayanti te ||
children.translated_text: have obtained each his own station, O mighty one; therefore they worship it.
Without worship of the <s>liṅga</s> there is no steadfastness; therefore <s>Janārdana</s>,
the Blessed Lord, worships it daily with faith as his own self.
Having spoken thus to <s>Brahmā</s> and shown him favor, <s>Maheśvara</s>
looked again at the lord of gods and vanished on that very spot.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, intending him, bowed with folded hands,
and the Blessed One, having received awareness from <s>Śaṅkara</s>, set out to create everything without remainder.
The sages said:
How is <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s> in the form of the <s>liṅga</s>, to be worshiped?
You should tell us this now, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: devyā pṛṣṭo mahādevaḥ kailāse tāṃ nagātmajām
children.translated_text: Questioned by the goddess on <s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the lord of gods,
spoke in order to that daughter of the mountain, seated on his lap, the rule for worship of the <s>liṅga</s>.
Then <s>Nandī</s>, the son of <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>, standing at his side,
heard it all in former times and told it to the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, O men of good vows,
to <s>Sanatkumāra</s>: the auspicious and supreme rule for worship of the <s>liṅga</s>.
From him the greatly radiant <s>Vyāsa</s> heard it, as authoritative as śruti.
I shall declare that rule beginning with bathing, the bathing, yoga, and services,
just as he heard them from the mouth of <s>Śailādi</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: atha snānavidhiṃ vakṣye brāhmaṇānāṃ hitāya ca
children.translated_text: Now I shall teach the rule for bathing, for the benefit of Brahmins,
which removes all sins directly and was formerly taught by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: anena vidhinā snātvā sakṛtpūjya ca śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: Having bathed by this rule, having worshiped <s>Śaṅkara</s> even once,

children.text: brahmakūrcaṃ ca pītvā tu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: and having drunk the <s>brahmakūrca</s> (purifying ritual drink), one is released from all sins.
The god of gods, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, has declared bathing to be threefold,
for the benefit of Brahmins and the others, O best son of the four-faced one.
First one should perform the <s>Vāruṇa</s> bath, and then the excellent <s>Āgneya</s> bath;
after that one should perform the mantra-bath and worship <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: bhāvaduṣṭo 'mbhasi snātvā bhasmanā ca na śudhyati
children.translated_text: One whose intention is corrupt is not purified by bathing in water, nor by ash.
One should practice purity with purified intention; otherwise one should not perform it.
Even if a man bathes in all rivers, lakes, and ponds until the dissolution of the world,
if his intention is corrupt, he is not purified; there is no doubt.
For when the lotus of men's mind has awakened,
after sleeping in darkness, by the light of the sun of knowledge, then it is pure.
Earth, cow-dung, sesame, flowers, and likewise ash for the bath

children.text: ādāya tīre niḥkṣipya snānatīrthe kuśāni ca ||
children.translated_text: he should take, set down on the bank, and place kuśa grasses at the bathing ford.

children.text: prakṣālyācamya pādau ca malaṃ dehādviśodhya ca
children.translated_text: Having washed and sipped water, washed his feet, and cleansed the impurity from his body,
then, with the materials that are on the bank, he should perform the bath.
With the mantra beginning "uddhṛtāsi" he should again purify the body;
then, taking clay and bathing, he should put on another garment, one that is not soiled.
The knower of mantras, with the mantra "gandhadvārām durādharṣām,"
should smear himself with tawny cow-dung that has been kept pure and dry.

children.text: punaḥ snātvā parityajya tadvastraṃ malinaṃ tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having bathed again, he should then discard that soiled garment;
wearing a white garment, he should perform the bath.
For the sake of purification from all sins, he should invoke <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: sampūjya manasā devaṃ dhyānayajñena vai bhavam ||
children.translated_text: and, mentally worshiping the god <s>Bhava</s> by the sacrifice of meditation,

children.text: ācamya tristadā tīrthe hyavagāhya bhavaṃ smaran
children.translated_text: he should sip water three times there at the ford and plunge in while remembering <s>Bhava</s>.
Again sipping water according to rule, he should consecrate the great water with mantras.
Having plunged again in it, he should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>.
Self-controlled, he should remember in that water the orbs of the sun, moon, and fire.
After sipping water again, the knower of mantras should rise from that water;
then, entering the middle of the ford again for the increase of merit,
with a horn and with leaf-cups made of washed palāśa leaves,
he should sprinkle himself with water that contains kuśa grass and flowers.
The knower of mantras should do so with the <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, and the mantra called <s>Tvarita</s>,
with the groups beginning with <s>Taratsamandī</s>, and also with the two <s>Śānti</s> mantras,
with one <s>Śāntidharma</s> mantra and with the five <s>Brahma</s> purifiers,
remembering the form of each mantra's presiding deity and its seers.

children.text: evaṃ hi cābhiṣicyātha svamūrdhni payasā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus sprinkled himself with milk on his own head, O twice-born men,

children.text: dhyāyecca tryambakaṃ devaṃ hṛdi pañcāsyam īśvaram ||
children.translated_text: he should meditate in his heart on the three-eyed god, the five-faced lord.
After sipping, he should perform the sipping rite, having considered what is stated in his own sūtra.
With a pavitra in his hand, seated in a pure place according to rule,

children.text: abhyukṣya sakuśaṃ cāpi dakṣiṇena kareṇa tu
children.translated_text: and sprinkling, together with kuśa grass, with his right hand,
he should drink water three times after setting it forth, making a circular motion and remaining attentive.
Then he should circumambulate for the pacification of the sin of harming.
Thus the excellent bath and sipping rite has been briefly taught
for the benefit of all Brahmins, O best of the twice-born.
Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the twenty-fifth chapter, named "The Rite of Bathing."
<s>Nandin</s> said:
Then he should invoke the goddess <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the mother of the Veda,
the great goddess, with this very mantra, "May the boon-giving goddess come."
He should offer her water for the feet, water for sipping, and an arghya.
Having performed three prāṇāyāmas, whether seated or standing,

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: he should recite a thousand times, or half of that, or one hundred and eight times.
One should practice <s>Gāyatrī</s> together with the praṇava, in any one of the three modes.

children.text: arghyaṃ dattvā samabhyarcya praṇamya śirasā svayam
children.translated_text: Having given an arghya, worshiped, and himself bowed with his head,
he should dismiss the mother, saying, "O goddess, on the highest peak."
Looking east, he should salute <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the mother of the Veda,
and, with his hands joined in reverence, should also pray to <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: udutyaṃ ca tathā citraṃ jātavedasameva ca
children.translated_text: He should recite "ud u tyam," likewise "citra," and "jātavedasam,"

children.text: abhivandya punaḥ sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then again salute the Sun and <s>Brahmā</s> according to rule.
Likewise, having recited the solar hymns that belong to the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman,

children.text: japtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ paścāttriḥ kṛtvā ca vibhāvasoḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should afterward circumambulate the fire three times.
He should salute the self, the inner self, and the supreme self,

children.text: abhivandya punaḥ sūryaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca vibhāvasum ||
children.translated_text: and again salute the Sun, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the fire.
Then he should invoke the sages and ancestors by their own names, as is proper;
saying, "I invoke all," he should invoke all the gods on every side.
Afterward he should satisfy them with offerings according to rule, facing east or north.
He should meditate on the form and principle of each and salute them in order.
For the gods, he should use water with flowers; for the seers, water with kuśa grass;
for the ancestors, sesame-water, everywhere mixed with fragrance.
Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder for the gods, and in the nivītī position for the seers' tarpaṇa,
with the thread over the right shoulder, O lord of Brahmins, he should satisfy the ancestors in order.
The wise man should perform the offering to the gods with the tips of his fingers;
the learned Vedic man should satisfy the seers with the little finger, for the attainment of all success.
The learned man should satisfy the ancestors with the right thumb.
In this same way, O tiger among sages, a twice-born man should perform the <s>brahmayajña</s>.

children.text: devayajñaṃ ca mānuṣyaṃ bhūtayajñaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He should perform the <s>devayajña</s>, the <s>mānuṣyayajña</s>, the <s>bhūtayajña</s>,
and the <s>pitṛyajña</s>, being pure in self and devoted to sacrificial action.
Study of one's own branch of the Veda, O Brahmin, is remembered as the <s>brahmayajña</s>.

children.text: agnau juhoti yaccānnaṃ devayajña iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The food that one offers into the fire is remembered as the <s>devayajña</s>.
The ritual presentation of bali to all beings
is called the <s>bhūtayajña</s>, bestowing prosperity on all embodied beings.
Those Brahmins who are together with their wives, know all principles, and have crossed to the far shore of the Veda:
the food given to them after bowing to them is called the human sacrifice.

children.text: pitṝn uddiśya yaddattaṃ pitṛyajñaḥ sa ucyate
children.translated_text: What is given with the ancestors in view is called the <s>pitṛyajña</s>.
Thus one should perform the five great sacrifices for the accomplishment of all aims.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ śṛṇu yajñānāṃ brahmayajñaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Hear, among all sacrifices, the <s>brahmayajña</s> is remembered as supreme.
A mortal devoted to the <s>brahmayajña</s> is honored in <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
By the <s>brahmayajña</s> all the gods, together with <s>Vāsava</s>, are pleased.
<s>Brahmā</s>, the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,

children.text: vedāś ca pitaraḥ sarve nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: and the Vedas and all the ancestors: no deliberation is to be made about this.
A Brahmin who knows the <s>Brahmayajña</s> should go outside the village,

children.text: yāvat tvadṛṣṭam abhavad uṭajānāṃ chadaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: as far as the covering of the huts is no longer visible to a man.
Facing east, north, northeast, or else also the northeast direction,
he should perform pure ācamana; that is precisely for the sake of the <s>Brahmayajña</s>.

children.text: prītyarthaṃ ca ṛcāṃ viprāḥ triḥ pītvā plāvya plāvya ca ||
children.translated_text: For the satisfaction of the ṛc-verses, O Brahmins, he should drink three times, rinsing again and again.

children.text: yajuṣāṃ parimṛjyaivaṃ dviḥ prakṣālya ca vāriṇā
children.translated_text: For the Yajus texts, he should wipe in this way, and wash twice with water.
For the satisfaction of the <s>Sāmaveda</s> chants he should sip and touch the head,
and for the <s>Atharvaveda</s> he should touch the eyes, and likewise for the Aṅgiras texts.

children.text: nāsike brāhmaṇo 'ṅgānāṃ kṣālya kṣālya ca vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: For the ancillary texts a Brahmin should touch the nostrils, washing again and again with water.
For the eighteen Purāṇas, beginning with the <s>Brahma</s> Purāṇa, and likewise
for the secondary Purāṇas, beginning with the <s>Saura</s>, in due order,
and likewise for the holy Itihāsas, beginning with the Śaiva texts,

children.text: śrotre spṛśeddhi tuṣṭyarthaṃ hṛddeśaṃ tu tataḥ spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: he should touch the ears for their satisfaction, and then touch the region of the heart.
For all the Kalpas and the rest, O knowers of Kalpa, best knowers of Kalpa,
having sipped thus, the wise man should spread a bundle of darbha grass for himself,
placing it on the palm of his hand, toward the south and north of himself.
Wearing a golden ring, or also furnished with a sacred band,
the one wearing the sacred thread, composed, should perform the <s>Brahmayajña</s> according to rule.
If an excellent twice-born sage eats without performing the five great sacrifices,

children.text: bhuktvā ca sūkarāṇāṃ tu yonau vai jāyate naraḥ
children.translated_text: that man is indeed born in the womb of pigs.
Therefore they must be performed with every effort by one who desires auspiciousness.
After the <s>Brahmayajña</s>, having first in every way performed his own bath,
the self-controlled man should collect sacred water according to rule and enter the camp.
Outside the house itself he should wash his feet and hands with water,
and then perform an ash-bath according to rule for purification of the body.
He should purify the ash in the proper manner, ash born from the agnihotra, with the praṇava.
Since, in the morning, when the sun has risen, one should offer with 'jyotiḥ sūryaḥ,'

children.text: jyotiragnis tathā sāyaṃ samyak cānudite mṛṣā
children.translated_text: and similarly in the evening with 'jyotir agniḥ'; if the sun has not risen properly, it is false.
Therefore ash connected with an offering after sunrise is purifying and auspicious.

children.text: nāsti satyasamaṃ yasmādasatyaṃ pātakaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: For there is nothing equal to truth, and untruth is sin.
With the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra he should sprinkle the region of the head, and the face with <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
With <s>Aghora</s> he should sprinkle the chest region, and the private part with <s>Vāma</s>, O good-vowed ones.
With <s>Sadya</s> he should sprinkle the feet, and the whole body with the praṇava.
Then the best of knowers of Brahman should wash his feet and hands.
After removing the ash and taking more, remembering the God of gods,
he should then perform the mantra-bath in sequence with the mantras beginning 'āpo hi ṣṭhā.'
And likewise with holy mantras arising from the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman,

children.text: dvijānāṃ tu hitāyaivaṃ kathitaṃ snānamadya te
children.translated_text: this bath has now been taught to you for the welfare of twice-born men.

children.text: saṃkṣipya yaḥ sakṛtkuryātsa yāti paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever performs it once, even in brief, goes to the supreme state.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge pañcayajñavidhānaṃ nāma ṣaḍviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the twenty-sixth chapter, named 'The Prescription of the Five Sacrifices,' is concluded.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
I shall state; listen in brief to the sequential rule for worship of the liṅga,

children.text: vaktuṃ varṣaśatenāpi na śakyaṃ vistareṇa yat ||
children.translated_text: which cannot be stated in detail even in a hundred years.

children.text: evaṃ snātvā yathānyāyaṃ pūjāsthānaṃ praviśya ca
children.translated_text: Having bathed thus according to rule and entered the place of worship,
he should perform three prāṇāyāmas and meditate on the god <s>Tryambaka</s>,
five-faced, ten-armed, resembling pure crystal,
adorned with all ornaments and decorated with variegated garments.
Taking refuge in that form, by burning, flooding, and the other rites,
and assuming a Śaiva body, he should worship <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: dehaśuddhiṃ ca kṛtvaiva mūlamantraṃ nyaset kramāt
children.translated_text: Having performed bodily purification, he should then place the root mantra in sequence,
everywhere with the praṇava alone, and the brahmans in due order.

children.text: sūtre namaḥ śivāyeti chandāṃsi parame śubhe
children.translated_text: In the sacred thread, with 'namaḥ śivāya,' O supremely auspicious one, the meters,
and the mantras are situated in subtle form, since that is so.

children.text: nyagrodhabīje nyagrodhas tathā sūtre tu śobhane
children.translated_text: As the banyan tree is in the banyan seed, so too, in the splendid thread,
the great Brahman, though great, is itself situated as something subtle.
He should sprinkle the place of worship with water scented with sandalwood fragrance,
and afterward purify the substances by washing, sprinkling, and the like.
Washing and sprinkling are prescribed with the praṇava.
He should set out in order the sprinkling vessel, the arghya vessel, and the pādya vessel,
and likewise the vessel prepared for ācamana.
The wise man should establish them according to rule, covering them in the proper manner.
He should cover them with darbha grasses and sprinkle them with pure water.
Then into each of them all he should pour very cool water.
The wise man should pour it into them with the praṇava, looking over the substances.

children.text: uśīraṃ candanaṃ caiva pādye tu parikalpayet ||
children.translated_text: He should arrange uśīra and sandalwood in the pādya vessel.
Jāti, kaṅkola, camphor, bahumūla, and tamālaka,
having powdered them according to rule, he should put them in the ācamana vessel.
Thus in all the vessels he should put sandalwood as well,

children.text: karpūraṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ puṣpāṇi vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and camphor according to rule, and various flowers.
Tips of kuśa grass, unhusked grains, barley, rice, and sesame,
ghee, siddhārtha seeds, flowers, and ash should be placed in the arghya vessel.
Kuśa, flowers, barley, rice, bahumūla, and tamālaka
he should place in the sprinkling vessel, and ash too, with the praṇava.
He should also place the five-syllabled mantra and the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, whose deity is <s>Rudra</s>.
or even only the praṇava, the unsurpassed essence of the Veda.
Then afterward he should sprinkle the substances with the praṇava,
which is placed in the sprinkling vessel, and with the five beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>.
At the side of the God of gods he should worship <s>Nandin</s>,
resembling ten thousand blazing fires, three-eyed, the lord of the gods,
with the young moon as his diadem, with a tawny face, four-armed,
wearing a garland of flowers, gentle, and adorned with every ornament.

children.text: uttare cātmanaḥ puṇyāṃ bhāryāṃ ca marutāṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: To the north he should also worship his own meritorious wife, the auspicious wife of the <s>Maruts</s>,
<s>Suyaśā</s>, well-vowed <s>Ambā</s>, intent on adorning the feet.
Having worshipped in this way, he should enter the inner shrine of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
With devotion he should offer a handful of flowers to the five heads with the five mantras.
After worshipping <s>Śaṅkara</s> with perfumes, flowers, and various incenses,

children.text: skandaṃ vināyakaṃ devīṃ liṅgaśuddhiṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Vināyaka</s>, and the Goddess, he should perform the purification of the liṅga.
Having recited all the mantras, beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ,
he should then fashion the seat called the lotus with the praṇava.
Its eastern petal is directly the imperishable one consisting of <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness),

children.text: laghimā dakṣiṇaṃ caiva mahimā paścimaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the southern is <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), and the western is <s>mahimā</s> (greatness).
The northern petal is <s>prāpti</s> (attainment), and the petal of the fire quarter is <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will).
The southwestern petal is <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), and <s>vaśitva</s> (mastery) is in the region of wind.
<s>Sarvajñatva</s> (omniscience) is in the northeast, and the pericarp is said to be the moon.
Below the moon is the sun, and below that is fire itself.
In the intermediate directions he should arrange <s>dharma</s> and the others, and then <s>Ananta</s> in due order.
In the four directions beginning with the unmanifest, at the end of the moon, he should arrange the three qualities.
Above that are the three selves, and beyond that is the pedestal of <s>Śiva</s>.
Invoking <s>Parameśvara</s> with the formula beginning 'I take refuge in <s>Sadyojāta</s>,'
he should establish him upon the seat with the <s>Vāmadeva</s> mantra.
With the <s>Rudragāyatrī</s> he should bring about presence, and with <s>Aghora</s> he should confine it.
He should worship him with the mantra '<s>Īśāna</s> is lord of all vidyās.'
He should offer water for the feet, water for sipping, and arghya to the Lord.
He should bathe <s>Rudra</s> according to rule with fragrant sandalwood water.
Taking the pañcagavya according to rule in a vessel, and consecrating it with mantra,
he should bathe him properly with the cow-products, using the praṇava alone.

children.text: ājyena madhunā caiva tathā cekṣurasena ca ||
children.translated_text: With ghee, honey, and likewise with sugarcane juice,
he should anoint <s>Mahādeva</s> with holy substances, using the praṇava.
Then, with pure water-jars, he should pour out water accompanied by mantras.
Having performed the purification in the proper manner, the sādhaka should use a white cloth.
With kuśa, apāmārga, camphor, jāti flowers, and campaka blossoms,
with white oleanders, and also with jasmine, lotuses, and blue lotuses,

children.text: āpūrya puṣpaiḥ suśubhaiḥ candanādyaiś ca tajjalam ||
children.translated_text: having filled that water with very auspicious flowers and with sandalwood and the like,
he should place the mantras beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s> into that water.
Then with a golden pitcher, or likewise with a silver one,
with a copper vessel, a lotus leaf, or a palāśa leaf,
with a conch, or with a purified and auspicious earthen vessel,
together with a bunch of darbha and flowers, he should bathe him, preceded by mantra.
I shall tell you those mantras; listen, for the accomplishment of all aims.
By them, after bathing the liṅga in this way even once, a human being is freed.
Those who know mantras should bathe him with the <s>Pavamāna</s> and likewise with the <s>Vāmīya</s>,
with the <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Nīlarudra</s>, and the auspicious <s>Śrīsūkta</s>,
with the <s>Rajanīsūkta</s> and with the auspicious <s>Camaka</s>,
with the <s>Hotṛ</s> hymn, with the auspicious <s>Atharvaśiras</s>,

children.text: śāntyā cātha punaḥ śāntyā bhāruṇḍenāruṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: with the <s>Śānti</s>, again with the <s>Śānti</s>, with the <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s> and the <s>Aruṇa</s>,

children.text: vāruṇena ca jyeṣṭhena tathā vedavratena ca
children.translated_text: with the <s>Vāruṇa</s>, with the <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, and likewise with the <s>Vedavrata</s>,
and with the sacred intermediate hymn and the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>.
With the swift <s>Rudra</s>, with the <s>Kapi</s>, and with the <s>Kapardin</s>,
with the Sāman beginning '<s>ā vo rājā</s>,' with the <s>Bṛhaccandra</s>, and with the <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
with the <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, with the <s>Skanda</s>, and with a hundred auspicious Ṛg-verses,
with the five <s>Brahman</s> mantras, with the sūtra, and with the praṇava alone,
he should bathe the Lord of the gods, for the pacification of all sins.
He should then give cloth, the sacred thread of <s>Śiva</s>, and likewise water for sipping,

children.text: gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā dhūpaṃ dīpamannaṃ krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: perfume, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food in sequence,
fragrant water, and again water for sipping.

children.text: mukuṭaṃ ca śubhaṃ channaṃ tathā vai bhūṣaṇāni ca
children.translated_text: He should give a fine crown, a covering, and likewise ornaments,
and mouth-perfumes and the other offerings, with the praṇava alone.
Then he should worship upon the head of the liṅga, with the praṇava mantra,
the God who resembles crystal, without parts, imperishable, the cause of all the gods,
supreme, consisting of all worlds, inaccessible to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the other sages and gods;
for the śruti says that he is inaccessible even to knowers of the Veda and to the Vedāntas.
Without beginning, middle, or end, the medicine for those afflicted by the disease of becoming,
known as <s>Śivatattva</s>, he is established in the Śiva liṅga.
With the praṇava mantra alone he should worship at the head of the liṅga.
He should recite a hymn according to rule, bow, and circumambulate.

children.text: arghyaṃ dattvātha puṣpāṇi pādayostu vikīrya ca
children.translated_text: Having given arghya and scattered flowers at the feet,
he should prostrate to the Lord of gods and install <s>Śiva</s> within himself.
Thus the unsurpassed worship of the liṅga has been briefly stated.
Now I shall teach you here the internal worship of the liṅga.
Thus in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the twenty-seventh chapter, named 'The Procedure for Worship of the Liṅga,' is concluded.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: āgneyaṃ sauramamṛtaṃ bimbaṃ bhāvyaṃ tata upari
children.translated_text: Above that one should contemplate the fiery, solar, immortal orb,

children.text: guṇatrayaṃ ca hṛdaye tathā cātmatrayaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: and in the heart the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and likewise the three selves in sequence.
Above it, by the science of meditation, one should worship <s>Mahādeva</s>, partless and yet possessing every form,
and having a body in which his beloved occupies one half.

children.text: tato bahuvidhaṃ proktaṃ cintyaṃ tatrāsti cedyataḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the object of thought is taught there as manifold, if such an object exists,
for only then does the thinker's thought make sense; otherwise it does not.
Therefore the sacrificer should remember the object of meditation, the meditation, and the purpose,
for otherwise this is never understood by a person.

children.text: pure śete puraṃ dehaṃ tasmātpuruṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: He lies in the city; the city is the body. Therefore he is called <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: yājyaṃ yajñena yajate yajamānastu sa smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And he is remembered as the sacrificer, because he worships what is to be sacrificed by sacrifice.

children.text: dhyeyo maheśvaro dhyānaṃ cintanaṃ nirvṛtiḥ phalam
children.translated_text: The object of meditation is <s>Maheśvara</s>; meditation is reflection; liberation is the fruit.
He attains, just as it truly is, the lord of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: iha ṣaḍviṃśako dhyeyo dhyātā vai pañcaviṃśakaḥ
children.translated_text: Here the twenty-sixth is to be meditated upon, while the meditator is indeed the twenty-fifth.
The unmanifest is the twenty-fourth, and the seven beginning with <s>mahat</s> are as follows:

children.text: mahāṃs tathā tvahaṅkāraṃ tanmātraṃ pañcakaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mahat</s>, likewise <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (egoity), and again the set of five subtle elements,
the five organs of action, and likewise the organs of cognition,

children.text: manaś ca pañca bhūtāni śivaḥ ṣaḍviṃśakastataḥ
children.translated_text: the mind and the five elements; after these, <s>Śiva</s> is the twenty-sixth.

children.text: sa eva bhartā kartā ca vidherapi maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He alone is the sustainer and maker, <s>Maheśvara</s> even of <s>Vidhi</s>.
That <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, brought forth <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.

children.text: viśvādhikaś ca viśvātmā viśvarūpa iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is remembered as beyond the universe, the soul of the universe, and universal in form.

children.text: vinā yathā hi pitaraṃ mātaraṃ tanayāstviha
children.translated_text: Just as sons here are not born without father and mother,

children.text: na jāyante tathā somaṃ vinā nāsti jagattrayam ||
children.translated_text: so without <s>Soma</s> the three worlds do not exist.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
If <s>Mahādeva</s>, the supreme self, <s>Maheśvara</s>, is the maker,
and likewise the one who causes the small self to act as it acts,

children.text: nityo viśuddho buddhaś ca niṣkalaḥ parameśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: and if <s>Parameśvara</s> is eternal, pure, awakened, and partless,

children.text: tvayokto muktidaḥ kiṃ vā niṣkalaścetkaroti kim ||
children.translated_text: and has been called by you the giver of liberation, then, if he is partless, what does he do?
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: kālaḥ karoti sakalaṃ kālaṃ kalayate sadā
children.translated_text: Time makes everything, and it continually measures time.

children.text: niṣkalaṃ ca manaḥ sarvaṃ manyate so'pi niṣkalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The mind also conceives everything as partless; that too is partless.
By his action this whole world is established here.
What need is there to say more? This world is the eightfold form of the God of gods.

children.text: vinākāśaṃ jagannaiva vinā kṣmāṃ vāyunā vinā
children.translated_text: The world does not exist without space, nor without earth, nor without wind,

children.text: tejasā vāriṇā caiva yajamānaṃ tathā vinā ||
children.translated_text: nor without fire and water, nor likewise without the sacrificer.
The world exists with the sun and moon; these are the bodies of that Lord.
When considered, this moving and unmoving world is the gross form of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ vadanti ṛṣayo yanna vācyaṃ dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: The seers call subtle that which cannot be spoken, O best of twice-born men,

children.text: yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha ||
children.translated_text: from which words turn back, not reaching it, together with the mind.
The one who knows the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> does not fear anything at all.
So too, having known the bliss of <s>Pinākin</s>, there is nothing to fear.

children.text: vibhūtayaś ca rudrasya matvā sarvatra bhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: Considering the manifestations of <s>Rudra</s> everywhere in reality,
the sages who see the truth say, 'All is <s>Rudra</s>.'
Through constant reverential salutation to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,

children.text: sarvaṃ tu khalvidaṃ brahma sarvo vai rudra īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: all this indeed is <s>Brahman</s>; all is truly <s>Rudra</s>, the Lord.

children.text: puruṣo vai mahādevo maheśānaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>puruṣa</s> is truly <s>Mahādeva</s>, the great Lord, the supreme <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus the all-pervading one has been described; meditation is reflection upon that very one.
Having considered and seen by means of the fourfold method, O good-vowed one,
one sees the cause of saṃsāra, saṃsāra itself, the cause of liberation, and release.
This fourfold arrangement has been explained here for the reflecting yogin.
Thought is known as manifold, but in <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> it is one.

children.text: suniṣṭhetyatra kathitā rudraṃ raudrī na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Here it is taught as firm devotion; thought of <s>Rudra</s> is <s>Raudrī</s>, without doubt.

children.text: aindrī cendre tathā saumyā some nārāyaṇe tathā ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>Aindrī</s> in <s>Indra</s>, and likewise <s>Saumyā</s> in <s>Soma</s> and in <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: sūrye vahnau ca sarveṣāṃ sarvatraivaṃ vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: In the sun, in fire, and in all beings, everywhere, when considered in this way,
one should establish it twofold in disposition, as 'that is I' and 'I am he.'

children.text: bhakto'sau nāsti yastasmāccintā brāhmī na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no devotee who is separate from him; therefore the thought is <s>Brāhmī</s>, without doubt.

children.text: evaṃ brahmamayaṃ dhyāyet pūrvaṃ vipra carācaram ||
children.translated_text: Thus, O brahmin, one should first meditate on the moving and unmoving world as made of <s>Brahman</s>.
Remembering what is desired, one should abandon the division between moving and unmoving.

children.text: tyājyaṃ grāhyam alabhyaṃ ca kṛtyaṃ cākṛtyameva ca ||
children.translated_text: For one who is fully satisfied, there is nothing to be abandoned or accepted, nothing unattainable, nothing to be done or not done.

children.text: yasya nāsti sutṛptasya tasya brāhmī na cānyathā
children.translated_text: For such a one the thought is <s>Brāhmī</s>, and not otherwise.
Thus internal worship has been described in sequence.
The internal worshippers are to be honored with salutations and the like.
Even if they are misshapen or deformed, proclaimers of <s>Brahman</s> are not to be blamed.
All internal worshippers should not be examined critically by one who understands.
Those of small mind who revile them will become afflicted with suffering.

children.text: yathā dāruvane rudraṃ vinindya munayaḥ purā
children.translated_text: It is as when the sages of old reviled <s>Rudra</s> in <s>Dāruvana</s>.
Therefore knowers of <s>Brahman</s> should always be served and saluted,
even when they are freed from the orders and stages of life, by those devoted to the orders and stages of life.
Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the twenty-eighth chapter, named 'The Description of the Principles and Enumeration of Śiva Worship,' is concluded.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now, O mighty one, I wish to hear what once took place in <s>Dāruvana</s>
among the forest-dwellers whose selves had been purified by austerity.
How did the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s> come to <s>Dāruvana</s>,
assuming a distorted form, with seed drawn upward, naked and clothed in the quarters?

children.text: kiṃ pravṛttaṃ vane tasmin rudrasya paramātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: What took place in that forest concerning <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme self?
You should tell truthfully the deed of the God of gods.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard that statement of his, the blessed son of <s>Śilāda</s>, best of those who know the essence of the <s>Śruti</s>,
spoke a little about <s>Bhava</s>, smiling.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
In the dense Dāru forest the sages performed very severe austerity,
for the satisfaction of the God of gods, together with their wives, sons, and sacred fires.
<s>Rudra</s>, lord of the world, perceptive, bull-bannered, was pleased,
<s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, the supreme Lord, the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s>.
In order to know the knowledge characterized by engagement among the dwellers in Dāruvana,

children.text: parīkṣārthaṃ jagannāthaḥ śraddhayā krīḍayā ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for the sake of testing them, the Lord of the world did this with faith and playfulness.
And <s>Śaṅkara</s>, in order to establish knowledge characterized by withdrawal,
among those dwelling in the devadāru forest, whose minds were fixed on knowledge of engagement,
assumed a distorted form: clothed in the directions, with uneven eyes,

children.text: mugdho dvihastaḥ kṛṣṇāṅgo divyaṃ dāruvanaṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: bewildering, two-armed, dark-limbed, he went to the divine Dāruvana.
The blessed one made a gentle smile, born from desire in the minds of the women,

children.text: bhrūvilāsaṃ ca gānaṃ ca cakārātīva suṃdaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and movements of the brows and song, being exceedingly beautiful.
Repeatedly glancing at the crowd of women, the destroyer of <s>Anaṅga</s>,
with an exceedingly sweet appearance, greatly increased their passion.

children.text: vane taṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṛtaṃ nīlalohitam
children.translated_text: Seeing that man in the forest, distorted and blue-red,
even the faithful wives followed him alone with eagerness.
And the women who were at the doors of the forest huts, their garments and ornaments loosened, unsteady,

children.text: labdhvā smitaṃ tasya mukhāravindād drumālayasthās tam athānvayustāḥ ||
children.translated_text: having received a smile from his lotus-face, followed him then, though they had been in the tree-dwellings.
Some women, seeing <s>Bhava</s>, their eyes rolling with intoxication,
though outside the bounds of decorum, made movements of the brows.
Then other women, seeing him, their faces slightly smiling,
their garments somewhat slipped and their girdle-strings loosened, sang.

children.text: kāścittadā taṃ vipine tu dṛṣṭvā viprāṅganāḥ srastanavāṃśukaṃ vā
children.translated_text: At that time, some brahmin women, seeing him in the forest with his fresh garment fallen away,

children.text: svānsvānvicitrān valayānpravidhya madānvitā bandhujanāṃś ca jagmuḥ ||
children.translated_text: put on their own various bracelets and, filled with passion, went to their kinsmen.

children.text: kācittadā taṃ na viveda dṛṣṭvā vivāsanā srastamahāṃśukā ca
children.translated_text: At that time one woman, seeing him, did not know herself; naked, with her great garment fallen away,
and others, filled with passion, went to their kinsmen among the famous branches and variegated boughs.
Some sang to him, danced, and fell on the ground,
while others sat down like elephants; the foremost twice-born men spoke.
Looking at one another with smiles, they embraced one another on every side;
blocking <s>Rudra</s>'s path, they displayed their arts.
Some said to him, 'Who are you?' and others, 'Please sit down.'
Then, 'Where are you going?' and 'Be gracious,' they chattered with delighted minds.
Inverted, they fell down, their garments and hair disheveled,
faithful wives in the very presence of their husbands, through <s>Bhava</s>'s māyā.
Seeing and hearing those actions and words of theirs, the imperishable <s>Bhava</s>,
the supreme Lord, said nothing, whether good or bad.
Seeing the company of women in that state, and <s>Śaṅkara</s> as he was,
the lordly sages spoke extremely harsh words.
All their austerities recoiled against <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
as stars stationed in the sky do before the light of the sun.
It is heard that through the curse of a seer, the sacrifice, the source of prosperity and welfare
for great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>, came to destruction.

children.text: bhṛgor api ca śāpena viṣṇuḥ paramavīryavān
children.translated_text: And by the curse of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of supreme valor,

children.text: prādurbhāvāndaśa prāpto duḥkhitaś ca sadā kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtained ten manifestations and was made ever afflicted.

children.text: indrasyāpi ca dharmajña chinnaṃ savṛṣaṇaṃ purā
children.translated_text: And, O knower of dharma, formerly the testicles of <s>Indra</s>, together with the scrotum, were cut off
and cast down on earth by the angry sage <s>Gautama</s>.

children.text: garbhavāso vasūnāṃ ca śāpena vihitas tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise dwelling in the womb was ordained for the <s>Vasus</s> by a curse,

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva śāpena nahuṣaḥ sarpatāṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and by the curse of seers <s>Nahuṣa</s> went to serpenthood.

children.text: kṣīrodaś ca samudro 'sau nivāsaḥ sarvadā hareḥ
children.translated_text: And that ocean of milk, the perpetual abode of <s>Hari</s>,
the second reservoir of nectar, was made undrinkable for brahmins.
Having reached <s>Avimukteśvara</s> in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>,
having bathed <s>Īśa</s>, the God of gods, <s>Tryambaka</s>, with milk,
being endowed with supreme faith, with the nectar of bodily contact,
with milk poured out, the god <s>Madhusūdana</s> himself,
after sprinkling him, the blessed Lord, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and the sages,
made the ocean of milk as before, and his own abode, the Lord.
And <s>Dharma</s> too was likewise cursed by the great-souled <s>Māṇḍavya</s>,
and the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and by great-souled ones beginning with <s>Durvāsas</s>.
<s>Rāghava</s>, together with his younger brother, was also cursed by the great-souled <s>Durvāsas</s>,
and the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> arose from the fall of that wise sage's foot.

children.text: ete cānye ca bahavo viprāṇāṃ vaśamāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: These and many others came under the power of brahmins,
except for the three-eyed God of gods, <s>Umāpati</s>.
Thus deluded by him, they did not recognize <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
They spoke exceedingly fierce words, and he too, fierce though he was, disappeared.
Then they too, from that Dāruvana, in the morning, with agitated minds,
went to the great-souled Grandfather seated on the highest seat.
Having gone, they reported the whole event concerning the Lord,
the sages of diminished minds, in that auspicious Dāruvana.
Then the Grandfather himself, after reflecting in his mind for a moment
on that whole event of theirs formerly in the holy Dāruvana,
rose, stood with joined palms, and bowed down to <s>Bhava</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> then quickly spoke to the eminent sages dwelling in Dāruvana:
'Shame on you, destined for ruin, for the unsurpassed great treasure
has been made vain by you, O brahmins bereft of fortune.
But he who in that Dāruvana was seen as a liṅgin (one bearing the sign) by those without a liṅga...
He alone, <s>Parameśvara</s>, has been seen by you in a deformed appearance.

children.text: gṛhasthaiś ca na nindyāstu sadā hyatithayo dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: And guests, especially twice-born men, should never be censured by householders,
whether they are ugly or handsome, dirty, or even unlearned.
In ancient times even <s>Kālamṛtyu</s> himself
was conquered on earth by the excellent twice-born sage <s>Sudarśana</s> through worship of a guest.

children.text: anyathā nāsti saṃtartuṃ gṛhasthaiś ca dvijottamaiḥ
children.translated_text: For excellent twice-born householders have no other means of crossing over,
if they abandon that worship of guests, the purification of oneself on earth.

children.text: gṛhastho 'pi purā jetuṃ sudarśana iti śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: In ancient times a householder named <s>Sudarśana</s>, it is heard,
made a vow in order to conquer, and spoke to his devoted wife:

children.text: suvrate subhru subhage śṛṇu sarvaṃ prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: "Good-vowed, fair-browed, fortunate lady, listen to everything with attention.

children.text: tvayā vai nāvamantavyā gṛhe hyatithayaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Guests in the house must never be slighted by you, at any time.
Every guest is himself, directly and visibly, the bearer of the bow <s>Pināka</s>.
Therefore, having given even yourself to a guest, worship him."
After he had spoken thus, his devoted wife was distressed and helpless,

children.text: patimāha rudantī ca kimuktaṃ bhavatā prabho ||
children.translated_text: and weeping she said to her husband, "What have you said, lord?"
Hearing that speech of hers, <s>Sudarśana</s> again said:

children.text: deyaṃ sarvaṃ śivāyārye śiva evātithiḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: "Everything must be given to <s>Śiva</s>, noble lady; the guest himself is <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore all are to be worshipped; all guests are always to be honored."

children.text: evamuktā tadā bhartrā bhāryā tasya pativratā ||
children.translated_text: Thus instructed at that time by her husband, his devoted wife
accepted the remaining command upon her head, as it were, and then acted accordingly.

children.text: parīkṣituṃ tathā śraddhāṃ tayoḥ sākṣād dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, O best of twice-born men, in order to test the faith of those two directly,
<s>Dharma</s> himself, becoming an excellent twice-born man, went to the sage's house.
Seeing him, the faultless woman honored the twice-born man with arghya and the other offerings.

children.text: sampūjitastayā tāṃ tu prāha dharmo dvijaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: After he had been fully honored by her, <s>Dharma</s>, himself in the form of a twice-born man, said to her:
"Good lady, where is your wise husband, your lord <s>Sudarśana</s>?
Food and the like are enough for me today, noble lady; you ought to give your own self here."

children.text: sā ca lajjāvṛtā nārī smarantī kathitaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: That woman, covered with shame, remembering what had formerly been said
by her husband, closed her eyes and trembled, devoted to her husband as she was.

children.text: kiṃcetyāha punastaṃ vai dharme cakre ca sā matim ||
children.translated_text: When he again said to her, "What then?" she fixed her mind on <s>Dharma</s>,
to offer herself to him here by her husband's command.
Meanwhile the husband of that woman, <s>Sudarśana</s>,
the wise great sage, came to the door of the house and called out to her.

children.text: ehyehi kva gatā bhadre tamuvācātithiḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: "Come, come! Where have you gone, good lady?" The guest himself said to him:
"With this wife of yours I am now engaged in sexual union.
Greatly fortunate <s>Sudarśana</s>, say what should be done here."
"When the love-making is ended, O best of Brahmins, I shall be satisfied, O excellent twice-born man."
Then <s>Sudarśana</s>, very delighted, said, O best of twice-born men:
"Enjoy her according to your desire, and I shall go, O excellent twice-born man."
Then the delighted king <s>Dharma</s> himself revealed his own true form.

children.text: pradadau cepsitaṃ sarvaṃ tamāha ca mahādyutiḥ
children.translated_text: He granted everything desired and, blazing with great radiance, said to him:

children.text: eṣā na bhuktā viprendra manasāpi suśobhanā ||
children.translated_text: "O best of Brahmins, this beautiful woman has not been enjoyed, even in thought,

children.text: mayā caiṣā na saṃdehaḥ śraddhāṃ jñātumihāgataḥ
children.translated_text: by me; there is no doubt of this. I came here to know your faith.
Death has indeed been conquered by you, good-vowed one, through <s>dharma</s> alone.

children.text: aho'sya tapaso vīryamityuktvā prayayau ca saḥ
children.translated_text: Ah, the power of this austerity!" Having spoken thus, he departed.
Therefore all guests are always to be worshipped in that same way.
What more need be said at length here? O excellent twice-born men, though bereft of fortune,
you should quickly go for refuge to that very <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Hearing that speech of <s>Brahmā</s>, the foremost Brahmins,
distressed and with troubled eyes, bowed to <s>Brahmā</s> and said:
The Brahmins said:
"Greatly fortunate one, life is no longer desired by us who have become disfigured.
We have seen <s>Mahādeva</s>, and the blameless one was censured by us.

children.text: śaptaś ca sarvagaḥ śūlī pinākī nīlalohitaḥ
children.translated_text: The all-pervading wielder of the spear, bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, dark-red lord, was cursed by us.
Because of ignorance, the power born from the curse was blunted by the sight of his face.

children.text: vaktumarhasi deveśa saṃnyāsaṃ vai krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: Lord of gods, you should state to us in proper order the path of renunciation,
so that we may see the fierce and terrible lord of the gods, the matted-haired one."
The Grandfather said:

children.text: ādau vedānadhītyaiva śraddhayā ca guroḥ sadā
children.translated_text: "First, having studied the Vedas with faith and constant obedience to the teacher,
having considered their meaning and vowed to follow the duties of a sage, O best of twice-born men,
the learned man should do so either until the end of the course of study or for twelve years.
Having bathed at graduation, taken a wife, and begotten good-vowed sons,
the sage should apportion those sons with occupations suitable to them.
Having worshipped the mighty Lord of sacrifice, the supreme Self,
with sacrifices such as the Agniṣṭoma, he should reach the forest and worship him in the fire.
There the sage, for twelve years, or even for only one year,
or for twelve fortnights, or for just twelve days,
living on milk, disciplined and peaceful, should worship all the gods.
Having sacrificed in this way, he should ritually cast the sacrificial vessels into the fire with mantras.

children.text: apsu vai pārthivaṃ nyasya gurave taijasāni tu ||
children.translated_text: He should place the earthen ones in the waters, and the fiery ones with the teacher.
He should give all his own wealth to Brahmins without hesitation.
Bowing down to the teacher on the ground, dispassionate, the ascetic should renounce.

children.text: nikṛtya keśān saśikhān upavītaṃ visṛjya ca
children.translated_text: Cutting off the hair together with the topknot, and casting away the sacred thread,

children.text: pañcabhir juhuyād apsu bhūḥ svāheti vicakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise man should offer into the waters with the five formulas, beginning, 'bhūḥ svāhā.'
Thereafter the ascetic should live in this way for liberation through <s>Śiva</s>,
whether by a vow, by fasting, or again by living on water,
or by living on leaves, by living on milk, or by living on fruits.

children.text: evaṃ jīvanmṛto no cet ṣaṇmāsādvatsarāttu vā ||
children.translated_text: Living thus, if he does not become as one dead while still alive, then after six months or after a year...
If an ascetic undertakes the bodily hardship of setting out and the like,
he attains <s>śivasāyujya</s> (union with Śiva), even by action when acting in this way.
Endowed with devotion and firm in his vows, he obtains liberation at once.

children.text: tyāgena vā kiṃ vidhināpyanena bhaktasya rudrasya śubhairvrataiśca
children.translated_text: For the devotee of <s>Rudra</s>, what need is there of renunciation, or of this rule, or of auspicious vows,

children.text: yajñaiś ca dānairvividhaiś ca homairlabdhaiścaśāstrairvividhaiś ca vedaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: or of sacrifices, gifts of various kinds, oblations, acquired scriptures of many sorts, and the Vedas?
Thus Death was conquered by the great-souled <s>Śveta</s> through devotion to <s>Bhava</s>.
May you have devotion to <s>Mahādeva</s>, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme Self.
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
When they had thus been addressed by <s>Brahmā</s>, O excellent brahmin seers,

children.text: śvetasya ca kathāṃ puṇyām apṛcchan paramarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the supreme sages asked about the holy story of <s>Śveta</s>.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:
There was a glorious sage named <s>Śveta</s>, whose lifespan had run out, in a mountain cave.

children.text: sakto hyabhyarcya yadbhaktyā tuṣṭāva ca maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: Intent upon worship, he worshiped with devotion and praised <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He did so with the holy <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, O twice-born ones, beginning with the words 'namas te.'
Then <s>Kāla</s>, of great splendor, considered the best of twice-born men whose time had come,
and, intending to take him away, O eminent brahmins, came into the sage's presence.

children.text: śveto'pi dṛṣṭvā taṃ kālaṃ kālaprāpto'pi śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: But <s>Śveta</s>, seeing that <s>Kāla</s>, although his own time had come, worshiped <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the holy-minded one remembering <s>Tryambaka</s>.
Thus he worshiped <s>Tryambaka</s>, fragrant and increasing nourishment.
What will Death do to me, since I am the death of Death?

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā sasmitaṃ prāha śvetaṃ lokabhayaṃkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the terror of the worlds said to <s>Śveta</s> with a smile:

children.text: ehyehi śveta cānena vidhinā kiṃ phalaṃ tava
children.translated_text: 'Come, come, <s>Śveta</s>. What fruit will this rite have for you?

children.text: rudro vā bhagavān viṣṇurbrahmā vā jagadīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether it is <s>Rudra</s>, blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the world,

children.text: kaḥ samarthaḥ paritrātuṃ mayā grastaṃ dvijottama
children.translated_text: who is able to rescue, O best of twice-born men, one who has been seized by me?

children.text: anena mama kiṃ vipra raudreṇa vidhinā prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: What use to me, O brahmin, is this fierce rite of the Lord,
when I have risen to take him to <s>Yama</s>'s world in a moment?
Since your lifespan is exhausted, O sage, I am therefore intent on taking you away from here.'
Having heard that terrifying speech, mingled with the law of death,

children.text: hā rudra rudra rudreti lalāpa munipuṅgavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the foremost of sages cried out, 'Ah, <s>Rudra</s>! <s>Rudra</s>! <s>Rudra</s>!'

children.text: taṃ prāha ca mahādevaṃ kālaṃ samprekṣya vai dṛśā
children.translated_text: Looking at <s>Kāla</s> with his eyes, he addressed <s>Mahādeva</s>,
his eye filled with tears, bewildered and greatly distressed.
<s>Śveta</s> said:

children.text: tvayā kiṃ kāla no nāthaścāsti ceddhi vṛṣadhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: What can you do, <s>Kāla</s>? We have a lord, since the bull-bannered one exists.
In this liṅga is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the source of all gods and beings.
For great souls like me, who are deeply devoted to <s>Bhava</s>,

children.text: vidhinā kiṃ mahābāho gaccha gaccha yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: what need is there of ritual procedure, O mighty-armed one? Go, go back as you came.
Then, hearing this, he became angry, sharp-fanged and terrifying.
Having heard that speech of <s>Śveta</s>, he stood fearsome, with noose in hand.
With a great lion-roar, and striking his arms again and again,

children.text: babandha ca muniṃ kālaḥ kālaprāptaṃ tamāha ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāla</s> bound the sage whose time had come and said to him:

children.text: mayā baddho'si viprarṣe śvetaṃ netuṃ yamālayam
children.translated_text: 'You are bound by me, O brahmin seer; I shall take <s>Śveta</s> to <s>Yama</s>'s abode.

children.text: adya vai devadevena tava rudreṇa kiṃ kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: What has your <s>Rudra</s>, the God of gods, done today?

children.text: kva śarvastava bhaktiś ca kva pūjā pūjayā phalam
children.translated_text: Where is your <s>Śarva</s>, where is your devotion, where is worship, and where is the fruit of worship?

children.text: kva cāhaṃ kva ca me bhītiḥ śveta baddho'si vai mayā ||
children.translated_text: Where am I, and where is fear of me? O <s>Śveta</s>, you are bound by me.

children.text: liṅge'smin saṃsthitaḥ śveta tava rudro maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Your <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, is established in this liṅga, O <s>Śveta</s>.
That <s>Mahādeva</s> is motionless. How is he to be worshiped as <s>Maheśvara</s>?'
Then <s>Sadāśiva</s> himself came to slay the one who had come to kill the twice-born man,
<s>Hara</s>, enemy of <s>Smara</s> and destroyer of the sacrifice, smiling as he came to kill <s>Antaka</s>.

children.text: tvaran vinirgataḥ paraḥ śivaḥ svayaṃ trilocanaḥ
children.translated_text: Hastening, the supreme <s>Śiva</s> himself, the three-eyed one, came forth,
<s>Tryambaka</s>, together with <s>Ambā</s>, with <s>Nandin</s>, and with the lords of the gaṇas.

children.text: sasarja jīvitaṃ kṣaṇād bhavaṃ nirīkṣya vai bhayāt
children.translated_text: In a moment, seeing <s>Bhava</s>, the mighty one lost his life through fear,

children.text: papāta cāśu vai balī munestu saṃnidhau dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and quickly fell near the sage, O twice-born ones.
He cried aloud upward, gazing upon the destroyer of <s>Antaka</s>,
upon <s>Antaka</s> slain by the glance of <s>Bhava</s>, O foremost brahmins.
The lords and the rulers of the gods shouted loudly to <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The delighted lordly sages bowed to <s>Ambikā</s>, to <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: sasarjur asya mūrdhni vai munerbhavasya khecarāḥ
children.translated_text: The sky-goers poured down upon the head of that sage of <s>Bhava</s>
a beautiful, very cool, excellent rain of flowers from the sky.

children.text: aho nirīkṣya cāntakaṃ mṛtaṃ tadā suvismitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, greatly astonished on seeing <s>Antaka</s> dead,
the son of <s>Śilāda</s> bowed to the imperishable <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: uvāca bāladhīrmṛtaḥ prasīda ceti vai muneḥ
children.translated_text: and said, with simple understanding, 'Be gracious indeed to the dead one, to the sage.'
The lord of the gaṇas, the attendant of <s>Maheśvara</s>, addressed <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Then the blessed Lord, having favored the best of twice-born men, entered back in.
In a moment he had seen <s>Antaka</s> destroyed, his body hidden away.
Therefore, O twice-born ones, worship with devotion <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the conqueror of death,
the giver of liberation and of worldly enjoyment to all.

children.text: bahunā kiṃ pralāpena saṃnyasyābhyarcya vai bhavam
children.translated_text: What is the use of much talk? Renouncing, and worshiping <s>Bhava</s>,

children.text: bhaktyā cāparayā tasmin viśokā vai bhaviṣyatha ||
children.translated_text: with unsurpassed devotion toward him, you will become free from sorrow.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
When they had thus been addressed by <s>Brahmā</s>, the speakers on Brahman
said, 'Be gracious. May devotion arise toward <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Pinākin</s>, the lord of gods.

children.text: kena vā tapasā deva yajñenāpyatha kena vā
children.translated_text: By what austerity, O god, or by what sacrifice,
or by what vows will the twice-born become devotees of the Blessed Lord?'
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:

children.text: na dānena muniśreṣṭhāstapasā ca na vidyayā
children.translated_text: Not by giving, O best of sages, nor by austerity, nor by learning,

children.text: yajñair homair vratair vedair yogaśāstrair nirodhanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor by sacrifices, oblations, vows, Vedas, yoga treatises, or restraints.

children.text: prasāde naiva sā bhaktiḥ śive paramakāraṇe
children.translated_text: There is no such devotion through favor alone toward <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause.

children.text: atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve te paramarṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having heard his words, all those supreme seers
together with their wives and sons, exhausted, bowed down to <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
Therefore <s>Pāśupatī bhakti</s> (devotion to <s>Paśupati</s>) grants the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
It also gives victory to the sage and grants the conquest of every death.
In ancient times <s>Dadhīca</s>, through devotion, conquered mighty <s>Hari</s> together with the immortals.

children.text: kṣayaṃ jaghāna pādena vajrāsthitvaṃ ca labdhavān
children.translated_text: He struck down destruction with his foot and obtained the state of having bones like the thunderbolt.
I too conquered death by praising <s>Mahādeva</s>.
And by the excellent sage <s>Śveta</s>, who had entered the mouth of Death,
death was conquered by the favor of <s>Mahādeva</s>, just as it was by me.
Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirtieth chapter is concluded.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
How, by the favor of <s>Bhava</s>, did the dwellers in the <s>Devadāru</s> forest

children.text: prapannāḥ śaraṇaṃ devaṃ vaktumarhasi me prabho ||
children.translated_text: take refuge in the god? You should tell me, O lord.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
The blessed self-born lord himself addressed those greatly fortunate ones,
who were dwelling in the <s>Devadāru</s> forest, blazing with austerity like fire.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:
This god is to be understood as <s>Mahādeva</s>, as <s>Maheśvara</s>.
No higher state than him is attained.

children.text: devānāṃ ca ṛṣīnāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ caiva sa prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: He is the lord of the gods, the seers, and the ancestors.
At the end of a thousand yugas, at the dissolution, all embodied beings
this blessed <s>Maheśvara</s> destroys, having become Time.

children.text: eṣa caiva prajāḥ sarvāḥ sṛjatyekaḥ svatejasā ||
children.translated_text: And he alone creates all creatures by his own splendor.

children.text: eṣa cakrī ca vajrī ca śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the wielder of the discus, the wielder of the thunderbolt, marked with the sign of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.

children.text: yogī kṛtayuge caiva tretāyāṃ kratur ucyate ||
children.translated_text: In the Kṛta age he is called the yogin, and in the Tretā age the sacrifice.

children.text: dvāpare caiva kālāgnir dharmaketuḥ kalau smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the Dvāpara age he is the fire of time, and in the Kali age he is remembered as <s>Dharmaketu</s>.
These are the forms of <s>Rudra</s>, on which the learned meditate.
Square outside and inside, and octagonal where it rests on the pedestal,
round and beautiful to look at: thus one should worship a proper <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: tamo hyagnī rajo brahmā sattvaṃ viṣṇuḥ prakāśakam
children.translated_text: Darkness is fire; passion is <s>Brahmā</s>; lucidity is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the illuminator.
One form of his stands there, while many forms are proclaimed.

children.text: yatra tiṣṭhati tadbrahma yogena tu samanvitam
children.translated_text: Where that <s>Brahman</s> stands, it is joined with yoga.
Therefore the best of brahmins worship the imperishable lord, <s>Īśāna</s>, the lord of the gods of gods,
having conquered anger and conquered their senses.
Having made a <s>liṅga</s> according to rule, endowed with all its marks,
of the measure of a thumb, very auspicious, well rounded, approved by all,
with an even navel, and either octagonal or sixteen-sided,
a well-rounded, divine disk, granting the fruit of every desire,

children.text: vedikā dviguṇā tasya samā vā sarvasaṃmatā ||
children.translated_text: its altar should be twice as large, or equal to it, as all approve.
A <s>gomukhī</s> spout, one third of the altar, should be furnished with the proper marks,
and there should be a border all around, O best of twice-born men, of the measure of a barley-grain.

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ śailaṃ kṛtvā tāmramayaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Making it of gold, silver, stone, or likewise copper,

children.text: vedikāyāś ca vistāraṃ triguṇaṃ vai samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: one should make the extent of the altar three times as large on every side.

children.text: vartulaṃ caturasraṃ vā ṣaḍasraṃ vā trirasrakam
children.translated_text: It may be round, square, hexagonal, or triangular,
without defects all around, bright, and well characterized by its marks.
Having installed it according to rule, together with the characteristics of worship,
one should place a water-pot in the middle of its altar, O twice-born men.
It should contain gold and seed, and be consecrated by brahmins with mantras.

children.text: secayecca tato liṅgaṃ pavitraiḥ pañcabhiḥ śubhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should sprinkle the <s>liṅga</s> with the five pure and auspicious substances.
One should worship according to one's means; then you will attain success.
With concentrated minds, worship together with your sons and relatives.
All of you, with folded hands, should resort to the wielder of the trident.
Then you will see the Lord of gods, who is hard to see for those whose selves are unpurified.
When he is seen, all ignorance and <s>adharma</s> perish.
Then, circumambulating <s>Brahmā</s> of immeasurable splendor,
those forest-dwellers set out from there for the <s>Devadāru</s> forest.
They began to worship, just as <s>Brahmā</s> had instructed.
On various sacrificial grounds, in caves of mountains,

children.text: nadīnāṃ ca vivikteṣu pulineṣu śubheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: and in solitary, auspicious sandbanks of rivers,
some were adorned with moss; some lay within the water;
some had only darbha grass for space, standing on the tips of their big toes.
Others used their teeth as mortars, and others pounded themselves with stones.
Others maintained heroic standing postures, while others delighted in the conduct of deer.

children.text: kālaṃ nayanti tapasā pūjayā ca mahādhiyaḥ
children.translated_text: Those great-minded ones passed their time in austerity and worship.
When a year had thus been completed and spring had arrived,
then, for the sake of favoring those devotees and out of compassion for them,
the god, in that Kṛta age, on the auspicious mountain of <s>Himavat</s>,
the gracious supreme lord came to the <s>Devadāru</s> forest.
His limbs were smeared with ash and dust; he was naked and strange in appearance.
He held a blazing firebrand in his restless hand, and his eyes were reddish tawny.
At one moment he laughs terribly; at another he sings in wonder.
At one moment he dances amorously; at another he cries out again and again.

children.text: āśrame hyaṭate bhaikṣyaṃ yācate ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He wanders through the hermitage for alms and begs again and again.
Having fashioned an illusion in such a form, the god came to that forest.

children.text: tataste munayaḥ sarve tuṣṭuvuś ca samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then all the sages, composed in mind, praised him.
With water, various garlands, incense, and likewise perfumes,
the greatly fortunate ones worshipped him together with their wives, sons, and attendants.

children.text: munayaste tathā vāgbhir īśvaraṃ cedam abruvan
children.translated_text: And those sages likewise addressed the Lord with these words:
"Out of ignorance, O lord of the gods of gods, whatever has been done by us,
by deed, by mind, or by speech, may you forgive all that.
Your deeds are wondrous, secret, and profound,

children.text: brahmādīnāṃ ca devānāṃ durvijñeyāni te hara
children.translated_text: O <s>Hara</s>, hard to be understood even by the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: agatiṃ te na jānīmo gatiṃ naiva ca naiva ca ||
children.translated_text: We do not know your pathlessness, nor indeed your path, not at all.

children.text: viśveśvara mahādeva yo'si so'si namo'stu te
children.translated_text: O Lord of the Universe, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, whatever you are, you are; homage to you.
The great-souled ones praise you, the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Homage to <s>Bhava</s>, to the auspicious one, to the maker of being, and to the source of arising.
Homage to the one of endless strength and valor, to the lord of beings.

children.text: saṃhartre ca piśaṅgāya avyayāya vyayāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the destroyer, to the tawny one, to the imperishable and to the perishable,
to the bearer of the stream of <s>Gaṅgā</s>'s water, to the support, to the one whose nature is the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).
Homage to <s>Tryambaka</s>, the three-eyed one, the bearer of the excellent trident,
to <s>Kandarpa</s>, to the fire, homage to the supreme Self.
Homage to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, marked by the bull, to the lord of the hosts.
Homage indeed to the one with the staff in his hand, to Time, and to the one with the noose in his hand.
Homage indeed to the one for whom Vedic mantras are chief, to the hundred-tongued one.

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ ca sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: The past, the future, and the present, and whatever is stationary or moving,
all this world, O god, has arisen from your body.

children.text: pāsi haṃsi ca bhadraṃ te prasīda bhagavaṃstataḥ ||
children.translated_text: You protect and you destroy; blessing to you. Therefore be gracious, O <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text: ajñānādyadi vijñānād yat kiṃcit kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: If a man does anything, whether from ignorance or from knowledge,
all that <s>Bhagavān</s> himself does through <s>yogamāyā</s> (the power of yoga).
Having praised him in this way, the sages, with their inner selves delighted,
endowed with austerity, asked, "May we see you as before."
Then the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>, pleased in himself, assuming his own

children.text: rūpaṃ tryakṣaṃ ca saṃdraṣṭuṃ divyaṃ cakṣuradātprabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: three-eyed form, the lord gave them divine sight in order to behold it.
Having obtained that sight and seen <s>Tryambaka</s>, the god of gods,
the residents of the <s>Devadāru</s> forest again praised <s>Īśāna</s>.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
"Homage always to the sky-clad one, to the end-maker, to the trident-bearer,
to the misshapen one, to the terrible one, and to the one with a terrible face.
Homage to you, the formless one, the well-formed one, the universal-formed one.
Homage indeed to the rattling one, to <s>Rudra</s>, to the one embodied in the cry svāhā.
Homage to the one whose body is bowed to by all, and to the one whose own self is bowed down.
Again and again homage to the ever blue-crested one, to <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.
Homage to the blue-throated god, whose limbs are smeared with funeral-pyre ash.
You are <s>Brahmā</s> among all the gods, <s>Nīlalohita</s> among the <s>Rudras</s>.

children.text: ātmā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ puruṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: You are also the Self of all beings, called <s>Puruṣa</s> by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>.
Among mountains you are great <s>Meru</s>, and among the lunar mansions the moon.

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca vasiṣṭhas tvaṃ devānāṃ vāsavas tathā
children.translated_text: Among the seers you are <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and among the gods you are <s>Vāsava</s>.

children.text: oṅkāraḥ sarvavedānāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sāma ca sāmasu ||
children.translated_text: Among all the Vedas you are the syllable oṃ, and among the Sāmans the finest <s>Sāman</s>.
Among wild animals you are the lion, O <s>Parameśvara</s>,
and among domestic animals you are the bull, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, worshipped by the world.

children.text: sarvathā vartamāno'pi yo yo bhāvo bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: In every way, whatever state exists now and whatever will come to be,

children.text: tvāmeva tatra paśyāmo brahmaṇā kathitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: there we see you alone, just as it was told by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhaś ca lobhaś ca viṣādo mada eva ca
children.translated_text: Desire, anger, greed, dejection, and pride:
we wish to understand this. Be gracious, O <s>Parameśvara</s>.
When the great dissolution had arrived, by you, O god, self-controlled,
a fire was produced by you when you placed your hand upon your forehead.

children.text: tenāgninā tadā lokā arcirbhiḥ sarvato vṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, by that fire, the worlds were surrounded on every side by flames.
Therefore these many distorted fires are like that fire:

children.text: kāmaḥ krodhaś ca lobhaś ca moho dambha upadravaḥ
children.translated_text: desire, anger, greed, delusion, hypocrisy, affliction,

children.text: yāni cānyāni bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other beings there are, stationary and moving.
Those living beings are burned by the fire that arises from you.
Be the protector of us as we are being burned, O lord of the gods.
And for the welfare of the world you sprinkle the beings with water,
O <s>Maheśvara</s>, greatly fortunate one, lord, whose glance is auspicious.

children.text: ājñāpaya vayaṃ nātha kartāro vacanaṃ tava
children.translated_text: Command us, O lord; we will carry out your word.
Among thousands of crores of beings and hundreds of crores of forms,

children.text: antaṃ gantuṃ na śaktāḥ sma devadeva namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: we are not able to reach the end, O god of gods. Homage to you."
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Nandī</s> said:
Then <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>, having shown favor, was pleased.
Hearing their praise, he, praised by them, spoke these words:
"Whoever reads or listens to the hymn proclaimed by you,
or whichever Brahmin makes twice-born men hear it, will obtain <s>gāṇapatya</s> (lordship among the hosts).

children.text: vakṣyāmi vo hitaṃ puṇyaṃ bhaktānāṃ munipuṅgavāḥ
children.translated_text: I shall tell you the holy good of devotees, O foremost sages.
The whole female <s>liṅga</s> is the goddess <s>Prakṛti</s>, born from my body.
The male <s>liṅga</s>, O Brahmins, is <s>Puruṣa</s>, arisen from my body.

children.text: ubhābhyāmeva vai sṛṣṭirmama viprā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through these two alone is my creation, O Brahmins; there is no doubt.
Therefore one should not revile the unsurpassed ascetic, the sky-clad one,
who behaves like a child or a madman, is devoted to me, and speaks of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: ye hi māṃ bhasmaniratā bhasmanā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are intent on ash, whose sins have been burned away by ash,
who act as prescribed, are restrained, Brahmins devoted to meditation,
always devoted to <s>Mahādeva</s>, moving about with seed drawn upward,
and who worship <s>Mahādeva</s> with speech, mind, and body controlled,
after reaching <s>Rudraloka</s>, do not return again.
Therefore this divine vow belongs to the Unmanifest, for those who bear the manifest <s>liṅga</s>."

children.text: bhasmavratāś ca muṇḍāś ca vratino viśvarūpiṇaḥ
children.translated_text: There are those who undertake the ash-vow, who are shaven-headed, vow-observers, and of manifold appearance.
A learned man should not revile them, nor should he overstep them.
He should not laugh at them nor speak unpleasantly, if he seeks welfare here and in the next world.
The foolish-minded man who censures them censures <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: yas tvetān pūjayen nityaṃ sa pūjayati śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: But whoever continually honors these people honors <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Thus this <s>Mahādeva</s>, wishing for the welfare of the worlds,
age after age, the great yogin sports smeared with ash.
Conduct yourselves in this way; blessing to you. Then you will attain perfection.

children.text: atulamiha mahābhayapraṇāśahetuṃ śivakathitaṃ paramaṃ padaṃ viditvā
children.translated_text: Having learned here the supreme state taught by <s>Śiva</s>, incomparable and a cause for the destruction of great fear,
with minds freed from the greed and delusion of becoming, they at once bowed down with their heads to the fierce one.

children.text: tataḥ pramuditā viprāḥ śrutvaivaṃ kathitaṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Then the delighted brahmins, having heard what had been spoken in this way,
with very pure scented waters mixed with kuśa grass and flowers,
bathed <s>Maheśvara</s> with waters from great jars.
They sang with various secret utterances and with resonant huṃ-cries.
Homage to the god over gods; indeed, homage to <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Homage to him whose body is half woman, the establisher of <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s>.
Homage to the dark one whose vehicle is the cloud, who wears an elephant-hide,
who has a black antelope skin as an upper garment and a serpent as his sacrificial thread.
To you with splendid, wondrous earrings and adorned with splendid garlands,
to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, who wears the excellent skin of the lord of beasts and whose fame is renowned, homage.

children.text: tatas tān sa munīn prītaḥ pratyuvāca maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Maheśvara</s>, pleased with those sages, replied to them:

children.text: prīto 'smi tapasā yuṣmān varaṃ vṛṇuta suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: "I am pleased with your austerity. Choose a boon, O men of good vows."
Then all those sages, bowing down to <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and likewise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>,

children.text: gautamo 'triḥ sukeśaś ca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Sukeśa</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,

children.text: marīciḥ kaśyapaḥ kaṇvaḥ saṃvartaś ca mahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Kaṇva</s>, and the greatly ascetic <s>Saṃvarta</s>,
having bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s>, spoke these words:
"Bathing in ash, nakedness, leftwardness, and going against the grain,
and also the distinction between what is to be served and not served: we wish to know this."
Then, hearing their words, the blessed supreme lord,
looking upon all those excellent sages, spoke with a smile.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge ṛṣivākyaṃ nāma trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-third chapter, named "The Speech of the Sages."
The Blessed Lord said:
I shall now explain this to you, the whole essence of the teaching.
For I am fire, the maker of soma, and soma is dependent upon fire.
Fire bears this that has been made, again because of its support of the world.
Again and again the world, moving and unmoving, has been burned by fire.
Everything has been reduced to ash; this is supremely purifying.
With ash, taking up my virile power, it sprinkles beings.

children.text: agnikāryaṃ ca yaḥ kṛtvā kariṣyati triyāyuṣam
children.translated_text: And he who, having performed the fire rite, will perform the <s>triyāyuṣa</s> rite,
is freed from all sins by ash, by my virile power.

children.text: bhāsata ityeva yadbhasma śubhaṃ bhāvayate ca yat
children.translated_text: Because ash shines, and because it brings about auspiciousness,
