and because it consumes all sins, it is called <s>bhasma</s>.

children.text: ūṣmapāḥ pitaro jñeyā devā vai somasaṃbhavāḥ
children.translated_text: The ancestors should be known as heat-drinkers; the gods indeed are born of soma.
The whole world, moving and unmoving, consists of fire and soma.
I am fire, of great splendor, and this great <s>Ambikā</s> is soma.

children.text: ahamagniś ca somaś ca prakṛtyā puruṣaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: I myself am fire and soma, <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Therefore, O greatly fortunate ones, ash is called my virile power,

children.text: svavīryaṃ vapuṣā caiva dhārayāmīti vai sthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the established rule is that I bear my own virile power upon my body.
From that time onward, in the worlds, for protection against inauspicious things,

children.text: bhasmanā kriyate rakṣā sūtikānāṃ gṛheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: protection is made with ash, even in the houses of women in childbirth.
A person whose self is purified by bathing in ash, who has conquered anger and the senses,
comes near me and does not return again.

children.text: vrataṃ pāśupataṃ yogaṃ kāpilaṃ caiva nirmitam
children.translated_text: The <s>Pāśupata</s> vow and yoga, and the <s>Kāpila</s> too, were established.
This <s>Pāśupata</s> was established first; that is unsurpassed.
All the remaining āśrama-dwellers were created later by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>.
This creation, constituted of shame, delusion, and fear, was created by me.

children.text: nagnā eva hi jāyante devatā munayas tathā
children.translated_text: For naked indeed are born the gods and the sages,

children.text: ye cānye mānavā loke sarve jāyantyavāsasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever other humans there are in the world, all are born without clothing.
A man with unconquered senses is naked even when covered with silk,

children.text: taireva saṃvṛtairgupto na vastraṃ kāraṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: but when protected by those same senses restrained, cloth is not regarded as the cause.

children.text: kṣamā dhṛtirahiṃsā ca vairāgyaṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Forbearance, steadiness, non-injury, and complete dispassion,
and honor and dishonor held equal: that is the supreme covering.
With limbs smeared by bathing in ash, one should meditate in the mind on <s>Bhava</s>.
If, after committing thousands of improper acts, one bathes with ash,
that ash burns all of it, as fire by its heat burns a forest.

children.text: tasmād yatnaparo bhūtvā trikālamapi yaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, becoming intent with effort, whoever always, even three times a day,

children.text: bhasmanā kurute snānaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ sa gacchati
children.translated_text: bathes with ash attains the <s>Gāṇapatya</s> state.
Having gathered all sacrifices and undertaken the supreme vow,
those who meditate on <s>Mahādeva</s>, imbued with the true state of his play,
by the northern noble path attain immortality.

children.text: dakṣiṇena ca panthānaṃ ye śmaśānāni bhejire
children.translated_text: And those who, by the southern path, resorted to cremation grounds,

children.text: aṇimā garimā caiva laghimā prāptireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), and <s>prāpti</s> (attainment),
control over desire and resolve, and likewise <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will),

children.text: īkṣaṇena ca panthānaṃ ye śmaśānāni bhejire
children.translated_text: and those who, by the path of seeing, resorted to cremation grounds,

children.text: aṇimā garimā caiva laghimā prāptireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), and <s>prāpti</s> (attainment).
<s>Indra</s> and the other gods likewise undertook the <s>kāmika</s> vow.
Having attained supreme sovereignty, they all became renowned for their splendor.
One should be free from pride and delusion, released from passion, with a nature devoid of the faults of darkness and passion.
Having understood this supreme overcoming of worldly disgrace, one should always be devoted to the yoga of <s>Paśupati</s>.
Meditating on this <s>Pāśupata</s>, which destroys all sins,
whoever recites it, having become pure, faithful, and self-controlled,
with his self purified from every sin, goes to <s>Rudraloka</s>.

children.text: te sarve munayaḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭhādyā dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When all those sages, the best of twice-born men beginning with <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, heard this,
their bodies became pale, smeared with ash, and they were free from longing.
Established by the splendor of <s>Śiva</s>, they were destined for <s>Rudraloka</s> at the end of the age.

children.text: tasmānna nindyāḥ pūjyāśca vikṛtā malinā api
children.translated_text: Therefore such people should not be censured but honored, even if deformed or dirty.
And those endowed with beauty as well, O best brahmins, should always be regarded with the thought that they may be foremost yogins.
What use is much talk, O best twice-born men? Devotees of <s>Bhava</s>
should be honored with every effort, just like <s>Śiva</s>; there is no doubt about this.
Even dirty brahmins, O best brahmins, if they are firm-vowed devotees of <s>Bhava</s>,
are like <s>Dadhīca</s>, who stood firm after conquering the God of gods,

children.text: nārāyaṇaṃ tathā loke rudrabhaktyā na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself in the world, through devotion to <s>Rudra</s>; there is no doubt.
Therefore, with every effort, those whose bodies and hair are smeared with ash,
wearers of matted hair, shaven-headed ascetics, naked ascetics, and those of many kinds
should always be honored like <s>Śiva</s>, in thought, action, and speech.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge yogipraśaṃsā nāma catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-fourth chapter, called the Praise of Yogins.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ jaghāna rājānaṃ kṣupaṃ pādena suvrata
children.translated_text: How did <s>Dadhīca</s> strike King <s>Kṣupa</s> with his foot, O virtuous one,
after defeating in battle <s>Janārdana</s>, the God of gods?
How did that great ascetic obtain from <s>Mahādeva</s> the state of having bones like the thunderbolt?
You should tell this, O <s>Śailādi</s>, just as death was conquered by you.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: brahmaputro mahātejā rājā kṣupa iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: There was a king remembered as <s>Kṣupa</s>, a son of <s>Brahmā</s>, of great splendor.
He was the friend of <s>Dadhīca</s>, lord of sages, O lord of men.
After a long time, through their association, a dispute arose between <s>Kṣupa</s> and <s>Dadhīca</s>:
whether the kṣatriya was supreme, or rather the brahmin, as is well known.
A king bears the bodies of the eight guardians of the worlds.

children.text: tasmādindro hyayaṃ vahniryamaś ca nirṛtis tathā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this king is <s>Indra</s>, Fire, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Nirṛti</s>;

children.text: varuṇaścaiva vāyuś ca somo dhanada eva ca
children.translated_text: he is <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and the giver of wealth.

children.text: īśvaro 'haṃ na saṃdeho nāvamantavya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: I am the lord; there is no doubt, and I am not to be disrespected.

children.text: mahatī devatā yā sā mahataścāpi suvrata
children.translated_text: That divinity is great, and it belongs among the great, O virtuous one.
Therefore, O greatly fortunate descendant of <s>Cyavana</s>, I must always
not be disrespected here by you, but worshiped in every way.

children.text: śrutvā tathā mataṃ tasya kṣupasya munisattamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard that opinion of <s>Kṣupa</s>, the excellent sage
<s>Dadhīca</s>, the fierce descendant of <s>Cyavana</s>, a brahmin proud of his own dignity,
struck <s>Kṣupa</s> on the head with his left fist.

children.text: cicheda vajreṇa ca taṃ dadhīcaṃ balavān kṣupaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then powerful <s>Kṣupa</s> cut down that <s>Dadhīca</s> with the thunderbolt.
Long ago in <s>Brahmaloka</s>, he had arisen from the sneeze of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: labdhaṃ vajraṃ ca kāryārthaṃ vajriṇā coditaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He had received the thunderbolt for a purpose, urged by the wielder of the thunderbolt, the lord.

children.text: svecchayaiva naro bhūtvā narapālo babhūva saḥ
children.translated_text: By his own will he became a man and became a protector of men.
Therefore that very mighty king conquered the best of brahmins.
Like the glorious bearer of the thunderbolt, powerful and filled with darkness,
the best of twice-born men fell to the ground, struck down by the thunderbolt.

children.text: sasmāra ca tadā tatra duḥkhādvai bhārgavaṃ munim
children.translated_text: Then, there, in his pain, he remembered the sage <s>Bhārgava</s>.
<s>Śukra</s> too restored him, who had been struck by the thunderbolt.
Coming through yoga into the body of <s>Dadhīca</s>, that best of embodied beings
joined <s>Dadhīca</s>'s body together as before, and <s>Bhārgava</s> said:
O <s>Dadhīca</s>, greatly fortunate one, worship the God of gods, the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
the God of gods, stainless and worthy of worship by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others.
Become invulnerable, O brahmin seer, through the grace of <s>Tryambaka</s>.
For this death-reviving power has been obtained by me from him, O brahmin.
There is no fear of death here anywhere for the devotees of <s>Śambhu</s>.
And now I shall tell you the Śaiva death-reviving mantra.
We worship <s>Tryambaka</s>, the lord, the father of the three worlds,
the father of the three spheres, <s>Maheśvara</s> of the three qualities,
of the three principles, of the three fires, and of what has become threefold in every way,
<s>Mahādeva</s> of the three Vedas, fragrant and increasing nourishment.
In all beings everywhere, and in <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) made of the three qualities,

children.text: indriyeṣu tathānyeṣu deveṣu ca gaṇeṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: in the senses and in other things, and among the gods and the hosts,
the supreme lord is subtle like fragrance in flowers; he is the fragrant one.
And since <s>prakṛti</s> is the nourishment of <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), O best of twice-born men,
and of the whole differentiated unfolding from <s>mahat</s> down to the specific elements, O virtuous one,
and also of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of the Grandfather, and of the sages, O great sage,
and even of <s>Indra</s> and the gods, therefore he is the increaser of nourishment.

children.text: taṃ devamamṛtaṃ rudraṃ karmaṇā tapasā tathā ||
children.translated_text: That immortal god, <s>Rudra</s>, by ritual action and by austerity,

children.text: svādhyāyena ca yogena dhyānena ca yajāmahe
children.translated_text: and by recitation, yoga, and meditation, we worship.
By this truth may <s>Bhava</s> himself release one from the noose of death.
For the lord causes both bondage and liberation, like a cucumber from its bond.
This death-reviving mantra has been obtained by me from <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Having muttered it, offered oblations with it, consecrated water in this way, and drunk it day and night,

children.text: liṅgasya saṃnidhau dhyātvā nāsti mṛtyubhayaṃ dvija ||
children.translated_text: and having meditated in the presence of the <s>liṅga</s>, there is no fear of death, O brahmin.
Having heard those words of his, he propitiated <s>Śaṅkara</s> through austerity.
he obtained hardness like the thunderbolt, invulnerability, and freedom from dejection.
Thus, having worshipped the lord of gods, the excellent sage <s>Dadhīca</s>,
through effort obtained invulnerability against others and a body firm as the thunderbolt.
And he struck the royal lord on the head with the sole of his foot.

children.text: kṣupo dadhīcaṃ vajreṇa jaghānorasi ca prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣupa</s>, the lord, then struck <s>Dadhīca</s> in the chest with the thunderbolt.
But that thunderbolt did not bring destruction to the great-souled <s>Dadhīca</s>,
whose body had been made thunderbolt-bound by the power of the supreme lord.

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpyavadhyatvamadīnatāṃ ca kṣupo dadhīcasya tadā prabhāvam
children.translated_text: Seeing then the invulnerability, fearlessness, and power of <s>Dadhīca</s>,
<s>Kṣupa</s> worshipped <s>Hari</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, the younger brother of <s>Indra</s>, the lotus-eyed one.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge kṣupābidhanṛpaparābhavavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, the thirty-fifth chapter, named the description of the defeat of King <s>Kṣupa</s>, is completed.
<s>Nandin</s> said:
The blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s>, pleased by his worship,
the glorious one together with <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Bhūmi</s>, bearing conch, discus, and mace,
crowned, with a lotus in his hand, adorned with every ornament,
clad in yellow garments, the blessed lord surrounded by gods and daityas,

children.text: pradadau darśanaṃ tasmai divyaṃ vai garuḍadhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> granted him a divine vision.
Having seen the god <s>Janārdana</s> by that very divine vision,
he praised <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> with pleasing words, after bowing down.
You are the beginning, and you are without beginning; you are <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), O <s>Janārdana</s>.
You are <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), lord of the world; you are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the universe.
This <s>Brahmā</s>, who is the <s>puruṣa</s>, the universe-formed grandfather,
is truly you yourself, the first principle, the supreme light, O <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: paramātmā paraṃ dhāma śrīpate bhūpate prabho ||
children.translated_text: You are the supreme self, the supreme abode, O <s>Śrīpati</s>, O <s>Bhūpati</s>, O lord.
<s>Rudra</s>, born from your anger, is enveloped by darkness.
By your favor <s>Pitāmaha</s>, the creator of the world, is joined with passion.
By your favor <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, is joined with lucidity.
O <s>Hari</s>, form of time, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, pervading the world,
the great principle, <s>bhūtādi</s> (the source of elements), the subtle elements, and the senses
are all governed by you alone, O universe-formed <s>Maheśvara</s>.
O <s>Mahādeva</s>, lord of the world, grandfather, teacher of the universe,
be gracious, lord of the gods of gods; be gracious, supreme lord.

children.text: prasīda tvaṃ jagannātha śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Be gracious, lord of the world; I have gone for refuge to you, the refuge.
O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, O <s>Śauri</s>, all-knowing <s>Vāsudeva</s>, mighty-armed one,
O <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, greatly fortunate one, O <s>Pradyumna</s>, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>,

children.text: aniruddha mahāviṣṇo sadā viṣṇo namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Aniruddha</s>, O <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>, O eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>, homage to you.
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, your divine seat is the unmanifest; in its midst, O all-pervading one,
is the bearer of the earth, formed of darkness and furnished with a thousand hoods.

children.text: adhaś ca dharmo deveśa jñānaṃ vairāgyameva ca
children.translated_text: And below, O lord of gods, are <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), knowledge, and detachment,
and sovereignty, as the feet of this seat, O you of good vows.
The seven netherworlds are your feet, and the earth is your hip.
The seven oceans are your garments, and the directions are your great arms.

children.text: dyaurmūrdhā te vibho nābhiḥ khaṃ vāyurnāsikāṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Heaven is your head, O all-pervading one; the sky is your navel, and wind has entered your nose.

children.text: netre somaś ca sūryaś ca keśā vai puṣkarādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The moon and the sun are your eyes, and <s>Puṣkara</s> and the others are your hairs.
The constellations, stars, and heaven are the ornament around your neck.

children.text: kathaṃ stoṣyāmi deveśaṃ pūjyaś ca puruṣottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: How shall I praise the lord of gods, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, who is worthy of worship?

children.text: śraddhayā ca kṛtaṃ divyaṃ yac chrutaṃ yacca kīrtitam
children.translated_text: Whatever divine praise has been made with faith, whatever has been heard and recited,
and whatever has been desired, forgive that, O lord; O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, homage to you.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
This Vaiṣṇava hymn destroys all sins.
Whoever recites or hears it, as it was proclaimed by <s>Kṣupa</s>,

children.text: śrāvayedvā dvijān bhaktyā viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: or has brahmins hear it with devotion, goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sampūjya caivaṃ tridaśeśvarādyaiḥ stutvā stutaṃ devamajeyamīśam
children.translated_text: Having worshipped in this way and praised the unconquered lord, the god praised by <s>Indra</s> and the other lords of the thirty gods,

children.text: vijñāpayāmāsa nirīkṣya bhaktyā janārdanāya praṇipatya mūrdhnā ||
children.translated_text: he looked upon <s>Janārdana</s> with devotion and, bowing his head, made his request.
The king said:
Blessed lord, a certain brahmin, renowned as <s>Dadhīca</s>,
a knower of <s>dharma</s> (sacred law), disciplined in self, was formerly my friend.
Always invulnerable to everyone and intent on worshipping <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: sāvajñaṃ vāmapādena sa māṃ mūrdhni sadasyatha ||
children.translated_text: he, contemptuously, struck me on the head with his left foot in the assembly.
O lord of gods, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the whole universe,

children.text: uvāca ca madāviṣṭo na bibhemīti sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: possessed by pride, he also said, 'I do not fear anything from any side.'
I wish to conquer that brahmin <s>Dadhīca</s>, O lord of the world.

children.text: yathā hitaṃ tathā kartuṃ tvamarhasi janārdana ||
children.translated_text: You, O <s>Janārdana</s>, should act in whatever way is beneficial.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Knowing also the invulnerability of the great-souled <s>Dadhīca</s>,
<s>Hari</s> remembered the incomparable power of <s>Maheśa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ smṛtvā hariḥ prāha brahmaṇaḥ kṣutasaṃbhavam
children.translated_text: Having remembered this, <s>Hari</s> spoke to <s>Kṣupa</s>, born from <s>Brahmā</s>'s sneeze:
For brahmins, O king, there is no fear when they have approached <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Especially for devotees of <s>Rudra</s>, O king, fearlessness is always theirs.
Even lowly people have it everywhere; how much more this <s>Dadhīca</s>?
Therefore, greatly fortunate king, there is no victory for you, O ruler.

children.text: duḥkhaṃ karomi viprasya śāpārthaṃ sasurasya me ||
children.translated_text: I shall cause distress to the brahmin so that a curse may fall upon me together with the gods.

children.text: bhavitā tasya śāpena dakṣayajñe suraiḥ samam
children.translated_text: By his curse, at <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, together with the gods,
my destruction will occur, O king, and then my arising again.
Therefore, having approached that best of brahmins with every effort, O king,
I shall make an effort, O king, for your victory over <s>Dadhīca</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: śrutvā vākyaṃ kṣupaḥ prāha tathāstviti janārdanam
children.translated_text: Hearing the speech, <s>Kṣupa</s> said 'So be it' to <s>Janārdana</s>.
The blessed lord then went to the hermitage of the brahmin <s>Dadhīca</s>.
Assuming the form of a brahmin, the blessed Lord, affectionate to his devotees,
bowed to the world-teacher, the brahmarṣi <s>Dadhīca</s>, and addressed him.
The Blessed Lord said:
Ho, ho, <s>Dadhīca</s>, brahmarṣi, imperishable one devoted to the worship of <s>Bhava</s>,
I ask one boon from you; you ought to grant it.
When requested by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god of gods, <s>Dadhīca</s> said:

children.text: jñātaṃ tavepsitaṃ sarvaṃ na bibhemi tavāpyaham ||
children.translated_text: I know everything you desire; I am not afraid even of you.
You have come in the form of a brahmin, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
Past, future, and present are known, O lord of gods, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
By the grace of <s>Rudra</s> I know this; abandon the brahmin state, O virtuous one.
You have been propitiated by <s>Kṣupa</s>, O lord of gods, O <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
I know this affection of yours for devotees, O blessed <s>Hari</s>.
This affection for devotees is fitting for you, O blessed <s>Hari</s>.
If there is any fear for me, who am devoted to the worship of <s>Bhava</s>, O blessed one,
you should say it plainly, O lotus-eyed giver of boons.

children.text: vadāmi na mṛṣā tasmānna bibhemi janārdana
children.translated_text: I speak no falsehood; therefore I am not afraid, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
In this world I am afraid neither of gods, nor of demons, nor even of brahmins.
<s>Nandin</s> said:
Hearing <s>Dadhīca</s>'s words, <s>Janārdana</s> then assumed

children.text: svarūpaṃ sasmitaṃ prāha saṃtyajya dvijatāṃ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: his own form, gave up the brahmin state at once, and spoke with a smile.
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: bhayaṃ dadhīca sarvatra nāstyeva tava suvrata
children.translated_text: There is no fear for you anywhere, <s>Dadhīca</s>, O virtuous one,
because you are devoted to the worship of <s>Bhava</s> and indeed are omniscient.
Yet you ought to say once, 'I am afraid'; homage to you.
At my command, O best of brahmins, say it before <s>Kṣupa</s> in the assembly.
Even after hearing that conciliatory speech of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the great sage

children.text: na bibhemīti taṃ prāha dadhīco devasattamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dadhīca</s> told that best of gods, 'I am not afraid.'
By the power of the god of gods, <s>Śambhu</s>, the very <s>Pinākin</s>,
of <s>Śarva</s>, of this omniscient <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the great sage stood firm.

children.text: tatastasya muneḥ śrutvā vacanaṃ kupito hariḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the sage's statement, <s>Hari</s> became angry.
The blessed Lord raised his discus, intending to burn up the best of sages.
But <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>Sudarśana</s> discus became blunted at its edge,
because of <s>Dadhīca</s>'s power, right there in <s>Kṣupa</s>'s presence.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tatkuṇṭhitāgraṃ hi cakraṃ cakriṇamāha saḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing that discus with its edge blunted, he spoke to the bearer of the discus:
<s>Dadhīca</s>, smiling, addressed the cause of the manifest and unmanifest, of being and nonbeing.
O blessed one, long ago you obtained with great effort
that very dreadful discus, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, renowned as <s>Sudarśana</s>.
This auspicious discus of <s>Bhava</s> does not wish to kill me here.
You should make an effort with the <s>brahmāstra</s> and other such weapons.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Hearing those words of his and seeing his weapon powerless,
he again launched all his weapons at him from every side.
Then the imperishable mighty gods aided that <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
who had set out to fight a single brahmin.
Then, taking a fistful of kuśa grass and remembering <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Dadhīca</s>,
self-controlled and having bones like a thunderbolt, hurled it at all the gods on every side.
It became a divine trident, blazing like the fire at the end of time,
and it resolved to burn the gods, like another fire of the age's end.
All the weapons cast by <s>Indra</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and the other gods
bowed down to the three-pointed weapon, O sage.

children.text: devāś ca dudruvuḥ sarve dhvastavīryā dvijottama
children.translated_text: And all the gods fled, their strength shattered, O best of twice-born men.
The blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme person, created from his own body
divine hosts like himself, hundreds of thousands and tens of thousands.
The best of sages suddenly burned all of them up.
Then, to produce astonishment, <s>Hari</s> became the cosmic form.
In the body of that <s>Hari</s>, before his eyes, the best of brahmins saw
the blessed brahmin <s>Dadhīca</s> saw the separate hosts of the deities,
and then crores of <s>Rudras</s> and crores of gaṇas,
and crores of cosmic eggs within the body of the cosmic form.
Seeing all this there, the descendant of <s>Cyavana</s> was amazed then.
He addressed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the world, unborn all-pervading lord made of the world.
The great sage sprinkled <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the universal form, with water and said:
Put aside this illusion, mighty-armed one; appearances are subject to analysis.
Thousands of forms of knowledge are hard to understand, O <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: mayi paśya jagat sarvaṃ tvayā sārdham anindita
children.translated_text: Behold the whole world in me, together with you, blameless one,

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ ca tathā rudraṃ divyāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ dadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s> as well as <s>Rudra</s>; I give you divine sight.
Having spoken thus, the sage showed the entire universe in his own body,

children.text: taṃ prāha ca hariṃ devaṃ sarvadevabhavodbhavam ||
children.translated_text: and addressed the god <s>Hari</s>, the source of all gods and all being.

children.text: māyayā hyanayā kiṃ vā mantraśaktyātha vā prabho
children.translated_text: What use is this illusion, or mantra-power, O lord,

children.text: vastuśaktyātha vā viṣṇo dhyānaśaktyātha vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or material power, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or again the power of meditation?
Therefore, abandoning this illusion, you ought to fight in earnest.

children.text: evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā māhātmyamadbhutam ||
children.translated_text: Hearing his words and seeing his wondrous greatness,

children.text: devāś ca dudruvurbhūyo devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ ca tam
children.translated_text: the gods again fled, and lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, the world-teacher,
restrained that god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> from action.
Hearing that statement of <s>Brahmā</s>, and defeated by him,
the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> bowed down to the great sage and departed.

children.text: kṣupo duḥkhāturo bhūtvā sampūjya ca munīśvaram
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣupa</s>, afflicted with grief, worshipped the lord of sages;
bowing quickly to <s>Dadhīca</s>, he entreated him in agitation:
<s>Dadhīca</s>, forgive me, O lord; what I did was from ignorance, my friend.

children.text: viṣṇunā hi surairvāpi rudrabhaktasya kiṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: For what can <s>Viṣṇu</s> or even the gods do to you, a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>?
Be gracious, O supreme lord. Devotion is hard to attain for wicked people, O twice-born one,
O best of the devout, for base kṣatriyas like me.
Hearing this and favoring him, the brahmin <s>Dadhīci</s>, best of ascetics,
the tiger among sages, cursed the king and the excellent gods.
May the gods, together with <s>Indra</s> and the lordly sages, by the fire of <s>Rudra</s>'s anger,

children.text: dhvastā bhavantu devena viṣṇunā ca samanvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: be shattered by the god, together also with <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
at the holy sacrifice of <s>Prajāpati</s>, of the great-souled <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śaptvā kṣupaṃ prekṣya punarāha dvijottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having cursed <s>Kṣupa</s> in this way and looked at him, the best of twice-born men spoke again:

children.text: devaiś ca pūjyā rājendra nṛpaiś ca vividhairgaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Honored by the gods, O king, and by kings and by various hosts,
brahmins alone, O king, are strong and mighty.
Having said this, the radiant brahmin entered his own hut,
and the king, having bowed to <s>Dadhīci</s>, went to his own dwelling.
That very tīrtha (sacred ford) became known as <s>Sthāneśvara</s>.
Having reached <s>Sthāneśvara</s>, one obtains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
I have briefly told you the dispute of <s>Kṣupa</s> and <s>Dadhīci</s>,

children.text: prabhāvaś ca dadhīcasya bhavasya ca mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: and the power of <s>Dadhīci</s> and of <s>Bhava</s>, O great sage.
Whoever recites this divine dispute of <s>Kṣupa</s> and <s>Dadhīci</s>,
having conquered untimely death, goes at the end of the body to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: ya idaṃ kīrtya saṃgrāmaṃ praviśettasya sarvadā
children.translated_text: And whoever, having recited this, enters battle at any time,

children.text: nāsti mṛtyubhayaṃ caiva vijayī ca bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: for him there is no fear of death at all, and he will be victorious.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge kṣupadadhīcisaṃvādo nāma ṣaṭtriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-sixth chapter, named "The Dialogue of <s>Kṣupa</s> and <s>Dadhīci</s>."
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
How did you attain <s>Mahādeva</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s>?
I wish to hear all that. You should tell me, O lord.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
My father <s>Śilāda</s>, desiring offspring, O great sage,
being childless, performed very difficult austerity for a very long time.
While he was practicing austerity, the lord <s>Vajradhṛk</s>, pleased by his austerity,
said to <s>Śilāda</s>, "I am pleased. Choose boons."
Then, bowing to the lord of gods, to <s>Sahasrākṣa</s> together with the immortals,
O tiger among sages, he spoke to <s>Hari</s> with his hands joined in reverence.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
O blessed slayer of the enemies of the gods, O thousand-eyed giver of boons,
O virtuous one, I desire a son who is not born from a womb and is free from death.
<s>Śakra</s> said:
I will give you a son, O brahmin-sage, born from a womb and joined with death.

children.text: anyathā te na dāsyāmi mṛtyuhīnā na santi vai ||
children.translated_text: Otherwise I will not give him to you, for indeed there are none who are free from death.
Even the blessed <s>Pitāmaha</s> will not give you here
a son who is deathless and not born from a womb; how much less others, O great sage?

children.text: so'pi devaḥ svayaṃ brahmā mṛtyuhīno na ceśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Even that god <s>Brahmā</s> himself is not deathless, nor is he the lord beyond all,
for he too, of great splendor, is womb-born, egg-born, and lotus-born.
And the powerful lord born from <s>Maheśvara</s>'s body, the son of <s>Bhavānī</s>,
even his lifespan is declared to be measured by two parārdhas.
As many thousands of crores upon crores of days
of the kalpas have passed, so much remains in the three later portions.
Therefore abandon, with effort, the hope for a deathless son not born from a womb,
O best of brahmins, and accept a son equal to yourself.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā pitā me lokaviśrutaḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing that speech of his, my father, famed in the world,

children.text: śilāda iti puṇyātmā punaḥ prāha śacīpatim ||
children.translated_text: the holy-souled <s>Śilāda</s>, again spoke to <s>Śacīpati</s>.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
O blessed one, I have indeed heard of egg-origin and lotus-origin,
and also of origin from <s>Maheśvara</s>'s body, in the case of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Long ago, O mighty-armed one, from <s>Nārada</s>, heir of <s>Mahendra</s>,
who was speaking of this former birth; tell us quickly how this is so.
<s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s> is such, and <s>Dakṣa</s> too is a god, son of the lotus-born one.
How is the mighty lord her son, since she is the granddaughter of <s>Kanakagarbha</s>?
<s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: sthāne saṃśayituṃ vipra tava vakṣyāmi kāraṇam
children.translated_text: Your doubt is proper, O brahmin. I shall tell you the reason,
what occurred in the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> kalpa of <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
In the <s>Meghavāhana</s> kalpa, the supreme lord <s>Janārdana</s>, lord of the world,
having meditated, created all things together with <s>Brahmā</s>.
For a thousand divine years, becoming a cloud,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> bore <s>Hara</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, with great honor and respect.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā bhāvaṃ mahādevo hareḥ svātmani śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Hari</s>'s devotion toward himself, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: pradadau tasya sakalaṃ sraṣṭuṃ vai brahmaṇā saha ||
children.translated_text: granted him everything, namely the power to create together with <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then they call that kalpa by the name <s>Meghavāhana</s>.
Seeing him then, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, who had arisen from his body,
the son of <s>Janārdana</s>, having attained <s>Śaṅkara</s> through austerity, said:
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is born from your left limb, and I am born from your right limb.
Though <s>Acyuta</s> created the whole world together with me,
because, becoming a cloud, the world-pervading one carried you day and night,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> carried you, the god of gods and teacher of the world.
O mighty <s>Śaṅkara</s>, I am your devotee even more than <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: prasīda dehi me sarvaṃ sarvātmatvaṃ tava prabho
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O lord; give me your all-selfhood in full.
Then, having received all-selfhood from <s>Bhava</s> in an instant, the blessed one
hurried forth and, approaching, saw <s>Puruṣottama</s>
in the pure abode of the single ocean, amid very terrible darkness,
in a divine place set with gold and jewels and fashioned by mind,
hard for wicked men to obtain and inaccessible even to virtuous ones such as <s>Sanaka</s>.
The unborn <s>Brahmā</s> saw the <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), in whose heart the world dwells,
reclining upon the couch of <s>Ananta</s>'s coils, lotus-eyed.
He had four arms and held the conch, discus, mace, and lotus;
he was adorned with every ornament and resembled the disk of the moon.
He was the god marked with the sign of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, with a serene face,
his lotus feet reddened by the touch of <s>Ramā</s>'s soft lotus hands.
He was the supreme self, the lord, in the form of Time through <s>tamas</s> (darkness),
and through <s>rajas</s> (activity) he sets in motion the play of creation for all the worlds.
Through <s>sattva</s> (clarity) he is the supreme lord who sustains all beings,
the self of all, the great self, the supreme self, the lord.
He reclined in yogic sleep in the milk-ocean, which was filled with nectar;

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha vai brahmā bhagavantaṃ janārdanam ||
children.translated_text: having seen him, <s>Brahmā</s> addressed the blessed <s>Janārdana</s>:
"By your grace I swallow you, as before, for you are myself."
Then the blessed one, smiling, awakened and looked at the Grandfather.
The mighty-armed one glanced at him and gave a slight smile.

children.text: viveśa cāṇḍajaṃ taṃ tu grastastena mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: He entered that egg-born one, swallowed by that great-souled being.
Then <s>Brahmā</s> emitted <s>Acyuta</s> through the space between his eyebrows.
When <s>Hari</s> had been created by him, he looked on and then stood in his presence.
Meanwhile <s>Rudra</s>, the source from whom all gods come into being,
assuming a distorted form, he who long ago had granted a boon to the two of them,
came to the place where <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the universal self and supreme lord, was.

children.text: prasādamatulaṃ kartuṃ brahmaṇaś ca hareḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Lord came to show incomparable grace to <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Hari</s>.
Then those two gods, coming together, saw the source from whom all gods come into being,
the god <s>Bhava</s>, the lord, resembling the fire of Time.
The two praised that <s>Śarva</s>, fierce and matted-haired,
and with great reverence bowed from afar to the giver of boons.
The blessed god <s>Bhava</s> also showed favor to the Grandfather
and to <s>Janārdana</s>, and the lord of the world disappeared right there.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge brahmaṇo varapradānaṃ nāma saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, named "The Granting of a Boon to <s>Brahmā</s>," in the first part of the blessed <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
When the god <s>Maheśvara</s> had gone, the blessed <s>Janārdana</s>, referring to him,
bowed and addressed the lotus-born one; he had arisen from the Unborn.
Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> said:
This supreme lord, lord of the world, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, is present everywhere.
<s>Maheśvara</s> is the lord and refuge of both of us and of everything.
I was born from the left limb of great <s>Śaṅkara</s>, O <s>Brahmā</s>;
you yourself were born from the right limb of the god <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: māmāhur ṛṣayaḥ prekṣya pradhānaṃ prakṛtiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Seeing me, the seers call me <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>prakṛti</s> (nature),
the unmanifest and unborn; they call you <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit).
Thus they say that <s>Mahādeva</s> is the cause even of us two,
the lord of the whole world, the imperishable master and ruler.
Then, at the words of that lord of immortals, the lotus-born one
praised and bowed to <s>Rudra</s>, the excellent giver of boons.
Then <s>Janārdana</s>, assuming the boar form, steadied the earth that had been flooded with water,
and established it as before.
The Lord made the rivers, streams, and oceans as they had been before,
after carefully making the earth free of hollows and heights.
On the earth he heaped up all the mountains, himself in the form of a bearer of the earth,
and he arranged the four worlds beginning with <s>Bhūr</s> as before.

children.text: sraṣṭuṃ ca bhagavāṃścakre matiṃ matimatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed one, best of the wise, then set his mind on creation,

children.text: mukhyaṃ ca tairyagyonyaṃ ca daivikaṃ mānuṣaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the chief creation, the animal-born, the divine, and the human.
There the all-pervading god, steadfast in mind, first created the Kaumāra creation of grace:
<s>Sananda</s> and <s>Sanaka</s>,

children.text: sanātanaṃ satāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ naiṣkarmyeṇa gatāḥ param
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s>, best of the good, who had reached the supreme state through non-action,
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>.
Through the knowledge of yoga he created <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,

children.text: saṃkalpaṃ caiva dharmaṃ ca hyadharmaṃ bhagavānprabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the Blessed Lord also created Resolve, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Adharma</s>.
These indeed are the twelve progeny of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth was from the unmanifest.
At the beginning the eternal one created <s>Ṛbhu</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>.
Those two divine elder-born ones were celibate, their seed directed upward, and were speakers of brahman.
The two boys were equal to <s>Brahmā</s>, omniscient and knowing all that was to be.
Having thus created the chief and other creations, O <s>Śilāśana</s>, the lotus-born creator of the universe
arranged all the <s>yuga-dharmas</s> (duties of the ages) without remainder.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, named "The Account concerning <s>Viṣṇu</s>," in the first part of the blessed <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: śrutvā śakreṇa kathitaṃ pitā mama mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard what was told by <s>Śakra</s>, my father, the great sage,
again questioned the lord of gods, bowing with joined palms.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
Blessed <s>Śakra</s>, all-knowing one, honored by the gods of gods,
lord of <s>Śacī</s>, lord of the world, thousand-eyed great lord,
how did the blessed lotus-born one establish the <s>yuga-dharmas</s>?

children.text: vaktumarhasi me sarvaṃ sāṃprataṃ praṇatāya me ||
children.translated_text: Be pleased now to tell me everything, for I bow before you.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Having heard that speech of great-souled <s>Śilāda</s>,
he described in full the <s>yuga-dharma</s> as he had seen it.
<s>Śakra</s> said:
Know the first age to be the <s>Kṛta-yuga</s>, and after that the <s>Tretā-yuga</s>, O sage;
then the <s>Dvāpara</s> and <s>Tiṣya</s>; these are the four in brief.

children.text: sattvaṃ kṛtaṃ rajastretā dvāparaṃ ca rajastamaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Kṛta</s> is <s>sattva</s> (clarity), the <s>Tretā</s> is <s>rajas</s> (activity), and the <s>Dvāpara</s> is <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s> (darkness).
The <s>Kali</s> is to be known as <s>tamas</s>, and so too is the condition of the ages within the ages.

children.text: dhyānaṃ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ yajña ucyate
children.translated_text: Meditation is supreme in the <s>Kṛta</s> age; in the <s>Tretā</s>, sacrifice is said to be so.

children.text: bhajanaṃ dvāpare śuddhaṃ dānameva kalau yuge ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Dvāpara</s> age pure worship is supreme, and in the <s>Kali</s> age giving alone.

children.text: catvāri ca sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tatkṛtaṃ yugam
children.translated_text: Four thousand years make that <s>Kṛta</s> age,

children.text: tasya tāvacchatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and its twilight is so many hundreds, with a twilight-portion of the same measure.
Four thousand human years, O <s>Śilāśana</s>,
know to be the lifespan of beings here in the <s>Kṛta</s> age, O virtuous one.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtayuge tasmin saṃdhyāṃśe ca gate tu vai
children.translated_text: Then, when that <s>Kṛta</s> age and its twilight-portion have passed away,
the <s>yuga-dharma</s> (law of the age) remains everywhere with only one quarter left.
The excellent <s>Tretā</s> age is deficient by one of the four parts.
Know <s>Dvāpara</s> as half of <s>Kṛta</s>; half of that is called <s>Tiṣya</s>.

children.text: triśatī dviśatī saṃdhyā tathā caikaśatī mune
children.translated_text: Three hundred, two hundred, and likewise one hundred are the twilights, O sage,
and the twilight-portions are likewise; so it is in the ages, age after age, in every kalpa.
In the first, the <s>Kṛta</s> age, eternal <s>dharma</s> stands on four feet.
In the <s>Tretā</s> age it has three feet, and in <s>Dvāpara</s> it stands on two.
In <s>Tiṣya</s>, lacking three feet, it is established merely by bare existence.
In <s>Kṛta</s>, beings arise in pairs, and their livelihood is directly the outpouring of rasa.

children.text: prajāstṛptāḥ sadā sarvāḥ sarvānandāś ca bhoginaḥ
children.translated_text: All beings are always satisfied then, full of every joy and enjoying pleasure.

children.text: adhamottamatā tāsāṃ na viśeṣāḥ prajāḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no lower or higher condition among them, no distinctions; the beings are auspicious.

children.text: tulyamāyuḥ sukhaṃ rūpaṃ tāsāṃ tasminkṛte yuge
children.translated_text: Their lifespan, happiness, and form are equal in that <s>Kṛta</s> age.

children.text: tāsāṃ prītirna ca dvandvaṃ na dveṣo nāsti ca klamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is affection among them, but no pair of opposites, no hatred, and no weariness.
They live on mountains and by the ocean, without fixed houses or shelters.
They are free from sorrow, rich in purity, and much given to solitude.
They move without desire, their minds always glad.
In the <s>Kṛta</s> age there is no engagement in either auspicious or sinful action.
The order of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s> exists then, and there is no mixture.
Through the conjunction of time, O twice-born one, the outpouring of rasa disappears in the age called <s>Tretā</s>.
When that <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) has perished, another <s>siddhi</s> arises.

children.text: apāṃ saukṣmye pratigate tadā meghātmanā tu vai ||
children.translated_text: When the subtle state of the waters has departed, then, indeed, it takes the form of clouds.
From clouds and thunderclouds the sending forth of rain begins.

children.text: sakṛd eva tathā vṛṣṭyā saṃyukte pṛthivītale ||
children.translated_text: When the surface of the earth has once been joined with rain,
there appear for those beings the trees called houses.
From them arises for those beings every means of subsistence and enjoyment.
From them the beings lived at the beginning of the <s>Tretā</s> age.
Then, after a long time, because of a reversal among those very beings,
a sudden disposition made of passion and greed arose.
Through that reversal among them, produced by the condition of that time,
all those trees called houses then perished.
When those had perished, the beings born from sexual union became bewildered.
Then, intent on truth in their meditation, they meditated upon that <s>siddhi</s>.
For them those trees called houses appeared again.
They produced garments, fruits, and ornaments.
In those trees there arose for them, endowed with scent, color, and taste,
honey in cup after cup, bee-less and the potency of the earth.

children.text: tena tā vartayanti sma sukhamāyuḥ sadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: By that they always maintained a happy life.
Through that <s>siddhi</s>, the beings were joyful, well nourished, and free from fever.
Then, after another interval of time, they were again covered by greed.
They seized those trees by force, and the honey too, or the honey made by bees.
Through that handling of them, caused once more by greed,
the <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s> (wish-fulfilling trees) perished here and there, together with the honey.
When that very <s>siddhi</s> had only a little left, under the sway of time,
the pairs of opposites arose in the <s>Tretā</s> age through its turning.
Then those beings were greatly afflicted by cold, rain, and fierce heat.

children.text: dvandvaiḥ sampīḍyamānāś ca cakrur āvaraṇāni tu
children.translated_text: Tormented by the pairs of opposites, they made coverings.
Having made defenses against the pairs of opposites, they then made shelters on the mountain.
Previously they had roamed at will and were without houses, but then they dwelt.
Again they lived in dwellings according to circumstance and according to their liking.
Having made protections against the injuries of the pairs of opposites, they considered a means of livelihood.

children.text: naṣṭeṣu madhunā sārdhaṃ kalpavṛkṣeṣu vai tadā ||
children.translated_text: For at that time the <s>kalpavṛkṣas</s>, together with the honey, had perished.
Those beings were confused by disputes and afflicted by thirst and hunger.
Then in the <s>Tretā</s> age another <s>siddhi</s> appeared for them again,
a rain, as they desired it, that brought about another support for livelihood.
From rainwater and the like there arose for them downward-flowing streams.
By the continuity of rain, the places of channels became rivers.
Thus rivers began at the second sending forth of rain.
And the small amounts of that water which fell upon the surface of the earth,
through the union of water and earth, became plants at that time.
Then the fourteen cultivated and wild plants, requiring little ploughing and not sown,
as well as seasonally flowering and fruiting trees and shrubs, were born.
These tree-born kinds and plants came into being.
By those plants the beings lived in the <s>Tretā</s> age at that time.

children.text: tataḥ punarabhūttāsāṃ rāgo lobhaś ca sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Then passion and greed again arose among them in every way,
because of an event that was necessarily to come and because of the force of the <s>Tretā</s> age.
Then they took possession of rivers, fields, and mountains,
and also trees, shrubs, and plants, violently and according to their strength.
Through that reversal, those fourteen plants perished.
Thinking, 'Those plants have entered the earth,' <s>Pitāmaha</s>
carefully milked the earth-cow for the welfare of all beings.
From then onward the plants, ploughed by the plough, were scattered here and there.
Seeking to live, they came with effort to vārtā, agriculture.
Vārtā is called a means of livelihood, because of effort directed toward agriculture.
Otherwise, at the end of the <s>Tretāyuga</s>, there is no life for them.
Then waters produced by the hand also come into being many times.
Even there, all people, overcome by anger, seized from one another
sons, wives, wealth, and the rest by force, through the force of the age.
Knowing all this, the mighty lotus-born one, for the establishment of boundaries,
created <s>Kṣatriyas</s> to protect people from injury.
By his own splendor he established <s>varṇāśrama</s>, the order of classes and life-stages,

children.text: vṛttena vṛttinā vṛttaṃ viśvātmā nirmame svayam ||
children.translated_text: and the world-soul himself fashioned conduct, livelihood, and ordered practice.
The institution of sacrifice also arose gradually in <s>Tretā</s>.
Even then some well-vowed people did not practice animal sacrifice.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-seeing, forcibly performed the sacrifice in due order.
Thereafter, O sage, the twice-born praised the non-violent rite.
In the <s>Dvāpara</s> ages too, differences of opinion arise among men.
By mind, act, and speech, livelihood is accomplished only with difficulty.
Then, gradually, for all beings, under the power of bodily distress,
there are greed, hired service, trade, war, and uncertainty about principles.
The production of branches of the <s>Veda</s> occurs, and so does the mingling of dharmas.
There is the collapse of <s>varṇāśrama</s>, and desire and hatred as well.

children.text: dvāpare tu pravartante rāgo lobho madas tathā
children.translated_text: In <s>Dvāpara</s> passion, greed, and intoxication also come forth.
At the beginnings of the <s>Dvāparas</s>, the <s>Veda</s> is divided fourfold by the <s>Vyāsas</s>.
Here in the <s>Tretās</s>, one four-footed <s>Veda</s> is prescribed.
But because life span declines, it is divided in the <s>Dvāparas</s>.
Further divisions are made by sons of sages through confusions of vision,
through arrangements of mantra and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> text, and through reversals of accent and phoneme.
The saṃhitās of <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> are compiled by wise men,
both general and modified forms, separately by those seers.
There are <s>brāhmaṇa</s> texts, <s>kalpasūtras</s>, and expositions of mantras.
Some proceed along those paths, while others stand opposed to them.
The <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> are divided because of the weight of time:

children.text: brāhmaṃ pādmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ ca śaivaṃ bhāgavataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Pādma</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, <s>Śaiva</s>, and <s>Bhāgavata</s>,
the <s>Bhaviṣya</s>, <s>Nāradīya</s>, and after that the <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>,
the <s>Āgneya</s>, <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>, <s>Laiṅga</s>, and also the <s>Vārāha</s>,

children.text: vāmanākhyaṃ tataḥ kūrmaṃ mātsyaṃ gāruḍameva ca
children.translated_text: the one called <s>Vāmana</s>, then the <s>Kūrma</s>, the <s>Mātsya</s>, and the <s>Gāruḍa</s>,

children.text: skāndaṃ tathā ca brahmāṇḍaṃ teṣāṃ bhedaḥ prakathyate ||
children.translated_text: as well as the <s>Skānda</s> and the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>; their division is proclaimed.
The auspicious <s>Laiṅga</s> is divided elevenfold in <s>Dvāpara</s>.
<s>Manu</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hārīta</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
<s>Yama</s>, <s>Āpastamba</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Likhita</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Gautama</s>,
<s>Śātātapa</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and thousands of others like these are named.
Drought, death, and calamities such as diseases also arise.
Then, from sufferings born of speech, mind, and action, disenchantment arises.
From disenchantment arises their reflection on release from suffering.
From reflection comes dispassion; from dispassion, the perception of faults.
And from the perception of faults, knowledge arises in <s>Dvāpara</s>.

children.text: eṣā rajastamoyuktā vṛttir vai dvāpare smṛtā
children.translated_text: This way of life in <s>Dvāpara</s> is remembered as joined with rajas and tamas.

children.text: ādye kṛte tu dharmo'sti sa tretāyāṃ pravartate ||
children.translated_text: In the first age, <s>Kṛta</s>, dharma exists; in <s>Tretā</s> it proceeds onward.
Having become disordered in <s>Dvāpara</s>, it perishes in the <s>Kali</s> age.
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śakra</s> said:

children.text: tiṣye māyāmasūyāṃ ca vadhaṃ caiva tapasvinām
children.translated_text: In <s>Tiṣya</s>, illusion, envy, and the killing of ascetics
are carried out there by men whose senses are bewildered by darkness.

children.text: kalau pramādako rogaḥ satataṃ kṣudbhayāni ca
children.translated_text: In <s>Kali</s> there is the disease of negligence, and constant dangers of hunger,
a dreadful fear of drought, and the overturning of countries.
There is no authority of <s>śruti</s>, and men practice adharma.
They are unrighteous, without proper conduct, very angry, and small-minded.

children.text: anṛtaṃ bruvate lubdhāstiṣye jātāś ca duṣprajāḥ
children.translated_text: Greedy men speak falsehood, and bad offspring are born in <s>Tiṣya</s>.
Through bad sacrifices, bad study, bad conduct, and bad doctrines,

children.text: viprāṇāṃ karma doṣeṇa prajānāṃ jāyate bhayam
children.translated_text: fear arises among the people because of defects in the rites of Brahmins.
At that time the twice-born do not study the <s>Vedas</s>, nor do they perform sacrifices.

children.text: utsīdanti narāścaiva kṣatriyāś ca viśaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: Men decline, and so in turn do <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>.
Through association and counsel with <s>Śūdras</s>, there is connection with Brahmins,
here in that <s>Kali</s>, through beds, seats, and meals.
Kings, mostly <s>Śūdras</s>, oppress the Brahmins.
Embryo-killing and hero-killing arise among the people.

children.text: śūdrāś ca brāhmaṇācārāḥ śūdrācārāś ca brāhmaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śūdras</s> have the conduct of Brahmins, and Brahmins have the conduct of <s>Śūdras</s>.
Thieves stand in the royal way of life, and rulers behave like thieves.
Women devoted to one husband will not remain; women who go to lovers will increase.
Instability of <s>varṇāśrama</s> arises everywhere among men.
Then the earth bears little fruit, though in some places it bears much fruit.
Kings are not protectors but plunderers, O <s>Śilāśana</s>.
<s>Śūdras</s> are all regarded as learned, honored by Brahmins.
Non-<s>Kṣatriyas</s> are kings, and Brahmins live dependent on <s>Śūdras</s>.
Seeing twice-born men seated, the small-minded do not rise.

children.text: tāḍayanti dvijendrāṃś ca śūdrā vai svalpabuddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: Low-witted <s>śūdras</s> strike the foremost twice-born men,

children.text: āsye nidhāya vai hastaṃ karṇaṃ śūdrasya vai dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the twice-born, placing a hand at the mouth, speak into a <s>śūdra</s>'s ear.

children.text: nīcasyeva tadā vākyaṃ vadanti vinayena tam
children.translated_text: Then they speak words to him humbly, as if to one of low rank.
O bull among the twice-born, <s>śūdras</s> will sit on high seats among the twice-born.

children.text: jñātvā na hiṃsate rājā kalau kālavaśena tu
children.translated_text: The king, knowing this, will not punish them, being under the power of Time in the Kali age.

children.text: puṣpaiś ca vāsitaiścaiva tathānyair maṅgalaiḥ śubhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With scented flowers and with other auspicious, blessed offerings,
men endowed with little learning, fortune, and strength will honor <s>śūdras</s>.

children.text: na prekṣante garvitāś ca śūdrā dvijavarān dvija ||
children.translated_text: Arrogant <s>śūdras</s>, O twice-born one, will not even look at the best of the twice-born.

children.text: sevāvasaram ālokya dvāre tiṣṭhanti vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing an opportunity for service, twice-born men will stand at the door.
Surrounding <s>śūdras</s> mounted on vehicles, and those who live dependent on <s>śūdras</s>,
<s>brāhmaṇas</s> will serve them there and praise them with praises in the Kali age.
The best of twice-born men will be sellers of the fruits of austerity and sacrifice.
And there will be many ascetics in this Kali age.
When the end of the age has arrived, there will be few men and many women.

children.text: nindanti vedavidyāṃ ca dvijāḥ karmāṇi vai kalau
children.translated_text: In the Kali age the twice-born will revile Vedic learning and the rites.
In the Kali age the god is <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the blue-and-red one.
For the establishment of <s>dharma</s> (sacred order), he manifests in a transformed form.

children.text: ye taṃ viprā niṣevante yena kenāpi śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: Those <s>vipras</s> who serve that <s>Śaṅkara</s> by whatever means
overcome the faults of Kali and go to the supreme state.
The predominance of wild beasts and the destruction of cattle
and the withdrawal of good people are to be known at that destruction of the age.
Then <s>dharma</s> will be subtle, greatly consequential, hard to find, and rooted in giving.
When the four āśramas have slackened, <s>dharma</s> will totter.
At the ends of the ages kings will not protect; they will seize the tax-share,
intent only on protecting themselves.
The countryside will have pikes on its ramparts, and crossroads will have pikes of <s>Śiva</s>.
Women will wear their hair like spears in the Kali age.
At that time the god will send variegated rain, when people declare the end of the age.
All merchants too will exist in the lowest age.
People's conduct will be corrupt, covered over by heretics with empty appearances.
People will become those who make one another perform many sacrifices.
When the age is exhausted, there will be no one who does not utter cruel words, no one straightforward, and no one free from envy.

children.text: na kṛte pratikartā ca yugakṣīṇe bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: Nor will there be anyone who repays a deed that has been done.
Reviling and fallen men too are a mark of the end of the age.
The earth will be without kings and not covered with grain and wealth.
Districts will arise in countries and in cities.
The earth will have little water and few fruits.
Protectors too will become non-protectors, without discipline.
They will be stealers of others' property and violators of others' wives,
lustful, evil-minded, base, and fond of violence.
Men will have ruined conduct, with loose hair and carrying pikes.
At the destruction of the age people will beget children at sixteen years of age.
With white teeth and eyes like antelope, shaven-headed and wearing ochre robes,
<s>śūdras</s> will practice <s>dharma</s> when the end of the age has arrived.
They will be stealers of crops and desirous of sturdy garments.
Thieves will steal the property of thieves, and another will steal from the thief.
When proper action has ceased and the world has fallen into inactivity,
insects, mice, and snakes will oppress human beings.
Good harvest, safety, health, and capacity will then be hard to obtain.
Countries, afflicted by fear of hunger, will resort to the <s>Kauśikī</s> region.
For those overwhelmed by suffering, the highest lifespan then will be a hundred years.

children.text: dṛśyante na ca dṛśyante vedāḥ kaliyuge 'khilāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the Kali age all the <s>Vedas</s> are seen and yet not seen.
Then sacrifices perish, oppressed by sheer <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
Here there will be many wearers of ochre who are nevertheless not free from bonds, and many <s>kāpālikas</s>.
Some will sell the <s>Veda</s>, and others will sell holy places.
And other heretics, hostile to the orders of caste and life-stage,

children.text: utpadyante tadā te vai samprāpte tu kalau yuge
children.translated_text: will arise then, when the Kali age has arrived.
Then <s>śūdras</s>, skilled in <s>dharma</s> and profit, will study the <s>Vedas</s>.
Kings born from <s>śūdra</s> wombs will sacrifice with the horse sacrifice.
Having killed women, children, and cows, and having slain one another,
people will then inflict troubles upon one another.
There will be abundant suffering, short life, wasting of the body, and sickness.
Because of fixation on <s>adharma</s>, the Kali age is remembered as moving in darkness.
Then among creatures <s>brahmahatyā</s> (brahmin-killing) and the like will come into operation.
Therefore, on reaching Kali, lifespan, strength, and beauty decline.

children.text: tadā tvalpena kālena siddhiṃ gacchanti mānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Yet then human beings attain perfection in a short time.
Blessed are those who practice <s>dharma</s> at the end of the age, O best of the twice-born.
Those who practice the <s>dharma</s> proclaimed by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, without envy,

children.text: tretāyāṃ vārṣiko dharmo dvāpare māsikaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: for them a year's <s>dharma</s> in the Tretā age, and a month's in the Dvāpara age, is remembered.
A wise man practicing it according to his hardship obtains that result in a single day in Kali.

children.text: eṣā kaliyugāvasthā saṃdhyāṃśaṃ tu nibodha me
children.translated_text: This is the condition of the Kali age; now learn from me the transitional portion.

children.text: yuge yuge ca hīyante trīṃstrīnpādāṃstu siddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In each age attainments diminish by three quarters at a time.
The natural states of the ages and their twilights remain here quarter by quarter.
The natural states of the twilights are established in their own parts, quarter by quarter.

children.text: evaṃ saṃdhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike
children.translated_text: Thus, when the time of the transitional portion has arrived near the end of the age,
the chastiser of those wicked beings arises from destruction.
In this lineage of the Moon he is known by the name <s>Pramiti</s>.
But through a portion of the divine <s>Mānava</s>, formerly in the <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s> interval,

children.text: samāḥ sa viṃśatiḥ pūrṇāḥ paryaṭanvai vasuṃdharām
children.translated_text: for twenty full years he wandered over the earth,
drawing along an army with horses, chariots, and elephants.
With brahmins holding weapons by the hundreds and thousands,

children.text: sa tadā taiḥ parivṛto mlecchān hanti sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: surrounded by them at that time, he slew <s>mlecchas</s> (outsiders) by the thousands.
Having completely slain those kings born from śūdra wombs,
then the lord made an end of all heretics without remainder.

children.text: nātyarthaṃ dhārmikā ye ca tān sarvān hanti sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: And those who were not especially righteous, he killed all of them everywhere,
as well as those born from confusion of <s>varṇas</s> and those who lived by them.
With his wheel set in motion, powerful, making an end of the <s>mlecchas</s>,
unassailable by all beings, he then roamed over the earth.
He was born here through a portion of that divine <s>Mānava</s>,
in a former birth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, a powerful one named <s>Pramiti</s>.

children.text: gotrato vai candramasaḥ pūrṇe kaliyuge prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: By lineage he was of the lunar race, a lord when <s>Kali Yuga</s> was complete.
When the thirty-second year had dawned, he set out for twenty years,
slaying all beings by the hundreds and thousands,
and, cruel in deed, making the earth one where only seed-remnants remained.
Through mutual causes and sudden anger,

children.text: sa sādhayitvā vṛṣalān prāyaśas tān adhārmikān ||
children.translated_text: he subdued those <s>vṛṣalas</s>, most of them unrighteous.
Together with his followers, he reached a station between the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: tato vyatīte kāle tu sāmātyaḥ sahasainikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after time had passed, with ministers and soldiers,
having eradicated all kings and thousands of <s>mlecchas</s>,

children.text: tatra saṃdhyāṃśake kāle samprāpte tu yugāntike ||
children.translated_text: when the twilight portion, the time at the end of the age, had arrived there,
and when only a few creatures remained here and there in this world,
then they, without restraint and wholly possessed by greed,
harmed one another, falling upon one another mutually.
In anarchy, by the force of the age, when danger had arisen,
all those people, afflicted by fear of one another,

children.text: vyākulāś ca paribhrāntāstyaktvā dārān gṛhāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: were bewildered and panic-stricken, abandoning wives and houses.
Not caring for their own lives, merciless and deeply miserable,
when <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> <s>dharma</s> had perished, they were slain by one another then.
They were without boundaries, driven away, without affection, and without shame.
When <s>dharma</s> had perished, they were struck down, short-lived, living only twenty-five years.

children.text: hitvā putrāṃś ca dārāṃś ca vivādavyākulendriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoning sons and wives, their senses disturbed by quarrels,
and stricken by drought, they cast their livelihoods far away.
They resorted to the border regions, abandoning their own settled lands.
They resorted to rivers, seas, wells, and mountains too.
They lived on honey, meat, roots, and fruits, in great misery.
Wearing bark, leaves, and skins, they were without rites and without possessions.
Fallen from <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>, they entered terrible distress.
Thus, when the people had reached hardship and only a few remained,
afflicted by old age, disease, and hunger, their minds became despondent from suffering.
From despondency comes reflection; reflection is a state of equilibrium.
Awakening has the nature of that state of equilibrium; from awakening comes devotion to <s>dharma</s>.
The survivors of <s>Kali</s> themselves then became joined with formless calm.
At that time, within a day and night, the age turned over for them.
Having caused bewilderment of their minds, as though they were asleep or intoxicated,
and by the force of the future event, <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> then began.

children.text: pravṛtte tu tatastasminpunaḥ kṛtayuge tu vai ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> had begun again,
the people who were survivors of <s>Kali</s> were born then as people of the <s>Kṛta</s> age.

children.text: tiṣṭhanti ceha ye siddhā adṛṣṭā vicaranti ca ||
children.translated_text: And those perfected beings who remain here and move about unseen,

children.text: sapta saptarṣibhiścaiva tatra te tu vyavasthitāḥ
children.translated_text: those seven, together with the <s>Saptarṣis</s>, were stationed there.

children.text: brahmakṣatraviśaḥ śūdrā bījārthaṃ ye smṛtā iha ||
children.translated_text: Brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras are remembered here as seed-stock.
Together with those born in <s>Kali</s>, all of them then became undifferentiated.
The <s>Saptarṣis</s>, and others as well, teach <s>dharma</s> to them.

children.text: varṇāśramācārayutaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ dvidhā tu yam
children.translated_text: That twofold <s>dharma</s>, <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s>, is joined with the conduct of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>.

children.text: tatasteṣu kriyāvatsu vardhante vai prajāḥ kṛte ||
children.translated_text: Then, when they perform the rites, the people increase in <s>Kṛta Yuga</s>.
In the <s>dharma</s> of <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> observances, shown by the <s>Saptarṣis</s>,
some remain here at the end of an age for the purpose of establishing <s>dharma</s>.
And sages remain in the offices belonging to the <s>manvantaras</s>.
Just as, when grasses here on earth have been burned by a forest fire,

children.text: vanānāṃ prathamaṃ vṛṣṭyā teṣāṃ mūleṣu saṃbhavaḥ
children.translated_text: the first growth of forests arises from their roots through rain,
so too the origin of people of the <s>Kṛta</s> age here comes from those born in <s>Kali</s>.
Thus, from age to age here, the succession is mutual.
It continues without interruption until the end of a <s>manvantara</s>.

children.text: sukhamāyurbalaṃ rūpaṃ dharmo'rthaḥ kāma eva ca
children.translated_text: Happiness, lifespan, strength, beauty, <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>

children.text: yugeṣvetāni hīyante trīṃstrīn pādān krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: diminish in the yugas, successively, by quarter after quarter.
In the yugas, together with their twilight portions, the attainments of <s>dharma</s> diminish.
This reconstitution has thus been recounted in sequence.
By this same reckoning there is the measure of all the four yugas.
This revolution of the four yugas, multiplied a thousandfold,
is called a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, and a night is remembered as being of the same length.
Crookedness and dullness among beings last until the destruction of an age.

children.text: etadeva tu sarveṣāṃ yugānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: This alone is remembered as the characteristic of all the yugas.
And when these four-yuga cycles are multiplied by seventy-one,
their orderly revolution is called a <s>manvantara</s>.

children.text: caturyuge yathaikasmin bhavatīha yadā tu yat ||
children.translated_text: Whatever occurs here in one cycle of four ages, at whatever time,
so too it occurs again in the others, precisely in that order.

children.text: sarge sarge yathā bhedā utpadyante tathaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: Just as distinctions arise in each creation, so indeed
they are limited to twenty-five, neither fewer nor more.

children.text: tathā kalpā yugaiḥ sārdhaṃ bhavanti saha lakṣaṇaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too the kalpas, together with the ages, occur along with their characteristics.
This indeed is the characteristic of all the manvantaras.
Just as the transformations of the ages have long gone on because of the nature of the ages,

children.text: tathā tu saṃtiṣṭhati jīvalokaḥ kṣayodayābhyāṃ parivartamānaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so the world of living beings remains, changing through decline and rise.
Thus this characteristic of the ages has been stated briefly,
of those past and future, in all the manvantaras.
And by one manvantara all the other intervals as well

children.text: vyākhyātāni na saṃdehaḥ kalpaḥ kalpena caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: have been explained, without doubt, and one kalpa by another.
With regard to those yet to come, the one who knows should reason in the same way,
in all the manvantaras here, past and future.
All have the same presiding identities, and they arise with names and forms:

children.text: devā hyaṣṭavidhā ye ca ye ca manvantareśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gods, who are of eight kinds, and those who are lords of the manvantaras,
the seers and the Manus as well, all having the same functions.

children.text: evaṃ varṇāśramāṇāṃ tu pravibhāgo yuge yuge ||
children.translated_text: Thus the division of varṇas and āśramas is made in each age.

children.text: yugasvabhāvaś ca tathā vidhatte vai tadā prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: And in the same way the Lord then ordains the nature of the age.
The divisions of varṇa and āśrama, the ages, and the attainments of the ages,

children.text: yugānāṃ parimāṇaṃ te kathitaṃ hi prasaṅgataḥ
children.translated_text: and the measure of the ages have been told to you incidentally.
I shall briefly tell of the sonship, through the goddess, of the lotus-born one.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge caturyugaparimāṇaṃ nāma catvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the fortieth chapter, named "The Measure of the Four Ages."
<s>Indra</s> said:
At the end of a thousand ages, at dawn, the Blessed Grandfather
again created the fallen creatures as before.

children.text: evaṃ parārdhe viprendra dviguṇe tu tathā gate
children.translated_text: Thus, O best of brahmins, when twice that half of his lifespan had passed,

children.text: tadā dharāmbhasi vyāptā hyāpo vahnau samīraṇe ||
children.translated_text: then earth was pervaded by water, water by fire, and fire by wind.
Fire and wind, together with the subtle elements, were merged in space.
The ten senses, the one mind, and the subtle elements, O best of twice-born men,
having reached ahaṃkāra (ego-principle), were dissolved in that very moment, alas.

children.text: abhimānastadā tatra mahāntaṃ vyāpya vai kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Then that principle of self-sense, having pervaded the great principle in an instant,
the great principle too, on reaching the manifest, became dissolved, O twice-born one.
The unmanifest, together with its own guṇas, was dissolved into <s>Bhava</s>.
Thereupon creation arose from that <s>Śiva</s>, the Puruṣa, just as before.

children.text: atha sṛṣṭāstadā tasya manasā tena mānasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the mind-born beings, created by him at that time through his mind,
the creatures of the lotus-born one, did not increase in this world.
For the sake of increase, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, together with his mind-born sons,
undertook hard-to-perform austerity himself, directing it toward the Lord.

children.text: tuṣṭastu tapasā tasya bhavo jñātvā sa vāñchitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhava</s>, pleased by his austerity and knowing his desire,
split the middle of the forehead of <s>Brahmā</s>, the cosmic person,
and, saying "affection for a son," then became female-and-male in form.
His son, the great god, became <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>.
The Blessed One burned everything, including <s>Brahmā</s>, the teacher of the world.
Then <s>Śiva</s>, for the sake of the growth of the worlds,
enjoyed by the path of yoga the auspicious half-measure, his own supreme goddess.

children.text: tasyāṃ hariṃ ca brahmāṇaṃ sasarja parameśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: In her the Supreme Lord created <s>Hari</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>,
the Lord of All, the Self of All, and likewise the Pāśupata weapon.
Therefore <s>Brahmā</s> is born from a portion of the great goddess, and so too is <s>Hari</s>.
He is egg-born, lotus-born, and also born from the limb of <s>Bhava</s>.
All this ancient history has been told to you,
in brief, as far as the half-lifespan of <s>Brahmā</s>, and his prosperity for that long.
I shall briefly tell of <s>Brahmā</s>'s detachment, born of darkness.
The Blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> too, having divided his own body in two,
created from that very limb of his the whole moving and unmoving world.
Then he created <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Brahmā</s>, the Grandfather, created <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: mune kalpāntare rudro hariṃ brahmāṇam īśvaram
children.translated_text: O sage, in another kalpa <s>Rudra</s> created <s>Hari</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the Lord.
Then, O sage, in another kalpa <s>Hari</s> created <s>Brahmā</s>.
Again <s>Brahmā</s> created <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Bhava</s> again created <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: tadā vicārya vai brahmā duḥkhaṃ saṃsāra ityajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the unborn <s>Brahmā</s>, considering that saṃsāra is suffering,
abandoned creation and, fixing himself in himself,
withdrew the movement of the breath and became motionless like a stone.
The Lord remained in samādhi for ten thousand years.

children.text: adhomukhaṃ tu yatpadmaṃ hṛdi saṃsthaṃ suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: The beautiful lotus situated in the heart, facing downward,
was filled by the inhalation and then awakened.
By breath-retention it became upward-facing, held in restraint.
He established the Lord in the middle of that lotus's pericarp.
Then, with the syllable oṃ, he established the god <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme one beyond the half-measure,
situated in one hundredth part of a single fiber of a lotus-stalk.
The self-controlled ascetic, his self purified by restraint, thus controlled the Lord in his heart.
He who was to be worshiped with the flowers of restraint and the like worshiped the imperishable one.
By the command of him who was situated in the lotus of his heart, the mighty one, born from a portion,
split his forehead and appeared from the Grandfather.
He was red and himself blue, born from the heart of <s>Śiva</s>.
And through union with fire, by nature the Lord became Puruṣa.

children.text: nīlaś ca lohitaścaiva yataḥ kālākṛtiḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: Because he was blue and red, that male had the form of Time.
The lord was called <s>Nīlalohita</s> by that god,
by <s>Brahmā</s>; blessed, all-pervading <s>Kāla</s> became pleased in spirit.
Then <s>Pitāmaha</s> praised the god whose mind was very well pleased,
with an eight-name hymn, O great sage; he, the soul of the universe, praised the soul of the universe.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:
Homage to you, blessed <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Bhāskara</s>, of immeasurable splendor;
homage to you as <s>Bhava</s>, the god, as rasa, water-formed.
Homage to <s>Śarva</s>, whose form is earth, ever fragrant;

children.text: īśāya vāyave tubhyaṃ saṃsparśāya namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: again and again homage to you as <s>Īśa</s>, as wind, as touch.
And to the lord of beasts, to fire of surpassing splendor;
homage to you as <s>Bhīma</s>, whose form is space, whose measure is sound.
Homage to you as <s>Mahādeva</s>, as Soma, as immortality;
homage to you as <s>Ugra</s>, as the sacrificer, as one yoked to ritual action.
Whoever recites or listens to this ancestral hymn,
or, concentrated, causes Brahmins to hear it as told for <s>Rudra</s>,
within one year obtains union with the eight-formed one;
having thus praised <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Pitāmaha</s> looked upon him.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s> established himself in eight ways on every side;
then the sun, fire, and the moon shone forth,
as earth, wind, man, water, and the all-pervading hollow space as well.
From then on they called that Lord the <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s> (eight-formed one).
Through the grace of the <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s>, <s>Virañci</s> created again.

children.text: sṛṣṭvaitad akhilaṃ brahmā punaḥ kalpāntare prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having created this whole universe, the lord <s>Brahmā</s>, again at the end of a kalpa,
while the moving and unmoving world slept for a thousand yugas,

children.text: prajāḥ sraṣṭumanās tepe tata ugraṃ tapo mahat ||
children.translated_text: desiring to create beings, then practiced a great and fierce austerity.
While he was practicing austerity in this way, nothing at all came about.
Then, after a long time, anger arose from his sorrow.
From the eyes of him who was seized by anger, drops of tears fell;
and from those tear-drops beings and departed spirits then arose.
Seeing all those first-born beings, ghosts, departed spirits, and night-wanderers,

children.text: anindata tadā devo brahmātmānam ajo vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the god <s>Brahmā</s>, unborn and all-pervading, then reproached himself.

children.text: jahau prāṇāṃś ca bhagavān krodhāviṣṭaḥ prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Prajāpati</s>, seized by anger, abandoned his life-breaths,
and then life-breath-made <s>Rudra</s> appeared from the lord's mouth.
Having become <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>, with radiance like the young sun,
he then divided himself elevenfold and stood established.
With one half portion that all-souled one created the auspicious <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: sā cāsṛjattadā lakṣmīṃ durgāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ sarasvatīm ||
children.translated_text: And she then created <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, excellent <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, lotus-eyed,
<s>Kalā</s> and <s>Vikiriṇī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and the lotus-dwelling goddess,
the goddess <s>Balavikariṇī</s>, and likewise <s>Balapramathinī</s>,
and <s>Damanī</s> of all beings; she also created <s>Manonmanī</s>.

children.text: tathānyā bahavaḥ sṛṣṭās tayā nāryaḥ sahasraśaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise many other women were created by her in thousands.
And with the <s>Rudras</s> and with those goddesses, <s>Mahādeva</s>, lord of the three worlds,
the supreme lord of all selves stood before him.
For that dead god, <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
