the compassionate <s>Maheśvara</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, again bestowed life-breaths.
The lord then gave back to <s>Brahmā</s> the life-breaths that were established in himself.
Then <s>Rudra</s> was delighted when his life had somewhat returned;
the lord of gods addressed <s>Brahmā</s> with this supreme speech:

children.text: mā bhairdeva mahābhāga viriñca jagatāṃ guro
children.translated_text: Do not fear, O god, greatly fortunate <s>Viriñca</s>, teacher of the worlds.
The life-breaths have been set here by me; therefore arise, O lord.
Then, having heard his speech, like a dream present in the mind,
<s>Pitāmaha</s>, pleased in spirit, with eyes shining like opened lotuses,
then, his life restored, looked up at <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: sa udvīkṣya ciraṃ kālaṃ snigdhagaṃbhīrayā girā ||
children.translated_text: After gazing upward for a long time, in a tender and deep voice,
blessed <s>Brahmā</s> spoke, rising with joined palms:

children.text: bho bho vada mahābhāga ānandayasi me manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Ah, ah, speak, greatly fortunate one; you gladden my mind.

children.text: ko bhavān aṣṭamūrtir vai sthita ekādaśātmakaḥ
children.translated_text: Who are you, eight-formed and yet standing with an elevenfold self?
<s>Indra</s> said:
Hearing those words of his, <s>Maheśvara</s> declared,
touching <s>Brahmā</s> with his two gentle hands, he, the slayer of the enemies of the gods.
<s>Śrīśaṅkara</s> said:
Know me as the supreme self, and this unborn <s>Māyā</s>.
These <s>Rudras</s> are stationed here; they have come to protect you.

children.text: tataḥ praṇamya taṃ brahmā devadevamuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s>, bowing to that god of gods, spoke:
having made the hollow of his joined palms, in a voice choked with joy,
Blessed lord, lord of the gods of gods, I am indeed overwhelmed by sorrows.
O <s>Īśāna</s>, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, you ought to free me here from worldly existence.
Then the blessed <s>Umāpati</s>, lord of the world, laughed toward <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
and then the all-pervading one disappeared with the <s>Rudras</s> and with her.
<s>Indra</s> said:
Therefore, O <s>Śilāda</s>, one born without a womb is indeed hard to obtain in the worlds;
understand: a deathless man is hard to obtain, for even the lotus-born one has death.
But if the lord of gods, <s>Rudra</s>, the Lord, is gracious,
then a deathless son for you, born without a womb, is not hard to obtain.

children.text: mayā ca viṣṇunā caiva brahmaṇā ca mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: By me, by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and also by great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>,
one born without a womb and free from death cannot be provided.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ vyāhṛtya viprendramanugṛhya ca taṃ ghṛṇī ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and having favored that best of Brahmins, the radiant one,

children.text: devairvṛto yayau devaḥ sitenebhena vai prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lordly god, surrounded by the gods, departed on a white elephant.
Thus ends the forty-first chapter, named "Indra's Speech," in the first part of the revered <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: gate puṇye ca varade sahasrākṣe śilāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: When the holy and boon-giving thousand-eyed one had departed, <s>Śilāśana</s>,
worshipping <s>Mahādeva</s> with austerity, pleased <s>Bhava</s>.
Then, while that twice-born sage was thus constantly intent upon him,
a thousand divine years passed, wonderfully, as though they were a moment.
The sage's limbs were covered by an anthill, and he was visible only through swarms of insects,
with mouths like diamond needles, and by other red insects everywhere.
Without flesh, blood, or skin, untouched, he stood like a wall,
and afterward he was reduced to bones alone; then <s>Śaṅkara</s> showed concern for him.

children.text: yadā spṛṣṭo munistena kareṇa ca smarāriṇā
children.translated_text: When the sage was touched by the hand of <s>Smarāri</s>,
at once that tiger among sages, the twice-born one, cast off his fatigue.
The lord <s>Śaṅkara</s>, pleased by the austerity of him who was practicing austerity,
then said, together with his attendants and with <s>Umā</s>, "I am pleased with you.
What need have you of this austerity, O great-minded one?
I grant you a son, all-knowing and having crossed to the far shore of the meaning of all śāstras."
Then, bowing to the lord of gods and praising him, <s>Śilāśana</s> spoke
with a voice choked by joy to <s>Soma</s>, who is adorned with the moon.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
O blessed lord, lord of gods, destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
I desire a son not born from a womb and free from death, O best of beings.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The supreme lord, <s>Rudra</s>, who had formerly been worshipped by austerity,

children.text: śilādaṃ brahmaṇā rudraḥ prītyā paramayā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>, again spoke to <s>Śilāda</s> with supreme affection.
The revered lord of gods said:
O brahmin, O treasure of austerity, I was formerly worshipped by <s>Brahmā</s>,
and with austerity by sages and by the best of gods, for the sake of an incarnation.
I shall become your son, named <s>Nandin</s>, not born from a womb.

children.text: pitā bhaviṣyasi mama piturvai jagatāṃ mune ||
children.translated_text: You shall be my father, O sage, indeed the father of the father of the worlds.

children.text: evamuktvā muniṃ prekṣya praṇipatya sthitaṃ ghṛṇī
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and looking upon the sage, who stood bowed down, the compassionate one,
<s>Soma</s>, bright like the moon and pleased, disappeared right there.
Having obtained a son from <s>Rudra</s>, my father was delighted, O great sage,
and, being best among knowers of sacrifice, he reached the great sacrificial enclosure for the sake of sacrifice.
From that enclosure I, the son of <s>Śambhu</s>, by his command,
was born there in ancient times, with a radiance like the fire at the end of an age.

children.text: vavarṣustadā puṣkarāvartakādyā jaguḥ khecarāḥ kinnarāḥ siddhasādhyāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Puṣkara</s> and <s>Āvartaka</s> clouds and the others rained; the sky-going <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>siddhas</s>, and <s>sādhyas</s> sang.

children.text: śilādātmajatvaṃ gate mayyupendraḥ sasarjātha vṛṣṭiṃ supuṣpaughamiśrām ||
children.translated_text: When I had become the son of <s>Śilāda</s>, <s>Upendra</s> then sent forth a rain mingled with masses of fine flowers.
Seeing me, with the appearance of the sun of time, wearing a crown of matted hair,
three-eyed, four-armed, an infant bearing a trident, axe, and mace,
bearing the thunderbolt, with thunderbolt-like fangs, a child worshipped by the wielder of the thunderbolt,
wearing thunderbolt earrings, terrible, with a sound like a rain cloud,
all, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, praised me, as did the lord of gods and the great sages.
All around they resounded, and the hosts of apsarases danced.
The seers, O tiger among sages, with mantras arising from the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>,
praised me with <s>Māheśvara</s> mantras and bowed down fully, filled with joy.

children.text: brahmā hariś ca rudraś ca śakraḥ sākṣācchivāṃbikā
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Śivāmbikā</s> herself,
<s>Jīva</s>, the moon, the greatly radiant sun, wind, and fire,

children.text: īśāno nirṛtiryakṣo yamo varuṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: viśvedevās tathā rudrā vasavaś ca mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the very mighty <s>Vasus</s>,

children.text: lakṣmīḥ sākṣācchacī jyeṣṭhā devī caiva sarasvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself, <s>Śacī</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: aditiś ca ditiścaiva śraddhā lajjā dhṛtis tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Diti</s>, and also <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,

children.text: nandā bhadrā ca surabhī suśīlā sumanās tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Nandā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Surabhī</s>, <s>Suśīlā</s>, and <s>Sumanas</s>,

children.text: vṛṣendraś ca mahātejā dharmo dharmātmajas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the lordly bull of great splendor, <s>Dharma</s>, and the son of <s>Dharma</s>,
surrounded me, embraced me, and praised me, O best of sages.

children.text: śilādo'pi munirdṛṣṭvā pitā me tādṛśaṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: And the sage <s>Śilāda</s>, my father, seeing me such as I was then,
the pure-souled one bowed with affection and praised his son, the giver of desired boons.
<s>Śilāda</s> said:
O blessed lord, lord of gods, three-eyed one, my imperishable one,

children.text: putro'si jagatāṃ yasmāttrātā duḥkhāddhi kiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: since you are the son and protector of the worlds from suffering, what more need be said?

children.text: rakṣako jagatāṃ yasmātpitā me putra sarvaga ||
children.translated_text: Since you are the protector of the worlds, you are my father, O son, O all-pervading one.
O womb-less one, homage to you, source of the world, grandfather.

children.text: pitā putra maheśāna jagatāṃ ca jagadguro ||
children.translated_text: O father, O son, O <s>Maheśāna</s>, O lord of the worlds and teacher of the world.

children.text: vatsa vatsa mahābhāga pāhi māṃ parameśvara
children.translated_text: Child, child, O greatly fortunate one, protect me, O supreme lord.
Because I have been gladdened by you, O lord of gods, you are named <s>Nandī</s>.
Therefore gladden me, O <s>Nandin</s>; I bow to the lord of the world.

children.text: prasīda pitarau me'dya rudralokaṃ gatau vibho ||
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O mighty one; my parents have today gone to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
And my grandfather too, O <s>Nandin</s>, since <s>Maheśvara</s> has descended,

children.text: mamaiva saphalaṃ loke janma vai jagatāṃ prabho ||
children.translated_text: my very birth in the world has become fruitful, O lord of the worlds.
Since you, O <s>Nandin</s>, have descended as my son for my protection, O lord,

children.text: tubhyaṃ namaḥ sureśāna nandīśvara namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: homage to you, O lord of gods; O <s>Nandīśvara</s>, homage to you.
O son, protect me, O mighty-armed one, O god of gods, O teacher of the world.
Whatever has been proclaimed by me, O <s>Nandīśa</s>, thinking only of your sonship,
may that be forgiven by you, dear child, O praiseworthy one praised by gods and asuras.
Whoever recites or hears this hymn spoken by me to my son,

children.text: śrāvayedvā dvijān bhaktyā mayā sārdhaṃ sa modate
children.translated_text: or causes twice-born men to hear it with devotion, rejoices together with me.

children.text: evaṃ stutvā sutaṃ bālaṃ praṇamya bahumānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having thus praised his infant son and bowed with great honor,

children.text: munīśvarāṃś ca samprekṣya śilāda uvāca suvrataḥ
children.translated_text: the good-vowed <s>Śilāda</s>, looking at the lords among sages, spoke:
Behold, all you sages, my imperishable great fortune,
for the lord, the god <s>Nandī</s>, has descended in the sacrificial enclosure.

children.text: matsamaḥ kaḥ pumāṃlloke devo vā dānavo'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: Who in the world, whether man, god, or even demon, is equal to me?

children.text: eṣa nandī yato jāto yajñabhūmau hitāya me ||
children.translated_text: For this <s>Nandin</s> was born on the sacrificial ground for my benefit.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge nandikeśvarotpattir nāma dvicatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the forty-second chapter, named 'The Birth of <s>Nandikeśvara</s>'.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:

children.text: mayā saha pitā hṛṣṭaḥ praṇamya ca maheśvaram
children.translated_text: My father, delighted, bowed to <s>Maheśvara</s> together with me

children.text: uṭajaṃ svaṃ jagāmāśu nidhiṃ labdhveva nirdhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and quickly went to his own hut, like a poor man who has obtained treasure.
When I had come to the hut of the great sage <s>Śilāda</s>,

children.text: tadā vai daivikaṃ rūpaṃ tyaktvā mānuṣyam āsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then, having abandoned my divine form, I assumed a human one.

children.text: naṣṭā caiva smṛtirdivyā yena kenāpi kāraṇāt
children.translated_text: And my divine memory was lost, for some reason or other.
Seeing that I had assumed a human state, my father, worshiped by the world,
lamented, extremely afflicted with sorrow and surrounded by his kinsmen.
The all-knowing one performed for me the <s>jātakarman</s> and the other rites.
<s>Śilāda</s>, son of <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>, was indeed affectionate to his son.

children.text: upadiṣṭā hi tenaiva ṛkśākhā yajuṣas tathā ||
children.translated_text: By him the branch of the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and also of the <s>Yajurveda</s> were taught,
and a thousand branches of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, together with their limbs and subsidiary limbs, O great sage,
as well as <s>Āyurveda</s>, <s>Dhanurveda</s>, music, and the marks of horses,

children.text: hastināṃ caritaṃ caiva narāṇāṃ caiva lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: the behavior of elephants and the marks of human beings.
Then, when my seventh year was complete, O two best sages,
two divine ones named <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, endowed with the power of austerity and yoga,

children.text: tasyāśramaṃ gatau divyau draṣṭuṃ māṃ cājñayā vibhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: came to his hermitage to see me, by the command of the Lord.

children.text: ūcatuś ca mahātmānau māṃ nirīkṣya muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: Those two great-souled ones, looking at me again and again, said:
'Dear child, this <s>Nandin</s> is short-lived, though he has mastered the meanings of all the <s>śāstras</s>.
No such wonder has been seen; his life will not extend beyond a year from now.'
When they had spoken thus, the eminent brahmin <s>Śilāda</s>, loving his son,
embraced me and, afflicted with sorrow, wept very loudly.

children.text: hā putra putra putreti papāta ca samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Crying, 'Alas, my son, my son, my son!' he fell down on every side.
Distressed, he said, 'Ah, the power of divine ordinance, of the creator!'
Having heard his pained cry, the inhabitants of that hermitage
fell down, utterly bewildered, and performed protective auspicious rites.
They praised <s>Mahādeva</s>, the three-eyed lord, husband of <s>Umā</s>.
They offered, with the <s>Tryambaka</s> mantra, oblations of dūrvā grass drenched in honey,
numbering ten thousand and accompanied by all ritual substances.

children.text: pitā vigatasaṃjñaś ca tathā caiva pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: My father lost consciousness, and so did my grandfather.
Motionless, he babbled and fell down like a dead man.
Fearing death would come soon, I bowed my head to him,
to my father and grandfather, who had fallen there like dead men.
Having circumambulated him, I became intent on reciting the <s>Rudra</s> formula.
In the hollow of the lotus of my heart I meditated on the god <s>Tryambaka</s>,
the three-eyed, ten-armed, peaceful, five-faced <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
While I stood within the holy river, the supreme Lord
<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, adorned with the half-moon, was pleased and said:
'Child <s>Nandin</s>, mighty-armed one, why should you fear death?

children.text: mayaiva preṣitau viprau matsamastvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: The two brahmins were sent by me; you are equal to me, without doubt.
Child, this body of yours is worldly only in the conventional sense;

children.text: nāstyeva daivikaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śilādena purā tava
children.translated_text: in truth it is not so. Your divine body was formerly seen by <s>Śilāda</s>,
and by gods, sages, siddhas, gandharvas, and foremost dānavas.
That divine body of yours, child <s>Nandikeśvara</s>, was formerly worshiped.

children.text: saṃsārasya svabhāvo'yaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the nature of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence): pleasure and pain again and again.
For discerning people there is in every way the abandonment of human birth.
Having spoken thus to me face to face, the great Lord of all gods,
the supreme Lord, with both his very beautiful hands,
the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Hara</s>, remover of supreme distress, touched me.
And <s>Mahādeva</s>, the bull-bannered one, pleased in heart, said,
after looking at the lords of the gaṇas and at the goddess, daughter of <s>Himavat</s>.
Looking around, <s>Mahādeva</s>, lord of the gods, pleased in heart, said:
'He shall be ageless, free from old age, and always devoid of suffering;
imperishable and undecaying, together with his father and his friends.
He shall be dear to me, lord of my gaṇas, possessed of my vigor and my valor.

children.text: iṣṭo mama sadā caiva mama pārśvagataḥ sadā
children.translated_text: He shall always be beloved of me and always stationed at my side.
He will have my strength and be endowed with great power of yoga.'

children.text: evamuktvā ca māṃ devo bhagavān sagaṇastadā
children.translated_text: Having thus spoken, the blessed god, together with his gaṇas,
then removed from himself a garland made of lotuses,
and the great-splendored bull-bannered god bound it upon me.
By that auspicious garland fastened at my neck,
I became three-eyed and ten-armed, like a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Then the supreme Lord took hold of me with his hand

children.text: uvāca brūhi kiṃ te'dya dadāmi varamuttamam
children.translated_text: and said, 'Tell me: what supreme boon shall I give you today?'
Then, taking the exceedingly pure water resting in his matted hair,
the bull-bannered one released it, saying, 'Become a river.'

children.text: tataḥ sā divyatoyā ca pūrṇāsitajalā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: Then that auspicious river, with divine water and full of dark water,
adorned with forests of lotuses and blue lotuses, began to flow as a great river.
<s>Mahādeva</s> addressed that exceedingly beautiful river:
'Because you have flowed forth from the water of my matted hair, O great river,
therefore you shall be the holy <s>Jaṭodakā</s>, the best of rivers.
Any man who bathes in you will be freed from all sins.'
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the Lord, said to the goddess about the son of <s>Śilāda</s>,
'This is your son,' and laid me down at her feet.
She smelled my head and stroked me with her hands.
Out of love for her son, with three streams from her breasts,
and with milk white as a conch, she anointed the god of gods as she gazed upon him.
Those three streams of hers then became flowing rivers,
and the blessed god <s>Bhava</s> called that river <s>Trisrotasā</s>.
Seeing the three-streamed river, the bull was filled with supreme joy,
and he bellowed; from that sound another river then arose.
That river became famed from the god of gods as <s>Vṛṣadhvani</s>.
A wondrous, auspicious crown, made of Jāmbūnada gold and set with every jewel,
his own marvelous and divine crown, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
the god, the bull-bannered Lord, bound upon my head.
And the two auspicious, divine earrings, adorned with diamond and vaiḍūrya,
the great god, <s>Maheśvara</s> himself, fastened on me.

children.text: māṃ tathābhyarcitaṃ vyomni dṛṣṭvā meghaiḥ prabhākaraḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing me thus honored in the sky, <s>Prabhākara</s>, with clouds,
anointed me, the son of <s>Śilāda</s>, with cloud-water, O sage.
From him, when he had been anointed then, a stream flowed forth in abundance;
because this river emerged from the gold, it came into being among the rivers.
The three-eyed god of gods called it <s>Svarṇodakā</s>.
And because a second auspicious river arose from the Jāmbūnada-gold crown,

children.text: prāvartata nadī puṇyā ūcur jambūnadīti tām
children.translated_text: they called that holy river <s>Jambūnadī</s>.
This place, called <s>Pañcanada</s>, lies near <s>Japyeśvara</s>.
Whoever reaches <s>Pañcanada</s>, bathes, and worships
<s>Japyeśvareśvara</s>, surely attains union with <s>Śiva</s>; there is no doubt.
Then the god <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, lord of all beings,
spoke to the goddess <s>Śarvāṇī</s>, <s>Umā</s>, the daughter born of the mountain:
"Goddess, I shall anoint the god <s>Nandīśvara</s> as lord of beings,

children.text: gaṇendraṃ vyāhariṣyāmi kiṃ vā tvaṃ manyase 'vyaye ||
children.translated_text: and I shall proclaim him lord of the gaṇas. What do you think, imperishable one?"
Hearing that speech of his, <s>Bhavānī</s>, her face delighted,

children.text: smayantī varadaṃ prāha bhavaṃ bhūtapatiṃ patim ||
children.translated_text: smiling, spoke to her husband <s>Bhava</s>, lord of beings and giver of boons:
"You ought to grant him lordship over all worlds
and also the status of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, O lord of gods; the son of <s>Śailādi</s> is my son."
Then the blessed <s>Śarva</s>, lord of the lords of all worlds,
the god of gods, the bull-bannered one, remembered the divine lords of the gaṇas.

Thus in the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the forty-third chapter, called "The Manifestation of <s>Nandikeśvara</s> and the Consecration-Mantra of <s>Nandikeśvara</s>," is concluded.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
By <s>Rudra</s>'s mere recollection the lords of the gaṇas arrived,
all with a thousand hands and weapons in a thousand hands.
They were three-eyed, great-souled, and honored even by the thirty gods,
like ten million fires of Time, wearing matted crowns.
Their faces were terrible with fangs; they were eternal, awakened, and stainless.
With crores upon crores of equal gaṇas, and themselves lords of gaṇas,
those countless great-souled beings came there filled with joy.

children.text: gāyantaś ca dravantaś ca nṛtyantaś ca mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: Singing, rushing, and dancing, those very mighty ones
played mouth-drums and other resounding instruments.
The gaṇas came by chariots, elephants, horses, and with lions and monkeys as vehicles,
and also mounted on golden, beautifully adorned aerial cars.
With kettledrums, mṛdaṅgas and the like, with paṇavas, ānakas, and gomukhas,
and with various other instruments, paṭahas and single-headed drums,
with the sounds of bherīs and murajas, and with āḍambaras and ḍiṇḍimas,
with mardalas, flutes, and vīṇās, and with various sounds of cymbals,
with darduras, hand-beats, kacchapas, and paṇavas as well,
those great yogins came to the divine assembly while the instruments were being played.
Those gaṇeśas, great beings and lords over the lords of all the gods,

children.text: praṇamya devaṃ devīṃ ca idaṃ vacanam abruvan ||
children.translated_text: bowed to the god and the goddess and spoke these words:
"Blessed lord, lord of gods, three-eyed bull-bannered one,

children.text: kimarthaṃ ca smṛtā deva ājñāpaya mahādyute ||
children.translated_text: for what purpose have we been remembered, O god? Command us, O greatly radiant one.

children.text: kiṃ sāgarāñśoṣayāmo yamaṃ vā saha kiṅkaraiḥ
children.translated_text: Shall we dry up the oceans, or <s>Yama</s> together with his servants?
Shall we kill <s>Mṛtyu</s>, the son of <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and slay the lotus-born one like a beast?

children.text: baddhvendraṃ saha devaiś ca saha viṣṇuṃ ca vāyunā
children.translated_text: Shall we bind <s>Indra</s> together with the gods, or <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with <s>Vāyu</s>,
or, filled with wrath, bring here the daityas together with the dānavas?
By your command, whose terrible misfortune shall we bring about today?
Or for whom is there to be a festival today, O god, for the attainment of every desire?"
To all those lords of the gaṇas, speaking in that way and approved by all,
the Lord, after honoring those hundreds of crores upon crores, spoke:
"Listen to the reason for which you, benefactors of the world, have been summoned here;
and after hearing it, with disciplined selves, do it without hesitation.
This <s>Nandīśvara</s> is our son, lord over all lords.
He is a brahmin, and he is your prosperous leader and commander.
Therefore, with my command and with all of you in agreement,
consecrate this lord, the great lord of yogins, as your commander."

children.text: evamuktā bhagavatā gaṇapāḥ sarva eva te
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the Blessed One, all those gaṇa-lords
agreed, saying "So be it," and then brought the requisites.
They brought for him an auspicious, divine, all-supporting seat
made of Jāmbūnada gold, resembling <s>Meru</s>, and charming.
It was made with many pillars and shone with the finest gold,
hung with strings of pearls and radiant with jewels and gems.
With pillars made of vaiḍūrya and covered with nets of little bells,
it was a pavilion, open on every side and furnished with lovely jewels.
Having made it and placed in its midst that excellent, auspicious seat,
they set before it a footstool shining like blue diamond.
For the placing of his feet they prepared two jars at its sides,
filled with supreme waters and with their mouths covered by lotuses.

children.text: kalaśānāṃ sahasraṃ tu sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: There were a thousand jars, made of gold and also of silver,
made of copper and of clay, filled with the waters of all tīrthas.

children.text: vāsoyugaṃ tathā divyaṃ gandhaṃ divyaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: A pair of garments, divine perfume as well,

children.text: keyūre kuṇḍale caiva mukuṭaṃ hārameva ca ||
children.translated_text: armlets, earrings, a crown, and a necklace too,
a parasol with a hundred ribs and a yak-tail fan:
these were given by that great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>, the supreme lord.
It was also splendid with a back pale like conch, necklace, and limbs,
and the moon-white fan had a golden handle and fine yak hair.
<s>Airāvata</s> and <s>Supratīka</s>, those two elephants, were greatly honored,
and a golden crown was made by <s>Viśvakarman</s>.

children.text: kuṇḍale cāmale divye vajraṃ caiva varāyudham
children.translated_text: There were two spotless divine earrings and the thunderbolt, the excellent weapon,
a cord made of jāmbūnada gold and also a pair of armlets.
And many other implements too, of various kinds,
the calm lords of the gaṇas, approved by the gods, brought from every side.

children.text: tato devāś ca sendrāś ca nārāyaṇamukhās tathā
children.translated_text: Then the gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, and those headed by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
the sages, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, and the nine <s>Brahmās</s>,

children.text: devaiś ca lokāḥ sarve te tato jagmurmudā yutāḥ
children.translated_text: and all the worlds together with the gods, went there filled with joy.
When all of them had arrived, the blessed supreme Lord
ordered <s>Pitāmaha</s> to perform the whole rite.
The blessed <s>Pitāmaha</s> too, by his command,
performed the whole consecration attentively.
Then, after worshiping him, <s>Brahmā</s> himself sprinkled him in consecration.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, then <s>Śakra</s>, and likewise the guardians of the worlds
consecrated the lord of the gaṇas according to rule, by <s>Śiva</s>'s command.
The sages also praised him, preceded by my father and grandfather.
When they had offered praise, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the whole world,
placing his joined palms upon his head, praised him attentively;

children.text: prāñjaliḥ praṇato bhūtvā jayaśabdaṃ cakāra ca ||
children.translated_text: standing with joined palms and bowing down, he also uttered cries of victory.
Then all the chiefs of the gaṇas, then the gods, then the asuras did the same.
Thus at that time he was praised and consecrated by the gods together with <s>Brahmā</s>.
A marriage too was performed there by order of the supreme lord.

children.text: marutāṃ ca sutā devī suyaśākhyā babhūva yā ||
children.translated_text: The goddess who was a daughter of the <s>Maruts</s> became known as <s>Suyaśā</s>.

children.text: labdhaṃ śaśiprabhaṃ chatraṃ tayā tatra vibhūṣitam
children.translated_text: A moon-bright parasol was received and adorned there by her.
There were also yak-tail fans, with groups of women whose hand-tips held the fans.

children.text: siṃhāsanaṃ ca paramaṃ tayā cādhiṣṭhitaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: The supreme lion-throne too was occupied by her together with me.
She was adorned with great splendor and with beautiful ornaments beginning with a crown.

children.text: labdho hāraś ca paramo devyāḥ kaṇṭhagatas tathā
children.translated_text: The supreme necklace too was received and placed upon the goddess's neck.

children.text: vṛṣendraś ca sito nāgaḥ siṃhaḥ siṃhadhvajas tathā ||
children.translated_text: There were the lordly bull, the white serpent, and the lion with the lion-banner,
as well as a chariot and a golden parasol, shining like the disk of the moon.

children.text: adyāpi sadṛśaḥ kaścinmayā nāsti vibhuḥ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Even today there is nowhere any mighty lord equal to me.
Taking her along with her family line and with relatives by marriage and kinsmen,

children.text: āruhya vṛṣamīśāno mayā devyā gataḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Lord <s>Śiva</s>, the ruler, mounted the bull and went with me and the goddess.

children.text: tadā devīṃ bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā mayā ca prārthayan gaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the goddess and <s>Bhava</s>, I and the gaṇas made our request.
Sages, divine seers, siddhas, and brahmins asked for the auspicious <s>Pāśupata</s> command.
Then, by the authority of the Lord, he gave that command to those worthy of it.
<s>Nandika</s>, husband of the mountain-born goddess, gave them that auspicious <s>Pāśupata</s> command.
Therefore, O sages, having received that command from the foremost sage,
they became devotees of <s>Bhava</s> at that time; therefore one should worship in this way.
But if one utters the name of <s>Bhava</s> without a bow of reverence,
his very grave sin is equal to that of ten brahmin-killers.
Therefore by every means one should utter it with salutation and the like.
One should make a bow of reverence at the beginning; then at the end one reaches the state of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge nandikeśvarābhiṣeko nāma catuścatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, the forty-fourth chapter, called The Consecration of <s>Nandikeśvara</s>.
The sages said:
O <s>Sūta</s>, you have clearly told the whole matter concerning <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Please tell us the all-self nature and the true form of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvas</s>, <s>Svar</s>, <s>Mahar</s>, <s>Jana</s>, and directly <s>Tapas</s>,
as well as <s>Satyaloka</s>, <s>Pātāla</s>, and crores of oceans of hells,
the stars, planets, moon, sun, <s>Dhruva</s>, and the seven seers,
and other aerial beings too, stand by his favor.
Created by him in this way, having him as their self, O best of twice-born seers,
<s>Śiva</s>, the aggregate form and self of all, is always established.
The deluded do not know that all-self, great-souled one,

children.text: na vijānanti saṃmūḍhā māyayā tasya mohitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great god <s>Maheśvara</s>, because they are bewildered by his māyā.

children.text: tasya devasya rudrasya śarīraṃ vai jagattrayam
children.translated_text: The threefold world is indeed the body of that god <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: tasmātpraṇamya taṃ vakṣye jagatāṃ nirṇayaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, after bowing to him, I shall explain the auspicious determination of the worlds.

children.text: purā vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ mayāṇḍasya yathā kṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly I told you all how the cosmic egg was made;
now I shall describe the nature of the worlds within the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>.

children.text: pṛthivī cāntarikṣaṃ ca svarmaharjana eva ca
children.translated_text: Earth, midspace, heaven, <s>Mahar</s>, and <s>Jana</s>,

children.text: tapaḥ satyaṃ ca saptaite lokāstvaṇḍodbhavāḥ śubhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Tapas</s> and <s>Satya</s>: these seven auspicious worlds are born from the egg.

children.text: adhastādatra caiteṣāṃ dvijāḥ sapta talāni tu
children.translated_text: Below these here, O twice-born ones, are the seven lower regions,
beginning with <s>Mahātala</s>; below them are the hells in order.
<s>Mahātala</s>, <s>Hematala</s>, adorned with all jewels,

children.text: prāsādaiś ca vicitraiś ca bhavasyāyatanais tathā ||
children.translated_text: with various palaces, and likewise with shrines of <s>Bhava</s>.
It was joined with <s>Ananta</s> and with wise <s>Mucukunda</s>,
a mighty king dwelling in the heaven of <s>Pātāla</s>.

children.text: śailaṃ rasātalaṃ viprāḥ śārkaraṃ hi talātalam
children.translated_text: O brahmins, <s>Rasātala</s> is rocky; <s>Talātala</s> is gravelly,
<s>Sutala</s> is said to be yellow, and <s>Vitala</s> has the luster of coral.

children.text: sitaṃ hi atalaṃ tacca talaṃ yacca sitetaram
children.translated_text: That <s>Atala</s> is indeed white, and the level called <s>Tala</s> is other than white.
As far as the extent of the earth reaches, O well-vowed ones, so far below are these regions.
And the full reckoning of all those lower worlds is correspondingly fixed.
The sky is one thousand yojanas, and indeed ten thousand besides.

children.text: lakṣaṃ saptasahasraṃ hi talānāṃ saghanasya tu
children.translated_text: For the dense expanse of the lower worlds it is one lakh and seven thousand,

children.text: vyomnaḥ pramāṇaṃ mūlaṃ tu triṃśatsāhasrakeṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: while the root-measure of the sky is thirty thousand.
With gold, O best of sages, and likewise with auspicious <s>Vāsuki</s>,
it is known as <s>Rasātala</s>, and is frequented by others as well.
Served by <s>Virocana</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, and others,
it is known as <s>Talātala</s>, endowed with every splendor.
Filled with the former gods, beginning with <s>Vināyaka</s> and led by <s>Kālanemi</s>,
and with others as well, that region is <s>Sutala</s>.
<s>Vitala</s> is occupied by dānavas and others, with <s>Tāraka</s> and <s>Agni</s> foremost,
and by serpents beginning with <s>Mahāntaka</s>, and by the asura <s>Prahlāda</s>.
Here <s>Vitala</s> is also famed as frequented by <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśva</s>,
by heroic <s>Mahākumbha</s>, and by wise <s>Hayagrīva</s>.
It is filled with <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>, and likewise with those headed by <s>Namuci</s>,
and that level is splendid with various other heroes as well.
In all those lower worlds, together with <s>Ambā</s>, the supreme Lord

children.text: skandena nandinā sārdhaṃ gaṇapaiḥ sarvato vṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is present with <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Nandin</s>, surrounded on every side by the lords of the gaṇas.
Above all the lower worlds are the seven and seven upper earth-levels;

children.text: kṣmātalāni dharā cāpi saptadhā kathayāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you of the earth and its sevenfold divisions.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge pātālavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the forty-fifth chapter, named 'Description of <s>Pātāla</s>', is concluded.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The earth, with its seven islands, is crowded with rivers and mountains,
and is adorned on every side with seven oceans.

children.text: jambūḥ plakṣaḥ śālmaliś ca kuśaḥ krauñcastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jambū</s>, <s>Plakṣa</s>, <s>Śālmali</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>,
<s>Śāka</s>, and the one named <s>Puṣkara</s> are the islands, in order, from within outward.
In all the seven islands, <s>Hara</s>, together with <s>Ambā</s> and surrounded by all his gaṇas,
assumes many forms of dress and makes his presence there.
The salt-water ocean, the sugarcane-juice ocean, the wine ocean, the ocean of ghee,
the ocean of curds, the milk ocean, and the sweet-water ocean come in that order.
In all these oceans, <s>Śiva</s>, with his gaṇas, is always present;
the glorious <s>Bhava</s>, taking the form of water, sports with waves as his arms.
In the milk ocean, <s>Hari</s> always reclines as the nectar of the milk ocean itself,
directly, through yogic sleep, with an intellect grounded in the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>.
When the blessed one awakens, the entire world awakens;

children.text: yadā suptastadā suptaṃ tanmayaṃ ca carācaram ||
children.translated_text: when he sleeps, the moving and unmoving universe, being filled with him, sleeps as well.
By him alone the whole universe is created, upheld, and protected,
and, by the grace of the supreme creator, the god of gods, it is withdrawn.
Those known as the <s>Suṣeṇas</s> worship the bull among persons,
<s>Aniruddha</s>, O best of sages, who bears conch, discus, and mace.
And those foremost among knowers of the self who meditate on <s>Aniruddha</s> as the Person
all become equal to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and endowed with every prosperity.

children.text: sanandanaś ca bhagavān sanakaś ca sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: Blessed <s>Sanandana</s>, <s>Sanaka</s>, and <s>Sanātana</s>,

children.text: vālakhilyāś ca siddhāś ca mitrāvaruṇakau tathā ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, the siddhas, and <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> too,

children.text: yajanti satataṃ tatra viśvasya prabhavaṃ harim
children.translated_text: constantly worship there <s>Hari</s>, the source of the universe.
In the seven islands stand many-peaked mountains of great rise.
Some mountains extend as far as the ocean, with caverns too,
and many lords of the earth existed through the weight of time.
By the power of the supreme lords, of the powerful father of the enemy of <s>Krauñca</s>,
in all the manvantaras here, past and future,
I shall proclaim to you the lords of the earth; I shall speak of them in the <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s> interval,
and in all the manvantaras, past and future.
All have equal self-regard and all have equal aims.
The grandsons of <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s> were of great strength.
The heroic sons of <s>Priyavrata</s> are celebrated here as ten in number:
<s>Āgnīdhra</s>, <s>Agnibāhu</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Medhātithi</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>,

children.text: jyotiṣmāndyutimān havyaḥ savanaḥ putra eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Jyotiṣmān</s>, <s>Dyutimān</s>, <s>Havya</s>, <s>Savana</s>, and another son.
<s>Priyavrata</s> anointed seven of them as kings over the seven islands.
He made mighty <s>Āgnīdhra</s> lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.
And <s>Medhātithi</s> was made by him lord of <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>.
He consecrated <s>Vapuṣmant</s> as king of <s>Śālmali</s>.
The king made <s>Jyotiṣmant</s> king in <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>.
He appointed <s>Dyutimant</s> as king in <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>.
<s>Priyavrata</s> made <s>Havya</s> lord of <s>Śākadvīpa</s>.
He also made <s>Savana</s> ruler of <s>Puṣkara</s>, O well-vowed ones.
In <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Savana</s> had a son, <s>Mahāvīta</s>.

children.text: dhātakī caiva dvāvetau putrau putravatāṃ varau
children.translated_text: And <s>Dhātakī</s> too: these two were sons, best among those who had sons.

children.text: mahāvītaṃ smṛtaṃ varṣaṃ tasya nāmnā mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The region named <s>Mahāvīta</s> is remembered after the name of that great-souled one.
And from the name of <s>Dhātakī</s> it is called <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>.
<s>Havya</s> too, the mighty lord of <s>Śākadvīpa</s>, begot sons.

children.text: jaladaṃ ca kumāraṃ ca sukumāraṃ maṇīcakam
children.translated_text: <s>Jalada</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Sukumāra</s>, <s>Maṇīcaka</s>,
<s>Kusumottara</s>, <s>Modākī</s>, and, as the seventh, the great tree <s>Mahādruma</s>.
Now <s>Alada</s> is said to be the first <s>varṣa</s> (region) of <s>Jalada</s>.
And <s>Kumāra</s>'s second is celebrated as <s>Kaumāra</s>.
The third, belonging to <s>Sukumāra</s>, is called <s>Sukumāra</s>,
and the fourth, belonging to <s>Maṇīcaka</s>, is here called <s>Māṇīcaka</s>.
The fifth region, belonging to <s>Kusumottara</s>, is indeed <s>Kusumottara</s>.
And the sixth region, belonging to <s>Modākī</s>, is proclaimed as <s>Modaka</s>.
The seventh, named after <s>Mahādruma</s>, is that <s>Mahādruma</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ tu nāmabhistāni sapta varṣāṇi tatra vai ||
children.translated_text: Thus those seven regions there are named by their own names.
The sons of <s>Dyutimat</s>, the lord of <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>, were also these:
<s>Kuśala</s>, <s>Manuga</s>, <s>Uṣṇa</s>, <s>Pīvara</s>, and <s>Andhakāraka</s>,
as well as <s>Muni</s> and <s>Dundubhi</s>; these were the sons of <s>Dyutimat</s>.
By their own names the auspicious countries resting in <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s> were named.
The country of <s>Kuśala</s> is <s>Kuśala</s>; that of <s>Manuga</s> is <s>Manonuga</s>.

children.text: uṣṇasyoṣṇaḥ smṛto deśaḥ pīvaraḥ pīvarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: The country of <s>Uṣṇa</s> is remembered as <s>Uṣṇa</s>, and <s>Pīvara</s> belongs to <s>Pīvara</s>.
The country of <s>Andhakāra</s> is said to be named <s>Andhakāraka</s>.

children.text: munerdeśo muniḥ prokto dundubher dundubhiḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The country of <s>Muni</s> is declared to be <s>Muni</s>, and that of <s>Dundubhi</s> is remembered as <s>Dundubhi</s>.
These seven peoples are radiant in <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>.
And in <s>Kuśadvīpa</s> there were seven brilliant ones of great vigor.
<s>Udbhida</s>, <s>Veṇumān</s>, <s>Dvairatha</s>, <s>Lavaṇa</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,
the sixth is remembered as <s>Prabhākara</s>, and the seventh as <s>Kapila</s>.
The first region is <s>Udbhida</s>, the second <s>Veṇumaṇḍala</s>,

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ dvairathaṃ caiva caturthaṃ lavaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: the third is <s>Dvairatha</s>, and the fourth is remembered as <s>Lavaṇa</s>.
The fifth is <s>Dhṛtimat</s>, the sixth the unsurpassed <s>Prabhākara</s>,
and the seventh, named <s>Kapila</s>, is proclaimed as belonging to <s>Kapila</s>.
The seven rulers of <s>Śālmala</s> were those sons of <s>Vapuṣmat</s>:

children.text: śvetaś ca haritaścaiva jīmūto rohitas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Harita</s>, <s>Jīmūta</s>, and <s>Rohita</s>,
as well as <s>Vaidyuta</s>, <s>Mānasa</s>, and likewise <s>Suprabha</s> as the seventh.

children.text: śvetasya deśaḥ śvetastu haritasya ca hāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The country of <s>Śveta</s> is <s>Śveta</s>, and that of <s>Harita</s> is <s>Hārita</s>.

children.text: jīmūtasya ca jīmūto rohitasya ca rohitaḥ
children.translated_text: That of <s>Jīmūta</s> is <s>Jīmūta</s>, and that of <s>Rohita</s> is <s>Rohita</s>.
<s>Vaidyuta</s> belongs to <s>Vaidyuta</s>, and <s>Mānasa</s> to <s>Mānasa</s>.
<s>Suprabha</s> belongs to <s>Suprabha</s>; these seven are the marks of the countries.
Now I shall tell of <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>, immediately after <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.
The seven sons of <s>Medhātithi</s> were kings and lords in <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>.
The eldest among them was <s>Śāntabhaya</s>; these are those seven regions.
After that <s>Śāntabhaya</s> came <s>Śiśira</s> and <s>Sukhodaya</s>,

children.text: ānandaś ca śivaścaiva kṣemakaś ca dhruvas tathā ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Kṣemaka</s>, and also <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: tāni teṣāṃ tu nāmāni saptavarṣāṇi bhāgaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Their own names were assigned, portion by portion, to the seven regions.
Those regions had formerly been established by them in the <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s> interval.
By those sons of <s>Medhātithi</s>, dwelling in <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>,
the people there were settled, furnished with the practices of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>.
In the regions beginning with <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s> and extending up to <s>Śākadvīpa</s>,
<s>dharma</s> is to be understood in five of them according to the division of <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>.

children.text: sukhamāyuḥ svarūpaṃ ca balaṃ dharmo dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Happiness, lifespan, bodily form, strength, and <s>dharma</s>, O best of twice-born ones,
are remembered as common to all these five dvīpas.
They are always devoted to worshiping <s>Rudra</s> and intent on <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: anye ca puṣkaradvīpe prajātāś ca prajeśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Others too were born in <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s> as lords of creatures,
overflowing with the nectar-like bliss of the nature of <s>Prajāpati</s> and <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge bhuvanakośe dvīpadvīpeśvarakathanaṃ nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the section on the world-containers, the forty-sixth chapter, called 'The Account of the Dvīpas and Their Lords,' is ended.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
King <s>Priyavrata</s> consecrated mighty <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, the eldest heir and son of <s>Kāmyā</s>,
as lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: so'tīva bhavabhaktaś ca tapasvī taruṇaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: He was exceedingly devoted to <s>Bhava</s>, an ascetic, ever youthful,
splendid, always intent on worshiping <s>Bhava</s>, possessed of wealth and wisdom, O bulls among twice-born men.
He had nine sons equal to Prajāpatis,
all devoted to <s>Maheśvara</s> and intent on <s>Mahādeva</s>.
The eldest was famed as <s>Nābhi</s>; his younger brother was <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>.
<s>Harivarṣa</s> was the third, and the fourth was <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.

children.text: ramyastu pañcamas tatra hiraṇmān ṣaṣṭha ucyate
children.translated_text: <s>Ramya</s> was the fifth there, and <s>Hiraṇmān</s> is called the sixth.
<s>Kuru</s> was the seventh among them; <s>Bhadrāśva</s> is remembered as the eighth.
The ninth was <s>Ketumāla</s>. Hear now of their countries.

children.text: nābhestu dakṣiṇaṃ varṣaṃ hemākhyaṃ tu pitā dadau ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Nābhi</s> the father gave the southern region named <s>Hema</s>.

children.text: hemakūṭaṃ tu yadvarṣaṃ dadau kiṃpuruṣāya saḥ
children.translated_text: The region called <s>Hemakūṭa</s> he gave to <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>.

children.text: naiṣadhaṃ yatsmṛtaṃ varṣaṃ haraye tatpitā dadau ||
children.translated_text: The region remembered as <s>Naiṣadha</s> the father gave to <s>Hari</s>.
To <s>Ilāvṛta</s> he gave the region where <s>Meru</s> stands in the middle.
The father gave to <s>Ramya</s> the region resting on <s>Nīlācala</s>.
The northern region called <s>Śveta</s> was given by the father to <s>Hiraṇmat</s>.
The northern <s>Śṛṅgavarṣa</s> the father gave to <s>Kuru</s>.
He assigned the region <s>Mālyavat</s> also to <s>Bhadrāśva</s>.
And he gave the <s>Gandhamādana</s> region to <s>Ketumāla</s>.
These, in order, are the nine great regions here.
Having consecrated those sons in those regions, <s>Āgnīdhra</s>,

children.text: yathākramaṃ sa dharmātmā tatastu tapasi sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: that righteous man, then took his stand in austerity in due order.
Refined by austerity, he became devoted to recitation and study.
Afterward, devoted to recitation and study, he became intent on meditation upon <s>Śiva</s>.
Those auspicious eight <s>varṣas</s> (regions), beginning with <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>,
have attainment by their very nature; they are chiefly happy without effort.

children.text: viparyayo na teṣvasti jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ na ca ||
children.translated_text: There is no contrary state for them, nor any fear of old age and death.
<s>Dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are not found among them, nor are there superior, inferior, or middling people.
In all the eight regions there is no condition of the ages for them.
And those who die in <s>Rudra</s>'s sacred field, whether moving beings or immobile ones,

children.text: bhaktāḥ prāsaṃgikāścāpi teṣu kṣetreṣu yānti te ||
children.translated_text: and devotees, even incidental ones, go to those sacred fields.
For their welfare <s>Rudra</s> created the eight sacred fields.

children.text: tatra teṣāṃ mahādevaḥ sānnidhyaṃ kurute sadā ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Mahādeva</s> always makes his presence for them.
Seeing <s>Mahādeva</s> in their hearts, the inhabitants of the eight sacred fields

children.text: sukhinaḥ sarvadā teṣāṃ sa eveha parā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are always happy; he alone is their supreme goal here.
Now I shall tell the origin of <s>Nābhi</s>; listen to it in this snowy region.
The wise <s>Nābhi</s> begot a son by <s>Merudevī</s>:
<s>Ṛṣabha</s>, best of kings, honored by all the kṣatriyas.
From <s>Ṛṣabha</s> was born <s>Bharata</s>, a hero, foremost of a hundred sons.
Then <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, loving his son, anointed <s>Bharata</s>
and, resorting to knowledge and detachment, having conquered the great serpents of the senses,
having established the supreme Lord, the <s>Paramātman</s>, in himself with his whole self,

children.text: nagno jaṭī nirāhāraścīrī dhvāntagato hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he became naked, matted-haired, without food, clad in rags, and withdrawn into darkness.
Free from expectation and having abandoned doubt, he attained the supreme <s>Śaiva</s> state.
He assigned the <s>varṣa</s> south of <s>Himādri</s> to <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: tasmāttu bhārataṃ varṣaṃ tasya nāmnā vidurbudhāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore the wise know that <s>varṣa</s> by his name as <s>Bhārata</s>.
<s>Bharata</s> had a wise and righteous son named <s>Sumati</s>.
He came into being, and <s>Bharata</s> installed that kingdom in him.
Having transferred his royal fortune to his son, the king entered the forest.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge bharatavarṣakathanaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the forty-seventh chapter, named 'The Description of <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s>.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: asya dvīpasya madhye tu merur nāma mahāgiriḥ
children.translated_text: In the middle of this island stands the great mountain named <s>Meru</s>,
the best of steadfast things, with peaks made of many kinds of jewels.
Its height is proclaimed as eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
It extends sixteen thousand below, and its breadth is likewise sixteen thousand.
Because it has the form of a shallow bowl, it is thirty-two thousand broad at the summit.
Its circumference, circular all around, is three times its breadth.
It was made golden by the touch of the auspicious limbs of <s>Maheśa</s>,
and is like a <s>dhattūra</s> flower, the abode of all the gods.
It is the playground of the gods, endowed with many wonders.
Such is the length, one hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>, of that great mountain.
Of that peaked mountain, sixteen thousand <s>yojanas</s> are below the earth,
and the remainder, O best of brahmins, is above the earth.
As for the measure of its base-length and the breadth from the mountain's base,
they said that the breadth of this mountain from the base is twice as great.
On the east it has the luster of ruby; on the south it resembles gold.
On the west it is like sapphire, and on the north it has the brilliance of coral.
On the eastern side is <s>Amarāvatī</s>, crowded with many palaces,
thronged with hosts of many gods and covered with lattices of jewels.
It has gateways of various forms, adorned with gold and jewels,
and golden, variegated arches, jewel-inlaid, standing along the road.
It is filled with women skilled in charming conversation and adorned with every ornament,
bent low by the weight of their breasts, their eyes rolling with intoxication.
It is crowded on every side with thousands of women and with apsarases,
with wondrous long ponds filled with blooming lotuses,
furnished with golden stairways and heaps of golden sand,
and with blue lotuses, lotuses, and fragrant golden lotuses as well.
Endowed with such ponds, and with rivers and streams,

children.text: virājate purī śubhrā tayāsau parvataḥ śubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the bright city shines; and by it that auspicious mountain shines.

children.text: tejasvinī nāma purī āgneyyāṃ pāvakasya tu
children.translated_text: In the southeast is the city named <s>Tejasvinī</s>, belonging to <s>Pāvaka</s>,
divine, equal to <s>Amarāvatī</s>, and endowed with every enjoyment.

children.text: vaivasvatī dakṣiṇe tu yamasya yamināṃ varāḥ
children.translated_text: In the south is <s>Vaivasvatī</s>, belonging to <s>Yama</s>, O best of the restrained,
surrounded by auspicious divine buildings made of <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.

children.text: nairṛte kṛṣṇavarṇā ca tathā śuddhavatī śubhā
children.translated_text: In the southwest is <s>Kṛṣṇavarṇā</s>, and likewise the auspicious <s>Śuddhavatī</s>.

children.text: tādṛśī gandhavantī ca vāyavyāṃ diśi śobhanā ||
children.translated_text: The similar <s>Gandhavantī</s> shines in the northwestern direction.

children.text: mahodayā cottare ca aiśānyāṃ tu yaśovatī
children.translated_text: <s>Mahodayā</s> is in the north, and <s>Yaśovatī</s> in the northeast.
At the ends of the mountain's directions they always shine in heaven.
The excellent mountain is the dwelling of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Maheśa</s>, and of others also,
holy, endowed with every enjoyment, and furnished with long ponds.
It is filled with siddhas and yakṣas, with gandharvas and foremost sages,
and with other fourfold hosts of beings of many forms.
Upon the mountain, O best of brahmins, resembling pure crystal,
there stands to the left a broad palace of a thousand stories.
In it is mighty-armed <s>Śarva</s>, whose eyes are <s>Soma</s>, the sun, and fire,
on a jeweled throne together with the goddess and with <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>.

children.text: harestadardhaṃ vistīrṇaṃ vimānaṃ tatra so'pi ca
children.translated_text: There too is <s>Hari</s>; his palace is half as broad as that,
divine and made of ruby, and to the south is that of <s>Padmaja</s>.

children.text: tasmin śakrasya vipulaṃ puraṃ ramyaṃ yamasya ca
children.translated_text: In it are the spacious, lovely cities of <s>Śakra</s> and of <s>Yama</s>,
of <s>Soma</s>, of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and then of <s>Nirṛti</s> and <s>Pāvaka</s>,
and of <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Rudra</s>, all around the abode of <s>Śarva</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ teṣāṃ vimāneṣu divyeṣu vividheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: in their respective divine palaces of various kinds.
In the northeast, in the sacred field of <s>Īśvara</s>, perpetual worship is established.
And with the <s>Siddheśvaras</s> is the blessed <s>Śailādi</s>, honored by his disciples.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, lord of the gods, sits there at ease with the perfected beings,

children.text: sanakaś ca sanandaś ca sadṛśāś ca sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sanaka</s> and <s>Sananda</s>, with thousands of others like them.
In that place, here and there, there is a ground of yoga, and here and there a ground of enjoyment.
There a splendid aerial palace shines, resembling the young sun.
There is also the auspicious abode of <s>Śailādi</s>; in it dwells the lord of the gaṇas.
There are thousands of attendants of the six-faced <s>Gaṇeśa</s> and of <s>Gaṇeśa</s> himself,
and of <s>Suyaśā</s>, <s>Sunetrā</s>, the Mothers, and <s>Madana</s>.
Around its base stands the river named <s>Jambūnadī</s>.
On its southern side is a beautiful <s>jambū</s> tree,
exceedingly high and very broad, giving fruit in every season.
All around <s>Meru</s> extends the auspicious region called <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
There some eat the fruits of the <s>jambū</s>, and others feed on nectar.
The enjoyers there are like <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold in appearance and are of many colors.
O Brahmins, this auspicious middle dvīpa rests at the foot of <s>Meru</s>.
It is furnished with nine varṣas, and with excellent rivers, streams, and mountains.
Now I shall describe accurately the nine-varṣa <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>,
with its extent, its circular measure, and its measurements in yojanas; listen.
Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: śatamekaṃ sahasrāṇāṃ yojanānāṃ sa tu smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: It is remembered as one hundred thousand yojanas in extent.
Each following dvīpa is twice as large as the preceding one, by thousands upon thousands.
The earth, together with the oceans, is remembered as extending for fifty crores,

children.text: dvīpaiś ca saptabhir yuktā lokālokāvṛtā śubhā ||
children.translated_text: auspicious, furnished with the seven dvīpas and enclosed by <s>Lokāloka</s>.
North of <s>Meru</s> is <s>Nīla</s>; north of that again is <s>Śveta</s>.
North of that is <s>Śṛṅgī</s>; O Brahmins, those three are mountains of the varṣas.

children.text: jaṭharo devakūṭaś ca pūrvasyāṃ diśi parvatau
children.translated_text: <s>Jaṭhara</s> and <s>Devakūṭa</s> are the two mountains in the eastern direction.
<s>Niṣadha</s> is south of <s>Meru</s>, and south of it is the mountain
known as <s>Hemakūṭa</s>; south of that is <s>Himavat</s>.
West of <s>Meru</s>, too, are two mountains, supporters of the earth:
<s>Mālyavān</s> and <s>Gandhamādana</s>; these two extend northward.
These kings of mountains are frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas.
The breadth of the space between each of them is nine thousand yojanas.

children.text: idaṃ haimavataṃ varṣaṃ bhārataṃ nāma viśrutam
children.translated_text: This region at <s>Himavat</s> is the famous varṣa named <s>Bhārata</s>.
Beyond it, at <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, is remembered the region named <s>Kiṃpuruṣa</s>.
From <s>Hemakūṭa</s> to <s>Niṣadha</s> is called <s>Harivarṣa</s>.
Beyond <s>Harivarṣa</s>, around auspicious <s>Meru</s>, is <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.
Beyond <s>Ilāvṛta</s>, at <s>Nīla</s>, is the famous region named <s>Ramyaka</s>.
Beyond <s>Ramya</s>, at <s>Śveta</s>, is the renowned <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>.

children.text: hiraṇmayātparaṃ cāpi śṛṅgī caiva kuruḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, at <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, is remembered <s>Kuru</s>.

children.text: dhanuḥsaṃsthe tu vijñeye dve varṣe dakṣiṇottare ||
children.translated_text: The two regions to the south and north should be understood as bow-shaped.
Four there are long, while <s>Ilāvṛta</s> is in the middle.

children.text: meroḥ paścimapūrveṇa dve tu dīrghetare smṛte ||
children.translated_text: To the west and east of <s>Meru</s>, two others are remembered as long in a different way.
Below <s>Niṣadha</s> the northern half of the altar is remembered,

children.text: vedyardhe dakṣiṇe trīṇi varṣāṇi trīṇi cottare ||
children.translated_text: and in the southern half of the altar there are three varṣas, and three in the northern half.
Between those two, with <s>Meru</s> in the center, <s>Ilāvṛta</s> should be known.
It lies south of <s>Nīla</s> and north of <s>Niṣadha</s>.
Extending northward is the great mountain named <s>Mālyavān</s>.
At its upper part it is spread out for two thousand yojanas.
Its length is declared to be thirty-four thousand yojanas.
To its west should be known the mountain <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
Its length should be known as equal to that of <s>Mālyavān</s>.
It extends evenly all around according to the breadth of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.
These six excellent mountains, the mountains of the varṣas, extend eastward.
On both sides they plunge into the eastern and western oceans.
<s>Himavat</s> is mostly snowy, while <s>Hemakūṭa</s> is golden.
<s>Niṣadha</s> is remembered as golden, shining like the young sun.
<s>Meru</s>, possessing four colors and gold, is remembered as rising upward.
It has a rounded circumference and rises in a square form.

children.text: nīlaś ca vaiḍūryamayaḥ śvetaḥ śuklo hiraṇmayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> is made of lapis lazuli, <s>Śveta</s> is white, and <s>Hiraṇmaya</s> is golden.
<s>Triśṛṅga</s> is the color of a peacock's tail and is made of fine gold, with three peaks.

children.text: evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktāḥ punaḥ śṛṇu girīśvarān
children.translated_text: Thus they have been stated briefly. Now hear again about the great mountains.

children.text: mandaro devakūṭaś ca pūrvasyāṃ diśi parvatau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mandara</s> and <s>Devakūṭa</s> are the two mountains in the eastern direction.
<s>Kailāsa</s>, <s>Gandhamādana</s>, and <s>Hemavān</s> are also mountains.
These extend eastward and are situated within the oceans.
<s>Niṣadha</s> and <s>Pāriyātra</s> are those two excellent mountains.

children.text: yathā pūrvau tathā yāmyāvetau paścimataḥ śritau ||
children.translated_text: Just as the former two, so these southern ones are established on the western side.
<s>Triśṛṅga</s> and <s>Jāruci</s> are the northern excellent mountains.
These extend eastward and are situated within the oceans.
The wise call these eight the boundary mountains.
That <s>Meru</s>, O best of twice-born ones, is a lofty golden mountain.
Its four feet, the best of mountains, stand in the four directions.
Supported by them, the earth with its seven dvīpas does not move.
Their length is taught as ten thousand yojanas.

children.text: pūrve tu mandaro nāma dakṣiṇe gandhamādanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the east is the one named <s>Mandara</s>; in the south, <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
<s>Vipula</s> is remembered on the western side, and <s>Supārśva</s> on the northern.
Four great trees have grown there, the banners of the dvīpa.
On the peak of <s>Mandara</s> mountain stands the great tree, the banner-bearing king,
a <s>kadamba</s>, the sacred tree, with long branches and a lofty crown.
And on the summit of the southern mountain, served by the gods,
there is a <s>jambū</s> tree, always bearing holy fruit and always adorned with garlands.
The banner-bearing <s>jambū</s> on the southern island is renowned in the worlds.
And on the western summit of the great mountain <s>Vipula</s>,
there has arisen a great <s>aśvattha</s>, a sacred tree.
And on the northern peak of <s>Supārśva</s> a great tree has grown:
a <s>nyagrodha</s> with vast trunk, extending over many yojanas.
Now I shall describe, in order, of those four lords of mountains
the delightful, non-human, season-pervading
and charming four forests, the playgrounds of the gods.
Learn them by name, the forests in the four directions.
In the east is the one called <s>Caitraratha</s>; in the south, <s>Gandhamādana</s>.
One should know <s>Vaibhrāja</s> in the west, and <s>Savitṛvana</s> in the north.

children.text: mitreśvaraṃ tu pūrve tu ṣaṣṭheśvaram ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: In the east is <s>Mitreśvara</s>, and next <s>Ṣaṣṭheśvara</s>.
In the west is <s>Varyeśvara</s>, and in the north <s>Āmrakeśvara</s>.
There are also four great lakes, O foremost sages,

children.text: yatra krīḍanti munayaḥ parvateṣu vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: where the sages sport on the mountains and in the forests.

children.text: aruṇodaṃ saraḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ mānasaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The eastern lake is <s>Aruṇoda</s>; the southern is remembered as <s>Mānasa</s>.
<s>Sitoda</s> is the western lake, and <s>Mahābhadra</s> the northern.

children.text: śākhasya dakṣiṇe kṣetraṃ viśākhasya ca paścime ||
children.translated_text: The field of <s>Śākha</s> lies to the south, and that of <s>Viśākha</s> to the west.
That of <s>Naigameya</s> is to the north, and that of <s>Kumāra</s> to the east.
East of <s>Aruṇoda</s> are mountain-lords remembered by name.

children.text: tāṃstu saṃkṣepato vakṣye na śakyaṃ vistareṇa tu
children.translated_text: I shall describe them briefly; it is not possible to do so in detail.
<s>Sitānta</s>, <s>Kuraṇḍa</s>, and <s>Kurara</s>, best of immovable mountains,
<s>Vikara</s>, <s>Maṇiśaila</s>, and <s>Vṛkṣavān</s>, best of mountains,
<s>Mahānīla</s>, then <s>Rucaka</s>, <s>Sabindu</s>, and <s>Dardura</s>,

children.text: veṇumāṃś ca sameghaś ca niṣadho devaparvataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Veṇumān</s>, <s>Samegha</s>, <s>Niṣadha</s>, and the divine mountain:

children.text: ityete parvatavarā hyanye ca girayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: these are the excellent mountains, and there are other mountains too.
These, east of <s>Mandara</s>, are declared to be abodes of siddhas.

children.text: teṣu teṣu girīndreṣu guhāsu ca vaneṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: On each of those lordly mountains, in caves and in forests,
there are divine <s>Rudra-kṣetras</s> (sacred fields of Rudra), and those of <s>Viṣṇu</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as well.
South of lake <s>Mānasa</s> here are great mountains.
I shall briefly tell all those that are being named.
<s>Śaila</s>, <s>Viśira</s>, and <s>Śikhara</s>, best of immovable mountains,
<s>Ekaśṛṅga</s>, <s>Mahāśūla</s>, <s>Gajaśaila</s>, and <s>Piśācaka</s>,
<s>Pañcaśaila</s>, then <s>Kailāsa</s>, and <s>Himavān</s>, best of mountains:
these are the exalted excellent mountains, frequented by the gods.

children.text: teṣu teṣu ca sarveṣu parvateṣu vaneṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: On each and every one of those mountains and in the forests
divine <s>Rudra-kṣetras</s> have been established by the best of gods.

children.text: digbhāge dakṣiṇe proktāḥ paścime ca vadāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those in the southern quarter have been stated; now I shall tell you those in the west.

children.text: apareṇa sitodaś ca surapaś ca mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: West of <s>Sitoda</s> are <s>Surapa</s>, mighty and strong,
<s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Madhumān</s>, <s>Añjana</s>, and likewise <s>Mukuṭa</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇaś ca pāṇḍuraścaiva sahasraśikharaś ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Pāṇḍura</s>, and the one called <s>Sahasraśikhara</s>,
the mountain-lord <s>Pārijāta</s>, and <s>Śrīśṛṅga</s>, best of immovable mountains.
These are the exalted excellent mountains, frequented by the gods.
All are in the western quarter and are endowed with <s>Rudra-kṣetras</s>.
North of lake <s>Mahābhadra</s> are mighty mountains.
Learn here briefly those that stand there and are being named:
<s>Śaṅkhakūṭa</s>, the great mountain, <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, <s>Haṃsaparvata</s>,

children.text: nāgaś ca kapilaścaiva indraśailaś ca sānumān ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Indraśaila</s> with its ridges,

children.text: nīlaḥ kaṇṭakaśṛṅgaś ca śataśṛṅgaś ca parvataḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Kaṇṭakaśṛṅga</s>, and the mountain <s>Śataśṛṅga</s>,
<s>Puṣpakośa</s>, <s>Praśaila</s>, and <s>Viraja</s>, best of immovable mountains,
as well as <s>Varāhaparvata</s> and <s>Mayūra</s>, best of mountains.
<s>Jārudhi</s> too is a lord of mountains; these are situated in the north.
On those divine mountains of the god of gods, the trident-bearing <s>Śūlin</s>,
there are countless divine aerial palaces, by the thousands.
Between these chief mountains, in due order,
there are inner valleys, lakes, and pleasure groves.

children.text: vasanti devā munayaḥ siddhāś ca śivabhāvitāḥ
children.translated_text: Gods, sages, and siddhas, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>, dwell there,
wearing hides, together with their wives, through the grace of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
In the bilva grove are <s>Kakubha</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and others beginning with <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Likewise, in the tāla grove the dwelling of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and the serpent-beings is declared.
In the uḍumbara grove is the abode of <s>Kardama</s> and of other great souls.
In the auspicious and holy mango grove dwell the vidyādharas and siddhas.
The nāgas and hosts of siddhas likewise have their station in the neem grove.
In the kiṃśuka grove is the dwelling of the sun, and also of <s>Rudra</s>'s gaṇa.
In the holy bījapūra grove the preceptor of the gods is established.
In the kaumuda grove are the great souls headed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the nyagrodha within the sthalapadma grove is the one who possesses endless coils.
<s>Śeṣa</s>, lord of all the worlds, abides there, exceedingly proud.

children.text: sa eva jagatāṃ kālaḥ pātāle ca vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: He himself is the Time of the worlds, and he is established in <s>Pātāla</s>.
He is a divine form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the teacher of the universe, directly the wielder of the plough.

children.text: śayanaṃ devadevasya sa hareḥ kaṅkaṇaṃ vibhoḥ
children.translated_text: He is the couch of the god of gods, and the bracelet of mighty <s>Hari</s>.
In the grove of jackfruit trees are <s>Śukra</s> along with the dānavas and others.
The kinnaras and serpent-beings are established in the <s>Viśākhaka</s> grove.
In the charming grove, with every kind of tree in countless multitudes,
<s>Nandīśvara</s> is established, praised by the foremost gaṇas.
In the midst of <s>Saṃtānakasthalī</s> is the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself, manifest before one's eyes.
Thus the forest-dwellers in the forests have been described in brief;

children.text: asaṃkhyātā mayāpyatra vaktuṃ no vistareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: but they are countless, and even by me they cannot be spoken of here in detail.
Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the forty-ninth chapter is ended.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
On the peak of <s>Śitānta</s>, in the auspicious <s>Pārijāta</s> forest, is <s>Śakra</s>;
to its east is that broad summit of <s>Kumudādri</s>.
Eight cities of the <s>Dānava</s>s are proclaimed there, O best of twice-born men,
in the holy <s>Suvarṇakoṭara</s>, belonging to the great-souled <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.
They say there are sixty-eight cities of the <s>Nīlaka</s>s, O best of twice-born men;

children.text: mahānīle'pi śailendre purāṇi daśa pañca ca ||
children.translated_text: and on the lordly mountain <s>Mahānīla</s> there are also fifteen cities.
Of the chief horse-faced beings and of the <s>Kinnara</s>s, O men of good vows,
on the great mountain <s>Veṇusaudha</s> there are three cities of the <s>Vidyādhara</s>s.
On <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is the illustrious <s>Garuḍa</s>; on <s>Karañja</s> is <s>Nīlalohita</s>.
At <s>Vasudhāra</s> the dwelling of the <s>Vasu</s>s is celebrated.
On the excellent mountain <s>Ratnadhāra</s> are those of the great-souled seven seers,
seven holy stations, together with abodes of perfected beings.
On the noble mountain <s>Ekaśṛṅga</s> is the place of great <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: gajaśaile tu durgādyāḥ sumedhe vasavas tathā ||
children.translated_text: on <s>Gajaśaila</s> are <s>Durgā</s> and the others, and on <s>Sumedha</s> are the <s>Vasu</s>s.
There too the <s>Āditya</s>s, the <s>Rudra</s>s, and the two <s>Aśvin</s>s have made their dwellings;
and on the noble mountain <s>Hemakakṣa</s> there are eighty cities of the gods.
On <s>Sunīla</s> are dwellings of <s>Rākṣasa</s>s, numbering five hundred crores;
on <s>Pañcakūṭa</s> there were cities amounting to five crores in number.
On <s>Śataśṛṅga</s> are a hundred cities of the immeasurably powerful <s>Yakṣa</s>s;

children.text: tāmrābhe kādraveyāṇāṃ viśākhe tu guhasya vai ||
children.translated_text: on <s>Tāmrābha</s> are those of the descendants of <s>Kadrū</s>, and on <s>Viśākha</s>, indeed, is that of <s>Guha</s>.
On <s>Śvetodara</s>, O best sages, is that of the great-souled <s>Suparṇa</s>;
on <s>Piśācaka</s> is <s>Kubera</s>'s, and on <s>Harikūṭa</s> is the house of <s>Hari</s>.
On <s>Kumuda</s> is the abode of the <s>Kinnara</s>s, and on <s>Añjana</s> the dwelling of the <s>Cāraṇa</s>s;
on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the residence of the <s>Gandharva</s>s, and on <s>Pāṇḍura</s> are seven cities
of the <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, O lords of brahmins, furnished with every enjoyment.
On the mountain <s>Sahasraśikhara</s> are those of the fierce-acting <s>Daitya</s>s;

children.text: purāṇāṃ tu sahasrāṇi sapta śakrāriṇāṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: there are seven thousand cities of the enemies of <s>Śakra</s>, O twice-born men.
On <s>Mukuṭa</s> is the dwelling of the serpents; on <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, O lordly sages,
of <s>Vaivasvata</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the lord of serpents,
and on the lordly mountain <s>Takṣaka</s>, there are four sanctuaries.
Of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and great-souled <s>Guha</s>,
and of <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and likewise of other great-souled ones,
there are chief sanctuaries even on the boundary mountains.
The cave-dwelling lord of <s>Śrīkaṇṭhādri</s>, the abode of all, is there with <s>Umā</s>.
The sovereignty belongs to <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, lord of all the gods;
and the activity of this cosmic egg proceeds from <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, without doubt.
<s>Ananteśa</s> and the others, each in this way guardians of a cosmic egg,
are called universal emperors; after them, here, are the <s>Vidyeśvara</s>s.
The places established by <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> here, in summary,
on the boundary mountains, now hear; I shall describe them.
This whole universe, the moving and unmoving world, is established by <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>,
down to <s>Kālāgniśiva</s>; how could I describe it in full detail?

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge bhuvanavinyāsoddeśasthānavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the fiftieth chapter, called 'Brief Description of the Arrangement of the Worlds and the Places,' is ended.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In the middle, on the mountain <s>Devakūṭa</s>, on the beautifully shining <s>Mahākūṭa</s>,
with the radiance of gold, beryl, ruby, sapphire, and hessonite,
and made of other chief jewels as well, stainless and auspicious,
rich with hundreds of thousands of branches and adorned with every kind of tree,
decorated with <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>puṃnāga</s>, <s>bakula</s>, and <s>āsana</s> trees,
filled with <s>pārijātaka</s> trees and attended by flocks of many kinds of birds,
variegated with hundreds of many minerals and crowded with varied blossoms,
with hanging flowers upon its slopes and thronged with many groups of beings,
with pure, sweet drinking water and furnished with many springs,
and adorned with many waterfalls strewn with flowers,
embellished by flowing streams that carry flower-rafts along,
there is a tree of glossy color, with a great root and many trunks,
lovely, with dense shade, extending over a circle of ten yojanas.
There is a forest called <s>Bhūtavana</s>, an abode of many hosts of beings.
There, of the great-souled god <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
is a radiant shrine, adorned with great jewels,
provided with a golden enclosure and decorated with jeweled gateways,

children.text: sphāṭikaiś ca vicitraiś ca gopuraiś ca samanvitam ||
children.translated_text: and furnished with crystal and many-colored towers.
It has lion-thrones made of jewels, with auspicious coverings,
well spread out upon the earth and auspiciously occupied by <s>Śarva</s>.
It is filled with unfading garlands and excellent houses of many colors,
and with very wonderful halls furnished with crystal pillars.
It is accompanied by all the lords of beings, worshiped by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Upendra</s>,
by attendants with faces of boars, elephants, lions, bears, tigers, and camels,
and by others with faces of vultures and owls, and also with faces of deer, camels, and goats,
by various <s>pramatha</s>s, stout, auspicious, and like mountain peaks,
terrible, tawny-haired, shaggy, and mighty-armed,
bearing forms of many colors and standing in many different shapes,
with blazing faces and blazing conduct, auspicious, headed by <s>Nandīśvara</s>,
and resembling <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, endowed with the powers beginning with minuteness.
It is never empty of immortals, nor of great assemblies.
There the gods continually perform worship of the Lord of beings.
With jharjharas, conches, drums, kettledrums, dindimas, and gomukhas,
with graceful songs and measured dancing and roaring sounds,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, the lord of the <s>pramathas</s>, was indeed worshiped by the <s>pramathas</s>,
by siddhas, seers, gods, gandharvas, and by great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>.
There <s>Śaṅkara</s> was worshiped by others also, led by <s>Upendra</s>.
There is that shell-bright mountain with lovely, distinct peaks,
<s>Kailāsa</s>, the dwelling of the great-souled yaksa-king <s>Kubera</s>,
the residence of crores of yaksas and of other great beings as well.
There too is the great shrine of <s>Bhava</s>, the god of gods.
In that shrine <s>Soma</s>, <s>Hara</s>, always dwells together with his hosts.
There is the lotus-filled river named <s>Mandākinī</s>, broad in water,
with stairways of gold and jewels on the auspicious peak of <s>Kubera</s>.
It has lotuses made of jambunada gold, endowed with fragrance and pleasant touch,
and great blue lotuses with petals of blue vaidurya, filled with fragrance.
It is adorned likewise with clusters of kumudas and with great lotuses,
and is frequented by yaksa and gandharva women and by apsarases.
Its waters are touched by gods, danavas, gandharvas, yaksas, raksasas, and kinnaras;
the holy river <s>Mandākinī</s> is auspicious.
On its northern side is the auspicious shrine of <s>Bhava</s>.
Rich in vaidurya gems, there imperishable <s>Śaṅkara</s> dwells.
O twice-born ones, on the eastern and southern bank of golden <s>Nandā</s>,
there is a forest rich in thousands of birds, crowded with beasts and birds.
There too, with his hosts and with <s>Ambā</s>, he sports in a house like a mountain.

children.text: nandāyāḥ paścime tīre kiṃcid vai dakṣiṇāśrite ||
children.translated_text: On the western bank of <s>Nandā</s>, somewhat toward the south,
there is a city named <s>Rudrapurī</s>, crowded with many palaces.

children.text: tatrāpi śatadhā kṛtvā hyātmānaṃ cāmbayā saha ||
children.translated_text: There too, having divided himself a hundredfold, together with <s>Ambā</s>,
he sports with his hosts and with <s>Ambā</s>; that is called a shrine of <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus there are hundreds of thousands of shrines of <s>Śarva</s>,
on every island, O best of sages, on mountains and in forests,
on the banks of rivers, streams, and ponds, and at the junctions of oceans.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: nadyaś ca bahavaḥ proktāḥ sadā bahujalāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: Many rivers have been described, always auspicious and rich in water,
born from lakes and countless in number, O best of twice-born ones.
Those facing east and south, and those auspicious ones arising in the north,
as well as the pure ones whose course is westward, are proclaimed in each region.
That ocean of heavenly water, which is called <s>Soma</s>,
is the support of all beings and the source of nectar for the gods.
From it has issued a holy-watered river that moves through the sky,
set in motion on the seventh path of wind and filled with nectar-like water.
Following the heavenly lights and attended by hosts of lights,
it is joined with the sky and with thousands of crores of stars.
It revolves day after day, just as <s>Soma</s> does.
Eighty-four thousand
yojanas high is great <s>Meru</s>, delightful as the playground of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>.

children.text: tatrāsīno yataḥ śarvaḥ sāmbaḥ saha gaṇeśvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since <s>Śarva</s>, together with <s>Ambā</s> and the lords of the hosts, sits there
and sports for a very long time, therefore that auspicious river has holy water.

children.text: giriṃ meruṃ nadī puṇyā sā prayāti pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: That holy river goes around Mount <s>Meru</s> in pradaksina.
Its waters, divided by their speed and by the wind,
fell upon all four inner peaks of <s>Meru</s>.
Having passed all the mountains on every side, portion by portion,
it entered the great ocean by command of the god of gods.
From it have issued hundreds and thousands of rivers,
many of which are proclaimed in all the islands, mountains, and regions.
The minor rivers are countless; as <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, they have water from the heavenly <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
In <s>Ketumāla</s> the men are dark, and all eat panasa fruit.
The women have the lustre of blue lotuses, and the lifespan is remembered as ten thousand years.
