In <s>Bhadrāśva</s> the people are white in color, and the women resemble rays of the moon.
All eat dark mangoes; they are free from affliction and fond of pleasure.
They live ten thousand years, absorbed in <s>Śiva</s>.
They are, as it were, exceedingly golden, with their minds offered to the Lord.
Likewise, in <s>Ramaṇaka</s>, the beings live on banyan fruits.
They live for ten thousand years and fifteen hundreds besides.
All of them are fair, wholly devoted to meditation on <s>Śiva</s>.
The <s>Hairaṇmayas</s> are greatly fortunate and dwell in golden forests.
For eleven thousand years and fifteen hundreds besides,
they live there, sustaining themselves by eating aśvattha fruit.
They are exceedingly like gold, with their minds offered to the Lord.
In <s>Kuruvarṣa</s>, the <s>Kurus</s> have fallen down from heaven.
All are born from sexual union, nourished by milk and feeding on milk.
They are mutually attached and have the nature of cakravaka birds.
They are free from illness and sorrow, always enjoying happiness.
For thirteen thousand years and fifteen hundreds besides,
those mighty ones live, and they do not resort to another's wife.
The <s>Kurus</s>, dwellers in heaven, die together,
joyful, fully grown, and eating all food as nectar.
They are always moonstone-like and always possessed of youth,
dark-limbed, their bodies always serving as the seat of every ornament.
But in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, even there, is the splendid <s>Kuruvarṣa</s>.
There is the moon-bright aerial palace of <s>Śambhu</s>, the moon-crested lord.

children.text: varṣe tu bhārate martyāḥ puṇyāḥ karmavaśāyuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: In the region of <s>Bhārata</s>, mortals are meritorious, their lifespans governed by their deeds;
they are said to live a hundred years, of many <s>varṇa</s>s (social classes), with small bodies.
They are engaged in worshiping many gods and desire the fruits of many kinds of action;
they are endowed with many kinds of knowledge and aims, yet are weak and enjoy little.
Some are in <s>Indradvīpa</s>, and likewise in <s>Kaseruka</s>;
some have gone to <s>Tāmradvīpa</s>, and some to the land called <s>Gabhastimat</s>.

children.text: nāgadvīpaṃ tathā saumyaṃ gāndharvaṃ vāruṇaṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: They have gone also to <s>Nāgadvīpa</s>, to pleasant <s>Saumya</s>, to <s>Gāndharva</s>, and to <s>Vāruṇa</s>;
some are <s>mleccha</s>s and <s>Pulinda</s>s, born from many different peoples.
In the east are the <s>Kirāta</s>s, and at its western end the <s>Yavana</s>s are remembered;

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyā madhye śūdrāś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in the middle are brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras everywhere.
They remain established, maintaining themselves by sacrifice, warfare, and trade;
this mutual social dealing of theirs takes place here among one another.
Among the <s>varṇa</s>s, in their own duties, it is joined with <s>dharma</s> (religious order), wealth, and desire;
and the resolve and self-conception of the <s>āśrama</s>s (life-stages) proceed according to rule.
Here human activity has heaven and liberation as its purpose;
and for them there are the actions proper to the ages, but nowhere else, O foremost sages.
In <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>, the duration of men is ten thousand years;
the men are golden in color, and the women are like apsarases.

children.text: anāmayā hyaśokāś ca sarve te śivabhāvitāḥ
children.translated_text: They are free from illness and sorrow, and all are devoted to <s>Śiva</s>;
pure in disposition and golden in radiance, living with their wives, they feed on plakṣa fruit.
In <s>Harivarṣa</s> too, human beings are like great silver in appearance;
all have fallen from the world of the gods and are in every way godlike in form.
They all worship <s>Hara</s>, the lord of all, and drink the auspicious juice of sugarcane;

children.text: na jarā bādhate tena na ca jīryanti te narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore old age does not trouble them, nor do those men grow decrepit.
Human beings live there for ten thousand years;
the middle region that I have mentioned is the varṣa named <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.

children.text: na tatra sūryastapati na te jīryanti mānavāḥ
children.translated_text: There the sun does not burn, and human beings do not grow old;

children.text: candrasūryau na nakṣatraṃ na prakāśam ilāvṛte ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Ilāvṛta</s> there is no moon, no sun, no constellation, and no such light.
Lotus-bright, lotus-faced, with eyes like lotus petals,
and fragrant like lotus petals, they are born there, formed by existence.
Feeding on the juice of jambu fruit, motionless and fragrant,
they are born there from the world of the gods, indeed ageless and deathless.
Those best of men live for thirteen thousand years,
the measure of their lifespan, in the divine varṣa of <s>Ilāvṛta</s>.

children.text: jaṃbūphalarasaṃ pītvā na jarā bādhate tvimān
children.translated_text: After drinking the juice of jambu fruit, old age does not afflict these people;

children.text: na kṣudhā na klamaścāpi na jano mṛtyumāṃs tathā ||
children.translated_text: there is no hunger, no fatigue, and no person subject to death there.
There is a gold called <s>jāmbūnada</s>, an ornament of the gods;
it arises there radiant, with the appearance of an indragopa insect.
Thus I have described, in brief and not in full detail,
the colors, lifespans, foods, and so forth belonging to the nine varṣas.
On <s>Hemakūṭa</s> should be understood the gandharvas and hosts of apsarases;
on <s>Niṣadha</s> are all the nāgas, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>.
Thirty-three mighty sacrificial gods sport there;
on <s>Nīla</s>, made of beryl, are the siddhas and stainless brahmarṣis.

children.text: daityānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca śvetaḥ parvata ucyate
children.translated_text: The white mountain is said to belong to the daityas and dānavas;
and the mountain <s>Śṛṅgavān</s> is always the dwelling of the ancestors.
<s>Himavān</s> belongs to the chief yakṣas, to the beings, and to the Lord;
among all mountains <s>Mahādeva</s> is present with <s>Hari</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Ambā</s>.

children.text: nandinā ca gaṇaiścaiva varṣeṣu ca vaneṣu ca
children.translated_text: With <s>Nandin</s> and with the gaṇas, in the varṣas and in the forests,
on <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Triśṛṅga</s>, abides the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s>.

children.text: siddhairdevaiś ca pitṛbhir dṛṣṭo nityaṃ viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: He is always seen especially by siddhas, gods, and ancestors.

children.text: nīlaś ca vaiḍūryamayaḥ śvetaḥ śuklo hiraṇmayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s> is made of beryl; <s>Śveta</s> is white and golden;
<s>Triśṛṅgavān</s> has the color of a peacock's tail and is of refined gold.
These kings of mountains are established in <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge bhuvanakośasvabhāvavarṇanaṃ nāma dvipañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, called 'Description of the Nature of the World-Storehouse,' in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In the islands beginning with <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>, there are seven mountains in each of the seven;
the varṣa-mountains are set in every direction, straight and extended lengthwise.

children.text: plakṣadvīpe tu vakṣyāmi sapta divyān mahācalān
children.translated_text: In <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s> I shall describe seven divine great mountains;
<s>Gomedaka</s> is the first here, and the second is called <s>Cāndra</s>.

children.text: tṛtīyo nārado nāma caturtho dundubhiḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The third is named <s>Nārada</s>, and the fourth is remembered as <s>Dundubhi</s>;

children.text: pañcamaḥ somako nāma sumanāḥ ṣaṣṭha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: the fifth is named <s>Somaka</s>, and the sixth is called <s>Sumanas</s>.

children.text: sa eva vaibhavaḥ prokto vaibhrājaḥ saptamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: That same is said to be <s>Vaibhava</s>; <s>Vaibhrāja</s> is remembered as the seventh.
These seven mountains have been declared especially in <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>.
There are seven in <s>Śālmalidvīpa</s>; I shall tell them in order.
<s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Uttama</s>, and the mountain <s>Balāhaka</s>;

children.text: droṇaḥ kaṅkaś ca mahiṣaḥ kakudmān saptamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Droṇa</s>, <s>Kaṅka</s>, <s>Mahiṣa</s>, and <s>Kakudmān</s> is remembered as the seventh.

children.text: kuśadvīpe tu saptaiva dvīpāś ca kulaparvatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Kuśadvīpa</s> too there are seven divisions and ancestral mountains;

children.text: tāṃstu saṃkṣepato vakṣye nāmamātreṇa vai kramāt
children.translated_text: I shall describe them briefly, in order, by name alone.
<s>Vidruma</s> is said to be the first, and the second is <s>Hemaparbata</s>.
The third is named <s>Dyutimān</s>, and the fourth is remembered as <s>Puṣpita</s>;
<s>Kuśeśaya</s> is the fifth, and the sixth is remembered as <s>Harigiri</s>.
The seventh is the glorious <s>Mandara</s>, the dwelling-place of <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: mandā iti hyapāṃ nāma mandaro dhāraṇād apām ||
children.translated_text: 'Mandā' is indeed a name for waters; because it holds the waters, it is <s>Mandara</s>.
There, directly present, is the bull-marked lord, <s>Viśveśa</s>, stainless <s>Śiva</s>;
the blessed <s>Soma</s>, together with <s>Nandī</s>, dwells in the excellent golden house.
Formerly <s>Maheśvara</s>, pleased by <s>Mandara</s>'s austerity,

children.text: avimukte mahākṣetre lebhe sa paramaṃ varam ||
children.translated_text: in the great sacred field <s>Avimukta</s>, granted him the supreme boon.
And <s>Mahādeva</s>, requested for the sake of residence together with <s>Ambā</s>,
came from <s>Avimukta</s> and made his dwelling on that <s>Mandara</s>.

children.text: sanandī sagaṇaḥ somas tenāsau tanna muñcati
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Soma</s>, together with <s>Nandī</s> and the hosts, does not leave it.
But in <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s> there are seven family mountains, beginning with <s>Krauñca</s>.
<s>Krauñca</s>, then <s>Vāmanaka</s>, and third <s>Andhakāraka</s>;
beyond <s>Andhakāra</s> too is the mountain named <s>Divāvṛt</s>.
Beyond <s>Divāvṛt</s> is also the mountain called <s>Vivinda</s>;
and beyond <s>Vivinda</s> is the great mountain <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>.
Beyond <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> is said to be <s>Dundubhisvana</s>;
these seven jewel-made mountains belong to <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s>.

children.text: śākadvīpe ca girayaḥ sapta tāṃstu nibodhata
children.translated_text: And in <s>Śākadvīpa</s> there are seven mountains; learn them now.
<s>Udaya</s>, <s>Raivata</s>, and <s>Śyāmaka</s>, O best of sages;
and the splendid silver mountain, the beautiful <s>Āmbikeya</s>;
beyond <s>Āmbikeya</s> is a lovely one, furnished with all medicinal herbs,
likewise called <s>Kesarī</s>, from which the wind is born.
In <s>Puṣkara</s> there is one splendid mountain, a single great rock,
raised high with variegated, jewel-made peaks and masses of stone;
in the eastern half of that island stands the great <s>Citrasānu</s>.
It rises upward fifty thousand yojanas,
and downward thirty-four thousand yojanas, that great mountain.
In the other half of the island lies the mountain <s>Mānasottara</s>, encircling it,
standing near the shore like a newly risen moon.
It rises upward fifty thousand yojanas,
and is just as broad, circular in measure from side to side.
That same earth-bearing <s>Mānasa</s> stands in the western half of the island;
it is one great-ridged mountain, made twofold by its arrangement.

children.text: tasmindvīpe smṛtau dvau tu puṇyau janapadau śubhau
children.translated_text: On that island two auspicious and holy regions are remembered,
silver regions encircling the mountain <s>Mānasa</s>.

children.text: mahāvītaṃ tu yadvarṣaṃ bāhyato mānasasya tu
children.translated_text: The region called <s>Mahāvīta</s> is outside <s>Mānasa</s>;
the one inside it is called <s>Dhātakīkhaṇḍa</s>.
<s>Puṣkara</s> is surrounded by the ocean of sweet water;
that ocean stretches all around to the same breadth as <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s>.
In breadth and in circular extent it is equal to <s>Puṣkara</s>.
Thus the islands are enclosed by seven oceans, each corresponding to the seven islands.
The ocean immediately after an island is indeed the seventh in order;
in this way the mutual increase of islands and oceans is to be understood.
Beyond <s>Puṣkara</s>, following its curve, there stands the great
ocean of sweet water, encircling it on every side.
Beyond it is seen the great arrangement of the world:
a golden land, twice as large, all like a single slab of stone.
Beyond that is the mountain forming the boundary circle;
it is called <s>Lokāloka</s>, both illuminated and unilluminated.
As far as that visible-and-invisible mountain extends, so far this earth extends, O twice-born men.
Its height is remembered as ten thousand yojanas.
Just so great is the breadth of that great mountain <s>Lokāloka</s>.
On this nearer half of it the rays of the sun move;

children.text: parārdhe tu tamo nityaṃ lokālokastataḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: but on the further half there is constant darkness; therefore it is remembered as <s>Lokāloka</s>.

children.text: evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ prokto bhūrlokasya ca vistaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus the extent of <s>Bhūrloka</s> has been stated in brief.

children.text: ā bhānorvai bhuvaḥ svastu ā dhruvānmunisattamāḥ
children.translated_text: From the sun up to <s>Bhuvas</s> and <s>Svar</s>, up to <s>Dhruva</s>, O best of sages,
there are the seven rims of wind, beginning with <s>Āvaha</s>, established there.
<s>Āvaha</s>, <s>Pravaha</s>, and then <s>Anuvaha</s>,
<s>Saṃvaha</s>, <s>Vivaha</s>, and above that <s>Parāvaha</s>,
and <s>Parivaha</s>, O twice-born men: these are the seven rims of wind.
The clouds, the sun, the moon, the constellations and zodiacal signs,

children.text: grahāṇi ṛṣayaḥ sapta dhruvo viprāḥ kramādiha
children.translated_text: the planets, the seven seers, and <s>Dhruva</s>, O brahmins, are arranged here in order.
From the surface of the earth upward as far as <s>Dhruva</s> are fifteen niyutas of yojanas.
The solar orb is one niyuta above the surface of the earth.
The chariot of <s>Bhāskara</s> is sixteen thousand yojanas; above it,
<s>Meru</s> is eighty-four thousand yojanas above the earth's surface.
Extending for a crore of yojanas, <s>Maharloka</s> lies above <s>Dhruva</s>.
<s>Janaloka</s> is two crores beyond <s>Maharloka</s>, O twice-born men;
<s>Tapoloka</s> is regarded as four crores beyond <s>Janaloka</s>.
<s>Brahmaloka</s> is six crores beyond the <s>Prājāpatya</s> world;
these seven holy worlds have been described within this cosmic egg, O twice-born men.

children.text: adhaḥ saptatalānāṃ tu narakāṇāṃ hi koṭayaḥ
children.translated_text: Below the seven underworlds are crores of hells,
twenty-eight in number, ending with <s>Māyā</s> and beginning with <s>Ghora</s>.
Sinners are cooked in them according to their own respective deeds.
Among them are all the hells beginning with <s>Raurava</s> and ending with <s>Avīci</s>.
They say that there are, in particular, five hells for each one.
At the beginning I described the cosmic egg and the coverings of the cosmic egg,
and, because the occasion allowed much expansion, the creation of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.
Cosmic eggs of this kind should be understood to exist by thousands of crores.

children.text: sarvagatvāt pradhānasya tiryag ūrdhvam adhas tathā
children.translated_text: Because <s>Pradhāna</s> is all-pervading, sideways, upward, and downward,
in all these cosmic eggs there are fourteen worlds.
For every cosmic egg, O tigers among twice-born men, <s>Maheśvara</s> is their cause,
both within the eggs, outside the eggs, and in the coverings of the eggs.
At the end of darkness and beyond darkness, he abides as the eight-formed one.
Of this self, of <s>Maheśa</s>, of wise <s>Mahādeva</s>,
though bodiless, behold, the whole body belongs to the supreme self.
Of this eight-formed <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, who is as a householder,
divine <s>Prakṛti</s> is the wife, and the progeny are <s>mahat</s> and the rest.
All beings who identify with bodies are his cattle and servants.
The blessed one, the infinite person, without beginning or end, together with the seven beginning with <s>Pradhāna</s>,
he himself is the form of <s>Pradhāna</s>, then sixteen-limbed, and <s>Maheśvara</s> with eight bodies.

children.text: ājñābalāttasya dharā sthiteha dharādharā vāridharāḥ samudrāḥ
children.translated_text: By the power of his command the earth stands here, and so do the mountains, the clouds, the oceans,

children.text: jyotirgaṇaḥ śakramukhāḥ surāś ca vaimānikāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāś ca ||
children.translated_text: the host of luminaries, the gods headed by <s>Śakra</s>, the dwellers in aerial palaces, and the stationary and moving beings.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yakṣaṃ lakṣaṇairhīnamīśaṃ dṛṣṭvā sendrāste kimetattviheti
children.translated_text: When they saw the yakṣa, the lord, devoid of distinguishing marks, <s>Indra</s> and the gods, seeing him, wondered, 'What indeed is this?'
Going to the yakṣa with determination, <s>Agni</s> and the others then became bereft of their power.

children.text: dagdhuṃ tṛṇaṃ vāpi samakṣamasya yakṣasya vahnirna śaśāka viprāḥ
children.translated_text: Fire was not able to burn even a blade of grass before that yakṣa, O brahmins,
nor could <s>Vāyu</s> move the blade of grass, nor the other lords of the immortals exercise their own powers.

children.text: tadā svayaṃ vṛtraripuḥ surendraiḥ sureśvaraḥ sarvasamṛddhihetuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the foe of <s>Vṛtra</s> himself, the lord of the gods with the lords of the gods, the cause of all prosperity,

children.text: sureśvaraṃ yakṣamuvāca ko vā bhavānitītthaṃ sa kutūhalātmā ||
children.translated_text: asked the lordly yakṣa, 'Who are you?' Thus he spoke, full of curiosity.

children.text: tadā hyadṛśyaṃ gata eva yakṣastadāṃbikā haimavatī śubhāsyā
children.translated_text: Then the yakṣa disappeared; and then fair-faced <s>Ambikā</s>, daughter of <s>Himavat</s>,
<s>Umā</s>, splendidly adorned with many bright ornaments, appeared there afterward.
The gods headed by <s>Śakra</s> asked that greatly radiant <s>Umā</s>, the unborn daughter of <s>Himavat</s>:
'O shining lady, O <s>Ambikā</s>, what is this yakṣa-form that has appeared?'
Hearing that, <s>Umā Ambikā</s> said, 'That yakṣa is beyond your perception.' Then the gods, with <s>Śakra</s>,
bowed to her, lion-gaited <s>Umā</s>, the unborn one, red, white, and black.
Honored by all the lords of the immortals, she, the source of all activity of gods and asuras,

children.text: ahaṃ purāsaṃ prakṛtiś ca puṃso yakṣasya cājñāvaśagetyathāha ||
children.translated_text: then said, 'In the beginning I was <s>Prakṛti</s>, and I am subject to the command of the person and of the yakṣa.'
Therefore, O twice-born men, by the command of that unborn one, the cosmic egg arose from the unborn,

children.text: ajaś ca aṇḍādakhilaṃ ca tasmājjyotirgaṇairlokamajātmakaṃ tat ||
children.translated_text: and the unborn one arose from the egg, and from him came the whole world, made of the unborn, together with the hosts of luminaries.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge bhuvanakośavinyāsanirṇayo nāma tripañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, named 'Determination of the Arrangement of the World-Receptacle,' in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall briefly describe the movement of the luminaries within the cosmic egg,
after considering the divine regions, for the understanding of the courses of the planets.

children.text: mānasopari māhendrī prācyāṃ meroḥ purī sthitā
children.translated_text: Above <s>Mānasa</s>, on the eastern side of <s>Meru</s>, stands the city of <s>Mahendra</s>;
to the south is that of the son of the sun, and the western city belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: saumye somasya vipulā tāsu digdevatāḥ sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: In the northern quarter is the spacious city of <s>Soma</s>; in these the directional deities reside.

children.text: amarāvatī saṃyamanī sukhā caiva vibhā kramāt ||
children.translated_text: They are, in order, <s>Amarāvatī</s>, <s>Saṃyamanī</s>, <s>Sukhā</s>, and <s>Vibhā</s>.
Above the world-protectors, on every side, during the southern course,

children.text: kāṣṭhāṃ gatasya sūryasya gatir yā tāṃ nibodhata ||
children.translated_text: listen to the path of the sun as it reaches its limit.
In the southern progression the sun runs like a discharged arrow,
taking up the wheel of the luminaries and continually going around.

children.text: purāntago yadā bhānuḥ śakrasya bhavati prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: When the powerful sun reaches the city of <s>Śakra</s>,

children.text: sarvaiḥ sāyamanaiḥ sauro hyudayo dṛśyate dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the solar rising is seen by all the people of <s>Saṃyamanī</s>, O twice-born men.

children.text: sa eva sukhavatyāṃ tu niśāntasthaḥ pradṛśyate
children.translated_text: The same sun is seen at the end of night in <s>Sukhavatī</s>;

children.text: astameti punaḥ sūryo vibhāyāṃ viśvadṛg vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the sun, the all-seeing lord, sets again in <s>Vibhā</s>.
As I have described him in <s>Amarāvatī</s>, O repeller of thieves,

children.text: tathā saṃyamanīṃ prāpya sukhāṃ caiva vibhāṃ khagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too the sky-goer, having reached <s>Saṃyamanī</s>, <s>Sukhā</s>, and <s>Vibhā</s>, proceeds.
When it is afternoon in the southeast, it is forenoon in the southwest, O twice-born men;
then in the northwestern quarter it is the later part of the night, very dreadful.
In the northeast it is the first part of the night; such is this motion everywhere.

children.text: evaṃ puṣkaramadhye tu yadā sarpati vāripaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when the lord of waters moves in the middle of <s>Puṣkara</s>,
he goes over a thirtieth part of the earth in a single muhūrta.
Now learn this number of yojanas for a muhūrta.
It is remembered as thirty-one full hundred-thousands,
and likewise fifty thousand more besides.
This is the per-muhūrta motion of the great-souled <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: etena gatiyogena yadā kāṣṭhāṃ tu dakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: By this manner of motion, when the winged one reaches the southern limit,
and also the northern quarter on the following day,
then, in the middle of <s>Puṣkara</s>, he revolves during the southern course.
On the mountain <s>Mānasottara</s>, the mighty-radiant <s>Vibhāvasu</s>,
the lord, traverses a full hundred and eighty circles.
The outer and the inner circles are said to belong to the northern and southern courses.

children.text: pratyahaṃ carate tāni sūryo vai maṇḍalāni tu ||
children.translated_text: The sun travels those circles day by day.
Just as the rim of a potter's wheel turns swiftly,
so the god turns swiftly in the southern progression.
Therefore he crosses a greater stretch of ground in a short time.
In the southern course the sun does so swiftly in twelve muhūrtas.
By day the sun travels thirteen and a half lunar mansions,
and at night he travels the same number of lunar mansions in eighteen muhūrtas.
Just as the middle of a potter's wheel creeps along slowly,
so in the northern course the sun creeps with slow movement.
Therefore, over a long time, it traverses only a small portion of the earth.
That chariot of <s>Bhānu</s> is occupied by the <s>Āditya</s>s and by sages as well,
by <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Apsaras</s>es, <s>Grāmaṇī</s>s, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.
The thousand-rayed one illumines in front, behind, and also below,

children.text: ūrdhvataś ca karaṃ tyaktvā sabhāṃ brāhmīmanuttamām
children.translated_text: and above, casting his ray toward the unsurpassed assembly of <s>Brahmā</s>.
With waters cast forth by the sages, at twilight, the night-wanderers

children.text: hatvā hatvā tu samprāptān brāhmaṇaiścarate raviḥ
children.translated_text: who come on are slain again and again; with the brahmins <s>Ravi</s> moves on.
At the end of the northern course the day is eighteen <s>muhūrta</s>s,
and even then he moves with slow pace.
At night <s>Ravi</s> passes thirteen and a half lunar mansions with twelve <s>muhūrta</s>s,
and by day he passes the same lunar mansions with eighteen <s>muhūrta</s>s.

children.text: tato mandataraṃ nābhyāṃ cakraṃ bhramati vai yathā
children.translated_text: Then the wheel turns more slowly at the hub, as indeed it does,

children.text: mṛtpiṇḍa iva madhyastho dhruvo bhramati vai tathā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Dhruva</s>, standing in the middle like a lump of clay, turns in just that way.
The knowers of ancient lore say that a day and night consist of thirty <s>muhūrta</s>s.
Between the two limits the circles revolve,
just as the nave of a potter's wheel remains there in its place.
<s>Auttānapāda</s>, the foremost of planets, turns together with the planets.

children.text: gaṇo munijyotiṣāṃ tu manasā tasya sarpati
children.translated_text: The host of sages and luminaries moves toward him in thought,
and, presided over by him, <s>Bhānu</s> stands again, drawing in
water from every side with his rays, the god together with the wind.
The fixed status of <s>Auttānapāda</s> as <s>Dhruva</s> was always obtained by the favor
of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by <s>Auttānapāda</s>, on account of his father.

children.text: āpaḥ pītāstu sūryeṇa kramante śaśinaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: The waters drunk by the sun proceed in due order to the moon,
and from the moon the waters flow out in due order toward the clouds.
The mass of water-bearing clouds, struck by the wind,
sends forth creation upon the earth; by that the sun makes it shine.

children.text: toyasya nāsti vai nāśaḥ tadaiva parivartate ||
children.translated_text: There is no destruction of water; at that very point it changes form.
For the welfare of all living beings, this course was fashioned by <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: bhūrbhuvaḥ svas tathā hyāpo hyannaṃ cāmṛtameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Earth, midspace, heaven, and likewise the waters, food, and immortality

children.text: prāṇā vai jagatāmāpo bhūtāni bhuvanāni ca
children.translated_text: are the waters; waters are the breaths of the worlds, the beings, and the realms.
What need is there to say much here? This whole moving and unmoving world
is established under the lordship of blessed <s>Śiva</s> over the waters.
The god who is lord over the waters is celebrated precisely as <s>Bhava</s>.
The whole world has <s>Bhava</s> as its nature; what wonder is there in this?
The <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-hood of the god, of mighty <s>Hari</s>, was made by the waters.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the abode of the worlds, and the waters are his abodes.
When moving and unmoving things are being burned, they issue forth in smoke-like form,

children.text: yā yā ūrdhvaṃ māruteneritā vai tāstāstvabhrāṇyagninā vāyunā ca ||
children.translated_text: and whatever is driven upward by the wind becomes clouds through fire and wind.
Thus the conjunction of smoke, fire, and wind is called a cloud.
Because it rains waters it is called <s>abhra</s>, and thousand-eyed <s>Indra</s> is lord of the cloud.
A cloud arising from sacrificial smoke is always beneficial to twice-born men.
A cloud produced from the smoke of a forest fire is remembered as beneficial to the forest.
A cloud arising from the smoke of the dead will be inauspicious,
and one risen from the smoke of an abhicāra fire brings destruction to beings, O twice-born men.
Thus, according to the particular kind of smoke, there is benefit and harm for the worlds.
Therefore a man should cover smoke produced by abhicāra rites.
If a twice-born man performs abhicāric smoke without covering it,
then, when it is directed in this way, it will become a cause of destruction for the world.
Clouds are reservoirs of waters here for six months, O well-vowed ones,
and they rain for the welfare of the worlds at the command of the wind.
Thunder here is born of wind, and lightning is born of fire.
The origin of clouds here is threefold, O bulls among sages.
Because clouds do not fall away, and because they rain, they are called <s>megha</s>.
Those carrying fuel, those belonging to <s>Viriñci</s>, and those born from wings are separate kinds.
For the first, smoke from fire is set in motion through contact with fuel,
and the origin of the second kind is through the exhaled wind of <s>Viriñci</s>.
Then the others arise from the wings of the mountains, cut off by <s>Maghavat</s>.
The fiery clouds are auspicious, abiding in the region of <s>Āvaha</s>.
All those born from <s>Viriñci</s>'s breath arise from the trunk of <s>Pravaha</s>.

children.text: pakṣajāḥ puṣkarādyāś ca varṣanti ca yadā jalam ||
children.translated_text: The wing-born ones, beginning with <s>Puṣkara</s>, rain water when their time comes.
Silent ones, noisy ones, and those with harmful directions have their functions in due order through these kinds.
They give scant rain for a long time and have cold winds.
The <s>Jīvaka</s> clouds too are weak and devoid of lightning and sound.
They stand only at the distance of a <s>krośa</s> from the surface of the earth.

children.text: ardhakrośe tu sarve vai jīmūtā girivāsinaḥ
children.translated_text: At half a <s>krośa</s> are all the mountain-dwelling clouds.
The clouds are at the measure of a <s>yojana</s>; because of their potency, they give much water.
From the surface of the earth down to the ground, O twice-born men, they are endowed with the quality of lightning.

children.text: teṣāṃ teṣāṃ vṛṣṭisargaṃ tredhā kathitamatra tu ||
children.translated_text: Here the discharge of rain for each of them has been described as threefold.
The wing-born and kalpa-born clouds are all very great, arising from the mountains.

children.text: kalpānte te ca varṣanti rātrau nāśāya śāradāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the end of a kalpa they rain at night, in autumn, for destruction.

children.text: pakṣajāḥ puṣkarādyāś ca varṣanti ca yadā jalam
children.translated_text: And when the wing-born clouds beginning with <s>Puṣkara</s> rain water,
then everything becomes ocean, and there the Lord lies down at night.
For the fiery, breath-born, and wing-born clouds, O best of twice-born sages,

children.text: jaladānāṃ sadā dhūmo hyāpyāyana iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: smoke is always remembered as the nourishment of the water-givers.
All <s>Pauṇḍra</s> rains are lightning-born and give cool crops.
Fallen in the regions of <s>Puṇḍra</s>, the cold sprays of the nāgas are snowy.
The Gāṅgā rain, born from the waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, is driven on by <s>Parjanya</s> through the <s>Parāvaha</s> winds,

children.text: nagānāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca diggajānāṃ samākulam ||
children.translated_text: crowded with mountains, rivers, and the elephants of the quarters.
And the water, separated from the clouds, went to the unfathomable depth.
The breath called <s>Parāvaha</s> carries that weight connected with <s>Ambikā</s>,
and, passing beyond the husband of <s>Menā</s>, O twice-born men, the highest remainder of rain
comes to <s>Bhārata-varṣa</s> for the increase of the western borderlands.

children.text: vṛṣṭayaḥ kathitā hyadya dvidhā vastu vivṛddhaye
children.translated_text: Thus today rains have been described as twofold for the increase of things.
For the two kinds of crops I shall speak briefly, according to my understanding.
The creator of rains is the sun, greatly radiant, all-seeing and powerful.
He too, directly, O best of twice-born men, is <s>Īśāna</s>, the supreme <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: sa eva tejastvojastu balaṃ viprā yaśaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: He himself is radiance, energy, strength, O priests, and fame itself.

children.text: cakṣuḥ śrotraṃ mano mṛtyurātmā manyur vidig diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is sight, hearing, mind, death, the self, wrath, the intermediate quarters, and the quarters.

children.text: satyaṃ ṛtaṃ tathā vāyuraṃbaraṃ khacaraś ca saḥ
children.translated_text: He is truth, cosmic order, wind, the sky, and the mover in the sky.
He is the world-protector, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and directly <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He is thousand-rayed, glorious, eight-handed, and most auspicious.
He has the body of the half-woman lord, is three-eyed, and is the ruler of the gods.
By his favor alone rain has here become manifold, O twice-born men.
In order to release it a thousandfold, he takes up water with his rays.
For him, when considered carefully, there is neither destruction nor increase of water.
The wind, established by <s>Dhruva</s>, again draws rain together.

children.text: grahān niḥsṛtya sūryāt tu kṛtsne nakṣatramaṇḍale
children.translated_text: Having gone forth from the planets and from the sun into the whole circle of constellations,
at the end of its course it enters the sun, directed by <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge jyotiścakre sūryagatyādikathanaṃ nāma catuḥpañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the auspicious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the fifty-fourth chapter, called “The Description of the Solar Course and So Forth in the Stellar Wheel.”
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: sauraṃ saṃkṣepato vakṣye rathaṃ śaśina eva ca
children.translated_text: I shall briefly describe the solar chariot and that of the moon,

children.text: grahāṇām itareṣāṃ ca yathā gacchati cāmbupaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those of the other planets, and how the water-drinker moves.
The solar chariot was created by <s>Brahmā</s>; it exists according to its purpose,
and it was fashioned from the limbs of the year, O bulls among twice-born sages.
It is furnished with a wheel having three naves and five spokes,
golden, the abode of all the gods, belonging to <s>Bhāskara</s>.
It is remembered as nine thousand <s>yojana</s>s in breadth and length.
The pole and shaft, in measure, are twice the chariot platform.
It is yoked with unattached horses, stationed according to where the wheel is;

children.text: vājinastasya vai sapta chandobhir nirmitāstu te ||
children.translated_text: its horses are seven, and they are made from the Vedic metres.
They are fastened to the side of the wheel, and the axle is fixed in <s>Dhruva</s>.
With its horses and wheel it revolves, and <s>Dhruva</s> revolves together with the axle.
That axle, together with the single wheel, revolves, impelled by <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: prerako jyotiṣāṃ dhīmān dhruvo vai vātaraśmibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhruva</s>, wise impeller of the lights, does so by means of wind-ropes.
Two ropes of the chariot are attached to the ends of the yoke and axle.
Bound by a rope to the yoke and axle, it revolves by means of <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: bhramato maṇḍalāni syuḥ khecarasya rathasya tu
children.translated_text: As the sky-moving chariot revolves, its circular courses come into being.

children.text: yugākṣakoṭī te tasya dakṣiṇe syandanasya hi ||
children.translated_text: Those two ends of its yoke and axle are on the southern side of the chariot.

children.text: dhruveṇa pragṛhīte vai vicakrāśve ca rajjubhiḥ
children.translated_text: When they are grasped by <s>Dhruva</s> with ropes, though the wheel and horses are irregular,
those two ropes follow <s>Dhruva</s> as he revolves.
The end of the yoke and axle of this chariot that moves on waves of wind
revolves in every direction like a rope fastened to a peg.
As it turns, its two ropes, in the circles of the northern course,

children.text: vardhete dakṣiṇe caiva bhramatā maṇḍalāni tu ||
children.translated_text: lengthen; and in the southern course also the circles turn.

children.text: ākṛṣyete yadā te vai dhruveṇādhiṣṭhite tadā
children.translated_text: When those two are drawn in by <s>Dhruva</s>, when they are controlled by him,
then the sun, situated inside, travels through the circles.
Between the two <s>kāṣṭhā</s>s there are one hundred and eighty circles.
When the two ropes are again released by <s>Dhruva</s>,

children.text: tathaiva bāhyataḥ sūryo bhramate maṇḍalāni tu
children.translated_text: then likewise the sun travels through the circles on the outside.

children.text: udveṣṭayan sa vegena maṇḍalāni tu gacchati ||
children.translated_text: Unwinding them, he goes through the circles with speed.

children.text: devāścaiva tathā nityaṃ munayaś ca divāniśam
children.translated_text: The gods and likewise the sages, constantly, day and night,
worship the god <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, the lord.
Together with his chariot he is attended by gods, by <s>Āditya</s>s, and by sages,
and by <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Apsaras</s>es, grāmaṇīs, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasa</s>s.

children.text: ete vasanti vai sūrye dvau dvau māsau krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: These dwell in the sun, two months each, in order.
With their splendors they nourish <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Śiva</s>.
The sages praise <s>Ravi</s> with their own woven words,
and the <s>Gandharva</s>s and <s>Apsaras</s>es worship him with dance and song.
The grāmaṇīs, <s>Yakṣa</s>s, and <s>Bhūta</s>s gather up the reins.

children.text: sarpā vahanti vai sūryaṃ yātudhānā anuyānti ca ||
children.translated_text: The serpents carry the sun, and the <s>Yātudhāna</s>s follow after him.
The <s>Vālakhilya</s>s surround <s>Ravi</s> from sunrise and lead him to setting.

children.text: ityete vai vasantīha dvau dvau māsau divākare ||
children.translated_text: Thus these dwell here in <s>Divākara</s>, two months each.

children.text: madhuś ca mādhavaścaiva śukraś ca śucireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Śuci</s>,
<s>Nabha</s> and <s>Nabhasya</s>, O lords of priests, and likewise <s>Iṣa</s> and <s>Ūrja</s>,

children.text: sahaḥsahasyau ca tathā tapasyaś ca tapaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and also <s>Sahas</s> and <s>Sahasya</s>, then <s>Tapasya</s> and again <s>Tapas</s>:

children.text: ete dvādaśa māsāstu varṣaṃ vai mānuṣaṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these twelve are the months, the human year, O twice-born men.

children.text: vāsantikas tathā graiṣmaḥ śubho vai vārṣikas tathā
children.translated_text: Spring, summer, the auspicious rainy season,

children.text: śāradaś ca himaścaiva śaiśira ṛtavaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: autumn, the dewy season, and late winter are remembered as the seasons.

children.text: dhātāryamātha mitraś ca varuṇaścendra eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, then <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: vivasvāṃścaiva pūṣā ca parjanyo'ṃśur bhagas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Aṃśu</s>, and likewise <s>Bhaga</s>.

children.text: tvaṣṭā viṣṇuḥ pulastyaś ca pulahaścātrireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Atri</s> too,
and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Bhṛgu</s>, best of the wise;

children.text: bhāradvājo gautamaś ca kaśyapaś ca kratus tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, and likewise <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Kaṅkaṇīkara</s>;

children.text: takṣakaś ca tathā nāga elāpatras tathā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Takṣaka</s>, and the nāga <s>Elāpatra</s>, O twice-born ones,
and likewise <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, and another remembered as <s>Airāvata</s>;
<s>Dhanañjaya</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and likewise <s>Karkoṭaka</s> is remembered,
and <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>, and <s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Nārada</s>;
<s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s>, best of sages, and excellent <s>Viśvāvasu</s>,
then <s>Ugrasena</s>, <s>Suruci</s>, and another, <s>Parāvasu</s>;
the very splendid <s>Citrasena</s>, and <s>Ūrṇāyu</s>, all well-vowed,
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Sūryavarcā</s>, and the goddess <s>Kṛtasthalā</s> herself;
fair-faced, fair-hipped, divine <s>Puñjikasthalā</s>,
<s>Menakā</s>, <s>Sahajanyā</s>, then <s>Pramlocā</s>, smiling brightly;

children.text: anumlocā ghṛtācī ca viśvācī corvaśī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Anumlocā</s>, <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, <s>Viśvācī</s>, and likewise <s>Urvaśī</s>,
she known as <s>Pūrvacitti</s>, and the goddess <s>Tilottamā</s> herself;
and lotus-faced <s>Rambhā</s>; <s>Rathakṛt</s>, <s>Grāmaṇī</s>, and auspicious <s>Śubha</s>,
<s>Rathaujā</s>, <s>Rathacitra</s>, and <s>Subāhu</s>, and <s>Rathasvana</s>;
and <s>Varuṇa</s>, and likewise another, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and auspicious <s>Senajit</s>,
<s>Tārkṣya</s>, <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, <s>Kṣatajit</s>, and likewise <s>Satyajit</s>;

children.text: rakṣohetiḥ prahetiś ca pauruṣeyo vadhas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Rakṣoheti</s> and <s>Praheti</s>, and <s>Pauruṣeya</s> and <s>Vadha</s>,
<s>Sarpa</s>, <s>Vyāghra</s>, then <s>Āpa</s>, <s>Vāta</s>, <s>Vidyut</s>, and <s>Divākara</s>;
<s>Brahmopeta</s>, lord of rākṣasas, and likewise <s>Yajñopeta</s>;

children.text: ete devādayaḥ sarve vasantyarke krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: all these, beginning with the gods, dwell in the sun in due sequence.
These are the deities presiding over the stations: twelve groups of seven,
the twelve gods, beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s> and ending with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, have been proclaimed.
They strengthen the supreme sun, the radiant one, with their rays;
the sages beginning with <s>Pulastya</s> and ending with <s>Kauśika</s>, O best of sages,
twelve in number, praise the sun with hymns in proper order.
The auspicious nāgas, beginning with <s>Vāsuki</s> and ending with <s>Aśvatara</s>,
also twelve in number, carry the great god in this same order.
In sequence, the excellent gandharvas, beginning with <s>Tumburu</s> and ending with <s>Sūryavarcā</s>,
worship him with songs, twelve foremost gandharvas.
The divine apsarases, beginning with <s>Kṛtasthalā</s> and ending with <s>Rambhā</s>,
all worship the sun with graceful dances in proper order.
The divine grāmaṇīs, beginning with <s>Rathakṛt</s> and ending with <s>Satyajit</s>,
twelve in number, take hold of his reins in sequence.
Those ending with <s>Yajñopeta</s>, beginning with <s>Rakṣoheti</s>, go along,
these twelve armed rākṣasas too, in proper order.

children.text: dhātāryamā pulastyaś ca pulahaś ca prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Prajāpati</s>;
the serpent <s>Vāsuki</s> and <s>Kaṅkaṇīka</s>, those two;
<s>Tumburu</s> and <s>Nārada</s>, the two gandharvas, best among singers;
the apsaras <s>Kṛtasthalā</s>, and likewise <s>Puñjikasthalā</s>;
the two grāmaṇīs <s>Rathakṛt</s> and <s>Rathaujā</s>;
<s>Rakṣoheti</s> and <s>Praheti</s> are declared to be yātudhānas.
This group dwells in the sun during the months <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: vasanti grīṣmakau māsau mitraś ca varuṇaś ca ha
children.translated_text: During the two summer months, <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> indeed dwell there,

children.text: ṛṣiratrirvasiṣṭhaś ca takṣako nāga eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the seers <s>Atri</s> and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and the nāga <s>Takṣaka</s> too,

children.text: menakā sahajanyā ca gandharvau ca hāhāhūhūḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Menakā</s> and <s>Sahajanyā</s>, and the two gandharvas <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s>,
the two grāmaṇīs named <s>Subāhu</s> and <s>Rathacitra</s>,
and <s>Pauruṣeya</s> and <s>Vadha</s>, declared to be yātudhānas.

children.text: ete vasanti vai sūrye māsayoḥ śuciśukrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: These dwell in the sun during the two months <s>Śuci</s> and <s>Śukra</s>.
Then again other deities dwell here in the sun:

children.text: indraścaiva vivasvāṃś ca aṅgirā bhṛgureva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vivasvat</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> and <s>Bhṛgu</s> too;

children.text: elāpatras tathā sarpaḥ śaṅkhapālaś ca tāvubhau
children.translated_text: then <s>Elāpatra</s> the serpent, and <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, those two;
<s>Viśvāvasu</s> and <s>Ugrasena</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Rathasvana</s>;

children.text: pramlocā caiva vikhyātā anumlocā ca te ubhe
children.translated_text: and the renowned <s>Pramlocā</s> and <s>Anumlocā</s>, those two;

children.text: yātudhānās tathā sarpo vyāghraścaiva tu tāvubhau ||
children.translated_text: and the yātudhānas <s>Sarpa</s> and <s>Vyāghra</s>, those two.
This group dwells in the sun during <s>Nabhas</s> and <s>Nabhasya</s>.
<s>Parjanya</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s>, and then <s>Bharadvāja</s> and <s>Gautama</s>;
<s>Dhanañjaya</s> and <s>Airāvata</s>, with <s>Suruci</s> and <s>Parāvasu</s>;
the foremost apsaras <s>Ghṛtācī</s> and the very beautiful <s>Viśvācī</s>;

children.text: senajicca suṣeṇaś ca senānīr grāmaṇīś ca tau
children.translated_text: and <s>Senajit</s> and <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, those two commanders and grāmaṇīs;

children.text: āpo vātaś ca tāvetau yātudhānāvubhau smṛtau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āpa</s> and <s>Vāta</s>, those two, are both remembered as yātudhānas.

children.text: vasantyete tu vai sūrye māsa ūrja iṣe ca ha
children.translated_text: These dwell in the sun in the months <s>Ūrja</s> and <s>Iṣa</s>.

children.text: haimantikau tu dvau māsau vasanti ca divākare ||
children.translated_text: And in the two wintry months they dwell in the sun:

children.text: aṃśurbhagaś ca dvāvetau kaśyapaś ca kratuḥ saha
children.translated_text: <s>Aṃśu</s> and <s>Bhaga</s>, those two, together with <s>Kaśyapa</s> and <s>Kratu</s>;

children.text: bhujaṅgaś ca mahāpadmaḥ sarpaḥ karkoṭakas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the serpent <s>Mahāpadma</s> and the serpent <s>Karkoṭaka</s>;
the gandharva <s>Citrasena</s> and <s>Ūrṇāyu</s>, those two;
<s>Urvaśī</s> and <s>Pūrvacitti</s>, likewise those two apsarases;

children.text: tārkṣyaścāriṣṭanemiś ca senānīr grāmaṇīś ca tau
children.translated_text: <s>Tārkṣya</s> and <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, those two commanders and grāmaṇīs;
and <s>Vidyut</s> and <s>Divākara</s>, those two are declared to be yātudhānas.

children.text: sahe caiva sahasye ca vasantyete divākare
children.translated_text: These dwell in the sun during <s>Saha</s> and <s>Sahasya</s>.
Then, during the two cold-season months also, they dwell there:
<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s>, and likewise <s>Viśvāmitra</s>;
and the two <s>Kādraveya</s> nāgas, <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>;
the gandharvas <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and likewise <s>Sūryavarcā</s>.
and the apsaras <s>Tilottamā</s>, and also the lovely goddess <s>Rambhā</s>.
And <s>Rathajit</s> and <s>Satyajit</s> are the two grāmaṇīs, famous in the world,

children.text: brahmopetas tathā rakṣo yajñopetaś ca yaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the rākṣasa called <s>Brahmopeta</s>, and the one remembered as <s>Yajñopeta</s>.

children.text: ete devā vasantyarke dvau dvau māsau krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: These deities dwell in <s>Arka</s>, two months each, in order,
for these are the place-presiding groups, twelve sets of seven.
They nourish <s>Sūrya</s> with their splendor, the supreme splendor,
and the sages praise <s>Ravi</s> with their own woven words.
The gandharvas and apsarases attend him with dance and song,
and the grāmaṇīs, yakṣas, and beings perform the gathering of the reins.

children.text: sarpā vahanti vai sūryaṃ yātudhānā anuyānti vai
children.translated_text: The serpents indeed bear <s>Sūrya</s>, and the yātudhānas follow along.
The <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, surrounding <s>Ravi</s> from sunrise onward, lead him to setting.

children.text: eteṣāmeva devānāṃ yathā tejo yathā tapaḥ
children.translated_text: According to the splendor and according to the austerity of these very deities,
according to their proper discipline, according to mantra, according to dharma, and according to strength,
so this <s>Sūrya</s> gives heat, kindled by their splendor.

children.text: ityete vai vasantīha dvau dvau māsau divākare ||
children.translated_text: Thus these indeed dwell here in the Day-maker, two months each.
The groups of sages, gods, gandharvas, serpents, and apsarases,

children.text: grāmaṇyaś ca tathā yakṣā yātudhānāś ca mukhyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the grāmaṇīs, the yakṣas, and chiefly the yātudhānas,

children.text: ete tapanti varṣanti bhānti vānti sṛjanti ca
children.translated_text: these give heat, rain, shine, blow, and create;
they are celebrated here as warding off the inauspicious karma of beings.

children.text: mānavānāṃ śubhaṃ hyete haranti ca durātmanām
children.translated_text: For wicked men they indeed take away what is auspicious,
while in some cases they ward off the misfortune of those who conduct themselves well.

children.text: vimāne ca sthitā divye kāmage vātaraṃhasi
children.translated_text: Standing in a divine aerial car, going wherever it wishes and swift as the wind,
these wander together with <s>Sūrya</s>, following the days.

children.text: varṣantaś ca tapantaś ca hlādayantaś ca vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Raining, giving heat, and gladdening, O twice-born men,
they protect here all beings, so long as the sky endures.
This is the station of the place-presiding ones throughout the manvantaras,

children.text: atītānāgatānāṃ vai vartante sāṃprataṃ ca ye ||
children.translated_text: of those past and future, and of those who exist at present.

children.text: ete vasanti vai sūrye saptakāste caturdaśa
children.translated_text: These sets of seven dwell in <s>Sūrya</s>, fourteen in number,
all these groups here in all the fourteen manvantaras.
In brief and in detail, according as it happened and according as it was heard,
it has been told, O tigers among sages, concerning the wise God of gods.

children.text: ete devā vasantyarke dvau dvau māsau krameṇa tu
children.translated_text: These deities dwell in <s>Arka</s>, two months each, in order,
for these are the place-presiding groups, twelve sets of seven.
Thus with a one-wheeled, swift chariot, <s>Sūrya</s>,
the Day-maker, travels with green, undecaying horses.
Day and night he wanders in that one-wheeled chariot,
and with seven horses he traverses in heaven the earth whose parts are the seven islands and oceans.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge sūryarathanirṇayo nāma pañcapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the blessed <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the fifty-fifth chapter, named "The Determination of the Sun's Chariot," is ended.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The Night-maker travels through the lunar mansions that rest upon the celestial paths.
His chariot should be understood as three-wheeled and furnished with horses on both sides.
It is yoked with three wheels having a hundred spokes, and with excellent white horses,
ten in number, sturdy, divine, unimpeded, and swift as thought.
With this chariot he goes together with the gods and the ancestors.
<s>Soma</s>, made of water, is white and white-rayed, with watery beams.
At the beginning of the bright fortnight, stationed beyond <s>Bhāskara</s>, he advances;
at the farther end he is continually filled, in the sequence of days.
When <s>Soma</s> has waned, having been drunk by the gods,
<s>Bhāskara</s> continually replenishes him, drunk for fifteen days, with a single ray.
Filling him by means of <s>Suṣumna</s>, portion by portion in sequence,
thus this body of the moon is nourished by the power of the sun.
On the full-moon day he is seen white, with his disk complete.
When <s>Soma</s> has thus been nourished day by day in the bright fortnight,
then, beginning with the second lunar day up to the fourteenth of the dark fortnight,
the gods drink the watery, honeyed, Soma-like nectar of immortality.
That nectar, gathered over half a month by the sun's splendor,
they attend as <s>Soma</s> on the full-moon day, nectar for drinking.
For one night all the gods, together with the ancestors and sages,
at the beginning of <s>Soma</s>'s dark fortnight, while he faces <s>Bhāskara</s>,
the digits are diminished at the farther end, as they are drunk in order.
Thirty-three hundreds, and also thirty-three,
and thirty-three thousands of gods indeed drink <s>Soma</s>.
Thus, when the Night-maker has been drunk by the gods in the sequence of days,
after drinking for half a month, the best of the gods depart on the new-moon day.
The ancestors too attend the Night-maker on the new-moon day.
Then, when a little remains in the fifteenth part, consisting of a digit,
in the afternoon the groups of ancestors attend the last portion.

children.text: pibanti dvikalaṃ kālaṃ śiṣṭā tasya kalā tu yā
children.translated_text: They drink for a period of two kalās; whatever digit of his remains,
that, issuing from the rays on the new-moon day, is the nectar of <s>svadhā</s>.
Having drunk it, they obtain foremost satisfaction for a month and go to immortality.

children.text: pitṛbhiḥ pīyamānasya pañcadaśyāṃ kalā tu yā ||
children.translated_text: While he is being drunk by the ancestors, the digit on the fifteenth day

children.text: yāvattu kṣīyate tasya bhāgaḥ pañcadaśastu saḥ
children.translated_text: is diminished for as long as that fifteenth portion of his lasts;
then, on the new-moon day, it is filled again in the interval.

children.text: vṛddhikṣayau vai pakṣādau ṣoḍaśyāṃ śaśinaḥ smṛtau
children.translated_text: The waxing and waning of the moon are remembered at the beginning of the fortnights, in relation to the sixteenth digit.
Thus this increase of the fortnight in the Night-maker is caused by the sun.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge somavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭpañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the blessed <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the fifty-sixth chapter, named "The Description of <s>Soma</s>," is ended.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: aṣṭabhiś ca hayairyuktaḥ somaputrasya vai rathaḥ
children.translated_text: The chariot of <s>Somaputra</s> is yoked with eight horses,
made of water and fire, tawny and beautiful.
The chariot of <s>Śukra</s>, the wise preceptor of the Daityas,
is remembered as yoked with ten unlean horses of many colors, made of earth.
And the chariot of <s>Bhauma</s> is golden, splendid, and drawn by eight horses;
that of <s>Jīva</s> is golden and eight-horsed, while that of <s>Manda</s> is made of iron.
The chariot of <s>Svarbhānu</s>, the enemy of <s>Bhāskara</s>,
is remembered with ten horses made of water, other than white, and likewise as eight-horsed.
All those planets are bound to <s>Dhruva</s> by wind-ropes,

children.text: etena bhrāmyamāṇāś ca yathāyogaṃ vrajanti vai ||
children.translated_text: and, being made to revolve by this, they proceed according to their proper course.
As many stars as there are, just so many are the rays;

children.text: sarve dhruvanibaddhāś ca bhramanto bhrāmayanti tam ||
children.translated_text: all are bound to <s>Dhruva</s>, and revolving, they make him revolve.
They move like a wheel made by a whirling firebrand, impelled by the wheel of wind;
because it carries the luminaries, it is therefore remembered as <s>Pravaha</s>.
The asterisms and the sun, together with the hosts of planets and stars,
all facing upward and toward one another, have become a wheel and rest in heaven.
Governed by <s>Dhruva</s>, they go around <s>Dhruva</s> himself in circumambulation,

children.text: prayānti ceśvaraṃ draṣṭuṃ meḍhībhūtaṃ dhruvaṃ divi ||
children.translated_text: to behold the Lord, <s>Dhruva</s>, who has become the pole-post in heaven.
The diameter of the sun is remembered as nine thousand yojanas;
the extent of its disk, by measure, is three times that.
The extent of the moon is remembered as twice the extent of the sun;
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, equal to those two, moves along below.
Having taken up the shadow of the earth, fashioned in the form of a disk,
that great third station of <s>Svarbhānu</s> is dark.
One sixteenth part of the moon is prescribed for <s>Bhārgava</s>,
in measure by diameter, disk, and yojanas.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> should be understood as a quarter less than <s>Bhārgava</s>,
and <s>Vakra</s> and <s>Saurī</s> as a quarter less in the measure of length.
<s>Budha</s> is a quarter less than those two in extent and disk.
Those embodied forms here that are stars and asterisms
are equal to <s>Budha</s> in extent and also in disk.
One who knows reality should know the asterisms as, for the most part, joined with the moon.
The forms of stars and asterisms are smaller in relation to one another:

children.text: śatāni pañca catvāri trīṇi dve caiva yojane ||
children.translated_text: five hundred, four hundred, three hundred, and two hundred yojanas.
The smallest star-disks, above all,
are only two yojanas; there is nothing smaller than them.
Above them are the three planets that move at a distance:

children.text: sauro'ṅgirāś ca vakraś ca jñeyā mandavicāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saurī</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, and <s>Vakra</s> are to be known as slow-moving.
Below them, again, are four other great planets:
the sun, the moon, <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Bhārgava</s>, which move swiftly.
As many crores of stars as there are asterisms in every way,
their fixed station in the path of the asterisms is due to the rule of <s>Dhruva</s>.
The lowness and highness, in sequence, of the seven-horsed sun is this:
when the moon, at the lunar junctions, stands on the path of the northern course,
because of its height it is quickly seen with rays that are not very distinct.
Then, standing on the southern path and resorting to the lower track,
the sun, covered by the earth's line, at full moon and new moon
is seen at the proper time and quickly goes to setting.
Therefore at new moon the night-maker, standing on the northern path,

children.text: dadṛśe dakṣiṇe mārge niyamāddṛśyate na ca ||
children.translated_text: is seen; on the southern path, by rule, it is not seen.
Through the conjunction of the motions of the luminaries, the sun is covered by darkness;
at the equinoxes their setting is at the same time and their rising is the same.
In the northern tracks, their setting and rising are separated;
at full moon and new moon they should be known as following the wheel of the luminaries.
When the radiant sun moves on the path of the southern course,
the sun passes below all the planets.

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā tasyordhvaṃ carate śaśī
children.translated_text: Having made a broad disk, the moon moves above it;
the whole sphere of the asterisms extends above <s>Soma</s>.
Above the asterisms is <s>Budha</s>, and above <s>Budha</s> is <s>Bhārgava</s>;
above <s>Bhārgava</s> is <s>Vakra</s>, and above <s>Vakra</s> is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Above that is <s>Śanaiścara</s>, and above that is the sphere of the <s>Saptarṣis</s>;
above the seven sages is the fixed station of <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: taṃ viṣṇulokaṃ paramaṃ jñātvā mucyeta kilbiṣāt
children.translated_text: Having known that supreme <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>, one is freed from sin.
In doubled thousands and hundreds of yojanas,
above the planets, asterisms, and stars, in due order,

children.text: grahāś ca candrasūryau ca yutau divyena tejasā ||
children.translated_text: the planets, the moon, and the sun, joined with divine radiance,
are constantly yoked to the asterisms as they go day and night in sequence.
Those planets, asterisms, and suns are situated as low, high, and straight;

children.text: samāgame ca bhede ca paśyanti yugapatprajāḥ
children.translated_text: people see them simultaneously in conjunction and separation.

children.text: ṛtavaḥ ṣaṭ smṛtāḥ sarve samāgacchanti pañcadhā ||
children.translated_text: All six seasons are remembered; they come together in five ways.
These are mutually established and are joined with one another;
their conjunction is to be understood by the wise without confusion.

children.text: evaṃ saṃkṣipya kathitaṃ grahāṇāṃ gamanaṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, O twice-born men, the movement of the planets
beginning with <s>Bhāskara</s> has been told briefly, as seen and as heard.
As to lordship over the planets, the Blessed One, by <s>Brahmā</s>, the lotus-born,

children.text: abhiṣiktaḥ sahasrāṃśū rudreṇa tu yathā guhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The thousand-rayed one was consecrated by <s>Rudra</s>, just as <s>Guha</s> was.
Therefore worship of the <s>grahas</s> (planets) should be performed, and the prescribed rite in the fire, according to rule,
when there is affliction from the <s>Āditya-graha</s>, by good men for the accomplishment of their aim.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge jyotiścakre grahacārakathanaṃ nāma saptapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, the fifty-seventh chapter, named the Description of the Course of the Planets in the Zodiac.
The sages said:
How did <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of creatures, consecrate them to lordship,
all those beginning with the gods and demons, he who is the self of all? Tell us now.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The blessed lord <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of creatures, consecrated <s>Divākara</s> over the planets,
and <s>Soma</s> over the constellations and medicinal plants.

children.text: apāṃ ca varuṇaṃ devaṃ dhanānāṃ yakṣapuṅgavam
children.translated_text: He consecrated the god <s>Varuṇa</s> over the waters, and the foremost of the <s>Yakṣas</s> over riches,

children.text: ādityānāṃ tathā viṣṇuṃ vasūnāṃ pāvakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: likewise <s>Viṣṇu</s> over the <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Pāvaka</s> over the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: prajāpatīnāṃ dakṣaṃ ca marutāṃ śakrameva ca
children.translated_text: He consecrated <s>Dakṣa</s> over the <s>Prajāpatis</s>, and <s>Śakra</s> over the <s>Maruts</s>,
and <s>Prahlāda</s>, foremost of the <s>Daityas</s>, over the <s>Daityas</s> and <s>Dānavas</s>.
He made <s>Dharma</s> lord of the fathers, and <s>Nirṛti</s> lord of the flesh-eaters,
<s>Rudra</s> lord of animals and beings, and <s>Nandin</s> leader of the <s>gaṇas</s>.
He made <s>Vīrabhadra</s> lord of heroes, and the Terrible One lord of the <s>Piśācas</s>,
and <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, honored by all the gods, lord of the mothers.
Over the <s>Rudras</s> he set the lord <s>Nīlalohita</s>, the god of gods,

children.text: vighnānāṃ vyomajaṃ devaṃ gajāsyaṃ tu vināyakam ||
children.translated_text: and over obstacles the sky-born god, elephant-faced <s>Vināyaka</s>.

children.text: strīṇāṃ devīmumāṃ devīṃ vacasāṃ ca sarasvatīm
children.translated_text: He made the goddess <s>Umā</s> lord of women, and the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> lord of speech,

children.text: viṣṇuṃ māyāvināṃ caiva svātmānaṃ jagatāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> lord of wielders of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and his own self lord of the worlds.

children.text: himavantaṃ girīṇāṃ tu nadīnāṃ caiva jāhnavīm
children.translated_text: He made <s>Himavant</s> lord of mountains, and <s>Jāhnavī</s> lord of rivers,
and the ocean, treasure-house of waters, lord of all seas.

children.text: vṛkṣāṇāṃ caiva cāśvatthaṃ plakṣaṃ ca prapitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The great-grandfather made the <s>Aśvattha</s> and the <s>Plakṣa</s> lords of trees.
Again he made <s>Citraratha</s> lord of <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s>,
<s>Vāsuki</s>, terrible in valor, lord of <s>Nāgas</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>, terrible in valor, lord of serpents.
He made the great elephant <s>Airāvata</s>, terrible in valor, lord of the elephants of the quarters,
and <s>Suparṇa</s> lord of flying creatures, and <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> king of horses.

children.text: siṃhaṃ mṛgāṇāṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gavāṃ ca mṛgādhipānāṃ śarabhaṃ cakāra
children.translated_text: He made the lion lord of wild beasts, the bull lord of cattle, and <s>Śarabha</s> lord of the lords of beasts,
<s>Guha</s>, the immeasurable one, lord of commanders, and <s>Lakulīśa</s> lord of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>.
He consecrated <s>Sudharman</s>, and likewise <s>Śaṅkhapada</s>, over the directions,
then, in order, <s>Ketumant</s> and also <s>Hemaroman</s>.
On earth he consecrated <s>Pṛthu</s> as lord, and over all he set <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, the all-knowing, bull-bannered one, among the four forms.
By the favor of blessed <s>Śambhu</s>, he consecrated them in due order;
having consecrated them long ago, that holy lord of the world shone forth.
This has been told to you in full detail, O bulls among sages;
then these distinguished ones were consecrated by the source of the universe.
Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, the fifty-eighth chapter, named the Account of the Consecration of the Sun and the Others.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard this, the sages, again filled with doubt,
then asked <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> further in reply.
The sages said:
What you have said here, O <s>Sūta</s>, best of speakers,
tell this in detail, and also the determination of the heavenly bodies.

children.text: śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ tadā sūtaḥ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing their words, <s>Sūta</s>, composed in mind,
spoke a supreme utterance for the resolution of their doubt.
On this matter, what has been said by the greatly wise, whose minds were peaceful,
that I shall declare to you: the course of the sun and the moon.
How, here, the planets beginning with the sun and moon are the houses of the gods,
thereafter I shall describe the threefold origin of fire.
It is the origin of divine fire, elemental fire, and also terrestrial fire.
When the night of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is unmanifest, had passed,
this unmanifest world was covered by the darkness of night.
When only a quarter remained in this world and it had especially perished,
there the blessed <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, accomplishing all purposes of the worlds,
moved about like a firefly, wishing to become manifest.
Then, at the beginning of the world, having created fire, connected with earth and water,
the Lord drew it together for the sake of illumination and divided it into three.
That which is wind in this world is called terrestrial fire,

children.text: yaścāsau lokādau sūrye śuciragnistu sa smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that pure fire which was in the sun at the beginning of the world is remembered as fire.
The lightning-born, water-born fire should be known; I shall describe their characteristics.
The three fires are the lightning-born, the digestive, the solar, and the water-wombed.
Therefore the powerful Sun, drinking the waters with his rays, shines.

children.text: jale cābjaḥ samāviṣṭo nādbhir agniḥ praśāmyati ||
children.translated_text: The water-born fire has entered water, and fire is not quenched by waters.

children.text: mānavānāṃ ca kukṣistho nāgniḥ śāmyati pāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor is the fire, <s>Pāvaka</s>, situated in the bellies of humans, quenched.
That blazing wind is fire, while the digestive fire is remembered as without visible radiance.
And this white disk is produced without heat.

children.text: prabhā saurī tu pādena hyastaṃ yāte divākare ||
children.translated_text: When <s>Divākara</s> has set, the solar light, by a quarter,
enters fire at night; therefore it shines from afar.

children.text: udyantaṃ ca punaḥ sūryam auṣṇyam agneḥ samāviśet ||
children.translated_text: And when the sun rises again, the heat of fire enters it,
by a quarter of terrestrial fire; therefore that fire gives heat.
In the two radiances, solar and fiery, whose natures are light and heat,
through mutual interpenetration they nourish one another.

children.text: uttare caiva bhūmyardhe tathā hyagniś ca dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: And likewise in the northern half of the earth; similarly fire is in the southern.

children.text: uttiṣṭhati punaḥ sūryaḥ punarvai praviśaty apaḥ
children.translated_text: The sun rises again, and again he enters the waters.
Therefore the waters become copper-colored, because he enters them by day and by night.

children.text: astaṃ yāti punaḥ sūryo 'harvai praviśaty apaḥ
children.translated_text: Again the sun sets; in the day, indeed, he enters the waters.

children.text: tasmānnaktaṃ punaḥ śuklā āpo dṛśyanti bhāsvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore at night the waters again appear white and radiant.
By this ordered sequence, in the southern and northern halves of the earth,
at rising and setting, day and night, he constantly enters the waters.
And that sun who burns while drinking water with his rays,
being mixed with terrestrial fire, is remembered as divine and pure.
That fire is remembered as thousand-footed and like a round jar.

children.text: ādatte sa tu nāḍīnāṃ sahasreṇa samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: By means of a thousand channels it takes up waters on every side:
river waters and ocean waters, wells also, and likewise waters in clouds,
waters both stationary and moving, and waters of reservoirs, canals, and the like.
That thousandfold mass of his rays pours forth cold, rain, and heat.
Of those, four hundred channels, of varied forms, send rain.

children.text: bhajanāścaiva mālyāś ca ketanāḥ patanās tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhajanā</s>, <s>Mālyā</s>, <s>Ketanā</s>, and <s>Patanā</s>
are all called <s>Amṛtā</s>; they are the rays that release rain.

children.text: himodvahāś ca tā nāḍyo raśmayas triśatāḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Again, those channels that carry snow, the rays, are three hundred.

children.text: reśā meghāś ca vātsyāś ca hlādinyo himasarjanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Reśā</s>, <s>Meghā</s>, <s>Vātsyā</s>, and <s>Hlādinī</s> are the producers of snow.

children.text: candrabhā nāmataḥ sarvā pītābhāś ca gabhastayaḥ
children.translated_text: All are named <s>Candrabhā</s>, and the sunbeams are yellowish in radiance.

children.text: śuklāś ca kakubhāścaiva gāvo viśvabhṛtas tathā ||
children.translated_text: There are also the white ones, the <s>Kakubhā</s>, the <s>Gāvaḥ</s>, and the <s>Viśvabhṛtaḥ</s>.
All those are named <s>Śuklā</s>; the three hundred produce heat.
By them <s>Soma</s> supports humans, ancestors, and deities.
Here he satisfies humans with plants, and the ancestors with <s>svadhā</s> (ancestral oblation),
and all the gods with <s>amṛta</s> (nectar); with these three he nourishes the three groups.

children.text: vasante caiva grīṣme ca śataiḥ sa tapate tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: In spring and in summer he heats with three hundreds,
and in the rains and then in autumn he pours rain with four hundreds.
In winter and in the cool season he releases snow with three hundreds.

children.text: indro dhātā bhagaḥ pūṣā mitro'tha varuṇo'ryamā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, then <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Aryaman</s>,

children.text: aṃśur vivasvāṃstvaṣṭā ca parjanyo viṣṇureva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṃśu</s>, <s>Vivasvant</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>:

children.text: varuṇo māghamāse tu sūrya eva tu phālgune ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s> is the sun in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, and in <s>Phālguna</s> it is the sun himself.
In the month of <s>Caitra</s> he is <s>Aṃśu</s>, and <s>Dhātṛ</s> is the heater in <s>Vaiśākha</s>.

children.text: jyeṣṭhe māsi bhavedindra āṣāḍhe cāryamā raviḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> he is <s>Indra</s>, and in <s>Āṣāḍha</s> the sun is <s>Aryaman</s>.

children.text: vivasvān śrāvaṇe māsi prauṣṭhapade bhagaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> he is <s>Vivasvant</s>; in <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s> he is remembered as <s>Bhaga</s>.

children.text: parjanyo'śvayuje māsi tvaṣṭā vai kārtike raviḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Aśvayuj</s> he is <s>Parjanya</s>, and in <s>Kārttika</s> the sun is <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.
In <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> he is <s>Mitra</s>; in <s>Pauṣa</s> he is eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
There are five thousand rays in <s>Varuṇa</s>'s work as the sun.

children.text: ṣaḍbhiḥ sahasraiḥ pūṣā tu devo'ṃśuḥ saptabhis tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s> has six thousand, and the god <s>Aṃśu</s> likewise has seven thousand.
<s>Dhātṛ</s> has eight thousand, and <s>Śatakratu</s> has nine thousand.
<s>Vivasvant</s> goes with ten thousand, and <s>Bhaga</s> goes with eleven thousand.
<s>Mitra</s> heats with seven thousand, and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> too is remembered as having eight thousand.

children.text: aryamā daśabhir yāti parjanyo navabhis tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Aryaman</s> goes with ten thousand, and <s>Parjanya</s> likewise with nine thousand.
With six thousand rays <s>Viṣṇu</s> heats the earth.
In spring the sun is tawny; in summer he has a golden splendor.

children.text: śveto varṣāsu varṇena pāṇḍuḥ śaradi bhāskaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the rainy season <s>Bhāskara</s> is white in color, and in autumn he is pale.
In winter the sun is copper-colored, and in the cool season the sun is red.
Thus the colors arising from the sun have been declared by me.

children.text: oṣadhīṣu balaṃ dhatte svadhayā ca pitṛṣvapi
children.translated_text: He places strength in plants, and <s>svadhā</s> among the ancestors.
The sun also assigns <s>amṛta</s> among the immortals; he fixes the three in the three.
Thus that thousandfold solar radiance accomplishes the purposes of the world.
Reaching the world, it is divided into outpourings of water, cold, and heat.
This, then, is the white, radiant disk called the sun.
It is the foundation and very womb of the lunar mansions, planets, and <s>Soma</s>.
The moon, the lunar mansions, and all the planets should be known as born from the sun.
<s>Soma</s>, lord of the lunar mansions, is the left eye of the Lord.

children.text: nayanaṃ caivam īśasya dakṣiṇaṃ bhāskaraḥ svayam
children.translated_text: And <s>Bhāskara</s> himself is the right eye of <s>Īśa</s>.
Because in this world it leads the sight of those people, it is called an eye.
Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the fifty-ninth chapter, named the Description of the Nature of the Sun's Rays.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: śeṣāḥ pañca grahā jñeyā īśvarāḥ kāmacāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The remaining five planets should be known as lords who move at will.
<s>Āditya</s> is recited as fire, and the moon is remembered as water.
Listen to the nature of the remaining ones, which will now be properly explained.
<s>Skanda</s>, commander of the gods, is recited as the planet <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.
People who know knowledge call <s>Budha</s> the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Yama</s>, visibly the lord of all worlds, is himself lord of the world.
O best of twice-born, the great planet, slow-moving, is <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
The two teachers of gods and asuras are the two radiant great planets.
They are said to be sons of <s>Prajāpati</s>; they are <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
The whole threefold world has <s>Āditya</s> as its root; of this there is no doubt.
From him this entire world arises, with gods, asuras, and humans.
Of <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Candra</s>, the chief Brahmins, <s>Agni</s>, and the gods,
the brilliance of all brilliant beings, whatever radiance is found in the whole world,
the Self of all, lord of all worlds, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>:
the sun himself is the lord of the three worlds, the root, the supreme deity.
From him everything is born, and into him alone it dissolves.
Indeed, the being and nonbeing of the worlds issued forth of old from <s>Āditya</s>.
O brahmins, the radiant sun, bright and very splendid, is an unknowable graha.

children.text: atra gacchanti nidhanaṃ jāyante ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Here they go to destruction and are born again and again:

children.text: kṣaṇā muhūrtā divasā niśāḥ pakṣāś ca kṛtsnaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: moments, muhūrtas, days, nights, and fortnights in their entirety,
months and years too, seasons, and then yugas.
Apart from that <s>Āditya</s>, this reckoning of time does not exist.

children.text: kālādṛte na niyamo na dīkṣā nāhnikakramaḥ
children.translated_text: Without time there is no rule, no consecration, and no daily rite;

children.text: ṛtūnāṃ ca vibhāgaś ca puṣpaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whence would there be the division of seasons, or flowers, roots, and fruits?
Whence would there be the production of crops, and also the multitude of grasses and herbs?

children.text: abhāvo vyavahārāṇāṃ jantūnāṃ divi ceha ca ||
children.translated_text: There would be the absence of all dealings among beings in heaven and here on earth,
without <s>Bhāskara</s>, who heats the world and has the form of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: sa eṣa kālaścāgniś ca dvādaśātmā prajāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very one is time, fire, and <s>Prajāpati</s> with twelve forms.
O best of twice-born ones, he heats the three worlds, with their moving and unmoving beings.

children.text: sa eṣa tejasāṃ rāśiḥ samastaḥ sārvalaukikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very one is the whole mass of all lights, belonging to all the worlds.
Having taken up the highest path, by nights and days he heats this world

children.text: pārśvata ūrdhvam adhaś caiva tāpayatyeṣa sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: from the sides, above, and below, in every way.
Just as a light-giving lamp hung in the middle of a house

children.text: pārśvata ūrdhvam adhaścaiva tamo nāśayate samam ||
children.translated_text: equally destroys darkness from the sides, above, and below,
so the thousand-rayed king of grahas, the lord of the world,

children.text: sūryo gobhir jagat sarvam ādīpayati sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sun, illumines the whole world everywhere with his rays.
Of the thousand rays of the sun which I mentioned before,

children.text: teṣāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ punaḥ sapta raśmayo grahayonayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seven rays among them are again the chief ones, the wombs of the planets.

children.text: suṣumno harikeśaś ca viśvakarmā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣumna</s>, <s>Harikeśa</s>, and likewise <s>Viśvakarman</s>,

children.text: viśvavyacāḥ punaścādyaḥ saṃnaddhaś ca tataḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Viśvavyacā</s> as the first, and after that <s>Saṃnaddha</s>;
again another is <s>Sarvāvasu</s>, and another is declared to be <s>Svarāṭ</s>.
The solar ray <s>Suṣumna</s> nourished the southern zodiacal sign.
Its course downward, upward, and below is said to be that of <s>Suṣumna</s>.
<s>Harikeśa</s>, which is in front, is declared to be the womb of the lunar mansions.
On the right, the ray <s>Viśvakarman</s> nourishes <s>Budha</s>.
<s>Viśvavyacā</s>, which is behind, is remembered by the wise as the womb of <s>Śukra</s>.

children.text: saṃnaddhaś ca tu yo raśmiḥ sa yonir lohitasya tu
children.translated_text: And the ray called <s>Saṃnaddha</s> is the womb of <s>Lohita</s>.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaḥ sarvāvasū raśmiḥ sa yonistu bṛhaspateḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sixth ray, <s>Sarvāvasu</s>, is the womb of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: śanaiścaraṃ punaś cāpi raśmir āpyāyate svarāṭ
children.translated_text: And again the ray <s>Svarāṭ</s> nourishes <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
Thus, through the power of the sun, the lunar mansions, planets, and stars

children.text: dṛśyante divi tāḥ sarvāḥ viśvaṃ cedaṃ punarjagat
children.translated_text: are all seen in heaven, and so too this whole universe.
Because they are not diminished, therefore they are remembered as nakṣatras.
Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the sixtieth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
All these fields are heated by the sunbeams.
Then the sun takes their fields, the lunar mansions and stars.
Having practiced good deeds here, when that merit is exhausted, they resort to the planets.
They are called tārakās because they carry across, and tārakās also because of their whiteness.

children.text: divyānāṃ pārthivānāṃ ca naiśānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
