children.translated_text: Of all divine, earthly, and nocturnal things, in every way,
because he constantly takes up their lights and even their darkness, he is <s>Āditya</s>.

children.text: savane syandane'rthe ca dhātur eṣa vibhāṣyate
children.translated_text: This verbal root is explained in the senses of pressing, flowing, and impelling.
Because of the pressing forth of light and waters, he is therefore considered <s>Savitṛ</s>.
This one is called the abundant moon; the root is said to mean gladdening.

children.text: śuklatve cāmṛtatve ca śītatve ca vibhāvyate ||
children.translated_text: It is understood also in whiteness, immortality, and coolness.
The two divine, shining, sky-going disks of the sun and moon
are made of water and fire, white, auspicious, and like round jars.
There the disk of the moon is remembered as having the nature of dense water.
But the disk of <s>Bhāskara</s> is white and made of dense fire.
All the gods dwell in all these stations.
In all the manvantaras they resort to the lunar mansions, the sun, and the planets.

children.text: tena grahā gṛhāṇyeva tadākhyāste bhavanti ca
children.translated_text: Therefore the grahas are indeed houses, and they come to have that name.
The sun entered the solar station, and <s>Soma</s> likewise the lunar one.
Powerful <s>Śukra</s>, with sixteen rays, entered the station of <s>Śukra</s>.
Great <s>Bṛhaspati</s> entered the great one, and <s>Lohita</s> the red one.
The god <s>Śanaiścara</s> likewise entered the station of <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
<s>Budha</s> entered the Mercurial station, and <s>Svarbhānu</s> took refuge in the station of <s>Svarbhānu</s>.

children.text: nakṣatrāṇi ca sarvāṇi nakṣatrāṇi viśanti ca
children.translated_text: And all the lunar mansions entered the lunar mansions.
All these houses are the lights of those whose selves are meritorious.
Set in motion at the beginning of the kalpa, they were created by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>.
These stations remain until the dissolution of created existence.
In all the manvantaras they are indeed the stations of the gods.
The presiding gods take their stand again and again in those stations.
Together with those of the past, and with gods who are to be and are not yet to be,

children.text: vartante vartamānaiś ca sthānibhistaiḥ suraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: they continue along with the present gods who occupy those stations.
In this manvantara the planets are remembered as aerial beings.
In the Vaivasvata interval, the sun is <s>Vivasvān</s>, son of <s>Aditi</s>.
The moon is remembered as the radiant god <s>Soma</s>, a <s>Vasu</s> and son of a sage.
<s>Śukra</s> should be known as the god, the <s>Bhārgava</s>, priest of the Asuras.
The god <s>Bṛhattejas</s>, son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, is remembered as the preceptor of the gods.
<s>Budha</s>, charming in form, is remembered as the son of a sage.
<s>Śanaiścara</s>, deformed in appearance, is the son of <s>Saṃjñā</s> and <s>Vivasvat</s>.
Fire was born from <s>Vikeśī</s>; he is young and has red flames.
Those named as lunar mansions and stars are remembered as daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>.
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, son of <s>Siṃhikā</s>, was the <s>asura</s> who torments beings.
The presiding powers in the moon, the lunar mansions, the planets, and the sun have been declared.
These stations have been described as stated, and so too the deities who occupy the stations.
The solar station of the thousand-rayed <s>Vivasvat</s> is fiery in nature.
The station of the moon, the cool-rayed one, is remembered as watery and white.

children.text: āpyaṃ śyāmaṃ manojñaṃ ca budharaśmigṛhaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The ray-house of <s>Budha</s> is remembered as watery, dark, and pleasing.
The station of <s>Śukra</s>, too, is watery, white, and like one possessed of sixteen rays.

children.text: navaraśmi tu bhaumasya lohitaṃ sthānam uttamam
children.translated_text: The excellent station of <s>Bhauma</s> is nine-rayed and red.
The station of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is yellowish in appearance, great, and sixteen-flamed.
For <s>Śanaiścara</s>, an eight-rayed house is also said to be black.
<s>Svarbhānu</s>'s station is dark, an abode that torments beings.
All the stars should be known as seers, and as having a single ray.
They are supports of those whose fame is meritorious, and they are also white according to their own color.
They should be known as consisting of compact water, formed at the very beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>.
Through contact with the rays of <s>Āditya</s>, they are remembered as having the nature of luminosity.
The diameter of the sun is remembered as nine thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
The breadth of its disk, by measure, is three times that.
The expanse of the moon is remembered as twice the expanse of the sun.
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, equal to those two, moves beneath them.
He raises up the earth's shadow, formed in the shape of a disk.
The great station of <s>Svarbhānu</s>, the third one, is made of darkness.
Coming forth from <s>Āditya</s>, it goes equally at the junctures.
From the moon it again goes to <s>Āditya</s> at the solar junctures.
Because it drives away <s>Svarbhānu</s>, therefore it is called <s>Svarbhānu</s>.
A sixteenth part of the moon is assigned to <s>Bhārgava</s>.
This is in measure with respect to diameter, disk, and the reckoning in <s>yojanas</s>.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> should be known as one quarter less than <s>Bhārgava</s>.
<s>Vakra</s> and <s>Saurī</s> are both remembered as one quarter less than <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
<s>Budha</s> is one quarter less than those two in expanse and disk.
Whatever embodied forms of stars and lunar mansions there are here,
they are equal to <s>Budha</s> in expanse and in disk.
The one who knows reality should know the lunar mansions as mostly joined with the moon.
The forms of the stars and lunar mansions are diminished in relation to one another.

children.text: śatāni pañca catvāri trīṇi dve caiva yojane
children.translated_text: They measure five hundred, four hundred, three hundred, and two hundred <s>yojanas</s>.
The disks of the stars are the smallest of all, though situated above all.
They also have half-measures in <s>yojanas</s>; none is known to be smaller than these.
Above them are three planets, moving at a distance.

children.text: sauro'ṅgirāś ca vakraś ca jñeyā mandavicāriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saurī</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, and <s>Vakra</s> should be known as slow-moving.
Their course, in due order, has already been described before.
All these planets have arisen among the lunar mansions.
<s>Vivasvat</s>, son of <s>Aditi</s>, is the sun, O best of sages.
He was born in the <s>Viśākhās</s>, the first planet among the planets.

children.text: tviṣimān dharmaputrastu somo devo vasustu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: The lustrous god <s>Soma</s>, son of <s>Dharma</s>, is that <s>Vasu</s>.
The cool-rayed maker of night was born in the <s>Kṛttikās</s>.
<s>Śukra</s>, son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, is sixteen-flamed and comes after the sun.
The best of the star-planets arose in the field of <s>Tiṣya</s>.
The planet <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, is twelve-flamed.
The teacher of the world was born in the lunar mansions called the former <s>Phālgunīs</s>.
The red-limbed, nine-flamed planet is the son of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
He is remembered here as having been born in the former <s>Āṣāḍhās</s>.
<s>Saurī</s>, <s>Śanaiścara</s>, is seven-flamed in his station in the <s>Revatīs</s>.

children.text: saumyo budho dhaniṣṭhāsu pañcārcir udito grahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s>, the son of <s>Soma</s>, is the five-flamed planet risen in the <s>Dhaniṣṭhās</s>.
<s>Śikhī</s>, son of <s>Mṛtyu</s>, is made of darkness and causes the destruction of creatures.
He was born in the <s>Āśleṣās</s>, a great planet that takes away everything.
Likewise the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s> arose in those that bear their own names.
<s>Rāhu</s> is made of the power of darkness and by nature has a black disk.
He was born in the <s>Bharaṇīs</s>, the planet that crushes the moon and the sun.
These star-planets, beginning with <s>Bhārgava</s>, should be understood.
For in afflictions of the birth-lunar-mansion they fall into malignity.
Through devotion to that planet one is released from that fault.
Of all these planets, <s>Āditya</s> is said to be the beginning.
Among the star-planets <s>Śukra</s> is first, and among the <s>ketus</s>, <s>Dhūmavān</s>.

children.text: dhruvaḥ kila grahāṇāṃ tu vibhaktānāṃ caturdiśam ||
children.translated_text: Among the planets divided into the four directions, <s>Dhruva</s> is supreme.
Among the lunar mansions it is <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>, and among the courses, the northern one.
Among the five years, the first is remembered as <s>Saṃvatsara</s>.
Among the seasons it is <s>Śiśira</s>, and among the months <s>Māgha</s> is named.
Among the fortnights it is the bright fortnight, and among the lunar days, <s>Pratipad</s>.
Among the divisions of day and night, day is proclaimed to be the beginning.
Likewise, among the <s>muhūrtas</s>, the first <s>muhūrta</s> has <s>Rudra</s> as its deity.
The <s>kṣaṇa</s> too, and time, begins with the <s>nimeṣa</s>, O best knowers of time.
The five-year <s>yuga</s> begins with <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> and ends with <s>Śravaṇa</s>.
Because of the particular motion of the sun, it turns like a wheel.
Therefore <s>Divākara</s> is remembered as the maker of time, the all-pervading lord.
He sets in motion and brings to rest the four kinds of beings.
Even of him, the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, the manifest god, is the mover.
Thus this is the arrangement of the heavenly lights and the determination of their meaning.
It was made by <s>Mahādeva</s> for the sake of worldly practice.
Set in motion deliberately by the blessed Lord at the beginning of the kalpa,
he is the support and the presiding self of everything, consisting of light.
This wondrous transformation of the one-formed primordial principle
cannot be reckoned by anyone exactly as it truly is.
The going and coming of the heavenly lights, by a human being with fleshly eyes,
from sacred tradition, inference, direct perception, and reasoning,
should be examined carefully with intelligence and accepted with faith by the wise.

children.text: cakṣuḥ śāstraṃ jalaṃ lekhyaṃ gaṇitaṃ munisattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The eye, the śāstra, water, written record, and calculation, O best of sages,
these five causes should be known in determining the measures of the heavenly lights.
Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the sixty-first chapter, named the Description of the Number of Planets.
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ viṣṇoḥ prasādādvai dhruvo buddhimatāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: How, by the grace of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, did <s>Dhruva</s>, best of the intelligent,
become the fixed pivot of the planets? You should tell us now.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Asked by me about this matter, the knower of many śāstras,

children.text: mārkaṇḍeyaḥ purā prāha mahyaṃ śuśrūṣave dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, in ancient times, spoke to me as I wished to hear, O twice-born ones.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
There was a universal sovereign, greatly radiant, foremost among all wielders of weapons,
king <s>Uttānapāda</s>, who ruled the earth.

children.text: tasya bhāryādvayam abhūt sunītiḥ surucis tathā
children.translated_text: He had two wives, <s>Sunīti</s> and also <s>Suruci</s>;
from the elder wife, from <s>Sunīti</s>, was born a son of great fame.
Named <s>Dhruva</s>, very wise, a lamp of the family, greatly intelligent,
once, though only seven years old, he sat on his father's lap.
<s>Suruci</s> pushed him away and, with affection for her own son,
placed that child on the lap, O best of brahmins, being honored for her beauty.
Not obtaining his father's lap, the wise boy, distressed in mind,

children.text: mātuḥ samīpamāgamya ruroda sa punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: came to his mother's side and wept again and again.
His mother, overwhelmed with grief, spoke this to her weeping son:
'<s>Suruci</s> is dear to your father, and her son is likewise so.
You were born as the son of me, ill-fated as I am, and so you too are unfortunate.

children.text: kiṃ śocasi kimarthaṃ tvaṃ rodamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Why do you grieve? For what reason do you weep again and again?
Becoming scorched at heart, you will only cause me grief.

children.text: svasthasthānaṃ dhruvaṃ putra svaśaktyā tvaṃ samāpnuyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: My son <s>Dhruva</s>, obtain a firm place by your own power.'

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa tu mātrā vai nirjagāma tadā vanam
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by his mother, he then went out to the forest,
and, seeing <s>Viśvāmitra</s> there, bowed down according to rule.
Standing with joined palms, he said, 'Blessed one, you should tell me:
By what means, O excellent one, shall I attain a place above all?
When I was seated on my father's lap, my mother <s>Suruci</s>, O sage,

children.text: vyadhūnayatsa taṃ rājā pitā novāca kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: shook me off, and that king, my father, said nothing at all.

children.text: etasmāt kāraṇād brahmaṃs trasto'haṃ mātaraṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: For this reason, O brahmin, frightened, I went to my mother.

children.text: sunītirāha me mātā mā kṛthāḥ śokamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sunīti</s>, my mother, said to me, "Do not fall into deep grief.
By your own karma you should attain the highest place, my child."

children.text: tasyā hi vacanaṃ śrutvā sthānaṃ tava mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: Having heard her words about such a place, O great sage,
I came to this forest, O brahmin, and today I have seen you, lord.
By your favor I shall obtain a wondrous, supreme place.'

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa muniḥ śrīmān prahasann idam abravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the glorious sage smiled and said this:
'Prince, listen to this; you shall obtain the highest place.
Having worshipped <s>Keśava</s>, lord of the worlds and destroyer of affliction,
who arose from the southern limb of wise <s>Śambhu</s>, the great god,
recite always, O very wise one, this destroyer of all sins,
bestower of what is desired, supreme, pure, holy, stainless, and highest.
Utter this divine mantra, joined with the <s>praṇava</s>,
namely, "Reverence be to <s>Vāsudeva</s>," with controlled senses,
meditating on eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s> and devoted to recitation and oblation.'
Thus addressed, the greatly famous one bowed down to <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
Facing east and controlled, he recited with a joyful mind,
eating vegetables, roots, and fruits for a year, untiring.
He recited the mantra day and night, constantly, again and again.

children.text: vetālā rākṣasā ghorāḥ siṃhādyāś ca mahāmṛgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Terrible <s>Vetālas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and great beasts such as lions
came against the great-souled boy, fearsome, in order to bewilder his understanding.

children.text: japan sa vāsudeveti na kiṃcit pratyapadyata ||
children.translated_text: As he repeated '<s>Vāsudeva</s>,' he took no notice of anything.

children.text: sunītir asya yā mātā tasyā rūpeṇa saṃvṛtā
children.translated_text: A female <s>Piśāca</s>, covered in the form of his mother <s>Sunīti</s>,
came near and wept, as if deeply afflicted.

children.text: mama tvamekaḥ putro'si kimarthaṃ kliśyate bhavān
children.translated_text: 'You are my only son; why are you tormenting yourself?
Having abandoned me, helpless, you have undertaken austerity.'
Though she was speaking words such as these, that greatly austere one,
without even looking at her, joyful in heart, recited the name of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: tataḥ praśemuḥ sarvatra vighnarūpāṇi tatra vai
children.translated_text: Then everywhere those forms of obstruction there became quiet.
Then, mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, dark as a black rain cloud,
surrounded by all the gods and praised by great seers,
the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, slayer of enemies, came near <s>Dhruva</s>.
Seeing him arrived, and thinking, 'Who is this?',
as though drinking in <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, lord of the world, with his two eyes,
<s>Dhruva</s>, of great radiance, stood there reciting '<s>Vāsudeva</s>'.

children.text: śaṅkhaprāntena govindaḥ pasparśāsyaṃ hi tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> touched his mouth with the tip of his conch.
Then, having obtained supreme knowledge of <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
he stood with joined palms and praised <s>Hari</s>, lord of all worlds:
'Be gracious, O god of gods, O lord of gods, bearer of conch, discus, and mace;
O self of the world, O self hidden in the Vedas, I have taken refuge in you, <s>Keśava</s>.'
Even the great-souled seers beginning with <s>Sanaka</s> do not know you,
so how could I know you? Reverence to you, lord of the worlds.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, laughing, said to him: Come, child; you are <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: sthānaṃ dhruvaṃ samāsādya jyotiṣām agrabhug bhava ||
children.translated_text: Having attained a fixed station, become foremost among the heavenly lights.
There, together with your mother, attain the station of the heavenly lights.
This supreme station of mine is fixed, eternal, and very beautiful.

children.text: tapasārādhya deveśaṃ purā labdhaṃ hi śaṅkarāt
children.translated_text: Long ago it was obtained from <s>Śaṅkara</s> through austerity, after worshiping the lord of the gods.
The learned man who constantly recites the formula 'for <s>Vāsudeva</s>,' joined with the praṇava,
combined with obeisance and joined with the word 'blessed lord,'

children.text: japedevaṃ hi yo vidvāndhruvaṃ sthānaṃ prapadyate ||
children.translated_text: he indeed attains the fixed station.

children.text: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods, together with the <s>Gandharvas</s>, the perfected beings, and the supreme seers,

children.text: mātrā saha dhruvaṃ sarve tasmin sthāne nyaveśayan ||
children.translated_text: all placed <s>Dhruva</s>, together with his mother, in that station.
Putting <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s command before them, he attained the station of the heavenly lights.
Thus the greatly radiant <s>Dhruva</s>, by means of the twelve-syllable knowledge,
attained great perfection. This has been told to you by me.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Therefore the man who makes obeisance to <s>Vāsudeva</s>

children.text: sa yāti dhruvasālokyaṃ dhruvatvaṃ tasya tattathā ||
children.translated_text: goes to the same world as <s>Dhruva</s>, and his state is likewise that of <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge bhuvanakośe dhruvasaṃsthānavarṇanaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga-mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, in the section on the arrangement of the worlds, the sixty-second chapter, named the Description of the Establishment of <s>Dhruva</s>.
The seers said:
Tell us now, O <s>Sūta</s>, in unsurpassed order, the origin
of the gods, demons, <s>Gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Among the earlier beings, creation is said to have arisen from intention, sight, and touch.
After <s>Dakṣa Prācetasa</s>, creation came to be born from sexual union.
But when the world did not increase as he created gods, seers, hosts, and serpents,
then it increased through the joining of male and female.
<s>Dakṣa</s> begot five thousand sons in <s>Sūtī</s>.
Seeing those highly blessed ones, he wished to create various creatures.
<s>Nārada</s> spoke to the <s>Haryaśvas</s>, the assembled sons of <s>Dakṣa</s>:

children.text: bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvordhvamadha eva ca ||
children.translated_text: After fully knowing the measure of the earth, above and below,
then, O best sages, carry out creation in full detail.

children.text: te tu tadvacanaṃ śrutvā prayātāḥ sarvatodiśam ||
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, they set out in every direction.
To this day they do not return, like rivers from the ocean.
When the <s>Haryaśvas</s> had disappeared, <s>Dakṣa</s> the lord of creatures again
created a thousand sons, the lord again doing so in <s>Sūtī</s>.

children.text: śabalā nāma te viprāḥ sametāḥ sṛṣṭihetavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those priests, called the <s>Śabalas</s>, had gathered as causes of creation.
<s>Nārada</s> again spoke to those sun-bright ones who had followed after:

children.text: bhuvaḥ pramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ tu jñātvā bhrātṝn punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having fully known the measure of the earth and your brothers again and again,

children.text: āgatya vātha sṛṣṭiṃ vai kariṣyatha viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: then, after returning, you will carry out creation in full detail.
They too went by that very path, following the course of their brothers.
Then, when they too had disappeared, <s>Dakṣa Prācetasa</s>, the lord of creatures,
begot sixty daughters in <s>Vairiṇī</s>.
He gave ten to <s>Dharma</s>, thirteen to <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
twenty-seven to <s>Soma</s>, and four to <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>.

children.text: dve caiva bhṛguputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate
children.translated_text: He gave two to the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, two to the wise <s>Kṛśāśva</s>,
and likewise two to <s>Aṅgiras</s>. Hear their names in detail.
Hear from the beginning the expansion of the progeny of the mothers of the gods:
<s>Marutvatī</s>, <s>Vasū</s>, <s>Yāmī</s>, <s>Lambā</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, and <s>Arundhatī</s>,

children.text: saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī
children.translated_text: and <s>Saṃkalpā</s>, <s>Muhūrtā</s>, <s>Sādhyā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, and <s>Bhāminī</s>.
These are declared to be the wives of <s>Dharma</s>; I shall tell you their sons.
The <s>Viśvedevas</s> were born from <s>Viśvā</s>; <s>Sādhyā</s> gave birth to the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
The <s>Marutvants</s> were born in <s>Marutvatī</s>, and the <s>Vasus</s> from <s>Vasū</s>.
The <s>Bhānus</s> are said to be from <s>Bhānu</s>, and the <s>Muhūrtakas</s> from <s>Muhūrtā</s>.
From <s>Lambā</s> came those named <s>Ghoṣa</s>, and <s>Nāgavīthi</s> was born of <s>Yāmī</s>.
From <s>Saṃkalpā</s> came <s>Saṃkalpa</s>. I shall tell you the creation of the <s>Vasus</s>.
Those radiant gods who pervade all directions
are called the <s>Vasus</s>, desiring the welfare of all beings.

children.text: āpo dhruvaś ca somaś ca dharaścaivānilo'nalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āpa</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Dhara</s>, and also <s>Anila</s> and <s>Anala</s>,

children.text: pratyūṣaś ca prabhāsaś ca vasavo'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyūṣa</s> and <s>Prabhāsa</s> are celebrated as the eight <s>Vasus</s>.
<s>Ajaikapād</s>, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s> together with <s>Bhairava</s>,

children.text: haraś ca bahurūpaś ca tryaṃbakaś ca sureśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, <s>Bahurūpa</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>, and <s>Sureśvara</s>,

children.text: sāvitraś ca jayantaś ca pinākī cāparājitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāvitra</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Pinākī</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>:
these are declared to be the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, lords of hosts.
I shall proclaim the sons and grandsons from the wives of <s>Kaśyapa</s>.

children.text: aditiś ca ditiścaiva ariṣṭā surasā muniḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Ariṣṭā</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Muni</s>,

children.text: surabhir vinatā tāmrā tadvat krodhavaśā ilā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Surabhi</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, <s>Tāmrā</s>, likewise <s>Krodhavaśā</s> and <s>Ilā</s>,
<s>Kadrū</s>, <s>Tviṣā</s>, and likewise <s>Danu</s>: I shall tell you their sons.
Those gods who were named <s>Tuṣitas</s> in the interval of <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s>

children.text: vaivasvatāntare te vai ādityā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: are remembered in the <s>Vaivasvata</s> interval as the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>.
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, then <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Aryaman</s>,
<s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Aṃśumān</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> as well:
these thousand-rayed ones are remembered as the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>.

children.text: ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapāditi naḥ śrutam
children.translated_text: <s>Diti</s> obtained two sons from <s>Kaśyapa</s>; so we have heard:
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and also <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
<s>Danu</s> obtained a hundred sons from <s>Kaśyapa</s>, proud in their strength.
<s>Vipracitti</s> was foremost among them, O best twice-born ones.

children.text: tāmrā ca janayāmāsa ṣaṭ kanyā dvijapuṅgavāḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Tāmrā</s> gave birth to six daughters, O bulls among twice-born men:

children.text: śukīṃ śyenīṃ ca bhāsīṃ ca sugrīvīṃ gṛdhrikāṃ śucim ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukī</s>, <s>Śyenī</s>, <s>Bhāsī</s>, <s>Sugrīvī</s>, <s>Gṛdhrikā</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>.
<s>Śukī</s>, in accordance with <s>dharma</s> (right order), gave birth to parrots and owls,

children.text: śyenī śyenāṃs tathā bhāsī kuraṅgāṃś ca vyajījanat ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Śyenī</s> produced hawks; likewise <s>Bhāsī</s> gave birth to kuraṅgas.

children.text: gṛdhrī gṛdhrān kapotāṃś ca pārāvatī vihaṃgamān
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛdhrī</s> produced vultures, pigeons, doves, and birds,
while <s>Śuci</s> gave birth to haṃsas, sārasas, kāraṇḍavas, and plavas.
And <s>Sugrīvī</s> produced goats, horses, sheep, camels, and donkeys.
The auspicious <s>Vinatā</s> gave birth to <s>Garuḍa</s> and <s>Aruṇa</s>,
and also to a daughter, <s>Saudāminī</s>, who was terrifying to all worlds.
Long ago a thousand serpents were born from <s>Surasā</s>.
The well-vowed <s>Kadrū</s> obtained a thousand thousand-headed serpents.
Among them twenty-six foremost ones are celebrated as unsurpassed:
<s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Karkoṭa</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Airāvata</s>, and <s>Kambala</s>,
<s>Dhanañjaya</s>, <s>Mahānīla</s>, <s>Padma</s>, <s>Aśvatara</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>,
<s>Elāpatra</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, and <s>Balāhaka</s>,
<s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, <s>Mahāśaṅkha</s>, <s>Puṣpadaṃṣṭra</s>, and <s>Śubhānana</s>,

children.text: śaṅkhalomā ca nahuṣo vāmanaḥ phaṇitas tathā
children.translated_text: and <s>Śaṅkhalomā</s>, <s>Nahuṣa</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and <s>Phaṇita</s>,
as well as <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Durmukha</s>, and <s>Patañjali</s>, so they are remembered.
<s>Krodhavaśā</s> produced the host of Rākṣasas, powerful in illusion,
and likewise the host of Rudras, while the beautiful <s>Gomahiṣī</s>
gave birth to <s>Surabhi</s> from <s>Kaśyapa</s>; so we have heard.
<s>Muni</s> produced the host of sages and also the host of Apsarases.
Likewise <s>Ariṣṭā</s> gave birth to many Kiṃnaras and Gandharvas.
<s>Ilā</s> produced all grasses, trees, creepers, and shrubs.
But <s>Tviṣā</s> gave birth to Yakṣas and Rākṣasas by the ten million.
These descendants of <s>Kaśyapa</s> have been briefly recounted.
Their many lineages of sons, grandsons, and so on are remembered.
Thus, when the creatures had been created by great-souled <s>Kaśyapa</s>
and all moving and unmoving beings had been established,
<s>Prajāpati</s>, having consecrated the chief ones over their realms,
then made <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> the lord of human beings.
Those who were formerly consecrated by <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s> interval
still protect this entire earth, with its seven continents and mountains,
according to instruction and in accordance with <s>dharma</s>.
Those who were formerly consecrated by <s>Brahmā</s> in the earlier <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s> interval

children.text: te hyete cābhiṣicyante manavaś ca bhavanti te ||
children.translated_text: are indeed consecrated here, and they become the Manus.
In the past manvantaras these kings have passed away among them.
In this way others are consecrated when the next manvantara arrives.
All kings, past and future, are remembered in a manvantara.
Having produced these sons for the continuation of offspring,
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, desiring a founder of his lineage, again performed austerity,

children.text: putro gotrakaro mahyaṃ bhavatād iti cintayan ||
children.translated_text: thinking, 'May a son be born to me who will establish my lineage.'
While the great-souled <s>Kaśyapa</s> was meditating in this way,
afterward, through union with <s>Brahmā</s>, two sons of great vigor appeared.
They were <s>Vatsara</s> and <s>Asita</s>, both expounders of <s>brahman</s>.
From <s>Vatsara</s> were born <s>Naidhruva</s> and <s>Raibhya</s>, of very great fame.

children.text: raibhyasya raibhyā vijñeyā naidhruvasya vadāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: The descendants of <s>Raibhya</s> should be known as Raibhyas; I shall tell you of <s>Naidhruva</s>.
From the daughter of <s>Cyavana</s>, <s>Sumedhā</s> was born.

children.text: naidhruvasya tu sā patnī mātā vai kuṇḍapāyinām
children.translated_text: She was the wife of <s>Naidhruva</s> and the mother of the Kuṇḍapāyins.
From <s>Asita</s>, by <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, was born one most devoted to <s>brahman</s>,
the splendid <s>Devala</s>, best of the Śāṇḍilyas and very great in austerity.
The Śāṇḍilyas, Naidhruvas, and Raibhyas are the three branches of the Kāśyapas.

children.text: nava prakṛtayo devāḥ pulastyasya vadāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall tell you of the nine divine progenitors of <s>Pulastya</s>.
When a four-yuga cycle had passed in the eleventh Manu's reign, O lord,
and when half of it remained, with the Dvāpara age underway,

children.text: mānavasya nariṣyantaḥ putra āsīd damaḥ kila ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dama</s>, the son of <s>Nariṣyanta</s> and descendant of <s>Manu</s>, existed.
The heir of that <s>Dama</s> is remembered as <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>.
At the beginning of the Tretā age, in the third age, he became king.
His daughter <s>Ilavilā</s> was incomparable in beauty.
That royal seer gave the girl to <s>Pulastya</s>.
By her the sage <s>Viśravas</s>, called Airavila, was born.
He had four wives, increasers of the Paulastya family.

children.text: bṛhaspateḥ śubhā kanyā nāmnā vai devavarṇinī
children.translated_text: The auspicious daughter of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> was named <s>Devavarṇinī</s>.

children.text: puṣpotkaṭā balākā ca sute mālyavataḥ smṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puṣpotkaṭā</s> and <s>Balākā</s> are remembered as daughters of <s>Mālyavat</s>.

children.text: kaikasī mālinaḥ kanyā tāsāṃ vai śṛṇuta prajāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kaikasī</s> was the daughter of <s>Mālin</s>; listen now to their offspring.
<s>Devavarṇinī</s> gave birth to the eldest, <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.
And <s>Kaikasī</s> gave birth to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of Rākṣasas,
to <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>, <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>, and the wise <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Puṣpotkaṭā</s>, O best of twice-born men, bore sons to him:

children.text: mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca mahāpārśvaṃ kharaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and also <s>Khara</s>,

children.text: kumbhīnasīṃ tathā kanyāṃ balāyāḥ śṛṇuta prajāḥ
children.translated_text: and a daughter, <s>Kumbhīnasī</s>. Hear now the offspring of <s>Balā</s>.
<s>Triśiras</s>, <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, and the Rākṣasa <s>Vidyujjihva</s>

children.text: kanyā vai mālikā cāpi balāyāḥ prasavaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: and a daughter, <s>Mālikā</s>, are remembered as the children of <s>Balā</s>.
Thus these nine Paulastya Rākṣasas were performers of cruel deeds.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> is proclaimed as exceedingly pure in self and a knower of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pulastyasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyāghrāś ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sons of <s>Pulastya</s> were all wild animals, tigers, and fanged beasts,

children.text: bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāś ca sūkarā hastinas tathā
children.translated_text: as well as Bhūtas, Piśācas, serpents, boars, and elephants.

children.text: vānarāḥ kiṃnarāścaiva ye ca kiṃpuruṣās tathā ||
children.translated_text: and also monkeys and <s>Kiṃnaras</s>, and likewise those who are <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>.
<s>Kratu</s> is remembered in that Vaivasvata interval as without offspring.

children.text: atreḥ patnyo daśaivāsan suṃdaryaś ca pativratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Atri had exactly ten wives, beautiful and devoted to their husband.
Of <s>Bhadrāśva</s>, through <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, there were ten offspring among the <s>Apsarases</s>:

children.text: bhadrābhadrā ca jaladā mandā nandā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Abhadrā</s>, <s>Jaladā</s>, <s>Mandā</s>, and likewise <s>Nandā</s>;

children.text: balābalā ca viprendrā yā ca gopābalā smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Balā</s> and <s>Abalā</s>, O best of brahmins, and she who is remembered as <s>Gopābalā</s>;

children.text: tathā tāmarasā caiva varakrīḍā ca vai daśa ||
children.translated_text: also <s>Tāmarasā</s> and <s>Varakrīḍā</s>: these are indeed the ten.
They arose from the lineage of <s>Atri</s>; their husband was <s>Prabhākara</s>.
When the sun had been covered by <s>Svarbhānu</s> and was falling from heaven to the earth,
and when this world was overpowered by darkness, light was set in motion by him.
When he said, 'May there be welfare for you,' as the maker of day was falling here,
through that brahmarṣi's word the mighty one did not fall from heaven.
Therefore the lord <s>Atri</s> was called <s>Prabhākara</s> by the great seers.
In <s>Bhadrā</s> he begot the glorious son <s>Soma</s>.
That treasure of austerity again begot sons among those women.
They were famous as the <s>Svastyātreyas</s>, seers who had reached the far shore of the Vedas.

children.text: teṣāṃ dvau khyātayaśasau brahmiṣṭhau ca mahaujasau ||
children.translated_text: Of them, two were renowned in fame, most devoted to brahman, and very powerful:
<s>Datta</s>, the eldest and excellent son of <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Durvāsas</s>, his younger brother.
Their youngest sister was the stainless <s>Amalā</s>, a speaker on brahman.
In his two gotras four men were born, famed upon the earth:
<s>Śyāva</s>, <s>Pratvasa</s>, <s>Vavalgu</s>, and then <s>Gahvara</s>.

children.text: ātreyāṇāṃ ca catvāraḥ smṛtāḥ pakṣā mahātmanām
children.translated_text: These four branches of the great-souled <s>Ātreyas</s> are remembered.
<s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Parvata</s>, and also <s>Anuddhata</s>:
know that these were mind-born sons of <s>Arundhatī</s>.
<s>Nārada</s> gave <s>Arundhatī</s> to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
Because of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s curse, <s>Nārada</s> was one whose seed flowed upward, of great radiance.

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe ghore vai tārakāmaye ||
children.translated_text: Long ago, in the terrible war of gods and demons called the <s>Tārakāmaya</s>,

children.text: anāvṛṣṭyā hate loke hyugre lokeśvaraiḥ saha
children.translated_text: when the world had been struck by drought, in a fierce age together with the lords of the world,
wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> sustained the creatures by his austerity,
bringing forth food and water, roots and fruits, and medicinal herbs.
Out of compassion he kept those creatures alive, and also by means of medicine.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> begot a hundred sons in <s>Arundhatī</s>.
<s>Adṛśyantī</s> bore <s>Parāśara</s> from <s>Śakti</s>, the eldest.

children.text: rakṣasā bhakṣite śaktau rudhireṇa tu vai tadā
children.translated_text: When <s>Śakti</s> was devoured by the demon <s>Rudhira</s>, at that time,
<s>Kālī</s> bore the lord <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> from <s>Parāśara</s>.
<s>Dvaipāyana</s>, in <s>Araṇī</s>, begot the son <s>Śuka</s>.
And through <s>Pīvarī</s> he had <s>Upamanyu</s>; know these as the sons of <s>Śuka</s>:

children.text: bhūriśravāḥ prabhuḥ śaṃbhuḥ kṛṣṇo gaurastu pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūriśravas</s>, <s>Prabhu</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Gaura</s> as the fifth.
And the daughter <s>Kīrtimatī</s>, mother of yoga, firm in her vows,

children.text: jananī brahmadattasya patnī sā tvanuhasya ca
children.translated_text: was the mother of <s>Brahmadatta</s> and the wife of <s>Anuha</s>.

children.text: śvetaḥ kṛṣṇaś ca gauraś ca śyāmo dhūmrastathāruṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Gaura</s>, <s>Śyāma</s>, <s>Dhūmra</s>, and <s>Aruṇa</s>,
<s>Nīla</s> and <s>Bādarika</s>: all these are <s>Parāśaras</s>.
These are said to be the eight branches of the great-souled <s>Parāśaras</s>.
After this, learn of the origin of <s>Indrapramiti</s>.
The <s>Kapiñjalī</s> of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was born through <s>Ghṛtācī</s>.
He who is called <s>Trimūrti</s> is known as <s>Indrapramiti</s>.
<s>Bhadra</s> was born from the daughter of <s>Pṛthu</s>; from her he had <s>Vasu</s>.
His son was <s>Upamanyu</s>, and the <s>Aupamanyavas</s> were many.
And those descended from <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> are widely heard of as <s>Kauṇḍinyas</s>.

children.text: ekārṣeyās tathā cānye vāsiṣṭhā nāma viśrutāḥ
children.translated_text: Others too, single-seer lineages, are famed under the name <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: ete pakṣā vasiṣṭhānāṃ smṛtā daśa mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: These ten branches of the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭhas</s> are remembered.

children.text: ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrā mānasā viśrutā bhuvi
children.translated_text: Thus these sons of <s>Brahmā</s>, mind-born, are renowned upon the earth.

children.text: bhartāraś ca mahābhāgā eṣāṃ vaṃśāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These greatly fortunate patriarchs and their lineages have been proclaimed.
Born in the families of divine seers, they are able to sustain the three worlds.

children.text: teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their sons and grandsons are in the hundreds and then in the thousands.
By them the three worlds are pervaded, like the sun by its rays.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge devādisṛṣṭikathanaṃ nāma triṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the sixty-third chapter, named 'The Account of the Creation of the Gods and Others.'
The seers said:

children.text: kathaṃ hi rakṣasā śaktir bhakṣitaḥ so'nujaiḥ saha
children.translated_text: How indeed was <s>Śakti</s> devoured by a demon, together with his younger brothers?
O <s>Sūta</s>, best of speakers, you should tell this here concerning <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: rākṣaso rudhiro nāma vasiṣṭhasya sutaṃ purā
children.translated_text: Long ago a demon named <s>Rudhira</s>
devoured <s>Śakti</s>, son of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, together with his younger brothers, because of <s>Śakti</s>'s curse.
O best of brahmins, having approached King <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, for whom <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> officiated at sacrifice,
<s>Rudhira</s> was urged on by <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.

children.text: bhakṣitaḥ sa iti śrutvā vasiṣṭhastena rakṣasā
children.translated_text: When <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> heard, 'He has been devoured by that demon,'

children.text: śaktiḥ śaktimatāṃ śreṣṭho bhrātṛbhiḥ saha dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: namely <s>Śakti</s>, the best of the powerful, a knower of dharma, together with his brothers,

children.text: hā putra putra putreti krandamāno muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: crying again and again, 'Alas, my son! My son! My son!'

children.text: arundhatyā saha muniḥ papāta bhuvi duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the sorrowing sage fell to the ground together with <s>Arundhatī</s>.

children.text: naṣṭaṃ kulamiti śrutvā martuṃ cakre matiṃ tadā
children.translated_text: Having heard that his family was destroyed, he then resolved to die,
remembering his hundred sons and <s>Śakti</s>, the eldest, powerful as he was.

children.text: na taṃ vināhaṃ jīviṣye iti niścitya duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In grief he decided, 'Without him I shall not live.'

children.text: āruhya mūrdhānam ajātmajo'sau tayātmavān sarvavid ātmavicca
children.translated_text: That sonless one, self-possessed, all-knowing, and a knower of the self, climbed to the summit,

children.text: dharādharasyaiva tadā dharāyāṃ papāta patnyā saha sāśrudṛṣṭiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then fell from the mountain to the ground, together with his wife, his eyes filled with tears.

children.text: dharādharāttaṃ patitaṃ dharā tadā dadhāra tatrāpi vicitrakaṇṭhī
children.translated_text: As he fell from the mountain, the earth, <s>Vicitrakaṇṭhī</s>, then held him even there.

children.text: karāṃbujābhyāṃ karikhelagāminī rudantamādāya ruroda sā ca ||
children.translated_text: With her lotus-hands she took up the weeping woman, whose gait was like an elephant at play, and she too wept.

children.text: tadā tasya snuṣā prāha patnī śaktermahāmunim
children.translated_text: Then his daughter-in-law, the wife of <s>Śakti</s>, spoke to the great sage,
to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of speakers, while she wept and trembled with fear:
“Blessed one, best of brahmins, this auspicious body of yours

children.text: pālayasva vibho draṣṭuṃ tava pautraṃ mamātmajam ||
children.translated_text: you must preserve, O lord, in order to see your grandson, my son.
O lord of brahmins, this very beautiful body of yours must not be abandoned,
for the child in my womb, born of <s>Śakti</s>, will accomplish every purpose.”
Having spoken thus, that knower of <s>dharma</s>, lotus-eyed and noble,

children.text: utthāpya śvaśuraṃ natvā netre saṃmṛjya vāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: raised her father-in-law with both hands, bowed to him, and wiped her eyes with water.
Though herself afflicted, then wishing to rescue her afflicted father-in-law,
the auspicious woman also entreated afflicted <s>Arundhatī</s>.

children.text: snuṣāvākyaṃ tataḥ śrutvā vasiṣṭha utthāya bhūtalāt
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the words of his daughter-in-law, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> rose from the ground,
regained consciousness, and embraced her; she fell down, deeply distressed.
<s>Arundhatī</s> touched her with both hands, her eyes filled with tears,
and the tiger among sages, loving his son, wept together with his wife.
Then, as four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> sits in the lotus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>’s navel,
that boy, seated on the bed of the womb, recited a Vedic verse.
Then blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, hearing the verse with reverence,
wondered, “By whom was this spoken?” and stood there composed in concentration.
Then <s>Hari</s>, lotus-eyed, standing in the expanse of the sky,
the soul of the universe and a treasury of compassion, spoke compassionately to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: bho vatsa vatsa viprendra vasiṣṭha sutavatsala
children.translated_text: “O child, child, O lord of brahmins, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, lover of your son,
this Vedic verse has now issued from the lotus-mouth of your grandson.
That grandson of yours, born of <s>Śakti</s>, is equal to me and powerful, O sage.
Therefore rise, casting aside grief, best son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
While still in the womb he is a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>, intent on the worship of <s>Rudra</s>.
By the power of the god <s>Rudra</s>, he will carry your lineage across.
Having spoken thus to the brahmin, the compassionate blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s>
vanished right there from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the tiger among sages.
Then <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, of great radiance, bowed his head to the lotus-eyed one,
and when he had disappeared, he reverently touched the belly of <s>Adṛśyantī</s>.

children.text: hā putra putra putreti papāta ca suduḥkhitaḥ
children.translated_text: “Alas, my son, my son, my son!” he cried, and fell down, overwhelmed with grief.
Seeing <s>Arundhatī</s> weeping then, he lamented, O twice-borns,
and, remembering his own son in sorrow, said, “Come again, come, my child.

children.text: tava putramimaṃ dṛṣṭvā bho śakte kuladhāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing this son of yours, O <s>Śakti</s>, the support of the family,

children.text: tavāntikaṃ gamiṣyāmi tava mātrā na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall go to your side together with your mother; there is no doubt.”
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the weeping brahmin then embraced <s>Arundhatī</s>,

children.text: papāta tāḍayantīva svasya kukṣī kareṇa vai
children.translated_text: and fell down; and <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, as though striking her own belly with her hand,
then struck that auspicious abode of the son of <s>Śakti</s>.

children.text: svodaraṃ duḥkhitā bhūmau lalāpa ca papāta ca
children.translated_text: Distressed, she beat her own belly on the ground, lamented, and fell.

children.text: arundhati tadā bhītā vasiṣṭhaś ca mahāmatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Arundhatī</s> and wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, frightened,
raised up their young daughter-in-law and, overcome with fear, said:

children.text: vicāramugdhe tava garbhamaṇḍalaṃ karāṃbujābhyāṃ vinihatya durlabham
children.translated_text: “O noble woman, bewildered by reflection, having struck with your lotus-hands

children.text: kulaṃ vasiṣṭhasya samastamapyaho nihantumārye kathamudyatā vada ||
children.translated_text: the precious circle of your womb, why are you intent on destroying the whole family of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>? Tell us.

children.text: tavātmajaṃ śaktisutaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cāsvādya vaktrāmṛtam āryasūnoḥ
children.translated_text: After seeing your son, the son of <s>Śakti</s>, and tasting the nectar of the noble boy’s face,

children.text: trātuṃ yato dehamimaṃ munīndraḥ suniścitaḥ pāhi tataḥ śarīram ||
children.translated_text: this lord of sages is firmly resolved to preserve this body; therefore protect your body.”
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having thus reproached her daughter-in-law, <s>Arundhatī</s> stood by the sage,
and, distressed and shaken, <s>Arundhatī</s> spoke to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>:

children.text: tvayyeva jīvitaṃ cāsya muner yat suvrate mama
children.translated_text: “O well-vowed one, since this sage’s life rests in you alone,

children.text: jīvitaṃ rakṣa dehasya dhātrī ca kuru yaddhitam ||
children.translated_text: preserve the life of your body, be its nurse, and do what is beneficial.”
<s>Adṛśyantī</s> said:

children.text: mayā yadi muniśreṣṭhas trātuṃ vai niścitaṃ svakam
children.translated_text: “If I have indeed resolved, O best of sages, to preserve my own body,
then somehow I shall preserve this body of mine, whether inauspicious or auspicious.
I have met the grief of losing my beloved; I am no true wife, of this there is no doubt.

children.text: mune duḥkhādahaṃ dagdhā yataḥ putrī mune tava ||
children.translated_text: O sage, I am burned by sorrow, for I am your daughter, O sage.

children.text: aho'dbhutaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ duḥkhapātrī hyahaṃ vibho
children.translated_text: Ah, a wonder has been seen by me; I am indeed a vessel of sorrow, O lord.
Be my rescuer from sorrow, O brahmin, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, teacher of the world.
Even so, a woman without her husband is pitiable here.

children.text: pāhi māṃ tata āryendra paribhūtā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore protect me, O noble lord, for otherwise I shall be despised.

children.text: pitā mātā ca putrāśca pautrāḥ śvaśura eva ca
children.translated_text: Father, mother, sons, grandsons, and father-in-law:

children.text: ete na bāndhavāḥ strīṇāṃ bhartā bandhuḥ parā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: these are not a woman’s true relatives; the husband is her relative, her supreme refuge.
Even what the learned have called half of one’s own self

children.text: tadapyatra mṛṣā hyāsīd gataḥ śaktirahaṃ sthitā ||
children.translated_text: has proved false here, for <s>Śakti</s> is gone and I remain.
Ah, O bull among sages, how hard my heart is here,

children.text: patiṃ prāṇasamaṃ tyaktvā sthitā yatra kṣaṇaṃ yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: since I have remained even a moment after abandoning my husband, who was equal to my life.
Like a vine that remains alive by clinging to an excellent aśvattha tree,
I too remain alive, though rootless, abandoned by my husband and wretched.”
Hearing the words of his daughter-in-law, wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, together with his wife,

children.text: tadā cakre matiṃ dhīmān yātuṃ svāśramamāśramī ||
children.translated_text: then, as a hermit, resolved to go to his own hermitage.
With difficulty, blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, together with his wife, quickly reached his hermitage,

children.text: adṛśyantyā ca puṇyātmā saṃviveśa sa cintayan ||
children.translated_text: and the holy one entered it with <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, absorbed in thought.
She, the chaste wife of <s>Śakti</s>, somehow preserved the womb, O bulls among sages,
for the sake of sustaining the lineage.

children.text: tataḥ sāsūta tanayaṃ daśame māsi suprabham
children.translated_text: Then in the tenth month she gave birth to a very radiant son.
As <s>Arundhatī</s>, the wife of <s>Śakti</s>, gave birth according to her power to the powerful one,

children.text: asūta sā ditirviṣṇuṃ yathā svāhā guhaṃ sutam
children.translated_text: so <s>Diti</s> bore <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as <s>Svāhā</s> bore <s>Guha</s> as her son,
and as the kindling-stick, the wife of fire, bore <s>Agni</s>; she gave birth directly to <s>Parāśara</s>, the son of <s>Śakti</s>.
When the son of <s>Śakti</s> had thus descended upon the surface of the earth,

children.text: śaktistyaktvā tadā duḥkhaṃ pitṝṇāṃ samatāṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s>, giving up his sorrow, attained equality with the ancestors.

children.text: bhrātṛbhiḥ saha puṇyātmā ādityair iva bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: Together with his brothers, the blessed one shone like the sun among the <s>Ādityas</s>,
dwelling in the world of the ancestors, that foremost sage of the line of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: jagustadā ca pitaro nanṛtuś ca pitāmahāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the ancestors sang, and the grandfathers danced,
and the great-grandfathers too, O best brahmins, when <s>Parāśara</s> had descended.

children.text: ye brahmavādino bhūmau nanṛtur divi devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who were expounders of <s>brahman</s> on earth danced, and the gods in heaven did the same.

children.text: puṣkarādyāś ca sasṛjuḥ puṣpavarṣaṃ ca khecarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sky-goers, beginning with <s>Puṣkara</s>, released a shower of flowers.

children.text: pureṣu rākṣasānāṃ ca praṇādaṃ viṣamaṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: In the cities of the rākṣasas there was a harsh tumult, O twice-born ones,
while the sages dwelling in their hermitages were filled with a continuity of joy.
That <s>Parāśara</s> too appeared as the sun appears from the cosmic egg,
four-faced to <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, like the day-maker emerging from a mass of clouds.
For <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, O twice-born ones, there was both happiness and sorrow:
happiness at seeing her son, and sorrow as she remembered her husband and the sage <s>Arundhatī</s>.
Seeing her son, the very radiant <s>Parāśara</s>, the young woman

children.text: lalāpa vihvalā bālā sannakaṇṭhī papāta ca ||
children.translated_text: lamented in agitation; choked in the throat, she fell down.

children.text: sā parāśaramaho mahāmatiṃ devadānavagaṇaiś ca pūjitam
children.translated_text: Seeing that great-minded <s>Parāśara</s>, honored by hosts of gods and dānavas,

children.text: jātamātram anaghaṃ śucismitā budhya sāśrunayanā lalāpa ca ||
children.translated_text: the sinless child just born, the pure-smiling woman, with tearful eyes, lamented.

children.text: hā vasiṣṭhasuta kutracidgataḥ paśya putramanaghaṃ tavātmajam
children.translated_text: "Alas, son of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, wherever you have gone, behold your son, your sinless child.
You have abandoned me, poor-faced, in the depths of the forest, O lord, intent on seeing a son.

children.text: śakte svaṃ ca sutaṃ paśya bhrātṛbhiḥ saha ṣaṇmukham
children.translated_text: O <s>Śakti</s>, behold your own son, six-faced together with his brothers,
just as <s>Maheśvara</s>, with his hosts and a delighted face, beheld his son."
Then, hearing her lament at that time, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the best of sages,

children.text: śrutvā snuṣāmuvācedaṃ mā rodīr iti duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke these words to his daughter-in-law in sorrow: "Do not weep."

children.text: ājñayā tasya sā śokaṃ vasiṣṭhasya kulāṅganā
children.translated_text: At the command of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, that woman of the family
cast off her grief and cared for the child, young and doe-eyed.
Seeing that powerless, virtuous woman seated there without auspicious ornaments,
distraught and with eyes clouded by tears, he said:
<s>Śākteya</s> said:

children.text: amba maṅgalavibhūṣaṇair vinā dehayaṣṭiranaghe na śobhate
children.translated_text: "Mother, O sinless one, your bodily form does not shine without auspicious adornments.
You ought to tell me the reason today, for you are like a night without the disk of the moon.
Mother, mother, why have you abandoned your auspicious ornaments
and sit like one whose husband is gone? You ought to tell me, beautiful one."

children.text: adṛśyantī tadā vākyaṃ śrutvā tasya sutasya sā
children.translated_text: When <s>Adṛśyantī</s> heard those words of her son at that time,

children.text: na kiṃcid abravīt putraṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vetarat ||
children.translated_text: she said nothing to the child, neither good nor otherwise.
Again the blessed <s>Śākteya</s> spoke to <s>Adṛśyantī</s>:

children.text: mātaḥ kutra mahātejāḥ pitā vada vadeti tām ||
children.translated_text: "Mother, where is my father, the greatly radiant one? Tell me, tell me," he said to her.

children.text: śrutvā ruroda sā vākyaṃ putrasyātīva vihvalā
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of her son, she wept, utterly overwhelmed,
and fell down, saying, "Your father, dear child, was eaten by a rākṣasa."

children.text: śrutvā vasiṣṭho 'pi papāta bhūmau pautrasya vākyaṃ sa rudandayāluḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing his grandson's words, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> too fell to the ground, weeping in compassion,
as did <s>Arundhatī</s>, the hermitage-dwellers, and the lordly sages of the sage <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.

children.text: bhakṣito rakṣasā mātuḥ pitā tava mukhāditi
children.translated_text: Hearing from his mother's mouth, "Your father was eaten by a rākṣasa,"
hearing this, wise <s>Parāśara</s> spoke, his eyes filled with tears.
<s>Parāśara</s> said:
"After worshiping the god of gods, I shall show you, mother,

children.text: kṣaṇena mātaḥ pitaraṃ darśayāmīti me matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: in a moment my father and the three worlds with all moving and unmoving beings: this is my resolve."

children.text: sā niśamya vacanaṃ tadā śubhaṃ sasmitā tanayamāha vismitā
children.translated_text: Hearing those auspicious words, she smiled and, astonished, addressed her son.

children.text: tathyam etaditi taṃ nirīkṣya sā putra putra bhavamarcayeti ca ||
children.translated_text: Looking at him, she said, "This is true. Son, son, worship <s>Bhava</s>."
Knowing the resolve of this son of <s>Śakti</s>, the foremost sage,
the blessed, wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, a treasure of compassion, spoke to his grandson:
"Your resolve is proper, grandson, best of sages, O well-vowed one.

children.text: tathāpi śṛṇu lokasya kṣayaṃ kartuṃ na cārhasi ||
children.translated_text: Even so, listen: you should not bring about the destruction of the world.
Perform worship of the Lord of all for the nonexistence of the rākṣasas.

children.text: trailokyaṃ śṛṇu śākteya aparādhyati kiṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Śākteya</s>: in what way has the triple world offended you?"
Then, at the instruction of that <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the son of <s>Śakti</s>,
being very wise, set his mind on the destruction of the rākṣasas.
After bowing to <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and then to <s>Arundhatī</s>,
he made a temporary single <s>liṅga</s> out of dust in the presence of the sage.
Having worshiped it with the <s>Śivasūkta</s> and the auspicious <s>Tryambaka</s>,
and having recited the <s>Tvaritarudra</s> and the <s>Śivasaṃkalpa</s>,

children.text: nīlarudraṃ ca śākteyastathā rudraṃ ca śobhanam
children.translated_text: as well as the <s>Nīlarudra</s>, the splendid <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: vāmīyaṃ pavamānaṃ ca pañcabrahma tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vāmīya</s>, the <s>Pavamāna</s>, and likewise the <s>Pañcabrahma</s>,

children.text: hotāraṃ liṅgasūktaṃ ca atharvaśira eva ca
children.translated_text: the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the <s>Liṅgasūkta</s>, and the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>,
he gave an eight-limbed oblation to <s>Rudra</s> and worshiped him according to rule.
<s>Parāśara</s> said:
"Blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, my greatly radiant father

children.text: pitā mama mahātejā bhrātṛbhiḥ saha śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: was indeed eaten in blood by a rākṣasa, together with his brothers.
Blessed one, I wish to see my father together with his brothers."
Thus making his petition to the <s>liṅga</s>, he bowed down again and again.

children.text: hā rudra rudra rudreti ruroda nipapāta ca
children.translated_text: Crying "Alas, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>!" he wept and fell down.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānrudro devīmāha ca śaṅkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, spoke to the goddess:
"Look, O highly blessed one, at the child whose eyes are clouded with tears,
absorbed in remembrance of me and wholly intent on worshiping me."
And when that blameless great goddess saw <s>Parāśara</s>,
his whole body drenched with sorrow and his eyes filled with tears,
intent upon the rite of worshiping the <s>liṅga</s> and saying, '<s>Hara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>,'
<s>Umā</s> spoke to her husband, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, lord of the worlds:
'Grant him everything he desires. Be gracious, O supreme lord.'
Hearing her words, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme lord,
the drinker of the <s>Hālāhala</s> poison, then said to his noble wife <s>Umā</s>:
'I shall protect this young twice-born boy, whose eyes are like full-blown blue lotuses.
I grant him sight; indeed he is able to behold my form.'
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s>, with divine gaṇas,
the supreme lord, surrounded by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the others,

children.text: dadau ca darśanaṃ tasmai muniputrāya dhīmate ||
children.translated_text: gave a vision of himself to that wise son of the sage.
He too, seeing <s>Mahādeva</s>, his eyes wet with tears of joy,
fell down with delighted heart at his feet, reverently.

children.text: punarbhavānyāḥ pādau ca nandinaś ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Again he bowed to the feet of <s>Bhavānī</s> and of the great-souled <s>Nandin</s>.
'Today my life is fruitful,' he then said to <s>Brahmā</s> and the others.
'The one adorned with the young moon has come today for my protection.

children.text: ko'nyaḥ samo mayā loke devo vā dānavo 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: What other god or even Dānava in the world is equal to me?'
Then, in that very instant, <s>Parāśara</s>, son of <s>Śakti</s>, saw in the sky
his father standing together with his brothers.
Seeing him, together with his brothers, in a celestial car shining like the disk of the sun and facing every direction,

children.text: bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā nanāma ca jaharṣa ca ||
children.translated_text: he bowed down and rejoiced.
Then the god whose banner bears the bull, together with his wife and the lord of the gaṇas,
spoke these words to the son of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, who was intent on seeing his son:
The blessed god said:
'O <s>Śakti</s>, behold your young son, his eyes wet with tears of joy,

children.text: adṛśyantīṃ ca viprendra vasiṣṭhaṃ pitaraṃ tava ||
children.translated_text: and behold <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, O best of Brahmins, and your father <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
and the very fortunate, auspicious <s>Arundhatī</s>, who is like a goddess.
Bow to both your mother and your father, O great-minded one.'
Then, by <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s command, <s>Śakti</s> quickly bowed to <s>Hara</s>, god of gods, and likewise to <s>Umā</s>,

children.text: vasiṣṭhaṃ ca tadā śreṣṭhaṃ śaktir vai śaṅkarājñayā ||
children.translated_text: and then to excellent <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
At the command of the lord of the world, mighty <s>Śakti</s> addressed his mother,
the very fortunate and auspicious <s>Arundhatī</s>, devoted to her husband.
The son of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said:

children.text: bho vatsa vatsa viprendra parāśara mahādyute
children.translated_text: 'Ah, child, child, O best of Brahmins, <s>Parāśara</s> of great splendor,
I was protected by you, dear son, great-souled even while still in the womb.
O child <s>Parāśara</s>, the lordly power of qualities beginning with minuteness has been obtained by me,
and today, O boy, your face has been seen by my command.
Protect the very fortunate <s>Adṛśyantī</s>, O child of great mind,

children.text: arundhatīṃ ca pitaraṃ vasiṣṭhaṃ mama sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: and always protect <s>Arundhatī</s> and my father <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>.
My entire lineage, dear child, has been carried across by you.
For it is always said by the good that one conquers the worlds through a son.
Choose what you desire from <s>Īśāna</s>, the lord who is the source of the worlds.
Having bowed to lord <s>Śaṅkara</s>, I shall go with my brothers.'
Thus addressing his son, and bowing to <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: nirīkṣya bhāryāṃ sadasi jagāma pitaraṃ vaśī ||
children.translated_text: the self-controlled one looked at his wife in the assembly and went to his father.
Then, seeing that his father had gone, the son of <s>Śakti</s> worshiped <s>Śaṅkara</s>
and praised the moon-crested one with chosen words.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, the crusher of <s>Manmatha</s> and <s>Andhaka</s>, was pleased,
and after favoring the son of <s>Śakti</s>, disappeared right there.

children.text: gate maheśvare sāṃbe praṇamya ca maheśvaram
children.translated_text: When <s>Maheśvara</s> had gone with <s>Ambā</s>, he bowed to <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: dadāha rākṣasānāṃ tu kulaṃ mantreṇa mantravit ||
children.translated_text: and, skilled in mantras, burned the family of the Rākṣasas by a mantra.

children.text: tadāha pautraṃ dharmajño vasiṣṭho munibhir vṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Then righteous <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, surrounded by sages, said to his grandson:
'Enough of excessive anger, dear son; abandon this wrath.

children.text: rākṣasā nāparādhyanti pitus te vihitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The Rākṣasas do not offend; what befell your father was ordained in that way.

children.text: mūḍhānāmeva bhavati krodho buddhimatāṃ na hi ||
children.translated_text: Anger belongs only to the deluded, not to the wise.

children.text: hanyate tāta kaḥ kena yataḥ svakṛtabhukpumān
children.translated_text: Who is killed by whom, dear son, since a man experiences the fruit of his own deeds?
That which has been accumulated by men with very great hardship, dear child,
fame and austerity alike, is said to be destroyed by anger.

children.text: alaṃ hi rākṣasair dagdhair dīnair anaparādhibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Enough of these wretched, innocent Rākṣasas being burned.
Let this sacrificial session of yours cease, for the good have forgiveness as their essence.'
Thus, because of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>'s words, the son of <s>Śakti</s>, bull among sages,
immediately brought the sacrificial session to an end, out of respect for his words.
Then the blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of sages, was pleased.

children.text: samprāptaś ca tadā satraṃ pulastyo brahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time <s>Pulastya</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, arrived at the sacrificial session,
and, after receiving arghya from <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, took the seat offered to him.
The sage spoke these words to <s>Parāśara</s>, who stood bowing before him:

children.text: vaire mahati yadvākyād guror adyāśritā kṣamā ||
children.translated_text: 'Since today, in the midst of great enmity, forgiveness has been adopted by you at your guru's word,
therefore, sir, you shall know all the śāstras.

children.text: saṃtatermama na chedaḥ kruddhenāpi yataḥ kṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And since no severing of my lineage was done by you, even though you were angry,
therefore, very fortunate one, I grant you another great boon.
You, dear child, shall become the maker of a compendium of the Purāṇas.
You shall know properly the supreme truth concerning the deities.

children.text: pravṛttau vā nivṛttau vā karmaṇas te 'malā matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whether in activity or in withdrawal, your stainless understanding of action
will be free from doubt by my favor, dear child.'

children.text: tataś ca prāha bhagavānvasiṣṭho vadatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the blessed <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, best of speakers, said:
'Everything that was spoken to you by <s>Pulastya</s> will come to pass.'

children.text: atha tasya pulastyasya vasiṣṭhasya ca dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, of that <s>Pulastya</s> and of wise <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>...
By his favor <s>Parāśara</s> composed the Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa long ago,
in six divisions, accomplishing every aim, a treasury of knowledge.
The whole of it measured six thousand verses and was joined with the meaning of the Veda;
it is the fourth among the Purāṇas, splendid among the Saṃhitās.

children.text: eṣa vaḥ kathitaḥ sarvo vāsiṣṭhānāṃ samāsataḥ
children.translated_text: Thus the whole origin of the Vāsiṣṭhas has been told to you in brief,
and also the greatness of the son of <s>Śakti</s>, O foremost sages.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge vāsiṣṭhakathanaṃ nāma catuḥṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, ends the sixty-fourth chapter, named The Narration of the Vāsiṣṭhas.
The sages said:
O best of those who know lineages, you should tell us the lineage of <s>Āditya</s> and the lineage of <s>Soma</s>,
briefly, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Aditi</s> bore from <s>Kaśyapa</s> a son, <s>Āditya</s>, O twice-borns.
That <s>Āditya</s> had three wives, and then another set besides:

children.text: saṃjñā rājñī prabhā chāyā putrāṃstāsāṃ vadāmi vaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃjñā</s>, <s>Rājñī</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, and <s>Chāyā</s>. I shall tell you their sons.
<s>Saṃjñā</s>, daughter of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, bore from <s>Sūrya</s> the excellent <s>Manu</s>,

children.text: yamaṃ ca yamunāṃ caiva rājñī revatameva ca
children.translated_text: and also <s>Yama</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>; <s>Rājñī</s> bore <s>Revata</s>.
<s>Prabhā</s> bore <s>Prabhāta</s> from <s>Āditya</s>; <s>Saṃjñā</s> fashioned <s>Chāyā</s>.
And <s>Chāyā</s> bore from that radiant <s>Bhāskara</s> <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, O twice-borns,

children.text: tataḥ śaniṃ ca tapatīṃ viṣṭiṃ caiva yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: and then, in order, <s>Śani</s>, <s>Tapatī</s>, and <s>Viṣṭi</s>.

children.text: chāyā svaputrābhyadhikaṃ snehaṃ cakre manau tadā
children.translated_text: At that time <s>Chāyā</s> showed greater affection for her own sons than for <s>Manu</s>.
The former <s>Manu</s> did not notice it, but <s>Yama</s>, overcome by anger,
angrily struck her, raising his right foot.

children.text: yamena tāḍitā sā tu chāyā vai duḥkhitābhavat ||
children.translated_text: Struck by <s>Yama</s>, <s>Chāyā</s> became distressed.
Because of <s>Chāyā</s>'s curse, one excellent foot of <s>Yama</s>
became wet, filled with pus and blood, and covered with a mass of worms.
He too resorted to <s>Gokarṇa</s>, eating only air, with a wooden board,
and worshiped <s>Mahādeva</s> for ten thousand times ten thousand years.
By the grace of <s>Bhava</s> he attained the excellent status of world-protector,
lordship over the ancestors, and also release from the curse.
He obtained these by the power of the god of gods, the trident-bearing one.
Long ago the faultless daughter of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, unable to endure the sun's fiery form,

children.text: rūpaṃ tvāṣṭrī svadehāttu chāyākhyāṃ sā tvakalpayat
children.translated_text: fashioned from her own body a likeness called <s>Chāyā</s>.
Taking the form of a mare, that well-vowed lady performed austerity.
In time, by careful effort, the lord, the husband of <s>Chāyā</s>, learned of the shadow.
<s>Bhāskara</s>, in the form of a horse, went to <s>Saṃjñā</s> in mare-form.

children.text: vaḍavā ca tadā tvāṣṭrī saṃjñā tasmāddivākarāt
children.translated_text: Then <s>Saṃjñā</s>, daughter of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, as a mare, from that <s>Divākara</s>

children.text: suṣuve cāśvinau devau devānāṃ tu bhiṣagvarau ||
children.translated_text: bore the two gods <s>Aśvins</s>, the best physicians of the gods.
Afterwards <s>Bhāskara</s> was pared down by the high-souled father of <s>Saṃjñā</s>.
From the disk of <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> made
the terrible discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the divine chief weapon.
By the grace of <s>Rudra</s> it is remembered as the auspicious <s>Sudarśana</s>.
The blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> obtained the discus, resembling the fire at the end of time.
Of the first <s>Manu</s> there were nine sons, equal to him:

children.text: ikṣvākur nabhagaś caiva dhṛṣṇuḥ śaryātireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Nabhaga</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śaryāti</s>,

children.text: nariṣyantaś ca vai dhīmān nābhāgo'riṣṭa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: wise <s>Nariṣyanta</s>, <s>Nābhāga</s>, and <s>Ariṣṭa</s>,

children.text: karūṣaś ca pṛṣadhraś ca navaite mānavāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Karūṣa</s> and <s>Pṛṣadhra</s>; these nine are remembered as sons of <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: ilā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhā ca puṃstvaṃ prāpa ca yā purā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ilā</s>, eldest and best, formerly obtained maleness.

children.text: sudyumna iti vikhyātā puṃstvaṃ prāptā tvilā purā
children.translated_text: <s>Ilā</s>, after obtaining maleness long ago, became renowned as <s>Sudyumna</s>,
through the favor of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> here, O foremost sages.

children.text: punaḥ śaravaṇaṃ prāpya strītvaṃ prāpto bhavājñayā
children.translated_text: But after again reaching <s>Śaravaṇa</s>, by <s>Bhava</s>'s command he obtained womanhood.
The glorious human <s>Sudyumna</s> existed for the increase of the lunar lineage.
Through <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s horse sacrifice, <s>Ilā</s> became a <s>kiṃpuruṣa</s>.

children.text: ilā kiṃpuruṣatve ca sudyumna iti cocyate ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Ilā</s>'s state as a <s>kiṃpuruṣa</s>, he is also called <s>Sudyumna</s>.
The hero was a man for one month, and again was a woman for one month.
<s>Ilā</s> resorted to the house of <s>Budha</s>, the son of <s>Soma</s>.
<s>Budha</s>, approaching her in the intervening month, engaged with her for intercourse.
From <s>Budha</s>, son of <s>Soma</s>, was born <s>Purūravas</s>, descendant of <s>Ilā</s>.
He was the first of the lunar lineage, wise, devoted to <s>Bhava</s>, and powerful.
I shall later tell the expansion of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>'s lineage, O rich in austerity.
That <s>Sudyumna</s> had three sons, O best of twice-borns:
<s>Utkala</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, and <s>Vinatāśva</s>.
<s>Utkala</s>'s realm was <s>Utkala</s>; <s>Vinatāśva</s>'s was the western land.
The exceedingly beautiful city <s>Gayā</s> is declared to belong to <s>Gaya</s>.

children.text: surāṇāṃ saṃsthitiryasyāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca sadā sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: In it the gods are established, and the ancestors always dwell there.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s>, the eldest heir, obtained the middle country.
Because of his condition as a woman, <s>Sudyumna</s> did not obtain a share.
Yet by the word of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, that greatly radiant one dwelt at <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.
There was the establishment of the righteous king, the great-souled <s>Sudyumna</s>.
Having obtained kingship, the very famous one gave that kingdom to <s>Purūravas</s>.
The fortunate descendant of <s>Manu</s> possessed the marks of both woman and man.
From <s>Ikṣvāku</s> was born the hero <s>Vikukṣi</s>, best of knowers of <s>dharma</s>.
He was the eldest of one hundred and fifteen sons.
The eldest was <s>Kakutstha</s>, and from <s>Kakutstha</s> came <s>Suyodhana</s>.
Then came <s>Pṛthu</s>, O best sages, and the king <s>Viśvaka</s>.
The wise <s>Ārdraka</s> was <s>Viśvaka</s>'s son, and <s>Yuvanāśva</s> was his son.
Then came the greatly radiant <s>Śābasti</s>, and after him <s>Vaṃśaka</s>.
By him <s>Śābastī</s> was founded in the <s>Gauḍa</s> country, O best of twice-borns.
From the lineage arose <s>Bṛhadaśva</s>; <s>Kuvalāśva</s> was his son.
Having killed the mighty <s>Dhundhu</s>, he obtained the status of <s>Dhundhumāra</s>.
The sons of <s>Dhundhumāra</s> were three, renowned in the three worlds:

children.text: dṛḍhāśvaścaiva caṇḍāśvaḥ kapilāśvaś ca te smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are remembered as <s>Dṛḍhāśva</s>, <s>Caṇḍāśva</s>, and <s>Kapilāśva</s>.
From <s>Dṛḍhāśva</s> came <s>Pramoda</s>, and his son was <s>Haryaśva</s>.
From <s>Haryaśva</s> came <s>Nikumbha</s>, and <s>Saṃhatāśva</s> was his son.
<s>Kṛśāśva</s> and <s>Raṇāśva</s> were both sons of <s>Saṃhatāśva</s>.

children.text: yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya māndhātā tasya vai sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yuvanāśva</s> was the son of <s>Raṇāśva</s>, and <s>Māndhātā</s> was his son.
From <s>Māndhātā</s> came <s>Purukutsa</s> and the heroic <s>Ambarīṣa</s>,
and <s>Mucukunda</s>, a holy soul; the three were renowned in the three worlds.
The heir of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> is remembered as another <s>Yuvanāśva</s>.
From <s>Yuvanāśva</s> came <s>Harita</s>, from whom the <s>Haritas</s> are remembered.
These twice-born men, on the side of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, were endowed with royal power.
The heir of <s>Purukutsa</s> was the very famous <s>Trasaddasyu</s>.
He was born from <s>Narmadā</s>, and <s>Sambhūti</s> was his son.
<s>Viṣṇuvṛddha</s> was his son, from whom the <s>Viṣṇuvṛddhas</s> are remembered.
These, on the side of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, took refuge as men endowed with royal power.
<s>Sambhūti</s> begot another son, <s>Anaraṇya</s>.
He, O brahmins, was slain by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> during his conquest of the three worlds.
<s>Bṛhadaśva</s> was the son of <s>Anaraṇya</s>, and <s>Haryaśva</s> was his son.
From <s>Haryaśva</s>, in <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>, King <s>Vasumanas</s> was born.
His son was King <s>Tridhanvan</s>, devoted to <s>Bhava</s>.
Through the favor of <s>Taṇḍin</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, he obtained discipleship,
and by his command he obtained the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.
Powerful and devoted to <s>Bhava</s>, he attained lordship among the <s>gaṇas</s>.
He reflected, "How indeed am I to perform a horse sacrifice?"

children.text: dhanahīnaś ca dharmātmā dṛṣṭavān brahmaṇaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Though righteous, he lacked wealth, and he saw the son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
From him, O best of brahmins, he obtained the brahmin named <s>Taṇḍi</s>.

children.text: nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ rudrasya brahmaṇā kathitaṃ purā
children.translated_text: The thousand names of <s>Rudra</s> had formerly been spoken by <s>Brahmā</s>.
With that thousand names <s>Taṇḍin</s> praised <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The best of brahmins, born from <s>Brahmā</s>, thereby gained <s>gāṇapatya</s> (lordship among the gaṇas).
Then the king received from him the thousand names formerly spoken by <s>Taṇḍin</s>.
Having recited the thousand names, he attained <s>gāṇapatya</s>.
The sages said:
The thousand names of <s>Rudra</s>, spoken by <s>Taṇḍin</s>, born from <s>Brahmā</s>,
are a gathering of the meanings of all the Vedas, O well-vowed <s>Sūta</s>.

children.text: nāmnāṃ sahasraṃ viprāṇāṃ vaktum arhasi śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: You ought to speak that auspicious thousand names for the brahmins.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Listen to the thousand and eight names of <s>Hara</s>, of immeasurable splendor,
who has become the self of all beings, O well-vowed ones.
By reciting it, O best sages, he attained <s>gāṇapatya</s>.

children.text: oṃ sthiraḥ sthāṇuḥ prabhurbhānuḥ pravaro varado varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Om: Steady, Firm, Lord, Radiant, Foremost, Boon-giver, Excellent;
Self of all, famed by all, All, maker of all, <s>Bhava</s>;

children.text: jaṭī daṇḍī śikhaṇḍī ca sarvagaḥ sarvabhāvanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: matted-haired, staff-bearing, crested, all-pervading, creator of all;

children.text: hariś ca hariṇākṣaś ca sarvabhūtaharaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, deer-eyed, remembered as the destroyer of all beings;

children.text: pravṛttiś ca nivṛttiś ca śāntātmā śāśvato dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: activity and withdrawal, peaceful-souled, eternal, fixed;
dweller in the cremation ground, blessed lord, sky-roaming, earth-roaming, crusher;
worthy of salutation, of great deeds, ascetic, supporter of beings;
wearing the guise of a madman, hidden, comprising all worlds, <s>Prajāpati</s>;
great in form, great-bodied, of every form, of great fame;

children.text: mahātmā sarvabhūtaś ca virūpo vāmano naraḥ
children.translated_text: great-souled, consisting of all beings, misshapen, dwarf, man;
protector of the worlds, whose self is hidden, gracious favor, giver of fearlessness, all-pervading;
pure and great, restrained, whose refuge is restraint;
self-born, performer of all acts, beginning, maker of the beginning, treasure;
thousand-eyed, wide-eyed, <s>Soma</s>, accomplisher of the constellations;
<s>Candra</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Śani</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, planet, regarded as lord of planets;
king, cause of the rise of kingdoms, maker, aimer of the deer-arrow, dense and mighty;
great in austerity, long in austerity, invisible, accomplisher of wealth;
the year, skillful, mantra, breath-control, scorcher of foes;
yogin, yoga, great seed, greatly delighted, of great strength;
golden-semened, all-knowing, good seed, bull-mounted;
ten-armed, unblinking, blue-throated, <s>Umāpati</s>;
universal-formed, self-excellent, strong hero, foremost in strength;
maker of the <s>gaṇas</s>, lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>, sky-clad, and truly desirable;
knower of mantras, supreme mantra, maker of all states, <s>Hara</s>;
holder of a water-pot, archer, arrow-handed, skull-bearing;

children.text: śarī śataghnī khaḍgī ca paṭṭiśī cāyudhī mahān
children.translated_text: arrow-bearing, armed with a hundred-slayer, sword-bearing, spear-bearing, great wielder of weapons;

children.text: ajaś ca mṛgarūpaś ca tejastejaskaro vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: unborn, deer-formed, splendor, maker of splendor, ordainer;

children.text: uṣṇīṣī ca suvaktraś ca udagro vinatas tathā
children.translated_text: turbaned, fair-faced, lofty, and humble;

children.text: dīrghaś ca harikeśaś ca sutīrthaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: long, tawny-haired, a good ford, and dark-colored;
jackal-formed, all-purpose, shaven-headed, maker of all auspiciousness;
lion-formed and tiger-formed, maker of fragrance, and matted-haired;
whose seed is raised upward, whose <s>liṅga</s> is raised upward, who lies upward, the expanse of the sky;

children.text: trijaṭī cīravāsāś ca rudraḥ senāpatir vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: three-matted-haired, wearing bark garments, <s>Rudra</s>, commander of the army, all-pervading;

children.text: ahorātraṃ ca naktaṃ ca tigmamanyuḥ suvarcasaḥ
children.translated_text: day-and-night, night, fierce in wrath, splendid;
elephant-slayer, demon-slayer, Time, establisher of worlds, source of qualities;
among those with forms of lion and tiger, wearer of a wet hide garment;
yogin of Time, great-sounding, dwelling in all, the crossroads.
He is the night-roaming one, the wanderer among ghosts, the all-seeing <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He has many forms of being, much wealth, the essence of all, the lord of immortality.
He delights in dance, dances eternally, is the dancer, and accomplishes all things.
He is armed with a bow, mighty-armed, very terrible, and great in austerity.
He has the great arrow and the great noose; he is eternal and is regarded as roaming on the mountain.
He is thousand-handed, victorious, resolute, and indeed blameless.
He is unforbearing, yet whose nature is forbearance; he destroys sacrifice and destroys desire.

children.text: dakṣahā paricārī ca prahaso madhyamas tathā ||
children.translated_text: He destroyed <s>Dakṣa</s>; he is the attendant, laughter, and also the middle one.
He takes away splendor; he is powerful, renowned, risen up, and manifold.
