He has a deep roar, is whose self is yoga; he destroys sacrifice and destroys desire.
He has deep wrath; he is deep, and he has deep strength as his vehicle.
He has the form of the banyan, is the banyan, is the maker of all, and the enjoyer of all.
He has sharp means; he has bay horses, is a helper, and knows the time for action.
He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, propitiated, sacrifice itself, the ocean, and the submarine fire.
He is aided by the sacrificial fire, tranquil in self, and the sacrificial fire itself.
He is fierce in radiance, great in radiance, victory, and the knower of the time of victory.
He is the course of the lights, success, alliance, and also conflict.

children.text: khaḍgī śaṅkhī jaṭī jvālī khacaro dyucaro balī ||
children.translated_text: He bears a sword, bears a conch, is matted-haired, flaming, sky-roaming, heaven-roaming, and strong.
He has the lute, has the drum; he is time, dark-throated, and harshly clattering.
He has the constellations as his body; he is being, non-being, and faces everywhere.
He is release, refuge, and born with a golden cuirass.
He has the form of a girdle, moves in the waters, and is praised.

children.text: vīṇī ca paṇavī tālī nālī kalikaṭus tathā
children.translated_text: He has the vīṇā, the drum, the cymbal, and the pipe; he is also sharp as a bitter bud.
He resounds with every musical instrument and embraces all-pervasion.
He has the form of a serpent, dwells in a hole, dwells in a cave, and knows the waves.
He is the tree, auspicious, of garlanded action, and the liberator from every bond.
He is the binder of the lords of the gods and, in battle, the destroyer of enemies.
He is friend, sojourner, hard to obtain, and attended by all the good.
He is rushing forth, also unmanifest, equal, and the knower of the shares of sacrifice.
He dwells everywhere, moves everywhere, is <s>Durvāsas</s>, and is regarded as <s>Vāsava</s>.
He is golden, maker of gold, sacrifice, bearer of all, and the best upholder.

children.text: ākāśo nirvirūpaś ca vivāsā uragaḥ khagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is space, without distorted form, naked, a serpent, and a bird.

children.text: bhikṣuś ca bhikṣurūpī ca raudrarūpaḥ surūpavān
children.translated_text: He is a mendicant and of mendicant form; he has a fierce form and also a beautiful form.
He has wealth as seed, speaks well, moves with the speed of wealth, and is very strong.
He moves with the speed of mind, roams by night, and bestows good on all worlds.
He dwells in all, dwells in the three Vedas, gives instruction, and is the supporter.

children.text: munirātmā munir lokaḥ sabhāgyaś ca sahasrabhuk
children.translated_text: He is the sage, the self, the sage as the world, fortunate, and the thousandfold enjoyer.

children.text: pakṣī ca pakṣarūpaś ca atidīpto niśākaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is a bird and bird-formed, exceedingly blazing, and the maker of night, the moon.
He is wind, has the form of restraint, is purpose, the maker of purpose, and control.

children.text: vāsudevaś ca devaś ca vāmadevaś ca vāmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the god, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, and <s>Vāmana</s>.
He removes perfected yoga; he is perfected and accomplishes every aim.

children.text: akṣuṇṇaḥ kṣuṇṇarūpaś ca vṛṣaṇo mṛdur avyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is unbroken and of broken form; he is virile, gentle, and imperishable.

children.text: mahāseno viśākhaś ca ṣaṣṭibhāgo gavāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: He is <s>Mahāsena</s> and <s>Viśākha</s>, the sixtieth share, and lord of cows.
He has the discus in hand, is the supporter, and the very fixing of the root.
He is the season and maker of seasons, the palm tree, sweet, honey-making, and excellent.
He belongs to the forest trees, is rich in food, and is always worshiped in hermitages.
He is the celibate student, the mover through the world, the mover everywhere, and knower of good conduct.
He is <s>Īśāna</s>, lord, time, night-roaming, and indeed many-eyed.

children.text: nimittastho nimittaṃ ca nandir nandikaro haraḥ
children.translated_text: He abides in omens, is the omen, is <s>Nandi</s>, maker of joy, and <s>Hara</s>.
He is <s>Nandīśvara</s>, very joyful, delighting, and crusher of poison.
He takes away fortune, is controller, time, and the grandsire of the world.
He is four-faced, the great <s>liṅga</s>, and likewise the beautiful <s>liṅga</s>.
He is superintendent of the <s>liṅga</s>, superintendent of the gods, superintendent of time, and bearer of the ages.
He is superintendent of seed, maker of seed, strength that has entered the inner self.

children.text: itihāsaś ca kalpaś ca damano jagadīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: He is history, the ritual cycle, the subduer, and the lord of the world.

children.text: dambho dambhakaro dātā vaṃśo vaṃśakaraḥ kaliḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is deceit, maker of deceit, giver, lineage, maker of lineage, and the Kali age.
He is maker of the world, <s>Paśupati</s>, the great maker, and indeed <s>Adhokṣaja</s>.

children.text: akṣaraṃ paramaṃ brahma balavāñchukta eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is the imperishable, the supreme <s>brahman</s>, powerful, and pure.

children.text: nityo hyanīśaḥ śuddhātmā śuddho māno gatirhaviḥ
children.translated_text: He is eternal, indeed without a superior lord, pure in self, pure, measure, course, and oblation.

children.text: prāsādastu balo darpo darpaṇo havya indrajit ||
children.translated_text: He is the palace, strength, pride, mirror, oblation, and conqueror of <s>Indra</s>.
He is maker of the Veda, maker of the sūtra, learned, and crusher of enemies.
He dwells in the great cloud, is very terrible, and brings under control.
He is the flame of fire, the great flame, surrounded by thick smoke, and the sun.
He is wisdom, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, eternal, lustrous, and smoke-eyed.
He is blue, with limbs smeared over, beautiful, and in human form.

children.text: svasti svastisvabhāvaś ca bhogī bhogakaro laghuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is welfare, whose nature is welfare, the enjoyer, maker of enjoyment, and swift.

children.text: utsaṅgaś ca mahāṅgaś ca mahāgarbhaḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: He is the lap, great-limbed, great-wombed, and mighty in splendor.
He is dark-colored, golden, the sense faculty, and having every color.
He has great feet, great hands, a great body, and great fame.
He has a great head, great measure, is a great friend, and dwells on mountains.
He has great shoulders, great ears, great lips, and a great jaw.
He has a great nose, great throat, great neck, and possesses the cremation ground.
He has great strength and great radiance; he is the inner self and has the deer as his abode.

children.text: lambitoṣṭhaś ca niṣṭhaś ca mahāmāyaḥ payonidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He has hanging lips, is steadfast, possesses great māyā, and is the ocean.
He has great teeth, great fangs, a great tongue, and a great mouth.
He has great nails, great hair on the body, great hair, and great matted locks.
He is without rival, graciousness, certainty, and the accomplisher of song.
He causes sweating and does not sweat; he is primordial and the great sage.
He is bull-like, bull-bannered, fire, and wind-borne.

children.text: maṇḍalī meruvāsaś ca devavāhana eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is coiled, dwelling on <s>Meru</s>, and indeed the vehicle of the gods.
He is the <s>Atharvaśīrṣa</s>, having the <s>Sāman</s> as his mouth, with a thousand <s>Ṛc</s>-verses and powerful sight;
with the <s>Yajus</s> as his feet and arms, secret, and likewise radiant with manifest vigor.
He is unfailing in purpose and grace, inwardly present, and of beautiful vision;
he is the offering, dear, all, golden, and established in gold.

children.text: nābhir nandikaro harmyaḥ puṣkaraḥ sthapatiḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the navel, maker of joy, a mansion, a lotus, the architect, and the established one;
he is all scripture, wealth, the first one, sacrifice, the sacrificer, and composed in concentration.

children.text: nago nīlaḥ kaviḥ kālo makaraḥ kālapūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: He is mountain-like, dark-blue, a poet, time, a makara, and worshiped by time;
with his hosts, maker of hosts, and charioteer who brings beings into existence.
He lies in ashes, protects ashes, has a body become ashes, and is a host;

children.text: āgamaś ca vilopaś ca mahātmā sarvapūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is tradition, dissolution, a great-souled one, and worshiped by all.
He is white, endowed with a female form, pure, and served by beings;
dwelling in the hermitage, dwelling among pigeons, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, lord, and sovereign.
He has broad branches and coppery lips; he is a net of lotuses and firmly ascertained;
tawny, a jar, massive, armed, and hairy.
He is a <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, unknowable, and very learned;
the god whose weapon is an axe, accomplisher of aims, and a good kinsman.
He has a gourd-vīṇā, is greatly wrathful, with seed drawn upward, and dwelling in water;
fierce, maker of lineage, lineage itself, speaker of lineage, and blameless.
He has the form of all limbs, is a magician, a friend, wind, and strength;
bondage, maker of bondage, and excellent liberator from bondage.
He is destroyer of rākṣasas, enemy of desire, great-fanged, and greatly armed;
hanging down, with hanging lips, long-armed, and giver of boons.
He is the arm, blameless, all, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and also free from anger;
lord of immortals, exceedingly terrible, the universal god, and destroyer of the enemies of the gods.

children.text: ahirbudhnyo nirṛtiś ca cekitāno halī tathā
children.translated_text: He is <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Cekitāna</s>, and likewise the plough-bearing one;
also <s>Ajaikapād</s>, the skull-bearing one, peace, <s>Kumāra</s>, and the great mountain.
He is <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Dhūmaketu</s>, the Sun, and likewise <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>;

children.text: dhātā viṣṇuś ca śakraś ca mitrastvaṣṭā dharo dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, the supporter, and <s>Dhruva</s>.
He is <s>Prabhāsa</s>, mountain, wind, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, and the sun;
also firmness, ordainer, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, and creator of beings.

children.text: nīrastīrthaś ca bhīmaś ca sarvakarmā guṇodvahaḥ
children.translated_text: He is waterless, a tīrtha, formidable, doer of all actions, and bearer of qualities;
lotus-wombed, great-wombed, moon-faced, sky, and sinless.
Strong, tranquil, ancient, and best among makers of merit;
doer of cruel acts, dwelling in harshness, the body, the self, and the great medicine.
He is the abode of all, moving everywhere, lord of breath, and lord of living beings;
god of gods, overflowing with happiness, and knower of all jewels, existent and nonexistent.
He dwells on <s>Kailāsa</s>, lives in caves, and has taken refuge in the <s>Himavat</s> mountain;
destroyer of families, creator of families, rich in many possessions and many offspring.

children.text: prāṇeśo bandhakī vṛkṣo nakulaś cādrikas tathā
children.translated_text: He is lord of breath, a bondwoman, a tree, a mongoose, and likewise mountain-born;
short-necked, great-kneed, unagitated, and a great herb.
Maker of doctrine, one whose aim is accomplished, meter, and born from grammar;
lion-roaring, lion-fanged, lion-faced, and lion-mounted.
He whose self is majesty, the time of the world, time itself, trembling, a tree, and the body;
a deer, marked with the circle of beings, banner-garlanded, and well-piercing.
Abode of beings, lord of beings, day and night, impurity and purity;
bearer of the Vasus, self of all beings, unmoving, very wise, and awakened.
Unfriendly to all beings, unmoving, and wise in what moves;
unfailing, restraint, delighted, food, and support of breath.
Possessed of firmness, possessed of intelligence, three-eyed, meritorious, and lord of battles;
cowherd, lord of cattle, village, wearing a cowhide, and <s>Hara</s>.
Golden-armed, and likewise dwelling in the cave and entering within;
great-minded, greatly desirous, desirous in mind, and conqueror of the senses.

children.text: gāndhāraś ca surāpaś ca tāpakarmarato hitaḥ
children.translated_text: He is <s>Gāndhāra</s>, drinker of liquor, devoted to austerity-rites, and beneficent;
a great being, surrounded by beings, and served by hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>.
Great-bannered, supporter of the earth, delighting in manifold continuity, and sound;
not to be known, to be made known, all-pervading, and bringer of happiness.
The deliverer, the refuge, the establisher, the enclosure, and the fully worshiped one;
joined in union, increaser, aged, the reckoner, and lord of hosts.

children.text: nityo dhātā sahāyaś ca devāsurapatiḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: Eternal, establisher, helper, lord of gods and asuras, and lord;

children.text: yuktaś ca yuktabāhuś ca sudevo'pi suparvaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: joined, with joined arms, a good god, and also one of auspicious joints.

children.text: āṣāḍhaś ca suṣāḍhaś ca skandhado harito haraḥ
children.translated_text: He is <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, well-strong, giver of <s>Skanda</s>, tawny, and <s>Hara</s>;
turning in form, another, best in form, and great-bodied.
Touching the head, adorned with all marks and characteristics;
imperishable, sung on the chariot, enjoyer of all, and very strong.
He is the sacred tradition of the <s>Sāman</s>, the great tradition, the deity of sacred fords, and greatly renowned;
lifeless, life-giving, mantra, fortunate, and very harsh.
Jewel-like, jewel-limbed, knower of descent into the great ocean;
root, vast, immortal, manifest and unmanifest, and treasure of austerity.
Ascent and climbing upward, bearer of good conduct, and greatly austere;
great-necked, great yogin, the age, maker of the age, and <s>Hari</s>.
Form of the age, great in form, bearer, deep, and mountain-like;
justice, extinguisher, footless, learned, and like an immovable mountain.
With many garlands, with a great garland, <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, and fair-eyed;
expansion, salt, a well, flower-bodied, and source of fruit.
Bull, chief bull, breaker, wearing matted hair with jewel-like disks;
the moon, emission, fair-faced, heroic, armed with every weapon, and enduring.
Presentation, born of nectar, gate of heaven, and bearer of a great bow;
dwelling on the mountain, emission, and knower of the marks of all characteristics.
He is fragrant-garlanded, blessed, endless, and marked by every auspicious sign.
He is continuity, abundance, the arm, the whole, and the purifier of all.
He is the hand-vessel, the skull-bearing one, high-compacted, and youthful.
He is famed in yantras and tantras, the world, the refuge of all, and gentle.

children.text: muṇḍo virūpo vikṛto daṇḍī kuṇḍī vikurvaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He is shaven-headed, misshapen, transformed, staff-bearing, pot-bearing, and assuming varied forms.
He is water-eyed, the quarter, the wielder of the thunderbolt, blazing in splendor, and thousand-footed.
He is thousand-headed, lord of the gods, made of all the gods, and the teacher.
He is thousand-armed, all-limbed, a refuge, and the maker of all worlds.
He is purity, the mantra of threefold sweetness, the youngest, and dark tawny.
He is the maker of <s>Brahmā</s>'s staff, the destroyer of hundreds, and holder of a hundred nooses.

children.text: kalā kāṣṭhā lavo mātrā muhūrto 'haḥ kṣapā kṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the unit <s>kalā</s>, <s>kāṣṭhā</s>, <s>lava</s>, <s>mātrā</s>, the muhūrta, day, night, and moment.
He is the giver of the universal field, the seed, the primordial <s>liṅga</s>, and the faceless one.
He is existent and nonexistent, manifest and unmanifest, father, mother, and grandfather.
He is the gate to heaven, the gate to liberation, the gate of creatures, and the highest heaven.
He is nirvāṇa, the heart itself, the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, and the supreme goal.
He is the creator of gods and Asuras, and the final refuge of gods and Asuras.
He is the god who is teacher of gods and Asuras, and is honored by gods and Asuras.
He is the great measure of gods and Asuras, and the support of the hosts of gods and Asuras.
He is the overseer of the hosts of gods and Asuras, and the foremost leader of the hosts of gods and Asuras.
He is the god above the gods, the seer among gods, and the giver of boons to gods and Asuras.
He is lord of gods and Asuras, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the great lord of gods and Asuras.
He is made of all the gods, inconceivable, the self of the deities, and self-born.
He is risen up, the three-striding one, the healer, the boon-giver, the younger-born, and the garment.

children.text: ijyo hastī tathā vyāghro devasiṃho maharṣabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is worthy of sacrifice, the elephant, likewise the tiger, the lion among gods, and the great bull.
He is foremost among the wise gods, divine, the best, the god of heaven, and likewise supreme.
He is joined together, beautiful, an eloquent speaker, the source of the quarters, and undecaying.

children.text: guruḥ kānto nijaḥ sargaḥ pavitraḥ sarvavāhanaḥ
children.translated_text: He is the teacher, beloved, innate, creation, pure, and mounted on every vehicle.
He is horned, fond of the horn, tawny, king of kings, and free from disease.
He is delightful, an excellent refuge, free from affliction, and the means of accomplishing everything.
He is the one with an eye in his forehead, whose body is the universe, the tawny one, and endowed with brahmanic splendor.
He is lord of immovable beings, and his conduct is restrained through controlled senses.
He is one whose purpose is accomplished, whose purpose is all beings, inconceivable, true, and pure in vow.

children.text: vratādhipaḥ paraṃ brahma muktānāṃ paramā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: He is lord of vows, the supreme <s>brahman</s>, and the highest goal of the liberated.
He is released, loose-haired, glorious, increaser of glory, and the world.

children.text: yathāpradhānaṃ bhagavān iti bhaktyā stuto mayā
children.translated_text: Thus the blessed one has been praised by me with devotion, according to what is chief.
Placing such devotion foremost, I have praised the mighty lord of sacrifice.

children.text: tato hyanujñāṃ prāpyaivaṃ stuto bhaktimatāṃ gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after permission had been obtained, the refuge of the devoted was thus praised.
Therefore, O king, having received the hymn of <s>Śambhu</s>, renowned in the three worlds,
the greatly famous one obtained the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices.
<s>Taṇḍin</s> attained lordship over the gaṇas through the splendor of the Lord.
Whoever recites it, hears it, or has it recited even to Brahmins,
obtains the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices, O twice-born ones.

children.text: brahmaghnaś ca surāpaś ca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ
children.translated_text: A killer of a Brahmin, a drinker of liquor, a thief, one who violates the teacher's bed,
one who kills a person who has sought refuge, and one who betrays a friend's trust,

children.text: mātṛhā pitṛhā caiva vīrahā bhrūṇahā tathā
children.translated_text: a killer of mother or father, a killer of a hero, and likewise a killer of an embryo,
if he recites it regularly for a year, at the three junctures of the day, in <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s hermitage,

children.text: devam iṣṭvā trisaṃdhyaṃ ca sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: and worships the god at the three junctures, is released from all sins.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge rudrasahasranāmakathanaṃ nāma pañcaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, ends the sixty-fifth chapter, named the Account of the Thousand Names of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
By the grace of the god of gods, <s>Taṇḍin</s> likewise, O <s>Tridhanvan</s>,
having carefully obtained the fruit of a thousand horse sacrifices,
firmly attained the state of a lord of gaṇas, honored by all the gods.
There was also a learned king descended from <s>Tridhanvan</s>, named <s>Trayyāruṇa</s>.
He had a very mighty prince named <s>Satyavrata</s>.
He carried off the wife of the king of <s>Vidarbha</s>, after killing <s>Amitaujas</s>.
Here, while the marriage mantras had not yet reached completion,
because of that unrighteous act King <s>Trayyāruṇa</s> abandoned him.

children.text: pitaraṃ so'bravīt tyaktaḥ kva gacchāmīti vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Abandoned, he said to his father, 'Where shall I go, O twice-born ones?'
Then his father said to him, 'Live together with the dog-cookers.'
So addressed, he went out from the city at his father's command.
That wise hero <s>Satyavrata</s> stayed near a dwelling of dog-cookers.

children.text: pitrā tyakto 'vasadvīraḥ pitā cāsya vanaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: Abandoned by his father, the hero dwelt there, and his father went to the forest.
The powerful one, famous in all the worlds, is known as <s>Triśaṅku</s>.
Long ago, through the anger of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the meritorious King <s>Satyavrata</s>
received a boon from the greatly radiant <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, who gave it to <s>Triśaṅku</s>.

children.text: rājye 'bhiṣicya taṃ pitrye yājayāmāsa taṃ muniḥ
children.translated_text: Consecrating him in his paternal kingdom, that sage performed sacrifice for him.

children.text: miṣatāṃ devatānāṃ ca vasiṣṭhasya ca kauśikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśika</s> did so while the gods and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> looked on.
Then the mighty one raised him bodily up to heaven.
His wife, named <s>Satyavatā</s>, was born in the <s>Kaikeya</s> lineage.
She gave birth to the faultless prince <s>Hariścandra</s>.

children.text: hariścandrasya ca suto rohito nāma vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Hariścandra</s> was named <s>Rohita</s>, a powerful man.
Then came <s>Harita</s>, son of <s>Rohita</s>; <s>Dhundhu</s> is called <s>Hārita</s>.

children.text: vijayaś ca sutejāś ca dhundhuputrau babhūvatuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vijaya</s> and <s>Sutejas</s> were the two sons of <s>Dhundhu</s>.

children.text: jetā kṣatrasya sarvatra vijayastena sa smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because <s>Vijaya</s> conquered the kṣatra everywhere, he is remembered by that name.
His son was <s>Rucaka</s>, a supremely righteous king.
<s>Rucaka</s>'s son was <s>Vṛka</s>; from him <s>Bāhu</s> was born.
<s>Sagara</s> became his son, a king of supreme righteousness.

children.text: dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Sagara</s> too had two wives, <s>Prabhā</s> and also <s>Bhānumatī</s>.
Long before, <s>Aurva</s>, the fire, had been worshiped by those two out of desire for sons.
And <s>Aurva</s>, being pleased with them, granted an excellent boon according to their wish.
One chose sixty thousand sons, while the other chose a single son.
<s>Prabhā</s> accepted many sons as continuers of the lineage,
while <s>Bhānumatī</s> accepted one son, <s>Asamañjasa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi suṣuve sā tu vai prabhā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prabhā</s> indeed gave birth to the sixty thousand sons.
While they were digging up the earth, they were burned by the arrows of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s hūṃkāra.
The son of <s>Asamañjasa</s> was the famous <s>Aṃśumān</s>.
His son was <s>Dilīpa</s>, and from <s>Dilīpa</s> came <s>Bhagīratha</s>.
By him, after he had performed austerity, the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, called <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, was brought down.
And <s>Bhagīratha</s>'s son became one named <s>Śruta</s>.
His heir was <s>Nābhāga</s>, devoted to <s>Bhava</s> and mighty in splendor.
His son was <s>Aṃbarīṣa</s>; after him came <s>Sindhudvīpa</s>.
Protected by the arms of <s>Nābhāga</s> and <s>Aṃbarīṣa</s>,
the earth became exceedingly free from the threefold affliction.
The heroic <s>Ayutāyus</s> was the son of that <s>Sindhudvīpa</s>.
The son of <s>Ayutāyus</s> was the wise and greatly renowned <s>Ṛtuparṇa</s>.
He was a king, powerful, a friend of <s>Nala</s>, and a knower of the divine secret of dice.
Two <s>Nalas</s>, both firm in vows, are famous in the Purāṇas:
one was the son of <s>Vīrasena</s>, and the other was born in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage.
The son of <s>Ṛtuparṇa</s> was <s>Sārvabhauma</s>, lord of subjects.
His son was <s>Sudāsa</s>, a king who was equal to <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: sudāsasya sutaḥ proktaḥ saudāso nāma pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Sudāsa</s> is said to have been the king named <s>Saudāsa</s>.

children.text: khyātaḥ kalmāṣapādo vai nāmnā mitrasahaś ca saḥ
children.translated_text: He was famed as <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>, and by name also as <s>Mitrasaha</s>.
But the greatly radiant <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, in the field of <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>,
begot <s>Aśmaka</s>, who increased the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage.
From <s>Aśmaka</s>, through <s>Uttarā</s>, was born the son <s>Mūlaka</s>.

children.text: sa hi rāmabhayādrājā strībhiḥ parivṛto vane
children.translated_text: For fear of <s>Rāma</s>, that king, surrounded by women in the forest,
seeking protection, wore the excellent armor of women.
The righteous king <s>Śataratha</s> was also the son of <s>Mūlaka</s>.
From that <s>Śataratha</s> was born the powerful king <s>Ilavila</s>.
There was the glorious <s>Ailavili</s>, the mighty <s>Vṛddhaśarman</s>.
His father's daughter bore a son for <s>Viśvasaha</s>.
His son was <s>Dilīpa</s>, famed as <s>Khaṭvāṅga</s>.

children.text: yena svargād ihāgatya muhūrtaṃ prāpya jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: Having come here from heaven and obtained life for only a moment,

children.text: trayo 'gnayastrayo lokā buddhyā satyena vai jitāḥ
children.translated_text: he conquered the three fires and the three worlds by intelligence and truth.
His son was <s>Dīrghabāhu</s>; from him was born <s>Raghu</s>.

children.text: ajaḥ putro raghoścāpi tasmājjajñe ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: <s>Aja</s> was the son of <s>Raghu</s>, and from him was born the heroic
king <s>Daśaratha</s>, the glorious maintainer of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage.
From <s>Daśaratha</s> came the heroic <s>Rāma</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> and renowned in the world,
and <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and mighty <s>Śatrughna</s>.
The best of them was <s>Rāma</s>, greatly radiant and supremely heroic.

children.text: rāvaṇaṃ samare hatvā yajñairiṣṭvā ca dharmavit ||
children.translated_text: After slaying <s>Rāvaṇa</s> in battle and performing sacrifices, that knower of <s>dharma</s>
<s>Rāma</s> ruled the kingdom for ten thousand years.
A son of <s>Rāma</s> was born, widely known as <s>Kuśa</s>.

children.text: lavaś ca sumahābhāgaḥ satyavān abhavat sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Lava</s>, very fortunate, truthful, and wise, also existed.
From <s>Kuśa</s> was born <s>Atithi</s>, and his son was <s>Niṣadha</s>.
From <s>Niṣadha</s> was born <s>Nala</s>, and from him came <s>Nabhas</s>.
From <s>Nabhas</s> came one called <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>; after him <s>Kṣemadhanvan</s> is remembered.
His son was the heroic and mighty <s>Devānīka</s>.
His son was <s>Ahīnara</s>; after him came <s>Sahasrāśva</s>.
Then came <s>Śubha</s>, <s>Candrāvaloka</s>, and <s>Tārāpīḍa</s>.
His son was <s>Candragiri</s>; after him came <s>Bhānucandra</s>.
From him was born <s>Śrutāyus</s>, remembered as <s>Bṛhadbala</s>,
the greatly radiant one who, in the <s>Bhārata</s>, was slain by the son of <s>Subhadrā</s>.
These are remembered, for the most part, as the kings who were heirs of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.
The principal ones in this lineage have been proclaimed according to their importance.
All of them studied the <s>Pāśupata</s> knowledge and worshiped <s>Parameśvara</s>,
according to their knowledge, and performed sacrifices according to rule.
Those great-souled ones went to heaven; some were liberated yogins whose selves were freed.
<s>Nṛga</s>, through the curse of a Brahmin, became a chameleon.

children.text: dhṛṣṭaś ca dhṛṣṭaketuś ca yamabālaś ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, and the powerful <s>Yamabāla</s>,
and <s>Raṇadhṛṣṭa</s> were his sons, three of them supremely righteous.

children.text: ānarto nāma śaryāteḥ sukanyā nāma dārikā
children.translated_text: <s>Śaryāti</s> had a son named <s>Ānarta</s> and a daughter named <s>Sukanyā</s>.
<s>Ānarta</s> had a mighty son, <s>Rocamāna</s>.

children.text: rocamānasya revo'bhūd revād raivata eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rocamāna</s>'s son was <s>Reva</s>, and from <s>Reva</s> came <s>Raivata</s>.
And <s>Kakudmī</s> was another, the eldest son among a hundred sons.

children.text: revatī yasya sā kanyā patnī rāmasya viśrutā
children.translated_text: His daughter was the famous <s>Revatī</s>, wife of <s>Rāma</s>.
The son of <s>Nariṣyanta</s> was self-controlled and very powerful.
From <s>Nābhāga</s> came <s>Aṃbarīṣa</s>, a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and mighty in splendor.
His son was the glorious <s>Ṛta</s>, best among all knowers of <s>dharma</s>.
His son <s>Kṛta</s> had a son named <s>Sudharmā</s>, famous as <s>Pṛṣita</s>.
And from <s>Karūṣa</s> came the <s>Kārūṣas</s>, all renowned for their fame.

children.text: pṛṣito hiṃsayitvā gāṃ guroḥ prāpa sukalmaṣam
children.translated_text: For injuring his teacher's cow, <s>Pṛṣita</s> incurred a grave sin.
Because of <s>Cyavana</s>'s curse, he attained the state of a <s>śūdra</s>; so it is known.
The son of <s>Diṣṭa</s> was <s>Nābhāga</s>, and from him also came <s>Bhalandana</s>.
The valiant king <s>Ajavāhana</s> was the son of <s>Bhalandana</s>.
These long-armed sons of <s>Manu</s> have been stated briefly.
Now I shall tell you of the sons, grandsons, and descendants of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, and of <s>Ela</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Aila</s>, named <s>Purūravas</s>, was a mighty devotee of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: cakre tvakaṇṭakaṃ rājyaṃ deśe puṇyatame dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He made his kingdom free from enemies in that most holy land, O twice-born ones.
On the northern bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, at <s>Prayāga</s> frequented by sages,
the glorious lord of <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s> was established in <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.

children.text: tasya putrāḥ sapta bhavan sarve vitatatejasaḥ
children.translated_text: He had seven sons, all of widely extended splendor,
renowned in the world of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, devotees of <s>Bhava</s>, and very strong.

children.text: āyur māyur amāyuś ca viśvāyuścaiva vīryavān
children.translated_text: <s>Āyu</s>, <s>Māyu</s>, <s>Amāyu</s>, and the valiant <s>Viśvāyu</s>,
and <s>Śrutāyu</s> and <s>Śatāyu</s>: these divine ones were the sons of <s>Urvaśī</s>.
The heroic sons of <s>Āyu</s> were exactly five, great in might.
Those kings were born to <s>Prabhā</s>, daughter of <s>Svarbhānu</s>.
First among them was <s>Nahuṣa</s>, knower of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), famed in the world.
The heirs of <s>Nahuṣa</s> were six, with splendor equal to <s>Indra</s>.
They were born, mighty in vigor, from <s>Virajā</s>, a daughter of the Fathers.
<s>Yati</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Saṃyāti</s>, <s>Āyāti</s>, and fifth <s>Andhaka</s>,
and <s>Vijāti</s>: these six were all of celebrated fame.

children.text: yatirjyeṣṭhaś ca teṣāṃ vai yayātistu tato 'varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yati</s> was the eldest of them, and <s>Yayāti</s> was next after him.
The eldest, <s>Yati</s>, seeking liberation, became absorbed in brahman, O lord.
Among those five, <s>Yayāti</s> was of great strength and valor.
He obtained <s>Devayānī</s>, daughter of <s>Uśanas</s>, as his wife,
and also the Asura maiden <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.

children.text: yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayānī vyajāyata
children.translated_text: <s>Devayānī</s> bore <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>.
Both of them were doers of auspicious deeds, praised, and skilled in knowledge.

children.text: druhyaṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, bore <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>.

children.text: yayātaye rathaṃ tasmai dadau śukraḥ pratāpavān ||
children.translated_text: Mighty <s>Śukra</s> gave that <s>Yayāti</s> a chariot.
That eminent brahmin, pleased and satisfied by him, gave a supremely radiant one,
well-fitted, golden, divine, and furnished with inexhaustible great quivers.

children.text: yuktaṃ manojavair aśvair yena kanyāṃ samudvahan
children.translated_text: It was yoked with horses swift as the mind; with it, after carrying off the maiden,
he conquered the earth in six months by means of that foremost chariot.
<s>Yayāti</s> was unassailable in battle by gods, <s>Dānavas</s>, and humans.
He was a devotee of <s>Bhava</s>, pure-souled, established in <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and upright.
He performed sacrifices, conquered anger, and showed compassion to all beings.

children.text: kauravāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sa bhavadratha uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among all the <s>Kauravas</s>, that excellent chariot endured.
Until the excellent king <s>Janamejaya</s>, a <s>Kaurava</s>,
a king of <s>Pūru</s>'s line and descendant of King <s>Parikṣit</s>,

children.text: jagāma sa ratho nāśaṃ śāpādgargasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: that chariot came to destruction through the curse of wise <s>Garga</s>.

children.text: gargasya hi sutaṃ bālaṃ sa rājā janamejayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For King <s>Janamejaya</s> harmed the young son of <s>Garga</s>,
an innocent boy, and he incurred the sin of killing a brahmin.
That royal sage, smelling of iron, ran here and there.
Abandoned by the people of city and countryside, he never found peace.

children.text: tataḥ sa duḥkhasaṃtapto na lebhe saṃvidaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: Then, tormented by suffering, he found no relief anywhere.
Distressed at that time, he went for refuge to the sage <s>Śaunaka</s>.
He was the generous-minded sage who was famous by the name <s>Indreti</s>.
And <s>Indreti</s> performed a sacrifice for that king <s>Janamejaya</s>,
a horse sacrifice for the king's purification, O best of twice-born ones.
Freed from the smell of iron and from sin, that greatly renowned one

children.text: yajñasyāvabhṛthe madhye yāto divyo rathaḥ śubhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: saw the auspicious divine chariot depart during the final bath of the sacrifice.
Thus, after falling away from that lineage, it came again to <s>Vasu</s>, lord of <s>Cedi</s>.

children.text: dattaḥ śakreṇa tuṣṭena lebhe tasmād bṛhadrathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From him <s>Bṛhadratha</s> obtained it, given by <s>Śakra</s> when he was pleased.
Then, after killing <s>Jarāsaṃdha</s>, <s>Bhīma</s> took that excellent chariot
and gave it with affection to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O delight of the <s>Kauravas</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Yayāti</s>, son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, the lord, anointed his son <s>Pūru</s>,
for he had been helped by that very <s>Pūru</s>, O best of twice-born ones.

children.text: abhiṣektukāmaṃ ca nṛpaṃ puruṃ putraṃ kanīyasam
children.translated_text: When the king wished to consecrate his youngest son <s>Pūru</s>,
the social classes, headed by the brahmins, spoke this statement:

children.text: kathaṃ śukrasya naptāraṃ devayānyāḥ sutaṃ prabho
children.translated_text: "How, O lord, can the grandson of <s>Śukra</s>, the son of <s>Devayānī</s>,
the eldest, <s>Yadu</s>, be passed over, while the younger deserves the kingdom?
We admonish you in this; observe <s>dharma</s> (righteous order)."
Thus ends the sixty-sixth chapter in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s> said:

children.text: brāhmaṇapramukhā varṇāḥ sarve śṛṇvantu me vacaḥ
children.translated_text: Let all the social classes headed by the brahmins hear my words.

children.text: jyeṣṭhaṃ prati yathā rājyaṃ na deyaṃ me kathañcana ||
children.translated_text: For this reason the kingdom is by no means to be given by me to the eldest.
My command was not obeyed by my eldest son, <s>Yadu</s>.

children.text: pratikūlamatiścaiva na sa putraḥ satāṃ mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: And because his mind was hostile, he is not considered a son by the good.
A son who carries out the word of his mother and father is praised by the good.

children.text: sa putraḥ putravad yas tu vartate mātṛpitṛṣu ||
children.translated_text: He is a true son who behaves as a son should toward his mother and father.
I was disregarded by <s>Yadu</s>, and likewise also by <s>Turvasu</s>.

children.text: druhyena cānunā caiva mayyavajñā kṛtā bhṛśam ||
children.translated_text: By <s>Druhyu</s> and <s>Anu</s> too, great disregard was shown toward me.

children.text: puruṇā ca kṛtaṃ vākyaṃ mānitaś ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Pūru</s> carried out my word, and I was especially honored.

children.text: kanīyānmama dāyādo jarā yena dhṛtā mama ||
children.translated_text: He is my youngest heir, by whom my old age was borne.

children.text: śukreṇa me samādiṣṭā devayānyāḥ kṛte jarā
children.translated_text: Old age was assigned to me by <s>Śukra</s> for <s>Devayānī</s>'s sake.
When he was requested again, that old age was made transferable.

children.text: śukreṇa ca varo dattaḥ kāvyenośanasā svayam
children.translated_text: And <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Kāvya</s> <s>Uśanas</s> himself, granted this boon:
"Whichever son follows your command shall be the bearer of your kingdom."
Let you also give permission: <s>Pūru</s> is to be consecrated in the kingdom.
The subjects said:
The son who is endowed with virtues and is always beneficial to his mother and father,

children.text: sarvamarhati kalyāṇaṃ kanīyān api sa prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: even if younger, that lord deserves every auspicious good.

children.text: arhaḥ pūruridaṃ rājyaṃ yaḥ suto vākyakṛttava ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pūru</s> deserves this kingdom, for he is the son who carries out your word.
Because of the boon granted by <s>Śukra</s>, it cannot be made otherwise.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus at that time the son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, addressed by the pleased townspeople,

children.text: abhiṣicya tato rājyaṃ pūruṃ sa sutam ātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: then consecrated his own son <s>Pūru</s> to the kingdom.
He assigned his son <s>Turvasu</s> to the south-eastern quarter.
Then the king appointed his eldest, <s>Yadu</s>, in the southern quarter,

children.text: pratīcyāmuttarasyāṃ tu druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca tāvubhau ||
children.translated_text: and in the western and northern quarters he appointed both <s>Druhyu</s> and <s>Anu</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s>, having conquered the earth with its seas and seven continents,
then, as the son of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, divided the kingdom threefold among his sons.
His splendor having been transferred to his sons, his mind filled with joy,
the king became delighted after placing the burden upon his kinsmen.

children.text: atra gāthā mahārājñā purā gītā yayātinā
children.translated_text: On this subject there were verses once sung by the great king <s>Yayāti</s>,
by which one should draw back desires from every side, like a tortoise its limbs.
By these alone does a man become prosperous, not otherwise, even if he performs ten million rites.
Desire is never appeased by the enjoyment of objects of desire.
Like a fire with offerings of ghee, it only increases still more.
Whatever rice and barley, gold, cattle, and women there are on earth,
all that is not enough for one man; thinking thus, one should go to tranquillity.

children.text: yadā na kurute bhāvaṃ sarvabhūteṣu pāpakam ||
children.translated_text: When one does not form an evil disposition toward any beings,

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā brahma sampadyate tadā
children.translated_text: by deed, mind, or speech, then one attains <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: yadā parānna bibheti pare cāsmānna bibhyati ||
children.translated_text: When one does not fear others, and others do not fear him,

children.text: yadā na nindenna dveṣṭi brahma sampadyate tadā
children.translated_text: when one neither reviles nor hates, then one attains <s>brahman</s>.
That which is hard for the foolish to abandon, which does not grow old as one grows old,

children.text: yo'sau prāṇāntiko rogastāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ tyajataḥ sukham
children.translated_text: that disease which lasts until the end of life, craving: happiness belongs to the one who abandons it.

children.text: jīryanti jīryataḥ keśā dantā jīryanti jīryataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hairs grow old as one grows old; the teeth grow old as one grows old;
the eye and ear also grow old, but craving alone remains unharmed.
All embodied beings grow old by their very nature, and not otherwise;

children.text: jīvitāśā dhanāśā ca jīryato'pi na jīryate
children.translated_text: but the hope for life and the hope for wealth do not grow old even in one who is growing old.

children.text: yacca kāmasukhaṃ loke yacca divyaṃ mahatsukham ||
children.translated_text: Whatever pleasure of desire exists in the world, and whatever great heavenly pleasure there is,
that is not worth even a sixteenth part of the happiness that comes from the destruction of craving.
Having spoken thus, that royal seer entered the forest together with his wife.
Having performed austerity there on <s>Bhṛgutuṅga</s>, the greatly renowned one,
and having accomplished fasting, attained heaven there together with his wife.
His five lineages are these, holy and honored by divine seers,
by whom the whole earth was pervaded, as by the rays of the sun.

children.text: dhanī prajāvān āyuṣmān kīrtimāṃś ca bhavennaraḥ
children.translated_text: A wise man who reads and hears the holy story of <s>Yayāti</s>
becomes wealthy, possessed of offspring, long-lived, and famous.
Freed from all sins, he is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge somavaṃśe yayāticaritaṃ nāma saptaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-seventh chapter, named 'The Story of <s>Yayāti</s> in the Lunar Dynasty,' in the first part of the glorious great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall describe the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, the eldest and of highest splendor;
listen to me as I speak concisely and in due order.

children.text: yadoḥ putrā babhūvur hi pañca devasutopamāḥ
children.translated_text: There were five sons of <s>Yadu</s>, equal to the sons of gods:
<s>Sahasrajit</s> was the eldest son, then <s>Kroṣṭu</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Ajaka</s>, and <s>Laghu</s>.
Likewise the son of <s>Sahasrajit</s> was the king named <s>Śatajit</s>.
The sons of <s>Śatajit</s> were renowned, three men of supreme fame:

children.text: haihayaś ca hayaścaiva rājā veṇuhayaś ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Haihaya</s>, <s>Haya</s>, and the king who was <s>Veṇuhaya</s>.
The heir of <s>Haihaya</s> was celebrated by the name <s>Dharma</s>.
His son, O brahmins, was known as <s>Dharmanetra</s>.

children.text: dharmanetrasya kīrtis tu saṃjayas tasya cātmajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Dharmanetra</s> was <s>Kīrti</s>, and his son was <s>Saṃjaya</s>.
The heir of <s>Saṃjaya</s> was the righteous one named <s>Mahiṣmān</s>.
The powerful <s>Bhadraśreṇya</s> was the son of <s>Mahiṣmat</s>.
The heir of <s>Bhadraśreṇya</s> was the king named <s>Durdama</s>.
The wise son of <s>Durdama</s> was renowned by the name <s>Dhanaka</s>.
The heirs of <s>Dhanaka</s> were four, esteemed by the world:

children.text: kṛtavīryaḥ kṛtāgniś ca kṛtavarmā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>, <s>Kṛtāgni</s>, and likewise <s>Kṛtavarmā</s>,
and <s>Kṛtaujās</s> was the fourth; from <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> came <s>Arjuna</s>,
born with a thousand arms, the foremost lord of the seven-continent earth.
At that time <s>Rāma</s>, whose nature was <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, became his death.
He had hundreds of sons; among them were five great chariot-warriors,
skilled in weapons, strong, heroic, righteous, and high-minded:

children.text: śūraś ca śūrasenaś ca dhṛṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇastathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Śūrasena</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, and likewise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: jayadhvajaś ca rājāsīd āvantīnāṃ viśāṃ patiḥ
children.translated_text: and King <s>Jayadhvaja</s>, lord of the people of <s>Avantī</s>.
The son of <s>Jayadhvaja</s> was mighty <s>Tālajaṅgha</s>.
His hundred sons here were celebrated as the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s>.
The eldest among them, a king of great valor, was <s>Vītihotra</s>.
The others, beginning with <s>Vṛṣa</s>, were his sons, doers of meritorious deeds.
<s>Vṛṣa</s> was the continuer of their lineage; his son was <s>Madhu</s>.

children.text: madhoḥ putraśataṃ cāsīd vṛṣṇistasya tu vaṃśabhāk
children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> had a hundred sons, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> inherited his lineage.

children.text: vṛṣṇestu vṛṣṇayaḥ sarve madhorvai mādhavāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> all are known as <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and from <s>Madhu</s> as <s>Mādhavas</s>.
By the lineage of <s>Yadu</s> the <s>Haihayas</s> are also explained as <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ pañca gaṇā hyete haihayānāṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: Of those great-souled <s>Haihayas</s>, these indeed are the five groups.
And the <s>Vītihotras</s>, the <s>Haryātas</s>, the <s>Bhojas</s>, and likewise the <s>Avantis</s>,
and the <s>Śūrasenas</s> are famous, and likewise the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s>.

children.text: śūraś ca śūrasenaś ca vṛṣaḥ kṛṣṇastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Śūrasena</s>, <s>Vṛṣa</s>, and likewise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
and <s>Jayadhvaja</s> as the fifth are famed as the best of the <s>Haihayas</s>.

children.text: śūraś ca śūravīraś ca śūrasenasya cānaghāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Śūravīra</s>, and the faultless descendants of <s>Śūrasena</s>
became known as the <s>Śūrasenas</s>; those were the lands of those great-souled ones.
The son of <s>Vītihotra</s> too was the famous one called <s>Narta</s>.
<s>Durjaya</s>, the son of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, became a tormentor of enemies.
Now hear the lineage of the royal seer <s>Kroṣṭu</s>, marked by excellent manly valor,
in whose line <s>Viṣṇu</s> was born, the bearer of the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> clan.
<s>Kroṣṭu</s> had one son, <s>Vṛjinīvān</s>, of great fame.
His son was <s>Svātī</s>; <s>Kuśaṅku</s> was his son.
Then <s>Kuśaṅku</s>, very mighty, desiring offspring,
sacrificed with great sacrifices of various kinds, furnished with ample sacrificial fees.
His son <s>Citraratha</s> was born, endowed with ritual acts;
and the heroic son of <s>Citraratha</s> was a sacrificer who gave abundant fees.

children.text: śaśabindus tu vai rājā anvayād vratam uttamam
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śaśabindu</s>, from that lineage, followed an excellent vow;
he was a universal emperor, great-hearted, very mighty, and rich in descendants.
Of <s>Śaśabindu</s>’s sons there were a hundred thousand,
and they praise <s>Anantaka</s> as the unsurpassed best among his sons.

children.text: anantakāt suto yajño yajñasya tanayo dhṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Anantaka</s> came the son <s>Yajña</s>; <s>Yajña</s>’s son was <s>Dhṛti</s>.
<s>Uśanas</s> was his son; having obtained this earth,
that supremely righteous one completed a hundred horse sacrifices.
<s>Uśanas</s>’s son is remembered as the king named <s>Siteṣu</s>.
<s>Maruta</s> was his son, a royal seer who increased the lineage.
The hero <s>Kambalabarhis</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Maruta</s>.
The learned <s>Rukmakavaca</s> was the son of <s>Kambalabarhis</s>.
Having slain armored heroes in battle, <s>Rukmakavaca</s>,
with sharp arrows against the bowmen, obtained supreme prosperity.

children.text: aśvamedhe tu dharmātmā ṛtvigbhyaḥ pṛthivīṃ dadau ||
children.translated_text: At a horse sacrifice the righteous one gave the earth to the officiating priests.
From <s>Rukmakavaca</s> was born <s>Parāvṛt</s>, slayer of enemy heroes.
Five sons of great courage were born to <s>Parāvṛt</s>.

children.text: rukmeṣuḥ pṛthurukmaś ca jyāmaghaḥ parigho hariḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmeṣu</s>, <s>Pṛthurukma</s>, <s>Jyāmagha</s>, <s>Parigha</s>, and <s>Hari</s>

children.text: parighaṃ ca hariṃ caiva videheṣu pitā nyasat ||
children.translated_text: The father settled <s>Parigha</s> and <s>Hari</s> among the <s>Videhas</s>.
<s>Rukmeṣu</s> became king, while <s>Pṛthurukma</s> remained under his protection.
Driven into exile by them, King <s>Jyāmagha</s> lived in a hermitage.
Though he dwelt in the forest, he was peaceful and was instructed by Brahmins.
Taking up his bow, he went to another country, with banner and chariot.
On the bank of the <s>Narmadā</s>, alone and accompanied only by his wife,
having gone to <s>Ṛkṣavant</s> mountain, he lived there, abandoned by others.
<s>Jyāmagha</s>’s wife was <s>Śaibyā</s>, virtuous and faithful.

children.text: sā caiva tapasogreṇa śaibyā vai samprasūyata ||
children.translated_text: And by fierce austerity that <s>Śaibyā</s> gave birth
to a fortunate son, <s>Vidarbha</s>, though she was advanced in age.
By the king, in the son’s daughter, the two learned ones <s>Kratha</s> and <s>Kaiśika</s> were born.
They were the two sons of King <s>Vidarbha</s>, heroes skilled in battle;
<s>Romapāda</s> was the third, and <s>Babhru</s> is remembered as his son.
His son was <s>Sudhṛti</s>, learned and supremely righteous.
From him came a son, <s>Kauśika</s>; from him the <s>Caidya</s> lineage is remembered.
<s>Kratha</s> was the son of <s>Vidarbha</s>; <s>Kunti</s> was his son.
From <s>Kunti</s> was then born <s>Vṛta</s>, and <s>Raṇadhṛṣṭa</s>, powerful in battle.
<s>Raṇadhṛṣṭa</s>’s son was <s>Nidhṛti</s>, slayer of enemy heroes.
The one descended from <s>Nidhṛti</s> was named <s>Daśārha</s>, destroyer of great hosts of enemies.

children.text: daśārhasya suto vyāpto jīmūta iti tatsutaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Daśārha</s>’s son was <s>Vyāpta</s>; <s>Jīmūta</s> was his son.
<s>Jīmūta</s>’s son was <s>Vikṛti</s>; his son was <s>Bhīmaratha</s>.
Then <s>Bhīmaratha</s> had a son named <s>Navaratha</s>,
always devoted to the <s>dharma</s> (religious duty) of giving and dedicated to truthful conduct.
He had <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, and <s>Śakuni</s> was his son.
From him <s>Karambha</s> was born; thereafter came <s>Devarāta</s>.
From <s>Devarāta</s> was born King <s>Devarāti</s>, of great fame.
One resembling a divine embryo was born, named <s>Devakṣatra</s>.
The illustrious son of <s>Devakṣatra</s> was named <s>Madhu</s>, of great fame.
King <s>Madhu</s> was the founder of the lineage of the <s>Madhus</s>; from <s>Madhu</s> came <s>Kuruvaṃśa</s>.
From <s>Kuruvaṃśa</s> came <s>Anu</s>; from him came <s>Purutvan</s>, best of men.
<s>Aṃśu</s> was born from <s>Purutvan</s> by the <s>Vaidarbhī</s> woman <s>Bhadravatī</s>.
<s>Aṃśu</s> married an <s>Aikṣvākī</s> woman; from her <s>Sattva</s> was born.
From <s>Sattva</s> came <s>Sātvata</s>, endowed with all virtues and increaser of the family.

children.text: jyāmaghasya mayā proktā sṛṣṭirvai vistareṇa vaḥ
children.translated_text: The generation of <s>Jyāmagha</s> has thus been told by me to you in detail.
Whoever reads or hears the lineage of <s>Jyāmagha</s>

children.text: prajīvatyeti vai svargaṃ rājyaṃ saukhyaṃ ca vindati ||
children.translated_text: lives long, goes to heaven, and obtains kingship and happiness.
Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, ends the sixty-eighth chapter, named “Description of the Lineages.”
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Sātvata</s>, endowed with truth, begot four sons:

children.text: bhajanaṃ bhrājamānaṃ ca divyaṃ devāvṛdhaṃ nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhajana</s>, <s>Bhrājamāna</s>, the divine king <s>Devāvṛdha</s>,

children.text: andhakaṃ ca mahābhāgaṃ vṛṣṇiṃ ca yadunandanam
children.translated_text: and greatly fortunate <s>Andhaka</s>, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, delight of the <s>Yadus</s>.
Hear now in detail the four lines descended from them.
From <s>Bhajana</s> and also from <s>Bhrājamāna</s>, through <s>Sṛñjayā</s>, were born
<s>Ayutāyu</s>, <s>Śatāyu</s>, <s>Balavān</s>, and <s>Harṣakṛt</s> is remembered.

children.text: teṣāṃ devāvṛdho rājā cacāra paramaṃ tapaḥ
children.translated_text: Among them, King <s>Devāvṛdha</s> practiced supreme austerity,
thinking, “May a son endowed with every virtue become mine.”
His son, famed as <s>Babhru</s>, was a best of kings, renowned for merit.
It is widely heard that those who know ancient genealogies sing of him.
Proclaiming the virtues of the great-souled <s>Devāvṛdha</s>,
they say, “Just as we hear from afar, so we see when close at hand.”
<s>Babhru</s> was the best of men; <s>Devāvṛdha</s> was equal to the gods.

children.text: puruṣāḥ pañca ṣaṣṭistu ṣaṭ sahasrāṇi cāṣṭa ca ||
children.translated_text: Sixty-five men, and six thousand and eight besides,
attained immortality through <s>Babhru</s> and even through <s>Devāvṛdha</s>.
He was a sacrificer, intent on giving, heroic, devoted to Brahmins, and firm in vow.
He was famous and very radiant, a great chariot-warrior of the <s>Sātvatas</s>.
In his lineage were born the <s>Bhojas</s>, indeed comparable to deities.

children.text: gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca vṛṣṇibhārye babhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndhārī</s> and <s>Mādrī</s> became wives of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>.
<s>Gāndhārī</s> gave birth to <s>Sumitra</s>, the delighter of friends.

children.text: mādrī lebhe ca taṃ putraṃ tataḥ sā devamīḍhuṣam
children.translated_text: <s>Mādrī</s> obtained that son, and then <s>Devamīḍhuṣa</s>,
and <s>Anamitra</s> and <s>Śini</s> as well, both excellent men.
<s>Anamitra</s>’s son was <s>Nighna</s>; <s>Nighna</s> had two sons,
the fortunate <s>Prasena</s> and <s>Satrājit</s>, those two sons.
For that <s>Satrājit</s>, the Sun became a friend as dear as life.
The jewel named <s>Syamantaka</s> was given to him by <s>Vivasvat</s>.
On earth that jewel was the king of all jewels.
Once, when <s>Prasena</s> went hunting together with it,
he met his death, helpless, from a very terrible lion.
Then a son of <s>Śini</s>, the younger descendant of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, was born.
He was truthful in speech and endowed with truth; <s>Satyaka</s> was his son.
<s>Sātyaki</s>, <s>Yuyudhāna</s>, was the powerful grandson of <s>Śini</s>.
<s>Asaṅga</s> was born from <s>Yuyudhāna</s>; <s>Kuṇi</s> was his son.

children.text: kuṇer yugaṃdharaḥ putraḥ śaineyā iti kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yugaṃdhara</s> was <s>Kuṇi</s>’s son; these are celebrated as the <s>Śaineyas</s>.
From <s>Mādrī</s>’s son was born a son, the <s>Vārṣṇi</s> <s>Yudhājit</s>,
famed as <s>Śvaphalka</s>, a benefactor of the three worlds.

children.text: śvaphalkaś ca mahārājo dharmātmā yatra vartate
children.translated_text: Where the great king <s>Śvaphalka</s>, righteous-souled, dwells,
there is no fear of disease there, nor any fear of drought.
<s>Śvaphalka</s> took as wife the daughter of the king of <s>Kāśi</s>.

children.text: gāndinīṃ nāma kāśyo hi dadau tasmai svakanyakām ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Kāśi</s> king gave him his own daughter, named <s>Gāndinī</s>.
She remained, it is said, in her mother’s womb for many years

children.text: vasantī na ca saṃjajñe garbhasthā tāṃ pitābravīt ||
children.translated_text: and was not born; while she was still in the womb, her father said to her:

children.text: jāyasva śīghraṃ bhadraṃ te kimarthaṃ cābhitiṣṭhasi
children.translated_text: “Be born quickly; may it be well with you. Why do you remain there?”

children.text: provāca cainaṃ garbhasthā sā kanyā gāndinī tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then that girl <s>Gāndinī</s>, still in the womb, said to him:
“If for three years you give one cow each day to a Brahmin,
then I will come out from the womb, father.”
“So be it,” her father said, and he fulfilled her wish.

children.text: dātā śūraś ca yajvā ca śrutavānatithipriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He was a giver, heroic, a sacrificer, learned, and fond of guests.
Her son from <s>Śvaphalka</s> is remembered as <s>Akrūra</s>, rich in sacrificial gifts.
<s>Akrūra</s> took <s>Ratnā</s>, daughter of <s>Śaiva</s>, as his wife.
In her he begot sons; hear of them.
<s>Upamanyu</s>, <s>Māṅgu</s>, <s>Vṛta</s>, and <s>Janamejaya</s>,
<s>Girirakṣa</s>, <s>Upekṣa</s>, and <s>Śatrughna</s>, who crushed his enemies,

children.text: dharmabhṛd vṛṣṭadharmā ca godhano'tha varas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmabhṛt</s>, <s>Vṛṣṭadharman</s>, <s>Godhana</s>, and <s>Vara</s> as well,
<s>Āvāha</s> and <s>Prativāha</s>, and <s>Sudhārā</s>, a beautiful woman.
By <s>Ugrasenī</s>, <s>Akrūra</s> had two sons, delights of the family:
<s>Devavān</s> and <s>Upadeva</s> were born, approved by the gods.

children.text: sumitrasya suto jajñe citrakaś ca mahāyaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A son of <s>Sumitra</s> was born, <s>Citraka</s>, very famous.
<s>Citraka</s>’s sons were <s>Vipṛthu</s> and <s>Pṛthu</s>,
<s>Aśvagrīva</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Sudhāsūka</s>, and <s>Gavekṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, <s>Aśva</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Dharmabhṛt</s>,
<s>Subhūmi</s> and <s>Bahubhūmi</s>, and the two women <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s> and <s>Śravaṇā</s>.
From <s>Andhaka</s>, the daughter of <s>Kāśi</s> obtained four sons:
<s>Kukura</s>, <s>Bhajamāna</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, and <s>Kambalabarhiṣa</s>.
<s>Kukura</s>’s son was <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>; from <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> came <s>Śūra</s>.
<s>Kapotaroman</s>, <s>Atibala</s>; his son was <s>Vilomaka</s>.
His learned son, <s>Nala</s>, was a friend of <s>Tumburu</s>, it is said.
He is famed by the good name <s>Candanānaka-Dundubhi</s>.
From him too a son, <s>Abhijit</s>, was born; his son was <s>Punarvasu</s>.
That best of men performed a horse sacrifice for the sake of a son.
In the midst of that <s>Atirātra</s> rite, he arose from the center of the sacrificial hall.

children.text: tatastu vidvān sarvajño dātā yajvā punarvasuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Punarvasu</s> was learned, all-knowing, a giver, and a sacrificer.
To him too, it is said, a pair of children was born from <s>Abhijit</s>:
<s>Āhuka</s> and <s>Āhukī</s>, both renowned and best among the famous.
From <s>Āhuka</s> and the daughter of <s>Kāśi</s>, two sons were born:
<s>Devaka</s> and <s>Ugrasena</s>, both like children of the gods.
To King <s>Devaka</s> were born sons resembling the thirty gods:
<s>Devavān</s>, <s>Upadeva</s>, <s>Sudeva</s>, and <s>Devarakṣita</s>.

children.text: teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptāsan vasudevāya tā dadau
children.translated_text: They had seven sisters; he gave them to <s>Vasudeva</s>.
<s>Vṛṣadevā</s>, <s>Upadevā</s>, and another, <s>Devarakṣitā</s>,
<s>Śrīdevā</s>, <s>Śāntidevā</s>, and also another, <s>Sahadevā</s>,
and <s>Devakī</s>, who among them was the best, with a lovely waist.
<s>Ugrasena</s> had nine sons; among them <s>Kaṃsa</s> was the eldest.

children.text: teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāś ca śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And their sons and grandsons were by the hundreds and by the thousands.
The daughter of <s>Devaka</s> became the wife of wise <s>Vasudeva</s>;

children.text: babhūva vandyā pūjyā ca devairapi pativratā ||
children.translated_text: she was honored and worshiped, a faithful wife, even by the gods.
And the greatly fortunate <s>Rohiṇī</s> was the wife of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>;
<s>Pauravī</s>, daughter of <s>Bāhlika</s>, was also worthy of honor even by the gods.
<s>Rohiṇī</s> bore <s>Rāma</s>, the best of the strong, wielder of the plough,
who, through fear of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, had taken refuge there, self-controlled and of tranquil splendor.
Then, when <s>Rāma</s> had been born and the six extremely righteous embryos had been killed,
wise <s>Vasudeva</s> begot <s>Hari</s> in <s>Devakī</s>.
He himself is that supreme self, the god of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>;
and the blessed <s>Halāyudha</s> is <s>Ananta</s>, shining like silver.
By the pretext of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s curse, honoring a human body,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, was born in that <s>Devakī</s>.
And <s>Yoganidrā</s>, <s>Kauśikī</s>, born from the body of <s>Umā</s>,
by command of the god of gods, became the daughter of <s>Yaśodā</s>.
She is indeed manifest <s>Prakṛti</s>, bowed to by all the gods,
while the blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is <s>Puruṣa</s>, bestowing the fruits of <s>dharma</s> and liberation.
Then, protecting his own son from <s>Kaṃsa</s>, he took that girl,
and the four-armed, broad-eyed <s>Janārdana</s>, marked with the sign of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>,
bearing conch, discus, mace, and lotus,

children.text: yaśodāyai pradattvā tu vasudevaś ca buddhimān ||
children.translated_text: wise <s>Vasudeva</s> gave to <s>Yaśodā</s>.
After giving him to <s>Nandagopa</s>, he said, "Protect him."
He was <s>Viṣṇu</s>, protector of the worlds, who had assumed a body by his own will.
And by the grace of the god <s>Śiva</s> of immeasurable splendor,

children.text: rāmeṇa sārdhaṃ taṃ dattvā varadaṃ parameśvaram ||
children.translated_text: having given that supreme lord, the giver of boons, together with <s>Rāma</s>,
the teacher of the world, who had descended for the purpose of restraining the burden of the earth,
therefore every good fortune will come to the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: ayaṃ sa garbho devakyā yo naḥ kleśyānhariṣyati
children.translated_text: "This is that embryo of <s>Devakī</s> who will remove our afflictions."
Then <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> reported this to <s>Kaṃsa</s>, son of <s>Ugrasena</s>:
at that time he announced that a well-marked girl had been born.
"This is your eighth embryo from <s>Devakī</s>, O <s>Kaṃsa</s>, observer of vows.

children.text: mṛtyur eva na saṃdeha iti vāṇī purātanī
children.translated_text: It is certainly your death; there is no doubt. Such was the ancient voice."
Then <s>Kaṃsa</s>, leaping up into the air, began to kill her.
The eight-armed goddess spoke with a voice deep as a cloud:
"Protect that body of yours; your death has indeed arrived.
While you guard the body of a deceitful one in <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s form,

children.text: kiṃ kṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ mūrkha jātaḥ khalu tavāntakṛt ||
children.translated_text: what evil deed have you done, fool? The one who will bring your end has surely been born.
<s>Kaṃsa</s>, out of fear of <s>Devakī</s>'s son, killed the eighth one, so they say;
they remember that the appointed death was the eighth son of <s>Devakī</s>.
The effort of the <s>Bhoja</s> king against that counter-image of <s>Hari</s> was in vain;
by her power too, O tigers among sages, he was made dull and helpless.
<s>Kaṃsa</s> also was slain by that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose deeds are effortless,
and many others, killers of gods and brahmins, were slain.
The sons of that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, beginning with <s>Pradyumna</s>,
are counted as many, all skilled in battle.
They are declared to be sons of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sons resembling <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Among all these sons, those of <s>Hari</s> beginning with <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>,
born of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, were especially strong and destroyers of enemies.
There were sixteen thousand wives and one hundred more.

children.text: kṛṣṇasya tāsu sarvāsu priyā jyeṣṭhā ca rukmiṇī
children.translated_text: Among all of them, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> was dear to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the eldest.
For twelve years, with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of effortless deeds
dwelling on air as food, <s>Hara</s> was worshiped for the sake of sons.
<s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, <s>Sucāru</s>, <s>Cāruveṣa</s>, and <s>Yaśodhara</s>,
<s>Cāruśravas</s>, <s>Cāruyaśas</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Sāmba</s>:
these were obtained by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> through the grace of the trident-bearing god.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā tanayānvīrān raukmiṇeyāṃś ca rukmiṇīm
children.translated_text: Seeing those heroic sons, the sons of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, and <s>Rukmiṇī</s> herself,
<s>Jāmbavatī</s>, the wife of wise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, said to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
"O lotus-eyed one, when pleased, you ought to give me
an excellent son, more endowed with virtues, equal to the lord of the gods."
Having heard <s>Jāmbavatī</s>'s words, <s>Hari</s>, lord of the world,
the blameless treasure of austerity, then began to perform austerity.
Then that <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
went to the excellent hermitage of the sage <s>Vyāghrapāda</s>.
Seeing the seer, the <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> bowed down,
and by his command obtained the divine <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga.
With beard and hair removed, smeared with ghee, wearing a girdle of muñja grass,
the blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, scorcher of foes, was initiated and performed severe austerity.
With arms raised, unsupported, standing on the tip of his big toe,
<s>Adhokṣaja</s> lived for three seasons on fruits, water, and air.

children.text: tapasā tasya saṃtuṣṭo dadau rudro bahūn varān
children.translated_text: Satisfied by his austerity, <s>Rudra</s> gave many boons
to great-souled <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, including <s>Sāmba</s>, son of <s>Jāmbavatī</s>.

children.text: tathā jāṃbavatī caiva sāṃbaṃ bhāryā hareḥ sutam
children.translated_text: And <s>Jāmbavatī</s> herself, <s>Hari</s>'s wife, having obtained her son <s>Sāmba</s>,
gained unsurpassed joy, as <s>Aditi</s> did on obtaining the sun.

children.text: bāṇasya ca tadā tena cheditaṃ munipuṅgavāḥ
children.translated_text: Then by him, O foremost sages, a thousand arms
of <s>Bāṇa</s> were cut off because of the curse of wise <s>Rudra</s>.
Then, with <s>Halāyudha</s> as his ally, he accomplished the slaughter of demons,
and likewise, merely in sport, of wicked kings on the battlefield.
Having slain <s>Naraka</s>, born from the gods and foremost among demons,
through the boon of the great-souled brahmin <s>Ūrdhvacakra</s>.
The one of incomparable valor took for his own enjoyment sixteen
thousand maidens, and more than a hundred, that mighty one.
Using the brahmins' curse as a pretext, he brought his own clan to an end;
and having destroyed that clan, <s>Acyuta</s> remained at <s>Prabhāsa</s>.

children.text: tadā tasyaiva tu gataṃ varṣāṇāmadhikaṃ śatam
children.translated_text: Then more than a hundred years had passed for him,
for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in <s>Dvārakā</s>, the remover of the distress of old age.
At that time he honored at <s>Piṇḍāraka</s> the curse of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, of <s>Kaṇva</s>,
and of wise <s>Nārada</s>, and the word of <s>Durvāsas</s>.

children.text: tyaktvā ca mānuṣaṃ rūpaṃ jarakāstracchalena tu
children.translated_text: And, abandoning his human form through the device of <s>Jarā</s>'s arrow,

children.text: anugṛhya ca kṛṣṇo'pi lubdhakaṃ prayayau divam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, after also showing favor to the hunter, went to heaven.
By the curse of <s>Aṣṭāvakra</s>, all the wives of wise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
were carried off by thieves, through his power of illusion as well.

children.text: balabhadro'pi saṃtyajya nāgo bhūtvā jagāma ca
children.translated_text: <s>Balabhadra</s> too, abandoning his body, became a serpent and departed.
The auspicious queens of that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with <s>Rukmiṇī</s> at their head,
all entered the fire together with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose deeds were unwearied.

children.text: revatī ca tathā devī balabhadreṇa dhīmatā ||
children.translated_text: And likewise the goddess <s>Revatī</s>, with wise <s>Balabhadra</s>,

children.text: praviṣṭā pāvakaṃ viprāḥ sā ca bhartṛpathaṃ gatā
children.translated_text: entered the fire, O brahmins; she followed the path of her husband.
Having performed the funeral rites of <s>Hari</s>, mighty <s>Pārtha</s>,
and likewise those of <s>Rāma</s> and of the other <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, O virtuous ones,
performed the offering for him with bulbs, roots, and fruits.

children.text: dravyābhāvāt svayaṃ pārtho bhrātṛbhiś ca divaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Because there was no wealth for the rites, <s>Pārtha</s> himself later went to heaven with his brothers.
Thus the power of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose deeds were unwearied,
and his dissolution by his own will have been briefly described.
This, O twice-born ones, is the story of the kings of the lunar dynasty.
Whoever reads it or hears it, or causes brahmins to hear it,

children.text: sa yāti vaiṣṇavaṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; no doubt need be entertained about this.
Thus ends the sixty-ninth chapter, named 'The Celebration of the Lunar Dynasty,' in the first part of the glorious great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The primordial creation has been indicated by you, O <s>Sūta</s>, but not made clear.
Now you ought to explain it in full, O virtuous one.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Maheśvara</s>, the great god, stands beyond both <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature)
and <s>puruṣa</s> (conscious spirit); he is the god, the supreme self, O lords among sages.
From that lord there arose the unmanifest, the supreme cause,
which thinkers on reality call <s>pradhāna</s> (primary matter) and <s>prakṛti</s>.
It is without smell, color, or taste, and devoid of sound and touch;
it is undecaying, fixed, imperishable, eternal, and established in itself.
It is the womb of the world, the great element, the supreme eternal <s>brahman</s>,
the embodiment of all beings, set in motion by the command of the Lord.
Without beginning or end, unborn, subtle, three-stranded with the <s>guṇas</s>, the source and the imperishable,
unmanifest and unknowable, it existed before <s>Brahmā</s>.
All this was pervaded by its self, according to the will of <s>Śiva</s>.
At that time, while the <s>guṇas</s> were in equilibrium in that undivided darkness,
at the time of creation, when <s>pradhāna</s> was presided over by the knower of the field,
through the alteration of the <s>guṇas</s>, <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) became manifest and appeared.
Then it was enveloped by the subtle, by <s>mahat</s>, and by the unmanifest.
At first <s>mahat</s>, predominated by <s>sattva</s>, made mere being manifest.
<s>Mahat</s> should be understood as mind; that one is remembered as its cause.
It arose as a mere <s>liṅga</s> (subtle mark), presided over by the knower of the field.
Forms such as <s>dharma</s> are causes for the purposes of the principles of the worlds;
impelled by the wish to create, <s>mahat</s> transforms itself into creation.
It is remembered as mind, <s>mahat</s>, thought, <s>brahman</s>, fullness, intellect, renown, lord,

children.text: prajñā citiḥ smṛtiḥ saṃvidviśveśaśceti sa smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: insight, consciousness, memory, awareness, and lord of the universe.
Because it thinks upon the activity and fruit of all beings,

children.text: saukṣmyāttena vibhaktaṃ tu yena tanmana ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and because, through its subtlety, it is that by which things are divided, it is called mind.
Because it is the first-born of the principles and is great in measure,
greater than the particulars and even than the <s>guṇas</s>, it is therefore remembered as <s>mahat</s>.

children.text: bibharti mānaṃ manute vibhāgaṃ manyate'pi ca
children.translated_text: It bears measure, thinks out division, and also forms conceptions;
because the <s>puruṣa</s> is connected with experience, this is therefore remembered as thought.
Because of its greatness, because it makes things grow, and because it is the support of all states,
and because it upholds existing things, it is therefore called <s>brahman</s>.
Because it fills all the gods completely with acts of grace,

children.text: nayate tattvabhāvaṃ ca tena pūriti cocyate ||
children.translated_text: and leads them to the state of the principles, it is therefore called fullness.

children.text: budhyate puruṣaścātra sarvān bhāvān hitaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Here the <s>puruṣa</s> understands all states and what is beneficial,
and because it also causes understanding, it is therefore explained as intellect.
Because manifestation and corresponding experience arise from it,
and because experience rests upon knowledge, it is therefore remembered as renown.
And because it is made manifest again and again by its qualities, such as knowledge,
therefore the name of <s>mahat</s> is declared to be renown.
Because the great self directly knows everything, it is therefore lord;
and because it follows upon knowledge, it is therefore called insight.
Because it gathers forms such as knowledge,
and many fruits of action for the sake of experience, it is therefore called consciousness.
Because it remembers all effects,
present and past, and likewise those yet to come, it is therefore called memory.
Because it finds complete knowledge, the highest greatness,
Therefore, from 'finding' and from 'knowing,' it is called <s>saṃvid</s> (conscious awareness).

children.text: vidyate'pi ca sarvatra tasminsarvaṃ ca vindati
children.translated_text: It exists everywhere, and in it one finds everything.
Therefore the great ones, O best of sages, have declared it to be <s>saṃvid</s>.
From 'knowing' they call it <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge); the blessed lord is a treasury of knowledge.
Because he is beyond bondage and the like, the wise call him <s>Īśvara</s>.
With synonymous words, the first and unsurpassed <s>tattva</s> (principle)
has been explained by knowers of the reality of principles, who discern true divine being.
<s>Mahat</s> transforms creation, impelled by the wish to create.
Resolve and ascertainment are remembered as its two functions.
Then, from the threefold guṇa-state dominated by rajas, <s>ahaṃkāra</s> arose.

children.text: mahatā ca vṛtaḥ sargo bhūtādir bāhyatastu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: The creation called <s>bhūtādi</s> is enclosed by <s>mahat</s>, and it is external to it.
From that same <s>ahaṃkāra</s>, dominated by tamas, there arose
the creation of the elemental <s>tanmātras</s>; that <s>bhūtādi</s> is tāmasa.
As <s>bhūtādi</s> was transforming, it created mere sound.
From that arose <s>ākāśa</s>, hollow space, characterized by sound.
<s>Ākāśa</s>, being mere sound, enveloped mere touch.
And <s>vāyu</s>, as it transformed, created mere form.
Light arises from <s>vāyu</s>; it is said to have form as its quality.
<s>Vāyu</s>, whose measure is touch, enveloped mere form.
Light too, as it transformed, created mere taste.

children.text: sambhavanti tato hyāpas tā vai sarvarasātmikāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that the waters arise; they are wholly of the nature of taste.
Fire, mere form, enveloped those waters that were mere taste.
The waters too, as they transformed, created mere smell.

children.text: saṃghāto jāyate tasmāttasya gandho guṇo mataḥ
children.translated_text: From that an aggregate is born; smell is regarded as its quality.

children.text: tasmiṃstasmiṃś ca tanmātraṃ tena tanmātratā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: In each and every case there is a <s>tanmātra</s>; because of that, tanmātra-ness is remembered.
Because they denote no specific distinction, they are therefore called <s>aviśeṣas</s> (undifferentiated entities).
Because they are calm, terrible, and deluded, they are again called <s>aviśeṣas</s>.
This creation of the elemental <s>tanmātras</s> should be understood as mutually related.
From <s>vaikārika ahaṃkāra</s>, the sāttvika form dominated by sattva,
that <s>vaikārika</s> creation proceeds all at once.
There are the five cognitive senses and the five organs of action.
The senses are instruments of accomplishment; the ten deities are <s>vaikārika</s>.
The eleventh there is the mind, by its own quality having the nature of both.

children.text: śrotraṃ tvak cakṣuṣī jihvā nāsikā caiva pañcamī
children.translated_text: Hearing, touch, the two eyes, the tongue, and the nose as the fifth,
these, furnished with cognition, are for the apprehension of sound and the rest.

children.text: pādau pāyurupasthaś ca hastau vāgdaśamī bhavet
children.translated_text: The two feet, the anus, the generative organ, the two hands, and speech are the tenth.

children.text: gatirvisargo hyānandaḥ śilpaṃ vākyaṃ ca karma tat ||
children.translated_text: Their actions are movement, evacuation, pleasure, craft, and utterance.
<s>Ākāśa</s>, mere sound, entered into mere touch.
Then <s>vāyu</s> became twofold in qualities, having sound and touch as its nature.
Likewise, when form entered those two qualities, sound and touch,
then fire became threefold in qualities, possessing sound, touch, and form.
And taste entered what possessed sound, touch, and form.
Therefore the waters, consisting of taste, should be understood as fourfold in qualities.

children.text: śabdasparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca raso vai gandhamāviśat
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, form, and taste entered smell.
United with mere smell, they entered this earth.
Therefore earth is praised as fivefold in qualities and gross among the elements.

children.text: śāntā ghorāś ca mūḍhāś ca viśeṣāstena te smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For that reason they are remembered as <s>viśeṣas</s> (differentiated entities): calm, terrible, and deluded.
Through mutual interpenetration they support one another.
Within earth is all this, enclosed by the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain.
The <s>viśeṣas</s> are grasped by the senses, and they are so called because they are determinate.
The later creations obtain the quality of the preceding creation, each in succession.

children.text: teṣāṃ yāvacca tad yacca yacca tāvadguṇaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever extent and whatever quality there is among them is remembered as just that much.

children.text: upalabhyāpsu vai gandhaṃ kecid brūyur apāṃ guṇam ||
children.translated_text: Perceiving smell in waters, some say that it is a quality of waters.

children.text: pṛthivyāmeva taṃ vidyād apāṃ vāyoś ca saṃśrayāt
children.translated_text: One should know that smell to belong only to earth, because of the association of waters and air.
These seven great entities, because they rely on one another,
and because they are presided over by <s>puruṣa</s> and assisted by the unmanifest,
from <s>mahat</s> down to the <s>viśeṣas</s>, produce the egg.
It arose at a single time, like a bubble in water.
From the <s>viśeṣas</s> the egg came into being, great and lying in the waters.
The egg was enveloped externally by waters ten times as great.
Those waters were externally enclosed by fire ten times as great.
Fire was externally enclosed by air ten times as great.
Air, ten times as great, was externally enclosed by space.
Air was enveloped by <s>ākāśa</s>; space was enveloped by <s>bhūtādi</s>.
<s>Bhūtādi</s> was enveloped by <s>mahat</s>, and <s>mahat</s> by the unmanifest.
<s>Śarva</s> abides in the shell of the egg, and <s>Bhava</s> in the water, O well-vowed ones.
The blessed <s>Rudra</s> is remembered as being in fire, and <s>Ugra</s> again in air.
<s>Bhīma</s> abides in the midst of earth, and <s>Maheśvara</s> in <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.
In buddhi is the blessed <s>Īśa</s>, and everywhere is <s>Parameśvara</s>.
By these seven natural coverings the egg is enclosed.
Having enveloped one another, these eight <s>prakṛtis</s> stand.
At the time of reabsorption, these consume one another.
Thus, mutually produced, they support one another.
As support and supported, those transformations subsist among what is transformed.
<s>Maheśvara</s> is beyond the unmanifest; the egg is born from the unmanifest.
From the egg was born that very Lord, the <s>puruṣa</s>, shining like the sun.
In him the cause of the effect was accomplished solely by his own will.

children.text: sa vai śarīrī prathamaḥ sa vai puruṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: He indeed is the first embodied one; he is called the <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person).
From his left side was born <s>Viṣṇu</s>, honored by all the gods.
Together with the goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s>, that god came into being by the will of the supreme lord.
From his right side was born <s>Brahmā</s>, the teacher of the world, together with <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Within that egg are these worlds, this universe, this whole cosmos.
The moon and sun, along with the stars and planets, are there together with the wind.
The two realms, the world and the non-world, are in some way set within this egg.

children.text: yattu sṛṣṭau prasaṃkhyātaṃ mayā kālāntaraṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And what I have enumerated at creation is another span of time, O twice-born ones.
This span of time should be known as a day belonging to <s>Parameśvara</s>.
