His night should be known to be of the same length, entirely, for the supreme lord.

children.text: ahastasya tu yā sṛṣṭiḥ rātriś ca pralayaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The creation that belongs to his day is remembered, and the night is dissolution.

children.text: nāhastu vidyate tasya na rātririti dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: Yet understand that for him there is truly no day and no night.
This conventional usage is made out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.
The senses, the objects of the senses, and the five great elements

children.text: tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni buddhiś ca saha daivataiḥ
children.translated_text: and from them all beings, together with intellect and the deities,
all abide during the day of wise <s>Parameśvara</s>.
At the end of the day they dissolve; at the end of the night the universe comes forth.
When he remains in his own self, when the manifest is drawn back and transformation has been reabsorbed,
then <s>pradhāna</s> (primary matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> both remain in a state of similarity.
Endowed with <s>tamas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>rajas</s>, they stand in equilibrium.
The two had become intermixed, woven warp and woof into one another.
When the <s>guṇas</s> are in balance, that is to be known as dissolution; when they are unequal, it is called creation.

children.text: tile yathā bhavettailaṃ ghṛtaṃ payasi vā sthitam
children.translated_text: As oil exists in sesame seeds, or as ghee is present in milk,

children.text: tathā tamasi sattve ca rajasyanusṛtaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: so the world is contained in <s>tamas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, and <s>rajas</s>.

children.text: upāsya rajanīṃ kṛtsnāṃ parāṃ māheśvarīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having passed the whole night, the supreme power of <s>Maheśvara</s>,
arising at the opening of day, proceeded from the supreme <s>prakṛti</s>.
Then <s>Parameśvara</s>, by supreme yoga, set it in motion.

children.text: pradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ caiva praviśya sa maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Maheśvara</s> entered both <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>.
From <s>Maheśvara</s>, from the lord of the world, the three gods were born.
They are eternal, supreme, hidden, embodied, and the selves of all.

children.text: eta eva trayo devā eta eva trayo guṇāḥ
children.translated_text: These very three gods are the three <s>guṇas</s>.

children.text: eta eva trayo lokā eta eva trayo'gnayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: These very ones are the three worlds; these very ones are the three fires.
They depend on one another and are devoted to one another.
They function through one another and support one another.
They are mutually paired with one another and live by one another.

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ viyogo na hyeṣāṃ na tyajanti parasparam ||
children.translated_text: There is not even a moment's separation for them; they do not abandon one another.

children.text: īśvarastu paro devo viṣṇuś ca mahataḥ paraḥ
children.translated_text: But <s>Īśvara</s> is the supreme god; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is beyond <s>mahat</s>.

children.text: brahmā ca rajasā yuktaḥ sargādau hi pravartate ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Brahmā</s>, joined with <s>rajas</s>, acts at the beginning of creation.

children.text: paraḥ sa puruṣo jñeyaḥ prakṛtiḥ sā parā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: He should be known as the supreme <s>puruṣa</s>; she is remembered as the supreme <s>prakṛti</s>.

children.text: adhiṣṭhitā sā hi maheśvareṇa pravartate codyamane samantāt
children.translated_text: Presided over by <s>Maheśvara</s>, she begins to act, being impelled on every side.

children.text: anupravṛttastu mahāṃstadenāṃ cirasthiratvād viṣayaṃ śriyaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: And <s>mahat</s>, following her, itself makes her, through her long stability, the sphere of prosperity.
From the disequilibrium of the qualities of <s>pradhāna</s>, the time of creation begins.
It proceeds from that earlier principle, presided over by <s>Īśvara</s>, whose nature is both being and non-being.
First <s>Rudra</s>, perfected for effect and cause, came into being.
He was wise, unmatched in brilliance, unmanifest, and the illuminator.

children.text: sa vai śarīrī prathamaḥ sa vai puruṣa ucyate
children.translated_text: He indeed is the first embodied one; he is called the <s>puruṣa</s>.
And from him came blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, the four-faced <s>Prajāpati</s>.
He likewise came into being, perfected in effect and cause.
The one <s>Mahādeva</s> alone is thus established in three forms.
They are endowed with unsurpassed knowledge and lordly power,
and also with unsurpassed <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and dispassion.
Whatever they desire by mind is born for them from the unmanifest.
This is because the three <s>guṇas</s> have been brought under control and because, by nature, they depend on it.
As the four-faced one he is remembered in the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, and as the end-maker in the state of time.
The thousand-headed <s>puruṣa</s> is the three states of the self-born one.
In the state of <s>Brahmā</s> he creates the worlds; in the state of time he also contracts them.
In the state of <s>puruṣa</s> he is indifferent; these are the three states of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> has the appearance of the womb of the lotus; <s>Rudra</s> resembles the fire of time.
The lotus-eyed <s>puruṣa</s> is that form of the supreme self.

children.text: ekadhā sa dvidhā caiva tridhā ca bahudhā punaḥ
children.translated_text: As one, as two, as three, and again as many,
<s>Maheśvara</s> makes bodies and transforms them.
Through his own play they possess various forms, actions, appearances, and names.
<s>Maheśvara</s> makes bodies and transforms them.
Because he exists in the world in three forms, he is called three-stranded with the <s>guṇas</s>.
Because he is divided into four, he is proclaimed the fourfold manifestation.
Because this one obtains, because he takes, and because he consumes the objects of sense,
and because his state is constant, he is therefore explained as <s>ātman</s> (self).
He is a seer because he goes everywhere; he is embodied because he is its lord.
Because all sovereignty belongs to him, he is lord; because he enters all, he is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Because he possesses the state of <s>Bhagavān</s>, he is <s>Bhagavān</s>; because of purity he is remembered as <s>Śiva</s>.
Because he is most excellent he is supreme; because he protects, he is remembered as <s>Oṃ</s>.
Because he knows all, he is omniscient; because he has all knowledge and because he consists of all, he is the All.
Dividing himself threefold, he sets the three worlds in motion.

children.text: sṛjate grasate caiva rakṣate ca tribhiḥ svayam
children.translated_text: By means of the three, he himself creates, devours, and protects.
Because he is first, he is the first god; because he is unborn, he is remembered as unborn.

children.text: pāti yasmātprajāḥ sarvāḥ prajāpatir iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Because he protects all creatures, he is remembered as <s>Prajāpati</s>.
And among the gods he is the great god; therefore he is remembered as <s>Mahādeva</s>.
And because he pervades all the gods and because he cannot be brought under control, he is <s>Īśvara</s>.
Because of greatness he is remembered as <s>Brahmā</s>; because he has become beings, he is called <s>Bhūta</s>.
He is the knower of the field because of knowledge of the field; because of oneness he is remembered as the solitary one.

children.text: yasmātpuryāṃ sa śete ca tasmātpūruṣa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: And because he lies in the city, therefore he is called <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Because he is beginningless and prior, he is known as <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, the self-born.
He is called sacrifice because he is to be sacrificed to; he is a seer because of far-reaching vision.
He is called strider because of striding and because he is to be approached, and he is protector because of protecting.
He is known by the names <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, first-born, and <s>Agni</s>.
Gold was his womb, and he too was born from the womb of gold;
therefore his state as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is explained in this purāṇa.
As for the time even of <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>, who has passed, and of the self of the universe,
it cannot be counted even by hundreds of years.
The first parārdha of <s>Brahmā</s> is remembered as the time unfolded by calculation;
just so much other time remains for him, and at its end dissolution occurs.
Tens of millions upon tens of millions of thousands of days, indeed,

children.text: samatītāni kalpānāṃ tāvaccheṣāḥ pare tu ye
children.translated_text: which have passed as kalpas, just so many remain in the future;
but understand that this present kalpa is the <s>Vārāha</s>.
This present kalpa is now the first of them, O twice-born ones,
in which the fourteen <s>Manus</s>, beginning with <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>,

children.text: atītā vartamānāś ca bhaviṣyā ye ca vai punaḥ
children.translated_text: those past, present, and future as well,
have ruled this whole earth, with its seven continents and mountains.
For a full thousand yugas it is to be protected by the great lords,
together with creatures and austerity; listen to their details.
And through one <s>manvantara</s>, all the intervening periods

children.text: kathitāni bhaviṣyanti kalpaḥ kalpena caiva hi ||
children.translated_text: will have been described, and indeed one kalpa by another.
Past kalpas, with their later portions and their lineages,
and likewise those in the future, should be inferred by one who understands.
Waters first came into being when the surface of the earth had perished;
in that single, tranquil expanse of water, nothing at all was perceived.
Then, in that single ocean, when the immovable and moving world had perished,

children.text: tadā bhavati vai brahmā sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Brahmā</s> comes into being, thousand-eyed and thousand-footed,
a thousand-headed <s>Puruṣa</s>, golden-colored and beyond the senses.
<s>Brahmā</s>, called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, then slept upon the water.
But awakened by an increase of <s>sattva</s>, he looked upon the empty world,
and here they cite this verse concerning <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>:

children.text: āpo nārāś ca sūnava ityapāṃ nāma śuśrumaḥ
children.translated_text: We have heard that the waters are named nārāḥ, for they are the offspring of <s>Nara</s>;
because he made his own resting-place filled with them.
Because he lies in the waters, therefore he is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
After he had passed the nighttime period of four thousand yugas,
at the end of night he assumes the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, because he is the cause of creation.
But <s>Brahmā</s>, in that water, became wind and moved about,
like a firefly at night in the rainy season.

children.text: tatas tu salile tasmin vijñāyāntargatāṃ mahīm ||
children.translated_text: Then, recognizing the earth hidden within that water,
unbewildered, by inference, he again undertook the raising of the earth,
assuming another body at the beginnings of kalpas, as before.
Then the great-souled blessed lord contemplated a divine form;

children.text: salilenāplutāṃ bhūmiṃ dṛṣṭvā sa tu samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having seen the earth flooded by water on every side,
he thought, "What form shall I make, with which I might raise this earth?"
He entered a boar form suited to play in the water,
irresistible to all beings, made of speech, and known as <s>brahman</s>.
For the sake of raising the earth, he entered <s>Rasātala</s>.

children.text: adbhiḥ saṃchāditāṃ bhūmiṃ sa tāmāśu prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Approaching that earth, which was covered by waters,
that <s>Prajāpati</s> quickly lifted her up, and entered the waters as well.

children.text: sāmudrā vai samudreṣu nādeyāś ca nadīṣu ca
children.translated_text: The oceanic waters went into the oceans, and the riverine waters into the rivers;
when the earth was sunk in the floor of <s>Rasātala</s>, gone into a cavern of <s>Rasātala</s>,
the lord, for the welfare of the worlds, lifted up the earth with his tusk.
Then, having brought the earth to her own place, the supporter of the earth
set her down as before, after supporting her, that bearer of the earth.
Above that flood of water she stood like a great boat;
because she was equal to it and broad-bodied, the earth did not sink into dissolution.

children.text: tata utkṣipya tāṃ devo jagataḥ sthāpanecchayā ||
children.translated_text: Then the god, lifting her up with the desire to establish the world,
the lotus-eyed one set his mind on dividing the earth.

children.text: pṛthivīṃ ca samāṃ kṛtvā pṛthivyāṃ so'cinod girīn ||
children.translated_text: And having made the earth level, he piled up mountains on the earth.
In the former creation, when it was burning then with the fire of dissolution,
by that fire those wide-spreading mountains had been shattered.
In that single ocean, through cold, they were compacted by that wind;
wherever they had been deposited, there and there they became immovable.
Because of that immovability they are called acalas, and because of their joints, parvatas;
for because they were swallowed they are giris, and because they lie down they are heaps of stone.
Then, when they had been scattered among mountains by the tens of millions,
<s>Viśvakarman</s> divides them again and again at the beginnings of kalpas.
This earth, with its seas, seven continents, and mountains,
then he again fashioned the four worlds beginning with <s>Bhūr</s>.
After fashioning the worlds, he then created the creation of beings.
The blessed self-born <s>Brahmā</s>, desiring to create various creatures,
created a creation of that same form at the beginnings of kalpas, as before.
As he contemplated creation in that way, deliberately and with prior intelligence,

children.text: buddhyāś ca samakāle vai prādurbhūtas tamomayaḥ
children.translated_text: at the same time as intelligence there appeared something made of <s>tamas</s> (darkness):
<s>tamas</s>, <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>mahāmoha</s> (great delusion), <s>tāmisra</s>, and that called <s>andha</s>.
This five-branched ignorance appeared from the great-souled one.
As he meditated, the creation, possessed of self-conceit, was established in five forms.
It was enveloped by darkness, covered like a seed-sprout,
unmanifest outwardly and inwardly, motionless, and wholly without consciousness.
Because their intelligence is covered, and because their instruments are marked by suffering,
therefore those beings whose selves are enveloped are proclaimed to be the chief mountains and trees.
When <s>Brahmā</s> saw that primary creation in such a state, unable to accomplish its purpose,
his mind was not pleased; then he thought of another creation.
As he contemplated, the horizontal-streamed creation came into being.

children.text: tasmāt tiryakpravṛttaḥ sa tiryaksrotās tataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because it proceeded obliquely, it is therefore remembered as the horizontal-streamed one.
Those are known as animals and the like, O twice-born ones, grasping at the wrong path.
As he contemplated another creation, one characterized by <s>sattva</s> came into being.
The third was the upward-streamed one, and it was established upward.
Because it moves upward, it is therefore remembered as the upward-streamed creation.
They are full of happiness and delight, and are enveloped both outwardly and inwardly.
Yet they are luminous outwardly and inwardly, and are remembered as born from the upward stream.

children.text: te sattvasya ca yogena sṛṣṭāḥ sattvodbhavāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Because they were created through union with <s>sattva</s>, they are remembered as arising from <s>sattva</s>.
That third upward-streamed creation is remembered as the creation of the gods.
They are remembered as born from the upward stream, luminous outwardly and inwardly.
The wise should know them as upward-streamed, and they are remembered as contented in self.
When the upward-streamed gods had been created, the boon-giving lord,
<s>Brahmā</s>, became delighted; then he thought of another creation.
The lord, the powerful master, created another creation, one capable of accomplishing its purpose.
Then, as he contemplated with true contemplation at that time,
there appeared from the manifest the downward-streamed creation, capable of accomplishment.
Because they turned downward, therefore they are the downward-streamed beings.
They are mostly luminous, mixed with <s>tamas</s>, and dominated by <s>rajas</s>.
Therefore they are full of suffering and act again and again.

children.text: saṃvṛtā bahirantaś ca manuṣyāḥ sādhakāś ca te ||
children.translated_text: They are enveloped outwardly and inwardly; they are humans, and they are agents of accomplishment.
By marks such as the saving ones, they are arranged in eight divisions.
Those humans whose selves are perfected share the nature of <s>Gandharvas</s>.
Thus this fiery creation is proclaimed as the downward-streamed one.
The fifth creation is <s>anugraha</s> (grace), arranged in four ways:

children.text: viparyayeṇa śaktyā ca siddhyā tuṣṭyā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: by error, by capacity, by perfection, and likewise by contentment.
Among immobile beings there is error; among animal births there is capacity.
Humans are perfected in self, and among sages and gods it is complete.

children.text: ityeṣa prākṛtaḥ sargo vaikṛto navamaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus this is the <s>prākṛta</s> (natural) creation; the ninth is remembered as <s>vaikṛta</s> (modified).

children.text: bhūtādikānāṃ bhūtānāṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ sargaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The sixth creation is called that of the beings beginning with the elements.

children.text: nivṛttaṃ vartamānaṃ ca teṣāṃ jānanti vai punaḥ
children.translated_text: They know what has ceased and what is present among those beings, again.

children.text: bhūtādikānāṃ bhūtānāṃ saptamaḥ sarga eva ca ||
children.translated_text: And the seventh creation is that of the beings beginning with the elements.
They are all appropriators, and again they delight in distribution.

children.text: svādanāś cāpyaśīlāś ca jñeyā bhūtādikāś ca te ||
children.translated_text: They are tasters and also not virtuous; these should be known as the beings beginning with the elements.
The element-origin is established through error and through incapacity.

children.text: prathamo mahataḥ sargo vijñeyo brahmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first creation of <s>mahat</s> should be known as belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>.
The second is the creation of the subtle elements; it is called the elemental creation.
The third, the modified creation, is remembered as the creation of the senses.
Thus this natural creation arose deliberately, with prior intelligence.

children.text: mukhyasargaścaturthaś ca mukhyā vai sthāvarāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fourth is the primary creation; the chief beings are remembered as the immobile ones.

children.text: tato'rvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the creation of the downward-streamed beings is the seventh, the human one.
The eighth is the creation of grace, and it is both sāttvic and tāmasic.

children.text: pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāstu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: These five creations are modified, while three are remembered as natural.
The ninth is remembered as the <s>Kaumāra</s> creation, both natural and modified.
The three natural creations are remembered as not preceded by deliberate intelligence.
But six creations of <s>Brahmā</s> proceed with prior intelligence.
Now understand the creation of extensive grace as it is being recounted.
It is established in four ways, completely among all beings.

children.text: ityete prākṛtāścaiva vaikṛtāś ca nava smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Thus these nine are remembered as natural and modified creations.

children.text: parasparānuraktāś ca kāraṇaiś ca budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise remember them as mutually connected and as having causes.

children.text: agre sasarja vai brahmā mānasānātmanaḥ samān
children.translated_text: At first <s>Brahmā</s> created mind-born sons like himself.
<s>Ṛbhu</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, these two, were upward-flowing in seed.
They had arisen before those others in ancient times, ancestors of all.
In the past eighth <s>kalpa</s>, they were ancient witnesses of the world.

children.text: tau vārāhe tu bhūrloke tejaḥ saṃkṣipya dhiṣṭhitau
children.translated_text: In the <s>Vārāha</s> age, on the earth-world, the two abided after contracting their radiance.
Both of them were devoted to the work of liberation, placing the self upon the self.

children.text: prajāṃ dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca tyaktvā vairāgyamāsthitau
children.translated_text: Having abandoned offspring, <s>dharma</s>, and desire, they took up detachment.
Because he is here just as he was when born, he is called <s>Kumāra</s> in this world.
Therefore his name is here proclaimed as <s>Sanatkumāra</s>.

children.text: sanandaṃ sanakaṃ caiva vidvāṃsaṃ ca sanātanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sananda</s>, <s>Sanaka</s>, and the learned <s>Sanātana</s>, too,
turned away through knowledge, those beings of great vigor.
They were awakened, yet did not engage in multiplicity; they were yogins who did not proceed.
Without creating the creation of progeny, they returned again to dissolution.
Then, when those had passed away, thereafter <s>Brahmā</s> created other accomplished sons,
mind-born ones, again presiding over their stations,
by whom this earth was upheld until the state of the dissolution of beings.
Water, fire, earth, wind, atmosphere, and heaven likewise,
and the oceans and rivers, as well as mountains, forests, and trees,
and likewise the selves of herbs, of creepers, trees, and shrubs,
creepers, wood, <s>kalā</s>s, <s>muhūrta</s>s, twilight, night, and days,

children.text: ardhamāsāṃś ca māsāṃś ca ayanābdayugāni ca
children.translated_text: half-months and months, courses of the sun, years, and ages:
all these were presiders over stations, and they are remembered as called <s>Sthāna</s>.
Listen as I tell of those great gods and sages.
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>: he created these nine mind-born sons.

children.text: nava brahmāṇa ityete purāṇe niścayaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These nine <s>Brahmā</s>s are held as certain in the <s>Purāṇa</s>.
For all of them, whose nature was <s>Brahman</s> and who spoke of <s>Brahman</s>,
the lotus-born one assigned stations as before.
Then he created <s>saṃkalpa</s> (intention) and also <s>dharma</s> (normative order), which brings happiness.
From resolve the god <s>Maheśvara</s> created <s>dharma</s>,
and from <s>saṃkalpa</s> the grandfather of all worlds created <s>saṃkalpa</s> itself.

children.text: mānasaś ca rucirnāma vijajñe brahmaṇaḥ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the mind-born one named <s>Ruci</s> was born from <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord.
From his breath <s>Brahmā</s> created <s>Dakṣa</s>, and from his eyes <s>Marīci</s>.
<s>Bhṛgu</s>, the seer, was born from the heart of the water-born one.
From his head came <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and from his ears he likewise created <s>Atri</s>.
He created <s>Pulastya</s> from the <s>udāna</s> breath, and again <s>Pulaha</s> from the <s>vyāna</s> breath.
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> was born from the <s>samāna</s> breath, and he fashioned <s>Kratu</s> from the <s>apāna</s> breath.

children.text: ityete brahmaṇaḥ putrā divyā ekādaśā smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These are remembered as the eleven divine sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: dharmādayaḥ prathamajāḥ sarve te brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> and the others, the first-born, were all sons of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others were those nine created speakers of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: gṛhamedhinaḥ purāṇās te dharmas taiḥ sampravartitaḥ
children.translated_text: They were ancient householders; through them <s>dharma</s> was set in motion.

children.text: teṣāṃ dvādaśa te vaṃśā divyā devaguṇānvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Their twelve lineages were divine and endowed with the qualities of gods,
active in rites, rich in progeny, and adorned by great seers.
<s>Ṛbhu</s> and <s>Sanatkumāra</s>: these two had their seed drawn upward.
They were born earlier, higher than those others, the ancestors of all.
In the past eighth <s>kalpa</s>, those ancient two, witnesses of the world,
shone in the world, established there with their radiance restrained.
Both were devoted to yogic action, having placed the self in the self.

children.text: prajāṃ dharmaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca tyaktvā vairāgyamāsthitau
children.translated_text: Having abandoned progeny, <s>dharma</s>, and desire, they stood in detachment.

children.text: yathotpannaḥ sa eveha kumāraḥ sa ihocyate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>kumāra</s> who was born in just this way is so called here.
Therefore the name <s>Sanatkumāra</s> was established for him here.
Then, as he meditated, mind-born creatures were born from him.
Together with those effects produced from his body and with their causes,
<s>kṣetrajña</s>s (knowers of the field) came forth from the limbs of that wise one.
Then, wishing to create the fourfold group of gods, asuras, ancestors, and humans,
he joined these waters with his own self.
Then, as he was engaged in yoga, a creation arose from darkness alone,
as <s>Prajāpati</s> meditated upon creation with effort.
Then first from his lower body the asuras were born as sons.

children.text: asuḥ prāṇaḥ smṛto viprās tajjanmānas tato'surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Asu</s> is remembered as breath, O brahmins; because they were born from that, they were asuras.

children.text: yayā sṛṣṭāsurāḥ sarve tāṃ tanuṃ sa vyapohata
children.translated_text: The body by which all the asuras were created he cast off.

children.text: sāpaviddhā tanus tena sadyo rātrir ajāyata ||
children.translated_text: That body, cast off by him, immediately became night.
Because it was full of darkness, night became the regulator.
Since creatures are covered by darkness at night, they sleep then.
After creating the asuras, he then took another body,
unmanifest and abundant in <s>sattva</s> (clarity), and he honored that body.

children.text: tatastāṃ yuñjatas tasya priyam āsīt prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: As he joined himself to it, it became dear to <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Then, from his mouth, as he shone, the deities came forth.
Because they were born as he shone, therefore they are called devas.

children.text: dhāturdiviti yaḥ proktaḥ krīḍāyāṃ sa vibhāvyate ||
children.translated_text: The root <s>div</s>, which is stated in the sense of play, is understood in this way.

children.text: yasmāttasya tu dīvyanto jajñire tena devatāḥ
children.translated_text: Because they were born while he was playing, therefore they are deities.
Having created the gods, the lord of gods then assumed another body.
That body, abandoned by him, immediately became day.
Therefore the deities worship day, which is joined with <s>dharma</s>.
Then he conceived another body, one whose nature was solely <s>sattva</s>.
As the lord thought of those sons in a fatherly way,
the ancestors came into being from the two side-portions between night and day.

children.text: tasmātte pitaro devāḥ pitṛtvaṃ tena teṣu tat ||
children.translated_text: Therefore those ancestors are gods; for that reason fatherhood belongs to them.

children.text: yayā sṛṣṭāstu pitarastanuṃ tāṃ sa vyapohata
children.translated_text: The body by which the ancestors had been created he cast off.
That body, cast off by him, immediately became twilight.
Since day belongs to the deities, while night is remembered as asuric,

children.text: tayormadhye tu paitrī yā tanuḥ sā tu garīyasī ||
children.translated_text: the ancestral body that lies between the two is the weightier one.

children.text: tasmāddevā surāḥ sarve ṛṣayo mānavās tathā
children.translated_text: Therefore all gods and asuras, sages and humans too,
gladly worship the middle body between night and day.

children.text: tato hyanyāṃ punarbrahmā tanuṃ vai samagṛhṇata
children.translated_text: Then again <s>Brahmā</s> took another body.
In that body, whose nature was solely <s>rajas</s> (passion), the lord created by mind.
Then he created mind-born sons who were fond of <s>rajas</s>.
From him, then, humans, endowed with mind, were born as his sons.

children.text: sṛṣṭvā punaḥ prajāścāpi svāṃ tanuṃ tām apohata
children.translated_text: Having again created creatures, he cast off that body of his own.
That body, cast off by him, immediately became moonlight.
For beings become delighted when moonlight arises.
Thus these bodies were cast off by that great-souled one.

children.text: sadyo rātryahanī caiva saṃdhyā jyotsnā ca jajñire
children.translated_text: At once night and day, twilight and moonlight were born.
Moonlight, twilight, and day are the three whose nature is solely <s>sattva</s> (clarity).
Night, whose nature is solely <s>tamas</s> (darkness), is therefore indeed night in essence.

children.text: tasmāddevā divātanvā tuṣṭyā sṛṣṭā mukhāttu vai ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the gods, created from his mouth with the body of day, were brought forth through satisfaction.

children.text: yasmātteṣāṃ divā janma balinastena vai divā
children.translated_text: Because their birth was in the day, they are strong by day.
With the body by which the lord created the asuras at night from his lower part,

children.text: prāṇebhyo niśijanmāno balino niśi tena te
children.translated_text: they were born from the vital breaths at night; therefore they are strong at night.
These very things become the causal signs for future gods together with the asuras,
and for the ancestors and humans, in past and future times,
through all <s>manvantara</s>s (ages of Manu).

children.text: jyotsnā rātryahanī saṃdhyā catvāryaṃbhāṃsi tāni vai
children.translated_text: Moonlight, night, day, and twilight are those four <s>ambhāṃsi</s> (luminous waters).
Because they shine, therefore this word <s>ambhāṃsi</s> is used by the wise.
The root <s>bhā</s> is stated in the sense of shining; and then again <s>Prajāpati</s>,
having created those <s>ambhāṃsi</s>, the gods, humans, and dānavas,
and the ancestors as well, again created many kinds with his own body.

children.text: tāmutsṛjya tanuṃ jyotsnāṃ tato'nyāṃ prāpya sa prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Abandoning that moonlight body, the lord then obtained another
form, mostly consisting of <s>tamas</s> and <s>rajas</s>, and again honored it.
Then in the darkness the lord created other beings, afflicted by hunger.
Created by him, they were hunger-bodied and eager to seize those waters.
Those among them who said, 'We shall protect these waters,'

children.text: rākṣasā nāma te yasmāt kṣudhāviṣṭā niśācarāḥ
children.translated_text: are called <s>rākṣasa</s>s, because they are hunger-afflicted wanderers of the night.
Those who said to one another, delighted, 'We shall consume the waters,'

children.text: tena te karmaṇā yakṣā guhyakā gūḍhakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: by that action became <s>yakṣa</s>s, <s>guhyaka</s>s through a hidden act.
The root <s>rakṣ</s> is explained in the sense of protection also.

children.text: evaṃ ca yakṣatir dhātur bhakṣaṇe sa nirucyate
children.translated_text: In the same way the root <s>yakṣ</s> is defined in the sense of eating.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā hyapriyeṇāsya keśāḥ śīrṇāstu dhīmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him with displeasure, the wise one's hairs fell from his head.

children.text: te śīrṇāścotthitā hyūrdhvaṃ te caivārurudhuḥ prabhum
children.translated_text: Those fallen hairs rose upward and cried out to the lord.
Because the hairs, fallen from his head, were deprived and creeping downward,
the hairs, having the nature of <s>vyāla</s>s, are remembered as <s>vāla</s>s; from their defect they are remembered as <s>ahi</s>s.
Because they fell they are <s>pannaga</s>s, and because they creep downward they are <s>sarpa</s>s.
That terrible being born from his anger, fire in its womb,
entered the serpents that had arisen together with him, taking the nature of poison.
Having created the serpents, then, angered, he fashioned beings whose nature was anger.
They were fierce, tawny in color, beings that ate flesh.
Because they were beings they are remembered as <s>bhūta</s>s, and because they ate flesh as <s>piśāca</s>s.
When, as he sang pleasantly, the <s>gandharva</s>s were born from him,
this root <s>dhay</s> is recited in the sense of drinking.

children.text: dhayanto jajñire vācaṃ gandharvāstena te smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They were born drinking speech; therefore they are remembered as <s>gandharva</s>s.
When these eight divine classes had been created, the lord,
then, of his own will, created other birds by his vitality.

children.text: svacchandataḥ svacchandāṃsi vayasā ca vayāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: Of their own will they were free-moving, and through vitality they were birds.
Having created the animals, the lord of gods also created the flocks of birds.
From his mouth he created goats, and from his chest he created sheep.
Then <s>Brahmā</s> produced cows from his belly and from his two sides.

children.text: padbhyāṃ cāśvān samātaṅgān rāsabhān āvayān mṛgān
children.translated_text: From his feet he made horses, elephants, donkeys, wild sheep, and deer,
camels, mules, and likewise other species.
Herbs bearing fruit and roots were born from his body hairs.
Having thus created animals and plants, the lord yoked them to the sacrifice.
The cow, goat, man, ram, horse, mule, and donkey:
these they call domestic animals; now learn the wild ones.
Beasts of prey, cloven-hoofed animals, elephants, monkeys, and birds as the fifth,
aquatic animals as the sixth, and reptiles as the seventh.

children.text: mahiṣā gavayākṣāś ca plavaṃgāḥ śarabhā vṛkāḥ
children.translated_text: Buffaloes, gavayas, bears, leaping animals, śarabhas, and wolves,
with the lion as the seventh among them, are remembered as wild animals.
The gāyatra, the ṛc, the trivṛt, and the rathantara <s>sāman</s>,

children.text: agniṣṭomaṃ ca yajñānāṃ nirmame prathamān mukhāt ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>agniṣṭoma</s> among sacrifices, he first fashioned from his eastern mouth.
The <s>yajus</s> formulas, the <s>traiṣṭubha</s> meter, and the fifteenfold <s>stoma</s>,
as well as the <s>bṛhat-sāman</s> and the <s>ukthya</s>, he created from his southern mouth.
The <s>sāman</s>s, the <s>jagatī</s> meter, and the seventeenfold <s>stoma</s>,
the <s>vairūpa</s> and the <s>atirātra</s>, he created from his western mouth.
The twenty-onefold <s>stoma</s>, the <s>atharvan</s>, and the <s>āptoryāma</s>,
together with the <s>anuṣṭubh</s> and the <s>savairāja</s>, he created from his northern mouth.
Lightning, thunderbolts, clouds, red lights, and rainbows,
and radiant powers the blessed lord created at the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>.
High and low beings were born from his limbs.
As <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, was creating the creation of beings,
having first created the fourfold group: gods, asuras, humans, and ancestors,

children.text: tato 'sṛjat sa bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: he then created beings both stationary and moving.
<s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>piśāca</s>s, <s>gandharva</s>s, and also hosts of <s>apsaras</s>es,
humans, <s>kinnara</s>s, <s>rākṣasa</s>s, birds, cattle, deer, and serpents,

children.text: avyayaṃ ca vyayaṃ cāpi yadidaṃ sthāṇujaṅgamam
children.translated_text: the imperishable and the perishable, whatever here is fixed or moving:

children.text: teṣāṃ vai yāni karmāṇi prāksṛṣṭyāṃ pratipedire ||
children.translated_text: whatever actions they had undertaken in the former creation,
those very actions they assume again and again when they are created.
Violent and nonviolent, gentle and cruel, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, truth and untruth:
being formed by that, they resort to it; therefore each one's own condition is pleasing to him.
When the great elements, the objects of the senses, and embodied forms had been created,

children.text: viniyogaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ dhātaiva vyadadhāt svayam
children.translated_text: the Creator himself arranged the assignment of beings.
Some wise men call action human effort,
while others, O brahmins, call it fate; those who reflect on beings call it nature.
Human effort, action, fate, and the natural mode of fruition:

children.text: na caikaṃ na pṛthagbhāvamadhikaṃ na tato viduḥ
children.translated_text: they know these as neither one, nor separate in nature, nor superior to one another.

children.text: etadevaṃ ca naikaṃ ca nāmabhedena nāpyubhe ||
children.translated_text: Thus this is not a single thing; nor, because of difference in name, is it two.
Those established in action speak of inequality; those established in <s>sattva</s> see with equal vision.

children.text: nāma rūpaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ kṛtānāṃ ca prapañcanam ||
children.translated_text: The name and form of beings, and the elaboration of those that had been made,
the great lord fashioned at the beginning from the sounds of the <s>Veda</s> alone.

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ nāmadheyāni yāś ca vedeṣu vṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The names of the seers, and the modes of conduct that are in the <s>Veda</s>,
the unborn one gives those very things to them when they are born at the end of the night.
Such are the creations of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is from the unmanifest;
at the end of the night they appear, relying on mental accomplishment.
When beings of this kind, both stationary and moving, had been created,

children.text: yadāsya tāḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭā na vyavardhanta sattamāḥ
children.translated_text: and when those creatures of his, once created, did not increase, O best ones,
<s>Brahmā</s>, covered only by darkness, was then afflicted with grief.
Then he formed an understanding that would lead to a determination of the matter.
Then within himself he saw the mere darkness as a restraining power,
functioning by its own nature after abandoning <s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s>.

children.text: tataḥ sa tena duḥkhena duḥkhaṃ cakre jagatpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, because of that sorrow, the lord of the world made sorrow.
Afterward he drove away darkness, and <s>rajas</s> and <s>sattva</s> covered the darkness.
When that darkness had been driven back, a pair came into being.
<s>Adharma</s> was born from darkness; <s>Hiṃsā</s> was born from grief.
Then, when that pair of dreadful nature had arisen,

children.text: gatāsur bhagavān āsīt prītiś cainam aśiśriyat
children.translated_text: the blessed lord became bereft of life-breath, and delight took hold of him.

children.text: svāṃ tanuṃ sa tato brahmā tāmapohata bhāsvarām ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Brahmā</s> cast off that radiant body of his own.
Dividing his own body in two, with one half he became male,

children.text: ardhena nārī sā tasya śatarūpā vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: and with the other half a woman was born from him; she was <s>Śatarūpā</s>.
The lord created her, <s>Prakṛti</s>, the bearer of beings, out of desire.

children.text: sā divaṃ pṛthivīṃ caiva mahimnā vyāpyadhiṣṭhitā ||
children.translated_text: By her greatness she pervaded and stood over heaven and earth.

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ sā tanuḥ pūrvā divamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: That former body of <s>Brahmā</s> stands covering heaven.
But the woman, <s>Śatarūpā</s>, who was born as he created from half of himself,

children.text: sā devī niyutaṃ taptvā tapaḥ paramaduścaram
children.translated_text: that goddess, after performing supremely difficult austerity for a myriad years,
obtained as her husband the man of blazing fame.

children.text: sa vai svāyaṃbhuvaḥ pūrvaṃ puruṣo manurucyate
children.translated_text: That man of old is called <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s>.
A <s>manvantara</s> of his is here said to be seventy yugas.

children.text: lebhe sa puruṣaḥ patnīṃ śatarūpām ayonijām
children.translated_text: That man obtained as his wife the womb-unborn <s>Śatarūpā</s>.

children.text: tayā sārdhaṃ sa ramate tasmātsā ratirucyate ||
children.translated_text: He delights together with her; therefore she is called <s>Rati</s>.
The first union, consisting in sexual conjunction, occurred at the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>.

children.text: virājam asṛjad brahmā so'bhavat puruṣo virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> created <s>Virāj</s>; that man became <s>Virāṭ</s>.

children.text: samrāṭ ca śatarūpā vai vairājaḥ sa manuḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And <s>Śatarūpā</s> was <s>Samrāṭ</s>; that <s>Manu</s> is remembered as <s>Vairāja</s>.

children.text: sa vairājaḥ prajāsargaṃ sasarja puruṣo manuḥ ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Vairāja</s>, the man <s>Manu</s>, created the creation of creatures.
From the heroic <s>Vairāja</s> man, <s>Śatarūpā</s> was born.
Two sons, <s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>, were honored by the world,

children.text: kanye dve ca mahābhāge yābhyāṃ jātā imāḥ prajāḥ
children.translated_text: and two highly fortunate daughters, from whom these creatures were born.

children.text: devī nāma tathākūtiḥ prasūtiścaiva te ubhe ||
children.translated_text: Those two goddesses were named <s>Ākūti</s> and <s>Prasūti</s>.

children.text: svāyaṃbhuvaḥ prasūtiṃ tu dakṣāya pradadau prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: The lord <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s> gave <s>Prasūti</s> to <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: prāṇo dakṣa iti jñeyaḥ saṃkalpo manurucyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> should be known as <s>Dakṣa</s>; resolve is called <s>Manu</s>.
Then he gave <s>Ākūti</s> to the <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Ruci</s>.

children.text: ākūtyāṃ mithunaṃ jajñe mānasasya ruceḥ śubham ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Ākūti</s> a fair pair was born to the mind-born <s>Ruci</s>.

children.text: yajñaś ca dakṣiṇā caiva yamalau saṃbabhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yajña</s> and <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> were born as twins.

children.text: yajñasya dakṣiṇāyāṃ tu putrā dvādaśa jajñire ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Yajña</s>, through <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>, twelve sons were born.
They were known as the <s>Yāmas</s>, gods in the age of <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>.

children.text: etasya putrā yajñasya tasmādyāmāś ca te smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These were the sons of <s>Yajña</s>; therefore they are remembered as <s>Yāmas</s>.

children.text: ajitaścaiva śukraś ca gaṇau dvau brahmaṇā kṛtau
children.translated_text: <s>Ajita</s> and <s>Śukra</s> were the two groups made by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: yāmāḥ pūrvaṃ prajātā ye te 'bhavaṃstu divaukasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Yāmas</s> who had been born before became dwellers in heaven.
But in <s>Prasūti</s>, the daughter of <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>, mothers of the world were born.
In her the lord <s>Dakṣa</s> begot twenty-four daughters.
All those highly fortunate women were all lotus-eyed.

children.text: bhogavatyaś ca tāḥ sarvāḥ sarvāstā yogamātaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: All of them were possessors of enjoyment, and all of them were mothers of yoga.

children.text: sarvāś ca brahmavādinyaḥ sarvā viśvasya mātaraḥ
children.translated_text: All were speakers of <s>Brahman</s>; all were mothers of the universe.
<s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, and <s>Kriyā</s>,
<s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Vapuḥ</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Siddhi</s>, and <s>Kīrti</s>: these thirteen
the lord <s>Dharma</s> accepted as wives, daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>.
These wives of his had been ordained by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>.
Apart from them, for the younger one, there were eleven lotus-eyed women:

children.text: satī khyātyatha saṃbhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Satī</s>, then <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Saṃbhūti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s>,

children.text: saṃnatiścānasūyā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Saṃnati</s>, <s>Anasūyā</s>, <s>Ūrjā</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, and <s>Svadhā</s>.
Other great seers likewise accepted them.

children.text: rudro bhṛgur marīciś ca aṅgirāḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Aṅgirāḥ</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the ancestors, and <s>Agni</s> as well:

children.text: satīṃ bhavāya prāyacchat khyātiṃ ca bhṛgave tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he gave <s>Satī</s> to <s>Bhava</s>, and then <s>Khyāti</s> to <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
He gave <s>Saṃbhūti</s> to <s>Marīci</s>, and <s>Smṛti</s> to <s>Aṅgiras</s>;

children.text: prītiṃ caiva pulastyāya kṣamāṃ vai pulahāya ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Prīti</s> to <s>Pulastya</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s> to <s>Pulaha</s>.
To <s>Kratu</s> he gave her named <s>Saṃnati</s>, and likewise <s>Anasūyā</s> to <s>Atri</s>;
he gave <s>Ūrjā</s> to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and he also gave <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>.
And <s>Svadhā</s> he gave to the <s>Pitṛ</s>s. Now learn their offspring.
All these highly blessed women remain established, continuing through progeny,
in all the <s>manvantara</s>s, until the dissolution of beings.

children.text: śraddhā kāmaṃ vijajñe vai darpo lakṣmīsutaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s> bore <s>Kāma</s>; <s>Darpa</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

children.text: dhṛtyāstu niyamaḥ putrastuṣṭyāḥ saṃtoṣa eva ca
children.translated_text: From <s>Dhṛti</s> came the son <s>Niyama</s>, and from <s>Tuṣṭi</s> came <s>Saṃtoṣa</s>.

children.text: puṣṭyā lobhaḥ sutaścāpi medhāputraḥ śrutas tathā ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Puṣṭi</s> too came the son <s>Lobha</s>; and <s>Śruta</s> was the son of <s>Medhā</s>.
In <s>Kriyā</s> there was a son, <s>Daṇḍa</s>, and <s>Samaya</s> as well.
In <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Bodha</s> was the son; likewise <s>Pramāda</s> also arose.

children.text: lajjāyāṃ vinayaḥ putro vyavasāyo vasoḥ sutaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Vinaya</s> was the son; <s>Vyavasāya</s> was the son of <s>Vasu</s>.
<s>Kṣema</s> was the son of <s>Śānti</s>, and <s>Sukha</s> was born from <s>Siddhi</s>.
<s>Yaśas</s> too was the son of <s>Kīrti</s>; these are the sons of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: kāmasya harṣaḥ putro vai devyāṃ prītyāṃ vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Harṣa</s> was the son of <s>Kāma</s>, born in the goddess <s>Prīti</s>.

children.text: ityeṣa vai sutodarkaḥ sargo dharmasya kīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus has been proclaimed this creation of <s>Dharma</s>, whose outcome is sons.

children.text: jajñe hiṃsā tvadharmādvai nikṛtiṃ cānṛtaṃ sutam ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Adharma</s> there were born <s>Hiṃsā</s>, and <s>Nikṛti</s>, and <s>Anṛta</s> as a son.

children.text: nikṛtyāṃ tu dvayaṃ jajñe bhayaṃ naraka eva ca
children.translated_text: In <s>Nikṛti</s> a pair was born: <s>Bhaya</s> and <s>Naraka</s>.
And <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Vedanā</s> also were a second pair for these two.

children.text: bhūyo jajñe'tha vai māyā mṛtyuṃ bhūtāpahāriṇam
children.translated_text: Then again <s>Māyā</s> bore <s>Mṛtyu</s>, the remover of beings.

children.text: vedanāyāḥ sutaścāpi duḥkhaṃ jajñe ca rauravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And from <s>Vedanā</s> a son was born, <s>Duḥkha</s>; <s>Raurava</s> too was born.
From <s>Mṛtyu</s> were born disease, old age, grief, anger, and envy.
These sons, all marked by <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), have suffering as their final result.

children.text: naiṣāṃ bhāryāstu putrāś ca sarve hyete parigrahāḥ
children.translated_text: They have no wives and no sons; all these are grasping attachments.
Thus this <s>tāmasa</s> (dark) creation arose, a regulator of <s>dharma</s>.
Ordered by <s>Brahmā</s>, 'Create creatures,' <s>Nīlalohita</s>
meditated on his wife <s>Satī</s> and fashioned beings born from himself.
They were neither greater nor lesser, mind-born beings equal to himself.
The hide-clad one created a thousand thousands of them,
all equal to himself in form, splendor, strength, and learning:
tawny ones, with quivers, with matted topknots, and reddish ones;
distinguished ones, yellow-haired ones, glance-destroying ones, and skull-bearing ones;
great-formed and misshapen ones, all-formed and self-formed ones;
chariot-warriors, shield-bearers, armored ones, and those with protecting troops;
those with hundreds of thousands of arms, divine beings moving on earth and through the midspace;
large-headed, eight-fanged, double-tongued, and three-eyed;
eaters of food and eaters of flesh, drinkers of clarified butter and also drinkers of soma;
bountiful ones, those with great skulls, blue-throated ones, and those whose seed is drawn upward;
eaters of oblations, knowers of sacred duty, righteous ones, and those furnished with sacrificial grass;
sitting and running, made of the five elements, by the thousands;
teachers and students, reciters and practitioners of yoga;
smoky ones, blazing ones, river-bearing ones, and exceedingly radiant ones;
old ones, intelligent ones, most devoted to <s>Brahman</s>, and auspicious to behold;
blue-necked, thousand-eyed, and all of them patient and forgiving;
invisible to all beings, great yogins of great power;
wandering, charging, and leaping by the thousands.
He created these tireless <s>Rudra</s>s, the best of gods.
Seeing them, <s>Brahmā</s> said to him, 'Do not create such creatures.

children.text: sraṣṭavyā nātmanastulyāḥ prajā deva namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: Creatures equal to yourself are not to be created, O god. Reverence to you.

children.text: anyāḥ sṛja tvaṃ bhadraṃ te prajā vai mṛtyusaṃyutāḥ
children.translated_text: Create others; welfare to you: creatures joined with death.
For creatures who have understood death will not undertake actions.'
Addressed in this way, he said to him, 'I will not create

children.text: prajāḥ srakṣyāmi bhadraṃ te sthito 'haṃ tvaṃ sṛja prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: creatures endowed with death and old age. Welfare to you. I stand firm; you create creatures.

children.text: ete ye vai mayā sṛṣṭā virūpā nīlalohitāḥ
children.translated_text: These beings that I have created, misshapen and blue-red,

children.text: sahasrāṇāṃ sahasraṃ tu ātmano niḥsṛtāḥ prajāḥ ||
children.translated_text: a thousand thousands of creatures, have issued from myself.

children.text: ete devā bhaviṣyanti rudrā nāma mahābalāḥ
children.translated_text: These will become gods, mighty ones named <s>Rudra</s>s,
residing on earth, in the midspace, and in the directions.
According to the ritualists, they will be the <s>Śatarudra</s>s, equal in self.
They will have shares in sacrifices together with all the hosts of gods.
Whatever gods will exist here in the <s>manvantara</s>s in their various divisions,

children.text: sārdhaṃ tair ījyamānās te sthāsyantīha ā yugakṣayāt ||
children.translated_text: worshiped together with them, these will remain here until the end of the age.'
When <s>Brahmā</s> had been addressed in this way by wise <s>Mahādeva</s>,
<s>Prajāpati</s>, bowing down and rejoicing, replied:

children.text: evaṃ bhavatu bhadraṃ te yathā te vyāhṛtaṃ vibho
children.translated_text: 'So be it; welfare to you, just as you have declared, O mighty lord.'
When <s>Brahmā</s> had given his assent, everything indeed became just so.

children.text: tataḥ prabhṛti deveśo na cāsūyata vai prajāḥ
children.translated_text: From then onward the lord of gods did not create creatures,
but stood with his seed drawn upward as <s>Sthāṇu</s>, until the dissolution of beings.
Because he said, 'I stand,' therefore he is remembered as <s>Sthāṇu</s>.
This god is <s>Mahādeva</s>, the <s>Puruṣa</s> with radiance equal to the sun,
with a body half woman and half man, blazing with splendor like fire.

children.text: svecchayāsau dvidhābhūtaḥ pṛthak strī puruṣaḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: By his own will he became twofold: separately woman, and separately man.
He is that <s>Parameśvara</s>, established with an elevenfold portion.
There, that highly blessed lady who formed half the body of <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: prāguktā tu mahādevī strī saiveha satī hyabhūt
children.translated_text: the great goddess mentioned before, that very female here became <s>Satī</s>.
Long ago, for the welfare of the worlds, the goddess was worshiped by <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: kāryārthaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ tasyāḥ śuklaṃ vāmaṃ tathāsitam
children.translated_text: For the sake of that task, her right side was white and her left side likewise black;
"Divide yourself," she was told by the god <s>Śaṃbhu</s>.

children.text: sā tathoktā dvidhābhūtā śuklā kṛṣṇā ca vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: When thus addressed, she became twofold, white and black, O brahmins.

children.text: tasyā nāmāni vakṣyāmi śṛṇvantu ca samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell her names; listen with concentrated minds.

children.text: svāhā svadhā mahāvidyā medhā lakṣmīḥ sarasvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>, <s>Mahāvidyā</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Satī</s>, <s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, <s>Icchāśakti</s>, and she whose nature is action.
<s>Aparṇā</s>, <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, and likewise <s>Ekapāṭalā</s>,
<s>Umā</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Kalyāṇī</s>, and <s>Ekamātṛkā</s>;

children.text: khyātiḥ prajñā mahābhāgā loke gaurīti viśrutā
children.translated_text: <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, the greatly fortunate one, renowned in the world as <s>Gaurī</s>;
<s>Gaṇāmbikā</s>, <s>Mahādevī</s>, <s>Nandinī</s>, and <s>Jātavedasī</s>.
Now, although she has one form, because of the conception of separate bodies,
she is <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Varadā</s>, holy, purifying, and renowned in the world.

children.text: ājñā āveśanī kṛṣṇā tāmasī sāttvikī śivā
children.translated_text: She is command, possession, black, dark, bright, and auspicious;
<s>Prakṛti</s>, transformed, terrible, <s>Durgā</s>, gracious, and overwhelming.
She is <s>Kālarātrī</s>, <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, and mistress of beings.
At the division at the end of the <s>Dvāpara</s> age these are her names, O well-vowed ones:

children.text: gautamī kauśikī cāryā caṇḍī kātyāyanī satī
children.translated_text: <s>Gautamī</s>, <s>Kauśikī</s>, noble <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, and <s>Satī</s>;
<s>Kumārī</s>, <s>Yādavī</s>, the goddess, <s>Varadā</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇapiṅgalā</s>;
<s>Barhidhvajā</s>, bearer of the trident, supreme, and vowed to brahmacarya;
sister of <s>Mahendra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>, holding a single spear;
<s>Aparājitā</s>, many-armed, bold, and riding a lion;
slayer of the daityas beginning with <s>Śumbha</s>, and great crusher of <s>Mahiṣa</s>.
<s>Amoghā</s>, dwelling in the <s>Vindhya</s>, powerful, and leader of the gaṇas:
these, in order, are the transformations of the goddess's names.
I have properly declared them as names of <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, and they grant their fruits.

children.text: ye paṭhanti narāsteṣāṃ vidyate na ca pātakam ||
children.translated_text: For those people who recite them there is no sin.

children.text: araṇye parvate vāpi pure vāpyathavā gṛhe
children.translated_text: In a forest or on a mountain, in a city or in a house,

children.text: rakṣāmetāṃ prayuñjīta jale vātha sthale'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: one should employ this protection, whether in water or on dry land.
Especially in places of danger from tigers, crocodiles, and thieves,

children.text: āpatsvapi ca sarvāsu devyā nāmāni kīrtayet ||
children.translated_text: and in all calamities, one should proclaim the names of the goddess.
When children are afflicted by <s>āryaka</s>-grahas, spirits, <s>Pūtanā</s>s, and mother-demons,
one should apply this protection for them.

children.text: mahādevīkale dve tu prajñā śrīś ca prakīrtite
children.translated_text: Two portions of <s>Mahādevī</s> are proclaimed as <s>Prajñā</s> and <s>Śrī</s>.
By these two, thousands of goddesses pervade the whole world.
Together with her as <s>Satī</s>, that god of gods, <s>Rudra Maheśvara</s>,
the supreme lord, stood firm for the welfare of all the worlds.
<s>Rudra</s> was <s>Paśupati</s> when the three cities were burned long ago.

children.text: devāś ca paśavaḥ sarve babhūvustasya tejasā ||
children.translated_text: All the gods became <s>paśu</s>s through his power.
Whoever recites or hears this auspicious sequence of the original creation

children.text: sa yāti brahmaṇo lokaṃ śrāvayedvā dvijottamān ||
children.translated_text: goes to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, or should have the best brahmins hear it.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge sṛṣṭivistāro nāma saptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventieth chapter, named "The Expansion of Creation," in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
You have taught the auspicious creation both in summary and in detail.
How did <s>Maheśvara</s> become <s>Paśupati</s> in order to burn the city?
And how did the gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, become the paśus of the lord?

children.text: mayasya tapasā pūrvaṃ sudurgaṃ nirmitaṃ puram ||
children.translated_text: We have formerly heard that, through the austerity of <s>Maya</s>, an exceedingly impregnable city was made:

children.text: haimaṃ ca rājataṃ divyam ayasmayam anuttamam
children.translated_text: one golden, one silver, divine, and one of iron, unsurpassed,
very hard to conquer, yet burned by the god of gods. So we have heard.
How did the blessed one, who struck down <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye, burn it?
How, then, with the fall of a single arrow, even a divine one?
That triple city was not burned by beings produced by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: purasya saṃbhavaḥ sarvo varalābhaḥ purā śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The whole origin of the city and the gaining of the boon have been heard before.
Now, O well-vowed one, you should tell the whole burning.
Having heard those words of theirs, <s>Sūta</s>, the best of narrators of old lore,

children.text: yathā śrutaṃ tathā prāha vyāsād viśvārthasūcakāt
children.translated_text: spoke just as he had heard from <s>Vyāsa</s>, who reveals the meaning of the universe.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Indeed, because of a curse upon this triple world, arising from mind, speech, and body,
when the daitya <s>Tāraka</s>, son of <s>Tārā</s>, had been slain together with his kinsmen,

children.text: skandena vā prayatnena tasya putrā mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Skanda</s> with great effort, his sons, mighty in strength,
<s>Vidyunmālī</s>, <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, and the valiant <s>Kamalākṣa</s>,
great-souled and of immense strength and prowess, undertook austerities.

children.text: tapa ugraṃ samāsthāya niyame parame sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Having resorted to fierce austerity and standing in supreme restraint,
those best of dānavas emaciated their own bodies through austerity.

children.text: teṣāṃ pitāmahaḥ prīto varadaḥ pradadau varam
children.translated_text: Pleased with them, the Grandfather, giver of boons, granted a boon.
The daityas said:
They together asked for invulnerability from all beings at all times.
Together they chose this from the grandfather of all the worlds.

children.text: tān abravīt tadā devo lokānāṃ prabhur avyayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the god, the imperishable lord of the worlds, said to them:
"There is no complete immortality. Turn away from that, O asuras.

children.text: anyaṃ varaṃ vṛṇīdhvaṃ vai yādṛśaṃ samprarocate ||
children.translated_text: Choose another boon, whatever seems pleasing to you."
Then the daityas, together, deliberated with one another.
Bowing down to <s>Brahmā</s>, the daityas spoke to the teacher of the world:
"Taking possession of just three cities upon this earth,
we shall roam, O lord of the world, by your favor, O teacher of the world.
And after a thousand years we shall come together with one another;
these cities, O sinless one, will become united into one.
When they have come together, whoever should strike them down then, O blessed one,
that god, with a single arrow alone, shall be death for us."
Saying to them, "So be it," the god entered heaven.

children.text: tato mayaḥ svatapasā cakre vīraḥ purāṇyatha ||
children.translated_text: Then the heroic <s>Maya</s>, by his own austerity, made the cities.
There one was golden in heaven, and one silver in the mid-region;

children.text: āyasaṃ cābhavad bhūmau puraṃ teṣāṃ mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: and on earth there was an iron city for those great-souled beings.
Each one was a hundred yojanas, equal in breadth and length.
The golden one belonged to <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, the silver one to <s>Kamalākṣa</s>,
and the iron one to <s>Vidyunmāli</s>: this threefold fortress was supreme.
And there mighty <s>Maya</s>, honored by daityas and dānavas,
in the golden, the silver, and likewise the black-iron city,
made a dwelling for himself and then lived there in strength.
Thus, O men of good vows, the daityas came to have very hard-to-assail
three cities, O best of brahmins, like another three worlds.

children.text: puratraye tadā jāte sarve daityā jagattraye
children.translated_text: When the three cities had thus come into being, all the daityas in the three worlds
entered those three cities and became exceedingly powerful.
It was filled with wish-granting trees and crowded with elephants and horses,
thronged with many kinds of palaces and covered with networks of jewels.
It shone with aircraft facing every direction, bright as the disk of the sun,
made of rubies, pure, and resembling the moon.
With palaces and divine gateways like the peaks of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
their <s>Tripura</s> was adorned, each part by itself unsurpassed.
It was completely filled with divine women, gandharvas, siddhas, and cāraṇas,
and, O best twice-born ones, with shrines of <s>Rudra</s> at every house and with agnihotras.
On every side it had stepwells, wells, ponds, and long reservoirs,
and it was splendid with herds of rutting elephants and with horses.
There were chariots of various forms, many-colored and facing every direction,
and halls, drinking-places, and separate pleasure grounds.
All around were many kinds of schools for Vedic study.
Through <s>Maya</s>'s own magic it could not be overcome even in thought by others.
Everywhere it was attended by faithful wives, O bulls among sages;
even after committing very great sin, they were sinless through worship of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
It was inhabited by fortunate daitya-lords, with their wives and sons, O brahmins,
who knew the meanings and duties of śrauta and smārta rites and were always devoted to that dharma.
Abandoning every god other than <s>Mahādeva</s>, they remained intent on worshiping him.
They had broad chests, bull-like shoulders, and always bore every weapon.
They were always hungry, with eyes like a forest fire,
both calm and wrathful, and also hunchbacked and dwarfish.
They were like blue lotus petals, with dark curled hair,
like blue mountains and <s>Meru</s>, with voices like thunderclouds.
All were guarded by <s>Maya</s>, trained, and eager for battle.
And that city was well served everywhere by those constantly delighted in war, whose valor had been well gained by worshiping <s>Śiva</s>'s feet,
by destroyers of the gods, firm and powerful, like the sun, the wind, and <s>Indra</s> among the immortals.

children.text: sendrā devā dvijaśreṣṭhā drumā dāvāgninā yathā
children.translated_text: O best twice-born ones, the gods together with <s>Indra</s>, like trees by a forest fire,
were burned by the fire of the three cities because of the daityas' splendor.

children.text: athaivaṃ te tadā dagdhā devā deveśvaraṃ harim
children.translated_text: Then, when the gods had thus been burned, they bowed to <s>Hari</s>, lord of gods,
and then addressed him, whose brilliance was without equal.
That glorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord, thought in his mind,

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ devakāryeṣu bhagavāniti sa prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'What is to be done in the business of the gods?'
Then <s>Janārdana</s>, whose form is sacrifice, remembered Sacrifice itself:
the sacrificer, the enjoyer of sacrifice, the lord, the master who grants fruit to sacrificers.
Then Sacrifice, remembered by him for the accomplishment of the gods' purpose, appeared.
They then bowed to and praised that god, the Puruṣa.

children.text: bhagavānapi taṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñaṃ prāha sanātanam
children.translated_text: The Blessed One, seeing that eternal Sacrifice, spoke to him;
and then the eternal, imperishable one looked upon the gods together with <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> said:
With this upasad rite, O gods, sacrifice to <s>Parameśvara</s>,
for the destruction of the three cities and for the prosperity of the three worlds.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā devadevasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Then, hearing the words of that wise god of gods,
the gods gave a great lion-roar and praised the lord of sacrifice.
Then the Blessed <s>Janārdana</s> himself, after reflecting,
again spoke to all those thirty gods, he the lord of the thirty gods:

children.text: hatvā dagdhvā ca bhūtāni bhuktvā cānyāyato 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Even if one kills and burns beings, or consumes them unjustly,
if he worships <s>Mahādeva</s>, he is sinless; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: apāpā naiva hantavyāḥ pāpā eva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are sinless must certainly not be killed; only the sinful, without doubt,
are to be killed by every effort. How then, O best of gods, are these to be slain?
The asuras are arrogant and sinful, though the gods are very powerful;
therefore they are not to be slain, because of the power of <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme lord.
Who am I, or <s>Brahmā</s>, or the gods, or the daityas, O slayers of the gods' enemies,

children.text: munayaś ca mahātmānaḥ prasādena vinā prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: or the great-souled sages, without the grace of the Lord?
He who is eternally the twenty-seventh, the Lord higher than the highest,
<s>Maheśvara</s>, lord of the immortals and of the universe, worthy of worship and support of the universe,
he alone is the lord of all gods, <s>Śaṅkara</s> for all beings.
In play, <s>Hara</s> made the division between the lords of gods and daityas.

children.text: tasyāṃśam ekaṃ sampūjya devā devatvam āgatāḥ
children.translated_text: Having worshiped a single portion of him, O gods, the gods attained godhood;

children.text: brahmā brahmatvam āpanno hyahaṃ viṣṇutvameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> attained the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, and I myself attained the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tam apūjya jagatyasmin kaḥ pumān siddhimicchati
children.translated_text: Without worshiping him, what man in this world desires perfection?
Therefore they are to be slain by him alone, through the power of the rule for worshiping the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: dharmaniṣṭhāś ca te sarve śrautasmārtavidhau sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: And all of them were devoted to <s>dharma</s>, established in the śrauta and smārta prescriptions.
Even so, after the sacrificer has worshiped the Lord <s>Rudra</s>
with the <s>Rudra</s> upasad according to rule, we shall conquer the best of the daityas.

children.text: satārakākṣeṇa mayena guptaṃ svasthaṃ ca guptaṃ sphaṭikābhamekam
children.translated_text: Who indeed is able to destroy <s>Tripura</s>, protected by <s>Maya</s> together with <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, secure, guarded, and shining like crystal,

children.text: ko nāma hantuṃ tripuraṃ samartho muktvā trinetraṃ bhagavantamekam ||
children.translated_text: except the one blessed three-eyed Lord alone?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s> worshiped the Lord with the upasad sacrifice,
and, seated there, then saw hosts of <s>bhūta</s>s by the thousand.
They held tridents, spears, and clubs in their hands, and had hatchets, stones, and rocks as weapons.
They were equipped with many kinds of weapons and at that time wore many kinds of forms.
They resembled <s>Kālāgnirudra</s> and were like <s>Kālarudra</s> then.

children.text: prāha devo hariḥ sākṣātpraṇipatya sthitān prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: The god <s>Hari</s> himself, the Lord, bowed down and spoke to them as they stood there.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:

children.text: dagdhvā bhittvā ca bhuktvā ca gatvā daityapuratrayam
children.translated_text: Having burned, split open, consumed, and entered the three cities of the daityas,
you heroes should return again as you came, for welfare.
Then the hosts of <s>bhūta</s>s bowed to the lord of gods and entered the three cities.

children.text: praviśya naṣṭāste sarve śalabhā iva pāvakam ||
children.translated_text: All of them perished there like moths entering a fire.
Then, when all those <s>bhūta</s>s had perished by the command of the lord of gods,

children.text: nanṛtur mumuduś caiva jagur daityāḥ sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the daityas danced, rejoiced, and sang by the thousand.
They praised the lord of the gods of gods, the supreme self, <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: tataḥ parājitā devā dhvastavīryāḥ kṣaṇena tu ||
children.translated_text: Then in a moment the gods were defeated and their strength was shattered.
Together with <s>Indra</s>, they assembled before the lord of gods, <s>Upendra</s>, taking refuge out of fear.
Seeing them, the blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s> began to reflect.
For a moment he was distressed, thinking, "What is to be done?", as those with <s>Indra</s> were distressed.

children.text: kathaṃ tu teṣāṃ daityānāṃ balaṃ hatvā prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: "How, after carefully destroying the strength of those daityas,
shall I accomplish the work of the gods by the grace of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>?

children.text: pāpaṃ vicārato nāsti dharmiṣṭhānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On reflection, there is no sin among those most firm in <s>dharma</s>; there is no doubt.
Therefore those daityas are not to be slain by the <s>bhūta</s>s born from the upasad.

children.text: pāpaṃ nudati dharmeṇa dharme sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> drives away sin; everything is established in <s>dharma</s>.
From <s>dharma</s> comes sovereignty: this is the ancient śruti.
And these daityas, all the residents of <s>Tripura</s>, are indeed most righteous.
Therefore they have attained inviolability, and not otherwise, O bulls among brahmins.
Even after committing a very great sin, those who worship <s>Rudra</s>
are freed from all transgressions, like a lotus leaf from water.
Through worship, the wealth of enjoyments necessarily arises, O brahmins.
Therefore those daityas are enjoyers and are wholly devoted to liṅga worship.
Therefore, creating an obstruction to <s>dharma</s> through my own <s>māyā</s>, O gods,
I shall conquer <s>Tripura</s> in a moment for the sake of the gods' task."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having considered in this way, the blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s>
then resolved to create an obstruction to the <s>dharma</s> of the enemies of the gods.
The greatly radiant one, <s>Acyuta</s>, created a man born from himself,
a master of <s>māyā</s>, made of <s>māyā</s>, for the purpose of obstructing their <s>dharma</s>.
Taking whatever form he wished, the teacher made a scripture for all,
a wholly deluding one, made by <s>māyā</s>, joined with appeal to visible proof.
Having taught this to the man born from his own body,
the master of <s>māyā</s> taught the <s>māyā</s>-made scripture, sixteen hundred thousand granthas in extent.
It was opposed to śrauta and smārta teaching and devoid of varṇa and āśrama.
Its doctrine was that heaven and hell are here alone, and not otherwise hereafter.
Having himself instructed that scripture to the man,
<s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Hari</s>, spoke to that man for the destruction of the three cities:
"Sir, you should go quickly for the ruin of the city-dwellers.

children.text: dharmās tathā praṇaśyantu śrautasmārtā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Let their śrauta and smārta <s>dharma</s>s perish; there is no doubt."
Then that master of <s>māyā</s>, expert in the scripture of <s>māyā</s>, bowed to him.
Entering that city quickly, the sage then performed <s>māyā</s>.
By his <s>māyā</s>, those daityas who dwelt in the three cities

children.text: śrautaṃ smārtaṃ ca saṃtyajya tasya śiṣyāstadābhavan ||
children.translated_text: abandoned śrauta and smārta teaching and then became his disciples.
They abandoned <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s>.
Then <s>Nārada</s> too, as a master of <s>māyā</s>, by the command of the lord who wielded <s>māyā</s>,

children.text: praviśya tatpuraṃ tena māyinā saha dīkṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: entered that city and was initiated together with that master of <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: muniḥ śiṣyaiḥ praśiṣyaiś ca saṃvṛtaḥ sarvataḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: The sage himself was surrounded on every side by disciples and by disciples' disciples.
He also fashioned a women's <s>dharma</s> for women, one that brought about the fruit of misconduct.

children.text: cakrustāḥ sarvadā labdhvā sadya eva phalaṃ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having obtained an immediate result, those women practiced it at all times.
Attached to worldly people, those women began to revile the idea that the husband is a deity.
Even today, in the Kali age, out of regard for that <s>Nārada</s>, O sage,
women, abandoning their husbands, behave wantonly and vainly, as the lowest ones.

children.text: strīṇāṃ mātā pitā bandhuḥ sakhā mitraṃ ca bāndhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For women, the husband alone is mother, father, kinsman, companion, friend, and relative;

children.text: bhartā eva na saṃdehas tathāpy āsahamāyayā
children.translated_text: there is no doubt. Yet through that unbearable <s>māyā</s>,
even if she has committed a very great sin, a woman who is joined with love for her husband

children.text: prāpnuyāt paramaṃ svargaṃ narakaṃ ca viparyayāt
children.translated_text: would attain the highest heaven, and hell by the contrary conduct.
Formerly, O tigers among sages, virtuous women always worshiped the husband, who embodies all <s>dharma</s>s,
having abandoned other gods, the teachers of the world.
Those women reached the heavenly world and rejoice free from distress.

children.text: narakaṃ ca jagāmānyā tasmādbhartā parā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Another woman went to hell; therefore the husband is the supreme goal.

children.text: tathāpi bhartṝn svāṃs tyaktvā babhūvuḥ svairavṛttayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nevertheless, abandoning their own husbands, they became wanton in conduct
through the <s>māyā</s> of that god of gods, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by the command of that Lord.

children.text: alakṣmīś ca svayaṃ tasya niyogāttripuraṃ gatā ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Alakṣmī</s> herself, by his command, went to <s>Tripura</s>.
The <s>Lakṣmī</s> that had been obtained by their austerity from the unborn lord of the gods
went outside and abandoned them by the command of lord <s>Brahmā</s>.
And that very delusion of understanding, produced by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s> (illusion),

children.text: teṣāṃ dattvā kṣaṇaṃ devastāsāṃ māyī ca nāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the divine and magical <s>Nārada</s> gave to them for a moment.
Those two imperishable ones sat happily and without agitation, for the sake of obstructing <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: evaṃ naṣṭe tadā dharme śrautasmārte suśobhane ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when the beautiful <s>śrauta</s> and <s>smārta</s> dharma had then perished,
when heresy had been made known by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the womb of the universe,
when <s>Maheśvara</s> had been abandoned by the daityas and worship of the <s>liṅga</s> had likewise been abandoned,
when women's dharma had wholly perished and misconduct had become established,
the lord of gods, as if his purpose had been accomplished, together with the gods,
approached by austerity the all-knowing lord of <s>Umā</s>, and <s>Puruṣottama</s> praised him.
The Blessed Lord said:
Homage to you, to <s>Maheśvara</s>, the god, the supreme self;
to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Brahmā</s>, to the one whose form is <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: śāśvatāya hyanantāya avyaktāya ca te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: homage to you, the eternal, the endless, and the unmanifest.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having praised <s>Mahādeva</s> in this way and having bowed down prostrate like a staff,
the blessed one stood in the water and recited the <s>Rudra</s> hymn ten million times.

children.text: devāś ca sarve te devaṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ parameśvaram
children.translated_text: And all those gods praised the god <s>Parameśvara</s>,
together with <s>Indra</s>, with the <s>Sādhyas</s>, with <s>Yama</s>, with the <s>Rudras</s>, and with the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.
The gods said:
Homage to you, the self of all, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, remover of distress,
to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Nīlarudra</s>, to <s>Kadrudra</s>, to the wise one.
You are always our refuge; you are to be worshiped by us, O crusher of the enemies of the gods.
You are the beginning, you are endless; you are infinite, imperishable, and lord.
You are manifest <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), the creator and destroyer, O teacher of the world.
In this world you are the protector and guide of brahmins, O lover of brahmins.
You are the giver of boons, made of speech, denotable, and yet free from denoted and denoter.
You are <s>Īśāna</s>, to be worshiped for liberation by yogins through the powers of yoga.
You are always established in the hollow of the heart-lotus of yogins.
The wise declare you to be existent, taking the form of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.
The noble call you the principle, the mass of splendor beyond the beyond.
In this world they call you the supreme self, O mighty one.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ sthitaṃ sarvaṃ jāyamānaṃ jagadguro
children.translated_text: All that is seen, heard, established, and being born is you, O teacher of the world.
They say you are smaller than the smallest atom and greater even than the great.
You have hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere,
and ears everywhere in the world; you stand pervading everything.
You are <s>Mahādeva</s>, indescribable, omniscient, free from disease,
the one whose form is the universe, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, free from affliction.
You shine like ten million suns and resemble ten million moons.
You blaze like ten million fires of time, the twenty-sixth principle, with no lord above you.
You are the impeller of nature in this world, the great-grandfather.
They call you the boon-giving god, the dwelling-place of all, the self-born one.
The <s>śruti</s>s, and people who know the essence of <s>śruti</s>, call you the essence of <s>śruti</s>.

children.text: adṛṣṭamasmābhir anekamūrte vinā kṛtaṃ yadbhavatātha loke
children.translated_text: O one of many forms, apart from you we have seen nothing done by you here in the world.

children.text: tvameva daityāsurabhūtasaṃghān devān narān sthāvarajaṅgamāṃś ca ||
children.translated_text: You alone encompass the hosts of daityas, asuras, and beings, the gods, men, and the moving and unmoving.
Protect us, O <s>Śaṃbhu</s>; there is no other refuge. Strike down the foremost asuras.
All are deluded by <s>māyā</s>, O <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: yathā taraṅgā laharīsamūhā yudhyanti cānyonyamapāṃnidhau ca
children.translated_text: Just as waves and masses of billows fight one another in the ocean
and, having water as their support, are made insentient, so are the gods and asuras; everything belongs to the unborn one.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
