A man who rises in the morning, becomes pure, and recites this,
or listens to this holy hymn, obtains every desire.
When <s>Maheśvara</s> had thus been praised by the gods and by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s recitation,
<s>Soma</s> then embraced <s>Somā</s> and, smiling, with his hand given to <s>Nandin</s>,
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, looking upon the gods, spoke in a deep voice:
Now I have understood this task of the gods, O lords of the gods,

children.text: viṣṇor māyābalaṃ caiva nāradasya ca dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: and also the power of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s> and of wise <s>Nārada</s>.
O best of gods, for those daityas devoted to unrighteousness,
I shall bring about the destruction of the three cities, O best of gods.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then the assembled gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Upendra</s>,

children.text: śrutvā prabhostadā vākyaṃ praṇemustuṣṭuvuś ca te
children.translated_text: heard the lord's words and bowed down and praised him.
But in the meantime the goddess, looking at the god, was astonished.
Striking <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> with a play-lotus, she spoke softly.
The goddess said:
Look, O mighty lord, at the playful six-faced one, shining like the sun,

children.text: putraṃ putravatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ bhūṣitaṃ bhūṣaṇaiḥ śubhaiḥ
children.translated_text: the son, best among those who have sons, adorned with auspicious ornaments,
with crowns, bracelets, earrings, and auspicious bangles,
with anklets, waist-garlands, and also belly-bands,
with many little bells and golden aśvattha leaves,
with auspicious curls adorned by flowers born from wish-fulfilling trees,
with necklaces and armlets made variegated with lotus-ruby and other jewels,
with necklaces made of pearls, shining like the full moon.

children.text: tilakaiś ca mahādeva paśya putraṃ suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, look at your exceedingly beautiful son, marked with tilakas,
marked with kuṅkuma and other substances, and encircled with lines made of ash.

children.text: vaktravṛndaṃ ca paśyeśa vṛndaṃ kāmalakaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: Look, O lord, at the cluster of faces, like a cluster of lovely lotuses.

children.text: netrāṇi ca vibho paśya śubhāni tvaṃ śubhāni ca
children.translated_text: And look, O mighty lord, at the auspicious eyes, truly auspicious,
and at the varied collyria applied for auspiciousness by the mothers,
by <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the others, by the <s>Kṛttikās</s> and especially by <s>Svāhā</s>.

children.text: ityevaṃ lokamātuś ca vāgbhiḥ saṃbodhitaḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Śiva</s>, addressed by the words of the mother of the world,
<s>Īśāna</s> did not reach satisfaction while drinking the nectar of <s>Skanda</s>'s face.
Nor did he remember those gods who were tormented by the weapons of the daityas.
Embracing <s>Skanda</s> and smelling him, he said, "Dance, my son!"
And that playful child too, the lord who removes distress, danced.
The other lords of the gaṇas danced together with him,
and there the entire three worlds danced for a moment by the command of <s>Īśa</s>.

children.text: nāgāś ca nanṛtuḥ sarve devāḥ sendrapurogamāḥ
children.translated_text: All the nāgas danced, and the gods with <s>Indra</s> at their head;
the gaṇapa chiefs praised <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Ambā</s> and the mothers rejoiced.
They sent forth showers of flowers, and the gandharvas and kinnaras sang.
Then, having drunk that nectar of dance, <s>Pārvatī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>

children.text: avāpatus tadā tṛptiṃ nandinā ca gaṇeśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: attained satisfaction, together with <s>Nandin</s> and the lords of the gaṇas.

children.text: tataḥ sa nandī saha ṣaṇmukhena tathā ca sārdhaṃ girirājaputryā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Nandī</s>, together with <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> and also with the daughter of the mountain,

children.text: viveśa divyaṃ bhavanaṃ bhavo'pi yathāmbudo 'nyāmbudam ambudābhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: entered the divine palace; <s>Bhava</s> too entered, like a cloud-colored cloud entering another cloud.

children.text: dvārasya pārśve te tasthurdevā devasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: The gods stood at the side of the door of that wise god,
and praised <s>Mahādeva</s>, their minds somewhat anxious.
Looking at one another and confused, they said, "But what? But what?"

children.text: pāpā vayam iti hyanye abhāgyāśceti cāpare ||
children.translated_text: Some said, "We are sinful," and others, "We are unfortunate."

children.text: bhāgyavantaś ca daityendrā iti cānye sureśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Other lords of the gods said, "The chiefs of the daityas are fortunate,"
and others said, "This is the fruit of their worship"; still others said, "No."
Meanwhile, hearing their many sounds,
<s>Kumbhodara</s>, mighty in splendor, struck the gods with his staff.
Those gods, seized with fear, fled crying, "Ah! Ah!"
and some sages and gods fell upon the ground.
The sages beginning with <s>Kaśyapa</s> said, "Ah, the power of fate!"
Even after seeing the Lord of gods, the Lord of the gods and the enemy of the asuras,
other brahmins said, "Because of misfortune, the task has not been completed."
They uttered, "Homage to <s>Śiva</s>," worshiping him, though only a little, in their hearts.
Then <s>Nandīśa</s>, the matted-haired one, the sage beloved of <s>Mahādeva</s>,

children.text: śūlī mālī tathā hālī kuṇḍalī valayī gadī ||
children.translated_text: bearing a trident and a garland, a plough, earrings, bracelets, and a mace,
mounted a very white bull and went then by his command.

children.text: tato vai nandinaṃ dṛṣṭvā gaṇaḥ kumbhodaro 'pi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, seeing <s>Nandin</s>, that gaṇa <s>Kumbhodara</s> too

children.text: praṇamya nandinaṃ mūrdhnā saha tena tvaran yayau
children.translated_text: bowed to <s>Nandin</s> with his head and hastened away with him.
<s>Nandī</s>, of great splendor, shone on the bull's back, marked by the bull-banner,
together with the gaṇas, the commander of the gaṇa army, like <s>Bhava</s> on the back of a cloud.
A white parasol, ten yojanas wide and adorned with nets of pearls,
shone like the sky above the mountain.
There, inside it, an auspicious garland strung with pearl-fruits
shone upon the lord's head like <s>Gaṅgā</s> fallen from the sky.
Then, when they saw the lord of the gaṇas, the auspicious divine drums,
all at the command of the wielder of the thunderbolt, sounded, O foremost sages.

children.text: tuṣṭuvuś ca gaṇeśānaṃ vāgbhir iṣṭapradaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: And with words they praised the auspicious lord of the gaṇas, the giver of desired boons.
As when the gods saw <s>Bhava</s>, their skin bristling with joy,
so, at the command of the wielder of the thunderbolt, the sky-goers showered flowers on his head.
They rained down a fragrant shower upon <s>Nandin</s>, rising in the sky.

children.text: vṛṣṭyā tuṣṭastadā reje tuṣṭyā puṣṭyā yathārthayā ||
children.translated_text: Pleased by that shower, <s>Nandī</s> then shone with true satisfaction and fullness.
<s>Nandī</s>, like <s>Bhava</s> adorned by the moon, was as though bathed with fragrant water.
There the back of that bull shone with flowers of many kinds,

children.text: saṃkīrṇaṃ tu divaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ nakṣatrairiva suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: crowded like the surface of heaven with stars, O virtuous ones.

children.text: kusumaiḥ saṃvṛto nandī vṛṣapṛṣṭhe rarāja saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Covered with blossoms, that <s>Nandī</s> shone on the bull's back

children.text: divaḥ pṛṣṭhe yathā candro nakṣatrairiva suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: like the moon on the surface of heaven among the stars, O virtuous ones.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nandinaṃ devāḥ sendropendrās tathāvidham ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that <s>Nandin</s> in such a form, the gods with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>
praised the lord of the gaṇas as if he were another God of gods.
The gods said:
Homage to you, devoted to <s>Rudra</s>, and delighting in the muttering of <s>Rudra</s>'s names.
Homage to you, destroyer of the distress of <s>Rudra</s>'s devotees, delighting in fierce <s>Rudra</s>-like acts.
Homage to the lord of the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> gaṇas, homage to the lord of yogins.
Homage to the giver of all, the refuge, the omniscient one, the remover of distress.

children.text: vedānāṃ pataye caiva vedavedyāya te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you, lord of the Vedas and the one to be known through the Vedas.
Homage to the thunderbolt-bearing one, the one with thunderbolt-fangs, the one who wards off the thunderbolt of <s>Vajrin</s>.
Homage to you whose body is adorned with thunderbolts and who are worshiped by <s>Vajrin</s>.
Homage to you, the red one, red-eyed and wearing red garments.
Homage to you who grant <s>Rudra</s>'s world to those devoted to the lotus feet of <s>Bhava</s>.
Homage to the commander of the army; homage to the lord of the <s>Rudras</s>.
Homage to the lord of beings and of the worlds, the remover of sin.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to the lord of <s>Rudra</s>, to you who remove fierce sins.

children.text: namaḥ śivāya saumyāya rudrabhaktāya te namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, the gentle one; homage to you, devotee of <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then the pleased lord of the gaṇas, born of <s>Śiva</s>, said to the gods:

children.text: rathaṃ ca sārathiṃ śaṃbhoḥ kārmukaṃ śaramuttamam ||
children.translated_text: You must carefully make <s>Śambhu</s>'s chariot and charioteer, his bow and excellent arrow,
regarding the three cities as already destroyed.

children.text: atha te brahmaṇā sārdhaṃ tathā vai viśvakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: Then they, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and likewise with <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
eagerly made the chariot of the wise God of gods.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge puradāhe nandikeśvaravākyaṃ nāma ekasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, in the Burning of the Cities, the seventy-first chapter, named "The Speech of <s>Nandikeśvara</s>."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then for the god <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viśvakarman</s> carefully
and reverently made a divine chariot consisting of all worlds,
consisting of all beings and honored by all gods.
And it was golden, made of all the gods, and approved by all.

children.text: rathāṅgaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ sūryo vāmāṅgaṃ soma eva ca
children.translated_text: The right wheel of the chariot was the sun, and the left wheel was indeed the moon;
the right had twelve spokes, and the northern, that is, the other, had sixteen spokes.
In those spokes, O foremost brahmins, were the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>,
and in the sixteen spokes of the moon were the digits of the left one, O men of good vows.

children.text: ṛkṣāṇi ca tadā tasya vāmasyaiva tu bhūṣaṇam
children.translated_text: And the constellations were then the ornament of that left wheel itself;
and the rims of those two were the six seasons, O best of brahmins.

children.text: puṣkaraṃ cāntarikṣaṃ vai rathanīḍaś ca mandaraḥ
children.translated_text: The nave was the midspace, and the chariot-seat was <s>Mandara</s>.

children.text: astādrirudayādriś ca ubhau tau kūbarau smṛtau ||
children.translated_text: The setting mountain and the rising mountain, those two, are remembered as the two yoke-pins.
Great <s>Meru</s> was the base, and the <s>Kesara</s> mountains were the supports.
Its speed was the year, and the two solstitial courses were the junctions of the wheels.
Its lovely fastenings were the muhūrtas, and the kalās are remembered as its yoke-bars.

children.text: tasya kāṣṭhāḥ smṛtā ghoṇā cākṣadaṇḍāḥ kṣaṇāś ca vai ||
children.translated_text: Its kāṣṭhās are remembered as the nose-piece, and the moments as the axle-rods.

children.text: nimeṣāścānukarṣāś ca īṣā cāsya lavāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The nimeṣas were the draw-pieces, and its pole was remembered as the lavas.
Heaven was the guard-rail of this chariot, and heaven and liberation were its two banners.

children.text: dharmo virāgo daṇḍo'sya yajñā daṇḍāśrayāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> and dispassion were its staff, and sacrifices are remembered as resting on that staff.
The gifts were its joints, and the metals were the fifty fires.
The two ends of the ages are remembered as its two parts, <s>dharma</s> and desire.
The pole-shaft was the unmanifest, and its reed-seat was the intellect.

children.text: koṇas tathā hyahaṅkāro bhūtāni ca balaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Its corner was ahaṃkāra (egoity), and the elements are remembered as its strength.
And the senses themselves were its ornaments on every side.

children.text: śraddhā ca gatirasyaiva vedāstasya hayāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Faith was its course, and the <s>Vedas</s> are remembered as its horses.
The words were ornaments, and the six ancillary sciences were further adornment.
The Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, and Dharmaśāstras, O men of good vows,
were its hair-supports and cloths, furnished with all auspicious marks.
The mantras are remembered as their bells, and the syllables, the Vedic feet, and the āśramas as well.
Its boundary was the endless one, adorned with a thousand hoods.

children.text: diśaḥ pādā rathasyāsya tathā copadiśaś ca ha
children.translated_text: The directions were the feet of this chariot, and so too the intermediate directions.
The banners, beginning with the nave, were golden and adorned with jewels.
The four oceans are remembered as its chariot-coverings.
The excellent rivers, beginning with <s>Gaṅgā</s>, were adorned with every ornament.
With chowries attached to the tips of their hands, all were splendid in female form.
Stationed here and there, they made the chariot shine.
The seven winds, beginning with <s>Āvaha</s>, were its excellent golden stairway.
The blessed <s>Brahmā</s> was the charioteer, and the gods are remembered as holding the reins.
The goad of that <s>Brahmā</s> was the praṇava, whose presiding deity is <s>Brahmā</s>.
The <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain, together with its stairway, was around it on every side.

children.text: viṣamaś ca tadā bāhyo mānasādriḥ suśobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Then outside was the uneven and beautiful <s>Mānasa</s> mountain.
All the mountains on every side are remembered as its noses.
The lower worlds and the grey doves were all dwellers in the lower regions.
<s>Meru</s> itself was the great parasol, and <s>Mandara</s> was the side-drum.

children.text: śailendraḥ kārmukaṃ caiva jyā bhujaṅgādhipaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: The lord of mountains was the bow, and the lord of serpents himself was its string.
So too here with <s>Kālarātrī</s>, and again with <s>Indra</s>'s bow.
The goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, in the form of revelation, was the bell of the bow.
The arrow was the greatly radiant <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the point of the arrow was the moon.
The fire at the end of time was that very arrow, directly present, sharp and very terrible.
Its front was born of poison, and the winds are remembered as its feathers.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā rathaṃ divyaṃ kārmukaṃ ca śaraṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having thus made the divine chariot, the bow, and likewise the arrow,
and having made <s>Brahmā</s>, lord and master of the worlds, the charioteer,
<s>Bhava</s>, bearing the adornment of battle, mounted the divine chariot,
joined by all the hosts of gods, as if shaking heaven and earth.

children.text: ṛṣibhiḥ stūyamānaś ca vandyamānaś ca bandibhiḥ
children.translated_text: He was praised by sages and lauded by panegyrists,
and attended in dance by groups of apsarases skilled in dancing.
The boon-giver, shining beautifully, looked upon the charioteer.
When he mounted that chariot, fashioned from the whole world,
the horses born from the <s>Vedas</s> fell to the ground on their heads.
Then beneath this chariot the blessed upholder of the earth,
in the form of the chief bull, lifted it and held it up for a moment.
After another moment, even the chief bull went down to the earth on his knees.
The blessed lord, holding the reins, raised up the horses,
and at the god's command he steadied the auspicious chariot.
Then he drove the horses, swift as mind and wind,
toward the sky-borne cities of the powerful dānavas.
Then the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, looking at the gods, said:
'Grant me lordship over paśus (bound beings); then I will slay the asuras.
O best of gods, the separate paśu-state of the gods and of others
must first be established; only then are they to be slain, and not otherwise, O best beings.'

children.text: iti śrutvā vacaḥ sarvaṃ devadevasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: Hearing all these words of the wise god of gods,
they all fell into despair, anxious about becoming paśus.
Then, knowing their feeling, the god said this to them:
'Let there be no fear for you in this paśu-state, O best of the gods.

children.text: śrūyatāṃ paśubhāvasya vimokṣaḥ kriyatāṃ ca saḥ
children.translated_text: Listen: release from paśu-state shall be made.

children.text: yo vai pāśupataṃ divyaṃ cariṣyati sa mokṣyati ||
children.translated_text: Whoever practices the divine Pāśupata observance will be released
from paśu-status. This truth has been promised, O composed ones.

children.text: ye cāpyanye cariṣyanti vrataṃ pāśupataṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: And whatever others practice my Pāśupata vow,

children.text: mokṣyanti te na saṃdehaḥ paśutvāt surasattamāḥ
children.translated_text: they too will be released from paśu-status; there is no doubt, O best of gods.'
whether as a naiṣṭhika observance for twelve years, or for half of that, or for three years.
Whoever performs such devoted service is released from the condition of a <s>paśu</s> (bound creature).
Therefore you shall undertake this supreme, divine observance, O best of gods.
"So be it," said the gods to <s>Śiva</s>, who is revered by the worlds.
Therefore all gods, asuras, and men are <s>paśus</s> of the Lord.
<s>Rudra</s> is <s>Paśupati</s>, and he is the releaser from the bonds of the <s>paśu</s>.
Whoever is a <s>paśu</s> abandons that state of being a <s>paśu</s> through this vow.

children.text: tatkṛtvā na ca pāpīyāniti śāstrasya niścayaḥ
children.translated_text: Having performed it, one does not become more sinful; this is the settled conclusion of the śāstra.
Then <s>Vināyaka</s> himself, a child whose valor was not childish,
being then unhonored by the gods, spoke to the gods, restraining them.
<s>Śrī Vināyaka</s> said:
Without honoring me in this world with auspicious eatables, foods, and the like,

children.text: kaḥ pumānsiddhimāpnoti devo vā dānavo'pi vā
children.translated_text: what man attains success, or even what god or dānava?
Therefore, at that very moment, in the gods' undertaking, O lords of the gods,

children.text: vighnaṃ kariṣye deveśa kathaṃ kartuṃ samudyatāḥ
children.translated_text: I shall create an obstacle, O lord of gods; how are you setting out to act?

children.text: tataḥ sendrāḥ surāḥ sarve bhītāḥ sampūjya taṃ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: Then all the gods, with <s>Indra</s>, were afraid, and they worshiped that lord
with eatables and foods, and with cakes and modakas.

children.text: abruvaṃste gaṇeśānaṃ nirvighnaṃ cāstu naḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: They said to <s>Gaṇeśāna</s>, "May there always be freedom from obstacles for us."

children.text: bhavo'pyanekaiḥ kusumair gaṇeśaṃ bhakṣyaiś ca bhojyaiḥ surasaiḥ sugandhaiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhava</s> too worshiped <s>Gaṇeśa</s> with many flowers and with delicious, fragrant eatables and foods;
then the foremost of all the lords of gods embraced and smelled the head of his son.
Having worshiped <s>Vināyaka</s>, the worshipful leader of the lords, together with the hosts of gods,
the wielder of the mountain-bow went off with the lords of the gaṇas to burn the three cities.

children.text: taṃ devadevaṃ surasiddhasaṃghā maheśvaraṃ bhūtagaṇāś ca sarve
children.translated_text: The hosts of gods and siddhas, and all the troops of beings, followed that god of gods,
<s>Maheśvara</s>; and the lords of gaṇas, headed by <s>Nandin</s>, followed the Lord at that time on their own vehicles.

children.text: agre surāṇāṃ ca gaṇeśvarāṇāṃ tadātha nandī girirājakalpam
children.translated_text: Then, in front of the gods and the lords of gaṇas, <s>Nandin</s>, like the king of mountains,

children.text: vimānamāruhya puraṃ prahartuṃ jagāma mṛtyuṃ bhagavāniveśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: mounted his aerial car and went to strike the city; the blessed Lord went like death itself.
As the son of <s>Śilāda</s> was going, mounted on excellent great serpents, bulls, and horses,

children.text: devāstadānīṃ gaṇapāś ca sarve gaṇā yayuḥ svāyudhacihnahastāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the gods, the gaṇa chiefs, and all the gaṇas went then, bearing their own weapons and emblems in their hands.

children.text: khagendramāruhya nagendrakalpaṃ khagadhvajo vāmata eva śaṃbhoḥ
children.translated_text: The one whose banner bears the bird, mounted on the lord of birds, like a great mountain, went on <s>Śambhu</s>'s left side,
with undiminished power, for the welfare of the worlds, to burn the three cities.
All the gods followed all around that god, the lord of the heavenly world, the immeasurable one,
and the sharp-rayed, thousand-rayed blessed one, lord of gods and asuras, followed as well.
The blessed one shone in the midst of the gods, vehicleless, with the color of a lotus petal,

children.text: yathā sumeroḥ śikharādhirūḍhaḥ sahasraraśmir bhagavān sutīkṣṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as the keen, thousand-rayed blessed sun shines when mounted on the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>.

children.text: sahasranetraḥ prathamaḥ surāṇāṃ gajendramāruhya ca dakṣiṇe 'sya
children.translated_text: The thousand-eyed one, foremost of the gods, mounted on the lord of elephants at his right side,

children.text: jagāma rudrasya puraṃ nihantuṃ yathoragāṃstatra tu vainateyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: went to destroy <s>Rudra</s>'s city, as <s>Vainateya</s> goes there to destroy serpents.
The siddhas, gandharvas, and heroic lords of gods praised him, <s>Indra</s>, lord of the hosts of gods,
the wish-granting lord, from every side, crying "Victory!" and showering excellent flowers on <s>Śakra</s>.
Then the dwellers in heaven beheld the lord of gods, the lord of the world, the lover of <s>Ahalyā</s>,
and bowed to the thousand-eyed one, as one might gracefully bow to <s>Indra</s>, the son of the Mother.
<s>Yama</s>, <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Vitteśa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and <s>Nirṛti</s>,
as well as the lord of waters and <s>Īśāna</s>, came after <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: vīrabhadro raṇe bhadro nairṛtyāṃ vai rathasya tu
children.translated_text: <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, auspicious in battle, was on the southwestern side of the chariot;
mounted on the lordly bull and surrounded by hair-born attendants,

children.text: sevāṃ cakre puraṃ hantuṃ devadevaṃ triyaṃbakam
children.translated_text: he rendered service to the three-eyed god of gods for the destruction of the city.
<s>Mahākāla</s>, greatly radiant, like another <s>Mahādeva</s>,

children.text: vāyavyāṃ sagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ sevāṃ cakre rathasya tu ||
children.translated_text: rendered service at the northwestern side of the chariot, together with his gaṇas.

children.text: ṣaṇmukho'pi saha siddhacāraṇaiḥ senayā ca girirājasaṃnibhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> too, with siddhas and cāraṇas and with an army like the king of mountains,
the fire-born one, surrounded by the hosts of the lords of the gods' gaṇas, went with an elephant as well.
<s>Gaṇeśa</s>, lord of obstacles, made obstacles for the lords of the asuras and freedom from obstacles for the gods,

children.text: vighneśvaro vighnagaṇaiś ca sārdhaṃ taṃ deśamīśānapadaṃ jagāma ||
children.translated_text: and went to that region, the place of <s>Īśāna</s>, together with the troops of obstacle-gaṇas.

children.text: kālī tadā kālaniśāprakāśaṃ śūlaṃ kapālābharaṇā kareṇa
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kālī</s>, holding in her hand a spear bright as the black night and adorned with skulls,
shook the lords of gods, intoxicated from drinking the blood-wine of great asuras.

children.text: mattebhagāmī madalolanetrā mattaiḥ piśācaiś ca gaṇaiś ca mattaiḥ
children.translated_text: She moved like a rutting elephant, her eyes rolling with intoxication, accompanied by drunken piśācas and intoxicated gaṇas;
her limbs wrapped in the hide of a rutting elephant, she went before the lord of gaṇas.
The siddhas, gandharvas, piśācas, yakṣas, vidyādharas, serpent-kings, and chief lords of gods
bowed to her and loudly praised the goddess, daughter of the snowy mountain, crying "Victory!"
The Mothers, destroyers of the enemies of the best gods, were reverently worshiped by the hosts of gods;
then they went to the Mother on their own vehicles, surrounded on all sides by their own banner-bearing gaṇas.

children.text: durgārūḍhamṛgādhipā duratigā dordaṇḍavṛndaiḥ śivā bibhrāṇāṅkuśaśūlapāśaparaśuṃ cakrāsiśaṅkhāyudham
children.translated_text: <s>Durgā</s>, mounted on the lord of beasts, hard to approach, auspicious, bearing in her many staff-like arms a goad, spear, noose, axe, discus, sword, conch, and other weapons,

children.text: prauḍhādityasahasrasadṛśairnetrairdahantī pathaṃ bālābālaparākramā bhagavatī daityānprahartuṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: burning the path with eyes like a thousand blazing suns, the goddess, a girl with more-than-childish valor, went to strike down the daityas.

children.text: taṃ devamīśaṃ tripuraṃ nihantuṃ tadā tu devendraraviprakāśāḥ
children.translated_text: Then, to destroy Tripura for that god, the Lord, chiefs of the gaṇas, radiant like <s>Devendra</s> and the sun,

children.text: gajairhayaiḥ siṃhavarai rathaiś ca vṛṣairyayuste gaṇarājamukhyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: went with elephants, horses, excellent lions, chariots, and bulls.

children.text: halaiś ca phālair musalair bhuśuṇḍair girīndrakūṭair girisannibhāste
children.translated_text: With ploughs, ploughshares, pestles, bhuśuṇḍī-clubs, and peaks of great mountains, those who were like mountains

children.text: yayuḥ purastāddhi maheśvarasya sureśvarā bhūtagaṇeśvarāś ca ||
children.translated_text: went in front of <s>Maheśvara</s>: the lords of gods and the lords of the hosts of beings.
Likewise the gods headed by <s>Indra</s>, <s>Padmodbhava</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the gaṇa-lords, addressed <s>Īśa</s>, the lord of gaṇas,
the Blessed Lord, with words of "Victory!" from every side, their joined hands lifted to their diadems.
All the sages danced, holding staffs and wearing matted locks;
the sky-going siddhas and cāraṇas rained down showers of flowers.
And the three cities, O best of brahmins, likewise seemed to breathe from every side.

children.text: gaṇeśvarair devagaṇaiś ca bhṛṅgī sahāvṛtaḥ sarvagaṇendravaryaḥ
children.translated_text: Surrounded by the lords of gaṇas and by the hosts of gods, <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, the foremost of all gaṇa-lords,

children.text: jagāma yogī tripuraṃ nihantuṃ vimānamāruhya yathā mahendraḥ ||
children.translated_text: the yogin, mounted an aerial car and went, like <s>Mahendra</s>, to destroy <s>Tripura</s>.
<s>Keśa</s>, <s>Vigatavāsa</s>, <s>Mahākeśa</s>, <s>Mahājvara</s>,

children.text: somavallī savarṇaś ca somapaḥ senakas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Somavallī</s>, <s>Savarṇa</s>, <s>Somapa</s>, and <s>Senaka</s>,
<s>Somadhṛk</s>, <s>Sūryavāca</s>, and <s>Sūryapeṣaṇaka</s>,

children.text: sūryākṣaḥ sūrināmā ca suraḥ sundara eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sūryākṣa</s>, the one named <s>Sūrin</s>, <s>Sura</s>, and <s>Sundara</s>,

children.text: prakudaḥ kakudantaś ca kampanaś ca prakampanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prakuda</s>, <s>Kakudanta</s>, <s>Kampana</s>, and <s>Prakampana</s>,
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Indrajaya</s>, and also <s>Mahābhī</s> and <s>Bhīmaka</s>,
<s>Śatākṣa</s>, <s>Pañcākṣa</s>, <s>Sahasrākṣa</s>, and <s>Mahodara</s>,
<s>Yamajihva</s>, <s>Śatāśva</s>, <s>Kaṇṭhana</s>, and <s>Kaṇṭhapūjana</s>,
<s>Dviśikha</s>, <s>Triśikha</s>, and likewise <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, O twice-born ones,
<s>Muṇḍa</s>, <s>Ardhamuṇḍa</s>, <s>Dīrgha</s>, <s>Piśācāsya</s>, and <s>Pinākadhṛk</s>,
<s>Pippalāyatana</s>, and likewise <s>Aṅgārakāśana</s>,

children.text: śithilaḥ śithilāsyaś ca akṣapādo hyajaḥ kujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śithila</s>, <s>Śithilāsya</s>, <s>Akṣapāda</s>, <s>Aja</s>, and <s>Kuja</s>,
<s>Ajavaktra</s>, <s>Hayavaktra</s>, <s>Gajavaktra</s>, and <s>Ardhavaktraka</s>:
such and others, devoid of definable signs and characteristics, surrounded the Lord.
Surrounding him in troops, they went with <s>Soma</s>, encircled by gaṇas.
Thousands upon thousands of <s>Rudras</s> whose seed flowed upward
surrounded <s>Mahādeva</s>, the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>;
they went to burn the three cities, accompanied by crores upon crores of gaṇas.
The thirty-three gods, and three hundreds as well,
and three thousands of gods, went from every side.
The Mothers of all the worlds, the Mothers of the gaṇas,
and the Mothers of the beings went behind the god.

children.text: bhāti madhye gaṇānāṃ ca rathamadhye gaṇeśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: In the midst of the gaṇas and in the midst of the chariot, the lord of gaṇas shone
like the lord of stars among the stars in a cloudless sky.
The goddess, <s>Girijā</s>, standing at the god's side, shone forth;
then <s>Gaurī</s>, through her power, appeared as though she were <s>Bhava</s>'s own universe-pervading energy.

children.text: śubhāvatī tadā devī pārśvasaṃsthā vibhāti sā
children.translated_text: That auspicious goddess, standing at his side, shone there,
the tips of her hands occupied with a yak-tail fan, her color like a golden lotus.
Then the clear body of the Lord, bright with ash, shone together with that <s>Ambikā</s>,

children.text: sitamivābhramaho saha vidyutā nabhasi devapateḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: like a white cloud in the sky together with lightning, in the supreme realm of the lord of gods.
As the sky shines with a rainbow, and the world with <s>Meru</s>,
so <s>Śambhu</s>'s gentle, moon-bright body shone with the golden bow.
The white parasol of the Supreme Lord, mingled with rays of jewels,
shone like the unbroken disk of the moon at its rising.

children.text: sadukūlā śive raktā lambitā bhāti mālikā
children.translated_text: A red garland, hanging with fine cloth beside <s>Śiva</s>, shone there,
as though, from the jeweled sky at the end of the parasol, a noble river were falling.
Then, with <s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Viriñci</s>, <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, and the others bowing to his lotus feet,

children.text: saha tadā ca jagāma tayāṃbayā sakalalokahitāya puratrayam ||
children.translated_text: he went at that time with that Mother to the three cities for the welfare of all worlds.

children.text: dagdhuṃ samartho manasā kṣaṇena carācaraṃ sarvamidaṃ triśūlī
children.translated_text: The trident-bearing one was able, by thought alone and in a single instant, to burn this entire moving and unmoving world;

children.text: kimatra dagdhuṃ tripuraṃ pinākī svayaṃ gataścātra gaṇaiś ca sārdham ||
children.translated_text: what need was there for <s>Pinākī</s> himself to go there with his gaṇas to burn <s>Tripura</s>?

children.text: rathena kiṃ ceṣuvareṇa tasya gaṇaiś ca kiṃ devagaṇaiś ca śaṃbhoḥ
children.translated_text: What need had <s>Śambhu</s> of a chariot or of that excellent arrow? What need had he of gaṇas or of hosts of gods,
when his power to burn the three cities was undiminished? So said those headed by <s>Aja</s> and <s>Indra</s>.
"Surely we think that the Blessed <s>Pinākī</s> has undertaken all this to unfold it as play;

children.text: vyavasthitaśceti tathānyathā ced āḍambareṇāsya phalaṃ kimanyat ||
children.translated_text: he is established so. Otherwise, what other fruit could there be in this pageantry of his?"

children.text: puratrayasyāsya samīpavartī sureśvarair nandimukhaiś ca nandī
children.translated_text: Near this <s>Tripura</s>, with the lords of gods and with gaṇas headed by <s>Nandin</s>,
<s>Nandin</s>, the lord of gaṇas, shone with the goddess like <s>Meru</s>, the world-chariot, with its eight peaks.
Then, seeing the lord of gods, <s>Īśvara</s>, together with his gaṇas and with the daughter of the mountain,
the host of gods, stationed above the arena-ground of <s>Tripura</s>, itself followed him.

children.text: jagattrayaṃ sarvamivāparaṃ tat puratrayaṃ tatra vibhāti samyak
children.translated_text: That <s>Tripura</s> shone there fully, like another whole triple world,

children.text: nareśvaraiścaiva gaṇaiś ca devaiḥ suretaraiś ca trividhairmunīndrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with kings, gaṇas, gods, non-gods, and the three classes, O chiefs of sages.

children.text: atha sajyaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā śarvaḥ saṃdhāya taṃ śaram
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śarva</s>, having strung the bow and set that arrow upon it,
joined it with the <s>Pāśupata</s> missile and fixed his thought on <s>Tripura</s>.
While <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, stood there with bow drawn wide,
at that time the cities swiftly came into oneness.
When <s>Tripura</s> had become one and had drawn together,
there arose a tumultuous joy among the high-souled deities.

children.text: tato devagaṇāḥ sarve siddhāś ca paramarṣayaḥ
children.translated_text: Then all the hosts of gods, the siddhas, and the supreme seers
sent forth cries of "Victory!" as they praised the eight-formed one.
Then the Blessed <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to the one who cast down <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye,
to <s>Umāpati</s>, moved by play, when the conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s> too had arrived.
This action of yours is fitting, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O <s>Parameśvara</s>,

children.text: pūrvadevāś ca devāś ca samāstava yataḥ prabho ||
children.translated_text: since the former gods and the gods are all equal to you, O lord.

children.text: tathāpi devā dharmiṣṭhāḥ pūrvadevāś ca pāpinaḥ
children.translated_text: Even so, the gods are most righteous, while the former gods are sinful;
therefore, O lord of the world, you ought here to give up this play.

children.text: kiṃ rathena dhvajeneśa tava dagdhuṃ puratrayam
children.translated_text: What need have you of a chariot or banner, O Lord, for burning the three cities,

children.text: iṣuṇā bhūtasaṃghaiś ca viṣṇunā ca mayā prabho ||
children.translated_text: or of an arrow, the hosts of beings, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or me, O lord?
When the conjunction with <s>Puṣya</s> has arrived, you ought here to burn the city;

children.text: yāvanna yānti deveśa viyogaṃ tāvadeva tu ||
children.translated_text: only before they fall apart, O lord of gods, before they enter separation,

children.text: dagdhumarhasi śīghraṃ tvaṃ trīṇyetāni purāṇi vai
children.translated_text: you ought swiftly to burn these three cities.
Then the god <s>Mahādeva</s>, the omniscient one, looked at it.
In that very instant three-eyed <s>Virūpākṣa</s> made the three cities into ashes.
<s>Soma</s>, the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Kālāgni</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s> too,

children.text: śare vyavasthitāḥ sarve devamūcuḥ praṇamya tam
children.translated_text: all positioned in the arrow, bowed to that god and said:
"Though the three cities have been burned by your glance, O lord of gods,
for our welfare, O lord of gods, you ought here to release the arrow."

children.text: atha saṃmṛjya dhanuṣo jyāṃ hasan tripurārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, smiling, <s>Tripurārdana</s> stroked the bowstring of his bow,
and the Lord, drawing it back to his ear, released the arrow, O best of brahmins.
Having burned <s>Tripura</s> in that instant, the arrow that ended <s>Tripura</s>
approached the god of gods, bowed, and stood before him.
The three burned cities, surrounded by hundreds of crores of daityas, shone forth,
burned by that arrow, like the three worlds by <s>Rudra</s> at the end of an aeon.

children.text: ye pūjayanti tatrāpi daityā rudraṃ sabāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those daityas there who worshiped <s>Rudra</s>, together with their kinsmen,
then attained the status of <s>Śambhu</s>'s gaṇas through the power of the rite of worship.

children.text: na kiṃcid abruvan devāḥ sendropendrā gaṇeśvarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and the lords of gaṇas, said nothing,
out of fear, merely looking at the god and at the goddess, the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>.
Seeing the army of the gods terrified, the foremost of gods
then said to the gods, "What is it?" They bowed to him on every side.
They venerated <s>Nandin</s>, the one adorned with the moon; they venerated the daughter of the mountain king.

children.text: vavandire cādrisutāsutaṃ prabhuṃ vavandire devagaṇā maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: They venerated the lord who was the son of the mountain-daughter; the hosts of gods venerated <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tuṣṭāva hṛdaye brahmā devaiḥ saha samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Together with the gods, <s>Brahmā</s>, composed in mind, praised
the god <s>Bhava</s>, the enemy of <s>Tripura</s>, the Lord, along with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The blessed Grandfather said:
Be gracious, O lord of gods; be gracious, O <s>Parameśvara</s>.
Be gracious, O lord of the worlds; be gracious, imperishable giver of bliss.
Homage to you, the five-faced <s>Rudra</s> of Rudras, whose forms are fifty crores,
who is seated in the three selves and is the principle of knowledge.
Homage, homage to <s>Śiva</s>, to the principle of <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Aghora</s>,
to the one who is the eightfold principle of <s>Aghora</s>, whose form is the twelvefold self.
Assuming in this world a very beautiful form, shining like crores of lightning flashes, an eightfold radiance,
you abide as the <s>Śiva</s>-self.
Homage to the fire-colored, terrible one, whose body is half <s>Ambikā</s>,
to the deathless one who grants liberation to the white, dark, and red forms.
Homage to the eldest, to the <s>Rudra</s>-formed one, to <s>Soma</s>, and to the giver of boons;
homage indeed to the one who is the three worlds, the three gods, and the vaṣaṭ-call.
Homage to you whose form is the sky in the middle, who stands in the sky;
homage to you who are the eight fields and eight forms, the eight principles.

children.text: caturdhā ca caturdhā ca caturdhā saṃsthitāya ca
children.translated_text: Homage to the one established fourfold, and fourfold, and fourfold,
and fivefold and fivefold, whose body is the five mantras.
Homage, homage to the one of sixty-four kinds, to the syllable A;
homage, homage to the one whose form is the thirty-two principles, to the syllable U.
Homage, homage to the one whose form is the sixteenfold self, to the syllable M;
homage to the one whose form is the eightfold self, whose nature is the half-mātrā.
Homage to you as <s>Oṃkāra</s>, and to the one established fourfold;
homage, homage to the god who is lord of the sky and lord of heaven.
Homage indeed to the seven worlds, to the lord of <s>Pātāla</s> and hell;
to the eight fields and eight forms, and to the one higher than the highest.

children.text: sahasraśirase tubhyaṃ sahasrāya ca te namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to you, the thousand-headed one, and homage to you as the thousandfold one;
to <s>Śarva</s>, the supreme-standing one, endowed with a thousand feet.
Homage to the one whose form is the principle of the nine selves, whose own power is ninefold and eightfold,
who again is the eightfold radiance and likewise the form of eight times eight.
Homage to you, whose principle is the sixty-fourfold self, and who again is eightfold;
to you who are encircled by the eight guṇas, who possess qualities and yet are without qualities.
Homage to you who stand at the root, who dwell in the eternal place,
who are established in the navel-circle and make the sound in the heart.
Homage to the one who stands in the throat and in the opening of the palate,
who is established between the brows and who stands within the sound.
Homage to the one established in the orb of the moon, to <s>Śiva</s>, whose form is <s>Śiva</s>,
whose form is fire, moon, and sun, whose form is the thirty-six powers.
Homage to the one who, having covered the worlds threefold, has the nature of a sleeping serpent,
who is established in three ways and whose form is made of the three sacred fires.
Homage to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the peaceful one, to <s>Maheśa</s>, to the wielder of <s>Pināka</s>,
to the omniscient refuge, and indeed to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Homage to you as <s>Aghora</s>; homage to you as <s>Vāmadeva</s>.
Homage to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; homage, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.
Homage to the one whose radiance is thirtyfold, who is beyond peace;
homage to you, <s>Ananteśa</s>, subtle and supreme.
Homage to you, the single-eyed one; homage to you, the one <s>Rudra</s>.
Homage to you of three forms, to <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, to the crested one;
to the one seated on <s>Ananta</s>'s seat, to the infinite maker of ends,
homage to the stainless, the vast, whose limbs are stainless.
To you who are established on the stainless seat, whose form is the meaning and object of the stainless reality,
who are established within the seat of yoga, the yogin who grants yoga.
To you who are always established in the hearts of yogins like the point of a grain of wild rice,
to you who are <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal), and to you who are ever intent on <s>pratyāhāra</s>.
And to you who stand in the proper station of those devoted to <s>pratyāhāra</s>,
obeisance to you as <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), and to you who delight in <s>dhāraṇā</s>.
And to you who are set before those joined to the practice of <s>dhāraṇā</s>,
obeisance to you as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), whose form is meditation, who are reached by meditation.
Obeisance to you who are to be meditated upon, who are reached by what is meditated upon, who are the meditation of the object of meditation;
obeisance to you who are the object of meditation even for those who are themselves objects of meditation, the most worthy object of meditation.
Obeisance to you who are attained by <s>samādhāna</s> (meditative absorption), and to you who are <s>samādhāna</s> itself;
to you whose form is the object beyond conceptual distinction for those devoted to <s>samādhāna</s>.

children.text: dagdhvoddhṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ tvayādya jagattrayaṃ rudra puratrayaṃ hi
children.translated_text: Today, O <s>Rudra</s>, you have burned and lifted away all this, the three worlds and indeed the three cities.

children.text: kaḥ stotumicchet kathamīdṛśaṃ tvāṃ stoṣye hi tuṣṭāya śivāya tubhyam ||
children.translated_text: Who would wish to praise you, and how? Yet I shall praise you, <s>Śiva</s>, because you are pleased.

children.text: bhaktyā ca tuṣṭyādbhutadarśanācca martyā amartyā api devadeva
children.translated_text: Through devotion, satisfaction, and the sight of this wonder, O god of gods, mortals and immortals alike,

children.text: ete gaṇāḥ siddhagaṇaiḥ praṇāmaṃ kurvanti deveśa gaṇeśa tubhyam ||
children.translated_text: these gaṇas, together with hosts of siddhas, make obeisance to you, O lord of gods, O lord of gaṇas.

children.text: nirīkṣaṇādeva vibho'si dagdhuṃ puratrayaṃ caiva jagattrayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: By a mere glance, O mighty one, you are able to burn the three cities and the three worlds.

children.text: līlālasenāṃbikayā kṣaṇena dagdhaṃ kileṣuś ca tadātha muktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With playful ease, together with <s>Ambikā</s>, they were burned in a moment; then the arrow too was released.

children.text: kṛto rathaśceṣuvaraś ca śubhraṃ śarasanaṃ te tripurakṣayāya
children.translated_text: A chariot was made, and also an excellent arrow and a bright bow for you, for the destruction of <s>Tripura</s>.

children.text: anekayatnaiś ca mayātha tubhyaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ phalaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ surasiddhasaṃghaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Though I made many efforts for you, no result was seen, nor was it seen by the hosts of gods and siddhas.

children.text: ratho rathī devavaro hariś ca rudraḥ svayaṃ śakrapitāmahau ca
children.translated_text: The chariot, the charioteer, the best of gods, <s>Hari</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> himself, and <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Pitāmaha</s> too:

children.text: tvameva sarve bhagavan kathaṃ tu stoṣye hyatoṣyaṃ praṇipatya mūrdhnā ||
children.translated_text: you alone are all of them, O blessed one. How then shall I praise you, who cannot be fully pleased, as I bow my head?

children.text: anantapādas tvam anantabāhur anantamūrdhāntakaraḥ śivaś ca
children.translated_text: You have infinite feet, infinite arms, and infinite heads; you are the maker of the end and <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: anantamūrtiḥ katham īdṛśaṃ tvāṃ toṣye kathamīdṛśaṃ tvām ||
children.translated_text: You have infinite forms. How shall I satisfy such a one as you? How shall I satisfy one such as you?

children.text: namonamaḥ sarvavide śivāya rudrāya śarvāya bhavāya tubhyam
children.translated_text: Obeisance again and again to <s>Śiva</s>, knower of all, to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Bhava</s>, to you.
To the gross, to the subtle, to the exceedingly subtle beyond subtlety, to the knower of the subtle meaning, to the ordainer.

children.text: sraṣṭre namaḥ sarvasurāsurāṇāṃ bhartre ca hartre jagatāṃ vidhātre
children.translated_text: Obeisance to the creator of all gods and asuras, to the sustainer and destroyer of the worlds, to the ordainer,

children.text: netre surāṇāmasureśvarāṇāṃ dātre praśāstre mama sarvaśāstre ||
children.translated_text: to the guide of the gods and of the lords of asuras, to the giver, the ruler, my teacher in every śāstra.
To you who are known through the Vedānta, who are utterly pure, who are constantly praised by those who know the meaning of the Veda,
to you whose form is the Veda itself, to <s>Bhava</s>, to you as end, as middle, and as the perfect middle.

children.text: ādyantaśūnyāya ca saṃsthitāya tathā tvaśūnyāya ca liṅgine ca
children.translated_text: To you who are established as without beginning or end, and likewise as not empty, and as the bearer of the liṅga,

children.text: aliṅgine liṅgamayāya tubhyaṃ liṅgāya vedādimayāya sākṣāt ||
children.translated_text: to you who are without liṅga, who are made of the liṅga, to you as the liṅga itself, directly made of the beginning of the Veda.
To <s>Rudra</s>, who cut off the head of my primal god, the sacrifice-formed one,

children.text: vidhvāntabhaṅgaṃ mama kartumīśa dṛṣṭvaiva bhūmau karajāgrakoṭyā ||
children.translated_text: O Lord, merely seeing you shatter my darkness on the earth with the tip of your fingernail.

children.text: aho vicitraṃ tava devadeva viceṣṭitaṃ sarvasurāsureśa
children.translated_text: Ah, wonderful is your activity, O god of gods, O lord of all gods and asuras.

children.text: dehīva devaiḥ saha devakāryaṃ kariṣyase nirguṇarūpatattva
children.translated_text: As if embodied, together with the gods you will perform the gods' task, though your true form is without qualities.

children.text: ekaṃ sthūlaṃ sūkṣmamekaṃ susūkṣmaṃ mūrtāmūrtaṃ mūrtamekaṃ hyamūrtam
children.translated_text: One, gross; one, subtle; one, exceedingly subtle; formed and formless; one formed, indeed formless:

children.text: ekaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vāṅmayaṃ caikamīśaṃ dhyeyaṃ caikaṃ tattvamatrādbhutaṃ te ||
children.translated_text: one seen, one made of speech, one Lord, one object of meditation; this single reality of yours is wondrous.

children.text: svapne dṛṣṭaṃ yatpadārthaṃ hyalakṣyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ nūnaṃ bhāti manye na cāpi
children.translated_text: What object is seen in a dream is hard to grasp; though seen, surely it appears, I think, and yet it does not.

children.text: mūrtirno vai daivakīśāna devairlakṣyā yatnairapyalakṣyaṃ kathaṃ tu ||
children.translated_text: Your divine form, O <s>Īśāna</s>, is not to be perceived by the gods; how could what is imperceptible be grasped even by efforts?

children.text: divyaḥ kva deveśa bhavatprabhāvo vayaṃ kva bhaktiḥ kva ca te stutiś ca
children.translated_text: Where, O lord of gods, is your divine majesty, and where are we? Where is devotion, and where is this praise of you?

children.text: tathāpi bhaktyā vilapantamīśa pitāmahaṃ māṃ bhagavankṣamasva ||
children.translated_text: Even so, O Lord, forgive me, <s>Pitāmaha</s>, who lament in devotion, O blessed one.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ya imaṃ śṛṇuyāddvijottamā bhuvi devaṃ praṇipatya paṭhet
children.translated_text: Whoever on earth hears this, O best twice-borns, and recites it after bowing to the god,

children.text: sa ca muñcati pāpabandhanaṃ bhavabhaktyā puraśāsituḥ stavam ||
children.translated_text: he is released from the bondage of sin through devotion to <s>Bhava</s>: this hymn to the ruler of the cities.

children.text: śrutvā ca bhaktyā caturānanena stuto hasañśailasutāṃ nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: Having heard the hymn by which he had been praised with devotion by the four-faced one, he smiled and looked at the daughter of the mountain.

children.text: stavaṃ tadā prāha mahānubhāvaṃ mahābhujo mandaraśṛṅgavāsī ||
children.translated_text: Then the great-armed, high-souled one who dwells on the peak of <s>Mandara</s> spoke.
<s>Śiva</s> said:

children.text: stavenānena tuṣṭo'smi tava bhaktyā ca padmaja
children.translated_text: I am pleased by this hymn and by your devotion, O lotus-born one.

children.text: varān varaya bhadraṃ te devānāṃ ca yathepsitān ||
children.translated_text: Choose boons, and may there be welfare for you, and also the things desired by the gods.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then the blessed lotus-born one bowed to the lord of gods,
and, folding his hands in reverence, spoke this with a joyful mind.
<s>Śrī Pitāmaha</s> said:
O blessed lord of the gods of gods, O <s>Tripurāntaka</s>, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: tvayi bhaktiṃ parāṃ me 'dya prasīda parameśvaram ||
children.translated_text: grant me today supreme devotion toward you; be gracious, O supreme Lord.
And for all the gods, O lord who grants every object of desire, may there be devotion toward you.
Be gracious through the yoga of devotion and by always being the charioteer.
The blessed <s>Janārdana</s> too bowed to <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and, folding his hands in reverence, spoke to the three-eyed one with <s>Ambā</s>.
O Lord, I always desire to be your vehicle; be gracious to me.

children.text: tvayi bhaktiṃ ca deveśa devadeva namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: And may I have devotion toward you, O lord of gods, O god of gods. Obeisance to you.

children.text: sāmarthyaṃ ca sadā mahyaṃ bhavantaṃ voḍhumīśvaram
children.translated_text: And may I always have the capacity to bear you, the Lord,

children.text: sarvajñatvaṃ ca varada sarvagatvaṃ ca śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: and omniscience, O boon-giver, and omnipresence, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard the request of those two, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the supreme Lord,

children.text: sārathye vāhanatve ca kalpayāmāsa vai bhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhava</s> indeed appointed them to the roles of charioteer and vehicle.

children.text: dattvā tasmai brahmaṇe viṣṇave ca dagdhvā daityāndevadevo mahātmā
children.translated_text: Having granted it to that <s>Brahmā</s> and to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and having burned the daityas, the great-souled god of gods

children.text: sārdhaṃ devyā nandinā bhūtasaṃghair antardhānaṃ kārayāmāsa śarvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s>, together with the goddess, <s>Nandin</s>, and the hosts of beings, made himself disappear.
Then, when <s>Maheśvara</s> had gone from the battle together with his gaṇas,
the lords of the gods, greatly amazed, bowed to <s>Bhava</s> and <s>Pārvatī</s>,
and, freed from sorrow, went then to heaven on their own vehicles.
The lords of gods, lords of sages, lords of gaṇas, and the radiant solar deities went as well.
This holy account of <s>Tripurāri</s>, made long ago by <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: yaḥ paṭhecchrāddhakāle vā daive karmaṇi ca dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever reads it at the time of a śrāddha or in a rite for the gods, O twice-born,

children.text: śrāvayedvā dvijān bhaktyā brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati
children.translated_text: or has the twice-born hear it with devotion, goes to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: mānasairvācikaiḥ pāpais tathā vai kāyikaiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From mental and verbal sins, and again from bodily ones,
from gross, subtle, and very subtle sins arising from great crimes,
and from sins, O best of the twice-born, arising from lesser transgressions,

children.text: pāpaiś ca mucyate jantuḥ śrutvādhyāyamimaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: a creature is freed by hearing this auspicious chapter.
His enemies come to destruction; in battle he becomes victorious.

children.text: sarvarogairna bādhyeta āpado na spṛśanti tam
children.translated_text: He is not afflicted by any diseases; calamities do not touch him.
He obtains wealth, long life, fame, knowledge, and incomparable power.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge tripuradāhe brahmastavo nāma dvisaptitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, in the burning of Tripura, the seventy-second chapter, called <s>Brahmastava</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: gate maheśvare deve dagdhvā ca tripuraṃ kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: When the god <s>Maheśvara</s> had gone, after burning Tripura in an instant,
the blessed lotus-born one spoke in the assembly of the lords of gods.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:
Having abandoned the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s> in <s>liṅga</s> form,
the great-radiant grandson of <s>Tāraka</s>, the powerful son of <s>Tāraka</s>,
the daitya <s>Tārakākṣa</s>, and valorous <s>Kamalākṣa</s>,

children.text: vidyunmālī ca daityeśaḥ anye cāpi sabāndhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, lord of daityas, and others too, together with their kinsmen,

children.text: tyaktvā devaṃ mahādevaṃ māyayā ca hareḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: having abandoned the god <s>Mahādeva</s>, and through the māyā of <s>Hari</s>, O lord,
all were destroyed and shattered, together with their own cities.
Therefore <s>Sadāśiva</s> in <s>liṅga</s> form is always to be worshiped,
for the lords of gods endure only so long as their worship lasts.
<s>Śiva</s> is to be worshiped constantly, with faith, by the foremost gods.
The world consists wholly of the <s>liṅga</s>; everything is established in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Therefore one who desires his own success should thoroughly worship the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: sarve liṅgārcanādeva devā daityāś ca dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All gods, daityas, and dānavas, through <s>liṅga</s> worship alone,
yakṣas, vidyādharas, siddhas, rākṣasas, flesh-eaters,
ancestors, sages, and also piśācas, kinnaras, and the rest,
having worshiped the form of the <s>liṅga</s>, attained perfection; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: tasmālliṅgaṃ yajennityaṃ yena kenāpi vā surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore worship the <s>liṅga</s> daily, by whatever means, O gods.

children.text: paśavaś ca vayaṃ tasya devadevasya dhīmataḥ
children.translated_text: We too are <s>paśus</s> (bound beings) of that wise god of gods;

children.text: paśutvaṃ ca parityajya kṛtvā pāśupataṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and after casting off the state of <s>paśu</s> and performing the <s>Pāśupata</s> observance,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, the eternal one in <s>liṅga</s> form, is to be worshiped.

children.text: viśodhya caiva bhūtāni pañcabhiḥ praṇavaiḥ samam ||
children.translated_text: Having purified the elements with five <s>praṇavas</s> (sacred syllables),
together with five <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls), O foremost gods,
and then with four <s>praṇavas</s>, intent on <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
with three <s>praṇavas</s>, O gods, and with such <s>prāṇāyāmas</s>,
having placed the <s>oṃkāra</s> in two ways, intent on <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
then, uttering the <s>oṃkāra</s> and restraining <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>,
and filling all the limbs with the nectar of knowledge and with the <s>praṇava</s>,
the three <s>guṇas</s>, what is called fourfold, and <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, O well-vowed ones,

children.text: tanmātrāṇi ca bhūtāni tathā buddhīndriyāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>tanmātras</s>, the elements, and also the organs of understanding,
having purified the organs of action and likewise the pair called <s>puruṣa</s>,
having made the body into the conscious self, he should touch himself, saying, "Fire is ash."

children.text: vāyurbhasmeti ca vyoma tathāmbhaḥ pṛthivī tathā
children.translated_text: Saying, "Air is ash," and likewise space, water, and earth,

children.text: triyāyuṣaṃ trisaṃdhyaṃ ca dhūlayed bhasitena yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whoever dusts himself with ash while reciting the Tryāyuṣa and at the three <s>sandhyās</s>,

children.text: sa yogī sarvatattvajño vrataṃ pāśupataṃ tvidam
children.translated_text: that yogin is a knower of all principles; this indeed is the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow,
taught by <s>Bhava</s> for release from the bond, O best of gods.
After performing the <s>Pāśupata</s> observance in this way and worshiping <s>Parameśvara</s>

children.text: liṅge purā mayā dṛṣṭe viṣṇunā ca mahātmanā ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>liṅga</s> that was seen long ago by me and by great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
within only a year, O gods, they are no longer born as <s>paśus</s>.
By us, having carefully worshiped the god in all undertakings,
I think the Lord should be made both external and internal.

children.text: pratijñā mama viṣṇoś ca divyaiṣā surasattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is my divine vow and <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s, O best of gods,

children.text: munīnāṃ ca na saṃdehas tasmāt sampūjayecchivam
children.translated_text: and also that of the sages; there is no doubt. Therefore one should worship <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: sā hānistanmahacchidraṃ sa mohaḥ sā ca mūkatā ||
children.translated_text: That is loss, that is a great breach, that is delusion, and that is dumbness:

children.text: yatkṣaṇaṃ vā muhūrtaṃ vā śivamekaṃ na cintayet
children.translated_text: any instant or muhūrta in which one does not think of <s>Śiva</s> alone.
Those who are devoted to <s>Bhava</s>, whose minds are bowed down to <s>Bhava</s>,
and who are intent on remembering <s>Bhava</s>, are not vessels of suffering.
Pleasant mansions, divine ornaments, and women,
and wealth up to the point of satisfaction: these are the fruit of the rite of <s>Śiva</s>-worship.

children.text: ye vāñchanti mahābhogān rājyaṃ ca tridaśālaye
children.translated_text: Those who desire great enjoyments and sovereignty in the abode of the Thirty,
let them worship always, at all times, <s>Maheśvara</s> in <s>liṅga</s> form.

children.text: hatvā bhittvā ca bhūtāni dagdhvā sarvamidaṃ jagat ||
children.translated_text: Even after slaying, splitting apart, and burning beings and this whole world,

children.text: yajedekaṃ virūpākṣaṃ na pāpaiḥ sa pralipyate
children.translated_text: if one worships the one <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, he is not stained by sins.
For the mountain-<s>liṅga</s> of mine is bowed to by all the gods.
Having spoken thus, and having formerly worshiped <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the three worlds,
he praised the three-eyed god of gods with words dear to him.
From that time onward, the gods headed by <s>Śakra</s> worshiped <s>Īśvara</s>,
having directly undertaken the <s>Pāśupata</s> observance, their bodies covered with ash.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge brahmaproktaliṅgārcanavidhir nāma trisaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the seventy-third chapter, called 'The Rule for Worshiping the Liṅga, Spoken by <s>Brahmā</s>.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having thus fashioned the liṅgas in accordance with their respective authority,
<s>Viśvakarman</s>, by the command of <s>Brahmā</s>, gave them to those beings, O lord.
The liṅga made of sapphire was always worshiped by <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
<s>Śakra</s> received one made of ruby, and the son of <s>Viśravas</s> one made of gold.

children.text: viśvedevās tathā raupyaṃ vasavaḥ kāntikaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: The <s>Viśvedevās</s> likewise received one of silver, and the <s>Vasus</s> an auspicious one of kāntika metal;
<s>Vāyu</s> received one made of ārakūṭa, and the two <s>Aśvins</s> an earthen one forever.
King <s>Varuṇa</s> received one of crystal, and the <s>Ādityas</s> one made of copper;
the wise moon-king received one of pearl, likewise an unsurpassed liṅga.
The great serpents beginning with <s>Ananta</s> received an auspicious one made of coral;

children.text: daityā hyayomayaṃ liṅgaṃ rākṣasāś ca mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the daityas received an iron liṅga, and the great-souled rākṣasas
one made of three metals; the guhyakas received one made of all metals, and so did the gaṇas.
<s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> herself received one of sand, and the Mothers also, O best of the twice-born.

children.text: dārujaṃ nairṛtir bhaktyā yamo mārakataṃ śubham
children.translated_text: <s>Nairṛti</s>, with devotion, received one made of wood, and <s>Yama</s> an auspicious one of emerald;

children.text: nīlādyāś ca tathā rudrāḥ śuddhaṃ bhasmamayaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Rudras</s> beginning with <s>Nīla</s> received an auspicious one made of pure ash.
<s>Lakṣmī</s> received one made from the lakṣmī tree, and <s>Guha</s> one consisting of cow dung;
the sages, O tigers among sages, received an excellent one made of tips of kuśa grass.
The goddesses beginning with <s>Vāmā</s> received a flower-liṅga, while <s>Manonmanī</s> received a perfume-liṅga;

children.text: sarasvatī ca ratnena kṛtaṃ rudrasya vāgbhavā ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sarasvatī</s>, born of speech, received one made of jewels for <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Durgā</s> received an unsurpassed golden liṅga of <s>Mahādeva</s>, together with its pedestal;

children.text: ugrā piṣṭamayaṃ sarve mantrā hyājyamayaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ugrā</s> received one made of flour, and all the mantras an auspicious one made of ghee.
All the <s>Vedas</s> received one made of curds, and the piśācas one made of lead;
each obtained its proper station by the favor of <s>Brahmā</s>.
What more need be said here? This world of moving and unmoving beings
stands here after fully worshiping the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>; there is no doubt.
They say that the liṅga is sixfold because of the distinctions among materials;
their subdivisions are remembered as forty-four.
The first is said to be stone-born, and that indeed is fourfold;
the second is jewel-born, and that, O best sages, is sevenfold.
The third, the metal-born liṅga of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, is eightfold;
the fourth is the wood-born liṅga, and that is said to be sixteenfold.

children.text: mṛnmayaṃ pañcamaṃ liṅgaṃ dvidhā bhinnaṃ dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: The fifth, the clay-made liṅga, is divided into two, O best of the twice-born;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ tu kṣaṇikaṃ liṅgaṃ saptadhā parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: but the sixth, the temporary liṅga, is proclaimed as sevenfold.
The jewel-born liṅga grants prosperity; the stone-born grants all accomplishments;
the metal-born directly grants wealth, and the wood-born grants success in enjoyment.
And the clay-made liṅga, O foremost brahmins, is auspicious and produces every accomplishment;

children.text: śailajaṃ cottamaṃ proktaṃ madhyamaṃ caiva dhātujam ||
children.translated_text: the stone-born is declared to be best, and the metal-born middling.

children.text: bahudhā liṅgabhedāś ca nava caiva samāsataḥ
children.translated_text: The distinctions of liṅgas are many, and, in summary, nine as well;
at the base is <s>Brahmā</s>, and in the middle <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the three worlds;
above is <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>; <s>Sadāśiva</s> is named the praṇava.
The liṅga's pedestal is <s>Mahādevī</s>, the three-guṇa, threefold <s>Ambikā</s>.

children.text: tayā ca pūjayedyastu devī devaś ca pūjitau
children.translated_text: Whoever worships by means of her has worshiped both the Goddess and the God.

children.text: śailajaṃ ratnajaṃ vāpi dhātujaṃ vāpi dārujam ||
children.translated_text: Whether stone-born, jewel-born, metal-born, or wood-born,

children.text: mṛnmayaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ vāpi bhaktyā sthāpya phalaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: or made of clay or temporary, when installed with devotion it brings an auspicious fruit.
Praised by <s>Surendra</s>, the lotus-born one, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the lord of waters, and the lord of wealth,
by siddhas, vidyādharas, serpent-kings, yakṣas, dānavas, and kinnaras,
and by the sounds of divine drums, the very meritorious soul
passes in order through the worlds <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svar</s>, and <s>Mahas</s>, and beyond the world of <s>Jana</s>,

children.text: tapaḥ satyaṃ parākramya bhāsayan svena tejasā ||
children.translated_text: then through <s>Tapas</s> and <s>Satya</s>, illuminating them with his own splendor.
With his own sword set upon the good path of liṅga-installation,
he quickly pierces the cosmic egg and goes forth without fear.

children.text: śailajaṃ ratnajaṃ vāpi dhātujaṃ vāpi dārujam
children.translated_text: Having set up a stone-born, jewel-born, metal-born, or wood-born liṅga,
or a clay-made or temporary one, he should establish the whole embodied form.

children.text: vidhinā caiva kṛtvā tu skandomāsahitaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: And having made it according to rule, auspicious and accompanied by <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Umā</s>,
the man who installs a liṅga resembling jasmine and cow's milk

children.text: nṛṇāṃ tanuṃ samāsthāya sthito rudro na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: has <s>Rudra</s> standing in him, having taken on a human body; there is no doubt.
By seeing it and touching it, people attain repose.
Even in hundreds of ages I could not properly describe his merit,

children.text: śakyate naiva viprendrās tasmād vai sthāpayet tathā ||
children.translated_text: O foremost brahmins; therefore one should install it in that way.
For all mortals, the auspicious divine body of the all-pervading Lord
is whole and fit for contemplation; for yogins alone it is without parts.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śivaliṅgabhedasaṃsthāpanādivarṇanaṃ nāma catuḥsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the seventy-fourth chapter, called 'Description of the Varieties and Installation of the <s>Śivaliṅga</s> and Related Matters.'
The sages said:

children.text: niṣkalo nirmalo nityaḥ sakalatvaṃ kathaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: How has the partless, stainless, eternal one come to possess parts?

children.text: vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ yathā śrutam ||
children.translated_text: You ought to tell us this, as before, just as it was heard.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Some knowers of ultimate reality, having heard of the unborn one as having the form of the praṇava,
at the head of the <s>Śruti</s>, O foremost brahmins, called him consciousness.
Knowledge whose object is sound and the other sense-fields is called knowledge;
others say that such knowledge is free from error, while still others say, 'Not so.'
Knowledge that is stainless, pure, without conceptual construction, and without support,
other sages, O twice-born, call the knowledge that illuminates the guru.
By knowledge alone liberation comes; grace is for the accomplishment of knowledge.
By both the yogin is released; there he becomes filled with bliss.
Some sages say that his connection is through action,
after he has withdrawn, by his own will alone, the form fashioned by imagination.

children.text: dyaurmūrdhā tu vibhostasya khaṃ nābhiḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ
children.translated_text: Heaven is the head of that all-pervading Lord, and space is the navel of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
The moon, sun, and fire are the eyes, and the directions are the hearing of the great-souled one.
The netherworld is his feet, and the ocean is his garment.

children.text: devāstasya bhujāḥ sarve nakṣatrāṇi ca bhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: All the gods are his arms, and the constellations are his ornaments.
<s>Prakṛti</s> is his wife, and <s>Puruṣa</s> is called the <s>liṅga</s> (sign).

children.text: vaktrādvai brāhmaṇāḥ sarve brahmā ca bhagavānprabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: From his mouth came all the brāhmaṇas, and the blessed lord <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: indropendrau bhujābhyāṃ tu kṣatriyāś ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: From the arms of the great-souled one came <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, and the kṣatriyas.
From the region of his thighs came the vaiśyas, and from the foot of <s>Pinākin</s> came the śūdras.
<s>Puṣkarāvartaka</s> and the others are proclaimed to be his hairs.

children.text: vāyavo ghrāṇajāstasya gatiḥ śrautaṃ smṛtis tathā ||
children.translated_text: The winds are born from his nostrils; his movement is the śruti and likewise the smṛti.
Thus by this very one, whose nature is action, the activity of <s>Prakṛti</s> is set in motion.

children.text: puṃsāṃ tu puruṣaḥ śrīmān jñānagamyo na cānyathā ||
children.translated_text: But for human beings, the glorious <s>Puruṣa</s> is reached through knowledge, and not otherwise.
Above thousands of sacrifices of action, the sacrifice of austerity is superior.
Above thousands of sacrifices of austerity, the sacrifice of <s>japa</s> (recitation) is superior.
Above thousands of sacrifices of <s>japa</s>, the sacrifice of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is superior.
There is nothing higher than the sacrifice of meditation; meditation is the means to knowledge.

children.text: yadā samarase niṣṭho yogī dhyānena paśyati
children.translated_text: When the yogin, fixed in sameness of essence, sees through meditation,
then <s>Śiva</s> is present to him who delights in the sacrifice of meditation.
For those who know, there is no injunction of purification, expiation, and the like.
All people who know the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> are purified by knowledge.

children.text: nāsti kriyā ca lokeṣu sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: When considered carefully, in the worlds there is no ritual action, pleasure, or pain.

children.text: dharmādharmau japo homo dhyānināṃ saṃnidhiḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: For meditators, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, recitation and oblation, are always present only as such.
The <s>liṅga</s> is to be known as consisting of supreme bliss, pure, <s>Śiva</s>, imperishable,

children.text: niṣkalaṃ sarvagaṃ jñeyaṃ yogināṃ hṛdi saṃsthitam ||
children.translated_text: partless, all-pervading, and established in the hearts of yogins.
The <s>liṅga</s>, O twice-borns, is said to be twofold: external and internal.
The external is gross, O best sages; the internal is subtle, O twice-borns.
Those devoted to sacrifices of action are gross; they delight in worship of the gross <s>liṅga</s>.
The gross image exists only for forming devotion among those who lack true being, and not otherwise.

children.text: ādhyātmikaṃ ca yalliṅgaṃ pratyakṣaṃ yasya no bhavet
children.translated_text: If the spiritual <s>liṅga</s> is not directly manifest to someone,

children.text: asau mūḍho bahiḥ sarvaṃ kalpayitvaiva nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: that fool simply imagines everything outside, and nothing else.
For those who know, the subtle, stainless, imperishable one becomes directly manifest,
just as the gross form is fashioned from clay, wood, and the like for those who are not fit.
Other knowers of the true meaning say, upon inquiry, that no object exists.
Therefore all is made of <s>Śiva</s>, whether partless or with parts.

children.text: vyomaikamapi dṛṣṭaṃ hi śarāvaṃ prati suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: Although space is one, it is indeed seen with reference to each bowl, O well-vowed ones.
Others say that there is both separateness and non-separateness in regard to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
For the sake of the world's cognition, the sun, though standing in one place,
is seen as manifold in vessels of water, O well-vowed ones, though it is one.

children.text: jantavo divi bhūmau ca sarve vai pāñcabhautikāḥ
children.translated_text: Creatures in heaven and on earth are all made of the five elements,
yet they are seen as many because of distinctions of species and individual.
Whatever is seen or heard, know that to have <s>Śiva</s> as its essence.
Difference among people in this world is, upon inquiry, an appearance.

children.text: svapne ca vipulān bhogān bhuktvā martyaḥ sukhī bhavet
children.translated_text: In a dream, after enjoying abundant pleasures, a mortal may become happy,

children.text: duḥkhī ca bhogaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca nānubhūtaṃ vicārataḥ ||
children.translated_text: or unhappy; but enjoyment, pleasure, and pain have not really been experienced, when considered carefully.
Thus also do others speak, all of them having reached the true meaning of the Veda:
in the hearts of transmigrating beings, the manifest supreme Lord is directly present.

children.text: yogināṃ niṣkalo devo jñānināṃ ca jaganmayaḥ
children.translated_text: For yogins the god is partless; for those who know, he is made of the whole world.
In the world the body of the supreme Lord is praised as threefold.
The first is the one that is partless; then comes the one both with parts and without parts.
The third is the one with parts alone, and not otherwise, O best twice-borns.
Some repeatedly worship always the form that is both with parts and without parts.
Some worship the omniscient one in the heart, some in the <s>Śiva-liṅga</s>, and some in fire.
Some sages, always moving within saṃsāra, worship the form with parts.
In this way men together with their wives and sons worship him constantly.

children.text: yathā śivas tathā devī yathā devī tathā śivaḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Śiva</s> is, so is the Goddess; as the Goddess is, so is <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore, with the understanding of non-difference, according to the twenty-seven divisions,

children.text: yajanti dehe bāhye ca catuṣkoṇe ṣaḍasrake
children.translated_text: they worship in the body and outside, in the four-cornered and the six-cornered form,
in the ten-spoked, twelve-spoked, sixteen-spoked, and triangular forms.

children.text: sa svecchayā śivaḥ sākṣāddevyā sārdhaṃ sthitaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: That lord <s>Śiva</s> himself, by his own will, stands together with the Goddess,
and for the sake of carrying beings across, <s>Śiva</s> is free from manifestation as being or non-being.
Some call that one twofold, and some call him possessed of the three guṇas.

children.text: ūcus tathā taṃ ca śivaṃ tathānye saṃsāriṇaṃ vedavido vadanti ||
children.translated_text: So too others spoke of him as <s>Śiva</s>, while knowers of the Veda call him the transmigrating one.

children.text: bhaktyā ca yogena śubhena yuktā viprāḥ sadā dharmaratā viśiṣṭāḥ
children.translated_text: Excellent brāhmaṇas, joined with devotion and wholesome yoga and always devoted to <s>dharma</s>,
worship the lord of yoga, the blessed one of boundless forms, in the middle of the six-cornered figure.

children.text: ye tatra paśyanti śivaṃ trirasre tritattvamadhye triguṇaṃ triyakṣam
children.translated_text: Those who there see <s>Śiva</s> in the triangle, amid the three principles, as three-guṇed and three-eyed,

children.text: te yānti cainaṃ na ca yogino 'nye tayā ca devyā puruṣaṃ purāṇam ||
children.translated_text: they, and no other yogins, attain this ancient <s>Puruṣa</s> together with that Goddess.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śivādvaitakathanaṃ nāma pañcasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventy-fifth chapter, named 'The Teaching of Nondual <s>Śiva</s>,' in the first part of the glorious great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
After this I shall proclaim the arising of the body assumed by his own will.
All the fruit of the consecration is indeed for the welfare of all worlds.
Having made the god seated on the supreme seat, together with <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Umā</s>,
and having consecrated him with devotion, one obtains all desires.
Having worshipped according to rule, even once, the god together with <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Umā</s>,
I shall tell the fruit that a mortal obtains from it, just as I have heard.
By <s>vimānas</s> (celestial vehicles) shining like ten million suns, granting every desire,
filled with <s>Rudra</s>'s maidens and furnished with song and dance,
the yogin sports like <s>Śiva</s> until the dissolution of created beings.
Having enjoyed great pleasures there, in wish-fulfilling <s>vimānas</s>,
he reaches the worlds called <s>Auma</s>, <s>Kaumāra</s>, <s>Aiśāna</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, and <s>Brāhma</s>,
then the <s>Prājāpatya</s> world, and, being of great splendor, <s>Janaloka</s> and <s>Maharloka</s> as well.

children.text: aindram āsādya caindratvaṃ kṛtvā varṣāyutaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having reached the <s>Aindra</s> world and gained the state of <s>Indra</s> for ten thousand years, again

children.text: bhuktvā caiva bhuvarloke bhogān divyān suśobhanān ||
children.translated_text: and having enjoyed in <s>Bhuvarloka</s> divine and splendid pleasures,
he reaches <s>Meru</s> and rejoices in the dwellings of the gods.
Having made him with one foot, four arms, three eyes, and furnished with a trident,

children.text: sṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ hariṃ vāme dakṣiṇe caturānanam
children.translated_text: standing there after creating <s>Hari</s> on his left and the four-faced one on his right,
with the crore of the twenty-eight <s>Rudras</s>, radiant in every limb,
and directly the twenty-fifth principle, <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), from his heart,
and <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) from his left side, and intellect from the region of intellect,
and ego from ego, and the subtle elements there,
and the senses from the senses themselves, as the supreme Lord does in play,
earth from the soles of his feet, and water from the secret region,
fire likewise from the navel region, and the sun from the heart,
the moon from the throat, the self as well, and heaven from the space between the brows and the head,
thus creating and standing visibly as the whole moving and unmoving universe,
having made the omniscient, all-pervading god according to the rule of sacred knowledge,
and having consecrated him properly, one attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
Having made <s>Yajñeśa</s>, the Lord, with three feet, seven hands, four horns, and two heads,
one is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Having enjoyed great pleasures there for a hundred thousand kalpas, the happy man
comes gradually into this world and becomes one who has completed all sacrifices.
But whoever makes <s>Soma</s> mounted on a bull, adorned with the half-moon,

children.text: hayamedhāyutaṃ kṛtvā yatpuṇyaṃ tad avāpya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: obtains the merit that would be gained by performing ten thousand horse sacrifices.
By a golden <s>vimāna</s>, garlanded with networks of little bells,

children.text: gatvā śivapuraṃ divyaṃ tatraiva sa vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: he goes to the divine city of <s>Śiva</s>, and there itself he is released.
Having made the god with <s>Nandin</s>, together with <s>Ambā</s>, surrounded by all the gaṇas,
I shall tell the fruit that one obtains from that, just as I have heard.
By <s>vimānas</s> resembling the disk of the sun, drawn by bulls,
crowded with hosts of apsarases, difficult even for gods and dānavas to obtain,
and adorned everywhere on every side with companies of dancing apsarases,
he goes to the divine city of <s>Śiva</s> and obtains lordship among the gaṇas.
Having made the Lord, the god of gods, dancing together with the daughter of the mountain,
the omniscient one with a thousand arms, or else with four arms,
