the supreme Lord surrounded by <s>Bhṛgu</s> and the others and by hosts of beings,
the Lord himself, with the daughter of the mountain, bearing the bull as his emblem,
always bowed to by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and all the others,
the supreme Lord surrounded by the Mothers and by sages,
and having consecrated him with devotion, I shall tell the fruit of that.
Whatever fruit exists in all sacrifices, austerities, gifts, holy places, and deities,

children.text: tatphalaṃ koṭiguṇitaṃ labdhvā yāti śivaṃ padam
children.translated_text: having obtained that fruit multiplied ten million times, he goes to the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having enjoyed great pleasures there until the dissolution of created beings,
when another creation has come again, he obtains the human state.
Having made the lord of gods naked, four-armed, white, three-eyed, with a serpent as his girdle,
holding a skull in his hand, with dark and curling hair,
and having consecrated him with devotion, one attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
Having made the lord with <s>Ambā</s>, the child of the lord of elephants, the giver of accomplished aims,
smoke-colored, red-eyed, three-eyed, adorned with the moon,
wearing crow-wing locks on his head, bearing serpent earrings, <s>Hara</s>,
with an upper garment of lion skin and a garment of deer skin, the Lord,
sharp-fanged, holding a mace, with a hand raised holding a skull,
making the quarters resound with the great sound of the syllables huṃ and phaṭ,
holding a white-lotus-colored hide in his arms, and also a water-pot,

children.text: hasantaṃ ca nadantaṃ ca pibantaṃ kṛṣṇasāgaram ||
children.translated_text: laughing, roaring, and drinking the black ocean,
dancing and adorned with hosts of beings and hosts of gaṇas,
and having consecrated him with devotion, in full measure according to one's means,
one passes beyond all obstacles and is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having enjoyed great pleasures there until the dissolution of created beings,
after gaining knowledge through discernment there from the <s>Rudras</s>, he is liberated.
Having made the unsurpassed four-armed god <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>,
with hands granting boons and fearlessness, the Lord holding a trident and a lotus,
established in the condition of female and male, adorned with every ornament,
and having consecrated him with devotion, one is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having enjoyed great pleasures there, endowed with powers such as minuteness,
he then gains knowledge lasting as long as the moon and stars, and is liberated.
Whoever should make <s>Lakulīśvara</s>, the omniscient lord of the gods of gods,
surrounded by disciples and pupils of disciples, with his hand raised for exposition,

children.text: kṛtvā bhaktyā pratiṣṭhāpya śivalokaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: having made and installed him with devotion, he goes to <s>Śivaloka</s>.

children.text: bhuktvā tu vipulāṃstatra bhogān yugaśataṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: But after enjoying abundant pleasures there for a hundred ages, the man
attains <s>jñānayoga</s> (the discipline of knowledge) and is liberated there itself.
And that station of the former gods and immortals, desired by all,
of the god who has made the ritual gesture and is smeared with funeral-pyre ash,
of him who bears the triple ash-mark and wears a garland of heads,
and who carries a single sacred thread made from a hair of <s>Brahmā</s>,
who holds in his left hand the excellent skull of <s>Brahmā</s>,
and who bears the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme lord,
having made and installed him with devotion, one is released from the ocean of becoming.
'<s>Oṃ namo Nīlakaṇṭhāya</s>' is this sacred eight-syllabled formula;

children.text: mantramāha sakṛdvā yaḥ pātakaiḥ sa vimucyate
children.translated_text: whoever utters the mantra even once is released from sins.
With this mantra, with fragrances and the like, with devotion according to his means,
after worshiping the Lord of the gods, he is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.
The god who is the destroyer of <s>Jālandhara</s>, the lord who bears <s>Sudarśana</s>,
having made and installed with devotion the form in which <s>Jālandhara</s> is split in two,
he attains union with <s>Śiva</s>; no deliberation is needed here.
The god who grants <s>Sudarśana</s>, visibly possessing the characteristics described before,
and worshiped by the god who adored him with an offering of his eye,
having made and installed him with devotion, one is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.
Then, placing the lotus foot properly on the back of <s>Nikumbha</s> as he stands,
the right foot well set down, and with the left side embracing the daughter of the mountain,
setting the elbow on the point of the trident, with a serpent made into a tinkling ornament,
and beholding <s>Andhaka</s> standing at the side with cupped hands joined in reverence,
having made the form according to rule, one would attain union with <s>Śiva</s>.
Whoever makes the Lord of the gods, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Tripurāntaka</s>,
joined with bow and arrow, with <s>Soma</s>, adorned with the half-moon,
the god well established in a chariot, with four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> as charioteer,
he too, becoming of that same form and going to <s>Śivapura</s>, happy,

children.text: krīḍate nātra saṃdeho dvitīya iva śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: sports there, without doubt, like a second <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: tatra bhuktvā mahābhogān yāvad icchā dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed great pleasures there as long as he wishes, O best twice-born sages,

children.text: jñānaṃ vicāritaṃ labdhvā tatraiva sa vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: and having obtained reflective knowledge, he is liberated there itself.
<s>Gaṅgādhara</s>, seated comfortably, and <s>Candraśekhara</s> as well,
together with <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and with <s>Ambikā</s> on his left lap,

children.text: vināyakaṃ tathā skandaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ durgāṃ suśobhanām ||
children.translated_text: likewise <s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and beautiful <s>Durgā</s>,

children.text: bhāskaraṃ ca tathā somaṃ brahmāṇīṃ ca maheśvarīm
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s> and <s>Soma</s>, <s>Brahmāṇī</s> and <s>Māheśvarī</s>,

children.text: kaumārīṃ vaiṣṇavīṃ devīṃ vārāhīṃ varadāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaumārī</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, the goddess <s>Vārāhī</s>, and also <s>Varadā</s>,
<s>Indrāṇī</s> and <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, accompanied by <s>Vīrabhadra</s>,
the wise man who makes him together with <s>Vighneśa</s> attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
The imperishable liṅga-form, covered by a garland of great flames,
and, in the middle of the liṅga, having made <s>Candraśekhara</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>,

children.text: vyomni kuryāt tathā liṅgaṃ brahmāṇaṃ haṃsarūpiṇam
children.translated_text: one should also make the liṅga in the sky, and <s>Brahmā</s> in the form of a swan,
and <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of a boar, facing downward beneath the liṅga;
with <s>Brahmā</s> standing to its right, his cupped hands joined in reverence,

children.text: madhye liṅgaṃ mahāghoraṃ mahāmbhasi ca saṃsthitam ||
children.translated_text: and in the middle the greatly terrifying liṅga, set within the great waters,
having made and installed it with devotion, one attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
The god who protects the sacred field, likewise the <s>Pāśupata</s> lord,
having made him with devotion according to rule, one is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śivamūrtipratiṣṭhāphalakathanaṃ nāma ṣaṭsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the seventy-sixth chapter, called 'Statement of the Fruits of Installing Forms of <s>Śiva</s>.'
The sages said:
The merit of installing a liṅga and the setting up of a liṅga,

children.text: liṅgānāṃ caiva bhedāś ca śrutaṃ tava mukhādiha ||
children.translated_text: and the distinctions among liṅgas, have been heard here from your mouth.
Having made a <s>Śiva</s> temple with materials beginning with clay and extending up to jewels,
what fruit a mortal obtains from that, you ought to tell us.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In this world even his devotee is constrained by sons, wife, house, and the like;

children.text: bādhyate jñānayuktaścenna ca tasya gṛhaistu kim ||
children.translated_text: but if he is endowed with knowledge, what need has he of houses?
Nevertheless, devotees of <s>Parameśvara</s>, even by making one with chosen clods,
go to <s>Rudraloka</s>, to a splendid divine aerial car of him who is honored by <s>Surendra</s> and the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: bālyāttu loṣṭena ca kṛtvā mṛdāpi vā pāṃsubhir ādidevam
children.translated_text: Even from childhood, by making for the Primordial God with a clod, or with clay, or with sand,

children.text: gṛhaṃ ca tādṛgvidhamasya śaṃbhoḥ sampūjya rudratvamavāpnuvanti ||
children.translated_text: a house of that kind for this <s>Śambhu</s>, and by worshiping it, they attain the state of <s>Rudra</s>.
Therefore, with every effort, devotees should build a <s>Śiva</s> temple with devotion,
by every effort, for the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.

children.text: kesaraṃ nāgaraṃ vāpi drāviḍaṃ vā tathāparam
children.translated_text: Whether <s>Kesara</s>, <s>Nāgara</s>, <s>Drāviḍa</s>, or some other type,
having made a temple of <s>Rudra</s> with devotion, one is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.
Whoever should make a palace named <s>Kailāsa</s> for <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
rejoices happily in aerial cars shaped like the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Or he may construct a <s>Mandara</s> for <s>Śiva</s> according to rule,
with devotion, according to his wealth, whether best, inferior, or middling.
In aerial cars resembling Mount <s>Mandara</s>, facing in every direction,
filled with hosts of apsarases and hard for gods and dānavas to obtain,

children.text: gatvā śivapuraṃ ramyaṃ bhuktvā bhogān yathepsitān
children.translated_text: having gone to beautiful <s>Śivapura</s> and enjoyed pleasures as desired,
after attaining <s>jñānayoga</s> (the discipline of knowledge), a man obtains the state of a lord of the gaṇas.
Whoever should make a palace named <s>Meru</s> for <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>

children.text: sa yatphalamavāpnoti na tat sarvair mahāmakhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fruit that he obtains is not gained by all the great sacrifices.
Whatever fruit there is in all sacrifices, austerities, gifts, sacred bathing-places, and the Vedas,
having obtained all that fruit, he rejoices for a long time like <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: niṣadhaṃ nāma yaḥ kuryātprāsādaṃ bhaktitaḥ sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: A wise man who, with devotion, makes a temple called <s>Niṣadha</s>,
having reached the world of <s>Śiva</s>, rejoices for a long time like <s>Śiva</s>.
Or whoever, O brahmins, makes the excellent auspicious <s>Himaśaila</s>,
going to the auspicious city of <s>Śiva</s> in vehicles like snow-mountains,
and attaining the yoga of knowledge, obtains the rank of a <s>Gaṇapati</s>.
Or whoever makes the beautiful temple called the peak of <s>Nīlādri</s>,
according to his means, with devotion for <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>,
I shall declare the fruit that a mortal receives from that.

children.text: himaśaile kṛte bhaktyā yatphalaṃ prāk tavoditam
children.translated_text: The fruit formerly told to you when <s>Himaśaila</s> is made with devotion,
having obtained all that fruit, and honored by all the gods,
he reaches the world of <s>Rudra</s> and rejoices together with the <s>Rudras</s>.
I shall declare the fruit one obtains by making the temple
named <s>Mahendraśaila</s>, approved by <s>Rudra</s>.
In aerial cars shaped like <s>Mahendra</s> mountain and joined with bulls,
having gone to the divine city of <s>Śiva</s> and enjoyed pleasures as desired,
having obtained knowledge investigated by the <s>Rudras</s>, O foremost sages,
he abandons sense-objects as if they were poison and attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
But the one who makes a temple of gold, adorned with jewels,

children.text: drāviḍaṃ nāgaraṃ vāpi kesaraṃ vā vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: whether <s>Drāviḍa</s>, <s>Nāgara</s>, or <s>Kesara</s>, according to rule,

children.text: kūṭaṃ vā maṇḍapaṃ vāpi samaṃ vā dīrgham eva ca ||
children.translated_text: or a kūṭa, a pavilion, one that is square, or one that is long,

children.text: na tasya śakyate vaktuṃ puṇyaṃ śatayugairapi
children.translated_text: his merit cannot be described even in a hundred ages.

children.text: jīrṇaṃ vā patitaṃ vāpi khaṇḍitaṃ sphuṭitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Whoever has an old, fallen, broken, or cracked
auspicious temple restored as before, with doors and the other parts, O twice-born ones,

children.text: prāsādaṃ maṇḍapaṃ vāpi prākāraṃ gopuraṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: or a temple, a pavilion, an enclosing wall, or a gateway tower,
obtains even greater merit than the original maker; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: vṛttyarthaṃ vā prakurvīta naraḥ karma śivālaye ||
children.translated_text: Or if a man performs work in a temple of <s>Śiva</s> for the sake of a livelihood,

children.text: yaḥ sa yāti na saṃdehaḥ svargalokaṃ sabāndhavaḥ
children.translated_text: he goes, without doubt, to the heavenly world together with his kinsmen.
And if, even once, in a temple of <s>Rudra</s>, for the sake of fulfilling his own enjoyment,

children.text: karma kuryādyadi sukhaṃ labdhvā cāpi pramodate
children.translated_text: a man should do work, he obtains happiness and rejoices.

children.text: tasmād āyatanaṃ bhaktyā yaḥ kuryān munisattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, O best of sages, the mortal who with devotion makes a shrine
from wood, bricks, and the like is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
For the favor of <s>Maheśa</s>, O foremost sages, in a temple
every effort should be made for <s>dharma</s>, pleasure, prosperity, and liberation.
If one is unable, O best of sages, to make an excellent temple,
then even by sweeping and similar service he obtains all desired things.
Whoever performs sweeping with a soft, fine broom
obtains in a month the fruit of a thousand <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> vows.
Whoever performs smearing, properly, with fragrant cow-dung water
strained through cloth obtains the fruit of a year-long <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
A field of <s>Śiva</s> extends half a krośa on every side from the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>.

children.text: yas tyajed dustyajān prāṇāñ śivasāyujyam āpnuyāt
children.translated_text: Whoever gives up his hard-to-give-up life there attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: svāyaṃbhuvasya mānaṃ hi tathā bāṇasya suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the self-manifest one, and likewise for a <s>Bāṇa</s> liṅga, O good-vowed ones, this is the measure;

children.text: svāyaṃbhuve tadardhaṃ syāt syād ārṣe ca tadardhakam
children.translated_text: for a self-manifest one it should be half of that, and for one established by seers half of that again.
For one made by men it should be half of that; this is the measure of the sacred field, O best of the twice-born.
In the same way, for the dwelling of ascetics, this is the measure of the field, O best of the twice-born.
In the case of an incarnation of <s>Rudra</s>, the first measure applies, and in the case of his disciple and grand-disciple;
in the case of a human incarnation, it applies to his disciple, and to that disciple's disciple and grand-disciple.

children.text: śrīparvate mahāpuṇye tasya prānte ca vā dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the highly meritorious <s>Śrīparvata</s>, or at its border, O twice-born ones,
or there itself, whoever gives up his life attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
So also at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, and especially at <s>Avimukta</s>,

children.text: kedāre ca mahākṣetre prayāge ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: at <s>Kedāra</s>, the great sacred field, and especially at <s>Prayāga</s>,
and whoever gives up his life at <s>Kurukṣetra</s> goes to release.
At <s>Prabhāsa</s>, <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Avantī</s>, and also at <s>Amareśvara</s>,
and at <s>Vaṇīśaila</s> and <s>Ākula</s>, one who dies goes to identity with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: vārāṇasyāṃ mṛto janturna jātu jantutāṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: A creature who dies at <s>Vārāṇasī</s> never again enters creaturehood.
At <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>, <s>Vimukta</s>, <s>Kedāra</s>, and <s>Saṃgameśvara</s>,

children.text: śālaṅke vā tyajetprāṇāṃs tathā vai jambukeśvare
children.translated_text: or if one gives up one's life at <s>Śālaṅka</s>, likewise at <s>Jambukeśvara</s>,
or at <s>Śukreśvara</s>, <s>Gokarṇa</s>, <s>Bhāskareśa</s>, or <s>Guheśvara</s>,

children.text: hiraṇyagarbhe nandīśe sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: at <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> or <s>Nandīśa</s>, he goes to the supreme state.

children.text: niyamaiḥ śoṣya yo dehaṃ tyajetkṣetre śivasya tu ||
children.translated_text: The yogin who dries up his body by observances and gives it up in a field of <s>Śiva</s>

children.text: sa yāti śivatāṃ yogī mānuṣe daivike'pi vā
children.translated_text: goes to <s>Śiva</s>-hood, whether in a human or a divine field,

children.text: ārṣe vāpi muniśreṣṭhās tathā svāyaṃbhuve'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: or also in one established by seers, O best of sages, and likewise in a self-manifest one.

children.text: svayaṃbhūte tathā deve nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: When the god is self-born, there is no need for deliberation about this.
Whoever, after kindling the fire in a field of <s>Śiva</s> and worshiping <s>Parameśvara</s>,

children.text: svadehapiṇḍaṃ juhuyādyaḥ sa yāti parāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: offers the lump of his own body as an oblation goes to the supreme state.
Or however long he may be, having become one who does not eat, he should abandon his life;
in a field of <s>Śiva</s>, O best of sages, he attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: chittvā pādadvayaṃ cāpi śivakṣetre vasettu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And whoever, even after cutting off both feet, remains in a field of <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sa yāti śivatāṃ caiva nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: he too goes to <s>Śiva</s>-hood; there is no need for deliberation about this.
The sight of the sacred field is meritorious; entering it is a hundred times greater.
Touching it and circumambulating it bring merit a hundred times greater than that.
Beyond that, bathing in water brings merit a hundred times greater still.
After that, O brahmins, bathing it with milk is unsurpassed and more than a hundred times greater.
With curds it is said to be a thousand; with honey, a hundred times greater than that.
And by bathing with ghee, it is endless; with sugar, a hundred times greater than that.
Having reached and bathed in a river situated near a sacred field of <s>Śiva</s>,
if one abandons the body there, giving up food, one is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
All rivers situated near sacred fields of <s>Śiva</s> are very auspicious,
and reservoirs, wells, and ponds are remembered as <s>śivatīrthas</s> (holy places of Śiva).

children.text: snātvā teṣu naro bhaktyā tīrtheṣu dvijasattamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man who bathes in those holy places with devotion, O best of twice-born men,
is freed from sins beginning with the killing of a <s>Brahmin</s>; there is no doubt of this.
A human being who bathes in the morning, O best sages, at the <s>śivatīrthas</s>,
obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice and goes to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
A man who bathes once with devotion at midday in the <s>śivatīrthas</s>
obtains merit equal to bathing in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; there is no doubt of this.

children.text: astaṃ gate tathā cārke snātvā gacchecchivaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: And when the sun has set, having bathed, a human being goes to the state of <s>Śiva</s>,
casting off the coat of sin at the <s>śivatīrthas</s>.
A twice-born man who bathes at the three junctions of the day, or even a man once at a <s>śivatīrtha</s>,
attains union with <s>Śiva</s>; no deliberation should be made about this.

children.text: purātha sūkaraḥ kaścit śvānaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhayātpathi ||
children.translated_text: Once, a certain boar, seeing a dog on the road and out of fear,
by chance plunged once into a <s>śivatīrtha</s>,
and, dying there of itself, O best of twice-born men, obtained the rank of a gaṇa.
Whoever in the morning sees <s>Śiva</s>, the Lord of the gods of gods, in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>,
goes to a destiny higher than all others.

children.text: madhyāhne ca mahādevaṃ dṛṣṭvā yajñaphalaṃ labhet
children.translated_text: And having seen <s>Mahādeva</s> at midday, one obtains the fruit of a sacrifice.
In the evening, having obtained the fruit of all sacrifices, one is released
from mental sins, verbal sins, and the very great bodily sins,
and likewise from secondary sins and lesser consequential sins.
At a transition time, having seen the god <s>Īśāna</s>, the Lord in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: māsena yatkṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tyaktvā yāti śivaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: one casts off the sin committed in a month and goes to the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
At the solstice, whether in the southern or northern course, within a half-month,

children.text: viṣuve caiva sampūjya prayāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and at the equinox too, having worshiped him, one proceeds to the supreme goal.
A pure man should make three circumambulations around the temple on every side,
by the rightward and leftward procedure, with a gentle gait.
At every step he obtains the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

children.text: vācā yastu śivaṃ nityaṃ saṃrauti parameśvaram ||
children.translated_text: But he who daily praises <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme Lord, with speech,

children.text: so'pi yāti śivaṃ sthānaṃ prāpya kiṃ punareva ca
children.translated_text: also goes to the place of <s>Śiva</s>; what more need be said after attaining it?
Having prepared the ritual area as a maṇḍala with fragrant cow-dung water,
with powders made of pearls and likewise made of sapphires,
and made of rubies and beautiful crystals,
and also with emeralds, gold, and silver,
or, if without wealth, with ordinary powders of those colors,
one should draw an auspicious lotus, measuring ten hands,
with its pericarp, O greatly fortunate ones, near <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Having invoked <s>Mahādeva</s> there, accompanied by the nine powers,
and the supreme giver of desired things with five, and likewise with six and with eight,
then again <s>Īśāna</s> with eight, and on the ten spokes with ten,

children.text: punarbāhye ca daśabhiḥ sampūjya praṇipatya ca ||
children.translated_text: and again outside with ten, having worshiped and bowed down,
having made offering to the god of gods, one obtains the fruit of giving land.
Or, if a poor man draws the lotus with rice-flour and the like,
he obtains all the merit stated before; there is no doubt of this.
Then, having drawn a twelve-spoked maṇḍala, the supreme station,
with powders such as jewel-powder and with the twelve forms,

children.text: maṇḍalasya ca madhye tu bhāskaraṃ sthāpya pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: one should place and worship <s>Bhāskara</s> in the middle of the maṇḍala,
surrounded by the planets, or else one attains supreme union with the sun.

children.text: evaṃ prākṛtam apyārthyāṃ ṣaḍasraṃ parikalpya ca ||
children.translated_text: In this same way, having also arranged the material maṇḍala desired, six-cornered,
one should place in the central region the lady of the gods, <s>Prakṛti</s>, whose form is <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: dakṣiṇe sattvamūrtiṃ ca vāmataś ca rajoguṇam ||
children.translated_text: On the right, the form of sattva, and on the left, the quality of rajas,
in front the form of tamas, and in the middle the goddess <s>Ambikā</s>.
The five elements and the set of five subtle elements are to be worshiped on the right,
and the five organs of action, and likewise the organs of cognition,
on the north, according to rule; in the six-cornered figure one should worship them.
The self, the inner self, the pair, and intellect,
and egoity together with the great principle; one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.

children.text: evaṃ vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ prākṛtaṃ maṇḍalaṃ param
children.translated_text: Thus the whole supreme maṇḍala of <s>Prakṛti</s> has been told to you.
Now I shall teach, O chiefs of Brahmins, what accomplishes all desired aims.
Having drawn a maṇḍala the size of a cowhide with cow-dung,
square according to rule, and having sprinkled it with water, the knower of mantras
should adorn it with canopies and the like, or with charming parasols,
with bubbles, half-moons, and golden aśvattha leaves,
with white fully opened lotuses and with red and blue water-lilies,
with strings of pearls hanging from the edge of the canopy and with white banners,
and with smooth white clay vessels and full jars,
with garlands of fruits and shoots, with vaijayantī garlands and cloths,
with fifty rows of lamps and likewise with five kinds of incense.
One should draw an excellent lotus furnished with fifty petals,
with powders of the respective colors, or else with white powders,
making the lotus by rule with a measure of one hand.

children.text: karṇikāyāṃ nyased devaṃ devyā deveśvaraṃ bhavam
children.translated_text: In the pericarp one should place the god <s>Bhava</s>, the lord of gods, together with the goddess.
And on the petals one should place the syllables with the <s>Rudras</s>, in order beginning from the east.
O you of good vows, all the syllables should begin with the praṇava and end with namaḥ.
Having thus worshipped them in order, O best of sages, with perfumes, flowers, and the like,
one should feed fifty Brahmins there according to rule.
A rosary, a sacred thread, earrings, and a water-pot,

children.text: āsanaṃ ca tathā daṇḍamuṣṇīṣaṃ vastrameva ca
children.translated_text: and likewise a seat, a staff, a turban, and clothing,
should be given to those great sages, for <s>Śambhu</s>, the god of gods.
Having thus offered a great caru oblation, and likewise a black pair of cows,
at the end one should cause the powdered maṇḍala to be given to the god of gods.
One should dedicate to <s>Śiva</s> the substances used for the sacrifice.
The wise man should recite, beginning with oṃ, for each syllable in sequence.
I shall briefly tell the fruit that a mortal obtains
when he writes out with devotion this whole excellent maṇḍala.
Having studied the Vedas with their auxiliaries properly and according to rule,
having sacrificed with sacrifices such as the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> in due order,
then with rites ending in the <s>Viśvajit</s>, and having produced sons of that kind,
having entered the forest-dweller's stage of life with his wife and with the sacred fires,

children.text: cāndrāyaṇādikāḥ sarvāḥ kṛtvā nyasya kriyā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: having performed all vows such as the cāndrāyaṇa and having laid aside ritual acts, O Brahmins,
having studied the knowledge of Brahman and gained knowledge with effort,
and having seen through knowledge the knowable object, whatever desired end a yogin obtains,
all that fruit he obtains from the sight of the varṇa-maṇḍala.
Or if a mortal, by whatever means, smears the area in front of a shrine,

children.text: uttare dakṣiṇe vāpi pṛṣṭhato vā dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or to the north, to the south, or behind it, O best of Brahmins,

children.text: catuṣkoṇaṃ tu vā cūrṇair alaṃkṛtya samantataḥ
children.translated_text: and decorates a four-cornered space all around with powders,
then, having worshipped with flowers, unbroken grains, and the like, he is released from all sins.
But whoever, with devotion, smears the sanctum all around even once
with sandal and other fragrant substances, together with camphor, on every side,
scattering perfumes and flowers and fumigating it with four kinds of incense,
and prays to the god <s>Īśāna</s>, goes to the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
There the man enjoys great pleasures for a hundred crores of kalpas,
filling the temple of <s>Śiva</s> with the fragrances and flowers of his own body.
Then, in due course, he attains the state of a <s>Gandharva</s> and is well honored by the <s>Gandharvas</s>.
Coming back in order into this world, he becomes a powerful king.
The primeval god <s>Mahādeva</s> is the maker of dissolution and continuance.
He is also creation, the lord of the worlds, all-pervading <s>Śarva</s>, eternal <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
The immortal Brahman that is <s>Śiva</s> is to be grasped as the supreme means to liberation.

children.text: vyaktāvyaktaṃ sadā nityam acintyam arcayet prabhum ||
children.translated_text: One should worship the Lord, manifest and unmanifest, always eternal and inconceivable.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge upalepanādikathanaṃ nāma saptasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the seventy-seventh chapter, named "The Description of Smearing and the Like."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Smearing should be done with water filtered through cloth.
In a field of <s>Śiva</s>, O best of sages, success is not held to come otherwise.
These waters become purified when drawn after being filtered through cloth.
They should be without foam, O tigers among sages, and especially not otherwise taken.
Therefore all divine rites, O best of Brahmins,
should be performed with purified waters, for the accomplishment of every task.
Waters are mixed with living beings, with tiny ones; and after killing them,
one would long incur all the sin connected with impure waters.

children.text: saṃmārjane tathā nṝṇāṃ mārjane ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: In sweeping, likewise in wiping for people, and especially in cleaning,
in the fire, in pounding, in grinding, and in collecting water,
there is always injury for householders; therefore one should avoid injury.

children.text: ahiṃseyaṃ paro dharmaḥ sarveṣāṃ prāṇināṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: This non-injury is the highest dharma of all living beings, O Brahmins.
Therefore, with every effort, one should use water filtered through cloth.
The gift of that is safety from fear, meritorious, and the very highest of all gifts.
Therefore injury should be avoided everywhere and always.
All beings protect the man who is always non-injurious in mind, deed, and speech,

children.text: rakṣanti jantavaḥ sarve hiṃsakaṃ bādhayanti ca
children.translated_text: and they afflict the injurious man.
O masters of the Veda, whatever fruit comes from giving the whole three worlds,
the non-injurious man obtains that fruit multiplied ten million times.
Those who are devoted to the welfare of all beings in mind, deed, and speech,
whose path is shown by compassion, go to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Those who protect many various beings as they would a master,
out of affection like that for sons and grandsons, go to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
Therefore, with every effort, with water filtered through cloth,
sprinkling should always be done, and bathing especially.
Whatever fruit is declared for killing the whole three worlds,
one obtains all that by killing even one being in a temple of <s>Śiva</s>.
For the sake of <s>Śiva</s>, injury to flowers should always be performed, O best of Brahmins,
as also animal-killing for the sake of sacrifice, and the punishment of the wicked by kṣatriyas.
For yogins who speak of Brahman there is no distinction of prescribed and forbidden.
For that reason they should not be killed because they resort to what is forbidden.
Having laid aside all actions, renouncers who speak of Brahman

children.text: na hantavyāḥ sadā pūjyāḥ pāpakarmaratā api
children.translated_text: should never be killed and should always be honored, even if they are devoted to sinful acts.

children.text: pavitrāstu striyaḥ sarvā atreś ca kulasaṃbhavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All women are pure, and so are those born in the lineage of <s>Atri</s>.
By killing an <s>Ātreyī</s> woman one incurs a sin equal to brahmin-murder.

children.text: striyaḥ sarvā na hantavyāḥ pāpakarmaratā api ||
children.translated_text: All women should not be killed, even if they are devoted to sinful acts.

children.text: na yajñārthaṃ striyo grāhyāḥ sarvaiḥ sarvatra sarvadā
children.translated_text: Women are not to be seized for the sake of sacrifice by anyone, anywhere, at any time,
among all varṇas, O best of brahmins, even if they are devoted to sinful deeds.
Whether impure and beautiful, or ugly and wearing soiled garments,

children.text: na hantavyāḥ sadā martyaiḥ śivavacchaṅkayā tathā ||
children.translated_text: they are never to be killed by mortals, likewise from the suspicion that they may be like <s>Śiva</s>.
Those whose vows and conduct are outside the Veda, cast out from śrauta and smārta observances,

children.text: pāṣaṇḍina iti khyātā na saṃbhāṣyā dvijātibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: are known as heretics and are not to be conversed with by the twice-born.

children.text: na spṛṣṭavyā na draṣṭavyā dṛṣṭvā bhānuṃ samīkṣate
children.translated_text: They are not to be touched or looked at; after seeing them one should look at the sun.

children.text: tathāpi tena vadhyāś ca nṛpairanyaiś ca jantubhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even so, they are liable to be killed by kings and by other beings.

children.text: prasaṃgādvāpi yo martyaḥ satāṃ sakṛdaho dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: But the mortal who, even by chance and even once, O brahmins, in the company of the good,
worships <s>Maheśvara</s>, attains the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
All become afflicted and pitiless, O best of sages,
all men who are without devotion to <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme cause.
Those who are devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, the god of gods and supreme lord,
are fortunate; after enjoying pleasures here itself, they are released.

children.text: putreṣu dāreṣu gṛheṣu nṝṇāṃ bhaktaṃ yathā cittamathādideve
children.translated_text: As the minds of men are attached to sons, wives, and houses, so should they be attached to the primordial god;
for such self-restrained ascetics, through even one occasion, the world of <s>Parameśa</s> is not far.
Thus in the revered <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the seventy-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Devotion'.
The sages said:
How is <s>Mahādeva</s>, O very wise one, to be worshipped by dull mortals,
by those whose lives are limited, whose strength is slight, and whose resolve is small, O lord of creatures?
Even the gods, after worshipping <s>Śaṅkara</s> with austerity for thousands of years,

children.text: na paśyanti surāścāpi kathaṃ devaṃ yajanti te ||
children.translated_text: do not see him; how then can those people worship the god?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
What you have said here is indeed true, O bulls among sages;

children.text: tathāpi śraddhayā dṛśyaḥ pūjyaḥ saṃbhāṣya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless, through faith he is visible, worshipable, and indeed approachable.
And even by chance he is to be fully worshipped, even by those without devotion, O brahmins;
for the Lord is declared to give fruit according to one's disposition.
A lowest twice-born man who worships while polluted by leftovers goes to a piśāca state;

children.text: saṃkruddho rākṣasaṃ sthānaṃ prāpnuyān mūḍhadhīr dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: if enraged, the foolish-minded man would attain a rākṣasa state, O brahmins.
A wicked man who eats forbidden food, after worshipping, obtains a yakṣa state;
one whose habit is singing attains a gandharva state, and likewise one whose habit is dancing.

children.text: khyātiśīlas tathā cāndraṃ strīṣu sakto narādhamaḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, one intent on fame attains the lunar realm; the lowest man, attached to women,
mad with intoxication, by worshipping <s>Rudra</s>, obtains the station of <s>Soma</s>.
Having worshipped the god with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one obtains the Prājāpatya realm;

children.text: brāhmaṃ hi praṇavenaiva vaiṣṇavaṃ cābhinandya ca ||
children.translated_text: with the praṇava alone one obtains the Brāhma realm, and by praising him, the Vaiṣṇava realm.
Having worshipped <s>Maheśvara</s> even once with faith,
one reaches the world of <s>Rudra</s> and rejoices together with the Rudras.
After purifying the auspicious <s>liṅga</s> worshipped by gods and asuras,
with pure waters, and after invoking the god on the pedestal with devotion,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā devaṃ yathānyāyaṃ praṇipatya ca śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: having viewed the god according to rule and bowed down to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
having placed him on a prepared auspicious seat made of dharma and knowledge,
endowed with detachment and lordly power, honored by all worlds,
in the middle of the lotus of Oṃ, arising from moon, sun, and fire,
having given foot-water, water for sipping, and arghya to <s>Rudra</s> <s>Śaṃbhu</s>,
one should bathe him with divine waters, and also with ghee and milk.
One should bathe <s>Rudra</s> with curd and purify him according to rule;

children.text: tataḥ śuddhāṃbunā snāpya candanādyaiś ca pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: then, having bathed him with pure water, one should worship him with sandalwood and the like.

children.text: rocanādyaiś ca sampūjya divyapuṣpaiś ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: After worshipping him with rocanā and the like, one should worship him with divine flowers,
with unbroken bilva leaves and with lotuses of many kinds,
with blue lotuses, red lotuses, nandyāvarta flowers, and jasmines,
with campaka blossoms, jāti flowers, bakula blossoms, and oleanders,
with śamī flowers, large flowers, and those produced from unmāda and agastya,
with apāmārga and kadamba, and also with beautiful ornaments.

children.text: dattvā pañcavidhaṃ dhūpaṃ pāyasaṃ ca nivedayet
children.translated_text: Having given five kinds of incense, one should offer rice pudding,
and then curd-rice drenched with honey and ghee.

children.text: śuddhānnaṃ caiva mudgānnaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ ca nivedayet
children.translated_text: One should offer pure rice, mung-bean rice, and six kinds of food,
or else five kinds, together with ghee.

children.text: kevalaṃ cāpi śuddhānnam āḍhakaṃ taṇḍulaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: Or one may cook only pure rice from an āḍhaka of grain;
then, after circumambulating at the end and bowing again and again,

children.text: stutvā ca devamīśānaṃ punaḥ sampūjya śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: after praising the Lord God and again worshipping <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: īśānaṃ puruṣaṃ caiva aghoraṃ vāmameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, and <s>Vāma</s>,
and reciting <s>Sadyojāta</s>, one should worship <s>Śiva</s> with the five mantras.
By this procedure the god <s>Maheśvara</s> becomes pleased.
Trees used in the worship of <s>Śiva</s> with flowers, leaves, and the like,
and cows as well, O best of twice-borns, go to the highest state.

children.text: pūjayedyaḥ śivaṃ rudraṃ śarvaṃ bhavamajaṃ sakṛt
children.translated_text: Whoever worships <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, the unborn, even once,
goes to union with <s>Śiva</s>, free from return.
Having worshipped the supreme Lord, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, the husband of <s>Umā</s>,
or even having seen him once by chance, one is released from all sins.
A mortal who sees <s>Mahādeva</s> worshipped, or else being worshipped,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā prayāti vai martyo brahmalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: goes to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, without doubt.
Having heard of it and approved it as well, one goes to the highest state;

children.text: yo dadyād ghṛtadīpaṃ ca sakṛlliṅgasya cāgrataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he who gives a ghee-lamp even once in front of the <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: sa tāṃ gatim avāpnoti svāśramair durlabhāṃ sthirām
children.translated_text: obtains that stable state, difficult to attain through one's own āśramas.

children.text: dīpavṛkṣaṃ pārthivaṃ vā dāravaṃ vā śivālaye ||
children.translated_text: A lamp-tree, whether earthen or wooden, in a temple of <s>Śiva</s>...
Having given it, he is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s> together with more than a hundred families.

children.text: āyasaṃ tāmrajaṃ vāpi raupyaṃ sauvarṇikaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: whether it is made of iron, copper, silver, or likewise gold.

children.text: śivāya dīpaṃ yo dadyādvidhinā vāpi bhaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever gives a lamp to <s>Śiva</s>, according to rule or simply from devotion,
goes to the city of <s>Śiva</s> in splendid vehicles equal to ten thousand suns.

children.text: kārtike māsi yo dadyād ghṛtadīpaṃ śivāgrataḥ
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, whoever gives a ghee-lamp before <s>Śiva</s>,
or sees <s>Parameśvara</s> being duly worshiped,

children.text: sa yāti brahmaṇo lokaṃ śraddhayā munisattamāḥ
children.translated_text: he goes to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>, through faith, O best of sages.
Invocation, gracious presence, installation, and worship
are declared to be performed with the <s>Rudragāyatrī</s>, and the seat with the <s>Praṇava</s>.

children.text: pañcabhiḥ snapanaṃ proktaṃ rudrādyaiś ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The bathing is said to be with the five mantras, especially those beginning with <s>Rudra</s>.
In this way one should worship daily the God of gods, the husband of <s>Umā</s>;
to his south one should worship <s>Brahmā</s> with the <s>Praṇava</s>.
To the north one should sacrifice to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the gods, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>;

children.text: vahnau hutvā yathānyāyaṃ pañcabhiḥ praṇavena ca ||
children.translated_text: having offered in the fire according to rule, with the five mantras and with the <s>Praṇava</s>,
he attains union with <s>Śiva</s>, after worshiping <s>Śaṅkara</s> in this way.
Thus the sequence of the rite of liṅga-worship has been told in brief,
as it was formerly told by <s>Vyāsa</s>, after he himself heard it from the mouth of <s>Rudra</s>.
Thus, in the first part of the <s>Śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, ends the seventy-ninth chapter, named 'The Rite of Worship of <s>Śiva</s>'.
The sages said:
How, after seeing <s>Paśupati</s>, the liberator from the bonds of creatures,
did the gods abandon creaturehood? Please tell us that here.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, in his own city called <s>Bhogyā</s>,
the gods assembled and, by his grace, approached the omniscient one.
For the welfare of all the gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>
<s>Puruṣottama</s> mounted the shoulder of <s>Garuḍa</s>,
and <s>Hari</s> went with the deities into the presence of the God of gods.

children.text: sarve samprāpya devasya sārdhaṃ girivaraṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: All of them, having reached the auspicious lordly mountain of the god,
with <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, and <s>Yama</s>, bowed to that highest mountain.
That blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the <s>Garuḍa</s>-bannered one,
descended from <s>Garuḍa</s> and climbed Mount <s>Meru</s> with the best of the gods.

children.text: sakaladuritahīnaṃ sarvadaṃ bhogamukhyaṃ muditakuraravṛndaṃ nāditaṃ nāgavṛndaiḥ
children.translated_text: It was free from every evil, granting all things, foremost among places of enjoyment, filled with delighted flocks of kurara birds and resounding with hosts of nāgas;
sweetly ringing with song, full of pleasant shade, with forest-edges patterned by paths and lovely waters stirred by the wind.

children.text: bhavanaśatasahasrair juṣṭam ādityakalpair lalitagatividagdhair haṃsavṛndaiś ca bhinnam
children.translated_text: It was adorned with hundreds of thousands of mansions like suns and broken up by flocks of swans skilled in graceful movement,
with dhava, khadira, palāśa, sandal, and other trees, and with hosts of excellent birds, cuckoos, and bees.
In places that best of mountains was crowded with every heavenly tree, with kurabaka, priyaka, and tilaka trees,
covered with many kadamba, tamāla, and creepers, and marked by various peaks.

children.text: gireḥ pṛṣṭhe paraṃ śārvaṃ kalpitaṃ viśvakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: On the summit of the mountain the supreme city of <s>Śarva</s> had been fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
for the sport of <s>Bhava</s>, the God of gods, the supreme lord.
The gods, with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, composed in mind, saw that city,
and bowed from afar solely because of the power of the Trident-bearer.

children.text: sahasrasūryapratimaṃ mahāntaṃ sahasraśaḥ sarvaguṇaiś ca bhinnam
children.translated_text: Great, resembling a thousand suns, and distinguished by thousands of every excellence,
the primeval god, the great-souled one, went to the city on Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, in the region of <s>Meru</s>.
Then the slayer of the enemies of the immortals, amid many chariots and a crowd of women, elephants, and horses,

children.text: gaṇairgaṇeśaiś ca girīndrasannibhaṃ mahāpuradvāramajo hariś ca ||
children.translated_text: together with hosts and gaṇa-lords, <s>Aja</s> and <s>Hari</s> came to the great city-gate, which resembled the king of mountains.
Then they saw buildings made of jāmbūnada gold and adorned with jewels,
surrounded by aerial palaces of many forms and by ramparts.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā śaṃbhoḥ puraṃ bāhyaṃ devaiḥ sabrahmakairhariḥ
children.translated_text: Seeing the outer city of <s>Śambhu</s> together with the gods and <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>,
his face delighted, then entered the city.
It was crowded with mansions and palaces and furnished with great watchtowers,
the splendid second, four-gated enclosure of the God of gods.
It was covered with networks of diamond, beryl, ruby, and other gems,
fitted with swinging seats and adorned with bells and fly-whisks.
It was filled with mṛdaṅgas and murajas, and resounded with vīṇās and flutes,
surrounded by troops of dancing apsarases and by hosts of spirits,
and by buildings like the palace of <s>Devendra</s>, enchanting to the eye.
Then on the palace-tops thousands of city women stood with flowers, fruits, unbroken rice, and the like,

children.text: sthitāḥ karaistasya hareḥ samantātpracikṣipurmūrdhni yathā bhavasya ||
children.translated_text: and from every side cast them with their hands upon the head of <s>Hari</s>, as upon that of <s>Bhava</s>.
When the women then saw <s>Viṣṇu</s>, their eyes rolling with intoxication,
broad-hipped, they at once danced, rejoiced, and sang.
Some women, seeing <s>Hari</s>, with faces slightly smiling,
with their garments somewhat slipped and the strings of their girdles loosened, sang.

children.text: caturthaṃ pañcamaṃ caiva ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca saptamaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: They passed the fourth, the fifth, the sixth, and likewise the seventh,

children.text: aṣṭamaṃ navamaṃ caiva daśamaṃ ca purottamam
children.translated_text: the eighth, the ninth, and the tenth, the most excellent city-enclosure,
and, having crossed them, reached the splendid city of the god <s>Śambhu</s>.
It was well-rounded and exceedingly bright on the auspicious peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
adorned with aerial palaces shining like the disk of the sun,
with bright crystal pavilions and also with ones made of jāmbūnada gold,
and in the quarters and intermediate quarters it was adorned with many kinds of jewels.
It had gateway towers belonging to <s>Śambhu</s>, lord of the herds, adorned with many ornaments,
and many <s>sarvatobhadra</s> buildings on every side, made of every jewel.
It was enclosed by twenty-eight ramparts of various forms,
with side-gates and great gates, various and strong, in the intermediate directions.
It had secret shrines, secret houses, and auspicious mansions of <s>Guha</s>,
and other dwellings, O greatly fortunate ones, made of pearls and bewildering to the sight.
It had divine temples of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, made of ruby as well,
and was beautiful with sandal trees of many forms and with flower gardens.
There were ponds and long pools with rows of golden steps,
attended on every side by swans whose gait surpassed that of women.
With peacocks, kāraṇḍa ducks, cuckoos, and cakravāka birds,
and with wells adorned by divine nectar-like waters,
with women skilled in conversation and speech, adorned with every ornament,
bending under the weight of their breasts and with eyes rolling from intoxication,
with thousands of divine <s>Rudra</s>-maidens delighting in the sound of song,
and with hosts of dancing apsarases, hard even for immortals to obtain,
with masses of full-blown lotuses and the like, and also with excellent birds,
and crowded with companies of <s>Rudra</s>'s women, intent on water-sport,
delighting in festivals of love, graceful at every step,
attached to village melodies, and shining like rubies,
such were the hosts of women belonging to the god of gods, <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme self.
Seeing them, the gods were filled with wonder and stood all around.
There the gods also saw a multitude of <s>Rudra</s>'s attendants,
and thousands of heroic lords of the gaṇas in assembly.
They saw the crystal aerial cars of the god of gods,
with stairways made of gold and adorned with diamond and vaidūrya gems.

children.text: teṣāṃ śṛṅgeṣu hṛṣṭāś ca nāryaḥ kamalalocanāḥ
children.translated_text: On their pinnacles were joyful women with lotus eyes,
broad-hipped yakṣas, gandharvas, and apsarases,
kinnarīs and kinnaras, serpents, and siddha maidens,
and others wearing many kinds of dress and adorned with many ornaments.
They possessed various powers and loved many enjoyments and pleasures,
resembling petals of blue lotuses, with eyes long like lotus leaves.
They were exceedingly beautiful in garments like lotus filaments,
with bracelets, anklets, necklaces, colorful parasols, and garments.
Adorned with these and other ornaments, they were embellished and fond of adornment.
Then, having seen the host of heavenly beauties, the heavenly beauties of the lords of the gaṇas,

children.text: jagmurgaṇeśasya puraṃ sureśāḥ puradviṣaḥ śakrapurogamāś ca ||
children.translated_text: the lords of the gods, together with the enemies of the cities and with <s>Śakra</s> at their head, went to the city of <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tasthuḥ surasiddhasaṃghāḥ purasya madhye puruhūtapūrvāḥ
children.translated_text: After seeing it, the hosts of gods and siddhas, led by <s>Puruhūta</s>, stood in the midst of the city,
before the foremost aerial palace of <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme lord, colored like a thousand young suns.

children.text: atha tasya vimānasya dvāri saṃsthaṃ gaṇeśvaram
children.translated_text: Then, at the doorway of that aerial palace, all the gods, led by <s>Śakra</s>,
saw <s>Nandin</s>, the lord of the gaṇas, standing there.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nandinaṃ sarve praṇamyāhur gaṇeśvaram
children.translated_text: Seeing that <s>Nandin</s>, they all bowed and addressed the lord of the gaṇas.

children.text: jayeti devāstaṃ dṛṣṭvā so'pyāha ca gaṇeśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the gods saw him they said, 'Victory!' and that lord of the gaṇas also spoke.

children.text: bho bho devā mahābhāgāḥ sarve nirdhūtakalmaṣāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Ho, ho, O greatly fortunate gods, all of you whose stains have been shaken off,
you have arrived, O lords of all worlds; O observers of good vows, you should state your purpose.'
They said to that boon-giving god, who shone like the lord of elephants,
'For the sake of release from the bonds of paśuhood, show us <s>Maheśvara</s>.'
'Long ago, when the three cities were to be burned, paśuhood was declared,

children.text: śaṅkitāś ca vayaṃ tatra paśutvaṃ prati suvrata ||
children.translated_text: and there we became anxious about that paśuhood, O observer of good vows.'
'The Pāśupata vow was taught by <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme lord;
by this vow, O lord of beings, paśuhood certainly does not exist.'

children.text: atha dvādaśavarṣaṃ vā māsadvādaśakaṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: 'Having performed that excellent vow for twelve years, or for twelve months,

children.text: dinadvādaśakaṃ vāpi kṛtvā tad vratam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: or even for twelve days,
all paśus are released from the bonds belonging to <s>Bhava</s>.'
He showed those gods, with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at their head,
<s>Nandin</s>, son of <s>Śilāda</s>, foremost among all hosts of beings.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā devamīśānaṃ sāṃbaṃ sagaṇam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that god <s>Īśāna</s>, together with <s>Ambā</s>, with his gaṇas, imperishable,
they bowed and praised him, their skin bristling with joy.
Having informed the blue-throated one of their release from the bonds of paśuhood,
they stood before <s>Śambhu</s>, bowing down again and again.
Then the god of gods, the bull-bannered lord, looked upon all those gods,
and the supreme lord purified the paśuhood of those gods.

children.text: vrataṃ pāśupataṃ caiva svayaṃ devo maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The god <s>Maheśvara</s> himself also taught the Pāśupata vow,

children.text: upadiśya munīnāṃ ca sahāste cāṃbayā bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Bhava</s> remained there with <s>Ambā</s>, along with the sages.

children.text: tadāprabhṛti te devāḥ sarve pāśupatāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From that time onward all those gods were remembered as Pāśupatas.
Because he is the lord of paśus, and because those deities are directly his,
therefore they were called Pāśupatas; and again they performed austerity.
Then, at the end of twelve years, the best of gods, freed from their bonds,
all went back the way they had come, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
All this has been told to you, as heard from the mouth of the Grandfather,
formerly by <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, and then by wise <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Whoever, being pure, recites this to Brahmins, or whoever, being pure, hears it,
upon the breaking of the body is released from the bonds of paśuhood.
Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the eightieth chapter, named 'The Greatness of the Pāśupata Vow.'
The sages said:
You have described this vow that brings release from the bonds of paśuhood,

children.text: vrataṃ pāśupataṃ laiṅgaṃ purā devair anuṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: the Liṅga-related Pāśupata vow, formerly practiced by the gods.
You should tell us, just as you formerly heard it.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, when <s>Sanatkumāra</s> respectfully questioned <s>Śailādi</s>,
<s>Nandī</s> spoke these words to him: I shall declare it briefly.
It is unsurpassed, practiced by gods, Daityas, Siddhas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas,
and by greatly fortunate sages:
the vow called the twelve-liṅga vow, which frees the bound soul from its bonds.

children.text: bhogadaṃ yogadaṃ caiva kāmadaṃ muktidaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: It gives enjoyment and yoga, grants desires and liberation, and is auspicious.
It prevents separation, is meritorious, and destroys the fears of devotees.
Having churned the Vedas together with their six limbs, he made it.
It is the best of all gifts, meritorious, and greater than ten thousand horse sacrifices.
It gives every auspicious blessing and destroys every enemy.
It even gives liberation to creatures sunk in the ocean of worldly existence.
It removes every disease and destroys every fever.
In former times it was practiced by the gods, and likewise by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Having made a smaller liṅga and bathed it with sandal-water,
beginning with the month of <s>Caitra</s>, O best of Brahmins, one should perform the vow of the <s>Śiva</s>-liṅga.
One should make an auspicious golden lotus, furnished with pericarp and filaments,
set with the nine jewels and having eight petals, according to rule.
In its pericarp one should place a crystal liṅga furnished with a pedestal.
There, with devotion and according to the proper rule, one should worship <s>Śiva</s> with bilva leaves,
with a thousand white lotuses, with red lotuses, and also with blue lotuses,
with white arka flowers, karṇikāra flowers, oleanders, and baka flowers.
With these and others, according to availability, O you of good vows, using the Gāyatrī,
and after fully worshipping with perfumes and the rest, with incenses, lamps, and auspicious rites,
and with waving of lights and other rites, one should worship <s>Maheśvara</s> whose form is the liṅga.
On the southern side, O best of the twice-born, one should offer agaru with the Aghora mantra.
On the western side, with the Sadya mantra, one should offer divine realgar.
On the northern side, with the Vāmadeva mantra, one should offer sandal, or have it offered.
On the eastern side, O best of sages, with the Puruṣa mantra, one should offer orpiment.
O Brahmins, there should also be incense produced from white agaru and from black agaru,
and likewise guggulu incense, unsurpassed in fragrance.

children.text: sitāraṃ nāma dhūpaṃ ca dadyād īśāya bhaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should also offer the incense called sitāra to <s>Īśa</s> with devotion.
A great caru offering should be presented, or else a prastha of cooked rice.
This meritorious great vow of the <s>Śiva</s>-liṅga has been told to you.
It is common to all months, and the particular distinction is also recited.

children.text: vaiśākhe vajraliṅgaṃ ca jyeṣṭhe mārakataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Vaiśākha</s> the liṅga should be made of diamond, and in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> of emerald.
In <s>Āṣāḍha</s> the liṅga should be of pearl, and in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> made of sapphire.
In the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s> the auspicious liṅga should be made of ruby.
In <s>Āśvina</s>, O best of Brahmins, it should auspiciously be made of gomeda.
In <s>Kārttika</s> it should be of coral, and likewise in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>
the liṅga should be made of vaiḍūrya; in <s>Pauṣa</s>, of topaz.

children.text: māghe ca sūryakāntena phālgune sphāṭikena ca ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Māgha</s> it should be made of sun-stone, and in <s>Phālguna</s> of crystal.
In all months one golden lotus is prescribed.

children.text: alābhe rājataṃ vāpi kevalaṃ kamalaṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: If that is unavailable, then a silver one may be used, or simply a lotus.

children.text: ratnānām apyalābhe tu hemnā vā rājatena vā
children.translated_text: If jewels too are unavailable, it may be made of gold or silver.
If silver also is unavailable, one should have it made from copper metal.

children.text: śailaṃ vā dārujaṃ vāpi mṛnmayaṃ vā savedikam
children.translated_text: Or one may fashion it from stone, wood, or clay, together with an altar,
or one may imagine a temporary one made of all perfumes.
In the cold season one should worship <s>Mahādeva</s> with śrī leaves.
In all months there may be one lotus, either golden,
or a silver lotus with an excellent golden pericarp.
If even silver is lacking, one should worship him with bilva leaves.
If a thousand lotuses are unavailable, one should worship with half that number,
or with half of that half, or with one hundred and eight, worshipping <s>Rudra</s>.
On the bilva leaf dwells the goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s>, endowed with auspicious marks.
In the blue lotus is <s>Ambikā</s> herself, and in the lotus is <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> himself.
In the lotus abides <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, lord of all the gods.
Therefore the wise man should by every effort not abandon the śrī leaf,

children.text: nīlotpalaṃ cotpalaṃ ca kamalaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: nor the blue lotus, the lotus, and especially the lotus flower.
The lotus brings all beings under one's control, and the stone grants accomplishment of all aims.
Incense produced from black agaru cuts away all sins.
The offering of guggulu and the like, and of lamps,
causes the destruction of all diseases; sandal grants every accomplishment.
Likewise fragrant incense accomplishes every desired object.
Incense produced from white agaru and likewise from black agaru,
and the gentle sitāri incense directly grant the attainment of nirvāṇa.
In the white arka flower is manifest <s>Prajāpati</s>, the four-faced one.
In the karṇikāra flower wisdom itself is established.
In the oleander is the lord of the gaṇas, and in the baka flower <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself.
In all fragrant flowers is the daughter of the mountain.
Therefore, with these flowers, incenses, and other auspicious things, according to availability,
one should worship the god of gods with devotion, according to one's wealth.
Then, with devotion, one should offer milk-rice and the great caru oblation,
with ghee, with side dishes, and furnished with every ingredient.

children.text: śuddhānnaṃ vāpi mudgānnamāḍhakaṃ cārdhakaṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: Or one may offer pure rice, or mudga-bean rice, an āḍhaka or a half measure.

children.text: cāmaraṃ tālavṛntaṃ ca tasmai bhaktyā nivedayet ||
children.translated_text: One should offer him, with devotion, a fly-whisk and a palm-leaf fan,
and meritorious gifts, properly acquired.
And various kinds of worthy offerings, sprinkled again with water,
he should present to <s>Rudra</s> with a mind joined to devotion.
From milk, indeed, comes the firm nectar of all the gods, for the sake of continuance.
By victorious <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, everything is established in food.
Through the gift of food to beings, <s>Śaṅkara</s> becomes pleased.

children.text: tasmāt sampūjayed devam anne prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore one should worship the god with food; the breaths are established in food.
In the offering there is satisfaction, and in the condiment there is the wind himself.
<s>Mahādeva</s>, the self of all, is in fragrant water as the lord of waters.
In the seat is <s>Prakṛti</s> herself, established together with <s>Mahat</s> and the rest.
Therefore one should worship the god with devotion every month, according to rule.
On the full-moon day the vow is to be performed for the accomplishment of every desired aim.

children.text: satyaṃ śaucaṃ dayā śāntiḥ saṃtoṣo dānameva ca
children.translated_text: Truth, purity, compassion, peace, contentment, and giving as well,
and fasting on the full-moon day and the new-moon day, he should have performed.
At the end of the year there should be the gift of a cow, and especially the release of a bull.
With devotion he should feed Brahmins who are learned in the Veda and have crossed through the Vedas.
By him that liṅga has been worshipped, furnished with every substance.

children.text: sthāpayed vā śivakṣetre dāpayed brāhmaṇāya vā ||
children.translated_text: He should either install it in a field of <s>Śiva</s>, or give it to a Brahmin.
Whoever, in all the months, performs this great vow of the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>

children.text: kuryādbhaktyā muniśreṣṭhāḥ sa eva tapatāṃ varaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with devotion, O best sages, he alone is the best of ascetics.
By aerial cars shining like crores of suns and adorned with jewels,
having gone to the divine city of <s>Śiva</s>, he never returns here.
Or else, if he observes this excellent vow for even one month,
he obtains the world of <s>Śiva</s>; no doubt should be entertained here.
Or, if his mind is attached, whatever boons he thinks upon,
observing it thus for one year, he obtains each of those and then goes to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: devatvaṃ vā pitṛtvaṃ vā devarājatvameva ca
children.translated_text: Godhood, or the state of an ancestor, or even the rank of king of the gods,
or the station of <s>Gāṇapatya</s>: a man obtains these even if he is attached.
One who seeks knowledge obtains knowledge; one who seeks enjoyment obtains enjoyment.

children.text: dravyārthī ca nidhiṃ paśyed āyuḥkāmaś cirāyuṣam ||
children.translated_text: One who seeks wealth sees treasure; one who desires long life obtains long life.
Whatever desires he thinks upon, he obtains each of them and rejoices here.
By the one-month vow alone, at the end he attains the state of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: idaṃ pavitraṃ paramaṃ rahasyaṃ vratottamaṃ viśvasṛjāpi sṛṣṭam
children.translated_text: This is purifying, supreme, secret, the best of vows, created even by the maker of the universe,
by <s>Śiva</s>, for the highest welfare of gods, Asuras, Siddhas, mortals, and Vidyādharas.

children.text: sampūjya pūjyaṃ vidhinaivamīśaṃ praṇamya mūrdhnā saha bhṛtyaputraiḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus worshipped the worshipful Lord according to rule, and bowed with his head together with servants and sons,

children.text: vyapohanaṃ nāma japetstavaṃ ca pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtya śivaṃ prayatnāt ||
children.translated_text: he should recite the praise called Vyapohana and carefully circumambulate <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: purākṛtaṃ viśvasṛjā stavaṃ ca hitāya devena jagattrayasya
children.translated_text: The praise was composed in ancient times by the maker of the universe, by the god, for the welfare of the three worlds,

children.text: pitāmahenaiva suraiśca sārdhaṃ mahānubhāvena mahārghyam etat ||
children.translated_text: by the <s>Pitāmaha</s> himself together with the gods; this is great and precious, belonging to the great-souled one.
Thus, in the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the eighty-first chapter, named 'The Description of the Worship of the Liṅga that Frees from the Bonds of Beasts and the Like.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall declare the auspicious Vyapohana hymn, which grants all accomplishments,
after it was heard from the mouth of <s>Nandin</s> by the great-souled <s>Kumāra</s>.
It was told by him to <s>Vyāsa</s>, and from him, with great respect, by me.
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, pure, stainless, glorious,
the ender of the wicked, the All, <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme self.
Five-faced and ten-armed, endowed with fifteen eyes,
shining like pure crystal and adorned with every ornament,
all-knowing, all-pervading, peaceful, and well established above all,
seated on a lotus seat, the lord of <s>Soma</s>; may he quickly remove sin.

children.text: īśānaḥ puruṣaścaiva aghoraḥ sadya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Sadya</s> as well,
and the blessed <s>Vāmadeva</s>: may he quickly remove sin.
<s>Ananta</s>, lord of all knowledge, all-knowing, all-giving, the master,
fully endowed with concentration on <s>Śiva</s>: may he remove my sin.
Subtle, lord of gods and Asuras, lord of the universe, worshipped by the hosts,
fully endowed with concentration on <s>Śiva</s>: may he remove my sin.
The highest <s>Śiva</s>, greatly worshipful, devoted to meditation on <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sarvagaḥ sarvadaḥ śāntaḥ sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
children.translated_text: all-pervading, all-giving, peaceful: may he remove my sin.
The blessed lord <s>Ekākṣa</s>, devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>,
fully endowed with concentration on <s>Śiva</s>: may he remove my sin.
The blessed lord <s>Trimūrti</s>, who awakens devotion to <s>Śiva</s>,
fully endowed with concentration on <s>Śiva</s>: may he remove my sin.
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, <s>Śrīpati</s>, the glorious one, always delighting in meditation on <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: śivārcanarataḥ śrīmān sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
children.translated_text: the glorious one delighting in worship of <s>Śiva</s>: may he remove my sin.
The goddess bowed to by the three worlds, ancient, with a meteor-like form,

children.text: śivārcanarataḥ śrīmān sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu
children.translated_text: the glorious one delighting in worship of <s>Śiva</s>: may he remove my sin.
The goddess bowed to by the three worlds, ancient, with a meteor-like form,
<s>Dākṣāyaṇī</s>, the great goddess, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Haimavatī</s>, the auspicious one,
gentle, elder sister of <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, and likewise <s>Ekapāṭalā</s>,
<s>Aparṇā</s>, the boon-giving goddess, intent solely on giving boons,
<s>Umā</s>, <s>Suraharā</s> herself, <s>Kauśikī</s>, or <s>Kapardinī</s>,
the divine bearer of the khaṭvāṅga, whose fingertips are like fresh tree shoots,
surrounded by four divine sons beginning with <s>Naigameya</s>,
the daughter of <s>Menā</s>, lotus-born, lotus-eyed,
the friend of <s>Ambā</s>, of <s>Vītaśoka</s>, and of great-souled <s>Nandin</s>,
the friend of <s>Śubhāvatī</s>, peaceful, five-crested, bestower of boons,
imperishable, she has assumed the state of <s>Prakṛti</s> for the creation of all beings.
She is expanded through the twenty-three <s>tattvas</s> beginning with <s>mahat</s>,
and is constantly bowed to by powers beginning with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Nandanandinī</s>.
She is <s>Manonmanī</s>, the great goddess, mistress of <s>māyā</s>, fond of adornment;
by her <s>māyā</s> she agitates and deludes the whole moving and unmoving world, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: kṣobhiṇī mohinī nityaṃ yogināṃ hṛdi saṃsthitā
children.translated_text: She is the eternal agitator and deluder, established in the hearts of yogins,
abiding as one and as many in the world, with eyes like blue lotuses.
With supreme devotion she is constantly praised by all the gods,
beginning with the lord of the gaṇas, the lotus-born one, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and the lord of wealth.
Praised by them, their mother, destroyer of all afflictions,
remover of the distress of devotees, auspicious, destroyer of worldly becoming,
divine giver of enjoyment and liberation to devotees without effort,

children.text: sā me sākṣānmahādevī pāpam āśu vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: may that manifest great goddess quickly drive away my sin.
<s>Caṇḍa</s>, lord of all the gaṇas, issued from the mouth of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>;

children.text: śivārcanarataḥ śrīmān sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: glorious and devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may he drive away my sin.
And the son of <s>Śālaṅkāyana</s>, the lord arisen from the path of the plough,
the divine son-in-law of the <s>Maruts</s>, the great lord of all beings,
all-pervading, all-seeing <s>Śarva</s>, a lord equal to the lord of all,
together with gods including <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the moon, and the sun,
and with Siddhas, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, beings, and creators of beings,
with serpents and seers, and with great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>,
praised as lord of the three worlds, the sage dwelling within the inner chamber,
always worshipped by all: may <s>Nandī</s> drive away my sin.
Great-bodied, greatly radiant, like another <s>Mahādeva</s>,
glorious and devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may he drive away my sin.
He cleaves the slopes and peaks of <s>Meru</s>, <s>Mandara</s>, and <s>Kailāsa</s>,
and is well worshipped by the divine elephants of the quarters, beginning with <s>Airāvata</s>.
His feet are the seven netherworlds, and his broad shanks are the seven continents;
his goad is the seven oceans, his belly all sacred fords; he is auspicious.
His body is space, his arms the directions, and his eyes the moon, sun, and fire;
he has felled the great tree of the asuras and is immensely fierce with the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>.
Bound by divine elephant-guides beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, furnished with yogic nooses,

children.text: baddho hṛtpuṇḍarīkākhye staṃbhe vṛttiṃ nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the pillar called the lotus of the heart, after restraining his activity,
he whose face is that of a lordly elephant, surrounded by hundreds of crores of gaṇas,
possessed solely of meditation on <s>Śiva</s>: may he drive away my sin.
<s>Bhṛṅgīśa</s>, that tawny-eyed one, ash-eating and embodied,
glorious and devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may he drive away my sin.
With four bodies, always destroyer of all asuras,
<s>Skanda</s>, bearing the spear, peaceful, the commander, riding the peacock,
the glorious general of the gods: may he drive away my sin.
<s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, likewise <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and also <s>Paśupati</s>,
<s>Ugra</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Mahādeva</s>, always devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>,
may these forms of the supreme lord drive away sin.
<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
<s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, god of gods, and source of <s>Bhava</s>,
and <s>Kapālīśa</s> are to be known as Rudras, born from portions of <s>Rudra</s>;
endowed with obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, may they drive away my impurity.

children.text: vikartano vivasvāṃś ca mārtaṇḍo bhāskaro raviḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vikartana</s>, <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Ravi</s>,
illuminator of the world, witness of the world, and <s>Trivikrama</s>,

children.text: ādityaś ca tathā sūryaś cāṃśumāṃś ca divākaraḥ
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Aṃśumān</s>, and <s>Divākara</s>:

children.text: ete vai dvādaśādityā vyapohantu malaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: these twelve <s>Ādityas</s> indeed may drive away my impurity.

children.text: gaganaṃ sparśanaṃ tejo rasaś ca pṛthivī tathā
children.translated_text: Space, touch, fire, taste, and earth,
the moon, the sun, and the self: these are bodies taught by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: pāpaṃ vyapohantu mama bhayaṃ nirṇāśayantu me
children.translated_text: May they drive away my sin and completely destroy my fear.
<s>Vāsava</s>, <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Nirṛti</s>,

children.text: varuṇo vāyusomau ca īśāno bhagavān hariḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, blessed <s>Hari</s>,
and the blessed grandsire, intent upon meditation on <s>Śiva</s>:

children.text: ete pāpaṃ vyapohantu manasā karmaṇā kṛtam
children.translated_text: may these drive away the sin done by mind and deed.
<s>Nabhasvān</s>, <s>Sparśana</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Anila</s>, and likewise <s>Māruta</s>,
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Prāṇeśa</s>, <s>Jīveśa</s>, and <s>Māruta</s>: these winds are taught by <s>Śiva</s>.
All devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may they drive away my impurity.
<s>Khecarī</s>, <s>Vasucārī</s>, <s>Brahmeśa</s>, and <s>Brahmabrahmadhī</s>,

children.text: suṣeṇaḥ śāśvataḥ pṛṣṭaḥ supuṣṭaś ca mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Śāśvata</s>, <s>Pṛṣṭa</s>, <s>Supuṣṭa</s>, and <s>Mahābala</s>:

children.text: ete vai cāraṇāḥ śaṃbhoḥ pūjayātīva bhāvitāḥ
children.translated_text: these Cāraṇas of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, deeply disposed by worship,

children.text: vyapohantu malaṃ sarvaṃ pāpaṃ caiva mayā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: may they drive away all impurity and the sin committed by me.
<s>Mantrajña</s>, <s>Mantravit</s>, <s>Prājña</s>, <s>Mantrarāṭ</s>, worshipped by Siddhas,
<s>Siddhavat</s>, <s>Parama</s>, and <s>Siddha</s>, givers of all accomplishments:
may all the Siddhas, worshippers of the feet of <s>Śiva</s>, drive away my impurity.
<s>Yakṣa</s>, <s>Yakṣeśa</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, <s>Jṛmbhaka</s>, and <s>Maṇibhadra</s>,
<s>Pūrṇabhadreśvara</s>, <s>Mālī</s>, and <s>Śitikuṇḍalin</s>,
and <s>Narendra</s>, the lords of Yakṣas: may they drive away my impurity.
<s>Ananta</s>, <s>Kulika</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and also <s>Takṣaka</s>,
<s>Karkoṭaka</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, mighty in strength,
endowed with obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, ornaments of <s>Śiva</s>'s body,
may they drive away my sin and the poison of what is stationary and moving.
<s>Vīṇājña</s>, <s>Kinnara</s>, <s>Surasena</s>, and <s>Pramardana</s>,
<s>Atīśaya</s>, <s>Prayogī</s>, and <s>Gītajña</s>: these are the Kinnaras.
Endowed with obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, may they drive away my impurity.
<s>Vidyādhara</s>, <s>Vibudha</s>, <s>Vidyārāśi</s>, and the best among the learned,
<s>Vibuddha</s>, <s>Vibudha</s>, the glorious one, grateful and of great fame,
all these <s>Vidyādhara</s>s are devoted to meditation on <s>Śiva</s>.
By the grace of <s>Mahādeva</s>, may they remove the terrible stain.
<s>Vāmadevī</s>, <s>Mahājambha</s>, and the mighty <s>Kālanemi</s>,
<s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Mardaka</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, and <s>Devamardana</s>,
<s>Prahrāda</s>, <s>Anuhrāda</s>, <s>Saṃhrāda</s>, and the <s>Bāṣkala</s> pair,

children.text: jambhaḥ kuṃbhaś ca māyāvī kārtavīryaḥ kṛtaṃjayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jambha</s>, <s>Kuṃbha</s>, the magician, <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, and <s>Kṛtaṃjaya</s>,
these great-souled Asuras are devoted to <s>Mahādeva</s>.
May they remove terrible fear and the Asuric disposition as well.
<s>Garutmān</s>, <s>Khagati</s>, the king of birds, and <s>Nāgamardana</s>,
<s>Nāgaśatru</s>, golden-limbed <s>Vainateya</s>, and <s>Prabhañjana</s>,
<s>Nāgāśīr</s>, <s>Viṣanāśa</s>, and the vehicle of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
these <s>Garuḍa</s>s, gleaming with golden color and serving as <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s vehicles,
endowed with many ornaments, may they remove my stain.

children.text: agastyaś ca vasiṣṭhaś ca aṅgirā bhṛgureva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, and <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
<s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Dadhīca</s>, and <s>Cyavana</s> as well,
<s>Upamanyu</s> and the other sages, all filled with devotion to <s>Śiva</s>,
all delighting in the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may they remove my stain.
The fathers, grandfathers, and likewise the great-grandfathers,
the <s>Agniṣvātta</s>s, the <s>Barhiṣad</s>s, and the maternal grandfathers and the rest,
devoted to meditation on <s>Śiva</s>, may they remove fear and sin.

children.text: lakṣmīś ca dharaṇī caiva gāyatrī ca sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dharaṇī</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: durgā uṣā śacī jyeṣṭhā mātaraḥ surapūjitāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Uṣā</s>, <s>Śacī</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, and the Mothers worshipped by the gods,

children.text: devānāṃ mātaraś caiva gaṇānāṃ mātaras tathā ||
children.translated_text: the mothers of the gods and likewise the mothers of the <s>Gaṇa</s>s,

children.text: bhūtānāṃ mātaraḥ sarvā yatra yā gaṇamātaraḥ
children.translated_text: all the mothers of the beings, and whatever <s>Gaṇamātṛ</s>s there are anywhere,
by the grace of the God of gods, may they remove my stain.
<s>Urvaśī</s>, <s>Menakā</s>, <s>Raṃbhā</s>, <s>Rati</s>, and <s>Tilottamā</s>,
<s>Sumukhī</s>, <s>Durmukhī</s>, <s>Kāmukī</s>, and <s>Kāmavardhanī</s>,
and the other divine <s>Apsaras</s>es throughout all worlds,
who constantly perform the <s>tāṇḍava</s> for <s>Śiva</s>, deeply absorbed in him,
those goddesses devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s> may remove my stain.
<s>Arka</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Śukra</s>, <s>Śanaiścara</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Ketu</s> as well,
as worshippers of <s>Śiva</s>, may they remove terrible fear and planetary affliction.

children.text: meṣo vṛṣo'tha mithunas tathā karkaṭakaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Meṣa</s>, <s>Vṛṣa</s>, then <s>Mithuna</s>, and auspicious <s>Karkaṭaka</s>,

children.text: siṃhaś ca kanyā vipulā tulā vai vṛścikas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Siṃha</s>, broad <s>Kanyā</s>, <s>Tulā</s>, and <s>Vṛścika</s>,

children.text: dhanuś ca makaraścaiva kuṃbho mīnastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Dhanu</s>, <s>Makara</s>, <s>Kuṃbha</s>, and <s>Mīna</s>,
these twelve zodiac signs are devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.
By the grace of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, may they remove fear and sin.

children.text: aśvinī bharaṇī caiva kṛttikā rohiṇī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Kṛttikā</s>, and <s>Rohiṇī</s>,
glorious <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, and the serpent asterism,
<s>Maghā</s>, <s>Pūrvaphālgunī</s>, and <s>Uttarāphālgunī</s>,
<s>Hasta</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and <s>Anurādhā</s>,

children.text: jyeṣṭhā mūlaṃ mahābhāgā pūrvāṣāḍhā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, and blessed <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s>,
<s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>, <s>Śravaṇa</s>, and <s>Śraviṣṭhā</s>,
<s>Śatabhiṣaj</s>, <s>Pūrvabhadrā</s>, and likewise <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>,

children.text: pauṣṇaṃ ca devyaḥ satataṃ vyapohantu malaṃ mama
children.translated_text: and the <s>Pauṣṇa</s> asterism: may these goddesses constantly remove my stain.
