<s>Jvara</s>, <s>Kumbhodara</s>, and mighty <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>,
<s>Mahākarṇa</s>, <s>Prabhāta</s>, and <s>Mahābhūtapramardana</s>,
<s>Śyenajit</s> and <s>Śivadūta</s>, Pramathas who increase delight,
together with hundreds of crores upon crores, and the mothers of beings always,
may they remove fear and sin by the grace of <s>Mahādeva</s>.
The lord of the bull, wholly endowed with meditation on <s>Śiva</s>, resembling snow and water,
having a form like jasmine and the moon, adorned with vessels, jasmine, and the moon,
the enemy of the submarine fire, who split the mare's mouth,
endowed with four feet and white like the milk ocean,

children.text: rudraloke sthito nityaṃ rudraiḥ sārdhaṃ gaṇeśvaraiḥ
children.translated_text: dwelling forever in <s>Rudra</s>'s world together with the <s>Rudra</s>s and the lords of hosts,

children.text: vṛṣendro viśvadhṛg devo viśvasya jagataḥ pitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣendra</s>, the god who supports the universe, the father of the whole world,
always surrounded by <s>Nanda</s> and the others and by the Mothers, the crusher of sacrifices,

children.text: śivārcanarato nityaṃ sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: always devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may he remove my sin.
<s>Gaṅgā</s>, the mother, the mother of the world, established in <s>Rudra</s>'s world,

children.text: śivabhaktā tu yā nandā sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Nandā</s> who is a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>, may she remove my sin.
<s>Bhadrā</s>, the goddess <s>Bhadrapadā</s>, established in <s>Śiva</s>'s world,

children.text: mātā gavāṃ mahābhāgā sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: the blessed mother of cows, may she remove my sin.
<s>Surabhi</s>, auspicious on every side, destroyer of every sin,

children.text: rudrapūjāratā nityaṃ sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: always delighting in the worship of <s>Rudra</s>, may she remove my sin.
<s>Suśīlā</s>, endowed with good conduct, giver of prosperity, filled with devotion to <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: śivaloke sthitā nityaṃ sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: dwelling forever in <s>Śiva</s>'s world, may she remove my sin.
Knower of the truth of the meaning of the Vedas and śāstras, mindful of every task,
endowed with all virtues, son of the lord of all gods,
the eldest, lord of all, gentle, himself having the body of great <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
noble, the commander of the army, manifest, profound, crusher of sacrifices,
mounted on the elephant <s>Airāvata</s>, with black curling hair,
dark-bodied, red-eyed, adorned with the moon and serpents,

children.text: bhūtaiḥ pretaiḥ piśācaiś ca kūṣmāṇḍaiś ca samāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: surrounded by beings, ghosts, piśācas, and kūṣmāṇḍas,
manifestly devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, may he remove my sin.

children.text: brahmāṇī caiva māheśī kaumārī vaiṣṇavī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, <s>Māheśī</s>, <s>Kaumārī</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>,
<s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>Māhendrī</s>, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, and <s>Āgneyikā</s> as well,
All these Mothers, worshipped by all worlds,
together with the <s>Yoginī</s>s, concentrated, may they remove great sin.
<s>Vīrabhadra</s>, of great splendor, resembling snow, jasmine, and the moon,
the fierce son of <s>Rudra</s>, whose great hand is set upon the trident,
thousand-armed, omniscient, himself bearing every weapon,
the god whose eyes are the three sacred fires, the lord who gives fearlessness to the three worlds,
the perpetual protector of the Mothers, mounted on a great bull,
glorious, bowed to by the three worlds, intent on worshipping the feet of <s>Śiva</s>,
the cutter-off of the sacrifice's head and the destroyer of <s>Pūṣan</s>'s teeth,
plainly the remover of <s>Agni</s>'s hands and the caster down of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eyes,
the crusher of <s>Soma</s>'s limb with his big toe, known as the lord,
the protector of the limbs of the gods beginning with <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Yama</s>,
the cutter of the nose and lips of the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: gaṇeśvaro yaḥ senānīḥ sa me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: he who is lord of hosts and general: may he remove my sin.
<s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, the most excellent, boon-giving, adorned with excellent ornaments,
the great <s>Lakṣmī</s>, mother of the world: may she remove my sin.
Greatly deluding, greatly fortunate, surrounded by hosts of great beings,

children.text: śivārcanaratā nityaṃ sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: always devoted to worship of <s>Śiva</s>: may she remove my sin.
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, endowed with every virtue and joined with every auspicious mark,

children.text: sarvadā sarvagā devī sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: the goddess who is always all-pervading: may she remove my sin.
The great goddess riding a lion, the imperishable daughter of <s>Pārvatī</s>,
the sleep of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the great <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, worshipped by the gods,
three-eyed, boon-giving goddess, the slayer of <s>Mahiṣāsura</s>,

children.text: śivārcanaratā durgā sā me pāpaṃ vyapohatu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Durgā</s>, devoted to worship of <s>Śiva</s>: may she remove my sin.
The <s>Rudra</s>s, bearers of the cosmic egg, worshipped by all worlds,

children.text: satyāś ca mānasāḥ sarve vyapohantu bhayaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: and all the true <s>Mānasa</s> beings: may they remove my fear.
<s>Bhūta</s>s, <s>Preta</s>s, <s>Piśāca</s>s, and leaders of the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s> hosts,

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍakāś ca te pāpaṃ vyapohantu samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those <s>Kūṣmāṇḍaka</s>s: may they, concentrated, remove sin.

children.text: anena devaṃ stutvā tu cānte sarvaṃ samāpayet
children.translated_text: Having praised the god with this, at the end he should bring everything to completion,
bowing with his head to the ground every month, O best of twice-born ones.
Whoever recites or even hears this divine Vyapohana hymn,
having shaken off all sins, is honored in <s>Rudra</s>'s world.

children.text: kanyārthī labhate kanyāṃ jayakāmo jayaṃ labhet
children.translated_text: One who seeks a maiden obtains a maiden; one who desires victory obtains victory.
One who seeks wealth obtains wealth; one who desires sons obtains many sons.
One who seeks knowledge obtains knowledge; one who seeks enjoyment obtains enjoyment.
Whatever desires a human prays for through hearing and the like here,

children.text: tānsarvān śīghramāpnoti devānāṃ ca priyo bhavet
children.translated_text: he quickly obtains all those, and becomes dear to the gods.
This holy text, being recited, for whomsoever it is recited,
diseases born of wind, bile, and the like do not afflict him;

children.text: nākāle maraṇaṃ tasya na sarpairapi daśyate ||
children.translated_text: he does not die untimely, nor is he bitten even by snakes.

children.text: yatpuṇyaṃ caiva tīrthānāṃ yajñānāṃ caiva yatphalam
children.translated_text: Whatever merit belongs to holy places, and whatever fruit belongs to sacrifices,

children.text: dānānāṃ caiva yatpuṇyaṃ vratānāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whatever merit belongs to gifts, and especially to vows,
a human obtains that merit multiplied ten million times by muttering it.

children.text: goghnaścaiva kṛtaghnaś ca vīrahā brahmahā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Even one who has killed a cow, an ingrate, a killer of a hero, or a Brahmin-killer,
one who kills a person who has sought refuge, and one who betrays a friend's trust,
wicked, of sinful conduct, and also a killer of mother or father,
having removed all sins, is honored in <s>Śiva</s>'s world.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge vyapohanastavanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvyaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the eighty-second chapter, named 'The Description of the Vyapohana Praise.'
The sages said:
The holy Vyapohana hymn has been heard by us with respect.
In connection with the gift of a <s>liṅga</s>, tell us also the vows.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall declare to you auspicious vows, O best of sages,
as told here by <s>Nandin</s> to the wise son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Having heard them from <s>Vyāsa</s>, I proclaim them to you.
On the eighth and fourteenth lunar days in both fortnights,

children.text: varṣamekaṃ tu bhuñjāno naktaṃ yaḥ pūjayecchivam
children.translated_text: he who, eating only at night for one year, worships <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sarvayajñaphalaṃ prāpya sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: obtains the fruit of all sacrifices and goes to the highest goal.

children.text: pṛthivīṃ bhājanaṃ kṛtvā bhuktvā parvasu mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: If a man, making the earth his vessel, eats on festival days,
by that single day and night he enjoys the fruit of a three-night vow.
On the two fifth days of the month and on the two first lunar days, a man
should perform the vow of streams of milk; he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
From the dark eighth day, with eating at night, until the dark fourteenth,
while eating, he obtains enjoyments and goes to <s>Brahmā</s>'s world.
One who for a single year undertakes eating at night on every festival day,
celibate, with anger conquered, devoted to meditation on <s>Śiva</s>,
at the end of the year should feed eminent Brahmins according to rule;

children.text: sa yāti śāṅkaraṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: he goes to the world of <s>Śaṅkara</s>; no doubt should be entertained here.

children.text: upavāsāt paraṃ bhaikṣyaṃ bhaikṣyāt param ayācitam
children.translated_text: Begging is better than fasting; unsolicited food is better than begging;

children.text: ayācitāt paraṃ naktaṃ tasmān naktena vartayet ||
children.translated_text: eating at night is better than unsolicited food; therefore one should live by eating at night.

children.text: devairbhuktaṃ tu pūrvāhṇe madhyāhne ṛṣibhis tathā
children.translated_text: In the forenoon the gods have eaten, and at midday the sages;
in the afternoon the ancestors, and at twilight the <s>Guhyaka</s>s and others.
After passing beyond all times, eating at night is best.
Eating sacrificial food, bathing, truthfulness, lightness of diet,
fire-rites, and sleeping on the ground should be practiced by one who eats at night.
Month by month I shall declare the unsurpassed vow of <s>Śiva</s>,
for <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation, and for purification from all sins.
In the month of <s>Puṣya</s>, having worshipped, whoever practices eating at night...
Truthful and having conquered anger, with rice, wheat, and cow products,
he should carefully observe the eighth day in both fortnights by fasting.
At the end of the month, on the full-moon day, lying on the ground, with ghee and the like,
he should bathe <s>Rudra</s>, the great god, and worship him according to rule.

children.text: yāvakaṃ caudanaṃ dattvā sakṣīraṃ saghṛtaṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Having given barley gruel and cooked rice with milk and ghee, O Brahmins,
he should feed disciplined Brahmins and especially recite a pacifying mantra.
Likewise he should present a tawny pair of cows
to <s>Bhava</s>, the god of gods, to <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord.
He goes, O tiger among sages, to the excellent realm of <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: bhuktvā sa vipulān lokān tatraiva sa vimucyate ||
children.translated_text: and, having enjoyed vast worlds there, he is liberated in that very place.

children.text: māghamāse tu sampūjya yaḥ kuryān naktabhojanam
children.translated_text: But in the month of <s>Māgha</s>, after worshipping, the one who undertakes night-eating,
eating kṛśara mixed with ghee, self-controlled in his senses,
should fast on the fourteenth day in both fortnights.
On the full-moon day he should give a blanket with ghee to <s>Rudra</s>.
He should give a black pair of cows and worship <s>Śaṃkara</s> as well,
and he should feed Brahmins to the full extent of his means.

children.text: yāmyamāsādya vai lokaṃ yamena saha modate
children.translated_text: Having reached the southern realm, he rejoices together with <s>Yama</s>.
And when <s>Phālguna</s> has arrived, he should undertake night-eating,
with food of śyāmāka grain, ghee, and milk, having conquered anger and mastered his senses.
On the fourteenth and then on the eighth day he should observe a fast.
On the full-moon day, having bathed the great god and worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
he should give a pair of cows, or one copper-colored, to the trident-bearing lord.
Having fed Brahmins, he should pray to the supreme lord.

children.text: sa yāti candrasāyujyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: He goes to union with <s>Candra</s>; there is no doubt to be entertained about this.
In <s>Caitra</s> also, after honoring <s>Rudra</s>, he should undertake night-eating,

children.text: śālyannaṃ payasā yuktaṃ ghṛtena ca yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: with rice food joined with milk and with ghee according to his pleasure.

children.text: goṣṭhaśāyī muniśreṣṭhāḥ kṣitau niśi bhavaṃ smaret
children.translated_text: Sleeping in a cowshed, O best of sages, he should remember <s>Bhava</s> on the ground at night.
On the full-moon day, having bathed <s>Śiva</s>, he should give a white pair of cows.
He should feed Brahmins as well, and he obtains the station of <s>Nirṛti</s>.

children.text: vaiśākhe ca tathā māse kṛtvā vai naktabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: And likewise in the month of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, after undertaking night-eating,
on the full-moon day, having bathed <s>Bhava</s> with the five products of the cow, ghee, and the like,
and having given a white pair of cows, he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

children.text: jyeṣṭhe māse ca deveśaṃ bhavaṃ śarvamumāpatim
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, the lord of gods, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, the husband of <s>Umā</s>,

children.text: sampūjya śraddhayā bhaktyā kṛtvā vai naktabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped him with faith and devotion, he should undertake night-eating.
With red rice food, honey, and water, purified with ghee and the like,

children.text: vīrāsano niśārdhaṃ ca gavāṃ śuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ ||
children.translated_text: seated in the heroic posture for half the night and devoted to serving cows,
on the full-moon day, having worshipped the god of gods, the husband of <s>Umā</s>,

children.text: snāpya śaktyā yathānyāyaṃ caruṃ dadyāc ca śūline ||
children.translated_text: having bathed him according to rule and according to his ability, he should give a caru offering to the trident-bearer.
Having fed Brahmins to the full extent of his means,
and having given a smoky-colored pair of cows, he is honored in the realm of <s>Vāyu</s>.
In the month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s> too, in this same way, intent on night-eating,
with abundant sugar, ghee, and sattu mixed with cow product,
on the full-moon day, having bathed him with ghee and the like and worshipped according to rule,
and having fed Brahmins who are śrotriyas and who have mastered the Vedas,
he should give a fair-colored pair of cows, and he obtains the realm of <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: śrāvaṇe ca dvijā māse kṛtvā vai naktabhojanam ||
children.translated_text: And in the month of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, O Brahmins, after undertaking night-eating,
having worshipped the bull-bannered lord with a meal of milk and sixty-day rice,
on the full-moon day, having bathed him with ghee and the like and worshipped according to rule,
and having fed Brahmins who are śrotriyas and who have mastered the Vedas,
he should again give a pair of cows, a white-footed bull in front and a pauṇḍra cow.
He goes to union with <s>Vāyu</s>, and becomes all-pervading like <s>Vāyu</s>.
When the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s> has arrived, having undertaken night-eating in this same way,
he should eat the remainder of oblations, O best Brahmins, and stay by day at the root of a tree.

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ tu deveśaṃ snāpya sampūjya śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: On the full-moon day, having bathed the lord of gods and worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: nīlaskandhaṃ vṛṣaṃ gāṃ ca dattvā bhaktyā yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: having given with devotion, according to rule, a bull and a cow with blue necks,
and having fed Brahmins who have mastered the Veda and Vedāṅgas,
a man, having reached the realm of the Yakṣas, becomes king of the Yakṣas.
Then in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, having undertaken night-eating in this same way,

children.text: saghṛtaṃ śaṅkaraṃ pūjya paurṇamāsyāṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: having worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s> with ghee on the full-moon day as before,

children.text: brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā ca śivabhaktān sadā śucīn ||
children.translated_text: and having fed Brahmins who are devotees of <s>Śiva</s> and always pure,
he should give a bull of bluish color, raised high in the chest,

children.text: gāṃ ca dattvā yathānyāyam aiśānaṃ lokamāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: and a cow according to rule, and he obtains the realm of <s>Īśāna</s>.

children.text: kārtike ca tathā māse kṛtvā vai naktabhojanam
children.translated_text: And likewise in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, after undertaking night-eating,

children.text: kṣīraudanena sājyena sampūjya ca bhavaṃ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped the lord <s>Bhava</s> with milk-rice together with ghee,

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ ca vidhivatsnāpya dattvā caruṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and on the full-moon day, having bathed him according to rule and again given a caru offering,
and having fed Brahmins to the full extent of his means,

children.text: dattvā gomithunaṃ caiva kāpilaṃ pūrvavad dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: having given a tawny pair of cows as before, O Brahmins,
he obtains union with <s>Sūrya</s>; there is no doubt to be entertained about this.
In the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> also, having undertaken night-eating in this same way,
with barley food according to rule, together with ghee, milk, and the like,

children.text: paurṇamāsyāṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ kṛtvā śarvāya śaṃbhave
children.translated_text: and on the full-moon day, having performed what was previously stated for <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>,
and having fed poor Brahmins who have mastered the Vedas,
having given a pale pair of cows according to rule,
he reaches the realm of <s>Soma</s> and rejoices together with <s>Soma</s>.
Nonviolence, truthfulness, non-stealing, chastity, forbearance, and compassion
Bathing three times a day, the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-offering), sleeping on the ground, and eating at night,
and fasting in the two fortnights, on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days,
all this has been taught as the monthly <s>Śiva</s>-vow.
One should perform it for a year, in the proper order or even in reverse order, O twice-born ones.
He goes to union with <s>Śiva</s> and obtains the yoga of knowledge.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śivavratakathanaṃ nāma tryaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the eighty-third chapter, named 'The Teaching of the <s>Śiva</s>-Vow.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall teach the <s>Umā-Maheśvara</s> vow, spoken by the Lord,
for the welfare of men, women, and other beings, O best of sages.
On the full-moon day, the new-moon day, and on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days,
one should observe night-eating for a year, eat sacrificial food, and worship <s>Bhava</s>.
Having made a very beautiful image of <s>Umā-Maheśa</s> in gold,
or one of silver, then at the end of the year, after installing it according to rule,

children.text: brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā ca dattvā śaktyā ca dakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: after feeding brahmins and giving a fee according to one's ability,
and after taking the lord of gods to a temple of <s>Rudra</s>, perhaps with chariots and the like,
with parasols, yak-tail fans, and ornaments endowed with every excellence,
one should present the vow itself to <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord.

children.text: sa yāti śivasāyujyaṃ nārī devyā yadi prabho
children.translated_text: He goes to union with <s>Śiva</s>; if it is a woman, O lord, she goes to union with the goddess.
On the eighth and the fourteenth lunar days, a restrained woman, living in celibacy,

children.text: varṣamekaṃ na bhuñjati kanyā vā vidhavāpi vā
children.translated_text: whether a maiden or a widow, does not eat for one year.
At the end of the year, after making an image by the procedure stated before,
installing it properly, and again giving it in a temple of <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: brāhmaṇān bhojayitvā ca bhavānyā saha modate ||
children.translated_text: and after feeding brahmins, she rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
The woman who in this way observes, for a year, one dark-fortnight fourteenth day,

children.text: varṣānte pratimāṃ kṛtvā yena kenāpi vā dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and at the end of the year makes an image, by whatever means she can, O twice-born ones,
and performs everything previously stated, rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
On the new-moon day she should remain without food for a year, very well restrained.

children.text: śūlaṃ ca vidhinā kṛtvā varṣānte vinivedayet
children.translated_text: At the end of the year, having made a trident according to rule, she should offer it.
After bathing <s>Īśāna</s>, she should worship him with devotion, with thousands of white lotuses.
She should also give a silver lotus, with a fine golden pericarp,

children.text: dattvā bhavāya viprebhyaḥ pradadyād dakṣiṇām api ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Bhava</s>, and she should give a fee to the brahmins as well.

children.text: kāmato'pi kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ bhrūṇahatyādikaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: Whatever sin has been committed even from desire, including the killing of an embryo,
a woman breaks all that by the gift of a trident; there is no doubt.
In this way she obtains union with <s>Bhavānī</s>, O best of twice-born ones.
Or, if a man should do this, he too obtains union with <s>Rudra</s>.
On the full-moon day and the new-moon day, for one year, without negligence,
a woman intent on fasting, and a man as well, O best of twice-born ones,
should perform that rite only at the command of their husbands, O best of twice-born ones,

children.text: japaṃ dānaṃ tapaḥ sarvamasvatantrā yataḥ striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: for women are not independent in recitation, gift, and every austerity.
At the end of the year she should present an image rich with all fragrances.

children.text: sā bhavānyāś ca sāyujyaṃ sārūpyaṃ cāpi suvratā ||
children.translated_text: That well-vowed woman obtains union with <s>Bhavānī</s> and also similarity of form,

children.text: labhate nātra saṃdehaḥ satyaṃ satyaṃ vadāmyaham
children.translated_text: there is no doubt here; truly, truly, I say this.

children.text: kārtikyāṃ vā tu yā nārī ekabhaktena vartate ||
children.translated_text: Or the woman who, in the month of <s>Kārttika</s>, lives on one meal,
joined with observances such as forbearance and non-violence, and living in celibacy,
should diligently give one load of black sesame seeds,
together with ghee and molasses, and cooked rice, to the supreme lord,

children.text: dattvā ca brāhmaṇebhyaś ca yathā vibhavavistaram ||
children.translated_text: and, according to the extent of her wealth, to the brahmins as well.

children.text: aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyām upavāsaratā ca sā
children.translated_text: On the eighth and the fourteenth lunar days, being intent on fasting,

children.text: bhavānyā modate sārdhaṃ sārūpyaṃ prāpya suvratā ||
children.translated_text: that well-vowed woman, having obtained similarity of form, rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
Forbearance, truth, compassion, giving, purity, and restraint of the senses:
this, together with the worship of <s>Rudra</s>, is the common <s>dharma</s> (rule) in all vows.
In summary I shall declare to you, month by month in sequence,
from the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> through <s>Kārttika</s>, in due order,
the very extensive and meritorious vow explained by <s>Nandin</s>.
Now, in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, one should adorn an excellent bull with all its limbs complete,
according to rule, and offer it to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: sā ca sārdhaṃ bhavānyā vai modate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She indeed rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>; there is no doubt here.

children.text: puṣyamāse tu vai śūlaṃ pratiṣṭhāpya nivedayet
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Puṣya</s>, one should set up a trident and offer it.
Having done everything previously stated, she rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
In the month of <s>Māgha</s>, having made a chariot marked with all auspicious characteristics,
one should give it after worshipping the lord of gods, and should also feed brahmins.

children.text: sā ca devyā mahābhāgā modate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: That greatly fortunate woman rejoices with the goddess; there is no doubt here.
In <s>Phālguna</s>, having made an image in gold according to rule,
or in silver or copper, according to the extent of one's wealth,
after installing and fully worshipping it, one should place it in a temple of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: sā ca sārdhaṃ mahādevyā modate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: She rejoices together with the great goddess; there is no doubt here.

children.text: caitre bhavaṃ kumāraṃ ca bhavānīṃ ca yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Caitra</s>, one should make <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, and <s>Bhavānī</s> according to rule,
properly, from copper and the like, and install them according to rule.

children.text: bhavānyā modate sārdhaṃ dattvā rudrāya śaṃbhave ||
children.translated_text: After giving them to <s>Rudra Śaṃbhu</s>, she rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.

children.text: kṛtvālayaṃ hi kauberaṃ rājataṃ rajatena vai
children.translated_text: Having made a splendid silver abode, like that of <s>Kubera</s>, from silver indeed,
furnished with <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Umā</s>, and with <s>Gaṇeśas</s> all around,
endowed with all jewels, and after installing it according to rule,
one should place it in the auspicious shrine of the supreme lord <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: vaiśākhe vai cared evaṃ kailāsākhyaṃ vratottamam
children.translated_text: In <s>Vaiśākha</s> one should thus perform the excellent vow called <s>Kailāsa</s>.
Having reached Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, she rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
In the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s>, in the form of a <s>liṅga</s>,
with joined hands folded in reverence by <s>Brahmā</s> himself and likewise by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
the liṅga-form, joined with <s>Bhava</s> in the middle, O best of Brahmins,

children.text: haṃsena ca varāheṇa kṛtvā tāmrādibhiḥ śubhām ||
children.translated_text: together with the haṃsa and the boar, having made an auspicious one from copper and other materials,
having installed it according to rule, he should then feed Brahmins.
Having reached the auspicious place of <s>Śiva</s>, in a shrine of <s>Śiva</s>, according to rule,
and having installed it together with Brahmins, he obtains union with the goddess.

children.text: āṣāḍhe ca śubhe māse gṛhaṃ kṛtvā suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: And in the auspicious month of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, having made a very beautiful house
with baked bricks, according to rule and as extensive as his means allow,
filled with the juices of all seeds and with every beautiful thing,
and with household implements, pestles, mortars, and the like,
and with female and male servants, beds, food, and the like,

children.text: sampūrṇaiś ca gṛhaṃ vastrairācchādya ca samantataḥ
children.translated_text: and having covered the house all around with abundant cloths,
having bathed the god, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the husband of <s>Umā</s>, with ghee and the like,
and having fed a thousand Brahmins according to rule,
a Brahmin endowed with learning and humility, who has mastered the Veda,
who is in the first āśrama, having honored him with devotion according to rule,
and a maiden with a beautiful waist, provided with maintenance for her whole life,

children.text: kṣetraṃ gomithunaṃ caiva tadgṛhe ca nivedayet
children.translated_text: he should present a field and a pair of cows to that house.
With various divine beds resembling Mount <s>Meru</s>,
having reached <s>Goloka</s>, she rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
Having become like <s>Bhavānī</s>, undecaying through all kalpas,
she obtains union with <s>Bhavānī</s>; there is no doubt about this.
Covered with all metals and adorned with variegated banners,
one should offer a mountain of sesame to <s>Śarva</s> in <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>.
With canopies, banners, cloths, and the like, and with metals, he should offer it.
And after feeding Brahmins, everything previously stated applies.
Having made in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s> a beautiful mountain of śāli rice,
he should offer it with canopies, banners, cloths, and the like, and with metals.
And after feeding Brahmins, he should give it according to rule.

children.text: sā ca sūryāṃśusaṃkāśā bhavānyā saha modate
children.translated_text: And she, radiant like the rays of the sun, rejoices together with <s>Bhavānī</s>.
And having made in the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s> a great mountain of grain,
joined with gold and cloth, having given it and worshipped <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
and after feeding Brahmins, everything previously stated applies.
It is furnished with every kind of grain and with all seed-juices and the like,
joined with all metals and adorned with all jewels,
provided with four horns and adorned with a canopy and umbrella,
well adorned with perfumes, garlands, and incense, and with various decorations,
with various dances and songs, and likewise with conches, vīṇās, and the like,
made greatly holy by Vedic recitations and especially by auspicious rites,
provided with eight great banners and bright with varied flowers:
the chief of mountains, named <s>Meru</s>, the excellent support of the three worlds.

children.text: tasya mūrdhni śivaṃ kuryānmadhyato dhātunaiva tu
children.translated_text: On its summit he should place <s>Śiva</s>, and in the middle with metal alone,

children.text: dakṣiṇe ca yathānyāyaṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca caturmukham ||
children.translated_text: to the south, according to rule, four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>,
and to the north the lord of the gods, flawless <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Having also made <s>Indra</s> and the other guardians of the worlds with devotion according to rule,
then having installed them, bathed them, and fully worshipped <s>Maheśvara</s>,
in the god's right hand he should place the trident worshipped by the thirty gods,

children.text: vāme pāśaṃ bhavānyāś ca kamalaṃ hemabhūṣitam
children.translated_text: in his left a noose, and in <s>Bhavānī</s>'s hand a lotus adorned with gold,

children.text: viṣṇoś ca śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ ca gadāmabjaṃ prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, carefully, a conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
and for <s>Brahmā</s> a rosary and an excellent water-pot,

children.text: indrasya vajram agneś ca śaktyākhyaṃ paramāyudham ||
children.translated_text: for <s>Indra</s> a thunderbolt, and for <s>Agni</s> the supreme weapon called the śakti,

children.text: yamasya daṇḍaṃ nirṛteḥ khaḍgaṃ niśicarasya tu
children.translated_text: for <s>Yama</s> a staff, and for <s>Nirṛti</s>, the night-rover, a sword,
for <s>Varuṇa</s> a great noose, and the wondrous <s>Rudra</s> called <s>Nāga</s>,
for <s>Vāyu</s> a staff, and for <s>Kubera</s> a mace worshipped by the world,
and the hatchet of the god <s>Īśāna</s>; having offered these in order,
and having performed <s>Śiva</s>'s great worship together with a caru oblation,
he should worship all the gods to the full extent of his means.
And after feeding Brahmins and carefully performing the worship,
having performed the great <s>Meru</s> vow, he should give it to <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Having reached great <s>Meru</s>, she rejoices with <s>Mahādevī</s>.

children.text: ciraṃ sāyujyam āpnoti mahādevyā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She obtains lasting union with <s>Mahādevī</s>; there is no doubt.

children.text: kārtikyāmapi yā nārī kṛtvā devīmumāṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Also at <s>Kārttikī</s>, any woman who, having made the auspicious goddess <s>Umā</s>
complete with all ornaments and marked by every auspicious characteristic,
from gold, copper, and the like, and having installed her according to rule,
and having made the god, the lord of gods, endowed with every auspicious characteristic,
and before the two of them the fire, and <s>Pitāmaha</s> with ladle in hand,
and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as giver, adorned with all ornaments,

children.text: lokapālais tathā siddhaiḥ saṃvṛtaṃ sthāpya yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: and having carefully set them surrounded by the guardians of the worlds and by siddhas,
should have that vow offered to him in a temple of <s>Rudra</s>, with devotion.

children.text: sā bhavānyāstanuṃ gatvā bhavena saha modate
children.translated_text: She, having entered the body of <s>Bhavānī</s>, rejoices together with <s>Bhava</s>.
The holy vow of eating once a day, month by month in sequence,
is practiced beginning with the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and ending with <s>Kārttika</s>,
for the welfare of creatures such as men and women, O best of sages.
A man, having performed this vow, obtains union with <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: nārī devyā na saṃdehaḥ śivena paribhāṣitam ||
children.translated_text: A woman obtains union with the goddess, without doubt; this was declared by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge umāmaheśvaravrataṃ nāma caturaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighty-fourth chapter, named the Umā-Maheśvara vow, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In all vows, having duly worshipped the god of gods, the husband of <s>Umā</s>,
one should recite the five-syllabled vidyā according to rule, O best of twice-born men.

children.text: japādeva na saṃdeho vratānāṃ vai viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: From recitation alone, and especially in the case of vows, there is no doubt:
their completion is not otherwise; therefore one should recite the auspicious five-syllabled mantra.
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ pañcākṣarī vidyā prabhāvo vā kathaṃ vada
children.translated_text: Tell us how the five-syllabled vidyā is, and how its power is;

children.text: kramopāyaṃ mahābhāga śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: O greatly fortunate one, we are eager to hear the sequence and the means.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago this holy teaching was told by the god <s>Rudra</s>, the god of gods, <s>Śaṃbhu</s>,
to <s>Pārvatī</s>; I shall state it briefly.
The blessed goddess said:
O blessed lord, lord of the gods of gods, great lord of all worlds,
I wish to hear truly the greatness of the five-syllabled mantra.
The blessed lord said:
The greatness of the five-syllabled mantra cannot be told even in a hundred crores of years,

children.text: na śakyaṃ kathituṃ devi tasmāt saṃkṣepataḥ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: O goddess; therefore listen to it in brief.
When dissolution has fully arrived, when the stationary and moving world has perished,
when gods and asuras alike have perished, and when serpents and rākṣasas have perished,
when everything has entered into prakṛti and will go to dissolution with you,

children.text: eko'haṃ saṃsthito devi na dvitīyo'sti kutracit ||
children.translated_text: I alone remain established, O goddess; nowhere is there a second.

children.text: tasminvedāś ca śāstrāṇi mantre pañcākṣare sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: At that time the Vedas and the śāstras abide in the five-syllabled mantra;

children.text: te nāśaṃ naiva samprāptā macchaktyā hyanupālitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they do not come to destruction, for they are protected by my power.
I alone also became twofold, through the distinction between prakṛti and self.

children.text: sa tu nārāyaṇaḥ śete devo māyāmayīṃ tanum ||
children.translated_text: That god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> lies down, assuming a body made of māyā,
resting on the couch of yoga-sleep, situated in the midst of the waters.
From the lotus of his navel was born the five-faced grandfather.
Desiring to create the three worlds, but unable and without a helper,
that <s>Brahmā</s> at first created ten mind-born sons of immeasurable might.
For the success of their creation, the grandfather said to me:
'O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, give power to my sons.'
Thus instructed by him, I, bearing five faces,
uttered the five syllables with my five mouths to the lotus-born one.
Receiving them with his five faces, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds,
understood <s>Parameśvara</s> through the relation of signified and signifier.
O goddess, <s>Śiva</s>, worshipped in the three worlds, is the signified by the five syllables;
the supreme mantra, the five-syllabled one, stands as his signifier.

children.text: jñātvā prayogaṃ vidhinā ca siddhiṃ labdhvā tathā pañcamukho mahātmā
children.translated_text: Having understood its application according to rule and having thereby obtained siddhi, the great-souled five-faced one

children.text: provāca putreṣu jagaddhitāya mantraṃ mahārthaṃ kila pañcavarṇam ||
children.translated_text: proclaimed to his sons, for the welfare of the world, the mantra of great meaning, consisting indeed of five sounds.
Having received that jewel of a mantra directly from the grandfather of the worlds,
they set out to worship that god, <s>Śiva</s>, higher than the highest.
Then the blessed <s>Śiva</s>, superior to the three forms, was pleased
and gave all knowledge and the eight qualities beginning with aṇimā.
They too, having received boons, O Brahmins, then desired worship.
On the lovely summit of <s>Meru</s> there is a mountain named <s>Muñjavān</s>,
dear to me, always prosperous, and guarded by my beings.
Near it, eager for the creation of the worlds,
they performed severe austerity for a thousand divine years, living on air,
standing there for the sake of grace, O goddess, those sages of old.
Seeing their devotion, I at once became visible to them.
I taught the seer, meter, deity, śakti, and seed of the five-syllabled mantra,
its nyāsa, six limbs, sealing of the directions, and its complete application,
to the noble ones, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.
Having heard the greatness of the mantra and its application,
those sages rich in austerity performed everything in full.
By its greatness, at that time, the worlds with gods, asuras, and humans,
the social classes with their divisions, and all auspicious dharmas,
as they had existed in previous kalpas, were heard of by them just as before.
And by the power of the five-syllabled mantra, the worlds, the Vedas, and the great sages

children.text: tiṣṭhanti śāśvatā dharmā devāḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: endure, as do the eternal dharmas, the gods, and this entire universe.
Now I shall proclaim that; listen to it all with attention.
It is few in syllables and great in meaning, the essence of the Veda, granting liberation,
established by command, free from doubt: this utterance is made of <s>Śiva</s>.
It is divine, endowed with many siddhis, pleasing to the minds of the world,
certain in meaning and profound: it is my supreme utterance of <s>Parameśvara</s>.
The mantra is easy and pleasant to pronounce with the mouth, accomplishing every purpose.
It is the seed of all vidyās, the first mantra, most splendid.
It is exceedingly subtle and great in meaning; it should be known like the seed of a banyan tree.
It is the Veda, beyond the three guṇas, omniscient, all-creating, the lord.
<s>Śiva</s>, all-pervading, abides in the one-syllabled mantra 'oṃ'.
In the subtle six-syllabled mantra, <s>Śiva</s> has the five-syllabled mantra as his body.
Through the relation of signified and signifier, he stands directly by his own nature.
<s>Śiva</s> is the signified because he is the object to be known; the mantra is remembered as his signifier.
This relation of signified and signifier between the two has existed from beginningless time.

children.text: vede śivāgame vāpi yatra yatra ṣaḍakṣaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the Veda or in the Śaiva āgama, wherever the six-syllabled

children.text: mantraḥ sthitaḥ sadā mukhyo loke pañcākṣaro mataḥ
children.translated_text: mantra stands, it is always chief; in the world it is regarded as the five-syllabled one.

children.text: kiṃ tasya bahubhir mantraiḥ śāstrairvā bahuvistṛtaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What use has he for many mantras, or for śāstras expanded at length,
if this supreme mantra of <s>Parameśvara</s> is established in his heart?
By him it has been studied, by him it has been heard, by him everything has been performed.
The learned man who recites it properly, only after studying it according to rule,
that much is the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>; that much is the supreme state.
And that much is <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of brahman); therefore the wise man should recite it constantly.
This mantra, consisting of the five syllables together with the <s>praṇava</s> (oṃ), is my heart.
More secret than the secret, directly the unsurpassed knowledge of liberation,
I shall tell the seer, meter, and presiding deity of this mantra,

children.text: bījaṃ śaktiṃ svaraṃ varṇaṃ sthānaṃ caivākṣaraṃ prati
children.translated_text: its seed, power, accent, color, place, and each syllable.
The seer is named <s>Vāmadeva</s>; the meter is declared to be <s>Paṅkti</s>.
The deity of this mantra is I myself, <s>Śiva</s>, O fair-faced one.
The seeds beginning with the syllable na are composed of the five elements.
Know the <s>praṇava</s> as the self, all-pervading and imperishable.
You yourself are the power, O goddess of gods, honored by all the gods.

children.text: tvadīyaṃ praṇavaṃ kiṃcin madīyaṃ praṇavaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Your <s>praṇava</s> is one thing, and likewise my <s>praṇava</s> is another.

children.text: tvadīyaṃ devi mantrāṇāṃ śaktibhūtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your own, O goddess, is the power of the mantras; there is no doubt.
The sounds a, u, and m are established in my <s>praṇava</s>.

children.text: ukāraṃ ca makāraṃ ca akāraṃ ca krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: The sounds u and m and a, in that order indeed,
know as your <s>praṇava</s>, three-moraed, protracted, and supreme.
Of the syllable oṃ the accent is acute, the seer is <s>Brahmā</s>, and its body is white.
The meter is the goddess <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the supreme self is the presiding deity.
The first is acute, and likewise the fourth and the second;
the fifth is circumflex, and the middle one is remembered as niṣāda.

children.text: nakāraḥ pītavarṇaś ca sthānaṃ pūrvamukhaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: The syllable na is yellow in color, and its place is remembered as the eastern face.
<s>Indra</s> is the presiding deity, the meter is <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Gautama</s> is the seer.
The syllable ma is black in color, and its place is indeed the southern face.
The meter is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, the seer here is <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> is called the deity.

children.text: śikāro dhūmravarṇo'sya sthānaṃ vai paścimaṃ mukham ||
children.translated_text: The syllable śi is smoky in color, and its place is indeed the western face.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> is the seer, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> the meter, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> the deity.
The syllable va is golden in color, and its place is the northern face.
<s>Brahmā</s> is the presiding deity, the meter is <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s> is the seer.

children.text: yakāro raktavarṇaś ca sthānam ūrdhvaṃ mukhaṃ virāṭ ||
children.translated_text: The syllable ya is red in color, and its place is the upward face, the Virāj.
The meter and seer is <s>Bharadvāja</s>; <s>Skanda</s> is called the deity.
I shall proclaim its <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement), auspicious and productive of all accomplishments.
It removes all sins, and the <s>nyāsa</s> is said to be threefold.
It is remembered as threefold according to the distinctions of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
It belongs respectively to brahmacārins, householders, and ascetics.
Creation is for brahmacārins, maintenance always for householders,

children.text: yatīnāṃ saṃhṛtir nyāsaḥ siddhir bhavati nānyathā
children.translated_text: and dissolution is the <s>nyāsa</s> for ascetics; otherwise success does not arise.
It is threefold: placement on the limbs, placement on the hands, and placement on the body.
According to the threefold distinction beginning with creation, it will be explained to you, O fair-faced one.
One should first perform the hand-placement, and then the body-placement.
After that, one should perform the limb-placement of the syllables in the prescribed order.
From the head down to the feet is called the creation-placement.
From the feet up to the head is the dissolution, O beloved.
The placement on the heart, mouth, and throat is declared to be the maintenance-placement.
For brahmacārins, householders, and ascetics too, O beautiful one,
one should then touch the whole body, including the head, with the entire mantra.

children.text: sa dehanyāsa ityuktaḥ sarveṣāṃ sama eva sa
children.translated_text: That is called body-placement; it is the same for everyone.
Beginning with the right thumb and ending with the left thumb,
what is placed is creation; the reverse, however, is dissolution.
On both hands, from the thumb through the little finger, it is placed.
O goddess, the maintenance-placement for householders is exceedingly productive of enjoyment.
Having first performed hand-placement and then body-placement,
one should afterwards perform limb-placement; this is the common rule.
Enclosing it with the syllable oṃ, one should place it on all the limbs,
and on both hands, in order, on the ten finger-tips.
Having washed the feet, sipped water, become pure, and concentrated,
one should perform the act of <s>nyāsa</s> facing east or facing north.

children.text: smaret pūrvam ṛṣiṃ chando daivataṃ bījameva ca ||
children.translated_text: First one should call to mind the seer, the meter, the deity, and the seed,

children.text: śaktiṃ ca paramātmānaṃ guruṃ caiva varānane
children.translated_text: and also the power, the supreme self, and the teacher, O fair-faced one.

children.text: mantreṇa pāṇī saṃmṛjya talayoḥ praṇavaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having wiped the hands with the mantra, one should place the <s>praṇava</s> on the palms.
And on all the fingers, likewise on the first and last joints,
one should place the five seed-syllables with bindu on the middle joints.
According to the threefold distinction beginning with creation, one should place them in order according to one's āśrama.
With both hands, from the soles of the feet up to the head,
one should touch the body with the mantra, enclosed by the <s>praṇava</s> itself.

children.text: mūrdhni vaktre ca kaṇṭhe ca hṛdaye guhyake tathā ||
children.translated_text: On the head, on the face, on the throat, on the heart, and likewise in the secret place,

children.text: pādayor ubhayoścaiva guhye ca hṛdaye tathā
children.translated_text: and on both feet, then in the secret place and likewise on the heart,

children.text: kaṇṭhe ca mukhamadhye ca mūrdhni ca praṇavādikam ||
children.translated_text: on the throat, in the middle of the mouth, and on the head, beginning with the <s>praṇava</s>,

children.text: hṛdaye guhyake caiva pādayormūrdhni vāci vā
children.translated_text: on the heart and in the secret place, or on the feet, the head, and the speech,
and on the throat too, one should place it according to the threefold distinction beginning with the <s>praṇava</s>.
Having thus performed the limb-placement, one should configure the faces.
From the east and so on up to the upper direction, with na and the following syllables in due order,
one should afterwards place the six limbs beautifully in their proper places.

children.text: namaḥ svāhā vaṣaḍḍhuṃ ca vauṣaṭphaṭkārakaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: This is done together with the formulae namaḥ, svāhā, vaṣaṭ, huṃ, vauṣaṭ, and phaṭ.

children.text: praṇavaṃ hṛdayaṃ vidyān nakāraḥ śira ucyate
children.translated_text: One should know the <s>praṇava</s> as the heart; the syllable na is called the head.

children.text: śikhā makāra ākhyātaḥ śikāraḥ kavacaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: The topknot is said to be the syllable ma, and the syllable śi is likewise the armor.
The syllable ā is declared to be the eye-weapon, while the syllable ya is so proclaimed.
Having thus placed the limbs, he should then bind the directions.

children.text: vighneśo mātaro durgā kṣetrajño devatā diśaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vighneśa</s>, the Mothers, <s>Durgā</s>, the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field), and the deities of the directions
are to be placed in the four corners beginning with the southeast, in due order.
With the tips of the thumb and forefinger, having established auspicious <s>Sumukha</s>,
and saying, "Protect!", he should bow to each one separately.
On the throat, the middle, and the thumb, and on the fingers beginning with the forefinger,
the wise man should perform hand-nyāsa with the thumb.
Thus this nyāsa has been taught as auspicious and remover of all sins,
as bringing all attainments, meritorious, protective in every way, and beneficent.
When the mantra has been placed, O fair one, he becomes equal to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Even sin committed in another birth perishes at that very moment.
Having placed it in this way, the intelligent man, pure in body and firm in vow,
should recite the five-syllabled mantra after obtaining the favor of the teacher.
After this, O auspicious one, I shall explain the holy receiving of the mantra,

children.text: yaṃ vinā niṣphalaṃ nityaṃ yena vā saphalaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: without which it is always fruitless, and by which it becomes fruitful.
A mantra that is without authorization, without ritual action, without faith, and without a focused mind,

children.text: ājñaptaṃ dakṣiṇāhīnaṃ sadā japtaṃ ca niṣphalam ||
children.translated_text: though commanded, if without a fee, and always recited, is fruitless.
A mantra accomplished through authorization, accomplished through ritual action, accomplished through faith, and joined with a good mind,

children.text: evaṃ ca dakṣiṇāsiddhaṃ mantraṃ siddhaṃ yatastataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise accomplished through the fee, is thereby a perfected mantra.
Having approached a brahmin guru who knows the true meaning of mantra,
who is wise, endowed with good qualities, and devoted to meditation and yoga,
the disciple, with purified intention, should please him with effort,

children.text: vācā ca manasā caiva kāyena draviṇena ca ||
children.translated_text: by speech and by mind, by body and by wealth.
The disciple should worship the teacher always with the greatest care,
with elephants, horses, chariots, jewels, fields, and houses,

children.text: bhūṣaṇāni ca vāsāṃsi dhānyāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: with ornaments, garments, and various kinds of grain.

children.text: etāni gurave dadyād bhaktyā ca vibhave sati ||
children.translated_text: He should give these to the guru with devotion, if he has the means.
He should not act deceitfully with his wealth if he desires attainment for himself.
Afterwards, O goddess, he should offer himself together with his possessions.
Having thus worshipped him according to rule and according to his ability, without cheating,

children.text: ādadīta gurormantraṃ jñānaṃ caiva krameṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: he should receive from the guru the mantra and, in due sequence, the knowledge as well.

children.text: evaṃ tuṣṭo guruḥ śiṣyaṃ pūjitaṃ vatsaroṣitam
children.translated_text: When the guru is thus pleased, he should instruct the disciple who has worshipped him and lived with him for a year,
who is obedient, free from arrogance, emaciated by fasting, and pure.

children.text: snāpayitvā tu śiṣyāya brāhmaṇānapi pūjya ca
children.translated_text: Having bathed the disciple and also worshipped the brahmins,

children.text: samudratīre nadyāṃ ca goṣṭhe devālaye'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: on the seashore, in a river, in a cow pen, or in a temple,

children.text: śucau deśe gṛhe vāpi kāle siddhikare tithau
children.translated_text: in a pure place or in a house, at an attainment-granting time and lunar date,
under an auspicious constellation and yoga, always free from defects,
then, having shown favor to him, he should give the unsurpassed knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>.
With a clear mind, even in solitude, he should pronounce it properly with his own voice.
The teacher himself, giver of attainment, should pronounce it and make him pronounce it.

children.text: śivaṃ cāstu śubhaṃ cāstu śobhano'stu priyo'stviti ||
children.translated_text: He should say, "May there be <s>Śiva</s>; may there be auspiciousness; may it be splendid; may it be pleasing."

children.text: evaṃ labdhvā paraṃ mantraṃ jñānaṃ caiva gurostataḥ
children.translated_text: Having thus received the supreme mantra and the knowledge from the guru,
he should recite it daily with a vow of intent, and should also perform the preliminary rite.
As long as he lives he should recite daily one thousand and eight times.

children.text: anaśnaṃstatparo bhūtvā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Remaining without food and intent upon it, he goes to the supreme goal.
With devotion he should recite one hundred thousand times for each syllable, multiplied fourfold.

children.text: naktāśī saṃyamī yaś ca pauraścaraṇikaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who eats at night, is restrained, and does this is remembered as one performing <s>puraścaraṇa</s>.
A reciter in the preliminary rite, or else a daily reciter,
if he desires attainment quickly, should become one or the other of these two.
The man who, after performing the preliminary rite, becomes a daily reciter

children.text: tasya nāsti samo loke sa siddhaḥ siddhido vaśī ||
children.translated_text: has no equal in the world; he is accomplished, a giver of accomplishment, and masterful.
Having assumed a pleasing seat, silent and with mind one-pointed,
he should recite the unsurpassed mantra facing east or facing north.
At the beginning and end of the recitation he should perform restraints of the breath,
and likewise at the end he should recite the auspicious seed one hundred and eight times.
Having restrained the breaths through forty repetitions, he should recollect.
This is called the prāṇāyāma of the five-syllabled mantra.
From prāṇāyāma there quickly comes the destruction of all sins,

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ vaśitvaṃ ca tasmātprāṇāṃś ca saṃyamet ||
children.translated_text: and mastery over the senses; therefore he should restrain the breaths.

children.text: gṛhe japaḥ samaṃ vidyādgoṣṭhe śataguṇaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Recitation at home should be known as equal in value; in a cow pen it becomes a hundredfold.
In a river it is a hundred thousandfold, and in the presence of <s>Śiva</s> it is infinite.
On the seashore, at a divine lake, on a mountain, in temples,
and in all holy hermitages, recitation becomes ten millionfold.
In the presence of <s>Śiva</s>, before the sun, before the guru,
before a lamp, a cow, or water, the act of recitation is praised.
Counting japa on the fingers is one by one, O auspicious-faced one.
Using the finger-lines is said to be eightfold, and with putrajīva seeds tenfold.

children.text: śataṃ vai śaṅkhamaṇibhiḥ pravālaiś ca sahasrakam
children.translated_text: With conch-shell beads it is a hundredfold, and with corals a thousandfold.
With crystal beads it is ten thousandfold, and with pearls it is said to be a hundred thousandfold.
With lotus seeds it is one millionfold, while with gold beads it is said to be ten millionfold.
With knots of kuśa grass and with rudrākṣa beads it is said to have infinite merit.
Twenty-five beads are for liberation; twenty-seven are for prosperity.
Thirty are for wealth and abundance, and fifty are for abhichāra rites.
Facing east is for subjugation, and facing south is for abhichāra rites.
Facing west should be known as wealth-giving, while facing north is for pacification.
One should know the thumb as granting liberation; the forefinger destroys enemies.

children.text: madhyamā dhanadā śāntiṃ karotyeṣā hy anāmikā ||
children.translated_text: The middle finger gives wealth; this ring finger brings peace.
The little finger is protective in the auspicious act of <s>japa</s> (recitation).
One should recite what is to be recited with the thumb together with the other fingers.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhena vinā karma kṛtaṃ tadaphalaṃ yataḥ
children.translated_text: For an act performed without the thumb is fruitless.
Listen: among all sacrifices, the sacrifice of <s>japa</s> is distinguished.

children.text: hiṃsayā te pravartante japayajño na hiṃsayā
children.translated_text: Those proceed with violence; the sacrifice of <s>japa</s> does not proceed with violence.

children.text: yāvantaḥ karmayajñāḥ syuḥ pradānāni tapāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: As many ritual sacrifices as there may be, and gifts and austerities as well,

children.text: sarve te japayajñasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm
children.translated_text: all of them are not worth a sixteenth part of the sacrifice of <s>japa</s>.
The greatness of the vocal sacrifice of <s>japa</s> has been proclaimed.
Therefore whispered recitation is remembered as a hundred times greater, and mental recitation as a thousand times greater.
When, with high, low, and accented sounds, with clearly pronounced words and syllables,
one utters a mantra with the voice, that is the vocal sacrifice of <s>japa</s>.
When one pronounces the mantra softly and moves the lips only slightly,

children.text: kiṃcit karṇāntaraṃ vidyād upāṃśuḥ sa japaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: so that it is known only a little at the ear, that recitation is remembered as whispered <s>japa</s>.
When, with the mind, through a sequence of syllables, from letter to letter and from word to word,

children.text: śabdārthaṃ cintayedbhūyaḥ sa tūkto mānaso japaḥ
children.translated_text: one repeatedly contemplates the sound and meaning, that is called mental <s>japa</s>.
Of the three sacrifices of <s>japa</s>, each later one is better than the preceding one.
By the special character of the sacrifice, there is also distinction in its fruit.
By <s>japa</s> the deity, constantly being praised, is pleased.
When pleased, the deity grants abundant enjoyments and eternal liberation.

children.text: yakṣarakṣaḥpiśācāś ca grahāḥ sarve ca bhīṣaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and all terrifying planetary spirits
do not approach the reciter, being afraid on every side.
By <s>japa</s> one pacifies completely whatever sin has been committed through successive births.

children.text: japena bhogān jayate ca mṛtyuṃ japena siddhiṃ labhate ca muktim ||
children.translated_text: By <s>japa</s> one wins enjoyments and conquers death; by <s>japa</s> one obtains accomplishment and liberation.

children.text: evaṃ labdhvā śivaṃ jñānaṃ jñātvā japavidhikramam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having obtained knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> and having understood the proper sequence for the method of <s>japa</s>,
a person of good conduct, reciting constantly and meditating, partakes of what is auspicious.
I shall explain good conduct, the proper means for true <s>dharma</s> (normative order).
For the practice of one who lacks conduct becomes fruitless.

children.text: ācāraḥ paramo dharma ācāraḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Conduct is the highest <s>dharma</s>; conduct is the highest austerity.

children.text: ācāraḥ paramā vidyā ācāraḥ paramā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Conduct is the highest knowledge; conduct is the highest goal.
For men who possess good conduct there is fearlessness everywhere.
Likewise, for those who lack conduct there is fear everywhere.
Through good conduct they attain divinity and sagehood, O fair-faced one.
Likewise, through transgression of conduct they come to birth in bad wombs.
A man without conduct becomes censured in the world.
Therefore one who desires complete success should possess proper conduct.
A person of bad conduct, though much purified, is more sinful and a defiler of knowledge.
One should diligently perform the <s>dharma</s> stated in the rules for <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s>.
Whatever action is prescribed for a person, by doing that he is always dear to me.
He should be devoted to <s>sandhyā</s> worship, evening and morning, with a clear mind.
Beginning before sunrise and sunset, he should perform it according to rule, being pure.
From desire, delusion, fear, or greed, a twice-born man should not neglect the <s>sandhyā</s>.
For through neglect of the <s>sandhyā</s>, a brahmin falls from brahminhood.

children.text: asatyaṃ na vadet kiṃcinna satyaṃ ca parityajet ||
children.translated_text: He should not speak any falsehood, nor should he abandon truth.
That which is truth they call <s>Brahman</s>; falsehood is a defilement of <s>Brahman</s>.
Untruth, harsh speech, deceit, and slander are causes of sin.
Another's wife, another's property, and injury to others, always,

children.text: kvaciccāpi na kurvīta vācā ca manasā tathā ||
children.translated_text: he should never commit anywhere, by speech or likewise by mind.
He should avoid food from <s>śūdras</s>, stale food, food offered to a deity, and food from a <s>śrāddha</s> rite,
food of groups, communal food, and food from a king.

children.text: annaśuddhau sattvaśuddhirna mṛdā na jalena vai
children.translated_text: When food is pure, <s>sattva</s> (inner clarity) is pure, not by clay or by water.
When <s>sattva</s> is pure, accomplishment arises; therefore one should purify food.
Brahmins who speak of <s>Brahman</s> are burned by gifts from kings;
even boiled seeds have no further birth.
A royal gift is terrible; knowing it from the start to be like poison,
a wise man should avoid it, and he should also avoid dog meat.

children.text: asnātvā na ca bhuñjīyād ajapo 'gnimapūjya ca
children.translated_text: He should not eat without bathing, without recitation, or without worshipping the fire.

children.text: parṇapṛṣṭhe na bhuñjīyādrātrau dīpaṃ vinā tathā ||
children.translated_text: He should not eat on the back of a leaf, nor at night without a lamp.

children.text: bhinnabhāṇḍe ca rathyāyāṃ patitānāṃ ca saṃnidhau
children.translated_text: Nor should he eat from a broken vessel, in a road, or in the presence of fallen people.
He should not eat leftovers from a <s>śūdra</s>, nor shared food even with children.
He should eat pure, unctuous food, prepared and consecrated by mantra.

children.text: bhoktā śiva iti smṛtvā maunī caikāgramānasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Remembering that the eater is <s>Śiva</s>, he should be silent and one-pointed in mind.
He should not drink water directly with his mouth, nor while standing, nor even from cupped hands,
nor with the left hand, on a bed, or likewise with another hand.
He should not take shelter in the shade of <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>arka</s>, <s>kārañja</s>, or <s>snuhi</s>,
nor in the shade of posts, lamps, human beings, or other living creatures.
One should not travel on a road alone, nor cross a river by means of the arms.
One should not descend into a well or the like, nor climb tall trees.
Facing away from the sun, fire, water, gods, or teachers, O auspicious one,

children.text: na kuryādiha kāryāṇi japakarma śubhāni vā ||
children.translated_text: one should not perform duties here, nor acts of <s>japa</s> or other auspicious rites.

children.text: agnau na tāpayetpādau hastaṃ padbhyāṃ na saṃspṛśet
children.translated_text: He should not warm his feet at the fire, nor touch his hand with his feet.

children.text: agnernocchrayam āsīta nāgnau kiṃcin malaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: He should not sit in a place higher than the fire, nor throw any impurity into the fire.
He should not strike water with his feet, nor cast bodily impurity into water.
He should wash impurity on the bank; after washing, he should perform his bath.
Water from bathing, cloth, or a pot, shaken off by the tips of nails and hair,
is inauspicious for human beings and impure, if one should touch it.
If a foolish-minded person touches particles produced by brushing goats, horses, hoofed animals, or camels,

children.text: saṃspṛśed yadi mūḍhātmā śriyaṃ hanti harerapi ||
children.translated_text: he destroys even the prosperity of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: mārjāraś ca gṛhe yasya so'pyantyajasamo naraḥ
children.translated_text: A man in whose house there is a cat is also equal to an outcaste.
And if one feeds eminent Brahmins in the presence of a cat,
that should be known as equal to a <s>Cāṇḍāla</s>; no deliberation is to be made about this.
Wind from the buttocks, wind from a winnowing basket, breath, and air from the mouth:
when these touch a person, they carry away his good deeds.
Wearing a turban, wearing a cuirass or jacket, naked, with hair loose, covered with dirt,
with an impure hand, unclean, or talking incoherently, one should never perform japa.
Anger, intoxication, hunger, drowsiness, spitting, and yawning,
the sight of a dog or a low person, sleep, and idle talk: these are enemies of japa.
Even if any of these occur, one should look at the sun and the other lights,

children.text: ācamya vā japeccheṣaṃ kṛtvā vā prāṇasaṃyamam
children.translated_text: or, having sipped water, recite the rest, or else restrain the breath.
The sun, fire, the moon, planets, lunar mansions, and stars:

children.text: ete jyotīṃṣi proktāni vidvadbhir brāhmaṇais tathā
children.translated_text: these are declared to be lights by learned Brahmins.

children.text: prasārya pādau na japetkukkuṭāsana eva ca ||
children.translated_text: One should not perform japa with the feet stretched out, nor in the cock posture,
nor without a seat, nor lying down, nor in a street, nor in the presence of a Śūdra.

children.text: raktabhūmyāṃ ca khaṭvāyāṃ na japejjāpakas tathā ||
children.translated_text: Likewise a reciter should not perform japa on red ground or on a bed.
Seated on a seat, he should recite properly, with his mind fixed on the meaning of the mantra.

children.text: kauśeyaṃ vyāghracarmaṃ vā cailaṃ taulamathāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: He should prepare a seat of silk, tiger-skin, cloth, or cotton,
or one made of wood or palm-leaf.

children.text: trisaṃdhyaṃ tu guroḥ pūjā kartavyā hitamicchatā ||
children.translated_text: One who desires welfare should worship the guru at the three twilights.

children.text: yo guruḥ sa śivaḥ prokto yaḥ śivaḥ sa guruḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The guru is declared to be <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> is remembered as the guru.

children.text: yathā śivas tathā vidyā yathā vidyā tathā guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: As <s>Śiva</s> is, so is vidyā; as vidyā is, so is the guru.
Therefore devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, vidyā, and the guru has an equal fruit.
O goddess, he consists of all the gods and indeed consists of all powers.

children.text: saguṇo nirguṇo vāpi tasyājñāṃ śirasā vahet
children.translated_text: Whether with attributes or without attributes, one should bear his command on one's head.

children.text: śreyo'rthī yastu gurvājñāṃ manasāpi na laṅghayet ||
children.translated_text: One who seeks the highest good should not transgress the guru's command even in thought.
One who properly obeys the guru's command attains the wealth of knowledge.
While walking, standing, sleeping, or eating, whatever action one may undertake,
if it is in his presence, all of it should be done with the guru's permission.
In the presence of the guru or of a god, one should not sit just as one pleases.
For the guru is directly a god, and his house is a temple of the gods.

children.text: pāpinā ca yathāsaṃgāt tatpāpaiḥ patanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Just as, through association with a sinner, one may fall because of those sins,
so, through association with the ācārya, one becomes a sharer in the fruit of his dharma.
Just as, from contact with fire, gold gives up its impurity,
so, from contact with the guru, a human being gives up sin.
Just as a jar of ghee placed near fire melts,
so sin melts away in the presence of the ācārya.

children.text: yathā prajvalito vahnir viṣṭhāṃ kāṣṭhaṃ ca nirdahet ||
children.translated_text: Just as a blazing fire burns up dung and wood,
so the guru, when pleased, burns up sin by the power of his mantra.

children.text: brahmā haris tathā rudro devāś ca munayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the gods, and likewise the sages

children.text: kurvantyanugrahaṃ tuṣṭā gurau tuṣṭe na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: bestow grace when the guru is pleased; there is no doubt.

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā guroḥ krodhaṃ na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: By deed, mind, and speech one should not cause the guru's anger.
By his anger, lifespan, prosperity, knowledge, and good rites are burned up.

children.text: tatkrodhaṃ ye kariṣyanti teṣāṃ yajñāś ca niṣphalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those who will provoke his anger have fruitless sacrifices,
and their japas and observances are fruitless too; no deliberation is needed about this.
With every effort one should not utter a word contrary to the guru.

children.text: vaded yadi mahāmohād rauravaṃ narakaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: If, from great delusion, one should utter it, one goes to the hell <s>Raurava</s>.

children.text: cittenaiva ca vittena tathā vācā ca suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: With mind, wealth, and likewise with speech, O well-vowed ones,

children.text: mithyā na kārayeddevi kriyayā ca guroḥ sadā
children.translated_text: O goddess, one should never behave falsely toward the guru, nor by ritual action.
When his bad qualities are proclaimed, one becomes a hundredfold sharer in the lack of qualities.

children.text: guṇe tu khyāpite tasya sārvaguṇyaphalaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: But when his good quality is proclaimed, the fruit is the possession of all qualities.

children.text: gurorhitaṃ priyaṃ kuryādādiṣṭo vā na vā sadā ||
children.translated_text: One should always do what is beneficial and pleasing to the guru, whether commanded or not.

children.text: asamakṣaṃ samakṣaṃ vā guroḥ kāryaṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: Whether outside his presence or in his presence, one should carry out the guru's business.
One should do what is beneficial and pleasing to the guru by actions of mind, speech, and body.
Acting otherwise, one falls downward and revolves there again and again.
Therefore he is always to be worshipped and always to be venerated.
Even when nearby, one should speak to the guru only after asking permission and without turning away from him.
Thus, one who has such conduct, who is devoted and always intent on japa,
and who does what is pleasing to the guru, is then fit to apply the mantra.
I shall explain the application and the purpose of a perfected mantra.
A mantra becomes weak for one who does not know its application.

children.text: yasya yena viyuñjīta kāryeṇa tu viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: The particular task to which one applies it,
that should be understood as viniyoga, bringing fruit in this world and the next.
From application arise longevity, health, and lasting soundness of the body,

children.text: rājyaiśvaryaṃ ca vijñānaṃ svargo nirvāṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: royal sovereignty, prosperity, discriminating knowledge, heaven, and even nirvāṇa.
Sprinkling, consecration, and aghamarṣaṇa,
and also in bathing and at the two twilights, should be done with the eleventh.
Being pure, one should climb a mountain and recite one hundred thousand times without sloth.
In a great river one should recite two hundred thousand times, and one obtains long life.
Dūrvā sprouts, sesame seeds, vāṇī, guḍūcī, and ghuṭikā:
an oblation of ten thousand of these increases longevity.
Taking shelter at an aśvattha tree, a wise person should recite two hundred thousand times.
On the day of <s>Śanaiścara</s>, having touched it, a man obtains long life.
On the day of <s>Śanaiścara</s>, the wise man should touch the aśvattha tree with his hands.
He should recite one hundred and eight times; <s>Soma</s> becomes a remover of death.
Facing <s>Āditya</s>, he should recite one hundred thousand times with undivided mind.
Having recited eight hundred times with arka offerings and making oblations, he is freed from disease.
For the pacification of all diseases, a man should use palāśa fuel-sticks.

children.text: hutvā daśasahasraṃ tu nirogī manujo bhavet
children.translated_text: Having offered ten thousand oblations, the human being becomes free from illness.
Having recited eight hundred times daily, he should drink water in the presence of the sun.
Within a single month he is freed from all abdominal diseases.
With eleven recitations he should eat food that has been consecrated by mantra.
Other edible food and drink as well, even poison, becomes nectar.

children.text: japel lakṣaṃ tu pūrvāhṇe hutvā cāṣṭaśatena vai ||
children.translated_text: He should recite one hundred thousand times in the forenoon and offer oblations with eight hundred recitations.
Attending upon the sun daily, he obtains complete health.
He should touch a fine jar filled with river water.
After reciting ten thousand times, bathing with that water becomes a remedy for diseases.
Pure, he should eat food each day after reciting over it twenty-eight times.

children.text: hutvā ca tāvatpālāśair evaṃ vārogyam aśnute
children.translated_text: And having offered the same number of oblations with palāśa sticks, he thus obtains health.
At an eclipse of the moon or sun, having first fasted according to rule and being pure,
as long as the eclipse lasts, he should remain concentrated in a river.
He should recite in a river that goes to the ocean until the release of the eclipse.
With one thousand and eight recitations he should drink the juice of brāhmī, O twice-born ones.
He obtains in this world auspicious intelligence that can retain all the śāstras.
The goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> becomes his speech, and his utterance is beyond human measure.
When there are afflictions from planets and constellations, a man should recite ten thousand times with devotion.
And having offered eight thousand oblations, he removes the affliction of the planets.
On seeing a bad dream, a man should bathe and recite ten thousand times.
Having offered eight hundred oblations with ghee, there will immediately be pacification.
At an eclipse of the moon or sun, having worshipped the liṅga according to rule,
whatever he should pray for, O goddess, he should recite ten thousand times with respect.
In the presence of this god, pure and with mind restrained,
a man obtains all desires; there is no doubt about this.
Especially for elephants, horses, and the breeds of cattle,
when disease has appeared, one should become pure and offer an oblation with fuel-sticks.
Having worshipped for a month according to rule, with ten thousand recitations and endowed with devotion,

children.text: teṣāmṛddhiś ca śāntiś ca bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: their increase and pacification will occur; there is no doubt.
In an upheaval or when troubled by enemies, the pure person should offer ten thousand oblations.
With palāśa fuel-sticks, O goddess, his pacification will occur.
When afflicted by an abhicāra rite, O goddess, he should perform this rite.

children.text: pratyag bhavati tacchaktiḥ śatroḥ pīḍā bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: That power turns back, and the enemy will suffer affliction.
For the purpose of causing enmity, he should offer eight vibhītaka fuel-sticks.
This is done with the syllables in reverse order, or with fresh blood.
Smeared with poison and blood, it causes enmity among people.
I shall proclaim expiation for purification from all sins.
When a man has undertaken to make purification from sin properly,
purification from sin is complete because it is caused by the attainment of knowledge.
If a person's purification from sin has not occurred, all rites are fruitless.
And knowledge declines; therefore purification from sin must be performed.
For the purification of knowledge and prosperity, having meditated on me with cupped hands, O auspicious one,
he should sprinkle himself all around with waters accompanied by the elevenfold <s>Śiva</s> mantra.
With one hundred and eight recitations he should bathe for purification from sin.
That is equal to the fruit of all tīrthas and is auspicious, removing all sins.
If the worship at the twilights has been interrupted, a man should recite eight hundred times.
Food touched by feces, pigs, caṇḍālas, wicked people, or even cocks

children.text: spṛṣṭamannaṃ na bhuñjīta bhuktvā cāṣṭaśataṃ japet ||
children.translated_text: he should not eat; if he has eaten it, he should recite eight hundred times.
For purification from brahmahatyā, a man should recite one hundred and ten thousand times.
For the pātakas, half of that is required; there is no need for deliberation here.
For those defiled by upapātakas, half of that is declared.
For the remaining sins also, he should recite five thousand times.
This is the secret teaching concerned with knowledge of the self and illuminating knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>.
He becomes <s>Śiva</s>; untroubled, he should recite the mantra five hundred thousand times.
A human being happily obtains mastery over the five vital airs, O gracious one.
He should recite five hundred thousand times, with the senses subdued and being pure.
Mastery over the five senses will arise, O beautiful-faced one.
Whoever, joined with meditation, recites five hundred thousand times without agitation,

children.text: viṣayāṇāṃ ca pañcānāṃ jayaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: that human being obtains mastery over the five sense-objects.
Whoever recites the fourth set of five hundred thousand with devotion,
that human being here obtains mastery over the five elements.
Whoever recites four hundred thousand times, carefully restraining the mind,
obtains full mastery over the inner faculties, O beautiful-faced one.
By reciting two million five hundred thousand times, O lotus-faced one,
a human being obtains mastery over the twenty-five tattvas.
At midnight, in utter stillness, he should recite ten thousand times with respect.
Through this vow he obtains brahman-attainment, O beautiful one.
Without laziness, he should recite one hundred thousand times in a windless place, free from sound.

children.text: madhyarātre ca śivayoḥ paśyatyeva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: At midnight he surely sees <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s>; there is no doubt.
And the destruction of darkness, like the shining of a lamp,
will occur within the heart or outside it; there is no doubt.
For the sake of complete prosperity, a self-possessed man should recite it ten thousand times.
Being pure, he should recite the mantra, enclosed together with its seed syllable, a hundred lakhs of times.
If he is devoted, he attains union with me; what is higher than this?
Thus I have told you the whole sequence of the rule for the <s>pañcākṣara</s> (five-syllabled mantra).

children.text: yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyādvāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: Whoever recites it or hears it goes to the supreme goal.
