And one who teaches the sequence of the rule for the <s>pañcākṣara</s> to pure twice-born men,

children.text: daive karmaṇi pitrye vā śivaloke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: whether in a divine rite or in an ancestral rite, is honored in <s>Śivaloka</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge pañcākṣaramāhātmyaṃ nāma pañcāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the illustrious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the eighty-fifth chapter, named "The Greatness of the Five-Syllabled Mantra."
The seers said:
Brahmins whose sins have been burned say that what is highest beyond <s>japa</s> (recitation)
is the splendid meditation-sacrifice for those who are detached and awakened.
Therefore tell us now, O <s>Sūta</s>, the meditation-sacrifice in its entirety,
in detail and with every care, for the great-souled ones who are detached.
Hearing those words of the sages who were engaged in a long sacrificial session,

children.text: rudreṇa kathitaṃ prāha guhāṃ prāpya mahātmanām ||
children.translated_text: he told the great-souled ones what had been spoken by <s>Rudra</s>, after reaching the cave,
after the poison called <s>Kālakūṭa</s> had indeed been taken in, in a deed for the whole world.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: guhāṃ prāpya sukhāsīnaṃ bhavānyā saha śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: Having reached the cave, where <s>Śaṅkara</s> was seated happily with <s>Bhavānī</s>,
the sages, with disciplined selves, bowed to him who dwelt in the cave,
and then all praised the blue-throated husband of <s>Umā</s>.
The extremely fierce poison called <s>Kālakūṭa</s> has been taken in by you, O blessed lord.

children.text: ataḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ sarvaṃ tvayā deva vṛṣadhvaja ||
children.translated_text: Therefore everything has been made firm by you, O god, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
Hearing those words of theirs, the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
the soul of the universe, smiling, spoke to those headed by <s>Sanandana</s>:
"What is the use of this, O best of the twice-born? I shall speak of a poison that is very terrible.

children.text: saṃharettadviṣaṃ yastu sa samartho hyanena kim ||
children.translated_text: Whoever can remove that poison is truly capable; what has he to do with this one?
The poison called <s>Kālakūṭa</s> is not poison; <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is called poison.
Therefore by every effort one should remove that very terrible poison.
<s>Saṃsāra</s> is said to be twofold, in accordance with one's own eligibility,
unexhausted and very terrible for men whose minds are utterly deluded.
Because of the fault of attachment to desires there is creation; by knowledge, O men of good vows,
under its power alone, for all beings, there are <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; there is no doubt.
Even with regard to an object not close at hand, scripture, when heard from the good,
surely produces understanding of <s>saṃsāra</s> among the learned, O twice-born men.
Therefore, since what is seen and what is learned from tradition are both tainted in nature,
one should abandon them with every effort; such a person is called detached.
The portion of revelation that concerns ritual actions is called scripture, O twice-born men;
it is the head of <s>Brahman</s>, the essence of the seers, and the fruit of action.

children.text: nanu svabhāvaḥ sarveṣāṃ kāmo dṛṣṭo na cānyathā
children.translated_text: But desire is seen to be the nature of all beings, and not otherwise;
for those who do not know this, revelation serves as an instigator toward ritual action.
Here <s>dharma</s> marked by cessation is taught for those who are capable.
Therefore the <s>saṃsāra</s> of all embodied beings is indeed rooted in ignorance.
The <s>kalā</s> (limiting power) dries up through action, because of an altered nature;
the soul furnished with <s>kalā</s> is threefold, lacking knowledge through ignorance.
The sinner becomes hell-bound, while the meritorious one becomes heaven-bound through the weight of merit;
through mixed action, the soul is established in four ways.
There are those born from sprouts, those born from sweat, those born from eggs, and those born from the womb.
Thus the embodied being is conditioned by karma, ignorant and not liberated.

children.text: prajayā karmaṇā muktirdhanena ca satāṃ na hi
children.translated_text: For the good there is no liberation by progeny, by ritual action, or by wealth.
Liberation comes by renunciation alone; in its absence this being wanders on.
Thus, because of the fault of ignorance and under the power of many actions,
this being takes on the body that has arisen as the sixfold sheath.
There are many sufferings in the womb, in the birth passage, and on the earth,

children.text: kaumāre yauvane caiva vārddhake maraṇe'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: in childhood and youth, and likewise in old age and even in death.
On reflection, for good people there is suffering from contact with women and the like, O twice-born men.
Here, for one who suffers, one suffering is indeed quieted by another suffering.

children.text: na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānām upabhogena śāmyati
children.translated_text: Desire is never appeased by the enjoyment of desired objects;
like fire with clarified butter, it grows still more.
Therefore, on reflection, there is no happiness for men even from union,

children.text: arthānām arjane'pyevaṃ pālane ca vyaye tathā ||
children.translated_text: and the same is so in the acquiring of wealth, in its guarding, and in its spending.

children.text: paiśāce rākṣase duḥkhaṃ yākṣe caiva vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: In the <s>Paiśāca</s> and <s>Rākṣasa</s> realms there is suffering, and likewise in the <s>Yākṣa</s> realm, on reflection,

children.text: gāndharve ca tathā cāndre saumyaloke dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and so too in the <s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Cāndra</s>, and gentle worlds, O best of the twice-born.

children.text: prājāpatye tathā brāhme prākṛte pauruṣe tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise in the <s>Prājāpatya</s>, <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prākṛta</s>, and <s>Pauruṣa</s> worlds,
through losses, excesses, and the like, O men of good vows, sufferings remain sufferings.
One should abandon those impure fortunes, and wealth as well.
Therefore enjoyment is eightfold, and likewise established in sixteen ways;
it is also established in twenty-four forms, O men of good vows,
in thirty-two divisions, O blameless ones, and again with forty qualities;
likewise in forty-eight and in fifty-six varieties,
and also in sixty-four forms; for the discerning, it is nothing but suffering.

children.text: pārthivaṃ ca tathāpyaṃ ca taijasaṃ ca vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: The earthly, the watery, and the fiery, on reflection,

children.text: vāyavyaṃ ca tathā vyaumamānasaṃ ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the airy, the etheric, and the mental in due order,
and so too the egoic, the intellectual, and the material,
are nothing but suffering for yogins who speak of <s>Brahman</s>; there is no doubt.
And the secondary state belonging to the <s>Gaṇeśvaras</s> too is nothing but suffering, on reflection.

children.text: ādau madhye tathā cānte sarvalokeṣu sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, in the middle, and at the end, in all worlds and at all times,
sufferings are present, and future sufferings too, exactly as they are.
In lands spoiled by faults there are manifold sufferings too;
yet the ignorant, thinking themselves wise, do not reflect on what has passed away.
Food is said to be for the removal of the affliction of hunger, not for happiness;
just as medicine for other diseases is not for happiness.
Through cold, heat, wind, rain, and the like, at their respective seasons, for embodied beings

children.text: duḥkhameva na saṃdeho na jānanti hyapaṇḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: there is suffering alone, without doubt; but the unlearned do not know it.
Even in heaven, likewise, O best of sages, because of impurity, decline, and the like,
they are afflicted by many kinds of diseases, by passion, hatred, fear, and so on.
As a tree whose root has been cut falls helplessly to the ground,
so, when the tree of merit is exhausted, the inhabitants of heaven fall to earth.
For those fixed in longing for painful things, whose attainments consist in the experience of pain and the like,
there is, from this, harsh suffering for the heavenly beings who fall from heaven.
In hell there is only suffering here, because of resorting to the hells,
and also because those belonging to the varṇas fail to do what is prescribed, O bulls among sages.

children.text: yathā mṛgo mṛtyubhayasya bhīta ucchinnavāso na labheta nidrām
children.translated_text: Just as a deer, terrified by fear of death and with its dwelling destroyed, would not find sleep,

children.text: evaṃ yatirdhyānaparo mahātmā saṃsārabhīto na labheta nidrām ||
children.translated_text: so a great-souled ascetic devoted to meditation, afraid of saṃsāra, would not find sleep.
For insects, birds, wild animals, domestic beasts, elephants, and horses,
unhappiness is plainly seen; therefore the highest happiness belongs to one who renounces.
So too there is suffering for the dwellers in celestial vehicles, for those appointed over a kalpa,
for presiding deities of places, and for <s>Manu</s> and the others, O you of good vows.
For gods and daityas too, because of their wish to conquer one another,
there is only suffering; and so also for kings and rākṣasas in the three worlds.
In truth, the āśrama too, for the varṇas, is for toil and discipline.

children.text: āśramairna ca devaiś ca yajñaiḥ sāṃkhyairvratais tathā ||
children.translated_text: Not by āśramas, nor by gods, nor by sacrifices, nor by Sāṃkhya doctrines, nor by vows,
nor by fierce and various austerities, nor even by many kinds of gifts,

children.text: na labhante tathātmānaṃ labhante jñāninaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: do they attain the Self in the way that knowers attain it by themselves.
Therefore, with every effort, one should practice the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.
A wise man should always lie on ashes while observing the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.
Endowed with knowledge of the five objects and concentrated on the principle of <s>Śiva</s>,
the wise man, possessing the yoga that brings kaivalya and cuts off various actions,
endowed with the yoga of the five objects, reaches the end of suffering, being intelligent.

children.text: parayā vidyayā vedyaṃ vidantyaparayā na hi ||
children.translated_text: By the higher knowledge they know what is to be known; by the lower knowledge they do not.

children.text: dve vidye veditavye hi parā caivāparā tathā
children.translated_text: Two kinds of knowledge are indeed to be known: the higher and also the lower.
Among these, the lower is the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda, O best of twice-born men,
and likewise the Sāmaveda and the Atharvaveda, the Veda that accomplishes all aims;

children.text: śikṣā kalpo vyākaraṇaṃ niruktaṃ chanda eva ca ||
children.translated_text: phonetics, ritual procedure, grammar, etymology, and meter,
and astrology: these are lower knowledge; the higher is established as the imperishable.
That is invisible, that is ungraspable, without lineage, without color;
that has no eye, no ear, no hand, and no foot.
That is unborn and uncreated; that is soundless, O best of twice-born men.
That is without touch and without form, devoid of taste and smell.

children.text: avyayaṃ cāpratiṣṭhaṃ ca tannityaṃ sarvagaṃ vibhum ||
children.translated_text: That is undecaying and without fixed support; that is eternal, all-pervading, mighty.

children.text: mahāntaṃ tad bṛhantaṃ ca tadajaṃ cinmayaṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: That is great and vast; that is unborn and made of consciousness, O twice-born men.
That is without breath and without mind, not moist and not red.
That is immeasurable, not gross, not long, and not excessive.
That is not short, is boundless, is bliss, and is unfailing.
That is uncovered, non-dual, endless, and beyond the range of the senses.

children.text: asaṃvṛtaṃ tadātmaikaṃ parā vidyā na cānyathā ||
children.translated_text: That is unobstructed, the one Self; higher knowledge is this, and not otherwise.
The higher and the lower have been described, but in ultimate truth they are not separate here.
I alone am the whole universe; in me alone is the entire universe.
From me it arises; it stands in me, and in me alone it dissolves.
One should behold nothing other than me through mind, speech, and action.
Being concentrated, one should see everything, both existent and nonexistent, in the Self.

children.text: sarvaṃ hyātmani saṃpaśyan na bāhye kurute manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seeing everything in the Self, one does not turn the mind toward what is external.
With the gaze directed downward, a span above the navel it is situated;
one should know that to be the heart, the great abode of the universe.
In the middle of this heart there is a lotus situated,
sprung from the bulb of dharma, with a beautiful stalk of knowledge.
It is white, with the eight powers as petals, and with supreme detachment as its pericarp.

children.text: chidrāṇi ca diśo yasya prāṇādyāś ca pratiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Its openings are the directions, and the breaths beginning with prāṇa are established there.
Joined with the breaths beginning with prāṇa, it sees in many ways, step by step.
There are ten nāḍīs that carry the vital breaths, O bulls among sages;
for each, seventy-two thousand nāḍīs are proclaimed.
One should know waking to be located in the eyes; one should assign dream to the throat.

children.text: suṣuptaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ tu turīyaṃ mūrdhani sthitam
children.translated_text: Deep sleep is located in the heart, while the fourth state, turīya, is situated in the head.

children.text: jāgre brahmā ca viṣṇuś ca svapne caiva yathākramāt ||
children.translated_text: In waking is <s>Brahmā</s>, and in dream is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, each in due order;

children.text: īśvarastu suṣupte tu turīye ca maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: but <s>Īśvara</s> is in deep sleep, and <s>Maheśvara</s> in turīya.
Now others too say this: when a person is functioning with all the instruments,
then that condition of his is called waking.
Mind, intellect, ego, and thought: this is the fourfold group.
When he is established with these, that is called dream.
When the instruments have dissolved into his own Self, O you of good vows,
he is in deep sleep; when separated from the instruments, he is called turīya.
Beyond turīya is <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause.
Waking, dream, deep sleep, and turīya are spoken of as pertaining to the elements,
and also as pertaining to the self and, O best of Brahmins, as pertaining to the deities.
One who understands should know that all that is indeed I myself.
The faculties of cognition, O best of brahmins, and also the organs of action,
mind, intellect, ego, and citta: this fourfold set
is separately remembered as the fourteenfold <s>adhyātma</s> (inner principle).

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ caiva śrotavyaṃ ghrātavyaṃ ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: What is to be seen, what is to be heard, and what is to be smelled, in order,
what is to be tasted, O best of sages, and likewise what is to be touched,
what is to be thought, what is to be understood, and what is to be ego-appropriated,
and likewise what is to be attended to, and what is to be spoken, O bulls among sages,
what is to be taken, what is to be gone to, what is to be emitted,
and what is to be enjoyed: these are the <s>adhibhūta</s> (elemental-object) factors in order.
<s>Āditya</s>, the directions, the earth, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: vāyuścandras tathā brahmā rudraḥ kṣetrajña eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, the moon, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field),
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, the god <s>Prajāpati</s>:
thus the <s>ādhidaivika</s> (divine) aspect is fourteenfold in order.

children.text: rājñī sudarśanā caiva jitā saumyā yathākramam
children.translated_text: <s>Rājñī</s>, <s>Sudarśanā</s>, <s>Jitā</s>, and <s>Saumyā</s>, in order,

children.text: moghā rudrāmṛtā satyā madhyamā ca dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Moghā</s>, <s>Rudrā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Madhyamā</s>, O best of twice-born,

children.text: nāḍī rāśiśukā caiva asurā caiva kṛttikā
children.translated_text: <s>Nāḍī</s>, <s>Rāśiśukā</s>, <s>Asurā</s>, and <s>Kṛttikā</s>,
and <s>Bhāsvatī</s>: these nāḍīs are the fourteen supports.
The vāyus situated in the middle of the nāḍīs, and the carriers, are fourteen:

children.text: prāṇo vyānastvapānaś ca udānaś ca samānakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Samāna</s>,

children.text: vairambhaś ca tathā mukhyo hyantaryāmaḥ prabhañjanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vairambha</s>, and likewise <s>Mukhya</s>, <s>Antaryāma</s>, and <s>Prabhañjana</s>,

children.text: kūrmakaś ca tathā śyenaḥ śvetaḥ kṛṣṇas tathānilaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kūrmaka</s>, and likewise <s>Śyena</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Anila</s>,

children.text: nāga ityeva kathitā vāyavaś ca caturdaśa
children.translated_text: and <s>Nāga</s>: so the vāyus are declared to be fourteen.
That one who is in the eyes, then in what is to be seen, and likewise in <s>Āditya</s>, O well-vowed ones,

children.text: nāḍyāṃ prāṇe ca vijñāne tvānande ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: in the nāḍī, in prāṇa, in cognition, and in bliss, in due order,
who is the supreme one within all this, in this ether of the heart,

children.text: ātmā ekaś ca carati tamupāsīta māṃ prabhum
children.translated_text: the one Self who moves there: one should worship him as me, the Lord,
that ageless, endless, sorrowless, immortal, and firm one.
He alone moves among the fourteenfold categories.

children.text: līyante tāni tatraiva yadanyaṃ nāsti vai dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They dissolve there alone, since there is truly nothing else, O twice-born.

children.text: eka eva hi sarvajñaḥ sarveśastveka eva saḥ
children.translated_text: He alone is the one omniscient being; he alone is the lord of all.
This god is the ruler of all, the inner controller, of great radiance.
Worshiped by all, he is eternal and consists of all happiness.
And he does not worship anything here, O best of twice-born; he is all happiness.
Though worshiped by the Vedas and by many kinds of śāstras,

children.text: na vaiṣa vedaśāstrāṇi sarvajño yāsyati prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: this omniscient Lord will not be encompassed by the Vedas and śāstras.

children.text: asyaivānnamidaṃ sarvaṃ na so'nnaṃ bhavati svayam
children.translated_text: All this is food for him alone; he himself does not become food.
Guarded by his own self, he may eat what has become food, but nowhere is he food.
Everywhere I am the food of living beings, the knot of living beings.
He is the ruler and guide, and is fivefold as self by division.
As food-made, he is the elemental self, and because he is eaten he is called food.
As prāṇa-made he is the self of the senses; as mind-made he is the self of resolve.
As time-self he is <s>Soma</s> here, and is called cognition-made.
Having become ever bliss-made, he is <s>Maheśa</s>, the supreme Lord.

children.text: so'ham evaṃ jagatsarvaṃ mayyeva sakalaṃ sthitam
children.translated_text: Thus I myself am the whole world; everything stands in me alone.
It is dependent even on the independent one, since, on examination, without that it does not exist.
Even oneness itself does not exist there; whence, then, could duality arise?
In this way even the mortal does not exist; whence the immortal, O <s>Ajodbhava</s>?
It is not inwardly conscious, not outwardly conscious, nor in both ways.
Nor, in this way, is it a mass of consciousness, nor a knowing subject preceded by knowledge.

children.text: viditaṃ nāsti vedyaṃ ca nirvāṇaṃ paramārthataḥ
children.translated_text: There is neither the known nor what is to be known; in the highest truth it is <s>nirvāṇa</s> (extinction).
<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>kaivalya</s> (aloneness), the highest good, and the disease-free state,
the immortal, the imperishable, <s>brahman</s>, the supreme Self, the higher and lower,
the nonconceptual, the appearance-free: these are synonyms for knowledge.

children.text: prasannaṃ ca yadekāgraṃ tadā jñānamiti smṛtam
children.translated_text: That which is clear and one-pointed is remembered as knowledge.
Everything else is ignorance; no deliberation is to be made about this.
Thus this clear cognition, certainly born from contact with the guru,
always untouched by attachment, aversion, falsehood, anger, desire, thirst, and the like,
should be recognized even now as this knowledge that grants liberation.
Because of the prior impurity of ignorance, the person is remembered as impure.
By the destruction of that impurity liberation comes to be, not otherwise in tens of millions of births.
Without knowledge alone, there is no destruction of merit and sin.
Therefore one should practice knowledge alone for the sake of liberation, O best knowers of brahman.
For by the practice of knowledge, the intellect of human beings becomes stainless.
Therefore one should always practice knowledge, being devoted to it and intent upon it.
For the yogin satisfied by knowledge alone and free from attachment,

children.text: kartavyaṃ nāsti viprendrā asti cettattvavinna ca
children.translated_text: there is nothing to be done, O best of brahmins; if there is, he is not a knower of reality.

children.text: iha loke pare cāpi kartavyaṃ nāsti tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: Neither in this world nor in the next is there anything for him to do.
Therefore he is liberated while living, truly a knower of brahman in the highest sense.
Always devoted to the practice of knowledge, he himself knows the meaning of the truth of knowledge.
Having abandoned the practice of duties, he attains knowledge alone.
Whoever is proud of caste and life-stage, even if he has abandoned anger, O best of twice-born,

children.text: anyatra ramate mūḍhaḥ so 'jñānī nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: and delights elsewhere, that fool is ignorant; there is no doubt about this.
Ignorance is the cause of saṃsāra; saṃsāra is the taking on of a body.
Likewise knowledge is the cause of mokṣa; the liberated one is established in his own self.

children.text: ajñāne sati viprendrāḥ krodhādyā nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When ignorance is present, O lords of brahmins, anger and the rest arise here; there is no doubt.

children.text: krodho harṣas tathā lobho moho dambho dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Anger, joy, greed, delusion, and pride arise, O best of twice-born ones,
and from them indeed come <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; under their control the taking up of a body occurs.

children.text: śarīre sati vai kleśaḥ so'vidyāṃ saṃtyajedbudhaḥ
children.translated_text: When there is a body there is certainly affliction; the wise man should therefore abandon ignorance.

children.text: avidyāṃ vidyayā hitvā sthitasyaiva ca yoginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the yogin who remains established after abandoning ignorance through knowledge,

children.text: krodhādyā nāśamāyānti dharmādharmau ca vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: anger and the rest perish, and so too do <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, O twice-born ones.
And through the destruction of these he is not again joined with a body.
He alone is liberated from <s>saṃsāra</s>, free from the threefold suffering.

children.text: evaṃ jñānaṃ vinā nāsti dhyānaṃ dhyātur dvijarṣabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus without knowledge there is no meditation, nor a meditator, O bulls among twice-born seers.
Knowledge truly comes from contact with the guru, not from speech in the highest sense.
Having understood it as the fourfold formation, the meditator should practice meditation.
Innate and adventitious sin, and likewise sin arising from body and speech,
the fire of knowledge quickly burns up, as fire burns dry fuel.
There is nothing higher than knowledge for the destruction of all sins.
One should always cultivate knowledge, free from every attachment.
For the knower, all sins waste away; there is no doubt about this.
Even while playing, he is not stained by sins, though they be of many kinds.

children.text: jñānaṃ yathā tathā dhyānaṃ tasmāddhyānaṃ samabhyaset
children.translated_text: As knowledge is, so is meditation; therefore one should practice meditation.

children.text: dhyānaṃ nirviṣayaṃ proktam ādau saviṣayaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Meditation is said to be without an object, and at first also with an object.
Having practiced it in six forms, and also through sets of four, six, and ten,

children.text: tathā dvādaśadhā caiva punaḥ ṣoḍaśadhā kramāt ||
children.translated_text: likewise twelvefold and again sixteenfold, in order,

children.text: dvidhābhyasya ca yogīndro mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: the lord among yogins, having practiced it in the two ways, is liberated; there is no doubt.
Like the form of pure Jāmbūnada gold, resembling smokeless embers,
yellow, red, white, and shining like many millions of lightning flashes,
or else, having carefully placed the mind in the brahmarandhra,

children.text: na sitaṃ vāsitaṃ pītaṃ na smared brahmavid bhavet
children.translated_text: one should not remember white, colored, or yellow; he may become a knower of brahman.
Nonviolent, truthful, and by every effort not stealing,
free from possessiveness, celibate, and firm in his vow,
contented, endowed with purity, and always devoted to self-study,
devoted to me, he should practice meditation that is certainly born from contact with the guru.

children.text: na budhyati tathā dhyātā sthāpya cittaṃ dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meditator does not cognize in that way after placing the mind, O best of twice-born ones.

children.text: na cābhimanyate yogī na paśyati samantataḥ
children.translated_text: The yogin does not form self-conceit, nor does he see anything around him.

children.text: na ghrāti na śṛṇotyeva līnaḥ svātmani yaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: He does not smell and does not hear, he who is himself absorbed in his own self.

children.text: na ca sparśaṃ vijānāti sa vai samarasaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: And he does not perceive touch; he is remembered as one of equal essence.

children.text: pārthive paṭale brahmā vāritattve hariḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: In the earthly layer is <s>Brahmā</s>; in the water principle is <s>Hari</s> himself.
In the fiery principle he is called <s>Kālarudra</s>; in the wind principle, <s>Maheśvara</s>.
In the hollow space he is <s>Śiva</s> directly; one should contemplate thus in order.

children.text: kṣitau śarvaḥ smṛto devo hy apāṃ bhava iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: On earth the god is remembered as <s>Śarva</s>; in the waters he is remembered as <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: rudra eva tathā vahnau ugro vāyau vyavasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In fire he is <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Ugra</s> is established in wind.
In the hollow sky he is <s>Bhīma</s>; he is situated in the solar orb.

children.text: īśānaḥ somabimbe ca mahādeva iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the lunar disk he is <s>Īśāna</s>, and he is remembered as <s>Mahādeva</s>.
For beings he is the god <s>Paśupati</s>; I am established in eight forms.
Whatever hardness there is in the body is all declared to be earthy.
The watery is said to be liquid, and fire is said to be what is called color.
What moves is wind; whatever is hollow, O best of twice-born ones,
that is space, and cognition born of sound arises from the ether.
Likewise, O brahmins, cognition called touch is born of wind.
Form is said to belong to fire; taste, O twice-born ones, is made of water.
What is called smell is earthy; then one should contemplate the sun in order.

children.text: netre ca dakṣiṇe vāme somaṃ hṛdi vibhuṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: One should contemplate it in the right eye, the moon in the left, and the all-pervading lord in the heart, O twice-born ones.
Up to the knees is the earth principle; up to the navel is the circle of water.
Up to the throat is the fire principle, O best of twice-born ones, and up to the forehead,

children.text: vāyavyaṃ vai lalāṭādyaṃ vyomākhyaṃ vā śikhāgrakam ||
children.translated_text: is the wind principle beginning from the forehead, or what is called space up to the tip of the topknot.

children.text: haṃsākhyaṃ ca tato brahma vyomnaścordhvaṃ tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Then comes brahman called <s>Haṃsa</s>, and beyond space there is thereafter the supreme.
One should remember this first principle, called space, situated in the middle of space.

children.text: na jīvaḥ prakṛtiḥ sattvaṃ rajaścātha tamaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Not the individual soul, nor prakṛti, nor sattva, nor rajas, nor again tamas,
nor mahat, nor ego, nor the subtle elements, nor the senses,
nor the elements beginning with space exist here in the highest reality.
Because he stands pervading the universe, he is called <s>Sthāṇu</s>.

children.text: udeti sūryo bhītaś ca pavate vāta eva ca
children.translated_text: In fear of him the sun rises, and the wind itself blows.
The moon shines, fire burns, and the waters flow.
The earth supports, and space gives room.
By his command all this is extended; therefore one should contemplate him, O twice-born ones.
Since all this, O best of twice-born ones, is governed by him alone,
one should remember <s>Bhava</s>, thinking that <s>Śarva</s> consists of all forms.
For those scorched by the poison of <s>saṃsāra</s>, through the nectar of knowledge and meditation,
the remedy has been explained, O best of twice-born ones, and not otherwise.
Knowledge is directly born from <s>dharma</s>; from knowledge arises dispassion.
From dispassion comes supreme knowledge, which illuminates the highest reality.
For one endowed with knowledge and dispassion, success in yoga arises, O best of twice-born ones.
Through success in yoga there is liberation for one established in sattva, and not otherwise.
That wondrous imperishable state is covered by the state of tamas and ignorance.
Relying on the power of sattva, one should worship <s>Śiva</s>, O twice-born ones.
He who is established in sattva, my devotee, devoted to my worship...
And in every respect he is devoted to <s>dharma</s>, always energetic and composed;
he endures all pairs of opposites, is steadfast, and delights in the welfare of all beings.
His nature is upright; his mind is always sound, and he is always gentle.
He is free from pride, intelligent, peaceful, and has abandoned rivalry, O best of twice-born men.
He always desires liberation, knows <s>dharma</s>, and is marked by the marks of his own Self.
Released from the three debts, he has a share of merit from a former birth.

children.text: jarāyukto dvijo bhūtvā śraddhayā ca guroḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Having become an aged twice-born man, with faith and in due order from his teacher,
or otherwise, having performed service free from artificiality,
he reaches the heavenly world and enjoys its pleasures in succession.
Then, attaining <s>Bhāratavarṣa</s>, he becomes a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, O twice-born men.
Through association he obtains knowledge, and from being knowledgeable he becomes a knower of yoga.
This is the sequence by which one filled with impurity obtains knowledge, O best of twice-born men.
Therefore, by this path, having abandoned attachment and being firm in his vow,
he is freed from what is called the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison of saṃsāra, O foremost sages.
Thus I have briefly declared to you the unfailing teaching,
the greatness of knowledge alone here, auspiciously in this connection.

children.text: evaṃ pāśupataṃ yogaṃ kathitaṃ tvīśvareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga was taught by the Lord.

children.text: na deyaṃ yasya kasyāpi śivoktaṃ munipuṅgavāḥ
children.translated_text: What was spoken by <s>Śiva</s>, O foremost sages, should not be given to just anyone.
It should always be given to a yogin who is devoted to ashes, as something very dear.
The man who recites or hears this calming of saṃsāra

children.text: sa yāti brahmasāyujyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: goes to union with <s>Brahman</s>; there is no need for deliberation about this.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge saṃsāraviṣakathanaṃ nāma ṣaḍaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighty-sixth chapter, named "The Account of the Poison of Saṃsāra," in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard <s>Pinākin</s>, those very wise ones, beginning with <s>Kumāra</s>,

children.text: procuḥ praṇamya vai bhītāḥ prasannaṃ parameśvaram ||
children.translated_text: bowed and, afraid, spoke to the gracious <s>Parameśvara</s>:
"If this is so, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, with this goddess, the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>,
you sport in various enjoyments; how are you fit to speak in this way here?"
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed, the Lord, <s>Pinākin</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>, laughed

children.text: prāha tām aṃbikāṃ prekṣya praṇipatya sthitān dvijān ||
children.translated_text: and, looking at <s>Ambikā</s>, spoke to the twice-born men who stood bowing down.

children.text: bandhamokṣau na caiveha mama svecchā śarīriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: "Bondage and liberation do not exist here for me, who have a body by my own will.
The <s>paśu</s>, the living soul, is ignorant of agency; the person is an enjoyer, all-pervading and yet minute.

children.text: māyī ca māyayā baddhaḥ karmabhir yujyate tu saḥ
children.translated_text: Possessing māyā and bound by māyā, he is joined to karmas.

children.text: jñānaṃ dhyānaṃ ca bandhaś ca mokṣo nāstyātmano dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge, meditation, bondage, and liberation do not belong to the Self, O twice-born men.

children.text: yadaivaṃ mayi vidvān yastasyāpi na ca sarvataḥ
children.translated_text: When one is thus a wise man in me, for him too none of these exists in any respect.

children.text: eṣā vidyā hyahaṃ vedyaḥ prajñaiṣā ca śrutiḥ smṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This knowledge indeed am I; I am what is to be known. This wisdom is śruti and smṛti.

children.text: dhṛtireṣā mayā niṣṭhā jñānaśaktiḥ kriyā tathā
children.translated_text: This is firmness, this is my steadfastness, and likewise the powers of knowledge and action.

children.text: icchākhyā ca tathā hyājñā dve vidye na ca saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So too are what are called will and command; these are the two forms of knowledge, without doubt.

children.text: na hyeṣā prakṛtirjaivī vikṛtiś ca vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: For this is not material prakṛti, nor is it a transformation belonging to the living soul, when considered.
This māyā is not a modification, being devoid of manifestation as either being or non-being.
Long ago my eternal command arose from my mouth,
five-faced, greatly blessed, and granting fearlessness to the worlds.
Entering that command, I, <s>Śiva</s>, contemplated the welfare of the worlds
and, through her, pervaded everything in twenty-seven forms.
From that time onward there has been the movement toward liberation, O best of twice-born men."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having spoken thus, <s>Parameśvara</s> then looked at <s>Bhavānī</s>.
And <s>Bhavānī</s>, seeing him, the imperishable one, removed the māyā.
Those sages, freed from the impurity of māyā, saw <s>Pārvatī</s>

children.text: prītā babhūvurmuktāś ca tasmādeṣā parā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: and became pleased and liberated; therefore this is the supreme goal.
There is truly no difference between <s>Umā</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s> in ultimate reality.

children.text: dvidhāsau rūpamāsthāya sthita eva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: That one remains, having assumed a twofold form; there is no doubt.
When a wise man becomes unattached through the command of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
then liberation comes in an instant, not otherwise through ten million actions.
Gradual sequence is not what is intended; it has been elaborated for beings by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
By the grace of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, liberation comes in an instant; this is the pledge, without doubt.

children.text: garbhastho jāyamāno vā bālo vā taruṇo'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: Whether in the womb, being born, a child, or even a young person,
or old, a creature is liberated by the grace of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.

children.text: aṇḍajaś codbhijjo vāpi svedajo vāpi mucyate ||
children.translated_text: An egg-born being, one born from a sprout, or one born from sweat is also liberated
by the grace of the God of gods; there is no need for deliberation about this.
This very <s>Śiva</s>, lord of the world, is the maker of bondage and liberation.
He is <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svar</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>, and <s>Jana</s>; he is directly <s>Tapas</s> itself,
and also <s>Satyaloka</s>, and hundreds upon hundreds of crores of cosmic eggs.
All these are the body of the God of gods, as are the eight coverings of the cosmic egg.
On all the seven continents, on mountains and in forests,
in all the oceans, and everywhere in the layers of wind,

children.text: tathānyeṣu ca lokeṣu vasanti ca carācarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise in other worlds, moving and unmoving beings dwell.

children.text: sarve bhavāṃśajā nūnaṃ gatistveṣāṃ sa eva vai
children.translated_text: All are surely portions of <s>Bhava</s>, and he alone is their goal.
All is <s>Rudra</s>. Reverence to that great-souled <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: viśvaṃ bhūtaṃ tathā jātaṃ bahudhā rudra eva saḥ
children.translated_text: The universe, what has been and what has come into being in many ways, is that <s>Rudra</s> alone.
This goddess <s>Ambikā</s> stands as <s>Rudra</s>'s command; through her there is liberation.
Thus the sky-roaming beings and the siddhas spoke with pleased minds.
When <s>Ambikā</s>, through her grace, looked upon them all,

children.text: tadā tiṣṭhanti sāyujyaṃ prāptāste khecarāḥ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: then those sky-roaming beings attained <s>sāyujya</s> (union) and abide with the Lord.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge munimohaśamanaṃ nāma saptāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighty-seventh chapter, named "The Pacification of the Sages' Delusion," in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The seers said:

children.text: kena yogena vai sūta guṇaprāptiḥ satāmiha
children.translated_text: "By what yoga, O <s>Sūta</s>, is the attainment of the qualities of the good gained here?
Do yogins here indeed become endowed with powers such as <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness)?"
All that, <s>Sūta</s>, you ought now to tell in detail.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
From this point onward I shall teach the yoga that is exceedingly difficult to obtain.
At the beginning one should recollect the eternal one in five ways, having established him in the mind.
One should imagine the seat as a lotus, joined with moon, sun, and fire,
endowed with twenty-six <s>śaktis</s> (powers), and also eightfold, O best of twice-born men.
Then, O twice-born men, it is sixteenfold and again twelvefold;

children.text: smarec ca tat tathā madhye devyā devam umāpatim ||
children.translated_text: and likewise one should remember, in its center, the god <s>Umāpati</s> together with the Goddess.
He is the unborn lord, eight-formed and endowed with the eight powers.
Together with these, the <s>Rudras</s> are eightfold, and again sixty-fourfold.
So too are all the powers, endowed with the set of eight qualities.
Thus one should remember in due order, after obtaining unsurpassed knowledge.
Thus the <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga is the giver of perfection in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
From it, O Brahmins, come the powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), and not otherwise, even by crores of rites.
There the eightfold lordly power of yogins is taught.
Listen to all that as it is now being explained according to the yoga of sequence.

children.text: aṇimā laghimā caiva mahimā prāptireva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>mahimā</s> (greatness), and <s>prāpti</s> (attainment),

children.text: prākāmyaṃ caiva sarvatra īśitvaṃ caiva sarvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>prākāmya</s> (free enjoyment) everywhere, and <s>īśitva</s> (lordship) in every respect,
then <s>vaśitva</s> (mastery) everywhere, and the power by which one's desire is fixed wherever one wishes:
that all-desire-fulfilling lordship too should be known as threefold.

children.text: sāvadyaṃ niravadyaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ caiva pravartate
children.translated_text: It proceeds as <s>sāvadya</s> (with defect), <s>niravadya</s> (without defect), and subtle.
That is called <s>sāvadya</s> which is remembered as consisting of the five elements.

children.text: indriyāṇi manaścaiva ahaṅkāraś ca yaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The senses, the mind, and what is remembered as ego are there.
In that, subtle activity again is constituted by the five elements,
and is designated as the senses, mind, thought, intellect, and ego.

children.text: tathā sarvamayaṃ caiva ātmasthā khyātireva ca ||
children.translated_text: Likewise it is all-formed, and there is recognition abiding in the Self.
The connection is threefold and operates only among subtle things.
Again, the eightfold quality too is prescribed only among subtle things.
I shall explain its form, just as the blessed Lord proclaimed it.
Hear how its rule is remembered among all beings in the three worlds.
Beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, and likewise unmanifest, it is established everywhere.
Among all beings in the three worlds it is declared difficult to obtain.

children.text: tat tasya bhavati prāpyaṃ prathamaṃ yogināṃ balam
children.translated_text: That becomes attainable for him; it is the first power of yogins.

children.text: laṅghanaṃ plavanaṃ loke rūpamasya sadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Its form in the world is always crossing over and floating.

children.text: śīghratvaṃ sarvabhūteṣu dvitīyaṃ tu padaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: Speed among all beings is remembered as the second state.
In the three worlds, among all beings, it is honored because of greatness.

children.text: mahitvaṃ cāpi loke'smiṃs tṛtīyo yoga ucyate
children.translated_text: And greatness in this world is called the third yoga.
Among all beings in the three worlds, free movement wherever one wishes is remembered.
He enjoys desired objects as he wishes, and is nowhere obstructed.
Pleasure and pain proceed among all beings in the three worlds.
The knower of yoga becomes lord everywhere, according to each division.
And beings in the three worlds, moving and unmoving, are subject to him.

children.text: icchayā tasya rūpāṇi bhavanti na bhavanti ca
children.translated_text: By his will his forms come into being, and they also do not come into being.
This is the fixing of desire wherever one wishes in the three worlds, moving and unmoving.

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśo raso gandho rūpaṃ caiva manas tathā
children.translated_text: Sound, touch, taste, smell, form, and also the mind
proceed by his will, or do not exist, just as he wishes.

children.text: na jāyate na mriyate chidyate na ca bhidyate
children.translated_text: He is not born, does not die, is not cut, and is not split.

children.text: na dahyate na muhyeta līyate na ca lipyate ||
children.translated_text: He is not burned, is not deluded, is not dissolved, and is not stained.

children.text: na kṣīyate na kṣarati khidyate na kadācana
children.translated_text: He does not diminish, does not flow away, and is never distressed.

children.text: kriyate vā na sarvatra tathā vikriyate na ca ||
children.translated_text: He is not made anywhere, nor is he transformed.
He is without smell, taste, or form, untouched and devoid of sound.
He is without color and without voice, and is never of any class.

children.text: sa bhuṅkte viṣayāṃścaiva viṣayairna ca yujyate
children.translated_text: He enjoys sense objects, yet he is not joined to the sense objects.
Because of minuteness he is beyond and subtle; because of subtlety he belongs to liberation.
Because of liberation he is pervasive, and because of pervasiveness he is remembered as the <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit).
The <s>puruṣa</s>, because of his subtle state, is established in supreme lordship.
In lordship beyond the qualities, he is said to be subtle in every respect.
Having attained unobstructed lordship and unsurpassed yoga,
one then goes to <s>apavarga</s> (release); that subtle state is the supreme goal.
Thus, O foremost sages, <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga is to be understood.
It gives the fruit of heaven and liberation, and it is the cause of union with <s>Śiva</s>.
Or, if one whose knowledge has departed performs action out of passion,

children.text: rājasaṃ tāmasaṃ vāpi bhuktvā tatraiva mucyate
children.translated_text: whether rajasic or tamasic, after experiencing it he is released there itself.

children.text: tathā sukṛtakarmā tu phalaṃ svarge samaśnute ||
children.translated_text: But one whose action is meritorious enjoys its fruit in heaven.
From that place he is born again in a superior human state.

children.text: tasmādbrahma paraṃ saukhyaṃ brahma śāśvatam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore <s>Brahman</s> is the supreme happiness; <s>Brahman</s> is eternal and highest.

children.text: brahma eva hi seveta brahmaiva hi paraṃ sukham
children.translated_text: Indeed one should serve <s>Brahman</s> alone, for <s>Brahman</s> alone is the supreme happiness.
For the exertion of sacrifices proceeds for the sake of a great goal.

children.text: bhūyo mṛtyuvaśaṃ yāti tasmānmokṣaḥ paraṃ sukham
children.translated_text: One goes again under the power of death; therefore <s>mokṣa</s> is the supreme happiness.
Or, joined with meditation and devoted to the truth of <s>Brahman</s>,
one cannot be made to fall away, even by hundreds of manvantaras.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu puruṣaṃ divyaṃ viśvākhyaṃ viśvatomukham ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the divine <s>puruṣa</s>, called the All, facing in every direction,
with the feet, heads, and necks of all, the lord of all, formed as all,
with all fragrances and all garlands, the lord wearing all garments,

children.text: gobhir mahīṃ saṃpatate patatriṇo naivaṃ bhūyo janayatyevameva
children.translated_text: with rays he comes together upon the earth; the flying ones do not generate again in this way.

children.text: kaviṃ purāṇam anuśāsitāraṃ sūkṣmācca sūkṣmaṃ mahato mahāntam ||
children.translated_text: the seer, ancient, the ruler, subtler than the subtle and greater than the great.

children.text: yogena paśyenna ca cakṣuṣā punarnirindriyaṃ puruṣaṃ rukmavarṇam
children.translated_text: Through yoga one should see, and not again with the eye, the man without senses, golden in color,

children.text: aliṅginaṃ nirguṇaṃ cetanaṃ ca nityaṃ sadā sarvagaṃ sarvasāram ||
children.translated_text: without a mark, without qualities, conscious, eternal, ever-present, all-pervading, and the essence of all.
By reasoning, those who have become absorbed in that see him whose light is unmoving, shining with splendor.
He has no hands, feet, belly, sides, or tongue; he is beyond the senses, extremely subtle, and one.

children.text: paśyatyacakṣuḥ sa śṛṇotyakarṇo na cāstyabuddhaṃ na ca buddhir asti
children.translated_text: Without eyes he sees; without ears he hears. There is nothing unknown to him, yet there is no ordinary intellect in him.

children.text: sa veda sarvaṃ na ca sarvavedyaṃ tamāhuragryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam ||
children.translated_text: He knows everything, but is not an object knowable by all; they call him the foremost, the great <s>puruṣa</s>.
Yogins, being disciplined, perceive <s>prakṛti</s>, unconscious, all-pervading, subtle,
having the nature of production, and belonging to all beings.
That has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces everywhere;
in the world it has hearing everywhere, and it stands enveloping everything.

children.text: yukto yogena ceśānaṃ sarvataś ca sanātanam
children.translated_text: Joined with yoga, a learned man does not become bewildered about that ruler,
the eternal <s>puruṣa</s> of all beings, present everywhere.
He who meditates on that being-self, the great self, the imperishable supreme self,

children.text: sarvātmānaṃ paraṃ brahma tadvai dhyātā na muhyati ||
children.translated_text: the self of all, the supreme brahman, does not become bewildered.
For just as the wind is perceived while moving among all forms,
so he lies in the city and is very hard to grasp; therefore he is called <s>puruṣa</s>.
But then, if its dharma has been cut off, yet some of its own karmas remain,
then it enters a womb produced from <s>Brahmā</s>, joined with semen and blood.

children.text: strīpuṃsoḥ saṃprayoge hi jāyate hi tataḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: For through the union of woman and man, the lord is then born;
then, over the time of pregnancy, what is called the kalala comes into being.
And in time that kalala becomes a bubble.
Just as a lump of clay on the wheel, pressed by the turning of the wheel,
and worked by the hands, comes to assume the form of an image,
so, joined with the internal principles and filled by wind,
he thinks, 'If I escape the womb, I will resort to <s>Maheśvara</s>.'
For as long as the Vaiṣṇava wind has not touched the child just born,
for that long he should think, 'I will worship <s>Mahādeva</s>.'
There a human being is born, according to form and according to age.

children.text: vāyuḥ saṃbhavate khāttu vātādbhavati vai jalam
children.translated_text: Wind arises from space, and from wind water comes to be;
from water life-breath arises, and from life-breath semen increases.
There are thirty-three portions of blood and fourteen portions of semen;
after making a half-result according to portion, the embryo is then infused.
Then, joined with the embryo and enclosed by the five winds,
the form of each limb of his arises from the father's body.
Then, from the mother's food, through what is drunk, licked, and ingested,

children.text: nābhideśena vai prāṇāste hyādhārā hi dehinām ||
children.translated_text: the breaths enter by way of the navel region; they are the supports of embodied beings.
Afflicted for nine months, with head and neck wrapped around,
and all his limbs enveloped, he has no adequate passage.
After dwelling for nine months, facing downward at the opening of the womb,
then, because of his own evil karmas, he reaches hell.
The forest of sword-leaves, the cutting of the śālmalī tree,
beating, being eaten, and eating pus and blood are there.

children.text: yathā hyāpastu saṃchinnāḥ saṃśleṣmam upayānti vai
children.translated_text: Just as waters that have been divided come together again,

children.text: tathā chinnāś ca bhinnāśca yātanāsthānam āgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too, when they have come to the place of torment, those cut and split apart are joined again.
Thus living beings, scorched by those self-made sins,

children.text: prāpnuyuḥ karmabhiḥ śeṣairduḥkhaṃ vā yadi vetarat ||
children.translated_text: may obtain suffering through the karmas that remain, or some other result.

children.text: ekenaiva tu gantavyaṃ sarvamutsṛjya vai janam
children.translated_text: One must go alone, abandoning all one's people;
one alone must experience the result. Therefore one should practice good action.

children.text: na hyenaṃ prasthitaṃ kaścid gacchantam anugacchati
children.translated_text: No one follows him when he has set out and is going away;
the karma that he has done follows him.

children.text: te nityaṃ yamaviṣayeṣu sampravṛttāḥ krośantaḥ satatamaniṣṭasaṃprayogaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are always engaged in the domains of <s>Yama</s>, crying out continually through contact with what is unwanted,
waste away in bodies overcome by pain, through many exceedingly fierce and endless torments.
Whatever one repeatedly practices by deed, mind, and speech,
that habit carries him away; therefore one should practice what is auspicious.
For an embodied being, there is a beginningless continuity based on former karma;
he enters dreadful, dark <s>saṃsāra</s>, which is sixfold.
From humanity comes the condition of an animal; from the animal condition one becomes a wild beast.
From being a wild beast comes the condition of a bird, and from that, a creeping creature.
From being a creeping creature one goes to the state of a plant, without doubt;

children.text: sthāvaratve punaḥ prāpte yāvad unmilate janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when the state of a plant has again been reached, until the person opens his eyes,
he wanders like a potter's wheel and revolves in that very place.
Thus this <s>saṃsāra</s>, beginning with human birth and ending in plants,
is to be known as dark; in it one revolves.
And the sāttvika <s>saṃsāra</s> is said to begin with <s>Brahmā</s>.
It is to be known as ending with piśācas among the heavenly stations of embodied beings.

children.text: brāhme tu kevalaṃ sattvaṃ sthāvare kevalaṃ tamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the Brahmic state there is sattva alone; in the plant state there is tamas alone.
In the middle of the fourteen stations, rajas is the supporting middle quality.
When the vital points are being cut, for an embodied being tormented by pain,
how will a Brahmin then remember that supreme brahman?
<s>Saṃsāra</s>, impelled by the dispositions formed from former dharma,
continually takes on human birth; therefore one should practice meditation.
Having understood this fourteenfold circle of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
one afflicted by fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> should always begin to practice <s>dharma</s>.
Then, transformed step by step, he crosses <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Therefore, constantly disciplined, intent on meditation, and applying himself,
he should undertake <s>yoga</s> in such a way that he sees the self.
This is the waters; this is the supreme light; this is the unsurpassed bridge.

children.text: vivṛtyā hyeṣa saṃbhedād bhūtānāṃ caiva śāśvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through unfolding and differentiation, this eternal one is indeed the source of beings.
Therefore one should worship this bridge, the self, the fire facing every direction,
the great lord <s>Maheśvara</s>, who dwells in the hearts of all beings.
Likewise one should worship the god established within, encircled by his own power,

children.text: aṣṭadhā cāṣṭadhā caiva tathā cāṣṭavidhena ca ||
children.translated_text: eightfold, again eightfold, and also according to an eightfold mode.

children.text: sṛṣṭyarthaṃ saṃsthitaṃ vahniṃ saṃkṣipya ca hṛdi sthitam
children.translated_text: Having drawn together the fire established for creation and situated in the heart,
and having duly meditated on <s>Rudra</s>, lord of gods and ruler of the worlds,
with his mind absorbed in that thought, he should properly offer the five oblations,
in due order, to <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the fire dwelling in the heart.

children.text: āpaḥ pūtāḥ sakṛtprāśya tūṣṇīṃ hutvā hyupāviśan
children.translated_text: Having once sipped purified water and made the offering silently, he should sit down.
Then the first oblation for him is remembered as 'to <s>Prāṇa</s>'.

children.text: apānāya dvitīyā ca vyānāyeti tathā parā
children.translated_text: The second is 'to <s>Apāna</s>', and the next is likewise 'to <s>Vyāna</s>'.
The fourth should be 'to <s>Udāna</s>', and the fifth 'to <s>Samāna</s>'.
Having offered them separately with the exclamation <s>svāhā</s>, he may eat the remainder as he wishes.

children.text: apaḥ punaḥ sakṛtprāśya ācamya hṛdayaṃ spṛśet ||
children.translated_text: Again he should sip water once, rinse his mouth, and touch his heart.
This self is the knot of the vital breaths; <s>Rudra</s> is the self, the ender of all.
Indeed <s>Rudra</s> is the vital breath of the self; thus he should refresh himself.
<s>Rudra</s> is established in the vital breath; therefore he himself consists of vital breath.
He offers the highest nectar to <s>Prāṇa</s> and to <s>Rudra</s>.
'O <s>Śiva</s>, O lord, enter me. Svāhā to the self of <s>Brahman</s> itself.'
Thus may the eternal lord be pleased by these five oblations.
'You are the <s>Puruṣa</s>; you remain in the city, having the measure of a thumb.
You, the lord and supreme cause, are also supported on the thumb.
May the eternal lord of the whole world be pleased.

children.text: tvaṃ devānāmasi jyeṣṭho rudrastvaṃ ca puro vṛṣā ||
children.translated_text: You are the eldest of the gods; you are <s>Rudra</s>, and you are the foremost bull.
You are gentle; may this food be ours, and may this offering be yours.'
Thus everything has been declared in connection with the particular attainment of the qualities.

children.text: yogācāraḥ svayaṃ tena brahmaṇā kathitaḥ purā
children.translated_text: This practice of <s>yoga</s> was formerly taught by <s>Brahmā</s> himself.

children.text: evaṃ pāśupataṃ jñānaṃ jñātavyaṃ ca prayatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus this Pāśupata knowledge should be learned with care.

children.text: bhasmasnāyī bhaven nityaṃ bhasmaliptaḥ sadā bhavet
children.translated_text: One should bathe in ashes constantly and always be smeared with ashes.
Whoever recites this, hears it, or causes excellent twice-born men to hear it,

children.text: daive karmaṇi pitrye vā sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: whether in rites for the gods or in rites for the ancestors, goes to the supreme goal.

Thus ends the eighty-eighth chapter in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, named 'Description of the Eight Siddhis beginning with Aṇimā, the Three Qualities, Saṃsāra, the Fire, and the Offering and Other Rites.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
From here onward I shall explain the marks of the practice of purity,
by performing which a purified self obtains the goal after death.
It was formerly taught by <s>Brahmā</s> for the welfare of all beings,
as a concise gathering of the whole meaning of the Vedas for those who speak of <s>Brahman</s>.
It is for the arising of purities and is the highest state of sages.
He who is then not careless there is a sage and does not sink down.
Honor and dishonor are these two; they are called poison and nectar.
Dishonor is nectar there, while respect is called poison.

children.text: gurorapi hite yuktaḥ sa tu saṃvatsaraṃ vaset
children.translated_text: Engaged even in the welfare of the guru, he should dwell for a year,
and should be ever heedful in the observances and also in the restraints.
Then, having obtained permission, he should practice the unsurpassed yoga of knowledge,
and should wander over this earth without conflict with <s>dharma</s>.
He should walk on a path purified by the eye and drink water purified by cloth.
He should speak words purified by truth and perform conduct purified by the mind.
Whatever sin is incurred by one who takes fish within six months,
that should be known to be equal in a single day when water is unpurified.
On drinking unpurified water, he should recite five hundred times
the mantra characterized as <s>Aghora</s>; then he obtains purification.
Or he may worship <s>Śambhu</s> with full rites such as bathing him in ghee.
Having circumambulated three times, he is purified; there is no doubt about this.
One who knows <s>yoga</s> should never go to hospitality rites, śrāddhas, or sacrifices.
Thus it has been considered that the yogin should be nonviolent.
When the fire is smokeless, when the coals are not too blazing, and when all the people have eaten,

children.text: carettu matimān bhaikṣyaṃ na tu teṣveva nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: then the wise man should go for alms, but not always among those same people.
Even if others slight him and insult him,

children.text: tathā yuktaṃ caredbhaikṣyaṃ satāṃ dharmam adūṣayan ||
children.translated_text: he should go for alms in such a disciplined way, not corrupting the <s>dharma</s> of the good.
He should seek alms among forest-dwellers and in the houses of wandering mendicants.
This first way of livelihood arises as the best for him.
After that, O twice-born ones, he should go among householders who are virtuous,
faithful, self-controlled, learned in scripture, and great-souled.
After that, again, he may go among those who are not wicked and not fallen.
Begging for alms among the social classes is called the lowest livelihood.

children.text: bhaikṣyaṃ yavāgūstakraṃ vā payo yāvakameva ca
children.translated_text: Alms, barley gruel, buttermilk, milk, or a preparation of barley,
ripe fruits and roots and the like, grains, oilcake, and meal,

children.text: ityeva te mayā proktā yogināṃ siddhivarddhanāḥ
children.translated_text: these have thus been told by me as foods that increase the accomplishment of yogins.
Among those, when available, alms are remembered as the best.

children.text: abbinduṃ yaḥ kuśāgreṇa māsi māsi samaśnute
children.translated_text: He who eats a drop of water from the tip of kuśa grass month after month
He who practices begging for alms according to rule is superior to the one described before.
For one who is afraid of old age, death, womb-births, and hells and the like,
it brings compassion in this way; therefore that is remembered as alms-begging.
Those who live on curds, those who live on milk, and whatever others are worn down in their livelihood,

children.text: sarve te bhaikṣyabhakṣasya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: all of them are not worth even a sixteenth part of one who lives on alms.
One should always sleep on ashes, live by begging, and have the senses conquered.

children.text: ya icchet paramaṃ sthānaṃ vrataṃ pāśupataṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: He who desires the supreme station should practice the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.

children.text: yogināṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And for all yogins, the <s>Cāndrāyaṇa</s> should be the best vow.

children.text: ekaṃ dve trīṇi catvāri śaktito vā samācaret ||
children.translated_text: One should perform one, two, three, or four, or as many as one is able.

children.text: asteyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ ca alobhastyāga eva ca
children.translated_text: Non-stealing, celibacy, freedom from greed, and renunciation,
are the five vows of mendicants; but non-injury is supreme here.
Freedom from anger, service to the guru, purity, lightness of food,
and constant self-recitation: these are proclaimed as the restraints.
Through seed, womb, qualities, attachment to things, and through actions themselves,
a bond is ordained for human beings, as for an elephant in the forest.

children.text: devaistulyāḥ sarvayajñakriyāstu yajñājjāpyaṃ jñānamāhuś ca jāpyāt
children.translated_text: All sacrificial rites are equal to the gods; they say recitation is higher than sacrifice, and knowledge higher than recitation.
Higher than knowledge is meditation, free from attachment and passion; when that is attained, there is apprehension of the eternal.

children.text: damaḥ śamaḥ satyamakalmaṣatvaṃ maunaṃ ca bhūteṣvakhileṣu cārjavam
children.translated_text: Self-restraint, tranquility, truth, stainlessness, silence, and straightforwardness toward all beings,

children.text: atīndriyaṃ jñānamidaṃ tathā śivaṃ prāhus tathā jñānaviśuddhabuddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this transcendent knowledge, and likewise auspiciousness, are taught by those whose minds are purified by knowledge.
Collected, intent on brahman, heedful, pure, devoted to solitude, and with senses conquered,
the great-souled one may complete this yoga; so also did the blameless and stainless great sages.
Restrained as if by a goad, he reaches the regions he desires.
By this pure path, with his seed burnt, he becomes stainless.
Those who delight in good conduct, who are peaceful, and who preserve their own <s>dharma</s>,
having conquered all worlds, go to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
This eternal <s>dharma</s> was taught directly by the Grandfather.
For the benefit of all worlds, listen: I shall proclaim it to you.
For elders who are joined to the instruction of the guru and who follow the proper succession,
one should cause all acts such as rising up before them, and also prostration, to be performed.
With an eight-limbed prostration, with the body placed down in three ways, O men of good vows,
and with three circumambulations, the guru of brahman is indeed to be honored.

children.text: jyeṣṭhānye 'pi ca te sarve vandanīyā vijānatā
children.translated_text: All those who are senior are also to be honored by one who understands.

children.text: ājñābhaṅgaṃ na kurvīta yadīcchet siddhim uttamām ||
children.translated_text: One should not break their command, if one desires highest success.
One should avoid every livelihood based on mines, empty pits or fields, and petty mantras,
and poison, possession, imposture, and the like, with every effort.
One should always avoid fraud, dishonesty concerning wealth, and slander.
One should avoid excessive laughter, haughtiness, and acting willfully in amusements.
One should avoid these by every effort, even in the presence of gurus.
And one should by every effort not speak what is contrary to their words, nor words improper toward the guru.
One should not say what is unwelcome, and should never keep it in mind.
The seats, garments, staffs and the like, and sandals of ascetics,

children.text: mālyaṃ ca śayanasthānaṃ pātraṃ chāyāṃ ca yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: their garlands, sleeping-places, bowls, and even their shadow, with care,

children.text: yajñopakaraṇāṅgaṃ ca na spṛśed vai padena ca ||
children.translated_text: and the implements and parts of sacrifice, one should not touch with the foot.
One should by every effort not commit offense against the gods or offense against the guru.
Having done so through negligence, O brahmins, one should recite the <s>praṇava</s> ten thousand times.
From offense against the gods or offense against the guru, one is purified by a crore in number.
And likewise, according to rule, for the purification of a great sin,
a sinner is purified by half that amount, if he is one who maintains proper conduct.
All those guilty of secondary sins are purified by half of that again, O men of good vows.
When the twilight rite has been omitted, a brahmin is purified simply by repeating it three times.
When the daily rite has been interrupted, one hundred and one is declared.

children.text: laṅghane samayānāṃ tu abhakṣyasya ca bhakṣaṇe
children.translated_text: But in the transgression of observances, in the eating of what must not be eaten,
and in speaking what should not be spoken, purification is said to come from one thousand.
In the killing of crows, owls, pigeons, and other birds,
having recited one hundred and eight times, one is released; there is no doubt here.
But he who is a knower of reality, a knower of brahman, and the best of brahmins,
obtains purification through remembrance; no deliberation is to be made about this.
For knowers of the self, there is no such injunction of expiations.

children.text: viśvasyaiva hi te śuddhā brahmavidyāvido janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those people who know the knowledge of brahman are themselves pure for the whole universe.
They are solely devoted to yoga and meditation, and are unstained, like gold.
For those who are pure there is no purification; they are purified by the knowledge of brahman.
With waters drawn out, not hot or foamy, and purified through cloth and inspection,
one should perform every act; one should avoid turbid water.
Water spoiled by smell, color, or taste, or situated in an impure place,
or polluted by mud and stones, and likewise seawater or pond water,
water with algae, or spoiled by other faults, one should avoid.
Possessed of garment-purity, O twice-born ones, one should perform all duties.
All acts such as salutation, service to the guru, and the like,
if one lacks garment-purity, make one impure; there is no doubt here.
For garments used in divine rites, purity is desired every day.

children.text: itareṣāṃ hi vastrāṇāṃ śaucaṃ kāryaṃ malāgame ||
children.translated_text: For other garments, purification should be performed when dirt appears.
O twice-born ones, one should by every effort avoid clothing worn by others.
For silk and woolen garments, with rough cleansing substances; for linen garments, with white mustard seeds;
for fine silk cloths, with śrīphala fruits; for woolen blankets, with soap-nuts...
For skins, split objects, and canes, purification is regarded as like that of cloth.
And for all bark-garments, and also for umbrellas and fly-whisks,
the cleansing has been declared to be like that of cloth by the knowers of brahman, the lords among sages.
Bronze is purified with ash; iron is said to be purified with alkali.
Copper is purified with acid, O Brahmins, and so too tin and lead.

children.text: haimam adbhiḥ śubhaṃ pātraṃ raupyapātraṃ dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: A golden vessel becomes pure with water, and so does a silver vessel, O best of twice-born men.
The cleansing of gems, stones, conch-shells, and pearls is remembered as like that of metal objects.
For all liquids here that have been greatly spoiled
by contact with fire and water, purification is remembered as skimming or pouring off.
For objects made of grass, wood, and the like, sprinkling with clean water is remembered.
Purification is by hot water, and so too for the sruk and sruva ladles.
Likewise for sacrificial vessels, and for the pestle and mortar,
horn, bone, wood, and ivory are purified simply by scraping.
For compact masses of substances, O greatly fortunate ones, sprinkling is remembered.
For substances not gathered into a mass, cleansing is prescribed for each one separately.
When one part of heaps of uneaten grain has been defiled,
one should remove just that much and sprinkle the rest with water touched by kuśa grass.
For vegetables, roots, fruits, and the like, purification is desired as it is for grain.
A house is purified by sweeping and wiping; an earthen object is purified by firing again.
By scraping, smearing, and also by sweeping,

children.text: gonivāsena vai śuddhā secanena dharā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the ground is remembered as purified by a cow's dwelling there and by sprinkling.

children.text: bhūmistham udakaṃ śuddhaṃ vaitṛṣṇyaṃ yatra gaurvrajet
children.translated_text: Water standing on the ground is pure where a cow would go and be free from thirst,
provided it is not pervaded by impurity and retains its smell, color, and taste.
A calf is pure at the flowing of milk, and a bird is pure when fruit falls.
For householders, the mouth of one's own wife is pure in sexual union, when one desires one's wife.

children.text: hastābhyāṃ kṣālitaṃ vastraṃ kāruṇā ca yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: A cloth washed with both hands, and the kāruṇā according to rule,
should be well sprinkled with kuśa-water and then taken up by the knower of dharma.
Goods spread out for sale, according to the divisions of varṇa and āśrama,
and things born from mines are pure for them; a dog is pure when catching game.

children.text: chāyā ca vipluṣo viprā makṣikādyā dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Shadows and splashes, O Brahmins, and flies and the like, O best of twice-born men,

children.text: rajo bhūr vāyur agniś ca medhyāni sparśane sadā ||
children.translated_text: as well as dust, the ground, wind, and fire, are always pure when touched.

children.text: suptvā bhuktvā ca vai viprāḥ kṣuttvā pītvā ca vai tathā
children.translated_text: After sleeping and eating, O Brahmins, and likewise after sneezing and drinking,
after spitting and at the beginning of study, even one who is pure should sip water again.
And drops from another person's ācamana that touch the feet

children.text: te pārthivaiḥ samā jñeyā na tairaprayato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: should be understood as equal to earth; one does not become impure through them.

children.text: kṛtvā ca maithunaṃ spṛṣṭvā patitaṃ kukkuṭādikam
children.translated_text: After having intercourse, or after touching a fallen person, a cock, and the like,

children.text: sūkaraṃ caiva kākādi śvānamuṣṭraṃ kharaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and also a pig, a crow and the like, a dog, a camel, or a donkey,

children.text: yūpaṃ cāṇḍālakādyāṃś ca spṛṣṭvā snānena śudhyati
children.translated_text: or after touching a sacrificial post and caṇḍālas and others, one is purified by bathing.
One should not touch a menstruating woman, a woman recently delivered, or an antyajā woman.
One who is affected by impurity from childbirth or joined with impurity from a corpse
should not touch their menstrual discharge; if he has touched it, he is purified only after bathing.
There is no impurity at all for renouncers, forest-dwellers, or celibate students,

children.text: naiṣṭhikānāṃ nṛpāṇāṃ ca maṇḍalīnāṃ ca suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: nor for lifelong celibates, kings, and regional rulers, O people of good vows.
For because it would obstruct their duties, it cannot be otherwise for kings.
For Vaikhānasa Brahmins there is no such thing as being fallen.
And because twice-born men do not accumulate possessions, purification is only by bathing, not otherwise.

children.text: tathā saṃnihitānāṃ ca yajñārthaṃ dīkṣitasya ca ||
children.translated_text: So too for those who are present nearby and for one consecrated for the sake of sacrifice.
For those who perform a sacrifice, purification after one day has been declared by <s>Svayaṃbhū</s>.
After that, for those who have studied their Vedic branch, purification is after four days for all embodied persons.

children.text: sūtakaṃ pretakaṃ nāsti tryahād ūrdhvam amutra vai
children.translated_text: Birth impurity and death impurity do not exist there beyond three days.
Before that, up to the end of eleven days, it applies to kinsmen, O best of twice-born men.
When a death has occurred, purification is by bathing alone.
Then, before three seasons have passed, one day is prescribed.

children.text: saptavarṣāt tataścārvāk trirātraṃ hi tataḥ param
children.translated_text: Before seven years have passed, there is then a three-night impurity; after that,

children.text: daśāhaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ vai prathame 'hani vā pituḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is ten-day impurity for Brahmins, or on the first day in the case of a father.
There is ten-day birth impurity for the mother also in just the same way, O imperishable ones.
Before three years have passed, there is always purification by bathing for the father's kinsmen.

children.text: aṣṭābdād ekarātreṇa śuddhiḥ syād bāndhavasya tu
children.translated_text: Before eight years have passed, purification for a kinsman is after one night.
Then, before twelve years have passed, there is a three-night impurity for women, O people of good vows.
For a man, sapiṇḍa kinship ceases in the seventh generation.
When ten days have passed, one is impure for three nights.

children.text: tataḥ saṃnihito vipraścārvāk pūrvaṃ tadeva vai
children.translated_text: Then, if a Brahmin is nearby before that, that same prior rule applies.
But when a year has passed, he is purified merely by bathing.
After touching a corpse, impurity lasts three nights; for a dharmic purpose, bathing is prescribed.
For burners and carriers of a non-kinsman's corpse, bathing alone is required.

children.text: anugamya ca vai snātvā ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati
children.translated_text: After following the funeral procession, one bathes, sips ghee, and becomes purified.
At the death of a teacher, and also when a learned Vedic Brahmin has died, there is impurity for three nights.

children.text: pakṣiṇī mātulānāṃ ca sodarāṇāṃ ca vā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: For maternal uncles and for brothers, O Brahmins, there is the pakṣiṇī impurity.
For kings, regional rulers, and those living outside the realm, purification is immediate.
For Kṣatriyas, O best of twice-born men, purification is simply after twelve days.
For one who is not consecrated as king there is no impurity in accidents or in battle.
A Vaiśya is purified after fifteen days, and a Śūdra after a month.
Thus the unsurpassed purification of substances has been stated briefly.
And impurity has been taught in due order; for renouncers it does not exist at all.
From the Tretā age onward, women have menstruation month by month, O Brahmins.

children.text: kṛte sakṛd yugavaśājjāyante vai sahaiva tu
children.translated_text: In the Kṛta age it occurred once, according to the age, and they were born together indeed.

children.text: prayānti ca mahābhāgā bhāryābhiḥ kuravo yathā ||
children.translated_text: and the greatly fortunate <s>Kurus</s> go with their wives, as is proper.
The ordering of <s>varṇāśrama</s> (class and life-stage) begins from the <s>Tretā</s>, O well-vowed ones;
in the southern region of <s>Bhārata</s> there is this arrangement, but not in the others.
In <s>Mahāvīta</s> and <s>Suvīta</s>, and likewise in the eight regions of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>,

children.text: śākadvīpādiṣu prokto dharmo vai bhārate yathā ||
children.translated_text: and in <s>Śākadvīpa</s> and the other islands, <s>dharma</s> is declared as it is in <s>Bhārata</s>.
In the <s>Kṛta</s> age livelihood was the overflowing of sap; in the <s>Tretā</s> it was born from household trees.
That very livelihood, through the fault produced by the seasons and through passion, hatred, and the like among men,
and through sexual intercourse prompted by desire, O Brahmins, and likewise through harsh acts and so on,
brought forth barley and the other crops, fourteen kinds, cultivated and wild.

children.text: oṣadhyaś ca rajodoṣāḥ strīṇāṃ rāgādibhir nṛṇām
children.translated_text: And herbs, along with the faults of menstrual blood in women, arose through passion and the like among men.
When ploughed out of season and destroyed, they were then produced again.
Therefore, with every effort, one should not converse with a menstruating woman.
On the first day a woman is to be avoided just as a <s>Caṇḍālī</s> is avoided.

children.text: dvitīye 'hani viprā hi yathā vai brahmaghātinī
children.translated_text: On the second day, O Brahmins, she is indeed like a slayer of a Brahmin;
on the third day she is so by half of that, and on the fourth day, O well-vowed ones,
after bathing she is purified by half a month; thereafter purity will arise.
From that until the sixteenth day, the purity of women is considered like that after urine.
If she continues with menstruation for five nights, she is untouchable in that way.
After twenty days she is again, through menstruation, as before.

children.text: snānaṃ śaucaṃ tathā gānaṃ rodanaṃ hasanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Bathing, cleansing, singing, weeping, and laughing,
riding in a vehicle, anointing herself, gambling, and applying unguents,
sleeping by day especially, and also cleaning the teeth,
sexual intercourse, whether mental or verbal, and worship of the deity,
a menstruating woman should avoid with every effort, as well as acts of reverence.
A menstruating woman should avoid touching and conversing with menstruating women,
and also the laying aside of garments, with every effort.
After bathing, a menstruating woman should not touch another man.
She should look upon the divine sun and then drink <s>brahmakūrca</s>,

children.text: kevalaṃ pañcagavyaṃ vā kṣīraṃ vā cātmaśuddhaye ||
children.translated_text: or simply <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five cow-products), or milk, for her own purification.

children.text: caturthyāṃ strī na gamyā tu gato'lpāyuḥ prasūyate
