children.translated_text: On the fourth day a woman is not to be approached; if a man approaches her, a short-lived child is born,
one without learning, fallen from vows, fallen in status, adulterous,
and plunged in the ocean of poverty: such a son she gives birth to.
One who desires a daughter should approach her again on the fifth day, according to rule.
From predominance of blood a female is born; from predominance of semen a male is born.

children.text: same napuṃsakaṃ caiva pañcamyāṃ kanyakā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When the two are equal, there is a neuter child; on the fifth day a girl is born.
On the sixth day she should be approached, O greatly fortunate ones; she will become the mother of a good son.
His sonship is indicated; a son already born will be of great splendor.

children.text: pumiti narakasyākhyā duḥkhaṃ ca narakaṃ viduḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pum</s> is said to be the name of hell, and they know hell as suffering.
She gives birth to a son who is endowed with rescue from that <s>pum</s>.
On the seventh day one desiring a daughter should approach her, and she gives birth to just that.
On the eighth day she gives birth to a son endowed with every excellence.
On the ninth day, one desiring a girl should approach; on the tenth, a learned son will be born.
On the eleventh, she gives birth to a woman, as before.
On the twelfth, she gives birth to one who knows the truth of <s>dharma</s> and promotes the śrauta and smārta rites.
On the thirteenth, she gives birth to a dull woman who causes every kind of mixture.
Because a woman gives birth in that way, one should not approach her with every effort.

children.text: caturdaśyāṃ yadā gacchet sā putrajananī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: When one approaches her on the fourteenth day, she becomes the mother of a son.
On the fifteenth, she gives birth to a most righteous child; on the sixteenth, to one who has crossed to the far shore of knowledge.

children.text: strīṇāṃ vai maithune kāle vāmapārśve prabhañjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the time of intercourse for women, if the wind moves on the left side,
a female will be born; if it is obtained on the right, a male.
At the time of intercourse with women, free from evil planets,
at the stated time, having become pure, one should approach the pure woman with a pure smile.
Thus, in this incidental discussion within the compendium of <s>dharma</s> for ascetics,
proper conduct has been proclaimed for all beings.
A pure man who reads or hears this proper conduct,
or who duly causes Brahmins whose sins have been burned away to hear it,
after reaching <s>Brahmaloka</s>, rejoices together with <s>Brahmā</s>.
Thus, in the first part of the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the eighty-ninth chapter, called 'The Teaching of Proper Conduct.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
From here onward I shall declare the settled teaching here for ascetics:
the expiation proclaimed by <s>Śiva</s>, the purification of sins for ascetics.
Sin is to be known as threefold, arising from speech, mind, and body.

children.text: satataṃ hi divā rātrau yenedaṃ veṣṭyate jagat ||
children.translated_text: By it this world is constantly enveloped, by day and by night.
Yet apart from that action this self remains, so says the higher revelation.

children.text: kṣaṇamevaṃ prayojyaṃ tu āyuṣyaṃ tu vidhāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: Only a moment should be directed in this way, for the sustaining of life.
For one who is not negligent, there will be <s>yoga</s>; indeed <s>yoga</s> is the highest strength.

children.text: na hi yogātparaṃ kiṃcin narāṇāṃ dṛśyate śubham ||
children.translated_text: No auspicious thing higher than <s>yoga</s> is seen for human beings.
Therefore wise men endowed with <s>dharma</s> praise <s>yoga</s>.
Having conquered ignorance by knowledge and obtained unsurpassed lordship,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā parāvaraṃ dhīrāḥ paraṃ gacchanti tatpadam
children.translated_text: the steadfast, having seen the higher and the lower, go to that supreme state.
Whatever vows there are for mendicants, and likewise the subordinate vows,
for each transgression of them an expiation is prescribed.
Having approached a woman through desire, he should prescribe the expiation.
He should perform the <s>sāṃtapana</s> vow, joined with breath-control.
Then, according to instruction, he performs a <s>kṛcchra</s> penance, composed at the end.
Having returned again to the hermitage, the mendicant should practice his discipline without indolence.
The wise say that an untruth joined with <s>dharma</s> does not destroy one.

children.text: tathāpi na ca kartavyaṃ prasaṃgo hyeṣa dāruṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Nevertheless it should not be done, for this is a dreadful attachment.
There should also be a fast for a day and night, and likewise a hundred breath-regulations.
False speech should not be uttered by a renunciant who desires <s>dharma</s>.
Even when he has fallen into the greatest distress, theft too must not be committed.
There is no <s>adharma</s> greater than theft; so says revelation.

children.text: hiṃsā hyeṣā parā sṛṣṭā stainyaṃ vai kathitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: For this has been created as supreme violence, and theft is declared to be so.
What is called wealth is indeed the life-breaths moving outside the body.

children.text: sa tasya harate prāṇānyo yasya harate dhanam ||
children.translated_text: He who takes another's wealth takes that man's life-breaths.
Having acted thus, with a very corrupt self, his conduct broken and fallen from his vow,
he should again become remorseful and perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow.
According to the rule seen in scripture, this is to last for a year, so says revelation.
Then, at the end of the year, his sin again diminished,
the mendicant, again filled with remorse, should practice his discipline without indolence.
Non-injury toward all beings is to be observed by deed, mind, and speech.

children.text: akāmādapi hiṃseta yadi bhikṣuḥ paśūn kṛmīn ||
children.translated_text: If a mendicant injures animals or worms even unintentionally,
he should perform a <s>kṛcchra</s>, an <s>atikṛcchra</s>, or else a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
If a renunciant, on seeing a woman, emits semen because of weakness of the senses,
then sixteen breath-retentions must indeed be maintained by him.
An expiation is prescribed for a Brahmin who has emitted semen by day.
There are also fasts for three nights, and likewise a hundred breath-regulations.

children.text: rātrau skannaḥ śuciḥ snātvā dvādaśaiva tu dhāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: If he emits semen at night, having bathed he is pure after twelve retentions only.
Through breath-regulation, with purified self, he becomes stainless, O twice-born ones.

children.text: ekānnaṃ madhumāṃsaṃ vā aśṛtānnaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Food from a single person, honey, meat, and likewise uncooked food,
and visibly salted foods are not to be eaten by renunciants.
For each single transgression concerning these, an expiation is prescribed.
By the <s>prājāpatya</s> <s>kṛcchra</s> he is then released from that sin.
Whatever transgressions arise from speech, mind, or body,
having determined the matter together with good people, he should do whatever they say.

children.text: careddhi śuddhaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanaḥ samastabhūteṣu ca satsamāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: For he should practice as one purified, regarding clod and gold alike, and well composed toward all beings.

children.text: sthānaṃ dhruvaṃ śāśvatamavyayaṃ tu paraṃ hi gatvā na punarhi jāyate ||
children.translated_text: Having reached the firm, eternal, imperishable, supreme place, he is indeed not born again.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge yatiprāyaścittaṃ nāma navatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the ninetieth chapter, named 'The Expiation of Renunciants.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
From here onward I shall teach the ominous signs; listen.
By this special knowledge yogins perceive death.
<s>Arundhatī</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, the moon's shadow, and the great path:

children.text: yo na paśyenna jīvetsa naraḥ saṃvatsarātparam ||
children.translated_text: the man who does not see them does not live beyond a year.
The sun without rays, and fire with rays:
he who sees this indeed does not live beyond eleven months.

children.text: vamenmūtraṃ purīṣaṃ ca suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: If he vomits urine, feces, gold, or silver,
either visibly or in a dream, he does not live ten months.
If he sees a tree of golden color and cities of the <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: paśyet pretapiśācāṃś ca navamāsān sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: and sees pretas and piśācas, he lives for nine months.
If he suddenly becomes stout, or suddenly becomes thin,

children.text: prakṛteś ca nivarteta cāṣṭau māsāṃś ca jīvati ||
children.translated_text: and departs from his natural condition, he lives for eight months.

children.text: agrataḥ pṛṣṭhato vāpi khaṇḍaṃ yasya padaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: If the footprint of a man is broken in front or behind,
whether in dust or in mud, he lives for seven months.

children.text: kākaḥ kapoto gṛdhro vā nilīyedyasya mūrdhani
children.translated_text: If a crow, pigeon, or vulture settles on someone's head,

children.text: kravyādo vā khago yasya ṣaṇmāsān nātivartate ||
children.translated_text: or if a flesh-eating bird does so, that man does not pass beyond six months.
If he is surrounded by rows of crows, or again by a shower of dust,
or sees his own shadow distorted, he lives four or five months.
If he sees lightning in a cloudless sky, standing in the southern quarter,

children.text: udake dhanur aindraṃ vā trīṇi dvau vā sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: or Indra's bow in water, he lives three or two months.

children.text: apsu vā yadi vādarśe yo hyātmānaṃ na paśyati
children.translated_text: If a man does not see himself in water or in a mirror,

children.text: aśiraskaṃ tathā paśyen māsād ūrdhvaṃ na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: or sees himself headless, he does not live beyond a month.
If his body has the smell of a corpse, or else the smell of fat,
death has approached him; he does not live for half a month.
If, just after bathing, his heart dries up,
or if he sees smoke from his head, he does not live ten days.
When his wind is disordered and cuts through the vital points,

children.text: adbhiḥ spṛṣṭo na hṛṣyeta tasya mṛtyurupasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, touched by water, he does not feel delight, death is present for him.
If in a dream he goes toward the southern direction on a chariot yoked with bears and monkeys,
singing and dancing as he goes, he should know that death is present.
If a dark woman wearing black garments, singing,

children.text: yaṃ nayeddakṣiṇāmāśāṃ svapne so'pi na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: leads him toward the southern direction in a dream, he too does not live.

children.text: chidraṃ vā svasya kaṇṭhasya svapne yo vīkṣate naraḥ
children.translated_text: If a man sees in a dream a hole in his own throat,
or sees a naked ascetic, he should know that death is present.
Whoever sinks into an ocean of mud up to the top of his head,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā tu tādṛśaṃ svapnaṃ sadya eva na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: after seeing such a dream, does not live even immediately afterward.

children.text: bhasmāṅgārāṃś ca keśāṃś ca nadīṃ śuṣkāṃ bhujaṅgamān
children.translated_text: If one sees ashes, embers, hair, a dried-up river, and serpents,

children.text: paśyedyo daśarātraṃ tu na sa jīvati tādṛśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: such a person does not live for ten nights.
If in a dream he is struck with stones by black and hideous men with weapons raised,

children.text: pāṣāṇaistāḍyate svapne yaḥ sadyo na sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: he does not live immediately thereafter.

children.text: sūryodaye pratyuṣasi pratyakṣaṃ yasya vai śivāḥ
children.translated_text: At sunrise, in the early morning, if jackals are plainly seen by someone...
Having died while crying out face to face with him, that man should be regarded as one whose lifespan is spent.

children.text: yasya vā snātamātrasya hṛdayaṃ pīḍyate bhṛśam
children.translated_text: Or, if just after bathing a man's heart is severely oppressed,
and his teeth begin to chatter, one should declare him to be one whose lifespan is spent.

children.text: bhūyobhūyastrasedyastu rātrau vā yadi vā divā
children.translated_text: But whoever trembles again and again, whether by night or by day,
and does not smell the fragrance of a lamp, one should know that death is at hand.
If at night he sees a rainbow, or by day the circle of stars,

children.text: paranetreṣu cātmānaṃ na paśyenna sa jīvati ||
children.translated_text: and does not see himself in another's eyes, he does not live.
He whose one eye runs, and whose ears slip from their proper place,

children.text: vakrā ca nāsā bhavati vijñeyo gatajīvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and whose nose becomes crooked, should be known as one whose life is gone.

children.text: yasya kṛṣṇā kharā jihvā padmābhāsaṃ ca vai mukham
children.translated_text: He whose tongue is black and rough, and whose face has the appearance of a lotus,
or whose cheeks have red lumps, death is present for him.

children.text: muktakeśo hasaṃścaiva gāyannṛtyaṃś ca yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: And the man who, with hair loosened, laughs, sings, and dances,
and goes facing the southern direction, for him that is the end of life.
He whose form repeatedly appears white, like a white dense mass,
and resembling white mustard seeds, for him death is at hand.

children.text: uṣṭrā vā rāsabhā vābhiyuktāḥ svapne rathe śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: If camels or asses, auspiciously yoked to a chariot, appear in a dream to a man,

children.text: yasya so'pi na jīvettu dakṣiṇābhimukho gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: he too does not live, having gone facing south.

children.text: dve vātha parame 'riṣṭe ekībhūtaḥ paraṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: And when two extreme <s>ariṣṭas</s> (fatal omens) have become one, there is the highest one:

children.text: ghoṣaṃ na śṛṇuyātkarṇe jyotir netre na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: he does not hear sound in his ear, and does not see light in his eye.

children.text: śvabhre yo nipatetsvapne dvāraṃ cāpi pidhīyate
children.translated_text: The man who in a dream falls into a pit, and its doorway is closed,

children.text: na cottiṣṭhati yaḥ śvabhrāttadantaṃ tasya jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: and who does not rise up from the pit, for him that is the end of life.

children.text: ūrdhvā ca dṛṣṭirna ca sampratiṣṭhā raktā punaḥ samparivartamānā
children.translated_text: His gaze is turned upward and has no steadiness; it is red and turns about again and again.

children.text: mukhasya śoṣaḥ suṣirā ca nābhiratyuṣṇamūtro viṣamastha eva ||
children.translated_text: There is dryness of the mouth, the navel is hollow, the urine is excessively hot, and he is in an uneven condition.

children.text: divā vā yadi vā rātrau pratyakṣaṃ yo nihanyate
children.translated_text: Whether by day or by night, the man who is visibly struck down,

children.text: hantāraṃ na ca paśyecca sa gatāyurna jīvati ||
children.translated_text: and yet does not see the striker, is one whose lifespan is spent; he does not live.
The human being who, at the end of a dream, enters into fire,
and who also does not recover memory, for him that is the end of life.

children.text: yastu prāvaraṇaṃ śuklaṃ svakaṃ paśyati mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: But the human being who sees his own white covering
as black or even red in a dream, for him death is at hand.
When an <s>ariṣṭa</s> (fatal omen) has been indicated in the body, and that time has arrived,

children.text: tyaktvā khedaṃ viṣādaṃ ca upekṣed buddhimān naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a wise man should abandon distress and despair and remain indifferent.

children.text: prācīṃ vā yadi vodīcīṃ diśaṃ niṣkramya vai śuciḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone out, pure, toward the eastern or else the northern direction,
to a level, very firm place, solitary and free from living creatures,

children.text: udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā svasthaś cācānta eva ca
children.translated_text: facing north or facing east, composed and having performed sipping purification,
seated in the svastika posture, he should bow to <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Holding body, head, and neck even, he should not look around;

children.text: yathā dīpo nivātastho neṅgate sopamā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: the comparison is remembered as that of a lamp standing in a windless place, which does not flicker.
In a place sloping eastward or northward, the knower of scripture should practice in that way.

children.text: kāmaṃ vitarkaṃ prītiṃ ca sukhaduḥkhe ubhe tathā ||
children.translated_text: Desire, discursive thought, joy, and likewise both pleasure and pain,

children.text: nigṛhya manasā sarvaṃ śuklaṃ dhyānam anusmaret
children.translated_text: restraining all by the mind, he should recollect pure meditation.

children.text: ghrāṇe ca rasane nityaṃ cakṣuṣī sparśane tathā ||
children.translated_text: At the nose and at the tongue always, and likewise at the two eyes and at touch,

children.text: śrotre manasi buddhau ca tatra vakṣasi dhārayet
children.translated_text: at hearing, at mind, and at intellect, he should fix it there in the chest.
Knowing the operations of time and karma, always within their groupings,
this is called the twelvefold internal yogic concentration.
He should hold the concentration at the head one hundred times, or fifty times.
For one exhausted by the yoga of concentration, the breath moves upward;
then, joined with the syllable <s>oṃ</s>, he should fill the body.
Thus the yogin made of <s>oṃ</s> becomes imperishable within the imperishable syllable.
From this point on I shall declare the marks of attaining <s>oṃkāra</s> (the syllable oṃ).

children.text: eṣa trimātro vijñeyo vyañjanaṃ cātra ceśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: This should be known as having three measures; and here the consonantal element is <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: prathamā vidyutī mātrā dvitīyā tāmasī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: The first measure is lightning-like; the second is remembered as dark.
The third measure is without qualities and leads to the imperishable syllable.
It should be known as <s>Gāndhārī</s>, born from the <s>gāndhāra</s> note.
Applied at the head, it is perceived as a touch like the movement of ants.
Just as the applied <s>oṃkāra</s> emerges back through the head,
so the yogin made of <s>oṃkāra</s> becomes imperishable, imperishable indeed.
The <s>praṇava</s> is the bow; the self is the arrow; the mark is said to be brahman.
It is to be pierced by one who is heedful; like an arrow, he should become one with that.
This single syllable <s>om</s> is the hidden word placed in the cave.
This <s>om</s> is the three worlds, the three <s>Vedas</s>, and the three fires.
These three are the strides of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the <s>Ṛks</s>, <s>Sāmans</s>, and <s>Yajuses</s>.

children.text: mātrā cārdhaṃ ca tisrastu vijñeyāḥ paramārthataḥ
children.translated_text: The three measures and the half-measure are to be known in the highest sense.
The yogin who is applied to that obtains dwelling in the same world as him.

children.text: akāro hyakṣaro jñeya ukāraḥ sahitaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The sound <s>a</s> is to be known as the imperishable syllable; the sound <s>u</s> is remembered as joined with it.
<s>Oṃkāra</s>, joined with the sound <s>m</s>, is designated as having three measures.

children.text: akāras tveṣa bhūrloka ukāro bhuva ucyate
children.translated_text: The sound <s>a</s> is this earth-world; <s>u</s> is called the mid-space.
The sound <s>m</s> with its consonantal element is sung as the heavenly world.
<s>Oṃkāra</s> is the three worlds; its head is <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.
All that is the body of the worlds; that is called the brahmanic word.

children.text: mātrāpādo rudraloko hyamātraṃ tu śivaṃ padam
children.translated_text: The quarter formed by a measure is <s>Rudraloka</s>; the measureless is the state of <s>Śiva</s>.
Through this special knowledge that state is worshipped and approached.
Therefore, one who desires eternal happiness should always delight in meditation, for that imperishable syllable is measureless.
It is to be worshipped with effort by one desiring eternal happiness.

children.text: hrasvā tu prathamā mātrā tato dīrghā tvanantaram
children.translated_text: The first measure is short; after that comes the long one.
Then the third is taught as protracted, as if pluta in length.
These <s>mātrā</s>s should be understood properly and in due order.

children.text: yāvadeva tu śakyante dhāryante tāvadeva hi ||
children.translated_text: For they are to be maintained only so long as they can in fact be maintained.

children.text: indriyāṇi mano buddhiṃ dhyāyannātmani yaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Whoever always meditates on the senses, the mind, and the intellect within the self,

children.text: ardhaṃ tanmātram api cec chṛṇu yat phalamāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: even for half of that measure, listen to the fruit that he obtains.

children.text: māse māse 'śvamedhena yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ
children.translated_text: If someone were to sacrifice with an <s>aśvamedha</s> month after month for a hundred years,
the merit that is obtained by that is obtained by a single <s>mātrā</s>.
Not by severe austerity, nor by sacrifices with abundant gifts,
is the fruit obtained in the same way as it is obtained by the <s>mātrā</s>.

children.text: tatra caiṣā tu yā mātrā plutā nāmopadiśyate
children.translated_text: And among them this measure, which is taught as the <s>plutā</s>,

children.text: eṣā eva bhavetkāryā gṛhasthānāṃ tu yoginām ||
children.translated_text: is precisely the one to be practiced by householding yogins.
Especially in regard to their eightfold sovereignty,

children.text: aṇimādye tu vijñeyā tasmādyuñjīta tāṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: beginning with <s>aṇimā</s>, it should be known; therefore practice it, twice-born ones.

children.text: evaṃ hi yogasaṃyuktaḥ śucir dānto jitendriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus joined with yoga, pure, restrained, and master of his senses,

children.text: ātmānaṃ vidyate yastu sa sarvaṃ vindate dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the one who knows the self obtains everything, twice-born ones.
Therefore the wise man should contemplate the self by the <s>Pāśupata</s> yogas.

children.text: ātmānaṃ jānate ye tu śucayaste na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those pure ones who know the self are so indeed; there is no doubt.
The <s>Ṛc</s>s, the <s>Yajus</s>es, the <s>Sāman</s>s, and the Vedic <s>Upaniṣad</s>s too
are attained through the knowledge of yoga by the brahmin who contemplates the self.

children.text: sarvadevamayo bhūtvā abhūtaḥ sa tu jāyate
children.translated_text: Having become formed of all the gods, he no longer comes into ordinary becoming.

children.text: yonisaṃkramaṇaṃ tyaktvā yāti vai śāśvataṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Abandoning passage from womb to womb, he goes to the eternal state.

children.text: yathā vṛkṣāt phalaṃ pakvaṃ pavanena samīritam
children.translated_text: As a ripe fruit, stirred by the wind, falls from a tree,
so by bowing to <s>Rudra</s> sin perishes.
Where there is bowing to <s>Rudra</s>, the fruit of all rites is certain.
From bowing to another deity one does not obtain that fruit.
Therefore the yogin should worship <s>Maheśvara</s> with the threefold <s>praṇava</s>,
with the tenfold expansion of <s>brahman</s> and with the expansions of <s>brahman</s>.
Whoever, thus joined with meditation, abandons his own body,
goes to union with <s>Śiva</s>, having lifted up three generations of his family.
Or, having perceived an ominous sign when death is near,
and having gone to <s>Avimukteśvara</s> in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the purifier,

children.text: yena kenāpi vā dehaṃ saṃtyajen mucyate naraḥ
children.translated_text: a man is released if he abandons the body by any means whatever.
Or, best of brahmins, a man may abandon his own body on <s>Śrīparvata</s>.

children.text: sa yāti śivasāyujyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: He goes to union with <s>Śiva</s>; no doubt is to be entertained about this.

children.text: avimuktaṃ paraṃ kṣetraṃ jantūnāṃ muktidaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Avimukta</s> is the supreme sacred field, always granting liberation to living beings.
A wise man should constantly attend upon it, especially at the time of death.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge ariṣṭakathanaṃ nāma ekanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the ninety-first chapter, named 'The Telling of Ominous Signs.'
The sages said:

children.text: evaṃ vārāṇasī puṇyā yadi sūta mahāmate
children.translated_text: If <s>Vārāṇasī</s> is thus holy, <s>Sūta</s> of great understanding,
you ought now to tell us its power.
We are eager to hear in full and properly

children.text: vistareṇa yathānyāyaṃ śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: the greatness of this sacred field, the beautiful <s>Avimukta</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall tell in brief, correctly, the splendid greatness
of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and <s>Avimukta</s>, as the blessed <s>Bhava</s> declared it.

children.text: vistareṇa mayā vaktuṃ brahmaṇā ca mahātmanā
children.translated_text: Even I, and the great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>, could not tell it in full,
best of brahmins, even in hundreds of crores of years.
Long ago, after his marriage, the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
came from the peak of <s>Himavat</s> with the goddess <s>Haimavatī</s> and the lords of the gaṇas.
Having reached <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s> showed

children.text: avimukteśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ vāsaṃ tatra cakāra saḥ ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Avimukteśvara</s> liṅga, and he made his dwelling there.
At <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Śrīparvata</s>, <s>Mahālaya</s>,

children.text: tuṅgeśvare ca kedāre tatsthāne yo yatirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: and at <s>Tuṅgeśvara</s> and <s>Kedāra</s>, in that place where one becomes an ascetic,
one should be an ascetic for one day, properly established in <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga.
Therefore, abandoning everything, one should practice the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.
One should dwell there in <s>Devodyāna</s>, the unsurpassed garden of <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: manasā nirmame rudro vimānaṃ ca suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s> mentally fashioned a very beautiful aerial palace.
And then the god himself showed that unsurpassed <s>Devodyāna</s>
to <s>Haimavatī</s>, together with <s>Nandī</s>, the supreme lord.
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme lord, spoke
to <s>Pārvatī</s>, for her delight, the greatness of this sacred field, <s>Avimukta</s>.
Outside, it was adorned with many kinds of blooming shrubs and lovely with networks of creepers and the like.

children.text: virūḍhapuṣpaiḥ paritaḥ priyaṅgubhiḥ supuṣpitaiḥ kaṇṭakitaiś ca ketakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: All around it had blossoming <s>priyaṅgu</s> plants with spreading flowers, and thorny <s>ketaka</s>s in full bloom.
It was filled on every side with fragrant <s>tamāla</s> thickets and with <s>vakula</s>s bearing abundant flowers.
It had hundreds of <s>aśoka</s>s and <s>punnāga</s>s in full bloom, with masses of flowers crowded by rows of bees.
In places it was adorned with the pollen of blossoming lotuses and with birds making varied soft cries.
It resounded everywhere with <s>sārasa</s> cranes and <s>cakravāka</s> birds, and with excellent intoxicated watercocks.
In one place it was auspiciously filled with the cries of peacocks, and in another with the calls of <s>kāraṇḍava</s> ducks.
In another place it was made dense with swarms of intoxicated bees and with the sounds of bee-females maddened by honey.
It was frequented by beautiful, fragrant flowers, and in places by <s>sahakāra</s> mango trees in fine bloom.
It was hidden by <s>tilaka</s> trees embraced by creepers, and filled with singing <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, <s>Siddha</s>s, and <s>Cāraṇa</s>s.
It had companies of <s>Apsaras</s> following ongoing dances, and was frequented by many delighted kinds of birds.
It resounded with flocks of dancing <s>hārīta</s> birds, while minds were excited by the roars of lions.
Here and there, with fragrant <s>kadamba</s>s and deer, its clusters of <s>darbha</s> shoots and flowers had been cropped.
adorned here and there with lakes and ponds, with lovely blooming lotuses of many kinds;
delightful with peacocks hidden in clusters of branches, with birds rejoicing in rut, and charming with their cries;
with intoxicated bees hidden in flowering tree-branches, its tall branches beautified by the beauty of fresh shoots;
here with lovely creepers marked by tooth-bites, and there with lovely trees embraced by vines;
here and there frequented by <s>kiṃpuruṣa</s> women, moving languidly in play;
with lovely peaks resounding with the cooing of pigeons, cloud-scraping, white, beautiful, and pleasing in form;
shining with many divine families of gods, with swans divided among masses of scattered flowers;
with the divine path adorned by reservoirs of water, furnished with thousands of expanses of blooming lotuses and water lilies;
provided with many shrubs and branches joined to variegated rows of flowers gathered along the side paths;

children.text: tuṅgāgrair nīlapuṣpastabakabharanataprāṃśuśākhair aśokair dolāprāntāntanīlaśrutisukhajanakair bhāsitāntaṃ manojñaiḥ
children.translated_text: its borders gleaming with delightful aśoka trees, lofty-tipped, with tall branches bent under the weight of clusters of blue flowers and pleasant to the ear;
at night made one with the moon's radiance by flowering tilaka trees, its tips of young dūrvā grass cropped by herds of deer sleeping, waking, and standing in the shade;
with clear, broad waters whose lotuses were stirred by the wind from swans' wings, and with peacocks dancing gracefully near plantains growing on the banks of the waters;

children.text: māyūraiḥ pakṣacandraiḥ kvacidavanigatai rañjitakṣmāpradeśaṃ deśe deśe vilīnapramuditavilasanmattahārītavṛndam ||
children.translated_text: with patches of ground here and there colored by the moonlike marks of peacocks' wings fallen to the earth, and with flocks of joyful, sportive, intoxicated green pigeons hidden in place after place;
with regions adorned here and there by deer, and elsewhere covered with varied heaps of flowers;
and here and there made musical by delighted <s>kinnara</s> women, whose vīṇās accompanied very sweet song and dance;
with trees surrounded by the hermitages of sages, here and there smeared and strewn with mixed flowers;
and here and there provided with broad, towering jackfruit trees laden with fruit from the root upward;
lovely with the sound of the golden anklets of siddhas and siddha women led into bowers of blooming atimukta creepers;
beautiful, with bees clinging to clusters of priyaṅgu trees and with rows of bees covering mango and kadamba flowers;
lovely with waters shaken by winds from masses of flowers, and with charming thickets made to droop by delightful bees;
with groups of does suddenly frightened among the thickets; stirred by the wind, it bestowed <s>apavarga</s> (release) on embodied beings;
with delightful tilaka trees dappled by networks of moonbeams, and with aśokas resembling vermilion, saffron, and kusumbha dye;
and then with karṇikāra trees like the brilliance of gold, heaped with masses of flowers and bearing very broad branches;
in places with flowers like powdered collyrium, in places with flowers like coral,
and in places with flowers resembling gold, the ground was covered;
among punnāga trees ringing with the cries of hundreds of birds, bent down by the weight of clusters of red aśoka flowers;
with charming outskirts and rest-houses that removed weariness, and with bees sporting among blooming lotuses;
then the sustainer of all worlds, the lord of beings, together with the daughter of the snowy mountain and his beloved <s>Gaṇeśas</s>,

children.text: vividhataruviśālaṃ mattahṛṣṭānnapuṣṭair upavanam atiramyaṃ darśayāmāsa devyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: showed the goddess an exceedingly lovely grove, spacious with many kinds of trees and filled with creatures intoxicated, joyful, and well nourished;

children.text: puṣpairvanyaiḥ śubhaśubhatamaiḥ kalpitairdivyabhūṣairdevīṃ divyāmupavanagatāṃ bhūṣayāmāsa śarvaḥ
children.translated_text: With wild flowers, most auspicious and arranged as divine ornaments, <s>Śarva</s> adorned the divine goddess who had entered the grove;

children.text: sā cāpyenaṃ tuhinagirisutā śaṅkaraṃ devadevaṃ puṣpairdivyaiḥ śubhataratamair bhūṣayāmāsa bhaktyā ||
children.translated_text: and she too, the daughter of the snowy mountain, adorned <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the god of gods, with divine and most auspicious flowers, in devotion;

children.text: sampūjya pūjyaṃ tridaśeśvarāṇāṃ samprekṣya codyānam atīva ramyam
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the one worshipful to the lords of the gods, and having looked upon the exceedingly lovely garden,

children.text: gaṇeśvarair nandimukhaiś ca sārdhamuvāca devaṃ praṇipatya devī ||
children.translated_text: the goddess, together with the lords of the gaṇas headed by <s>Nandi</s>, spoke to the god after bowing down;
<s>Śrī Devī</s> said:

children.text: udyānaṃ darśitaṃ deva prabhayā parayā yutam
children.translated_text: O god, the garden has been shown to me, endowed with supreme radiance;
please tell me again all the qualities of this <s>kṣetra</s> (sacred field);
please tell me in every way the greatness of this <s>kṣetra</s>, <s>Avimukta</s>;
O lord of gods, god of gods, bull-bannered one, please speak;
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing those words of the goddess, the god of gods, the excellent lord,
kissed her lotus-face and then, smiling, spoke to <s>Girijā</s>;
The Blessed Lord said:

children.text: idaṃ guhyatamaṃ kṣetraṃ sadā vārāṇasī mama
children.translated_text: This most secret <s>kṣetra</s>, <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, is always mine;
for all living beings it is always the cause of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);
In this place, O goddess, siddhas always remain, observing my vow;
always bearing various <s>liṅgas</s>, they desire my world;
with selves disciplined and senses conquered, they practice the highest yoga;
in this place filled with many kinds of trees and adorned by many kinds of birds;
adorned with lakes rich in lotus and water-lily flowers;
and auspicious, always attended by hosts of apsarases and gandharvas;

children.text: rocate me sadā vāso yena kāryeṇa tacchṛṇu
children.translated_text: Hear the reason why residence here is always pleasing to me;

children.text: manmanā mama bhaktaś ca mayi nityārpitakriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: one whose mind is on me, who is my devotee, and whose acts are always offered to me,

children.text: yathā mokṣamavāpnoti anyatra na tathā kvacit
children.translated_text: attains liberation here as he does nowhere else;

children.text: kāmaṃ hyatra mṛto devi janturmokṣāya kalpate ||
children.translated_text: for, O goddess, a creature who dies here is indeed fit for <s>mokṣa</s>;
This divine city of mine is great, more secret than what is secret;

children.text: brahmādayo vijānanti ye ca siddhā mumukṣavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and the others know it, as do the siddhas who desire liberation;

children.text: ataḥ paramidaṃ kṣetraṃ parā ceyaṃ gatirmama
children.translated_text: therefore this <s>kṣetra</s> is supreme, and this is my supreme goal;

children.text: vimuktaṃ na mayā yasmānmokṣyate vā kadācana ||
children.translated_text: because it has never been abandoned by me, nor will it ever be abandoned.
Since this is my <s>kṣetra</s> (sacred field), it is remembered as <s>Avimukta</s>.

children.text: naimiṣe ca kurukṣetre gaṅgādvāre ca puṣkare ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Naimiṣa</s>, at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, and at <s>Puṣkara</s>,
since <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is not attained by bathing or even by resorting to them,
whereas it is attained here, therefore this place is superior to those.

children.text: prayāge vā bhavenmokṣa iha vā matparigrahāt
children.translated_text: There may be <s>mokṣa</s> at <s>Prayāga</s>, or here through my protection;
this auspicious <s>Avimukta</s> is superior even to <s>Prayāga</s>, the foremost of <s>tīrthas</s> (holy fords).
Truth is the secret teaching of <s>dharma</s>; tranquility is the secret teaching of <s>mokṣa</s>.
But even the best of the wise do not know the secret teaching of <s>kṣetra</s> and <s>tīrtha</s>.

children.text: kāmaṃ bhuñjan svapan krīḍan kurvan hi vividhāḥ kriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Eating as he wishes, sleeping, playing, and indeed performing many kinds of acts,
if a creature gives up his life in <s>Avimukta</s>, he becomes fit for <s>mokṣa</s>.
For men who have committed thousands of sins, even becoming a <s>piśāca</s> is better,

children.text: na tu śakrasahasratvaṃ svarge kāśīpurīṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: but not becoming a thousand <s>Śakras</s> in heaven without the city of <s>Kāśī</s>.
Therefore <s>Avimukta</s> is indeed to be resorted to for the sake of liberation,

children.text: jaigīṣavyaḥ parāṃ siddhiṃ gato yatra mahātapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: where the great ascetic <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> attained supreme perfection.

children.text: asya kṣetrasya māhātmyādbhaktyā ca mama bhāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: By the greatness of this <s>kṣetra</s>, and because he was filled with devotion to me,
the cave of <s>Jaigīṣavya</s> is regarded as the foremost abode of yogins.
Meditating on me there constantly, the fire of yoga blazes intensely,
and one reaches supreme <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation/liberation), difficult even for the gods to obtain.
For sages whose marks are hidden, knowers of all established doctrines,
<s>mokṣa</s>, difficult to obtain anywhere else, is attained here.
And to them I shall proclaim unsurpassed yogic sovereignty,
union with myself and the desired state itself.
<s>Kubera</s>, here in my <s>kṣetra</s>, with all his acts offered to me,
obtained the rank of lord of the <s>gaṇas</s> simply by resorting to this <s>kṣetra</s>.

children.text: saṃvarto bhavitā yaś ca so'pi bhakto mamaiva tu
children.translated_text: And <s>Saṃvarta</s>, who is to come, is also truly my devotee;
having worshipped me right here, O goddess, he will attain unsurpassed perfection.
The yogin sage <s>Vyāsa</s>, son of <s>Parāśara</s>, a great ascetic,
will be my devotee and the founder of the arrangement of the <s>Vedas</s>.
He too, lotus-eyed one, that bull among sages, will delight in this <s>kṣetra</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> together with the divine seers, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and also the Sun,
and likewise <s>Śakra</s>, king of the gods, and whatever other heaven-dwellers there are,
all these great-souled ones worship me here, O woman of good vows.
Other divine yogins too, great-souled and moving in hidden forms,
having become single-minded, always worship me here.
Even a man whose mind is attached to sense objects and whose delight in <s>dharma</s> has been abandoned,

children.text: iha kṣetre mṛtaḥ so'pi saṃsāre na punarbhavet ||
children.translated_text: if he dies here in this <s>kṣetra</s>, does not come again into <s>saṃsāra</s>.
But those who are free from possessiveness, firm, established in <s>sattva</s>, and have conquered their senses,

children.text: vratinaś ca nirārambhāḥ sarve te mayi bhāvitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who keep vows and undertake no worldly enterprises, all of them are absorbed in me.
Those wise ones, free from attachment, having reached the God of gods,

children.text: gatā iha paraṃ mokṣaṃ prasādānmama suvrate ||
children.translated_text: attained supreme <s>mokṣa</s> here through my grace, O woman of good vows.
That supreme <s>mokṣa</s> which a yogin would not obtain in thousands of other births,
he obtains right here through my grace, O woman of good vows.

children.text: goprekṣakam idaṃ kṣetraṃ brahmaṇā sthāpitaṃ purā
children.translated_text: This <s>kṣetra</s> called <s>Goprekṣaka</s> was established by <s>Brahmā</s> long ago;
and see here the divine abode of <s>Kailāsa</s>, O beautiful-faced one.
Then, having come to <s>Goprekṣaka</s> and seen me here, a human being
does not meet with a bad destiny and is freed from impurities.

children.text: kapilāhradam ityevaṃ tathā vai brahmaṇā kṛtam
children.translated_text: This is also called <s>Kapilāhrada</s>, and likewise it was made by <s>Brahmā</s>,
a great and most holy <s>tīrtha</s>, with water born from the milk of cows.
Here too I myself am remembered as <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>;

children.text: sānnidhyaṃ kṛtavān devi sadāhaṃ dṛśyate tvayā ||
children.translated_text: I have established my presence, O goddess, and I am always visible to you.

children.text: bhadratoyaṃ ca paśyeha brahmaṇā ca kṛtaṃ hradam
children.translated_text: Look here at <s>Bhadratoya</s>, a lake also made by <s>Brahmā</s>;
by all the gods I was propitiated in this place, O goddess.
'Become pacified, O Lord,' they said, and <s>Śiva</s> was likewise pacified.
Here I was brought by <s>Brahmā</s> and installed by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.

children.text: brahmaṇā cāpi saṃgṛhya viṣṇunā sthāpitaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: And after it had been taken up by <s>Brahmā</s>, it was again installed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, agitated in mind, said to <s>Viṣṇu</s>:
'Why have you installed this <s>liṅga</s> that was brought by me?'
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s> answered <s>Brahmā</s>, whose face was angry:
'I have supreme and very great devotion to the god <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: mayaiva sthāpitaṃ liṅgaṃ tava nāmnā bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s> was installed by me; it will exist under your name.'
Thus I became established here as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.
Having seen this Lord of gods also, a man goes to my world.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi brahmā mama liṅgamidaṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Then once again <s>Brahmā</s> established this auspicious <s>liṅga</s> of mine,
according to rule and endowed with the highest devotion.
As <s>Svarlīneśvara</s>, I myself came here.

children.text: prāṇān iha narastyaktvā na punarjāyate kvacit ||
children.translated_text: A man who gives up his life here is not born again anywhere.

children.text: ananyā sā gatistasya yogināṃ caiva yā smṛtā
children.translated_text: That is his unique goal, the very one remembered for yogins.
In this place also, by me, a <s>Daitya</s>, a thorn to the gods,
having assumed the form of a tiger, arrogant and strong, was slain.
Known as <s>Vyāghreśvara</s>, I am always established here.
Having seen this <s>Vyāghramīśvara</s>, one does not go again to a bad destiny.

children.text: utpalo vidalaścaiva yau daityau brahmaṇā purā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Utpala</s> and <s>Vidala</s>, the two <s>Daityas</s> whom <s>Brahmā</s> in former times

children.text: strīvadhyau darpitau dṛṣṭvā tvayaiva nihatau raṇe
children.translated_text: saw as arrogant and destined to be killed by a woman, were slain by you yourself in battle.
Here, contemptuously, with a ball, this body of his was taken over.
At the beginning, after coming here, I set out together with the lords of the <s>gaṇas</s>.
Therefore this is <s>Jyeṣṭhasthāna</s>; this is my holy sight.
By the gods on every side these <s>liṅgas</s> have therefore been established.

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpi niyato martyo dehabhede gaṇo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Even by seeing them, a disciplined mortal becomes a <s>gaṇa</s> after the body is broken apart.

children.text: pitrā te śailarājena purā himavatā svayam
children.translated_text: By your father, the king of mountains, <s>Himavat</s> himself, long ago,

children.text: mama priyahitaṃ sthānaṃ jñātvā liṅgaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: a <s>liṅga</s> was installed when he knew this place to be dear and beneficial to me.
It is famed as <s>Śaileśvara</s>; let it be seen here with reverence.
Having seen this, O goddess, a human being would not go to a bad destiny.
This river is <s>Varuṇā</s>, O goddess, holy and freeing from sin.
Adorning this sacred field, it has joined together with <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
And by <s>Brahmā</s> too the excellent <s>liṅga</s> was established at the confluence;
it is famed in the world as <s>Saṃgameśvara</s>; let it be seen.

children.text: saṃgame devanadyā hi yaḥ snātvā manujaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: At the confluence of the divine river, the pure man who bathes
and worships <s>Saṃgameśvara</s>: whence could there be fear of birth for him?

children.text: idaṃ manye mahākṣetraṃ nivāso yogināṃ param
children.translated_text: I consider this a great sacred field, the supreme dwelling of yogins,
where, in the middle of the field, I myself have appeared and taken the foremost seat.
I am famed there as <s>Madhyameśvara</s> among all gods and asuras.
For this is the place of siddhas who maintain my vow,
of yogins who desire liberation and whose selves delight in the yoga of knowledge.

children.text: dṛṣṭvainaṃ madhyameśānaṃ janma prati na śocati ||
children.translated_text: Having seen this <s>Madhyameśāna</s>, one does not grieve over birth.
This <s>liṅga</s> was established by <s>Śukra</s>, the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
By name it is called <s>Śukreśvara</s>, worshipped by all siddhas and immortals.
Having seen this, a disciplined person is immediately released from all sins.

children.text: mṛtaś ca na punarjantuḥ saṃsārī tu bhavennaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: And when dead, the creature, the man, does not again become one who wanders in <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Long ago, in the form of a jackal, an asura who was a thorn to the gods,
having obtained a boon from <s>Brahmā</s>, was a jackal afraid of captivity.
He was slain, O daughter of <s>Himavat</s>; from that I became <s>Jambūkeśa</s>,
still famous in the world today and bowed to by gods and asuras.
Having seen even this lord of gods, one would obtain all desires.

children.text: grahaiḥ śukrapurogaiś ca etāni sthāpitāni ha ||
children.translated_text: And these were indeed established by the planets headed by <s>Śukra</s>.
Behold the holy <s>liṅgas</s>, which grant all desires.
Thus these holy dwellings of mine, O <s>Pārvatī</s>,

children.text: kathitāni mama kṣetre guhyaṃ cānyadidaṃ śṛṇu
children.translated_text: have been told in my sacred field; now hear this other secret.
This field is proclaimed as four <s>krośas</s> in the four directions.
Know it as a <s>yojana</s>, O fair-limbed one, granting immortality at the time of death.
Seeing me situated on Mount <s>Mahālaya</s> and established at <s>Kedāra</s>,
one obtains the state of a <s>gaṇa</s>; in this place liberation is obtained.
Since one obtains <s>gāṇapatya</s> (the state of belonging to Gaṇapati) from it, that is the highest liberation.
Therefore, beyond that <s>Mahālaya</s>, beyond <s>Kedāra</s>, and beyond <s>Madhyama</s> too,
<s>Avimukta</s> is remembered as the holiest field, O fair-faced one.

children.text: kedāraṃ madhyamaṃ kṣetraṃ sthānaṃ caiva mahālayam
children.translated_text: <s>Kedāra</s>, the <s>Madhyama</s> field, and the station called <s>Mahālaya</s>

children.text: mama puṇyāni bhūrloke tebhyaḥ śreṣṭhatamaṃ tvidam ||
children.translated_text: are my holy places on earth; but this one is the best of them.
Because these worlds were created from it, therefore this field is auspicious.
It was never abandoned by me; therefore it became <s>Avimukta</s>.
A human being who sees my <s>Avimukteśvara</s> <s>liṅga</s> here
is at once freed from sin and released from the bonds that bind the <s>paśu</s> (individual soul).
<s>Śaileśa</s> and <s>Saṃgameśa</s>, <s>Svarlīna</s>, <s>Madhyameśvara</s>,
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Goprekṣa</s>, and <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>,
<s>Upaśānta</s> and <s>Śiva</s>, dwelling in the <s>Jyeṣṭhasthāna</s>,
and the famed <s>Śukreśvara</s>, <s>Vyāghreśa</s>, and <s>Jambukeśvara</s>:

children.text: dṛṣṭvā na jāyate martyaḥ saṃsāre duḥkhasāgare
children.translated_text: having seen them, a mortal is not born in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the ocean of suffering.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evam uktvā mahādevo diśaḥ sarvā vyalokayat ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, <s>Mahādeva</s> looked toward all the directions.
After the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>, had looked and stood there,
suddenly that whole region became as if brilliantly illumined.
Then Pāśupata siddhas, white in radiance from being anointed with ashes,
great-souled devotees of <s>Maheśvara</s>, likewise observant of strict vows,
many hundreds of them, having approached, bowed to <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Having again beheld the lord of yoga and the entire yoga of meditation,
they stood, established in the self, as if dissolving into <s>Īśvara</s>.

children.text: sthitānāṃ sa tadā teṣāṃ devadeva umāpatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: While they stood there, the god of gods, <s>Umāpati</s>,

children.text: sa bibhratparamāṃ mūrtiṃ babhūva puruṣaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: bearing the supreme form, became the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the Lord,

children.text: kṛtsnaṃ jagadihaikasthaṃ kartum anta iva sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: as if he were standing here to make the whole universe abide in one place.
When the lord of the world had assumed that supreme form,
the daughter of the mountain king, her hairs bristling, could no longer see it.
Then, understanding that form to be unseen and established in <s>prakṛti</s>,
the supreme goddess assumed the form of <s>prakṛti</s> through yoga,

children.text: taṃ śaśāka punardraṣṭuṃ harasya ca mahātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: and was again able to see that great-souled <s>Hara</s>.
Then the yogins, placing themselves in dissolution in the <s>Puruṣa</s>,
all entered his heart, their seeds of <s>saṃsāra</s> burned away,
remembering the beautiful seed of the five-syllabled mantra,
divine, removing all sins, and revealed long ago.
Established in the blue-red form, he again made his body auspicious.
Seeing him, <s>Śailajā</s>, with every hair on her body thrilled, spoke,

children.text: stuvatī caraṇau natvā ka ime bhagavanniti ||
children.translated_text: praising him and bowing to his feet: "Who are these, Blessed One?"
Then the best of gods spoke to that goddess, the daughter of the mountain king.
The Blessed Lord said:
By the best twice-born, endowed with devotion and taking refuge in my vow,
whatever yogas were practiced here, for them in a single birth,

children.text: kṣetrasyāsya prabhāvena bhaktyā ca mama bhāmini ||
children.translated_text: through the power of this sacred field and through devotion to me, O lovely one, ...

children.text: anugraho mayā hyevaṃ kriyate mūrtitaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Thus favor is bestowed by me myself in embodied form.

children.text: tasmād etan mahat kṣetraṃ brahmādyaiḥ sevitaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Therefore this is a great sacred field, attended likewise by <s>Brahmā</s> and the others,

children.text: śrutimadbhiś ca viprendraiḥ saṃsiddhaiś ca tapasvibhiḥ
children.translated_text: and by learned chief brahmins, perfected beings, and ascetics.
Every month, on the eighth lunar day, and every month on the fourteenth,
in both fortnights, O goddess, it is worshipped at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
And at eclipses of the moon and sun, and especially on the <s>Kārttikī</s> full moon,
on all holy festival days, at the equinoxes and solstitial passages,
all the tīrthas on earth come to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, to the <s>Jāhnavī</s>,
holy, flowing northward, issued from my crest,
the auspicious daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, king of mountains, your father,
holy, standing in a holy place, always flowing toward a holy direction.
Hear, fair-faced one, of those who come from every side and worship her.
Together with hundreds of tīrthas, <s>Kurukṣetra</s> draws near there,

children.text: puṣkaraṃ nimiṣaṃ caiva prayāgaṃ ca pṛthūdakam ||
children.translated_text: as do <s>Puṣkara</s>, <s>Nimiṣa</s>, <s>Prayāga</s>, and <s>Pṛthūdaka</s>;
<s>Drumakṣetra</s>, <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, and <s>Naimiṣa</s> with its tīrthas,

children.text: kṣetrāṇi sarvato devi devatā ṛṣayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: sacred fields from every side, O goddess, and likewise deities and sages,

children.text: saṃdhyā ca ṛtavaścaiva sarvā nadyaḥ sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: twilight, the seasons, all rivers and lakes,
the seven oceans, and all divine tīrthas completely,
will assemble at the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> on all festival days, O virtuous one.
Having seen <s>Avimukteśvara</s>, and having seen <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>,
and having approached <s>Kālabhairava</s>, their sins are shaken off entirely,
O queen of the gods, on every single festival day.
Whatever holy and great sanctuaries there are on earth,
always come and enter the holy place on each festival day,
the excellent field <s>Avimukta</s>, which destroys great sins.

children.text: kedāre caiva yalliṅgaṃ yacca liṅgaṃ mahālaye ||
children.translated_text: The liṅga at <s>Kedāra</s>, and the liṅga at <s>Mahālaya</s>,
the one called <s>Madhyameśvara</s>, and likewise <s>Pāśupateśvara</s>,

children.text: śaṅkukarṇeśvaraṃ caiva gokarṇau ca tathā hyubhau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkukarṇeśvara</s>, and likewise both <s>Gokarṇa</s> shrines,
the one named <s>Drumacaṇḍeśvara</s>, and the unsurpassed <s>Bhadreśvara</s>,
<s>Sthāneśvara</s>, also <s>Ekāgra</s>, <s>Kāleśvara</s>, and <s>Ajeśvara</s>,
<s>Bhairaveśvara</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and likewise the one named <s>Oṃkāraka</s>,
<s>Amareśa</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Jyotiṣa</s>, and <s>Bhasmagātraka</s>,

children.text: yāni cānyāni puṇyāni sthānāni mama bhūtale
children.translated_text: and whatever other holy places of mine there are on the earth,
renowned as sixty-eight, and all the others that are established,
all those without remainder enter me at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
This secret has been declared for all holy festival days.
Therefore a creature who dies here obtains the divine immortal state.

children.text: snātasya caiva gaṅgāyāṃ dṛṣṭena ca mayā śubhe ||
children.translated_text: For one who has bathed in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and has been seen by me, O auspicious one,
the result is equal to the fruits of all sacrifices, performed by the hundred-thousand,

children.text: sadya eva samāpnoti kiṃ tataḥ paramādbhutam ||
children.translated_text: and he obtains it immediately. What could be more wondrous than that?
The chief of all sanctuaries, in heaven, on earth, and even in the mountains,
is higher than the highest, O goddess. Know this, as I have said.
By the word <s>avi</s>, sin is denoted in the <s>Veda</s>, so the brahmins say.

children.text: tena muktaṃ mayā juṣṭamavimuktam ata ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Because it is freed from that and cherished by me, it is therefore called <s>Avimukta</s>.
Having spoken thus, blessed <s>Rudra</s>, the great lord of all worlds, said:

children.text: sudṛṣṭaṃ kuru deveśi avimuktaṃ gṛhaṃ mama ||
children.translated_text: 'Look well, O queen of the gods, at <s>Avimukta</s>, my own abode.'

children.text: ityuktvā bhagavān devas tayā sārdham umāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the blessed god <s>Umāpati</s>, together with her,
the blessed one showed the unsurpassed <s>Śrīparvata</s>.
He dwelt always with her at <s>Avimukteśvara</s>,
and because he is all-pervading and is all, the self of all is composed of being and non-being.
Having reached <s>Śrīparvata</s> with the goddess, <s>Hara</s>, lord of the gods,
<s>Bhava</s>, lord of all beings, showed the sacred fields.
He showed <s>Kuṇḍīprabha</s>, and the supreme, divine <s>Vaiśravaṇeśvara</s>,

children.text: āśāliṅgaṃ ca deveśaṃ divyaṃ yacca bileśvaram ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Āśāliṅga</s>, the lord of gods, and the divine <s>Bileśvara</s>,
and the supreme <s>Rāmeśvara</s>, which was established by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
At the side of the southern gate stands the lord <s>Kuṇḍaleśvara</s>;
near the eastern gate is the excellent <s>Tripurāntaka</s>,
grown great together with the mountain and honored by the god of gods.
It is called <s>Madhyameśvara</s>, renowned in the three worlds.

children.text: amareśvaraṃ ca varadaṃ devaiḥ pūrvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam ||
children.translated_text: And there is boon-giving <s>Amareśvara</s>, formerly established by the gods,
the lord <s>Gocarmeśvara</s>, and likewise the wondrous <s>Indreśvara</s>,

children.text: karmeśvaraṃ ca vipulaṃ kāryārthaṃ brahmaṇā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and vast <s>Karmeśvara</s>, made by <s>Brahmā</s> for the sake of the work.
And the glorious <s>Siddhavaṭa</s>, my everlasting, constant abode,
and the auspicious, divine <s>Ajabila</s>, fashioned by the unborn one himself.

children.text: tatraiva pāduke divye madīye ca bileśvare
children.translated_text: There too are my divine sandals at <s>Bileśvara</s>.
There, in the middle of <s>Śṛṅgāṭācala</s>, shaped like a junction of four roads,
is the one named <s>Śṛṅgāṭakeśvara</s>, established by the glorious goddess,
and also <s>Mallikārjunaka</s>; this is my auspicious dwelling.
And <s>Rajeśvara</s>, in due order, was well established by <s>Rajas</s>.
There are <s>Gajeśvara</s>, <s>Vaiśākha</s>, and imperishable <s>Kapoteśvara</s>,
and <s>Koṭīśvara</s>, the great tīrtha, attended long ago by hosts of crores of <s>Rudras</s>.
See it today, O goddess, auspicious and greater than all else.
The auspicious one called <s>Dvidevakula</s> was established by <s>Brahmā</s> to the south,

children.text: uttare sthāpitaṃ caiva viṣṇunā caiva śailajam ||
children.translated_text: and to the north was established by <s>Viṣṇu</s> the mountain-born shrine.
And the great-measured liṅga was formerly established by me.
On the western mountain, see <s>Brahmeśvara</s> and <s>Aleśvara</s>,

children.text: alaṃkṛtaṃ tvayā brahman purastān munibhiḥ saha
children.translated_text: adorned by you, O <s>Brahman</s>, in front together with the sages.
Having said this, he stayed in that house; it is remembered as <s>Alaṃgṛha</s>.

children.text: tatrāpi tīrthaṃ tīrthajñe vyomaliṅgaṃ ca paśya me
children.translated_text: There too, O knower of tīrthas, see my tīrtha and the <s>Vyomaliṅga</s>.
For this <s>Kadambeśvara</s> was established by <s>Skanda</s> himself.
And <s>Gomaṇḍaleśvara</s> was well established by <s>Nanda</s> and the others;
these were installed by all the gods, beginning with <s>Śakra</s>, O fair-faced one.
At the edge of glorious <s>Devahrada</s>, see these places of mine.

children.text: tathā hārapure devi tava hāre nipātite ||
children.translated_text: Likewise in <s>Hārapura</s>, O goddess, where your necklace fell,
you made this <s>Hārakuṇḍa</s> for the welfare of the worlds.
And in <s>Śivarudrapura</s>, O virtuous one, upon that body,
your father, the good mountain, established <s>Tvacaleśvara</s> there.

children.text: alaṃkṛtaṃ mayā brahma purastān munibhiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, adorned by me, stands before it together with the sages.
O goddess, the shrine <s>Caṇḍikeśvara</s> belongs to <s>Caṇḍikeśā</s>, your daughter;
the place made by <s>Caṇḍikā</s> is the excellent <s>Ambikātīrtha</s>.
And there is <s>Rucikeśvara</s>; this auspicious stream is <s>Kapilā</s>.

children.text: eteṣu devi sthāneṣu tīrtheṣu vividheṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: In these places, O goddess, and in these various tīrthas,

children.text: pūjayenmāṃ sadā bhaktyā mayā sārdhaṃ hi modate
children.translated_text: one should always worship me with devotion; he rejoices together with me.
A brāhmaṇa who abandons the body on <s>Śrīśaila</s>, his sins burned away,

children.text: mucyate nātra saṃdeho hyavimukte yathā śubham
children.translated_text: is released; there is no doubt here, just as auspiciously at <s>Avimukta</s>.

children.text: mahāsnānaṃ ca yaḥ kuryādghṛtena vidhinaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: And whoever should perform the great bath with ghee according to rule,

children.text: sa yāti mama sāyujyaṃ sthāneṣveteṣu suvrate
children.translated_text: goes to union with me in these places, O virtuous one.
An ordinary bath should be known as one hundred palas, and an anointing as twenty-five;

children.text: palānāṃ dve sahasre tu mahāsnānaṃ prakīrtitam
children.translated_text: but two thousand palas is proclaimed to be the great bath.

children.text: snāpya liṅgaṃ madīyaṃ tu gavyenaiva ghṛtena ca ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed my <s>liṅga</s> with cow products and with ghee,
and having purified it with all substances, he pours water over it.
By sweeping it clean he obtains the merit of a hundred sacrifices, and by bathing it likewise ten thousand.
By worship he obtains a hundred thousand, and by song and instruments an endless merit.
A bath connected with the great bath is remembered as eight times a bath,
even with water alone, or with scented water, when done devotionally.

children.text: anulepanaṃ tu tat sarvaṃ pañcaviṃśatpalena vai ||
children.translated_text: All that anointing, however, is with twenty-five palas.

children.text: śamīpuṣpaṃ ca vidhinā bilvapatraṃ ca paṅkajam
children.translated_text: The śamī flower, and according to rule the bilva leaf and lotus,

children.text: anyānyapi ca puṣpāṇi bilvapatraṃ na saṃtyajet ||
children.translated_text: and also other flowers; one should not omit the bilva leaf.
With four droṇas, or else with eight droṇas, one should honor <s>Mahādeva</s>;
and with ten droṇas, or else with eight droṇas, one should make the <s>naivedya</s> (food offering).
Even in an āḍhaka, merit equal to a hundred droṇas is prescribed.
No deliberation about this is to be made for a poor brāhmaṇa.
With bherīs, mṛdaṅgas, murajas, timiras, paṭahas, and the like,
and with various other instruments and many kinds of sounds,
whoever causes a night vigil to be held and prays in proper order,
together with servants, sons, wives, and also kinsmen and relatives,
having circumambulated, should pray to the excellent <s>liṅga</s>:
"Lacking substance, lacking rite, lacking faith, O lord of gods,

children.text: kṛtaṃ vā na kṛtaṃ vāpi kṣantumarhasi śaṅkara
children.translated_text: whether done or not done, you should forgive it, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>."

children.text: ityuktvā vai japedrudraṃ tvaritaṃ śāntimeva ca ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, he should quickly recite the <s>Rudra</s> and also the <s>Śānti</s>.
Having thus recited the great seed-syllable and likewise the five-syllabled mantra,
the fruit that there is in all tīrthas and in all sacrifices,
that fruit he obtains, as one who has died in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> does.

children.text: tathaiva mama sāyujyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise he attains union with me; there is no doubt about this.
This should be done according to rule by my devotees for love of me.

children.text: ye na kurvanti te bhaktā na bhavanti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those devotees who do not do it are not devotees; there is no doubt.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: niśamya vacanaṃ devī gatvā vārāṇasīṃ purīm
children.translated_text: Having heard the words, the goddess went to the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.

children.text: avimukteśvaraṃ liṅgaṃ payasā ca ghṛtena ca ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Avimukta</s>, with milk and ghee, she worshipped the <s>liṅga</s> of <s>Avimukteśvara</s>;
she worshipped <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of gods, the leader of the worlds.
And at <s>Avimukta</s>, through the austerity of great-souled <s>Mandara</s>,
he created a sacred field on <s>Mandara</s>, in a beautiful cave.
There the lord, after subduing <s>Andhaka</s>, the great Daitya, son of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,
graciously bestowed <s>gaṇatva</s> (status among the gaṇas) on him in sport.
I have told you all this, the whole essence of the tale, with reverence.
Whoever reads or hears this excellent greatness of the sacred field,
quickly obtains all the merit that is found in all sacred fields.
Or if he has all the twice-born hear it, purified and with senses mastered,

children.text: sa eva sarvayajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that man obtains the fruit of every sacrifice.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge vārāṇasīśrīśailamāhātmyakathanaṃ nāma dvinavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the venerable <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the ninety-second chapter, named "The Narration of the Greatness of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and <s>Śrīśaila</s>."
The sages said:
How did the lord of Daityas named <s>Andhaka</s>, in the lovely cave on <s>Mandara</s>,
after being subdued, obtain lordship among the gaṇas from <s>Maheśvara</s>?
You ought to tell us how it happened and how you heard it.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The favor shown to <s>Andhaka</s> and the drying up of <s>Mandara</s>,
and the gaining of boons in full, I shall declare briefly.
The son of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, whose eyes were like gold,
formerly known as <s>Andhaka</s>, had gained prowess through austerity.
Through the favor of <s>Brahmā</s> himself he obtained invulnerability,
and, having enjoyed the whole triple world and conquered the city of <s>Indra</s> long ago,
he terrified <s>Vāsava</s> in play and without effort.
Afflicted, struck, bound, and cast down by him, those gods,
frightened, entered <s>Mandara</s>, with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> at their head.

children.text: evaṃ saṃpīḍya vai devān andhako'pi mahāsuraḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, having oppressed the gods, <s>Andhaka</s> too, the great Asura,
By chance he reached beautiful-caverned Mount <s>Mandara</s>.

children.text: tataste samastāḥ surendrāḥ sasādhyāḥ sureśaṃ maheśaṃ puretyāhurevam
children.translated_text: Then all those chief gods, together with the <s>Sādhyas</s>, approached the lord of gods, <s>Maheśa</s>, and spoke thus:
'Quickly, our bodies have been split and broken by his slight force; we have been cut down by the weapons of the king of the <s>Daityas</s>.'
Having heard all this about the unequalled coming of the <s>Daitya</s>,
the Blessed Lord, together with the lords of the <s>gaṇas</s>, went toward <s>Andhaka</s>.
There <s>Indra</s>, lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the foremost lords of gods, and all the best brahmins,

children.text: jayeti vācā bhagavantam ūcuḥ kirīṭabaddhāñjalayaḥ samantāt ||
children.translated_text: with their crests and joined palms bent, cried out to the Blessed Lord on every side, 'Victory!'
Then <s>Mahādeva</s> reduced all his demons, in hundreds of crores upon crores,
to ashes, and at that time he pierced <s>Andhaka</s>.
Seeing <s>Andhaka</s> transfixed by the trident of the trident-bearing Lord, his covering of sin burned away,
the Grandfather bowed down and made a roar in many regions.
At the sound of that roar the gods roared too, after bowing to that god.
All the sages danced, and the foremost <s>gaṇas</s> rejoiced.
The gods poured showers of flowers then upon <s>Śambhu</s>.
All the three worlds rejoiced with joy and resounded.

children.text: dagdho'gninā ca śūlena protaḥ preta ivāndhakaḥ
children.translated_text: Burned by fire and transfixed by the trident, <s>Andhaka</s> was like a corpse.
Having assumed a <s>sāttvika</s> disposition, he reflected in his mind:
'Since in another birth too I was burned by the god, by <s>Śiva</s> himself,
and since <s>Śambhu</s>, the manifest <s>Maheśvara</s>, was worshipped by me before,
therefore this has been obtained by me; otherwise it would not be fitting.

children.text: yaḥ smarenmanasā rudraṃ prāṇānte sakṛdeva vā ||
children.translated_text: Whoever remembers <s>Rudra</s> in his mind even once at the end of life,

children.text: sa yāti śivasāyujyaṃ kiṃ punarbahuśaḥ smaran
children.translated_text: goes to union with <s>Śiva</s>; how much more one who remembers him often?

children.text: brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and all the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s>

children.text: śaraṇaṃ prāpya tiṣṭhanti tameva śaraṇaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: stand after attaining him as refuge; one should go to him alone as refuge.'
Having reflected in this way, <s>Andhaka</s>, pleased in himself, praised <s>Śiva</s>, the lord <s>Īśāna</s>, destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s>,
together with his <s>gaṇas</s>, out of the weight of his merit.
The Blessed Lord <s>Hara</s>, remover of supreme distress, was entreated by him.
The lord of gods, seeing the <s>Dānava</s>, the son of <s>Hiraṇyanetra</s>, fixed on the point of the trident,
<s>Nīlalohita</s> spoke to him with compassion:

children.text: tuṣṭo'smi vatsa bhadraṃ te kāmaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi te
children.translated_text: 'I am pleased, child. Good fortune to you. What desire shall I fulfill for you?
Choose boons, lord of <s>Daityas</s>; I am your boon-giver, <s>Andhaka</s>.'
Then, hearing that speech of <s>Śambhu</s>, the son of <s>Hiraṇyanayana</s>
spoke these words to <s>Maheśvara</s> in a voice choked with joy:
'Blessed Lord, god of gods, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, remover of the distress of devotees,

children.text: tvayi bhaktiḥ prasīdeśa yadi deyo varaś ca me ||
children.translated_text: may there be devotion to you. Be gracious, Lord, if a boon is to be given to me.'
Having heard the words of great-souled <s>Andhaka</s>, <s>Bhava</s> also,
the greatly radiant one, bestowed rare faith upon the lord of <s>Daityas</s>.

children.text: gāṇapatyaṃ ca daityāya pradadau cāvaropya tam
children.translated_text: He also gave <s>gāṇapatya</s>, lordship among the <s>gaṇas</s>, to the <s>Daitya</s>, after taking him down.
The chief gods and others bowed to him, established in <s>gāṇapatya</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge andhakagāṇapatyātmako nāma trinavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the ninety-third chapter, named 'The Gāṇapatya of <s>Andhaka</s>,' is completed.
The sages said:
How was his father, the terrible <s>Daitya</s> <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,

children.text: viṣṇunā sūdito viṣṇur vārāhatvaṃ kathaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: slain by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and how did <s>Viṣṇu</s> come to be a boar?

children.text: tasya śṛṅgaṃ maheśasya bhūṣaṇatvaṃ kathaṃ gatam
children.translated_text: How did his horn become an ornament of <s>Maheśa</s>?
You ought to tell all this here in detail, <s>Sūta</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The brother of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> is remembered as <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
In ancient times he was the father of <s>Andhaka</s>, lord of demons, and was like Death at the end of time.
Having conquered the gods, that lord of <s>Daityas</s> bound this earth,
carried her to <s>Rasātala</s>, and made the blue-lotus-hued one a prisoner.
Then the gods, with <s>Brahmā</s> among them, their faces withered in splendor,
oppressed, struck, and bound by that <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,
the powerful, cruel, very wicked chief of <s>Daityas</s>,
bowed their heads to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, crusher of crores of <s>Daityas</s>.
They all reported to <s>Hari</s> the binding of the earth.
Hearing of that binding of the earth, the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hari</s>,
became the sacrificial boar, as in the arising of the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: daityaiś ca sārdhaṃ daityendraṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ mahābalam ||
children.translated_text: Together with the <s>Daityas</s>, he attacked the mighty lord of <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
Having slain him with the tip of the point of his tusk, the Lord, destroyer of <s>Daityas</s>, shone forth.
As at the beginnings of kalpas, as before, he entered <s>Rasātala</s>
and, bringing up the goddess Earth, placed her outside upon his lap.
Then the god of gods, the Grandfather, praised the lord of gods,
together with <s>Śakra</s> and the others, in a voice choked with joy:
'Homage to the eternal <s>Varāha</s>, the tusked one, the staff-bearing one;
to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, to the All, to <s>Brahmā</s>, to the supreme Self;

children.text: kartre dhartre dharāyāstu hartre devāriṇāṃ svayam
children.translated_text: to the maker, bearer, and remover of the earth, and himself the remover of the enemies of the gods;

children.text: kartre netre surendrāṇāṃ śāstre ca sakalasya ca ||
children.translated_text: to the maker and leader of the chief gods, and to the ruler of all.'
'You are the eight-formed one; you are the endlessly formed one; you are the primal god, known as endless.

children.text: tvayā kṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ prasīda sureśa lokeśa varāha viṣṇo ||
children.translated_text: All this has been made by you. Be gracious, lord of gods, lord of the world, <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
With one fraction of even half of one part of the foremost point of your single tusk, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: hatāḥ kṣaṇāt kāmada daityamukhyāḥ svadaṃṣṭrakoṭyā saha putrabhṛtyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the chief <s>Daityas</s>, grantor of desires, were slain in an instant by the point of your tusk, together with their sons and servants.

children.text: tvayoddhṛtā deva dharā dhareśa dharādharākāra dhṛtāgradaṃṣṭre
children.translated_text: By you, O god, the earth was lifted up, lord of the earth, mountain-formed one, whose raised tusk is held aloft,
moon-faced one served by mountains, all peoples, oceans, gods, and demons.'

children.text: tvayaiva deveśa vibho kṛtaś ca jayaḥ surāṇāmasureśvarāṇām
children.translated_text: By you alone, O lord of gods, O mighty one, was the victory of the gods over the lords of the Asuras accomplished.

children.text: aho pradattastu varaḥ prasīda vāgdevatā vārijasaṃbhavāya ||
children.translated_text: Ah, the boon has indeed been granted. Be gracious, O deity of speech, to the lotus-born one.

children.text: tava romṇi sakalāmareśvarā nayanadvaye śaśiravī padadvaye
children.translated_text: In your hair are all the lords of the immortals; in your two eyes are the moon and the sun, and in your two feet

children.text: nihitā rasātalagatā vasuṃdharā tava pṛṣṭhataḥ sakalatārakādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is set the earth that had gone down to <s>Rasātala</s>; behind your back are all the stars and the rest.

children.text: jagatāṃ hitāya bhavatā vasuṃdharā bhagavan rasātalapuṭaṃ gatā tadā
children.translated_text: For the welfare of the worlds, O blessed one, when the earth had gone into the hollow of <s>Rasātala</s>,

children.text: abaloddhṛtā ca bhagavaṃstavaiva sakalaṃ tvayaiva hi dhṛtaṃ jagadguro ||
children.translated_text: the helpless one was raised up by you, O blessed one; by you alone the whole universe is upheld, O teacher of the world.
Thus <s>Vākpati</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, having bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the immortals through many praises and acts of worship,
obtained various boons from the mouth of <s>Hari</s>; he himself had a body born from the lotus of <s>Hari</s>'s navel.

children.text: atha tāmuddhṛtāṃ tena dharāṃ devā munīśvarāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the gods and the great sages lifted that earth which had been raised by him
onto their heads and bowed down at that time in the presence of the discus-bearer.
By this very <s>Varāha</s> you have been raised, O giver of boons,
by dark <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose work is unwearied and who has a hundred hands.
O <s>Dharaṇī</s>, you are of great abundance; you are <s>Bhūmi</s>, the inexhaustible cow.

children.text: lokānāṃ dhāriṇī tvaṃ hi mṛttike hara pātakam ||
children.translated_text: You are indeed the bearer of the worlds; O clay, remove sin.
By mind, by deed, and by speech, O boon-giver, O lotus-eyed one,
we live through your grace, with sin destroyed by you.

children.text: ityuktā sā tadā devī dharā devair athābravīt
children.translated_text: Thus addressed then by the gods, that goddess <s>Dharā</s> said:
“O twice-born ones, the clay from the earth split by <s>Varāha</s>'s tusk,
when a man bears it on his head with this mantra, frees him from sin.
He becomes long-lived, strong, fortunate, and endowed with sons and grandsons.

children.text: kramādbhuvi divaṃ prāpya karmānte modate suraiḥ
children.translated_text: In due course, having gained heaven from the earth, at the end of his karma he rejoices with the gods.

children.text: atha deve gate tyaktvā varāhe kṣīrasāgaram ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the god had gone to the milk-ocean, abandoning
the stainless form of <s>Varāha</s>, the earth moved again.
Marked by the weight of the tusk of that wise god of gods,
<s>Bhava</s>, the lord of the world, happened to see it and came there.
Seeing that tusk, he took it for the sake of making it his own ornament.

children.text: dadhāra ca mahādevaḥ kūrcānte vai mahorasi
children.translated_text: And <s>Mahādeva</s> wore it at the end of his crest upon his mighty breast.

children.text: devāś ca tuṣṭuvuḥ sendrā devadevasya vaibhavam ||
children.translated_text: The gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, praised the majesty of the god of gods.
Thus the earth was established by the god of gods in play.
Even at the dissolution of beings, the body of <s>Viṣṇu</s>
and likewise that of <s>Brahmā</s> and of the other gods, through play,
would not adorn the Lord with the division of the all-pervading one's limbs, if the Lord were not adorned by it.
How then could there be liberation for brahmins? Therefore <s>Maheśvara</s> is tusked.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge varāhaprādurbhāvo nāma caturnavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the ninety-fourth chapter, named “The Manifestation of <s>Varāha</s>.”
The sages said:
We have heard that the elder brother of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was formerly killed by <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>.
Tell us how <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was slain by him.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> had a son, renowned as <s>Prahrāda</s>.
He knew <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), was endowed with truth, was ascetic, and was wise.
From birth he worshiped the imperishable lord of gods,
all-knowing, all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the source of the being of all the gods,
that primeval person, with devotion, as the form of the supreme <s>brahman</s>,
the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>, the cause of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
When he saw his son thus absorbed in <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
again and again saying, “Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,” and “O <s>Govinda</s>,”
the enemy of the gods, wicked-minded and as if burning, spoke to him as he praised:
“Do you not know me, fool, the lord of all Daityas and immortals?
O heroic <s>Prahrāda</s>, bad son, cause of suffering to brahmins and gods,

children.text: ko viṣṇuḥ padmajo vāpi śakraś ca varuṇo'thavā ||
children.translated_text: who is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, or the lotus-born one, or <s>Śakra</s>, or <s>Varuṇa</s>?

children.text: vāyuḥ somastatheśānaḥ pāvako mama yaḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: Who are <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and <s>Pāvaka</s>, equal to me?

children.text: māmevārcaya bhaktyā ca svalpaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: Worship me alone with devotion, and always regard <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as slight.

children.text: prahrāda jīvite vāñchā tavaiṣā śṛṇu cāsti cet
children.translated_text: O <s>Prahrāda</s>, if you have any desire for life, listen to this.”
Even after hearing that speech of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, the wise
<s>Prahrāda</s> worshiped, saying, “Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,”
and he taught all the sons of the Daityas, “Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,”
and that most beautiful knowledge of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: durlaṅghyāṃ cātmano dṛṣṭvā śakrādibhir api svayam ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that his command, difficult for even <s>Śakra</s> and the others themselves to transgress,
had been transgressed by his son, <s>Hiraṇya</s> said to the Dānavas:
“You must kill this bad son, fit to be slain by many kinds of execution.”
