Thus ordered then by that very evil-minded Daitya,
they assailed imperishable <s>Prahrāda</s>, the servant of the god of gods.
There, whatever was done against the son of the Daitya king, O best of the twice-born,
became fruitless through the splendor of the lord who lies upon the milk-ocean.
Then the Lord, before <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, whose pride was broken,
appeared right there to kill him, assuming the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>.

children.text: jaghāna ca sutaṃ prekṣya pitaraṃ dānavādhamam
children.translated_text: Seeing the son, he struck down the father, that lowest of Dānavas,
and in that very moment tore him apart with hundreds of sharp claws.
Then, after killing that Daitya together with his kinsmen, the remover of sin
tormented the lord of Daityas like another fire at the end of an age.
By the terrible roars of that <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the world was frightened,

children.text: ā brahmabhuvanād viprāḥ pracacāla ca suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, O brahmins of good vows, it shook as far as the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā surāsuramahoragasiddhasādhyās tasmin kṣaṇe hariviriñcimukhā nṛsiṃham
children.translated_text: Seeing <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> at that moment, the gods, Asuras, great serpents, Siddhas, and Sādhyas, with <s>Hari</s> and <s>Viriñci</s> at their head,

children.text: dhairyaṃ balaṃ ca samavāpya yayurvisṛjya ā diṅmukhāntam asurakṣaṇatatparāś ca ||
children.translated_text: Having regained courage and strength, they went away, released, intent on guarding as far as the openings of the quarters.

children.text: tatastairgataiḥ saiṣa devo nṛsiṃhaḥ sahasrākṛtiḥ sarvapāt sarvabāhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when they had gone, this god <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, of a thousand forms, with feet everywhere and arms everywhere,
thousand-eyed, with moon, sun, and fire as his eyes, stood then, enveloping all things, the master of māyā (cosmic power).

children.text: taṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ suraśreṣṭhā lokā lokācale sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: The best of the gods praised him, while the worlds stood on the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain,
together with <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>.
"You are <s>brahman</s> beyond what is beyond, the truest truth beyond truth;

children.text: jyotiṣāṃ tu paraṃ jyotiḥ paramātmā jaganmayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the supreme light of lights, the supreme self, consisting of the universe.

children.text: sthūlaṃ sūkṣmaṃ susūkṣmaṃ ca śabdabrahmamayaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: You are the gross, the subtle, and the very subtle; auspicious, consisting of <s>śabdabrahman</s> (brahman as sacred sound),
beyond speech, without support, free from duality, free from disturbance.
You are the enjoyer of the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), the embodiment of the <s>yajña</s>, O lord, giver of fruit to sacrificers.
You, having taken the form of a fish, and having assumed the tortoise form, stood in the world;
and having assumed that boar form and this lion form, you have appeared here,
for the protection of the gods, after killing the lord of the sons of <s>Diti</s>.
Through the pretext of a brahmin's curse, you have thus descended in play.

children.text: na dṛṣṭaṃ yattvadanyaṃ hi bhavān sarvaṃ carācaram ||
children.translated_text: Nothing apart from you is seen; you are all that moves and does not move.
You are <s>Viṣṇu</s>; you are <s>Rudra</s>; you alone are the grandsire <s>Brahmā</s>.
You are the beginning; you are the end; you alone are we, O mighty one.
You alone are the whole universe. What need is there of more speech, O lord?
O lord, you are established in many ways through māyā, yet are non-dual.
How shall we praise you, who shine forth, O god of gods, O lord of beasts?
Even though praised by various hymns of praise and by many kinds of dispositions, the lord
did not come to peace, O brahmins, honoring his own birth-form.
Whoever recites the hymn to <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> with devotion, or reflects on its meaning,
or causes all brahmins to hear it, is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tadantare śivaṃ devāḥ sendrāḥ sabrahmakāḥ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: Meanwhile the gods, together with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, approached the lord <s>Śiva</s>,
praised him, and made everything known concerning the one in beast-form.
Then <s>Brahmā</s> and the others quickly praised the supreme lord;
for their own protection they went for refuge to the supreme cause,
the great god dwelling on <s>Mandara</s>, sporting together with <s>Umā</s>,
served by hosts of <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants) and <s>Gandharvas</s>, by <s>Siddhas</s> and groups of <s>Apsarases</s>.
Together with the deities, <s>Brahmā</s>, very much afraid and with a faltering voice,
prostrated like a staff upon the ground and praised the supreme lord.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"Homage to you, death of Time; homage to you, <s>Rudra</s>, to wrath.

children.text: namaḥ śivāya rudrāya śaṅkarāya śivāya te ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>; homage to you as <s>Śiva</s>.
You are fierce toward all beings; you are the controller; you are auspicious for us.
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, remover of distress.
Homage to the maker of delight, to the all-formed one, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Homage to you as <s>Antaka</s>; homage to the husband of <s>Umā</s>.
Homage to the golden-armed one, indeed; homage to the golden lord.
Again and again homage to <s>Śarva</s>, to the one of all forms, to the <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Homage to you who are beyond manifestation as being and non-being, the cause of the great principle;
homage to you who are eternal, of universal form, and yet coming into birth.
Again and again homage to you, born in many ways in the world, abundantly manifested.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to dark-blue <s>Rudra</s>, to the terrible <s>Rudra</s>, to the wise one.
Homage to Time, to the one whose form is Time, to the remover of Time's limbs.
Homage to you, the most bounteous god, the white-throated one.
Homage to you, the greater one, always the slayer of the enemies of the gods.
Again and again homage to the savior, to the good savior, and to the act of carrying across.
Homage to the god <s>Harikeśa</s>, to <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, the supreme self.

children.text: devānāṃ śaṃbhave tubhyaṃ bhūtānāṃ śaṃbhave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you as the benefactor of the gods; homage to the benefactor of beings.
Homage to the benefactor of <s>Haimavatī</s>, and to wrath in the form of <s>Rudra</s>.
Homage to you, matted-haired one; homage to you, black-throated one.
Again and again homage to the golden one, to <s>Maheśa</s>, to the glorious-throated one.
Homage to him whose body is smeared with ash, and to the staff-bearing, shaven-headed lord.
Homage to the short one, to the long one, to the dwarf; again and again homage.

children.text: nama ugratriśūlāya ugrāya ca namo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the fierce trident-bearer, and homage again and again to the fierce one.
Homage to the terrible one, terrible in form, devoted to terrible deeds.

children.text: agrevadhāya vai bhūtvā namo dūrevadhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Homage to you who become the slayer in front, and homage also to the slayer from afar.

children.text: dhanvine śūline tubhyaṃ gadine haline namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to you as bowman, spear-bearer, mace-bearer, and plough-bearer.
Homage always to the discus-bearer, the armored one, the destroyer of the works of the demons.
Homage to the immediate one, immediate in form, to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Homage to <s>Vāma</s>, to the one of gentle form, to the one with a left-side eye.
Homage to you of non-terrible form, to the formidable one, to you whose body is formidable.
Homage indeed to the one in the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>, the one <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> among persons.
Homage to the giver of the aims of life, to the lord, to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
Homage to you as <s>Īśāna</s>; again and again homage to <s>Īśvara</s>.
Homage to <s>Brahmā</s>, to the one whose form is <s>brahman</s>; homage to you who are directly <s>Śiva</s>.
The maker of the universe, wholly <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having assumed the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>,
after himself killing <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> with his sharp claws,
together with many lords of demons, for the welfare of the worlds, O lord,
is bringing together the lion-birth and afflicts the whole universe.
Whatever is to be done here, O lord of gods, do that now, O <s>Bhava</s>.
You are fierce toward all the wicked; you are the controller; you are auspicious for us.
With a body like the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison, protect us who have come for refuge.

children.text: śukraṃ tu vṛttaṃ viśveśa krīḍā vai kevalaṃ vayam
children.translated_text: O lord of all, what has happened is pure sport; we are only the play.
By your opening and closing of the eyes arise our dissolution and creation."

children.text: unmīlayet tvayi brahman vināśo'sti na te śiva
children.translated_text: Even if he should open upon you, O holy one, there is no destruction for you, O <s>Śiva</s>.
We are scorched, O god, by <s>Hari</s> of immeasurable splendor.
For the welfare of all worlds, you truly wish to subdue him.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: vijñāpitas tathā devaḥ prahasanprāha tān surān ||
children.translated_text: Thus petitioned, the god laughed and spoke to those gods.

children.text: abhayaṃ ca dadau teṣāṃ haniṣyāmīti taṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: And the lord gave them fearlessness, saying, "I shall slay him."

children.text: so'pi śakraḥ suraiḥ sārdhaṃ praṇipatya yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s> too, together with the gods, bowed down and went back as he had come.

children.text: jagāma bhagavān brahmā tathānye ca surottamāḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Brahmā</s> went, and so did the other excellent gods.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s> arose and assumed the form of <s>Śarabha</s>.
He went to the border of proud <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the eater of beasts.
Then <s>Śarabha</s>, worshiped by the gods, took away his life-breaths.

children.text: siṃhāttato naro bhūtvā jagāma ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: After that, becoming a man from the lion, he went away in due order.
Thus praised then by the gods, he went away in due order.
Whoever reads or hears this excellent praise of <s>Śarva</s>,
after reaching <s>Rudraloka</s>, rejoices together with <s>Rudra</s>.
Thus, in the venerable great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the first part, the ninety-fifth chapter, concerning <s>Nārasiṃha</s>.
The sages said:
How did the god <s>Mahādeva</s>, the maker of the dissolution of the universe,
assume the very terrible and misshapen form called <s>Śarabha</s>?

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ dhairyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena brūhi sarvam aśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: What deeds of courage were performed by him? Tell everything without remainder.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus entreated by the gods, the abode of compassion formed his intention:
the supreme lord would subdue that fiery power called <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>.
For that purpose <s>Rudra</s> remembered mighty <s>Vīrabhadra</s>,
his own <s>Bhairava</s> form, the maker of the great dissolution.
He came at once, laughing, at the head of the <s>gaṇas</s>.
He was accompanied by the best of the <s>gaṇas</s>, who gave loud laughs and sprang here and there,
and was surrounded by crores of beings in exceedingly fierce <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> forms.
He was surrounded on all sides by so many heroes, dancing and filled with joy,
and by very bold ones playing with <s>Brahmā</s> and the others as if with balls.
Honored by heroes, he was surrounded by others never seen before,
with three flashing eyes like the flames of the fire at the end of an aeon.
He held a weapon and was adorned in his matted crest with a blazing young moon.
He had two sharp sprouting fangs shaped like a pair of young moons.
He had creeper-like brows resembling fragments of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s>'s bow.
He deafened the faces of the quarters with a very fierce roar of huṃ.
His wondrous and terrifying beard was the color of a dark cloud and collyrium.
Again and again he whirled a three-pointed weapon with his two unbroken arms.
The blessed <s>Vīrabhadra</s> too, expanded by heroic power,
himself asked, "What is the reason for remembering me here?"
"Command me, lord of the world; let favor be shown to me."
The blessed lord said:
"An untimely fear has arisen even for the gods, O <s>Bhairava</s>.
That fire of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> is blazing; pacify this unapproachable one.

children.text: sāntvayan bodhayādau taṃ tena kiṃ nopaśāmyati ||
children.translated_text: First soothe him and instruct him. By that, why should he not become calm?
Then display my supreme <s>Bhairava</s> state.

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmeṇa saṃhṛtya sthūlaṃ sthūlena tejasā ||
children.translated_text: Having withdrawn the subtle by subtle power, and the gross by gross fiery power,
bring the face and the hide by my command, O <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
Thus commanded, the chief of the <s>gaṇas</s> assumed a peaceful body.
He went swiftly there, where the man-lion was staying.
Then <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, <s>Hara</s>, awakened <s>Hari</s>.
The lord spoke words like a father to his own legitimate son.
The venerable <s>Vīrabhadra</s> said:
"For the happiness of the world, blessed <s>Mādhava</s>, you have descended.
And you have been appointed by the supreme <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> for the purpose of preservation.
The circle of creatures was protected by the blessed one in the form of <s>Matsya</s>.
In ancient times you bound it merely with your tail while moving about in the single ocean.
You uphold it in the form of <s>Kūrma</s>; by <s>Varāha</s> the earth was raised up.
In this form of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> has been slain.
Again, as <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Bali</s> was bound by you when you strode out.

children.text: tvam eva sarvabhūtānāṃ prabhāvaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ
children.translated_text: You alone are the source of all beings, the imperishable lord.

children.text: yadā yadā hi lokasya duḥkhaṃ kiṃcit prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: Whenever any suffering of the world arises,
then and then, having descended, you will make it free from affliction.
There is none greater than you, nor even anyone equal to you, O <s>Hari</s>, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: tvayā dharmāś ca vedāś ca śubhe mārge pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: By you the <s>dharmas</s> and the Vedas have been established on the auspicious path.
The one for whose sake this descent occurred has been slain, O <s>Keśava</s>.
Your body, O blessed <s>Narasiṃha</s>, is extremely terrible.
Withdraw it yourself, O soul of the universe, here in my presence."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed by <s>Vīrabhadra</s> in a peaceful voice, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>
then, as <s>Hari</s>, kindled an even greater and very terrible anger.
The venerable <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> said:

children.text: āgato'si yatastatra gaccha tvaṃ mā hitaṃ vada
children.translated_text: "Go back to where you came from; do not speak to me of what is beneficial.
Now I shall destroy this whole moving and unmoving universe.

children.text: saṃhartur na hi saṃhāraḥ svato vā parato'pi vā
children.translated_text: For the destroyer there is no destruction, either from himself or from another.

children.text: śāsitaṃ mama sarvatra śāstā ko'pi na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: My command extends everywhere; no ruler over me exists.
By my favor everything proceeds within its bounds.
For I am the activator and restrainer of all powers.

children.text: yad yad vibhūtimat sattvaṃ śrīmadūrjitameva vā
children.translated_text: Whatever being is possessed of majesty, prosperity, or force,
know that, O chief of the <s>gaṇas</s>, to be an expansion of my splendor.
Those who know the supreme truth of the deities know me alone as supreme.
The gods <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and the rest, endowed with power, are portions of me."
Long ago the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s> was born from the lotus-mud of my navel,
and the blessed bull-bannered one arose from his forehead.
The creator is governed by <s>rajas</s> (passion); <s>Rudra</s> is said to be <s>tāmasa</s> (marked by darkness).

children.text: ahaṃ niyantā sarvasya matparaṃ nāsti daivatam ||
children.translated_text: I am the controller of everything; there is no deity higher than me.
I surpass the universe, I am independent, the maker, the destroyer, the lord of all.

children.text: idaṃ tu matparaṃ tejaḥ kaḥ punaḥ śrotumicchati ||
children.translated_text: This splendor is subordinate to me; who again wishes to hear it?

children.text: ato māṃ śaraṇaṃ prāpya gaccha tvaṃ vigatajvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore come to me for refuge, and go, free from feverish distress.
Know this supreme state, O great lord of beings.
I am Time; I am the cause of the destruction of Time, engaged in gathering up the worlds.

children.text: mṛtyormṛtyuṃ viddhi māṃ vīrabhadra jīvantyete matprasādena devāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Know me as the death of death, O <s>Vīrabhadra</s>; these gods live by my favor.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Hearing this speech of <s>Hari</s>, full of self-conceit, the hero of immeasurable valor,
laughed and then spoke contemptuously, his lip quivering.
The glorious <s>Vīrabhadra</s> said:

children.text: kiṃ na jānāsi viśveśaṃ saṃhartāraṃ pinākinam
children.translated_text: Do you not know the lord of the universe, the destroyer, the bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> bow?
False speech, dispute, and ruin alone are present in you.
Which of your mutual incarnations remain now?
By whomever they were made, only the story of them will remain.
Look at your own fault; you have come to such a condition as this.
By him who is skilled in destruction you will come to destruction in an instant.
You are <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), while <s>Rudra</s> is the <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit); potency is deposited in you.
From the lotus of your navel the five-faced grandsire was born.
For the sake of creation, in the beginning of the world, he meditated on <s>Śaṅkara</s>, dark-blue and red,
in his forehead, while he was fixed in fierce austerity.
From the forehead of <s>Śaṃbhu</s> he arose for creation; that is no reproach.
I am a portion of the god of gods, who has the form of <s>Mahābhairava</s>.
I have been appointed to destroy you, both by discipline and by force.

children.text: evaṃ rakṣo vidāryaiva tvaṃ śaktikalayā yutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after tearing apart the demon, you were endowed with only a fraction of power.
Through the arrogance of ego you roar without weariness.
For help given to the wicked serves only as injury.
If, O lion, you think <s>Maheśāna</s> to have come into being again from yourself,

children.text: na tvaṃ sraṣṭā na saṃhartā na svatantro hi kutracit ||
children.translated_text: you are not the creator, not the destroyer, and not independent anywhere.
Like a potter's wheel, you are set in motion by the power of the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>.
Even now your skull, in the form of the tortoise, has been set down
among the garland-vines of <s>Hara</s>; foolish one, why do you not understand?
Have you forgotten how, through a portion of him, you were tormented by the tearing out of your tusk,
when you had the boar-form? And today, crying aloud, by the foe of <s>Tāraka</s>,
you were burned on the tip of his trident, having become one in the guise of <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.
At <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice your head, O one whose form is sacrifice, was cut off by me.

children.text: adyāpi tava putrasya brahmaṇaḥ pañcamaṃ śiraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even now the fifth head of your son <s>Brahmā</s>
was cut off; that connection, that portion of him, and that power of his were cut away.
You were conquered by <s>Dadhīca</s> in battle, together with the host of <s>Rudras</s>.
When your head is being scratched, how have you forgotten that?

children.text: cakraṃ vikramato yasya cakrapāṇe tava priyam ||
children.translated_text: That discus dear to you, O <s>Cakrapāṇi</s>, whose power was it?

children.text: kutaḥ prāptaṃ kṛtaṃ kena tvayā tadapi vismṛtam
children.translated_text: From where was it obtained, and by whom was it made? You have forgotten even that.

children.text: te mayā sakalā lokā gṛhītāstvaṃ payonidhau ||
children.translated_text: All those worlds were seized by me; as for you, in the ocean,

children.text: nidrāparavaśaḥ śeṣe sa kathaṃ sāttviko bhavān
children.translated_text: you lie subject to sleep. How then are you <s>sāttvika</s> (pure in quality)?
From your beginning to the end of the pillar there was the expansion of <s>Rudra</s>'s power.
You were surrounded by power, and you as fire too were deluded.

children.text: tattejaso'pi māhātmyaṃ yuvāṃ draṣṭuṃ na hi kṣamau ||
children.translated_text: You two were not able to behold even the greatness of that radiance.

children.text: sthūlā ye hi prapaśyanti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam
children.translated_text: Those who are gross in understanding see that as <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s supreme abode.
Of heaven and earth, of <s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,
and of the moon in the womb of darkness, <s>Parameśvara</s> is the producer.
You are Time, great Time; <s>Maheśvara</s> is the Time of Time.
Therefore, through a fierce portion, you will become the death of death.

children.text: sthiradhanvā kṣayo vīro vīro viśvādhikaḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the firm-bowed one, destruction, the hero, the hero, the lord who surpasses the universe,
terrible, subduing fever at hand, golden, with beast and bird form.
He is the ruler of the whole world, not you and not the four-faced one.
Having considered all this in this way, destroy yourself by yourself.
Otherwise, right now, from the wrath of the one whose form is <s>Mahābhairava</s>,
death will fall upon you from <s>Sthāṇu</s>, like a thunderbolt and lightning-flash.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed by <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, overwhelmed by anger,
roared with the force of his body and set out to seize him.
At that moment a very terrible form, causing fear to the hostile side,
pervading the sky, unassailable, arisen from Śaiva splendor,
that form of <s>Vīrabhadra</s> was seen immediately.

children.text: na taddhiraṇmayaṃ saumyaṃ na sauraṃ nāgnisaṃbhavam
children.translated_text: It was not golden, not gentle, not solar, and not born of fire;
it was not like lightning or the moon, but incomparable and belonging to <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tadā tejāṃsi sarvāṇi tasmin līnāni śāṅkare
children.translated_text: Then all splendors were absorbed into that form of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Thereupon, when the manifest form had arisen, a great radiance became visible.
It bore marks common to <s>Rudra</s> and had a distorted shape.
Then <s>Parameśvara</s> was clearly manifest in the form of destruction,
as all the gods looked on, amid auspicious cries of victory and the rest.
He had a thousand arms, matted hair, and a crest adorned with the half-moon.
With a half-animal body, with wings and a beak, O twice-born ones,
he had very sharp great fangs and claws like thunderbolts as weapons.
Black at the throat, mighty-armed, four-footed, and born of fire,
he had a terrifying, deep roar like a cloud risen at the end of an age.
At once, with the fire of anger in his conduct and his three eyes rolled back,
<s>Hara</s>, with his fangs clearly visible and his lower lip exposed, uttered a roar of huṃ.
By the very sight of him, <s>Hari</s> lost his strength and valor;
he bore the appearance of a firefly beneath the thousand-rayed sun.
Then, whirling with his two wings, he tore upward at his navel and feet;
binding his feet with his tail and encircling his arms with his own arms,
<s>Hara</s>, splitting his chest with his arms, seized <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: tato jagāma gaganaṃ devaiḥ saha maharṣibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he went into the sky together with the gods and the great seers.
All at once, from fear, he took up <s>Viṣṇu</s> as a bird takes up a serpent;

children.text: utkṣipyotkṣipya saṃgṛhya nipātya ca nipātya ca ||
children.translated_text: lifting him up again and again, grasping him, and dashing him down again and again.
Flying up again and again, the Blessed Lord stunned <s>Hari</s> with the blows of his wings.
The gods all followed that lord, the bull, the lord of the universe, as he carried <s>Hari</s>,
and they praised him with words of homage.
<s>Hari</s>, being led away, was overpowered, with a wretched face and joined palms;
with graceful syllables he praised that supreme lord.
<s>Śrīnṛsiṃha</s> said:
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to the great devourer, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: nama ugrāya bhīmāya namaḥ krodhāya manyave
children.translated_text: Homage to the fierce one, to the terrible one; homage to wrath and fury.

children.text: namo bhavāya śarvāya śaṅkarāya śivāya te ||
children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Bhava</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>; homage to you as <s>Śiva</s>.
Homage to the death of Time, to Time, to great Time, and to Death.
Homage to the hero, to <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, to the destroyer of heroes, to the trident-bearer.
Homage to the great god, the great one, the lord of creatures.
Homage to the single one, the blue-throated one, the fair-throated one, the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>.
Homage to the endless and subtle one; homage to you, wrath of death.
Homage to the transcendent one, the supreme lord, to you who are higher than the highest.
Homage to the one beyond the highest, to the all, to you whose form is the universe.
Homage to the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to the field of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to the radiant one.
Homage to the fisherman, the mountain hunter, the great huntsman, the eternal one.
Homage to <s>Bhairava</s>, the refuge, the one whose form is great <s>Bhairava</s>.
Homage to the destroyer of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the enemy of <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, and <s>Pura</s>.
Homage to the destroyer of the great flood of bonds, the maker of the end of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s māyā.
Homage to the three-eyed one, the three-syllabled one, to <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, to the bountiful one.
Homage to the conqueror of death, to <s>Śarva</s>, to the all-knowing one, the enemy of sacrifice.
Homage to the lord of sacrifice, the most excellent one; homage to you whose form is fire.
Homage to the great nose, to the tongue, to the mover of breath and downward breath.
Homage to the one of three qualities, to the trident, to the yogin beyond the qualities.
Homage to saṃsāra, to the current, to the one who sets the great machine in motion.
Homage to the moon, fire, and sun, to the cause of manifold liberation.
Homage to the boon-giver, to the avatāra, to the cause of every cause.
Homage to the skull-bearer, the dreadful one, the lord of blessed fame.
Homage to the unfailing one, the fire-eyed one, to <s>Lakulīśa</s>, to <s>Śaṃbhu</s>.
Homage to the supreme physician, the shaven-headed one, the staff-bearer, whose form is yoga.
Homage to the god whose vehicle is the cloud, to the husband of <s>Pārvatī</s>.
Homage to the unmanifest one, free from sorrow, firm, and firm-bowed.
Homage to <s>Sthāṇu</s>, the hide-clad one, the cause of the five objects.
Homage to the boon-giver, the one-footed one; homage to the one whose crest bears the half-moon.
Homage to you, king of sacrifice; homage to the lord of birds.
Homage to the lord of yogins, the eternal, the true one, the supreme-standing one.
Homage to you, the self of all; homage to you, the lord of all.
May there be homage and homage to you once, twice, three, four, and five times.
And homage and homage to you ten times and a thousand times.
Having made homage without measure, homage and homage to you infinite times.
Homage, homage, and homage again; again and again, homage and homage.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having praised him in this way with an eight-hundred-name hymn made of nectar,
<s>Nṛsiṃha</s> again petitioned <s>Śarabheśvara</s>.
Whenever my ignorance is stained by excessive ego,
then, each time, it must be removed by you alone, O supreme lord.
Thus the man-lion, pleased, made his request to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Surely you are powerless, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, defeated to the very end of life.
Having reduced the whole body to only what remained at that mouth,
then <s>Vīrabhadra</s> in an instant made that limb shell-white, as the text stands.
The gods said:

children.text: atha brahmādayaḥ sarve vīrabhadra tvayā dṛśā
children.translated_text: Now, O <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, through you and through your sight, all of us beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>

children.text: jīvitāḥ smo vayaṃ devāḥ parjanyeneva pādapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: have been brought back to life, we gods, like trees by rain-clouds.

children.text: yasya bhīṣā dahatyagnir udeti ca raviḥ svayam
children.translated_text: From fear of him fire burns, and the sun rises by itself;

children.text: vāto vāti ca so 'si tvaṃ mṛtyurdhāvati pañcamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wind blows, and Death runs as the fifth: that one are you.
That unmanifest supreme sky, beyond the kalās, the eternal <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
O Blessed One, the speakers about brahman call you alone <s>Bhava</s>.
Who are we, O supreme lord, to know the elements and understanding?
We do not know the supreme abode through descriptions of form and beauty.
In all calamities protect us, O lord of the <s>gaṇas</s>.
The Blessed <s>Hara</s>, the elevenfold self, abides as one who has form.
Having seen such many avatāras of yours, O <s>Śiva</s>, and such darkness,
may we never at any time fall into doubt, for our thought is fixed on you in that way.
Your forms, whether as small as a guñjā berry or as vast as the slopes of great mountains, are everywhere.

children.text: abhyasaṃhara gamyaṃ te na nītavyaṃ parāparā ||
children.translated_text: Withdraw them together; what is to be reached is yours, and the higher and lower should not be led away.

children.text: dve tanū tava rudrasya vedajñā brāhmaṇā viduḥ
children.translated_text: Veda-knowing brahmins know two bodies of your <s>Rudra</s>:
one is terrible and another auspicious, and each of them is manifold.
Protect us here, O Blessed One, you of ever-unbroken great power.

children.text: bhavatā hi jagatsarvaṃ vyāptaṃ svenaiva tejasā ||
children.translated_text: For the whole world is pervaded by you with your own radiance.
We, the chief gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the moon,
and all gods and asuras, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, have been brought forth from you.

children.text: brahmā ca indro viṣṇuś ca yamādyā na surāsurān
children.translated_text: neither <s>Brahmā</s>, nor <s>Indra</s>, nor <s>Viṣṇu</s>, nor <s>Yama</s> and the others among the gods and Asuras...

children.text: tato nigṛhya ca hariṃ siṃha ity upacetasam ||
children.translated_text: Then, having subdued <s>Hari</s>, the lion, the one of heightened awareness...
Since you bear the whole universe, dividing your body eightfold,

children.text: ato 'smān pāhi bhagavan surān dānair abhīpsitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore protect us gods, Blessed Lord, with the desired boons.

children.text: uvāca tān surāndevo maharṣīṃś ca purātanān
children.translated_text: The god spoke to those gods and to the ancient great seers:

children.text: yathā jale jalaṃ kṣiptaṃ kṣīraṃ kṣīre ghṛtaṃ ghṛte ||
children.translated_text: "Just as water cast into water, milk into milk, and ghee into ghee,

children.text: eka eva tadā viṣṇuḥ śivalīno na cānyathā
children.translated_text: so at that time <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone was merged in <s>Śiva</s>, and not otherwise.

children.text: eṣa eva nṛsiṃhātmā sadarpaś ca mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This very one, whose self is <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, is proud and very powerful.
The man-lion has set himself in motion with the purpose of destroying the world.
He should be worshiped with the salutation 'homage to him' by those who desire success in devotion to me."
Having said only this, the blessed, very powerful <s>Vīrabhadra</s>,
became invisible to all beings and disappeared right there.
From that time onward <s>Śaṅkara</s> has worn the hide of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>,
and that face was set as the chief one in his garland of severed heads.
Then the gods, free from fear and praising this tale,
their eyes opened wide with wonder, all went back as they had come.

children.text: ya idaṃ paramākhyānaṃ puṇyaṃ vedaiḥ samanvitam
children.translated_text: Whoever recites this supreme, holy narrative, joined with the Vedas,
and also hears it after reciting it, finds it the destroyer of all suffering.
It brings blessedness, fame, long life, health, and increase of nourishment;
it pacifies all obstacles and destroys all diseases.
It pacifies untimely death; it is auspicious and brings great peace.
It pacifies circles of enemies and destroys every affliction.
It then pacifies bad dreams and wards off all beings;
it destroys poison and seizures by spirits, and increases sons, grandsons, and the like.
It grants yogic accomplishment properly and makes the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> shine forth.
It is a staircase to the world of <s>Śeṣa</s> and the single means for gaining what is desired.
It dispels the illusion of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and gives the supreme truth concerning the deities.
It grants fulfillment of wishes and is the means to prosperity, wisdom, and the rest.

children.text: idaṃ tu śarabhākāraṃ paraṃ rūpaṃ pinākinaḥ
children.translated_text: This supreme form of <s>Pinākin</s>, the form of <s>Śarabha</s>,
is to be revealed among devotees and among those who have long made effort.

children.text: taireva paṭhitavyaṃ ca śrotavyaṃ ca śivātmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: By those alone, whose selves are devoted to <s>Śiva</s>, it is to be recited and heard,
at all festivals of <s>Śiva</s>, and on the fourteenth and eighth lunar days.
One should recite it at times of consecration, as a cause for the presence of <s>Śiva</s>,
and amid fears caused by thieves, tigers, snakes, lions, deadly foes, and kings.
Also amid other portents, earthquakes, forest fires, and rains of dust,
at the falling of meteors, in great winds, in drought, and in excessive rain.
Therefore there a learned man, a devotee of <s>Śiva</s> firm in his vow, should recite it.
Whoever recites or even hears this praise, unsurpassed among all,
attains the state of <s>Rudra</s> and becomes an attendant of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śarabhaprādurbhāvo nāma ṣaṇṇavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninety-sixth chapter, called "The Manifestation of <s>Śarabha</s>," in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The seers said:
How did the matted-haired one formerly slay <s>Jalandhara</s>, whose valor was like that of the enemy of <s>Jambha</s>?
How did the blessed lord <s>Hara</s>, remover of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye, kill him?
You should tell us this, O well-vowed <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
There was one known as <s>Jalandhara</s>, born from the circle of waters.
He resembled <s>Antaka</s> and had gained might through austerity.
By him the gods, together with <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: nirjitāḥ samare sarve brahmā ca bhagavānajaḥ
children.translated_text: and also the blessed unborn <s>Brahmā</s>, were all conquered in battle.
After conquering the multitude of gods and <s>Brahmā</s>,
<s>Jalandhara</s> went to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the gods, guru and taker of the universe.
Between those two there arose a battle, day and night, without rest.
By that <s>Jalandhara</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s> was defeated.
And <s>Jalandhara</s>, having conquered that god of gods <s>Janārdana</s>,
spoke these words to the sons of <s>Diti</s>, resolved by policy to conquer <s>Īśvara</s>:

children.text: sarve jitā mayā yuddhe śaṅkaro hyajito raṇe ||
children.translated_text: "All have been conquered by me in battle; only <s>Śaṅkara</s> remains unconquered in war.

children.text: taṃ jitvā sarvamīśānaṃ gaṇapair nandinā kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Having conquered that all-powerful <s>Īśāna</s> in an instant, together with the <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants) and <s>Nandin</s>,

children.text: ahameva bhavatvaṃ ca brahmatvaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: I alone will give you the state of <s>Bhava</s>, and also the state of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and the state of <s>Vāsava</s>, O foremost <s>Dānavas</s>."
Hearing the words of <s>Jalandhara</s>, all those lowest <s>Dānavas</s>,
most wicked and intent on seeing death, roared loudly.
With these <s>Daityas</s> and with others, with chariots, elephants, and horses,

children.text: saṃnaddhaiḥ saha saṃnahya śarvaṃ prati yayau balī
children.translated_text: armed and arrayed together, the mighty one marched against <s>Śarva</s>.
<s>Bhava</s> too, seeing the lord of <s>Daityas</s> standing like a peak of <s>Meru</s>,
and hearing from others of his invulnerability, the destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye,

children.text: brahmaṇo vacanaṃ rakṣan rakṣako jagatāṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: protecting the word of <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord and protector of the worlds,
together with <s>Ambā</s>, with <s>Nandin</s>, and with his <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants), said as if smiling:
"What need is there now of this battle, O lord of Asuras?
With all your limbs split by my arrows, you rise up gladly to die."
<s>Jalandhara</s> too, hearing that ear-splitting speech,
lord of the power of the anti-gods, spoke this to the lord of the gods:
"Enough of words, great-armed god of gods, bull-bannered one.
O <s>Hara</s>, I have come here to fight with weapons like rays of the moon."
Hearing his words, the trident-bearer, playfully with his big toe,
quickly made in the great waters a discus, a fierce weapon.

children.text: kṛtvārṇavāṃbhasi sitaṃ bhagavān rathāṅgaṃ smṛtvā jagattrayamanena hatāḥ surāś ca
children.translated_text: Having made the bright discus in the waters of the ocean, the blessed lord remembered the three worlds and the gods struck down by it;
the destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Andhaka</s>, the three cities, and the sacrifice, maker of the end of the three worlds, then laughed and spoke.
O Daitya <s>Jalandhara</s>, this was made with my foot in the great ocean;

children.text: balavān yadi coddhartuṃ tiṣṭha yoddhuṃ na cānyathā ||
children.translated_text: if you are strong enough to lift it, then stand and fight, and not otherwise.
Hearing those words of his, his eyes blazing with anger,
as if burning the three worlds with his eyes, he looked around and spoke.
<s>Jalandhara</s> said:

children.text: gadāmuddhṛtya hatvā ca nandinaṃ tvāṃ ca śaṅkara
children.translated_text: "Having lifted my mace, and having killed <s>Nandin</s> and you too, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: hatvā lokānsuraiḥ sārdhaṃ ḍuṇḍubhān garuḍo yathā ||
children.translated_text: having killed the worlds together with the gods, as <s>Garuḍa</s> kills the <s>Ḍuṇḍubhas</s>,
I am able to destroy all moving and unmoving beings, together with <s>Vāsava</s>.
O <s>Maheśvara</s>, who in the three worlds cannot be cut down by my arrows?
Even as a child the blessed lord was conquered by my ascetic power;

children.text: brahmā balī yauvane vai munayaḥ surapuṅgavaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: powerful <s>Brahmā</s> was conquered in youth, and the sages along with the foremost gods.
In a moment the entire triple world, with its moving and unmoving beings, was burned

children.text: tapasā kiṃ tvayā rudra nirjito bhagavānapi ||
children.translated_text: by ascetic power. What then of you, O <s>Rudra</s>? Even the blessed lord was conquered.
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Vitteśa</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Vārīśvara</s>, and the others

children.text: na sehire yathā nāgā gandhaṃ pakṣipateriva ||
children.translated_text: could not endure me, just as serpents cannot endure the scent of the lord of birds.

children.text: na labdhvā divi bhūmau ca bāhavo mama śaṅkara
children.translated_text: Finding no scope in heaven or on earth, my arms, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
reached all the mountains and were rubbed against them, O lord of <s>gaṇas</s>.
The glorious chief mountain <s>Mandara</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and splendid <s>Meru</s>
fell when rubbed by my club-like arm for the purpose of relieving an itch.
The <s>Gaṅgā</s> was dammed by my arms, merely in sport, on <s>Himavat</s> mountain,

children.text: nārīṇāṃ mama bhṛtyaiś ca vajro baddho divaukasām ||
children.translated_text: and the thunderbolt of the heaven-dwellers was bound by my servants for the women.

children.text: vaḍavāyā mukhaṃ bhagnaṃ gṛhītvā vai kareṇa tu
children.translated_text: I broke the mouth of <s>Vaḍavā</s> after seizing it in my hand,
and at that very instant this entire world became one ocean.
The elephants headed by <s>Airāvata</s> were hurled upon the waters of the ocean,
and blessed <s>Indra</s>, together with his chariot, was hurled a hundred yojanas away.
Even <s>Garuḍa</s>, together with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, was bound by me with a serpent-noose.
The women beginning with <s>Urvaśī</s> were taken by me into prison.
Only somehow did <s>Śakra</s> obtain <s>Śacī</s> alone, after bowing down to me.
Do you not know me, the Daitya lord <s>Jalandhara</s>, O <s>Umāpati</s>?"
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed, <s>Mahādeva</s> then burned his chariot
with only a half of a half of a portion of the fire of his eye, throwing it into ruin.

children.text: daityānāmatulabalairhayaiś ca nāgair daityendrās tripuraripor nirīkṣaṇena
children.translated_text: By the glance of the foe of <s>Tripura</s>, the lords of the Daityas, with their horses and elephants of incomparable strength, were stricken;

children.text: nāgād vaiśasam anusaṃvṛtaś ca nāgairdeveśaṃ vacanamuvāca cālpabuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the dull-witted one, hemmed in amid violence from the elephants and by the elephants, spoke these words to the lord of gods.

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ mama yudhi devadaityasaṃghairhantuṃ yatsakalamidaṃ kṣaṇātsamarthaḥ
children.translated_text: "What use have I in battle for hosts of gods and Daityas, when I am able to destroy all this in a moment?

children.text: yattasmādbhayamihanāsti yoddhum īśa vāñchaiṣā vipulatarā na saṃśayo'tra ||
children.translated_text: Since there is no fear here from that, O Lord, my desire to fight is very great; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: tasmāttvaṃ mama madanāridakṣaśatro yajñāre tripuraripo mamaiva vīraiḥ
children.translated_text: Therefore you, O enemy of <s>Madana</s>, foe of <s>Dakṣa</s>, enemy of the sacrifice, foe of <s>Tripura</s>, with my own heroes,

children.text: bhūtendrairharivadanena devasaṃghairyoddhuṃ te balamiha cāsti ceddhi tiṣṭha ||
children.translated_text: with the lords of beings, with the <s>Hari</s>-faced one, and with the hosts of gods, if you have strength to fight here, then stand."
Having thus addressed <s>Mahādeva</s>, the delighter of <s>Mahādeva</s>'s enemies
did not move and did not remember his kinsmen slain in battle.
Arrogant with pride and undisciplined in spirit, he slapped his arms with the strength of his arms,
and set himself to kill with that discus named <s>Sudarśana</s>.
With the irresistible wheel, even though with difficulty, O best of Brahmins,

children.text: sthāpayāmāsa vai skandhe dvidhābhūtaś ca tena vai ||
children.translated_text: he placed it on his shoulder, and by that very wheel he was split in two.

children.text: kuliśena yathā chinno dvidhā girivaro dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: Like a great mountain split in two by a thunderbolt, O Brahmins,
the powerful Daitya fell like another <s>Añjana</s> mountain.
With his terrible blood, in a moment, everything was filled;
and all that blood, by <s>Rudra</s>'s command, became flesh as well.
Having reached <s>Mahāraurava</s>, it became a pool of blood. Ah!
Seeing <s>Jalandhara</s> slain, the gods, Gandharvas, and attendants
made a great lion-roar and said, "Well done, O god!"
Whoever reads or hears of the crushing of <s>Jalandhara</s>,
or recites it duly, obtains <s>gāṇapatya</s> (the state of belonging to Gaṇapati's hosts).

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge jalandharavadho nāma saptanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninety-seventh chapter, named "The Slaying of <s>Jalandhara</s>," in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
How, O <s>Sūta</s>, was the discus named <s>Sudarśana</s> obtained by the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>
from <s>Maheśvara</s>, the god of gods? You ought to tell us.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
A very terrible conflict arose between the gods and the lords of the Asuras,
a great one that brought about the destruction of all beings.
Those gods, pierced by spears, clubs, arrows with bent joints,
and lances, fled, bewildered with fear.
Then the defeated gods bowed to <s>Hari</s>, the lord of the lord of gods,
that lord of the gods, their minds shaken with grief.
Then the blessed <s>Hari</s>, lord of the lord of gods, seeing those gods
standing there after bowing down, spoke these words:
"Children, why, O gods, have you come here with your ornaments and valor fallen away,
together with distress? You should speak, O you of good vows."
Hearing those words of his, the best of the gods, in such a condition,
bowed down and told <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god of gods, what had happened:
"Blessed lord, lord of gods, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O victorious <s>Janārdana</s>,
we have all been oppressed by the Dānavas and have come to you for refuge.
You alone, O lord of gods, are our refuge, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

children.text: tvameva paramātmā hi tvaṃ pitā jagatāmapi ||
children.translated_text: You alone are the supreme self, and you are the father even of the worlds.

children.text: tvameva bhartā hartā ca bhoktā dātā janārdana
children.translated_text: You alone are the sustainer, destroyer, enjoyer, and giver, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
Therefore you ought to slay the Dānavas, O crusher of Dānavas."
And the <s>Daityas</s>, by the Vaiṣṇava, Brāhma, Raudra, and Yāmya missiles, very terrible,
and by the Kaubera, Saumya, Nairṛtya, and firm Vāruṇa weapons,

children.text: vāyavyaiś ca tathāgneyair aiśānair vārṣikaiḥ śubhaiḥ
children.translated_text: and likewise by the Vāyavya, Agneya, Aiśāna, and auspicious Vārṣika ones,

children.text: saurai raudrais tathā bhīmaiḥ kampanair jṛmbhaṇair dṛḍhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: by the Saura and Raudra weapons, and by the fearsome, firm Kampana and Jṛmbhaṇa missiles,
are all invulnerable because of the boon they obtained, O lotus-eyed one.
Your raised discus, born from the orb of the sun,
has indeed been blunted by <s>Dadhīca</s> and by <s>Cyāvana</s>, O teacher of the world.

children.text: daṇḍaṃ śārṅgaṃ tavāstraṃ ca labdhaṃ daityaiḥ prasādataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Your staff, your <s>Śārṅga</s> bow, and your weapon have been obtained by the demons through favor.
Long ago, to kill <s>Jalandhara</s>, a terrible, well-sharpened discus

children.text: rathāṅgaṃ suśitaṃ ghoraṃ tena tān hantum arhasi ||
children.translated_text: was fashioned by the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>; with that you ought to kill them.
Therefore they must be slain by that, and not even by hundreds of other weapons.

children.text: tato niśamya teṣāṃ vai vacanaṃ vārijekṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having heard their words, the lotus-eyed one
<s>Hari</s> himself, bearer of the discus, spoke to those headed by <s>Vācaspati</s>.
<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> said:

children.text: bhobho devā mahādevaṃ sarvair devaiḥ sanātanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: O gods, reaching <s>Mahādeva</s> now together with all the eternal gods,
I shall accomplish everything for the dwellers in heaven.

children.text: devā jalandharaṃ hantuṃ nirmitaṃ hi purāriṇā ||
children.translated_text: O gods, to kill <s>Jalandhara</s> it was indeed made by the foe of <s>Pura</s>.

children.text: labdhvā rathāṅgaṃ tenaiva nihatya ca mahāsurān
children.translated_text: Having obtained that very discus and having slain the great asuras with it,
all the <s>Daityas</s> headed by <s>Dhundhu</s>, sixty-eight hundreds of them, O gods,
together with their kinsmen, I shall deliver you in a single moment.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having thus spoken to the best of the gods, and remembering the best of gods,
that most excellent one then worshiped the excellent <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Having duly established a liṅga on an auspicious peak of <s>Himavat</s>,
like Mount <s>Meru</s>, fashioned by <s>Viśvakarman</s>,
<s>Janārdana</s>, with the Rudra called <s>Tvarita</s> and with the Raudra rite,
bathed and worshiped that delightful flame-shaped liṅga with perfumes and the like.

children.text: tuṣṭāva ca tadā rudraṃ sampūjyāgnau praṇamya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then, after worshiping in the fire and bowing down, he praised <s>Rudra</s>,
the god, with the thousand names beginning with <s>Bhava</s>, in due order.
He worshiped <s>Śiva</s>, beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ,
the god <s>Maheśvara</s>, with the thousand names beginning with <s>Bhava</s>.
For each name he worshiped <s>Śaṅkara</s> with a lotus.

children.text: agnau ca nāmabhir devaṃ bhavādyaiḥ samidādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: And in the fire, with the names beginning with <s>Bhava</s>, with fuel-sticks and the like,
ending each with svāhā, he duly offered ten thousand oblations to the lord for each one.
Then again he praised <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, the lord, with the names beginning with <s>Bhava</s>.
<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> said:

children.text: bhavaḥ śivo haro rudraḥ puruṣaḥ padmalocanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the Person, the lotus-eyed one;
he is the one to be entreated, of good conduct, all-auspicious, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He is the Lord, the pillar-like one, <s>Īśāna</s>, thousand-eyed and thousand-footed;
the greater one, the boon-giver, the venerable one, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Parameśvara</s>.
He bears the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and the trident; his single purpose is the good of others.
He is all-knowing, the first of all gods, mountain-bowed, and matted-haired.
He wears the moon as his crest, has the moon on his head, is wise, and is lord of the gods of the universe.
He is the collected essence of the <s>Vedānta</s>, the skull-bearer, blue and red.
He is the basis of meditation, beyond delimitation, husband of <s>Gaurī</s>, and lord of the gaṇas.
He has eight forms and universal form; he is the three aims of life and the means to heaven.
He is reached through knowledge, firm in wisdom, the god of gods, and three-eyed.
He is <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, pale, very steadfast, and firm.
He is of universal form, odd-eyed, lord of speech, pure and inward.
He responds to every devotion; he has the bull as his mark and the bull as his vehicle.
He is the Lord, bearer of <s>Pināka</s>, bearer of the skull-staff, wondrously clad and ancient.
He removes darkness; he is the great yogin, protector, remover of <s>Brahmā</s>'s limb, and matted-haired.
He is the time of Time, clad in a hide, gracious, and whose nature is the praṇava.
He wears the guise of a madman, is pleasing to the sight, is <s>Durvāsas</s>, and is the chastiser of <s>Smara</s>.
He has a firm weapon, is the teacher of <s>Skanda</s>, the supreme-standing one, and the highest refuge.
He has no beginning, middle, or end; he is lord of the mountain and kinsman of the mountain.
He is friend of <s>Kubera</s>, blue-throated, and the highest of the highest classes of beings.
He is the common god, bow-bearing, blue-throated, and axe-bearing.
He is wide-eyed, the hunter of beasts, lord of the gods, and scorcher like the sun.
He is incapable of unrighteous action, the sacred field, the blessed one, and the breaker of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye.
He is fierce, lord of beasts, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, dear to devotees and sweet-spoken.
He is giver, compassionate, skillful, wearing matted hair, and chastiser of desire.
He dwells in the cremation ground, is subtle, stands in the cremation ground, and is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He is maker of the world, lord of beings, great maker, and great remedy.
He is higher, lord of cows, protector, attainable by knowledge, and ancient.

children.text: nītiḥ sunītiḥ śuddhātmā somaḥ somarataḥ sukhī
children.translated_text: He is rule, good rule, pure-souled, <s>Soma</s>, delighting in <s>Soma</s>, and happy.
He drinks <s>Soma</s>, drinks nectar, is <s>Soma</s>, of great guidance and great intelligence.
He has no born enemy, is light, worthy of honor, and the carrier of oblations.
He is maker of the world, maker of the Veda, maker of the sūtras, and eternal.
He is a great seer, <s>Kapila</s> the teacher, the light of the universe, and three-eyed.
He holds <s>Pināka</s> in his hand, is divine upon earth, giver of well-being, and always maker of well-being.
He has three abodes, is fortunate, <s>Śarva</s>, all-knowing, and moving everywhere.

children.text: brahmadhṛg viśvasṛk svargaḥ karṇikāraḥ priyaḥ kaviḥ ||
children.translated_text: He upholds <s>Brahmā</s>, creates the universe, is heaven, the karṇikāra tree, beloved, and a poet.

children.text: śākho viśākho gośākhaḥ śivo naikaḥ kratuḥ samaḥ
children.translated_text: He is <s>Śākha</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, <s>Gośākha</s>, auspicious, manifold, sacrifice, and equal.
He is the water of the flood of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, being, whole, the master-builder, and firm.
He has conquered himself, has his self under control, and is charioteer of the vehicle of beings.
He is attended by his gaṇa, performs the work of the gaṇas, is of good fame, and has cut away doubt.
He is <s>Kāmadeva</s>, protector of desire, and has a body dusted with ashes.
He loves ashes, lies upon ashes, is desirous, beloved, and maker of the āgama (sacred tradition).
He is fully joined, inwardly withdrawn, united with <s>dharma</s> (normative order), and <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
He is four-faced and four-armed, hard to dwell with and hard to approach.
He is difficult to reach, hard to obtain, a fortress, and skilled in every weapon.
He is the abode of the yoga of the self, the good thread, and the increaser of the thread.
He has auspicious limbs, has the worlds as his limbs, is lord of the universe, and feeds on immortality.
He purifies with ashes; he is <s>Meru</s>, vigorous, and of pure form.
He is golden-seeded, the sun, a ray, and the abode of greatness.
He is the great lake, the great womb, and is revered by hosts of perfected beings.
He wears a tiger skin, is serpent-like, a great being, and a great treasure.
He has immortal limbs and an immortal body; he is the five sacrifices and the wind.
He knows the twenty-five principles; he is the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree and both the far and the near.
He is easy to obtain, excellent in vows, heroic, and the sole treasure of speech and scripture.
He is guru of the orders and life-stages, marked by social order, conqueror of enemies, and tormentor of enemies.
He is the hermitage, the emaciating ascetic, lean, possessed of knowledge, and both unmoving and moving.
He is the standard of proof, hard to know, <s>Suparṇa</s>, and borne by the wind.
He bears the bow; he is the science of archery, the mass of qualities, and the mine of qualities.
He has endless vision; he is bliss, the staff, the subduer, and restraint.
He is worthy of reverence, the great teacher, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, and skilled.
He is free from passion, disciplined in self, ascetic, and producer of beings.
He wears the guise of a madman, is hidden, has conquered desire, and has conquered what is dear.
His nature is auspicious; he is a cosmic age and the lord of creatures in all worlds.
He is ascetic, the deliverer, wise, the lord of primordial nature, and imperishable.
He is guardian of the world, hidden in self, the beginning of the aeon, and lotus-eyed.
He knows the true meaning of the Vedas and śāstras; he is rule and the support of rule.
He is the moon, the sun, <s>Śani</s>, and <s>Ketu</s>; he is cessation and coral-hued.
He is reached through devotion; he is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the offerer of the deer-arrow, and stainless.
His abode is the king of mountains; he is beloved, the supreme self, and guru of the world.
He performs every act, is immovable, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, auspicious, and surrounded by auspiciousness.
He has great austerity and long austerity; he is the most massive, ancient, and firm.

children.text: ahaḥ saṃvatsaro vyāptiḥ pramāṇaṃ paramaṃ tapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the day, the year, pervasion, measure, and supreme austerity.
He makes the year; he is mantra, certainty, and the vision of all.
He is unborn, lord of all, gentle, great-seeded, and very strong.

children.text: yogī yogyo mahāretāḥ siddhaḥ sarvādir agnidaḥ
children.translated_text: He is a yogin, fit for yoga, great-seeded, perfected, beginning of all, and giver of fire.
He is a Vasu, rich in wealth, true, remover of all sin, and <s>Hara</s>.
He is immortal, eternal, peaceful, arrow in hand, and majestic.
He carries a water-pot and a bow; he is the Vedāṅga, a knower of the Veda, and a sage.
He is shining, food, the eater, leader of the world, and hard to restrain.
He is beyond the senses, possessed of great māyā, the dwelling of all, and the crossroads.
He is joined with time, of great sound, of great energy, and of great strength.
He has great intelligence and great valor; he moves among beings and is destroyer of cities.
He moves by night, moves among spirits, has great power, and has great splendor.
His body cannot be defined; he is glorious, irresistible to all, and of immeasurable course.
He is much learned, made of many forms, self-controlled, and source of existence.
He makes vigor, brilliance, and radiance; he is dancer and fulfiller of all desires.
He loves dance, is dance and dancer, whose self is light, and who gives heat.
He is the mantra whose syllables are clearly awakened, honor itself, and the flood of essence.
He makes the beginning of an age, turns the age, is deep, and rides the bull.

children.text: iṣṭo viśiṣṭaḥ śiṣṭeṣṭaḥ śarabhaḥ śarabho dhanuḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is desired, distinguished, desired by the disciplined, <s>Śarabha</s>, the śarabha, and the bow.
He is the ocean, the foundation, victory, and the knower of the time of victory.
He is established, knows valid measure, wears a golden cuirass, and is <s>Hari</s>.
He is shining, the host of gods, lord of knowledge, and refuge of the wise gods.
He has the form of a child, crushes strength, is transformation, deep, and guru.
He is the instrument, the cause, the doer, and the liberator from every bond.
He is the most learned, free from fear, bearer of the universe, and maker of night.
He is resolve, establishment, giver of place, and born at the beginning of the world.
He is the war-drum, graceful, the universe, and the self of becoming established in the self.
He is lord of heroes, <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, slayer of heroes, supporter of heroes, and sovereign.
He is the crest-jewel of heroes, the knower, of piercing sound, and holder of rivers.
He bears command, carries the trident, is <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, and the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.
He is a <s>Vālakhilya</s>, bearer of the great bow, sharp-rayed, and imperishable treasure.
He is delightful, a good refuge, <s>Subrahmaṇya</s>, and lord of nectar.
He is <s>Maghavan</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, possessor of cattle, rest, and the whole commandment.
He has an eye in his forehead, a universal body, is essence, and bears the wheel of transmigration.
He bears an unfailing staff, stands in the middle, is golden, and has the splendor of brahman.
He is the highest meaning, made of the supreme, <s>Śambara</s>, tiger-like, and fire.
He is brightness, excellent radiance, worthy of praise, <s>Vācaspati</s>, and lord of the day.
He is the sun, the radiant one, the shoulder, the teacher, <s>Vaivasvata</s>, and the people.
He is reasoning, lofty fame, passion pacified, and defeat.
He is lord of <s>Kailāsa</s>, enemy of desire, impeller, and sun-eyed.
He is the most learned, free from fear, remover of the universe, and the restrainer.
He is eternal, of constant auspiciousness, and meritorious to hear and praise.
He is far-heard, endurer of the universe, fit to be meditated upon, and destroyer of bad dreams.
He carries across, destroys evil deeds, is unassailable, hard to endure, and fearless.
He is beginningless; he is <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvar</s>, prosperity, crowned, and lord of the thirty gods.
He protects the universe, bears the universe, is very steady, and has lovely armlets.
He generates; he is the beginning of the birth of creatures, affectionate, ethical, and polity itself.
He is distinguished, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the sun, terrible, and of terrible valor.
He is the praṇava, sevenfold conduct, great-bodied, and bearing a great bow.
He is lord over birth, <s>Mahādeva</s>, one who has gone beyond all the <s>āgamas</s> (scriptural traditions).
His nature is discernment of reality and unreality; he is all-pervading, adorned with sacred ash.
He is the seer, knower of the Brahman, victorious, beyond birth, death, and old age.
He is sacrifice, lord of sacrifice, the sacrificer, the end of sacrifice, of unfailing stride.
He is great <s>Indra</s>, hard to bear, possessed of armies, the limb of sacrifice and the vehicle of sacrifice.
He is the origin of the five Brahmans, lord of the universe, the stainless manifestation.
He is self-born, without beginning or end, supporter of the twenty-six principles and the seven worlds.
He is beloved of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, lofty, the dwelling of the universe, the maker of light.
He is the child, delighted in the mountain, sovereign, well-armed, slayer of the enemies of the gods.
He is unfailing, crusher of misfortune, <s>Mukunda</s>, free from fever.
He is self-luminous, the light after light, the light of the self, unmoving.
He is tawny, with tawny beard, having scripture as his eye and the three Vedas as his body.
He is a mass of knowledge, very wise, without origination, beyond calamity.
He is <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, teacher of yoga, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
He is of noble fame, energetic, a true yogin, composed of being and non-being.
He wears a garland of stars, is lord of the full moon, firmly established, resting on six supports.
His hand is purifying; he is enemy of sin, <s>Maṇipūra</s>, moving as mind moves.
He sits in the lotus of the heart, white, peaceful, <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>.
He is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the planets, dark-hued, capable, destroyer of misfortune.
He is enemy of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), imperishable, invoked by many, praised by many.
He is the womb of <s>Brahmā</s>, the great womb, the cow of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), the source of wealth.
He seeks the welfare of the world, is well-gone, <s>Kumāra</s>, and the arrival of what is auspicious.
He is golden in color, radiant, bearer of many beings, sound itself.
He is free from disease, overseer of rule, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the best of twice-borns.
He is great light, also having a pure abode, the unsurpassed great light.
He is the grandsire, <s>Mātariśvan</s>, <s>Nabhasvān</s>, wearing serpents as a necklace.
He is <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Jātūkarṇya</s>, and <s>Parāśara</s>.
He knows unobstructed <s>dharma</s>; he is <s>Viriñca</s>, whose fame is widespread.
He is <s>Ātmabhū</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Atri</s>, the embodiment of knowledge, greatly renowned.
He is the crest-jewel of the world, heroic, fierce, true in valor.
He is like a serpent, the great cosmic cycle, the great tree, bearer of the arts.
He is an adornment, immovable, shining, supreme in stride.
He is lord of swift sound, rapid, a leaper, having fire as his charioteer.
He is unattached, the guest, <s>Śakra</s>, the crusher, destroyer of sin.
He is of good fame among the <s>Vasus</s>, carrier of oblations to the ancestors, blazing, food of the universe.
He is subjecting things to age, pacifier of old age, red-hued, and <s>Tanūnapāt</s>.
He is <s>Pṛṣadaśva</s>, sky-born, fair-faced, destroyer of darkness.
He is summer heat, the heater, the cloud, the wing, conqueror of enemy cities.
He is the wind from the mouth, well accomplished, fragrant, of a cool nature.
He is spring, <s>Mādhava</s>, summer, the rainy season, bearer of seed.
He is <s>Aṅgiras</s>, the sage <s>Ātreya</s>, stainless, bearer of the universe.
He is purifier, conqueror of many, <s>Śakra</s>, knower of the three Vedas, borne by men.
He is mind, intellect, ego, the knower of the field and guardian of the field.
He is a treasury of brilliance, a treasury of knowledge, maturation, maker of obstacles.
He is the lower and the unsurpassed, the knowable, the eldest, the abode of the highest good.
He is the mountain, the tree, the body as form, enemy of <s>Dānavas</s>, subduer of foes.
He has lovely intelligence; he is the progenitor, charming, free from darts, and maker of the world's dart.
He is the four Vedas, the four states, skillful, and fond of the fourfold.
He is sacred transmission and full transmission, the holy ford, the god, the abode of <s>Śiva</s>.
He is many-formed, great-formed, all-formed, both moving and unmoving.
He carries out justice; he is justice, reachable through justice, stainless.
He is thousand-headed, lord of gods, shatterer of every weapon.

children.text: muṇḍo virūpo vikṛto daṇḍī dānto guṇottamaḥ
children.translated_text: He is shaven-headed, misshapen, transformed, staff-bearing, restrained, highest in qualities.
He is tawny-eyed and yellow-eyed, blue-throated, free from disease.
He is thousand-armed, lord of all, giver of refuge, bearer of all worlds.

children.text: padmāsanaḥ paraṃ jyotiḥ parāvaraṃ paraṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: He is seated on a lotus, the supreme light, the near and far, the supreme fruit.
He is lotus-wombed, great-wombed, universe-wombed, discerning.
He knows the far and near, is lord of seed, fair-faced, greatly resounding.
He is the god who is teacher of gods and anti-gods, honored by gods and anti-gods.
He is the great measure of gods and anti-gods, the great refuge of gods and anti-gods.
He is god of gods, giver of boons to divine seers, gods, and anti-gods.
He is lord of gods and anti-gods, divine, the great lord of gods and anti-gods.
He consists of all gods, is inconceivable, the self of the deities, born from himself.
He is worthy of praise, without a master, tiger among the gods, lion among the gods, maker of the day.
He is the best and foremost among the wise gods, the highest of all gods.
He delights in the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, is splendid, and loves <s>Śikhi</s> and <s>Śrīparvata</s>.
He is the pillar of victory, the distinguished support, the caster down of <s>Narasiṃha</s>.
He practices celibacy, moves in the world, walks in <s>dharma</s>, lord of wealth.
He is <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Nandīśvara</s>, naked, bearer of the naked vow, pure.
He is overseer of the <s>liṅga</s>, overseer of the gods, overseer of the ages, bringer of the age.
He is self-controlled, controlling others, heaven, sound, and a sound made of tones.
He is overseer of seed, maker of seed, maker of wealth, increaser of <s>dharma</s>.
He is pride, freedom from pride, great pride, the great lord of all beings.
He dwells in the cremation ground; he is <s>Tiṣya</s>, the bridge, of incomparable form.
He is transcendent, a clear light, three-eyed, adorned with serpents.
He is enemy of <s>Andhaka</s>, hater of the sacrifice, caster down of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s neck.
He is free from faults, of imperishable qualities, enemy of <s>Dakṣa</s>, remover of <s>Pūṣan</s>'s teeth.
He is <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, bearing the broken axe, whole, partless, sinless.
He is the foundation, foundation of all, pale in radiance, <s>Mṛḍa</s>, the dancer.
Complete, the fulfiller, meritorious, delicate, fair-eyed.
To be sung in <s>Sāman</s> chants, dear-making, of holy fame, free from disease.
Swift as thought, maker of sacred fords, matted-haired, lord of life.
Maker of the end of life, eternal, rich in seed, dear to the <s>Vasus</s>.
The good goal, good honor, attached, dark-throated, bearer of the digit of the moon.
Honored, worthy of honor, <s>Mahākāla</s>, true prosperity, wholly devoted to the good.
Reviver through the moon, ruler, hidden in the worlds, lord of the immortals.
Kinsman of the world, lord of the world, grateful, adorned with noble deeds.
Imperishable and undecaying, lovely, the best among bearers of all śāstras.
Made of splendor, bearer of radiance, magical power of the world, leader, minute.
Pure-smiling, gracious in self, hard to conquer, hard to overstep.
Made of light, formless, lord of the world, lord of the waters.
Holder of the lute called Tumbavīṇī, great-bodied, without sorrow, destroyer of sorrow.
Self of the three worlds, lord of the three worlds, pure, purifier, born from the chariot axle.
Marked by the unmanifest, manifest, both manifest and unmanifest, lord of the people.
Noble in conduct, unequaled in excellence, honor itself, rich in honor, made of wondrous power.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, protector of creatures, <s>Haṃsa</s>, the goal of <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: vedhā dhātā vidhātā ca attā hartā caturmukhaḥ
children.translated_text: Ordainer, sustainer, disposer, eater, remover, four-faced.
Dweller on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, dweller in all, the goal of the good.
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, tawny one, <s>Puruṣa</s>, first-born, father.
Abode of beings, lord of beings, giver of prosperity, lord of the worlds.
Joined in yoga, knower of yoga, <s>Brahman</s>, favorable to brahmins, dear to brahmins.
Dear to the gods, lord of the gods, knower of the gods, contemplator of the gods.
Uneven-eyed, overseer of the arts, bull-marked, increaser of the bull of dharma.
Free from pride, free from ego, free from delusion, free from affliction.
Destroyer of arrogance, proud, haughty, turner of all seasons.
Seven-tongued, thousand-rayed, gentle, naturally skillful.
Lord of past, future, and present beings, source, destroyer of confusion.
Meaning and non-meaning, great treasury, uniquely wise in another's task.
Thornless, maker of joy, guileless, crusher of guile.
Possessed of sattva, sāttvika, of true fame, establisher of sacred tradition.
Unshaken, receiver of virtues, many-souled, performer of many acts.
Well pleased, fair-faced, subtle, easy to approach, skillful, fire.
Shoulder, bearer of the shoulder, load-bearer, manifest, increaser of affection.
Unconquered, enduring all, clever, mounted on every vehicle.
Unsupported, self-supported, to be accomplished, primordial form, bearer of fame.
Bearer of the boar's tusk, wind, powerful, sole leader.
Illuminator of śruti, learned in śruti, single kinsman, bearer of many forms.
Beloved of Śrī, beginning with Śiva, peaceful and auspicious, fitting.
Lying on the earth, maker of prosperity, prosperity itself, ornament, vehicle of beings.
Bodiless, abiding in the bodies of devotees, knower of time, whose body is art.
True-vowed, greatly renouncing, devoted to steadiness and peace.
Acting for the sake of others, boon-giver, secluded, ocean of śruti.
Unwearied, receiver of virtues, marked with a stain, remover of stains.
By nature <s>Rudra</s>, impartial, slayer of enemies, destroyer of the middle.

children.text: śikhaṇḍī kavacī śūlī caṇḍī muṇḍī ca kuṇḍalī
children.translated_text: Crested, armored, trident-bearing, fierce, shaven-headed, and earringed.
Girdled, armored, sword-bearing, master of māyā, charioteer of saṃsāra.
Deathless, all-seeing, lion-like, mass of splendor, great jewel.
Innumerable, immeasurable in self, heroic, skilled in what is to be done.
To be known, knower and protector of the meaning of the Veda, observant of all conduct, lord of sages.
Unsurpassed, hard to assail, sweet, pleasant to behold.

children.text: sureśaḥ śaraṇaṃ sarvaḥ śabdabrahma satāṃ gatiḥ
children.translated_text: Lord of the gods, refuge, the all, word-Brahman, goal of the good.
Devourer of time, maker of stains, one who has made <s>Vāsuki</s> into a bracelet.
Great archer, bearer of the earth, stainless, unfettered.
Sun-jewel, sun, blessed, giver of siddhi, means of siddhi.
Withdrawn, enclosed, art itself, broad-chested, great-armed.
The single light, free from distress, man, dear to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Unstained, whose self is free of manifestation, untroubled, destroyer of trouble.
Praiseworthy, fond of praise, praiser, having the form of <s>Vyāsa</s>, unconfused.
A faultless means of words, mass of knowledge, unchecked in valor.
Peaceful-minded, not petty, destroyer of pettiness, eternally beautiful.
Foremost bearer of firmness, lord of the earth, <s>Śākalya</s>, lord of night.
Teacher of the highest truth, sight itself, guru, affectionate to those who take refuge.
Essence, knower of essence, omniscient, support of all beings.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus he praised the bull-bannered one with a thousand names.
The mighty one bathed him and worshiped him with lotuses.
For the sake of testing <s>Hari</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, lord of the worlds,
then hid one lotus among the lotuses for worship.
When the flower had been taken away there, <s>Hari</s> thought, 'What is this?'
Understanding it, he plucked out his own eye, the support of all beings,
and with devotion worshiped the teacher of the world by that name.
Then <s>Hara</s>, seeing <s>Hari</s> there in such a state,
quickly descended from the circle of fire.
He was like ten million suns, adorned with a crown of matted hair,
divine, encircled by a garland of flames, sharp-fanged and terrifying.
He was <s>Hara</s>, holding trident, axe, mace, discus, lance, and noose,
with hands granting boons and fearlessness, and with a leopard skin as his upper garment.
Seeing <s>Bhava</s> at that time in such a state, adorned with ashes,
<s>Janārdana</s>, delighted, quickly bowed to the god of gods.
The gods, together with <s>Indra</s>, after circumambulating that three-eyed one, ran away.
<s>Brahmā</s>'s world shook, and the earth trembled.
That radiance of <s>Śambhu</s> burned a region of a hundred yojanas.
From below and above as well, a cry of "hā hā" arose on the earth.
Then <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, spoke, as if laughing,
looking with affection at <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who stood with his joined hands folded.
"I now know this work of the gods, O <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: sudarśanākhyaṃ cakraṃ ca dadāmi tava śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: I give you the splendid discus called <s>Sudarśana</s>.
The form that was seen by you, terrifying to all the worlds,

children.text: hitāya tava yatnena tava bhāvāya suvrata ||
children.translated_text: was for your benefit, undertaken with effort for your devotion, O you of good vow.
A peaceful weapon on the battlefield, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, brings suffering for the gods.

children.text: śāntasya cāstraṃ śāntaḥ syācchāntenāstreṇa kiṃ phalam ||
children.translated_text: For one who is peaceful the weapon too would be peaceful; what fruit is there from a peaceful weapon?
For one who is peaceful in battle, peace itself is the weapon of ascetics.
Through peace a warrior's strength is cut down, and the enemy's strength is increased.
When the gods, not peaceful, meditate on this imperishable form of mine,
what need is there of a weapon for fighting, O destroyer of the enemies of the gods?

children.text: kṣamā yudhi na kāryaṃ vai yoddhuṃ devārisūdana
children.translated_text: Forbearance is not to be practiced in battle, O destroyer of the enemies of the gods,
nor with what has not yet come or what has passed, nor in weakness, nor when one's own people are ascendant,
nor at an improper time, nor in unrighteousness, nor in calamity, O destroyer of foes."
Having spoken thus, he gave the discus, equal in brilliance to ten thousand suns.

children.text: netraṃ ca netā jagatāṃ prabhurvai padmasannibham
children.translated_text: And the lord, leader of the worlds, gave the eye resembling a lotus.
From that time onward they call that man of good vow <s>Padmākṣa</s>, the lotus-eyed.
Having given that eye and the discus to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>

children.text: pasparśa ca karābhyāṃ vai suśubhābhyāmuvāca ha ||
children.translated_text: touched him with both of his beautiful hands and spoke:
"I am the giver of boons, O best receiver of boons; choose the boons you desire.
Surely I have been brought under your power by devotion, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>."
Thus addressed by the god of gods, he bowed to that god of gods and said:
"May I have devotion toward you, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; be gracious. This is the highest boon.
I desire no other, O Lord, for devotees have no afflictions."

children.text: tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya dayāvān sutarāṃ bhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing those words of his, <s>Bhava</s> became still more compassionate.

children.text: pasparśa ca dadau tasmai śraddhāṃ śītāṃśubhūṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The moon-adorned one touched him and gave him faith.
And <s>Mahādeva</s> spoke thus to <s>Acyuta</s>, the supreme self:

children.text: mayi bhaktaś ca vandyaś ca pūjyaścaiva surāsuraiḥ
children.translated_text: "You will be devoted to me, and worthy of reverence and worship by gods and asuras alike.
There is no doubt, O best of gods, through my favor.
When <s>Satī</s>, the fair-eyed daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>, after censuring
her mother and her father <s>Dakṣa</s>, will become the lady of the gods,

children.text: divyā haimavatī viṣṇo tadā tvamapi suvrata
children.translated_text: and when, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, she is the divine daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, then you also, O you of good vow,
will give to me that blessed goddess <s>Umā</s>, the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>, your sister,

children.text: niyogād brahmaṇaḥ sādhvīṃ pradāsyasi mamaiva tām
children.translated_text: that virtuous woman, by the command of <s>Brahmā</s> himself.

children.text: matsaṃbandhī ca lokānāṃ madhye pūjyo bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: As one connected with me, you will be worshiped among the worlds.

children.text: māṃ divyena ca bhāvena tadāprabhṛti śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: From that time onward you will see me, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, with a divine disposition,
graciously, as though I were a friend to your very self."
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>, disappeared.
The blessed <s>Janārdana</s> too, in the presence even of the gods,
made a request of <s>Mahādeva</s> and of <s>Brahmā</s> together with the sages:

children.text: mayā proktaṃ stavaṃ divyaṃ padmayone suśobhanam ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Padmayoni</s>, this splendid divine hymn has been spoken by me.
Whoever recites it, or hears it, or has it recited to the best of twice-born men,

children.text: pratināmni hiraṇyasya tat tasya phalam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: for each name will obtain the fruit belonging to that gift of gold.
Indeed, the fruit for him is equal to a thousand horse-sacrifices.

children.text: ghṛtādyaiḥ snāpayedrudraṃ sthālyā vai kalaśaiḥ śubhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If he bathes <s>Rudra</s> with ghee and the like, with vessels and auspicious jars,
and with faith worships <s>Śiva</s>, the Lord, by means of this thousand names,
he too, having obtained the fruit of a thousand sacrifices, will be honored by the lords of the gods.

children.text: pūjyo bhavati rudrasya prītirbhavati tasya vai
children.translated_text: And <s>Rudra</s>'s favor will belong to him."
Then <s>Padmayoni</s> said to <s>Janārdana</s>, "So be it; so indeed."
They went away after bowing to that god of gods, the teacher of the world.
Therefore, O sinless twice-born ones, one should worship with the thousand names,

children.text: japennāmnāṃ sahasraṃ ca sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and one should recite the thousand names; he goes to the supreme goal.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge sahasranāmabhiḥ pūjanād viṣṇucakralābho nāmāṣṭanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, the ninety-eighth chapter, called "Viṣṇu's acquisition of the discus through worship with the thousand names."
The seers said:
