"The birth of the goddess has been indicated by you, O greatly wise <s>Sūta</s>.
Tell it now in detail, exactly as it was in her state as <s>Satī</s>.
Tell of the great goddess's birth from <s>Menā</s> and the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice,

children.text: viṣṇunā ca kathaṃ dattā devadevāya śaṃbhave ||
children.translated_text: and how she was given by <s>Viṣṇu</s> to <s>Śambhu</s>, the god of gods.

children.text: kalyāṇaṃ vā kathaṃ tasya vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam
children.translated_text: Or tell now how his auspicious marriage took place."
Having heard those words of theirs, <s>Sūta</s>, the foremost narrator of purāṇas,

children.text: saṃbhavaṃ ca mahādevyāḥ prāha teṣāṃ mahātmanām
children.translated_text: told those great-souled ones of the birth of the great goddess.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: brahmaṇā kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ daṇḍine tat suvistaram ||
children.translated_text: "This was formerly told in full detail by <s>Brahmā</s> to <s>Daṇḍin</s>.

children.text: yuṣmābhir vai kumārāya tena vyāsāya dhīmate
children.translated_text: By you it was told to <s>Kumāra</s>, and by him to wise <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Therefore, having heard it, I proclaim it in full detail.
At your word, O greatly fortunate ones, after bowing to <s>Umā</s> and also to <s>Bhava</s>:
She, called <s>Bhagā</s>, is the mother of the world and the threefold Vedic power of the liṅga-form.
The liṅga is the Blessed Lord; through the two there is the creation of the world, O best twice-born ones.
<s>Śiva</s>, whose form is the liṅga, is the light stationed above darkness."
From the union with the liṅga-altar he became <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>;
at the beginning he made the god <s>Brahmā</s>, his four-faced son.

children.text: prāhiṇoti sma tasyaiva jñānaṃ jñānamayo haraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, whose nature is knowledge, sent forth knowledge to him himself;
that blessed, all-surpassing lord is the powerful <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>.
The god saw that <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> as he was being born;
and <s>Brahmā</s> too saw <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Seeing that god, the lord <s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>, standing there,
the lotus-born one praised the boon-giver with words dear to him.
The unborn, powerful one said to the lord of the universe, the self of the universe, 'Divide yourself';
and he created the Goddess from his left side, a wife equal to himself.

children.text: śraddhā hyasya śubhā patnī tataḥ puṃsaḥ purātanī
children.translated_text: For auspicious <s>Śraddhā</s> was his wife, the ancient wife of the Person;
by the command of the powerful lord that same Goddess became the daughter of <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: satīsaṃjñā tadā sā vai rudramevāśritā patim
children.translated_text: Then she, known as <s>Satī</s>, took <s>Rudra</s> alone as her husband;

children.text: dakṣaṃ vinindya kālena devī mainā hyabhūtpunaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in time, after censuring <s>Dakṣa</s>, the Goddess was born again as <s>Mainā</s>'s daughter.
Because of <s>Nārada</s>'s curse, <s>Dakṣa</s> also reviled him in this way;
arrogant and maddened by contempt, <s>Dakṣa</s> reviled the god of gods, <s>Umāpati</s>.

children.text: anādṛtya kṛtiṃ jñātvā satī dakṣeṇa tatkṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: When <s>Satī</s> understood that <s>Dakṣa</s> had disregarded her act, then at once,
having reduced her own body to ashes by the path of yoga, she again

children.text: babhūva pārvatī devī tapasā ca gireḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: became the Goddess <s>Pārvatī</s> through the austerity of the lord of the mountain.
Knowing this, the blessed lord <s>Bharga</s>, angered, burned
the vast sacrifice of <s>Dakṣa</s>, even in accordance with the word of the descendant of <s>Cyavana</s>.

children.text: cyavanasya suto dhīmān dadhīca iti viśrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise son of <s>Cyavana</s> was renowned as <s>Dadhīca</s>;

children.text: vijitya viṣṇuṃ samare prasādāt tryaṃbakasya ca
children.translated_text: having defeated <s>Viṣṇu</s> in battle through the favor of <s>Tryambaka</s>,

children.text: viṣṇunā lokapālāṃś ca śaśāpa ca munīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: that lord of sages cursed <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the guardians of the worlds.
By the fire born of <s>Rudra</s>'s anger, the gods, together with the oblation,

children.text: vināśo vai kṣaṇādeva māyayā śaṅkarasya vai ||
children.translated_text: were indeed destroyed in an instant through the māyā of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge devīsaṃbhavo nāma navanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the first part of the venerable great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, is the ninety-ninth chapter, named 'The Birth of the Goddess.'
The sages said:
After conquering along with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, how did the blessed <s>Parameśvara</s>,
<s>Maheśvara</s>, apportion all of them in accordance with <s>Dadhīca</s>'s statement?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
At the very great sacrifice of <s>Dakṣa</s>, the blessed <s>Rudra</s> burned

children.text: dadāha bhagavān rudraḥ sarvān munigaṇān api ||
children.translated_text: all the gods, with <s>Viṣṇu</s> at their head, and also all the hosts of sages.
A gaṇa named <s>Bhadra</s> was sent by that supreme lord,
because of the unbearable separation from the Goddess, O men of good vows.
He created <s>Vīrabhadra</s> and auspicious lords of gaṇas born from his hairs;
and powerful <s>Bhadra</s>, accompanied by the lords of gaṇas, mounted a chariot.
He set his mind on going, and the blessed unborn one was his charioteer;
all those lords of gaṇas held various weapons in their hands.
Then the gods followed him on auspicious aerial cars from every side,
to the lovely peak of <s>Himavat</s>, shining with golden summits.
There was his sacrificial enclosure near <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>;

children.text: taddeśe caiva vikhyātaṃ śubhaṃ kanakhalaṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: in that region, O twice-born ones, the auspicious place called <s>Kankhala</s> is renowned.
He had been sent there by the blessed supreme lord to burn it;
then an ominous portent arose, announcing fear for the worlds.
The mountains split apart and the earth trembled;
the winds whirled, and the ocean, abode of makaras, was disturbed.

children.text: agnayo naiva dīpyanti na ca dīpyati bhāskaraḥ
children.translated_text: The fires did not blaze, and the sun did not shine;

children.text: grahāś ca na prakāśyante na devā na ca dānavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the planets did not give light, nor did the gods or the demons.
Then in an instant, having entered the sacrificial enclosure of the great-souled one,
<s>Bhadra</s>, accompanied by those born from the hairs, was like another fire of Time.
The blessed <s>Bhadra</s> spoke to <s>Dakṣa</s>, who was of immeasurable splendor:
'Because of your connection, <s>Dakṣa</s>, I have now been sent by the bearer of <s>Pināka</s>
to burn you, together with the chief sages and the gods.'
Having spoken thus, that foremost of the gaṇas burned that sacrificial hall.
The lords of gaṇas, enraged, tore up the sacrificial posts and hurled them away;

children.text: prastotrā saha hotrā ca dagdhaṃ caiva gaṇeśvaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the prastotṛ and the hotṛ were burned by the lords of gaṇas.
The leaders of the gaṇas seized everyone and threw them into the stream of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Mighty <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, seeing <s>Śakra</s> raising his arm,
restrained it with undaunted spirit, and likewise the arms of the other dwellers in heaven.
With the tip of his nail, in sport, he tore out the eyes of <s>Bhaga</s>;
and, striking with his fist, he knocked out the teeth of <s>Pūṣan</s>.
Likewise, in sport, with the big toe of his foot,
the blessed and powerful <s>Vīrabhadra</s> rubbed down the god <s>Candra</s>.
The blessed lord cut off the head of that <s>Śakra</s>.
Having cut off both hands of <s>Vahni</s> and torn out his tongue in sport,
mighty <s>Vīrabhadra</s> struck him on the head with his foot.

children.text: yamasya daṇḍaṃ bhagavān pracicheda svayaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed lord himself cut apart the staff of <s>Yama</s>;
with his trident he struck the mighty god <s>Īśāna</s>.
Thus, without effort, he struck down the thirty-three gods,

children.text: trayaś ca triśataṃ teṣāṃ trisāhasraṃ ca līlayā ||
children.translated_text: and three hundred and three of them, and three thousand, in sport.

children.text: trayaṃ caiva surendrāṇāṃ jaghāna ca munīśvarān
children.translated_text: He struck down three lords of the gods and the chief sages as well;

children.text: anyāṃś ca devān devo'sau sarvānyuddhāya saṃsthitān ||
children.translated_text: and that god struck down all the other gods who stood ready for battle.
The blessed <s>Rudra</s> struck them down with sword, fist, and other missiles.
Then mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>, though stunned, raised his discus;
the blessed <s>Mādhava</s> fought with that <s>Rudra</s>.
Between the two there arose a very terrible battle that made the hairs stand on end.
By the yogic power of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, terrifying divine bodies were born from him,
countless beings with conch, discus, and mace in their hands.
That god killed all of them, though they had a splendor equal to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s,
and then struck <s>Viṣṇu</s> on the head with his mace.
Then, in the battlefield, he struck that god on the chest as if in play,

children.text: papāta ca tadā bhūmau visaṃjñaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Puruṣottama</s> fell unconscious on the ground.

children.text: punarutthāya taṃ hantuṃ cakramudyamya sa prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rising again, that glorious lord, best of men, raised his discus to kill him,
and stood there with eyes reddened by anger.
But his fierce discus, shining like the sun at the end of time,

children.text: vyaṣṭambhayad adīnātmā karasthaṃ na cacāla saḥ
children.translated_text: the undaunted one checked in his hand; it did not move.
Checked by him, he stood still and motionless, like a horned mountain.

children.text: tribhiś ca dharṣitaṃ śārṅgaṃ tridhābhūtaṃ prabhostadā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śārṅga</s>, assailed by three blows, was broken into three pieces in the lord's hand.

children.text: śārṅgakoṭiprasaṅgād vai cicheda ca śiraḥ prabhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: And by contact with the tip of <s>Śārṅga</s>, he cut off the lord's head.
When cut off, his head at once fell into <s>Rasātala</s>.
Driven by the vital wind, and by <s>Pinākin</s>,
it then entered his own <s>āhavanīya</s> fire.
Seeing the sacrifice with its vessels shattered, its posts broken, and its gateways destroyed,
and its great hall set ablaze, even the sacrifice fled.

children.text: taṃ tadā mṛgarūpeṇa dhāvantaṃ gaganaṃ prati ||
children.translated_text: As it ran in the form of a deer toward the sky,
<s>Vīrabhadra</s> took aim at it and made it headless.

children.text: tataḥ prajāpatiṃ dharmaṃ kaśyapaṃ ca jagadgurum ||
children.translated_text: Then the hero struck <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the teacher of the world,
<s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, and the great sage <s>Bahuputra</s>,

children.text: munim aṅgirasaṃ caiva kṛṣṇāśvaṃ ca mahābalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and mighty as he was, also the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇāśva</s>.

children.text: jaghāna mūrdhni pādena dakṣaṃ caiva yaśasvinam
children.translated_text: With his foot he struck famous <s>Dakṣa</s> on the head as well.
He cut off his head and burned it in the fire, O best of twice-born men.
And the tip of <s>Sarasvatī</s>'s nose, and likewise that of the mother of the gods,
powerful <s>Vīrabhadra</s> cut off with the tip of his nail.

children.text: tasthau śriyā vṛto madhye pretasthāne yathā bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Then he stood in the middle, encircled by splendor, like <s>Bhava</s> in a cremation ground.
At that very time the blessed lotus-born lord,
the greatly radiant master, bowed down and appealed to <s>Bhadra</s>.

children.text: alaṃ krodhena vai bhadra naṣṭāścaiva divaukasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Enough of anger, <s>Bhadra</s>; the gods have indeed been destroyed.

children.text: prasīda kṣamyatāṃ sarvaṃ romajaiḥ saha suvrata
children.translated_text: Be gracious, O good-vowed one; let everything be forgiven, together with those born from the hairs."
Then <s>Bhadra</s> too, through the power of <s>Brahmā</s> <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>,
gradually became calm; pacified, he stood at his command.
There also in the sky was the blessed god whose banner bears the bull,
<s>Śarva</s>, accompanied by his hosts, ever-giving, the great lord of all worlds.
And the blessed <s>Bhava</s>, entreated by the god <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: hatānāṃ ca tadā teṣāṃ pradadau pūrvavattanum
children.translated_text: gave back to those who had been slain bodies as before.
The great lord restored the head of <s>Indra</s>, and that of noble <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
and that of the sage <s>Dakṣa</s>, and likewise those of the others.
He restored the tip of the nose of <s>Vāgīśī</s>, and likewise that of the mother of the gods,

children.text: naṣṭānāṃ jīvitaṃ caiva varāṇi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: and life to those who had lost it, along with various boons.
For <s>Dakṣa</s>, whose face had been ruined, the blessed great lord

children.text: kalpayāmāsa vai vaktraṃ līlayā ca mahān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bhava</s> playfully fashioned a face with a head.
Then <s>Dakṣa</s> too, having regained consciousness, rose up with joined palms
and praised <s>Śaṅkara</s>, lord of the gods of gods, whose banner bears the bull.
Praised by him, the greatly radiant one granted various boons
and gave lordship over the <s>gaṇas</s> to <s>Dakṣa</s>, whose acts were unwearied.

children.text: devāś ca sarve deveśaṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ parameśvaram ||
children.translated_text: All the gods praised <s>Parameśvara</s>, the lord of gods,

children.text: nārāyaṇaś ca bhagavān tuṣṭāva ca kṛtāñjaliḥ
children.translated_text: and the blessed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> too praised him with joined palms.
<s>Brahmā</s> and all the sages, each separately, praised the unborn one,
the lord of the gods of gods, blue-throated, whose banner bears the bull.
After bestowing favor on those gods, <s>Bhava</s> too disappeared.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śivakṛddakṣayajñavidhvaṃsano nāma śatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one-hundredth chapter in the first part of the blessed <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, called "The Destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s Sacrifice Caused by <s>Śiva</s>."
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ himavataḥ putrī babhūvāṃbā satī śubhā
children.translated_text: How did the auspicious <s>Ambā</s>, <s>Satī</s>, become the daughter of <s>Himavat</s>?
And how did she obtain as her husband <s>Īśvara</s>, the lord of the gods of gods?
<s>Sūta</s> said:
That lovely woman, taking refuge in the body of <s>Menā</s> by her own will,

children.text: tadā haimavatī jajñe tapasā ca dvijottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: was then born as <s>Haimavatī</s> through ascetic power, O best of twice-born men.
The lord of mountains performed all the rites beginning with the birth ceremony.

children.text: dvādaśe ca tadā varṣe pūrṇe haimavatī śubhā ||
children.translated_text: When the auspicious <s>Haimavatī</s> had completed her twelfth year,
she practiced austerity together with her younger sister, fair-faced as she was.

children.text: anyā ca devī hyanujā sarvaloke namaskṛtā ||
children.translated_text: There was also another goddess, a younger sister, honored in every world.
Then all the sages praised the goddess, the great lady of all worlds,
surrounding her on every side as she performed austerity.
The eldest was <s>Aparṇā</s>, and the younger one, fair-faced, was <s>Ekaparṇā</s>.
The third, lovely-hipped one, was likewise <s>Ekapāṭalā</s>.
By the austerity of the great goddess <s>Pārvatī</s>,
the great god <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, lord of all beings, was won over.

children.text: etasminneva kāle tu tārako nāma dānavaḥ
children.translated_text: At this same time there was a demon named <s>Tāraka</s>,
the greatly radiant son of <s>Tāra</s>, a descendant of <s>Diti</s>.
He too had three sons: the great demon <s>Tārakākṣa</s>,

children.text: vidyunmālī ca bhagavān kamalākṣaś ca vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: blessed <s>Vidyunmālī</s>, and powerful <s>Kamalākṣa</s>.

children.text: pitāmahas tathā caiṣāṃ tāro nāma mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Their grandfather also was named <s>Tāra</s>, exceedingly mighty,
and he had gained valor through austerity by the grace of lord <s>Brahmā</s>.
That greatly radiant <s>Tāra</s> had formerly conquered the three worlds, moving and unmoving,

children.text: vijitya samare pūrvaṃ viṣṇuṃ ca jitavān asau ||
children.translated_text: and in battle he had even conquered <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Between those two there arose a very terrible battle, making the hair stand on end,
divine, for a thousand years, day and night, without rest.
Taking <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with his chariot, he hurled him a hundred yojanas.
Defeated by <s>Tāra</s> in battle, <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s> fled.
<s>Tāra</s>, having obtained a boon and strength a hundredfold greater,
the son of <s>Diti</s> gained the whole world from the Grandsire.
Having conquered the gods headed by <s>Devendra</s>, that lord over the lords of gods
kept those gods back in all the worlds by his māyā (supernatural power).
The deities, together with <s>Indra</s>, oppressed by fear of <s>Tāraka</s>,

children.text: na śāntiṃ lebhire śūrāḥ śaraṇaṃ vā bhayārditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: found no peace or refuge, though they were heroes, being tormented by fear.
Then the glorious lord of the immortals, the ruler of the immortals, having assembled them,
the god spoke to <s>Aṅgiras</s> even in the presence of the gods.
"Blessed one, there is an excellent dānava named <s>Tāraka</s>, born of <s>Tāra</s>.

children.text: tena saṃnihatā yuddhe vatsā gopatinā yathā ||
children.translated_text: By him we have been struck down in battle like calves by a cowherd.
From fear of him, O greatly fortunate <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, in the great war,
these gods wander without shelter, like birds in a cage.

children.text: asmākaṃ yāny amoghāni āyudhāny aṅgiro vara
children.translated_text: Those weapons of ours, O best of the <s>Aṅgiras</s> line, which are unfailing,
become futile because of the power of the enemy of the immortals.
For twenty thousand years, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: viṣṇunā yodhito yuddhe tenāpi na ca sūditaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he was fought in battle by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, yet even by him he was not slain.
Since he was not conquered in battle by mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
how will one such as we stand before him in combat?"

children.text: evam uktas tu śakreṇa jīvaḥ sārdhaṃ surādhipaiḥ
children.translated_text: Thus addressed by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Jīva</s>, together with the lords of the gods,
and with the thousand-eyed one, approached the mighty <s>Kuśadhvaja</s> and spoke.
He too, hearing it from his mouth, out of affection, the remover of the distress of those who bow to him,
the Grandsire, with all the gods and <s>Indra</s>, spoke to <s>Jīva</s>.

children.text: jāne vo'rtiṃ surendrāṇāṃ tathāpi śṛṇu sāṃpratam
children.translated_text: "I know your distress, O lords of the gods; nevertheless, listen now.

children.text: vinindya dakṣaṃ yā devī satī rudrāṅgasaṃbhavā ||
children.translated_text: The goddess <s>Satī</s>, born from the body of <s>Rudra</s>, who reviled <s>Dakṣa</s>,
has been born as <s>Umā Haimavatī</s>, honored by all the worlds.
With regard to this very form of hers here, O gods, best of gods,
strive to draw toward her the great mind of this mighty <s>Rudra</s>.
From the union of those two will be born <s>Skanda</s>, the powerful lord who bears the spear,
six-faced, twelve-armed, the commander, the fiery lord,
son of <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Kārttikeya</s>, <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, and born in the reed-thicket,

children.text: devaḥ śākho viśākhaś ca naigameśaś ca vīryavān
children.translated_text: the god <s>Śākha</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, and valiant <s>Naigameśa</s>,
the army-leader called <s>Kumāra</s>, honored by all the worlds.
In mere play, <s>Mahāsena</s> alone, though still a child,
will slay the mighty <s>Tārakāsura</s> and will deliver the gods."

children.text: evam uktas tadā tena brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā
children.translated_text: When the supreme <s>Brahmā</s> had spoken thus then,

children.text: bṛhaspatis tathā sendrair devair devaṃ praṇamya tam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, together with <s>Indra</s> and the gods, bowed to that god.
Reaching the peak of <s>Meru</s>, the well-vowed one remembered <s>Smara</s>.
Because of the recollection of the god of gods, <s>Smara</s> too, together with his wife,
came with <s>Rati</s>, bowed, and stood with joined palms.
O best twice-borns, the life of the world addressed that <s>Jīva</s> along with <s>Śakra</s>:
"Since I have been remembered by you, O <s>Jīva</s>, I have come to your presence.
Tell me what is to be done by me." Then the one worshiped by the gods spoke to him.
Blessed <s>Śakra</s>, honoring <s>Makaradhvaja</s>, said to him,
"Unite <s>Ambikā</s> with <s>Śaṅkara</s> today, as best you can.

children.text: tayā sa ramate yena bhagavān vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ
children.translated_text: Seek that means by which blessed <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>

children.text: tena mārgeṇa mārgasva patnyā ratyānayā saha ||
children.translated_text: may delight in her, together with this wife of yours, <s>Rati</s>.

children.text: so'pi tuṣṭo mahādevaḥ pradāsyati śubhāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Then pleased <s>Mahādeva</s> will grant you an auspicious state,
having obtained that <s>Girijā Umā</s>, from whom he had formerly been separated."
Thus addressed, he bowed to the god of gods, the husband of <s>Śacī</s>,

children.text: devadevāśramaṃ gantuṃ matiṃ cakre tayā saha ||
children.translated_text: and with her resolved to go to the hermitage of the god of gods.

children.text: gatvā tadāśraye śaṃbhoḥ saha ratyā mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: Having gone then to the refuge of <s>Śambhu</s>, the mighty one, together with <s>Rati</s>,
and with <s>Vasanta</s> as his helper, became intent on joining the god with her.

children.text: tataḥ samprekṣya madanaṃ hasan devas triyaṃbakaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the god <s>Tryambaka</s>, seeing <s>Madana</s>, laughed,
and with his third eye looked at him disdainfully.
Then fire born from his eye burned <s>Madana</s>, who was standing at his side,
at that very instant; and <s>Rati</s> lamented piteously.
Hearing the lament of <s>Rati</s>, the god of gods, <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>,

children.text: kṛpayā parayā prāha kāmapatnīṃ nirīkṣya ca ||
children.translated_text: looked upon the wife of <s>Kāma</s> and spoke with supreme compassion:

children.text: amūrto'pi dhruvaṃ bhadre kāryaṃ sarvaṃ patistava
children.translated_text: "Though bodiless, good lady, your husband will certainly accomplish every function.

children.text: ratikāle dhruve bhadre kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the time of love, good lady, he will certainly act; there is no doubt.

children.text: yadā viṣṇuś ca bhavitā vāsudevo mahāyaśāḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the greatly famous one, shall become <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
the great-splendored one, because of <s>Bhṛgu</s>'s curse and for the welfare of all worlds,

children.text: tadā tasya suto yaś ca sa patiste bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: then the son who is his will be your husband."

children.text: sā praṇamya tadā rudraṃ kāmapatnī śucismitā ||
children.translated_text: Then the sweet-smiling wife of <s>Kāma</s> bowed to <s>Rudra</s>,
and, having regained <s>Madana</s>, departed, accompanied by <s>Vasanta</s>.
Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-first chapter, named "The Burning of <s>Madana</s>."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
By the austerity of the great goddess <s>Pārvatī</s>, the bull-bannered one,
blessed <s>Śarva</s>, was then pleased by the word of <s>Brahmā</s>.
And for the welfare of the āśramas (religious orders) and for sport, blessed <s>Bhava</s>
then married the goddess <s>Haimavatī</s> according to rule.
<s>Brahmā</s> himself, with the great seers beginning with <s>Marīci</s>, went
to the ascetic grove of the great goddess <s>Pārvatī</s>, O lotus-born one.

children.text: pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ca tāṃ devīṃ sa jagato'raṇīm
children.translated_text: And having circumambulated that goddess, the fire-stick that brings forth the world,
For what purpose, O daughter of the mountain, do you heat the worlds with your austerity?

children.text: tvayā sṛṣṭaṃ jagatsarvaṃ mātastvaṃ mā vināśaya
children.translated_text: The whole universe was created by you; mother, do not destroy it.

children.text: tvaṃ hi saṃdhārayellokān imān sarvān svatejasā ||
children.translated_text: For you sustain all these worlds by your own splendor.
The blessed <s>Bhava</s>, lord of all gods, lord of all worlds,
that god of gods of whom we speak as servants,

children.text: sa evaṃ parameśānaḥ svayaṃ ca varayiṣyati
children.translated_text: that same supreme lord himself will choose you.

children.text: varade yena sṛṣṭāsi na vinā yastvayāṃbike ||
children.translated_text: O bestower of boons, O <s>Ambikā</s>, he by whom you were created, and who is not apart from you,
he will become your husband; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: ityuktvā tāṃ namaskṛtya muhuḥ samprekṣya pārvatīm ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, bowing to her and repeatedly gazing upon <s>Pārvatī</s>,
when <s>Pitāmaha</s> had gone, the god, the blessed <s>Parameśvara</s>,
went to the hermitage, in the form of a twice-born man, to show favor.

children.text: sā ca dṛṣṭvā mahādevaṃ dvijarūpeṇa saṃsthitam
children.translated_text: And she, seeing <s>Mahādeva</s> standing there in the form of a twice-born man,
recognized the lord through intuition and other signs, and bowed to the bull-bannered one.
After worshiping the boon-giving god who had come under the guise of a Brahmin,
<s>Pārvatī</s> praised <s>Parameśāna</s>, the supreme lord.
Then, having favored the goddess, he spoke, as if smiling:
'Protecting the family <s>dharma</s> (duty) of the great-souled mountain,
and for sport among the good, <s>Bhava</s>, lord of all gods,
O great goddess, at your divine and beautifully splendid svayaṃvara,

children.text: āsthāya rūpaṃ yatsaumyaṃ sameṣye'haṃ saha tvayā
children.translated_text: will assume whatever gentle form, and I shall join with you.'

children.text: ityuktvā tāṃ samālokya devo divyena cakṣuṣā ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and looked upon her with his divine eye,

children.text: jagāmeṣṭaṃ tadā divyaṃ svapuraṃ prayayau ca sā
children.translated_text: the god then went as he wished to his divine city, and she too departed.
Then the snowy mountain, together with <s>Menā</s>, seeing the goddess delighted,
embraced, smelled, and honored his daughter, herself an ascetic.
Not knowing that his daughter had been addressed by the god of gods,
he then proclaimed the goddess's svayaṃvara throughout all the worlds.

children.text: atha brahmā ca bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sākṣājjanārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> himself, <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: śakraś ca bhagavān vahnirbhāskaro bhaga eva ca
children.translated_text: and blessed <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Vahni</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, and <s>Bhaga</s>,

children.text: tvaṣṭāryamā vivasvāṃś ca yamo varuṇa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: vāyuḥ somastatheśāno rudrāś ca munayas tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and likewise <s>Īśāna</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the sages too,
the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Gandharvas</s>, and <s>Garuḍa</s>,
the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, <s>Daityas</s>, <s>Kiṃpuruṣas</s>, and <s>Uragas</s>,

children.text: samudrāś ca nadā vedā mantrāḥ stotrādayaḥ kṣaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the oceans and rivers, the <s>Vedas</s>, mantras, hymns and the divisions of time,

children.text: nāgāś ca parvatāḥ sarve yajñāḥ sūryādayo grahāḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Nāgas</s>, all the mountains, sacrifices, and the planets beginning with the sun,

children.text: trayastriṃśacca devānāṃ trayaś ca triśataṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the thirty-three gods, the three hundred and three as well,

children.text: trayaś ca trisahasraṃ ca tathānye bahavaḥ surā
children.translated_text: the three thousand and three, and many other gods also,
went to the unsurpassed svayaṃvara of the daughter of the lord of mountains.
Then the goddess, the daughter of the mountain, mounted a lovely golden
aerial car, auspicious on every side and adorned with all jewels.
It was adorned by dancing <s>Apsarases</s>, decked with every ornament,
and by various <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, and beautiful <s>Kinnaras</s>.

children.text: bandibhiḥ stūyamānā ca sthitā śailasutā tadā
children.translated_text: Praised by bards, the daughter of the mountain stood there.
<s>Mālinī</s> likewise carried a white parasol mingled with jewel-rays,
for the mountain's daughter, like twilight bearing the full moon's disk.
She was surrounded by divine women whose hands held fly-whisks.
<s>Jayā</s> stood holding a garland born from a heavenly tree.

children.text: vijayā vyajanaṃ gṛhya sthitā devyāḥ samīpagā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s> stood near the goddess, holding a fan.

children.text: mālāṃ pragṛhya devyāṃ tu sthitāyāṃ devasaṃsadi
children.translated_text: When the goddess stood in the assembly of the gods, holding the garland,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, the bull-bannered one, became a child for sport.
The blessed <s>Bhava</s> lay sleeping in her lap.
Then, seeing the child situated in her lap,

children.text: ko'yam atreti saṃmantrya cukṣubhuś ca samāgatāḥ
children.translated_text: the assembled gods deliberated, 'Who is this here?' and became agitated.
The slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> raised his arm and brought his thunderbolt against him.
That raised arm of his remained fixed just as it was,
paralyzed in sport by the god of gods in the form of a child.

children.text: vajraṃ kṣeptuṃ na śaśāka bāhuṃ cālayituṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He could not hurl the thunderbolt, nor could he move his arm.

children.text: vahniḥ śaktiṃ tathā kṣeptuṃ na śaśāka tathā sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vahni</s>, standing in the same way, could not hurl his spear.
<s>Yama</s> too stood with his staff, and <s>Nirṛti</s> with his sword, O foremost sages.
<s>Varuṇa</s> stood with his serpent-noose, and <s>Samīraṇa</s> with his banner-staff.

children.text: somo gadāṃ dhaneśaś ca daṇḍaṃ daṇḍabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> stood with his mace, and <s>Dhaneśa</s>, best of staff-bearers, with his staff.

children.text: īśānaś ca tathā śūlaṃ tīvramudyamya saṃsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Īśāna</s> likewise stood raising his fierce trident.

children.text: rudrāś ca śūlamādityā muśalaṃ vasavas tathā
children.translated_text: The <s>Rudras</s> raised tridents, the <s>Ādityas</s> pestles, and the <s>Vasus</s> likewise
mallets; all the dwellers in heaven were quickly paralyzed by the god.
The gods were paralyzed by the god of gods, and so were the other dwellers in heaven.

children.text: śiraḥ prakampayan viṣṇuś cakram udyamya saṃsthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, shaking his head, stood raising his discus.

children.text: tasyāpi śiraso bālaḥ sthiratvaṃ pracakāra ha
children.translated_text: The child made even his head motionless.

children.text: cakraṃ kṣeptuṃ na śaśāka bāhūṃścālayituṃ na ca ||
children.translated_text: He could not hurl the discus, nor could he move his arms.

children.text: pūṣā dantān daśan dantair bālamaikṣata mohitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Pūṣan</s>, gnashing his teeth with his teeth, looked at the child, bewildered.
His teeth too fell out when he was merely glanced at by <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: balaṃ tejaś ca yogaṃ ca tathaivāstambhayad vibhuḥ
children.translated_text: The powerful lord likewise paralyzed their strength, splendor, and yoga.
Then, while they remained just so, and even while the gods were angry,
<s>Brahmā</s>, greatly alarmed, entered meditation upon <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
He understood that the god <s>Īśāna</s> was seated in <s>Umā</s>'s lap.

children.text: sa buddhvā devamīśānaṃ śīghram utthāya vismitaḥ
children.translated_text: Realizing him to be the god <s>Īśāna</s>, he quickly rose, amazed,
and <s>Pitāmaha</s> bowed to <s>Śambhu</s>'s feet and praised him.
You are the <s>buddhi</s> (intelligence) of all worlds; you are <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle), O <s>Īśvara</s>.
Of beings and of the senses, you alone, O Lord, are the impeller.
I, the ancient one, was formerly created from your right hand;
from your left hand, O mighty-armed one, came the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord.

children.text: iyaṃ ca prakṛtirdevī sadā te sṛṣṭikāraṇa
children.translated_text: And this goddess <s>Prakṛti</s>, ever the cause of your creation,
having assumed the form of a wife, has come as the cause of the world.
Homage to you, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; homage again and again to <s>Mahādevī</s>.
By your grace, O lord of gods, and by your command, the creatures
beginning with the gods have been created by me; yet they are bewildered, deluded by your yoga.
Show favor to them, so that they may become as they were before.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
After <s>Brahmā</s> had thus petitioned the god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
the blessed lotus-born one then spoke to those who had been paralyzed by him:

children.text: mūḍhāstha devatāḥ sarvā naiva budhyata śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: 'You are bewildered, all you deities; you do not understand <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the god of gods, honored by all the gods, who has come here.
Go quickly for refuge, O gods headed by <s>Śakra</s>,
all of you together with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with the sages, to <s>Śaṅkara</s> the lord,
along with me, to the lord of gods, the supreme self, the ruler,

children.text: anayā haimavatyā ca prakṛtyā saha sattamam ||
children.translated_text: together with this <s>Haimavatī</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, the most excellent one.'
Then, still paralyzed by him in just that way, O best of gods,
all of them, together with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, bowed mentally to the lord.
Then the three-eyed god of gods became pleased with them,
and the lord, at <s>Brahmā</s>'s word, quickly restored them as before.
Then, when he was thus pleased, the lord of gods
assumed a divine, supreme, most marvelous body, dispelling the obstruction of all the gods.
By his splendor those gods, with <s>Indra</s>, <s>Candra</s>, and <s>Divākara</s>,
with <s>Brahmā</s>, with the <s>Sādhyas</s>, and likewise with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: sayamāś ca sarudrāś ca cakṣuraprārthayan vibhum
children.translated_text: with <s>Yama</s> and with the <s>Rudras</s>, sought sight of the all-pervading lord.

children.text: tebhyaś ca paramaṃ cakṣuḥ sarvadṛṣṭau ca śaktimat ||
children.translated_text: And to them he gave the supreme eye, powerful for seeing everything;

children.text: dadāvaṃbāpatiḥ śarvo bhavānyāś ca calasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s>, husband of <s>Ambā</s>, granted it so they could behold <s>Bhavānī</s> and the mountain-born Lord.
Having then obtained sight, the gods, headed by <s>Indra</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
with <s>Brahmā</s> and with <s>Śakra</s>, beheld <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: brahmādyā nemire tūrṇaṃ bhavānī ca girīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and the others quickly bowed to <s>Bhavānī</s> and <s>Girīśvara</s>;
the sages also bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s>, and the <s>Gaṇeśas</s> approved by <s>Śiva</s>.
The sky-going <s>Siddhas</s> and <s>Cāraṇas</s> sent down a shower of flowers.
The divine drums sounded; the sages praised the lord.
The foremost <s>Gandharvas</s> sang, and the companies of <s>Apsarases</s> danced.
All the lords of gaṇas were enraptured, and <s>Ambā Pārvatī</s> rejoiced.

children.text: tasya devī tadā hṛṣṭā samakṣaṃ tridivaukasām ||
children.translated_text: Then that delighted goddess, before the inhabitants of heaven,
placed a divine, fragrant garland at his feet.

children.text: sādhu sādhviti samprocya tayā tatraiva cārcitam ||
children.translated_text: Saying 'Good, good!' she worshiped him right there.
Together with the goddess, they bowed with their heads resting on the ground,
all the gods with <s>Brahmā</s>, along with <s>Yakṣas</s>, serpents, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge umāsvayaṃvaro nāma dvyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one-hundred-and-second chapter, named The Self-choice of <s>Umā</s>, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, having bowed to <s>Mahādeva</s> with joined palms,
said to <s>Maheśvara</s>, 'O god, let the wedding be performed.'
Hearing that statement of <s>Brahmā Parameṣṭhin</s>,
the lord, master of beings, said to the lord of the world, 'As you wish.'
For <s>Maheśa</s>'s wedding, at that very moment, O men of good vows,

children.text: brahmaṇā kalpitaṃ divyaṃ puraṃ ratnamayaṃ śubham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> fashioned a divine, auspicious city made of jewels.
Then <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Danu</s>, <s>Kadru</s>, and <s>Sukālikā</s> herself,

children.text: pulomā surasā caiva siṃhikā vinatā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pulomā</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Siṃhikā</s>, and likewise <s>Vinatā</s>,

children.text: siddhirmāyā kriyā durgā devī sākṣātsudhā svadhā
children.translated_text: <s>Siddhi</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, the goddess herself, <s>Sudhā</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>,

children.text: sāvitrī vedamātā ca rajanī dakṣiṇā dyutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāvitrī</s>, mother of the Veda, and <s>Rajanī</s>, <s>Dakṣiṇā</s>, <s>Dyuti</s>,

children.text: svāhā svāhāmatir buddhir ṛddhir vṛddhiḥ sarasvatī
children.translated_text: <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Svāhāmati</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Vṛddhi</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: rākā kuhūḥ sinīvālī devī anumatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rākā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Sinīvālī</s>, and also the goddess <s>Anumatī</s>,

children.text: dharaṇī dhāraṇī celā śacī nārāyaṇī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Dharaṇī</s>, <s>Dhāraṇī</s>, <s>Celā</s>, <s>Śacī</s>, and likewise <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>;

children.text: etāścānyāś ca devānāṃ mātaraḥ patnayas tathā ||
children.translated_text: these and other mothers and wives of the gods,
all went joyfully, saying, 'It is <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s wedding.'

children.text: uragā garuḍā yakṣā gandharvāḥ kinnarā gaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Serpents, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and gaṇas,

children.text: sāgarā girayo meghā māsāḥ saṃvatsarās tathā
children.translated_text: oceans, mountains, clouds, months, and years,

children.text: vedā mantrās tathā yajñāḥ stomā dharmāś ca sarvaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the Vedas, mantras, sacrifices, stomas, and all forms of <s>dharma</s>,
the <s>huṅkāra</s> and the <s>praṇava</s>, and thousands of <s>pratihāras</s>,
a crore of divine <s>Apsarases</s>, together with their attendants,

children.text: yāś ca sarveṣu dvīpeṣu devalokeṣu nimnagāḥ
children.translated_text: and all the rivers in all the continents and in the worlds of the gods,
all of them, assuming female bodies, assembled with joyful minds.
The greatly blessed lords of gaṇas, honored by all the worlds,
came there joyfully, saying, 'It is <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s wedding.'
The conch-colored lords of gaṇas approached with crores of gaṇas;

children.text: daśabhiḥ kekarākṣaś ca vidyuto'ṣṭābhir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kekarākṣa</s> came with ten crores, and <s>Vidyut</s> with eight.
<s>Viśākha</s> came with sixty-four crores, and <s>Pārayātrika</s> with nine;
glorious <s>Sarvāntaka</s> with six, and likewise <s>Vikṛtānana</s>.
<s>Jvālākeśa</s>, foremost among gaṇas, came with twelve crores,

children.text: saptabhiḥ samadaḥ śrīmān dundubho'ṣṭābhir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: glorious <s>Samada</s> with seven, and <s>Dundubha</s> with eight.

children.text: pañcabhiś ca kapālīśaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃdārakaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kapālīśa</s> came with five, and auspicious <s>Saṃdāraka</s> with six;
and here <s>Gaṇḍaka</s> and <s>Kumbhaka</s> came with crore upon crore.
<s>Viṣṭambha</s>, here with eight, and <s>Gaṇapa</s>, best of all beings,

children.text: pippalaś ca sahasreṇa saṃnādaś ca tathā dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Pippala</s> with a thousand, and <s>Saṃnāda</s> likewise, O twice-borns;
also <s>Āveṣṭana</s> with eight, and <s>Candratāpana</s> with seven,
and the gaṇapa <s>Mahākeśa</s>, surrounded by a thousand crores;

children.text: kuṇḍī dvādaśabhir vīras tathā parvatakaḥ śubhaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kuṇḍī</s> with twelve, the hero, and likewise auspicious <s>Parvataka</s>,

children.text: kālaś ca kālakaścaiva mahākālaḥ śatena vai ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Kālaka</s>, and <s>Mahākāla</s>, indeed with a hundred;

children.text: āgnikaḥ śatakoṭyā vai koṭyāgnimukha eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Āgnika</s> with a hundred crores, and <s>Agnimukha</s> with a crore,

children.text: ādityamūrdhā koṭyā ca tathā caiva dhanāvahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ādityamūrdhā</s> with a crore, and likewise <s>Dhanāvaha</s>;

children.text: saṃnāmaś ca śatenaiva kumudaḥ koṭibhis tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃnāma</s> with a hundred, and <s>Kumuda</s> with crores,
<s>Amogha</s> and <s>Kokila</s>, and <s>Sumantraka</s> with a crore of crores;
another, <s>Kākapāṭa</s>, with sixty, and lord <s>Saṃtānaka</s> with sixty,

children.text: mahābalaś ca navabhir madhupiṅgaś ca piṅgalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Mahābala</s> with nine, and <s>Madhupiṅga</s> and <s>Piṅgala</s>;
blue <s>Deveśa</s> with ninety, and likewise <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>,
and mighty <s>Caturvaktra</s> with seventy crores;
surrounded by twenty hundreds of thousands of crores upon crores,

children.text: tatrājagmus tathā devāste sarve śaṅkaraṃ bhavam ||
children.translated_text: all those gods then came there to <s>Śaṅkara</s>, to <s>Bhava</s>.
<s>Pramatha</s> came with a thousand crores of bhūtas (spirits), and <s>Vīrabhadra</s> with three crores,
and the hair-born ones with sixty-four crores.
And <s>Karaṇa</s> with twenty, and auspicious <s>Kevala</s> with ninety,

children.text: pañcākṣaḥ śatamanyuś ca meghamanyus tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pañcākṣa</s>, <s>Śatamanyu</s>, and likewise <s>Meghamanyu</s>;
<s>Kāṣṭhakūṭa</s> with sixty-four, and <s>Sukeśa</s> and <s>Vṛṣabha</s> likewise,
and blessed <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, eternal, with sixty-four;

children.text: tāluketuḥ ṣaḍāsyaś ca pañcāsyaś ca sanātanaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Tāluketu</s>, <s>Ṣaḍāsya</s>, and eternal <s>Pañcāsya</s>,

children.text: saṃvartakas tathā caitro lakulīśaḥ svayaṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: also <s>Saṃvartaka</s>, <s>Caitra</s>, and lord <s>Lakulīśa</s> himself;

children.text: lokāntakaś ca dīptāsyas tathā daityāntakaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Lokāntaka</s>, <s>Dīptāsya</s>, and lord <s>Daityāntaka</s>,
<s>Mṛtyuhṛt</s>, <s>Kālahā</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, and <s>Mṛtyuñjayakara</s> likewise;
<s>Viṣāda</s>, <s>Viṣada</s>, <s>Vidyuta</s>, and lord <s>Kāntaka</s>,

children.text: devo bhṛṅgī riṭiḥ śrīmān devadevapriyas tathā ||
children.translated_text: the god <s>Bhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Riṭi</s>, the glorious one, and <s>Devadevapriya</s> likewise;
<s>Aśani</s> and <s>Bhāsaka</s>, and <s>Sahasrapāt</s> with sixty-four;

children.text: ete cānye ca gaṇapā asaṃkhyātā mahābalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these and other gaṇapas, innumerable and very mighty,
all thousand-armed and wearing crowns of matted hair,
wearing the crescent moon as an ornament, blue-throated and three-eyed,
adorned with necklaces, earrings, armlets, crowns, and the like,
resembling <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, endowed with qualities such as aṇimā (minuteness),
the lords of the gaṇas, shining like crores of suns, came there,
moving in the underworld and dwelling in all the worlds.
<s>Tuṃbaru</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Hāhā</s>, and <s>Hūhū</s>, singers of Sāman hymns,
taking jewels and musical instruments, then came there to the city.
All the seers there, rich in austerity and praised by the gods,
with delighted minds chanted the auspicious wedding mantras.

children.text: tata evaṃ pravṛtte tu sarvataś ca samāgame
children.translated_text: Then, when the gathering had thus begun on every side,
after adorning that fair-smiling <s>Girijā</s> himself,
<s>Keśava</s>, taking her himself, led her into the city.
And in the assembly <s>Aja</s> addressed <s>Nārāyaṇa Hari</s>, lord of gods:
"You were produced first, together with <s>Bhavānī</s> and the deities,
from the left limb of this <s>Rudra</s>; I from the right limb, O lord.
The lord of the snowy mountain is my own form, indeed created for the sake of sacrifice;
this <s>Haimavatī</s> was born by the māyā of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.
You have come here for the promotion of śrauta and smārta rites, and for the wedding;

children.text: ato'sau jagatāṃ dhātrī dhātā tava mamāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: therefore she is the supporter of the worlds, the sustainer of you and of me as well.

children.text: asya devasya rudrasya mūrtibhir vihitaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: By the forms of this god <s>Rudra</s> the world has been ordained;
for <s>Bhava</s> is earth, water, fire, ether, moon, sun, self, and wind.
Even so, she must be given to him because of the word of the mountain and of me.

children.text: eṣā hy ajā śuklakṛṣṇā lohitā prakṛtirbhavān ||
children.translated_text: For she is the unborn <s>Prakṛti</s>, white, black, and red, O sir,
and this connection with the king of mountains is auspicious for you too.
In your Padma kalpa I was born from the lotus of your navel;
you are the guru of this mountain, who is a portion of me, and of me as well."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The god of gods <s>Janārdana</s> said to <s>Aja</s>, "Certainly."

children.text: devāś ca munayaḥ sarve devadevaś ca śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: The gods and all the sages, and <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the god of gods, were present.
Then learned <s>Padmanābha</s> rose and bowed to her.
The lotus-eyed one washed the feet of the god with his hands,

children.text: abhyukṣad ātmano mūrdhni brahmaṇaś ca gires tathā ||
children.translated_text: and sprinkled the water on his own head, and on that of <s>Brahmā</s> and of the mountain.
"For your marriage, this daughter of <s>Menā</s> is my younger sister."

children.text: ityuktvā sodakaṃ dattvā devīṃ deveśvarāya tām ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and given water, he gave that goddess to the lord of gods.
<s>Hari</s> even gave his own self to the god, together with water.
Then all the best sages, who had reached the meaning of all the Vedas,

children.text: ūcurdātā gṛhītā ca phalaṃ dravyaṃ vicārataḥ
children.translated_text: said, after considering donor, receiver, fruit, and substance:

children.text: eṣa devo haro nūnaṃ māyayā hi tato jagat ||
children.translated_text: "This god is surely <s>Hara</s>; through māyā the world comes from him."
Having said this, they bowed to him, their skin bristling with joy.
The sky-going siddhas and cāraṇas poured down showers of flowers.
The divine drums sounded, and the hosts of apsarases danced.
And the Vedas, embodied, bowed to that <s>Maheśvara</s>,
to the god of gods, husband of <s>Umā</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and the sages.
The god too, looking at the shy goddess, daughter of the snow mountain,

children.text: na tṛpyatyanavadyāṅgī sā ca devaṃ vṛṣadhvajam
children.translated_text: was not sated; nor was she, blameless-limbed, sated with the god <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.

children.text: varado 'smīti taṃ prāha hariṃ so'pyāha śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: He said to <s>Hari</s>, "I am the giver of boons"; he too said to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: tvayi bhaktiḥ prasīdeti brahmākhyāṃ ca dadau tu saḥ
children.translated_text: "May devotion to you be gracious to me," and he gave him the name connected with <s>Brahmā</s>.
Then again <s>Brahmā</s>, making a request to the lord, said:
"Standing in the position of preceptor, I shall offer the oblation into the fire.

children.text: dadāsi mama yadyājñāṃ kartavyo hyakṛto vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: If you grant me permission, the rite that has not yet been performed must be carried out."
Then <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the god of gods and lord of the world, said to that god:
"Whatever is desired, O best of gods, do that just as you wish.
I shall carry out your every word, O god of gods, O grandfather."
Then, bowing, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds, with delighted spirit,

children.text: hastaṃ devasya devyāś ca yuyoja paramaṃ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: joined the hand of the god with that of the goddess, the supreme lord.
And <s>Jvalana</s> himself stood there with joined palms.
With those śrauta great mantras present in embodied form,
having offered into the fire according to the prescribed rule, and the parched grains in due order,
and having honored the brahmins brought by <s>Viṣṇu</s> with various gifts,

children.text: triś ca taṃ jvalanaṃ devaṃ kārayitvā pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: he made the god circumambulate that <s>Jvalana</s> three times.
Then, releasing the joining of hands, together with all the gods,
and with all the gods and human beings, with a rejoicing inner heart,
blessed <s>Brahmā</s> bowed to the god of gods, the lord of <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pādyaṃ tayor dattvā śaṃbhorācamanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Then, having given pādya to the two of them, and likewise water for rinsing to <s>Śambhu</s>,

children.text: madhuparkaṃ tathā gāṃ ca praṇamya ca punaḥ śivam
children.translated_text: and also madhuparka and a cow, and having again bowed to <s>Śiva</s>,
blessed <s>Brahmā</s> stood with the gods headed by <s>Indra</s>.
All the sages beginning with <s>Bhṛgu</s>, with unbroken grains, sesame, and rice,
and those beginning with <s>Sūrya</s>, worshiped and praised <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
<s>Śiva</s>, completing what had been spoken by the gods and placing the fire within himself,
<s>Rudra</s> united with her for the welfare of all the worlds.
Whoever reads or hears the wedding of <s>Bhava</s> with a pure smile,
or causes it to be heard by pure brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,

children.text: sa labdhvā gāṇapatyaṃ ca bhavena saha modate
children.translated_text: obtaining the rank of a gaṇapati, rejoices together with <s>Bhava</s>.
Wherever this is recited by brahmins, <s>Bhava</s> remains there for that long.
Therefore, O twice-borns, one should worship according to rule and recite it, not otherwise.
At the weddings of eminent brahmins and of kṣatriyas, O best twice-borns,
this whole unsurpassed wedding of <s>Bhava</s> is to be recited.
Then <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>, having married the goddess <s>Haimavatī</s>,
together with his gaṇas, with <s>Nandin</s>, and surrounded by all the hosts of gods,
came, greatly radiant, to the divine city <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
To <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>, seated happily in <s>Avimukta</s>,
<s>Bhavānī</s>, with delighted face, bowed and asked about the greatness of the sacred field.
Then the one marked with the half-moon spoke of the supreme greatness of the sacred field:
"The greatness of <s>Avimukta</s> cannot be described at length
by me, O queen of the gods, for it is worshiped by hosts of seers.
What can I describe, O goddess, about the arising of the fruit of <s>Avimukta</s>,
where sinners, after dying, obtain liberation through a single birth?

children.text: anyatra tu kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ vārāṇasyāṃ vyapohati ||
children.translated_text: A sin committed elsewhere is removed in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
A sin committed in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> leads to ghosthood and hell.
For human beings, after committing thousands of sins, ghosthood is preferable,

children.text: na tu śakrasahasratvaṃ svarge kāśīpurīṃ vinā
children.translated_text: but not a thousandfold <s>Śakra</s>-hood in heaven without the city <s>Kāśī</s>.

children.text: yatra triviṣṭapo devo yatra viśveśvaro vibhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where there is the god of <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>, where there is the mighty <s>Viśveśvara</s>,
<s>Oṃkāreśa</s> and <s>Kṛttivāsa</s>, for those who die there there is no rebirth."
Having briefly stated the greatness of the sacred field, the moon-crested one
showed the garden, leaving behind the lords of the gaṇas.
There itself the blessed elephant-faced <s>Vināyaka</s> was born,
as an embodiment of obstacles for the daityas, and for the absence of obstacles for the gods.
This entire excellent essence of all stories has been told to you,
all just as I heard it, splendid through your favor.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge pārvatīvivāhavarṇanaṃ nāma tryadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-third chapter, named "The Description of <s>Pārvatī</s>'s Wedding."
The sages said:
"How was the elephant-faced <s>Vināyaka</s>, lord of the gaṇas, born?
And what was his power like? O <s>Sūta</s>, you ought to tell it here."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
At this point the gods, together with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, assembled.
Then, O twice-borns, they came to create an obstruction to the dharma of the daityas.
The asuras, yātudhānas, and rākṣasas, of cruel deeds,

children.text: tāmasāś ca tathā cānye rājasāś ca tathā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: and also other beings on earth, of tamasic and rajasic nature,
without impediment, honored <s>Maheśvara</s> with sacrifices, gifts, and the like,

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ ca hariṃ viprā labdhepsitavarā yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Hari</s>, O brahmins, because they had obtained the boons they desired.
Then, O best gods, victory would always arise for them.
Therefore, to obstruct them and to remove obstruction for the gods,
for the sake of sons for women and for the success of men's rites,
you should praise <s>Śaṅkara</s> so that he will create <s>Vighneśa</s>, the lord of the gaṇas.
Having spoken thus, they praised one another's stainless lord <s>Śiva</s>:
"Obeisance to you, the self of all, the all-knowing bearer of <s>Pināka</s>,
to the stainless one, to <s>Viriñca</s>, to the giver of what is needed for the goddess's purpose,
to the bodiless one, to the one whose body is meaning, to the one who removes the body of <s>Hari</s>,
to you who are established in the circle that is the support of nectar within the body,
obeisance to you who are time divided as the Kṛta age and the rest, and who are the speed of time,
to the one whose form is <s>Kālāgnirudra</s>, and to the one whose eightfold station begins with dharma,
to you whose body is purified by <s>Kālī</s>, and who are the cause of <s>Kālikā</s>,
to the dark-throated one, the chief one, to the vehicle, to the excellent one,
obeisance to you, lord of <s>Ambikā</s>, lord of gold.
And to the golden-seeded one, obeisance to <s>Śarva</s>, the trident-bearer."
Homage to you who bear a skull, staff, noose, sword, hide, and goad;

children.text: pataye haimavatyāś ca hemaśuklāya te namaḥ
children.translated_text: homage to you, the husband of <s>Haimavatī</s>, golden and white.
For the protection of the gods, homage to you who are yellow-white and whose path is dark.
Homage to the fifth one, and to the giver of fruits to those who perform the five great sacrifices.
Homage to you who wear a garland of five-faced serpents and are made of the five-syllabled mantra.
Homage to the one whose form is worshiped in fivefold ways by the gods of the fivefold isolation.
To you whose vision is the five-syllabled mantra, to you who are higher than the highest, homage.
Homage to the imperishable one whose face has the sixteen vowels as thunderbolt-like limbs.
Homage to you whose hands are the five beginning with ka, and whose hand begins with ca.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, whose feet are the series beginning with ṭa; homage to you whose feet are the series beginning with ta.
Homage to the one whose organ is the series beginning with pa, and who bears the seven constituents of any body.
Homage to the one whose own form is peace itself, and whose wrath reaches to final kṣa.
Homage to you whose limbs are la, va, repha, and ha, and who are without limbs.
Homage to the one who makes the inner resonance in the hearts of all beings.
Homage to the exceedingly radiant one, always seen by the good at the end of the brows.
Homage to the one whose eyes are sun, moon, and fire, whose nature is the supreme self.
Homage to you who stand above the three guṇas and whose feet are sacred fords.
Homage to you who are the truth and essence of the sacred fords, and who are beyond even that.
Homage again and again to you who are the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas, and the syllable Oṃ.
Taking on a threefold form in Oṃ, you dwell above.
You are yellow, dark-colored, red, and of supreme splendor.
You abide in the five stations and, in fivefold order, beyond the cosmic egg.
Homage again and again to you as <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Kumāra</s>.
Homage to you, supreme lord of <s>Ambā</s>, who move above all.
Homage to you whose form is root and subtle, who are both gross and subtle.
Homage to you who are empty of all intentions and safeguarded beyond all things.
Homage again and again to you who are without beginning, middle, or end, and established as consciousness.
Homage to you who are worshiped by <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the waters, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, and night-roamers,

children.text: diṅmukhe diṅmukhe nityaṃ sagaṇaiḥ pūjitāya te ||
children.translated_text: always, with their hosts, at every face of every direction.
Homage to you who are worshiped everywhere, always, on every path.
Homage to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Rudranīla</s>, to <s>Kadrudra</s>, to <s>Pracetās</s>,
homage to you, <s>Maheśvara</s>, the steadfast one, directly <s>Śiva</s> himself.

children.text: atha śṛṇu bhagavan stavacchalena kathitamajendramukhaiḥ surāsureśaiḥ
children.translated_text: Now listen, Blessed One: by the lords of gods and asuras, headed by <s>Aja</s> and <s>Indra</s>, this has been spoken under the pretext of a hymn;
forgive the wondrous deeds: the destruction of sacrifice, of <s>Madana</s>, of <s>Yama</s>, of <s>Agni</s>, and of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: yaḥ paṭhettu stavaṃ bhaktyā śakrāgnipramukhaiḥ suraiḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever reads with devotion this hymn praised by the gods beginning with <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Agni</s>,

children.text: kīrtitaṃ śrāvayedvidvān sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and whoever, being learned, causes it to be heard, goes to the supreme goal.
Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-fourth chapter, named 'The Praise by the Gods.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When the lords of gods stood there after bowing in this way to the Lord,
then <s>Bhava</s>, lord of <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, bearer of the <s>Pināka</s> bow,
granted them his glance in an instant; <s>Bhava</s> looked upon those best of gods,
and the gods bowed reverently to <s>Hara</s>, their eyes moist with joy.
With glances like nectar and ambrosia, <s>Bhava</s>, by looking on them,
then <s>Maheśvara</s> said to the lords of gods, 'May there be welfare for you.'
'For the sake of a boon, O Lord, these gods have come to your house.'

children.text: praṇamya cāha vākpatiḥ patiṃ nirīkṣya nirbhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed, <s>Vākpati</s> spoke fearlessly, looking upon the Lord.
'You are always entreated, without obstruction, by beings other than gods,
by those who act to harm the gods, for the accomplishment of all their undertakings.
Therefore may you be gracious: become the cause of obstacle-making action
for those who harm the gods. This alone is our boon here.'
Then, having heard that, the wielder of <s>Pināka</s>, the lord of gods,
that <s>Śiva</s>, assumed a form as <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>, lord of the gods.
The lords of the hosts and the lords of gods praised <s>Maheśvara</s>,
the auspicious one, source of all worlds and remover of the distress of existence.
He took a boon-giving form, resting on an elephant face and bearing trident and noose;
then <s>Ambikā</s> beheld <s>Gajānana</s>, born for all the worlds.

children.text: daduḥ puṣpavarṣaṃ hi siddhā munīndrās tathā khecarā devasaṃghāstadānīm
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Siddhas</s>, chief sages, sky-goers, and hosts of gods sent down a shower of flowers.

children.text: tadā tuṣṭuvuścaikadantaṃ sureśāḥ praṇemurgaṇeśaṃ maheśaṃ vitandrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the lords of gods praised <s>Ekadanta</s> and, diligent, bowed to <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, the great lord.
Then from the two of them emerged a very fierce embodied being;
the child stood and danced, the abode of every auspicious thing.
The elephant-faced one was adorned with variegated clothes and ornaments;
the little son of <s>Maheśvara</s> bowed to his father and to <s>Ambikā</s>.
Seeing his son as soon as he was born, the blessed <s>Bhava</s>,
the Lord of all himself performed all the rites for <s>Gajānana</s>.

children.text: ādāya ca karābhyāṃ ca susukhābhyāṃ bhavaḥ svayam
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhava</s> himself took him with both his gentle hands,
and <s>Mahādeva</s>, teacher of the world, embraced him and smelled his head.
'Your descent, my son, is for the destruction of the <s>Daityas</s>,
and for the benefit of the gods and of the twice-born expounders of <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: yajñaś ca dakṣiṇāhīnaḥ kṛto yena mahītale
children.translated_text: For one by whom a sacrifice is performed on earth without dakṣiṇā,

children.text: tasya dharmasya vighnaṃ ca kuru svargapathe sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: create an obstacle to that <s>dharma</s> while you stand on the path to heaven.

children.text: adhyāpanaṃ cādhyayanaṃ vyākhyānaṃ karma eva ca
children.translated_text: Teaching, study, exposition, and ritual action:
whoever performs these improperly in this world, always take away his life.
O best of men, from women and men fallen from their varṇa,
and devoid of their own <s>dharma</s>, take away their lives, O lord.

children.text: yāḥ striyastvāṃ sadā kālaṃ puruṣāś ca vināyaka
children.translated_text: The women and men, O <s>Vināyaka</s>, who worship you at all times,

children.text: yajanti tāsāṃ teṣāṃ ca tvatsāmyaṃ dātumarhasi ||
children.translated_text: you should grant them equality with yourself.
Protect your devotees with every effort, O young lord of the gaṇas.'

children.text: yauvanasthāṃś ca vṛddhāṃś ca ihāmutra ca pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by those in youth and by the aged; you will be honored here and in the next world.
In the three worlds, here and everywhere, you are indeed the lord of the hosts of obstacles,

children.text: saṃpūjyo vandanīyaś ca bhaviṣyasi na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and you will be worshiped and worthy of veneration; there is no doubt.

children.text: māṃ ca nārāyaṇaṃ vāpi brahmāṇam api putraka
children.translated_text: Even if they worship me, or <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, or even <s>Brahmā</s>, my son,
with sacrifices performed by Brahmins, you will be worshiped first.

children.text: tvām anabhyarcya kalyāṇaṃ śrautaṃ smārtaṃ ca laukikam
children.translated_text: If anyone performs an auspicious rite, whether śrauta, smārta, or worldly, without first honoring you, auspicious one,
his auspicious act will become inauspicious.
By Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras, O elephant-faced one,
you are to be worshiped for every accomplishment with fine foods, eatables, and the like.
In all the three worlds, without honoring you with perfumes, flowers, incense, and the rest,

children.text: devairapi tathānyaiś ca labdhavyaṃ nāsti kutracit ||
children.translated_text: nothing at all is obtainable anywhere, even by the gods or by others.
Those people, human beings, who worship <s>Vināyaka</s>

children.text: te cārcanīyāḥ śakrādyair bhaviṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will become worthy of worship by <s>Śakra</s> and the others; there is no doubt.

children.text: ajaṃ hariṃ ca māṃ vāpi śakramanyānsurānapi
children.translated_text: Those who seek results and worship <s>Aja</s>, <s>Hari</s>, me, <s>Śakra</s>, or other gods,
but do not worship you, you shall afflict with obstacles.

children.text: sasarja ca tadā vighnagaṇaṃ gaṇapatiḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Then the lord <s>Gaṇapati</s> created the host of obstacles,
and, after bowing together with the hosts, he stood before him.
From that time onward, people in this world worship <s>Gaṇeśvara</s>,
and that <s>Gaṇeśvara</s> caused obstruction to the dharma of the Daityas.
This whole origin of <s>Skanda</s>'s elder brother has been told to you.
Whoever reads it, hears it, or has it recited becomes happy.
Thus, in the first part of the holy <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-fifth chapter, named 'The Origin of <s>Vināyaka</s>'.
The sages said:

children.text: nṛtyārambhaḥ kathaṃ śaṃbhoḥ kimarthaṃ vā yathātatham
children.translated_text: How did the beginning of <s>Śambhu</s>'s dance take place, and for what purpose, exactly?
You should tell us; the birth of <s>Skanda</s>'s elder brother has been heard.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Dāruka</s>, born among the Asuras and having gained prowess through austerity,
destroyed the gods and the best of Brahmins like the fire at the end of time.
At that time the gods, struck by <s>Dāruka</s> and deeply oppressed,

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ ca tatheśānaṃ kumāraṃ viṣṇumeva ca ||
children.translated_text: approached <s>Brahmā</s>, and likewise <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Together with <s>Yama</s> and <s>Indra</s>, they knew that the Asura was to be slain by a woman,
while <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, praiseworthy and assuming female forms, stood in battle.

children.text: bādhitāstena te sarve brahmāṇaṃ prāpya vai dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: All those beings, afflicted by him, approached <s>Brahmā</s>, O twice-born ones,
and, after informing him of all that, together with him they approached the lord of <s>Umā</s>.
They all praised him, with the Grandfather at their head,

children.text: brahmā prāpya ca deveśaṃ praṇamya bahudhā nataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s>, having come to the lord of the gods, bowed down with many prostrations.
'The blessed <s>Dāru</s> is terrible; formerly we were conquered by him.
Please kill the Daitya <s>Dāruka</s>, who is to be slain by a woman, and rescue us.'
Hearing <s>Brahmā</s>'s petition, the blessed destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye,
the lord of the gods, spoke to the goddess <s>Girijā</s>, as if smiling:
'Auspicious one, today I ask you for the welfare of the worlds,
fair-faced lady, for the sake of slaying this <s>Dāruka</s>, who is destined to be slain by a woman.'

children.text: atha sā tasya vacanaṃ niśamya jagato'raṇiḥ
children.translated_text: Then she, hearing his words, the fire-drill of the world,
entered the body of the god, the goddess of gods intent on taking birth.
Having entered the excellent god, the lord of gods, with a single portion,
she was not perceived then by <s>Brahmā</s> or by the gods headed by <s>Indra</s>.
Seeing <s>Girijā</s> standing beside <s>Śambhu</s> just as before,
even the all-knowing four-faced one was bewildered by her māyā.

children.text: sā praviṣṭā tanuṃ tasya devadevasya pārvatī
children.translated_text: That <s>Pārvatī</s> had entered the body of the god of gods,
and by means of the poison lodged in his throat she then made that body her own.

children.text: tāṃ ca jñātvā tathābhūtāṃ tṛtīyenekṣaṇena vai
children.translated_text: Knowing her to have become so, with his third eye,
the enemy of <s>Kāma</s> created <s>Kālī</s>, black-throated and matted-haired.

children.text: jātā yadā kālimakālakaṇṭhī jātā tadānīṃ vipulā jayaśrīḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Kālī</s>, dark and black-throated, was born, then vast victory and splendor arose,
while defeat and failure came to the non-gods, and satisfaction came to <s>Bhavānī</s> and <s>Parameśvara</s>.

children.text: jātāṃ tadānīṃ surasiddhasaṃghā dṛṣṭvā bhayād dudruvur agnikalpām
children.translated_text: At that time, seeing her born like fire, the hosts of gods and Siddhas fled in fear,
from <s>Kālī</s>, whose dark throat was adorned with poison, with <s>Upendra</s>, the lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śakra</s> foremost among them.

children.text: tathaiva jātaṃ nayanaṃ lalāṭe sitāṃśulekhā ca śirasyudagrā
children.translated_text: Likewise an eye appeared on her forehead, and a lofty crescent moon upon her head,

children.text: kaṇṭhe karālaṃ niśitaṃ triśūlaṃ kare karālaṃ ca vibhūṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: a terrible sharp trident at her neck and in her hand, and fearsome ornaments.
Together with divine garments, the goddess was adorned with every ornament,

children.text: siddhendrasiddhāś ca tathā piśācā jajñire punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and Siddhas, lords of Siddhas, and Piśācas also came into being again.
At the command of that <s>Pārvatī</s>, the supreme goddess,
she slew the Dānava <s>Dāruka</s>, who had been destroying the lords of the gods.
Because of the excessive force of her fury, this whole world
became afflicted then by the fire of her anger, O foremost Brahmins.
<s>Bhava</s> too, in the form of an infant, in a cremation ground crowded with corpses,

children.text: ruroda māyayā tasyāḥ krodhāgniṃ pātum īśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: cried by means of his māyā, in order to drink up her fire of anger.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bālamīśānaṃ māyayā tasya mohitā
children.translated_text: Seeing that infant <s>Īśāna</s>, she was bewildered by his māyā,

children.text: utthāpyāghrāya vakṣojaṃ stanaṃ sā pradadau dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and, lifting him up and smelling him, she gave him the breast, O twice-born ones.

children.text: stanajena tadā sārdhaṃ kopamasyāḥ papau punaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, together with the breast-milk, he again drank up her anger.
Through that anger, the child became the protector of sacred fields.
And there were eight forms of that wise <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> as well.

children.text: evaṃ vai tena bālena kṛtā sā krodhamūrchitā ||
children.translated_text: In this way, by that child, she was brought under control while overcome by anger.
For the sake of winning her favor, the tāṇḍava was performed by the god of gods.
At twilight, with all the lords of beings and with the pretas, by the pleased trident-bearer,
the supreme goddess, having drunk up to her throat the nectar of <s>Śambhu</s>'s dance,

children.text: nanarta sā ca yoginyaḥ pretasthāne yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: danced; and the yoginīs too danced in the place of pretas as they pleased.
There the gods, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>, on every side
bowed and praised <s>Kālī</s>, and again the goddess <s>Pārvatī</s>.

children.text: evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ tāṇḍavaṃ śūlinaḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: Thus, in brief, the <s>tāṇḍava</s> of the lord <s>Śūlin</s> has been described;
others also call it the <s>tāṇḍava</s> of the all-pervading lord, born of the bliss of yoga.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge śivatāṇḍavakathanaṃ nāma ṣaḍadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-and-sixth chapter, named "The Account of <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>Tāṇḍava</s>."
The sages said:
Formerly, O <s>Sūta</s>, how did <s>Upamanyu</s> obtain lordship over the gaṇas from <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and how was the ocean of milk obtained? You ought to tell us this now.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: evaṃ kālīm upālabhya gate deve triyaṃbake
children.translated_text: Thus, after the god <s>Tryambaka</s> had reproached <s>Kālī</s> and departed,
<s>Upamanyu</s>, having worshiped him, obtained the fruit through austerity.
The sage known as <s>Upamanyu</s>, O best of twice-borns,
was radiant like <s>Kumāra</s>, playing about as chance led him.

children.text: kadācit kṣīram alpaṃ ca pītavān mātulāśrame
children.translated_text: Once, in his maternal uncle's hermitage, he drank a little milk,

children.text: īrṣyayā mātulasuto hy apibat kṣīram uttamam ||
children.translated_text: while his maternal uncle's son, out of envy, drank excellent milk.

children.text: pītvā sthitaṃ yathākāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā provāca mātaram
children.translated_text: Seeing him standing there as he pleased after drinking it, he spoke to his mother:
"Mother, mother, greatly fortunate ascetic, give me some,
very sweet cow's milk, warm and not scant; I bow to you."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus coaxed by her son, she embraced her son with affection;
distressed and pained, she lamented, remembering her own poverty.
But <s>Upamanyu</s> too, O brahmins, remembering the milk again and again,
said to her, "Give it, give it," as he cried, the greatly radiant one.

children.text: uñchavṛttyārjitān bījān svayaṃ piṣṭvā ca sā tadā
children.translated_text: Then she herself ground seeds obtained by gleaning,
and the sweet-speaking woman mixed that seed flour with water.

children.text: aihyehi mama putreti sāmapūrvaṃ tataḥ sutam
children.translated_text: Then, with gentle words, "Come, come, my son,"
she embraced him, took up her son, and, afflicted with sorrow, gave him artificial milk.

children.text: pītvā ca kṛtrimaṃ kṣīraṃ mātrā dattaṃ dvijottamāḥ
children.translated_text: Having drunk the artificial milk given by his mother, O best of twice-borns,
he said to his mother, in great distress, "This is not milk."

children.text: duḥkhitā sā tadā prāha samprekṣyāghrāya mūrdhani
children.translated_text: Then she, distressed, looked at him, smelled the crown of his head,
and with her hands wiped the lotus-wide eyes of her son.
"Those rivers, filled with jewels, lie within the range of heaven and the netherworlds;

children.text: bhāgyahīnā na paśyanti bhaktihīnāś ca ye śive ||
children.translated_text: those who are without fortune and without devotion to <s>Śiva</s> do not see them.

children.text: rājyaṃ svargaṃ ca mokṣaṃ ca bhojanaṃ kṣīrasaṃbhavam
children.translated_text: Kingdom, heaven, liberation, food, and what is born from milk,

children.text: na labhante priyāṇyeṣāṃ no tuṣyati sadā bhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: these dear things they do not obtain, nor is <s>Bhava</s> ever pleased with them.
Everything is born from <s>Bhava</s>'s grace, not from the grace of another god.
Those devoted to other gods wander about afflicted by sorrow.

children.text: kṣīraṃ tatra kuto 'smākaṃ mahādevo na pūjitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whence could there be milk for us, when <s>Mahādeva</s> has not been worshiped?
What was given in a former birth by striving toward <s>Śiva</s>, O son,

children.text: tadeva labhyaṃ nānyattu viṣṇumudyamya vā prabhum
children.translated_text: that alone is obtained, and nothing else, even by striving toward <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord."
Hearing his mother's words, <s>Upamanyu</s>, greatly radiant,
though only a boy, bowed down and spoke to his ascetic mother:
"Abandon grief, greatly fortunate one; if <s>Mahādeva</s> exists anywhere,
whether after a long time or after a short time, I shall obtain the ocean of milk."
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tāṃ praṇamyaivamuktvā sa tapaḥ kartuṃ pracakrame ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed to her and spoken thus, he set about performing austerity.

children.text: tamāha mātā suśubhaṃ kurviti sutarāṃ sutam
children.translated_text: His mother said to her son, "May it be very auspicious; do it,"
and, permitted by her, he practiced there an extremely difficult austerity.
Having reached Mount <s>Himavat</s>, concentrated and living on air,
through that brahmin's austerity the world became smoke-tormented.
All those best gods bowed and spoke to <s>Hari</s>;
then, having heard their words, the blessed <s>Puruṣottama</s>

children.text: kimidaṃ tviti saṃcintya jñātvā tatkāraṇaṃ ca saḥ
children.translated_text: thought, "What is this?" and, knowing its cause,
quickly went to <s>Mandara</s>, wishing to see <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Seeing the god and bowing, he said this with joined palms:
"Blessed lord, a certain brahmin, known as <s>Upamanyu</s>,
is burning up everything with austerity for the sake of milk; restrain him."
Meanwhile the god <s>Pinākī</s>, the supreme lord,

children.text: śakrarūpaṃ samāsthāya gantuṃ cakre matiṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: assumed the form of <s>Śakra</s> and then resolved to go.

children.text: atha jagāma munestu tapovanaṃ gajavareṇa sitena sadāśivaḥ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Sadāśiva</s> went to the sage's grove of austerity on a noble white elephant,
together with gods, asuras, siddhas, and great serpents, himself assuming the body of the king of immortals.

children.text: sahaiva cāruhya tadā dvipaṃ taṃ pragṛhya vālavyajanaṃ vivasvān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vivasvān</s>, mounting that elephant along with him, took up the yak-tail fan,

children.text: vāmena śacyā sahitaṃ surendraṃ kareṇa cānyena sitātapatram ||
children.translated_text: while <s>Surendra</s>, accompanied by <s>Śacī</s> on his left, held a white parasol in his other hand.
The blessed <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s> in the form of <s>Śakra</s>, shone forth
with the white parasol, like <s>Mandara</s> with the disk of the moon.
Thus assuming the very form of <s>Śakra</s>, the supreme lord
went to <s>Upamanyu</s>'s hermitage in order to bestow favor.
Seeing that supreme lord, <s>Śiva</s>, bearing the form of <s>Śakra</s>,
the sage himself, O best sages, bowed with his head and said:
"This hermitage of mine has been purified, for the lord of gods himself,
<s>Śakra</s>, lord of the world, the blessed lord, has arrived together with <s>Bhānu</s>."
After he had spoken thus and stood with the hollow of his joined hands raised,
<s>Hara</s>, bearing the form of <s>Śakra</s>, looked at the twice-born and said in a deep voice:

children.text: tuṣṭo'smi te varaṃ brūhi tapasānena suvrata
children.translated_text: "I am pleased with you; choose a boon by this austerity, O good-vowed one."
I shall give all the things you desire, O elder brother of <s>Dhaumya</s>, great-minded one.
When the best of sages had thus been addressed then by that <s>Śakra</s>,
he said with joined palms, "I choose devotion to <s>Śiva</s>."
Then, hearing the sage's words, the lord, as if angry,
himself bearing the form of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Īśāna</s> spoke in agitation:
"Do you not know me, O divine sage, as the lord, the king of the gods,
<s>Śakra</s>, ruler of the three worlds, honored by all the gods?
Become my devotee, O brahmin sage; worship me alone always.

children.text: dadāmi sarvaṃ bhadraṃ te tyaja rudraṃ ca nirguṇam ||
children.translated_text: I shall give you everything auspicious. Abandon <s>Rudra</s>, who is without qualities."
Then, having heard <s>Śakra</s>'s words, which tore the ears,
<s>Upamanyu</s> said this while muttering the auspicious five-syllabled mantra:

children.text: manye śakrasya rūpeṇa nūnam atrāgataḥ svayam
children.translated_text: "Surely some lowest daitya has come here in the form of <s>Śakra</s> himself,

children.text: kartuṃ daityādhamaḥ kaścid dharmavighnaṃ ca nānyathā ||
children.translated_text: to make an obstruction to dharma, and not otherwise.
For you yourself, devoted to reviling <s>Bhava</s>, have said all this,
and, in passing, that the great-souled god of gods is without qualities.
