What need is there of saying much here? Today a great thing has been inferred by me:

children.text: bhavāntarakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ śrutā nindā bhavasya tu ||
children.translated_text: because abuse of <s>Bhava</s> has been heard, there must be sin committed in another birth.
After hearing abuse of <s>Bhava</s>, one should abandon

children.text: svadehaṃ taṃ nihatyāśu śivalokaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: one's own body that very instant; having struck down the abuser at once, he goes to the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Whoever tears out with speech the tongue of one devoted to abusing <s>Śiva</s>,
after raising up twenty-one generations, goes to the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Enough, then, of my desire for milk from this lowest of gods.
Having slain you with the weapon of <s>Śiva</s>, I shall abandon this body.

children.text: purā mātrā tu kathitaṃ tathyameva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: What was formerly told by my mother is true indeed; there is no doubt:
in a previous birth the lord was not worshiped by us."
Having spoken thus to that god, <s>Upamanyu</s>, fearless,

children.text: śakraṃ cakre matiṃ hantum atharvāstreṇa mantravit ||
children.translated_text: knower of mantras, resolved to kill <s>Śakra</s> with the Atharvan weapon.
The greatly radiant one took a handful of ash from the ash-container,

children.text: atharvāstraṃ tatastasmai sasarja ca nanāda ca ||
children.translated_text: then hurled that Atharvan weapon at him and roared.

children.text: dagdhuṃ svadeham āgneyīṃ dhyātvā vai dhāraṇāṃ tadā
children.translated_text: And then, meditating on a fiery concentration in order to burn his own body,
the greatly radiant, imperishable one stood like dry fuel.
When the brahmin had thus resolved, the blessed destroyer of <s>Bhaga</s>'s eye
checked that yogin's concentration by a gentle one.

children.text: atharvāstraṃ tadā tasya saṃhṛtaṃ candrakeṇa tu
children.translated_text: At that time his Atharvan weapon, like the fire of time,
was withdrawn by <s>Candraka</s>, and likewise by the command of <s>Nandin</s>.
The blessed <s>Parameśvara</s>, assuming his own form,
showed himself to the brahmin with the young moon set as his crest.
He showed a thousand streams of milk, and the ocean of milk itself,
an ocean of curds and the other substances, and also an ocean of ghee,
an ocean of fruit, and for the boy an ocean of foods to be chewed and eaten,
and mountains of cakes too stood on every side.
Smiling, the blessed one, surrounded by his kinsmen, spoke to <s>Upamanyu</s>.

children.text: girijām avalokya sasmitāṃ saghṛṇaṃ prekṣyatu taṃ tadā ghṛṇī ||
children.translated_text: Looking at smiling <s>Girijā</s>, and then compassionately gazing at him, the compassionate one said:

children.text: bhuṅkṣva bhogānyathākāmaṃ bāndhavaiḥ paśya vatsa me
children.translated_text: "Enjoy pleasures as you wish with your relatives. Behold, my child:
O greatly fortunate <s>Upamanyu</s>, this <s>Pārvatī</s> is your mother.
Today you have been made my son by me, and the ocean of milk has been given to you,
as well as an ocean of honey and an ocean of curds.
There is also an ocean of rice cooked with ghee, and an ocean of fruits and lickable foods,
and mountains of cakes too, and again an ocean of foods to be chewed and eaten.

children.text: pitā tava mahādevaḥ pitā vai jagatāṃ mune
children.translated_text: <s>Mahādeva</s> is your father, O sage, indeed the father of the worlds;

children.text: mātā tava mahābhāgā jaganmātā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: your greatly fortunate mother is the mother of the world, without doubt.

children.text: amaratvaṃ mayā dattaṃ gāṇapatyaṃ ca śāśvatam
children.translated_text: Immortality has been given by me, and eternal lordship among the gaṇas.
Choose boons; I shall grant them. No hesitation should be made here."
Having spoken thus, <s>Mahādeva</s> took him with both hands,
smelled him on the head, and then <s>Bhava</s>, the lord, gave him to the goddess.
Seeing her son, the goddess, daughter of the lord of mountains,
being pleased, then gave him yogic sovereignty and knowledge of brahman, O best twice-borns.

children.text: so'pi labdhvā varaṃ tasyāḥ kumāratvaṃ ca sarvadā
children.translated_text: He too, having received her boon and perpetual boyhood,
praised <s>Mahādeva</s> with a voice choked by joy.
Then, with joined palms, he asked the boon-worthy one, whose eyes were stainless, for a boon,
having bowed down again and again.
"Be gracious, O lord of the gods of gods. May there be in me unwavering

children.text: śraddhā caiva mahādeva sānnidhyaṃ caiva sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: faith in you, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, and also your presence always."
When he had been addressed thus by him, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, as if laughing,
granted what the brahmin desired and disappeared right there.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe pūrvabhāge upamanyucaritaṃ nāma saptādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-seventh chapter, named "The Deeds of <s>Upamanyu</s>."
The sages said:
"He was seen by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of unwearied action.
Then the elder brother of <s>Dhaumya</s> obtained the divine Pāśupata vow.

children.text: kathaṃ labdhaṃ tadā jñānaṃ tasmātkṛṣṇena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: How was that knowledge then obtained from him by wise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?
You ought to tell that sin-destroying story, O <s>Sūta</s>."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Although the eternal <s>Vāsudeva</s> had descended by his own will,
he purified his body while blaming its human condition.
For the sake of a son, the blessed one went there to perform austerity,
to the hermitage of <s>Upamanyu</s>, and saw that sage there.
Having seen that elder brother of <s>Dhaumya</s>, O twice-borns, he bowed to him.

children.text: bahumānena vai kṛṣṇastriḥ kṛtvā vai pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: With great respect <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> performed circumambulation three times.
By merely beholding that sage, for the wise <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

children.text: naṣṭameva malaṃ sarvaṃ kāyajaṃ karmmajaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: all impurity born of the body and also born of karma was destroyed.
The greatly radiant <s>Upamanyu</s>, after smearing him with ash,
with the sequence beginning, O best brahmins, with 'you are Agni' and 'you are Vāyu,'
gave him the divine Pāśupata knowledge, his mind well pleased.
Through the sage's favor, O twice-borns, that honored <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> became esteemed among the Pāśupatas.
Then, after one year of austerity, having seen the god <s>Maheśvara</s>,
with <s>Ambā</s>, with his gaṇas, and undisturbed, he obtained a son for himself.
From that time onward, all the divine Pāśupata sages of strict vows

children.text: divyāḥ pāśupatāḥ sarve tasthuḥ saṃvṛtya sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: always stood around that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, surrounding him.

children.text: anyaṃ ca kathayiṣyāmi muktyarthaṃ prāṇināṃ sadā
children.translated_text: I shall tell you something else too, always for the liberation of living beings.
Having made a golden girdle, a support, and a staff to be carried,

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ piṇḍikaṃ cāpi vyajanaṃ daṇḍameva ca
children.translated_text: as well as a golden seat, a fan, and a staff,
men, or women also, should provide an ink-pot and a writing implement.

children.text: kṣurāḥ kartarikā cāpi atha pātramathāpi vā
children.translated_text: Razors and scissors, and also a vessel,
should be given to a Pāśupata whose body is smeared with ash.

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi tāmraṃ vātha nivedayet
children.translated_text: One should present something of gold, or of silver, or else of copper.
The wise person should worship the yogin according to his own wealth.
All those people, freed from sin and together with all their families,

children.text: yānti rudrapadaṃ divyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: go to the divine state of <s>Rudra</s>; no doubt should be entertained here.
Therefore, by this gift the householder is freed from worldly existence.
Through bestowing it upon yogins, <s>Śiva</s> is quickly pleased.

children.text: rājyaṃ putraṃ dhanaṃ bhavyamaśvaṃ yānamathāpi vā
children.translated_text: A kingdom, a son, wealth, auspicious goods, a horse, or even a vehicle,
or all one's possessions, should be given if one desires the highest <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
With the impermanent body, the permanent goal should be accomplished with effort.
The auspicious Pāśupata observance is eternal and carries one across the ocean of saṃsāra.

children.text: etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ saṃkṣepānna ca saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: All this has been told to you in brief, and there is no doubt.
Whoever reads it or hears it goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Thus, in the first part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the one-hundred-eighth chapter.
The sages said:
By what is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lord of the lords of all the gods, pleased here?
You, O <s>Sūta</s>, knower of all meanings, ought to tell this to us.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In ancient times the great sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, of great splendor, was asked
by <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, O best brahmins; I shall tell that just as it was.
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:
O sage, you have reached the far shore of all dharmas, O great-minded one.
O <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, you are ancient and skilled in the meaning of the Purāṇas.
Among the divine dharmas relating to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, what is the best and highest?
Tell that here, O very wise one, for the devotees, O you of good vows.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having heard those words of his, he rose up with joined palms,

children.text: smaran nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ kṛṣṇam acyutam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: remembering the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the imperishable.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O king, in due order, to what is holy and has <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as its essence:
remembering, worshiping, and bowing down with devotion.
Each of these is said to be equal to an aśvamedha sacrifice.

children.text: ya ekaḥ puruṣaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ paramātmā janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the one supreme person, the supreme self, <s>Janārdana</s>.
From him comes <s>Brahmā</s>, and by taking refuge in him everything is indeed liberated.
I shall proclaim the one dharma that I have seen and known.

children.text: purā tretāyuge kaścit kauśiko nāma vai dvijaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, in the <s>Tretā</s> age, there was a certain twice-born man named <s>Kauśika</s>.
He was always devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s> and constantly delighted in the singing of Sāman chants.
At meals, while sitting, and on his bed, his mind was always fixed on him,
as he sang again and again of the noble deeds of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Having reached the place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the unsurpassed sacred field of <s>Hari</s>,
he sang of <s>Hari</s> there, endowed with measure, syllabic pattern, and rhythm.
It was varied by the joining of musical modes and notes and by distinctions of pitch.

children.text: bhaktiyogaṃ samāpanno bhikṣāmātraṃ hi tatra vai ||
children.translated_text: He had attained <s>bhaktiyoga</s> (devotional discipline), and there he lived only on alms.
Seeing him singing there in this way, a certain twice-born man at that time,

children.text: padmākhya iti vikhyātastasmai cānnaṃ dadau tadā ||
children.translated_text: famous as <s>Padmākhya</s>, then gave him food.

children.text: sakuṭumbo mahātejā hyuṣṇamannaṃ hi tatra vai
children.translated_text: That greatly radiant man, together with his family, gave hot food there.

children.text: kauśiko hi tadā hṛṣṭo gāyannāste hariṃ prabhum ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kauśika</s>, delighted, remained there singing of <s>Hari</s> the lord.

children.text: śṛṇvannāste sa padmākhyaḥ kāle kāle vinirgataḥ
children.translated_text: That <s>Padmākhya</s> remained listening, going out at the proper times.

children.text: kālayogena samprāptāḥ śiṣyā vai kauśikasya ca ||
children.translated_text: In the course of time the disciples of <s>Kauśika</s> also arrived.
There were seven, born in families of kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and brahmins,
abundant in knowledge and learning, pure, and wholly devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: teṣām api tathānnādyaṃ padmākṣaḥ pradadau svayam
children.translated_text: <s>Padmākṣa</s> himself likewise gave food and provisions to them too.
Together with his disciples, <s>Kauśika</s>, with a delighted mind,
stayed there at the place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, singing of <s>Hari</s> according to rule.
There also was a vaiśya named <s>Mālava</s>, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
With a pleased mind he regularly made garlands of lamps for <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: mālavī nāma bhāryā ca tasya nityaṃ pativratā ||
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Mālavī</s>, was always devoted to her husband.
Having smeared the sacred field of <s>Hari</s> all around with cow-dung,
she stayed there happily with her husband, listening to the excellent song.
From <s>Kuśasthala</s> there came brahmins of praised vows,
fifty of them came for the sake of the excellent singing of <s>Hari</s>.
Carrying out the tasks of the great-souled <s>Kauśika</s>,
knowers of the truth of knowledge, learning, and meaning, they lived there listening.

children.text: khyātamāsīttadā tasya gānaṃ vai kauśikasya tat
children.translated_text: At that time that song of his, of <s>Kauśika</s>, became well known.
Hearing it, the king <s>Kaliṅga</s> approached and spoke these words.

children.text: kauśikādya gaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ gāyasveha ca māṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: "<s>Kauśika</s>, now sing of me here again, together with your groups,

children.text: śṛṇudhvaṃ ca tathā yūyaṃ kuśasthalajanā api ||
children.translated_text: and you people of <s>Kuśasthala</s> also listen."

children.text: tacchrutvā kauśikaḥ prāha rājānaṃ sāntvayā girā
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kauśika</s> spoke to the king with conciliatory speech:

children.text: na jihvā me mahārājan vāṇī ca mama sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: "Great king, my tongue and my voice, at all times,

children.text: harer anyam apindraṃ vā stauti naiva ca vakṣyati
children.translated_text: do not praise anyone other than <s>Hari</s>, even <s>Indra</s>, and will not utter such praise."

children.text: evamukte tu tacchiṣyo vāsiṣṭho gautamo hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: When this had been said, his disciples, <s>Vāsiṣṭha</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Hari</s>,
and likewise <s>Sārasvata</s>, <s>Citra</s>, <s>Citramālya</s>, and <s>Śiśu</s>,

children.text: ūcuste pārthivaṃ tadvadyathā prāha ca kauśikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: spoke to the king in just the same way as <s>Kauśika</s> had spoken.
Likewise the listeners, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, said to the king:
"O king, these ears hear no one other than <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: gānakīrtiṃ vayaṃ tasya śṛṇumo 'nyāṃ na ca stutim
children.translated_text: We listen to the sung fame of him, and to no other praise."
Hearing that, the king became angry and said, "Sing!"

children.text: svabhṛtyānbrāhmaṇā hyete kīrtiṃ śṛṇvanti me yathā
children.translated_text: "How is it that these Brahmins, when my own servants

children.text: na śṛṇvanti kathaṃ tasmāt gāyamāne samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: sing my fame everywhere, do not listen to it?"
Thus addressed, the servants then sang of the excellent king.

children.text: niruddhamārgā viprāste gāne vṛtte tu duḥkhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The Brahmins, their path blocked, were distressed when the singing had begun.
The twice-born men stopped up one another's ears with wooden pegs.

children.text: kauśikādyāśca tāṃ jñātvā manovṛttiṃ nṛpasya vai ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Kauśika</s> and the others, having understood that disposition of the king's mind, said:
"This king, fixed on his own song, would forcibly make us sing of him."

children.text: iti viprāḥ suniyatā jihvāgraṃ cichiduḥ karaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: So the well-restrained Brahmins cut off the tips of their tongues with their hands.
Then the king, extremely enraged, banished them from his own country.

children.text: ādāya sarvaṃ vittaṃ ca tataste jagmuruttarām ||
children.translated_text: Taking all their wealth, they then went to the northern
quarter, and in time they were joined to the law of time, death.

children.text: tānāgatānyamo dṛṣṭvā kiṃ kartavyamiti sma ha ||
children.translated_text: Seeing them arrived, <s>Yama</s> wondered, "What should be done?"

children.text: coṣṭitaṃ tatkṣaṇe rājan brahmā prāha surādhipān
children.translated_text: At that very moment, O king, <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to the lords of the gods:
"Now settle the twice-born men headed by <s>Kauśika</s> comfortably.
Bring those who constantly worship <s>Janārdana</s>
through the discipline of song, good fortune to you, if you desire godhood."
Thus addressed, the guardians of the worlds, crying again and again, "<s>Kauśika</s>!"
and some likewise, "<s>Mālava</s>!" and others, "<s>Padmākṣa</s>!",
approached them, took them up through the sky,

children.text: brahmalokaṃ gatāḥ śīghraṃ muhūrtenaiva te surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those gods quickly went to <s>Brahmaloka</s> in a single moment.
Then, seeing <s>Kauśika</s> and the others, <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandfather of the worlds,
came forward and, as was proper, honored them with words of welcome.
Then a tumult arose, intense and full of great honor,
when the gods saw what had been done by <s>Brahmā</s>, O best of kings.
The blessed <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, restraining those foremost gods,
took <s>Kauśika</s> and the other sages and, surrounded by the gods,
quickly went to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, being devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
There the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, attended by the inhabitants of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>,
by Siddhas who were lords of the yoga of knowledge, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and concentrated,
divine, equal to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, auspicious, and bearing four arms,
endowed with the marks of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, shining and stainless,
and by eighty-eight thousand great beings,
by us, beginning with <s>Nārada</s>, and by the stainless ones beginning with <s>Sanaka</s>,
and by various beings and divine women on every side,
was being served in the middle of a pure, wondrous, divine, jewel-made aerial palace,
enclosed by a thousand doors and extending a thousand yojanas,
where <s>Hari</s> sat on an auspicious throne-seat,
and <s>Mādhava</s> had turned his gaze toward the business of the worlds.
At that time the blessed one, surrounded by <s>Kauśika</s> and the others,
came, bowed down before the bearer of <s>Garuḍa</s> on his banner, and praised him.
Then, seeing them, the blessed <s>Hari</s>, lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
said with affection, "<s>Kauśika</s>," and addressed them all in order.
A great cry of victory arose when that great wonder had appeared.
The Self of the universe said to <s>Brahmā</s>, "Listen, <s>Brahmā</s>, to what is said by me.
These Brahmins of <s>Kauśika</s>, intent on both the goal and the means,
have set out for the welfare of the inhabitants of <s>Kuśasthala</s>.
Engaged in hearing my fame, skilled in the true meaning of knowledge,
and devoted to no other deity, let these become Sādhya gods.
Possessing a divine form and splendor, and hearing song here, O lord,

children.text: āsva nityaṃ yathākāmaṃ yāvallokā bhavanti vai ||
children.translated_text: remain here always at will, as long as the worlds exist."
The blessed lord, <s>Mādhava</s>, told <s>Padmākṣa</s>, "Become <s>Dhanada</s>,

children.text: dhanānāmīśvaro bhūtvā yathākālaṃ hi māṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of wealth, and in due time come to me again."

children.text: mālavaṃ mālavīṃ caivaṃ prāha dāmodaro hariḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Hari</s>, spoke thus to <s>Mālava</s> and <s>Mālavī</s>:

children.text: mama loke yathākālaṃ bhāryayā saha mālava ||
children.translated_text: "In my world, in due time, O <s>Mālava</s>, together with your wife,
possessing a divine form and splendor, and hearing song here, O lord,

children.text: āsva nityaṃ yathākāmaṃ yāvallokā bhavanti vai ||
children.translated_text: remain here always at will, as long as the worlds exist."
The blessed lord, <s>Mādhava</s>, told <s>Padmākṣa</s>, "Become <s>Dhanada</s>,

children.text: dhanānāmīśvaro bhūtvā yathākālaṃ hi māṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the lord of wealth, and in due time come to me again.

children.text: āgamya dṛṣṭvā māṃ nityaṃ kuru rājyaṃ yathāsukham
children.translated_text: Having come and seen me always, rule as you please."
Having spoken thus, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, said this to <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.text: kauśikasyāsya gānena yoganidrā ca me gatā
children.translated_text: "By this song of <s>Kauśika</s>, my yogic sleep has departed.

children.text: viṣṇusthale ca māṃ stauti śiṣyaireṣa samantataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He praises me everywhere at <s>Viṣṇusthala</s> with his disciples."
Rejected by the king, the cruel and mighty <s>Kaliṅga</s>,
he cut out his tongue, determined never, in any way, to praise anyone other than <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: na stoṣyāmīti niyataḥ prāpto 'sau mama lokatām
children.translated_text: Thus resolved, saying, 'I will not praise another,' he reached my world.

children.text: ete ca viprā niyatā mama bhaktā yaśasvinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And these renowned Brahmins, disciplined and devoted to me,
struck the openings of their ears with spikes, each against the other,

children.text: śroṣyāmo naiva cānyadvai hareḥ kīrtimitisma ha ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'We will certainly not listen to anything other than the praise of <s>Hari</s>.'

children.text: ete viprāśca devatvaṃ mama sānnidhyameva ca
children.translated_text: These Brahmins attained divine status and nearness to me.

children.text: mālavo bhāryayā sārdhaṃ matkṣetraṃ parimṛjya vai ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mālava</s>, together with his wife, swept my sacred field,
and, worshiping me constantly and always with rows of lamps and the like,
disciplined in vow, he listened to songs furnished with the deeds of my glory.
By that he attained my eternal world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
<s>Padmākṣa</s> gave food to the high-souled <s>Kauśika</s>.
He attained lordship over wealth and nearness to me.
Having spoken thus there in the assembly, <s>Hari</s>, honored by the worlds,
at that very moment was approached by the goddess, with syllables sweet and graceful,
by those who knew the principles of the strings of the vīṇā and were skilled in the art of instruments.
The goddess came slowly, softly smiling, adorned with various ornaments,
singing as she arrived: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
She was surrounded on every side by hundreds of crores of women.
Then the lords of the gaṇas, seeing her, armed with clubs and iron bars,
threatening <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, the sages and the gods all around,
joyfully drove them away and took their places, like mountains.

children.text: sarve vayaṃ hi niryātāḥ sārdhaṃ vai brahmaṇā suraiḥ
children.translated_text: All of us went out, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and the gods.
At that moment <s>Tuṃbaru</s>, the excellent sage, was summoned,

children.text: praviveśa samīpaṃ vai devyā devasya caiva hi
children.translated_text: and he entered the presence of the goddess and of the god himself.
Seated there as was fitting, endowed with many modes of melody,
he joyfully sang a melodious song and played the vīṇā.
With divine and excellent ornaments set with many jewels,
and with divine garlands, bright and auspicious, that best of sages was honored.

children.text: nirgatas tuṃbarur hṛṣṭo 'nye ca ṛṣayaḥ surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tuṃbaru</s> then departed rejoicing, as did the other sages and gods.
Seeing him go, honored as was proper, O subduer of foes,
the sage <s>Nārada</s>, seeing <s>Hari</s>'s honor paid to <s>Tuṃbaru</s>,
with a mind overwhelmed by grief, his heart and eyes burning with pain,
fell into anxious thought there, his self confused by grief and faintness.
'By what means shall I have access to <s>Hari</s>'s mouth, near the goddess?

children.text: aho tuṃbaruṇā prāptaṃ dhiṅ māṃ mūḍhaṃ vicetasam ||
children.translated_text: Ah, <s>Tuṃbaru</s> has attained it. Shame on me, foolish and senseless as I am!
How is it that I, near <s>Hari</s>, have been driven out by the attendants?
Where shall I go while still living? Ah, what has been done by <s>Tuṃbaru</s>!'
Thinking thus, the Brahmin sage undertook austerity,
for a thousand divine years, joined with breath-restraint.
Meditating on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he remained there, remembering <s>Tuṃbaru</s>'s honor,

children.text: rodamāno muhurvidvān dhiṅ māmiti ca cintayan ||
children.translated_text: weeping again and again, wise though he was, and thinking, 'Shame on me!'
Hear what <s>Viṣṇu</s> did for him there, O lord of men.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge kauśikavṛttakathanaṃ nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the first chapter, named 'The narration of the story of <s>Kauśika</s>.'
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: tato nārāyaṇo devastasmai sarvaṃ pradāya vai
children.translated_text: Then the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the soul of the universe, having granted him everything,
in due course made him equal to <s>Tuṃbaru</s>.
This happened in ancient times to the tiger among sages, <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: nārāyaṇasya gītānāṃ gānaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again and again, song is the best among the songs of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, worshiped through song, grants good fame, knowledge, and splendor,

children.text: dadāti tuṣṭiṃ sthānaṃ ca yathāsau kauśikasya vai ||
children.translated_text: as well as satisfaction and a place, just as he did to <s>Kauśika</s>.
And <s>Hari</s> gave success to <s>Padmākṣa</s> and the others.
Therefore, O great king, especially in a sacred field of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
worship, song, dance, and the like, together with instrumental music and festivals,
should be performed ceaselessly by men devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O king.

children.text: śrotavyaṃ ca sadā nityaṃ śrotavyo'sau haristathā
children.translated_text: And it should always and constantly be heard; <s>Hari</s> himself likewise should be heard.
The learned man who, in a sacred field of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, with devotion causes to be performed
song, dance, and the like, and also the narrative account of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: jātismṛtiṃ ca medhāṃ ca tathaivoparame smṛtim ||
children.translated_text: obtains memory of former births, intelligence, and likewise memory at the end,
and attains union with <s>Viṣṇu</s>. This is true, O lord of kings.

children.text: etatte kathitaṃ rājan yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi ||
children.translated_text: This has been told to you, O king, about what you asked me.

children.text: kiṃ vadāmi ca te bhūyo vada dharmabhṛtāṃ vara ||
children.translated_text: What more shall I say to you? Speak, O best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge viṣṇumāhātmyaṃ nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the second chapter, named 'The greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.'
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:
O very wise <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, by what discipline did the blessed sage <s>Nārada</s>,
greatly fortunate as he is, obtain the science of song?
At what time did he come to equality with <s>Tuṃbaru</s>?
Tell me all this; you are all-knowing, O great-minded one.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
I heard this matter from <s>Nārada</s>, who had seen the gods.
That glorious and very wise <s>Nārada</s> himself told it.
The blessed one, burning with remorse for a thousand divine years,
engaged in breath-restraint and remembering <s>Tuṃbaru</s>'s honor,
practiced a most terrible and supreme austerity, a mass of ascetic power.
Then that great sage <s>Nārada</s> heard in the sky
a divine voice, very resonant, marvelous, and bodiless:
'For what purpose, tiger among sages, are you practicing this difficult austerity?'

children.text: ulūkaṃ paśya gatvā tvaṃ yadi gāne ratā matiḥ
children.translated_text: Go and see the owl, if your mind is devoted to singing.
On Mount <s>Mānasottara</s> he is remembered as <s>Gānabandhu</s>.

children.text: gaccha śīghraṃ ca paśyainaṃ gānavittvaṃ bhaviṣyasi
children.translated_text: Go quickly and see him; you will become a knower of song.
Thus addressed, <s>Nārada</s>, the best of those skilled in speech, was filled with wonder.
He went to <s>Gānabandhu</s> on Mount <s>Mānasottara</s>.
Gandharvas, kinnaras, yakṣas, and hosts of apsarases
were seated all around <s>Gānabandhu</s>, on every side.
They had attained the science of singing, having been taught by that bird.
There they sat joyfully, with smooth throats and voices.
Then, seeing <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Gānabandhu</s> spoke.
After bowing down according to rule, he honored him with words of welcome.
For what purpose, venerable one, have you come here, O great-minded one?

children.text: kiṃ kāryaṃ hi mayā brahman brūhi kiṃ karavāṇi te
children.translated_text: What task is there for me, O brahmin? Tell me what I may do for you.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
O lord of owls, greatly wise one, hear everything exactly as it is.

children.text: mama vṛttaṃ pravakṣyāmi purā bhūtaṃ mahādbhutam
children.translated_text: I shall tell my story, a very wondrous thing that happened long ago.
In a past age, O learned one, I had gone near <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: māṃ vinirdhūya saṃhṛṣṭaḥ samāhūya ca tuṃbarum
children.translated_text: But, dismissing me, he joyfully summoned <s>Tuṃbaru</s>.
Together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> listened to his excellent singing.
All the gods, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, were displaced from their positions by <s>Acyuta</s>.
<s>Kauśika</s> and the others sat there, honoring <s>Hari</s> through gānayoga (devotional musical practice).
Having worshiped in this way, they attained gāṇapatya as they pleased.
Because of that, greatly afflicted with sorrow, I came here to perform austerity.

children.text: yaddattaṃ yaddhutaṃ caiva yathā vā śrutameva ca
children.translated_text: Whatever I had given, whatever I had offered in fire, and whatever I had heard,

children.text: yadadhītaṃ mayā sarvaṃ kalāṃ nārhati ṣoḍaśīm ||
children.translated_text: and all that I had studied, did not deserve even a sixteenth part
of that gānayoga joined with the greatness of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: saṃcintyāhaṃ tapo ghoraṃ tadarthaṃ taptavān dvija ||
children.translated_text: Reflecting on this, O twice-born one, I performed severe austerity for that purpose.
For a thousand divine years; then again I heard
a voice arisen from the sky, referring to you, O bird.
'Go to the owl, O divine seer, to <s>Gānabandhu</s>, if your mind

children.text: gāne cedvartate brahman tatra tvaṃ vetsyase cirāt ||
children.translated_text: is set on singing, O brahmin; there, after a long time, you will understand.'
Thus impelled by that voice, I have come here into your presence.

children.text: kiṃ kariṣyāmi śiṣyo'haṃ tava māṃ pālayāvyaya ||
children.translated_text: What shall I do? I am your pupil; protect me, O imperishable one.
<s>Gānabandhu</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu nārada yadvṛttaṃ purā mama mahāmate
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Nārada</s>, great-minded one, to what happened to me long ago,
an auspicious tale, joined with great marvel and removing all sin.

children.text: bhuvaneśa iti khyāto rājābhūd dhārmikaḥ purā
children.translated_text: Long ago there was a righteous king known as <s>Bhuvaneśa</s>.
With a thousand aśvamedha sacrifices and ten thousand vājapeyas,

children.text: gavāṃ koṭyarbude caiva suvarṇasya tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: and with crores and arbudas of cows, and likewise of gold,
as well as garments, chariots, elephants, maidens, and horses,

children.text: dattvā sa rājā viprebhyo medinīṃ pratipālayan
children.translated_text: that king gave gifts to brahmins while protecting the earth.
In his own kingdom he prohibited singing of <s>Keśava</s> through geyayoga (song-practice).

children.text: anyaṃ vā geyayogena gāyanyadi sa me bhavet
children.translated_text: If anyone were to sing another by geyayoga,

children.text: vadhyaḥ sarvātmanā tasmād vedair īḍyaḥ paraḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: he was to be punished in every way; therefore the supreme person, praised by the Vedas,
was to be sung everywhere by women through gānayoga, constantly.
And groups of sūtas and māgadhas were to have that song performed.
Having given this command, the greatly radiant king ruled the kingdom.

children.text: tasya rājñaḥ purābhyāśe harimitra iti śrutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Near that king, in former times, there was one known as <s>Harimitra</s>,
a brahmin and devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from all pairs of opposites.
Having reached the sandy bank of a river and a beautiful image of <s>Hari</s>,
he worshiped it according to rule with much ghee and curds besides.
After offering sweet food, milk-rice, and cake to <s>Hari</s>,
he bowed down properly and fixed his mind there.
There he sang of <s>Hari</s>, endowed with beat, syllabic measure, and rhythm.
He was filled with intense affection, his inner self absorbed in him.
Then, by the king's command, spies came there.
They swept away all that worship and its accessories on every side.

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ gṛhītvā te rājñe samyaṅnyavedayan ||
children.translated_text: Taking that brahmin, they reported everything properly to the king.
Then the wicked-minded king rebuked that best of twice-born men
and banished him from the kingdom, after seizing all his wealth and property.

children.text: pratimāṃ ca hareścaiva mlecchā hṛtvā yayuḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: The mlecchas also took away the image of <s>Hari</s> and departed again.
Then, after a long time, the king came under the law of death.
Though he was honored everywhere in all the worlds, that king
was afflicted by hunger and distressed; in great sorrow he spoke to <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: kṣuttṛṭ ca vartate deva svargatasyāpi me sadā
children.translated_text: Hunger and thirst, O god, remain with me always, even though I have gone to heaven.

children.text: mayā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ kiṃ vā kiṃ kariṣyāmi vai yama ||
children.translated_text: What sin did I commit? What shall I do, O <s>Yama</s>?
<s>Yama</s> said:
You committed a very great sin through the delusion of ignorance,
at that time against <s>Harimitra</s>, who was devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
The sin committed against <s>Harimitra</s>, in the matter of worshiping <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: tena pāpena samprāptaḥ kṣudrogastvāṃ sadā nṛpa ||
children.translated_text: by that sin, O king, a disease of hunger has always come upon you.
All your gifts, sacrifices, and the rest have been destroyed, O lord of men.
When the great-minded <s>Harimitra</s> was singing with song and instruments,
you had him summoned and took away his wealth,
and all the offerings and other things in the presence of <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
At that time your servants plundered it; they committed sin by your command.

children.text: hareḥ kīrtiṃ vinā cānyad brāhmaṇena nṛpottama ||
children.translated_text: Apart from the glory of <s>Hari</s>, O best of kings, nothing else

children.text: na geyayoge gātavyaṃ tasmātpāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā
children.translated_text: is to be sung by a brahmin in geyayoga; therefore sin was committed by you.
All your worlds are now lost. Go to a mountain cave,

children.text: pūrvotsṛṣṭaṃ svadehaṃ taṃ khādannityaṃ nikṛtya vai
children.translated_text: and there, cutting up the body that you cast off before, eat it constantly.

children.text: tasmin kāle tvimaṃ dehaṃ khādannityaṃ kṣudhānvitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: At that time, constantly eating this body, afflicted with hunger,
you will remain established in the great hell until the end of a <s>manvantara</s>.

children.text: manvantare tato 'tīte bhūmyāṃ tvaṃ ca bhaviṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: Then, when that <s>manvantara</s> has passed, you will be on the earth.
After that, in time, you will attain human birth.
<s>Gānabandhu</s> said:
Having spoken thus, the wise <s>Yama</s> disappeared right there.
The glorious <s>Harimitra</s>, praised by the lords of the hosts,
went by an aerial car to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, gathering his companions among the hosts.

children.text: bhuvaneśo nṛpo hyasmin koṭare parvatasya vai
children.translated_text: But king <s>Bhuvaneśa</s> is there in this hollow of the mountain,
constantly eating a corpse, afflicted by hunger and thirst.
I saw that king there, and he told me all this.
Having seen and understood it, I came to <s>Harimitra</s>,
who was going in a sun-colored aerial car, surrounded by immortals.
By the favor of <s>Indradyumna</s> I obtained an excellent span of life.

children.text: tenāhaṃ harimitraṃ vai dṛṣṭavān asmi suvrata
children.translated_text: Through that, O you of good vows, I indeed saw <s>Harimitra</s>.
Then, by the power of that majesty, a thought arose in my mind.
At that time I approached the <s>kinnaras</s> for the knowledge of music.
For sixty thousand years, O sage, through the discipline of music,
my tongue was made clear and gracious; then I learned singing.
Then, in just twice that length of time, this art became mine.
Endowed with the discipline of music, ten <s>manvantaras</s> passed for me.
There I became a teacher of music, and <s>gandharvas</s> and others gathered.
These companies of <s>kinnaras</s> came to me as their teacher.

children.text: tapasā naiva śakyā vai gānavidyā tapodhana ||
children.translated_text: Knowledge of music, O treasure of austerity, is not attainable by austerity alone.
Therefore, joined with instruction, obtain music from me.

children.text: evamukto munistaṃ vai praṇipatya jagau tadā ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, the sage bowed down to him and then sang.
Listen to that, O best of sages, after bowing to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Thus addressed by <s>Ulūka</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, the best of sages,
learned music there, together with the proper course of instruction.
Then <s>Gānabandhu</s> said this: Now become free from shame.
<s>Ulūka</s> said:
In union with women, in song, in gambling, and in gatherings for exposition,
and likewise in legal dealings, in eating, and in the acquisition of wealth,

children.text: āye vyaye tathā nityaṃ tyaktalajjastu vai bhavet
children.translated_text: in income and expense too, one should always be free from shame.
One must never sing while contracted, concealed, or always covered with wraps and the like,
nor with gestures of throwing the hands about, nor with the mouth held wide open,
nor with the tongue protruding; in no way should one sing like that.
One should not sing with arms raised, nor in any way with the gaze lifted upward,
nor while looking at one's own limbs, nor while staring at another person.

children.text: saṃghaṭṭe ca tathotthāne kaṭisthānaṃ na śasyate
children.translated_text: In striking the rhythm and in rising up, a position at the waist is not commended.

children.text: hāso roṣastathā kampas tathānyatra smṛtiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Laughter, anger, trembling, and again the mind's being elsewhere:
these are not approved forms in the discipline of music, O great-minded one.
It is not possible, O sage, to strike the rhythm with one hand.
One who is afflicted by hunger, afflicted by fear, or afflicted by thirst,
should not perform the discipline of music; nor should it ever be done in darkness.
These and other such things should not be done by one who sings.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Thus instructed, that blessed one, by the marks of rule taught by him,
learned the divine song for a thousand divine years.
Then he became accomplished in all matters such as the extension of song,
accomplished in the <s>vipañcī</s> and other instruments, and a knower of all divisions of notes.
Thirty-six ten-thousands, thousands, and hundreds
of distinctions among notes the best of sages came to know.
Then the companies of <s>gandharvas</s> and likewise of <s>kinnaras</s>,

children.text: muninā saha saṃyuktāḥ prītiyuktā bhavanti te ||
children.translated_text: joined with the sage, became full of affection.
Having obtained unsurpassed music, the sage said to <s>Gānabandhu</s>:

children.text: tvāṃ samāsādya sampannas tvaṃ hi gītaviśāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having reached you, I am fulfilled, for you are skilled in song.
O enemy of crows, O very wise teacher, what may I do for you?
<s>Gānabandhu</s> said:
In a day of <s>Brahmā</s>, O brahmin, there are fourteen <s>Manus</s>.
After that there will be a great dissolution of the three worlds, O great sage.
Until then let there be the state of life for me; until then let there be my highest good.
Let what I have contemplated in my mind be my teacher's fee, O best of sages.
<s>Nārada</s> said:
When the former <s>kalpa</s> has passed, you will become <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: svasti te 'stu mahāprājña gamiṣyāmi prasīda mām
children.translated_text: May it be well with you, O very wise one. I shall go; be gracious to me.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Having spoken thus, <s>Nārada</s> too then went to <s>Janārdana</s>.
On <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> he sang songs before <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>.

children.text: tatra śrutvā tu bhagavānnāradaṃ prāha mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard them there, the blessed <s>Mādhava</s> said to <s>Nārada</s>:
Even now, <s>Nārada</s>, you are not superior to <s>Tuṃbaru</s> in songs.

children.text: yadā viśiṣṭo bhavitā taṃ kālaṃ pravadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you the time when you will become superior.
Having approached <s>Gānabandhu</s>, you have become a knower of the meaning of music.
In the twenty-eighth age of <s>Manu Vaivasvata</s>,
at the end of the <s>Dvāpara</s>, I shall be born in the family of the <s>Yadu</s> lineage,
from <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s>, by the name <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O great-minded one.
Then, having come to me, you should remind me exactly.
There I shall make you complete in song, O great-vowed one,
equal to <s>Tuṃbaru</s> and also endowed with superiority.
Until that time, as is proper, among births as gods and <s>gandharvas</s>,
train yourself according to rule. Having said this, he disappeared.
Then the sage bowed to him, who was endowed with such surpassing excellence.
The divine seer, resembling a god, adorned with every ornament,
an utter treasure of austerities and wholly devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
placed the vipañcī lute on his shoulder and traveled through all the worlds.

children.text: vāruṇaṃ yāmyam āgneyam aindraṃ kauberameva ca ||
children.translated_text: He went to the regions of <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Kubera</s>,

children.text: vāyavyaṃ ca tatheśānaṃ saṃsadaṃ prāpya dharmavit
children.translated_text: and likewise to the assemblies of <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>, knowing dharma,
properly singing <s>Hari</s> and skilled in playing the vīṇā.
Being honored everywhere by hosts of gandharvas and apsarases,
at a certain turn of time he reached <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
The gandharvas <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Hūhū</s>, expert in song and instrumental music,
were divine singers of <s>Brahmā</s>, eternal and the best of gandharvas.

children.text: tatra tābhyāṃ samāsādya gāyamāno hariṃ prabhum
children.translated_text: There, having approached those two while singing <s>Hari</s> the lord,
the very radiant best of sages was also honored by <s>Brahmā</s>.
After bowing to that great-souled grandsire of all the worlds,
<s>Nārada</s> roamed at will through all the worlds.

children.text: tataḥ kālena mahatā gṛhaṃ prāpya ca tumbaroḥ
children.translated_text: Then, after a long time, having reached the house of <s>Tumburu</s>,
the great sage took up the vīṇā and, staying there, sang.

children.text: svarakalpāstu tatrasthāḥ ṣaḍjādyāḥ sapta vai matāḥ
children.translated_text: There were present the tonal forms, the seven beginning with ṣaḍja, as they are understood.
Seeing them at play, the venerable one went out very quickly.
The great-minded one instructed him many times, here and there,
and the great sage <s>Nārada</s> too applied himself with arduous practice.
Seeing the seven maidens of the notes, expert in the science of singing,
he was engaged with the vīṇā, but the strings did not reach them.
Then the great sage bowed down to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> on <s>Raivataka</s>,

children.text: vijñāpayadaśeṣaṃ tu śvetadvīpe tu yat purā ||
children.translated_text: and reported in full what had formerly occurred on <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>,
the unsurpassed discipline of singing that had been taught by <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Hearing this, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> laughed and joyfully said to <s>Jāmbavatī</s>:
"Good lady, instruct this best of sages according to rule
in the practice of singing with the vīṇā." Saying "So be it" to <s>Hari</s>,
she smilingly instructed that sage in the proper manner.
Then, when a year was complete, he again came to <s>Mādhava</s>.
Bowing down, he stood before him, and <s>Keśava</s> again said:
"Go into the presence of <s>Satyā</s> and be instructed according to rule."
Saying "So be it," the sage bowed to <s>Satyabhāmā</s> and sang.

children.text: tayā sa śikṣito vidvān pūrṇe saṃvatsare punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taught by her, that learned one, when a year was complete, again
was directed by <s>Vāsudeva</s> and went to the residence of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.
Then that best of sages was addressed by the women there, by the maidservants:

children.text: ukto 'sau gāyamāno'pi na svaraṃ vetsi vai mune
children.translated_text: "Even though you are singing, O sage, you do not know the note."
Then, with great exertion, for three years

children.text: śikṣito'sau tadā devyā rukmiṇyāpi jagau muniḥ
children.translated_text: he was instructed by the goddess <s>Rukmiṇī</s> too, and the sage sang.
Then the maidens of the notes attained union with the great sage's strings.
Calling the great sage, blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself,
the immeasurable one, instructed him in the unsurpassed discipline of singing.
Then the best of sages gained an excellence beyond <s>Tumburu</s>.
Then the divine seer danced, after bowing down to <s>Janārdana</s>.
And <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> said, laughing: "You are all-knowing, O great sage.
Sing with the discipline of song in my presence.

children.text: etatte prārthitaṃ prāptaṃ mama loke tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: This thing you asked for has been obtained, and likewise in my world

children.text: nityaṃ tumbaruṇā sārdhaṃ gāyasva ca yathātatham ||
children.translated_text: you shall always sing correctly together with <s>Tumburu</s>."
Thus addressed there, the sage acted in the proper manner.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was worshiping <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the worlds,
then, at <s>Hari</s>'s command, he sang to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,

children.text: rukmiṇyā saha satyā ca jāṃbavatyā mahāmuniḥ ||
children.translated_text: the great sage together with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
and with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O best of kings, skilled in the classes of sacred melody.

children.text: eṣa vo muniśārdūlāḥ prokto gītakramo muneḥ ||
children.translated_text: This sequence of the sage's singing has been told to you, O tigers among sages.
A brahmin, singing the name of <s>Vāsudeva</s> intensely, O king,
attains residence in the same world as <s>Hari</s>; singing of <s>Rudra</s> would be still greater.
Otherwise, singing of anything else, he would go to hell.
Devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s> by action, mind, and speech,
singing and listening, he attains him; therefore they know him as the supreme one to be sung.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge vaiṣṇavagītakathanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the third chapter, named "The Teaching of Vaiṣṇava Singing."
The sages said:
Those who are called Vaiṣṇavas, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: kāni cihnāni teṣāṃ vai tanno brūhi mahāmate ||
children.translated_text: what are their distinguishing marks? Tell that to us, O great-minded one.

children.text: teṣāṃ vā kiṃ karotyeṣa bhagavān bhūtabhāvanaḥ
children.translated_text: And what does this blessed creator of beings do for them?
Tell me all this, O <s>Sūta</s>, best knower of every meaning.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: aṃbarīṣeṇa vai pṛṣṭo mārkaṇḍeyaḥ purā muniḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago the sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> was asked by <s>Ambarīṣa</s>

children.text: yuṣmābhir adya yat proktaṃ tadvadāmi yathātatham ||
children.translated_text: what you have asked today; I shall tell it just as it was.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O king, in due order to what you are asking me.
Wherever a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> dwells, there <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is present.

children.text: viṣṇureva hi sarvatra yeṣāṃ vai devatā smṛtā
children.translated_text: For those for whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is everywhere remembered as the deity,

children.text: kīrtyamāne harau nityaṃ romāñco yasya vartate ||
children.translated_text: and for whom, when <s>Hari</s> is constantly being praised, horripilation arises,
trembling, sweat, and drops of water are seen in the eyes,
who are joined with devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and promote śrauta and smārta rites,

children.text: prīto bhavati yo dṛṣṭvā vaiṣṇavo 'sau prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: one who becomes pleased on seeing them is proclaimed a Vaiṣṇava.
A Vaiṣṇava should not cover himself with another garment in the battle of the world.
And when he sees a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> approaching and standing before him,
he should perform bowing and the like in this way, just as toward <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: sa vai bhakta iti jñeyaḥ sa jayī syājjagattraye
children.translated_text: He indeed should be known as a devotee; he would be victorious in the three worlds.
Even when hearing harsh words spoken by a <s>Bhāgavata</s>,

children.text: praṇāmapūrvaṃ kṣāntyā vai yo vadedvaiṣṇavo hi saḥ
children.translated_text: the one who speaks with forbearance, after first bowing, is indeed a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.

children.text: gandhapuṣpādi kiṃ sarvaṃ śirasā yo hi dhārayet ||
children.translated_text: And the one who bears on his head all such things as perfumes and flowers,
thinking, "All this belongs to <s>Hari</s>," is remembered as a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
In a sacred field of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he performs only auspicious acts, filled with affection.
And he should daily worship the image of <s>Hari</s>, self-restrained and pure in spirit.

children.text: viṣṇubhaktaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ karmaṇā manasā girā ||
children.translated_text: He should be known as a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in action, mind, and speech.
Always intent on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he is indeed a great <s>Bhāgavata</s>.
Whoever, according to his ability, performs every act of feeding and worship,

children.text: viṣṇubhaktasya ca sadā yathānyāyaṃ hi kathyate
children.translated_text: of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is always spoken of according to the proper rule.
When a learned man intent on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with a pleased mind, eats his food,
that food has gone into the mouth of <s>Hari</s>; there is no doubt.
The universe-souled <s>Mādhava</s> becomes more pleased than by his own worship.
Seeing that in a great <s>Bhāgavata</s>, that lover of devotees is pleased.
Seeing a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> intent on <s>Vāsudeva</s>, whose sins have been burned away,
even the gods go to him in fear, bow down, and return as they came.
Hear now the ancient event, the majesty of a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā yamo 'pi vai bhaktaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ dagdhakilbiṣam
children.translated_text: Even <s>Yama</s>, seeing a devotee, a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> whose sins had been burned away,
rose up, stood with joined palms, and bowed to the descendant of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
Therefore a man should worship <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> with devotion, just as he worships <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: sa yāti viṣṇusāmīpyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: He goes to nearness to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; no deliberation is to be made about this.
A devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is superior to thousands of devotees of others.
A devotee of <s>Rudra</s> is superior to thousands of devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
There is no one higher than a devotee of <s>Rudra</s> in the world; there is no doubt.
Therefore, whether a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> or a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>,
one should worship him with every effort, for <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge viṣṇubhaktakathanaṃ nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the fourth chapter, named "The Statement about Devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
The sages said:
<s>Ambarīṣa</s>, descendant of <s>Ikṣvāku</s> and devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
ruled the earth, acting under the command of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
We have heard this, O greatly wise one; you should tell all of that.
It is heard in the world that the discus of <s>Hari</s> always destroys enemies, diseases, fears, and the rest
for that righteous great-souled man.
Tell us the whole account of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, O best of the good.
We wish to hear, just as it was, his greatness, power, and unsurpassed yoga of devotion.
O <s>Sūta</s>, you are able to tell it.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Listen, O tigers among sages, to the account of that wise man,
the supreme greatness of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, which removes all sins.
The beloved wife of <s>Triśaṅku</s>, adorned with every auspicious mark,
was the mother of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, always endowed with purity.
She worshiped great <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, mounted in yogic sleep and lying on the couch of <s>Śeṣa</s>,
born from the lotus of the cosmic egg,
known through darkness as <s>Kālarudra</s>, through passion as the golden egg-born one,
and through purity as all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bowed to by all the gods.
She worshiped him constantly by acts of speech, mind, and body.
She herself performed everything, such as the offering of garlands.
Likewise the grinding of perfumes and other substances, the preparation of incense materials,
the smearing of the ground, and the cooking of oblations,
absorbed in delight in that service, she herself performed.

children.text: śubhā padmāvatī nityaṃ vācā nārāyaṇeti vai ||
children.translated_text: Auspicious <s>Padmāvatī</s> always said with her voice, "<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,"
and likewise always spoke, "<s>Ananta</s>," that faithful wife.
For ten thousand years, with her inner self intent on him,
she worshiped <s>Govinda</s> with perfumes, flowers, and the like, pure as she was.
She pleased the greatly fortunate devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from every sin,
daily with gifts, honors, worship, wealth, and jewels.

children.text: tataḥ kadācitsā devī dvādaśīṃ samupoṣya vai ||
children.translated_text: Then one day that goddess, after properly fasting on the twelfth lunar day,
slept before <s>Hari</s>, together with her husband.
There the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, said to her:

children.text: kim icchasi varaṃ bhadre mattas tvam brūhi bhāmini
children.translated_text: "What boon do you desire from me, auspicious lady? Speak, beautiful woman."

children.text: sā dṛṣṭvā tu varaṃ vavre putro me vaiṣṇavo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Seeing him, she chose the boon: "May I have a son who is a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>,
a universal sovereign, very splendid, devoted to his own duty, and pure."

children.text: tathetyuktvā dadau tasyai phalam ekaṃ janārdanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "So be it," <s>Janārdana</s> gave her a single fruit.

children.text: sā prabuddhā phalaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhartre sarvaṃ nyavedayat
children.translated_text: She awoke, saw the fruit, and told her husband everything.
Delighted, she ate the fruit, her mind fixed on him.

children.text: tataḥ kālena sā devī putraṃ kulavivardhanam
children.translated_text: Then in time that goddess gave birth to a son who increased his family,
a man of good conduct, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
He was endowed with auspicious marks, and his limbs bore the mark of the discus.

children.text: jātaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitā putraṃ kriyāḥ sarvāścakāra vai ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that his son had been born, the father performed all the rites.
The lord became renowned in the world as <s>Ambarīṣa</s>.
When his father had passed away, the glorious one was consecrated, O great sage.

children.text: mantriṣvādhāya rājyaṃ ca tapa ugraṃ cakāra saḥ
children.translated_text: Entrusting the kingdom to his ministers, he performed severe austerity.
For a thousand years he repeated the name of the lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
who dwells in the middle of the heart-lotus and in the middle of the solar orb,
four-armed, bearing conch, discus, mace, and lotus,
resembling pure <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold, and consisting of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
the Lord adorned with all ornaments and wearing yellow garments.
the god with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> on his chest, the Person, the supreme Person,
then, mounting <s>Garuḍa</s>, praised by all the gods,
he, the soul of the universe, came, honored by all the worlds,
<s>Hari</s> having made <s>Garuḍa</s> inconceivable, like <s>Airāvata</s>.
Seated like <s>Śakra</s> himself, he said to that best of kings,

children.text: indro 'hamasmi bhadraṃ te kiṃ dadāmi varaṃ ca te ||
children.translated_text: "I am <s>Indra</s>. Blessing to you. What boon shall I give you?
I am the lord of all worlds; I have come here to protect you."
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:
"I have not undertaken austerity here with you in view.

children.text: tvayā dattaṃ ca neṣyāmi gaccha śakra yathāsukham
children.translated_text: And I will not accept what is given by you. Go, <s>Śakra</s>, as you please.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is my lord; I bow to him, the lord of the universe.
Go, <s>Indra</s>; do not bring about the overthrow of my understanding here."
Then the blessed <s>Hari</s>, laughing, made manifest his own form.
<s>Janārdana</s>, holding <s>Śārṅga</s>, discus, and mace, with sword in hand,
the soul of all, upon <s>Garuḍa</s>, was like another blue mountain.
He was praised on every side by hosts of gods and gandharvas.
Bowing, he, delighted and satisfied, praised the one whose banner is <s>Garuḍa</s>.
"Be gracious, O lord of the lord of worlds, O my lord <s>Janārdana</s>.
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the universe, honored by all the worlds,
you are the beginning, you are without beginning, you are endless, the Person, the lord.
You are immeasurable, all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, lotus-eyed one.
You are born from the body of <s>Maheśvara</s>; you are the middle, <s>Puṣkara</s>, the sky-goer, the bird.
You are <s>Kavyavāha</s>, <s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Havyavāha</s>, and <s>Prabhañjana</s>.
You are the primordial god, delighting in action, the supreme self established in the self.
I have taken refuge in you, <s>Govinda</s>. Victory to you, son of <s>Devakī</s>.

children.text: jaya deva jagannātha pāhi māṃ puṣkarekṣaṇa ||
children.translated_text: Victory, O god, lord of the universe; protect me, lotus-eyed one.

children.text: nānyā gatistvadanyā me tvameva śaraṇaṃ mama
children.translated_text: I have no other course apart from you; you alone are my refuge."
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tamāha bhagavānviṣṇuḥ kiṃ te hṛdi cikīrṣitam ||
children.translated_text: The blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> said to him, "What do you desire to do in your heart?

children.text: tatsarvaṃ te pradāsyāmi bhakto'si mama suvrata
children.translated_text: All that I will grant you, for you are my devotee, O well-vowed one.
I am always fond of devotion; therefore I have come here to give."
<s>Ambarīṣa</s> said:

children.text: lokanātha parānanda nityaṃ me vartate matiḥ
children.translated_text: "O lord of the worlds, supreme bliss, my thought is always fixed:
it is always directed toward <s>Vāsudeva</s> through speech, mind, body, and acts.
As you are devoted to <s>Bhava</s>, the god of gods, the supreme self,

children.text: tathā bhavāmyahaṃ viṣṇo tava deva janārdana ||
children.translated_text: so may I be devoted to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O god <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: pālayiṣyāmi pṛthivīṃ kṛtvā vai vaiṣṇavaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: I shall protect the earth, making the world Vaiṣṇava,
and by sacrifices, oblations, and worship I shall satisfy the best of gods.
I shall protect Vaiṣṇavas and destroy enemies;

children.text: lokatāpabhaye bhīta iti me dhīyate matiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am afraid of the danger of the world's affliction; such is my thought."
The blessed lord said:
"So be it, just as you wish. This discus, <s>Sudarśana</s>,

children.text: purā rudraprasādena labdhaṃ vai durlabhaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: which long ago I obtained by <s>Rudra</s>'s favor and which is hard to obtain,
will always destroy for you suffering arising from sages' curses and the like, and likewise enemies, disease, and the like."
Having spoken thus, he disappeared.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: tataḥ praṇamya mudito rājā nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum
children.translated_text: Then the king, delighted, bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lord,
entered the lovely city <s>Ayodhyā</s>, and ruled it.
He set the Brahmins and the other varṇas in their own proper duties,
always devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and he protected the sinless devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The king, with a joyful self, protected them especially.
Having sacrificed with a hundred horse-sacrifices and with a hundred <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifices,
he protected this earth bounded by the oceans.

children.text: gṛhe gṛhe haristasthau vedaghoṣo gṛhe gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> was present in every house; Vedic recitation was in every house.
There was the proclamation of <s>Hari</s>'s name, and likewise the proclamation of sacrifice,
O tiger among kings, while he was governing the kingdom.
The earth was not without crops, not without grass, nor afflicted by famine and the like.
The subjects were always free from passion and devoid of all calamities.
The greatly splendid <s>Ambarīṣa</s> protected the earth.
As he was living in this way, he had a lotus-eyed daughter,
famed by the name <s>Śrīmatī</s>, endowed with every auspicious mark.
She had reached the time for being given in marriage, beautiful like divine Māyā.
At that time the glorious sage <s>Nārada</s> arrived,
at the palace of king <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and so did the very wise <s>Parvata</s>.
Seeing both of them arrived, and bowing according to rule,
the greatly splendid <s>Ambarīṣa</s> honored those two sages.

children.text: kanyāṃ tāṃ ramamāṇāṃ vai meghamadhye śatahradām
children.translated_text: As the girl was playing, like lightning amid clouds,

children.text: prāha tāṃ prekṣya bhagavān nāradaḥ sasmitas tadā ||
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Nārada</s>, seeing her then, said with a smile,
"Who is this greatly fortunate girl, O king, like a daughter of the gods?
Tell me, best of those who uphold <s>dharma</s>; she is adorned with every mark."
The king said:

children.text: duhiteyaṃ mama vibho śrīmatī nāma nāmataḥ
children.translated_text: "This is my daughter, lord; she is named <s>Śrīmatī</s>.
She has reached the time for being given, and the auspicious girl seeks a husband."
Thus addressed, that tiger among sages, <s>Nārada</s>, desired her, O Brahmins.
The sage <s>Parvata</s> too desired her, O best of sages.
Having asked the king's permission, <s>Nārada</s> spoke these words:
Calling him aside in private, the righteous one said, "Give me this daughter of yours."

children.text: parvato hi tathā prāha rājānaṃ rahasi prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Parvata</s> too likewise spoke to the king in private, O lord.
The righteous king, frightened and bowing to them both together, said:

children.text: ubhau bhavantau kanyāṃ me prārthayānau kathaṃ tvaham
children.translated_text: "Since both of you are seeking my daughter, how shall I,

children.text: kariṣyāmi mahāprājña śṛṇu nārada me vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O very wise one, proceed? Hear my words, <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: tvaṃ ca parvata me vākyaṃ śṛṇu vakṣyāmi yatprabho
children.translated_text: And you too, <s>Parvata</s>, hear the words that I shall speak, O lord.
This auspicious girl will choose one of you two."

children.text: tasmai kanyāṃ prayacchāmi nānyathā śaktirasti me
children.translated_text: I shall give the maiden to him; otherwise I have no power.

children.text: tathetyuktvā tato bhūyaḥ śvo yāsyāva iti sma ha ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "So be it," they then said again, "Tomorrow we two shall come."
Having spoken thus, the two tigers among sages went away with delighted minds,
both constantly devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, both the best among knowers of knowledge.
Then the excellent sage <s>Nārada</s>, having gone to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
bowed down to <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> and spoke these words:
"There is something to be heard, O blessed lord, O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, O master.
In private I will tell you; homage to you, lord of the worlds."

children.text: tataḥ prahasya govindaḥ sarvānutsārya taṃ munim
children.translated_text: Then <s>Govinda</s>, laughing, dismissed everyone and said to that sage,

children.text: brūhītyāha ca viśvātmā munirāha ca keśavam ||
children.translated_text: "Speak." And the soul of the universe spoke; the sage then said to <s>Keśava</s>:
"Your illustrious king, the ruler of the earth <s>Ambarīṣa</s>,

children.text: tasya kanyā viśālākṣī śrīmatī nāma nāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: has a wide-eyed daughter, named <s>Śrīmatī</s> by name.
I went there intending to marry her; hear what happened.
This illustrious sage <s>Parvata</s>, your servant and a treasure of austerity,
also desired her, O blessed one. The lord of men said to us two,
the mighty <s>Ambarīṣa</s>: 'This maiden will choose the better of you two.
If she chooses one endowed with beauty, I will give her to him.'
Thus the king spoke to us there; saying 'So be it,' I have come here.

children.text: āgamiṣyāmi te rājan śvaḥ prabhāte gṛhaṃ tviti
children.translated_text: 'I shall come to your house, O king, tomorrow at dawn' - so I said.
I have come, O lord of the world; you ought to do what is dear to me.
Make <s>Parvata</s>'s face appear like the face of a monkey,

children.text: tathā kuru jagannātha mama cedicchasi priyam ||
children.translated_text: in that way, O lord of the world, if you wish to do what is dear to me."
Saying "So be it," <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>, laughed

children.text: tvayoktaṃ ca kariṣyāmi gaccha saumya yathāgatam ||
children.translated_text: and said, "I shall do what you have said; go, gentle one, as you came."
Thus addressed, the sage, delighted, bowed down to <s>Janārdana</s>
and, thinking himself successful, went then to <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
When that best of sages had gone, <s>Parvata</s> too, the great sage,
bowed to <s>Mādhava</s> and, delighted, spoke this to him in private:
After first reporting what had happened with <s>Nārada</s>, O lord of the world,
he said, "Make his face appear like the face of a langur."
Hearing that, blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> said, "What you have said I shall indeed do.

children.text: gaccha śīghramayodhyāṃ vai māvedīr nāradasya vai ||
children.translated_text: Go quickly to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, and do not let <s>Nārada</s> know of this.

children.text: tvayā me saṃvidaṃ tatra tathetyuktvā jagāma saḥ
children.translated_text: This agreement of yours with me is there." Saying "So be it," he went away.

children.text: tato rājā samājñāya prāptau munivarau tadā ||
children.translated_text: Then the king, learning that the two best sages had arrived at that time,
adorned all <s>Ayodhyā</s>, garlanded with banners, with various auspicious objects,
and with flowers and parched grain on every side.
He made the city one whose house-doors were sprinkled with water, whose market streets and great roads were watered,
filled with divine fragrant essences and perfumed with divine incense.

children.text: kṛtvā ca nagarīṃ rājā maṇḍayāmāsa tāṃ sabhām
children.translated_text: Having made the city so, the king adorned that assembly hall
with divine fragrances, with incense, and with various jewels as well,
decorated with jeweled pillars, shining with many garlands,
furnished with excellent coverings, and surrounded by divine auspicious seats.

children.text: kṛtvā nṛpendrastāṃ kanyāṃ hyādāya praviveśa ha
children.translated_text: After doing this, the lord of men took that maiden and entered,
she being endowed with every ornament, wide-eyed like <s>Śrī</s> herself,
with a waist that could be spanned by the hand, possessing the five kinds of smooth beauty, and having an auspicious face,

children.text: strībhiḥ parivṛtāṃ divyāṃ śrīmatīṃ saṃśritāṃ tadā ||
children.translated_text: the divine <s>Śrīmatī</s>, then attended by women.

children.text: sabhā ca sā bhūpateḥ samṛddhā maṇipravekottamaratnacitrā
children.translated_text: That prosperous assembly of the king, variegated with excellent chief jewels and gems,
with seats set out, garlanded, and well arranged, was approached by those ranks of kings.
Then another great-souled blessed one, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, learned in the three Vedas,
the great sage <s>Nārada</s>, together with <s>Parvata</s>, foremost among knowers of brahman, arrived.
Seeing that the two had arrived, the king, his mind agitated with respect,
brought divine seats and honored both of them.

children.text: ubhau devarṣisiddhau tau ubhau jñānavidāṃ varau
children.translated_text: Both were divine seers and siddhas; both were the best among knowers of knowledge,
the two great-souled excellent sages seated there for the sake of the maiden.

children.text: tāvubhau praṇipatyāgre kanyāṃ tāṃ śrīmatīṃ śubhām
children.translated_text: Bowing first to both of them, the king addressed that auspicious maiden <s>Śrīmatī</s>,
his famous daughter, lotus-petal-eyed:

children.text: anayoryaṃ varaṃ bhadre manasā tvam ihecchasi
children.translated_text: "O gracious one, whichever of these two you desire in your mind here as husband,

children.text: tasmai mālām imāṃ dehi praṇipatya yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: give him this garland, after bowing according to rule."

children.text: evamuktā tu sā kanyā strībhiḥ parivṛtā tadā
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that maiden, surrounded by women at that time,
took up a divine golden garland, O fair-eyed one.
Coming to where the two great-souled ones were seated, she stood there,
looking at the two best sages, <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>.
Seeing <s>Nārada</s> with the face of a branch-animal, that is, a monkey, and <s>Parvata</s>
with the face of a langur, the maiden became somewhat frightened.
With her mind bewildered there, like a plantain tree in the wind,

children.text: tasthau tām āha rājāsau vatse kiṃ tvaṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: she stood still. The king said to her, "Child, what will you do?

children.text: anayor ekam uddiśya dehi mālāmimāṃ śubhe
children.translated_text: Choose one of these two and give this garland, O auspicious one."

children.text: sā prāha pitaraṃ trastā imau tau naravānarau ||
children.translated_text: She, frightened, said to her father, "These two are men with monkey faces.

children.text: muniśreṣṭhaṃ na paśyāmi nāradaṃ parvataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: I do not see the best sages, <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>.
But between these two there is one not yet sixteen years old,
endowed with every ornament, resembling an atasī flower,
long-armed, wide-eyed, with a high and excellent chest,
with waist and neck marked by lines, with long eyes red at the corners,
beautified by a pair of skillfully arched brows resembling a bent bow,
with the three folds clearly divided, and with a beautiful belly made evident by his navel,
clothed in golden garments, auspicious, with lofty jewel-like nails.
This one has lotus-shaped hands, a lotus face, and lotus eyes;
he has a fine nose, a lotus heart, and a lotus-navel, and is surrounded by splendor.
With rows of teeth very much resembling jasmine buds,

children.text: hasantaṃ māṃ samālokya dakṣiṇaṃ ca prasārya vai
children.translated_text: he smiles as he looks at me, and stretching out his right
hand, he stands there; I see him with auspicious hair upon his head.
Thereupon, while she stood trembling like a plantain tree, her mind confused,

children.text: sthitāṃ tāmāha rājāsau vatse kiṃ tvaṃ kariṣyasi ||
children.translated_text: that king said to her, "Dear child, what will you do?"

children.text: evamukte muniḥ prāha nāradaḥ saṃśayaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: When this had been said, the sage <s>Nārada</s>, fallen into doubt, spoke:
"How many arms does he have, maiden? Tell me exactly."
"I see two arms," said the maiden with a pure smile.

children.text: prāha tāṃ parvatastatra tasya vakṣaḥsthale śubhe ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Parvata</s> said to her, "On his auspicious chest,

children.text: kiṃ paśyasi ca me brūhi kare kiṃ vāsya paśyasi
children.translated_text: what do you see? Tell me. And what do you see in his hand?"
The maiden said to him, "I see a garland of five forms, unsurpassed,
on his chest, and a bow and arrows in his hand."
When this had been said, those two best sages, unsurpassed among one another,

children.text: manasā cintayantau tau māyeyaṃ kasyacid bhavet
children.translated_text: thought in their minds, "This must be someone's illusion.
Surely the magician, the thief, is <s>Janārdana</s> himself.

children.text: āgato na yathā kuryātkatham asmanmukhaṃ tvidam
children.translated_text: He has come. How could this monkey-face upon us not be of his making?"
Thus <s>Nārada</s> thought: "This very state of having a langur-face ..."
<s>Parvata</s> too, in the same way, thought anxiously in his mind,
"How has monkeyhood properly come upon me?"

children.text: tato rājā praṇamyāsau nāradaṃ parvataṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Then that king bowed to <s>Nārada</s> and likewise to <s>Parvata</s>,
and said, "What has been done here by you two, causing bewilderment of mind?

children.text: svasthau bhavantau tiṣṭhetāṃ yathā kanyārtham udyatau
children.translated_text: Let both of you remain composed, as you are engaged for the sake of the maiden."
Thus addressed, the two best sages, fierce with the king, said to him:
"You yourself are causing the delusion. We two are not at all to blame here.
Let this daughter of yours choose one of us two without delay."
Then that maiden again bowed down to her chosen deity,
and, having taken on the illusion, saw him standing collected between the two of them,
adorned with all ornaments and resembling the flower of the flax plant,
long-armed, with well-nourished limbs and eyes extending to his ears.

children.text: pūrvavatpuruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā mālāṃ tasmai dadau hi sā
children.translated_text: Seeing the man as before, she indeed gave the garland to him.

children.text: anantaraṃ hi sā kanyā na dṛṣṭā manujaiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Immediately afterward that maiden was no longer seen again by human beings.
Then a cry arose, and the two, amazed, said, "What is this?"
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme person, had taken her and gone to his own abode.
Long ago, for that very purpose, the lovely woman had constantly performed austerity;

children.text: śrīmatī sā samutpannā sā gatā ca tathā harim ||
children.translated_text: that blessed <s>Śrīmatī</s> had been born, and she went in that way to <s>Hari</s>.
Those two tiger-like sages, both disgraced and deeply distressed,
then went to the dwelling of <s>Hari</s>, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Seeing that the two had arrived, blessed <s>Hari</s> said to <s>Śrīmatī</s>,
"The two best sages have come here; conceal yourself now."

children.text: tathetyuktvā ca sā devī prahasantī cakāra ha
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it," that goddess, laughing, did so.
<s>Nārada</s>, bowing down before him, spoke to <s>Hari</s>, <s>Dāmodara</s>:

children.text: priyaṃ hi kṛtavānadya mama tvaṃ parvatasya hi
children.translated_text: "Today you have indeed done something dear for me and for <s>Parvata</s>.

children.text: tvameva nūnaṃ govinda kanyāṃ tāṃ hṛtavān asi ||
children.translated_text: Surely you yourself, O <s>Govinda</s>, carried off that maiden,
bewildering us two by your own intelligence and deceiving us, O best of gods."
When this was said, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the imperishable person, covered his ears
with his two hands, and the blessed one said, "What has been uttered by you two?
Though there may be desire, this is the disposition of sages? Ah indeed, such is ascetic conduct!"

children.text: evamukto muniḥ prāha vāsudevaṃ sa nāradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that sage <s>Nārada</s> said to <s>Vāsudeva</s>:
"How did a langur-face come to be at the root of my ears?"
At the root of his ear he said this: "The monkeyhood was made by me.
O learned one, I made <s>Parvata</s>'s face a langur-face for you,

children.text: mayā tava kṛtaṃ tatra priyārthaṃ nānyathā tviti ||
children.translated_text: and I made yours for him there for a dear purpose, and not otherwise."

children.text: parvato 'pi tathā prāha tasyāpyevaṃ jagāda saḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Parvata</s> also spoke in the same way, and he said the same thing to him.
While both were listening there, <s>Dāmodara</s> spoke these words:
"I have done what is dear for you two; by truth I swear by myself."
Righteous <s>Nārada</s> said, "Who is this bow-bearing man

children.text: dhanuṣmān puruṣaḥ ko 'tra tāṃ hṛtvā gatavānkila
children.translated_text: standing between us two here, who surely carried her off and went away?"

children.text: tac chrutvā vāsudevo 'sau prāha tau munisattamau ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that, that <s>Vāsudeva</s> said to the two best sages:
"There are many great-souled magicians, O excellent ones.
There surely <s>Śrīmatī</s>, not seeing the two best sages,
thought, 'I am always the discus-bearing, four-armed one.'

children.text: tāṃ tathā nāhamaicchaṃ vai bhavadbhyāṃ viditaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: But in that way I did not desire her; that is known to you two."
When this had been said, bowing down to him, the two spoke with pleased minds:
"What fault is there in you here, O mighty <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, lord of the world?
That was the wickedness of the king alone; he indeed made the illusion."
Having said this, the sages <s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s> went away from him.
Coming to <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, they bound him with a curse,
<s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s> saying, "Since we two came here,
and, after summoning us, you afterward gave the maiden to another,
therefore, through the power of illusion, darkness will overwhelm you.
And by it you will know yourself very fully, just as you really are."
When the curse had thus been given, a mass of darkness then arose.

children.text: nṛpaṃ prati tataścakraṃ viṣṇoḥ prādurabhūt kṣaṇāt
children.translated_text: Then, against the king, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus appeared in an instant,
and the terrible darkness, terrified by the discus, went toward those two.
Then the two great sages, all their limbs frightened, ran away.
Seeing behind them the discus and the mass of darkness, hard to approach,
the two hastened, thinking, "Ah, success with the maiden has indeed been obtained by us,"
running ceaselessly as far as the boundary of <s>Lokāloka</s>, afflicted by fear.
Afflicted by fear, crying "Protect us! protect us!" to <s>Govinda</s>,
they then went to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>: "O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, lord of the world,
O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, lotus-naveled one, <s>Janārdana</s>,
protect us two, O lotus-eyed one; you are our lord, O supreme person."
Then <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the glorious one marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, considered the matter,
and, wishing to favor his devotees, checked the discus and the darkness.
