"<s>Ambarīṣa</s> is my devotee, and these two also are best of sages;

children.text: anayorasya ca tathā hitaṃ kāryaṃ mayādhunā ||
children.translated_text: now I must do what is beneficial both for them and for him."

children.text: āhūya tattamaḥ śrīmān girā prahlādayan hariḥ
children.translated_text: The glorious <s>Hari</s> summoned that darkness and, gladdening it with his voice,

children.text: provāca bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śṛṇutāṃ ma idaṃvacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> said, "Listen to this word of mine.

children.text: ṛṣiśāpo na caivāsīdanyathā ca varo mama
children.translated_text: The seer's curse certainly was not otherwise, and my boon

children.text: datto nṛpāya rakṣārthaṃ nāsti tasyānyathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: was given to the king for protection; it cannot again be otherwise.
A greatly famous descendant, the son of the grandson of <s>Ambarīṣa</s>'s son,

children.text: śrīmān daśaratho nāma rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will be a righteous king, glorious, named <s>Daśaratha</s>.
I shall become his eldest son, named <s>Rāma</s>.

children.text: tatra me dakṣiṇo bāhur bharato nāma vai bhavet ||
children.translated_text: There my right arm will indeed be named <s>Bharata</s>.

children.text: śatrughno nāma savyaśca śeṣo 'sau lakṣmaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The left one will be named <s>Śatrughna</s>, and that <s>Śeṣa</s> is remembered as <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.

children.text: tatra māṃ samupāgaccha gacchedānīṃ nṛpaṃ vinā ||
children.translated_text: Come to me there; now go without the king.

children.text: muniśreṣṭhau ca hitvā tvamiti smāha ca mādhavaḥ
children.translated_text: And leave the two best of sages." Thus spoke <s>Mādhava</s>.

children.text: evam uktaṃ tamo nāśaṃ tatkṣaṇāc ca jagāma vai ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, that darkness at that very moment went to destruction.
The discus, restrained by <s>Hari</s>, stood as before.
The two best of sages, freed from fear, bowed down to <s>Janārdana</s>
and departed, tormented by grief; the two said to each other:
"From today until the end of our bodies, we two shall not take a maiden in marriage."

children.text: na kariṣyāva ityuktvā pratijñāya ca tāvṛṣī
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus and made that vow, the two seers
remained as before, pure and intent on yoga and meditation.
And that king <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, after ruling the earth,
endowed with servants and kinsmen, went to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
For the sake of honoring <s>Ambarīṣa</s> and likewise the two lions among sages,
<s>Rāma</s>, becoming the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, did not act as the lord who knew his own self.
And all the sages too, <s>Bhṛgu</s> and the other excellent sages,

children.text: māyā na kāryā vidvadbhirityāhuḥ prekṣya taṃ harim ||
children.translated_text: seeing that <s>Hari</s>, said, "<s>māyā</s> (deceptive illusion) should not be practiced by learned men."
<s>Nārada</s> and <s>Parvata</s>, after recognizing his conduct for a long time,
condemned the <s>māyā</s> (deceptive illusion) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and became devotees of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: etaddhi kathitaṃ sarvaṃ mayā yuṣmākamadya vai
children.translated_text: All this has indeed been told today by me to you:

children.text: aṃbarīṣasya māhātmyaṃ māyāvitvaṃ ca vai hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: the greatness of <s>Ambarīṣa</s> and also the possession of <s>māyā</s> by <s>Hari</s>.
Whatever man reads, or hears, or causes others to hear this,

children.text: māyāṃ visṛjya puṇyātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati ||
children.translated_text: abandoning <s>māyā</s> (illusion), pure-souled, he goes to the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
This is supremely purifying and holy, proclaimed by the Vedas.
If he reads it always, evening and morning, he obtains union with <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge śrīmatyākhyānaṃ nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the fifth chapter, named "The Account of the Glorious One."
The sages said:
We have heard of the power of <s>māyā</s> in <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the wise god of gods.
How did <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> arise from <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods?
You ought to tell this to us truthfully, O <s>Lomaharṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The glorious lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, creator, without beginning or end,
the lord of the world, made this world twofold in order to bewilder it.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> assigned the brahmins, the Vedas, and the eternal Vedic <s>dharmas</s> (sacred norms)
and excellent <s>Śrī</s> <s>Padmā</s> to one portion.
<s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Alakṣmī</s>, the inauspicious one, men outside the Veda, and the lowest of men,
and <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), the greatly radiant one assigned to one portion.
Having first created <s>Alakṣmī</s>, <s>Janārdana</s> afterwards created <s>Padmā</s>.
Therefore <s>Alakṣmī</s> is called <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, O best of twice-born men.
At the time when the nectar arose, after the terrible poison,

children.text: aśubhā sā tathotpannā jyeṣṭhā iti ca vai śrutam
children.translated_text: that inauspicious one arose; thus she is indeed heard of as <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.
Then <s>Śrī</s> arose, <s>Padmā</s>, the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
At that time a brahmin-seer named <s>Duḥsaha</s> married that inauspicious one,

children.text: jyeṣṭhāṃ tāṃ paripūrṇo 'sau manasā vīkṣya dhiṣṭhitām ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>; fully satisfied, he saw her as established in his mind.

children.text: lokaṃ cacāra hṛṣṭātmā tayā saha munistadā
children.translated_text: Then the sage, delighted in heart, wandered through the world with her.

children.text: yasmin ghoṣo hareścaiva harasya ca mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Wherever there was the sound of <s>Hari</s> and also of great-souled <s>Hara</s>,
and the sound of the Veda, O brahmins, and likewise the smoke of oblations,
or wherever there were men whose limbs were smeared with ash, there, afflicted by fear,
she covered her ears and went running here and there.
Seeing <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> to be of such a kind, <s>Duḥsaha</s> became bewildered.

children.text: tayā saha vanaṃ gatvā cacāra sa mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Going with her to the forest, that great sage wandered.

children.text: tapo mahadvane ghore yāti kanyā pratigraham ||
children.translated_text: In the dreadful forest, regarding great austerity and the taking of a maiden,

children.text: na kariṣyāmi cetyuktvā pratijñāya ca tāmṛṣiḥ
children.translated_text: the sage said, "I will not do it," and made that vow.
Pure and intent on yogic knowledge, where the sage, lord of yogins, was,
there he saw the great-souled <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> approaching.
Bowing down to the great-souled sage, <s>Duḥsaha</s> said:
"This wife of mine, blessed one, will not remain anywhere at all.

children.text: kiṃ karomīti viprarṣe hyanayā saha bhāryayā ||
children.translated_text: What should I do, O brahmin-seer, with this wife?

children.text: praviśāmi tathā kutra kuto na praviśāmyaham
children.translated_text: Where may I enter, and where may I not enter?"
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Duḥsaha</s>: everywhere ill fame is joined with misfortune.
This unequaled <s>Alakṣmī</s> is called <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.
Where those devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> follow the path of the Veda,
where great-souled devotees of <s>Rudra</s>, their bodies smeared with ash,

children.text: sthitā yatra janā nityaṃ mā viśethāḥ kathañcana ||
children.translated_text: always dwell, there you must never enter in any way.
Those who say, '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>,
<s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: rudra rudreti rudreti śivāya ca namo namaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and homage, homage to <s>Śiva</s>,
homage to the most auspicious one, to <s>Śaṅkara</s>,' always,
and who proclaim, '<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>,'
and always say, 'to the husband of <s>Umā</s> and to the golden lord,'
'homage, homage to you of golden arms, marked with the bull,'

children.text: nṛsiṃha vāmanācintya mādhaveti ca ye janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those people who joyfully and constantly utter '<s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, inconceivable <s>Mādhava</s>,'
whether they are Brahmins or Kṣatriyas,

children.text: vaiśyāḥ śūdrāśca ye nityaṃ teṣāṃ dhanagṛhādiṣu
children.translated_text: or Vaiśyas or Śūdras, you must never enter

children.text: ārāme caiva goṣṭheṣu na viśethāḥ kathañcana ||
children.translated_text: their wealth, houses, gardens, or cow-pens in any way.
The very terrible discus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, frightful with a garland of flames
and resembling a thousand suns, always destroys their misfortune.

children.text: svāhākāro vaṣaṭkāro gṛhe yasmin hi vartate
children.translated_text: In whatever house the exclamations svāhā and vaṣaṭ are present,
leave that and go to another, or to a place where the chanting of the Sāman is heard.
Those who are always intent on Vedic study and devoted to their daily duties,
and intent on worshiping <s>Vāsudeva</s>, you should dismiss from afar.

children.text: agnihotraṃ gṛhe yeṣāṃ liṅgārcā vā gṛheṣu ca
children.translated_text: Those in whose house there is the agnihotra, or worship of the liṅga in their homes,
or an image of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, or where <s>Caṇḍikā</s> stands,
go away from them from afar, leaving those who are free from all sin.
They worship <s>Maheśvara</s> with daily and occasional sacrifices.

children.text: tān hitvā vraja cānyatra duḥsaha tvaṃ sahānayā
children.translated_text: Leaving them, go elsewhere, O <s>Duḥsaha</s>, together with her.
Those by whom learned Brahmins, cows, teachers, and guests
and devotees of <s>Rudra</s> are always honored, you should avoid them.
<s>Duḥsaha</s> said:
Tell me, best of sages, the place into which entry is suitable for me.
Freed from fear by your word, I shall always enter their house.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:

children.text: na śrotriyā dvijā gāvo guravo 'tithayaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Where there are not learned twice-born men, cows, teachers, or guests,

children.text: yatra bhartā ca bhāryā ca parasparavirodhinau ||
children.translated_text: and where husband and wife are hostile to one another,
enter that man's house with your wife, free from fear.
Where the god of gods, <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the three worlds,
the blessed one, is reviled, enter there free from fear.
Where there is no devotion to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, where <s>Sadāśiva</s> is not present,

children.text: japahomādikaṃ nāsti bhasma nāsti gṛhe nṛṇām
children.translated_text: where there is no recitation, oblation, and the like, and no ash in men's houses,
where there is no worship on festival days, especially on the fourteenth lunar day,
where on the dark eighth day there is no worship of <s>Rudra</s>, and people are without ash at twilight,

children.text: caturdaśyāṃ mahādevaṃ na yajanti ca yatra vai ||
children.translated_text: and where they do not worship <s>Mahādeva</s> on the fourteenth lunar day,
where people are without the names of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and associate with the wicked,
and where foolish, evil-minded Brahmins and men do not say,

children.text: brāhmaṇāśca narā mūḍhā na vadanti durātmakāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Homage to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>, to the supreme lord,'
there indeed, child, you should constantly enter together with your wife.

children.text: vedaghoṣo na yatrāsti gurupūjādayo na ca
children.translated_text: Where there is no sound of Vedic recitation and no honoring of teachers and the like,
and where ancestral rites are absent, enter together with your wife.

children.text: rātrau rātrau gṛhe yasmin kalaho vartate mithaḥ
children.translated_text: In whatever house quarrel arises with one another night after night,
enter there with her constantly, free from fear.

children.text: liṅgārcanaṃ yasya nāsti yasya nāsti japādikam
children.translated_text: Where a man has no worship of the liṅga, and where he has no recitation and the like,
and where there is reviling of devotion to <s>Rudra</s>, enter there fearlessly.

children.text: atithiḥ śrotriyo vāpi gurur vā vaiṣṇavo'pi vā
children.translated_text: In whose house there is no guest, no learned Vedic Brahmin,

children.text: na santi yadgṛhe gāvaḥ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa ||
children.translated_text: no teacher, no Vaiṣṇava, and no cows, enter together with your wife.
Where, while children look on, a man eats food without first giving it to them,
there, delighted, enter together with your wife.
Where, without worshiping <s>Mahādeva</s> or <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
and without making offerings according to rule, people act, enter there always.
In whatever house or land fools devoted to sinful acts, without compassion for one another,

children.text: gṛhe yasmin samāsante deśe vā tatra saṃviśa ||
children.translated_text: dwell together, enter there.
Where walls and houses are ruined, and the housewife is not praiseworthy,

children.text: tadgṛhaṃ tu samāsādya vasa nityaṃ hi hṛṣṭadhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: having reached that house, dwell there always with a joyful mind.
Where there are thorny trees, where there is a bean-creeper,
and where there is a brahma-tree, enter together with your wife.
Where there are agastya, arka, and similar plants, or bandhujīva, in the houses,
especially oleander, or nandyāvarta as well,

children.text: mallikā vā gṛhe yeṣāṃ sabhāryastvaṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: or jasmine in their house, enter together with your wife.

children.text: kanyā ca yatra vai vallī drohī vā ca jaṭī gṛhe ||
children.translated_text: Where there is a kanyā creeper, or a hostile ascetic with matted hair in the house,
where there is abundant plantain, enter together with your wife.
Where there is palm, tamāla, bhallāta, and also tittiḍī wood,
or kadamba or khadira, enter together with your wife.

children.text: nyagrodhaṃ vā gṛhe yeṣāmaśvatthaṃ cūtameva vā ||
children.translated_text: In whose houses there is a banyan, an aśvattha, or a mango tree,
or an udumbara or a jackfruit tree, enter together with your wife.

children.text: yasya kākagṛhaṃ niṃbe ārāme vā gṛhe'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: If someone has a crow's nest in a neem tree, in a garden or even in the house,
or a daṇḍinī or a muṇḍinī, enter together with your wife.

children.text: ekā dāsī gṛhe yatra trigavaṃ pañcamāhiṣam ||
children.translated_text: Where in a house there is one maidservant, three cows, five buffaloes,
six horses, or seven elephants, enter together with your wife.

children.text: yasya kālī gṛhe devī pretarūpā ca ḍākinī ||
children.translated_text: In whose house there is the goddess <s>Kālī</s>, and a <s>Ḍākinī</s> in the form of a corpse,
Or wherever there is a <s>kṣetrapāla</s> (field-guardian), enter there together with your wife;

children.text: bhikṣubiṃbaṃ ca vai yasya gṛhe kṣapaṇakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: and in whose house there is an image of a monk, and likewise a <s>kṣapaṇaka</s> ascetic.

children.text: bauddhaṃ vā biṃbamāsādya tatra pūrṇaṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: Or, having reached an image of a Buddhist, enter there completely.
At times of lying down and sitting, in eating, wandering, and livelihood,

children.text: yeṣāṃ vadati no vāṇī nāmāni ca hareḥ sadā
children.translated_text: those whose speech does not always utter the names of <s>Hari</s>:
their house has been declared to you as a place to dwell together with your wife.
Those devoted to heretical conduct, excluded from śrauta and smārta observances,
devoid of devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and revilers of <s>Mahādeva</s>:

children.text: nāstikāśca śaṭhā yatra sabhāryas tvaṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: where there are atheists and deceitful men, enter there together with your wife.
Those who do not say that <s>Pinākin</s> is superior to everything
and remember him as merely common: enter among them together with your wife.
Those wicked souls do not say, "<s>Brahmā</s>, blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śakra</s>, lord of all gods,
are born from <s>Rudra</s>'s favor."

children.text: brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ śakraśca sama eva ca ||
children.translated_text: They say, "<s>Brahmā</s>, blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śakra</s> are just equal."

children.text: vadanti mūḍhāḥ khadyotaṃ bhānuṃ vā mūḍhacetasaḥ
children.translated_text: Those fools, their minds deluded, call a firefly equal to the sun.

children.text: teṣāṃ gṛhe tathā kṣetra āvāse vā sadānayā ||
children.translated_text: In their house, likewise in their field or dwelling, always with this wife,

children.text: viśa bhuṅkṣva gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ api pūrṇamananyadhīḥ
children.translated_text: enter and consume their house, even if it is full, intent on nothing else.
The fools and senseless people who eat only cooked food,

children.text: snānamaṅgalahīnāś ca teṣāṃ tvaṃ gṛham āviśa
children.translated_text: and are without bathing and auspicious rites: enter their house.
A woman who has fallen from purity and is without bodily refinement,
always inclined to eat everything: enter her place.
Enter the house of mortals with dirty faces, wearing dirty garments,
and of householders with dirty teeth.
Those who do not wash their feet and who lie down at twilight,

children.text: saṃdhyāyām aśnute ye vai gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: and those who eat at twilight: enter their house.
Mortals devoted to overeating and men devoted to excessive drinking,
deluded by gambling and contentious acts: enter their house.
Those who steal a Brahmin's property, or who sacrifice for unfit persons,
or who eat a <s>Śūdra</s>'s food: enter their house.
Sinful men devoted to drinking liquor and intent on eating meat,
mortals devoted to other men's wives: enter their house.
Those who delight in failing to worship on festival days, or who are given to intercourse by day,

children.text: saṃdhyāyāṃ maithunaṃ yeṣāṃ gṛhe teṣāṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: and those in whose house intercourse occurs at twilight: enter their house.
Those who have intercourse from behind, like dogs or like beasts,

children.text: jale vā maithunaṃ kuryāt sabhāryas tvaṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: or who have intercourse in water: enter there together with your wife.
If the lowest of men approaches a menstruating woman or a <s>Caṇḍālī</s>,

children.text: kanyāṃ vā gogṛhe vāpi gṛhaṃ teṣāṃ samāviśa
children.translated_text: or a maiden, or even in a cow-shed: enter their house.
What need is there of much talk? Those who are excluded from daily rites,
and who are without devotion to <s>Rudra</s>: enter their house.
If a man goes after smearing his penis with horns and petty potent herbs,
and from this causes a flow from the vulva, enter there together with your wife.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ityuktvā sa muniḥ śrīmān nirmārjya nayane tadā ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, that blessed sage then wiped his eyes,
and the Brahmarṣi, shining like <s>Brahmā</s>, vanished right there.
<s>Duḥsaha</s> then went to the places that had been described,
especially to those whose minds were devoted to reviling <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god of gods.

children.text: sabhāryo muniśārdūlaḥ saiṣā jyeṣṭhā iti smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: He was together with his wife, O tiger among sages; she is remembered as <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.
<s>Duḥsaha</s> said this to her in the space between a pond and a hermitage:

children.text: āsva tvamatra cāhaṃ vai pravekṣyāmi rasātalam ||
children.translated_text: "Stay here, and I will enter <s>Rasātala</s>.
After looking for a place of residence for the two of us, then again
I shall come to your side." When he had said this, she said to him:

children.text: kim aśnāmi mahābhāga ko me dāsyati vai balim
children.translated_text: "What shall I eat, great one? Who will give me an offering?"

children.text: ityuktastāṃ muniḥ prāha yāḥ striyastvāṃ yajanti vai ||
children.translated_text: Addressed in this way, the sage said to her, "Those women who worship you

children.text: balibhiḥ puṣpadhūpaiśca na tāsāṃ ca gṛhaṃ viśa
children.translated_text: with offerings, flowers, and incense: do not enter their house."
Having said this, he entered <s>Pātāla</s> there by means of a hole.

children.text: adyāpi ca vinirmagno muniḥ sa jalasaṃstare
children.translated_text: Even today the sage remains sunk in that expanse of water.
And she, the inauspicious one, always stays outside villages and mountains.
On one occasion she saw <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of gods and lord of the three worlds,

children.text: lakṣmyā dṛṣṭastayā lakṣmīḥ sā tamāha janārdanam ||
children.translated_text: together with <s>Lakṣmī</s>; that <s>Lakṣmī</s> said to <s>Janārdana</s>:

children.text: bhartā gato mahābāho bilaṃ tyaktvā sa māṃ prabho
children.translated_text: "My husband has gone into the hole, O mighty-armed lord, leaving me behind.

children.text: anāthāhaṃ jagannātha vṛttiṃ dehi namo'stu te ||
children.translated_text: I am helpless, lord of the world; grant me a means of livelihood. Homage to you."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus addressed, blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, laughed and spoke
to <s>Jyeṣṭhā-Alakṣmī</s>, the lord of gods, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
Blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> said:
"Those who here revile sinless <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
or <s>Ambā Haimavatī</s>, the mother even of the worlds,
or my devotees: their wealth is yours alone.

children.text: ye'pi caiva mahādevaṃ vinindyaiva yajanti mām ||
children.translated_text: And those who revile <s>Mahādeva</s> and then worship me,

children.text: mūḍhā hyabhāgyā madbhaktā api teṣāṃ dhanaṃ tava
children.translated_text: fools and ill-fated though they may be my devotees: their wealth too is yours.
By whose command, and by whose favor, I and <s>Brahmā</s> always exist:
those who worship me after reviling him are makers of hatred toward me.

children.text: madbhaktā naiva te bhaktā iva vartanti durmadāḥ ||
children.translated_text: They are not my devotees; arrogant men merely behave as if they were devotees.

children.text: teṣāṃ gṛhaṃ dhanaṃ kṣetramiṣṭāpūrtaṃ tavaiva hi
children.translated_text: Their house, wealth, field, and works of sacrifice and charity are yours alone.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having said this, <s>Janārdana</s>, with <s>Lakṣmī</s>, abandoned <s>Alakṣmī</s>,
and the blessed one recited to <s>Rudra</s> for the accomplishment of <s>Alakṣmī</s>'s destruction.
Therefore an offering should be given to her every day, O lords among sages,
by devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, without doubt, with every effort and always.
It should always be worshiped by women with various offerings, O brahmins.
Whoever reads it, hears it, or has the best of brahmins hear it,
that sinless one, through the account of <s>Alakṣmī</s>, becomes possessed of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and obtains the goal.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge alakṣmīvṛttaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the sixth chapter, named "The Account of <s>Alakṣmī</s>."
The sages said:
By reciting what is a creature freed from all worldly fears and the like,
released from every sin, and does he attain the supreme goal?

children.text: alakṣmīṃ vātha saṃtyajya gamiṣyati japena vai
children.translated_text: Or, having abandoned <s>Alakṣmī</s>, will he indeed go by means of recitation?
Will a mortal become an abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>? O <s>Sūta</s>, you ought to tell this here.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall tell in brief everything that was formerly spoken by <s>Pitāmaha</s> to the great-souled <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
for the welfare of all worlds.
Let all hear the word, having bowed down to <s>Janārdana</s>,
to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, god of gods, unborn, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the imperishable.
He is pure, remover of all sins, giver of liberation, and speaker of brahman.
The wise man who performs meritorious acts by mind, deed, and speech,
should constantly recite <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, after bowing to <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
Sleeping, he should remember the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; going, likewise <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Eating, O brahmins, standing, and waking, he should remember eternal <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Whether opening or closing his eyes, he should say, "Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>."

children.text: bhojyaṃ peyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca namo nārāyaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: Food, drink, and what is to be licked should be consecrated with "Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,"

children.text: abhimantrya spṛśanbhuṅkte sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: and, touching it after consecration, he eats; he goes to the supreme goal.
Freed from every sin, he also attains the state of the good.

children.text: alakṣmīśca mayā proktā patnī yā duḥsahasya ca ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Alakṣmī</s>, who is the wife of <s>Duḥsaha</s>, has been described by me.
Hearing the word <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, she surely goes away; there is no doubt.
That <s>Lakṣmī</s>, beloved of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the god of gods,

children.text: gṛhe kṣetre tathāvāse tanau vasati suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: dwells in the house, in the field, in the dwelling place, and in the body, O you of good vows.

children.text: āloḍya sarvaśāstrāṇi vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having stirred through all the śāstras (authoritative teachings) and considered again and again,

children.text: idam ekaṃ suniṣpannaṃ dhyeyo nārāyaṇaḥ sadā
children.translated_text: this one thing is well established: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is always to be meditated upon.

children.text: kiṃ tasya bahubhirmantraiḥ kiṃ tasya bahubhirvrataiḥ ||
children.translated_text: What need has he of many mantras? What need has he of many vows?
The mantra "Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>" accomplishes every aim.
Therefore at all times one should recite, "Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>."
He goes, O best of brahmins, with his kinsmen to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And hear another mantra of the god of gods, O best of sages,
formerly practiced by me, which accomplishes the meaning of all the Vedas.
It is joined with twelve syllables, twelvefold in nature, and ancient.
Here I shall briefly proclaim to you its very greatness.
There was a certain very wise brahmin who somehow performed austerity.
Having begotten one son and performed the saṃskāras (life-cycle rites) in due order,
and, at the proper time, having connected him with study and then performed his initiation,

children.text: adhyāpayāmāsa tadā sa ca novāca kiṃcana
children.translated_text: he taught him then, but the boy did not say anything.
His tongue did not move, and the best brahmin became distressed.
Only "<s>Vāsudeva</s>" did that <s>Aitareya</s> constantly say.

children.text: pitā tasya tathā cānyāṃ pariṇīya yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: Then his father, having married another woman according to rule,
begot sons, likewise in the prescribed manner.
Having studied the Vedas, they became accomplished and approved by all.
But <s>Aitareya</s>'s mother, distressed and faint with grief,
said, "The sons are accomplished and have mastered the Veda and Vedāṅgas.

children.text: brāhmaṇaiḥ pūjyamānā vai modayanti ca mātaram
children.translated_text: Honored by brahmins, they delight their mother.

children.text: mama tvaṃ bhāgyahīnāyāḥ putro jāto nirākṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: But you have been born as the son of unlucky me, without proper form.

children.text: mamātra nidhanaṃ śreyo na kathañcana jīvitam
children.translated_text: Death for me here would be better; life is in no way worthwhile."

children.text: ityuktaḥ sa ca nirgamya yajñavāṭaṃ jagāma vai ||
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, he went out and went to the sacrificial enclosure.

children.text: tasminyāte dvijānāṃ tu na mantrāḥ pratipedire
children.translated_text: When he had gone there, the mantras of the brahmins did not appear to them.
While <s>Aitareya</s> stood there, the brahmins were then bewildered.
Then speech arose from the chanting of "<s>Vāsudeva</s>."
Those brahmins bowed down to <s>Aitareya</s> exactly as was proper.
Then they performed worship, and the sacrifice itself came together.
Then, after completing that sacrifice, <s>Aitareya</s>, with wealth and the like,
attentively taught all the Vedas with their six auxiliaries to the assembled priests.

children.text: tuṣṭuvuśca tathā viprā brahmādyāśca tathā dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The brahmins praised him, and so too did <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, O brahmins.
Sky-ranging siddhas and cāraṇas sent down showers of flowers.
Thus, O best of brahmins, after completing the sacrifice, <s>Aitareya</s>

children.text: mātaraṃ pūjayitvā tu viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ jagāma ha
children.translated_text: honored his mother and then went to the place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
All this has been told: the splendor of the twelve-syllabled mantra,
which destroys great sins for those who read and hear it constantly.
The man who constantly recites the imperishable twelve-syllabled mantra
goes to that divine, matchless, supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Even one whose conduct is sinful, if devoted to the twelve-syllabled mantra,

children.text: prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: attains the supreme place; no deliberation is to be made about this.
How much more those great-souled ones who stand in their own <s>dharma</s> (right duty)
and are devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>: they attain the divine place, O you of good vows.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge dvādaśākṣarapraśaṃsā nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the seventh chapter, named "Praise of the Twelve-Syllabled Mantra."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
O best of twice-born men, there is the eight-syllabled mantra, "Homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,"
and the twelve-syllabled mantra of the supreme self is supreme.
O brahmins, the six-syllabled mantra is the compendium of the meaning of all the Vedas,
and the mantra "Oṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s>" accomplishes every aim.
Likewise "to <s>Śivatara</s>" is a divine, auspicious five-syllabled mantra.
and, in this way, "to <s>Mayaskara</s>"; and homage to <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
This seven-syllabled mantra belongs to <s>Rudra</s>, the chief person indeed.

children.text: brahmā ca bhagavānviṣṇuḥ sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and all the gods together with <s>Vāsava</s>
worship him with these mantras, O best of twice-born men, as do the sages.
They worship <s>Śaṅkara</s>, lord of the gods of gods, <s>Mayaskara</s>, born from the unborn,
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, the god of gods, the lord of <s>Umā</s>.
They declare, "Homage to <s>Śiva</s>; and homage to <s>Śaṅkara</s>."
"To <s>Mayaskara</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, and likewise to the one more auspicious than the auspicious";

children.text: japtvā mucyeta vai vipro brahmahatyādibhiḥ kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: having recited this, a Brahmin is freed at once from sins beginning with Brahmin-murder.

children.text: purā kaściddvijaḥ śakto dhundhumūka iti śrutaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago there was a certain capable twice-born man, known as <s>Dhundhumūka</s>,
in the third <s>Tretā</s> cycle, in the revolution of <s>Manu</s>, O lord.
In the <s>Meghavāhana</s> kalpa of supreme <s>Brahmā</s>,
having become a cloud, the god of gods <s>Janārdana</s> bore <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Kṛttivāsas</s>, the lord,
bearing <s>Rudra</s>, the god of gods, with great honor.
Wearied by <s>Rudra</s>'s excessive weight and deprived of inhalation and exhalation,
the lotus-eyed one, after making this known to <s>Śitikaṇṭha</s>, performed austerity.
Through austerity he obtained supreme lordship and also marvelous strength
from the supreme lord <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme self.
Therefore that kalpa then came to be called <s>Meghavāhana</s>.
In that kalpa, because of a sage's curse, there was the birth of <s>Dhundhumūka</s>.
From <s>Dhundhumūka</s>, because of that, his son too became evil-minded.
Formerly <s>Dhundhumūka</s> was attached, bewildered together with his wife.

children.text: tasyāṃ vai sthāpito garbhaḥ kāmāsaktena cetasā ||
children.translated_text: A fetus was placed in her by him with a mind attached to desire.
On the very day of the new moon, in a moment presided over by <s>Rudra</s>,

children.text: antarvatnī tadā bhāryā muktā tena yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: his wife, then pregnant, was released by him as he pleased.

children.text: asūta sā ca tanayaṃ viśalyākhyā prayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: She then carefully bore a son named <s>Viśalya</s>,
at a <s>Rudra</s> moment, while he was viewed by <s>Manda</s>, O best of sages.
He was born as a misfortune for his mother, for his father, and also for himself.
Then, O Brahmins, the two seers spoke privately to <s>Dhundhumūka</s> about him,
the two excellent ones named <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, saying, "He is a bad son."
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> said, "Though he is low, through the power of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
this son of yours, although evil-minded, will be freed from sin."
That <s>Dhundhumūka</s> was distressed when he saw his son before him.
Having himself performed the birth-rite and the others according to rule,
he taught him properly, O best of twice-born men.
That son, <s>Dhaundhumūka</s>, studied according to rule, O men of good vows.
Then, having married, he went and was intent on service to his teacher.
This very <s>Dhaundhumūka</s>, O best sages, out of arrogance,
after enjoying another woman, a low-caste woman, saw her as his own wife day and night.
<s>Dhaundhumūka</s>, the lowest of twice-born men, shared one bed and seat with her.
Thus that evil-minded man behaved, abandoning the supreme path of <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: mādhvī pītā tayā sārdhaṃ tena rāgavivṛddhaye
children.translated_text: He drank mādhvī liquor together with her, to increase his passion.
Then, for some reason or other, with reference to her, O best of twice-born men,

children.text: nihatā sā ca pāpena vṛṣalī gatamaṅgalā
children.translated_text: that ill-fated low-caste woman was killed by the sinful man.
After that, his father was killed by her brothers.

children.text: mātā ca tasya durbuddher dhaundhumūkasya śobhanā
children.translated_text: And the good mother of that evil-minded <s>Dhaundhumūka</s>,

children.text: bhāryā ca tasya durbuddheḥ śyālāste cāpi suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: his wife, and those brothers-in-law too, O men of good vows,

children.text: rājñā kṣaṇādaho naṣṭaṃ kulaṃ tasyāśca tasya ca
children.translated_text: were destroyed in an instant by the king. Alas, his family and hers were ruined.
Then that <s>Dhaundhumūka</s> went away, however he could, in a careless manner.
Seeing that best sage devoted to the muttering of <s>Rudra</s>'s name,
he obtained that <s>Pāśupata</s> from the god <s>Maheśvara</s> in ancient times.
He also obtained the five-syllabled mantra and the unsurpassed six-syllabled one,

children.text: punaḥ pañcākṣaraṃ caiva japtvā lakṣaṃ pṛthak pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and again the five-syllabled one, reciting each separately a hundred thousand times.

children.text: vrataṃ kṛtvā ca vidhinā divyaṃ dvādaśamāsikam
children.translated_text: Having performed, according to rule, a divine vow lasting twelve months,

children.text: kāladharmaṃ gataḥ kalpe pūjitaśca yamena vai ||
children.translated_text: he reached the law of time in that kalpa and was honored by <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: uddhṛtā ca tathā mātā pitā śyālāśca suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise his mother, father, and brothers-in-law were rescued, O men of good vows.

children.text: patnī ca subhagā jātā susmitā ca pativratā ||
children.translated_text: His wife became fortunate, smiling, and devoted to her husband.

children.text: tābhir vimānam āruhya devaiḥ sendrair abhiṣṭutaḥ
children.translated_text: Having mounted an aerial chariot with them, he was praised by the gods together with <s>Indra</s>.
Attaining the rank of a gaṇa-lord, he became dear to <s>Rudra</s>.
Therefore, from the eight-syllabled mantra and likewise from the twelve-syllabled mantra,
there arises merit multiplied ten million times; no doubt should be entertained here.
Therefore a wise man should recite it constantly according to the rule stated before,
joined with the seed-syllable of Śakti; he goes to the highest state.
All this, the excellent essence of every tale, has been told to you.
Whoever reads it, hears it, or has it recited to the best of twice-born men,
goes to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>; this muttering of <s>Rudra</s>'s name is unsurpassed.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the eighth chapter.
The sages said:

children.text: devaiḥ purā kṛtaṃ divyaṃ vrataṃ pāśupataṃ śubham
children.translated_text: Long ago the gods performed the auspicious, divine <s>Pāśupata</s> vow,
as did <s>Brahmā</s> himself, O <s>Sūta</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of unwearied action.

children.text: patitena ca vipreṇa dhaundhumūkena vai tathā
children.translated_text: Likewise, by the fallen Brahmin <s>Dhaundhumūka</s>,

children.text: kṛtvā japtvā gatiḥ prāptā kathaṃ pāśupataṃ vratam ||
children.translated_text: the goal was attained by performing it and by reciting. What is the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow?
How is the god <s>Paśupati</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme lord?

children.text: vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ ||
children.translated_text: You should tell us, for we have the highest curiosity.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, freed from a curse, a very glorious son of <s>Brahmā</s>
came here from the desert region of <s>Rudra</s>, the god of gods,
after abandoning, by <s>Rudra</s>'s favor and at <s>Aja</s>'s command, the body of a camel.
Having approached the son of <s>Śilāda</s> and bowed according to rule,
the best of sages, on the summit of <s>Meru</s>, after hearing the unsurpassed
<s>Māheśvara dharma</s>, asked again and again, O best of sages.
Having bowed to <s>Nandin</s>, he asked, "How is the lord <s>Paśupati</s>?"

children.text: vaktumarhasi cāsmākaṃ tatsarvaṃ ca tadāha saḥ ||
children.translated_text: "You ought to tell us all that." And then he told it.
The powerful <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>, heard all that;

children.text: tasmād aham upaśrutya yuṣmākaṃ pravadāmi vai ||
children.translated_text: having heard it from him, I now declare it to you.
Let everyone hear this statement, after bowing to <s>Maheśvara</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
How is the god <s>Paśupati</s>? Who are called the <s>paśus</s>?

children.text: kaiḥ pāśaiste nibadhyante vimucyante ca te katham
children.translated_text: By what <s>pāśas</s> are they bound, and how are they released?
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
O <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, I shall tell all this exactly as it is,
to you, a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>, peaceful and of auspicious mind.
From <s>Brahmā</s> and the others down to immobile beings, all belong to the wise god of gods;
they are called <s>paśus</s>, since they are subject to saṃsāra.
Because he is lord over them, blessed <s>Rudra</s> is remembered as <s>Paśupati</s>.
The beginningless and endless creator, the blessed, imperishable, all-pervading one,
the supreme lord, binds them like beasts with the bond of <s>māyā</s>.
He alone is their liberator, when served through <s>jñānayoga</s>.
For those bound by the bond of <s>avidyā</s>, no other liberator is accepted.
Apart from that supreme self, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme lord,
the twenty-four <s>tattvas</s> are indeed the bonds belonging to the supreme one.
With those bonds, the one <s>Śiva</s>, worshiped by the <s>jīvas</s>, releases them.
The one binds the <s>paśus</s> with twenty-four bonds;
that same blessed <s>Rudra</s> also releases them when he is served.
From bonds made of the ten senses and arising from the inner organ,
and from the bonds of elements and subtle elements, the lord releases the <s>paśus</s>.
Having bound sense-seeking beings with bonds made of sense-objects, the lord
quickly makes them become devotees in this way, through service to the supreme lord.

children.text: bhaja ityeṣa dhātur vai sevāyāṃ parikīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This verbal root <s>bhaj</s> is declared to have the sense of service.
Therefore service, when abundant, is called by the wise by the word <s>bhakti</s>.
Having bound the <s>paśus</s>, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a post,
with bonds consisting of the three <s>guṇas</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s> himself makes them act.
When worshiped by the <s>paśus</s> through firm <s>bhaktiyoga</s>,
<s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme lord, at once releases them.
Worship is called <s>bhakti</s>, performed by acts of speech, mind, and body.
Because it is the cause in every action, it is most skilled at cutting bonds.
Contemplation of <s>Śiva</s>'s qualities, such as truthfulness and omnipresence,
and contemplation taking his form as support: these they know as mental worship.
The wise know verbal worship to be recitation of the praṇava and the like.
Bodily worship is said by good people to be breath-control and the like.
This bondage of embodied beings is by bonds made of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>.
Blessed <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord, alone is the liberator.
The twenty-four <s>tattvas</s>, <s>māyā</s>, karma, and the <s>guṇas</s>,
and also the sense-objects, are called <s>pāśas</s> because they bind the <s>jīva</s>.
Bound by them, all embodied beings are released only through devotion to <s>Śiva</s>.
<s>Śaṅkara</s> binds the <s>paśus</s> with bonds made of the five <s>kleśas</s>.

children.text: sa eva mocakas teṣāṃ bhaktyā samyagupāsitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That same one, properly worshiped with devotion, is their liberator.

children.text: avidyāmasmitāṃ rāgaṃ dveṣaṃ ca dvipadāṃ varāḥ
children.translated_text: Avidyā, asmitā, rāga, and dveṣa, O best of twice-born men,
and abhiniveśa as well: these they call <s>kleśas</s> that have become bonds.

children.text: tamo moho mahāmohas tāmisra iti paṇḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: Tamas, moha, mahāmoha, and tāmisra, so the learned say,
and andhatāmisra: these they call <s>avidyā</s> established in five forms.
All those <s>jīvas</s>, O tigers among sages, and all beings through <s>avidyā</s>,
glorious <s>Śiva</s> releases; there is no other liberator.
They call <s>avidyā</s> tamas, and asmitā also moha;
the wise devoted to yoga call rāga mahāmoha.
They call dveṣa tāmisra, and likewise
abhiniveśa andhatāmisra, false knowledge, so the discerning say.
The divisions of tamas are eightfold, and moha is remembered as eightfold.
The subdivisions of mahāmoha are considered by the wise to be ten.
The perceptive say that tāmisra is eighteenfold,
and the divisions of andhatāmisra are likewise remembered as eighteenfold.
There is no connection of his with <s>avidyā</s>, neither past nor future;
nor could there be connection through rāga for the god <s>Śambhu</s>, who dwells in the body.

children.text: kāleṣu triṣu saṃbandhastasya dveṣeṇa no bhavet
children.translated_text: In the three times there is no connection of his through dveṣa,
of the god beyond <s>māyā</s>, <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Paśupati</s>, the all-pervading lord.
Likewise there is never any connection through abhiniveśa
for <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the giver of refuge, <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme self.
He has no connection at all with good or bad actions;
there could be none in the three times for <s>Śambhu</s>, who has transcended <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: vipākaiḥ karmaṇāṃ vāpi na bhavedeva saṃgamaḥ
children.translated_text: Nor could there be any contact with the ripenings of actions
in the three times for <s>Śiva</s>, the giver of welfare to all.
He is untouched by pleasures and pains occurring in the three times;

children.text: sa tair vinaśvaraiḥ śaṃbhur bodhānandātmakaḥ paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: apart from those perishable things, <s>Śambhu</s> is supreme, whose nature is knowledge and bliss.
He is untouched by latent dispositions that fall within the three times;

children.text: dhiyāṃ patiḥ svabhūr eṣa mahādevo maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: this self-born <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, is the lord of minds.
He is untouched by karmic impressions occurring in the three times,
and likewise by impressions from experience: the blessed destroyer of <s>Antaka</s>.
The blessed supreme lord is the god who transcends any special individual person;
he is beyond the entire manifest world composed of conscious and unconscious beings.
In the world, knowledge and lordly power are seen as having degrees of excellence;
because <s>Śiva</s> surpasses all in excellence, the wise call him <s>Śiva</s>.
At each re-creation, he at the beginning teaches the vast body of scripture
to the newly born <s>Brahmās</s>, who operate within the divisions of time.
He is the teacher even of teachers who are subject to temporal limitation;
he alone is the lord of all, free from temporal limitation.
This relation belonging to supreme excellences of knowledge is beginningless;
all such excellences, remaining in this way, are by nature entirely pure.
When there is no purpose of his own, grace toward others alone
is the purpose of all the acts of the supreme lord.
The <s>praṇava</s> is the expression of that <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme self;
the <s>praṇava</s> is remembered as higher even than words such as <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Rudra</s>.
Through meditation on <s>Śambhu</s>, who is denoted by the <s>praṇava</s>, and through recitation of it,

children.text: yā siddhiḥ svaparā prāpyā bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the accomplishment, both one's own and supreme, which is to be attained, surely arises; there is no doubt.
The truth of knowledge, the supreme <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga,
was taught by the god of gods out of compassion for all.
Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> indeed said: that imperishable which the yogins, O <s>Gārgī</s>, proclaim

children.text: abhivadanti sthūlamanantaṃ mahāścaryam adīrgham alohitam amastakam āsāyam ata evopurānasamasaṃgam agandham arasam acakṣuṣkam aśrotram avāṅmano 'tejaskam apramāṇam anusukham anāmagotram amaram ajaram anāmayam amṛtam oṃśabdam amṛtam asaṃvṛtam apūrvam anaparam anantam abāhyaṃ tad aśnāti kiṃcana na tad aśnāti kiṃcana ||
children.translated_text: as not gross, infinite, greatly wondrous, not long, not red, headless, shadowless, without old attachment, without smell, without taste, without eyes, without ears, beyond speech and mind, without light, immeasurable, without pleasure, without name or lineage, deathless, ageless, free from disease, immortal, the immortal syllable Om, uncovered, without before or after, endless and without exterior: that does not consume anything, nor does anything consume that.
Having known this supreme <s>Pāśupata</s> lord at the passing of time,

children.text: yoge pāśupate cāsmin yasyārthaḥ kila uttame ||
children.translated_text: there is indeed purpose in this highest <s>Pāśupata</s> yoga for the one for whom it is intended.

children.text: kṛtvauṃkāraṃ pradīpaṃ mṛgaya gṛhapatiṃ sūkṣmam ādyantarasthaṃ saṃyamya dvāravāsaṃ pavanapaṭutaraṃ nāyakaṃ cendriyāṇām
children.translated_text: Making the syllable Om into a lamp, seek the subtle lord of the house who abides at beginning and end, restraining the door-dwelling wind, swifter than wind, the leader of the senses.

children.text: vāgjālaiḥ kasya hetor vibhaṭasi tu bhayaṃ dṛśyate naiva kiṃcid dehasthaṃ paśya śaṃbhuṃ bhramasi kimu pare śāstrajāle 'ndhakāre ||
children.translated_text: Why do you dispute with nets of words? No fear at all is seen. Behold <s>Śambhu</s> dwelling in the body; why do you wander in the darkness of other nets of scripture?
Having understood thus correctly, the wise know what was then spoken by <s>Śiva</s> to the sages:

children.text: asamarasaṃ pañcadhā kṛtvā bhavaṃ cātmani yojayet ||
children.translated_text: having made the unequal condition fivefold, one should join <s>Bhava</s> to the self.
Thus ends the ninth chapter in the latter part of the blessed great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me again the greatness of <s>Umāpati</s>,
O devotee of <s>Bhava</s>, greatly wise blessed <s>Nandikeśvara</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
O <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, I shall tell you concisely and completely
the greatness of <s>Maheśa</s>, of <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme one.
He had no bond of <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), nor any bond of intellect;
nor was there a bond of ego, nor was there a bond of mind.
There was no bond of consciousness for him, nor was there any bond of hearing;

children.text: na tvacāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ vāpi bandho jajñe kadācana ||
children.translated_text: no bond of skin or eyes was ever produced.
He had no bond of tongue, nor any bond of smell;
nor any bond of feet, hands, or speech, O you of good vows.
There was no bond of the generative organ, nor bondage by the elements and subtle elements.
By his eternally pure nature, he is eternally awakened by nature itself.
He is called eternally liberated by sages who know reality,
this <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme one, who has no beginning, middle, or end.

children.text: buddhiṃ sūte niyogena prakṛtiḥ puruṣasya ca
children.translated_text: By his command, <s>prakṛti</s> produces the intellect of the person;
by his command, that intellect produces ego for him.
Of the self-born one, famous in bodies as the inner controller,

children.text: indriyāṇi daśaikaṃ ca tanmātrāṇi ca śāsanāt ||
children.translated_text: ego produces, by his rule, the ten senses and the one more, and the subtle elements.
Ego, under the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, brings them forth;
by the command of that lord, the subtle elements produce in turn.
All the great elements, belonging to wise <s>Mahādeva</s>,
produce, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to grass, the bodily condition of embodied beings.
All the great elements generate it by <s>Śiva</s>'s command.
The intellect determines all objects by the command of that all-pervading lord,
the self-born one, famous in bodies as the inner controller.
His lordly power is established by nature, and his powers arise by nature itself.
By his command, ego thinks itself to be all objects;
consciousness cognizes, and the mind also forms intentions.

children.text: śrotraṃ śṛṇoti tacchaktyā śabdasparśādikaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: By his power the ear hears whatever is sound, touch, and the rest;
this occurs by the force of the command of <s>Śambhu</s>, of <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme one.
Speech performs utterance and statement, and never grasping or the like;
it does so by the rule of that god over all bodies.
The hand performs grasping, never going and the like;
this is by the ordinance of the creator for all creatures.
The foot performs movement, never evacuation and the like;
this is by the command of <s>Śiva</s> over the whole multitude of embodied beings.
The anus performs evacuation, and never speech;
this is by the rule of the supreme lord over every creature that is born.
The generative organ continually produces pleasure by the word of the all-pervading lord;
this is by the command of the lord alone over all beings.
It grants space to all beings without exception.
the ether too, always, by the command of that supreme one.
At the instruction of <s>Śiva</s> himself, through its own divisions such as prāṇa and the rest,
the wind bears the bodies of all beings.
At the instruction of the god of gods, the wind, abiding in the seven aggregates,
sustains the course of the world through its own divisions such as āvaha and the others.
With the five divisions beginning with nāga, it operates in bodies,
by the command of the supreme god, as the moving air.
Fire carries the havya offerings of the gods and the kavya offerings of the eaters of kavya,

children.text: pākaṃ ca kurute vahniḥ śaṅkarasyaiva śāsanāt ||
children.translated_text: and it also performs cooking, only by the command of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Likewise, the fire that is always situated in the belly
digests the various food that has been eaten by embodied beings, at the order of the lord of the universe.
The waters revive all beings at his command;
for his weighty command is not to be transgressed by anyone.
By his command indeed it supports moving and unmoving beings;
by the command of that god, <s>Purandara</s>, the god of gods,
causes pain to the living through diseases and to the dead through hundreds of torments.
As <s>Viśvambhara</s>, at all times, by a command untransgressed by all the worlds,
he protects the gods and kills the Asuras, standing over the whole triple world.
By <s>Śiva</s>'s command he brings about the destruction of the unrighteous.
<s>Varuṇa</s>, by command, prospers the worlds with waters;
at his command he sinks the Asuras and binds them with nooses.
The lord of wealth grants wealth, according to merit,
to all living beings, by the command of that supreme lord.
Making rising and setting, the sun produces time
by the command of that eternal, true supreme self.
The moon, bearer of digits and having immortal rays, gladdens flowers, plants,
and creatures by the command of the death of Time.
The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s>,
and all the other deities are brought into being by his command.

children.text: gandharvā devasaṃghāś ca siddhāḥ sādhyāśca cāraṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Gandharvas</s>, hosts of gods, <s>Siddhas</s>, <s>Sādhyas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
and <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rakṣases</s>, and <s>Piśācas</s> are established in the ordinances of the creator.
Planets, lunar mansions, stars, sacrifices, Vedas, and austerities,

children.text: ṛṣīṇāṃ ca gaṇāḥ sarve śāsanaṃ tasya dhiṣṭhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all the groups of seers are founded upon his command.
The seven groups of the kavya-eaters, the oceans, mountains, and rivers,

children.text: śāsane tasya vartante kānanāni sarāṃsi ca ||
children.translated_text: as well as forests and lakes, abide under his command.
Kalās, kāṣṭhās, nimeṣas, muhūrtas, days, and nights,
as well as seasons, years, fortnights, and months, are established by his appointment.
Yugas and manvantaras stand by the command of this <s>Śambhu</s>,
as do parās, parārdhas, and other divisions of time.
The eight classes of gods, the five classes of animals,
and human beings proceed by the will of the wise god of gods.
The multitudes of beings born in the fourteen wombs,
settled in all the worlds, stand by his command alone.

children.text: caturdaśasu lokeṣu sthitā jātāḥ prajāḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: The creatures born and established in the fourteen worlds
are all subject to the appointment of that lord, the lord of all.
All the netherworlds and worlds exist by his command,

children.text: brahmāṇḍāni ca śeṣāṇi tathā sāvaraṇāni ca ||
children.translated_text: as do the remaining cosmic eggs, together with their coverings.
All present cosmic eggs, by his command,
exist everywhere together with all the elements and beings.
By his command, innumerable cosmic eggs that are past
have proceeded, surrounded on every side by masses of entities.
Cosmic eggs will come to be, together with the things belonging to them,
and, along with all their coverings, they will carry out <s>Śiva</s>'s command.
Thus ends the tenth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me the manifestations of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s>, O lord of gaṇas,
O best of those who know the higher and the lower, absorbed in the supreme lord.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Come, I shall tell you the manifestations of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śivā</s>,
O <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, lord of yogins, best son of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: paramātmā śivaḥ proktaḥ śivā sā ca prakīrtitā
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is declared to be the supreme self, and she is proclaimed as <s>Śivā</s>.
They call <s>Śiva</s> the lord, and the wise know <s>Gaurī</s> as māyā.

children.text: puruṣaṃ śaṅkaraṃ prāhurgaurīṃ ca prakṛtiṃ dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: The twice-born call <s>Śaṅkara</s> puruṣa, and <s>Gaurī</s> prakṛti.

children.text: arthaḥ śaṃbhuḥ śivā vāṇī divaso 'jaḥ śivā niśā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s> is meaning, <s>Śivā</s> is speech; <s>Aja</s> is day, and <s>Śivā</s> is night.
<s>Mahādeva</s> is the seven-stranded sacrifice, and <s>Rudrāṇī</s> is remembered as the sacrificial fee.
The god <s>Śaṅkara</s> is ether, and the beloved of <s>Śaṅkara</s> is the earth.
The blessed <s>Rudra</s> is the ocean, and the daughter of the lord of mountains is the shore.
The god who bears the trident is the tree, and the beloved of the trident-bearer is the creeper.
<s>Hara</s> is also <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Sāvitrī</s> is she who has <s>Śaṅkara</s> as half her body.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is <s>Maheśvara</s>; <s>Lakṣmī</s> is <s>Bhavānī</s>, the supreme lady.
<s>Mahādeva</s> is the wielder of the thunderbolt, and <s>Śacī</s> is the daughter of the lord of mountains.
<s>Rudra</s> himself is <s>Jātavedas</s>, and <s>Svāhā</s> is she whose body is half <s>Śarva</s>.
<s>Tryambaka</s> is the god <s>Yama</s>, and his beloved is the daughter of the mountain.
<s>Varuṇa</s> is the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Gaurī</s> is the giver of every good.
The wind is the one whose crest bears the young moon; <s>Śivā</s> is charming to <s>Śiva</s>.
The lord of yakṣas is the one whose diadem bears the half-moon; Prosperity herself is remembered as <s>Śivā</s>.
The moon is the one whose crest bears the half-moon, and <s>Rohiṇī</s> is beloved of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: saptasaptiḥ śivaḥ kāntā umā devī suvarcalā ||
children.translated_text: The sun is <s>Śiva</s>, and his beloved is the goddess <s>Umā</s>, radiant with good splendor.
<s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> is the destroyer of the triple city, and <s>Devasenā</s> is beloved of <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: umā prasūtir vai jñeyā dakṣo devo maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s> should indeed be known as <s>Prasūti</s>, and <s>Dakṣa</s> as the god <s>Maheśvara</s>.
<s>Manu</s>, called <s>Puruṣa</s>, is <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, and <s>Śatarūpā</s> is dear to <s>Śiva</s>.
They know <s>Bhavānī</s> as <s>Ākūti</s>, and <s>Ruci</s> as <s>Parameśvara</s>.
<s>Bhṛgu</s> is the god who struck out <s>Bhaga</s>'s eyes, and <s>Khyāti</s> is beloved of the Three-eyed One.
The blessed <s>Marīci</s> is <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Saṃbhūti</s> is beloved of the Lord.
They know lovely <s>Bhavānī</s>, and <s>Kavi</s> as <s>Parameśvara</s>.
<s>Aṅgiras</s> should be known as <s>Gaṅgādhara</s>, and <s>Smṛti</s> is remembered as <s>Umā</s> herself.
<s>Pulastya</s> is the moon-crested one, and <s>Prīti</s> is the beloved of <s>Pinākin</s>.
<s>Pulaha</s> is the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, and <s>Dayā</s> is dear to the enemy of <s>Kāla</s>.
<s>Kratu</s> is the destroyer of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice, and <s>Saṃnati</s> is beloved of the Lord.
<s>Atri</s> is the Three-eyed One, and <s>Anasūyā</s> is remembered by the wise as <s>Umā</s> herself.
The elders call <s>Ūrjā</s> ancient <s>Umā</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: śaṅkaraḥ puruṣāḥ sarve striyaḥ sarvā maheśvarī ||
children.translated_text: All men are <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and all women are <s>Maheśvarī</s>.

children.text: pulliṅgaśabdavācyā ye te ca rudrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are denoted by words in the masculine gender are proclaimed to be <s>Rudras</s>.
Those who are denoted by words in the feminine gender are all manifestations of <s>Gaurī</s>.
All females and males are said to be manifestations of those two alone.

children.text: padārthaśaktayo yā yās tā gaurīti vidurbudhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever powers of things there are, the wise know them as <s>Gaurī</s>.

children.text: sā sā viśveśvarī devī sa ca sarvo maheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Each such power is the goddess <s>Viśveśvarī</s>, and that whole thing is <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: śaktimantaḥ padārthā ye sa sa sarvo maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever things possess power, each and every one of them is <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The eight <s>prakṛtis</s> (primordial constituents) are proclaimed as forms of the goddess.
Likewise, her <s>vikṛtis</s> (derivative forms) are embodied manifestations.

children.text: visphuliṅgā yathā tāvadagnau ca bahudhā smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Just as sparks in fire are remembered as manyfold,
so all living beings are <s>Śarva</s>, having entered into paired existence.
All bodies of embodied beings are forms of <s>Gaurī</s>.
Likewise all embodied beings are established as portions of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Everything audible is the form of <s>Umā</s>; the hearer is the god <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The Lord assumes the state of the subject, while <s>Umā</s> assumes the nature of the object.
The beloved of <s>Śaṅkara</s> assumes the whole class of things to be created.
He himself, the soul of the universe, the bearer of half the young moon, is the creator.
<s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> bears visible objecthood in the form of creatures.
The seer is the god <s>Viśveśvara</s>, whose crest-jewel is a fragment of the moon.
The whole class of tastes, and everything that can be smelled, is the form of <s>Umā</s>.
The god <s>Śaṃbhu</s> is the taster, and <s>Bhuvaneśvara</s> is also the smeller.
The great goddess <s>Maheśvarī</s> assumes the character of an object to be thought.

children.text: mantā sa eva viśvātmā mahādevo maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: He himself, the soul of the universe, <s>Mahādeva</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>, is the thinker.

children.text: boddhavyaṃ vastu rūpaṃ ca bibharti bhavavallabhā
children.translated_text: The beloved of <s>Bhava</s> bears the object and form to be known.

children.text: devaḥ sa eva bhagavān boddhā bālenduśekharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He himself, the blessed god, the bearer of the young moon, is the knower.
The goddess <s>Umā</s> has the shape of the <s>pīṭha</s> (pedestal), and <s>Śaṅkara</s> has the form of the <s>liṅga</s>.
Having installed them with care, gods and asuras worship them.

children.text: ye ye padārthā liṅgāṅkās te te śarvavibhūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: Whatever things are marked by the <s>liṅga</s>, they are manifestations of <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: arthā bhagāṅkitā ye ye te te gauryā vibhūtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever objects are marked by the <s>bhaga</s> (yoni), they are manifestations of <s>Gaurī</s>.
From heaven and the subterranean worlds up to the eight coverings of the cosmic egg,
everything knowable should be known as the form of <s>Umā</s>; the knower is the god <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The goddess, beloved of the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>, bears the state of the field.
And the blessed destroyer of <s>Andhaka</s> assumes the state of the knower of the field.
If a king abandons the <s>Śivaliṅga</s> and worships other deities,

children.text: sa nṛpaḥ saha deśena rauravaṃ narakaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: he, together with his country, would go to the <s>Raurava</s> hell.

children.text: śivabhakto na yo rājā bhakto 'nyeṣu sureṣu yaḥ
children.translated_text: A king who is not a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>, but is devoted to other gods,

children.text: svapatiṃ yuvatis tyaktvā yathā jāreṣu rājate ||
children.translated_text: is like a young woman who abandons her husband and shines among paramours.
All the gods beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, and kings of great prosperity,

children.text: mānavā munayaścaiva sarve liṅgaṃ yajanti ca ||
children.translated_text: humans and sages too, all worship the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: viṣṇunā rāvaṇaṃ hatvā sasainyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ sutam
children.translated_text: After <s>Viṣṇu</s> slew <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, son of <s>Brahmā</s>, together with his army,
a <s>liṅga</s> was established according to rule and with devotion on the shore of the lord of rivers.
After committing thousands of sins and killing a hundred Brahmins as well,
one who takes refuge in <s>Rudra</s> with devotion is released; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: sarve liṅgamayā lokāḥ sarve liṅge pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: All worlds are made of the <s>liṅga</s>; all are established in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Therefore one should worship the <s>liṅga</s>, if one desires the eternal state.
These two auspicious ones, abiding in every form, should be worshipped by people seeking the highest good,
should be bowed to, and should always be contemplated.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the eleventh chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me the eight forms of the great-souled <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
of the god whose form is the universe, O lord of gaṇas, great-minded one.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Come then, I shall tell you the greatness of the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
of the god whose form is the universe, O offspring of the lotus-born one.

children.text: bhūr āpo 'gnir marud vyoma bhāskaro dīkṣitaḥ śaśī
children.translated_text: Earth, waters, fire, wind, ether, the sun, the consecrated sacrificer, and the moon
are declared to be the forms of <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Śiva</s> the supreme lord.
Ether, self, moon, fire, sun, waters, earth, and wind too
are declared to be the eight forms of that wise god of gods.
When an offering is placed in the <s>Agnihotra</s> for him, the great one whose nature is the sun,
then all the gods, as his manifestations, are always satisfied.
Just as, by watering the root of a tree, its branches and smaller branches are nourished,

children.text: tathā tasyārcayā devās tathā syus tadvibhūtayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: so, by worshipping him, the gods and his manifestations are likewise satisfied.

children.text: tasya dvādaśadhā bhinnaṃ rūpaṃ sūryātmakaṃ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: The lord's form, divided twelvefold and having the nature of the sun,
all-god-natured and fit for sacrifice, is worshipped by the foremost sages.
His digit called <s>Amṛtā</s>, belonging to that one whose form is all and who has the form of <s>Āditya</s>,
The activity that revives beings is always drunk in this world.
The rays called <s>Candra</s> of that <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>, whose nature is the sun,
send forth frost and rain for the growth of the herbs.
The rays called <s>Śukla</s> of that <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, whose form is the sun,
extend <s>dharma</s> (normative order) in the world, being the cause of the ripening of grain and the like.
The ray named <s>Harikeśa</s> of him whose nature is the day-maker,
is also famous as the nourisher of the constellations, belonging to the supreme lord.
The ray of his called <s>Viśvakarman</s> is the nourisher of <s>Budha</s>,
of the lord of all, the god whose form is the seven-horsed sun.
The ray of that bearer of the trident, known as <s>Viśvavyacas</s>,
is recognized, in its capacity as nourisher of <s>Śukra</s>, as belonging to him whose form is the sun.
The ray of the bearer of the trident called <s>Saṃyadvasu</s>
nourishes <s>Lohitāṅga</s>, being of him whose nature is a thousand rays.
The ray of that bearer of the bow <s>Pināka</s>, known as <s>Arvāvasu</s>,
always nourishes <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, belonging to him whose nature is heat.
The beam of <s>Śiva</s> called <s>Svarāṭ</s> nourishes <s>Śanaiścara</s>
day and night, belonging to him whose nature is the green-horsed sun.
Of the god whose nature is the sun, the source of the universe, the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
the ray called <s>Suṣumṇā</s> always nourishes the cool-rayed moon.
Having come to be the material source of the gentle ones born among the <s>Vasus</s>,
the form of that <s>Śaṅkara</s>, teacher of the world, is called <s>Soma</s>.
That lunar form of his, as <s>Śukra</s>, is established
in all embodied beings, of the god who chastises <s>Antaka</s>.
It is established in the mind of all embodied beings without exception:
the lunar body of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, that teacher of the whole world.
The form called <s>Soma</s>, the excellent one, of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, whose immortal digit is divided sixteenfold,
is situated in the bodies of all beings.
It always nourishes gods and ancestors with nectar-like ambrosia:
the form called <s>Soma</s> of that god of gods, the ruler.
It nourishes the classes of herbs for the purification of embodied beings' selves;
one should designate that body of his called <s>Soma</s> as <s>Bhavānī</s>.
As lord of sacrifices and also of living beings and austerities,
this lunar form of the lord of <s>Umā</s> is indeed well known.
As lord of waters and herbs it is renowned:
the lunar body of that blessed lord <s>Śaṃbhu</s>.
The golden god, pure, discriminating among one another,
is the formless divinity of all the instruments without exception.
When that lord <s>Śiva</s>, lunar in nature, abides as the living soul,
the sweet, sole protector of all the worlds, comes to dissolution.
The Śaiva form called the <s>Yajamāna</s>, by oblations day and night,
nourishes all the deities, and also the hosts of ancestors by offerings to the ancestors.
That body called the <s>Yajamāna</s>, born from offerings,
clearly brings all that is higher and lower into being by rain.

children.text: antaḥsthaṃ ca bahiḥsthaṃ ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ sthitaṃ jalam
children.translated_text: The water that is within and without, situated in the cosmic eggs,
and that is in the bodies of beings, is the weighty form of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>.
The nectar of rivers and likewise of streams at all times,
and of the oceans everywhere, the lord of <s>Umā</s> pervades all.
The reviving and purifying power of all beings,

children.text: aṃbikā prāṇasaṃsthā yā mūrtir ambumayī parā ||
children.translated_text: the supreme water-made form that is <s>Ambikā</s>, established as breath,

children.text: antaḥsthaś ca bahiḥsthaś ca brahmāṇḍānāṃ vibhāvasuḥ
children.translated_text: is the fire within and without the cosmic eggs,
and embodied in sacrifices: the weighty form of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>.
Situated in the bodies of beings, it is an auspicious lordly form,
the form established in fire, exceedingly worshiped as <s>Śaṃbhu</s>'s.
Forty-nine divisions are taught by those who know the Veda;
it carries the oblation of the gods, the sacrificial body of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>.
And the ancestral offering of the hosts of ancestors, being poured by twice-born men,
is declared by the knowers of Veda and śāstra to be <s>Śaṃbhu</s>'s best fire-natured body, consisting of all the gods;
and they worship it according to rule.
The wind is within the world-eggs and also outside them,
and in the bodies of beings; it is the very powerful Śaiva form.
The winds beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>, and those beginning with <s>Nāga</s> and <s>Kūrma</s>, and those beginning with <s>Āvaha</s>,
are all proclaimed to be divisions of the one form of <s>Īśāna</s>.
What is within the world-eggs and what is outside them is the space of the all-pervading lord;

children.text: śarīrasthaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ śaṃbhor mūrtir garīyasī
children.translated_text: and in the bodies of beings it is <s>Śaṃbhu</s>'s weighty form.
<s>Śaṃbhu</s>'s form as earth, the bearer of the universe, is the presiding divinity over all, beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>.
It is regarded as sustaining all beings, moving and unmoving.
The wise know the bodies of beings, moving and unmoving,
to have been completely begun from the set of five forms of the lord.
The five elements, the moon and sun, and the self, O bulls among sages,
are said to be the eight forms of wise <s>Śiva</s>, the god of gods.
His eighth form is the self, the supreme one called <s>Yajamāna</s>,
then situated in all bodies, moving and unmoving.
The lords of sages call the initiated Brahmin the self.
The form called <s>Yajamāna</s> belongs to <s>Śiva</s>, the giver of auspiciousness.
These eight forms of <s>Śiva</s> are to be carefully venerated
always by men who seek the good, for they are the single cause of all goods.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the twelfth chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me again, <s>Nandin</s>, the greatness of the lord of <s>Umā</s>.
of <s>Maheśa</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord, who has eight forms.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
I shall tell you the greatness of <s>Maheśa</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
of the supreme lord who, as the eight-formed one, pervades the world and abides there.
As the sustainer of moving and unmoving beings, whose nature is the supporter of the universe,
the god is called <s>Śarva</s> by those who have mastered the meaning of all śāstras.
Of that <s>Śarva</s>, the supreme lord whose nature is the supporter of the universe,
<s>Vikeśī</s> is said to be the wife, and <s>Aṅgāraka</s> is remembered as the son.
The blessed god is called <s>Bhava</s> by the expounders of the Veda,
he who gives life to the worlds, <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme self.

children.text: umā saṃkīrtitā devī sutaḥ śukraśca sūribhiḥ
children.translated_text: The goddess <s>Umā</s> is proclaimed as his wife, and <s>Śukra</s> as his son by the wise.
Pervading the seven worlds and the cosmic egg, the sole protector of all worlds,
the blessed god whose nature is fire is remembered by the learned as <s>Paśupati</s>.
<s>Svāhā</s> is declared to be the dear wife of that <s>Paśupati</s>, whose nature is fire.

children.text: ṣaṇmukho bhagavān devo budhaiḥ putra udāhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The blessed god <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s> is stated by the learned to be his son.
Pervading all the worlds, the bearer of all embodied beings,
the god whose nature is wind is celebrated by the learned as <s>Īśāna</s>.
Of <s>Īśāna</s>, the god who creates the world and whose nature is wind,

children.text: śivā devī budhair uktā putraścāsya manojavaḥ
children.translated_text: the goddess <s>Śivā</s> is called his wife by the learned, and his son is <s>Manojava</s>.
The giver of every desire to all moving and unmoving beings,
the blessed god whose nature is ether is called <s>Bhīma</s> by the learned.
Of the god <s>Bhīma</s>, of great majesty, whose nature is sky,

children.text: diśo daśa smṛtā devyaḥ sutaḥ sargaśca sūribhiḥ
children.translated_text: the ten directions are remembered as the goddesses, and <s>Sarga</s> as the son by the wise.
The blessed god whose nature is the sun, the giver of prosperity to all,
is called <s>Rudra</s> by the gods, the blessed giver of enjoyment and liberation.
Of <s>Rudra</s>, whose nature is the sun and who grants devotion to devotees,
the goddess <s>Suvarcalā</s> is remembered, and his son is <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
Renowned as the material source of all gentle things,
the god whose nature is the moon is remembered by the learned as <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Of the moon-natured god <s>Mahādeva</s>, by the wise,
his beloved is said to be <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and <s>Budha</s> is born from his body.
Then, maintaining the offerings to gods and ancestors among those who eat oblations and ancestral offerings,
the lordly god whose nature is the sacrificer is called <s>Mahādeva</s> by the learned;
he is called <s>Ugra</s> by the good, and <s>Īśāna</s> by others.
Of the lordly god called <s>Ugra</s>, whose nature is the sacrificer,
<s>Dīkṣā</s> is called his wife by the learned, and likewise his son is named <s>Saṃtāna</s>.
In the bodies of embodied beings, the hard substance, such as koṅkaṇa and the like,
should be known as his earthly body by those who wish to understand the reality of <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: dehe dehe tu deveśo dehabhājāṃ yadavyayam
children.translated_text: In each body, what belongs to the lord of gods and is imperishable among embodied beings,
that substance-natured material aspect belongs to <s>Bhava</s>, the supreme self.
It should be known by knowers of reality, who have mastered the meaning of all the Vedas.
The fiery transformation that exists in the bodies of embodied beings
should be known as the form of <s>Paśupati</s> by those who wish to know that reality.
The airy transformation that exists in the bodies of embodied beings,

children.text: budhair īśeti sā tasya tanurjñeyā na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: the learned should know as his body called <s>Īśa</s>; there is no doubt.
The hollow space that exists within the bodies of all embodied beings
should be known as the body of <s>Bhīma</s> by those who desire knowledge of reality.
The radiance situated in the eye and the other senses, which exists in the bodies of embodied beings,
should also be known as the body of <s>Rudra</s> by those who wish to understand the highest meaning.
In the bodies of all beings, the mind whose nature is lunar
should be understood as the form of <s>Mahādeva</s> by contemplators of reality.
The self called the sacrificer, present in the bodies of all beings,
should be known as the form of <s>Ugra</s> by those who wish to understand the supreme self.
Of all beings born in the fourteen wombs,
the great seers declare non-difference from the eight-formed one.
They say the limbs of embodied beings consist of the seven forms of <s>Īśa</s>;
the self, present in the bodies of all beings, is his eighth form.
This god of eight forms, the all-pervading one whose nature is all worlds,
worship with your whole being, if you wish to obtain the good.
If favor is shown to any living being whatsoever,
then worship has been performed for <s>Maheśa</s>, the eight-formed one.

children.text: nigrahaścet kṛto loke dehino yasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: And if restraint is imposed in the world on any embodied being whatsoever,
that very act is deemed to have been directed at <s>Maheśa</s>, the eight-formed one.

children.text: yadyavajñā kṛtā loke yasya kasyacid aṅginaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If contempt is shown in the world toward any embodied being whatsoever,
that would be contempt offered to the powerful <s>Maheśa</s>, the eight-formed one.

children.text: abhayaṃ yat pradattaṃ syādaṅgino yasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: If fearlessness is granted to any embodied being whatsoever,
thereby worship of the eight-formed one has been performed, without doubt.
Doing good to all and granting freedom from fear
is indeed worship of the god, the eight-formed one; there is no doubt.
Doing good to all and showing favor to all
is declared by the lords of sages to be the supreme worship of the eight-formed one.
Therefore favor is to be shown by you to other embodied beings,
and fearlessness is to be granted to all by one who desires to worship <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, latter part, the thirteenth chapter ends.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me the five <s>Brahmans</s>, O <s>Nandin</s>, best of gaṇas,
which bring about the good and are purifying for embodied beings.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
They are indeed the forms of <s>Śiva</s>, called the five <s>Brahmans</s>;
I shall tell them to you according to reality, O best son of <s>Padmayoni</s>.
He is the sole destroyer of all worlds and the sole protector of all worlds,
the sole creator of all worlds: <s>Śiva</s>, whose nature consists of the five <s>Brahmans</s>.
That which is the material cause of all the worlds

children.text: nimittakāraṇaṃ cāhuḥ sa śivaḥ pañcadhā smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they also call the instrumental cause; that <s>Śiva</s> is remembered as fivefold.

children.text: mūrtayaḥ pañca vikhyātāḥ pañca brahmāhvayāḥ parāḥ
children.translated_text: The five forms are celebrated, supreme, and called the five <s>Brahmans</s>,
belonging to <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme self and refuge of all worlds.
The <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field) is the first form of <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord,
the enjoyer of the class of <s>prakṛti</s> and of what is enjoyed, named <s>Īśāna</s>.
The second form of <s>Sthāṇu</s> is called <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>;
it should be known as <s>prakṛti</s>, whose nature is the hidden chamber of the supreme self.
The third, called <s>Aghora</s>, is the most weighty form of <s>Śambhu</s>;
that is said to be the form of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), joined with the eight constituents beginning with <s>dharma</s>.
