The fourth, called <s>Vāmadeva</s>, is the most weighty form of <s>Śambhu</s>;
it is established by pervading everything in the form of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-principle).
The fifth form of <s>Śambhu</s> is called <s>Sadyojāta</s>;
it abides in all embodied beings as the principle of mind.
<s>Īśāna</s>, the supreme god, the eternal supreme lord,
is established in all beings as the faculty of hearing.
The god <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> abides in the bodies of embodied beings,
and is declared by knowers of reality to have the nature of the faculty of touch.
Wise men also praise <s>Aghora</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, as having the nature of sight,
established in the bodies of all beings.
<s>Vāmadeva</s> too is known as having the nature of the faculty of taste,
dwelling throughout the limbs of all those who possess limbs.
Wise men remember <s>Sadyojāta</s> as having the nature of the faculty of smell,
established in the bodies of all beings that possess breath.
In all the bodies of beings that possess breath, he is established
as the faculty of speech; wise men call him <s>Īśāna</s>.
Wise men say that <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> is established as the faculty of the hands
in the bodies of all bearers of bodies.
<s>Aghora</s> too is established in the bodies of all embodied beings;
he is praised by knowers of reality as having the nature of the faculty of the feet.
<s>Vāmadeva</s> is established as the faculty of excretion,
remembered by sages in the bodies of all classes of beings.
The lordly god <s>Sadyojāta</s> stands as the organ of generation,
as accepted by those who know the Vedas and śāstras in the bodies of living beings.
The descendants among hosts of sages call <s>Īśāna</s>, the god of living creatures,
the form of the sound-tanmātra and the producer of ether.
The lordly sages call the god <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>
the essence of the touch-tanmātra and the blessed producer of wind.
The foremost knowers of the Veda call the god <s>Aghora</s>, even the fierce one,
the form-tanmātra and the producer of <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire).
Because he has the nature of the taste-tanmātra, knowers of reality declare
<s>Vāmadeva</s> to be established as the producer of the waters.
Those who know the meaning of all the principles praise <s>Sadyojāta</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>,
as the form of the smell-tanmātra and as the self of the earth.
The lordly sages call <s>Īśāna</s>, the first god, the self of ether,
wondrous, born from supreme greatness.
The wise know the lordly god <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> as wind and wind-natured,
celebrated because he pervades all the worlds.
And those who know the meaning of Vedic utterance describe
the great-souled <s>Aghora</s> as famed in worship and having the nature of fire.
Sages know the charming <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, as water-natured,
spoken of as the reviver of the world.
The best poets know <s>Sadyojāta</s>, the god, teacher of the world, as having the nature of the all-bearing earth,
the supreme supporter of all that moves and does not move.
The whole world, moving and unmoving, has the nature of the five <s>Brahmans</s>;
the sages who see reality say that this is the bliss of <s>Śiva</s>.
He who is seen in the manifest world as having the nature of the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>
is <s>Śiva</s> through having the nature of the five <s>Brahmans</s>; he has not become otherwise.
<s>Śiva</s>, whose nature is the twenty-five <s>tattvas</s>, has the nature of the five <s>Brahmans</s>;
therefore those who seek the highest good should always contemplate him with care.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge pañcabrahmakathanaṃ nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, called the Teaching of the Five <s>Brahmans</s>, in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Tell me once more of the greatness of <s>Śiva</s>, O wise one;
for you are omniscient concerning beings, O overlord, rich in great qualities.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Listen with one-pointed mind, O sage, and I shall tell you the greatness of <s>Śiva</s>,
praised in many ways and with many words by the best of sages.
Some sages and wise men call that <s>Śiva</s> the form of being and non-being,

children.text: taṃ śivaṃ munayaḥ kecitpravadanti ca sūrayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and also the lord of being and non-being.
He is called the second through the transformation of beings and states;
because he is without the manifest, he is also the unmanifest, called non-being.

children.text: ubhe te śivarūpe hi śivādanyaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Both of these are forms of <s>Śiva</s>, for nothing exists apart from <s>Śiva</s>.
And because he is lord over both of them, <s>Śiva</s> is called the lord of being and non-being.
Some sages who contemplate reality call <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
the nature of the perishable and imperishable, and also beyond the perishable and imperishable.
The imperishable has been said to be the unmanifest, and the manifest is declared to be the perishable;

children.text: rūpe te śaṅkarasyaiva tasmānna para ucyate ||
children.translated_text: those two are forms of <s>Śaṅkara</s> alone, and therefore nothing is said to be higher than him.

children.text: tayoḥ paraḥ śivaḥ śāntaḥ kṣarākṣaraparo budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Beyond those two is <s>Śiva</s>, peaceful and beyond the perishable and the imperishable, as the wise say;
in the highest sense he is called <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: samastavyaktarūpaṃ tu tataḥ smṛtvā sa mucyate
children.translated_text: Then, remembering him as having the form of all that is manifest, one is liberated.
He has the form of the collective and the individual, and is the cause of the collective and the individual.
Some teachers say that <s>Śiva</s> is the supreme cause.
The lordly sages know the collective as unmanifest and the individual as manifest.

children.text: rūpe te gadite śaṃbhor nāstyanyad vastusaṃbhavam
children.translated_text: These two forms of <s>Śambhu</s> have been stated; there is no arising of any other reality.
Because he is the cause of those two, <s>Śiva</s> is indeed the supreme lord.
By those who know the yoga śāstras he is called the cause of the collective and the individual.
And by some, <s>Śiva</s> is described as having the form of the field and the knower of the field.
He is the supreme self, the supreme light, the blessed supreme lord.
The twenty-four principles are the cause of the collective and the individual.
By the word 'knower of the field' they also call the experiencer, the <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit).
These two, the field and the knower of the field, are the forms of that self-born one.
The wise say that there is nothing at all apart from <s>Śiva</s>.
Some call <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, the form of the lower brahman and the nature of the higher brahman,
the lord without beginning or end.
He consists of the elements, senses, internal organ, <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), and objects.

children.text: aparaṃ brahma nirdiṣṭaṃ paraṃ brahma cidātmakam
children.translated_text: The lower brahman is so defined, while the higher brahman is of the nature of consciousness.
Those two brahmans belong to <s>Maheśa</s>, to this self-born <s>Śiva</s>.
Apart from that supreme <s>Śaṅkara</s>, apart from <s>Śiva</s>, nothing exists.
And by some <s>Śaṅkara</s> is said to have the nature of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
The establisher and ordainer of the worlds is <s>Maheśvara</s>, the primordial god.
The lordly sages call him <s>vidyā</s>, and they call him <s>avidyā</s> as well.
The whole produced manifold world is the form of that self-born one.
Delusion, knowledge, and the supreme: this is the unsurpassed form of <s>Śiva</s>.
Some sages versed in the āgamas attained this through yoga.
Cognition in relation to manifold objects is called delusion.
Consciousness in the form of the self is celebrated by the wise as knowledge.
Reality free from conceptual distinction is called the supreme.
There is no other third form of the Lord anywhere at all.
Some declare <s>Śiva</s> to have the form of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.
He is the ordainer of all worlds, the establisher, the supreme lord.
The wise speak of the twenty-three principles by the word 'manifest'.
By the word 'unmanifest' they also describe <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), the higher one.
By the word 'knower' they speak of the <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit), the enjoyer of the guṇas.

children.text: tattrayaṃ śāṅkaraṃ rūpaṃ nānyat kiṃcid aśāṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: That triad is the form of <s>Śaṅkara</s>; there is nothing at all that is not <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Again, O greatly wise one, I wish to hear truly
the forms that have been named by the lordly sages with many words in many ways.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ pravakṣyāmi śivarūpāṇi te mune
children.translated_text: Again and again I shall proclaim to you, O sage, the forms of <s>Śiva</s>,
which have been named by the lordly sages with many words in many ways.
By some lordly sages and teachers, he is called knower of the field, <s>prakṛti</s>, the manifest, and the self as time,
by those who have crossed the ocean of āgamas.

children.text: kṣetrajñaṃ puruṣaṃ prāhuḥ pradhānaṃ prakṛtiṃ budhāḥ
children.translated_text: The wise call the knower of the field the <s>puruṣa</s>, and <s>pradhāna</s> they call <s>prakṛti</s>.
They also call the entire mass of transformations, without remainder, the manifest product of <s>prakṛti</s>.
Time is the single cause of transformation for <s>pradhāna</s> and the manifest.
That fourfold set is indeed the fourfold set of the Lord's forms.
Some teachers describe <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord, as <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>,
<s>pradhāna</s>, and the one whose form is the manifest.
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the maker of this world, and the <s>puruṣa</s> is the experiencer of the universe.
The mass of transformations is called the manifest, and <s>pradhāna</s> is the supreme cause.
Their fourfold set, O wise one, is called the fourfold form of <s>Śiva</s>.
There is no reality at all apart from <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
By some the Lord is said to have the form of the individual body and the universal class.
All moving and unmoving bodies are called individual bodies.
All universals, and the great universal itself,
are spoken of by the word 'class'; these are the forms of the wise one.
By some the Lord is called <s>Virāj</s>, whose self is <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>.
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is the cause of the worlds, and <s>Virāj</s> has the worlds as his body.
Some praise <s>Śiva</s> as having the form of the thread and the undifferentiated.
The undifferentiated is indeed <s>pradhāna</s>; that is the form of <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>.

children.text: lokā yenaiva tiṣṭhanti sūtre maṇigaṇā iva
children.translated_text: That by which the worlds stand, like clusters of jewels on a thread,
should be known as the thread, a form of wondrous power.
By some he is proclaimed the inner controller and the supreme; by others, the Lord.
Self-luminous and known by himself is <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>.
<s>Śiva</s> is remembered as the inner controller of all beings.
Because he is beyond all beings, he is called the supreme.
He is the supreme self, <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme lord.
They know his threefold form as <s>Prājña</s>, <s>Taijasa</s>, and <s>Viśva</s>.
That is precisely the three states: deep sleep, dream, and waking.
It is also named <s>Virāj</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and the state called the undifferentiated.
For this <s>Śiva</s>, the fourth, who passes through the three states,

children.text: hiraṇyagarbhaḥ puruṣaḥ kāla ity eva kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>puruṣa</s>, and time are so proclaimed.
The three states are the causes of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the world.
Named <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Viriñca</s>, they are the three states of the ruler.

children.text: ārādhya bhaktyā muktiṃ ca prāpnuvanti śarīriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Having worshiped him with devotion, embodied beings attain liberation.

children.text: kartā kriyā ca kāryaṃ ca karaṇaṃ ceti sūribhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The agent, the action, the effect, and the instrument, so say the wise,
are proclaimed to be the four forms of <s>Śaṃbhu</s>, the supreme lord.

children.text: pramātā ca pramāṇaṃ ca prameyaṃ pramitistathā ||
children.translated_text: The knower, the means of knowledge, the object known, and likewise knowledge itself:
these four are the forms of <s>Śiva</s> alone; there is no doubt.
That which consists of <s>Īśvara</s>, the unmanifest, breath, <s>Virāṭ</s>, the elements, and the senses
is this transformation of <s>Śiva</s> alone, like waves of the ocean.
They call <s>Īśvara</s> the efficient cause of the worlds,
and the unmanifest is indeed <s>Pradhāna</s>; so it is said by those who teach the Veda.
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is called breath, and <s>Virāṭ</s> is remembered as the soul of the worlds.
The great elements, the beings, the effects, and the senses
the best of sages declare to be these forms of <s>Śiva</s>.
Poets know that there is no supreme self other than <s>Śiva</s>.
The twenty-five principles are said by the wise to have been born from <s>Śiva</s>;
they are not other than him, like a mass of waves from water.
They know the principle of <s>Śiva</s> to be higher than the twenty-five categories;
therefore those are not different from him, like bracelets and the like from gold.
The principles beginning with <s>Sadāśiva</s> and <s>Īśvara</s>, from the principle of <s>Śiva</s>,
have arisen and are not other than it, like the distinctions of pots from clay substance.
<s>Māyā</s>, knowledge, action, power, the power of knowledge, and the power consisting of action

children.text: jātāḥ śivānna saṃdehaḥ kiraṇā iva sūryataḥ
children.translated_text: have arisen from <s>Śiva</s>, without doubt, like rays from the sun.
Worship the god <s>Śiva</s>, who is the self of all and establishes the support of all,
with your whole being, if you wish to attain the highest good.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the sixteenth chapter.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Again, best of the hosts of gods, as I hear the supreme greatness of <s>Śiva</s>,
I have no satisfaction from drinking the nectar of your words.
How is the blessed one embodied? Why is powerful <s>Rudra</s>

children.text: sarvātmā ca kathaṃ śambhuḥ kathaṃ pāśupataṃ vratam ||
children.translated_text: the self of all, and how is <s>Śaṃbhu</s> so? How is the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow?

children.text: kathaṃ vā devamukhyaiśca śruto dṛṣṭaśca śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: And how was <s>Śaṅkara</s> heard and seen by the chief gods?
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
From the unmanifest arose <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause.
Endowed with every cause, he is the sage, the lord superior to the universe.
At first he saw <s>Brahmā</s>, born from the lotus of his mouth,
as the first god of the gods before him, and by command he looked upon him.

children.text: dṛṣṭo rudreṇa deveśaḥ sasarja sakalaṃ ca saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Seen by <s>Rudra</s>, the lord of gods then created everything.
And <s>Virāṭ</s> established the arrangements of the classes and life-stages.
He created <s>Soma</s> for the sake of sacrifice; from <s>Soma</s> this arose:
the oblation, the fire, the sacrifice, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the husband of <s>Śacī</s>,
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the glorious one; the whole world consists of <s>Soma</s>.
With the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, those gods praised <s>Rudra</s>, the lord.
The lord stood in the midst of the gods with a gracious face.
Then <s>Maheśvara</s> took away their understanding,

children.text: devā hyapṛcchaṃstaṃ devaṃ ko bhavāniti śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: and the gods asked that god <s>Śaṅkara</s>, 'Who are you?'
The blessed <s>Rudra</s> said, 'I alone am the ancient one.

children.text: āsaṃ prathama evāhaṃ vartāmi ca surottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: I alone existed first, and I exist now, best of gods.
I shall exist in this world; apart from me there is no one anywhere.

children.text: vyatiriktaṃ na matto 'sti nānyat kiṃcit surottamāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Nothing is separate from me; there is nothing else, best of gods.
I am eternal and non-eternal, sinless; I am <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>.
I am the directions and the intermediate directions; I am <s>Prakṛti</s> and the person.
I am the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meters; I am <s>Śiva</s>, made of them.
I am truth, all-pervading and peaceful; I am the triple sacred fire, reverence, and the teacher.
I am the tawny one, and I am the cavern; I am always whose range is hidden.
I am the eldest of all principles; I am the highest, the lord of waters.
I am the waters; I am the blessed lord; I am fire, and I am the altar.
I am the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>; I am the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the self-born.
I am the <s>Atharvan</s>; I am mantra, and also the best among the <s>Aṅgirases</s>.
I am the histories and Purāṇas; I am ritual procedure, and I am also ordering.

children.text: akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ cāhaṃ kṣāntiḥ śāntirahaṃ kṣamā
children.translated_text: I am the imperishable and the perishable; I am forbearance, peace, and patience.
I am hidden in all the Vedas; I am the most excellent, though unborn.

children.text: puṣkaraṃ ca pavitraṃ ca madhyaṃ cāhaṃ tataḥ param
children.translated_text: I am the lotus and the pure; I am the middle and what is beyond it.
I am outside and also inside; I am before all, imperishable.
I am light and I am darkness; I am <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
I am intellect and egoity, and the subtle elements and the senses.

children.text: evaṃ sarvaṃ ca māmeva yo veda surasattamāḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever knows all this to be me alone, best of gods,
he alone is all-knowing, everything, the self of all, the supreme lord.

children.text: gāṃ gobhirbrāhmaṇān sarvān brāhmaṇyena havīṃṣi ca
children.translated_text: I satisfy the cows by means of cows, all Brahmins by Brahminhood, and the oblations
by life; likewise I satisfy truth by truth, best of gods.
I satisfy <s>dharma</s> by <s>dharma</s>, and all beings by my own splendor.
Having spoken thus at the beginning, the blessed one disappeared right there.
Then they did not see the god <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme cause.

children.text: te devāḥ paramātmānaṃ rudraṃ dhyāyanti śaṅkaram ||
children.translated_text: Those gods meditate on <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the supreme self.
The gods together with <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, with <s>Indra</s>, and the sages likewise,
and the gods with arms raised upward praise <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the seventeenth chapter.
The gods said:
This blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
and also <s>Skanda</s>, likewise <s>Indra</s>, and the fourteen worlds,

children.text: aśvinau grahatārāśca nakṣatrāṇi ca khaṃ diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the planets and stars, the lunar mansions, space, and the directions

children.text: bhūtāni ca tathā sūryaḥ somaścāṣṭau grahāstathā
children.translated_text: The beings, likewise the sun, the moon, and the eight planets as well,
breath, time, <s>Yama</s>, death, immortality, and the supreme lord are he.
Past, future, what will be, and the present are <s>Maheśvara</s>;

children.text: viśvaṃ kṛtsnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ satyaṃ tasmai namonamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the whole universe, the entire world, and truth itself are he. To him, reverence again and again.

children.text: tvamādau ca tathā bhūto bhūrbhuvaḥ svastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: You were in the beginning, and likewise you are earth, midspace, and heaven;

children.text: ante tvaṃ viśvarūpo 'si śīrṣaṃ tu jagataḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: at the end you are the one whose form is all, always the head of the world.
You alone are <s>brahman</s>; for the sake of the twofold and threefold meaning, you are also below, O lord of gods.
You are peace, and likewise prosperity and contentment; you are what has not been offered and what has been offered.

children.text: viśvaṃ caiva tathāviśvaṃ dattaṃ vādattam īśvaram
children.translated_text: You are the universe and also what is beyond the universe; you are what is given and what is not given, O Lord.
You are what has been done and what has not been done, O god; you are the higher, the lower, and the fixed.
You are the final refuge of the good and also of the wicked, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: apāma somam amṛtā abhūmāganma jyotiravidāma devān
children.translated_text: We have drunk the soma; we have become immortal; we have gone to the light; we have found the gods.

children.text: kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ kimu dhūrtiramṛtaṃ martyasya ||
children.translated_text: What can hostility do to us now? What can the deceit of a mortal do to the immortal?
This is the divine, imperishable, subtle, undecaying welfare of the world.
It belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>, is purifying, lunar, ungraspable, and undecaying;
even by what is ungraspable it is to be grasped, as wind is grasped by what pertains to air.

children.text: saumyena saumyaṃ grasati tejasā svena līlayā
children.translated_text: By what is lunar he consumes the lunar, and by his own fiery power, in sport.
Reverence to him, the withdrawer of the waters, the great devourer, the bearer of the trident.

children.text: hṛdisthā devatāḥ sarvā hṛdi prāṇe pratiṣṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: All deities are established in the heart; they are established in the heart, in the breath.

children.text: hṛdi tvamasi yo nityaṃ tisro mātrāḥ parastu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: You are in the heart eternally; he who is beyond the three measures is that one.
The head is to the north, and the feet likewise to the south;

children.text: yo vai cottarataḥ sākṣātsa oṅkāraḥ sanātanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he who is directly to the north is the eternal <s>oṃkāra</s>.

children.text: oṅkāro yaḥ sa eveha praṇavo vyāpya tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: That <s>oṃkāra</s> is itself here the <s>praṇava</s> (sacred syllable), standing after pervading all.
It is endless, the <s>tāra</s> (that which carries across), subtle, white, and lightning-like.

children.text: paraṃ brahmā sa īśāna eko rudraḥ sa eva ca
children.translated_text: He is the supreme <s>brahman</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>; he alone is <s>Rudra</s> as well.
You are directly <s>Maheśvara</s>, the great god; of this there is no doubt.
Because it raises upward, it is proclaimed to be <s>oṃkāra</s>.
Because it protects the breaths, it is therefore called <s>praṇava</s>.
Because it pervades everything, it is the eternal all-pervader.
<s>Brahmā</s> and blessed <s>Hari</s> did not find its beginning or end.
Likewise others did not; therefore <s>Rudra</s>, the supreme cause, is endless.
Because he carries one across from <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), he is called <s>tāra</s>.
Becoming subtle, he always presides over bodies.
Therefore the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s> is renowned as subtle.
He is blue and red through his connection with <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>puruṣa</s> (spirit).

children.text: skandate 'sya yataḥ śukraṃ tathā śukram apaiti ca ||
children.translated_text: Because his seed flows forth, and because the seed departs, he is also called white.
Because he makes things flash forth, he is celebrated as lightning-like.
Because of greatness and because he causes growth, and because he grows in the higher and lower,
therefore, since he expands, he is proclaimed the supreme <s>brahman</s>.
The blessed supreme lord is without a second, and is the fourth state.
He is the ruler of this world, the eye of those who see heaven, the Lord.
<s>Indra</s>, the seers, and all others always call him <s>Īśāna</s>.
He is <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of all branches of knowledge; for that reason he is called <s>Īśāna</s>.
And because the blessed one sees, by his command what is to be seen is called the object of sight.
The great god himself leads one to self-knowledge and yoga.
The god is also called blessed, god of gods, <s>Maheśvara</s>.
<s>Maheśvara</s> grasps all the worlds in due order,
and this lord of gods sends them forth and causes them to dwell, all in sport.

children.text: eṣo hi devaḥ pradiśo 'nusarvāḥ pūrvo hi jātaḥ sa u garbhe antaḥ
children.translated_text: This god follows all the directions; born before, he is also within the womb.

children.text: sa eva jātaḥ sa janiṣyamāṇaḥ pratyaṅmukhāstiṣṭhati sarvatomukhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He alone has been born, and he will be born; facing inward, he stands facing every direction.
This imperishable one should be worshiped with effort by the good,

children.text: yato vāco nivartante hyaprāpya manasā saha ||
children.translated_text: from whom words turn back, together with the mind, without reaching him.
Here, that very non-grasping is what speech tries to express with effort,

children.text: aparaṃ ca paraṃ veti parāyaṇamiti svayam ||
children.translated_text: saying, 'It is lower and higher,' and 'It is the final refuge.'
Words call the omniscient <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>.

children.text: eṣa sarvo namastasmai puruṣaḥ piṅgalaḥ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This all, this <s>puruṣa</s>, tawny <s>Śiva</s>, is he; reverence to him.

children.text: sa eṣa sa mahārudro viśvaṃ bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: He is this, he is the great <s>Rudra</s>; he has been and will be the universe.
The world, born in many forms and arising here and there, is he.
The blessed one has golden arms; he is the golden lord and ruler.
He is the husband of <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, golden-seeded, with the bull as his banner.
He is the husband of <s>Umā</s>, the odd-eyed one, creator of the universe and bearer of the universe.
He who in the beginning fashioned ancient <s>Brahmā</s> as his son,
sent forth to him knowledge that reveals the self.
That single <s>puruṣa</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, much-invoked and much-praised,

children.text: vālāgramātraṃ hṛdayasya madhye viśvaṃ devaṃ vahnirūpaṃ vareṇyam
children.translated_text: minute as the tip of a hair, in the middle of the heart, the universal god, fire-formed, most excellent,

children.text: tamātmasthaṃ ye 'nupaśyanti dhīrāsteṣāṃ śāntiḥ śāśvatī netareṣām ||
children.translated_text: those wise ones who behold him abiding in the self have eternal peace, not others.
He is greater than the great and smaller even than the small, imperishable;
the self, <s>Maheśvara</s>, is hidden in the cave of this creature.
He himself, lodged in the lotus of the heart, is the dwelling-place of this universe.
Deep and hard to penetrate, he stands within it, and inside it he is situated above.
There too is the small space, <s>oṃkāra</s>, the supreme lord.
In the midst of that, minute as the tip of a hair, is truth, the supreme cause.
He is truth, <s>brahman</s>, the great god, the dark-tawny <s>puruṣa</s>,
whose seed is raised upward, <s>Īśāna</s>, the odd-eyed one, unborn yet source-born.

children.text: adhitiṣṭhati yoniṃ yo yoniṃ vācaika īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: He who presides over the womb, or over speech as womb, is the one Lord.
that ancient <s>Īśāna</s>, by whom the body is fivefold.

children.text: prāṇeṣvantarmanaso liṅgamāhuryasminkrodho yā ca tṛṣṇā kṣamā ca
children.translated_text: They call the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle mark) within the mind, among the breaths, that in which are anger, thirst, and forgiveness.

children.text: tṛṣṇāṃ chittvā hetujālasya mūlaṃ buddhyā cintyaṃ sthāpayitvā ca rudre ||
children.translated_text: Having cut off thirst, the root of the net of causes, and having fixed in <s>Rudra</s> what is to be contemplated by the intellect,
they call that one <s>Rudra</s>, eternal, the supreme lord,
higher even than the highest, higher than the highest, fixed and certain.
<s>Sadāśiva</s>, the begetter of <s>Brahmā</s>, of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, of fire and wind,

children.text: dhyātvāgninā ca śodhyāṅgaṃ viśodhya ca pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: having meditated on him, one should purify the body with fire and purify it part by part.
Restraining the five elements according to the sequence of measure, rule, and quality,

children.text: mātrāḥ pañca catasraśca trimātrā dvistataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: there are five <s>mātrās</s> (measures), then four, three measures, then two thereafter,
one measure, and indeed the measureless, established at the twelfth endpoint.

children.text: sthitvā sthāpyāmṛto bhūtvā vrataṃ pāśupataṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: Having stood there, having established it, and having become immortal, one should practice the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.
I shall perform this <s>Pāśupata</s> vow in brief.
Having laid the fire according to rule, with mantras arising from the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>,
having fasted, pure, bathed, and himself wearing white garments,
wearing a white sacred thread, and adorned with white garlands and unguents,
the learned man, free from impurity, should offer oblations, and he will become free from impurity.
Let the five vital winds be purified, and speech, mind, feet, and the rest.

children.text: śrotraṃ jihvā tataḥ prāṇastato buddhistathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Let hearing, the tongue, then breath, and then the intellect likewise be purified.
Let the head, hands, side, back, and belly thereafter be purified.

children.text: jaṅghe śiśnam upasthaṃ ca pāyurmeḍhraṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Let the shanks, penis, generative organ, anus, and member likewise be purified.

children.text: tvacā māṃsaṃ ca rudhiraṃ medo 'sthīni tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Let skin, flesh, blood, fat, and bones likewise be purified.

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśaṃ ca rūpaṃ ca raso gandhastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Let sound, touch, form, taste, and smell likewise be purified.
Let the elements themselves be purified, and in the body fat and the rest likewise.

children.text: annaṃ prāṇe mano jñānaṃ śudhyantāṃ vai śivecchayā
children.translated_text: Let food, breath, mind, and knowledge be purified by the will of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having offered oblations with ghee, fuel sticks, and <s>caru</s> (sacrificial porridge), each in due order,
having gathered in the <s>Rudra</s>-fire and carefully taken the ash,
with the formula beginning 'Agnir,' the wise man should rub his limbs and touch them.
This divine <s>Pāśupata</s> vow releases one from bondage.

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ hitaṃ proktaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: It has been declared beneficial for brāhmaṇas, and likewise for kṣatriyas,
also suitable for vaiśyas, and especially for ascetics,
for those dwelling in the forest-hermit stage, and also for virtuous householders.
Liberation by this method is indeed seen for brahmacārins as well.
Taking ash produced from the <s>agnihotra</s> with the formula beginning 'Agnir,'
that brāhmaṇa too, being <s>Pāśupata</s>, should rub his limbs and touch them.
A learned twice-born man covered with ash, from sins born of great crimes,

children.text: pāpair vimucyate sadyo mucyate ca na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: is freed at once; he is released, without doubt.
Since ash is the potency of fire, one joined with ash is potent.
A brāhmaṇa devoted to bathing in ash, sleeping on ash, and master of his senses,
freed from every sin, attains union with <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore the wise man should, with every effort, worship his limbs with <s>bhūti</s> (sacred ash).
The cry 're re' is not to be made, nor likewise the sound 'tuṃ tuṃ.'

children.text: na tatkṣamati deveśo brahmā vā yadi keśavaḥ
children.translated_text: The lord of gods does not forgive that, even if <s>Brahmā</s> or <s>Keśava</s> does.
O fair-faced one, my son <s>Gaṇeśa</s> is a bearer of ash.

children.text: teṣāṃ viruddhaṃ yattyājyaṃ sa yāti narakārṇavam
children.translated_text: Whatever is opposed to them is to be abandoned; such a man goes to the ocean of hell.

children.text: gṛhastho brahmahīno'pi tripuṇḍraṃ yo na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Even a householder lacking sacred knowledge, if he does not make the <s>tripuṇḍra</s> (three ash-lines),

children.text: pūjā karma kriyā tasya dānaṃ snānaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: his worship, rite, ritual action, gift, and bathing likewise

children.text: niṣphalaṃ jāyate sarvaṃ yathā bhasmani vai hutam ||
children.translated_text: all become fruitless, just as an oblation offered into ashes.
Therefore, in all undertakings, the wise man should wear the <s>tripuṇḍra</s>.

children.text: ityuktvā bhagavānbrahmā stutvā devaiḥ samaṃ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord, having praised together with the gods,
himself covered with ash among those covered with ash, ceased, O lord of men.
Then, for the sake of showing favor to them, <s>Īśvara</s>, the lord of creatures,
the lord, together with his gaṇas and with <s>Ambā</s>, made his presence there.
Then they praised <s>Rudra</s>, present there, the chief of the gods,
the lord of all, the god of gods, the husband of <s>Umā</s>, with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>.
The god too, <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>, seeing the gods with compassion,
said to the gods, 'I am pleased,' wishing to grant a boon, he who destroys the enemies of the gods.
Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Having bowed down to that lord, <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>, whose mind was pleased,
the sages and gods asked, their skin bristling with joy.
The gods said:
Blessed lord, by what path should you be worshiped by twice-born men?

children.text: kutra vā kena rūpeṇa vaktumarhasi śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: And where, and in what form? You should tell us, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Who has authority in worship? How is it for a brāhmaṇa, O lord?
How is it for kṣatriyas, O god, and for vaiśyas, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>?

children.text: strīśūdrāṇāṃ kathaṃ vāpi kuṇḍagolādināṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: And how is it for women and śūdras, or for <s>kuṇḍa</s>, <s>gola</s>, and the like?
For the welfare of all the worlds, you should tell us everything.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Seeing the disposition of those sages, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
<s>Sadāśiva</s>, standing in the maṇḍala, spoke in a deep voice.
In the maṇḍala before them they saw the god of gods together with <s>Umā</s>,
and all the gods and sages, brilliant as ten million flashes of lightning,
the god with eight arms, four faces, twelve eyes, and mighty arms,
<s>Ardhanārīśvara</s>, wearing a crown of matted hair,
adorned with every ornament, with red garlands and unguents,
wearing red garments, the maker of creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
His eastern face was yellow, serene, and of the nature of <s>Puruṣa</s>.
His southern face was <s>Aghora</s>, like a mass of blue-black collyrium,
terribly fierce, dreadful with fangs, and enveloped in a garland of flames.
It had a red beard and matted hair; and on the north was a coral-colored radiance.
The face called <s>Vāmadeva</s> was gracious, boon-giving, and of universal form.
His western face was auspicious, white as cow's milk,
adorned with necklaces made of pearls and shining with a tilaka.
That divine face of the enemy of <s>Smara</s>, called <s>Sadyojāta</s>, belonged to <s>Bhāskara</s>.
In front he saw <s>Āditya</s>, four-faced as before,

children.text: bhāskaraṃ purato devaṃ caturvaktraṃ ca pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: the god <s>Bhāskara</s> before him, likewise four-faced as before.

children.text: bhānuṃ dakṣiṇato devaṃ caturvaktraṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: To the south he saw the god <s>Bhānu</s>, likewise four-faced as before,
and to the north he saw <s>Ravi</s>, four-faced as before.

children.text: vistārāṃ maṇḍale pūrve uttarāṃ dakṣiṇe sthitām
children.translated_text: In the eastern maṇḍala stood <s>Vistārā</s>, and in the southern stood <s>Uttarā</s>.
In the western part of <s>Prajāpati</s>'s maṇḍala stood <s>Bodhanī</s>,
and in the northern quarter stood <s>Adhyāyanī</s>, one-faced and four-armed.
These śaktis, richly furnished with every ornament, were approved by all.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge viṣṇuṃ vāme janārdanam
children.translated_text: On the southern side was <s>Brahmā</s>, and on the left was <s>Viṣṇu Janārdana</s>.
By the path of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Śiva</s> consisted of the three forms.
He was <s>Īśāna</s>, the boon-giving god, <s>Īśāna</s>, the supreme lord,
seated on the seat of <s>Brahmā</s>, granting boons, upon the seat of <s>dharma</s> and knowledge,
joined with detachment and lordly power, abundant and stainless as well.
He was the essence, the god who is lord of all, worthy of worship, supreme happiness.
He stood in the middle of a white lotus, surrounded by <s>Dīptā</s> and the others:
<s>Dīptā</s>, shaped like a lamp-flame, subtle, auspicious, with the brilliance of lightning;
<s>Jayā</s>, shaped like a flame of fire; <s>Prabhā</s>, with the radiance of gold;
<s>Vibhūti</s>, resembling coral; <s>Vimalā</s>, like a lotus;
<s>Amoghā</s>, shaped like a pericarp; and <s>Vidyut</s>, colored with all hues.
The goddess was four-faced, four-colored, and facing in every direction.
There were the gods <s>Soma</s> and <s>Maṅgāraka</s>, and <s>Budha</s>, best of the intelligent,
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, of great wisdom, and <s>Bhārgava</s>, a storehouse of brilliance,

children.text: mandaṃ mandagatiṃ caiva samantāttasya te sadā
children.translated_text: and <s>Manda</s>, slow in motion; they are always all around him.

children.text: sūryaṃ śivo jagannāthaḥ somaḥ sākṣādumā svayam ||
children.translated_text: The sun was <s>Śiva</s>, lord of the world; the moon was directly <s>Umā</s> herself.
The remaining five elements, and all that moves and does not move, were made of him.
Seeing <s>Umāpati</s>, the god of gods, all the sages,
all the sages and the deities likewise, with their palms joined in reverence,
praised the boon-giving <s>Nīlalohita</s> with words dear to them.
The sages said:
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Rudra</s>, to the fierce <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Pracetasa</s>,
to the most bountiful, to <s>Śarva</s>, to <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, to the powerful one.

children.text: prabhūte vimale sāre hyādhāre parame sukhe
children.translated_text: In the abundant, stainless essence, in the support, in the supreme happiness,
I bow to the god, the lord <s>Bhāskara</s>, seated on a lotus and surrounded by the nine śaktis.

children.text: ādityaṃ bhāskaraṃ bhānuṃ raviṃ devaṃ divākaram
children.translated_text: I bow to <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, <s>Ravi</s>, the god <s>Divākara</s>,

children.text: umāṃ prabhāṃ tathā prajñāṃ saṃdhyāṃ sāvitrikāmapi ||
children.translated_text: and also to <s>Umā</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Saṃdhyā</s>, and <s>Sāvitrikā</s>;
to the goddess <s>Vistārā</s>, to <s>Uttarā</s>, and to <s>Bodhanī</s> I bow.

children.text: āpyāyanīṃ ca varadāṃ brahmāṇaṃ keśavaṃ haram ||
children.translated_text: I bow also to boon-giving <s>Āpyāyanī</s>, to <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, and <s>Hara</s>.
Having worshiped the group beginning with <s>Soma</s> in order, with mantras and according to the prescribed sequence,
I remember the god <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the primal god, stationed in the disk of <s>Ravi</s>.
I remember the gods beginning with <s>Indra</s>, and likewise the lords, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the lotus-born primal god,

children.text: prāgādyadhordhvaṃ ca yathākrameṇa vajrādipadmaṃ ca tathā smarāmi ||
children.translated_text: and, in order, the eastern and other directions, below and above, and likewise the lotus beginning with the thunderbolt.
To you who are vermilion-colored, accompanied by the maṇḍala, and adorned with gold and vajra ornaments,
whose eyes resemble lotuses and who are together with the lotus, the cause of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, homage.

children.text: rathaṃ ca saptāśvamanūruvīraṃ gaṇaṃ tathā saptavidhaṃ krameṇa
children.translated_text: I remember the chariot with seven horses and mighty <s>Anūru</s>, and likewise the sevenfold host in order,

children.text: ṛtupravāheṇa ca vālakhilyān smarāmi mandehagaṇakṣayaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vālakhilyas</s> along with the flow of the seasons, and the destruction of the host of <s>Mandehas</s>.

children.text: hutvā tilādyair vividhais tathāgnau punaḥ samāpyaiva tathaiva sarvam
children.translated_text: Having offered sesame and various other things into the fire, and then completed everything again in the same way,

children.text: udvāsya hṛtpaṅkajamadhyasaṃsthaṃ smarāmi biṃbaṃ tava devadeva ||
children.translated_text: after dismissing the image established in the middle of the heart-lotus, I remember your disk, god of gods.
I remember the disks in order, red, with eyes like spotless lotuses,

children.text: padmaṃ ca savye varadaṃ ca vāme kare tathā bhūṣitabhūṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: with a lotus in the right hand and the boon-granting gesture in the left, and with the hands adorned with ornaments.

children.text: daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ tava divyavaktraṃ vidyutprabhaṃ daityabhayaṅkaraṃ ca
children.translated_text: I remember your divine face, dreadful with fangs, lightning-bright and terrifying to demons,
intent on protecting twice-born men and rebuking the host of <s>Mandeha</s> demons.

children.text: somaṃ sitaṃ bhūmijam agnivarṇaṃ cāmīkarābhaṃ budhamindusūnum
children.translated_text: I remember white <s>Soma</s>, fire-colored <s>Bhūmija</s>, and <s>Budha</s>, son of the moon, shining like gold,

children.text: bṛhaspatiṃ kāñcanasaṃnikāśaṃ śukraṃ sitaṃ kṛṣṇataraṃ ca mandam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, resembling gold, white <s>Śukra</s>, and <s>Manda</s>, very dark.
I remember the right hand granting fearlessness and the left hand giving the boon at the thigh,
and <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, extending to the boundary of all the maṇḍapas.

children.text: pūrṇenduvarṇena ca puṣpagandhaprasthena toyena śubhena pūrṇam
children.translated_text: Having prepared a firm copper vessel, filled with pure water together with flowers and fragrance, the color of the full moon,

children.text: pātraṃ dṛḍhaṃ tāmramayaṃ prakalpya dāsye tavārghyaṃ bhagavanprasīda ||
children.translated_text: I shall give you the arghya offering; blessed lord, be gracious.
Homage to <s>Śiva</s>, the god, to <s>Īśvara</s>, the matted-haired one,
to <s>Rudra</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; homage to you as <s>Brahmā</s> and as the solar form.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: yaḥ śivaṃ maṇḍale devaṃ sampūjyaivaṃ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever, concentrated, worships <s>Śiva</s>, the god in the maṇḍala, in this way,
and recites this unsurpassed hymn in the morning, at midday, and in the evening,

children.text: itthaṃ śivena sāyujyaṃ labhate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: thereby obtains union with <s>Śiva</s>; there is no doubt about this.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the nineteenth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Therefore <s>Rudra</s>, the great god, the grandfather standing in the maṇḍala,

children.text: pūjyo vai brāhmaṇānāṃ ca kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: is indeed to be worshiped by Brahmins, and especially by Kṣatriyas.

children.text: vaiśyānāṃ naiva śūdrāṇāṃ śuśrūṣāṃ pūjakasya ca
children.translated_text: There is no such right for Vaiśyas or for Śūdras; and attendance upon the worshiper
is not the entitlement of women in acts of worship and the like; of this there is no doubt.
For women and Śūdras, through worship performed by the best of twice-born men, that fruit may arise,
especially through Brahmins and others, for the benefit of kings.
Thus Brahmins and the rest should always worship <s>Sadāśiva</s> fully.
Having spoken thus, the blessed <s>Rudra</s> himself disappeared right there.

children.text: te devā munayaḥ sarve śivamuddiśya śaṅkaram
children.translated_text: All those gods and sages, intent upon <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the great-souled ones, bowed down, overwhelmed by meditation on <s>Rudra</s>.
The gods and the sages rich in austerity went away as they had come;
therefore one should constantly worship the sun as having the form of <s>Śiva</s>,
for the sake of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desire, wealth, and liberation, with mind, deed, and speech.
The sages said:
O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>, all-knowing one, best of those who bear all the śāstras,
greatly blessed disciple of <s>Vyāsa</s>, now tell us the fire-related teaching
that was given by <s>Śiva</s>, the god of gods, from desire for the welfare of his devotees.
Having drawn it out from the Veda with its six limbs, and from <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and Yoga in every respect,
and having practiced vast austerity, hard for gods and demons to perform,
joined with matters of purpose, place, and the like, hidden, censured by ignorance,
sometimes contrary to, and sometimes in agreement with, the dharmas established by class and life-stage,
the śāstra taught by <s>Śiva</s> for <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation,
measuring a hundred crores of verses: how is the Lord's worship taught there?

children.text: snānayogādayo vāpi śrotuṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ
children.translated_text: And what of bathing, yoga, and the rest? We are eager to hear.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago, on the beautiful summit of <s>Meru</s>, by <s>Sanatkumāra</s>
the god <s>Nandīśvara</s>, <s>Śailādi</s>, approved by <s>Śiva</s>, was questioned.
He was questioned in this way, after bowing down, by the chief sages on every side.
What was told to that <s>Sanatkumāra</s> by <s>Nandin</s>, the joy of his family,
that knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, hear it, O bulls among sages.
The Śaiva teaching, summarized from what is taught in the Veda, was defined by <s>Śiva</s>;
it is free from praise, blame, and the like, and immediately brings certainty.
It is born from the grace of the guru, divine, and grants liberation without toil.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Blessed lord of all beings, <s>Nandīśvara</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>,
how are the worship and other rites of <s>Śambhu</s> performed for <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation?
You ought to tell me, O <s>Śailādi</s>, since I have come to you with humility.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Seeing him and hearing his words again, the blessed <s>Nandin</s>,
best of speakers, spoke about the proper time, occasion, eligibility, and the rest.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
I shall state eligibility in this way, according to the guru and according to the śāstra.
This designation belongs to a Śivācārya by reason of reverence, and not otherwise.
One who himself practices, and who also establishes others in proper conduct,
and who gathers the meanings of the śāstras, is thereby called an ācārya.
Therefore a devotee should seek a teacher who knows the truth of the meaning of the Veda, who lies upon ashes,
a guru who is fortunate and pleasant to behold,
committed, delighting people, following the path of scripture and tradition,
a giver of fearlessness through knowledge, free from greed and fickleness,
a guardian of proper conduct, steadfast, established in the proper observances.
Having seen such a one, he should worship the guru in every way like <s>Śiva</s>,
with his own person and with wealth, according to his faith and means.
The disciple should worship him until he becomes pleased.
When that greatly blessed one is well pleased, the destruction of bondage comes at once.
The guru is to be honored, the guru is to be worshiped; the guru himself is <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
For three years, or else for a year, he should test Brahmin disciples
by the giving of life and wealth, and by commands here and there.
The best may be set among low tasks, and the lowly among excellent things.

children.text: ākṛṣṭāstāḍitā vāpi ye viṣādaṃ na yānti vai ||
children.translated_text: Those who do not fall into dejection, even when dragged away or struck,
they are fit, most devoted to the <s>Śiva-dharma</s> and intent upon the <s>Śiva-dharma</s>.
They are restrained, endowed with <s>dharma</s>, and follow the path of scripture and tradition.
They endure all pairs of opposites, are steadfast, and have minds always ready;
they are devoted to helping others and delight in service to the guru.
They are upright, gentle, sound in themselves, compliant, and pleasant-spoken;
free from pride, intelligent, having abandoned rivalry, and without craving.
Endowed with purity, proper conduct, and virtues, free from hypocrisy and envy,
such twice-born men, all intent upon devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, are fit.
Endowed with such conduct in the actions of speech, mind, and body,
such men should be purified for the purification of the principles.
A disciple who is pure, endowed with humility, free from falsehood and harshness,
and who obeys the guru's command, deserves favor.
And the guru, knowing the śāstra, wise, ascetic, affectionate toward people,
devoted to worldly custom and knowing the principles, is remembered as a giver of liberation.
Even if he is endowed with all marks and skilled in all the śāstras,
knowledge of every method and procedure is fruitless for one who lacks the truth of the principles.

children.text: svasaṃvedya pare tattve niścayo yasya nātmani
children.translated_text: If one has no certainty in oneself regarding the supreme principle, which is to be known by one's own awareness,
there is no favoring of oneself; how, then, could there be favoring of another?

children.text: prabuddhastu dvijo yastu sa śuddhaḥ sādhayatyapi
children.translated_text: But a twice-born man who is awakened is pure and can accomplish the practice.
For one without the truth of the principles, whence could awakening come, and whence self-possession?
Those who are bereft of self-possession are all declared to be bound souls.

children.text: paśubhiḥ preritā ye tu sarve te paśavaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And those who are set in motion by bound souls are all remembered as bound souls.

children.text: tasmāt tattvavido ye tu te muktā mocayanty api
children.translated_text: Therefore those who know the truth of the principles are liberated, and they liberate others as well.
the principle that gives rise to consciousness, born from supreme bliss.

children.text: tattvaṃ tu viditaṃ yena sa evānandadarśakaḥ
children.translated_text: But the one by whom reality has been known is himself a revealer of bliss;
not so by the mere name, if he is devoid of consciousness.
One cannot carry another across; how could a stone carry a stone across?
For those whose liberation comes by the mere name, that liberation is merely nominal.
Even from seeing yogins, from touching them, or even from speaking with them,
there arises at once an authoritative insight that brings about the wasting away of the bonds.
Or else, by the path of yoga, having entered the disciple's body,

children.text: bodhayed eva yogena sarvatattvāni śodhya ca ||
children.translated_text: he should awaken him through yoga, after purifying all the <s>tattvas</s> (principles).
For yogins, the purification of the sixfold path is prescribed through the yoga of knowledge.
Having examined a disciple who knows <s>dharma</s>, is righteous, and has mastered the Veda,
whether a Brahmin, a Kshatriya, or a Vaishya, and one free from many faults,
having perceived by knowledge what is to be known, through what has come from ear to ear,

children.text: dīpāddīpo yathā cānyaḥ saṃcared vidhivad guruḥ
children.translated_text: as one lamp is kindled from another lamp, the guru should transmit it according to rule.

children.text: bhauvanaṃ ca padaṃ caiva varṇākhyaṃ mātramuttamam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>bhuvana</s> path, the <s>pada</s> path, the one called <s>varṇa</s>, and the supreme <s>mantra</s>,
the path of <s>kalā</s>, great-fortuned one, and the path called <s>tattva</s>, approved by all,
is opened everywhere by whose power, by mere command alone:
his accomplishment and liberation arise from the guru's compassion.
Earth and the other elements enter into the <s>bhuvana</s> path,

children.text: śabdaḥ sparśastathā rūpaṃ raso gandhaśca bhāvataḥ
children.translated_text: and sound, touch, form, taste, and smell according to their real nature.
The <s>pada</s> path and the one called <s>varṇa</s>, O Brahmin, are a differentiation of the cognitive senses;

children.text: karmendriyāṇi mātraṃ hi mano buddhirataḥ param
children.translated_text: the organs of action, the subtle elements, mind, and then, beyond that, intellect,
then egoity and the unmanifest: this is remembered as the path of <s>kalā</s>.
From <s>Puruṣa</s> through <s>Viriñci</s>, the state beyond mind and higher than the highest,
and likewise lordship: so it is taught, making known the meaning of all the <s>tattvas</s>.
One who is not a yogin does not know the purification of the <s>tattvas</s> whose essence is <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the twentieth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having examined the ground according to rule by its smell, color, taste, and so on,
and having adorned it with canopies and the like, so that it is fit for the invocation of <s>Īśvara</s>,
one should prepare a <s>maṇḍala</s> measuring one hasta,
and in the middle he should draw a lotus furnished with five gems.

children.text: cūrṇairaṣṭadalaṃ vṛttaṃ sitaṃ vā raktameva ca
children.translated_text: With powders he should make it round, eight-petaled, either white or red,
provided with its retinue and endowed with great beauty.
Having invoked <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause, in the pericarp,
he should worship him with every effort, in full accordance with his means.
The powers are said to be in the petals, and in the pericarp, great sage,
detachment and knowledge are the stalk, and <s>dharma</s> is the pleasing root-bulb.

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca kālī vikaraṇī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and <s>Vikaraṇī</s>,
then <s>Balavikaraṇī</s> and <s>Balapramathinī</s>, in due order,
and <s>Damanī</s> of all beings; in the filaments are the <s>śaktis</s> (powers).
<s>Manonmanī</s> and <s>Mahāmāyā</s> are in the pericarp, on <s>Śiva</s>'s seat.
Together with <s>Vāmadeva</s> and the others, he should install them according to the paired arrangement.
He should place <s>Manonmana</s>, <s>Mahādeva</s>, and then <s>Manonmanī</s> in the center.
Because of its connection with sun, moon, and fire, it is called the <s>praṇava</s>, whose essence is <s>Śiva</s>.
He should install <s>Puruṣa</s> as the face in the eastern petal, bright as the sun.
He should place <s>Aghora</s> in the southern petal, resembling a mass of dark-blue collyrium,
and in the northern petal the one called <s>Vāmadeva</s>, resembling a hibiscus flower.
In the western petal he should place <s>Sadya</s>, white as cow's milk,
and <s>Īśāna</s> in the pericarp, resembling pure crystal.
With the mantra 'hṛdayāya', he should place the one shining like the disk of the moon.
In the fiery quarter, in <s>Rudra</s>'s direction, he should place 'śirase', smoky in radiance.

children.text: śikhāyai ca namaśceti raktābhe nairṛte dale
children.translated_text: And saying 'namaḥ to the crest-lock', he should place the red-hued one in the southwestern petal.
Saying 'kavacāya', he should place the collyrium-colored one in the petal of the wind.
Saying 'astrāya', for the one like the flame of fire, he should install it in the directions.
And saying 'netrebhyaḥ', he should install the tawny-eyed ones in the northeast.
He should visualize <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the god, and beyond him <s>Maheśvara</s>,

children.text: rudraṃ viṣṇuṃ viriñciṃ ca sṛṣṭinyāyena bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: then <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Viriñci</s>, according to the order of creation.
To <s>Śiva</s>, whose form is <s>Rudra</s>, who is beyond peace, to <s>Śaṃbhu</s>,
to the peaceful one, to the pacifier of demons, and likewise obeisance to <s>Candramas</s>;
to the knowable one, to the support of knowledge, to <s>Vahni</s>, to the one with the splendor of fire;
to <s>Kālā</s>, to <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>, to <s>Tārakā</s>, and to <s>Antaka</s>;
to <s>Nivṛtti</s>, to <s>Dhanadeva</s>, to <s>Dhārā</s>, and to <s>Dhāraṇā</s>;
with these mantras he should worship <s>Sadāśiva</s>, whose body is the great elements,
the god whose crown is <s>Īśāna</s>, whose face is <s>Puruṣa</s>, the ancient one,
the joyous <s>Maheśvara</s>, whose heart is <s>Aghora</s> and whose secret part is <s>Vāma</s>.
He should remember the god with <s>Sadya</s> as his form, the cause of the manifestation of being and non-being,
five-faced, ten-armed, and composed of thirty-eight <s>kalās</s> (parts).
He should divide <s>Sadya</s>, made of <s>kalās</s>, in an eightfold manner,
and divide the expansive lord <s>Vāma</s> in thirteen ways.
Having made <s>Aghora</s> eightfold, established in the form of <s>kalās</s>,

children.text: puruṣaṃ ca caturdhā vai vibhajya ca kalāmayam ||
children.translated_text: and having divided <s>Puruṣa</s> fourfold, as made of <s>kalās</s>,
having made <s>Īśāna</s> fivefold, established as the fivefold form,
he should do this with the mantra 'haṃsa, haṃsa', endowed with devotion to <s>Śiva</s>.
He should contemplate the <s>oṅkāra</s> simply as <s>oṅkāra</s>, and the letter a as having the same form,

children.text: ā ī ū e tathā aṃbānukrameṇātmarūpiṇam ||
children.translated_text: and the syllables ā, ī, ū, e, and aṃ in sequence as forms of the self.
He should contemplate the god together with <s>Pradhāna</s>, free from dissolution and arising,
smaller than the smallest atom, unborn, and greater even than the great,
the upward-seeded <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s>.
He is to meditate upon the thousand-headed god, the eternal one with a thousand eyes,
with a thousand hands and feet, ending in sound and having sound as his form,
the lord whose form is like a firefly and whose shape is like the crescent of the moon.
In order, at the <s>dvādaśānta</s>, between the eyebrows, in the middle of the palate, in the throat,
and in the region of the heart, he should contemplate the god, his own bliss, the nectar, <s>Śiva</s>.
He shines like a circle of lightning and has the radiance of ten million bolts of lightning;
he is dark, red, formed as a kalā, and his seat is made by the three powers.
He should remember the god <s>Sadāśiva</s>, endowed with the three principles,
and should worship the god, consisting of the forms of knowledge, in the proper order.
Then, with the <s>astra</s> mantra, he should worship the guardians of the worlds separately, beginning in the east,
and, having prepared the <s>caru</s> according to rule, he should offer it to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: ardhaṃ śivāya dattvaiva śeṣārdhena tu homayet
children.translated_text: Having given one half to <s>Śiva</s>, he should perform the homa with the remaining half,
and then, with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, he should have the disciple eat the excellent portion.
Having sipped water and become pure, he should worship the <s>Puruṣa</s> according to rule.
Then he should drink <s>pañcagavya</s>, consecrated with the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra.
With the <s>Vāmadeva</s> mantra, his limbs covered with ash, he should smear himself with ash in order.
And in the disciple's ears he should recite the goddess <s>Gāyatrī</s>, whose deity is <s>Rudra</s>.
Then he should place five golden jars, fitted with cords and lids and wrapped in a pair of cloths,
previously perfumed and adorned with heaps of gold and jewels,
with the help of five Brahmins.
He should perform the homa with <s>caru</s>, as extensively as his means allow.

children.text: śiṣyaṃ ca vāsayedbhaktaṃ dakṣiṇe maṇḍalasya tu
children.translated_text: He should lodge the devoted disciple to the south of the maṇḍala,
lying on a bed of darbha grass and wholly intent on meditation upon <s>Śiva</s>.
Again, according to rule, with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, he should offer one hundred and eight oblations
with ghee, and at dawn he should purify away the impurity of bad dreams.
Having thus made the disciple fast, bathed him, and adorned his body,
clothing him in a new garment and upper cloth, with a turban, and after performing auspicious rites,
he should bind his eyes with a cloth such as fine silk and lead him in.
The offering should be mixed with golden flowers, as abundantly as his means allow.
With the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra he should make a flower-offering to the Lord.
He should circumambulate three times, either with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>
or simply with the <s>praṇava</s>, intent upon meditation on <s>Śiva</s>.
Having meditated on the lord of the gods, he himself should cast the flowers toward <s>Īśāna</s>.
On whichever mantra the flower falls, that mantra becomes effective for him.

children.text: śivāṃbhasā tu saṃspṛśya aghoreṇa ca bhasmanā ||
children.translated_text: Touching him with <s>Śiva</s>-water and with ash consecrated by the <s>Aghora</s> mantra,
he should place it on the disciple's head and worship the disciple with sandal and the other offerings.

children.text: vāruṇaṃ paramaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dvāraṃ vai sarvavarṇinām ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vāruṇa</s>, the supreme and best door, is indeed for men of all classes,

children.text: kṣattriyāṇāṃ viśeṣeṇa dvāraṃ vai paścimaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: and for kṣatriyas in particular the western door is remembered.
Then, removing the covering from his eyes, he should show him the maṇḍala.
Seating him on a seat of kuśa grass, he should assume the position of <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>.
Then he should perform the purification of the principles according to the fivefold division of principles.
By <s>Nivṛtti</s>, up to <s>Rudra</s>, O son born from the sphere of the cosmic egg,
and by <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> above that, as far as the range of the unmanifest,
by <s>Vidyā</s> alone as a kalā, as far as <s>Viśveśvara</s>, O man of good vows,
having purified the path above that, through devotion to <s>Śiva</s> he should lead him to <s>Śiva</s>.
For the worship of that principle, of that lord of enjoyment,
according to the division into three principles, or likewise with four,
he should offer oblations to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, beyond <s>Śānti</s>, with the limb-mantra.
With the four beginning with <s>Sadya</s> and ending with <s>Śānti</s>, each should be treated separately by kalā.
Or again, O best of sages, he may treat <s>Śāntyatīta</s> with <s>Īśāna</s>.
In each direction he should cause one hundred and eight oblations to be offered separately.
Then in the northeast, with the fifth mantra, the principal rite is proclaimed.

children.text: samidājyacarūṃl lājān sarṣapāṃś ca yavāṃs tilān ||
children.translated_text: Fuel-sticks, ghee, <s>caru</s>, parched grain, mustard seeds, barley, and sesame:
these seven substances are to be offered, ending with <s>svāhā</s> and beginning with the <s>praṇava</s>.
For them, O Brahmin, the final oblation is prescribed with the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra.
With the <s>Haṃsa</s> mantra, according to rule, preceded by the <s>praṇava</s>, O man of good vows,
and with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, an expiatory rite is prescribed.
The fire rite, from the <s>Jaya</s> offerings through the <s>Sviṣṭa</s> rite, should be performed in order,
and he should arrange it according to the number of qualities and with the principal mantra.
The elements may also be arranged with the Brahma-mantras, or silently with seed-syllables and the like.
Then, with the principal mantra alone, having restrained the breaths <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>,
with the sixth he should pierce the self, up to the <s>praṇava</s>, both <s>kula</s> and <s>akula</s>.
Dissolving one into another, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, and <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: rudre rudraṃ tamīśāne śive devaṃ maheśvaram
children.translated_text: and <s>Rudra</s> into <s>Rudra</s>, that one into <s>Īśāna</s>, and the god <s>Maheśvara</s> into <s>Śiva</s>,
thereafter he should visualize the destroyer of existence according to the procedure of creation.
Having established this self, the individual soul, he should perform striking and the showing of the door,

children.text: dīpanaṃ grahaṇaṃ caiva bandhanaṃ pūjayā saha ||
children.translated_text: kindling, grasping, and binding, together with worship,
and also immortalization, all according to rule.
The mantra ending with the sixth, joined with <s>Sadya</s> and combined with the third,
ending in <s>phaḍ</s>, is taught as withdrawal according to the fivefold division of elements.
Beginning with <s>Sadya</s>, together with the sixth, ending in the crest and also ending in <s>phaḍ</s>,
the striking has been explained as the door even of the principles, O yogin.
Enclosing the principal mantra with the third is kindling.
Enclosing the principal mantra with the first is remembered as grasping.
Enclosing the principal mantra with the first, just as before,
is binding; with the complete one it is flooding, and with nectar it is immortalizing.
Then come <s>Śāntyatītā</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, and <s>Vidyā</s>, the stainless kalā by name.
Establishment and withdrawal are remembered as the transference of the kalās.
It is joined, in due order, with the principles, syllables, kalās, and worlds.

children.text: mantraiḥ pādaiḥ stavaṃ kuryādviśodhya ca yathāvidhi
children.translated_text: With mantras and ritual portions he should make the praise, having purified it according to rule;
and he should arrange it beforehand, as before, with the first yoni-bīja.
Know worship and sprinkling, striking and removal as well,

children.text: saṃhatasya ca saṃyogaṃ vikṣepaṃ ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: the conjunction of what has been gathered together, and dispersal, in due order.

children.text: arcanā ca tathā garbhadhāraṇaṃ jananaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: There are worship, then the bearing of the embryo, and birth again;
there is the authority of the sun, and especially dissolution.
With the first among the highest, and likewise with the last yoni-bīja, O you of good vow,

children.text: uddhāre prokṣaṇe caiva tāḍane ca mahāmune ||
children.translated_text: in uplifting, sprinkling, and also in striking, O great sage,
with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra ending in phaṭ there is the onward passage; there is no doubt.
For each principle this indeed is the sequence, by the path of yoga, O you of good vow.
And for as long as it is done with the fist, for that length of time he should lead it in sequence;
through the yoga of the equinox, from <s>Nivṛtti</s> up to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: ekatra samatāṃ yāti nānyathā tu pṛthakpṛthak
children.translated_text: It reaches equality in one place, and not otherwise, separately one by one.
For yogins it extends from the tip of the nose to the dvādaśānta point, together with the back.
This is to be patiently accepted, O best of Brahmins; such is the command of the God of gods.
With gold, silver, copper, and the like, and with an object ritually prepared according to rule,
furnished with a brush and cloth, and wrapped with thread,
filled with sacred water and containing jewels, O you of good vow,
empowered with Saṃhitā mantras and praised with the Rudrādhyāya,

children.text: secayecca tataḥ śiṣyaṃ śivabhaktaṃ ca dhārmikam ||
children.translated_text: he should then sprinkle the disciple, a devotee of <s>Śiva</s> and righteous.

children.text: so 'pi śiṣyaḥ śivasyāgre guror agre ca sādaram
children.translated_text: That disciple too, before <s>Śiva</s> and before the guru, respectfully,
should perform initiation at the fire; and, once initiated, he should act accordingly.
Better the giving up of life, or even the cutting off of the head,
than that one should eat without first worshiping blessed <s>Sadāśiva</s>.

children.text: evaṃ dīkṣā prakartavyā pūjā caiva yathākramam
children.translated_text: Thus initiation should be performed, and worship too in due order.
He should worship <s>Parameśvara</s> three times a day, or once a day.
The agnihotra, the Vedas, and sacrifices with abundant gifts
are not equal even to a fraction of the worship of the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>.

children.text: sadā yajati yajñena sadā dānaṃ prayacchati
children.translated_text: He always sacrifices with sacrifice, and always gives gifts,
and is always as one who lives on air, if he worships <s>Śiva</s> even once.

children.text: ekakālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā trikālaṃ nityameva vā
children.translated_text: Once, twice, or three times a day, or constantly every day,

children.text: ye'rcayanti mahādevaṃ te rudrā nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who worship <s>Mahādeva</s> are <s>Rudras</s>; there is no doubt.
One who is not <s>Rudra</s> should not touch <s>Rudra</s>; one who is not <s>Rudra</s> should not worship <s>Rudra</s>;
one who is not <s>Rudra</s> should not praise <s>Rudra</s>, and one who is not <s>Rudra</s> does not attain <s>Rudra</s>.
Thus the sequence of the rule of eligibility has been stated briefly,
for the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, bestowing the fruits of dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation.
Thus in the holy great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the twenty-first chapter, named "The Rule of Initiation."
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Having performed bathing, sacrifice, and other rites for <s>Bhāskara</s>,
then one should perform the bath of <s>Śiva</s>, the ash bath, and the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.
Taking clay with the sixth mantra, he should devoutly place the clay on the ground;
then, after sprinkling it with the second, he should purify it with the third.
With the fourth he should divide it, and with one mantra purify the impurity;

children.text: snātvā ṣaṣṭhena taccheṣāṃ mṛdaṃ hastagatāṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having bathed with the sixth, he should again take the remaining clay held in the hand,

children.text: tridhā vibhajya sarvaṃ ca caturbhirmadhyamaṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: divide all of it into three parts, and again divide the middle part into four.
With the sixth mantra he should touch the left side seven times, and also with the root mantra;

children.text: daśavāraṃ ca ṣaṣṭhena diśāṃ bandhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and ten times with the sixth; this is called the binding of the directions.
With the left hand he should anoint the sacred water, and with the right his body;
having bathed while remembering <s>Bhānu</s> with all the mantras, he should perform the sprinkling.
With a horn, with leaf-cups, or with a leaf of the palāśa tree,
with these various solar, auspicious formulas that grant every accomplishment.
I shall teach the solar formulas, beginning with <s>Bāṣkala</s>, O you of good vow,
the limbs among all the gods, everywhere the essential ones.

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ oṃ bhuvaḥ oṃsvaḥ oṃ mahaḥ oṃ janaḥ oṃ tapaḥ oṃsatyam oṃ ṛtam oṃ brahmā
children.translated_text: Oṃ bhūḥ, oṃ bhuvaḥ, oṃ svaḥ, oṃ mahaḥ, oṃ janaḥ, oṃ tapaḥ, oṃ satyam, oṃ ṛtam, oṃ <s>Brahmā</s>.
The mantra consisting of nine syllables is proclaimed as <s>Bāṣkala</s>.
Because the worlds do not perish, ṛta is called imperishable.
Satyam is said to be imperishable; it begins with the praṇava and ends with namaḥ.

children.text: oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi
children.translated_text: Oṃ, earth, atmosphere, heaven: may we meditate on the excellent radiance of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Sūrya</s>; homage to <s>Khakholka</s>.
This is declared to be the root mantra of the great <s>Bhāskara</s>.
With the nine-syllabled mantra he should worship blazing-faced <s>Bhāskara</s> with the root mantra.
I shall state the limb-mantras in due order.
The first begins with the Veda and the rest, and the middle with the praṇava.

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ brahma hṛdayāya oṃ bhuvaḥ viṣṇuśirase oṃsvaḥ rudraśikhāyai oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ jvālāmālinīśikhāyai oṃ mahaḥ maheśvarāya kavacāya oṃ janaḥ śivāya netrebhyaḥ oṃ tapaḥ tāpakāya astrāya phaṭ mantrāṇi kathitānyevaṃ saurāṇi vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: Oṃ bhūḥ, <s>Brahmā</s>, to the heart; oṃ bhuvaḥ, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to the head; oṃ svaḥ, <s>Rudra</s>, to the crest; oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, to the flame-garlanded crest; oṃ mahaḥ, to <s>Maheśvara</s> as armor; oṃ janaḥ, to <s>Śiva</s> for the eyes; oṃ tapaḥ, to <s>Tāpaka</s> as the missile, phaṭ. Thus the various solar mantras have been stated.
With these vessels, horns and the like, he should sprinkle himself.

children.text: tāmrakuṃbhena vā vipraḥ kṣatriyo vaiśya eva ca
children.translated_text: Or with a copper pot, whether he is a Brahmin, Kṣatriya, or Vaiśya,
together with kuśa grass and flowers, concentrated, using all the mantras.
Wearing red garments, he should sip water according to rule;
by day with "Sūryaś ca," and by night, O best of the twice-born, with "Agniś ca."
"May the waters purify" at midday is called the mantra-sipping.
Having performed purification by means of the sixth, he should recite the first, unsurpassed mantra.
Likewise he should recite the root mantra ending in vauṣaṭ, the unsurpassed nine-syllabled one,
and he should place it on the branches of the hand, and on the thumb, middle finger, and ring finger.
On the palm he should place the forefinger and thumb, and also the portions of the fist.
Having made the body consist of the nine-syllabled mantra and purified it also with the limbs,
he should think, "I am the sun," with these mantras in due order.
With water held in the left hand, mixed with fragrance and white mustard,
and with a bunch of kuśa, he should sprinkle himself, using roots and tips arranged eightfold.

children.text: āpo hi ṣṭhādibhiścaiva śeṣamāghrāya vai jalam ||
children.translated_text: With the verses beginning "āpo hi ṣṭhā," and after smelling the remaining water,
through the left nostril he should visualize <s>Śiva</s> within the body.
Taking the arghya, he should also visualize the one present in the body through the left nostril,
and he should imagine the black-colored one outside, situated in a stone.
He should satisfy all the gods, and especially the seers,
and he should have the arghya offered according to rule to the beings and to the ancestors.

children.text: vyāpinīṃ ca parāṃ jyotsnāṃ saṃdhyāṃ samyag upāsayet ||
children.translated_text: He should properly worship <s>Sandhyā</s>, the pervasive, supreme radiance.
At morning, midday, and evening he should offer the arghya.
With water mixed with red sandal, he should fashion on the ground
a well-rounded maṇḍala, a hand's breadth in size, O best of twice-borns, and should make his prayer.
Facing east, he should set down a copper vessel, fragrant and filled to a prastha.
He should fill it with scented water and with red sandal,
with red flowers, sesame seeds, kuśa, and unbroken grains,
with dūrvā grass, apāmārga, a cow-product, and pure ghee.
Having filled it by means of the root mantra, consisting of the nine syllables,

children.text: jānubhyāṃ dharaṇīṃ gatvā devadevaṃ namasya ca ||
children.translated_text: and having gone down to the earth on his knees and bowed to the god of gods,
he should place that vessel on his head and offer the arghya with the root mantra of the arghya.
The fruit that is proclaimed for performing ten thousand horse sacrifices,
that fruit he obtains by giving the solar arghya, approved by all.
After giving the arghya, he should worship with devotion the god of gods, <s>Tryambaka</s>.
Or, after worshiping <s>Bhāskara</s>, he should perform the fiery bath.
The bath of <s>Śiva</s> is as before, differing only by the mantra.

children.text: dantadhāvanapūrvaṃ ca snānaṃ sauraṃ ca śāṅkaram
children.translated_text: The solar and Śaṅkara bath are preceded by tooth-cleaning.

children.text: vighneśaṃ varuṇaṃ caiva guruṃ tīrthaṃ samarcayet ||
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Vighneśa</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, the guru, and the sacred water-place.

children.text: baddhvā padmāsanaṃ tīrthe tathā tīrthaṃ samarcayet
children.translated_text: Having assumed the lotus posture at the sacred water-place, he should likewise worship the sacred water-place.

children.text: tīrthaṃ saṃgṛhya vidhinā pūjāsthānaṃ praviśya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having collected sacred water according to rule and entered the place of worship,
he should proceed by the path purified with arghya and step upon the sandals.
As before, he should perform the hand-nyāsa and the body-nyāsa.
The preparation of the arghya has thus been briefly stated.
Having assumed the lotus posture, the yogin should practice breath control.
Having gathered red flowers, he should visualize lotuses and the rest.

children.text: ātmano dakṣiṇe sthāpya jalabhāṇḍaṃ ca vāmataḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should set them on his own right side, and the water vessel on the left.
The copper vessels for the solar rite are for the accomplishment of every desire and aim.
Taking the arghya vessel, he should rinse it according to rule,
together with the water previously mentioned, and likewise in the water vessel.
With water consecrated by the astra mantra, the arghya should be joined with the arghya ingredients.
Having made it consecrated by the saṃhitā mantra and worshiped it first with the first mantra,
he should cover it with the fourth and place it before himself.
Water for washing the feet and water for sipping, furnished with fragrance and flowers,

children.text: aṃbhasā śodhite pātre sthāpayet pūrvavat pṛthak
children.translated_text: he should place separately, as before, in vessels purified with water.
He should place the saṃhitā mantra there and cover it with the kavaca mantra.
With the arghya water he should sprinkle the substances in particular.
He should recite to the god <s>Āditya</s>, who is saluted by all the gods.

children.text: ādityo vai teja ūrjo balaṃ yaśo vivardhati
children.translated_text: "<s>Āditya</s> indeed increases radiance, vigor, strength, and fame";
with this and the following words, having bowed, he should prepare the seat of the lord,

children.text: prabhūtaṃ vimalaṃ sāram ārādhyaṃ paramaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: abundant, stainless, essential, worshipful, and supremely pleasing.
In the corners beginning with the southeast, down to the center, he should place it with the heart mantra.
He should also place the limb, the seed, and the sprout,
the hollow stalk, furnished with filaments and thorns,

children.text: dalaṃ dalāgraṃ suśvetaṃ hemābhaṃ raktameva ca
children.translated_text: the petal and the petal-tip, brilliant white, golden-hued, and red,
and the pericarp with its filaments, surrounded by the śaktis beginning with <s>Dīptā</s>.

children.text: dīptā sūkṣmā jayā bhadrā vibhūtir vimalā kramāt
children.translated_text: <s>Dīptā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Vibhūti</s>, and <s>Vimalā</s> in order,
and <s>Aghorā</s> and <s>Vikṛtā</s>: these are the eight śaktis beginning with <s>Dīptā</s>.
All are auspicious, facing <s>Bhāskara</s>, with the hollows of their hands joined in reverence,
or else holding lotuses in their hands, adorned with every ornament.
In the middle he should place the goddess <s>Varadā</s>, facing every direction.
Then he should invoke the goddess and <s>Bhāskara</s>, the supreme lord.
With the nine-syllabled mantra taught by <s>Bāṣkala</s>, he should invoke <s>Bhāskara</s>.
At the invocation, presence is established by this very mantra.
The mudrā of great-souled <s>Bhāskara</s> is the one called the lotus-mudrā.
Then with the root mantra he should offer arghya, water for the feet, and sipping water separately.
