Again, by the presentation of arghya, the rite is performed according to <s>Bāṣkala</s>'s rule.
Red lotus flowers and red sandal,
lamp, incense, food offering, mouth-perfume, and the rest,
betel, wick, lamp, and so on are prescribed according to <s>Bāṣkala</s>.
In the southeast, likewise in the northeast, in the southwest, and in the northwest,
in the east and also in the west, the sixfold procedure is prescribed.
Having worshiped according to rule up to the eyes, he should use the mantra beginning with praṇava and ending with namaḥ.
Having placed it in the pericarp, he should perform meditation on the form.
All are peaceful, with the splendor of lightning; this is proclaimed as the <s>Raudra</s> weapon.
The eight-formed one is terrifying, with a mouth dreadful from its fangs.
His right hand grants boons, and his left is adorned with a lotus,
and all the forms are furnished with every ornament and anointed with red garlands and unguents.
All his forms stand there wearing red garments.
<s>Mahādeva</s>, together with the maṇḍala, has a body red as vermilion.
The lord holds a lotus, has an ambrosial mouth, and has two hands and two eyes.
He is adorned with red ornaments and anointed with red garlands and unguents.
One should meditate on <s>Bhāskara</s>, lord of the worlds, bearing such a form.
Outside the lotus, in the auspicious maṇḍalas here on every side,
one should place <s>Soma</s>, <s>Maṅgāraka</s>, and <s>Budha</s>, best of the intelligent,
<s>Bṛhaspati</s>, of great wisdom, the son of <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Bhārgava</s>,

children.text: śanaiścaraṃ tathā rāhuṃ ketuṃ dhūmraṃ prakīrtitam
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Śanaiścara</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, and smoky <s>Ketu</s>, as they are proclaimed.
All have two eyes and two arms, while <s>Rāhu</s> bears only an upper body.
With open mouth, making añjali, with eyes crooked by a frown,
<s>Śanaiścara</s> has a fanged face and holds hands of boon-giving and fearlessness.

children.text: svaiḥ svair bhāvaiḥ svanāmnā ca praṇavādinamo'ntakam
children.translated_text: With their own respective attributes and names, using a formula that begins with the <s>praṇava</s> (oṃ) and ends with <s>namaḥ</s>,
they are to be worshiped carefully for the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
Outside the deity one should worship the seven groups of seven,
the seers, gods, gandharvas, pannagas, and hosts of apsarases,
the grāmaṇīs, yātudhānas, and likewise the yakṣas above all.
In front one should worship the lord's seven horses, composed of the seven meters.
One should also worship the host of <s>Vālakhilyas</s> and the recipient of the lord's nirmālya (ritual remnants).
One should worship the seat of the image, and also worship the deity.
One should have arghya offered to them separately according to rule.
This is done at their invocation, at the end of the worship, and also at their dismissal.

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: One may recite a thousand times, or half of that, or else one hundred and eight times;

children.text: bāṣkalaṃ ca japedagre daśāṃśena ca yojayet ||
children.translated_text: first he should recite the <s>Bāṣkala</s> mantra, and should apply a tenth part.

children.text: kuṇḍaṃ ca paścime kuryādvartulaṃ caiva mekhalam
children.translated_text: He should make the fire-pit to the west, circular, with a mekhalā (rim),
measuring four aṅgulas in height and also in breadth.
For both daily and occasional rites it should measure one hasta;
in the pit he should make a navel, ten aṅgulas, in the shape of an aśvattha leaf.
In front, with half that measure, it is remembered as resembling an elephant's lip.
The neck is one aṅgula, and the remaining part is twice as broad.
Leaving that measure for the pit, he should make the rim accordingly.
Having carefully prepared it, afterward he should perform the homa (fire offering).
With the sixth mantra he should make the marking and then sprinkle again with water.
Collected in mind, he should arrange the seat in the middle with the first mantra.
Then with that first mantra he should install the śakti called <s>Prabhāvatī</s>.
After worshiping with the <s>Bāṣkala</s> mantra, in order, with perfumes, flowers, and the rest,
with the <s>Bāṣkala</s> mantra itself he should worship each rite separately.
Afterward, by rule, the final oblation should be made with the root mantra.
Thus, step by step, by this procedure, the solar fire is produced.
By the procedure stated before, he should place the lotus previously described.
Having worshiped above the mouth, as before, the lord <s>Bhāskara</s>,
ten oblations are to be given with the <s>Bāṣkala</s> mantra, O great sage.

children.text: aṅgānāṃ ca tathaikaikaṃ saṃhitābhiḥ pṛthak punaḥ
children.translated_text: And likewise, one by one, for the limbs, again separately with the saṃhitās,
from <s>Jayā</s> and the rest up to <s>Sviṣṭa</s>, and the casting in of fuel,
all this is common to all paths, according to the sequence of tradition.
Having made the offering to <s>Bhāskara</s>, god of gods, the immeasurable self,
having given all the worship, homa, and other rites, the arghya, and circumambulation,

children.text: aṅgaiḥ sampūjya saṃkṣipya hṛdyudvāsya namasya ca ||
children.translated_text: having worshiped with the ancillary mantras, gathered him into the heart, dismissed him, and bowed,
then he should perform the worship of <s>Śiva</s> for the attainment of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.

children.text: evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ yajanaṃ bhāskarasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus the worship of <s>Bhāskara</s> has been briefly stated.
Whoever worships even once the god, the god of gods, the teacher of the world,

children.text: bhāskaraṃ paramātmānaṃ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāskara</s>, the supreme self, goes to the highest goal.
Released from all sin and utterly free of every sin,
he is endowed with all sovereignty and matchless in splendor.
Together on every side with sons, grandsons, friends, and kinsmen,
having enjoyed abundant pleasures in this very world, rich in wealth and grain,
possessed of conveyances and vehicles and also of various ornaments,
even when his time has passed, he rejoices with <s>Sūrya</s> for an imperishable span of time.
Then, returning here again from that state, he becomes a righteous king,
or he is born here as a Brahmin endowed with the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.
Again, through the force of former dispositions, righteous and versed in the Veda,
he worships <s>Sūrya</s> alone and obtains union with <s>Sūrya</s>.
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter of the latter part of the revered <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Now I shall fully declare to you the unsurpassed worship of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: trisaṃdhyam arcayed īśam agnikāryaṃ ca śaktitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One should worship the Lord at the three junctures of the day and perform the fire rite according to one's capacity.

children.text: śivasnānaṃ purā kṛtvā tattvaśuddhiṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: First, having performed the bath of <s>Śiva</s> and the purification of the principles as before,
then, with flowers in hand, one should enter the place of worship, composed in mind.
Having performed three prāṇāyāmas, along with the dāhana and āplāvana rites (burning and flooding visualizations),
with his hands perfumed by sandal and the rest, he should set forth the great mudrā.
Having carefully formed the body through knowledge, even from the fire of <s>Brahman</s>,
a body arising from <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego), and the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements),
purified by the nectar of <s>Śiva</s>, and exactly according to the true nature of <s>Śiva</s>.
It stands above the navel, below at a distance of a vitasti.
One should know that to be the heart, the great abode of the universe,
and in the pericarp of the heart-lotus, the god <s>Sadāśiva</s> directly.
One should meditate on him as five-faced, ten-armed, adorned with every ornament,
with three eyes on each face, and with the moon set as his crest-jewel.
He is seated in the bound lotus posture and resembles pure crystal.
One should meditate on the upward face as white, and the eastern one as like saffron.
The southern face is bluish, and the northern one very red,
while the western face of the supreme lord is divine, white as cow's milk.

children.text: śūlaṃ paraśukhaḍgaṃ ca vajraṃ śaktiṃ ca dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: In his right hands are a trident, axe, sword, thunderbolt, and spear;
in the left are a noose, goad, bell, serpent, and excellent arrow.
Or he has hands granting boons and fearlessness; the rest is just as before.
One should contemplate <s>Śiva</s> furnished with every ornament and wearing variegated garments,
the god whose form consists of the limbs of <s>Brahman</s>, the highest of all the gods.
With complete devotion one should worship the lord of <s>Brahmā</s> by means of the brahmāṅgas.

children.text: uktāni pañca brahmāṇi śivāṅgāni śṛṇuṣva me
children.translated_text: The five <s>Brahmans</s>, the limbs of <s>Śiva</s>, have been stated; listen to me,
O well-vowed one, as I explain the heart and the other limbs, which likewise are forms of power.

children.text: oṃ īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāṃ hṛdayāya śaktibījāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Om. To <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of all vidyās, obeisance to the heart, to the seed of power.
Om. To <s>Īśvara</s>, lord of all beings, obeisance to the head, to immortality.
Om. To the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose form is the fire of time, obeisance to the crest-lock.
Om. To the lord of <s>Brahman</s>, to the time-fierce wind, obeisance to the armor.

children.text: oṃ brahmaṇe bṛṃhaṇāya jñānamūrtaye netrāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Om. To <s>Brahman</s>, to the increaser, to the embodiment of knowledge, obeisance to the eye.

children.text: oṃ śivāya sadāśivāya pāśupatāstrāya apratihatāya phaṭphaṭ ||
children.translated_text: Om. To <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, to the unobstructed Pāśupata weapon: phaṭ, phaṭ.

children.text: oṃ sadyojātāya bhavenānibhave bhavasya māṃ bhavodbhavāya śivamūrtaye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Om. To <s>Sadyojāta</s>, to <s>Bhava</s> and non-<s>Bhava</s>; may <s>Bhava</s> not overwhelm me; obeisance to the source of becoming, to the form of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: oṃ haṃsaśikhāya vidyādehāya ātmasvarūpāya parāparāya śivāya śivatamāya namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Om. To the swan-crested one, whose body is vidyā, whose nature is the self, who is higher and lower, to <s>Śiva</s>, the most auspicious, obeisance.

children.text: kathitāni śivāṅgāni mūrtividyā ca tasya vai
children.translated_text: The limbs of <s>Śiva</s> and his mūrti-vidyā have thus been told,
together with the brahmāṅga form and the limbs of vidyā, in the teaching of <s>Śiva</s>.
Now I shall explain the solar mantras, beginning with the Bāṣkala, O well-vowed one,
the limb-mantras found in all the Vedas and consisting of their essence, O well-vowed one.

children.text: oṃbhūḥ oṃbhuvaḥ oṃ svaḥ oṃmahaḥ oṃ janaḥ oṃ tapaḥ oṃsatyam oṃṛtam oṃ brahmā navākṣaramayaṃ mantraṃ bāṣkalaṃ parikīrtitam
children.translated_text: Om bhūḥ, om bhuvaḥ, om svaḥ, om mahaḥ, om janaḥ, om tapaḥ, om satyam, om ṛtam, om brahmā: this mantra, made of nine syllables, is called the Bāṣkala.
Because it does not perish in this world, it is therefore called imperishable.
It is said to be truth and imperishable, beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ.

children.text: oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi
children.translated_text: Om bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>.
May he impel our thoughts.
Obeisance to <s>Sūrya</s>, to <s>Khakholka</s>; obeisance.
This is called the root mantra of the great <s>Bhāskara</s>.
With the nine-syllabled mantra and the root mantra beginning with Dīpta, one should worship <s>Bhāskara</s>.
I shall briefly explain the limb-mantras.
They begin with the Vedas and the elements, while the praṇava stands in the middle.
Om bhūḥ. Obeisance to <s>Brahmā</s>, to the heart.
Om bhuvaḥ. Obeisance to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to the head.

children.text: oṃsvaḥ rudrāya śikhāyai namaḥ oṃbhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ jvālāmālinyai devāya namaḥ oṃmahaḥ maheśvarāya kavacāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Om svaḥ. Obeisance to <s>Rudra</s>, to the crest-lock. Om bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. Obeisance to the god <s>Jvālāmālinī</s>. Om mahaḥ. Obeisance to <s>Maheśvara</s>, to the armor.
Om janaḥ. Obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>, to the eyes.
Om tapas. Obeisance to <s>Tāpana</s>, to the weapon.
Thus, incidentally, the solar mantras have been stated here,
and the Śaiva ones as well, in summary, through the practice of nyāsa, O well-vowed one.
In this way one should worship the god made of mantra in the lotus of the heart.

children.text: nābhau homaṃ tu kartavyaṃ janayitvā yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: At the navel one should perform the homa, having generated it in due order.
Mentally, all rites are to be performed in the Śiva-fire for the lordly god,
the <s>Śiva</s>-form <s>Sadāśiva</s>, arisen from the limbs of the five <s>Brahmans</s>.
Carefully dividing him into parts, seated on a red lotus-seat,
with the root mantra, the mūrti-mantra, and the brahmāṅgas and the rest, O well-vowed one,
having mentally offered oblations of fuel-sticks and ghee from the disk of the moon,
one should remember a full stream arising from the lunar station.
By the rite of the full oblation, according to <s>Śiva</s>'s teaching for the wise,
one should meditate on <s>Śiva</s> as present in the mouth, and on the Śaṅkara radiance as pure light.
On the forehead, or again between the brows, one should remember the lord of gods,
and all that is in the heart-lotus, having completed the full extent of the rite.
One should contemplate him as having the form of a pure lamp-flame, the destroyer of becoming.

children.text: liṅge ca pūjayeddevaṃ sthaṇḍile vā sadāśivam ||
children.translated_text: And one should worship the god <s>Sadāśiva</s> in the liṅga or on the altar-ground.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
I shall briefly explain the exposition of the procedure of worship,
according to the path taught in the Śivaśāstra, as told formerly by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: athobhau candanacarcitau hastau vauṣaḍantenādyañjaliṃ kṛtvā mūrtividyāśivādīni japtvā aṅguṣṭhādikaniṣṭhikānta īśānādyaṃ kaniṣṭhikādimadhyamāntaṃ hṛdayāditṛtīyāntaṃ turīyamaṅguṣṭhenānāmikayā pañcamaṃ taladvayena ṣaṣṭhaṃ tarjanyaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nārācāstraprayogeṇa punarapi mūlaṃ japtvā turīyenāvaguṇṭhya śivahastam ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, after smearing both hands with sandal paste, making an añjali first with the ending vauṣaṭ, and reciting the mūrti-vidyā and the Śiva mantras, one applies <s>Īśāna</s> and the rest from the thumb through the little finger, then from the little finger through the middle finger, the heart and the rest through the third, the fourth with the thumb and ring finger, the fifth with both palms, and the sixth with the forefinger and thumb, using the Nārāca weapon application. Having again recited the root mantra and enveloped it with the fourth, this is called the Śiva-hand.
Worship of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed with that hand.
Having established the self as abiding in the tattvas, one should perform purification of the tattvas as before.

children.text: kṣmāmbho'gnivāyuvyomāntaṃ pañcacatuḥśuddhakoṭyante dhārāsahitena vyavasthāpya tacchuddhiṃ pūrvaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having arranged the sequence ending with earth, water, fire, wind, and ether, at the end of the five and four purified koṭis and together with the streams, he should first perform that purification.
Tattva-purification is with the sixth; earth-purification is from the third <s>Sadya</s> mantra ending in phaḍ.
Water-tattva purification is with the third <s>Sadya</s> mantra, joined with the sixth and ending in phaḍ.
Fire-purification is with the third Vāhneya mantra ending in phaḍ.
Wind-purification is with the fourth Vāyavya mantra, joined with the sixth and ending in phaḍ.
Space-purification is with the sixth, together with <s>Sadya</s>, and with the third mantra ending in phaḍ.

children.text: upasaṃhṛtyaivaṃ sadyaṣaṣṭhena tṛtīyena mūlena phaḍantena tāḍanaṃ tṛtīyena saṃpuṭīkṛtya grahaṇaṃ mūlameva yonibījena saṃpuṭīkṛtvā bandhanaṃ bandhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having drawn it in thus, striking is done with the root mantra, with the third and the <s>Sadya</s>-sixth, ending in phaḍ; grasping is done by enclosing it with the third; binding is done by enclosing the root mantra itself with the yoni-bīja. This is the bandha.

children.text: evaṃ kṣāntātītādinivṛttiparyantaṃ pūrvavatkṛtvā praṇavena tattvatrayakam anudhyāya ātmānaṃ dīpaśikhākāraṃ puryaṣṭakasahitaṃ trayātītaṃ śaktikṣobheṇāmṛtadhārāṃ suṣumṇāyāṃ dhyātvā ||
children.translated_text: Having thus performed the procedure from what is beyond kṣānta and the rest down to nivṛtti, as before, he should meditate with the praṇava on the triad of tattvas, and visualize himself in the form of a lamp-flame, together with the puryaṣṭaka, beyond the three, and an amṛta stream in the suṣumṇā through the stirring of śakti.

children.text: śāntyatītādinivṛttiparyantānāṃ cāntarnādabindvakārokāramakārāntaṃ śivaṃ sadāśivaṃ rudraviṣṇubrahmāntaṃ sṛṣṭikrameṇāmṛtīkaraṇaṃ brahmanyāsaṃ kṛtvā pañcavaktreṣu pañcadaśanayanaṃ vinyasya mūlena pādādikeśāntaṃ mahāmudrāmapi baddhvā śivo'hamiti dhyātvā śaktyādīni vinyasya hṛdi śaktyā bījāṅkurānantarāt sasuṣirasūtrakaṇṭakapatrakesaradharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasūryasomāgnivāmājyeṣṭhāraudrīkālīkalavikaraṇībalavikaraṇībalapramathanīsarvabhūtadamanīḥ kesareṣu karṇikāyāṃ manonmanīmapi dhyātvā ||
children.translated_text: For the series from śāntyatīta down to nivṛtti, ending with inner nāda, bindu, akāra, ukāra, and makāra, and ending with <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>, he should perform nectarization in the order of creation; having performed brahma-nyāsa, he should place the fifteen eyes in the five faces. With the root mantra he should place it from the feet to the hair, bind the mahāmudrā, meditate, 'I am <s>Śiva</s>,' and place the śaktis and the rest. In the heart, after śakti, he should visualize the seed, sprout, hollow stalk, filaments, thorns, petals, pericarp, and the filaments of dharma, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, sun, moon, fire, <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Kalavikaraṇī</s>, <s>Balavikaraṇī</s>, <s>Balapramathanī</s>, and <s>Sarvabhūtadamanī</s>; in the pericarp he should also visualize <s>Manonmanī</s>.

children.text: āsanaṃ parikalpyaivaṃ sarvopacārasahitaṃ bahiryogopacāreṇāntaḥkaraṇaṃ kṛtvā nābhau vahnikuṇḍe pūrvavadāsanaṃ parikalpya sadāśivaṃ dhyātvā binduto 'mṛtadhārāṃ śivamaṇḍale nipatitāṃ dhyātvā lalāṭe maheśvaraṃ dīpaśikhākāraṃ dhyātvā ātmaśuddhiritthaṃ prāṇāpānau saṃyamya suṣumṇayā vāyuṃ vyavasthāpya ṣaṣṭhena tālumudrāṃ kṛtvā digbandhaṃ kṛtvā ṣaṣṭhena sthānaśuddhir vastrādipūtāntararghyapātrādiṣu praṇavena tattvatrayaṃ vinyasya tadupari binduṃ dhyātvā vipūrya dravyāṇi ca vidhāya amṛtaplāvanaṃ kṛtvā pādyapātrādiṣu teṣāmarghyavadāsanaṃ parikalpya saṃhitayābhimantryādyenābhyarcya dvitīyenāmṛtīkṛtvā tṛtīyena viśodhya caturthenāvaguṇṭhya pañcamenāvalokya ṣaṣṭhena rakṣāṃvidhāya caturthena kuśapuñjenārghyāṃbhasābhyukṣya ātmānamapi dravyāṇi punar arghyāṃbhasābhyukṣya sapuṣpeṇa sarvadravyāṇi pṛthakpṛthak śodhayet ||
children.translated_text: Having thus imagined the seat with all services, and having performed the inner act by means of the outer yogic service, he should imagine the seat as before in the fire-pit at the navel, meditate on <s>Sadāśiva</s>, visualize an amṛta stream fallen from the bindu into the Śiva-maṇḍala, and visualize <s>Maheśvara</s> at the forehead in the form of a lamp-flame. This is self-purification: restraining prāṇa and apāna, establishing the breath through the suṣumṇā, making the tālu-mudrā with the sixth, making the binding of the directions, purifying the place with the sixth, placing the three tattvas with the praṇava in the cloth-purified inner arghya vessel and the other vessels, visualizing the bindu above it, filling it, arranging the substances, flooding them with amṛta, imagining seats for them in the vessels for foot-water and the rest as for the arghya, consecrating them with the saṃhitā, worshiping with the first, making them nectar with the second, purifying with the third, covering with the fourth, looking upon them with the fifth, establishing protection with the sixth, sprinkling them with arghya water by means of a bundle of kuśa grass and the fourth, sprinkling himself and the substances again with arghya water, and then purifying all the substances separately with flowers.
With <s>Sadya</s> he should consecrate fragrance, and with <s>Vāma</s> the garment.
With <s>Aghora</s> he should consecrate ornaments, and with <s>Puruṣa</s> the food offering.
With <s>Īśāna</s> he should consecrate the flowers; then he should empower them with mantra.
With the Śiva-gāyatrī he should sprinkle the remainder.
The five nectars, the five cow-products, and so on he should consecrate with the brahma, aṅga, root, and other mantras.

children.text: pṛthakpṛthaṅmūlenārghyaṃ dhūpaṃ dattvācamanīyaṃ ca teṣāmapi dhenumudrāṃ ca darśayitvā kavacenāvaguṇṭhyāstreṇa rakṣāṃ ca vidhāya dravyaśuddhiṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Separately, with the root mantra, after giving arghya, incense, and water for sipping, and after showing the dhenu-mudrā to those also, covering them with the kavaca mantra and establishing protection with the astra mantra, he should perform the purification of the substances.

children.text: arghyodakamagre hṛdā gandham ādāyāstreṇa viśodhya pūjāprabhṛtikaraṇaṃ rakṣāntaṃ kṛtvaivaṃ dravyaśuddhiṃ pūjāsamarpaṇāntaṃ maunamāsthāya puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā sarvamantrāṇi praṇavādinamo'ntājjapitvā puṣpāñjaliṃ tyajenmantraśuddhirittham ||
children.translated_text: First, from the arghya water, taking fragrance with the heart mantra and purifying it with the astra mantra, he should perform the acts beginning with worship and ending with protection. Thus, having completed the purification of substances up to the offering of worship, he should keep silence, give a handful of flowers, recite all the mantras beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ, and release the flower-offering. Mantra-purification is thus.

children.text: agre sāmānyārghyapātraṃ payasāpūrya gandhapuṣpādinā saṃhitayābhimantrya dhenumudrāṃ dattvā kavacenāvaguṇṭhyāstreṇa rakṣayet
children.translated_text: In front, having filled the common arghya vessel with milk, consecrated it with the saṃhitā together with fragrance, flowers, and the rest, shown the dhenu-mudrā, covered it with the kavaca mantra, he should protect it with the astra mantra.

children.text: pūjāṃ paryuṣitāṃ gāyatryā samabhyarcya sāmānyārghyaṃ dattvā gandhapuṣpadhūpācamanīyaṃ svadhāntaṃ namo'ntaṃ vā dattvā brahmabhiḥ pṛthakpṛthakpuṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā phaḍantāstreṇa nirmālyaṃ vyapohya īśānyāṃ caṇḍam abhyarcyāsanamūrticaṇḍaṃ sāmānyāstreṇa liṅgapīṭhaṃ śivaṃ pāśupatāstreṇa viśodhya mūrdhni puṣpaṃ nidhāya pūjayelliṅgaśuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having duly worshiped the worship that has become stale with the Gāyatrī, he should give the common arghya; having offered fragrance, flowers, incense, and water for sipping, ending with svadhā or else ending with namaḥ, and having given separate flower-offerings with the brahma mantras, he should remove the nirmālya with the astra mantra ending in phaḍ. In the northeast he should worship <s>Caṇḍa</s>; he should purify the seat, the image, and <s>Caṇḍa</s>, then the liṅga-pedestal of <s>Śiva</s> with the common astra and the Pāśupata astra, place a flower on the head, and worship. This is liṅga-purification.

children.text: āsanaṃ kūrmaśilāyāṃ bījāṅkuraṃ tadupari brahmaśilāyām anantanālasuṣire sūtrapatrakaṇṭakakarṇikākesaradharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryasūryasomāgnikesaraśaktiṃ manonmanīṃ karṇikāyāṃ manonmanenānantāsanāyeti samāsenāsanaṃ parikalpya tadupari nivṛttyādikalāmayaṃ ṣaḍvidhasahitaṃ karmakalāṅgadehaṃ sadāśivaṃ bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: Having imagined the seat on the tortoise-stone, the seed and sprout, and above that on the brahma-stone, in the hollow of <s>Ananta</s>'s stalk, the filaments, petals, thorns, pericarp, filaments of dharma, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, sun, moon, and fire, the śakti in the filaments, and <s>Manonmanī</s> in the pericarp with the Manonmana mantra, using in brief the formula 'for the seat of <s>Ananta</s>,' he should arrange the seat. Above it he should visualize <s>Sadāśiva</s>, consisting of the kalās beginning with nivṛtti, accompanied by the sixfold set, and having a body formed of karmakalā and limbs.

children.text: ubhābhyāṃ sapuṣpābhyāṃ hastābhyāmaṅguṣṭhena puṣpamāpīḍya āvāhanamudrayā śanaiḥśanaiḥ hṛdayādimastakāntam āropya hṛdā saha mūlaṃ plutam uccārya sadyena bindusthānādabhyadhikaṃ dīpaśikhākāraṃ sarvatomukhahastaṃ vyāpyavyāpakam āvāhya sthāpayet ||
children.translated_text: With both hands filled with flowers, pressing the flower with the thumbs, by means of the invocation-mudrā one should slowly raise it from the heart and so on up to the head. Having uttered the prolonged root mantra together with the heart-mantra and <s>Sadya</s>, one should invoke from the place of the bindu a form somewhat higher, shaped like the flame of a lamp, with hands facing all directions, pervading and pervaded, and should establish it.

children.text: pūrvahṛdā śivaśaktisamavāyena paramīkaraṇam amṛtīkaraṇaṃ hṛdayādimūlena sadyenāvāhanaṃ hṛdā mūlopari aghoreṇa saṃnirodhaṃ hṛdā mūlopari puruṣeṇa sānnidhyaṃ hṛdā mūlena īśānena pūjayediti upadeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the former heart-mantra there is making supreme through the union of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, and making immortal; by the heart-mantra and root-mantra, with <s>Sadya</s>, invocation; by the heart-mantra over the root, with <s>Aghora</s>, restraint; by the heart-mantra over the root, with <s>Puruṣa</s>, presence; by the heart-mantra, the root-mantra, and <s>Īśāna</s>, one should worship. This is the instruction.

children.text: pañcamantrasahitena yathāpūrvamātmano dehanirmāṇaṃ tathā devasyāpi vahneścaivamupadeśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Just as the construction of one's own body was done before with the five mantras, so also it is for the deity and for the fire. This is the instruction.

children.text: rūpakadhyānaṃ kṛtvā mūlena namaskārāntamāpādya svadhāntamācamanīyaṃ sarvaṃ namaskārāntaṃ vā svāhākārāntamarghyaṃ mūlena puṣpāñjaliṃ vauṣaḍantena sarvaṃ namaskārāntaṃ hṛdā vā īśānena vā rudragāyatryā oṃnamaḥ śivāyeti mūlamantreṇa vā pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Having performed meditation on the manifest form, one should, with the root mantra, bring it to the ending namaḥ; the water for sipping should end in svadhā; everything may end in namaḥ, or the arghya may end with svāhā; the flower-offering is made with the root mantra ending in vauṣaṭ. One should worship with everything ending in namaḥ, or with the heart-mantra, or with <s>Īśāna</s>, or with the <s>Rudra</s>-Gāyatrī, or with the root mantra, "Oṃ namaḥ śivāya."

children.text: puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā punar dhūpācamanīyaṃ ṣaṣṭhena puṣpāvasaraṇaṃ visarjanaṃ mantrodakena mūlena saṃsnāpya sarvadravyābhiṣekamīśānena pratidravyamaṣṭapuṣpaṃ dattvaivamarghyaṃ ca gandhapuṣpadhūpācamanīyaṃ phaḍantāstreṇa pūjāpasaraṇaṃ śuddhodakena mūlena saṃsnāpya piṣṭāmalakādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After giving the flower-offering, again incense and water for sipping are offered; with the sixth mantra there is removal of the flowers and dismissal. Having bathed it with mantra-water by the root mantra, one performs ablution with all substances by <s>Īśāna</s>; for each substance one gives eight flowers, and likewise arghya, fragrance, flowers, incense, and water for sipping. With the weapon-mantra ending in phaṭ there is removal of the worship; having bathed it with pure water by the root mantra, with ground āmalaka and the like,

children.text: uṣṇodakena haridrādyena liṅgamūrtiṃ pīṭhasahitāṃ viśodhya gandhodakahiraṇyodakamantrodakena rudrādhyāyaṃ paṭhamānaḥ nīlarudratvaritarudrapañcabrahmādibhiḥ namaḥ śivāyeti snāpayet ||
children.translated_text: with warm water and with turmeric and the rest, one should cleanse the liṅga-image together with its pedestal. Then, while reciting the <s>Rudra</s> chapter, with scented water, golden water, and mantra-water, and with the <s>Nīlarudra</s>, <s>Tvaritarudra</s>, <s>Pañcabrahma</s>, and the like, and with "namaḥ śivāya," one should bathe it.

children.text: mūrdhni puṣpaṃ nidhāyaivaṃ na śūnyaṃ liṅgamastakaṃ kuryādatra ślokaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having placed a flower on its head in this way, one should not leave the head of the liṅga empty. On this point there is a verse:

children.text: yasya rāṣṭre tu liṅgasya mastakaṃ śūnyalakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: In whose kingdom the head of the liṅga has the mark of emptiness,
for him there will be misfortune, great disease, famine, or destruction of vehicles.
Therefore the king should avoid this, for the sake of dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation.

children.text: śūnye liṅge svayaṃ rājā rāṣṭraṃ caiva praṇaśyati ||
children.translated_text: When the liṅga is empty, the king himself and the kingdom indeed perish.

children.text: evaṃ susnāpyārghyaṃ ca dattvā saṃmṛjya vastreṇa gandhapuṣpavastrālaṅkārādīṃśca mūlena dadyāt ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed it well in this way, given arghya, and wiped it with a cloth, one should give fragrance, flowers, garments, ornaments, and the rest with the root mantra.
Incense, water for sipping, lamp, food-offering, and the rest are also given with the root mantra; worship above with the principal mantra is called purification.

children.text: ārārtidīpādīṃścaiva dhenumudrāmudritāni kavacenāvaguṇṭhitāni ṣaṣṭhena rakṣitāni liṅge ca liṅgasyādhaḥ sādhāraṇaṃ ca darśayet ||
children.translated_text: The ārati lamps and the like, sealed with the cow-mudrā, veiled with the armor-mantra, and protected with the sixth mantra, should be shown to the liṅga, below the liṅga, and generally around it.

Having respectfully announced the salutation with the root mantra, one should worship by the path of brahmāṅga enjoyment, furnished with the services of invocation, establishment, restraint, presence, water for the feet, water for sipping, arghya, fragrance, flowers, incense, food-offering, water for sipping, rubbing of the hands, mouth-perfume, and the like.
Meditation on the manifest, recollection of the unmanifest, meditation on the higher and lower, and recitation of the root mantra,

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ brahmāṅgajapasamarpaṇam ātmanivedanastutinamaskārādayaśca gurupūjā ca pūrvato dakṣiṇe vināyakasya ||
children.translated_text: the offering of a tenth part as brahmāṅga-recitation, self-surrender, praise, obeisance, and the rest, and worship of the guru; in the east and to the south is worship of <s>Vināyaka</s>.

children.text: ādau cānte ca saṃpūjyo vighneśo jagadīśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: At the beginning and at the end, <s>Vighneśa</s>, lord of the world, should be fully worshiped,
together with the deities and the twice-born, for the accomplishment of the aims of all rites.

children.text: yaḥ śivaṃ pūjayedevaṃ liṅge vā sthaṇḍile'pi vā
children.translated_text: Whoever worships <s>Śiva</s> in this way, whether in a liṅga or even on an altar-ground,
goes to union with <s>Śiva</s> by a rite of only one year.
A worshiper of the liṅga does so in six months; no deliberation is needed here.

children.text: sapta pradakṣiṇāḥ kṛtvā daṇḍavat praṇamed budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made seven circumambulations, the wise man should bow down like a staff.
With each step in the course of circumambulation there is the fruit of a hundred horse-sacrifices.
Therefore one should worship him daily for the accomplishment of the aims of all rites.
One who desires enjoyment obtains enjoyment; one who desires a kingdom obtains a kingdom.
One who desires a son obtains an excellent son; a sick person is freed from disease.
Whatever desires a person contemplates, those he obtains.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
I shall explain the rite of the <s>Śiva</s>-fire, as defined by <s>Śiva</s>.
Having first produced the eastern direction in front, in an auspicious and well-prepared place,
one should make three auspicious cords, one with its end to the east and one with its end to the north.
When the ground has been made square, one should carefully make the fire-pits.
The fire-pit for the daily homa should be furnished with three girdles.
The girdles should measure four, three, and two finger-breadths, and be a cubit in extent.
The pit should be a cubit in size, and the yoni should be a span in size.
One should arrange the yoni, like an aśvattha leaf, above the girdle.
In the middle of the pit there should be a navel, an eight-petaled form with a pericarp.
O son of <s>Brahmā</s>, one should make it according to rule, a span in size.
Scratching the lines with the sixth mantra is prescribed; sprinkling is remembered as being done with the armor-mantra.
Having inspected the pit with the eye-mantra, the wise man should make six lines.
O best of Brahmins, along the lines extended eastward are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
The lines whose ends are to the north are auspicious; he should sprinkle them again with the armor-mantra.
Taking a fire-stick born of śamī and pippala wood, sixteen finger-breadths long,
having churned it with the fire-seed, he should make the placement of <s>Śakti</s> with the heart-mantra.
One should place the fire according to rule, having performed the anvādhāna in due manner,
silently, with auspicious sacrificial splinters measuring a prādeśa.
One should perform the complete sprinkling with water in the eight directions,
and strew the barhis according to rule, beginning with the east and proceeding in that order.
In front it should have its tips toward the north; in the south, again, its tips should face east.

children.text: paścime cottarāgraṃ tu saumye pūrvāgrameva tu ||
children.translated_text: In the west its tips should face north, and in the northern quarter its tips should face east.
In the Indra quarter one should place it with tips toward Indra; in the Yama quarter the same rule is prescribed.
Above the northern side is the lunar fire, and below is the Varuṇa-fire.
Having set the vessels down in pairs on the barhis, O well-vowed one,
all of them face downward, one should likewise place the ritual substances to the north.
Above that one should place darbhas, and one should set <s>Śiva</s> to the south.
One should worship with the root mantra, and afterwards perform the homa.
Taking the prokṣaṇī vessel, one should again fill it with water.
One should place two kuśa blades, each measuring a prādeśa, on top of the water.

children.text: plāvayecca kuśāgraṃ tu vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ
children.translated_text: One should moisten the tip of the kuśa with the rays of the sun, O Vasu,
and, having scattered all the vessels, sprinkle them thoroughly according to rule.
Taking the praṇītā vessel, one should again fill it with water.
With other water and kuśa tips, one should cover it properly, O well-vowed one.
With both hands one should set the vessel, its mouth like a nose, in the northeastern direction.
One should make the auspicious ājyādhiśrayaṇa to the northwest.
One should take coals mixed with ash by means of a sacrificial splinter,
carry them to the northwest, and there heat the ghee.
Having lit kuśa blades in the fire, one should carry them around the fire three times.
Having thrown all of them there, one should set the ghee down in front.

children.text: aṅguṣṭhamātrau tu kuśau prakṣālya vidhinaiva tu
children.translated_text: One should wash two kuśa blades, each the size of a thumb, according to rule,

children.text: paryagniṃ ca tataḥ kuryāttaireva navabhiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then again perform the circling of the fire with those same nine.
One should again carry them around the fire, and then take down that ghee.
Then one should draw the vessel away in order toward the northwest.
Having joined the fire with a piece of wood, washed it, and placed it in the west,
one should perform the purification of the ghee together with the two pavitras.
Taking them separately with the two hands, in a flowing motion, in due order,
with the thumb and ring finger, with both hands, and with the root vidyā,
one should sprinkle them and put the two pavitras, smeared with ghee, into the fire.
One should make the sruk and sruva of gold, measuring an aratni, O well-vowed one,
or of silver, as is proper, endowed with all the prescribed marks.
Alternatively, both the sruk and the sruva should be made from sacrificial trees.
Their length should be an aratni; in its bowl there should be a hollow.
The base of the handle, O great sage, should have a circumference of six aṅgulas.
The neck-tube should be half of that, and the lotus bowl should be like the base.
The handle should resemble a cow's tail, and the tip of the sruva should be like a nose.
It should be furnished with two cups and filled with pearls and the like.
It should be thirty-six aṅgulas long and eight aṅgulas broad.
Its height should be half of that, and it should then be measured with a cord.
The mouth should be seven aṅgulas in both breadth and length.
The tip should be one third; after making it, one should discard the remainder.
The neck should be two aṅgulas long and four aṅgulas wide.
The altar should be eight aṅgulas long, with a breadth equal to that measure.
In its middle one should make a hollow measuring four aṅgulas.
The hollow should be well-rounded, with eight petals and a fine pericarp.
Around it, outside the hollow, there should be a band of half an aṅgula.
Outside that, without a gap, it should be ornamented with lotus petals.
Outside that there should be a band measuring two barley-corns.
In the middle of the small altar, the opening should be the measure of the little finger.
The depression should extend down to the mouth, with the hollow's measure descending.
The handle should be six aṅgulas, the tube so made, and at the end of the handle three small rods,
increasing by half an aṅgula, are to be made four aṅgulas.
At the base of the handle there should be a jar thirteen aṅgulas long.
The kumbha should be two aṅgulas, and the navel should be known as ten aṅgulas.

children.text: vedimadhye tathā kṛtvā pādaṃ kuryācca dvyaṅgulam
children.translated_text: Having made it thus in the middle of the altar, one should make a foot two aṅgulas long.
The foot should have the shape of the back of a lotus and the form of a pericarp.
Its rear shape should be like an elephant's lip.
For abhicāra and similar rites, one should make it of black iron.
One should again wipe the sruk and sruva with twenty-five kuśa blades.
One should cleanse the tip with the tip, the middle with the middle, O well-vowed one,

children.text: mūlaṃ mūlena vidhinā agnau tāpya hṛdā punaḥ
children.translated_text: and the root with the root according to rule, and heat them in the fire with the heart mantra.

children.text: ājyasthālī praṇītā ca prokṣaṇī tisra eva ca ||
children.translated_text: There are exactly three vessels: the ājya-sthālī, the praṇītā, and the prokṣaṇī.

children.text: sauvarṇī rājatī vāpi tāmrī vā mṛnmayī tu vā
children.translated_text: They may be of gold, silver, copper, or clay.

children.text: anyathā naiva kartavyaṃ śāntike pauṣṭike śubhe ||
children.translated_text: They are not to be made otherwise in auspicious rites for peace and prosperity.

children.text: āyasī tvabhicāre tu śāntike mṛnmayī tu vā
children.translated_text: For abhicāra rites, however, they may be of iron; for peaceful rites, they may also be of clay.
The mouth of the vessels is said to be six aṅgulas broad.
The prokṣaṇī is two aṅgulas high, and the praṇītā is two aṅgulas higher.
After that, the ājya-sthālī has a height two aṅgulas higher than that.
The enclosing sticks should be made from the same fuel-sticks with which oblation is prescribed.
They should be of the circumference of the middle finger, straight, unblemished, and even.
Three paridhi sticks, each thirty-two aṅgulas long, are remembered.
With thirty darbhas, each thirty-two aṅgulas long, one should spread the enclosure.
But within a span of four aṅgulas it is to be tied clockwise,
in rites such as abhicāra, excluding the establishment of the <s>Śiva</s>-fire.
For abhicāra rites, O Brahmin, firm sticks that are not tender should be collected,
complete, very even, thick, and measuring a little finger in girth.
They should not be crooked, should be without wounds and smooth, and should measure twelve aṅgulas.
For fuel-sticks, O well-vowed one, this is the proper measure in all rites.

children.text: gavyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tataḥ śreṣṭha kāpilaṃ tu tato 'dhikam
children.translated_text: Ghee from cows is best; that from a tawny cow is still superior.

children.text: āhutīnāṃ pramāṇaṃ tu sruvaṃ pūrṇaṃ yathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The measure of oblations should be such that the sruva is full.
Cooked food should be the size of an akṣa; sesame should be by the measure of a śukti.
For barley the measure should be half of that, and for fruits according to their own size.
For milk, honey, and curds, the measure should be the same as for ghee.
A full oblation is made with a sruva in the measure of four sruvas.

children.text: tadardhaṃ sviṣṭakṛt proktaṃ śeṣaṃ sarvamathāpi vā
children.translated_text: The sviṣṭakṛt is said to be half of that, or else all that remains.
One should always offer pacificatory and prosperity rites in the <s>Śiva</s>-fire.
In an ordinary fire, O greatly fortunate one, rites such as bewildering and expulsion are performed.
But after generating the <s>Śiva</s>-fire, O well-vowed one, in every rite
one should establish the seven tongues and then have all rites performed.
Or else all rites are accomplished with a single tongue alone.
The <s>Śiva</s>-fire, O best of Brahmins, is effective with a single tongue alone.

children.text: oṃ bahurūpāyai madhyajihvāyai anekavarṇāyai dakṣiṇottaramadhyagāyai śāntipauṣṭikamokṣādiphalapradāyai svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Om, to <s>Bahurūpā</s>, the middle tongue, the many-colored one, moving in the middle from south to north, the giver of fruits such as peace, prosperity, and liberation: svāhā.

children.text: oṃ hiraṇyāyai cāmīkarābhāyai īśānajihvāyai jñānapradāyai svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Om, to <s>Hiraṇyā</s>, the golden one, having the appearance of refined gold, the <s>Īśāna</s> tongue, the giver of knowledge: svāhā.

children.text: oṃ kanakāyai kanakanibhāyai ramyāyai aindrajihvāyai svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Om, to <s>Kanakā</s>, resembling gold, lovely, the Aindra tongue: svāhā.

children.text: oṃ raktāyai raktavarṇāyai āgneyajihvāyai anekavarṇāyai vidveṣaṇamohanāyai svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Om, to <s>Raktā</s>, red in color, the Āgneya tongue, many-colored, causing hostility and bewilderment: svāhā.
Om, to <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, the Nairṛta tongue, for killing rites: svāhā.

children.text: oṃ suprabhāyai paścimajihvāyai muktāphalāyai śāntikāyai pauṣṭikāyai svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Om, to <s>Suprabhā</s>, the western tongue, pearl-like, pacificatory and prosperity-giving: svāhā.
Om, to <s>Abhivyaktā</s>, the Vāyavya tongue, for the expulsion of enemies: svāhā.
Om, to <s>Vahni</s>, the fiery one: svāhā.
This much is the consecration of fire; or, in fire rites
and in occasional rites, he should again prepare the <s>Śiva</s>-fire according to rule.

children.text: nirīkṣaṇaṃ prokṣaṇaṃ tāḍanaṃ ca ṣaṣṭhena phaḍantena abhyukṣaṇaṃ caturthena khananotkiraṇaṃ ṣaṣṭhena pūraṇaṃ samīkaraṇamādyena secanaṃ vauṣaḍantena kuṭṭanaṃ ṣaṣṭhena saṃmārjanopalepane turīyeṇa kuṇḍaparikalpanaṃ nivṛttyā tribhireva kuṇḍaparidhānaṃ caturthena kuṇḍārcanamādyena rekhācatuṣṭayasaṃpādanaṃ ṣaṣṭhena phaḍantena vajrīkaraṇaṃ catuṣpadāpādanamādyena evaṃ kuṇḍasaṃskāramaṣṭādaśavidham ||
children.translated_text: Inspection, sprinkling, and striking are done with the sixth mantra ending in phaḍ; additional sprinkling with the fourth; digging and casting up with the sixth; filling and leveling with the first; pouring with the mantra ending in vauṣaḍ; pounding with the sixth; sweeping and plastering with the fourth; laying out the fire-pit with nivṛtti; enclosing the fire-pit with the three alone; worship of the fire-pit with the fourth; completing the four lines with the first; making it vajra-like with the sixth ending in phaḍ; and producing the four-footed form with the first: thus the consecration of the fire-pit is eighteenfold.
After the consecration of the fire-pit, the casting of akṣa is done with the sixth, the placing of the viṣṭara with the first, and the invocation of <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> on the vajra-seat.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ vāgīśvarīṃ śyāmavarṇāṃ viśālākṣīṃ yauvanonmattavigrahām
children.translated_text: Om hrīṃ, I invoke <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>, dark in color, wide-eyed, with a form intoxicated by youth,
menstruating, the śakti of <s>Vāgīśvara</s>.
I worship <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>.
Om īṃ, obeisance to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>.
Having honored <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> through invocation, establishment, presence, restraint, and worship, he performs the garbhādhāna consecration of the fire.

children.text: ekavaktraṃ caturbhujaṃ śuddhasphaṭikābhaṃ varadābhayahastaṃ paraśumṛgadharaṃ jaṭāmukuṭamaṇḍitaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitamāvāhayāmi ||
children.translated_text: I invoke the one-faced, four-armed one, shining like pure crystal, whose hands grant boons and fearlessness, who holds an axe and a deer, adorned with a matted-hair crown and ornamented with every ornament.
Om īṃ, obeisance to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>.
Having honored <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> through invocation, establishment, presence, restraint, and worship, he performs the garbhādhāna consecration of the fire.

children.text: araṇījanitaṃ kāntodbhavaṃ vā agnihotrajaṃ vā tāmrapātre śarāve vā ānīya nirīkṣaṇatāḍanābhyukṣaṇaprakṣālanam ādyena kravyādā śivaparityāgo 'pi prathamena vahnes traikāraṇaṃ jaṭharabhrūmadhyād āvāhyāgniṃ vaikāraṇamūrtāvāgneyena uddīpanamādyena puruṣeṇa saṃhitayā dhāraṇā dhenumudrāṃ turīyeṇāvaguṇṭhya jānubhyāmavaniṃ gatvā śarāvotthāpanaṃ kuṇḍopari nidhāya pradakṣiṇamāvartya turīyeṇātmasammukhāṃ vāgīśvarīṃ garbhanāḍyāṃ garbhādhānāntarīyeṇa kamalapradānamādyena vauṣaḍantena kuśārghyaṃ dattvā indhanapradānamādyena prajvālanaṃ garbhādhānaṃ ca sadyenādyena pūjanaṃ vāmena pūjanaṃ dvitīyena sīmantonnayanam aghoreṇa tṛtīyena pūjanam ||
children.translated_text: Having brought fire generated from the araṇis, or arising from kānta, or from the agnihotra, in a copper vessel or in a dish, he should perform inspection, striking, sprinkling, and washing with the first mantra. With the first there is also the abandonment of the flesh-eating and non-Śiva aspect. Having invoked the threefold causal fire from the belly and the space between the brows, and the fire in the vaikāraṇa form, he should kindle it with the Āgneya, the first, and the Puruṣa saṃhitā; perform dhāraṇā; cover it with the dhenu-mudrā by means of the fourth; kneel on the ground; lift up the dish; place it over the fire-pit; turn it clockwise; with the fourth make <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> face himself; with the garbhādhāna intermediate rite place the lotus in the womb-channel; with the first ending in vauṣaḍ give kuśa-water; with the first give fuel; kindle it; perform garbhādhāna; worship with the Sadya and the first; worship with the Vāma and the second; perform the parting of the hair with the Aghora and the third; and worship.

children.text: avayavavyāptir vaktrodghāṭanaṃ vaktraniṣkṛtiriti tṛtīyena garbhajātakarmapuruṣeṇa pūjanaṃ turīyeṇa ṣaṣṭhena prokṣaṇaṃ sūtakaśuddhaye cāgnisūnurakṣākuśāstreṇa vaktreṇāgnau mūlam īśāgraṃ nairṛtimūlaṃ vāyavyāgraṃ vāyavyamūlamīśāgramiti kuśāstaraṇam iti pūrvoktam idhmam agramūlaghṛtāktaṃ lālāpanodāya ṣaṣṭhena juhuyāt ||
children.translated_text: Pervasion of the limbs, opening of the mouth, and purification of the mouth are performed with the third; worship is done with the Puruṣa of the garbha-jātakarma, sprinkling with the fourth and sixth. For purification from birth impurity, by means of the fire-son protection and the kuśa-weapon, the kuśa grass is spread in the fire with its mouth, with the root at <s>Īśāna</s> and the tip at Nairṛta, or the root at Vāyavya and the tip at <s>Īśāna</s>. The previously mentioned fuel-stick, smeared with ghee at tip and root, should be offered with the sixth for removing saliva.

children.text: pañcapūrvātikrameṇa paridhiviṣṭaranyāso 'pi ādyena viṣṭaropari hiraṇyagarbhaharanārāyaṇānapi pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: In the sequence after the five preliminaries, he should also perform the placing of the enclosing sticks and the spread; with the first mantra he should worship <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as well, above the spread.
And he should worship the guardians of the worlds beginning with <s>Indra</s>.
He should also worship those extending as far as <s>Vajrāvarta</s>.
Beginning with the worship of <s>Vāgīśvara</s> and <s>Vāgīśvarī</s>, he should dismiss them with the first mantra and release what has been offered in the fire.

children.text: sraksruvasaṃskāramatho nirīkṣaṇaprokṣaṇatāḍanābhyukṣaṇādīni pūrvavat sraksruvaṃ ca hastadvaye gṛhītvā saṃsthāpanamādyena tāḍanamapi sruksruvopari darbhānulekhanamūlamadhyamāgreṇa tritvena srukśaktiṃ sruvamapi śaṃbhuṃ dakṣiṇapārśve kuśopari śaktaye namaḥ śaṃbhave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Next is the consecration of the sruk and sruva ladles: inspection, sprinkling, striking, asperging, and the rest are as before. Taking the sruk and sruva in both hands, he should establish them with the first mantra, strike them, and trace with darbha grass over the sruk and sruva at root, middle, and tip, in three parts. On kuśa grass at the right side, he should regard the sruk as <s>Śakti</s> and the sruva as <s>Śambhu</s>, saying, 'obeisance to <s>Śakti</s>, obeisance to <s>Śambhu</s>.'
Then, with the final thread, he should wrap the sruk and sruva with the fourth mantra and worship them.

children.text: dhenumudrāṃ darśayitvā turīyeṇāvaguṇṭhya ṣaṣṭhena rakṣāṃ vidhāya sruksruvasaṃskāraḥ pūrvamevoktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having shown the dhenumudrā, covered them with the fourth mantra, and made protection with the sixth, the consecration of the sruk and sruva is as already stated before.
Again, the consecration of the ghee has already been stated before: inspection, sprinkling, striking, asperging, and the rest are as before.

children.text: ājyapratāpanamaiśānyāṃ vā ṣaṣṭhena vedyupari vinyasya ghṛtapātraṃ vitastimātraṃ kuśapavitraṃ vāmahastāṅguṣṭhānāmikāgraṃ gṛhītvā dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhānāmikāmūlaṃ gṛhītvāgnijvālotpavanaṃ svāhāntena turīyeṇa punaḥ ṣaḍ darbhān gṛhītvā pūrvavatsvātmasaṃplavanaṃ svāhāntenādyena kuśadvayapavitrabandhanaṃ cādyena ghṛte nyasediti pavitrīkaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: For heating the ghee, he should place the ghee vessel on the altar in the northeast, or with the sixth mantra; taking a kuśa purifier measuring a span with the tips of the left thumb and ring finger, and taking it at the root with the right thumb and ring finger, he should fan the fire-flame with the fourth mantra ending in svāhā. Again taking six darbhas as before, he should sprinkle himself with the first mantra ending in svāhā; with the first mantra he should bind two kuśas as a purifier and place them in the ghee. This is the purification.
Taking two darbhas, he should kindle the fire and turn the ghee three times.
Having sprinkled it, he should place it in the fire; this is nīrājana.

children.text: punardarbhān gṛhītvā kīṭakādi nirīkṣyārghyeṇa saṃprokṣya darbhānagnau nidhāya ityavadyotanam ||
children.translated_text: Again taking darbhas, inspecting for insects and the like, sprinkling them with arghya water, and placing the darbhas in the fire: this is the illumination.
Taking two darbhas, he should inspect the ghee by means of the flame of the fire.

children.text: darbheṇa gṛhītvā tenāgradvayena śuklapakṣadvayenādyeneti kṛṣṇapakṣasampātanaṃ ghṛtaṃ tribhāgena vibhajya sruveṇaikabhāgenājyenāgnaye svāhā dvitīyenājyena somāya svāhā ājyena oṃ agnīṣomābhyāṃ svāhā ājyenāgnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Taking it with darbha grass, with those two tips and with the first mantra, as the two bright fortnights, he should make the dark fortnight descend. Dividing the ghee into three parts, with one part of ghee from the sruva he should offer, 'to <s>Agni</s>, svāhā'; with the second ghee, 'to <s>Soma</s>, svāhā'; with ghee, 'oṃ, to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, svāhā'; and with ghee, 'to <s>Agni</s> Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā.'
Again taking it with kuśa grass, he should consecrate it with the saṃhitā-mantra ending in namaḥ.
Having consecrated it, he should make protection by showing the dhenumudrā, by covering with the kavaca, and by means of the astra mantra.
Then he should place it in the consecrated vessel. This is the consecration of the ghee.
With ghee, through the mouth of the sruk, he should make the circular anointing: with the śakti-bīja and the rest, 'to the <s>Īśāna</s> form, svāhā.'

children.text: pūrvavat puruṣavaktrāya svāhā aghorahṛdayāya svāhā vāmadevāya guhyāya svāhā sadyojātamūrtaye svāhā
children.translated_text: As before: 'to the <s>Puruṣa</s> face, svāhā; to the <s>Aghora</s> heart, svāhā; to <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the secret one, svāhā; to the <s>Sadyojāta</s> form, svāhā.'
This is the opening of the faces.

children.text: īśānamūrtaye tatpuruṣavaktrāya svāhā tatpuruṣavaktrāya aghorahṛdayāya svāhā aghorahṛdayāya vāmaguhyāya sadyojātamūrtaye svāhā iti vaktrasaṃdhānam ||
children.translated_text: 'To the <s>Īśāna</s> form and to the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> face, svāhā; to the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> face and to the <s>Aghora</s> heart, svāhā; to the <s>Aghora</s> heart, to the secret <s>Vāma</s>, and to the <s>Sadyojāta</s> form, svāhā.' This is the joining of the faces.

children.text: īśānamūrtaye tatpuruṣāya vaktrāya aghorahṛdayāya vāmadevāya guhyāya sadyojātāya svāhā iti vaktrasaṃdhānam ||
children.translated_text: 'To the <s>Īśāna</s> form, to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> as face, to the <s>Aghora</s> heart, to <s>Vāmadeva</s> as secret, and to <s>Sadyojāta</s>, svāhā.' This is the joining of the faces.

children.text: īśānamūrtaye tatpuruṣāya vaktrāya aghorahṛdayāya vāmadevāya guhyāya sadyojātamūrtaye svāhā iti vaktraikyakaraṇam ||
children.translated_text: 'To the <s>Īśāna</s> form, to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> as face, to the <s>Aghora</s> heart, to <s>Vāmadeva</s> as secret, and to the <s>Sadyojāta</s> form, svāhā.' This is the making of the faces into one.
Having thus produced the <s>Śivāgni</s> (Śiva-fire), he should have all rites performed.
Or even simply with its tongue, rites beginning with pacification are always to be performed.
In acts beginning with garbhādhāna, for each fire separately, O imperishable one,
ten oblations are to be given, fivefold, with the yoni-bīja.
In the <s>Śivāgni</s> he should prepare the divine supreme seat as before,

children.text: āvāhanaṃ tathā nyāsaṃ yathā deve tathārcanam ||
children.translated_text: and the invocation, the nyāsa, and the worship should be just as for the deity.
Having recited the root mantra once and bowed to the god of gods,
and having performed three prāṇāyāmas, together with the garbha, approved by all,
preceded by sprinkling around, and having anointed that fuel,
he should offer in the middle of the fire when it is blazing, O great sage.
Having also placed the two āghāras, and with ghee alone, O <s>Ṣaṇmukha</s>,
he should offer the two portions of ghee according to rule, with ghee.

children.text: cakṣuṣī cājyabhāgau tu cāgnaye ca tathottare
children.translated_text: The two portions of ghee are the eyes; one is for <s>Agni</s>, and likewise the northern one,
and on one's own right side indeed, saying 'to <s>Soma</s>,' O best of the twice-born.
For the west-facing deity, the <s>Śivāgni</s>, O son of <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: akṣi vai dakṣiṇaṃ caiva cottaraṃ cottaraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: the right eye indeed is the northern one, and the northern one is likewise

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ tu mahābhāga bhavatyeva na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: the right one, O greatly fortunate one; this is certainly so, without doubt.
There, ten oblations with ghee are to be made with the root mantra alone.

children.text: caruṇā ca yathāvaddhi samidbhiśca tathā smṛtam
children.translated_text: And with caru as prescribed, and likewise with fuel-sticks, it is remembered.
Then he should give the full oblation with the root mantra, O well-vowed one.
For all the deities of the enclosures, five and five offerings are to be made as before,
in the order beginning with <s>Īśāna</s> and in the order of the śakti-bījas.
Expiation is remembered as before with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, ending with one's chosen deity.
The beautiful fire-rite has been taught by me as threefold.
Thus, as occasion allows, one should perform it every day, O great sage.
At the end of life he obtains heaven, and he obtains the kindling of the fire.

children.text: narakaṃ caiva nāpnoti yasya kasyāpi karmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: And he does not reach hell on account of any action whatsoever.
The practitioner who desires liberation should perform a nonviolent homa.
He should contemplate the fire situated in the heart and should offer by the sacrifice of meditation.
He should contemplate <s>Śiva</s>, dwelling in the bodies of all beings, the lord of the whole universe.
Having known him, he should offer with devotion constantly, by means of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control).
But the giver of an external homa becomes a frog in a stone.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter in the latter part of the venerable <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Or else a Brahmin who is a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>, intent on meditation on <s>Śiva</s>,
should properly worship the god <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Having taken ash produced from the agnihotra fire with the mantra beginning "agnir",
he should smear all his limbs, from the soles of the feet to the head.
Wearing the sacred thread and facing north, he should sip water with the brahma-tīrtha.

children.text: athauṃ namaḥ śivāyeti tanuṃ kṛtvātmanaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, with "oṃ namaḥ śivāya", he should again make his own body ritually fit.

children.text: devaṃ ca tena mantreṇa pūjayetpraṇavena ca
children.translated_text: And with that mantra and with the praṇava he should worship the deity.
The worship of <s>Aghoreśa</s>, the trident-bearing one, is superior to all.
All worship and the fire-rite are common, O well-vowed one;
the distinction lies in the mantra of that lord and in meditation on <s>Aghora</s>.
The mantra:

children.text: aghorebhyo 'tha ghorebhyo ghoraghoratarebhyaḥ śarvebhyaḥ sarvaśarvebhyo namaste astu rudrarūpebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to the non-terrible ones, then to the terrible ones, to those more terrible than the terrible; to all the <s>Śarvas</s>, to all destroyers, let there be homage to the forms of <s>Rudra</s>.
Homage to the non-terrible ones, to the one whose heart is pacified.
Then svāhā to the terrible ones, to the Brahma-head of the all-self.
Vaṣaṭ to those more terrible than the terrible, to the crest that is garlanded with flames.
Huṃ to all, to all the <s>Śarvas</s>, to the tawny armor.
Vaṣaṭ to "let there be homage to the forms of <s>Rudra</s>", to the three eyes.
Huṃ phaṭ to the thousand-eyed, hard-to-pierce <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon.
Having bathed, sipped water, made the body ritually fit, sprinkled thoroughly, and performed aghamarṣaṇa,
he should perform tarpaṇa according to rule, offer arghya to the sun, and worship the sun.
In the worship of <s>Aghora</s> this is the same, distinguished only by the mantra.
Likewise he should perform the purification of the path and the worship at the doorway of the lord of the site.
Having done this and first purified his hand, he should sit on an auspicious seat.
Placing the burnt syllable in the lotus at the tip of the nose with the kṣubhikā fire,

children.text: vāyunā prerya tadbhasma viśodhya ca śubhāṃbhasā
children.translated_text: and impelling that ash by the wind, he should purify it with auspicious water.
In the power that consists of nectar, he should imagine the brahma-kalā there.
Having made <s>Aghora</s> fivefold and again furnished with the five limbs,
he should in this way install knowledge and action according to the prescribed rule.
The nyāsa, together with the three eyes, is to be meditated on in the heart, on the excellent seat.
He should remember the lord at the navel as situated in fire, and at the midpoint between the brows as shining like a lamp.
He should meditate on him as joined with Śānti, Bīja, Aṅkura, Ananta, Dharma, and the rest,
endowed with moon, sun, and fire, and furnished with the three forms.
He is accompanied by <s>Vāma</s> and the others and presided over by <s>Manonmanī</s>.
On the seat of <s>Śiva</s>, abiding in the form of the self, he has an imperishable form.
He is <s>Śiva</s>, whose body consists of thirty-eight kalās and who is accompanied by the three tattvas.
He is the eighteen-armed god, wearing an elephant hide as his upper garment,
<s>Aghora</s>, the supreme lord, wearing a lion skin as his garment.
In the form of the thirty-two syllables, he is surrounded by the thirty-two powers.
He is adorned with all ornaments and is saluted by all the gods.
He is ornamented with a garland of skulls and decorated with all scorpions.
His face is like the full moon; he is gentle and has the splendor of ten million moons.
He bears a crescent moon, is accompanied by Śakti, and has a blue form.

children.text: haste khaḍgaṃ kheṭakaṃ pāśam eke ratnaiścitraṃ cāṅkuśaṃ nāgakakṣām
children.translated_text: In his hands are a sword, a shield, a noose, a variegated jewel-adorned goad, and a serpent-girdle;

children.text: śarāsanaṃ pāśupataṃ tathāstraṃ daṇḍaṃ ca khaṭvāṅgamathāpare ca ||
children.translated_text: a bow, the <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon and missile, a staff, and in other hands a khaṭvāṅga;

children.text: tantrīṃ ca ghaṇṭāṃ vipulaṃ ca śūlaṃ tathāpare ḍāmarukaṃ ca divyam
children.translated_text: a lute and a bell, a great trident, and in other hands a divine ḍamaru,

children.text: vajraṃ gadāṃ ṭaṅkamekaṃ ca dīptaṃ samudgaraṃ hastamathāsya śaṃbhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: a vajra, a mace, a single blazing axe, and a hammer in the hands of this <s>Śambhu</s>.
He has hands granting boons and fearlessness; he is the excellent supreme lord.
One should visualize and worship him, and should also cause homa to be performed in the fire.
The whole homa is as before, and the distinction in mantra has been stated.
There are worship with the eight flowers and the like, scents and the like, praise, and offering.
The internal bali of the fire-pit is to be done according to the Vāhneya procedure.
Having made the maṇḍala according to rule, with these mantras in order,

children.text: rudrebhyo mātṛgaṇebhyo yakṣebhyo 'surebhyo grahebhyo rākṣasebhyo nāgebhyo nakṣatrebhyo viśvagaṇebhyaḥ kṣetrapālebhyaḥ atha vāyuvaruṇadigbhāge kṣetrapālabaliṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: one should cast the bali for the field-guardian in the quarter of <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, or for the <s>Rudras</s>, the Mothers, Yakṣas, Asuras, planets, Rākṣasas, Nāgas, constellations, all hosts, and field-guardians.

children.text: arghyaṃ gandhaṃ ca puṣpaṃ ca dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ ca suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: O well-vowed ones, arghya, scent, flowers, incense, and a lamp,
as well as food-offering, mouth-perfume, and the rest, should be presented according to rule.
Having thus made the request and then dismissed them, there is worship with the eight flowers.
All this is common in worship, O foremost sages.
Thus the worship of <s>Aghora</s> and the rest has been briefly taught, O well-vowed one.

children.text: aghorārcāvidhānaṃ ca liṅge vā sthaṇḍile 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: This is the procedure for worship of <s>Aghora</s>, whether in a <s>liṅga</s> or on an altar.
Worship in a <s>liṅga</s> is unsurpassed, ten million times greater than worship on an altar.
A Brahmin devoted to worship of the <s>liṅga</s>, even by sins arising from great transgressions,
is not stained, just as a lotus leaf is not stained by water.
The sight of the <s>liṅga</s> is meritorious; better than sight is touching it.
There is nothing greater than worship, O son of <s>Brahmā</s>; there is no doubt.
Thus the excellent worship of <s>Aghora</s> has been briefly taught.
Even in a hundred crores of years it cannot be described in detail.
Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter in the latter part of the blessed <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
We have heard the greatness of <s>Nandin</s> and the fruit of worshiping the <s>liṅga</s> (emblem of Śiva),
all of it in agreement with the <s>śrutis</s> (revealed texts), O well-vowed <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>.
The <s>jayābhiṣeka</s> (victory consecration) was formerly taught by <s>Īśa</s> to <s>Manu</s>,
by the trident-bearing lord on the peak of <s>Meru</s>, for the welfare of kṣatriyas.
Tell us that, and also the auspicious sixteenfold <s>mahādāna</s> (great gift),
O <s>Sūta</s>, best of the wise, for you are able to speak of it.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: jīvacchrāddhaṃ purā kṛtvā manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvaḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, after performing the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> (funeral rite performed while alive), the lord <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s>
went to <s>Meru</s> and praised the lord of the gods, <s>Nīlalohita</s>.

children.text: tapasā ca vinītāya prahṛṣṭaḥ pradadau bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Pleased with him, who was humble through austerity, <s>Bhava</s>, the ruling lord,
granted a divine vision; through that he saw the imperishable one.
Having bowed and worshiped him according to rule, he stood with joined palms,

children.text: harṣagadgadayā vācā provāca ca nanāma ca ||
children.translated_text: and with a voice choked by joy he spoke and bowed again.
'God of gods, lord of the world, homage to you, O lord of beings.
O <s>Mahādeva</s>, by your favor the <s>jīvacchrāddha</s> has been completed.

children.text: pūjitaś ca tato devo dṛṣṭaś caiva mayādhunā
children.translated_text: Then the god has been worshiped, and now he has indeed been seen by me.
O lord of gods, you formerly taught <s>Śakra</s> the <s>jayābhiṣeka</s>,
which grants <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desire, wealth, and liberation. Deign to tell it to me, O lord.'
<s>Sūta</s> said:
To him the god <s>Mahādeva</s>, the blessed <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
the supreme lord, explained the entire <s>jayābhiṣeka</s>.
The blessed Lord said:
I shall teach the <s>jayābhiṣeka</s>, desiring the welfare of kings,
for victory over untimely death and for victory over all enemies.
When the time for battle has arrived, after performing this consecration,
and after consecrating his own lord, one should go to fight on the battlefield.

children.text: vidhinā maṇḍapaṃ kṛtvā prapāṃ vā kūṭameva vā ||
children.translated_text: According to rule, having made a <s>maṇḍapa</s> (ritual pavilion), or a water pavilion, or simply a covered structure,
a brāhmaṇa learned in the Veda should establish the fire in nine divisions.
Then, for the whole consecration, he should have the measuring cords laid down.

children.text: prāgādyaṃ varṇasūtraṃ ca dakṣiṇādyaṃ tathā punaḥ
children.translated_text: There should be a colored cord beginning from the east, and again one beginning from the south.

children.text: sahasrāṇāṃ dvayaṃ tatra śatānāṃ ca catuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: There, two thousand and four hundred

children.text: śeṣameva śubhaṃ koṣṭhaṃ teṣu koṣṭhaṃ tu saṃharet
children.translated_text: are the remaining auspicious compartments; among those compartments he should collect them.
On the outer path he should take away one pada on every side.
Having taken the subsidiary cords, each separately and according to rule,

children.text: prāgādyaṃ varṇasūtraṃ ca dakṣiṇādyaṃ tathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there should be the colored cord beginning from the east, and again one beginning from the south.

children.text: prāgādyaṃ dakṣiṇādyaṃ ca ṣaṭtriṃśat saṃharet kramāt
children.translated_text: Beginning from the east and beginning from the south, he should remove thirty-six in order.
There are seven rows beginning from the east, and likewise beginning from the south.
Therefore forty-nine rows are proclaimed.
In the middle he should remove nine rows with scented water mixed with cow dung,
and there draw a beautiful lotus measuring one hasta.
It should be white, round, with eight petals, and furnished with pericarp and filaments.
By the measure of eight aṅgulas, the pericarp should be like gold.
The place of the filaments is said to measure four aṅgulas.

children.text: dharmo jñānaṃ ca vairāgyamaiśvaryaṃ ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, and sovereignty, in that order,
should be placed in the corners beginning with the southeast, with the <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable Oṃ).

children.text: avyaktādīni vai dikṣu gātrākāreṇa vai nyaset
children.translated_text: In the directions, beginning with the unmanifest, he should place them in the form of limbs.

children.text: avyaktaṃ niyataḥ kālaḥ kālī ceti catuṣṭayam ||
children.translated_text: The four are the unmanifest, the fixed order, time, and <s>Kālī</s>.
White, red, golden-hued, and black are the colors of <s>dharma</s> and the others in order.
O well-vowed ones, the body is in the form of a haṃsa and has the radiance of gold.
In the middle of the support-power is the lotus, the cause of creation.
In the middle of the <s>kalā</s> (subtle part) is a mere bindu; beyond that is the form of <s>nāda</s> (resonance).
Above the <s>nāda</s> one should meditate on <s>Śiva</s>, called <s>Oṃkāra</s>, the teacher of the world.

children.text: manonmanīṃ ca padmābhaṃ mahādevaṃ ca bhāvayet ||
children.translated_text: One should also contemplate <s>Manonmanī</s>, lotus-like, and <s>Mahādeva</s>.
The powers beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>, in due order, are to be placed on the filaments beginning from the east:

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā tathā raudrī kālī vikaraṇī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, then <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and <s>Vikaraṇī</s>,

children.text: balā pramathinī devī damanī ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: <s>Balā</s>, the goddess <s>Pramathinī</s>, and <s>Damanī</s>, in that order.
Together with <s>Vāmadeva</s> and the others, he should install them with the <s>praṇava</s> alone.
'Homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>; homage to <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, to the trident-bearer,
to <s>Rudra</s>, whose form is time, and to the transformer of the <s>kalās</s>.

children.text: balāya ca tathā sarvabhūtasya damanāya ca ||
children.translated_text: And homage to <s>Balā</s>, and likewise to the subduer of every being.
Homage to the god <s>Manonmana</s>; homage, homage to <s>Manonmanī</s>.'
With these mantras he should worship the complete circle according to rule.
The first enclosure has been stated; now hear the second enclosure.
In the second enclosure there are precisely sixteen powers.
In the third enclosure there are twenty-four in sequence.
In the middle is the path of the piśācas, and all around is the navel path.
With these mantras, according to rule, those belonging to the piśācas are proclaimed.
There are one thousand and eight padas, furnished with eight spokes.

children.text: teṣu teṣu pṛthaktvena padeṣu kamalaṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: In those respective padas, in order, he should fashion a lotus,
with śāli rice, wild rice, wheat, barley, and the like,
or with husked rice, sesame, or white mustard seed,
or he may fashion it with these according to the season and prescription.
In each of them he should draw an eight-petaled lotus, furnished with pericarp and filaments.
For each lotus an āḍhaka of śāli rice is prescribed.
There should be half of that amount of husked rice, and half of that again for barley and the others.
A droṇa is prescribed for the principal kumbha; half of that is remembered for the husked rice.
In the middle there should be an āḍhaka of sesame, and half of that of barley.
Then, having sprinkled the lotus thoroughly with water and the <s>praṇava</s>,
Into all these, according to rule, one should place the <s>praṇava</s> in sequence.
Having thus completed it and sprinkled that excellent thousand-word recitation,

children.text: kalaśānāṃ sahasrāṇi haimāni ca śubhāni ca
children.translated_text: one should have thousands of jars made, golden and auspicious,
endowed with the stated characteristics, or else made of silver.
Alternatively they may be made of copper, as proper, with arghya-water empowered by the <s>praṇava</s>.
The belly is declared to be twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.
Its navel is prescribed as half of that when rounded.
The neck should be two <s>aṅgulas</s> high and four <s>aṅgulas</s> wide.

children.text: oṣṭhaṃ ca dvyaṅgulotsedhaṃ nirgamaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ smṛtam
children.translated_text: The lip should be two <s>aṅgulas</s> high, and the projection is remembered as two <s>aṅgulas</s>.
In the <s>Śivakumbha</s>, each of these respective parts is proclaimed divine and twice as large.
One should wrap it properly with a thread, leaving an interval the size of a barley-corn.
Having covered it and then sprinkled it according to rule upon <s>kuśa</s> grass,
one should fill it, as before, with scented water by means of the <s>praṇava</s> alone.
According to the rite, one should set down the <s>vardhanī</s> together with the splendid <s>Śivakumbha</s>.

children.text: madhyapadmasya madhye tu sakūrcaṃ sākṣataṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: In the middle of the central lotus, with a brush and unbroken rice, in order,
having wrapped it in a pair of cloths and covered it with a lotus,
with a golden, many-jewelled lotus, one should treat the thousand jars separately.

children.text: śivakuṃbhe śivaṃ sthāpya gāyatryā praṇaveṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: Having installed <s>Śiva</s> in the <s>Śivakumbha</s> with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the <s>praṇava</s>,
'We know the <s>Puruṣa</s>; we meditate upon <s>Mahādeva</s>.'
'May that <s>Rudra</s> impel us.'
By this mantra the constant presence of <s>Rudra</s> is remembered.
In the <s>vardhanī</s>, with the Goddess-<s>Gāyatrī</s>, one should install and worship the Goddess.
'We know <s>Gaṇāmbikā</s>; we meditate upon the great ascetic.'
'May that <s>Gaurī</s> impel us.'
In the first enclosure, the goddesses beginning with <s>Vāmā</s> are taught.
The first enclosure has been stated; listen to the second enclosure.
Here there are sixteen <s>śaktis</s> at the limits beginning from the east, O well-vowed one.

children.text: aindravyūhasya madhye tu subhadrāṃ sthāpya pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: In the middle of the <s>Aindra</s> array one should install and worship <s>Subhadrā</s>.
In the <s>Āgneya</s> circle one should place <s>Bhadrā</s>, and in the southern one <s>Kanakāṇḍajā</s>.

children.text: aṃbikāṃ nairṛte vyūhe madhyakuṃbhe tu pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: In the southwest array one should worship <s>Ambikā</s>, and also in the central jar.
In the western quarter one should worship <s>Śrīdevī</s>, and in the region of <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Vāgīśā</s>.

children.text: gomukhīṃ saumyabhāge tu madhyakuṃbhe tu pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: In the northern region one should worship <s>Gomukhī</s>, and also in the central jar.
In the middle of the <s>Rudra</s> array one should worship <s>Bhadrakarṇā</s>.
Between the <s>Aindra</s> and <s>Agni</s> directions one should worship the auspicious <s>Aṇimā</s>.
Between the southern and fiery directions one should place <s>Laghimā</s> on the lotus.
Between the <s>Rākṣasa</s> and <s>Antaka</s> directions one should worship <s>Mahimā</s> in the middle.
Between <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Asura</s> one should worship <s>Prāpti</s> in the middle.
Between <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Anila</s> one should place <s>Prākāmya</s> on the lotus.
Between <s>Vitteśa</s> and <s>Anila</s> one should install and worship <s>Īśitva</s>.
Between <s>Vitteśa</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> one should install and worship <s>Vaśitva</s>.
Between <s>Aindra</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> one should worship <s>Kāmāvasāyaka</s>.
The second enclosure has been stated; listen to the third enclosure.
The <s>śaktis</s> are twenty-four in the offering jars,
and one should worship them in the middle of the array as before, following the rule.
<s>Dīkṣā</s> and <s>Dīkṣāyikā</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s> and <s>Caṇḍāṃśunāyikā</s>,

children.text: sumatiṃ sumatyāyīṃ ca gopāṃ gopāyikāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumati</s> and <s>Sumatyāyī</s>, and likewise <s>Gopā</s> and <s>Gopāyikā</s>,

children.text: atha nandaṃ ca nandāyīṃ pitāmahamataḥ param
children.translated_text: then <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Nandāyī</s>, and after that <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
and <s>Pitāmahāyī</s>: beginning from the east, one should install and worship them according to rule.
Having thus worshipped according to rule the auspicious third enclosure,
one should approach the <s>Saubhadra</s> array; in the first enclosure, in order,
one should install the group of eight <s>śaktis</s>, beginning from the east, according to rule.
And in the second enclosure, beginning from the east, listen to the <s>śaktis</s>.

children.text: ṣoḍaśaiva tu abhyarcya padmamudrāṃ tu darśayet
children.translated_text: After worshipping the sixteen, one should show the lotus <s>mudrā</s>.
<s>Bindukā</s>, <s>Bindugarbhā</s>, <s>Nādinī</s>, and <s>Nādagarbhajā</s>,

children.text: śaktikā śaktigarbhā ca parā caiva parāparā
children.translated_text: <s>Śaktikā</s>, <s>Śaktigarbhā</s>, <s>Parā</s>, and <s>Parāparā</s>:
these eight <s>śaktis</s> have been taught in the first enclosure.
<s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Caṇḍamukhī</s>, <s>Caṇḍavegā</s>, and <s>Manojavā</s>,
<s>Caṇḍākṣī</s>, <s>Caṇḍanirghoṣā</s>, <s>Bhṛkuṭī</s>, and <s>Caṇḍanāyikā</s>,
<s>Manotsedhā</s>, <s>Manodhyakṣā</s>, <s>Mānasī</s>, and <s>Mānanāyikā</s>,
<s>Manoharī</s>, <s>Manohlādī</s>, <s>Manaḥprīti</s>, and <s>Maheśvarī</s>:
these sixteen are taught in the second enclosure.

children.text: saubhadraḥ kathito vyūho bhadraṃ vyūhaṃ śṛṇuṣva me ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Saubhadra</s> array has been described; listen to me about the <s>Bhadra</s> array.

children.text: aindrī hautāśanī yāmyā nairṛtī vāruṇī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Aindrī</s>, <s>Hautāśanī</s>, <s>Yāmyā</s>, <s>Nairṛtī</s>, and likewise <s>Vāruṇī</s>,
<s>Vāyavyā</s>, <s>Kauberī</s>, and <s>Aiśānī</s> are the eight <s>śaktis</s>.
The first enclosure has been stated; listen to the second.

children.text: hariṇī ca suvarṇā ca kāñcanī hāṭakī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hariṇī</s>, <s>Suvarṇā</s>, <s>Kāñcanī</s>, and <s>Hāṭakī</s>,
<s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, <s>Subhagā</s>, and <s>Jambunāyikā</s>,

children.text: vāgbhavā vākpathā vāṇī bhīmā citrarathā sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāgbhavā</s>, <s>Vākpathā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s>, <s>Bhīmā</s>, <s>Citrarathā</s>, and <s>Sudhī</s>,
<s>Vedamātā</s> and <s>Hiraṇyākṣī</s> are remembered in the second enclosure.

children.text: bhadrākhyaḥ kathito vyūhaḥ kanakākhyaṃ śṛṇuṣva me ||
