children.translated_text: The array called <s>Bhadra</s> has been described; listen to the one called <s>Kanaka</s>.

children.text: vajraṃ śaktiṃ ca daṇḍaṃ ca khaḍgaṃ pāśaṃ dhvajaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt, spear, staff, sword, noose, and banner,
mace and trident are remembered in order in the first enclosure.

children.text: yuddhā prabuddhā caṇḍā ca muṇḍā caiva kapālinī
children.translated_text: <s>Yuddhā</s>, <s>Prabuddhā</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Muṇḍā</s>, and <s>Kapālinī</s>,
<s>Mṛtyuhantrī</s>, <s>Virūpākṣī</s>, <s>Kapardā</s>, and <s>Kamalāsanā</s>,
<s>Daṃṣṭriṇī</s> and <s>Raṅgiṇī</s>, <s>Lambākṣī</s> and <s>Kaṅkabhūṣaṇī</s>,
<s>Sambhāvā</s> and <s>Bhāvinī</s>: these sixteen are taught.
The first array has been explained; now listen to the one called <s>Ambikā</s>.

children.text: khecarī cātmanā sā ca bhavānī vahnirūpiṇī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khecarī</s>, and she as <s>Ātmanā</s>, <s>Bhavānī</s>, and <s>Vahnirūpiṇī</s>...
and <s>Vahninī</s>, <s>Vahninābhā</s>, and <s>Mahimāmṛtalālasā</s>;
in the first enclosure these eight powers are accepted by all.

children.text: kṣamā ca śikharā devī ṛturatnā śilā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣamā</s>, the goddess <s>Śikharā</s>, <s>Ṛturatnā</s>, and likewise <s>Śilā</s>,

children.text: chāyā bhūtapatī dhanyā indramātā ca vaiṣṇavī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Chāyā</s>, <s>Bhūtapatī</s>, <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Indramātā</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>;
<s>Tṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Rāgavatī</s>, <s>Mohā</s>, <s>Kāmakopā</s>, and <s>Mahotkaṭā</s>,

children.text: indrā ca badhirā devī ṣoḍaśaitāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with <s>Indrā</s> and the goddess <s>Badhirā</s>: these sixteen are proclaimed.
The <s>Ambikā-vyūha</s> has been described; hear the <s>Śrī-vyūha</s>, O well-vowed one.
<s>Sparśā</s>, <s>Sparśavatī</s>, <s>Gandhā</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, and <s>Samānikā</s>,
with <s>Udāna</s> and the one named <s>Vyāna</s>, are remembered in the first enclosure.
<s>Tamohatā</s>, <s>Prabhāmoghā</s>, <s>Tejinī</s>, and likewise <s>Dahanī</s>,
<s>Bhīmāsyā</s>, <s>Jālinī</s>, <s>Uṣā</s>, <s>Śoṣiṇī</s>, and <s>Rudranāyikā</s>,
<s>Vīrabhadrā</s>, <s>Gaṇādhyakṣā</s>, <s>Candrahāsā</s>, and <s>Gahvarā</s>,
together with <s>Gaṇamātā</s> and <s>Ambikā</s>: these powers are accepted by all.
They are taught, exactly sixteen in order, in the second enclosure.

children.text: śrīvyūhaḥ kathito bhadraṃ vāgīśaṃ śṛṇu suvrata
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrī-vyūha</s> has been described. May there be well-being. Hear <s>Vāgīśa</s>, O well-vowed one.

children.text: dhārā vāridharā caiva vahnikī nāśakī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhārā</s>, <s>Vāridharā</s>, <s>Vahnikī</s>, and likewise <s>Nāśakī</s>,
<s>Martyātītā</s>, <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, <s>Vajriṇī</s>, and <s>Kāmadhenukā</s>;
in this way, in the first enclosure too, eight powers are proclaimed.

children.text: payoṣṇī vāruṇī śāntā jayantī ca varapradā
children.translated_text: <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, <s>Vāruṇī</s>, <s>Śāntā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, and <s>Varapradā</s>,
<s>Plāvinī</s>, <s>Jalamātā</s>, <s>Payomātā</s>, and <s>Mahāmbikā</s>,
<s>Raktā</s>, <s>Karālī</s>, <s>Caṇḍākṣī</s>, <s>Mahocchuṣmā</s>, and <s>Payasvinī</s>,

children.text: māyā vidyeśvarī kālī kālikā ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vidyeśvarī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, and <s>Kālikā</s>, in that order;
sixteen powers, accepted by all, have thus been named.

children.text: vyūho vāgīśvaraḥ prokto gomukho vyūha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Vāgīśvara-vyūha</s> has been stated; the <s>Gomukha-vyūha</s> is now described.

children.text: śaṅkhinī hālinī caiva laṅkāvarṇā ca kalkinī
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkhinī</s>, <s>Hālinī</s>, <s>Laṅkāvarṇā</s>, and <s>Kalkinī</s>,

children.text: yakṣiṇī mālinī caiva vamanī ca rasātmanī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yakṣiṇī</s>, <s>Mālinī</s>, <s>Vamanī</s>, and <s>Rasātmanī</s>;
in the first enclosure, indeed, these eight powers are proclaimed.

children.text: caṇḍā ghaṇṭā mahānādā sumukhī durmukhī balā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Ghaṇṭā</s>, <s>Mahānādā</s>, <s>Sumukhī</s>, <s>Durmukhī</s>, and <s>Balā</s>,

children.text: revatī prathamā ghorā sainyā līnā mahābalā
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Prathamā</s>, <s>Ghorā</s>, <s>Sainyā</s>, <s>Līnā</s>, and <s>Mahābalā</s>,

children.text: jayā ca vijayā caiva aparā cāparājitā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jayā</s> and <s>Vijayā</s>, and also <s>Aparā</s> and <s>Aparājitā</s>;
in the second enclosure there are precisely sixteen powers.
The <s>Gomukhī-vyūha</s> has been described; hear from me the <s>Bhadrakarṇī</s>.
<s>Mahājayā</s>, <s>Virūpākṣī</s>, <s>Śuklābhā</s>, and <s>Kāśamātṛkā</s>,
<s>Saṃhārī</s>, <s>Jātahārī</s>, <s>Daṃṣṭrālī</s>, and <s>Śuṣkarevatī</s>;
in the first enclosure eight powers are proclaimed.
<s>Pipīlikā</s>, <s>Puṇyahārī</s>, <s>Aśanī</s>, and <s>Sarvahāriṇī</s>,

children.text: bhadrahā viśvahārī ca himā yogeśvarī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrahā</s>, <s>Viśvahārī</s>, <s>Himā</s>, and likewise <s>Yogeśvarī</s>,

children.text: chidrā bhānumatī chidrā saiṃhikī surabhī samā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Chidrā</s>, <s>Bhānumatī</s>, another <s>Chidrā</s>, <s>Saiṃhikī</s>, <s>Surabhī</s>, and <s>Samā</s>,

children.text: sarvabhavyā ca vegākhyā śaktayaḥ ṣoḍaśaiva tu
children.translated_text: with <s>Sarvabhavyā</s> and the one named <s>Vegā</s>: these powers are precisely sixteen.
The eight great <s>vyūhas</s> have been stated; hear the eight subsidiary <s>vyūhas</s>.
Encircling the <s>Aṇimā-vyūha</s>, in the first enclosure, in order, are:

children.text: aindrā tu citrabhānuśca vāruṇī daṇḍireva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aindrā</s>, <s>Citrabhānu</s>, <s>Vāruṇī</s>, and <s>Daṇḍin</s>,
then <s>Prāṇarūpin</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Svātmaśakti</s>, and <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Keśava</s>, the blessed <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Candramas</s>, and likewise <s>Bhāskara</s>,

children.text: mahātmā ca tathā hyātmā hyantarātmā maheśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mahātman</s>, and likewise <s>Ātman</s>, <s>Antarātman</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Paramātman</s>, <s>Aṇu</s>, <s>Jīva</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and <s>Paśu</s>,
<s>Bhoktṛ</s>, <s>Bhūtapati</s>, and <s>Bhīma</s> are remembered in the second enclosure.
The <s>Aṇimā-vyūha</s> has been described; I shall tell you the one called <s>Laghimā</s>.
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, <s>Anta</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Trimūrti</s>, and likewise <s>Śaśaka</s>,
<s>Amareśa</s>, <s>Sthitīśa</s>, and <s>Dārata</s> as the eighth;
the first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Daṇḍeśa</s>, <s>Bhauktīśa</s>, and <s>Surapuṅgava</s>,
<s>Sadyojāta</s>, <s>Anugraheśa</s>, <s>Krūrasena</s>, and <s>Sureśvara</s>,

children.text: krodhīśaśca tathā caṇḍaḥ pracaṇḍaḥ śiva eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Krodhīśa</s>, and likewise <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
<s>Ekarudra</s>, then <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Ekanetra</s>, and <s>Caturmukha</s>;
in the second enclosure the Rudras are proclaimed as precisely sixteen.
The <s>Laghimā-vyūha</s> has been described; hear <s>Mahimā</s>, O well-vowed one.
<s>Ajeśa</s>, <s>Kṣemarudra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Aṃśa</s>, and likewise <s>Lāṅgalī</s>,

children.text: daṇḍāruś cārdhanārī ca ekāntaścānta eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Daṇḍāru</s>, <s>Ardhanārī</s>, <s>Ekānta</s>, and <s>Anta</s>,

children.text: pālī bhujaṅganāmā ca pinākī khaḍgir eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Pālī</s>, the one named <s>Bhujaṅga</s>, <s>Pinākī</s>, and <s>Khaḍgin</s>,

children.text: kāma īśastathā śveto bhṛguḥ ṣoḍaśa vai smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Bhṛgu</s>: these sixteen are remembered.
The <s>Mahimā-vyūha</s> has been described; hear from me the <s>Prāpti-vyūha</s>.

children.text: saṃvarto lakulīśaśca vāḍavo hastir eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Lakulīśa</s>, <s>Vāḍava</s>, and <s>Hasti</s>,
<s>Caṇḍayakṣa</s>, <s>Gaṇapati</s>, <s>Mahātman</s>, and <s>Bhṛguja</s> as the eighth;
the first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.

children.text: trivikramo mahājihva ṛkṣaḥ śrībhadra eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Trivikrama</s>, <s>Mahājihva</s>, <s>Ṛkṣa</s>, and <s>Śrībhadra</s>,
<s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Dadhīca</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, and <s>Parāvara</s>,
<s>Mahādaṃṣṭra</s>, <s>Karāla</s>, <s>Sūcaka</s>, and <s>Suvardhana</s>,
<s>Mahādhvāṅkṣa</s>, <s>Mahānanda</s>, <s>Daṇḍin</s>, and <s>Gopālaka</s>;
The <s>Prāpti-vyūha</s> has been named; hear <s>Prākāmya</s>, O well-vowed one.
<s>Puṣpadanta</s>, <s>Mahānāga</s>, and <s>Vipulānandakāraka</s>,

children.text: śuklo viśālaḥ kamalo bilvaścāruṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Śukla</s>, <s>Viśāla</s>, <s>Kamala</s>, <s>Bilva</s>, and <s>Aruṇa</s>;
the first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Ratipriya</s>, <s>Sureśāna</s>, <s>Citrāṅga</s>, and <s>Sudurjaya</s>,
<s>Vināyaka</s>, <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>, <s>Mahāmoha</s>, and <s>Jaṅgala</s>,
<s>Vatsaputra</s>, <s>Mahāputra</s>, and likewise <s>Grāmadeśādhipa</s>,
the god <s>Sarvāvasthādhipa</s>, <s>Meghanāda</s>, and <s>Pracaṇḍaka</s>,
and <s>Kāladūta</s> are stated; this is remembered as the second enclosure.

children.text: prākāmyaḥ kathito vyūha aiśvaryaṃ kathayāmi te ||
children.translated_text: The array of <s>Prākāmya</s> has been described; I shall tell you <s>Aiśvarya</s>.
They are <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Carcikā</s>, likewise <s>Yogeśā</s> and <s>Haradāyikā</s>,
<s>Bhāsurā</s>, <s>Suramātā</s>, and <s>Sundarī</s>; <s>Mātṛkā</s> is the eighth.
They are declared in the first enclosure; hear the second enclosure.
There are <s>Gaṇādhipa</s>, <s>Mantrajña</s>, <s>Varadeva</s>, and <s>Ṣaḍānana</s>,

children.text: vidagdhaśca vicitraśca amogho mogha eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vidagdha</s>, <s>Vicitra</s>, <s>Amogha</s>, and <s>Mogha</s> too,
<s>Aśvīrudra</s>, <s>Someśa</s>, and also <s>Uttamodumbara</s>,
<s>Nārasiṃha</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, and likewise the lord <s>Indraguha</s>,
and <s>Apāṃpati</s>; by rule this is remembered as the second enclosure.
The array of <s>Aiśvarya</s> has been described; <s>Vaśitva</s> is now stated.
There are <s>Gagana</s>, <s>Bhavana</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, and likewise <s>Ajaya</s>,
and <s>Mahājaya</s>, <s>Gāra</s>, <s>Vyaṅgāra</s>, and the greatly renowned <s>Mahāyaśas</s>.
They are declared in the first enclosure; hear those in the second enclosure.
There are <s>Sundara</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍeśa</s>, <s>Mahāvarṇa</s>, and <s>Mahāsura</s>,
<s>Mahāroman</s>, <s>Mahāgarbha</s>, <s>Prathama</s>, and likewise <s>Kanaka</s>,
<s>Kharaja</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s>, <s>Meghanāda</s>, and then <s>Garjaka</s>,
<s>Gaja</s>, <s>Cchedaka</s>, <s>Bāhu</s>, <s>Triśikha</s>, and <s>Māri</s> as well.
The array of <s>Vaśitva</s> has been described; hear <s>Kāmāvasāyika</s>.
There are <s>Vināda</s>, <s>Vikaṭa</s>, <s>Vasanta</s>, and <s>Abhaya</s>,
<s>Vidyunmahābala</s>, <s>Kamala</s>, and likewise <s>Damana</s>.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
There are <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Atibala</s>, <s>Sarpa</s>, <s>Mahākāya</s>, and <s>Mahāhanu</s>,
<s>Sabala</s>, <s>Bhasmāṅgī</s>, <s>Durjaya</s>, and <s>Duratikrama</s>,

children.text: vetālo rauravaścaiva durdharo bhoga eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vetāla</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Durdhara</s>, and <s>Bhoga</s> too,
<s>Vajra</s>, <s>Kālāgnirudra</s>, <s>Sadyonāda</s>, and <s>Mahāguha</s>.
The second enclosure has been stated, and so has the <s>Avāsāyika</s> array.
The sixteenfold array has been described; hear the second enclosure.
In the second enclosure, and in the <s>Dakṣa</s> array, there are śaktis (powers);

children.text: prathamāvaraṇe cāṣṭau bāhye ṣoḍaśa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: there are eight in the first enclosure and sixteen outside.
There are <s>Manoharā</s>, <s>Mahānādā</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, and likewise <s>Citrarathā</s>,
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Citrāṅgī</s>, <s>Citrarekhā</s>, and <s>Vicitrikā</s>.
They are declared in the first enclosure; hear the second enclosure.

children.text: citrā vicitrarūpā ca śubhadā kāmadā subhā ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Vicitrarūpā</s>, <s>Śubhadā</s>, <s>Kāmadā</s>, and <s>Śubhā</s>,

children.text: krūrā ca piṅgalā devī khaḍgikā laṃbikāsatī
children.translated_text: <s>Krūrā</s>, the tawny goddess <s>Piṅgalā</s>, <s>Khaḍgikā</s>, and the chaste <s>Lambikā</s>,
<s>Daṃṣṭrālī</s>, <s>Rākṣasīdhvaṃsī</s>, <s>Lolupā</s>, and <s>Lohitāmukhī</s>.
In the second enclosure the sixteen have been stated in brief.
The <s>Dakṣa</s> array has been fully declared; hear from me the <s>Dākṣa</s> array.
There are <s>Sarvāsatī</s>, <s>Viśvarūpā</s>, <s>Lampaṭā</s>, and <s>Āmiṣapriyā</s>,

children.text: dīrghadaṃṣṭrā ca vajrā ca laṃboṣṭhī prāṇahāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dīrghadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Vajrā</s>, <s>Lamboṣṭhī</s>, and <s>Prāṇahāriṇī</s>.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
There are <s>Gajakarṇā</s>, <s>Aśvakarṇā</s>, <s>Mahākālī</s>, and <s>Subhīṣaṇā</s>,
<s>Vātavegaravā</s>, <s>Ghorā</s>, and likewise <s>Ghanāghanaravā</s>,
<s>Varaghoṣā</s>, <s>Mahāvarṇā</s>, <s>Sughaṇṭā</s>, and <s>Ghaṇṭikā</s>,
<s>Ghaṇṭaśvarī</s>, <s>Mahāghorā</s>, <s>Ghorā</s>, and <s>Atighorikā</s>.
In the second enclosure the sixteen are indeed proclaimed.
The <s>Dākṣa</s> array has been declared; hear from me the <s>Caṇḍa</s> array.
There are <s>Atighaṇṭā</s>, <s>Atighorā</s>, <s>Karālā</s>, and likewise <s>Karabhā</s>,
<s>Vibhūti</s>, <s>Bhogadā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> are remembered as the eighth.
They are declared in the first enclosure; hear those in the second enclosure.
There are <s>Patriṇī</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Yogamātā</s>, and <s>Supīvarā</s>,
<s>Raktā</s>, <s>Mālāṃśukā</s>, <s>Vīrā</s>, <s>Saṃhārī</s>, and <s>Māṃsahāriṇī</s>,
<s>Phalahārī</s>, <s>Jīvahārī</s>, <s>Svecchāhārī</s>, and <s>Tuṇḍikā</s>,

children.text: revatī raṅgiṇī saṃgā dvitīye ṣoḍaśaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Raṅgiṇī</s>, and <s>Saṃgā</s>; in the second enclosure there are sixteen.
The <s>Caṇḍa</s> array has been declared; likewise the <s>Caṇḍā</s> array is stated.
There are <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Caṇḍamukhī</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Caṇḍavegā</s>, and <s>Mahāravā</s>,
<s>Bhrukuṭī</s>, <s>Caṇḍabhū</s>, and <s>Caṇḍarūpā</s> is remembered as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
There are <s>Candraghrāṇā</s>, <s>Balā</s>, <s>Balajihvā</s>, and <s>Baleśvarī</s>,
<s>Balavegā</s>, <s>Mahākāyā</s>, <s>Mahākopā</s>, and <s>Vidyutā</s>,
<s>Kaṅkālī</s>, <s>Kalaśī</s>, <s>Vidyutā</s>, and <s>Caṇḍaghoṣikā</s>,
<s>Mahāghoṣā</s>, <s>Mahārāvā</s>, <s>Caṇḍabhānā</s>, and <s>Aṅgacaṇḍikā</s>.

children.text: caṇḍāyāḥ kathito vyūho haravyūhaṃ śṛṇuṣva me
children.translated_text: The array of <s>Caṇḍā</s> has been described; hear from me the <s>Hara</s> array.
There are <s>Caṇḍākṣī</s>, the wish-granting goddess <s>Kāmadā</s>, <s>Sūkarī</s>, and <s>Kukkuṭānanā</s>,

children.text: gāndhārī dandubhī durgā saumitrā cāṣṭamī smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Dandubhī</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, and <s>Saumitrā</s> is remembered as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
There are <s>Mṛtodbhavā</s>, <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, <s>Varṇadā</s>, and <s>Jīvarakṣiṇī</s>,
<s>Hariṇī</s>, <s>Kṣīṇajīvā</s>, <s>Daṇḍavaktrā</s>, and <s>Caturbhujā</s>,
<s>Vyomacārī</s>, <s>Vyomarūpā</s>, <s>Vyomavyāpī</s>, and <s>Śubhodayā</s>,
<s>Gṛhacārī</s>, <s>Sucārī</s>, <s>Viṣāhārī</s>, and <s>Viṣārtihā</s>.
The <s>Hara</s> array has been declared; the array of <s>Harā</s> is stated.
There are <s>Jambhācyutā</s>, <s>Kaṅkārī</s>, <s>Devikā</s>, and <s>Durdharāvahā</s>,
<s>Caṇḍikā</s> and <s>Capalā</s>; these are remembered in the first enclosure.

children.text: cañjikā cāmarī caiva bhaṇḍikā ca śubhānanā ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>Cañjikā</s>, <s>Cāmarī</s>, <s>Bhaṇḍikā</s>, and <s>Śubhānanā</s>,

children.text: piṇḍikā muṇḍikā muṇḍā śākinī śāṅkarī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Piṇḍikā</s>, <s>Muṇḍikā</s>, <s>Muṇḍā</s>, <s>Śākinī</s>, and likewise <s>Śāṅkarī</s>,
<s>Kartarī</s>, <s>Bhartarī</s>, <s>Bhāginī</s>, and <s>Yajñadāyinī</s>,
<s>Yamadaṃṣṭrā</s>, <s>Mahādaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>Karālā</s>; these are the śaktis.

children.text: harāyāḥ kathito vyūhaḥ śaiṇḍavyūhaṃ śṛṇuṣva me ||
children.translated_text: The array of <s>Harā</s> has been described; hear from me the <s>Śaiṇḍa</s> array.
There are <s>Vikarālī</s>, <s>Karālī</s>, <s>Kālajaṅghā</s>, and <s>Yaśasvinī</s>,

children.text: vegā vegavatī yajñā vedāṅgā cāṣṭamī smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vegā</s>, <s>Vegavatī</s>, <s>Yajñā</s>, and <s>Vedāṅgā</s> is remembered as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.

children.text: vajrā śaṅkhātiśaṅkhā vā balā caivābalā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajrā</s>, <s>Śaṅkhā</s>, <s>Atiśaṅkhā</s>, and likewise <s>Balā</s> and <s>Abalā</s>;

children.text: añjanī mohinī māyā vikaṭāṅgī nalī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Añjanī</s>, <s>Mohinī</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Vikaṭāṅgī</s>, and <s>Nalī</s> likewise,

children.text: gaṇḍakī daḍakī ghoṇā śoṇā satyavatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṇḍakī</s>, <s>Daḍakī</s>, <s>Ghoṇā</s>, <s>Śoṇā</s>, and <s>Satyavatī</s> likewise;
and <s>Kallolā</s>: thus, in sequence, there are just sixteen according to rule.
The <s>Śaiṇḍa-vyūha</s> has been declared; it is called the array of <s>Śaiṇḍā</s>.

children.text: danturā raudrabhāgā ca amṛtā sakulā śubhā
children.translated_text: <s>Danturā</s>, <s>Raudrabhāgā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Sakulā</s>, and auspicious <s>Śubhā</s>,
<s>Calajihvā</s>, <s>Aryanetrā</s>, <s>Rūpiṇī</s>, and <s>Dārikā</s> likewise:
the first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.

children.text: khādikā rūpanāmā ca saṃhārī ca kṣamāntakā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khādikā</s>, <s>Rūpanāmā</s>, <s>Saṃhārī</s>, and <s>Kṣamāntakā</s>,
<s>Kaṇḍinī</s> and <s>Peṣiṇī</s>, <s>Mahātrāsā</s> and <s>Kṛtāntikā</s>,
<s>Daṇḍinī</s>, <s>Kiṅkarī</s>, <s>Biṃbā</s>, <s>Varṇinī</s>, and <s>Amalāṅginī</s>;

children.text: draviṇī drāviṇī caiva śaktayaḥ ṣoḍaśaiva tu
children.translated_text: <s>Draviṇī</s> and <s>Drāviṇī</s>: these powers are indeed sixteen.

children.text: kathito hi manoramyaḥ śauṇḍāyā vyūha uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The excellent and truly delightful array of <s>Śauṇḍā</s> has been told.
I shall proclaim the array called the first, supremely beautiful.

children.text: plavinī plāvanī śobhā mandā caiva madotkaṭā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Plavinī</s>, <s>Plāvanī</s>, <s>Śobhā</s>, <s>Mandā</s>, and <s>Madotkaṭā</s>,
<s>Mandākṣepā</s> and <s>Mahādevī</s> are remembered in the first enclosure.
The goddess <s>Kāmasaṃdīpinī</s>, <s>Atirūpā</s>, and <s>Manoharā</s>,
<s>Mahāvaśā</s>, <s>Mahāgrāhā</s>, <s>Vihvalā</s>, and <s>Madavihvalā</s>,
<s>Aruṇā</s>, <s>Śoṣaṇā</s>, divine <s>Revatī</s>, and <s>Bhāṇḍanāyikā</s>,
<s>Staṃbhinī</s>, <s>Ghoraraktākṣī</s>, <s>Smararūpā</s>, and <s>Sughoṣaṇā</s>:

children.text: vyūhaḥ prathama ākhyātaḥ svāyaṃbhuva yathā tathā ||
children.translated_text: the first array has thus been declared, O <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>.
The first array has been told; now I shall proclaim it, listen to me.
<s>Ghorā</s>, <s>Ghoratarā</s>, <s>Aghorā</s>, <s>Atighorā</s>, and <s>Aghanāyikā</s>,
<s>Dhāvanī</s>, <s>Kroṣṭukā</s>, and <s>Muṇḍā</s> are proclaimed as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.

children.text: bhīmā bhīmatarā bhīmā śastā caiva suvartulā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhīmā</s>, <s>Bhīmatarā</s>, <s>Bhīmā</s>, <s>Śastā</s>, and <s>Suvartulā</s>,
<s>Staṃbhinī</s>, <s>Rodanī</s>, <s>Raudrā</s>, <s>Rudravatī</s>, <s>Acalā</s>, and <s>Calā</s>,
<s>Mahābalā</s>, <s>Mahāśānti</s>, <s>Śālā</s>, <s>Śāntā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, and <s>Aśivā</s>,
<s>Bṛhatkakṣā</s> and <s>Mahānāsā</s>: exactly sixteen are proclaimed.
The <s>Manmatha-vyūha</s> of the first one has been described.

children.text: tālakarṇī ca bālā ca kalyāṇī kapilā śivā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tālakarṇī</s>, <s>Bālā</s>, <s>Kalyāṇī</s>, <s>Kapilā</s>, and <s>Śivā</s>,
<s>Iṣṭi</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, and <s>Pratijñā</s> are remembered in the first enclosure.
<s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Puṣṭikarī</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Jalā</s>, <s>Śruti</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,
<s>Kāmadā</s>, <s>Śubhadā</s>, <s>Saumyā</s>, <s>Tejinī</s>, and <s>Kāmatantrikā</s>,
<s>Dharmā</s>, <s>Dharmavaśā</s>, <s>Śīlā</s>, <s>Pāpahā</s>, and <s>Dharmavardhinī</s>:

children.text: manmathaḥ kathito vyūho manmathāyāḥ śṛṇuṣva me
children.translated_text: the <s>Manmatha</s> array has been told; hear from me the array of <s>Manmathā</s>.

children.text: dharmarakṣā vidhānā ca dharmā dharmavatī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmarakṣā</s>, <s>Vidhānā</s>, <s>Dharmā</s>, and <s>Dharmavatī</s> likewise,
<s>Sumati</s>, <s>Durmati</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, and <s>Vimalā</s> are remembered as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Śuddhi</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Dyuti</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Vartulā</s>, and <s>Mohavardhinī</s>,
<s>Balā</s>, <s>Atibalā</s>, <s>Bhīmā</s>, and likewise <s>Prāṇavṛddhikarī</s>,
<s>Nirlajjā</s>, <s>Nirghṛṇā</s>, <s>Mandā</s>, and <s>Sarvapāpakṣayaṅkarī</s>,
<s>Kapilā</s> and <s>Atividhurā</s>: these sixteen are proclaimed.
The <s>Manmatāyika</s> has been stated to you; and I shall tell the <s>Bhīma-vyūha</s>.

children.text: raktā caiva viraktā ca udvegā śokavardhinī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Raktā</s>, <s>Viraktā</s>, <s>Udvegā</s>, and <s>Śokavardhinī</s>,

children.text: kāmā tṛṣṇā kṣudhā mohā cāṣṭamī parikīrtitā
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmā</s>, <s>Tṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Kṣudhā</s>, and <s>Mohā</s> are proclaimed as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Jayā</s>, <s>Nidrā</s>, <s>Bhaya</s>, <s>Ālasyā</s>, <s>Jalatṛṣṇodarī</s>, and <s>Darā</s>,
<s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇāṅginī</s>, <s>Vṛddhā</s>, <s>Śuddhocchiṣṭāśanī</s>, and <s>Vṛṣā</s>,
<s>Kāmanā</s>, <s>Śobhinī</s>, <s>Dagdhā</s>, <s>Duḥkhadā</s>, and the row of <s>Sukhadā</s>;
the <s>Bhīma-vyūha</s> has been described; it is called the array of <s>Bhīmāyī</s>.

children.text: ānandā ca sunandā ca mahānandā subhaṅkarī
children.translated_text: <s>Ānandā</s>, <s>Sunandā</s>, <s>Mahānandā</s>, and <s>Subhaṅkarī</s>,
<s>Vatirāgā</s>, <s>Mahotsāhā</s>, <s>Jitarāgā</s>, and <s>Manoratā</s>,
the first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Manonmanī</s>, <s>Manaḥkṣobhā</s>, <s>Madonmattā</s>, and <s>Gadākulā</s>,
<s>Mandagārbhā</s>, <s>Mahābhāsā</s>, <s>Kāmānandā</s>, and <s>Suvuhvalā</s>,
<s>Mahāvegā</s>, <s>Suvegā</s>, <s>Mahābhogā</s>, and <s>Kṣayāvahā</s>,
<s>Kramiṇī</s>, <s>Kramiṇī</s>, and <s>Vakraā</s> are remembered in the second enclosure.
I have told you the supremely beautiful <s>Bhīmāyī-vyūha</s>.
Now, O <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>, I shall describe the eager-minded <s>Śākuna</s> array.

children.text: yogā vegā suvegā ca ativegā suvāsinī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yogā</s>, <s>Vegā</s>, <s>Suvegā</s>, <s>Ativegā</s>, and <s>Suvāsinī</s>,

children.text: devī manorayā vegā jalāvartā ca dhīmatī
children.translated_text: the goddess <s>Manorayā</s>, <s>Vegā</s>, <s>Jalāvartā</s>, and <s>Dhīmatī</s>,
the first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.
<s>Rodhinī</s>, <s>Kṣobhiṇī</s>, <s>Bālā</s>, <s>Viprāśeṣā</s>, and <s>Suśoṣiṇī</s>,

children.text: vidyutā bhāsinī devī manovegā ca cāpalā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyutā</s>, the shining goddess <s>Bhāsinī</s>, <s>Manovegā</s>, and <s>Cāpalā</s>,
<s>Vidyujjihvā</s>, <s>Mahājihvā</s>, and she whose face is crooked with a frown, <s>Bhṛkuṭīkuṭilānanā</s>,
<s>Phullajvālā</s>, <s>Mahājvālā</s>, <s>Sujvālā</s>, and <s>Kṣayāntikā</s>;
the <s>Śākuna</s> array has been told; hear from me the array of <s>Śākunā</s>.

children.text: jvālinī caiva bhasmāṅgī tathā bhasmāntagā tatā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Bhasmāṅgī</s>, and likewise <s>Bhasmāntagā</s>, and <s>Tatā</s>,

children.text: bhāvinī ca prajā vidyā khyātiścaivāṣṭamī smṛtā
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāvinī</s>, <s>Prajā</s>, <s>Vidyā</s>, and <s>Khyāti</s> are remembered as the eighth.
The first enclosure has been stated; hear the second enclosure.

children.text: ullekhā ca patākā ca bhogābhogavatī khagā
children.translated_text: <s>Ullekhā</s>, <s>Patākā</s>, <s>Bhogā</s>, <s>Bhogavatī</s>, and <s>Khagā</s>,
<s>Bhogabhogavratā</s>, <s>Yogā</s>, <s>Bhogākhyā</s>, and <s>Yogapāragā</s>,
<s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Śruti</s> manifestly, and <s>Dharā</s>:
the great array of <s>Śākunā</s>, which grants desires, has been told.
O <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>, hear the beautiful array called <s>Sumatī</s>.

children.text: pareṣṭā ca parā dṛṣṭā hyamṛtā phalanāśinī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pareṣṭā</s>, <s>Parā</s>, <s>Dṛṣṭā</s>, <s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Phalanāśinī</s>,
<s>Hiraṇyākṣī</s>, <s>Suvarṇākṣī</s>, the goddess <s>Kapiñjalā</s> herself,
and <s>Kāmarekhā</s>: the first enclosure has been told; listen.
<s>Ratnadvīpā</s>, <s>Sudvīpā</s>, <s>Ratnadā</s>, and <s>Ratnamālinī</s>
<s>Ratnaśobhā</s>, <s>Suśobhā</s>, <s>Mahāśobhā</s>, and <s>Mahādyuti</s>;
<s>Śāṃbarī</s>, <s>Bandhurā</s>, <s>Granthi</s>, <s>Pādakarṇā</s>, and <s>Karānanā</s>,

children.text: hayagrīvā ca jihvā ca sarvabhāsoti śaktayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hayagrīvā</s>, <s>Jihvā</s>, and <s>Sarvabhāsā</s>: these are the <s>śaktis</s> (powers).
The <s>Sumati</s> array has been described; the array of <s>Sumatyā</s> is now stated.
<s>Sarvāśī</s>, <s>Mahābhakṣā</s>, <s>Mahādaṃṣṭrā</s>, and <s>Atirauravā</s>,
<s>Visphuliṅgā</s>, <s>Viliṅgā</s>, <s>Kṛtāntā</s>, and <s>Bhāskarānanā</s>;
the first enclosure has been stated; listen to the second enclosure.

children.text: rāgā raṅgāvatī śreṣṭhā mahākrodhā ca rauravā
children.translated_text: <s>Rāgā</s>, <s>Raṅgāvatī</s>, <s>Śreṣṭhā</s>, <s>Mahākrodhā</s>, and <s>Rauravā</s>,
<s>Krodhanī</s>, <s>Vasanī</s>, <s>Kalahā</s>, and <s>Mahābalā</s>,
<s>Kalantikā</s>, <s>Caturbhedā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, and <s>Durgamāninī</s>,

children.text: nālī sunālī saumyā ca ityevaṃ kathitaṃ mayā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nālī</s>, <s>Sunālī</s>, and <s>Saumyā</s>: thus it has been told by me.
Here I shall tell the complete <s>Gopa</s> array; listen, O <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>.

children.text: pāṭalī pāṭavī caiva pāṭī vidipiṭā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṭalī</s>, <s>Pāṭavī</s>, <s>Pāṭī</s>, and likewise <s>Vidipiṭā</s>,

children.text: kaṅkaṭā supaṭā caiva praghaṭā ca ghaṭodbhavā
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkaṭā</s>, <s>Supaṭā</s>, <s>Praghaṭā</s>, and <s>Ghaṭodbhavā</s>;
and here the first enclosure has been described by me in ordinary speech.
<s>Nādākṣī</s>, <s>Nādarūpā</s>, <s>Sarvakārī</s>, and <s>Gamāgamā</s>,
<s>Anucārī</s>, <s>Sucārī</s>, <s>Caṇḍanāḍī</s>, and <s>Suvāhinī</s>,

children.text: suyogā ca viyogā ca haṃsākhyā ca vilāsinī
children.translated_text: <s>Suyogā</s>, <s>Viyogā</s>, the one called <s>Haṃsā</s>, and <s>Vilāsinī</s>,

children.text: sarvagā suvicārā ca vañcanī ceti śaktayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sarvagā</s>, <s>Suvicārā</s>, and <s>Vañcanī</s>: these are the <s>śaktis</s>.
The <s>Gopa</s> array has been explained; the <s>Gopāyī</s> array is now stated.
<s>Bhedinī</s>, <s>Chedinī</s>, <s>Sarvakārī</s>, and <s>Kṣudhāśanī</s>,
<s>Ucchuṣmā</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Bhasmāśī</s>, and <s>Vaḍavānalā</s>;
this is the first enclosure; now listen to the second enclosure.

children.text: andhā bāhvāsinī bālā dīkṣapāmā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Andhā</s>, <s>Bāhvāsinī</s>, <s>Bālā</s>, and likewise <s>Dīkṣapāmā</s>,
<s>Akṣā</s>, <s>Tryakṣā</s>, <s>Hṛllekhā</s>, <s>Hṛdgatā</s>, and the further <s>Māyikā</s>,
<s>Āmayāsādinī</s>, <s>Bhillī</s>, <s>Sahyā</s>, <s>Asahyā</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Rudraśakti</s>, <s>Mahāśakti</s>, <s>Mahāmohā</s>, and <s>Gonadī</s>.

children.text: gopāyī kathito vyūho nandavyūhaṃ vadāmi te
children.translated_text: The <s>Gopāyī</s> array has been described; I shall tell you the <s>Nanda</s> array.

children.text: nandinī ca nivṛttiśca pratiṣṭhā ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Nivṛtti</s>, and <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>, in due order,
<s>Vidyānāsā</s>, <s>Khagrasinī</s>, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, and <s>Priyadarśinī</s>;
the first enclosure has been stated; listen to the second enclosure.

children.text: gṛhyā nārāyaṇī mohā prajā devī ca cakriṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Gṛhyā</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, <s>Mohā</s>, <s>Prajā</s>, <s>Devī</s>, and <s>Cakriṇī</s>,

children.text: kaṅkaṭā ca tathā kālī śivādyoṣā tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaṅkaṭā</s>, and likewise <s>Kālī</s>; after that comes <s>Śivādyoṣā</s>.

children.text: virāmā yā ca vāgīśī vāhinībhīṣaṇī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Virāmā</s>, <s>Vāgīśī</s>, <s>Vāhinī</s>, and <s>Bhīṣaṇī</s>,
and <s>Sugamā</s> too is prescribed; these are remembered in the second enclosure.

children.text: nandavyūho mayā khyāto nandāyā vyūha ucyate
children.translated_text: The <s>Nanda</s> array has been told by me; the array of <s>Nandā</s> is now stated.

children.text: vināyakī pūrṇimā ca raṅkārī kuṇḍalī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vināyakī</s>, <s>Pūrṇimā</s>, <s>Raṅkārī</s>, and <s>Kuṇḍalī</s>,

children.text: icchā kapālinī caiva dvīpinī ca jayantikā
children.translated_text: <s>Icchā</s>, <s>Kapālinī</s>, <s>Dvīpinī</s>, and <s>Jayantikā</s>;
these eight <s>śaktis</s> are proclaimed in the first enclosure.
The first enclosure has been stated; listen to the second enclosure.

children.text: pāvanī cāṃbikā caiva sarvātmā pūtanā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāvanī</s>, <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Sarvātmā</s>, and likewise <s>Pūtanā</s>,
<s>Chagalī</s>, <s>Modinī</s>, the manifest goddess, and likewise <s>Lambodarī</s>,

children.text: saṃhāri kālinī caiva kusumā ca yatākramam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃhārī</s>, <s>Kālinī</s>, and <s>Kusumā</s>, in due order,

children.text: śukraā tārā tathā jñānā kriyā gāyatrikā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Śukrā</s>, <s>Tārā</s>, <s>Jñānā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, and likewise <s>Gāyatrikā</s>,

children.text: sāvitrī ceti vidhinā dvitīyā varaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Sāvitrī</s>: according to rule, this is remembered as the second enclosure.
The array of <s>Nandā</s> has been described; next comes the <s>Paitāmaha</s> array.

children.text: nandinī caiva phetkārī krodhā haṃsā ṣaḍaṅgulā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nandinī</s>, <s>Phetkārī</s>, <s>Krodhā</s>, <s>Haṃsā</s>, and <s>Ṣaḍaṅgulā</s>,
<s>Ānandā</s>, <s>Vasudurgā</s>, <s>Saṃhārā</s>, and <s>Amṛtāṣṭamī</s>;
the first enclosure has been stated; listen to the second enclosure.
<s>Kulāntikā</s>, <s>Analā</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍā</s>, and likewise <s>Mardinī</s>,
<s>Sarvabhūtābhayā</s>, <s>Dayā</s>, and <s>Vaḍavāmukhī</s>,
<s>Lampaṭā</s>, <s>Pannagā</s>, <s>Devī</s>, <s>Kusumā</s>, and <s>Vipulāntakā</s>,

children.text: kedārā ca tathā kūrmā duritā mandarodarī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kedārā</s>, <s>Kūrmā</s>, <s>Duritā</s>, and <s>Mandarodarī</s>;
<s>Khaḍgacakrā</s>, according to rule, is remembered in the second enclosure.
The <s>Paitāmaha</s> array has been stated; it grants <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desire, wealth, and liberation.

children.text: pitāmahāyā vyūhaṃ ca kathayāmi śṛṇuṣva me
children.translated_text: Listen to me: I shall tell the array of <s>Pitāmahā</s>.
<s>Vajrā</s>, <s>Nandanā</s>, <s>Śāvarāvikā</s>, and <s>Ripubhedinī</s>,

children.text: rūpā caturthā yogā ca prathamāvaraṇe smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpā</s> as the fourth, and <s>Yogā</s>, are remembered in the first enclosure.

children.text: bhūtā nādā mahābālā kharparā ca tathā parā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūtā</s>, <s>Nādā</s>, <s>Mahābālā</s>, <s>Kharparā</s>, and likewise the further <s>Parā</s>,
<s>Bhasmā</s>, <s>Kāntā</s>, <s>Vṛṣṭi</s>, <s>Dvibhujā</s>, and <s>Brahmarūpiṇī</s>,
<s>Saihyā</s>, <s>Vaikārikā</s>, <s>Jātā</s>, and the further <s>Karmamoṭī</s>,
<s>Mahāmohā</s>, <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, <s>Gāndhārī</s>, and <s>Puṣpamālinī</s>,
<s>Śabdāpī</s> and <s>Mahāghoṣā</s>: these sixteen are likewise in the final enclosure.
All the goddesses have two arms and are like the young sun in radiance.
They hold a lotus and a conch, are peaceful, and are adorned with red garlands and garments.
They are complete with every ornament and adorned with crowns and the like,
with divine pearl ornaments and charming, variegated jewels.
The goddesses, rich in fair complexion, should each be meditated upon separately as thus adorned.

children.text: evaṃ sahasrakalaśaṃ tāmrajaṃ mṛnmayaṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: In this way one should set up a thousand jars, made of copper or of clay,
furnished with the characteristics stated before and established in the <s>Rudra</s> field.
After worshipping with the thousand names taught by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, beginning with <s>Bhava</s>,
one should place them in front and sprinkle the image of <s>Bāṇa</s>.
Having consecrated it and made the declaration, one should sprinkle the king.
Thus the thousand jars bestow the fruit of all attainments.
The forty great arrays are marked by every characteristic.
For all of them the jar is said, as before, to be made of gold.
All are filled with fragrant water and furnished with the five jewels,
as well as joined with gold; those of the god are filled with ghee,

children.text: kṣīreṇa vātha dadhnā vā pañcagavyena vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or else with milk, or with curds, or again with the five products of the cow.
Or an intermediate consecration is prescribed with the <s>brahmakūrca</s> (Brahmā-sprinkling brush).
Listen, best of the virtuous, to the king's consecration for <s>Rudra</s> by means of the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>.
"To those who are not terrible, and then to those who are terrible, to those more terrible than the terrible,
to all, to all forms of <s>Śarva</s>: homage be to you, to the forms of <s>Rudra</s>."
With this mantra he should sprinkle the king who has been consecrated.
And with this <s>Aghora</s> mantra, which removes sin, he should perform the oblation.

children.text: prāgādyaṃ devakuṇḍe vā sthāṇḍile vā ghṛtādibhiḥ
children.translated_text: Beginning from the east, in divine fire pits or on a ritual altar, with ghee and the other substances,
with fuel sticks, ghee, sacrificial porridge, parched grain, rice, and grains of wild rice,
having offered one hundred and eight oblations, he should ritually prepare the king.
With the words "A blessed day! Hail to <s>Rudra</s>!" he should prepare a golden protective band,
and ashes, and should bind them with lotus fiber on the right hand.
"We worship <s>Tryambaka</s>, fragrant and increasing nourishment.
Like a cucumber from its stem, may I be released from death, not from immortality."
With this mantra he should either sprinkle the king or perform the oblation.
The consecration with all substances, and the oblation with the oblation-substances, are to be done in order.
Beginning from the east, this has been declared by the Brahmins, with all substances in due sequence.
"May we know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; may we meditate on <s>Mahādeva</s>.
May that <s>Rudra</s> impel us."
With this <s>Puruṣa</s> mantra ending in svāhā, a twice-born man should offer into the eastern fire pit.
And with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, wearing black garments, he should offer in the southern fire pit.

children.text: vāmadevāya namo jyeṣṭhāya namaḥ śreṣṭhāya namo rudrāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: "Homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>; homage to the eldest; homage to the best; homage to <s>Rudra</s>; homage."
Following the order taught beginning in this way, a man should offer in the western fire pit.
With the <s>Sadya</s> mantra, the western oblation is made with all substances in order.
"I take refuge in <s>Sadyojāta</s>; indeed, homage to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.

children.text: bhave bhavenāti bhave bhavasva māṃ bhavodbhavāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Do not bring me into existence after existence; bring me into being. Homage to the source of being."
The wise man should offer into the fire with this mantra, accompanied by svāhā.

children.text: āgneyyāṃ ca vidhānena ṛcā raudreṇa homayet
children.translated_text: In the southeast, according to rule, he should offer with the <s>Raudra</s> verse.
Then with the verse beginning, "For <s>Jātavedas</s> we shall press Soma," and so on,
in the southwest the oblation is prescribed as before, with all the substances.
With this divine mantra, which brings every accomplishment,

children.text: nimi niśi diśa svāhā khaḍga rākṣasa bhedana ||
children.translated_text: "Nimi, niśi, diśa, svāhā! O sword, splitter of rākṣasas!"
"Wet with blood and ghee, to <s>Nairṛtī</s>, svāhā; homage, svadhā, homage."
With this mantra he should offer as desired, according to rule, with the substances.
In the southern fire pit, best of twice-born men, he should offer with various substances and the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra.
Then in the northeastern fire pit he should perform the oblation with the substances stated before.

children.text: iśānāya kadrudrāya pracetase tryaṃbakāya śarvāya tanno rudraḥ pracodayāt ||
children.translated_text: "To <s>Īśāna</s>, to <s>Kadrudra</s>, to <s>Pracetas</s>, to <s>Tryambaka</s>, to <s>Śarva</s>; may that <s>Rudra</s> impel us."
The principal oblation, best of twice-born men, is made as before with the substances and the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra.
In the presence of the king, he should offer a thousand oblations for each substance.
Or the king himself, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>, may offer into the fire.

children.text: īśānaḥ sarvavidyānāmīśvīraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ brahmādhipatirbrahmaṇo 'dhipatirbrahmā śivo me astu sadā śivom ||
children.translated_text: "<s>Īśāna</s> is lord of all branches of knowledge, lord of all beings, overlord of Brahmā, overlord of the Veda. May Brahmā, may <s>Śiva</s>, be auspicious for me; may he always be auspicious."
He should perform the expiation with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra, and carry out the rest in the common manner.
When the king has been ritually prepared, with the sounds of conches, kettledrums, and the like,
with divine cries of victory and with splendid recitations of the Veda,
he should sprinkle, or else asperse, the excellent king with water from the sprinkling brush.
He should do this by the rite of the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, while the king bears <s>Rudra</s>-ashes on his limbs.
A conch, fly-whisk, kettledrum, and other emblems, an umbrella shining like the moon,
a palanquin, and an auspicious <s>Vaijayantī</s> should be prepared for the king.
They are prescribed for a kṣatriya who has undergone the royal consecration, or for a sovereign lord.
Royal insignia are not prescribed for those who are not kṣatriyas.
The measure of all of them is said to be twelve finger-breadths.
Palāśa, udumbara, aśvattha, and vaṭa wood are used in order, beginning from the east.
There the arches and other structures are made with bands and strips of cloth.
They should be enclosed with darbha garlands measuring eight finger-breadths,
provided with eight directional banners, and made splendid with jars at the doors.
Adorned with golden arches and jars, he should bathe the king.
When the king is seated above all, he should sprinkle him with the <s>Śiva</s>-jar.
"May we know that <s>Maheśa</s>; may we meditate on the one whose speech is purified.
May that <s>Śiva</s> impel us."
With this mantra and rite, with the <s>Vardhanī</s> and with the <s>Gaurī</s> song,
or with the whole <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, or again with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra,
with divine white ornaments, well-arranged crowns and the like,
and with linen garments, he should duly and gradually honor the king.
Having made a <s>Sudarśana</s> from sixty-eight palas of gold,
and adorned it with nine jewels, he should give the ritual fees to the guru.
He should give ten cows together with garments, and a beautiful field,
and a hundred droṇas of sesame, and a hundred droṇas of rice.
He should have a bed, a vehicle, and a couch with pillows given.
For all the yogins, thirty palas are prescribed.
For all the remaining ones the gift is half of that, and for the devotees of <s>Śiva</s>, half of that again.
Then the king should perform a great worship of <s>Mahādeva</s>.
Thus the excellent victory-sprinkling has been described in summary.
Consecrated in this way of old, <s>Śakra</s> attained the state of <s>Śakra</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> attained the state of <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> attained the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And <s>Ambikā</s> attained the state of <s>Ambikā</s>, as well as incomparable good fortune.

children.text: sāvitrī ca tathā lakṣmīrdevī kātyāyanī tathā
children.translated_text: So too did <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the goddess <s>Kātyāyanī</s>,

children.text: nandinātha purā mṛtyū rudrādhyāyena vai jitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Nandinātha</s> formerly conquered death by means of the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>.
Formerly an asura named <s>Tāraka</s>, very mighty, was consecrated;
<s>Vidyunmālī</s> and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> were indeed vanquished by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Long ago the daitya <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> was slain by <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>,
and <s>Tāraka</s> and the others by <s>Skanda</s> and by <s>Kauśikī</s>, the ancient Mother.
The two sons of <s>Sunda</s> and <s>Upasunda</s>, honored by the lords of daityas, were defeated,
and <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Sudeva</s> were slain by <s>Kṛtakṛtyā</s>.
Through the rite of bathing, made according to rule by <s>Brahmā</s>,
in the conflict of gods and asuras the blameless gods defeated the sons of <s>Diti</s>.
By being bathed by all kings and also by other <s>bhūsuras</s> (brahmins),
they obtained divine perfections; no deliberation is to be made about this.
Ah, the greatness of <s>abhiṣeka</s> (consecration)! Ah, the pure and excellent saying,
that by being consecrated in this way death was conquered by the siddhas.
The sin that has been accumulated even over a hundred crores of kalpas,
the king is freed from all that sin by bathing in this way; there is no doubt.
The king is freed from illness, again from consumption, leprosy, and the like;
becoming always victorious and endowed with sons, grandsons, and so forth,
possessed of the people's affection, like another king of the gods,
and free from sin, he rejoices with his beloved wife who is devoted to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
Only a brief indication of the supremely auspicious fruit has been told
by me for the benefit of kings, O <s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s>.
Thus, in the glorious <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the twenty-seventh chapter, named the Rite of Consecration.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having bathed, worshiped the god, and bowed to the god of gods, the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
to <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>, the Lord, with divine sight,
and having seen him, he praised the boon-giving <s>Śaṅkara</s> with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>.

children.text: devo 'pi tuṣṭyā nirvāṇaṃ rājyānte karmaṇaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: The god too, being pleased, said that at the end of his reign <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation) would be his by action alone.
Saying once, 'It is yours,' he disappeared right there.
<s>Svāyaṃbhuva Manu</s> bowed to the god whose banner bears the bull,
and ascended great <s>Meru</s>, as the Lord ascends the great bull.
There he saw the golden-hued god, endowed with yogic sovereignty,
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, the boon-giver, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
He bowed to the boon-giver, devoted to brahman, whose form is brahman,
and, with hands joined in reverence, the greatly radiant one praised him.
He too, the god and sage, seeing <s>Manu</s>, had his hairs stand up with joy.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s>, O treasury of compassion, spoke this with compassion:
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Having come after seeing the peaceful <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>, the lord of all,
and having obtained consecration, you have arrived wishing to speak; speak, whatever it is.
Hearing that statement of his, he bowed down with joined palms
and petitioned, 'How is release obtained through action, O lord?
You should tell us whether it is by action alone,

children.text: jñānena nirvṛtiḥ siddhā vibho miśreṇa vā kvacit
children.translated_text: or whether release is accomplished by knowledge, O lord, or sometimes by a mixture.'

children.text: atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā śrutisāravidāṃ nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, hearing his words, the treasure of those who know the essence of the <s>śruti</s> (revelation),
the blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, said: 'Through action, release comes gradually;

children.text: miśreṇa ca kramādeva kṣaṇājjñānena vai mune ||
children.translated_text: and likewise gradually through the mixed path, but in an instant through knowledge, O sage.

children.text: purā mānena coṣṭratvam agamaṃ nandinaḥ prabhoḥ
children.translated_text: Formerly, because of pride, I entered the state of a camel through the curse of the lord <s>Nandin</s>;
then, by his grace, having worshiped the auspicious <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
by the favor of that <s>Nandin</s>, through action alone, indeed I became his son.
Having heard of the supreme divine goal, I attained that state.
It was by the method of worshiping <s>Śiva</s>, by <s>Śiva-dharma</s> (Śaiva religious practice), and not otherwise.
The sixteen gifts of kings were taught by <s>Nandin</s>,
the great-souled one, for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation, through action alone.
Hear them exactly, beginning with ascending the balance and the others.
At times such as eclipses and in auspicious places, the rite is excellent.
A <s>maṇḍapa</s> (pavilion) and an upper structure should measure twenty hastas,
or again eighteen hastas, or sixteen hastas,
and a <s>vedi</s> (altar) should be made in the middle, measuring nine hastas.

children.text: aṣṭahastena vā kāryā saptahastena vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: It may also be made eight hastas, or again seven hastas;
the altar may be two hastas or one and a half hastas, and very beautiful.
It should be furnished with twelve pillars, proper, charming, and with a surrounding passage.
All around, he should have nine square fire-pits made.
Between the <s>Aindra</s> and <s>Īśāna</s> directions is the chief one, O son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Alternatively it may be square, and after that yoni-shaped.
For women, O best of brahmins, the fire-pits should be made yoni-shaped;

children.text: ardhacandraṃ trikoṇaṃ ca vartulaṃ kuṇḍameva ca ||
children.translated_text: there may also be a half-moon, a triangle, or a circular fire-pit,
or one six-cornered on all sides, or triangular, resembling a lotus.

children.text: aṣṭāsraṃ sarvamāne tu sthaṇḍilaṃ kevalaṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: In every measure it may be eight-cornered, or merely a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (sacrificial ground).
It should be furnished with four doors and adorned with four <s>toraṇas</s> (arches).
It should be provided with the eight directional elephants and covered with garlands of darbha grass.
It should be furnished with the eight auspicious emblems and adorned above with a canopy.
Here, for the trees used as balance-posts, bilva and the others are especially prescribed;
bilva, aśvattha, palāśa, and the like, or simply khadira.

children.text: yena staṃbhaḥ kṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ tena sarvaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: With whatever wood the pillar was first made, with that all the rest should be made.
Alternatively, it may be arranged by a mixed method, or with bamboo.
The balance-post should measure eight hastas, together with two additional hastas.
The diameter of the balance-post is considered threefold and unbroken.

children.text: dvyaṅgulena vihīnaṃ tu suvṛttaṃ nirvraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: It should be less by two aṅgulas, well rounded, and without blemish.
The distance between the two is remembered as six hastas, O king,
and the space between the two pillars also is made four hastas.
The space between the two pillars, set above, should be known as six hastas.
The breadth is the measure of a span, and the upper cross-beam has that same diameter.
In accordance with the measure of the two pillars, it is equal to the northern doorway.
It should be joined with thirty-six measures; the exertion is to be in the form of a balance.
Its diameter is eight measures, together with five barley-grains.
Its nave should be thirty-six measures; from its construction it is round and auspicious.

children.text: agre mūle ca madhye ca hemapaṭṭena bandhayet
children.translated_text: At the front, the base, and the middle one should bind it with a strip of gold.
In the middle of the strip three supports should be made.
The three supports should be made of copper.
Or they may be made of bronze; one should certainly not make them of iron.
In the middle, a beautiful support should be made facing upward.
With cords, or at the front of the arch, one should fasten it according to rule.
One tongue is prescribed in the middle of the balance, and the arch is also prescribed.

children.text: uttarasya ca madhye ca śaṅkuṃ dṛḍhamanuttamam ||
children.translated_text: And in the middle of the upper part there should be a firm, excellent peg.
Having covered it above with an awning, one should attach it firmly and properly.
O sage, one should make a ring furnished with a hole for the peg.
In the middle of the balance, with the awning, and likewise on the pendant of the balance,
a hanging ring, or an earring-shaped suspension, should be attached by means of the ring.
It should be very firm in the middle of the balance, measuring nine aṅgulas.
The breadth of the strip itself should be of five measures.
One should make two other very firm weights from auspicious material.
They should be made beneath the sling, each five prādeśas wide,
and both should be made as supports for a thousand palas.
Or one may make them with eight hundred palas, or with six hundred palas.
The width should be four tālas, and the middle should be likewise so made.
The width of the jar is prescribed as three and a half tālas.
One should fasten a five-vessel arrangement; three measures, it is said, make a group of six.
It should be furnished with four doors, each door measuring an aṅgula,
and provided with rings that are complete and pure white.
On each ring there should be a circular arrangement of chain.
One should connect the support-ring of the chain with the suspension.
Leaving a prādeśa, or four measures, from the ground, one should suspend it.
Two jars, each of a man's measure, should be made, both beautiful.

children.text: tau vālukābhiḥ sampūrya śivaṃ tatra viniṣkṣipet
children.translated_text: Having filled them with sand, one should place <s>Śiva</s> there.
They should be carefully set in a pit measuring two hastas.
The learned man should fill it completely all around with sand,
and should arrange it by whatever means it becomes immovable.
Hear the supreme secret, the circular arrangement upon the altar,
joined with eight aṅgulas and adorned with auspicious sprouts.
It should be strewn with fruits and flowers and furnished with incense and lamps.
In the middle of the altar one should make it like the hollow of a mirror.
First one should draw a maṇḍala furnished with four doors,
complete with beauty and secondary ornaments, and furnished with pericarp and filaments.
It should be endowed with classes of colors; one should make it five-colored.
In the eastern intermediate part one should draw a thunderbolt, and in the southeast a blazing spear.
In the south one should draw a staff, and in the southwest one should draw a sword.

children.text: pāśaś ca vāruṇe lekhyo dhvajaṃ vai vāyugocare ||
children.translated_text: A noose should be drawn in the western quarter, and a banner in the domain of <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: kauberyāṃ tu gadā lekhyā aiśānyāṃ śūlamālikhet
children.translated_text: In the quarter of <s>Kubera</s> a mace should be drawn, and in the northeast one should draw a trident.

children.text: śūlasya vāmadeśena cakraṃ padmaṃ tu dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: On the left side of the trident should be a discus, and on the right a lotus.
Having drawn it in this way, one should afterward perform the homa rite.
The principal oblation is made with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>: svāhā to <s>Śakra</s>, to <s>Vahni</s>,
to <s>Yama</s>, to the lord of the rākṣasas, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, and to <s>Vāyu</s>,
to <s>Kubera</s>, then to <s>Īśvara</s>, again to <s>Viṣṇu</s> and to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Ending with svāhā, and with the praṇava, it should be offered according to rule.
With the fire-mouth of one's own Vedic branch, joined with the rites beginning with victory,
one should then perform all acts according to rule, ending with the sviṣṭa offering.
For the preliminary oblation of all homas, the fuel-stick is said to be of palāśa wood.
Counting twenty-one, one should offer with this mantra:

children.text: ayanta idhma ātmā jātavedas tenedhyasva vardhasva ceddhavardhaya cāsmān prajayā paśubhir brahmavarcasenānnādyena sa medhaya svāhā
children.translated_text: This fuel is your self, O <s>Jātavedas</s>; by it be kindled and grow, and may you increase us with offspring, cattle, sacred brilliance, food, and nourishment. Svāhā.

children.text: bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā svaḥ svāhā bhūrbhuvaḥ svastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Bhūḥ svāhā, bhuvaḥ svāhā, svaḥ svāhā, and likewise bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ.
The fuel-offering, with the caru and with ghee, is performed in due order.
White cooked rice, milk-rice, and mung-bean rice are remembered as the carus.

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: The number may be a thousand, or half of that, or one hundred and eight.

children.text: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa āsuvor jamiṣaṃ ca naḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, purify the life-spans; bring vigor and favor to us.
Drive far away the harmful powers.
<s>Agni</s>, the seer, purifying, born of the five peoples, is the priest set in front.
We seek him, the greatly enriching one.

children.text: agne pavasva svapā asme varcaḥ suvīryam
children.translated_text: O <s>Agni</s>, purify for us good drinking, brilliance, and heroic strength,
placing wealth and nourishment in me.

children.text: prajāpate na tvadetānyanyo viśvā jātāni paritā babhūva
children.translated_text: O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you has encompassed all these created beings.

children.text: yatkāmāste juhumastanno astu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇām
children.translated_text: Whatever desires we sacrifice for, may that be ours; may we be lords of riches.
With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of the principal rite, and likewise with the fuel-offering,

children.text: caruṇā ca tathājyasya śakrādīnāṃ ca homayet ||
children.translated_text: and similarly with the caru and with ghee, one should offer to <s>Śakra</s> and the others.

children.text: vajrādīnāṃ ca hotavyaṃ sahasrārdhaṃ tataḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: For the thunderbolt and the other weapons also, one should offer half a thousand in sequence.
With the mantra beginning 'brahmayajña,' one should offer to <s>Brahmā</s> and again to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
May we know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; may we meditate on <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
May that <s>Viṣṇu</s> impel us.
This special and very splendid method of <s>homa</s> (fire offering) has been described:
with <s>dūrvā</s> grass mixed with milk, twenty-five offerings each, separately.
We worship <s>Tryambaka</s>, fragrant and increasing nourishment;

children.text: urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt ||
children.translated_text: like a cucumber from its bond, may I be released from death, not from immortality.
This <s>dūrvā-homa</s> is praised, and the <s>vāstuhoma</s> is praised in every respect;
the expiation is to be made with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra and with ghee, hundreds upon hundreds of offerings.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ dakṣiṇe vāme viṣṇuṃ viśvaguruṃ śivam
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> should be known on the right, <s>Viṣṇu</s> on the left, and <s>Śiva</s>, the teacher of the universe,
in the middle together with the Goddess, surrounded by the hosts beginning with <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: ādityaṃ bhāskaraṃ bhānuṃ raviṃ devaṃ divākaram
children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Āditya</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, <s>Ravi</s>, the god <s>Divākara</s>,

children.text: uṣāṃ prabhāṃ tathā prajñāṃ saṃdhyāṃ sāvitrimeva ca ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Uṣā</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Saṃdhyā</s>, and <s>Sāvitrī</s> as well.
By the fivefold rite one should worship the great-souled <s>Khakholka</s>,

children.text: viṣṭarāṃ subhagāṃ caiva vardhanīṃ ca pradakṣiṇām ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Viṣṭarā</s>, <s>Subhagā</s>, <s>Vardhanī</s>, and <s>Pradakṣiṇā</s>,

children.text: āpyāyanīṃ ca sampūjya devīṃ padmāsane ravim
children.translated_text: and <s>Āpyāyanī</s>; after worshipping the goddess and <s>Ravi</s> on the lotus-seat,

children.text: prabhūtaṃ vātha kartavyaṃ vimalaṃ dakṣiṇe tathā ||
children.translated_text: one should also set <s>Prabhūtā</s>, or else <s>Vimalā</s>, on the southern side.

children.text: sāraṃ paścimabhāge ca ārādhyaṃ cottare yajet
children.translated_text: On the western side one should worship <s>Sārā</s>, and on the northern side <s>Ārādhyā</s>;
in the center one should recognize <s>Sukhā</s>, and on the filaments, in due order,

children.text: dīptāṃ sūkṣmāṃ jayāṃ bhadrāṃ vibhūtiṃ vimalāṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: <s>Dīptā</s>, <s>Sūkṣmā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Vibhūti</s>, and <s>Vimalā</s> successively,
and <s>Amoghā</s> and <s>Vidyutā</s>; in the center is <s>Sarvatomukhī</s>.
Then, in sequence, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Guru</s>,

children.text: bhārgavaṃ ca tathā mandaṃ rāhuṃ ketuṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: and likewise <s>Bhārgava</s>, <s>Manda</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Ketu</s>.
Having worshipped and offered <s>homa</s> in this way, he should especially cause gifts to be given.
There he should feed yogins who have crossed to the sole truth of <s>Śiva</s>.
They should be accomplished in sacred study. Having made the rite expansive in this way,
when the <s>homa</s> is proceeding, in the middle of the place in the eastern quarter,
he should raise the king according to rule, with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>.
He should keep the ruler there for one <s>ghaṭikā</s>, according to the rite.
The sacrificer should recite the mantra called the <s>Rudra-Gāyatrī</s>
for half a <s>ghaṭikā</s>, or for half of that; there he should then take his seat.
The wise man, intent and holding a bunch of <s>kuśa</s> grass, should look toward the <s>Vāruṇa</s> direction;
and the king, adorned with ornaments, should hold a sword and shield.
With formulas beginning with 'svasti' at the start and especially also at the end,
the <s>puṇyāha</s> proclamation should be performed by brahmins versed in the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>.
With cries of victory and auspiciousness and with splendid sacred recitations,
with dancing, instruments, and songs, furnished with every splendor,
in this way he should cast the gold there in the quarter of the moon.

children.text: tulādhārau samau vṛttau tulābhāraḥ sadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The two pans of the balance should be equal and round; the weighing in the balance should always be made.
An amount exceeding one hundred <s>niṣkas</s> is best; half of that is remembered as middling.

children.text: tasyārdhaṃ ca kaniṣṭhaṃ syāttrividhaṃ tatra kalpitam ||
children.translated_text: Half of that again is the lowest; thus three grades are prescribed there.
A pair of garments, then a turban, earrings, an ornament beautifying the neck,
finger ornaments, and an ornament for the wrist:
all these, at the beginning of the righteous rite,
should be given to the ash-smeared man devoted to the <s>Pāśupata</s> vow.
All the ornaments mentioned before, together with turban and garments,
the wise man should give to the officiants, along with a covering cloth.

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ ca śataṃ sārdhaṃ tadardhaṃ vā pradāpayet
children.translated_text: He should have a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> of one hundred and fifty, or half of that, given.
And to all the yogins he should give one separate <s>niṣka</s> each.
He should give the sacred implements of the sacrifice to the teacher,
and to the other ascetics he should give one separate <s>niṣka</s> each.
The gold from the ascent onto the balance should be offered to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: prāsādaṃ maṇḍapaṃ caiva prākāraṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: A temple, a pavilion, a surrounding wall, and ornaments too,

children.text: suvarṇapuṣpaṃ paṭahaṃ khaḍgaṃ vai kośameva ca
children.translated_text: a golden flower, a drum, a sword, and also its sheath:

children.text: kṛtvā dattvā śivāyātha kiṃciccheṣaṃ ca buddhimān ||
children.translated_text: having made and given these to <s>Śiva</s>, the wise man should give whatever small remainder there is
to the teachers, and especially to the ash-smeared ascetics.
Then he should release prisoners confined in the prison-house.
There he should bathe <s>Parameśvara</s> with a thousand jars,
even with pure ghee, the god of gods, the lord of <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: payasā vātha dadhnā vā sarvadravyairathāpi vā
children.translated_text: Or else with milk, or with curds, or even with all substances,

children.text: brahmakūrcena vā devaṃ pañcagavyena vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: or with <s>brahmakūrca</s>, or again with the five products of the cow.

children.text: gāyatryā caiva gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ praṇavena vā
children.translated_text: With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> one should use cow urine, and with the <s>praṇava</s> cow dung.

children.text: āpyāyasveti vai kṣīraṃ dadhikrāvṇoti vai dadhi ||
children.translated_text: With the formula 'āpyāyasva' one should use milk, and with 'dadhikrāvṇo' curds.
With 'tejo 'si' one should use ghee; with the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra one should perform the bathing.
With 'devasya tvā' one should bathe the lord of gods with a jar of <s>kuśa</s>-water.
Or with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s> one should bathe <s>Parameśvara</s> with everything.
The thousand jars of <s>Śambhu</s> should be accompanied by thousands of his names,
whether taught by <s>Viṣṇu</s> or taught by <s>Taṇḍin</s>,
or again proclaimed by <s>Dakṣa</s>, the foremost sage.
The great worship of <s>Mahādeva</s> should be performed with devotion.
A <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should always be given to the worshipper of <s>Śiva</s>, as to one's own teacher.

children.text: dehārṇavaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ dakṣiṇā ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: And to all, according to order, the gift called <s>dehārṇava</s> and the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be given.
The poor, the blind, the destitute, children, the aged, the emaciated, and the sick
should be fed according to rule, and a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should also be given to them.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the twenty-eighth chapter, on the rite of the <s>tulāpuruṣa</s> gift, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:

children.text: tulā te kathitā hyeṣā ādyā sāmānyarūpiṇī
children.translated_text: This balance, the first and general in form, has indeed been told to you.
I shall describe <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the second rite, which grants all accomplishments.
The lower vessel is prescribed with a thousand measures of gold.
The upper vessel should be half of that, and the mouth only large enough for insertion.
He should make it of gold in this way, auspicious and furnished with every ornament.
In the lower vessel he should contemplate the Goddess, endowed with the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).
He should contemplate the Goddess as the twenty-fourfold one, whose forms are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and Fire.
In the upper vessel he should contemplate <s>Umāpati</s>, beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, as the twenty-sixth principle.
He should meditate on himself as the <s>Puruṣa</s>, the twenty-fifth, the primordial one.
Then, in the middle of the place previously described, on the altar, within the <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram),
having brought it, he should place it among rice grains and wrap it with new cloths.
Smearing it with bean paste, he should worship it with the five substances.
He should worship it fully with the five beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>, according to the proper rule.
The worship of <s>Śiva</s> and the oblation should be performed as before, in due order.
Having recited the Goddess as <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he himself should enter facing east.
Having duly carried out the rite beginning with impregnation according to the rule,
the best of brahmins should perform it by the sixteenfold procedure and according to prescription.
Sprinkling should be done in the southern fold with sprouts of <s>dūrvā</s> grass.
Together with fruits of the audumbara tree, water containing twenty-one <s>kuśa</s> grasses should be used.
At the northeast he should do just as much here in the <s>sīmanta</s> ceremony.
He should give a beautiful maiden in marriage, having made her for thirty <s>niṣkas</s>.
After adorning her and making the oblation, he should present her to <s>Śiva</s>.
At the first feeding of rice, the learned man should feed with milk-rice and the like.
Thus the rites beginning with conception, up to the <s>Viśvajit</s>,
are to be performed with the <s>śakti-bīja</s> (seed syllable of power) by brahmins who have mastered the Vedas.
All the remainder should be performed according to rule, as in the gift of gold equal to one's weight.
Thus, in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the twenty-ninth chapter ends.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now I shall declare the excellent sesame-mountain gift.
At the place and time previously stated, having prepared it and worshiped carefully,

children.text: susame bhūtale ramye vedinā ca vivarjite
children.translated_text: on very level, pleasant ground, free from an altar,
he should set up a staff measuring ten <s>tālas</s>, O sage.
After sprinkling it with water, he should then cast sesame seeds upon it.
The best of brahmins should sprinkle that place with <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow).
The learned man should lay out the <s>maṇḍala</s> on all sides as before.
Having established it with new cloths and scattered charming flowers,
the piling-up should be done there, especially with loads of sesame.
A height of a staff and a span is declared to be the superior measure.
One four finger-breadths less is the middling measure, O foremost sages.
The lowest should be equal to the staff; it should not be made less than a staff.
Having wrapped it all around with new cloths, he should worship it in order.
Installing the forms beginning with <s>Sadya</s>, he should worship according to rule.

children.text: aṣṭadikṣu ca kartavyāḥ pūrvoktā mūrtayaḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: In the eight directions the previously mentioned images should be made in order.
He should have each made, in due sequence, with gold of three <s>niṣkas</s>.
The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee) should be given according to rule, just as in the <s>tulābhāra</s> rite.
The oblation too is taught as before, exactly, O best of sages.
He should worship the Lord of the gods, surrounded by the guardians of the worlds,
standing in the midst of the sesame mountain and having the form of the sesame mountain.
The worship of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed with a thousand pitchers and the other requisites.
He should display <s>Umāpati</s>, the God of gods, standing in the midst of the sesame.
Having worshiped him according to prescription, he should dismiss him in due order.
He should cause the sesame mountain to be given to a poor <s>śrotriya</s> (Veda-learned brahmin).
Thus the sesame mountain has been taught as supreme, higher than all others.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge tilaparvatadānaṃ nāma triṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirtieth chapter, named 'The Gift of the Sesame Mountain,' ends.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now I shall teach another mountain rite, subtle, requiring little material but bearing great fruit.
When only a limited amount of material is available, the middling form is prescribed at the proper time.
On ground smeared with cow-dung, he should spread cloths,
and in their middle the wise man should place three loads of auspicious sesame.
He should make an eight-petalled lotus, furnished with pericarp and filaments.
That should be made with ten <s>niṣkas</s>, or again with half or a quarter of that.
He should set the lotus in the midst of the sesame, and <s>Maheśvara</s> in the middle of the lotus.
Having worshiped the god according to rule, he should worship the forms beginning with <s>Vāma</s>.
He should make the form of <s>Śakti</s> from gold of three <s>niṣkas</s>.
He should perform the placement all around, with the Lords of Obstacles in the surrounding divisions.
He should also make the Lords of Obstacles with the measure of gold stated before.
He should worship them in order according to prescription, with perfumes, flowers, and the like.
Thus, in the <s>Uttarabhāga</s> of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-first chapter ends.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Recitation, oblation, worship, gift, consecration, and the rest are as before.
I shall briefly proclaim the gift of the golden earth.
At the place and time previously stated, he should have it made together with sages,
according to the previous characteristics, either in a fire-pit or in a <s>maṇḍala</s>.
He should have a divine earth made, even with a thousand pieces of gold.
It should be made one hasta in size, square, and very beautiful.
It should be surrounded by the seven continents, the oceans and the rest, and by mountains,
endowed with all sacred bathing places and furnished with <s>Meru</s> in the middle.
Or else he should fashion an island in the center, divided into nine regions.
Having done everything as before, in the <s>maṇḍala</s> at the center of the altar,
with one seventh part of the thousand, according to rule,
it should be given to a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>; the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> has been prescribed before.
And with a thousand pitchers and the like he should worship auspicious <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Śiva</s>.
In this <s>liṅga</s>, the gift described as the golden earth is supreme.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge suvarṇamedinīdānaṃ nāma dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-second chapter, named The Gift of the Golden Earth.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now I shall proclaim another excellent <s>kalpapādapa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree).
Making it in this way with a hundred <s>niṣkas</s>, furnished with all its branches,
making the branches varied, with strings of pearls and the like hanging down,
he should set the tips of the shoots with divine emeralds.
The learned man should make the shoots of the tree with coral,
and he should make it splendid all around with fruits made of rubies.
The root should be made with sapphire and the excellent trunk with diamond,
the top of the tree with cat's-eye, and the crown with topaz.
The bulb should be made with hessonite, O good observer of vows, and with sunstone;

children.text: candrakāntena vā vedīṃ drumasya sphaṭikena vā ||
children.translated_text: or the altar of the tree may be made with moonstone or with crystal.
The tree is declared to have a length of one span,
and the measure of its eight branches, their breadth, and their upward extent are likewise stated.
At its root he should place a <s>liṅga</s>, surrounded by the guardians of the worlds.
Having set the tree in a <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram), in the middle of the previously described <s>vedi</s> (altar),
he should carefully worship lord <s>Īśāna</s> and the guardians of the worlds.
As before, he should perform the recitation, <s>homa</s> (fire offering), and the rest, in the manner of the balance-gift.
He should offer the tree to <s>Śambhu</s>, or else to yogins, O king.
Or, if the king gives it to those whose limbs are smeared with ash, he will become a universal sovereign.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge kalpapādapadānavidhir nāma trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-third chapter, named The Rule for the Gift of the Wish-Fulfilling Tree.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall proclaim the gift of <s>Gaṇeśeśa</s>, in the previously described pavilion.
Having worshiped the lord of gods, surrounded by the guardians of the worlds,
and the <s>Viśveśvaras</s>, according to rule, furnished with every ornament,

children.text: daśaniṣkeṇa vai kṛtvā sampūjya ca vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: having made them with ten <s>niṣkas</s> and worshiped them according to prescription,
he should perform the <s>homa</s> as before in eight fire-pits in the eight directions,
by the path of the five enclosures and in the traditional sequence.
He should honor seven brahmins, and likewise one maiden in the northern direction.
He should have all the mantras bestowed in order, each with its own mantra.
Having given in this way, he is freed from all sins; of this there is no doubt.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge gaṇeśeśadānavidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-fourth chapter, named The Explanation of the Rule for the Gift of Gaṇeśeśa.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now I shall proclaim to you the sequence of the rule for the golden cow.
It pacifies all sins and destroys planetary affliction and famine;
it pacifies calamities and wards off every disease.

children.text: niṣkāṇāṃ ca sahasreṇa suvarṇena tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be made with a thousand <s>niṣkas</s> of gold,

children.text: tadardhenāpi vā samyak tadardhārdhena vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: or properly with half of that, or again with half of that half,
or it should be made with one hundred, endowed with every form and quality.
The shape of a cow should be divine, with fine hooves and furnished with all auspicious marks.
He should set a diamond at the tips of the hooves and a ruby on the horns.
Between the brows he should set a divine pearl, O best of sages.

children.text: vaiḍūryeṇa stanāḥ kāryā lāṅgūlaṃ nīlataḥ śubham ||
children.translated_text: The udders should be made with cat's-eye, and the auspicious tail with sapphire.
A splendid topaz should be made in the place of the teeth.
Having made it like an animal, he should make a beautiful calf.
It should be adorned with all jewels and with ten <s>niṣkas</s> of gold.
Having prepared a <s>maṇḍala</s> in the middle of the previously described altar,
the knower of all principles should place <s>Surabhi</s> there in the middle, together with her calf.
There he should wrap <s>Surabhi</s> with her calf in a pair of garments.

children.text: sampūjayed gāṃ gāyatryā savatsāṃ surabhiṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: He should worship the cow with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and again <s>Surabhi</s> together with her calf.
Then, by the rule of the single sacred fire, he should perform the <s>homa</s> according to prescription.
With fuel-sticks and clarified butter according to rule, he should perform the remainder as before.
The worship of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed, after bathing the <s>liṅga</s> with ghee and the like.
Having touched the cow with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he should give that auspicious cow to <s>Śivā</s>.
The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee), O great-minded one, should be thirty <s>niṣkas</s>.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge hemadhenudānavidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the thirty-fifth chapter, named The Explanation of the Rule for the Gift of the Golden Cow.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall proclaim the gift of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, which increases great sovereignty.
It should be performed in the previously described pavilion, in the <s>maṇḍala</s> above the altar.
Having made an incomparable image of <s>Śrīdevī</s> from gold according to rule,
with a thousand, or half of that, or again half of that half,
or even with one hundred and eight, endowed with every auspicious mark,
he should place <s>Lakṣmī</s> in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, furnished with every ornament.
On her right side, on a <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (sacrificial ground), he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Having worshiped the queen of the gods according to rule with the <s>Śrīsūkta</s>,
he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hari</s>, the teacher of the world, with the <s>Viṣṇu Gāyatrī</s>.
Having ritually propitiated the goddess, he should perform the <s>homa</s> as before.
Having offered the fuel-sticks according to rule, he should then make the oblation of clarified butter.
The best of brahmins should make one hundred and eight oblations separately.

children.text: āhūya yajamānaṃ tu tasyāḥ pūrvadiśi sthale
children.translated_text: Then, having summoned the sacrificer to the place east of her,

children.text: tasmai tāṃ darśayeddevīṃ daṇḍavat praṇamet kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: he should show him the goddess, and he should bow like a staff upon the ground.
Having bowed to <s>Viṣṇu</s> stationed there, he should worship <s>Śiva</s> as before.
A twentieth part of her value is declared to be the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee).
Half of that share should be given to the others according to worthiness.
Then the devoted yogin should offer oblations to <s>Śambhu</s>, especially.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge lakṣmīdānavidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṭtriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the thirty-sixth chapter, named the description of the rite for the gift of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now then I shall fully explain the proper sequence of the rite of the <s>tiladhenu</s> gift.
In the previously described pavilion he should perform the worship of <s>Śiva</s> on the western side.
In front of it, in the middle of the ground, he should draw a beautiful lotus.
Having covered the lotus with cloths, he should place an auspicious object in its center.
Then, having made a sesame-flower, he should place a golden lotus there.
It should be made with thirty <s>niṣkas</s>, or again with half of half of that.
It may be made with five <s>niṣkas</s>, or again with half of half of that.
Having worshipped it according to rule, in order, with perfumes, flowers, and the like,
he should set eleven brahmins on the northern side of the lotus.
Having honored them according to rule, in order, with perfumes, flowers, and the like,
he should have a covering cloth and upper garment given to the brahmins in due order.

children.text: uṣṇīṣaṃ ca pradātavyaṃ kuṇḍale ca vibhūṣite ||
children.translated_text: A turban should also be given, and two adorned earrings.
Having given a golden finger-ring to the brahmins according to rule,

children.text: ekaṃ daśa ca vastrāṇi teṣāmagre prakīrya ca ||
children.translated_text: and having spread eleven garments before them,
he should place sesame seeds and the other things separately on those garments.
He should divide a bronze vessel of one hundred <s>palas</s> into eleven portions.
A sugarcane staff should also be given especially to the brahmins.

children.text: gośṛṅge tu hiraṇyena dviniṣkeṇa tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: He should have the cow's horns made of gold with two <s>niṣkas</s>.

children.text: rajatena tu kartavyāḥ khurā niṣkadvayena tu
children.translated_text: The hooves should be made of silver with two <s>niṣkas</s>.
