Having thus given each item separately, he should place it among those sesame seeds.
Then he should have it given to the <s>Rudras</s> with the eleven <s>Rudra</s> mantras.
On the eastern side of the lotus he should place twelve honored brahmins.
By this very procedure, with faith directed toward them,
he should likewise have the gift made with the twelve <s>Āditya</s> mantras.
As before, on the southern side, he should set sixteen brahmins in place.
Again, as before, he should have the image given with the <s>Vighneśa</s> mantras.
All this should be done by the sacrificer in the proper order.
Or only the <s>Rudra</s> gift may be made, or again the gift to the <s>Ādityas</s>.
Or the gift may be made to the images and the others, according to the full extent of one's means.

children.text: padmaṃ vinyasya rājāsau śeṣaṃ vā kārayennṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having set down the lotus, that king, O king, should have the remainder made as well.
And as <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, an ornament worth five <s>niṣkas</s> should be given.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge tiladhenudānavidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the thirty-seventh chapter, named the description of the rite for the gift of the <s>tiladhenu</s>, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall tell of the gift of a thousand cows; listen, O you of good vows.
Having taken a thousand cows, together with calves, endowed with good qualities and auspicious,

children.text: tās tv abhyarcya yathāśāstram aṣṭau samyakprayatnataḥ
children.translated_text: he should carefully honor those eight in the proper manner according to scripture.
Then he should bind their horns with gold, one <s>niṣka</s> for each.
He should bind their hooves with silver, and at the region of the neck

children.text: pratiniṣkeṇa kartavyaṃ karṇe vajraṃ ca śobhanam ||
children.translated_text: there should be made, with one <s>niṣka</s> each, a beautiful jewel at the ear.
He should give them to <s>Śiva</s> through the brahmins, and give <s>dakṣiṇā</s> separately.

children.text: daśaniṣkaṃ tadardhaṃ vā tasyārdhārdham athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: Ten <s>niṣkas</s>, or half of that, or even half of half of that,
or, according to the full extent of one's means, even just one <s>niṣka</s>,
and a pair of garments should be given separately to the brahmins, splendidly.
Having carefully worshipped the cows, one should give them, very pleasing as they are.
Having thus given according to rule and having worshipped <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
he should recite before them, in the proper way, the unsurpassed hymn of the cows:

children.text: gāvo mamāgrato nityaṃ gāvo naḥ pṛṣṭhatastathā ||
children.translated_text: "May cows always be before me; may cows likewise be behind us.

children.text: hṛdaye me sadā gāvo gavāṃ madhye vasāmy aham
children.translated_text: May cows be always in my heart; I dwell among the cows."

children.text: iti kṛtvā dvijāgryebhyo dattvā gatvā pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: Having done this, and having given them to the foremost twice-born men, he should go around them in <s>pradakṣiṇa</s>.
For as many years as the number of hairs on them, he is honored in heaven.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the thirty-eighth chapter, named the gift of a thousand cows, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall also describe the gift of a golden horse, which brings victory.
I shall describe it as superior even to the <s>aśvamedha</s>; listen, O you of good vows.
With one thousand and eight, or with one hundred and eight,
he should make a horse furnished with the proper marks and adorned with every ornament.
He should have it made endowed with the five auspicious qualities and of divine form,
possessing every mark and complete in all its limbs,
equipped with all weapons, the excellent vehicle of <s>Indra</s>.
Having placed the horse, endowed with its own qualities, in the middle of it,
he should regard it as <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> and worship it with devotion.
On its eastern side he should place a brahmin who has mastered the <s>Veda</s>.
Honoring him with the thought that he is <s>Surendra</s>, he should have five <s>niṣkas</s> given.

children.text: sa cāśvaḥ śivabhaktāya dātavyo vidhinaiva tu ||
children.translated_text: And that horse should be given according to rule to a devotee of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having given the golden horse, he should also honor the teacher.
According to the full extent of his means, he should give five <s>niṣkas</s>, or even less.
The poor, the blind, the destitute, the helpless, children, the aged, the emaciated, and the sick
he should satisfy with gifts of food, and especially the brahmins.
The man who performs this gift of a horse with devotion
enjoys the pleasures of <s>Indra</s> for a long time and becomes possessed of beautiful sovereignty.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the thirty-ninth chapter, named the gift of a golden horse, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall proclaim <s>kanyādāna</s> (the gift of a maiden), the very highest of all gifts.
A maiden endowed with auspicious marks and free from every defect,

children.text: mātāpitrostu saṃvādaṃ kṛtvā dattvā dhanaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: after consultation has been made with her mother and father, after great wealth has been given,

children.text: ātmīkṛtyātha saṃsnāpya vastraṃ dattvā śubhaṃ navam ||
children.translated_text: after she has been made one's own, bathed, and given a fine new garment,
after adorning her with ornaments, one should honor her with perfumes and garlands.
Then, having examined the omens, the family lineages, lunar mansions, and so forth,
and having observed the minds of both parties, one should carefully honor them both.
She should be given only to a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>śrotriya</s>, an ascetic,
one who has directly studied the <s>Veda</s>, and, according to rule, a celibate student.
Male and female servants, abundant wealth, and ornaments in particular,

children.text: kṣetrāṇi ca dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ vāsāṃsi ca pradāpayet
children.translated_text: fields, money, grain, and garments should also be caused to be given.

children.text: yāvanti dehe romāṇi kanyāyāḥ saṃtatau punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As many hairs as there are on the maiden's body and then in her offspring,
for that many thousands of years he is honored in <s>Rudra</s>'s world.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge kanyādānavidhir nāma catvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the fortieth chapter, named the rite of <s>kanyādāna</s>, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall briefly describe the gift of a golden bull.
One should have the bull-form made with a thousand measures of gold,
or, if one is wise, with half of that, or again with half of that half.
Even with one hundred and eight measures one may make the bull, which embodies <s>dharma</s>.
On its forehead one should make a mark shaped like the digit of a half-moon.

children.text: sphaṭikena tu kartavyaṃ khuraṃ tu rajatena vai ||
children.translated_text: The hoof should be made of crystal, or else of silver.
The neck should be made with ruby, and the hump with gomedaka stone.
On the neck one should make a bell-collar, variegated with jewels.
There one should make the bull's emblem, encircled with tinkling ornaments and bracelets.
At the previously stated place and time, on the upper circular area of the altar,
one should place the chief bull there in front, facing west.
With devotion one should worship <s>Īśvara</s>, mounted on the bull and bearing the bull-banner.
Having worshipped the chief bull with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one should bow with collected mind:
"May we know the sharp-horned one; may we meditate on the one whose feet are <s>dharma</s>.
May that bull impel us."
Having worshipped the bull with this mantra for the increase of <s>dharma</s>,
one should make oblations with ghee, food, and the like, to the full extent of one's resources.

children.text: vṛṣabhaḥ pūjya dātavyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ śivāya vā
children.translated_text: The bull, after being worshipped, should be given to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> or to <s>Śiva</s>.
A <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should also be given according to one's wealth.
Whoever performs this unsurpassed gift of a bull with devotion,
having become an attendant of <s>Śiva</s>, rejoices together with him.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the forty-first chapter, named the gift of a golden bull, is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
I shall proclaim the gift of an elephant properly and in due order.

children.text: dvijāya vā śivāyātha dātavyaḥ pūjya pūrvavat ||
children.translated_text: After being worshipped as before, it should be given either to a twice-born man or to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: gajaṃ sulakṣaṇopetaṃ haimaṃ vā rājataṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: One should have made an elephant endowed with fine marks, either of gold or of silver,
with a measure of one thousand <s>niṣkas</s>, or even with half of that.
Or one may make it with half of that half, adorned with all auspicious marks.
At the previously stated place and time, one should offer it to the deity.
Or it should be given on the eighth lunar day to <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord,
or to a poor <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>śrotriya</s>, and one who maintains the sacred fires.
It should be given with <s>Śiva</s> in view, after worshipping <s>Śiva</s> as before.
Whoever performs this gift with focused devotion to <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: sthitvā svarge ciraṃ kālaṃ rājā gajapatirbhavet ||
children.translated_text: after dwelling in heaven for a long time, becomes a king, a lord of elephants.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the forty-second chapter is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
The divine group of eight <s>lokapālas</s>, directly very hard to obtain,
brings every prosperity, is secret, and destroys an enemy army.
It divinely protects one's own country and increases elephants and horses.
It is meritorious, increases sons, and brings benefit to cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
At the previously stated place and time, on the upper circular area of the altar,
having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> in the middle properly and in due sequence,
one should prepare sand altars in the cardinal and intermediate directions.
One should honor eight learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who have mastered the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>,
self-controlled, born in good families, and endowed with all auspicious marks,
seated facing <s>Śiva</s> and wearing fresh garments.
With garments and divine ornaments, with the mantras of the <s>lokapālas</s>,
one should honor the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> in order with perfumes, flowers, and fine incense.
In the east one should make offerings in the fire with the mantras of the <s>lokapālas</s>.
The fire-rite should be performed in order, making oblations with fuel-sticks and ghee.
Having offered oblations according to rule, the teacher, devoted to <s>Śiva</s>,
should summon the sacrificer and those adorned with all ornaments.
Then, having had him worship them, he should cause wealth to be given to the twice-born men.
With the separate mantras for each, he should give an ornament worth ten <s>niṣkas</s>.
A separate seat should be made for each with ten <s>niṣkas</s>.
There the bathing of <s>Śiva</s> should be performed according to rule.
A <s>dakṣiṇā</s> should be given to the full extent of one's resources.

children.text: evaṃ yaḥ kurute dānaṃ lokeśānāṃ tu bhaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever performs this gift to the lords of the worlds with devotion,
after dwelling long among the lords of the worlds, becomes a wise universal sovereign.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the forty-third chapter is complete.
<s>Sanatkumāra</s> said:
Now I shall proclaim another gift, the very highest of all gifts.
At the previously stated place and time, in a pavilion according to rule,
with affection, in the middle of the pit, on the altar, in the presence of <s>Śiva</s>,
First, having approached <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is supreme according to <s>Padmayoni</s>,
with the two mantras stated by the rule, together with a mantra beginning with the <s>praṇava</s> (oṃ):
May we know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; may we meditate on <s>Vāsudeva</s>;
may that <s>Viṣṇu</s> impel us.
To <s>Brahmā</s>, grown great through brahman and brahmins, the maker of the universe,

children.text: śivāya haraye svāhā svadhā vauṣaḍ vaṣaṭ tathā ||
children.translated_text: to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Hara</s>: svāhā, svadhā, vauṣaṭ, and likewise vaṣaṭ.
Having worshipped according to the prescribed rule, he should afterward perform the homa.
For all the materials are to be offered with the two mantras, according to the arrangement of the altar-pit.
Two officiants, learned in the Veda, should be appointed by the teacher.
With them in view, according to rule, he should cause wealth to be given to the brahmins.
To them separately he should give one hundred and eight, unsurpassed,
together with garments and ornaments, furnished with every adornment.

children.text: gurureko hi vai śrīmān brahmā viṣṇurmaheśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: For the one blessed teacher is indeed <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
A separate gift should be given to each of them, and he should feed the brahmins also.
Worship of <s>Śiva</s> too should be performed, with bathing and the rest in due order.
Thus, in the revered great <s>Liṅgapurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the forty-fourth chapter is complete.
The sages said:

children.text: evaṃ ṣoḍaśa dānāni kathitāni śubhāni ca
children.translated_text: Thus the sixteen auspicious gifts have been described.
Now you should tell us the procedure for jīvacchrāddha.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall briefly describe the rite of jīvacchrāddha, approved by all,
which was taught long ago to <s>Manu</s> by <s>Brahmā</s>, the god of gods,

children.text: vasiṣṭhāya ca śiṣṭāya bhṛgave bhārgavāya ca
children.translated_text: and to the virtuous <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and to <s>Bhṛgu</s> the <s>Bhārgava</s>.
Listen with complete attention to the supreme rite that brings every accomplishment.
I shall state directly the order of the path of śrāddha and also the order of those worthy of śrāddha,
and the special rule for jīvacchrāddha, O you of good vows.

children.text: parvate vā nadītīre vane vāyatane 'pi vā
children.translated_text: On a mountain, on a riverbank, in a forest, or even in a shrine,
jīvacchrāddha should be performed carefully at the time of death.
When jīvacchrāddha has been performed, the living person is liberated while still alive,
whether he performs rites or does not perform them, whether he is knowledgeable or without knowledge.
Whether he is a learned Vedic brahmin or not, whether he is a brahmin or even a kṣatriya,

children.text: vaiśyo vā nātra saṃdeho yogamārgagato yathā ||
children.translated_text: or a vaiśya, there is no doubt here; he is as one who has entered the path of yoga.
Having examined the ground according to rule by its smell, color, taste, and the like,
and having carefully removed obstructions, he should make a sandy altar-ground on the earth.
In the middle, by a cubit measure, he should make a beautiful oblong altar-pit,
or else an altar-ground, again and again, of the measure of an arrow.
Having smeared it according to rule, having plastered it, and having established the fire,
having performed the anvādhāna according to scripture and enclosed it on every side,
having spread the ritual grass according to his own Vedic branch, in the order received by tradition,
he should complete the entire opening rite of the fire with these mantras in due order.
After worshipping on the altar-ground and in the fire, he should offer oblations with kindling sticks and the like.

children.text: ādau kṛtvā samiddhomaṃ caruṇā ca pṛthakpṛthak ||
children.translated_text: First, having performed the kindling-stick oblation, he should offer separately with the caru.

children.text: ghṛtena ca pṛthak pātre śodhitena pṛthakpṛthak
children.translated_text: And with ghee, purified in a separate vessel, he should make the offerings separately,
drawing out by himself, on every side, all the entities that are the principles.
Oṃ bhūḥ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oṃ bhūḥ, svāhā to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oṃ bhuvaḥ, homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Oṃ bhuvaḥ, svāhā to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Oṃ svaḥ, homage to <s>Rudra</s>.
Oṃ svaḥ, svāhā to <s>Rudra</s>.
Oṃ mahaḥ, homage to <s>Īśvara</s>.
Oṃ mahaḥ, svāhā to <s>Īśvara</s>.
Oṃ janaḥ, homage to <s>Prakṛti</s>.
Oṃ janaḥ, svāhā to <s>Prakṛti</s>.
Oṃ tapaḥ, homage to <s>Mudgala</s>.
Oṃ tapaḥ, svāhā to <s>Mudgala</s>.
Oṃ ṛtam, homage to <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Oṃ ṛtam, svāhā to <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Oṃ satyam, homage to <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ satyam, svāhā to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvāya devāya bhūrnamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Śarva</s>, protect my earth; in the nose, scent; homage in bhūḥ to the god <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvāya bhūḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Śarva</s>, protect my earth; in the nose, scent; svāhā in bhūḥ to <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvasya devasya patnyai bhūrnamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śarva</s>, protect my earth; in the nose, scent; homage in bhūḥ to the wife of the god <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me gopāya ghrāṇe gandhaṃ śarvapatnyai bhūḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Śarva</s>, protect my earth; in the nose, scent; svāhā in bhūḥ to the wife of <s>Śarva</s>.

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavāya devāya bhuvo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Bhava</s>, protect my water; on the tongue, taste; homage in bhuvaḥ to the god <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavāya devāya bhuvaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Bhava</s>, protect my water; on the tongue, taste; svāhā in bhuvaḥ to the god <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavasya devasya patnyai bhuvo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Bhava</s>, protect my water; on the tongue, taste; homage in bhuvaḥ to the wife of the god <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: oṃ bhava jalaṃ me gopāya jihvāyāṃ rasaṃ bhavasya patnyai bhuvaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Bhava</s>, protect my water; on the tongue, taste; svāhā in bhuvaḥ to the wife of <s>Bhava</s>.

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrāya devāya svaroṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, protect my fire; in the eyes, form; oṃ svaḥ, homage to the god <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrāya devāya svaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, protect my fire; in the eyes, form; svāhā in svaḥ to the god <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrasya patnyai svaroṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, protect my fire; in the eyes, form; oṃ svaḥ, homage to the wife of <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: rudrāgniṃ me gopāya netre rūpaṃ rudrasya devasya patnyai svaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rudra</s>, protect my fire; in the eyes, form; svāhā in svaḥ to the wife of the god <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: ugra vāyuṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśaṃ ugrāya devāya maharnamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ugra</s>, protect my wind; in the skin, touch; homage in mahaḥ to the god <s>Ugra</s>.

children.text: ugra vāyuṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśamugrāya devāya mahaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ugra</s>, protect my wind; in the skin, touch; svāhā in mahaḥ to the god <s>Ugra</s>.

children.text: ugra vāyuṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśamugrasya devasya patnyai mahar oṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ugra</s>, protect my wind; in the skin, touch; oṃ mahaḥ, homage to the wife of the god <s>Ugra</s>.

children.text: oṃ ugra vāyuṃ me gopāya tvaci sparśamugrasya devasya patnyai devāya janaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ <s>Ugra</s>, protect my wind; in the skin, touch; svāhā in janaḥ to the wife of the god <s>Ugra</s>.

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmāya devāya jano namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect my aperture; protect sound in the ear. Homage, with the mantra-word janaḥ, to the god <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmāya devāya janaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect my aperture; protect sound in the ear. Svāhā, with the mantra-word janaḥ, to the god <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmasya patnyai jano namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect my aperture; protect sound in the ear. Homage, with the mantra-word janaḥ, to the wife of <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: bhīma suṣiraṃ me gopāya śrotre śabdaṃ bhīmasya devasya patnyai janaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Bhīma</s>, protect my aperture; protect sound in the ear. Svāhā, with the mantra-word janaḥ, to the wife of the god <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: īśa rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇāmīśāya devāya tapo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Īśa</s>, protect passion for me; protect thirst in material things. Homage, with tapas, to the god <s>Īśa</s>.

children.text: īśa rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇām īśāya devāya tapaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Īśa</s>, protect passion for me; protect thirst in material things. Svāhā, with tapas, to the god <s>Īśa</s>.

children.text: rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇāmīśasya patnyai tapo namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Protect passion for me; protect thirst in material things. Homage, with tapas, to the wife of <s>Īśa</s>.

children.text: īśa rajo me gopāya dravye tṛṣṇām īśasya patnyai tapaḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Īśa</s>, protect passion for me; protect thirst in material things. Svāhā, with tapas, to the wife of <s>Īśa</s>.

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevāya ṛtaṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect truth for me; protect faith in <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty). Homage, with ṛta, to <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevāya ṛtaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect truth for me; protect faith in <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty). Svāhā, with ṛta, to <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevasya patnyai ṛtaṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect truth for me; protect faith in <s>dharma</s> (sacred duty). Homage, with ṛta, to the wife of <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ mahādevasya patnyai ṛtaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Mahādeva</s>, protect truth for me; protect faith. Svāhā, with ṛta, to the wife of <s>Mahādeva</s>.

children.text: paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupataye devāya satyaṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; protect the state of enjoyer and enjoyed. Homage, with satya, to the god <s>Paśupati</s>.

children.text: paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupataye devasya satyaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; protect the state of enjoyer and enjoyed. Svāhā, with satya, to the god <s>Paśupati</s>.

children.text: oṃ paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupater devasya patnyai satyaṃ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; protect the state of enjoyer and enjoyed. Homage, with satya, to the wife of the god <s>Paśupati</s>.

children.text: oṃ paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupaterdevasya patnyai satyaṃ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O <s>Paśupati</s>, protect my bond; protect the state of enjoyer and enjoyed. Svāhā, with satya, to the wife of the god <s>Paśupati</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ. Svāhā, with satya, to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śivāya hotavyaṃ viriñcyādyaṃ ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: Thus the oblation should be offered to <s>Śiva</s>, beginning with <s>Viriñci</s>, as before,
and beginning with <s>Viriñci</s>, as previously stated, in the paths of creation, O you of good vows.

children.text: punaḥ paśupateḥ patnīṃ tathā paśupatiṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: Again, after worshiping the wife of <s>Paśupati</s> and then <s>Paśupati</s> in order,

children.text: sampūjya pūrvavanmantrair hotavyaṃ ca krameṇa vai ||
children.translated_text: the oblation should be offered in sequence with the mantras as before.
Intent, he should offer the caru, preceded by ghee and ending with fuel-sticks.

children.text: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me chinddhi ghrāṇe gandhaṃ chinddhi meghaṃ jahi bhūḥ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O <s>Śarva</s>, cut away earth for me; cut away smell in the nose; strike down the cloud. Bhūḥ, svāhā.
Bhuvaḥ, svāhā.
Svaḥ, svāhā.
Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, svāhā.
Having thus offered oblations separately, or with ghee alone,

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: either one thousand, or half of that, or one hundred and eight,
he should offer the <s>virajā</s> separately with ghee alone, one hundred and eight times,
and with the prāṇa and the others he should offer oblations with ghee alone.

children.text: oṃ prāṇe niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi śivo mā viśā pradāhāya prāṇāya svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Established in the breath, I offer the immortal oblation. May <s>Śiva</s> not enter me for burning. To the breath, svāhā.
To <s>Rudra</s>, lord of the breath and ender of the bull, svāhā.
Oṃ. Bhūḥ, svāhā.
Oṃ. Bhuvaḥ, svāhā.
Oṃ. Svaḥ, svāhā.
Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ, svāhā.
In this order he should offer the oblations, and also what is prescribed for the <s>śrāddha</s> in due sequence.
On the seventh day he should feed the foremost yogins who are worthy of the <s>śrāddha</s>.
To the brahmins representing <s>Śarva</s> and the others he should give garments, ornaments, and blankets,
a vehicle, a bed, a conveyance, and vessels of bronze, copper, and the like,

children.text: haimaṃ ca rājataṃ dhenuṃ tilān kṣetraṃ ca vaibhavam
children.translated_text: gold and silver, a cow, sesame seeds, land, and wealth,
as well as a host of female and male servants; the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (priestly fee) too should be given.
He should give the rice-ball as before, separately in eight forms,
and he should feed a thousand brahmins together with <s>dakṣiṇā</s>.
Or he may feed one man devoted to yoga, steadfast in ashes, and self-controlled.
For three days there should also be the offering of the great caru to <s>Rudra</s>.
Thus a special rite has been taught, enjoined for the whole <s>śrāddha</s>.

children.text: mṛte kuryānna kuryādvā jīvanmukto yataḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: When someone has died he may perform it or not perform it, for he himself is liberated while alive.

children.text: nityanaimittikādīni kuryād vā saṃtyajet tu vā
children.translated_text: He may perform or abandon the regular and occasional rites and the rest.

children.text: bāndhave 'pi mṛte tasya śaucāśaucaṃ na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Even when a kinsman of his has died, purity and impurity do not apply to him.

children.text: sūtakaṃ ca na saṃdehaḥ snānamātreṇa śudhyati
children.translated_text: There is also no birth-impurity; there is no doubt. He becomes pure by bathing alone,

children.text: paścājjāte kumāre ca sve kṣetre cātmano yadi ||
children.translated_text: if later a son is born in his own field, from himself.

children.text: tasya sarvaṃ prakartavyaṃ putro 'pi brahmavid bhavet
children.translated_text: Everything should be performed for him; even the son should become a knower of <s>brahman</s>.
If a daughter is born afterward to that great-souled one,

children.text: ekaparṇā iva jñeyā aparṇā iva suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: she should be known as like <s>Ekaparṇā</s>, like <s>Aparṇā</s>, O you of good vows.
This indeed occurs, without doubt, and even those born in her lineage
are freed; there is no doubt here. The ancestors too are freed even from hell.
By this rite they are freed on the mother's side and likewise on the father's side.

children.text: kālaṃ gate dvije bhūmau khaneccāpi dahettu vā
children.translated_text: When time has passed for a brahmin on earth, one may bury him or burn him.

children.text: putrakṛtyamaśeṣaṃ ca kṛtvā doṣo na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: Having performed all the duties of a son, there is no fault.
By any later rite no further course is obtained for him.
All this was told by <s>Brahmā</s> to the sages whose minds were cultivated.
Again it was told to <s>Sanatkumāra</s> by that wise one,
and to <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s> by the son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By the grace of that god, the wise <s>Vedavyāsa</s>,

children.text: jñātaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ caiva niyogādeva tasya tu ||
children.translated_text: I came to know it, and I have performed it by his command alone.
All this secret, which bestows perfection in <s>brahman</s>, has been told to you.
It should be given to the son of a sage, not to one who is not devoted, O you of good vows.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge jīvacchrāddhavidhir nāma pañcacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the forty-fifth chapter, named The Procedure for the Living <s>Śrāddha</s>.
The sages said:
The procedure for the living <s>śrāddha</s> has been taught by you, O greatly wise <s>Sūta</s>.
O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>, for the sake of liberation even for foolish people such as us,
O you of good vows, for the <s>Rudras</s>, <s>Ādityas</s>, and <s>Vasus</s>, and for <s>Śakra</s> and the others,
what sort of beautiful <s>pratiṣṭhā</s> (consecration) is there for <s>Śambhu</s> and for his <s>liṅga</s>-form?
And for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, for the god <s>Śakra</s>, and for great-souled <s>Brahmā</s>,
for <s>Agni</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, O greatly radiant one,
for <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Soma</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s>, and immeasurable-souled <s>Kubera</s>,
for <s>Īśāna</s> and for <s>Dharā</s>, how is the auspicious consecration to be done?
And what is the beautiful consecration of <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, and <s>Haimavatī</s>,
of <s>Skanda</s>, of the lord of the <s>Gaṇas</s>, and especially of <s>Nandin</s>?

children.text: tathānyeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ gaṇānāmapi vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: And again, for the other gods and also for the <s>gaṇas</s>,
you ought to tell us in full the entire defining rule of consecration.
You know the truth of all matters and are a devotee of <s>Rudra</s>, O you of good vows.
You are directly another body of <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>.
<s>Sumantu</s>, <s>Jaimini</s>, and <s>Paila</s> are indeed supreme seers;
and <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s> too is able to show devotion to the teacher.
Such was the extensive account of <s>Vyāsa</s> on the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>;

children.text: ekaḥ samo vā bhinno vā śiṣyastasya mahādyuteḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether that great-radiant one's pupil was equal or distinct,
on earth you are equal to <s>Vaiśaṃpāyana</s> among the pupils of <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Therefore you ought now to tell us everything without remainder.

children.text: evamuktvā sthiteṣveva teṣu sarveṣu tatra ca
children.translated_text: When they had spoken thus and were standing there, all of them together,
an exceedingly great wonder arose before those sages and him.
Then in the sky the great goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> herself

children.text: alaṃ munīnāṃ praśno 'yamiti vācā babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: spoke with a voice: 'This question of the sages is sufficient.'

children.text: sarvaṃ liṅgamayaṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ liṅge pratiṣṭhitam
children.translated_text: The whole world is made of <s>liṅga</s>; everything is established in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Therefore, abandoning everything else, one should install and worship it.
With oneself set upon the true path of installing the <s>liṅga</s>,
one quickly pierces the cosmic egg and goes forth without fear.
<s>Upendra</s>, lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and the lord of wealth,

children.text: tathānye ca śivaṃ sthāpya liṅgamūrtiṃ maheśvaram ||
children.translated_text: and likewise others, having installed <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s> in the form of the <s>liṅga</s>,

children.text: sveṣu sveṣu ca pakṣeṣu pradhānāste yathā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: are principal in their own respective divisions, O twice-born ones.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hara</s> the blessed one, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the goddess, <s>Ramā</s>, and <s>Dharā</s>,

children.text: lakṣmīrdhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ prajñā dharā durgā śacī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Prajñā</s>, <s>Dharā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, and likewise <s>Śacī</s>,

children.text: rudrāśca vasavaḥ skando viśākhaḥ śākha eva ca ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Rudras</s> and the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, and <s>Śākha</s>,
the blessed <s>Naigameśa</s>, and the <s>Lokapālas</s> and the planets,
all the <s>gaṇas</s> headed by <s>Nandin</s>, and the lord <s>Gaṇapati</s>,
the ancestors and all the sages, and the radiant ones beginning with <s>Kubera</s>,

children.text: ādityā vasavaḥ sāṃkhyā aśvinau ca bhiṣagvarau ||
children.translated_text: the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, and the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the best physicians,
the <s>Viśvedevās</s> and the <s>Sādhyas</s>, beasts, birds, and deer,
from <s>Brahmā</s> down to immovable things: everything is established in the <s>liṅga</s>.
Therefore, abandoning everything else, one should install the imperishable <s>liṅga</s>.
If one worships it, everything has thereby been carefully installed and worshiped.
Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the forty-sixth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: iti niśamya kṛtāñjalayas tadā divi mahāmunayaḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard this then in heaven, the great sages, with joined palms and firm resolve,

children.text: śivataraṃ śivamīśvaramavyayaṃ manasi liṅgamayaṃ praṇipatya te ||
children.translated_text: bowed in their minds to the most auspicious <s>Śiva</s>, the imperishable Lord, who is made of the <s>liṅga</s>.
The blessed unborn lord of all gods, <s>Hari</s>, lord of all, together with the teacher himself,

children.text: munivarāśca gaṇāśca surāsurā naravarāḥ śivaliṅgamayāḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the best sages, the <s>gaṇas</s>, gods and demons, and best men were again made of the <s>Śiva-liṅga</s>.
Having heard this, all the sages of the six families became concentrated,
and, abandoning everything else, set out to perform the consecration of the god.
With voices choked by joy they asked the sinless <s>Sūta</s>,
all those whose vows were renowned, about the extensive consecration of the <s>liṅga</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain to you the consecration of the <s>liṅga</s>-form,
properly and in sequence, briefly, for <s>dharma</s>, desire, prosperity, and liberation.

children.text: kṛtvaiva liṅgaṃ vidhinā bhuvi liṅgeṣu yatnataḥ
children.translated_text: Having made a <s>liṅga</s> according to rule, with care among <s>liṅgas</s> upon the earth,
one should choose a single stone <s>liṅga</s>, consisting of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,

children.text: hemaratnamayaṃ vāpi rājataṃ tāmrajaṃ tu vā
children.translated_text: or one made of gold and jewels, or else made of silver or copper,
with its pedestal and thread-mark, and with its head properly proportioned.
Having purified it, he should install with devotion the unsurpassed one, together with its pedestal.
The pedestal of the <s>liṅga</s> is the goddess <s>Umā</s>; the <s>liṅga</s> is directly <s>Maheśvara</s>.

children.text: tayoḥ sampūjanād eva devī devaśca pūjitau
children.translated_text: By worshiping those two, the goddess and the god are indeed worshiped.

children.text: pratiṣṭhayā ca deveśo devyā sārdhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Through the consecration the lord of gods is installed together with the goddess.
Therefore the best installer should install a <s>liṅga</s> together with its pedestal.

children.text: mūle brahmā vasati bhagavānmadhyabhāge ca viṣṇuḥ sarveśānaḥ paśupatirajo rudramūrtirvareṇyaḥ
children.translated_text: At the base dwells blessed <s>Brahmā</s>; in the middle part is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; and <s>Paśupati</s>, lord of all, the unborn one in <s>Rudra</s>-form, is supreme.

children.text: tasmālliṅgaṃ gurutarataraṃ pūjayetsthāpayedvā yasmātpūjyo gaṇapatirasau devamukhyaiḥ samastaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should worship or install the <s>liṅga</s> as exceedingly venerable, because it is worthy of worship by <s>Gaṇapati</s> and all the chief gods.

children.text: gandhaiḥ sragdhūpadīpaiḥ snapanahutabalistotramantropahārairnityaṃ ye 'bhyarcayanti tridaśavaratanuṃ liṅgamūrtiṃ maheśam
children.translated_text: Those who daily worship <s>Maheśa</s>, the <s>liṅga</s>-form whose body is the best of the gods, with perfumes, garlands, incense, lamps, baths, oblations, offerings, hymns, mantras, and gifts,

children.text: garbhādhānādināśakṣayabhayarahitā devagandharvamukhyaiḥ siddhairvandyāśca pūjyā gaṇavaranamitāste bhavantyaprameyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: become immeasurable, free from destruction, decay, and fear beginning with conception, honored by leading gods and gandharvas, worshiped by siddhas, and bowed to by the best <s>gaṇas</s>.
Therefore one should install <s>Parameśvara</s> with devotion and ritual service,
and should worship the <s>liṅga</s> especially, for the accomplishment of all aims.
Having worshiped it, he should install the <s>liṅga</s> in the midst of a sacred place, on the seat of <s>Śiva</s>,
and he should cover the <s>liṅga</s> with a <s>kūrca</s> (ritual brush), cloths, and the like, and then with jars.
with auspicious vessels sacred to the <s>Lokapālas</s> and other deities, furnished with <s>kūrcas</s> (ritual brushes) and unbroken grains,
with raised <s>kūrcas</s>, svastikas, and the like, wound about with variegated threads,
equipped with weapons such as the vajra, furnished with cloths and covers,
one should mark them all around the <s>liṅga</s>, which has been established by <s>Īśāna</s>.
It should be accompanied by incense and lamps, with canopies and spread cloths extended over it,
and with flags of the world-protectors, with painted elephants, buffaloes, and the like.
These should be painted and worshipped; and there should be a beautiful garland of darbha grass,
complete with all auspicious marks; with that he should wrap the outside.
Then he should let it rest ritually in water, accompanied by incense and lamps,

children.text: pañcāhaṃ vā tryahaṃ vātha ekarātram athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: for five days, or for three days, or else even for a single night.
There should be recitation of the Vedas, and auspicious dancing, singing, and the like,
accompanied by the sound of small bells and also by the sounds of cymbals and vīṇās.
The <s>yajamāna</s> (sacrificer), composed and undistracted, should watch for the proper time.
Having raised it up, he should meditate on the svastika in a pavilion furnished with the proper marks,
purified, supplied with an altar, and enclosed by nine fire-pits,
endowed with the rule stated before and complete with all the proper characteristics.
It should be furnished with eight maṇḍalas and with eight directional flags,
and with fire-pits possessing the characteristics described before, arranged in order beginning from the east.
The principal fire-pit, in the northeast, is prescribed as square,
or else there may be a set of five fire-pits, or just a single <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (ritual ground).
With all sacrificial implements and ornaments for the worship of <s>Śiva</s>,
he should prepare, in the middle of the altar, a great couch made with five layers of cotton,
adorned with gold and covered over with white cloth.
Having prepared it in this way, he should place <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme lord <s>Parameśvara</s>, there.
According to rule, with the <s>Īśāna</s> mantra, he should lay down the <s>liṅga</s> with its head toward the east.

children.text: ratnanyāse kṛte pūrvaṃ kevalaṃ kalaśaṃ nyaset ||
children.translated_text: When the deposition of gems has first been performed, he should place the <s>kalaśa</s> (consecration vessel) alone,
covering the <s>liṅga</s> on every side with two cloths and with a <s>kūrca</s>.
When the deposition of gems is underway, then the nine <s>śaktis</s> beginning with <s>Vāmā</s>,
together with the nine gems, gold and other substances, and the <s>pañcagavya</s> (five cow-products),
and accompanied by every kind of grain, he should also place upon the stone.
He should establish the <s>Brahma-liṅga</s> together with the <s>Śivagāyatrī</s>,
or he may establish imperishable <s>Śiva</s> simply with the <s>praṇava</s>.
With the <s>brahmajajñāna</s> mantra, likewise, he should install the Brahma portion of the lord,
and then he should install the Vaiṣṇava portion with the <s>Viṣṇugāyatrī</s>.
On the thread endowed with the three <s>tattvas</s> (principles), he should install it with the <s>praṇava</s>,

children.text: sarvaṃ namaḥ śivāyeti namo haṃsaḥ śivāya ca ||
children.translated_text: all with the formulas 'namaḥ śivāya' and 'namo haṃsaḥ śivāya'.

children.text: rudrādhyāyena vā sarvaṃ parimṛjya ca vinyaset
children.translated_text: Or, after purifying everything with the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, he should install it.
He should also set the <s>kalaśas</s> all around together with the brahmins,
and place all of them in the middle of the altar, furnished according to the rule stated before.
In the central <s>kumbha</s> he should place <s>Śiva</s> and the goddess; to the south, <s>Parameśvarī</s>;

children.text: skandaṃ tayośca madhye tu skandakuṃbhe sucitrite
children.translated_text: and <s>Skanda</s> between the two, in a well-painted <s>Skanda-kumbha</s>.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ skandakuṃbhe vā īśakumbhe hariṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He may place <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Skanda-kumbha</s>, or <s>Hari</s> likewise in the <s>Īśa-kumbha</s>,

children.text: athavā śivakuṃbhe ca brahmāṅgāni ca vinyaset
children.translated_text: or else he should install the limbs of <s>Brahmā</s> in the <s>Śiva-kumbha</s>.
<s>Śiva</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
these, in brief, are the brahma-forms; and <s>Ambikā</s> is connected with the heart and the other limbs.
He should place all of them in the middle of the altar, furnished according to the rule stated before.
He should establish the goddess in the <s>vardhanī</s> vessel and fill it with scented water.
He should place gold, silver, and gems in the <s>Śiva-kumbha</s>,
and carefully in the <s>vardhanī</s> also, O good-vowed ones, together with the limbs of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
He should place the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> in the directional <s>kumbhas</s>, filled with the <s>Brahma-kūrca</s>,
and the gods beginning with <s>Ananteśa</s>, with the formula beginning with the <s>praṇava</s> and ending in 'namaḥ'.
He should have a new cloth given for each jar among the eight <s>kumbhas</s>.
In the <s>kumbhas</s> of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> he should place gold, gems, and the like.
The oblation is to be offered in the order of the faces and in the order of the limbs of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
From the rite beginning with <s>Jayā</s> up to the <s>sviṣṭa</s> offering, he should perform everything as before.
He should sprinkle with the <s>Śiva-kumbha</s>, with the <s>vardhanī</s>, and with the Vaiṣṇava vessel,
and especially the Brahma portion with the <s>Paitāmaha-kumbha</s>.
He should sprinkle <s>Parameśvara</s> with the <s>kumbhas</s> of the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> also.
Fully concentrated, he should install all the mantras as before.
Having performed the bathing rite, he should worship with offerings produced in thousands and other such numbers.
A <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee) should be given; a thousand <s>paṇas</s> is the best amount.
For the others it should be half of that, or half of that again is prescribed.
Cloths should be given for the principal officiant, along with land, ornaments, and wealth in cows.
A festival should also be performed, with <s>homa</s>, sacrifice, and <s>bali</s> offerings in sequence.

children.text: navāhaṃ vāpi saptāham ekāhaṃ ca tryahaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: It may last for nine days, or seven days, or for one day, and likewise for three days.
The <s>homa</s> has been declared as before, after <s>Śaṅkara</s> has been worshipped daily.
For the gods beginning with <s>Bhāskara</s>, the <s>homa</s> is likewise just as before.

children.text: abhyantare tathā bāhye vahnau nityaṃ samarcayet ||
children.translated_text: Inside and outside, in the fire, he should worship every day.

children.text: ya evaṃ sthāpayelliṅgaṃ sa eva parameśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Whoever establishes the <s>liṅga</s> in this way is himself <s>Parameśvara</s>.
By him the hosts of gods, the <s>Rudras</s>, the seers, and the apsarases,
and the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings, have been established and worshipped.

children.text: iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge liṅgasthāpanaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>, in the latter part, the forty-seventh chapter, named 'Installation of the <s>Liṅga</s>'.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
For all the gods as well, he should perform the installation in detail,
laying out the sacrificial fire-pits one by one with their own mantras.
After performing a festival, he should establish each deity and worship it according to rule.
For <s>Bhānu</s>, the rite should be done with five fires, or according to the sequence of twelve fires.
All the altar-pits are round and lotus-shaped, O well-vowed ones.
For <s>Ambā</s> there should be a yoni-pit, and one vardhanī vessel is prescribed.
In all rites for the <s>Śaktis</s>, a yoni-pit is prescribed.
One should carefully fashion the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of <s>Śambhu</s> for all of them,
since all are born from portions of <s>Rudra</s>; I shall tell you briefly.
The varieties of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>:
May we know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; may we meditate on the one whose speech is purified;
may <s>Śiva</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Gaṇāmbikā</s>; may we meditate on success in rites;
may <s>Gaurī</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; may we meditate on <s>Mahādeva</s>;
may <s>Rudra</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; may we meditate on <s>Vakratuṇḍa</s>;
may <s>Dantin</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Mahāsena</s>; may we meditate on the one whose speech is purified;
may <s>Skanda</s> impel us.
May we know the sharp-horned one; may we meditate on the one whose feet are the Vedas;
may <s>Vṛṣa</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Harivaktra</s>; may we meditate on <s>Rudravaktra</s>;
may <s>Nandī</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; may we meditate on <s>Vāsudeva</s>;
may <s>Viṣṇu</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Mahāmbikā</s>; may we meditate on success in rites;
may <s>Lakṣmī</s> impel us.
May we know the one raised up; may we meditate on the one raised by <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone;
may <s>Dharā</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Vainateya</s>; may we meditate on the golden-winged one;
may <s>Garuḍa</s> impel us.
May we know the lotus-born one; may we meditate on the one whose face is the Veda;
may the Creator impel us.
May we know the one born from <s>Śiva</s>'s mouth; may we meditate on the one whose form is divine;
may <s>Vāc</s> impel us.
May we know the king of the gods; may we meditate on the one with the thunderbolt in his hand;
may <s>Śakra</s> impel us.
May we know the one who is <s>Rudra</s>'s eye; may we meditate on the one with the spear in his hand;
may <s>Vahni</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Vaivasvata</s>; may we meditate on the one with the staff in his hand;
may <s>Yama</s> impel us.
May we know the night-roaming one; may we meditate on the one with the sword in his hand;
may <s>Nirṛti</s> impel us.
May we know the pure-handed one; may we meditate on the one with the noose in his hand;
may <s>Varuṇa</s> impel us.
May we know the one whose breath is serpents; may we meditate on the one with the staff in his hand;
may <s>Vāyu</s> impel us.
May we know the lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>; may we meditate on the one with the mace in his hand;
may <s>Yakṣa</s> impel us.
May we know the lord of all; may we meditate on the one with the trident in his hand;
may <s>Rudra</s> impel us.
May we know <s>Kātyāyanī</s>; may we meditate on <s>Kanyākumārī</s>;
may <s>Durgā</s> impel us.
Having thus divided the <s>Gāyatrī</s> according to each deity,
he should worship and install them; the praṇava is remembered as their seat.
Or else, by means of the <s>Viṣṇu</s> hymn or the <s>Puruṣa</s> hymn,
he should install <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>, and <s>Sadāviṣṇu</s> in sequence.
He should install them with the deity's <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having arranged them according to rule.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> is the principal one; then comes <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> himself,
and <s>Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s>; these are indeed distinct forms of the Lord.
Here there are many and various forms of his, including those arising from a curse.

children.text: sarvāvarteṣu rūpāṇi jagatāṃ ca hitāya vai
children.translated_text: In every cycle, his forms exist for the welfare of the worlds:
<s>Matsya</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, then <s>Vārāha</s>, <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, and <s>Vāmana</s>;

children.text: rāmo rāmaśca kṛṣṇaśca bauddhaḥ kalkī tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Buddha</s>, and likewise <s>Kalki</s>;

children.text: tathānyāni na devasya hareḥ śāpodbhavāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and also other forms of the god <s>Hari</s>, including those arising from a curse.

children.text: teṣāmapi ca gāyatrīṃ kṛtvā sthāpya ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: Having made their <s>Gāyatrī</s> also, he should install and worship them.
These are the secret teachings of the god of gods, <s>Hari</s> <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
the sacred knowledges, yantras, and mantra-upaniṣads,
born here from the limbs of the five <s>Brahmans</s> and made of the five elements.
The mantra "namo nārāyaṇāya" is supremely splendid;
these are the eight syllables of <s>Hari</s>, together with the praṇava, in brief.

children.text: oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and homage to <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>;
homage indeed to <s>Pradyumna</s>, the chief one, and to <s>Aniruddha</s>.
With each mantra, one by one, he should install the Supreme Lord.
Whatever images there are of the god, of <s>Śiva</s>, of the supreme one,
their consecration and worship are like those of the liṅga, O best of sages.
The placing of jewels is included, and the protective wrist-bands for <s>Hari</s> as well.
For a fixed image he should have all this performed; for a movable one too, it is done according to this rule.
Then he should perform the opening of its eyes with the eye-mantra, O well-vowed ones.
The circumambulation of the sacred field, of the garden, and of the town,
and the immersion in water have been declared as before.
The construction of the pit and pavilion and the ritual bed are prescribed.
Having offered oblations according to rule in the nine pits with the division into nine fires,
or else in five pits, or only in the principal one,
the divine consecration has been taught, handed down in the traditional order.
For images made of stone, or again for a painted likeness,
immersion in water has been stated; that of the lordly bull has been proclaimed.
In the consecration of a temple, consecration has been described
for every limb of the temple, just as for the limbs of a body.
The bull, <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Mothers</s>, <s>Vighneśa</s>, and <s>Kumāra</s> too should be installed carefully,

children.text: śreṣṭhāṃ durgāṃ tathā caṇḍīṃ gāyatryā vai yathāvidhi ||
children.translated_text: as well as excellent <s>Durgā</s> and <s>Caṇḍī</s>, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> according to rule.
Beginning in the east, he should install the excellent eightfold enclosure of <s>Śambhu</s>,
and he should also arrange the <s>Lokapālas</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and the others belonging to <s>Śambhu</s>.

children.text: umā caṇḍī ca nandī ca mahākālo mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Umā</s>, <s>Caṇḍī</s>, <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and the great sage,
<s>Vighneśvara</s>, <s>Mahābhṛṅgī</s>, <s>Skanda</s>, and <s>Saumya</s> and the others, in sequence.
He should carefully establish <s>Indra</s> and the others in their own places, and also <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Janārdana</s>,
and likewise <s>Kṣetreśa</s> within the area of the entrance.
On the lion-throne he should establish <s>Ananta</s> and the others, and the <s>Vidyeśas</s> as well, in due order;
and with the praṇava he should establish the secret limbs and the rest in the lotus.
Thus the excellent mobile installation has been stated in brief
for all the gods and especially for the goddesses.
Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The greatness of <s>Aghoreśa</s> has previously been told by you.
O venerable one, you should tell us the worship and installation of that god.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The installation should be done especially according to rule with the <s>Aghora</s> mantra together with its limbs,
and by the rule for installing a liṅga; not otherwise, O best of sages.

children.text: tathāgnipūjāṃ vai kuryādyathā pūjā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Likewise one should perform the fire-worship just as the worship itself is performed:

children.text: sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā ||
children.translated_text: a thousand oblations, or half of that, or one hundred and eight.
The homa should be performed with sesame seeds mixed with curds, honey, and ghee,
and with ghee, roasted flour, and honey; it wipes away every sorrow.
The sesame homa destroys diseases and bestows prosperity.
With a thousand oblations there is great prosperity; with a hundred there is destruction of disease.
By japa one is freed from every sorrow; there is no doubt of this,
when it is done three times a day, according to rule, one hundred and eight times.
With one thousand and eight repetitions, after six months, there certainly arise
siddhis, without doubt, and even royal dominion.

children.text: sahasreṇa jvaro yāti kṣīreṇa ca juhoti yam
children.translated_text: Fever departs by a thousand oblations, when one offers with milk.
For one month, three times a day, he should offer a thousand oblations of milk.
Within a month his supreme great good fortune is accomplished.
It is also accomplished by a year-long homa joined with honey, ghee, and curds.
By a homa with barley, milk, and ghee, or with fine rice,
the blessed lord <s>Aghora</s>, the supreme <s>Īśvara</s>, is pleased.
With curds there is nourishment for kings, and by a milk homa there is pacification.
Having offered ghee for six months, there is destruction of all diseases.
Consumption disappears within a year from homas with sesame seeds.
By a barley homa there is long life, and by ghee there is victory.
For the removal of all skin disease and wasting, with rice grains smeared with honey
one should daily offer ten thousand oblations for six months, always self-restrained.
Ghee, milk, and honey are called the three sweet substances.
When used all together, the Lord is pleased with him, and it destroys fistula.
By a homa with ghee alone, the destruction of all disease is taught.
Meditation, installation according to rule, and worship remove every illness.
Thus, in brief, the entire installation and worship

children.text: pratiṣṭhā yajanaṃ sarvaṃ nandinā kathitaṃ purā ||
children.translated_text: of great-souled <s>Aghora</s> has been stated; it was formerly told by <s>Nandin</s>
to the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, his disciple, and by him to <s>Vyāsa</s>, O men of good vows.
Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The act of restraint, used against those who have committed offenses,
was taught by him, by the trident-bearing <s>Śiva</s>; you should tell us that, O man of good vows.

children.text: tvayā na viditaṃ nāsti laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: There is nothing, whether worldly or Vedic, unknown to you,
whether śrauta or smārta, O greatly fortunate <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>, O man of good vows.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Long ago the rite of restraint was taught to <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>, O men of good vows,
by the son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, the disciple of <s>Aghora</s>, whose splendor was imperishable.
By his favor, the mighty demon-lord <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>,
having conquered the whole triple world with its gods, demons, and humans,
and having begotten the son <s>Gaṇapa</s> and valiant <s>Andhaka</s>,
ruled in the world, until he was slain by the god in boar form.
For one who causes harm to women, harm to children,
and especially harm to cows, there is no victory on earth by this method.

children.text: tena daityena sā devī dharā nītā rasātalam
children.translated_text: By that demon the goddess Earth was carried down to <s>Rasātala</s>;
therefore the rite of restraint was made fruitless by the god <s>Aghora</s>.
At the end of a thousand years he was slain by <s>Varāha</s>.
Therefore, for the accomplishment of <s>Aghora</s>, one should never harm brahmins,
nor women in particular, and one should not cause harm to cows either.

children.text: guhyād guhyatamaṃ gopyam atiguhyaṃ vadāmi vaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell you a secret more secret than the secret, exceedingly secret and to be guarded.
It should be performed by the best of kings against an aggressor.

children.text: brāhmaṇebhyo na kartavyaṃ svarāṣṭreśasya vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should not be performed against brahmins, nor again against the lord of one's own realm.
When an exceedingly hard-to-conquer force has arrived, when all one's army has been destroyed,
and when an unrighteous war has arisen, then one should perform this unsurpassed rite.
It must be performed by one without pity, and he should have it performed by one without pity.
As soon as it has been done, there is no doubt, the restraint comes into being.
After a man has recited one hundred thousand times the terrible-formed <s>Aghora</s>,
he should offer a tenth part according to rule with sesame seeds, O best of twice-born men.
Having worshipped according to rule with one hundred thousand white flowers,
in a <s>bāṇaliṅga</s> or in the fire, resorting to <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti</s>,
he becomes one whose mantra is perfected; otherwise there is no seer, nor siddhis and the like.
One whose mantra is perfected should perform it himself, especially in a place of the dead,
or else in a place of the Mothers; the wise brahmin, versed in the Veda and Vedāṅgas,
or one merely perfected in mantra and filled with the nature of <s>Śiva</s>,
should perform this rite, being intelligent, for his own sake or for the sake of a king.
The learned man should place the set of eight <s>śūlas</s> (spears), beginning in the east and ending with the northeast.
He should make both the three-crested and the three-pronged spear, with twenty-four points at the tips,
and, having formed the image of <s>Aghora</s>, he should make his own body ritually identified with it.
Meditating on it as the destroyer of all, he should perform all the rites.
He should also conceive his own body as shining like ten million fires of time.

children.text: śūlaṃ kapālaṃ pāśaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ caiva śarāsanam
children.translated_text: The spear, skull, noose, staff, bow,
arrow, ḍamaru drum, and sword are the eight weapons in order.
He has eight hands, grants boons, is blue-throated, and is clothed in the directions.
The lord is mounted upon the five principles and bears the half-moon.
His face is terrible with fangs; his fierce gaze is fearsome.
The great sound of his cries of huṃ and phaṭ makes all the quarters resound.
He is three-eyed, and his crown itself is tightly bound with a serpent-noose.
He is endowed with every ornament and enveloped in ashes from corpses.
He is surrounded by bhūtas, pretas, piśācas, ḍākinīs, and rākṣasas,
covered with an elephant hide and adorned with ornaments of snakes.
One should meditate on the god adorned with scorpions, whose roar is like a dark rain-cloud,
who resembles a mountain of black collyrium and has a lion skin as his upper garment.
Thus should one meditate on <s>Aghoreśa</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, terrible and more than terrible.
With <s>prāṇāyāma</s> performed for the thirty-six stated measures, O you of good vows,
and joined with the great mudrā, he should perform all the rites.
With a perfected mantra, in a funeral fire or in a place of corpses, according to rule,

children.text: sthāpayenmadhyadeśe tu aindre yāmye ca vāruṇe
children.translated_text: he should establish it in the central region, and in the eastern, southern, western,
and northern directions, making the fire-pits properly according to the scripture.

children.text: ācāryo madhyakuṇḍe tu sādhakāśca diśāsu vai
children.translated_text: The ācārya should be at the central pit, and the practitioners in the directions.
Having strewn the ground counterclockwise, equipped with the spear as before,
he himself should stand in the middle of the seat of the fire of time, together with disciples like himself,
and meditate on the terrible <s>Aghoreśa</s>, endowed with the thirty-two-syllabled mantra.
Making an image from vibhītaka wood, measuring twelve finger-breadths,
he should place it on the seat for the king's enemy with charcoal on a Tuesday.
A brahmin, overcome with wrath, should dig the enemy beneath the pit,
carefully in all the pits, face downward and feet upward.
Having brought charcoal from the cremation ground, he should burn it together with husks.
There he should set up the fire silently, devoted to celibacy.
Then, by means of the peacock weapon, he should kindle the fire at the navel.
With a coat mixed with husks and together with cotton seeds,
with mixtures equal to red cloth, and especially with gold substances,
and with oils produced by hand-presses, he should cause the oblation to be performed.
He should offer one thousand and eight oblations, one after another,
beginning on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight in due order,
continuing until the eighth day, while avoiding the place of the charcoal circle.

children.text: evaṃ kṛte nṛpendrasya śatravaḥ kulajaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: When this is done, the enemies of the king, together with their families,
afflicted by every suffering, go to the abode of <s>Yama</s>.
Taking with this mantra, in a human skull, a nail,

children.text: keśaṃ nṛṇāṃ tathāṅgāraṃ tuṣaṃ kañcukameva ca
children.translated_text: the hair of men, charcoal, husks, and the coat,
a ragged strip of cloth, royal dust, or the sweepings of a house,
the teeth of a poisonous snake, and the teeth of bulls,
and likewise, in order, those of cows, and the teeth and claws of a tiger,

children.text: tathā kṛṣṇamṛgāṇāṃ ca biḍālasya ca pūrvavat
children.translated_text: and similarly of black antelopes and of a cat as before,
and the teeth of a mongoose, especially the tusks of a boar,
after preparing them with this mantra, O you of good vows,
he should recite the excellent Aghora mantra one hundred and eight times.

children.text: tatkapālaṃ nakhaṃ kṣetre gṛhe vā nagare 'pi vā
children.translated_text: That skull and nail, in a field, a house, or even a city,
or in a place of corpses or a kingdom, he should wrap in a dead man's cloth.
When the sun is surrounded by a halo in the eighth sign from the enemy,

children.text: some vā pariviṣṭe tu mantreṇānena suvratāḥ ||
children.translated_text: or when the moon is surrounded by a halo, with this mantra, O you of good vows,
the destruction of that place will occur, and the enemy's destruction will arise.
Having drawn the king's enemy when he is ready to depart,
on ground like a mirror, adorned above with a canopy,
furnished with four arches and surrounded by garlands of darbha grass,
in a kingdom endowed with Vedic study and manifesting prosperity,
he himself should strike the enemy's head with his right foot.
When this is done, the king's enemy will be destroyed.
Whoever performs an abhicāra rite aimed at the lord of his own kingdom,

children.text: sa ātmānaṃ nihatyaiva svakulaṃ nāśayet kudhīḥ
children.translated_text: that foolish man destroys himself and destroys his own family.
Therefore one should always protect the king, the guardian of one's own kingdom,
with mantras, herbs, rites, and the like, with every effort at all times.

children.text: etadrahasyaṃ kathitaṃ na deyaṃ yasya kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: This secret has been told; it should not be given to just anyone.
Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the fiftieth chapter.
The sages said:
This restraint, terrible in form, has been taught to us as supreme.
You should teach the <s>vajravāhanikā</s> vidyā, O best of the good.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The vidyā called <s>vajravāhanikā</s> is terrifying to all enemies.
With it one should sprinkle the vajra, and thereby accomplish the aims of kings.
Having made the vajra according to rule and consecrated that vajra,

children.text: anayā vidyayā tasmin vinyaset kāñcanena ca ||
children.translated_text: with this vidyā he should install something golden upon it.
Then the learned man, concentrated, should recite one hundred thousand syllables,
and one possessing the vajra should offer a tenth part in the vajra-fire-pit with ghee and other substances.
He should always keep that vajra hidden, and afterward cause it to be given to the king.
With that thunderbolt, going forth, one would conquer enemies on the battlefield.
Long ago the vidyā was obtained with effort by <s>Pitāmaha</s> himself.
The goddess, directly <s>Vajreśvarī</s>, was for the sake of aiding <s>Śakra</s>.
Long ago <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, lord of creatures, whose son had been killed by the lord of the gods,
out of enmity toward <s>Indra</s>, O men of good vows, was taking away the soma by means of the vidyā.
In that sacrifice, the oblation that had been properly prepared according to rule,
the mighty-armed destroyer of <s>Viśvarūpa</s> then desired.

children.text: matputramavadhīḥ śakra na dāsye tava śobhanam
children.translated_text: "You have killed my son, O <s>Śakra</s>; I will not give you what is fitting.
The share is not yours by right to a share; <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, who was entitled to the share, was killed by you."
Having spoken thus, he bewildered the whole hermitage with his māyā (illusion).
Then, breaking through that māyā, the destroyer of <s>Viśvarūpa</s>
forcibly drank the soma together with his hosts, the lord of <s>Śacī</s>.
Then, taking what remained of it, the lord of creatures, filled with anger,

children.text: indrasya śatror vardhasva svāhetyagnau juhāva ha
children.translated_text: offered it into the fire, saying, "Grow, enemy of <s>Indra</s>; svāhā."
Then one like the fire of time, called <s>Vṛtra</s> from his enveloping movement,
appeared as the enemy of the lords of the gods, and the destroyer of foes fled.
Then the blessed crowned one, abandoning heaven in an instant,
the thousand-eyed one with his hosts, fled, distraught with fear.

children.text: tadā tamāha sa vibhur hṛṣṭo brahmā ca viśvasṛṭ ||
children.translated_text: Then that powerful <s>Brahmā</s>, creator of the universe, delighted, said to him:
"Hurl the thunderbolt; with this kill that enemy, O subduer of enemies."

children.text: so 'pi saṃnahya devendro devaiḥ sārdhaṃ mahābhujaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Devendra</s> too, the mighty-armed one, having armed himself together with the gods,
killed him without effort and went away, free from feverish distress.
Therefore the Vajreśvarī vidyā is terrifying to all enemies.

children.text: mandehā rākṣasā nityaṃ vijitā vidyayaiva tu
children.translated_text: The <s>Mandeha</s> rākṣasas are always conquered by this vidyā alone.
I shall teach that vidyā, which releases one from all sins.

children.text: oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyaṃ bhargo devasya dhīmahi
children.translated_text: Oṃ, earth, midspace, heaven: let us meditate on that excellent radiance of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>;
may he impel our thoughts.

children.text: oṃ phaṭ jahi huṃ phaṭ chinddhi bhinddhi jahi hana hana svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ phaṭ, strike! huṃ phaṭ, cut, split, strike, slay, slay, svāhā.
This is the vidyā called <s>Vajreśvarī</s>, terrifying to all enemies.
By this vidyā, O foremost sages, there is <s>Śambhu</s>'s power of destruction.
Thus ends the fifty-first chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
We have heard the Brāhmī Vajreśvarī vidyā, which aids <s>Śakra</s>.
By it all the undertakings of kings are accomplished; so we have heard.
Tell us the application of this vidyā, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Subjugation and attraction, and after that the causing of hatred,

children.text: uccāṭanaṃ stambhanaṃ ca mohanaṃ tāḍanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: expulsion, immobilization, bewilderment, and striking,
destruction, cutting, killing, and binding,
and such acts as immobilizing an army: one should perform all these by means of the Sāvitrī.
"Come, boon-giving goddess, to the earth, to the mountain peak;
permitted by the brahmins, go, goddess, as you please."
With this mantra she is to be dismissed; it should not be done otherwise, O twice-born men.

children.text: pratikāryaṃ tathā bāhyaṃ kṛtvā vaśyādikāṃ kriyām
children.translated_text: After performing the counter-rite and the external rite, and the action such as subjugation,
one should dismiss her, establish the fire, and then, again, another rite according to rule.

children.text: devīmāvāhya ca punar japet sampūjayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having invoked the goddess again, one should recite and worship again.

children.text: homaṃ ca vidhinā vahnau punareva samācaret ||
children.translated_text: Again one should duly perform the homa in the fire.
By the vidyā one should again accomplish all undertakings according to rule.
One who seeks subjugation should offer thirty thousand oblations with jasmine flowers.
With ghee and oleander one should perform attraction, O twice-born men.
One should especially perform the causing of hatred with <s>lāṅgalaka</s>.
Expulsion is said to be done with oil; immobilization is remembered as done with honey.

children.text: tilena mohanaṃ proktaṃ tāḍanaṃ rudhireṇa ca ||
children.translated_text: Bewilderment is said to be done with sesame, and striking with blood,

children.text: kharasya ca gajasyātha uṣṭrasya ca yathākramam
children.translated_text: of a donkey, an elephant, and then a camel, respectively.

children.text: staṃbhanaṃ sarṣapeṇāpi pāṭanaṃ ca kuśena ca ||
children.translated_text: Immobilization is also done with mustard seed, and splitting with kuśa grass.
Killing and expulsion are done with <s>rohī</s> seed, O men of good vows.
Binding, however, is done with snake-leaf; next comes immobilization of an army.
One should know it is certainly done with <s>kunaṭī</s>, and should worship <s>Parameśvarī</s>.
With ghee there is success in everything; with milk one is purified.
With sesame there is destruction of disease, and with lotus there is wealth.
With madhūka flowers there is beauty, through the Sāvitrī, with thirty thousand recitations.
All rites beginning with victory and ending with the sviṣṭa offering are remembered as before.
Thus, in brief, the very extensive application has been stated.

children.text: japedvā kevalāṃ vidyāṃ sampūjya ca vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: Or, having worshipped according to rule, one may recite the vidyā alone.
He obtains every accomplishment; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus ends the fifty-second chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
The rite of Mṛtyuñjaya for brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, O <s>Sūta</s>,
you should tell us, for you are all-knowing, O great-minded one.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain the Mṛtyuñjaya rite; what need is there of much speech, O best twice-born men?
With the <s>Rudrādhyāya</s>, according to rule, one should offer one hundred thousand oblations with ghee in sequence;
also with sesame together with ghee, and carefully with lotus,
with dūrvā grass mixed with ghee and cow's milk, and with honey,
with caru together with ghee, or even with milk alone.
One should offer oblations; this is proclaimed as the remedy against time and death.
Thus ends the fifty-third chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
With the Tryambaka mantra one should worship the god of gods, <s>Tryambaka</s>,
either in a <s>bāṇaliṅga</s>, or again in a self-born liṅga.
or also by those versed in <s>āyurveda</s>, properly and in due sequence,
one should worship <s>Śaṅkara</s> with one thousand and eight white lotuses.
Likewise, with a thousand lotuses, or else with blue water-lilies,

children.text: sampūjya pāyasaṃ dattvā saghṛtaṃ caudanaṃ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: having worshipped him, one should give milk-rice with ghee, and again boiled rice.

children.text: mudgānnaṃ madhunā yuktaṃ bhakṣyāṇi surabhīṇi ca
children.translated_text: There should be rice with mung beans mixed with honey, and fragrant foods as well,
and an ample <s>homa</s> in the fire, properly and in due sequence.
With the flowers mentioned before, and especially with the sacrificial porridge,

children.text: japedvai niyutaṃ samyak samāpya ca yathākramam ||
children.translated_text: one should duly recite one <s>niyuta</s> times, and complete the rite in order.
He should feed a thousand brahmins, together with gifts of honor,

children.text: gavāṃ sahasraṃ dattvā tu hiraṇyamapi dāpayet ||
children.translated_text: and, after giving a thousand cows, he should also have gold given.
All this has been told to you, together with its secret, in brief,
by <s>Śiva</s>, the god of gods, by <s>Śarva</s>, the very fierce trident-bearer.
It was told on the summit of <s>Meru</s> to <s>Skanda</s> of immeasurable splendor,
and by <s>Skanda</s>, the god of gods, to the wise son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
By <s>Sanatkumāra</s> himself, who seeks the welfare of all worlds,
it was told to <s>Pārāśarya</s>, having come down in the order of tradition.

children.text: śuke gate paraṃ dhāma dṛṣṭvā rudraṃ triyaṃbakam
children.translated_text: When <s>Śuka</s> had gone to the supreme abode after seeing <s>Rudra</s>, the three-eyed one,

children.text: gataśoko mahābhāgo vyāsaḥ para ṛṣiḥ prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: the greatly fortunate <s>Vyāsa</s>, the supreme seer and lord, became free from grief.

children.text: skandasya saṃbhavaṃ śrutvā sthitāya ca mahātmane
children.translated_text: To that great-souled one, who remained after hearing of the birth of <s>Skanda</s>,
the greatness of <s>Triyaṃbaka</s>, and especially of the <s>mantra</s>,
was told in many ways to <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> himself.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ kathayiṣyāmi prasādādeva tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: All that I shall tell, solely through his grace.
Having worshipped the god according to rule, one should recite the <s>Triyaṃbaka</s> mantra.
He is freed even from all sins committed through seven births.
In battle, having obtained all that, he will possess incomparable good fortune.

children.text: lakṣahomena rājyārthī rājyaṃ labdhvā sukhī bhavet ||
children.translated_text: One who desires a kingdom, by a <s>homa</s> of one hundred thousand oblations, obtains a kingdom and becomes happy.
One who desires a son obtains a son by a <s>niyuta</s> of recitations; there is no doubt.
One who desires wealth should recite with a <s>prayuta</s> of repetitions; there is no doubt.
Filled with all wealth, grain, and the rest, and with every auspicious thing,
he sports with sons and grandsons, and after death is born in heaven.

children.text: nānena sadṛśo mantro loke vede ca suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: There is no <s>mantra</s> equal to this in the world or in the Veda, O men of good vows.
Therefore one should worship the god <s>Triyaṃbaka</s> with it every day.
The result is eight times that of the <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifice.
He is the lord even of the three worlds and of the guṇas.
He is lord also of the Vedas, of the gods, and of brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas,
and he is the expresser of the syllables a, u, and m, and of their measures.
Likewise he is lord of the moon, the sun, fire, and the three sacred fires.
<s>Ambā</s>, <s>Umā</s>, and <s>Mahādeva</s>: he is <s>Ambaka</s>, indeed <s>Triyaṃbaka</s>.
As the very beautiful fragrance of a tree in full flower

children.text: vāti dūrāt tathā tasya gandhaḥ śaṃbhormahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: wafts from afar, so too is the fragrance of that great-souled <s>Śambhu</s>.
Therefore the blessed <s>Śaṅkara</s> is fragrant and makes things fragrant.
<s>Mahādeva</s> is also <s>Gāndhāra</s>, even among the gods, by his play.
His fragrance in this world is the wind that blows in the expanse of the sky.
Therefore we worship that fragrant god, fragrant and increasing nourishment.
The seed of <s>Śambhu</s> was formerly placed in the womb of <s>Hari</s>.
From his virility arose the golden egg, unborn in origin.
The moon and sun, together with the stars, and the worlds <s>bhūr</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svar</s>, <s>mahas</s>, and <s>tapas</s>,
having surpassed even <s>Satyaloka</s>, are the nourishment of that virility.
The five elements, ego, intellect, and primordial nature as well
are the nourishment of that very seed; therefore he is the increaser of nourishment.

children.text: taṃ puṣṭivardhanaṃ devaṃ ghṛtena payasā tathā
children.translated_text: We worship that god who increases nourishment with ghee and also with milk,
with honey, barley, wheat, black gram, and bilva fruit,
with water-lilies, arka leaves, śamī leaves, white mustard, and rice,

children.text: hutvā liṅge yathānyāyaṃ bhaktyā devaṃ yajāmahe ||
children.translated_text: having offered them properly at the <s>liṅga</s>, worshipping the god with devotion.
By this truth, from the noose, from bondage arising from the connection of karma,
and from death's bondage as well, may I be released, O <s>Bhava</s>, through your power.
Just as ripe cucumbers, when their time has come, are separated again,

children.text: tathaiva kālaḥ samprāpto manunā tena yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: so too the time has arrived, through that <s>mantra</s>, with effort.
Knowing the rite of the <s>mantra</s> in this way, one should worship the <s>Śivaliṅga</s>.
For him there is utter destruction of bonds, and for the yogin, restraint of death.
There is no god equal to <s>Triyaṃbaka</s>, endowed with compassion,
gracious by nature and pleased; likewise the <s>mantra</s> is so, O men of good vows.
Therefore, abandoning everything else, one should worship <s>Triyaṃbaka</s>, the lord of <s>Umā</s>,
with the <s>Triyaṃbaka</s> mantra, being well concentrated.
Even one who has reached every condition is freed from all sins
by meditation on <s>Śiva</s>; there is no doubt. As is <s>Rudra</s>, so he himself becomes.

children.text: hatvā bhittvā ca bhūtāni bhuktvā cānyāyato 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Even after killing and breaking living beings, or eating what is improper,
by remembering <s>Śiva</s> alone once, one is released from all sins.
