Thus ends the fifty-fourth chapter in the latter part of the glorious <s>Liṅgamahāpurāṇa</s>.
The sages said:
How should the god <s>Triyaṃbaka</s>, the god of gods whose banner bears the bull,
be meditated upon by the path of yoga for the accomplishment of all aims, O man of good vows?
All this has indeed been heard before, and again as equal to revelation,
but you should tell all that at length and also in summary.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus <s>Nandī</s>, shining like the sun, was formerly asked by the son of <s>Brahmā</s>
on the back of <s>Meru</s>, surrounded by assemblies of sages.
He too spoke it to that <s>Kumāra</s>, the son of <s>Brahmā</s>, O men of good vows.
Then the Blessed Lord, composed, spoke privately to the one who had bowed down.
<s>Nandikeśvara</s> said:
Thus in ancient times the Blessed <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
while sharing one couch with the blessed goddess <s>Ambā</s>, daughter of the Mountain,
was questioned on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>, the hairs of his body bristling with delight.
The revered Goddess said:
How many kinds of yoga are taught, and what is it, and what is its character?

children.text: jñānaṃ ca mokṣadaṃ divyaṃ mucyante yena jantavaḥ
children.translated_text: And what is the divine knowledge that grants liberation, by which living beings are released?
The Blessed Lord said:
The first is mantra-yoga, and sparśa-yoga is the second.
Bhāva-yoga is the third, abhāva is the fourth,
and the supreme of all, mahāyoga, is proclaimed as the fifth.
The practice of japa joined with meditation is called mantra-yoga.
That which chiefly purifies the nāḍīs and is furnished with the sequence beginning with exhalation,
the mastery of breath through combined and separate yoga, is declared to be victory over the wind.
A practice endowed with strong and steady action and with auspicious dhāraṇās,
illumined by the three dhāraṇās and purifying the three divisions,
an exercise established in kumbhaka, is called sparśa-yoga.
Free from mantra and touch, taking refuge in <s>Mahādeva</s>,
standing in the distinction between outer and inner, and consisting of manifestation and withdrawal,
it is called bhāva-yoga, the giver of purity of mind.
Where the whole world, moving and unmoving, has all its members dissolved,

children.text: śūnyaṃ sarvaṃ nirābhāsaṃ svarūpaṃ yatra cintyate
children.translated_text: and everything is contemplated as empty, without appearance, as its own true form,
that is taught as abhāva-yoga, which brings about the extinction of the mind.

children.text: nīrūpaḥ kevalaḥ śuddhaḥ svacchandaṃ ca suśobhanaḥ
children.translated_text: Formless, solitary, pure, free, and most beautiful,
indescribable, ever luminous, self-known, and then equal,
where one's own nature shines forth: that is called mahāyoga.
Ever arisen, self-luminous, arising in every mind,

children.text: nirmalaḥ kevalo hyātmā mahāyoga iti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: the stainless, solitary self is remembered as mahāyoga.
All these grant powers such as aṇimā, and all are givers of knowledge.
Among these yogas there is, in order, a successively higher distinction.
I am free from attachment, supreme, like the great ether,
freed from every covering, and inconceivable by my own essence.
This knowable reality has been described, though it is not graspable even by the gods.
Fully dissolved, great, self-known, and witness to itself,
it shines with a body of bliss; therefore this is regarded as the knowable reality.
It should be given in due order to a tested disciple, to a brahmin who maintains the sacred fires,
to one who is righteous and not ungrateful.
It should be given to one devoted to guru and deity; otherwise one should never impart it.
One becomes censured, diseased, and short-lived, and is born so again,
and the giver too becomes the same, O sinless one; therefore one should impart it only after knowing this.
A practitioner free from all attachment, devoted to me and intent upon me,
joined with knowledge and expert in śrauta and smārta tradition,
devoted to the guru, pure-souled, fit, and always intent on yoga, is worthy.
Thus, O Goddess, the eternal path of yoga has been explained,
the sweet nectar of the lotus of all the Vedas and Āgamas, O fair-waisted one.
Having drunk the nectar of yoga, the yogin, best knower of brahman, is released.
Thus this Pāśupata yoga, the unsurpassed yogic sovereignty,
should be understood as beyond the āśramas and for liberation. By whom is it obtained?
Therefore, O dear one, it is obtained by those of proper conduct who are devoted to the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having spoken thus and having dismissed the Goddess, the Blessed Lord, whose banner bears the bull,
approached <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s> and yoked the self in the self.
<s>Śailādi</s> said:
Therefore you too, O lord of yogins, should be devoted to the practice of yoga.
The supreme form of the Self-born is surely excellent and made of brahman.
Therefore, with every effort, a supreme person seeking liberation
should always bathe in ashes and be devoted to Pāśupata yoga.

children.text: dhyeyā yathākrameṇaiva vaiṣṇavī ca tataḥ parā
children.translated_text: The Vaiṣṇavī form is to be meditated upon in proper order, and then the higher one after that;
afterward the supreme Māheśvarī form is to be meditated upon, just in that order.

children.text: yogeśvarasya yā niṣṭhā saiṣā saṃhṛtya varṇitā ||
children.translated_text: This firm state of the Lord of Yogins has now been described in summary.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus Pāśupata yoga was taught by <s>Nandin</s>, the son of <s>Śilāda</s>, joy of his family,
the wise one firmly established in ashes.
The Blessed <s>Sanatkumāra</s> taught it to <s>Vyāsa</s> of immeasurable splendor;
and having heard it from him, I too, by the command of the sacrificial priests,

children.text: kṛtakṛtyo 'smi viprebhyo namo yajñebhya eva ca
children.translated_text: am fulfilled in my duty toward the brahmins. Homage also to the sacrifices.

children.text: namaḥ śivāya śāntāya vyāsāya munaye namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Homage to peaceful <s>Śiva</s>; homage to the sage <s>Vyāsa</s>.
This excellent <s>Liṅga Purāṇa</s> has eleven thousand verses;
its first part has one hundred and eight chapters, and after that
there is a section of forty-six chapters, granting <s>dharma</s>, desire, wealth, and liberation.

children.text: atha te munayaḥ sarve naimiṣeyāḥ samāhitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then all those sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, composed in mind,
bowed to the god <s>Īśāna</s>, their skin bristling with joy.
Having thus made the Purāṇic branch elevenfold, the lord,
the Blessed Self-born <s>Brahmā</s>, spoke these words:
Whoever reads or even hears the entire <s>Liṅga Purāṇa</s>, from beginning to end,

children.text: dvijebhyaḥ śrāvayedvāpi sa yāti paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: or causes brahmins to hear it, goes to the supreme state.
By austerity, sacrifice, giving, and study,

children.text: yā gatistasya vipulā śāstravidyā ca vaidikī
children.translated_text: and by Vedic knowledge of the śāstras, whatever vast state is his,

children.text: karmaṇā cāpi miśreṇa kevalaṃ vidyayāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: whether through mixed ritual action or through knowledge alone,
cessation will arise for that brahmin, and eternal devotion too,

children.text: mayi nārāyaṇe deve śraddhā cāstu mahātmanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and may the great-souled one have faith in me, the god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
And there was imperishable knowledge of the lineage, and heedfulness in every respect;
such was the command of <s>Brahmā</s>. Therefore everything belonged to that great-souled one.
The sages said:

children.text: ṛṣeḥ sūtasya cāsmākam eteṣām api cāsya ca
children.translated_text: The attainment that belongs to the sage, to <s>Sūta</s>, to us, to these men, and also to him,
and to <s>Nārada</s>, who delights in pilgrimage to holy places,
and the abundant favor by which it is ours, O <s>Romaharṣaṇa</s>,
may that always be present everywhere through the grace of <s>Virūpākṣa</s>.
When the brahmins had spoken thus, the blessed <s>Nārada</s> also
touched <s>Sūta</s> on the body with his two hands, whose fingertips were beautiful.

children.text: svastyastu sūta bhadraṃ te mahādeve vṛṣadhvaje ||
children.translated_text: May there be well-being, O <s>Sūta</s>; good fortune to you in <s>Mahādeva</s>, the bull-bannered one.

children.text: śraddhā tavāstu cāsmākaṃ namastasmai śivāya ca ||
children.translated_text: May you have faith, and may we have it too. Homage also to that <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus, in the latter part of the holy <s>Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa</s>, the fifty-fifth chapter.
